title: GitHub sign-in: a bad code answered HTTP 200 {error} is not refused - the adapter calls /user with 'Bearer undefined' and relies on GitHub's 401
description:
**BLUF:** GitHub answers a bad or expired sign-in code with **HTTP 200** and an `{error, error_description}` body, not an error status. The GitHub adapter never checks that the answer carries an `access_token`: it calls `/user` with `Bearer undefined` and relies on GitHub answering that 401. Low, defence in depth. Against real GitHub the profile call fails and no sign-in happens; the guard is GitHub's 401, not this code.

* **Where.** `services/auth/src/providers/social/github.ts` at #1788's head `7eeedb825c5c`:
  * `:79-84`: the `!tokenRes.ok` branch handles only a non-2xx answer.
  * `:86`: `const { access_token } = (await tokenRes.json())`, with no check that it exists.
  * `:88-91`: the profile call sends `Authorization: Bearer ${access_token}`.
* **Measured** by the tier-1 delta gate on #1788 (gate 7, probe P4, real routes, stub provider). GitHub's token endpoint answering `200 {error, error_description}` completed the sign-in under the test stub, because the stub's `/user` ignores the Bearer. Against real GitHub, `/user` answers 401, the adapter throws "Failed to fetch GitHub user profile", and the callback answers 400. Not driven against GitHub.
* **Fix.** Refuse a token answer with no `access_token` (or one carrying an `error` field) as a token-exchange failure, before any profile call. Then a stub, a proxy or a GitHub change in that 401 cannot turn a refused code into a sign-in.
* **Not in #1788's scope.** #1788 bounds the calls and classifies timeouts and unreachable providers; it does not change how a 200 answer is read.

**Searched before filing.** Team KS, issue titles and descriptions including archived, plus comment bodies, 2026-10-28 \~12:2xZ (issues / comments):

* No hits: "Bearer undefined" 0 / 0, "bad_verification_code" 0 / 0.
* "access_token": 3 issues, KS-942 (wallet auth), KS-632 (M365) and KS-488 (S↔K review), all Done and none about GitHub or social sign-in.
* "github.ts": KS-722, about the OAuth state check.
* Positive control "KS-1791": 1 comment, on KS-1617. A freshly coined zero control: 0 / 0.

**Refs:** KS-1240; PR #1788; gate verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-28_gate7-tier1/verdict.md`, finding 1788-13. Filed on the coordinator's instruction (ANSWER 12:18Z), assigned to the board account.

title: check-no-sql-injection.sh: the pre-push scan reads all 26 node_modules trees under services/ and packages/ (125-172 s cold per fresh worktree), and a real hit dies under set -u unreported
description:
**BLUF:** Two faults in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-sql-injection.sh`, the pen-test M6 guard that leg 15/16 of the pre-push preflight runs on every push.

1. **The scan reads every installed package.** Its grep walks all 26 `node_modules` trees under `services/` and `packages/` (14,439 files) and drops their hits only afterwards. On a freshly created worktree that costs 125-172 s cold, so about 2 minutes of every push from a new worktree. With `--exclude-dir=node_modules` the same run takes 9 s.
2. **A real hit is not reported.** When the scan does find a violation, the error headline expands `$queryRawUnsafe` and `$executeRawUnsafe` unescaped under `set -u`. The script dies with `queryRawUnsafe: unbound variable` (exit 1) and prints neither the offending file and line nor the Fix hint.

Both were measured at develop `85cd24d81cb9` on 2026-10-30.

## Fault 1: the scan reads node_modules

* Line 28, `grep -rEn --include=... services/ packages/`, has no `--exclude-dir`. Line 31's `grep -v 'node_modules|...'` removes those paths only after every file has been read. Its sibling guards `check-no-trust-header-reads.sh`, `check-no-default-passwords.sh` and `check-no-math-random.sh` exclude at the grep instead.
* Measured on darwin arm64 at load 8-12. No cache purge was available, so "cold" means a worktree whose cloned files had never been read:

| Run | As-is | With the exclusion |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Fresh worktree, cold (the excluded run went first) | 125.26 s | 9.03 s |
| A second fresh worktree, cold | 172.46 s | not run |
| Warm, three alternated runs (median) | 3.08 s | 0.33 s |

* The whole `run-code-guards.sh` (13 guards) on a fresh worktree takes 211.35 s cold and 15-19 s warm, so this guard is most of it. The three sibling tree-walkers cost 0.4-7.4 s cold each.
* Both forms give the same result on the tree: 0 hits, exit 0.

## Fault 2: a real hit is not reported

* Line 35 is `echo "::error::SQL injection risk — $queryRawUnsafe / $executeRawUnsafe used with template-literal interpolation:"`, inside double quotes, under `set -euo pipefail`.
* Reproduced with the real `/usr/bin/grep` and `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 on a throwaway tree, with one planted violation in `services/x/src/repo.ts`. Exit is 1, and the only output is `line 35: queryRawUnsafe: unbound variable`. The push is refused, but nothing names the file.

## Fix (in review)

Two held Spark passes, raised as one pull request:

* `--exclude-dir=node_modules` on the line-28 grep. The post-filter stays as a second safeguard.
* The two `$` on line 35 escaped.

Each fix has its own shell suite in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/`, red at develop and green after. The pull request links here.

## Not in scope

* The timing comment at `run-code-guards.sh` lines 72-76 ("\~10 s", measured 2026-09-14) is stale against these numbers. It is not changed here.
* `--exclude-dir=dist` is not added: `dist` is one directory of 360 files here.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request returns any tenant document's content hash and a signing nonce to any authenticated caller
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1223-1265` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only. For any document in the tenant it returns the document's `contentHash` and a signing nonce, and stores a signing request, even to a caller that `GET /api/documents/:id` refuses with its ownership 404 (:1142-1160). Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role, scope, owner, recipient or creating-connector check between :1223 and :1265. `getDocument` (:1236) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response carries `hash` (the document's `contentHash`), `nonce`, `message` and `expiresAt` (:1253-1259), and `saveSigningRequest` (:1245) stores the nonce that `POST /:id/sign` accepts (filed separately).
* So a same-tenant user who is not the owner, an admin or the recipient learns a document's content hash that `GET /:id` cloaks from them, and can mint the nonce the sign route needs.
* Callers: the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1027`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it writes nothing to the document, so the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check, plus whatever the sign route's own signer policy decides.

**Priority 3:** a read gap. It mutates no document; it stores an in-memory signing request.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign: any tenant user can sign any document, can turn a revoked document into signed, and no signature is verified
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1271-1346` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the request body, the caller's tenant and the signing nonce, and nothing about the caller or the document's state. It then appends a signature and writes `status: 'signed'` (:1326-1329) through `updateDocument` with no options, so a revoked or deleted document is written back to `signed`. The signature itself is not verified: `isValidSignature` (:1313) accepts any string that starts `mock_signature_` or is longer than 50 characters, in every environment. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role or scope gate, no owner or signer check and no terminal-status check between :1271 and :1346. `getDocument` (:1294) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The nonce (:1299-1311) ties the call to a `POST /:id/sign/request` for the same document id, and that route is open to any authenticated user in the tenant (filed separately).
* `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { signatures, status: 'signed' })` passes no `preserveTerminalStatuses`, so documentRepo's KS-521 guard (it keeps `revoked` and `deleted` only when asked) is off for this write.
* `isValidSignature = signature.startsWith('mock_signature_') || signature.length > 50` (:1313): no cryptographic check and no environment guard. KS-627 is the wallet-connector analogue (`POST /api/wallets/verify`), not this route.
* Callers: the issuer UI's Sign button posts here (`frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx:252`); the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1026`). Platform S does not list this verb among the ones it sends (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's predicate (a write role or scope, then admin, owner or creating connector) does not apply unchanged here. A signer is not necessarily the owner or a write-role holder, so who may sign is this route's own policy question. A terminal-status refusal would apply, but on its own it does not close the route.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates a document (its signatures and its status).

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; whether any environment relies on the `mock_signature_` prefix today is not measured.

title: GET /api/analytics/exports lists every caller's exports with their files inline, and any signed-in user can request users and revenue exports: no role, tenant or user is used (KS-1703 covers only the by-id read)
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/analytics/exports` returns every analytics export the service holds, whoever asked for it, and a completed export carries its file inline (`downloadUrl` is a `data:` URI), so one list call returns other callers' files; and any signed-in caller can request the `users` and `revenue` report types, because the analytics service checks no role. KS-1703 already covers the by-id read (`GET /api/analytics/exports/{id}`, found by Schemathesis) and records that for exports "it may be deliberate" and needs a ruling; this ticket adds the list route, the missing role check on creation, and a rule the docs state that the code does not meet. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, `WORKFLOWS.md` section 3). Related: KS-1703.

## What is not in KS-1703

* **The list route:** `router.get('/exports')` in `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` calls `exportService.listExports(limit)` (default 20), which returns the values of the service's process-wide map (`memExports` in `services/analytics/src/services/exportService.ts`) with no caller or tenant filter. KS-1703's table names the by-id read only. The list makes ids discoverable, so the by-id read does not even need a guessed id.
* **Creation has no role check and stores no caller:** `router.post('/exports')` parses the body and calls `exportService.createExport(request)`; the request carries no identity and `createExport` stores none. Accepted report types: `certifications`, `verifications`, `users`, `governance`, `revenue`, each built from `analyticsService.get<Type>Metrics(query)` where `query` holds only `period`, `startDate` and `endDate`. The gateway mount `/api/analytics` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`) is `authenticateToken(true)` and the service mounts only `jwtAuthenticate` (`services/analytics/src/index.ts`): no role, no scope.
* **Persistence:** the newest 500 export rows are reloaded into the map at boot, so the exposure survives a restart.
* **Tenancy:** the word `tenant` appears in the analytics service's non-test source only in `db.ts`; the routes and `exportService.ts` never read a tenant or user from the request (control: the same search finds `req.params` in the routes file).

## A rule the docs state that this contradicts

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` section 2.1 (as rewritten in KS-1807 PR-1) says services without a role gate "rely on gateway-level auth plus ownership and tenant checks"; for the analytics exports neither exists. PR-1 lists five routes as exceptions; this is a sixth, and PR-1's text will need one more name once this is ruled.

## How to confirm

As two users in different tenants: user A creates a `revenue` export and waits for `completed`; user B calls `GET /api/analytics/exports`. Expected by the platform's tenancy rule: B sees nothing of A's. By this reading: B receives A's export including the file. Not run. Not assessed: whether the metrics functions return platform-wide totals or are narrowed by a database tenant setting that this reading did not find.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves, and KS-1703 holds the open question whether exports are meant to be shared. If they are not: store the creating principal and tenant with each export, filter the list and the by-id read the same way and answer 404 to anyone else (as KS-1116 did for credentials), and decide which roles may request `users` and `revenue`.

Searched the board before filing: `analytics exports`, `listExports`, `exportService` and `analytics/exports` returned KS-1703 (by-id read, referenced above), KS-1853 and KS-1846 (this pass's tickets, about the export contract and the scope table) and KS-188 (stateful testing); none covers the list route or the missing role check. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: The gateway answers four admin and verify routes from stand-ins registered before the proxy: fixed audit-log arrays, an always-empty verification queue, and certification verify that always says verified:false
description:
**BLUF:** The api-gateway answers four routes itself, from stand-ins registered before the proxy to the real service, with no environment guard around them: `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` and `GET /api/security/audit` return fixed arrays of fabricated rows (actor `admin` at `test.local`), `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` returns an array nothing ever writes to (so it is always empty) and its action route answers `success: true` for any id without changing anything, and `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` always answers `verified: false` with a hard-coded issuer `test-issuer`. The real database-backed handlers in originate are never reached for the first three. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, document lifecycle, status codes, error envelope). The docs and the published spec describe these as real operations; the code comment on the queue says "in-memory, development only" but nothing enforces that.

## Evidence

* **Registration order:** `app.use(createAdminRoutes(...))` and `app.use(createVerificationRoutes(...))` in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` come before `app.use(createProxyRoutes(...))`, so a route defined in `routes/admin.ts` or `routes/verification.ts` answers before the `/api/admin/` proxy to originate is reached. The only environment check in `routes/admin.ts` is the demo-seed flag; none wraps these handlers.
* **Audit logs:** `router.get('/api/admin/audit-logs', requireAdmin, ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` filters a literal 4-row array (`evt-1` to `evt-4`, actor `admin` at `test.local`) by `action` and `resourceType` and returns `{ success, logs, events, total }`. `router.get('/api/security/audit', ...)` does the same with a literal 3-row array. Originate has the real handler (`adminConfigRouter.get('/audit-logs')` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`); it is shadowed.
* **Verification queue:** `const mockVerificationQueue = []` ("in-memory, development only") backs `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` (always `items: []`, `total: 0`) and `POST /api/admin/verification-queue/{id}/action`, which validates the action word, updates the array entry only if one exists, and answers `{ success: true, id, action, ... }` for any id. Originate's database-backed `GET`/`POST` for the same paths (`adminConfig.ts`) are shadowed.
* **Certification verify:** `router.post('/api/certifications/:id/verify', ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` ("MOCK ... ENDPOINTS (for E2E tests)", "for test compatibility") checks that the certification exists, then answers `verified: false`, `status: 'issued'`, `issuer: { id: 'test-issuer', verified: true }`, `blockchain.anchored: false`, `confidence: 'pending-onchain'` whatever the certification is. Its comment says it is a stopgap "until the originate→anchoring rewire lands". Originate's own verify handler is never reached.
* **What the docs and spec say:** `QUICK-REFERENCE.md` lists all four as working endpoints (certification verify, the verification queue and its action, audit logs and the `security/audit` alias). The published spec declares only `GET /api/security/audit`; certification verify, `admin/audit-logs` and the two queue routes are live routes with no spec entry (0 hits for each path in `secuura-api.yaml`; control: `/api/billing/customers/by-email` hits).

## How to confirm

As a platform admin, call `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` on a stack with real audit rows and compare with the database; call the verification-queue action with a random id and read `success: true`; call certification verify on a real certification. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Either remove the gateway stand-ins so the proxy reaches originate, or gate them to test environments behind an explicit flag and document that they are test doubles.

Searched the board before filing: `verification-queue` and `audit-logs` are not covered by an existing ticket about the gateway stand-ins; KS-736 is about mount authentication, not these handlers. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Reset-password has no rate limit of its own (the limiter is mounted on /api/auth/password-reset, which has no route) and billing GET /customers/by-email can never match (/customers/:id is registered first)
description:
**BLUF:** Two routing slips in code that the docs describe as working: `POST /api/auth/reset-password`, the route that consumes a reset token, has no rate limit of its own because the reset limiter is mounted on `/api/auth/password-reset`, a path no route serves; and billing `GET /customers/by-email` can never match because `GET /customers/:id` is registered first and takes `by-email` as an id. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). `WORKFLOWS.md`'s rate-limit sheet lists `password_reset` as 15 minutes, 5 attempts, on `POST /api/auth/password-reset`; the published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## 1. The reset limiter guards a path with no handler

* **Limiter mounts** in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` (`app.use(...)`, in this order): `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register`, `/api/auth/forgot-password` (1 hour, 5 in production, `PASSWORD_RESET_RATE_LIMIT`), `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/auth/password-reset` (15 minutes, 5 in production, 50 otherwise), `/api/auth/verify-email`.
* **Auth routes** in `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` for the same flow: `POST /forgot-password` and `POST /reset-password`. There is no `/password-reset` route (control: the `/login` route is found by the same search).
* So `/api/auth/forgot-password` is limited, and `/api/auth/reset-password`, which takes the token and a new password, is limited only by the global limiter (300 per 60 s per IP in production). The 15-minute limiter on the dead path never sees a request. Not assessed: how guessable a reset token is; not probed.
* The login brute-force guard has a related defect already on the board: KS-1372 (nothing calls `recordFailure`).

## 2. Billing by-email is unreachable

`services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts` registers `router.get('/customers/:id', ...)` before `router.get('/customers/by-email', ...)`, so Express matches `by-email` as an `:id` and the by-email handler is never reached. The published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## Not a finding (recorded in the PR for KS-1807 PR-2 as a doc correction)

`GET /billing/pricing` needs a login although a code comment calls it public: `services/billing/src/index.ts` says the public marketing endpoints are "intentionally behind JWT" (`app.use('/billing', jwtAuthenticate())`), so the doc is what is wrong.

Searched the board before filing: `password-reset`, `reset-password` and `by-email` returned no ticket about these two slips. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Mount the limiter on `/api/auth/reset-password` (and drop or fix the dead mount), and register `/customers/by-email` before `/customers/:id`.

title: Spec and docs describe contracts the code does not follow: analytics export sends no Location or Retry-After and returns a data URI; kyc/submit and kyc/status are listed but absent; KYC approval never raises a verification level
description:
**BLUF:** In three areas the published spec and the docs describe a contract the code does not follow: the analytics export, the KYC steps, and the link between KYC and a user's verification level. The analytics export 202 declares `Location` and `Retry-After` headers and a poll-until-`done` flow; the code sends neither header, returns the file inline as a `data:` URI, and calls the field `downloadUrl`, not `url`. The spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`, which do not exist. And no code path raises a user's verification level when a KYC verification is approved, although `WORKFLOWS.md` says it does. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The contract is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held (findings only this round); this ticket is where it is decided which side moves.

## Analytics export (`services/analytics`)

* **Headers:** the spec's `POST /api/analytics/exports` 202 says "poll the URL in the `Location` header until state=`done`" and declares `Location` and `Retry-After` response headers. `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` sets no header (zero hits for `setHeader`, `res.set`, `location` or `retry-after`; control: `setHeader('Location'` has hits in originate's `documents.ts`).
* **Status values and fields:** `exportService.ts` sets `pending`, `processing`, `completed` and `failed`; the spec's `AnalyticsExport` schema has `completed` in its status enum but also declares `url`, `sizeBytes` and `completedAt`, which the code does not send. The code sends `downloadUrl` and `expiresAt`. `WORKFLOWS.md` says `ready` and `url` (a presigned URL with a finite TTL).
* **The download:** `downloadUrl` is `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` (`createDownloadUrl` in `exportService.ts`), so the file travels inside the status response; there is no separate download request. `pdf` and `xlsx` exports contain JSON text, and `pdf` is labelled `application/octet-stream` (a placeholder, per its own comment).
* **Request and 202 body:** the spec's request declares `from` and `to`; the code reads `period` (required) with `startDate` and `endDate`, and also accepts `xlsx`. The 202 body is `{ success, data: { id, status, type, format, createdAt } }`, not the bare object.

## KYC (`services/kyc`)

* **Steps:** the spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`. `services/kyc/src/index.ts` registers `initiate`, `/:id`, `/user/:userId`, `/:id/document`, `/:id/selfie`, `/:id/complete`, `/:id/review`, `/:id/result` and `DELETE /user/:userId/data`. `GET /api/kyc/status` is read as `/:id` with id `status` and answers 404; `POST /api/kyc/submit` matches no service route (by reading the gateway's method map it would answer 405, because the path matches the spec's `/api/kyc/{id}`, which allows only GET; not executed). `initiate` answers 201 (not 202) with `verificationId`; statuses are lowercase `pending`, `in_progress`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`.
* **The level never moves:** `WORKFLOWS.md` says `GET /api/users/me` shows the new `verificationLevel` after KYC and that a raised level unlocks higher-tier document types. A search of service source (tests excluded) finds `users.verification_level` written only by the gateway admin route, the social-login path in auth and originate's admin route; the kyc service has no access to the users table (0 hits for `FROM users`, `UPDATE users`, `INTO users` in `services/kyc/src`; control: `verification_level` has 5 hits in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`). So an approved KYC verification does not change a token's level by this reading. The seeded `PROPERTY_DEED` document type also needs no level (`creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`), though the gate itself exists.

## Not repeated here

The create-document response shape (flat, not `DocumentDetail`), the `/anchor` 202 body, the verify `source` values and the error messages are recorded in the PR-2 pull request body as doc corrections, because there the code is plainly the intended behaviour; if you want them in the contract-corrections batch, say so.

Searched the board before filing: `kyc/submit`, `analytics exports`, `Retry-After` returned no ticket about these contract differences (KS-1327 is about KYC write races, KS-1372 about the login lockout). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. For the export, either send the headers and a real download, or change the spec and docs to the inline `data:` form; for KYC, remove the two steps from `x-workflows` and decide whether approval should raise the level.

title: Please bring the platform-k docs up to date with current behaviour, so systemTest can be written to the docs rather than to the source
description:
## BLUF

Kamil, when you have the capacity, could you please update the platform-k documentation so that it describes how the platform is meant to behave today? The systemTest suites take their expected results from the docs, not from the platform-k source code, so up-to-date docs are what let the tests check the platform against its intended behaviour.

## Why this matters

* **The tests are written to the docs, on purpose.** A test whose expectation comes from the source can only confirm that the code does what the code does. It cannot catch a bug. When the expectation comes from the docs, a difference between the two is a real finding.
* **This follows the ruling already recorded under** [KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or)**:** the docs lead and the code aligns to the docs. That ticket added your Linear rulings to the docs. This one asks for the wider pass that only you can do, because you know the intended behaviour best.
* **Where the docs are silent or out of date**, the test has no source for its expectation. It then either goes unwritten, or it is written against the code, which is the habit we are trying to avoid.

## What would help most

* Endpoint behaviour as it is meant to be: status codes, error bodies, auth and role requirements, and tenancy and ownership rules.
* Flows across services, such as originate, anchoring, certification, transfer and S↔K, including what happens when a step fails.
* Removing or marking anything retired, so a test does not keep asserting behaviour that is gone.
* Where the intended behaviour is not yet decided, a short line saying so is very useful. It tells us to wait rather than guess.

The order and the split into smaller pieces are entirely up to you. Child tickets per area are welcome if that suits you better.

## Done when

The platform-k docs describe current intended behaviour for the areas above, and anything still undecided is marked as such.

Thank you very much, Kamil. It makes a real difference to how much we can trust the test results.

title: KS-1570 PR A follow-up (pull request 1535 gate m1-m3, n1-n3): 503 on an infrastructure fault, EXPECTED_TABLES drift, PR B write-time checks, three nits
description:
## BLUF

**The follow-up to pull request 1535 (KS-1570 PR A): three Minors and three Nits from its Opus gate**, plus the inputs that PR B must honour. Verdict sha256/16 `908a786016f5c2f2`. Facts only, from the gate's report; line numbers at 1535's head `335dfd78`. The Major (M1) is its own ticket. Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## Minors

* **m1:** a scope read that hits a database **infrastructure** fault answers a generic **500**, not the retryable **503** that the KS-888 classifier gives the same fault on save.
  * Where: `services/security/src/index.ts:1181` (mint, through the catch at `:1323` → `errorHandler`) and `:1419-1421` (revoke, `next(err)`).
  * Measured with the app role cut off (connection limit 0, backends terminated): head 500/500; develop's save path 503/503. Fail-closed holds either way.
  * Fix: run the scope-read error through the same SQLSTATE 08/53/57 + socket classifier, and answer 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.
* **m2:** `scripts/rls/verify-fail-closed.sh:53` has `EXPECTED_TABLES` without `admin_organisation_scopes`. The script's own selector picks the table up (measured), so every verification run prints a `DRIFT` line. Fix: add the table.
* **m3 (PR B's input, not a defect of 049):** "rows are written only by a platform role" is an application convention.
  * Measured as `secuura_app`:
    * an INSERT into its own tenant under the GUC succeeds;
    * WITH CHECK refuses another tenant;
    * a self-set `app.tenant_scope_bypass` inserts into any tenant. That is the repo-wide model, the same as 041.
  * There are no foreign keys: `user_id` is not checked against `users`, and `organization_id` is not checked against that tenant's `organizations`.
  * **PR B must** validate at write time that the user exists with role ADMIN in that tenant and that each organisation belongs to the tenant, decide on purging rows when a user is deleted or changes role, and keep the writer platform-only and audited.

## Nits

* **n1:** a stale docstring at `services/security/src/__tests__/ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts:80` ("UNDECIDED POLICY, KS-1535"). The cell itself is rewritten correctly. Reword to RULED (KS-1570).
* **n2:** the comment at `ks1570-admin-organisation-scope.integration.test.ts:19` and the PR body's M6 overstate.
  * "Read under the platform bypass, another tenant's rows would count" is true only if `WHERE tenant_id = $1` is also removed.
  * The gate's G1 (bypass only, WHERE kept) survives every cell. It is equivalent in behaviour.
  * The GUC property is pinned by no cell. Reword, or add a log- or `pg_stat_activity`-based pin.
* **n3 (pre-existing):** `services/security/src/db.ts:27-33` sets no `statement_timeout`, so a scope read blocked by a lock waits.
  * Measured: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held 4 s, the client aborts at 2 s, nothing is minted while locked, and after release the A2 mint is refused and the A1 mint completes. It never allows.
  * Optional: a statement timeout. Referral got one in KS-1582.

## Also from the gate's NOT-tested list, for the deploy seat

The deploy seat must confirm that `secuura_app` has SELECT on `admin_organisation_scopes` on Azure. Otherwise every organisation-naming ADMIN mint and revoke answers 500: fail closed, but an outage of that feature.

title: The tenant-level ADMIN role can mint API keys for any organisation in its tenant; it must be organisation-bounded before the erasure deployment
description:
## BLUF

**The tenant-level** `ADMIN` **role can mint API keys for ANY organisation inside its own tenant**, because the KS-764 organisation arm never engages for it. Kam ruled to **leave it unbounded for now**, with the note that **it must be changed before deployment**. That makes this a deploy blocker.

**⚠ The blast radius was widened by a second ruling.** Kam ruled the erasure merge-timing card **b** — *"Merge now and accept that every later develop deploy carries the live erasure"*. So **once PR #1497 (KS-695 part ii) is on develop, this ADMIN bound blocks EVERY later deploy**, not only an erasure deploy. Kam was told this on the panel and offered to keep the merge back.

Facts only; no build. The SHAPE of the bound is Kam's to rule (candidates below, unranked).

## Kam's rulings, verbatim

Times as the board stamped them (13 Oct 2026, board time, `view=wednesday`), relayed by Wednesday:

* **09:53:40** — *"Decision secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013: a — Leave ADMIN unbounded for now | note: keep a note that this needs to be changed before deployment"*
* **09:56:23** — the erasure merge-timing card, option **b**: *"Merge now and accept that every later develop deploy carries the live erasure"*

## Measured behaviour (develop `7c6b3d88`)

I ran `services/security/src/__tests__/ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts` on develop's tree myself: **20 / 20 pass**. Three cells carry the point:

| cell | what it shows |
| -- | -- |
| `:162` **RED (R1)** | an `ISSUER_ADMIN` of org A1 naming org A2 (same tenant) is **REFUSED** — the arm works for an org-bounded role |
| `:195` **UNDECIDED POLICY (KS-1535)** | an `ADMIN` naming another organisation **STILL MINTS (201)** — the arm never engages for it |
| `:204` **MEASURED** | `platform_admin` cannot mint at all: `decideMint` refuses it before the arm, so it is **not** a vector |

## Why: which roles are bounded today, read at `7c6b3d88`

| set | where | members |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` | `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49` | `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN` |
| `PLATFORM_ROLES` | `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59` | `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` |
| `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` | `keyRevokePolicy.ts:76` | `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` |

* `decideMint` (`provisioningPolicy.ts:95`) returns `{allow: true, via: 'admin'}` at `:98` for every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member.
* `decideTenantAccess` (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:141`) engages the organisation arm only at `:173`, `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))`. `ADMIN` is in neither `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, so the arm is skipped and it returns `same-tenant` (`:208`, `:225`).
* **Revoke, by reading only (NOT measured):** `decideKeyRevoke` (`:239`) builds its organisation scope from the key and routes through the same `decideTenantAccess`, so `ADMIN` is equally unbounded on **revoke** inside its tenant.

## Why it matters

The **KS-695 part (ii)** connector erasure trusts the key row it is called with, and the erasure is **irreversible**: it destroys another organisation's titles, descriptions and organisation name. A key minted by a tenant `ADMIN` carrying another organisation's id is exactly the shape the round-4 Opus gate named as **M-1** on PR #1497. KS-1533 arm 1 closed that path for `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`; `ADMIN` is the remaining role.

## Candidate shapes (UNRANKED — Kam's to rule)

* **A role change:** add `ADMIN` to `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, so the existing arm engages for it.
* **A per-organisation scope on the admin:** an `ADMIN` carries the organisation(s) it may act for, and the arm checks against that.
* **An allow-list:** a per-admin list of organisations it may mint or revoke for.
* **Remove** `ADMIN` **from** `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`**:** it may not mint or revoke keys at all.

Each changes what an existing `ADMIN` account can do on the day it ships; the KS-779 ruling on org-less accounts (*"record all ten as intentionally org-less"*) is the precedent for how an org-less admin is treated.

## Related

* **KS-1533** — the parent; arm 1 merged as PR #1521.
* **KS-695** — the erasure this must precede.
* **KS-1535** — the policy question, now ruled; it records the decision, and this ticket is the work it requires.
* **KS-1536** — the role vocabulary split.

title: T-2: the connector-token / key-validate fetch has no timeout — a slow upstream hangs the request
description:
**The sharpest of the four candidates the gate surfaced, and the only one that is request-reachable today.**

The api-gateway's connector-token exchange / key-validate `fetch` carries **no timeout**. A slow or non-answering upstream turns into a gateway request with no bound on how long it hangs, while the process carries on serving everything else.

## Measured on BOTH trees (head and develop) — so it is pre-existing

* an exchange that **never answers** → the request hangs;
* an exchange whose body arrives **2.5 s late** → the request hangs for that long.

Graded **Major**. Request-reachable, unlike T-1.

## What to do

Give the fetch an explicit timeout (AbortSignal / `AbortController`) and decide the refusal shape — a 503 on timeout is consistent with how the connector branch already answers a refused exchange.

---

Filed from the #1034 / KS-1215 tier-1 gate report `2026-09-18-ks1215-1034-e4624218b-tier1-r1`, at merge of `a105cd32b1ed9c6927ae6e797f8259224d8480c6`. Pre-existing unless stated; **not** introduced by #1034.

title: api-gateway collapses every API-key failure into 401 'Invalid API key' — forward the security validate reason as a distinct code, and answer 503 when the security service is unavailable
description:
## BLUF

**A Platform S connector cannot tell a dead key from an unavailable security service.** The api-gateway collapses every API-key failure — revoked, expired, unknown, security-service 5xx, security-service unreachable, non-JSON reply — into one response: `401 {code:'UNAUTHORIZED', message:'Invalid API key'}`. The security service's own `reason` is computed and then discarded.

Platform S is building a `KeyInvalid` state (PS-740) so a rotated-away key is *seen* rather than reported as an anchor backlog. Because of this collapse it has to be built as a persistence heuristic (two refusals ≥ 60 s apart) rather than a definitive classification, and it can never be made exact without a change here.

## Measured on `develop` @ `48e65c43` (2026-09-15)

**Security computes the reason** — `services/security/src/index.ts`, `POST /api/keys/validate`, all HTTP 200:

| line | condition | response |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:1314-1316` | hash miss in `memApiKeys` and DB fallback empty **or thrown** | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key not found' }` |
| `:1318-1320` | `!apiKey.isActive` | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key revoked' }` |
| `:1322-1324` | `expiresAt < now` | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key expired' }` |

**The gateway throws it away** — `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`:

| line | what happens |
| -- | -- |
| `:219` | security non-2xx → `null`, negative-cached 30 s |
| `:225` | `if (!data?.valid) → null` — `reason` **is never read** |
| `:240` | fetch throws (unreachable, DNS, reset, hang — `:214` has no timeout/AbortSignal) → `null` |
| `:265` | every `null` → `401 { code:'UNAUTHORIZED', message:'Invalid API key' }` |

So `'Key revoked'`, `'Key expired'`, `'Key not found'`, a security 500, and a security outage are **byte-identical to the caller**. A second transport-shaped 401 exists too: when the connector-bearer exchange fails (`:179-203`) the request goes downstream with no Bearer and answers `401 'No token provided'`.

Also: `:1309-1311` swallows a DB error in the validate fallback and reports `'Key not found'` — a cache-miss during a DB outage reads as an unknown key.

## Ask

1. **Forward the reason as a distinct error code** at `auth.ts:265`: `API_KEY_REVOKED`, `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, `API_KEY_NOT_FOUND` (the `ErrorResponse` schema's `code` enum would gain three values). Status can stay 401.
2. **Answer 503** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`**, not 401, when the security service is unreachable or errors** (`:219`, `:240`) — that is the platform's own fault, not the caller's credential, and it must not be negative-cached as if it were.
3. Give the validate fetch at `:214` a timeout.
4. (Docs) `docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` §5 still says a rotate leaves the *"old key untouched"* and tells the admin to revoke by hand — stale since KS-577 (#880) retires prior keys as part of the mint. The OpenAPI 401 prose (32× "Missing or invalid Bearer token") documents no API-key body at all; the three strings above appear nowhere in the spec.

## Why it matters to the S↔K re-key cluster

KS-577 is merged with instant revoke by default, and KS-889's 39-key re-mint and KS-576's bulk re-key are waiting on S being able to survive a rotation. S's side of that (PS-740) lands as a heuristic because of this ticket; with (1) and (2) it becomes exact and the heuristic is deleted. Until then, a security-service outage on K will look to S like every connector key dying at once — and S's design deliberately keeps presenting the key so that false positive costs nothing, but it is still a lie on the dashboard.

Filed from PS-740's planning pass. Cited in prose, no `Refs` trailer.

title: KS-1240 gate follow-ups (#1785): exchange timeout still reads as a downstream 401; two http.request forwards unbounded; the non-OK 4xx validate branch has no cell
description:
**Three follow-ups from the tier-1 gate on #1785 (KS-1240 part 1, api-gateway). None blocks that merge.**

1. **A connector-exchange timeout still ends as a downstream 401.**
   * Where: `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`, `getConnectorBearer`, bounded at 5 s by #1785.
   * What happens: the base's fail-closed answer is kept. On a timeout the request goes on with no Bearer, and a Bearer-only upstream answers 401 for a key that was just validated. The client reads a transient fault as an auth failure.
   * Why it differs from the ticket: KS-1240's text suggests "a 503 on timeout".
   * Pinned today: the two "the exchange ..." cells in `ks1240b-front-door-key-exchange-timeout-answers-503-not-401.test.ts` pin the 401.
   * Why #1785 kept it: the gateway cannot tell whether a mount needs the connector Bearer. Gateway-local handlers serve `sk_` callers from `req.user` without it, so a gateway 503 would refuse requests that succeed today.
   * Related: auth's `/internal/connector-token` (`services/auth/src/routes/internal.ts:42`) has its own unbounded fetch to the security service, and answers 502 on any non-2xx from it.
2. **Two hand-built forwards are still unbounded.**
   * Where: `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:620` (`http.request` for `POST /api/documents/upload`) and `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:900` (`http.request` for document create).
   * Read at #1785's head `e01a5094771d`: no `setTimeout`, timeout or abort in `proxy.ts` 600-660 or `verification.ts` 885-940.
   * The sibling at `verification.ts:559` has one: `proxyReq.setTimeout(originateForwardTimeoutMs, ...)`.
   * It is the same hang shape as KS-1240. Neither call is a `fetch(`, so #1785's census does not see them. Not executed.
3. **Test gap: the non-OK 4xx branch of** `checkApiKey` **has no cell.**
   * Three gate mutants survive with all 40 cells green:
     * F7: a 429 treated as a rejection.
     * F8: every non-OK status treated as unavailable, so a 4xx rejection becomes 503.
     * F18: a non-OK 4xx rejection not cached.
   * Unpinned: the `!resp.ok` branch for a status that is not 5xx, 408 or 429 (cache 30 s, answer 401), and the 429 classification.
   * Why it is harmless today: the security service rejects with 200 `valid:false`, and answers 400 only for a missing key. An edit that changes either branch would still go unseen.
   * Fix: one cell with a 403 stub and one with a 429 stub.

**Searched before filing.** Team KS, issue titles and descriptions including archived, plus comment bodies, 2026-10-28 \~10:30Z (issues / comments):

* No hits: "exchange timed out" 0 / 0, "proxy.ts:620" 0 / 0, "verification.ts:900" 0 / 0, "non-OK 4xx" 0 / 0, "checkApiKey" 0 / 0.
* "documents/upload": 2 issues. KS-1724 is about uncapped arrays and KS-1222 about the MIME screen; neither is this.
* "http.request": 4 issues (KS-1329, KS-1087, KS-1083, KS-955); none is about a missing timeout.
* Positive control "connector-token": 10 issues, KS-1240 among them. A freshly coined zero control: 0 / 0.

**Refs:** KS-1240; PR #1785 at head `e01a5094771d`; gate verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-28_gate4-tier1/verdict.md`, findings 1785-1, 1785-3 and 1785-4. Filed on the coordinator's instruction (gate result, 10:26Z).

title: api-gateway: a 401 or 403 from in front of the security service is cached as a 30 s key rejection; should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer"? (gate 31, F2)
description:
**BLUF:** A design question, not a defect found today. The gateway's `checkApiKey` treats any non-OK status from the key-validate call outside 5xx, 408 and 429 as a key rejection and negative-caches it for about 30 s (answering 401 `Invalid API key`). By the gate's reading, the real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403 (`security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path; the handler near line 1800 answers 400, 503 or 200 with `valid: false`), so a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or a WAF) and would make every key, valid ones included, answer 401 `Invalid API key` for 30 s. Pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3) now pins today's behaviour for a 403, which turns it into a tested contract. Should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer" (503, not cached) instead?

**Source.** QA gate 31 on pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F2 (Note, a design question for Kam, not that pull request's defect). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate31-1827/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1788, where the 403 cell was asked for; KS-1174, which is about forwarding a distinct code per key failure and not about this classification; KS-1240, the original timeout work. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2, lines 56 to 59 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F2 (Note, design question for Kam, not this PR's defect).** The cell freezes "any non-OK status outside {5xx, 408, 429} is a key rejection, negative-cached 30 s".
  * The real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403. `security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path, and the handler at l.1800 answers 400 (schema), 503 (KS-1370) or 200 `valid:false`.
  * So a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or WAF). Today that would answer every key, valid ones included, `401 Invalid API key` for 30 s.
  * Pinning today's behaviour is what the ticket asked for, so this is fine to merge. But this PR now makes it a pinned contract, so whether an infrastructure 401/403 should count as "could not answer" deserves a ruling.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `checkApiKey` 1 hit (KS-1788). `couldNotAnswer` 0, `infrastructure 401` 0, `negative cache` 2 (KS-1788, KS-1207: neither asks this), `keys/validate` 23 (read: KS-1174, KS-1788, KS-1240 for ingress, WAF, status or "could not answer" text: none asks whether an infrastructure 401/403 is a rejection), `WAF` 8 (none about the key-validate call).

**Not measured by this filing:** the security service's routes (the statements about them are the gate's reading, not re-read here); what any ingress or WAF in front of the service answers in practice; whether one exists on any box.

title: For one anchor id the anchor row reads failed while its document reads confirmed; a document read and a verify can settle it either way
description:
**BLUF:** On kintsugi, for anchor id `anchor_c09c1b1f-c639-49e3-8afc-f1fb31906732` (document `deb6d3c3-1d79-4993-82a1-7a49a75aae00`), the anchor row and the document disagree. The reconciler marked the anchor row `failed` at 2026-10-29 08:56:14Z (the 24 hour give-up). The document's stored blob reads `confirmed` against the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` (block 4801203), written at 08:56:52Z after two `POST /api/verification/verify` calls. The code has two readers that can settle the same pair in opposite directions: a document read can write `anchor_failed`, a verify wrote `confirmed`. Only the verify-first order was observed.

**Measured** (Seat T 6th, kintsugi, read-only, 09:02:43Z and 09:04:53Z):

* Anchor row: status `failed`, error "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)", `created_at` 2026-10-28T08:55:38.299Z, `updated_at` 2026-10-29T08:56:14.459Z, `retry_count` 0. Its stored transaction `e1df3f61…` is not on the preview chain; the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` is (Seat T 6th's earlier reading).
* Document (originate store, found through `documents.external_id`): row status `anchored`, `updated_at` 08:56:52.914Z; blob `blockchain.status` `confirmed`, `blockHeight` 4801203, txHash `b1cc72f9…`. originate log, 08:56:52.921Z: "KS-584: healed anchor state written back to document". audit_logs: two `verification.verify` requests answered 200 at 08:56:52.930Z and 08:56:52.951Z, and no request to the retry route `/anchor` for this document.
* Not measured: who sent the two verify calls, and why the once-a-minute document reads stopped at 05:53:39Z.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`; not exercised):

* Document read: `documents.ts:1167` calls `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` (`services/anchorStateSync.ts:353`). At `:399-400`, when the document is in flight and the anchor row's status is `failed`, it calls `markDocumentAnchorFailed`, which writes `status: 'anchor_failed'` and returns early only when the blob is already `confirmed` (`anchorStateSync.ts:173` onward). `documents.ts:1458` lets the retry route run for an `anchor_failed` blob.
* Verify: `routes/verification.ts` `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:426`) and `persistHealedAnchor` (`:496`), called at `:802-803` and `:1324-1325`; the log line above comes from `:504`.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread2_0902Z_t6.txt` (anchor row, document, logs, audit_logs, with controls)
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread3_trigger_t6.txt` (the two verify calls and the gateway lines)

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): the phrase "anchor row failed" 0 hits; `anchorStateSync.ts:399` 1 hit, read: KS-772, in Seat T 6th's comments of 05:50Z and 09:09Z on the stuck row. They describe this same mechanism as stream comments, not as a ticket, and the 09:09Z comment says the same shape on another document can end either way and that only one outcome was measured; `markDocumentAnchorFailed` 10 hits, `confirmStalePendingAnchor` 6 hits and `persistHealedAnchor` 7 hits, read by title: they concern threadToken erasure (KS-1058, KS-1074), block heights (KS-1509, KS-1333), unpinned guard clauses (KS-1676), the simulated flag (KS-1661) and others, and none describes a failed anchor row beside a confirmed document. KS-1384 records this kintsugi row up to 2026-10-29 00:52Z, before the row failed.

**Related:** KS-1384 (the per-event anchor design under revision), KS-772 (the review stream whose comments record the kintsugi row), KS-1676.

title: One anchor row per (document_id, network): a repeat POST /api/anchors resets the existing row to pending and nulls its transaction hash — so Platform-S's per-event anchoring collapses to one anchor per document (PS-895 companion)
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-s `477eb57`, platform-k `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching this). Companion to [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one), which asked the question from the S side after seeing six lifecycle events on one document share one External Ref, and one on-chain transaction for register + declare on dev-ps.

## What the code does

`dbPersistAnchor` upserts on the composite key and rewrites the chain columns from the **new** request:

```
services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1334-1372
  INSERT INTO anchor_store (...)
  ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET
    status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash,
    block_hash/block_number/slot/fee/confirmations/confirmed_at = EXCLUDED.…,
    error_message, retry_count, simulated, updated_at = EXCLUDED.…
  RETURNING id
```

`metadata_payload` and `content_hash` are **not** in the update list, so the first event's label and hash stay on the row. Every `POST /api/anchors` builds the anchor with `status: 'pending'` and a null hash (`index.ts:463-560`), so on a conflict the existing row goes back to `pending` with `transaction_hash = NULL`, and `processAnchor(persistedId)` runs again (`:535`).

K's own share, transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle-event routes all go through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to that same flat endpoint (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1275-1297`). So every non-mutating verb S records re-enters the same row for the document.

Migration 031 records the one-row-per-(document, network) decision. `anchorSubmission.ts:383-386` (guard 1) reads the row's `transaction_hash` to avoid a second fee-paying transaction — the upsert has just nulled it.

## What this means for the S↔K contract

* Platform-S's user-facing promise (`docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §1, §7) is that every declare, sign and share event is anchored. K anchors **one row per document version per network**; later events reset and re-process it.
* For every verb S routes through `/lifecycle-events`, `/share` or `/transfer-custody`, the chain record carries **no** `documentType` **and no** `identity` — `emitLifecycleAnchor` sends neither, and the lifecycle-events handler reads only `action` and `payload` (`documents.ts:2440-2545`). That is a [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) gap; filed separately.

## Decisions needed (Kamil)

1. Is one anchor per (document, network) the intended contract? If yes, S will label its External Ref column "anchor for version X" and group events ([PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) item 2), and the USER-MANUAL wording changes.
2. If events should each anchor, the upsert key needs an event dimension and `emitLifecycleAnchor` needs the verb.
3. Either way: **what happens on the reset.** Trace whether `processAnchor` after a conflict mints a second Cardano transaction for the same document (guard 1 cannot see the previous hash any more), or is caught by another guard. Not verified live in the review; [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one)'s dev-ps observation was one transaction for two events.

## Verify

* Unit: a second `POST /api/anchors` for the same `(documentId, network)` returns the existing id **and** either leaves a confirmed row's `transaction_hash` intact (per-document contract) or creates a distinct row (per-event contract) — whichever is ruled.
* Live on a paired slot: originate → declare → share on one document; count anchor rows and Cardano transactions; quote both on this ticket.

Related: [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) (the S-side question), [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (identity block), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb).

title: POST /api/kyc/:id/review has no role or owner check: any signed-in caller can approve a verification and set its level, though the spec declares 403 "Reviewer role required" (four more admin-labelled routes ungated)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` approves or rejects a KYC verification and sets its `currentLevel` (up to `GOVERNMENT`), but it checks no role and no ownership. The only authentication in front of it is `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` inside the kyc service and `authenticateToken(true)` on the `/api/kyc` gateway mount, so any signed-in caller who knows the id of a verification in state `under_review` can decide it. The published spec declares `403 Reviewer role required` on this operation. Four more routes that their own comments or the spec call admin-only have the same shape. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; nothing was probed against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Doc-versus-code difference: the spec (and the inventory's "they rely on gateway auth + ownership/tenant checks") says a gate exists; the code has none.

## The routes

1. **kyc review** — `services/kyc/src/index.ts`, handler for `POST /api/kyc/:id/review`. It parses `reviewVerificationSchema` (`status` approved or rejected, optional `reviewNotes`, optional `newLevel` NONE to GOVERNMENT), takes `reviewerId` from `req.user?.userId` (falling back to the string `admin`), then writes `verification.status` and, on approval, `verification.currentLevel = data.newLevel || verification.requestedLevel` and saves it. There is no `requireRole`, and nothing compares the verification's owner with the caller. Spec: `services/kyc/src/kyc.openapi.ts` declares the 403 with the description "Reviewer role required". Gateway: the `/api/kyc` mount in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(true)` plus the proxy. Not checked: whether the verification's `currentLevel` is read back into a user's token level elsewhere.
2. **governance** — `POST /api/governance/process-expired` in `services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` (comment: "admin/cron endpoint"); spec `governance.openapi.ts` declares 403 "Admin role required". The gateway mount `/api/governance` uses `authenticateToken(false)` (the shape KS-736 tracks).
3. **transfer** — `POST /api/delegations/admin/process-expired` in `services/transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (comment: "admin trigger"). Mount is authentication only.
4. **staking** — `GET /api/stake/all` in `services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts` (comment: "List all stakes (admin)"); the handler pages `SELECT * FROM svc_stake_positions`. Mount is authentication only. Not checked: whether that table is tenant-scoped.
5. **wallet-connector** — `GET /api/wallets/sessions` in `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts` (comment: "List active sessions (admin)"). Mount is authentication only.

For all five the service mounts no role gate (a census of `services/*/src` for `requireRole`, role comparisons and `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` finds none in kyc, governance, transfer, staking or wallet-connector; the same census finds originate's 73 hits, so the instrument fires).

## Evidence and how to confirm

Read at `develop` `530f09112`. A live check is one request per route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (the self-registration default); the expected answer by the spec is 403, and by this reading it is 2xx (or 404 for an unknown id). Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Peter's ruling recorded on KS-1668: the docs lead and the code aligns to them; Kam decides which side moves. The aligned fix is a role gate on each route (the shared `requireRole` in `packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts` is already mounted in billing, tokenisation and vc-issuer), and for the kyc review an owner-not-reviewer check as well. KS-1807's PR-1 documents the difference rather than the intended gate, and marks the passage so a test is not written against current behaviour.

Searched the board before filing: `Reviewer role required` 0 hits, `process-expired` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1762), `kyc/:id/review` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1327, a read-modify-write race). Control in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

title: KS-1020 item 2: which subject OWNS a presentation (and a credential) — the ownership model for GET /api/presentations/:id and GET /credentials/:id, and the policy for the existing holder_id NULL rows
description:
## BLUF

**This is a decision for Kam, not a build.** KS-1020 recommendation item 2 — *"Add the ownership/tenant check the path never had"* — needs an ownership model before any code: which subject OWNS a presentation (and a credential), and what happens to the rows that have no owner today. Item 1 (exact-or-404) is PR #966 and closes KS-1020 on its merge; this ticket is where items 2 and 3 live.

## What was measured (develop `721b333a6`, `services/vc-issuer/src`)

* `holder_id` is written from `(presentation as any).holder || null` at `routes/presentations.ts:102` — non-null only when `POST /` was given `holderDID`; KS-1020 records every stored row as `holder_id NULL`.
* `GET /api/presentations/:id` sits behind `jwtAuthenticate` at `index.ts:86-92`, whose `publicOps` names only `POST /credentials/verify`, `POST /presentations/verify` and `GET /identity-credentials/types`; the spec agrees (`security: [{ bearerAuth: [] }]`, `vc-issuer.openapi.ts:1262`). So the caller is an authenticated bearer — **a SUBJECT exists** (`req.user`'s userId / organizationId) — but `routes/presentations.ts` never reads `req.user` (0 occurrences), and **no stored OWNER exists**: `holder_id` is a DID string when present and NULL otherwise, and the route writes no tenant/organisation column.
  * Correction of record: the s198 brief said *"*`GET /:id` *is mounted PUBLIC per the KS-442 note at* `:52-54`*"*. That note is about `/presentations/verify`. Wednesday has accepted the correction as her brief's error.
* The sibling `repositories/credentialRepo.getById` (`:75-108`, reached from `GET /credentials/:id` at `routes/credentials.ts:268`) has the same no-owner property; whatever is decided here applies to credentials too.
* Adjacent on Platform S, not touched: PS-690 (In Progress, Stuart) — *Adopt org-owned documents: ownership model for single- vs multi-user orgs, user/org deletion semantics, and the S→K erasure bridge*. The K-side answer here should not contradict whatever S adopts there.
* Adjacent ruling, not acted on: `secuura-org-trust-boundary-within-tenant` → **bind** (shipped in #954, on kintsugi). An ownership/tenant check on these paths is a trust-boundary question of the same family and should be decided against that ruling, not beside it.

## The decision needed

1. **What owns a presentation / a credential?** The minting caller's organisation, the holder DID mapped to a user, the tenant of the bearer — or something else.
2. **Policy for the existing** `holder_id NULL` **rows:** deny-all, allow-any-authenticated, or owner-less-means-issuer-org (with or without a backfill).
3. Then **item 3 of KS-1020**: re-test the cross-holder question against rows that actually carry an owner, so the inferred half of KS-1020 becomes measured either way.

## What is NOT established

* Cross-holder disclosure remains inferred from the mechanism, not measured (KS-1020's own bound).
* Whether any of this is reachable in a deployed environment — not probed; taken separately, per KS-1020.

## Provenance

Measured by s198 (seat D) on 2026-09-13 while shipping KS-1020 item 1 (PR #966 @ `1f0d08841`); filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-09-13 02:27:19Z ("its OWN ticket … Kam's decision, carded after #966's gate").

title: vc-issuer POST /api/credentials/{id}/revoke checks neither owner nor role: any signed-in caller can revoke any credential by id (the KS-1116 binding covers reads only)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/credentials/{id}/revoke` in vc-issuer checks neither the caller's role nor who created the credential. Any signed-in caller who knows a credential id can revoke it. KS-1116 bound the credential and presentation READS to the creating principal; the revoke write was left out. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Filed on the coordinator's word (2026-10-30 ANSWER, 01:40Z). Related: KS-1116 (the creator binding, reads only) and KS-1845 (admin or owner checks missing on routes that need them).

## Evidence

* **Route:** `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts`, `router.post('/:id/revoke', ...)`: takes `id` from the path and an optional `reason` from the body, calls `credentialRepo.revoke(id, reason)`, answers 404 "Credential not found" when it returns nothing, otherwise 200 with `credentialId` and `revokedAt`. There is no role check and no comparison with the credential's creator.
* **Repository:** `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`, `revoke()`: looks the credential up with `getById(id)` (the exact-id lookup that KS-1116 deliberately left unbound for the public verify path), rewrites its `credentialStatus` (`revoked: true`, `revokedAt`, `revocationReason`) in the in-memory store, and runs `UPDATE vc_credentials_store SET credential = $1 WHERE id = $2`. The SQL has no owner or tenant condition. Not checked: whether row-level security on that table limits the update to the caller's tenant.
* **What sits in front:** the gateway mount `/api/credentials` is `authenticateToken(false)`; the service's own `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` requires a valid token for everything except its three public operations (verify credential, verify presentation, the identity-credential types), so an anonymous caller is refused. Any valid token passes, whatever its role or tenant.
* **The binding that exists:** `services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts` (`mayRead`) binds `GET /api/credentials/{id}`, the credential list and the by-hash read (KS-1683) to the creating principal; its header names only the public verify path's revocation lookup as deliberately unbound and does not mention revoke. `ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts` exercises revoke only by the creator.
* **Why it matters:** the public verify path's revocation lookup reads the stored revoked status (`credentialStatus.revoked`), so this is a write that changes another principal's credential into a revoked one. Not assessed: how guessable a credential id is, and whether the verify routes act on the flag (KS-1352 and KS-1375 are about exactly that).

## How to confirm

Create a credential as user A, revoke it by id with a token for user B in the same tenant (and one in another tenant). Expected by the KS-1116 ruling's intent: 404 or 403. By this reading: 200. Not run.

## What the docs say

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` (KS-1807 PR-1) records the gap as a fact with an `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)` line, because the KS-1116 ruling covers reads and no ruling says who may revoke.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. The shape of the existing binding would extend naturally: read the owner with `getRecordById`, apply `mayRead` (or a revoke variant that also admits the tenant administrators), and answer a refused caller exactly like an unknown id.

Searched the board before filing: `credentials/{id}/revoke`, `credential revoke`, `credentialRepo.revoke` and `revoke a credential` returned KS-188, KS-1352, KS-1375, KS-1684 and KS-692 and none is about the missing owner or role check on this route (KS-1352 and KS-1375: a revoked credential still verifies; KS-1684: the creator refused a read after a revoke on the memory path; KS-692: the status revoke route's tenant check; KS-1116 and KS-1683 are about reads). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Two admin routes admit OWNER, the self-registration default: billing POST /admin/credits and nft-certificate PUT /admin/platform-fee answer 403 "Admin access required" but let any registered user through
description:
**BLUF:** Two routes that answer 403 "Admin access required" let `OWNER` through. `OWNER` is the role every self-registered user gets (registration always assigns it), so any registered user passes both: `POST /admin/credits` in `services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts`, which adds certification credits to a customer (credits are money), and `PUT /admin/platform-fee` in `services/nft-certificate/src/routes/nft.routes.ts`, which sets the NFT platform fee. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Filed on the coordinator's word (2026-10-30 ANSWER, 01:40Z). Related: KS-1845 (the same class: admin-labelled routes with no or too wide a role gate).

## The routes

1. **billing** `POST /admin/credits` — comment "Add certification credits to a customer (admin only)". The handler reads `req.user?.role` and answers 403 `FORBIDDEN` "Admin access required" unless the role is in `['SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN', 'OWNER']`. It then parses `{ customerId: string, credits: positive integer }` and calls `getStripeService().addCertificationCredits(customerId, credits)`, answering `{ customerId, creditsAdded, newBalance }`. Nothing ties `customerId` to the caller's own account or organisation. The gateway mount `/api/billing` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(false)` plus the proxy.
2. **nft-certificate** `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee` — comment "Update platform fee configuration (admin only)". Same role list and the same 403 body. It then parses `{ percentage: 0-100, fixed: >= 0 }` and calls `costEstimatorService.updatePlatformFee(percentage, fixed)`, answering the new values. The gateway mount `/api/nft` is `authenticateToken(false)` plus a proxy guard.

`OWNER` is assigned on every registration path (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` sets `role: 'OWNER'`; an explicit `role` in the request is refused 422), so for these two routes "Admin access required" admits every registered user. A search of `services` and `packages` source (tests and docs excluded) for a bracketed list containing the string `'OWNER'` returns exactly these two lines; the control, the same pattern on the billing file alone, hits it.

## How to confirm

One request to each route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (a freshly registered user). Expected by the route's own message: 403. By this reading: 200 with the new balance, and 200 with the new fee. Not run.

## What the docs say

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` (KS-1807 PR-1) records the two inline lists as a fact with an `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)` line, because no ruling says whether `OWNER` is meant to pass; this ticket is where that is decided.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. If "admin only" is the intent, drop `OWNER` from both lists (or use the shared `requireRole`) and, for credits, bind `customerId` to the caller's own customer unless the caller is a platform admin.

Searched the board before filing: `admin/credits` 0 hits, `platform-fee` 1 hit (KS-1820, about the NFT mint and the platform wallet, not these role lists). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: auth: the single-use backup-code burn is not atomic (passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285, userRepo.ts:891-894), so concurrent sign-ins can reuse a spent code (gate 30, F1)
description:
**BLUF:** The single-use backup-code burn in the password-login gate is not atomic. It reads the stored code array, splices the used code out in memory and writes the whole array back matched by user id only (`passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285`, `userRepo.ts:891-894`). **Measured against a stateful stub, not against Postgres:** two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both get a credential, and two concurrent sign-ins with different codes can leave a spent code stored and accepted again (a lost update). Pre-existing; no current change introduces it.

**Source.** QA gate 30 on pull request 1826 (KS-1804 note 2; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F1 (Major, pre-existing product, out of that pull request's scope; the gate recommends filing). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate30-1826/verdict.md`; the probe `g30-probe-race.test.ts` (P1 and P2) sits beside it. Related: KS-1804, where it was found, and the neighbours the gate named, KS-809, KS-1052 and KS-1081, none of which is about concurrency. KS-1327 is the same whole-row read-modify-write class on KYC writes, not on backup codes. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F1, lines 46 to 50 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F1 (Major, PRE-EXISTING product, out of this PR's scope; recommend filing).** The single-use burn is not atomic.
  * **Where:** `passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285` + `userRepo.ts:891-894`. The code reads, then splices in memory, then writes the whole array by `WHERE id` only.
  * **Effect:** two concurrent logins with one backup code both get a credential, and two concurrent logins with different codes can leave a spent code valid (a lost update). Measured against a stateful stub (probe P1 and P2), NOT against Postgres.
  * **Board search (Linear** `searchIssues`**, includeArchived):** no ticket matched literally on "backup code concurrent", "backup code race", "mfa_backup_codes race" or "backup code twice"; the fuzzy hits were KS-809, KS-1052 and KS-1081, none about concurrency. Control: a nonsense term gave 0. KS-1052 and KS-533 contain no race or concurrency text (grep).
  * **Possible remedies (not built):** `UPDATE … SET mfa_backup_codes = array_remove(mfa_backup_codes, $hash) WHERE id = $id AND $hash = ANY(mfa_backup_codes)`, requiring rowCount 1; or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` in a transaction.

**Fix shape (the gate's, not built here):** a conditional update that removes exactly the presented code and requires it to be present, or a row lock, as quoted above. It touches the credential path, so the fix would get a tier-1 gate.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `passwordLoginGate` 13 hits including KS-1804. `mfa_backup_codes` 5 hits (KS-1052, KS-938, KS-809, KS-795, KS-783), `mfaBackupCodes` 6 (KS-938, KS-809, KS-783, KS-732, KS-622, KS-256), `array_remove` 0, `backup code race` 0, `backup code twice` 0, `burn is not atomic` 0, `lost update` 4 (KS-1377, KS-1370, KS-772, KS-485: none about backup codes), `FOR UPDATE` 2 (KS-1327, KS-757: neither about backup codes). KS-809, KS-1052, KS-1081, KS-533 and KS-1804 read whole for race or concurrency text: no statement about concurrent burns.

**Not measured by this filing:** anything against Postgres; both effects were shown against a stateful stub by the gate's probe, and this ticket does not repeat it.

title: services/auth passwordLoginGate: two KS-1188 F3 gate notes carried on KS-1467 are not done (const among imports; no exactly-once burn cell)
