title: CONFIG DRIFT: two tracked env templates disagree by ~39 vars — bootstrap-env.sh reads .env.example, CLAUDE.md documents env.example
description:
**BLUF —** `Blockchain/Dev/` **carries TWO tracked env templates that disagree by ~39 variables, and the two consumers read different ones:** `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` **reads** `.env.example` **while the project** `CLAUDE.md` **documents** `env.example`**. A developer who follows the docs and a developer who runs the script get different environments.**

## Measured

| file | lines | vars (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=`) | tracked |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` | 444 | **103** | yes |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | 302 | **64** | yes |

They are **separate files**, not a symlink or hardlink — different inodes (13295153 / 13295132).

**Consumers disagree:**

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:26` — `ENV_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"`, and it errors with *".env.example not found"* / succeeds with *"Created .env from .env.example"*.
* The project `CLAUDE.md` documents `cp Blockchain/Dev/env.example Blockchain/Dev/.env`.

**Divergence is substantial, not cosmetic.** Variables present in one and absent from the other include `ADMIN_USER_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ENCRYPTION_SALT`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID`/`ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS`, `API_BASE_URL` — against `API_GATEWAY_PORT`, `AUTH0_*`, `AZURE_AD_*`, `BILLING_SERVICE_URL`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS` in the other direction. **Several are security-relevant gates** (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS`), so which template a developer copies determines which gates they even know exist.

## Class — this is the KS-1077 shape

**Two competing sources of truth for the same configuration, where each consumer picks one and nobody reconciles them.** That is exactly [KS-1077](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1077)'s two npm-audit allow-lists, where Kam ruled `one-list-triage-two` (2026-09-10 11:29) — make the local triage record the single source. **Worth resolving as ONE decision with KS-1077 rather than twice**, because the same ruling shape almost certainly applies: name one file the source, and reconcile the other into it.

## How it surfaced

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) doing the KS-1041 Step 2 config-drift pass required by the PR verification protocol Kam adopted the same day (§3b: *"a var read in code but absent from the template is a finding"*). Adding `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` meant choosing a template — and there were two.

## Explicitly NOT done

**No winner picked.** The var was added to **both** templates in [PR #951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) so neither consumer is left short, but reconciling the files is a decision about which is authoritative and what the ~39-var delta means — not a drive-by edit. **Scoped and evidenced only.**

Related: KS-1041, KS-1077.

title: Docs claim rules the code does not apply: share checks no document access, ownerless documents skip the read check, a revoked key works 60 s at the gateway, the admin dashboard reads X-Tenant-Override, metering is certification-only
description:
**BLUF:** Five statements in the platform-k security docs describe a rule the code does not apply: document share checks no per-document access, a document with no recorded owner skips the read check, a revoked API key is still accepted by the gateway for up to 60 seconds, `GET /api/admin/dashboard` reads `X-Tenant-Override` from the raw header for an `ORG_ADMIN`, and the claim that agent document operations are metered holds only for certification operations. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; none of these was exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). The docs and the code disagree on each; PR-1 describes what is built, names this ticket beside the passage, and does not write either behaviour as the intended one.

## Items

1. **Share has no per-document access check.** `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`): after the role-or-scope gate (`DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` or `documents:share`) the handler runs `getDocument(id, tenantId)` and answers 404 only when the document is absent from the tenant; it never compares the caller with the owner, a recipient or an admin. `AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` R4 says "ownership checks still apply on read/share/revoke". Same class as KS-1688 (version) and KS-1814 (anchor; fixed), and as KS-1833/KS-1834 (lifecycle events).
2. **Ownerless documents skip the read check.** `GET /api/documents/{id}`: the refusal is guarded by `userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient`. `documentRepo` maps the owner as `row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`, so a row with neither column set has `owner.id === ''` and the guard is false for every caller in the tenant. The inventory (§2.3) says reading needs owner, admin, recipient or creating connector. Not measured: how many rows have no owner.
3. **A revoked key keeps working at the gateway.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` caches a valid `sk_` key in `apiKeyCache` for 60 s (a rejection for 30 s); nothing outside tests deletes or clears the cache (zero hits for `apiKeyCache.delete` and `apiKeyCache.clear`; control: `apiKeyCache.set` has two). The security service's revoke is immediate. The rules doc R6 says keys are "revocable immediately", contract §5 says "takes effect on next validate", and the rotation grace default `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS=0` was ruled "instant revoke" (2026-08-07, KS-577).
4. `X-Tenant-Override` **is read raw by one admin route.** The inventory (§2.4) says the override is "honoured only for the super-admin list". The gateway applies that list when it sets the tenant GUC, but it also allow-lists the header through to the services (`TRUST_HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` in `services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), and `GET /api/admin/dashboard` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` reads `req.headers['x-tenant-override']` itself and, if it is a UUID, counts documents, users and verifications for that tenant under `runWithPlatformScope`; with no header it returns platform-wide totals. That router admits `ORG_ADMIN` (`requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`) and so does the gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy (`enforceAdminProxy`). By this reading an `ORG_ADMIN` can read counts for another tenant. Counts only; not exercised live.
5. **Metering covers certifications only.** The rules doc R7 says agent document operations are metered (KS-320). `charge_events` rows are inserted only by `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts`, which only `routes/certifications.ts` calls for writes; `documents.ts` and anchoring do not import it. Create, version, share, revoke, transfer-custody and anchor write none. Which operations should be metered is a product call, not a code reading.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (connectors cannot revoke; unenforced scopes), KS-1688, KS-1833, KS-1834, KS-1814.

Searched the board before filing: `x-tenant-override` 8 hits (none about the dashboard; KS-1704 is about a super-admin's override), `apiKeyCache` 0, `charge_events` 1 (KS-1401, RLS on the table, not coverage), `lifecycle-events` hits KS-1833 and KS-1834 (excluded above). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns. Items 1 and 2 are access checks in originate; item 3 is a cache invalidation or a stated TTL; item 4 is to read the override from the verified request context, not the header; item 5 needs a ruling on what is metered first.

title: Scope vocabulary and enforcement drift: five scopes gate nothing or name missing routes, gateway requireScope ignores <resource>:*, mints never call validateScopes, * is mintable by every key-admin role (SCOPES.md vs code)
description:
**BLUF:** Six differences between what `SCOPES.md` (and the KS-540 inventory) say about scopes and what the code enforces. Five scopes in the vocabulary gate nothing or name routes that do not exist; the gateway's `requireScope` does not honour `<resource>:*` although the shared helper does; the key mints never call `validateScopes`; `*` can be minted by every key-admin role although the docs say super-admin only; and gates and mints use scope strings that are not in the 32-member `SCOPES` array. `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke` (minted but unenforced) are already tracked in KS-1433 and are not repeated here. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; the gateway and mint behaviour was not exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). PR-1 rewrites `SCOPES.md` to describe what is built and marks each open question `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)`; this ticket is where the code side is decided.

## Items

1. **Declared, enforced nowhere.** `certifications:share`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/share` exists in `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` with no scope or role check (and is not in the published spec). `certifications:revoke`: the route checks the caller is the certification's issuer, no scope (not in the spec). `analytics:read`: the `/api/analytics` gateway mount is authentication only. `analytics:export`: `POST /api/analytics/exports` exists (in the spec) with no scope check. `users:write`: no reference in any source file outside `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts`.
2. **Names routes that do not exist.** `certifications:sign` (no `/{id}/sign` route in originate, not in the spec), `kyc:submit` (no `/api/kyc/submit`), `kyc:read` (no `/api/kyc/status`). The vocabulary entries are pinned by `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks843-subjects-erase-scope.test.ts`, so removing them is a decision and a test edit.
3. **Gateway wildcard.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` tests `userScopes.includes(s)` (exact) plus a lone `*`; the imported shared `hasScope` is shadowed by a local `const hasScope` in the same function. A key holding only `documents:*` is refused 403 on `GET /api/documents` and every other `/api/documents` method except create (the gateway's create handler in `routes/verification.ts` does accept `documents:*`). The KS-843 comment in the same file already calls the exact match "silent". No gateway test covers a `<resource>:*` key (control: the shared tests have 8 such cells).
4. **No validation at mint.** `services/security/src/index.ts` mint schema is `scopes: z.array(z.string()).default(['read'])`; originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`) stores the list as given; the shared `validateScopes` has no caller outside its own tests. The default `read` is not a vocabulary scope.
5. `*` **is not reserved.** `decideMint` in `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` allows every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member (`SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN`) with any scope list, `*` included; only a provisioning key is refused wildcards. `SCOPES.md` says `*` is "reserved for super-admin keys".
6. **Out-of-vocabulary strings in use.** `webhooks:manage` (gates `/api/webhooks`), `users:create` (accepted by auth's `POST /api/users/stub`), `register` (legacy literal in the gateway's create handler), `metering:read` (minted onto the metering key by `services/tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts`; no gate reads it), `read`/`write` (mint defaults and the fixed set the admin portal sends), and the OAuth list (`verify:read`, `admin:read`, `admin:write` in `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts`). The KS-540 inventory raised items 3, 4 and 6 as F-3, F-4 and F-5 on 2026-07-31; none is done.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (anchors:read, documents:revoke), KS-1777 (the flat 403 body of `requireScope`), KS-1653 (`certifications:write` admits `POST /api/users/stub`), KS-839 (OAuth `*`), KS-1535 and KS-1536 (which roles may mint keys).

Searched the board before filing: `certifications:share`, `certifications:revoke`, `analytics:read`, `users:write`, `kyc:submit`, `certifications:sign`, `metering:read` and `hasScope` each 0 hits; `wildcard` 4 hits (KS-839, KS-1584, KS-1156, KS-1210, none about the gateway helper); `validateScopes` 2 hits (KS-839, KS-1156). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843 and `documents:revoke` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 (docs lead, code aligns), either make each declared scope gate its route, or take the entry out of the vocabulary and out of the docs; make `requireScope` call `hasScope`; call `validateScopes` at both mints; restrict `*` to the roles the docs name. Which of these is intended is open, and PR-1 says so in the docs.

title: #1013 gate findings (KS-999): the getUserById route-level 503 and its log line are unpinned; a burnt backup code is told to retry
description:
## BLUF

The tier-1 QA gate for PR #1013 (KS-999, merged as `e0f41a8fafd64fa31524390cfeab320e822f3d15`) returned GO WITH FINDINGS. Three findings sit outside the merged change and are collected here. None is a defect in #1013's code.

* **F1 (Minor, test coverage):** no test pins the route-level HTTP 503 on the routes that call `getUserById`. A caller that fails OPEN on a 503 goes unnoticed.
* **F2 (Polish, test coverage):** no test pins the shape of the new classifier log line. A user id or a stack added to it later goes unnoticed.
* **F3 (Minor, product):** in a backup-code sign-in, the single-use code can be burnt and then the user is told "please retry". The retry with the same code is refused 401 and counts toward the lockout.

## Recommendation

Not built. Wednesday routes these.

* F1 and F2 are test-only pins.
* **F3 is a product decision** about the order of the burn versus the wording of the 503. It is described below with no proposed fix.

## Detail

**Source:** gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks999-1013-5fbfb66a9-tier1-r1/report.md`, section 4. Measured in-process against the real auth routers and the real `passwordLoginGate`, with the DB, the DEK store and the logger stubbed and witnessed. There was no live stack.

### F1: the route-level 503 is unpinned (Minor)

* **Tamper** `G-CALLER-FAILOPEN`**:** in `routes/mfa.ts`, make `getUserById(userId)` swallow a 503 to null. Project tsc rc 0; the whole auth suite ran 745 cells with **0 red**.
* The gate's HTTP probe under the same tamper: `GET /api/auth/mfa/status` goes from **503 to 200 with** `mfaEnabled: false`. That happens under an all-reads DEK fault, under three `getUserById`-only DEK faults (message form, pg `53300`, `ECONNREFUSED`) and under a `query()` fault.
* The ks999 cells pin the repository-level throw only. No cell covers any `getUserById` route over HTTP.
* **The pin the gate asks for:** one HTTP cell per route family (for example `GET /api/users/me` and `GET /api/auth/mfa/status`) where `getDek` rejects with an infrastructure error, expecting 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Add a control where a non-infrastructure rejection gives 500.

### F2: the classifier log line's shape is unpinned (Polish)

* **Tamper** `Q-LOG-LEAK`**:** `getUserById`'s catch also logs `stack` and `userId`. Project tsc rc 0; 745 run, **0 red**.
* The ks999 log cell matches with `objectContaining({ error })`, so extra keys pass.
* Today the line's meta is `{ error, code }`, with no user id (measured).
* **The pin the gate asks for:** assert that the meta key set is exactly `{ error, code }`.

### F3: a burnt backup code is told to retry (Minor, product decision)

**Where:** `services/passwordLoginGate.ts:267` burns the code through `userRepo.updateUserOrThrow(...)`. `updateUser` then reads the row back through `getUserById`. Line numbers are at develop `e0f41a8fa`.

**Steps (gate harness: real argon2 backup-code hashing):**

1. A user with MFA on and 2 backup codes.
2. `POST /api/auth/login` with email, password and a valid backup code as the MFA code, while the DEK read inside the read-back `getUserById` fails with `connection terminated unexpectedly`.
3. Retry the same request with healthy reads.

**What happens:**

| Tree | Step 2 | Codes left after step 2 | Step 3 (same code) | Lockout failures |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Head (after #1013) | **503** "Authentication service temporarily unavailable, please retry", no token | 2 → **1** (the burn landed) | **401** "Invalid email or password" | 1 |
| Base (before #1013) | 500, no token | 2 → 1 (same burn) | 401 | 1 |

**Gate controls:**

* A healthy login, then reuse of the same code: 200, then 401. The fixture's code really is single-use.
* A `query()` fault BEFORE the burn: 503, then **200** on retry. The retry advice is right when nothing was burnt.

**Why it reads as a problem:**

* `updateUserOrThrow`'s own doc comment (`repositories/userRepo.ts:955-958`) gives 503 as the right answer mainly "where the caller still holds an unburnt single-use token". Here the token is already burnt.
* `updateUserOrThrow`'s own 503 message hedges: "Please retry — if you already succeeded, you may not need to."
* But in this path the 503 is raised earlier, by `getUserById`'s classifier during the read-back. The user therefore sees the plain "please retry" text, and following it costs a refusal plus a lockout increment.
* Before #1013 the same burn answered 500, so the burn itself is not new. What #1013 added is the invitation to retry.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches in title, description or comments:

* `getUserById`: 21 fuzzy results, 21 literal hits.
* `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`: 114 fuzzy, 16 literal.
* `backup-code`: 94 fuzzy, 13 literal.
* `userRepo.ts`: 98 fuzzy, 54 literal.

None covers these three findings:

* KS-999 and KS-1186 are the parent and the sibling-site ticket, related here.
* KS-1052 (Done, archived) introduced `updateUserOrThrow` and the backup-code burn check. It is named here rather than related, because archived issues refuse relations.
* KS-253 (Done, archived) is the classifier contract.
* KS-1132 / KS-1005 / KS-1018 / KS-943 / KS-1050 are other `getUserById` or `userRepo.ts` defects, not these pins.

title: FLAKE (3rd occurrence, first with a name): ks949 seed-site enumeration fails ~1 in 7 full auth runs and passes alone — timeout hypothesis refuted
description:
## BLUF

`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` **fails intermittently in the FULL** `services/auth` **suite and passes on every re-run.** This is the **third** occurrence of a self-healing auth failure. It is the first one with a **name**, which is the only reason it is a ticket rather than a memory.

**Cell:** `the real person is gone from every EXECUTABLE seed site › the enumeration actually finds seed sites, including the one the gate planted in`

## The measurement, 2026-09-09

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full `services/auth` suite | **FAILED** — `Error: STACK_TRACE_ERROR` at `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:314` |
| 2, 3 | full suite, identical tree | 642/642 green |
| 4, 5 | full suite, after an unrelated mock fix | 641/642 then 641/642 (a *different*, deterministic failure, since fixed) |
| 6, 7 | full suite | **642/642 green** |
| — | that file ALONE | **30/30 green, 2.73 s** |
| control | full suite on clean develop `d4cf7e3cf`, separate worktree | **635/635 green** |

## Hypothesis TESTED and NOT SUPPORTED — do not re-propose without new evidence

**Timeout under full-suite parallelism.** The failing cell walks the whole `Blockchain/Dev` tree reading every `.ts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.sql/.sh` file, which is the slowest thing in the suite, and `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is a shape vitest produces for a task-level abort. **Refuted by the same instrument:** it passes under *identical* parallelism on runs 2, 3, 6 and 7. A timeout that fires once in seven identical runs is not explained by the walk being slow.

**Mechanism therefore UNESTABLISHED.**

## 🔑 How this was caught — the part worth keeping

`HANDOVER-s161.md` **§3 records two earlier occurrences (**`api-gateway` **1/293,** `auth` **2/633) whose test names were NEVER captured.** Without a name there is nothing to pick up, which is precisely why s161 declined to file them and why that was the right call at the time.

That handover shipped an instrument for the next occurrence:

```bash
npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/vitest-run-$(date +%s).json
```

…with the standing instruction: **capture the name FIRST, before re-running, because a re-run destroys the evidence** — and both earlier events were lost to exactly that.

**It was used on the third occurrence and it produced the name. The instrument paid inside one day of being written.** That is the difference between *"we keep seeing flakes"* and *"we caught the third one because the second one left us a tool."* This ticket exists to make that fact survive the handover it came from.

## Why this is now closeable when the first two were not

It carries a **named subject**, a **reproduction attempt with its result** (7 full runs + 1 isolated + 1 clean-develop control), and a **refuted hypothesis** so the next person does not spend the hour re-proposing it. Mechanism-unestablished is a fine state for a ticket; *unidentified* was not.

## Where to start

1. Re-run the full suite in a loop capturing JSON per run until it reproduces (it took 1 in 7 here) — **do NOT pipe through** `tail`**/**`head`, which is how the first two names were lost.
2. When it reproduces, read `failureMessages` from the JSON rather than the terminal: `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is what the JSON reporter emitted, and the human reporter may carry more.
3. `ks949…test.ts:314` is the tree-walk control cell — `expect(sites.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3)`. Worth logging `sites` on failure, since an enumeration that transiently returns fewer sites is a different defect from a timeout, and both would present this way.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — found during that work; carries the same record.
* `5_Project_History/HANDOVER-s161.md` §3 — the two earlier occurrences and the instrument.

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling.*

title: Two reconciler.ts comments are false: a provider error does not leave the row untouched past 24 h, and the poll never touches updated_at
description:
**BLUF:** Two comments in anchoring's `reconciler.ts` say something the code does not do. I read both against the code at develop `6d41673e0f79`. (1) The header property at `:22`, "a chain-provider error leaves the row untouched for the next pass", holds only below the 24 hour give-up age: past it, the same provider error is read as absence and the row is written `failed`. (2) The comment at `:63-64`, "MIN_AGE keeps the reconciler off rows the live submit/confirm loop is still actively working (it touches updated_at as it goes)", is false for the confirmation phase: the poll writes nothing, so `updated_at` does not move between `submitted` and `confirmed`, and the poll outlasts `MIN_AGE`. Both are source readings; nothing was run.

**Comment 1,** `reconciler.ts:22` (header "Properties" list): "a chain-provider error leaves the row untouched for the next pass."

* `index.ts:2192` wires `checkTx` as `waitForConfirmation(tx, 1, 0, 0)`. `cardano/confirmation.ts:98-99` catches a provider error inside the loop (`errored += 1`) and `:110-119` returns `{ confirmed: false, polled, errored, … }`; it does not throw. So the reconciler's own `catch` at `reconciler.ts:106-109` ("chain check errored; leaving row as-is") is not reached by a provider outage.
* `reconciler.ts:98` then tests `now() - created_at > giveUpMs` (default 24 h, `index.ts:2198`) and writes `status: 'failed'` with "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h". So below the give-up age an outage leaves the row alone (no statement runs); at or past it, the row is failed. The property is true only for the first case. This is the defect filed separately as KS-1810; this ticket is only about what the comment says.

**Comment 2,** `reconciler.ts:63-64`: "MIN_AGE keeps the reconciler off rows the live submit/confirm loop is still actively working (it touches updated_at as it goes)."

* The reconciler's SELECT takes rows with `updated_at < NOW() - MIN_AGE` (`reconciler.ts:76`); the default is 10 minutes (`index.ts:2197`).
* Every status write goes through `buildAnchorStatusUpdate`, which always adds `updated_at` (`anchorStatusUpdate.ts:101`), so each transition (`submitting`, `submitted`, `confirmed`) moves it.
* Between `submitted` and `confirmed` nothing is written: the poll's callback only logs (`anchorSubmission.ts:280-281` and `:488-489`, "Anchor confirmation poll"), and `bumpRetryCount` updates `retry_count` only (`index.ts:1872-1874`).
* The poll is `waitForConfirmation(txHash, 30, 10_000, 60_000)` (`index.ts:1870`): a sleep of `delay` plus 0 to 2 s jitter follows each of 30 attempts, with `delay` starting at 10 s, multiplied by 1.5 and capped at 60 s (`confirmation.ts:105-107`). I summed it: 10, 15, 22.5, 33.75, 50.6 s and then 60 s for the remaining 25, which is 1631.9 s to 1691.8 s, **27.2 to 28.2 minutes** before request time. So a row still being polled becomes eligible for the reconciler 10 minutes in and stays eligible for more than 17 further minutes.
* What follows from it in the code: the reconciler can scan and confirm a row the live loop is still polling (both writing `confirmed`). Below 24 h it cannot fail it. I did not run that race.

**Seen, outside this item:** the header's property at `reconciler.ts:16-19` says a row goes to `failed` "when the tx has not appeared within the give-up window", while the code measures that window from `created_at` (KS-1808).

**Source of the claim:** Seat W 7th's KS-1384 design revision, section 16 item 7 and section 4.1 (sub-agent A's census, which W 7th spot-checked at `anchorStatusUpdate.ts:101-102` and `index.ts:1874`). I re-read every line above myself.

**Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, lines 172-193 and 494; develop `6d41673e0f79`, the files named above.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 18 hits, a random token 0 hits): `reconciler.ts:63-64` and "touches updated_at as it goes" were checked by the filing tool at 0 hits. The first comment's substance is filed as KS-1810 and the give-up basis as KS-1808; neither mentions the wording of either comment.

**Related:** KS-1810, KS-1808, KS-1384.

title: governance GET /api/governance/proposals can still be silently unfiltered or under-validated (KS-1722 gate residue): misspelled filter names are dropped, no upper-case pin, NUL/control characters and unbounded length in proposerId
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-1722 fix (PR #1696, merged as develop** `18ffc05cda55`**) closed the blank and unusable filter values, but the proposals list can still be silently unfiltered or under-validated by four routes.** All four were **measured by the tier-1 gate on PR #1696** (round 1, GO WITH NOTES), not by the filer. They are one logical path, so this is one ticket. **Not fixed in #1696.**

## The four, as the gate measured them

1. **A misspelled filter name is dropped, and the list comes back unfiltered** (gate Minor 1).
   * `?proposerid=`, `?proposer_id=` and `?Status=` each return the **unfiltered** list.
   * So does a real filter that falls past **Express's 1000-parameter cap** on the query string.
   * Why, from the source: `ProposalListQuerySchema` (`services/governance/src/types/governance.types.ts`) is a plain `z.object`, not `.strict()`, so unknown keys are stripped rather than refused. A caller that misspells the filter it relies on gets everyone's proposals — the same trap KS-1722 closed for a blank value.
2. **No cell pins upper case** (gate Minor 2). A case-insensitive status check stayed **green on all 43 cells** of `ks1722-proposals-list-refuses-an-unusable-filter.test.ts`, including S2, the spec/runtime agreement cell. Nothing would catch `?status=ACTIVE` starting to be accepted.
3. **NUL and control characters in** `proposerId` **pass validation** (gate Note 3). The schema requires only a non-whitespace character. The service's existing NUL guard covers request **bodies** only, per the gate; it is `rejectNulBytes()` in governance `index.ts`.
4. `proposerId` **has no length limit** (gate Note 6). A **15 KB** value was accepted.

## Where

* `services/governance/src/types/governance.types.ts` — `ProposalListQuerySchema` and its value lists.
* `services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` — `GET /proposals`.

title: mapGdprWriteDbError reads err.pgCode before extractPgCode: a hostile throw gets no answer
description:
**BLUF:** `mapGdprWriteDbError` in `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts` reads `(err as { pgCode?: string } | null)?.pgCode` at line 139, **before** it calls `extractPgCode(err)`, which KS-1780 made safe against a hostile thrown value. The read touches the thrown value itself, so a revoked Proxy, or an Error whose `pgCode` getter throws, makes the read throw from inside the `catch` of both callers, and the request gets **no response at all**. Measured on `POST /api/gdpr/dsr`; the gate that raised it (gate 12, finding 1795-2) had it as read only. Low. Related to KS-1780; it is outside that ticket's 17 sites.

**Why KS-1780's own scan did not list it:** that scan classified the first use of the thrown value inside each `catch` and reported, for `gdpr.ts`, "13 go straight, 0 read first, 4 pass the value to something else first". This is the fourth class: the `catch` passes the value to `mapGdprWriteDbError`, and the read happens inside that callee.

**Read, at develop** `5dccdcb29ec2`**:** the function starts at line 138 and line 139 is the read. It has two callers, each directly inside an `async` handler's `catch`, one line before `fail500`: line 264 (`POST /api/gdpr/consent`) and line 346 (`POST /api/gdpr/dsr`). The handlers are `async` on Express 4, so a throw out of the `catch` rejects a promise that Express never sees (the same mechanism the KS 1772 test documents).

**Measured** (a scratch test on develop with the ks1772 harness: the real `gdprRouter` on a loopback listener, the service mocked, a 2500 ms window for an answer; the scratch file was not committed):

1. An Error carrying `pgCode` `23503`, thrown by `createDSR`: answered **404** `NOT_FOUND` (control: `mapGdprWriteDbError` is reached and works).
2. An ordinary `Error('boom')`: answered the constant **500** (control).
3. A revoked Proxy: **no answer within 2500 ms**. The jest log names the escaping error as `TypeError: Cannot perform 'get' on a proxy that has been revoked` at `gdpr.ts:139:53`, called from `gdpr.ts:346:9`.
4. An Error whose `pgCode` getter throws: **no answer within 2500 ms**.

**Not measured:** `POST /api/gdpr/consent` itself (read only: its call is the same, at line 264, but an ownership check runs before it, so I drove `/dsr`); any other caller; production exposure. The pg driver throws ordinary Errors, so reaching this needs a thrown value whose property read throws; it is recorded for consistency with the KS-1780 hardening, not as a reproduced incident.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** call `extractPgCode(err)` first and read `pgCode` through the same guarded path, or put the `pgCode` read inside a `try` that falls through to `fail500`. A cell per caller in the style of the KS-1780 cells would pin it.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 22:3xZ): `mapGdprWriteDbError` 1 hit, KS 591, read: it cites the function only to explain a 400 mapping, not this; `gdpr.ts:139` 1 hit, KS 228 (Done), an ownership-check ticket; `pgCode` 2 hits, KS-1780 (its scan is quoted above) and KS 1341 (error text in webhooks 500s); `revoked Proxy` 5 hits, read by title (KS 1780, KS 1772, KS 1771, KS 1614, KS 1524), none covers `mapGdprWriteDbError`. The positive control `parseScopeString` found 4; a nonsense token generated at run time found 0 and was not recorded in this ticket.

title: certifications.ts GET /:id catch reads code, meta.code and message of the thrown value unguarded: a hostile throw gets no answer
description:
**BLUF:** The catch of originate `GET /api/certifications/:id` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`: handler at :1020, catch at :1065, the unguarded reads at :1073 and :1074, develop `530f091120d5`) reads `code`, `meta.code` and `message` straight off the thrown value, and tests `error instanceof Error`, with no try of its own. A thrown value whose property read throws (a revoked Proxy, or a getter that throws) therefore throws inside the catch of an async Express 4 handler, and the request gets no answer. Same family as KS-1798 (the GDPR write routes, in review) and KS-1780 (Done: systemErrors, adminConfig, `extractPgCode`). Found while building KS-1798. Read, and probed at the language level; not run on this route.

**What I read**

* `certifications.ts:1020` is `GET /:id`, an `async` handler. Its `catch (error)` at :1065 runs `const pgCode = (error as { code?: string })?.code ?? (error as { meta?: { code?: string } })?.meta?.code;` (:1073), then `error instanceof Error && error.message.includes('22P02')` (:1074), then `logger.error(... error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error))` (:1077). None of the three is inside a try.
* The same file already does the safe thing elsewhere: :926 reads the code through `extractPgCode(error)`, which KS-1780 made safe against a hostile thrown value.
* Express in this tree is 4.22.3, which does not forward a rejected async handler promise, so a throw out of the catch block leaves the request unanswered. KS-1798's cells D1 and D2 show exactly that on the gdpr routes (a request with no answer in 1500 ms; 3 of 20 red before the guard). That is the measured mechanism; it was not run on this route.
* Language-level probe on Node v26.8.1: with a revoked Proxy, `error?.code` throws a TypeError and so does `error instanceof Error`; with an Error whose `code` getter throws, `error?.code` throws; an ordinary Error reads without throwing.
* A scan of non-test originate `src` for the pattern `(error as { code?` finds this site only (the other hit, `documentRepo.ts:903`, writes a code onto its own Error).

**Why it is not fixed here**

* `certifications.ts` is outside the pass that found it, and Wednesday ruled this is a separate lane (the file was changed by pull request 1822, merged at `530f091120d5`).
* Exposure is low: the value comes from `getCertification`, a database layer that raises Prisma and pg errors; a hostile value cannot be sent from outside (KS-1780 records the same). Priority 4.

**Suggested shape (not designed, not tested):** classify through `extractPgCode(error)`, put the `instanceof` and `message` reads behind one guarded helper, and add cells like KS-1798's D1 and D2 for this route.

**Searched** (whole-board census, 1832 issues of which 1009 archived, 5195 comments, local regex over title, description and comments; every hit read): `certifications\.ts:?\s*10[67][0-9]` 0 hits; `meta\??\.code` 3 hits (KS-1799, KS-1798, KS-1780: all about `extractPgCode` in `pgErrors.ts`, a different file); `certifications\.ts.{0,80}(meta|code)` 3 hits (KS-1666, a comment-only change to two comments in the same file; KS-1475 `certifications.ts:563` and KS-537 `certifications.ts:513/521`, both different defects); a random token 0 (not recorded here). No ticket covers this site.

**Not measured:** a reproduction on this route (no cell run); whether `getCertification` can throw a non-Error value at all; other originate catches that read a thrown value (KS-1780's own census was 17).

title: POST /api/certifications/issue anchors BEFORE it writes its documents row, so any failure of that write leaves an orphan anchor_store row forever
description:
**Filed on Wednesday's instruction (2026-10-19T21:27:45Z), separated OUT of #1568 round 4 deliberately. Pre-existing on develop, independent of migration 051 — 051 merely made it visible. Measured read-only at develop** `83ed01af70fd5ed6cca9ac66f28ddcb8a1034105`**.**

## The order

`POST /api/certifications/issue` (`services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`):

| step | line | what |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `:363` | `const id = uuidv4()` — the certification's primary key |
| 2 | `:445` | POSTs `{ documentId: id, … }` to anchoring `/api/anchors`, **which persists the** `anchor_store` **row before it answers 202** (`anchoring/src/index.ts` — `await dbPersistAnchor(...)` precedes `res.status(202)`) |
| 3 | `:518` | `await saveCertification(...)` → `repositories/certificationRepo.ts:198`, `INSERT INTO documents (id, …) … ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` |

So the `anchor_store` row for the certification's id **always exists before the** `documents` **row does**.

## The defect

**If step 3 fails for any reason, step 2's anchor row is already committed and nothing removes it.** The result is an `anchor_store` row whose `document_id` names no `documents` row — an orphan anchor — created by a legitimate, authenticated product flow, permanently.

This is the same class the #1568 round-2 gate identified as **MAJ-A**: orphan anchors are the rows whose anchored identity can be rewritten by whoever next registers that id (and whose ids are public through verify-by-hash). So this route manufactures members of the attack surface as a side effect of failing.

**Observed, not hypothetical.** The gate L1 report for #1568 round 3 (verdict sha256/16 `92e27bf688ddaf7f`) drove exactly this: with migration 051 installed, step 3 was refused, and the route answered **500 with 0** `documents` **rows written and the anchor row for that id present** — a new orphan, from one request. 051 is the cause of the refusal there; the orphan-on-failure is the pre-existing behaviour the refusal exposed.

## Why it is not a 051 problem

051 is being reworked (round 4 drops the primary-key arm that refused step 3). Once it does, this route stops failing *for that reason* — but **the ordering is unchanged**, so any other failure of `saveCertification` (a constraint, a tenant/FK problem, a connection drop between steps 2 and 3) still leaves the orphan. Fixing 051 does not fix this.

## Suggested shape — a choice for whoever picks it up

1. **Write the** `documents` **row first, then anchor** (what `POST /api/documents` already does: `documentRepo.saveDocument` before the anchor POST). This is the structural fix and it also removes the whole "a certification's primary key is already an anchor id" shape, which is what made the 051 arm unsafe in the first place.
2. **Compensate on failure** — delete or mark the anchor row when step 3 fails. Weaker: the delete can itself fail, and the anchor may already be on chain.
3. **Anchor asynchronously after the row lands.** Largest change; also the one that stops a slow chain blocking the response.

**My recommendation is (1)**, because it is the only one that removes the window rather than narrowing it, and because it makes certifications consistent with documents.

**A cell either way:** a forced failure of `saveCertification` must leave `anchor_store` with **no** row for that id. There is currently no cell on this ordering at all.

## Rating

Filed **Medium**: it creates rows in the exact class a Major was opened about, from a legitimate flow, with no cleanup — but nobody has shown live harm on a real box, and the failure requires step 3 to fail. **A re-rate may well be justified and is not mine to do.**

## Related

* **KS-1612 / PR #1568** — where this surfaced; round 4 must NOT be blocked on it.
* **KS-1603** (the unconditional columns on both `anchor_store` upserts) and **KS-1384** (no tenant column on `anchor_store`) — the structural answers for what an orphan anchor allows once it exists.
* **KS-1229** (Done) names "a refused issue can mint a holder stub or an anchor" among its ten test-only tampers. That was a **coverage** observation on the `documentType` relabel guard; this ticket is the ordering defect itself, which remains unfixed and uncelled.

## Dedupe

Searched the KS board with `issues(filter:{description:{contains:…}})` **and** the same on `title`, for: `certifications.ts:445`, `certificationRepo.ts`, `saveCertification`, `orphan anchor`, `certifications/issue`. Hits were KS-1229 and KS-1267 (both Done, both test-coverage on other guards) and ten `certifications/issue` mentions, none about this ordering. A nonsense-symbol control returned **0**, so the zeroes discriminate. `searchIssues` was NOT used — its control returns a full page for a nonsense term.

*Seat J 13th. Nothing deployed.*

title: KS-1633 follow-ups (PR #1623, gate AK1's nine notes): the row left behind when the reservation lands and the save fails (a design question), two surviving pool mutants, the untested provisionalWritten branch, two stale comments and a warn line that carries the DB error text
description:
## BLUF

**Gate AK1's nine notes on PR #1623 (KS-1633), in one checklist.** The PR merged **GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers**, as develop `adb0dfd58fc582f24ab2a7db021a2027544f566c`, landed tree `e598e00e890284ae6b85a9fe0379eac3c28a72ca`.

**Rated Medium because of item (a)**, which is a design question rather than a defect with an obvious fix: it is asked here, not answered.

## (a) A row left behind when the reservation lands and the save then fails — THE DESIGN QUESTION

`POST /api/certifications/issue` now writes its `documents` row **before** it anchors. If that reservation **succeeds** and the authoritative `saveCertification` then **fails**, the request answers a failure to the client while a row remains, reading `certified` **with anchoring** `failed`**, no anchor id, and zero** `certification_events` **rows**.

It is **not** an orphan anchor — nothing was anchored, so the claimable shape the ticket was about does not arise. It is a certification the caller does not know exists, with no event behind it.

**The question, and it is genuinely open:** compensate it (the same delete the production-503 path uses), or document why not? Arguments both ways: compensating it is consistent with the 503 path and keeps "a failed request wrote nothing" true for one more case; **not** compensating it preserves evidence of a half-completed write that an operator may want, and every compensation is itself a write that can fail. **Whoever picks this up should decide and record the decision — it is not assumed here.**

## (b) Two surviving pool mutants — N1

Both of these **survive** the suite as merged:

1. the route passes **no** pool to `deleteCertification`;
2. `withTenant` **ignores** the pool it is handed.

The unit cell `ks1633-the-compensating-delete-uses-the-requests-pool.test.ts` pins that the route *hands over* `req.tenantPool`, and nothing pins that `withTenant` then *uses* it. **Cells needed that red both.** The honest constraint: no second tenant database was stood up for #1623 (no Docker on that machine, one scratch Postgres instance), so the cross-database path is covered by **no cell at all** — a real second database, or an injected pool whose `connect()` is observed, is what would close it.

## (c) The `provisionalWritten` branch is untested — N2

Nothing exercises the path where the reservation **failed** and the compensation is therefore skipped (`provisionalWritten === false`, which substitutes `1` for the row count). A regression that inverted that flag would either raise a **false** "removed no row" alarm or **suppress a real one**, and nothing would redden. **One cell: reservation made to fail, production + anchoring down, assert the 503 and that no "removed no row" line is logged.**

## (d) Two stale code comments — N5

`services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`:

* `:467` — *"Writing the row first removes the window rather than narrowing it."* **Wrong.** It narrows it: when the reservation itself fails, the anchor-then-fail path is unchanged.
* `:474` — *"the sub-second window before the second write"*. **Wrong.** The window is bounded by the anchoring timeout, `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` — **up to 10 seconds**.

Both were corrected in the PR body before the merge and **deliberately left in the code**, because changing them would have moved the head the GO was pinned to. They are wrong in the merged tree today.

## (e) The ks1633 suite header — N6

`ks1633-certify-writes-its-row-before-it-anchors.integration.test.ts` at `:23`, `:31` and `:262` — the gate asked for the header's wording to be brought in line with the behaviour the cells now assert (the same "narrows / up to 10 s" corrections, and the narrowed ORPHAN claim).

## (f) The warn line carries the database error text — N7

`certifications.ts:530` logs `error: reserveErr.message` alongside `certId` and `tenantId` — the database's **own error text**, not ids alone. **Not new** (this file's warn lines already did this), but **PR #1623's body claimed "ids only" and that claim was wrong**; it was corrected in the body before the merge. Worth a decision here: either the claim goes (and the text stays, consistent with the file's other warns), or the text is dropped to match what the rest of this route promises. A database error message can carry row values.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues`, archived included: `reserveCertificationRow` **→ 0 hits**, `provisionalWritten` **→ 0 hits** (both symbols are new with #1623), and `KS-1633 follow-up compensating delete pool mutants` → 25 hits whose near neighbours are **KS-1633** itself and **KS-1664** (the `/recertify` sibling), neither covering these notes.

## Related

**KS-1633** (merged as `adb0dfd58fc5`) · **KS-1664** (`/recertify` has the same ordering and will need the same three lessons) · **KS-1612 / KS-1384** (what an orphan anchor allows) · **KS-1124 F4** (Kam's ruling on the stored anchor state, which AK1 confirmed still holds) · **KS-1090** (originate's tsconfig excludes its tests, so `tsc -p` cannot catch a type error in any cell above).

title: nft-certificate GET /api/nft/certificates takes userId from the query string, so any authenticated caller lists every recorded NFT
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. `GET /api/nft/certificates` reads `userId` from the query string and defaults it to `'user-id'`, and `mintNFT` and `/record` store every NFT with `userId: 'user-id'`. So a bare `GET /api/nft/certificates` by any authenticated caller lists every recorded NFT across users and tenants, while `?userId=<a real id>` lists none. A `?walletAddress=<any wallet>` selector on the same route has no owner check either. Priority 2 (security), as ruled by Wednesday.

## What I read (develop d7ddfa1f6433)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/routes/nft.routes.ts:224-235`: `const userId = req.query.userId as string || 'user-id';` under the comment "In production, get userId from auth context". If `walletAddress` is in the query the route calls `getWalletNFTCertificates(walletAddress)`; otherwise it calls `getUserNFTCertificates(userId)`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/services/minting.service.ts:224` (`mintNFT`) and `:410` (the `/record` path) store `userId: 'user-id'`, with the comments "Would come from auth context".
* `minting.service.ts:514-522`: `getUserNFTCertificates` keeps in-memory records whose `userId` equals its argument; `:550` is `SELECT * FROM svc_nft_certificates WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC`.
* `minting.service.ts:594-602`: `getWalletNFTCertificates` keeps in-memory records whose `walletAddress` equals its argument and compares nothing to the caller. This is a second selector on the same route and part of this finding, not a separate one.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/app.ts:45-47`: `/api` requires a JWT except the two verify operations. The caller is therefore authenticated, but nothing compares the caller to a record's owner or tenant.

## What I did not run or read

* No reproduction, no database, no box. Whether any NFT record exists on a box: UNMEASURED.
* The database branch of `getWalletNFTCertificates` past its row type (`:605` onward), and `GET /api/nft/certificates/:id` (`nft.routes.ts:257`).
* How the gateway forwards `/api/nft`, and which caller uses this list route. Seat A 17th's note says the gateway mounts the route with optional auth and that the issuer portal calls `/nft/record`; I did not re-read either.

## Source and searches

title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor has no role, owner or revoked-document check: any authenticated tenant user can trigger a re-anchor
description:
**BLUF:** Surface: originate `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`, the retry route. I read the route and every layer in front of and behind it at develop `6d41673e0f79`. The only gates are authentication (a Bearer token and an active session), tenant scoping, and the refusal "Document is already anchored". There is no role gate, no owner check and no terminal-status guard. So any authenticated user in the tenant, including the public-signup `OWNER` role, which the share and transfer-custody gates exclude by design (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:24-27`), can make originate call the anchoring service for a document whose blob is missing or `anchor_failed`; on success the route writes `status: 'anchored'` over the document, revoked or deleted ones included. This is a source reading. I ran no request against any box and did not execute the route.

**Route** (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `:1437-1571`):

* `:1442` `getUserFromRequest` and a 401 when absent; `:1449` `getDocument(id, tenantId, req.db)` and a 404 when the document is not found in the caller's tenant.
* `:1458` the only state check: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored". A document with no blob at all passes it.
* `:1474-1478` it calls `${ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL}/api/anchors` with the caller's own `Authorization` header; `:1489` the body carries `...anchorIdentityFields(req.body)`, so the caller's request body supplies the identity fields (the comment above it, `:1488`, is "the re-anchor path carries S's identity too").
* `:1534-1537` `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' })` with no options; `:1545` starts the confirmation poll; `:1560` answers 202.
* Within `:1437-1571` there is none of `ALLOWED_*_ROLES`, `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES`, `hasAnyRole`, `requireRole`, `requireSelfOrRole` or `requireScope` (census of the file below).

**Siblings in the same file:** `POST /` (`:373`, `ALLOWED_CREATION_ROLES`), `transfer-custody` (`:1789`, `ALLOWED_TRANSFER_CUSTODY_ROLES`, declared `:1782`), `version` (`:2263`, `:2258`), `share` (`:2464`, `:2458`), `sign-cert` (`:2936`) and `sign-wallet` (`:3204`) each check a constant built from `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:37`: `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`; the file says at `:24` that `OWNER` is deliberately absent). `revoke` (`:2650`) is owner-only: `if (document.owner?.id !== user.id)` then 403 "Only the owner can revoke this document" (`:2677-2679`). The token census finds no gate in `sign`, `sign/request` or the lifecycle-events routes; I did not read whether they have another kind of check, so this ticket does not claim the retry route is the only route without one. W 7th's comparison, `GET /:id` (`:1078-1217`), is not a role gate either: its matches are the admin cross-tenant fallback terms.

**Layers in front** (read):

* originate `index.ts`: gateway provenance (`:219`), emitter-marker strip (`:223`), the multi-tenancy block (`:226-244`), request tenant resolution (`:259-262`) and `tenantGucContext()` (`:263`). They establish where a request came from and which tenant it is in; none checks a role or an owner.
* `documentsRouter.use(authenticate())` (`documents.ts:175`). `authenticate()` (`middleware/auth.ts:82-137`) verifies the RS256 token and the session; it sets the user and checks no role.
* api-gateway `routes/proxy.ts:657`: `requireScope('documents:read', 'documents:write')` on the whole `/api/documents` mount. `middleware/scopes.ts:34-36` lets JWT and email users straight through ("controlled by RBAC, not scopes"), and `:51` passes an OAuth or API-key caller on ANY ONE of the listed scopes or `*`, with no distinction by method. A search of the gateway's non-test source for `documents:write` and for a method-aware scope check found none for this path. Whether an OAuth or API-key principal reaches originate in a form originate accepts, I did not read (`utils/originateForward.ts`).

**Layer behind** (read): anchoring `index.ts:469` is `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, authentication only. `POST /api/anchors` (`:475`) has no role gate; the only role reference near it is the connector branch (`:554`). KS-1603 already tracks that anchoring does not check who owns `documentId`.

**Terminal status** (read): `documentRepo.ts:598` and `:621-622` make the status write `WHEN preserveTerminal AND status IN ('revoked','deleted') THEN status ELSE <new>`, and `preserveTerminalStatuses` defaults to false (documented at `:520-534`, KS-521: the async anchor pipeline "stomped a revoked set by the owner ... so a revoked document verified again"). The create path passes it (`documents.ts:1015`, `:1038`); the retry route does not. `revoke` writes the status only (`documents.ts:2705`), so a revoked document whose blob is absent or `anchor_failed` satisfies the route's entry condition.

**Cost, as logged:** each accepted anchor logs a submission with a fee. Seat D 42nd's demo log shows `"Anchor submitted to Cardano"` with `"fee":179449` (lovelace) in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatD-42nd/evidence/demo/moved_logs.txt`. Whose wallet pays on each box, I did not verify here.

**Real callers:** Platform S uses this route in its normal flow; KS-1688's comment of 2026-10-19 describes "the anchor kick that follows it (`POST /{newId}/anchor`)" signed with the owning organisation's connector key. Any gate has to keep that principal working; `transfer-custody` shows one shape (a write role OR a scope, documented at `documents.ts:1589-1591`). I am not proposing the fix.

**Not run, not read:** no request to any box; the route was not executed; cross-tenant behaviour beyond the tenant-scoped `getDocument` and the RLS context was not exercised; the gateway's API-key and OAuth path into originate; `sign`, `sign/request` and the lifecycle-events routes, which show no role token.

**Evidence:**

* Source: develop `6d41673e0f79c0f02c2ec7b893cc960b6fa3ec10`, the files named above.
* Seat W 7th's section 16, item 9 (and item 10, the revival): `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, lines 496 and 497. Its claim was a lexical count "not verified against upstream middleware"; this ticket is that verification.
* My route census and reads: `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/filings/board_search_i.txt` for the board search.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1437` 0 hits; "/:id/anchor" 6 hits and "POST /api/documents/:id/anchor" 4 hits, read: KS-1557 (quotes the route name inside an error message), KS-1385 (lists the route among six sites that forward identity), KS-520, KS-319, KS-535, KS-566 (archived, other defects); `anchorIdentityFields` 1 hit (KS-1709, other defect); `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` 10 hits, read by title: KS-1688 is the same class on `POST /:id/version` (a missing per-document check on the source document), KS-547 (archived) is a decision about `/certifications/issue`; `preserveTerminalStatuses` 5 hits: KS-1424's table of unguarded `updateDocument` callers lists `documents.ts:1408` and the sync writers, not this route's call at `:1534`. No ticket names this route's missing gate or its missing terminal-status guard.

**Related:** KS-1688 (same class, the version route), KS-1603 (the anchoring side), KS-485 (the security review plan).

title: Security review — plan, methodology & handover (Platform K)
description:
> **This issue is the coordination hub and living plan for the Platform K security review.** It holds the scope, threat model, methodology, the index of review work-streams, the evidence-cited findings register, remediation sequencing, and full handover context so anyone can pick this up cold. Modelled on the Platform S plan [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175).
>
> **v1 — grounded 2026-07-21 against** `develop` **@** `fcf2d878c` (161 commits since 2026-07-01). Register built from a 6-stream parallel recon (A–F); each finding cites `file:line` under `Blockchain/Dev/` on develop.

## 1. Target & threat context

* **System:** platform-k = the Secuura Cardano/blockchain anchoring platform. Node.js microservices monorepo (28 backend services: api-gateway, auth, originate, anchoring, timestamping, kyc, billing, analytics, m365-integration, tenant-provisioning, wallet-connector, nft-certificate, vc-issuer, security, governance, guardian, etc.), PostgreSQL/Prisma + RLS, Redis, Aiken smart contracts on Cardano, three React frontends (Issuer/Verifier/Admin) + Outlook/Gmail add-ins.
* **Code:** `Distributed_Secuura`, remote `github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git`, branch `develop`. Platform under `Blockchain/Dev/`.
* **Live env (2026-07-08,** [KS-414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-414/demo-env-cost-pivot-replace-container-apps-with-a-single-vm-running)): single Azure VM — Caddy auto-TLS → compose nginx gateway (`nginx-demo.conf`) at `https://demo-pk.secuura.net`. The Container Apps template + hardened `nginx-production.conf` are **decommissioned/unused**. **⚠ v1 claimed** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING=true` **in the demo. That is FALSE (corrected 2026-08-13).** The demo does **real** Cardano `preview`-testnet anchoring: `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is unset, `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` is set, anchoring boots `cardanoMode: REAL (Blockfrost)`, and a funded **platform wallet mnemonic is present on the VM**. Treat the anchoring path on the live target as a live chain-submission path with key material, not a simulation — see the re-grounding comment (2026-08-13) and KS-535 / KS-607.
* **Integrations:** platform-s (SSD document platform, the S↔K channel — K is the server), Stripe (billing), Microsoft 365 / Entra Verified-ID (KYC/IDV), M365 Graph (Outlook/Gmail add-ins), Cardano (Blockfrost).
* **Protects:** legally-significant artefacts (on-chain anchors, timestamps, VCs/NFTs, document hashes), PII, org/tenant data, payment flows, per-tenant connector credentials.
* **Threat assumptions:** millions of users, high public profile, under continuous attack. Treat availability, tenant isolation, and **anchor/signature integrity** as first-order.

## 2. Objectives

1. Evidence-cited findings register (`file:line`, severity) across the whole attack surface — kept current with develop.
2. Prioritised, **sequenced** remediation issues with owners and acceptance criteria (see §5).
3. Strategic hardening for scale — WAF, bot/anti-automation, edge rate-limits/body-caps, secret manager at runtime, DDoS protection, observability/alerting.
4. Repeatable security gates (make the report-only CI scans blocking; keep the [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) audit-gate + lockfile clean-room green) so posture doesn't regress.
5. A **security regression test** for every confirmed finding, in the right harness (systemTest — schemathesis / Akto / cross-tenant-isolation / Playwright).

## 3. Scope & review work-streams

Recon streams A–F are **complete** (this v1 pass). Work-stream owners: **Kamil** for A–F + H; **Peter** for G (systemTest).

> **Table amended 2026-08-13** — the v1 table showed six streams all reading "Recon done", which had drifted from the board in both directions and **omitted Review H entirely** (created by comment on 2026-07-21, closed 2026-08-02). A wrong index costs every future reader. `Status` below is the live Linear state; `Recon` records whether the v1 recon pass covered it.

| \# | Work-stream | Issue | Owner | Recon | Status (live 2026-08-13) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A | AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR | [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| B | Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto | [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| C | S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations (M365 / KYC / wallet / email) | [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| D | Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity | [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| E | Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain | [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| F | Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation | [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491) | Kamil | done | **Todo — IN PROGRESS 2026-08-13** (untouched 07-21 → 08-13) |
| **G** | **systemTest security regression coverage** | [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492) | **Peter** | n/a | Standing (Todo) |
| **H** | **Dependency currency & known-vuln package upgrades** | [KS-493](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-493) | Kamil | done (pass-2) | ✅ **Done 2026-08-02** |

**Deferred as its own sequenced pass:** re-recon of streams A–F against the 168 commits / 202 changed files landed since v1's baseline `fcf2d878c`. Tracked as [KS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-612) (child of this issue) — this re-grounding refreshed the *plan*, not the findings.

## 4. Methodology

Recon → findings register (severity-rated, evidence-cited, mapped loosely to OWASP ASVS / Top 10) → triage (severity × exploitability × blast-radius-at-scale) → sequenced remediation issues with acceptance criteria → verification (reproduce pre-fix, confirm blocked post-fix, add a systemTest regression). **Re-ground the register against develop whenever the branch has materially moved** (the [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s) v2 pass is the template).

## 5. Findings register + remediation sequencing

**Legend:** Sev = severity as found on develop @ `fcf2d878c`. All rows cite `Blockchain/Dev/…`. Full evidence + GREEN notes live on each work-stream issue.

### A — AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242-272` | `POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body, no self/admin check → spoofed `security`/`system` notifications w/ `actionUrl` to anyone (in-app phishing / BOLA). |
| Med | `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:173-205`; transfer `routes/documents.ts:1318` | Documents scoped by `tenant_id` only, never `owner_user_id` — any user in a tenant can read/mutate/transfer another user's doc. Confirm intended tenant==org boundary. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/index.ts:220-227`; `routes/documents.ts:131-133` | Tenant scope derived from inbound `x-tenant-id`; originate JWT has no `tenantId` to cross-check → pure header trust. Safe only via gateway strip + RLS; header-forwarding/SSRF re-opens [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug)-class cross-tenant read. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/routes/mfa.ts:225-236` | `mfa/verify` validates TOTP with no proof factor-1 passed (standalone TOTP oracle; issues no tokens). |
| Low | gateway `middleware/auth.ts:106-150` vs auth `middleware/authenticate.ts:19-65` | `test_token_*` backdoor guarded asymmetrically — one mis-set env = role/tenant spoof. |

### B — Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto — [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:1072,1202` | Teams `webhookUrl` validated only by `z.string().url()` — no SSRF guard; `fetch()` to `169.254.169.254`/RFC1918/localhost. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:153-205,455-490` | `validateWebhookUrl` blocks only IP literals (no DNS resolution → DNS-rebind) and only at registration, not send time. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1769-1773` (+`:36`) | `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` mints ORG_ADMIN/OWNER w/ hardcoded `admin123`; no `NODE_ENV`/`ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` gate. |
| Med | `services/kyc/src/index.ts:251` | ID images stored from caller-supplied `mimeType`, no magic-byte verification. |
| Low | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/taskpane/index.tsx:60` | `el.innerHTML` interpolates `${e.message}` — unescaped sink (error path). |

### C — S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations — [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts:201` | Callback authed by static `api-key` w/ hardcoded default `'secuura-kyc-callback'` → forge Entra Verified-ID results. |
| High | `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts:246-259` | `POST /api/wallets/verify` is a stub — always `verified:true`. Wallet-ownership proof fully bypassable. |
| Med | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:138-161,235-243` | Graph access+refresh tokens persisted to Postgres in plaintext. |
| Med | `services/billing/src/routes/webhooks.ts:34-37` | `isEventProcessed` fails **open** on DB-unavailable → redelivered Stripe event re-adds credits. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/services/email.ts:40-45,148-149` | No CRLF sanitisation on `documentTitle`→`subject`; no recipient-domain allow-list. |
| Low | `frontend/gmail-addon/Code.gs:17-18` | Hardcoded to decommissioned Container Apps URLs (stale). |

### D — Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity — [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:582-593` | On anchoring-POST failure with `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` unset (**default**), fabricates `tx_sim_…` + `status:'anchored'` — outage → fake anchored doc. No `NODE_ENV` guard. |
| Med | `services/timestamping/src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:305-325` | TSA error/timeout → `success:true` self-generated `mock:true` token for eIDAS/UETA artefacts. |
| Med | `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts:38-50` | First non-null Blockfrost `getTransaction` → `confirmed:true`; no finality threshold. |
| Med | `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:982-1041` | `verify` derives `verified:true` from local DB row only; single anchors get no chain re-fetch/hash compare. |

### E — Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain — [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:61` (repeated) | 32-char `APP_DB_PASSWORD` literal committed as `:-default` across **51** conn strings — `grep -c 'APP_DB_PASSWORD:-' Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` at the grounding SHA `fcf2d878c` **and** at develop `87384a8ba` (2026-09-06); the original "\~20" was wrong when written, not drifted. See comment `ef553d29`. |
| High | `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml:99,112,134,138,272,298` | Trivy/Gitleaks/Semgrep/Checkov all `continue-on-error` → report-only, can't block a merge. |
| Med | `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:365-366,369,377` | KV secrets → `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` unmasked + inlined into `DATABASE_URL`. |
| Med | `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:64,119` | Postgres (`:6432`) + Redis (`:6379`) publish to host by default. |
| Med | root `package-lock.json` axios 1.16.1; kyc 1.15.2; mobile 1.13.2 | Stale-lock axios drift vs 1.18.1 (other advisories already patched — axios is the only live drift). [KS-420](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-420/dependency-and-tooling-version-hygiene-audit-from-clean-rebuild) #6. |
| Low | all `services/*/Dockerfile`, `frontend/*` | Base images tag- not digest-pinned; `auth/Dockerfile:46` ships build tooling in runtime layer. |

### F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation — [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere (Cloudflare DNS-only). Product owner wants WAF — greenfield. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` | Live gateway has no `limit_req`/`client_max_body_size`; hardened `nginx-production.conf` is decommissioned-path only. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | Real TLS edge (Caddy on VM) not version-controlled. |
| High | repo-wide absent | No CAPTCHA/Turnstile on signup/login/verify. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on Redis error ([KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |

### Remediation sequencing (amplifier-first)

* **Wave 1 — active exposure + one-liners:** ungated `seed-demo-users` (B), KYC callback default-secret (C), wallet-verify stub (C), committed `APP_DB_PASSWORD` + lock pg/redis to internal (E/F), make CI scan gates blocking (E).
* **Wave 2 — integrity criticals (K's crown jewels):** anchor-fabrication-on-outage + `NODE_ENV` guard (D), qualified-TSA mock fallback (D), verify-against-chain not DB (D), finality threshold (D), m365 SSRF + originate webhook DNS-rebind/send-time revalidation (B).
* **Wave 3 — authz/tenancy hardening:** notification BOLA (A), document owner-scoping decision + fix (A), close header-trust tenancy path / add JWT `tenantId` cross-check (A), M365 token encryption at rest (C), billing idempotency fail-closed (C).
* **Wave 4 — edge & strategic (scale):** WAF at the edge (F), bot/anti-automation (F), version-control the Caddy edge + port `nginx-production.conf` rate-limits/body-caps/headers to the live conf (F/E), runtime secret manager on the VM (E), observability/alerting (F).
* **Wave 5 — hygiene backlog:** axios lockfile regen (E, [KS-420](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-420/dependency-and-tooling-version-hygiene-audit-from-clean-rebuild) #6), digest-pin base images + drop build tooling from auth runtime (E), MFA-verify factor-1 binding + test-token env symmetry (A), email CRLF/allow-list + gmail-addon dead URLs (C).

## 6. Handover / continuity

* **Grounded against** `develop` @ `fcf2d878c` (2026-07-21). All findings cite `file:line` under `Blockchain/Dev/`.
* **Owners:** Kamil (A–F remediation); Peter (G / all systemTest security work — per project convention).
* **Live env reality:** the demo runs on a single VM (Caddy → `nginx-demo.conf`), **not** the Container Apps template — treat `nginx-production.conf` as an unused hardening template, not today's edge. See `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`.
* **Related tickets/programs:** [KS-201](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-201/enforce-utc-for-all-datetime-handling-across-backend-services-and) (UTC), [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) (on-chain PII-min), [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) (npm-audit gate), [KS-420](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-420/dependency-and-tooling-version-hygiene-audit-from-clean-rebuild) [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#6](https://linear.app/secuura/review/openapi-track-2-ks-2-demo-deploy-hardening-verifier-fixes-035a046e49aa) (lockfile drift), [KS-384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-384/lockfiles-gate-blind-spot-manifest-only-dependency-bumps-the) (lockfiles-gate blind spot), [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug) (historical cross-tenant leak — see A header-trust residual), [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis) (rate-limit fail-open), [KS-258](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-258/testschemathesis-add-gdpr-idor-ownership-guard-regression-tests-ks-228)/[KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing) (schemathesis security checks), [KS-263](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-263/enable-code-security-ghas-so-security-scans-populate-the-security-tab) (enable GHAS), and the Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration — cross-reference where crypto/auth findings overlap. Cross-boundary trust with platform-s is covered from S's side in [PS-178](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-178). **S↔K data-loss / unrecoverability register:** [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) (18 likelihood-rated rows from the [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) sign-off) — **closed Done 2026-09-14**, every row dispositioned to an owner ticket; see the closure comment on this issue dated 2026-09-14. K-side residue: [KS-532](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532/sk-dr-k-side-key-store-restore-path-joint-restore-point-coverage-demo) (DR rows #8/#14/#18, Kam), [KS-581](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-581/register-connector-volume-alerting-rate-limit-and-correlation-of) (row #15 — `externalRef` GUID validation + env-scoped provisioning creds, Kam), [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) (rows #16/#17 systemTest regression, Peter, blocked on [KS-516](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516/schemathesis-systemtest-seed-a-real-sk-api-key-documentswrite-so-the)).
* **Test harness for verification (G):** `systemTest/schemathesis` (custom checks incl. GDPR/IDOR ownership guard + 5xx guard), `systemTest/akto` (OWASP scan), `systemTest/cross-tenant-isolation` (IDOR repro), `systemTest/playwright`, spec-auth conformance in `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh`.

**Status:** recon complete (A–F, v1); register grounded to develop; work-stream issues [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor)…[KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) filed with pre-seeded findings; remediation not yet started — sequenced above.

title: Review stream: S<->K integration contract
description:
**Review stream for Stuart — one review, one test pass, 20 tickets.**

## The one test pass — run from Platform S against Platform K

The acceptance here is an S-side behaviour, so this is the only stream whose pass the K-side author cannot run alone:

register-connector -> originate carrying `identityCommitment` -> anchor -> verify -> read anchor status -> erasure by `external_ref` -> rotate and bulk re-key -> confirm revoke-on-rotate.

Plus the K-side `systemTest` **Integration mode** that KS-608 already names (`GET /api/anchors/{id}` and verify must not contradict each other).

title: nft-certificate: the row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths, and getWalletNFTCertificates still gets the raw ?walletAddress (gate 23, F2 and F3)
description:
**BLUF:** Two follow-ups from the gate on pull request 1819 (KS-1836), neither a regression. F2 (Low): `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner, while `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, so a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. The trim never lets a different owner through; mutant Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell; no write path stamps a padded owner today. F3 (Info): `getWalletNFTCertificates` still receives the raw `?walletAddress` string (parameterised equality, no injection); removing that is a design choice, not a defect.

**Source.** QA gate 23 on pull request 1819 (KS-1836; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F2 and F3 only. F1 of the same gate (the foreign-selector log arm) is being worked separately under KS-1836 and is not part of this filing. Related: KS-1836. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate23-1819/verdict.md`.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2 and F3, lines 32 to 52 of the verdict, unedited):**

**F2 (Low, consistency). The row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths.**

* **What happens:**
  * `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner.
  * `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, both in memory and in SQL.
  * So a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. Attack cell A-M2 logged `padded-row/null-row -> ["n2"]`.
* **What does not happen:** the trim never lets a different owner through. It only matters for rows whose trimmed owner equals the caller.
* **Mutant:** Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell. No fixture has a padded owner.
* **Reachability:** no write path stamps a padded owner today; every row is `'user-id'`.

**F3 (Info). The wallet reader still receives attacker-controlled strings.**

* **What I saw:** `getWalletNFTCertificates` is called with the raw `?walletAddress` string, for example `" "`, `"%"` and `" addr_..."` (A-Q log lines).
* **No injection:** the query is parameterised equality (`wallet_address = $1`), not LIKE.
* **Side effects:**
  * The foreign wallet's rows are read and cached into `memNftCertificates`, which `loadFromDb` already fills at boot anyway.
  * In-process timing difference, a median of 15 calls:
    * foreign wallet with 0 rows: 1.59 ms;
    * foreign wallet with 2000 rows: 1.91 ms.
  * That is a weak size oracle at best. I measured it over loopback in-process, not over a network.
* **What would remove both:** querying by `ownerId` and narrowing by wallet in memory. That is a design choice, not a defect.
* The userId selector never reaches a service method. Every A-Q cell shows the user reader called only with `["user-A"]`.

**Where this lands.** Its own ticket and not a comment on KS-1836, because KS-1836 closes when a deploy round carries pull request 1819's merge, and these follow-ups outlive it. KS-1836 read whole: it holds neither F2 nor F3.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `getUserNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836). `selectReadableCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `getWalletNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `row-owner` 0; `userId.trim` 0; `padded` 20 hits, of which the first 15 titles were read and none is about the NFT read paths.

**Not measured by this filing:** nothing was run here; the timing figures in F3 are the gate's in-process loopback measurements.
