title: api-gateway Dockerfile:35: the backup `rm -f` glob misses six name shapes, a backup-named directory fails the build, and the backups stay in the build context (gate 24, F1 to F3)
description: **BLUF:** The api-gateway Dockerfile line `RUN rm -f ./docs/openapi/*.pre-* ./docs/openapi/*.rollback-*` (`services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:35`, added by pull request 1820 for KS-1823) removes two backup-name shapes. Six other shapes still reach the final image (F1), the backups still enter the build context and the builder layer (F2), and a directory named like a backup fails the build (F3). Hygiene, not a stated exposure: the gate's runtime check found no reader of the backups (the only spec reader is `index.ts:590-605`, fixed path `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`). **Source.** QA gate 24 on pull request 1820 (tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F1, F2 and F3 of its verdict. The two shapes that actually sit on the demo host are covered, so this is not a regression. Related: KS-1823. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate24-1820/verdict.md`. **The verdict text, quoted (lines 32 to 66 of the verdict, unedited):** **F1 (Low, completeness). The glob removes two name shapes. Six other backup shapes still reach the image.** * **Where:** `services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:35`. * **What:** I planted these in `docs/openapi` in my clone and built with the head's Dockerfile. | Shape | Result | | -- | -- | | `x.pre-test` | REMOVED | | `x.rollback-test` | REMOVED | | `secuura-api.yaml.pre-ks508` (the real host shape) | REMOVED | | `secuura-api.yaml.rollback-2026-08-27-ks661` (the real host shape) | REMOVED | | `.z.pre-test` (a dotfile; busybox `*` does not match a leading dot) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `secuura-api.yaml.PRE-upper` (the glob is case-sensitive) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `sub/y.pre-test` (the glob covers the top level only) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x.bak` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x.orig` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x~` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | * **Control:** all 10 shapes are present in the develop-Dockerfile image (`ls_develop_decoys.txt`). * **The .dockerignore does not cover any of them.** `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` has `docs` then `!docs/openapi`, which re-includes the whole directory. Its `*.md` is root-only, which is why WORKFLOWS.md and TRACK2_OPENAPI_MIGRATION.md also ship. No `.dockerignore` sits beside the api-gateway Dockerfile. * **Scope:** the author's mail already states "the line removes two name shapes only". The two shapes that actually sit on the demo host are covered, so this is not a regression. * **Possible follow-up:** an allow-list (`COPY docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml ./docs/openapi/`), or `.dockerignore` lines for these shapes. That would also keep them out of the build context and the builder layer (F2). * **Reproduce:** plant the files above, then run `docker build -f services/api-gateway/Dockerfile Blockchain/Dev`, then `docker run --rm --entrypoint ls -la /app/docs/openapi`. **F2 (Info, by design). The backups still enter the build context and the builder-stage layer.** * The rm runs in the `builder` stage. The final stage copies the post-rm directory (`COPY --from=builder /app/docs/openapi`, Dockerfile:71), so the final image is clean; the layer scan above shows 0 entries. * The files are still uploaded as build context, which matters for a remote `az acr build`. They also stay in the builder's `COPY docs/openapi/` cache layer on the build host, and in any `--target builder` image. * The .dockerignore route from F1 would close this too. **F3 (Low, robustness). A directory with a matching name breaks the build.** * **What:** I planted `docs/openapi/old.rollback-dir/` and built with the head's Dockerfile. * **Result:** `rm: './docs/openapi/old.rollback-dir' is a directory`, then `exit code: 1`. The build failed. * **Why it is Low:** it fails closed, and no such directory exists today. * **What does not fail:** a clean tree with no match. busybox `rm -f` on an unmatched literal glob gives rc 0, and the clean build passed. * **Possible fix:** `rm -rf`, or `find … -type f`. **Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `rollback-` 21 hits including KS-1823. `.pre-*` 1 hit (KS-1823); `old.rollback-dir` 0; `x.bak` 0; `rm -f ./docs/openapi` 0; `dockerignore` 14 hits, of which KS-1289 (Done) is the `tests` versus `__tests__` pattern, a different defect. KS-1826 and KS-1813 read whole: neither mentions backups or the Dockerfile. KS-1823's own pull request comment lists "any name shape other than the two" as not done. **Not measured by this filing:** nothing was built or run here; the table and the failing build are the gate's measurements on a local arm64 Docker daemon.

title: Social sign-in callback echoes any exchange error's message: a provider 200 with a non-JSON body leaks its first 10 characters into the 400
description:
**BLUF:** a social sign-in provider that answers **200 with a body that is not JSON** still leaks the start of that body to the client. The login callback answers 400 `OAuth authentication failed: Unexpected token '<', "<html>PROV"... is not valid JSON`: V8's `SyntaxError` quotes the body's first 10 characters, and the callback echoes any exchange error's message. Low. It is the same class as the leak #1788 (KS-1240 part 2) closed, but on other lines.

* **Where.** The adapters in `services/auth/src/providers/social/` parse every answer with `.json()`: 12 reads at #1788's head `7eeedb825c5c` (token and profile in each adapter, plus GitHub's emails call). The login callback (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:1075-1080` at develop `b67a1c8d3a52`) wraps `exchangeErr.message` into its `BadRequestError` (line 1078). `POST /social/link` does not leak; it answers a generic 500.
* **Measured** by the tier-1 delta gate on #1788 (gate 7, probes P1 and P2, real routes, stub provider). GitHub's token endpoint answering `200 text/html` `<html>PROVIDER_TEXT_MARKER...` reaches the client as `"<html>PROV"...`. Google's userinfo answering the same does too. Apple's non-JSON `id_token` payload shows a parse position only.
* **Why #1788 did not fix it.** #1788 changed the error-status lines (the provider's error body is now logged, and the Error carries only the status), not the `.json()` lines or the route. `routes/auth.ts` is reserved for another lane.
* **Root fix (the gate's suggestion).** The callback maps any non-`AppError` exchange failure to a neutral text and logs the detail, instead of fixing one adapter line at a time.
* **Exposure today.** It needs a provider answering a malformed 200, and no deployment configures a social provider (`routes/auth.ts:995-996`).

**Searched before filing.** Team KS, issue titles and descriptions including archived, plus comment bodies, 2026-10-28 \~12:2xZ (issues / comments):

* No hits: "OAuth authentication failed" 0 / 0, "exchangeErr" 0 / 0.
* "is not valid JSON": 3 issues, KS-878, KS-452 and KS-224, all Done and none about the social callback. 1 comment, on KS-593.
* "Unexpected token": 4 issues. KS-634 is a CI-gate SyntaxError; KS-452, KS-224 and KS-149 are Done. None is this.
* Positive control "internal.ts:43": 1 comment, on KS-1788. A freshly coined zero control: 0 / 0.

**Refs:** KS-1240; PR #1788; gate verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-28_gate7-tier1/verdict.md`, finding 1788-10. Filed on the coordinator's instruction (ANSWER 12:12Z).

title: anchoring POST /api/anchors/thread-mint spends the platform wallet outside withWalletLock for any authenticated caller (fee drain)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/anchors/thread-mint` has no role check, and a non-dry-run call signs and submits a mint transaction from the platform wallet without taking `withWalletLock`, which the anchoring paths use. By the source, any caller with a valid token that reaches the anchoring service can spend the platform wallet's funds, and its spend can race the anchoring queue for the same UTxOs (the failure class KS-535 recorded; the race is inferred, not reproduced). High, security.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:470`: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, so the route is authenticated, nothing more.
* `index.ts:1008-1089`: the handler validates the body, then (when `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` and `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` are set) imports `mintAndLock` (`:1052`) and calls it. It reads no caller, role or tenant, and runs no database query.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/threadTokenMint.ts`: `mintAndLock` picks a seed UTxO from the platform wallet (`:262-266`), builds, signs and calls `signed.submit()` (`:339`). `dryRun: true` returns before the submit (`:322`).
* `withWalletLock` appears 0 times in `threadTokenMint.ts` and in the handler. Control: 5 times in `anchorSubmission.ts`, and the batch path calls it at `index.ts:1991`.

## What I did not run or read

* No request to any box or process. Whether the gateway routes this path to outside callers: not read. How much each call costs (I did not read `threadTokenMint.ts:262-340` beyond the lines above): not measured. Whether the race with anchoring happens in practice: not reproduced.

## Source and searches

title: nft-certificate is handed the same platform wallet mnemonic as anchoring, and POST /api/nft/mint has no role check
description:
**BLUF:** The nft-certificate service is configured with the same `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` as anchoring, so two processes can spend one wallet with no shared lock, and `POST /api/nft/mint` has no role check, so any authenticated caller can trigger a real mint when the chain keys are set. The double-spend race (the KS-535 class) is inferred, not reproduced. High, security and money.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1311` (anchoring) and `:1694` (nft-certificate): both set `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC=${PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC:-}`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/cardano/index.ts:30-42`: with `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` and `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` set it initialises the real wallet; without them it runs in mock mode. Submission goes through `blockfrost.txSubmit` (`cardano/provider.ts:84`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/app.ts:44`: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate({ publicOps: [the two verify operations] }))`, so the mint is authenticated only. `routes/nft.routes.ts:62` (the mint handler) has no role check; the only role check in that file is on `PUT /admin/platform-fee` (`:687-693`).
* A search of the service's non-test source for walletlock, mutex and advisory finds 0 hits. `minting.service.ts:224` and `:410` set `userId: 'user-id'` with the comment "Would come from auth context".

## What I did not run or read

* Whether the service runs, or has the chain keys set, on any box: UNMEASURED. Whether `mintNFT` checks that the certification belongs to the caller: not read. No request was sent.

## Source and searches

Raised by the KS-1384 design rev3 section 18.15 (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-8th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev3.md). Board, archived included: "nft/mint" 5 hits (all spec-sweep tickets, none about authorisation); "nft-certificate" is too broad to read (67 hits); the KS-1384 text has no match for PLATFORM_WALLET or nft-certificate.
Register note: this belongs to security work-stream D (KS-489, blockchain / anchoring integrity). KS-489 is archived, so it is not revived; the finding is recorded here and in one facts-only comment on KS-485.

title: nft-certificate mock mint answers 201 with a fabricated 64-hex transaction hash and no simulated marker
description:
**BLUF:** Read from the code, not reproduced. nft-certificate's mock mint returns a fabricated 64-hex transaction hash, and the mint route answers 201 with it and carries no marker that it was simulated. This is the honesty class of KS 520 and KS 522, where a simulated anchor is never presented as on-chain proof (`txHash` null, `simulated: true`); the NFT mint path has no equivalent.

## What I read (develop d7ddfa1f6433)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/services/minting.service.ts:779-796` (Cardano, mock mode): `const mockTxHash = Buffer.from(uuidv4() + uuidv4()).toString('hex').slice(0, 64);` at `:781`, a 2 s delay, a log line "Minting Cardano NFT (MOCK)", and a return of `{ txHash: mockTxHash, policyId: mockPolicyId }`.
* `minting.service.ts:802-815` (EVM): the method I read is a "Mock implementation" (`:807`) with no real branch in it, and `:815` is `` const mockTxHash = `0x${Buffer.from(uuidv4() + uuidv4()).toString('hex').slice(0, 64)}`; ``.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/routes/nft.routes.ts:84-96`: a successful mint answers 201 with `nftCertificateId`, `transactionHash`, `policyId`, `assetName`, `assetId`, `ipfsCid` and `costs`. No field says the result was simulated.
* A search of nft-certificate's non-test source (20 files) for "simulat", case-insensitive, finds one hit: the comment "Simulate transaction time" at `minting.service.ts:817`.

## What I did not run or read

* Which boxes run the mock branch (the boot line of nft-certificate and its `NODE_ENV`): UNMEASURED. The code before `:776` that decides when mock mode applies.
* What `mintNFT` stores for such a hash, and what the issuer portal or the verify operations show for it. The `/record` response.
* Whether any other EVM minting code exists outside the method I read.

## Source and searches

Seat A 17th's design note (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-30_seatA-17th/KS-1819-KS-1820-design-note.md, section 7 item 2, and row 22 of its section 1 table) and Wednesday's addendum, item E3. Board search (archived included, 2026-10-29 UTC, controls fired): "mockTxHash" 0 hits.
Register note: this belongs to security work-stream D (KS 489, blockchain, anchoring and integrity). KS 489 is archived, so it is not revived; the finding is recorded here and in one facts-only comment on KS 485.

title: nft-certificate mintNFT fetches the certification with no Authorization header: production mints fail, other envs mint on fabricated data
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. `mintNFT` fetches the certification from originate with a bare `fetch` and no Authorization header, against a router that authenticates every request. In production that request should never succeed, so a mint ends in "Certification not found". Outside production the same failure falls through to a fabricated "Secuura Demo Issuer" certification, and the mint goes ahead on that.

## What I read (develop d7ddfa1f6433)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/services/minting.service.ts:146-168` (production): `` fetch(`${ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL}/api/certifications/${certificationId}`) `` at `:148`, no headers. A non-ok answer logs and returns null (`:154`); an exception logs and returns null (`:167`). `mintNFT` then throws "Certification not found" (`:237-239`), after it has already saved the PENDING record (`:234`).
* `minting.service.ts:171-184` (not production): the same fetch at `:173`. A non-ok answer or an exception falls through to `:186-205`, which logs "Using mock certification data ... DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION" and builds a certification with issuer "Secuura Demo Issuer" (`did:prism:demo123`), recipient "Demo Recipient" and a `documentHash` derived from the certification id, caches it (`:204`) and returns it.
* `minting.service.ts:140-143`: a cached certification is returned before any fetch, so once the fabricated entry is cached that id keeps the fabricated data without calling originate again.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:62-66`: `certificationsRouter.use(authenticate());`, with a comment that every route there requires an authenticated Bearer JWT.

## What I did not run or read

* No run, no box. Whether any box runs nft-certificate with `NODE_ENV=production`, what `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL` points at there, and whether a mint has ever been attempted: UNMEASURED.
* The catch block of `mintNFT`: what happens to the PENDING record saved at `:234` when the certification lookup throws.
* What `mintNFT` stores for a mint that went ahead on the fabricated data.
* Whether the mint route could supply the certification some other way: `nft.routes.ts:75-80` sets `documentData: undefined` with the comment "Would be fetched from certification", and I read nothing further.

## Source and searches

Seat A 17th's design note (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-30_seatA-17th/KS-1819-KS-1820-design-note.md, section 7 item 1, and rows 19 and 20 of its section 1 table) and Wednesday's addendum, item E2. Board search (archived included, 2026-10-29 UTC, controls fired): "getCertificationData" 0 hits; "Certification not found" 2 hits (KS 834, an open decision about a different route; KS 210, archived), neither about this fetch.
Register note: this belongs to security work-stream A (KS 486, authN, authZ, tenancy and IDOR; here the service-to-service call carries no credential). KS 486 is archived, so it is not revived; the finding is recorded here and in one facts-only comment on KS 485.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor answers status 'anchored' in its 202 body even when a mid-flight revoke kept the row revoked
description:
**BLUF:** after pull request 1814 (KS-1814), `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor` writes `status: 'anchored'` with `preserveTerminalStatuses: true`, so a revoke that lands while the anchoring call is in flight keeps `revoked` in the row. The handler still always answers `202` with `status: 'anchored'`; it never reads what `updateDocument` returned. The row is right; the response body misreports it. Found by QA gate 19 on pull request 1814 (finding 1814-2), measured over a mocked repository only.

**What was read and measured**

* The write: `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' }, undefined, { preserveTerminalStatuses: true })` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1584-1587` at the pull request 1814 head `277e5ba6b7ae`; `:1534-1537` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`, where the write has no options at all). documentRepo's KS-521 CASE keeps `revoked` / `deleted` when that option is set.
* The answer: `res.status(202).json({ id, status: 'anchored', transactionHash, blockchain })` (`:1611-1613` at the head; `:1560-1562` at develop). It does not read `updateDocument`'s return value, which is `Promise<DocumentRecord | null>` (`services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`).
* Gate 19's cell B6: a mocked `updateDocument` that returns a revoked record. The body still says `anchored`.

**Fix shape (the gate's):** answer from the returned record, or say plainly that the row's status was not updated. Whether the real repository's returned record carries the kept `revoked` status was not measured, so read that before choosing.

**Priority 3:** the response is wrong but the stored data is right, so it is not a data-integrity defect. A caller that trusts the 202 body over a read-back would believe a revoked document is anchored.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written. The race window (a revoke during the anchoring call) was not driven against a database.

title: Declare metadata.signatureHash and the signatureHash read-back fields in the published OpenAPI spec (the other half of KS-1454)
description:
**BLUF:** The published OpenAPI spec does not declare `metadata.signatureHash` on the anchor request, nor the `signatureHash` field on the two anchor reads. The anchoring-side pull request for KS-1454 adds all three in code; the spec declaration is the other half and nothing in that pull request does it. KS-1454's own text says Platform S switches `AnchorSignatureHash` on per environment only after K serves a spec that declares `FlatAnchorRequest.metadata.signatureHash`, so until this exists the field cannot be turned on. Ruled a follow-up ticket, not a hold on the pull request, by the coordinator (2026-10-30 00:11 AEDT).

## What I read

* `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at develop be2cd084d0f1: 0 occurrences of `signatureHash`. Control: `identityCommitment`, an earlier anchor field, has 6.
* KS-1454's description, one matching line: the switch-on condition quoted above.
* The code side, on the KS-1454 branch (commit d7d3a6e3ed4b): the request field in `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts` (64 lowercase hex, `sign` verb only, 400 otherwise); the read side in `anchorReadback.ts` (verify-by-hash carries it under `metadata.signatureHash` beside `documentType`) and in the by-id handler in `index.ts` (spread into the response beside the identity fields; `null` when absent).
* Where the spec comes from: `services/anchoring/src/anchoring.openapi.ts` exists, and the root `package.json` defines `generate-openapi` (line 50) and `check:openapi` (line 42: `generate-openapi --check` and `check:spec-examples`).
* The gateway's source: no request-body validation against the published spec that I could find (no validator package or option in `services/api-gateway/src`; control: `specPath` has 15 hits). The spec feeds the 405 method map, the edge auth gate and the docs routes. This is a source read only.

## What I did not run or read

* No generation, no spec edit, no request to any box or live gateway. Which spec component carries the field (KS-1454's text names `FlatAnchorRequest.metadata.signatureHash`): not read in the spec. Whether the change also needs the two Projects Documents sections and updated examples: not measured. Whether a live gateway refuses an undeclared field: not measured (the QA gate on the KS-1454 pull request is asked to measure it).

## Searched

Board, archived included: "signatureHash" 4 hits (KS-1596, KS-1575, KS-1454, KS-1385; titles read, none declares it in the spec); "signature hash" 2 hits (KS-1454, KS-772); "declare signatureHash" 0 hits.

title: anchoring fetchUtxos reads one page of the wallet's UTxOs (Blockfrost addressesUtxos without pagination)
description:
**BLUF:** `fetchUtxos` makes one `blockfrost.addressesUtxos(address)` call, which fetches a single page, so the transaction builder can see only the first page of a wallet that holds more UTxOs than the page size. Harmless for safety (fewer candidates), but it caps what the builder can choose from. Inferred from the call shape; not run against a wallet.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/provider.ts:329-332`: `return await blockfrost.addressesUtxos(address)`, with no pagination argument. The builder calls it at `cardano/transaction.ts:29`.
* The Blockfrost SDK installed in the repo (version 6.1.1, not the pinned 6.2.0): `addressesUtxos(address, pagination)` sends page, count and order from `getPaginationOptions(pagination)` (`lib/endpoints/api/addresses/index.js:121-135`), and a separate `addressesUtxosAll` paginates (`:149`).

## What I did not run or read

* The SDK's default page size (I did not print `getPaginationOptions`; Blockfrost documents 100, not verified here), the pinned 6.2.0 source, and any run against a wallet with many UTxOs.

## Source and searches

KS-1384 design rev3 section 18.17 (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-8th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev3.md), marked INFERRED there. Board, archived included: "addressesUtxos" 0 hits; "fetchUtxos" 0 hits.

title: originate documentRepo.updateDocument rebuilds metadata and certification_metadata from its JavaScript read; a concurrent write can be lost
description:
**BLUF:** `updateDocument` builds the new `metadata` JSON from the document object it read earlier and assigns that JSON in the UPDATE, and it assigns `certification_metadata` from `{signatures}` plus a blockchain case. So a concurrent write to another metadata key between the read and the UPDATE can be overwritten, and any `certification_metadata` key other than `signatures` and `blockchain` is not carried. Inferred from the code (the design review's sub-agent marked it "INFERRED, not spot-checked"); not reproduced.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:586-590`: `metadata = JSON.stringify({ ...stripReservedMetadataKeys(updated.data), walletAddress, signatures })`, with `updated` from the earlier `getDocument` read; `:591-593`: `certMeta = JSON.stringify({ signatures })`.
* `documentRepo.ts:626`: `metadata = ${metadata}::jsonb || CASE ...` and `:634`: `certification_metadata = ${certMeta}::jsonb || CASE ...`. I read the first lines of the CASE bodies (they build a `blockchain` object), not all of them.

## What I did not run or read

* No concurrent run, no database. Whether any other `certification_metadata` key exists in practice: not measured. The full CASE bodies were not read to the end.

## Source and searches

KS-1384 design rev3 section 18.16 (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-8th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev3.md). Board, archived included: "JavaScript read" 0 hits; "stripReservedMetadataKeys" 1 hit (KS-1508, about versionedById being caller-set, not this).

title: anchoring: the in-lock confirmed write omits the transaction hash, so a same-payload upsert can leave a confirmed row with a NULL hash
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. The in-lock `confirmed` write carries no `transactionHash`, the front-door upsert overwrites the stored hash on conflict, and guard 2 treats a row without a 64-hex hash as "no known submission". A same-payload upsert that lands during the roughly 27-minute in-lock confirmation poll could therefore leave the row `confirmed` with a NULL hash, and the queued call would build and submit a second transaction. Money-class; ruled High by Wednesday.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts:490-499`: the `confirmed` update sets status, confirmations, block number, slot, block hash, `confirmedAt` and `expectMetadataPayload`, and no `transactionHash`; the earlier `submitted` update (`:482`) does set it.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1454-1456`: the front-door insert is `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash, ...`.
* `anchorSubmission.ts:430-432` (guard 2 re-reads the row inside the lock and returns "already" only if `knownChainSubmission` yields a hash) and `:244-251` (`knownChainSubmission` needs status submitting, submitted or confirmed AND a 64-hex `transactionHash`).
* The poll length comes from Seat R 61st's arithmetic on KS-1816 (27.2 to 28.2 minutes); I did not recompute it.

## What I did not run or read

* No reproduction, no database, no box. I did not read the compare-and-set in `anchorStatusUpdate.ts` or whether `expectMetadataPayload` would restore the hash on the `confirmed` write.

## Source and searches

KS-1384 design rev4 section 18.20 (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-9th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev4.md). Board, archived included: "knownChainSubmission" 1 hit (KS-726, archived; its description says guards 1 and 2 need a populated hash, which is this finding's premise); "NULL hash" 6 hits, read KS-1384: no match for this finding.
Register note: this belongs to security work-stream D (KS-489, blockchain / anchoring integrity). KS-489 is archived, so it is not revived; the finding is recorded here and in one facts-only comment on KS-485.

title: GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events lists any tenant document's events without the ownership 404 that GET /:id applies
description:
**BLUF:** originate `GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2885-2907` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only, then returns every lifecycle event of the document (`listLifecycleEvents`, :2900). The ownership 404 that `GET /api/documents/:id` applies (:1142-1160) is missing, so a same-tenant caller who cannot read the document can read its events. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No owner, admin, recipient or creating-connector check between :2885 and :2907. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response is `{ documentId, count, events }`: the events as stored, with their actions and payloads.

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it is a read, and the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape for it. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check (owner, admin, recipient or creating connector, else the same 404).

**Priority 3:** a read gap; it mutates nothing.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; what the stored payloads contain for real documents is not measured.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events: any tenant user can record a lifecycle event on any document and trigger its anchor emission
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2757-2877` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the action vocabulary, the payload's shape and the caller's tenant, and nothing about the caller's role or relation to the document. Any authenticated user in the tenant can record a lifecycle event on any document. The route then calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), which posts to the anchoring service with the caller's bearer. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No `isAllowedByRoleOrScope`, no owner check and no creating-connector check between :2757 and :2877. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* It writes an event row (`createLifecycleEvent`, :2809), records connector provenance for a connector caller, and calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), then stores the anchor id on the event.
* `emitLifecycleAnchor`'s comment (:1349-1362) says anchoring is idempotent per (document, network): re-anchoring an already-anchored document returns its existing anchor id. For a document with no anchor row, whether the call submits a new transaction (and spends a fee) is UNMEASURED; I did not read anchoring's `POST /api/anchors` wallet path.
* The vocabulary includes `delete` and `restore` (`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:38-46`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's checks do not apply unchanged. A terminal-status refusal would break `restore` on a deleted document. Platform S sends this route under the owning organisation's connector key (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19), and which humans should be allowed is not settled, so it needs its own predicate.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates the document's record (an event row) and may cause an anchoring submission.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; the fee question above is unmeasured.

title: Security: GET /api/auth/wallet/status returns userId + role to ANY anonymous caller — enumeration surface, and nothing consumes the fields
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/auth/wallet/status/:walletAddress` **is unauthenticated by design and returns** `userId`**,**
`role` **and** `createdAt` **for a registered wallet.** A Cardano wallet address is public, so anyone holding
one resolves it to an internal user id and that user's role, with no token.

**Nothing consumes those three fields.** Trimming the response to `{ exists: true | false }` costs
nothing, and it removes the enumeration surface entirely.

Raised as a question by @PeterObeden on PR #802 — *"Would trimming it to* `{exists: true|false}` *lose*
*anything the sign-in flow needs?"* — and answered here by measurement rather than opinion.

## The endpoint

`services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts:402`

```
walletRoutes.get('/status/:walletAddress', async (req, res, next) => {
  const result = await query('SELECT id, role, created_at FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet($1)', [walletAddress]);
  ...
  if (!userId) { res.json({ exists: false, message: 'Wallet not registered' }); return; }
  res.json({ exists: true, userId, role, createdAt });
});
```

No `authenticate()`, deliberately — `wallet.ts:438` records that `/challenge`, `/verify`,
`/authenticate` and `/status/:walletAddress` are public by design (KS-720), and requiring a token
would make wallet sign-in impossible. **The auth requirement is not in question. The payload is.**

## The measurement that answers the question

Repo-wide search for consumers of `wallet/status`, excluding `node_modules` and `dist`:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| references in `frontend/` | **0** |
| references reading `userId` / `role` / `createdAt` from a status response | **0** |
| total references anywhere | 5 — the handler, the spec, the service's own route list, one e2e fixture, one e2e test |
| **CONTROL —** `wallet/verify`**, a sibling that IS consumed** | **17** |

The control is what makes the zero mean something: the same search over the same trees finds 17 hits
for the sibling endpoint, so it reaches the frontends and the zero is a real absence rather than a
search that cannot match.

⚠ One of the two e2e references calls `/api/wallet/status` (`tests/e2e/.../happy-path-wallet.spec.ts:255`),
which is not this route's path — `/api/auth/wallet/status`. Worth a look separately; it is not evidence
of consumption.

## The contract currently publishes the surface as intended behaviour

`docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` declares the operation with `security: []` and this description:

> *"For a REGISTERED one it is not:* `wallet.ts:369` *returns* `{exists:true, userId, role, createdAt}` *to*
> *an unauthenticated caller, so a known public address resolves to an internal user id and role."*

So the enumeration surface is documented rather than hidden — which is good practice, and also means an
integrator reading the contract is told this is deliberate.

## Suggested fix

Return `{ exists: true }` / `{ exists: false }` only. The sign-in flow needs to know whether to offer
"sign in" or "register"; it does not need the id or the role, and no code asks for them.

If some consumer outside this repo does depend on the fields, that is a contract change and belongs to
whoever owns that consumer — but nothing inside the repo does.

## Also: @PeterObeden's registry blocker on this endpoint is already lifted

On #802 he wrote that the `public-by-design` entry for this route could not be added because *"it is*
*absent from the OpenAPI spec (KS-712), so it cannot meet the registry's evidence standard — which is*
*the spec declaring the endpoint public."*

**The declaration landed on 2026-09-01 in #760 (KS-712)** — `git log -S` on `auth.openapi.ts` names
commit `9b89f4fce`, a week before #802 merged. The spec declares it with `security: []`, which is
exactly the standard he named. **The KS-417 spec guard should accept the entry now.** (Control: the
same `-S` search for a term that should not exist returns 0 commits.)

*Filed by s152 from PR #802's open question. Measured on* `origin/develop`*.*

title: Akto full scan reports three LOW HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES results (wallet-status ×2, GET /api/settings/notifications) that no ticket or allowlist covers — classify them: by-design or a finding
description:
## BLUF

The one `test:security` run on 2026-10-07 reported three **LOW** results from `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES` on two public routes. No ticket covers them and no allowlist mechanism can express them. They are probably expected for public routes that ignore request headers, but that is **not established**, and today they fail the Full OWASP workflow on their own because the gate fails on any severity, LOW included.

## Measured (slot 1, Mac, Akto 2.37.1, 2026-10-07, run `security`, full OWASP summary `6ac60a95a141e9203079d8bf`, 50,450 result docs)

| Result |  |
| -- | -- |
| Template | `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES`, category INPUT, severity LOW, CWE-20, nature INTRUSIVE |
| Docs for the template | 350; **90 executed** (a captured exchange); **3 flagged** (raw `vulnerable: true`); 347 not |
| Flagged 1 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/dt-seed-7` |
| Flagged 2 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/STRING` (the `{walletAddress}` placeholder) |
| Flagged 3 | `GET /api/settings/notifications` |

**What the template does** (read from the library file): it selects a 2xx, non-error response, replaces **every request header value** with invalid values, and flags the result when an attempt still returns 2xx with a body more than 90% identical to the original and the same schema.

**What the data shows.** Each flagged result has 4 attempts. Attempts 0–2 returned **400** (102-character body, 0% match). **Attempt 3 returned 200** (50 characters for wallet-status, 83 for settings/notifications) with a **100% match** — that attempt is what tripped the template. The altered request carried 3 headers for wallet-status (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`, `authorization`) and 2 for settings/notifications (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`). Which values attempt 3 used was **not examined**.

## Why this needs a ticket

* The two routes are already known to be public: `wallet/status` is public by necessity and cannot be allowlisted ([KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous); Kamil, PR #802, quoted in `endpointFalsePositives.ts`: "the registry has no representation for a parameterised route"), and `GET /api/settings/notifications` keeps optional auth by ruling ([KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), quoted in the same file from `routes/admin.ts`: "The GET above keeps optional auth so anonymous readers still get the documented defaults").
* No existing allowlist mechanism fits. `KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVE_ENDPOINT_TESTS` admits two ruled kinds with compile-time bounds (`public-by-design` only for `REMOVE_TOKENS`; `similarity-undiscriminating` only for three templates — Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) bound), and a LOW from an INPUT template is neither. The wallet-status URL also carries a path parameter the registry cannot express.
* The gate (`assertNoVulnerabilities`) fails on any severity. So even after [KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous)'s HIGH is fixed, any of these LOWs that recurs will keep the Full OWASP workflow red.

## Not established

* **Whether it is a real input-validation gap (CWE-20) or expected** for routes that never read the headers being altered. For `settings/notifications` the altered headers do not include `authorization`, so "it ignores a bad token" does not explain it.
* **Why it was not reported before.** The 2026-10-05 full runs on slots 2 and 4 listed only the nginx LOW ([KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)). This stack's collection also carried authenticated samples for these URLs (a `feed-har` added them, 343 → 349 endpoints). Not shown to be the cause.
* Related, not claimed: [KS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1207/security-an-unknown-sk-key-on-an-optional-auth-mount-skips-the) (In Progress, Kamil) covers an unknown key on an optional-auth mount skipping the Bearer check.

## Proposed next steps (smallest first)

1. Re-run **only** this template on those three URLs with a targeted Akto `CUSTOM` run (`apiInfoKeyList`; the technique used for [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)) and read attempt 3's actual request: which headers, which values.
2. Classify each: by design, or a finding. Kamil's call for the platform side.
3. If by design: accept it by a **narrow** rule with the ruling quoted verbatim (the [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low) pattern), and a control showing another endpoint or template still fails. Extending the allowlist's compile-time bound needs Kamil's ruling first. If a finding: a platform ticket for Kamil.

## Done means

1. Each of the three results has a recorded classification, with the attempt-3 evidence.
2. If by design: the Full OWASP workflow no longer fails on them, a control still fails, and Console = Akto = HTML agree on the known-FP and vulnerable counts.
3. If a finding: it is ticketed for the owner and the test keeps failing honestly.

Found while verifying [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1411](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1440-akto-23610-2371-with-the-ks-1416-ks-1421-and-ks-724-fixes-it-5f3e7f62426b), merged; history entry PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1412](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docs-project-history-for-the-2026-10-07-akto-2371-batch-one-pr-merged-06305b942330)). Nothing was changed for this finding.

title: The published did:jwk pattern admits values the runtime refuses (5,000 of 5,000 sampled); POST /api/anchors has no Schemathesis override
description:
**BLUF:** The published `did:jwk` pattern admits values the runtime refuses. In a seeded sample of 5,000 values that satisfy the published pattern, `identitySchema` refused 5,000 of 5,000 `did:jwk` values, against 0 of 5,000 for `did:key` and 0 of 5,000 for `did:web`. `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` has no `[[operations]]` entry for `POST /api/anchors`, so a Schemathesis positive-data sweep that generates a `did:jwk` for `actorDid` or `orgDid` is expected to meet a 400. Not measured against a stack: no sweep was run.

**Facts** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:1295` and `:1320` publish `pattern: ^did:(key|web|jwk):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` for both identity DID fields. `POST /api/anchors` is published at `:14619`. The yaml holds 0 `did:jwk` examples and 1 `did:key` example.
* Since KS-1175's private-key guard, the runtime refuses a `did:jwk` unless the payload is unpadded base64url of a JSON object with none of `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `k` (`anchorSchema.ts:165-178`). A random string over the pattern's alphabet almost never decodes to a JSON object. The JSON-decodability half cannot be written as a JSON-Schema pattern at all, so some gap is irreducible.
* `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml`: `[checks.positive_data_acceptance]` at `:128`; the file's per-operation entries scope some paths (for example `include-name = "POST /api/auth/login"`), and the only line that names an anchors operation is `include-name = "POST /api/anchors/thread-mint"` at `:424`; the mentions of flat `/api/anchors` at `:509-515` are in a comment. The global positive-data-acceptance list excludes 400.
* The description text on both fields states the rule and the 400; gate 16 records that it is generated from the imported member list and that `generate-openapi --check` goes rc 1 when a member is dropped.

**Measured:**

* By me, on develop `6d41673e0f79`: `tools/probe_didjwk_r61.ts` draws 5,000 values per method, seeded, length 1 to 40, uniform over the 67-character alphabet, keeps those that pass `DID_PATTERN`, and counts refusals by `identitySchema`: did:key 0 of 5000, did:web 0 of 5000, did:jwk 5000 of 5000. Positive controls in the same run: a public P-256 `did:jwk`, a `did:key` and a `did:web` are accepted; a private `did:jwk` is refused.
* By QA gate 16 on the KS-1175 guard's pull request head: the same sampling gave the same three figures.

**Fix-shape (gate 16 and Wednesday's addendum prefer (a); not ruled):**

* (a) In the KS-571 style, a `map_case` hook (like `systemTest/schemathesis/config/connector_only_field.py`) that swaps a generated `did:jwk` for a valid public one in POSITIVE bodies of `POST /api/anchors`. Not a widened `expected-statuses`, which the file's own KS-544 rule calls masking.
* (b) Optional: a per-method pattern, `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$|^did:jwk:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. That aligns the alphabet half with the runtime's strict check but changes the error code for a stray `.`, `:` or `%` from `custom` to `invalid_string`, so cells move.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/probe_didjwk_develop_6d41673e.log`
* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate16-1807/verdict.md`, finding 1807-2 (`evidence/probe/spec_positive_sample.out`, `evidence/probe/openapi.out`)

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `spec_positive_sample` and `schemathesis.toml:424` were checked by the filing tool at 0 hits; `map_case` 6 hits, read by title (KS-1439, KS-1408, KS-575, KS-571 and KS-472 are archived and concern other operations; KS-1175 holds the gate's note about this as a comment); `positive_data_acceptance` 69 hits, not discriminating, none about `POST /api/anchors` by title.

**Related:** KS-1175.

title: Anchor / originate / lifecycle-event schemas: accept and anchor platform-s's non-PII actor + organisation identity fields (actorDid, actorLevel, actorSource, actorVerified, orgDid, orgTrust, orgVerified) beside identityCommitment
description:
## What platform-s needs

Follow-on to [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment) (which accepted `metadata.identityCommitment`). Platform-S now needs the Cardano record to **show** who acted and at what identity level, for the actor and their organisation — readable, not only committed. The S-side ruling on what is allowed in clear is [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) (decision) under epic [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and); the field list there is the contract:

| Field | Type | Pattern / values |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `actorDid` | string ≤ 512 | `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` |
| `actorLevel` | integer | `1`, `2`, `3` — NIST 800-63A IAL alignment |
| `actorSource` | string | `platform` | `stripe` | `entra-verified-id` |
| `actorVerified` | boolean |  |
| `orgDid` | string ≤ 512 | as `actorDid` |
| `orgTrust` | string | `unverified` | `domain` | `document` | `kyc` | `government` |
| `orgVerified` | boolean |  |
| `identityCommitment` | string ≤ 128 | already accepted ([KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment)); the `vN` will move to `v2` |

All optional; all non-PII (DIDs are pseudonymous, levels and sources are enumerations, no dates, no names, no emails). Consistent with [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) — no free text, nothing recoverable to a natural person.

## Suggested work

1. Accept the block as `metadata.identity` (or flat under `metadata` — say which) on **every** endpoint S anchors through: `POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/documents` (originate), `POST /{id}/version`, `POST /{id}/anchor`, `POST /{id}/share`, `POST /{id}/transfer-custody`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, `POST /{id}/lifecycle-events`. Today `anchorSchema.ts` strips unknown keys, so S will not send until K is live (the [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) ordering).
2. Carry it into the on-chain record beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` / `identityCommitment`.
3. Return it in provenance / verify / anchor-status responses so S can render "on chain: Level 2, entra-verified-id" beside its local snapshot and flag any mismatch.
4. **State which existing request fields reach Cardano metadata**: `holderEmail`, `recipients[].email`, `newHolderEmail`, `onBehalfOf.email` / `displayName`. S sends these today; the requirement is that no PII is stored on the blockchain. If any of them is written to chain metadata, file the defect and link it here.
5. OpenAPI spec + Schemathesis / Akto examples updated in the same PR ([KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) pattern), and both K-side testing HTML docs.

## Ordering

**K deploys first**, then PS-870 adds the fields on the S request. Pair-test from S against K on paired slots (S slot N ↔ K slot N) and quote the counts.

title: KS-1175 follow-on: the anchors K emits for share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events carry no documentType and drop Platform-S's identity block — only originate and the flat anchor anchor identity
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-k `0aa9b52c6`, platform-s `477eb57`).

## The gap

[KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (merged `cbae988db`, `910687394`) accepts the `identity` block on `POST /api/anchors` and anchors it beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:128-151, 261-315`). Platform-S sends that block on **every** write once `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity` is on — flat anchors, originate, version, certifications, share, transfer-custody and lifecycle-events (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:1606-1631`).

On K, three of those routes never carry it to the anchor:

* `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` reads only `action` and `payload`; an `identity` key in the body is ignored (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2440-2545`).
* `POST /{id}/share` and `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` likewise.
* All three anchor through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, whose body is `{documentId, contentHash, network}` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `identity` (`documents.ts:1275-1297`).

Result: for every non-mutating verb (delete, share-revoke, the share-\* edits, rights-unassign, note, certified, verified, share, rights-assign/reassign) the chain record has no verb and no actor/organisation identity, whatever S sends. Only `upload` (originate) and the flat-anchor fallback carry them.

## Ask

1. Carry `identity` (and the verb as `metadata.documentType`) from the share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events request bodies into the `emitLifecycleAnchor` call, so the anchor records them — subject to the per-document-anchor ruling on the companion ticket (a reset row would not keep them anyway).
2. Declare `identity` on `DocumentShareRequest`, `TransferCustodyRequest` and `LifecycleEventRequest` in `originate.openapi.ts` so S's [PS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614/check-ss-verb-vocabulary-against-platform-ks-openapi-enum-at-gate-time) gate can see it (today S's `k_openapi_vocabulary.test.ts` only checks `onBehalfOf` placement).
3. Echo what was anchored on the lifecycle-event response, so S's read-back ([PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb) item 5) works on these verbs too.

## Verify

Paired slot with `AnchorIdentity=true` on S: a `share-revoke` on an originated document → the anchor read (`GET /api/anchors/{id}`) returns `identity.actorDid` and `metadata.documentType = share-revoke`. Today it returns neither.

Related: [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb), [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and), the [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) companion ticket (one anchor per document).

title: Akto suppressions and exclusions: one cites the wrong ticket (KS-442 → KS-510), and two coverage trade-offs (VOLATILE_PATH_RE, 8 built-in data-exposure templates) have no ruling or owner
description:
**BLUF:** the [KS-1478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1478/akto-image-2371-2383-release-v2383-2026-10-13-testing-image-has-no) audit of every rule that stops an Akto result from counting checked each one against the ticket it cites. Most stand and are no wider than their ruling: [KS-308](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-308/akto-scans-report-100percent-skipped-tests-testing-container-cant), [KS-323](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-323/akto-after-ks-314-drive-connectivity-skip-bucket-to-0-confirm-mongo)/324, [KS-397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-397/are-apidocument-types-and-apioauthscopes-intentionally-public-or)/364, [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) (narrower than the ruling), [KS-1397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1397/the-gateway-answers-every-request-with-server-nginx-aktos-unwanted)/1421 (narrower, fails closed, **seen firing live on 2026-10-14** on `POST /api/certifications/issue`), [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not), [KS-417](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-417/akto-spec-consistency-guard-for-the-endpoint-scoped-known-fp-allowlist)/425/524 and [KS-1416](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1416/akto-the-three-code-injection-sqli-scans-run-0-sqlnosql-templates-akto). **Three do not.** The citation fix was made and then **backed out at Peter's instruction (update the app only, log issues)**. Re-verified against `develop` 3c0a52221 on 2026-10-14.

## 1. Wrong citation: `/api/identity-credentials/types`

`systemTest/akto/src/core/endpointFalsePositives.ts:148` (and the docblock at `:117-119`) suppresses `REMOVE_TOKENS` on this endpoint, citing [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424). [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424)'s ruling (Kam, 2026-07-11) covers **only the five verify operations** and says *"reference reads stay protected"*. The ticket that actually registered this endpoint as public by design is [KS-510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-510/akto-register-get-apiidentity-credentialstypes-as-by-design-public) (Done, 2026-07-23), resting on the spec's `security: []`. The test comment `tests/unit/core/endpointFalsePositives.test.ts:34` carries the same citation.

## 2. `VOLATILE_PATH_RE` drops whole paths from HAR replay with no ruling

`src/setup/harSpec.ts:26`: `/\/(analytics|dashboard|realtime|metrics)\b/i` means those endpoints get **no real HAR sample**, so authz templates skip them for **every** template, not just the similarity ones ([KS-357](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-357/akto-drive-authz-precondition-skips-0-complete-attacker-role-auth)). Today's feed excluded **19** volatile endpoints of 141 GET endpoints. Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) analysis (2026-08-28) warns that this exact mechanism *"removes the audit log from the scan"* and that the `analytics` paths *"already make"* that trade, *"worth asking whether they should be making it either"*. No ticket reviews it, and its scope is wider than any ruling.

## 3. 8 Akto built-in data-exposure templates are loaded but never selected

`tests/aktoSetup.test.ts:329-338` (`KNOWN_CATALOG_DRIFT.loadedNotInCatalog`): `SENSITIVE_DATA_EXPOSURE_{ADDRESS,CREDIT_CARD,EMAIL,IP_ADDRESS,JWT,PHONE_NUMBER,SSN,VIN}`. Its own comment calls this *"a REAL, previously-unrecorded coverage observation … a coverage decision … deliberately not folded into* [KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717/akto-test-id-catalog-and-the-loaded-template-library-drift-silently)*'s drift fix"*. Today on 2.38.2 the library is again 208 = 199 bundled + 9 built-ins, so it is unchanged. No ticket owns the decision.

## Also stale

`endpointFalsePositives.ts:206` quotes `routes/admin.ts:1437`; the quoted code is now at `:1487` / `:1523`. Staleness detection for similarity entries is already [KS-761](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-761/similarity-undiscriminating-fp-entries-have-no-staleness-detection-a), so it is not duplicated here.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The `/api/identity-credentials/types` entry and its test cite [KS-510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-510/akto-register-get-apiidentity-credentialstypes-as-by-design-public) (with "spec `security: []`, no Kam ruling"), not [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424). **A test demonstrates it:** a unit test that every `public-by-design` entry's cited ticket is one whose text names that endpoint (or a recorded reason), red on the [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) citation.
2. `VOLATILE_PATH_RE`: a recorded decision (Kamil's input sought, per the [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) discussion): narrow it, scope it to the similarity templates as [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) Option B did for the tolerance, or accept it with a reason. Report the number of endpoints it excludes in the run's coverage section so the trade is visible.
3. The 8 data-exposure templates: enable them (and measure the tier-budget cost and any false positives on a platform that legitimately returns emails and addresses), or record why not, with the decision recorded where the catalog selection lives.
4. The stale `admin.ts:1437` pointer is corrected or replaced by a symbol reference.

title: A deploy that rsyncs the OpenAPI spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a silently stale published contract — rsync breaks the bind mount by inode
description:
## BLUF

**The demo redeploy runbook can ship a stale published API contract with every check passing.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a **file-level** bind mount into `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml:542`, `:ro`). `rsync` **writes a temp file and renames it, so the updated file gets a NEW INODE** — and a Docker file bind mount resolves to the inode at container-create time. The container goes on serving the **old** file indefinitely.

It is not stale cache. The container is looking at a **different file on the same path**.

## Measured during the 2026-09-08 deploy (632f16dfe → 400517aaf)

After the rsync, before any restart:

|  | md5 | bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| host `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `7e43a8d89afb…` | 1332983 (new) |
| inside `api-gateway` `/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `c014b2fce71c…` | 1329831 (**old**, dated Sep 7 03:45) |
| served `GET /api/docs/openapi.yaml` | — | 1329831 = the container's copy |

After `docker compose restart api-gateway`: container md5 `7e43a8d89afb…`, identical to the host; served bytes 1332983; the new text `BOUND TO THE` went **0 → 1** and `DIFFERS FROM the ACTING` **0 → 2**, with `organizationUuid` **1 → 2** as a control and an impossible string at 0.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure mode is exactly KS-978's**, which this same deploy shipped the fix for: *the published contract says something the route does not do*. KS-978 was a wrong sentence in the source. This is the **delivery mechanism** producing the same outcome from a correct source — and it is quieter, because every signal an operator would check looks right:

* `rsync` exits 0 and reports the file transferred ✅
* the file on the VM disk **is** correct ✅
* rebuilding the image does nothing (the spec is mounted, not baked) — so "I rebuilt it" feels like the fix and is not ✅
* the container is healthy, the endpoint returns 200 ✅

Nothing surfaces the divergence except comparing the md5 **inside** the container against the host.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Add the gateway restart to the runbook as a required step**, not an optional one — `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §Redeploy runbook. Wording should carry the mechanism (inode), because "restart to pick up the spec" reads as cargo-cult and gets dropped.
- [ ] **2. Correct the existing guidance.** The current understanding recorded in project notes is "a rebuild does not publish it, a restart does" — true but incomplete, and it does not say the container will serve the old file *forever* until something re-resolves the mount.
- [ ] **3. Add a post-deploy assertion** that fails loudly: compare `md5sum` of the host spec against `docker exec api-gateway md5sum` of the mounted path, and refuse to call a deploy complete when they differ. This is the check that would have caught it with no human judgement involved.
- [ ] **4. Audit for other file-level bind mounts with the same exposure** — `nginx-demo.conf` is the known sibling. Directory mounts are not affected; only single-file mounts are.

## Not a live defect right now

The 2026-09-08 deploy restarted `api-gateway` and the served spec is verified correct. This ticket is about the **next** deploy, by whoever does not know.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the deploy itself.

title: Akto reports a PASS for a test that executed NOTHING — 'clean 0 / not-applicable 969 ✓' is a second false-zero axis that richCaptureFailed does not catch
description:
## BLUF

**KS-700 closes one false-zero axis and this is the other one.** On @PeterObeden's 2026-08-28 review run, `analytics: code injection` returned **clean 0 · not-applicable 969** and reported **✓**. The capture *succeeded* — so `richCaptureFailed` is correctly false — and the scan still measured nothing that actually executed. A green tick on zero executed requests.

⚠ **Provenance: Peter's measurement from his** `test:security` **run, not independently reproduced here.** Filed so the class is tracked rather than living in a PR thread.

## ✅ Done so far — PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and)), merged 2026-09-28

These sections are delivered; the ticket stays open for criteria 1 and 3 below.

* ✅ **A 429 result is no longer scored as a pass** — its own `rateLimited` bucket (it was 79% of a full scan's "passes"); COVERAGE DEGRADED when refusals outnumber what executed.
* ✅ **A zero-run report says NO COVERAGE** instead of "0 vulnerable" (the `-t` filter case in Kamil's comment).
* ✅ **Pacing** so the platform's limiter no longer decides coverage — 0 of 50,306 full-scan results refused (open decision on the platform side: [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times)).

## Why KS-700's fix does not cover it

KS-700 distinguishes *"asked Mongo and got nothing"* (`richCaptureFailed`) from *"never asked"*. Both are about the **capture**. This is a third state the capture cannot see: **the capture worked, and what it faithfully reports is that nothing ran.** `clean 0` with `not-applicable 969` means every candidate was filtered out before a request was sent — so the ✓ attests to an empty set, not to a clean one.

Read the way a reader naturally reads it, *"analytics: code injection ✓"* means the endpoints were tested and were fine. It means neither.

`DEV-PROCESS.md` already says an Akto PASS should be read as *"nothing was reported"*, not *"nothing is there"* — this is the sharpest instance of why.

## Suggested shape

Treat **executed == 0 with a non-zero candidate count** as its own verdict, the way `richCaptureFailed` is — not PASS. Something like `NO COVERAGE — 969 candidates, 0 executed`, failing or warning per tier. The count is already computed: `executedResultCount(breakdown)` in `src/scan/runTiming.ts`, and `clean + vulnerable` is the executed figure.

Note the same shape appears in the aggregate: this session's `test:pr` runs report `not-applicable 3281` and `not-on-stack 360` against `clean ~803` — so roughly 80% of every run is filtered before a request is sent. That is not necessarily wrong, but nothing currently asserts a floor on it.

## Done means

1. A scan where a whole test category executes nothing does **not** report ✓.
2. ✅ **Done** — a control: a category that genuinely executes and is clean still passes (so the fix is not "fail everything"). Shown live on slot 2, 2026-09-28: `clean 140 · rate-limited 0` reported PASS three times in the same run.
3. Reproduced from a real run, not only a unit test — the [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700/akto-harness-prints-a-false-zero-when-its-mongo-capture-fails-no) review's own standard.

title: Reconciler gives up a RE-ANCHORED old anchor row at its first pass: the 24 h test reads created_at, not the new submission's age
description:
**BLUF:** On demo, an anchor row created on 2026-09-30 received a new transaction on 2026-10-29 at 05:53Z. The node refused it, so nothing was on chain, and the reconciler marked the row `failed` at its first pass, 06:07:07Z, about 14 minutes later, with the message "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)". The give-up test measures the row's age from `created_at`, which a re-anchor does not change, so an old row that is re-anchored is eligible for the 24 hour give-up as soon as the reconciler next scans it.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`): `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts:98` reads `now() - new Date(row.created_at).getTime() > config.giveUpMs` and then writes `status: 'failed'` with "transaction never appeared on chain within Nh (reconciler)". The reconciler scans rows with `status IN ('pending', 'submitted', 'submitting')`, a non-null `transaction_hash`, `simulated = FALSE` and `updated_at` older than `minAgeMs` (`reconciler.ts:73-76`). `created_at` is selected but is not in that WHERE clause; it is read only by the give-up test.

**Measured on demo** (Seat D 42nd, read-only, host `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-10-29 06:16Z and 06:17Z; files `moved_C.txt`, `attrib_C.txt` and `moved_logs.txt`):

* The row: `created=2026-09-30 04:20:54.978+00` (unchanged by the 29 Oct submissions), `updated=2026-10-29 06:07:07.096+00`, `status=failed`, `retries=0`, `confirmed_at=null`, error "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)".
* Anchoring log lines that name the row, 05:10Z to 06:10Z: 05:52:41Z "Anchor created"; 05:52:44Z a transaction submitted (`e563c41d…`); 05:53:11Z "Anchor created" again; 05:53:13Z that transaction confirmed on Cardano (block 4804058), together with the warning "KS-1385: declined to record a transaction against an anchor whose metadata changed under it"; 05:53:13Z a second submission, "Node REFUSED the written-ahead transaction — the reply arrived, nothing is on chain" (`c8fe9420…`); then "Anchor already submitted — re-polling the known transaction"; 06:07:07Z "Reconciler: stale anchor marked failed — tx never appeared (KS-584)" naming `c8fe9420…`, pass summary `scanned 1, confirmed 0, failed 1`.
* In the same read, by status: confirmed 249, failed 93; 3 failed rows carry a `confirmed_at` (they were confirmed once). That count is as read; I did not analyse its cause.

**Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatD-42nd/evidence/demo/moved_C.txt`, `attrib_C.txt`, `moved_logs.txt`. Seat D 42nd reported the finding to Wednesday in its STATUS C mail (2026-10-29 06:22Z).

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `reconciler.ts:98` 0 hits; `giveUpMs` 1 hit (KS-726, archived, the write-ahead of the transaction hash); "never appeared on chain within" 1 hit (KS-772, comments only); "re-anchored" 1 hit (KS-963, archived, unrelated); `created_at` 28 hits, read by title (KS-1630 concerns which clock sets `created_at`, a different defect).

**Not measured:** why the row received a second submission (the repeat-POST reset of an existing row is described in KS-1384; I did not verify it here), and whether any chain state exists for `c8fe9420…`.

**Related:** KS-1384 (a repeat `POST /api/anchors` resets the existing row), KS-1171.

title: Reconciler cannot tell a provider outage from an absent transaction at the 24 h give-up: waitForConfirmation swallows the throw
description:
**BLUF:** The anchoring reconciler gives up on a row at 24 hours when its transaction reads `confirmed: false`, and it cannot tell "the chain answered not found" from "the chain could not be asked". The confirmation checker it calls catches provider errors itself and returns `confirmed: false` with `polled` and `errored` counts, and the reconciler never reads them. So a provider outage at the pass that crosses 24 hours can write `failed` ("transaction never appeared on chain") onto a row whose transaction is on chain. This is a source reading; it has not been exercised.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts:34`: `checkTx` is typed as returning `{ confirmed, blockHash?, blockNumber?, slot?, confirmations? }`, with no `polled` or `errored`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:2192`: `checkTx: (tx) => waitForConfirmation(tx, 1, 0, 0)`, one attempt.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts:98-99`: the `catch` inside the polling loop does `errored += 1` and carries on; `:110-119` returns `{ confirmed: false, polled, errored, … }` with the error text "could not be checked: … attempts failed to reach the chain" when `polled === 0`. It does not throw. The type comment at `:18-26` (KS 726) says `confirmed: false` with `polled: 0` means the chain was never asked, "which says nothing about the transaction", and that a caller that reads it as "absent" re-submits a transaction that may already be in a block.
* `reconciler.ts:86-105`: the branch tests `confirmation.confirmed`, then `now() - row.created_at > config.giveUpMs`, and writes `status: 'failed'` with "transaction never appeared on chain within Nh (reconciler)". `polled` and `errored` are not read. The reconciler's own `catch` at `:106-109` ("chain check errored; leaving row as-is") cannot be reached by a provider outage, because the throw is swallowed one call earlier.
* `failed` is terminal for the reconciler: its SELECT takes only `status IN ('pending', 'submitted', 'submitting')` (`reconciler.ts:73`).

**What was and was not seen:**

* Seat T 6th read this in the source while measuring the kintsugi stuck row and recorded it as "source reading (not tested, not mutated)". That row is not this case: its hash really is absent from the chain (Koios agrees).
* Kintsugi's anchoring log, 2026-10-29 01:06Z to 09:02Z: 95 reconciler passes, 'chain check errored' 0, 'stale anchor marked failed' 1. That count is consistent with either reading.
* Tests: `ks584-reconciler.test.ts` has 0 matches for `errored` or `polled`.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/mail/04_measured_body.txt` (finding F2) and `HANDOVER.md`
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread2_0902Z_t6.txt` (the log counts above)

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `waitForConfirmation` 4 hits, read: KS-1171 (the submit-path re-poll treats a mixed window as absent, and its ruling rests unknown rows "for the reconciler", which is how rows reach this give-up), KS-726 (archived, the write-ahead of the hash), KS-671 (archived, /health), KS-485 (the security plan); 'chain check errored' 1 hit (KS-772, comments only). None describes the reconciler's 24 hour give-up reading an unreachable chain as absence.

**Not measured:** no reconciler pass was run against a failing provider.

**Related:** KS-1171, KS-1384.

title: The ruled-retry cell (ks726:414) paraphrases the node's reply: with the real text it fails, and deleting the clause breaks no cell
description:
**BLUF:** The cell that pins the ruled retry after a node rejection, `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414`, feeds the guard a paraphrase of the node's reply (`"All inputs are spent"`). The node's real text, stored in `ks705-submission-idempotency.test.ts:48-50`, carries a second phrase, "already been included", and the `ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY` clause in `anchorSubmission.ts` turns the retry off for any text that contains it. No test pairs the real text with a write-ahead and an absent re-poll. I deleted the clause on develop `6d41673e0f79` and the whole anchoring suite's failing set stayed identical to the control; and when I gave the `:414` cell the real text, it failed. So the clause that makes the ruled retry unreachable for the real reply is unpinned, and the cell that should have caught it tests a text the node does not send.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/`):

* `anchorSubmission.ts:112` `const ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY = /already been included/i;`, also listed among the patterns `isAlreadySubmittedError` matches (`:115-124`).
* `anchorSubmission.ts:637-641`: `refusedAndAbsent = found === 'absent' && known === writtenAheadTxHash && !ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY.test(message ?? '')`, then `if (!refusedAndAbsent) return;`. The comment at `:635-636` says "already been included" names this transaction as in the ledger and never reaches this branch's retry.
* `__tests__/ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414` the cell "a 400 "All inputs are spent" after onSigned, the re-poll finds the hash ABSENT with DEFINITIVE evidence → scheduleRetry, no submitting rest"; its fixture at `:417` is `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"`. The control at `:452` uses `'this transaction has already been included'` (`:453`), a text that matches no reply recorded in the repo.
* `__tests__/ks705-submission-idempotency.test.ts:47-50`: "The node reply measured on demo, as Blockfrost surfaces it": `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent. Transaction has probably already been included in a successfully applied block."`
* Phrase census at the pin: "already been included" appears in `ks705` (4 times), `ks726` (2), `anchorSubmission.ts` (3) and `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (1); the long form "probably already been included" appears in `ks705` only, and `ks705` has no write-ahead, no `status_code` and no absent re-poll (per Seat W 7th's reading; I did not re-read every cell of that file). The KS-1171 files that use `onSigned` or the poll constants contain neither phrase.

**Measured by me** (develop `6d41673e0f79`, `services/anchoring`, vitest, Node v26.8.1; logs in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/`, files `j_*`):

* Control, whole suite, nothing planted: 33 files, 456 cells, **1 failed** (`threadTokenMint … parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId`, which is red on develop already).
* Control mutant M0, `&& false` appended to the conjunction: **4 failed**; the three extra reds are `ks726…:414`, `ks1171-b1-absent-boundary-is-inclusive` and `ks1171b-absent-needs-both-conditions`. So the suite does notice changes to this line.
* Mutant X, the `!ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY.test(message ?? '')` line deleted (an exact-once replace, restored afterwards with the file's blob read back equal to the staged blob): **1 failed**, and the failing set is byte-identical to the control's (`j_failset_control.txt`, `j_failset_x.txt`). X survives.
* Probe, three untracked copies of `ks726`, each run on that one cell and then deleted: (1) unchanged, short text: **passes**; (2) the line-417 fixture replaced with the `ks705` text, clause present: **fails**, `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` (`scheduleRetry` never called); (3) the same real text with mutant X planted: **passes**. So for the node's real reply the clause is exactly what stops the retry.
* Reproduce: copy `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts`, replace line 417 with the string from `ks705:48-50`, run the cell with `vitest run <copy> -t "the re-poll finds the hash ABSENT with DEFINITIVE evidence"`.

**What this does and does not say:** it says the real reply makes the `:414` cell fail on today's code and that no cell would notice the clause going. It does not say which side is right: whether the clause should stay is a product question, and Seat W 7th's KS-1384 revision (section 3.2) proposes dropping it. Whether the node's refusal text at the two incidents of 28 and 29 October was this long form was not measured (the logs are cut; Seat W 7th lists it as unmeasured).

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/` : `j_control_whole_anchoring_suite.log`, `j_m0_conjunction_false.log`, `j_x_clause_deleted.log`, `j_probe_short.log`, `j_probe_long.log`, `j_probe_long_x.log`, `j_failset_*.txt`
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, section 3.2 (the code path) and 3.5 (the six cells; sub-agent B's reading, "not run" there, which this ticket now runs); section 16 item 4.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY` 0 hits; `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414` 0 hits; `refusedAndAbsent` 1 hit, read: KS-1171 calls `refusedAndAbsent` the reader of the "absent" verdict and says nothing about the text clause; "already been included" 4 hits and "probably already been included" 4 hits, read: KS-726, KS-705 and KS-535 (all archived) record the reply, and KS-607 (Backlog) tabulates UAT anchors by the node's text `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"`, which is a different defect (GET /api/anchors and verify disagree on status). No ticket describes the paraphrased cell or the unpinned clause.

**Related:** KS-1384 (the revision that proposes dropping the clause), KS-1171 (the absence rule the retry depends on), KS-726 (the write-ahead; archived, so Linear refuses a relation to it: named here only).

title: Guard 3's re-poll reads a MIXED window as ABSENT — one early "not found" then an unreachable chain still schedules a retry that can re-mint a written-ahead transaction (#805 tier-1 r3 residue)
description:
## BLUF

After #805 (KS-726) merged as `48e65c435` on 2026-09-15, `reconfirmKnownSubmission` treats a bounded re-poll as `'unknown'` **only when NO attempt reached the chain** (`polled === 0`). A window in which at least one attempt answered "not found" (a Blockfrost 404) and every remaining attempt THREW (5xx / 402 quota / DNS) still reads `'absent'`, guard 3 calls it a definitive rejection, and the ordinary retry mints a second fee-paying transaction for a document whose first — the hash just written ahead — may be on its way to a block. This is the same class as the F1 the merge closed (an unreachable chain read as absent), one neighbour over: the fix weights **whether** the chain ever answered, not **when**.
