Measured by the tier-1 delta gate (round 3) at `a4d182bf9` and on the merged tree — report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-15-ks726-805-a4d182bf9-tier1-r3/report.md` §5 (cells R3a/b/c, R3b-2nd): with the answer early / middle / late in a 3-attempt window, `polled 1 / errored 2` each time → `'absent'` → `scheduleRetry` 1; R3b's second call minted TX_B (`minted [TX_B]`, `signedHashes [TX_A, TX_B]`, row `confirmed`/TX_B). Grade: **TICKET, ships-with** — the gate's, endorsed by the coordinator; filed by the merge seat as the ADDENDUM required.

## Why the early 404 is a likely FALSE negative in exactly the case that matters

The retry is wrong only when TX_A is in fact accepted while the node says "inputs spent" for it — a same-hash duplicate submit, the two-process race the module's NOT HANDLED list already names. In that premise TX_A entered the mempool seconds before the 400; Blockfrost's `/txs/{hash}` answers 404 until the tx is in a block **and** indexed; the production poll's first attempt lands \~10–12 s after the 400, the second \~15–17 s later, the third \~22 s later. So an early "not found" says little, and a rule that accepts any single answer as definitive is weakest at the start of the window — where a fresh transaction is most likely to be unindexed.

## Blast radius (round 2's units, the gate's reading)

Severity **HIGH** — a duplicate fee-paying transaction (\~181,825 lovelace) and an unrecorded on-chain anchor for the document (TX_B is a valid anchor; TX_A is the orphan; no data loss, no false "anchored" claim). Likelihood **LOW** — {a same-hash duplicate submit} ∧ {TX_A unindexed at every answered attempt} ∧ {the provider unreachable from the first unanswered attempt through attempt 30, \~27 min}. Blast radius one document per occurrence. The gate did not accept "rarer than F1": by its arithmetic the residue's outage-start window is of the same order as the closed case's; both hang on a long provider outage (or a 402 quota exhaustion, a sustained state that naturally arrives mid-poll) beginning within tens of seconds of a duplicate submit.

## Where it lives (at `48e65c435`)

* `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts` — `waitForConfirmation` reports `polled` / `errored` counts only; nothing says WHEN the last answer came.
* `services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts` — `reconfirmKnownSubmission`: the `confirmation.polled === 0` → `'unknown'` arm (after the `confirmed` return, before the `'absent'` return); guard 3's `refusedAndAbsent` reads `'absent'` as definitive.
* The shipped cells that pin today's rule: `__tests__/ks726-gate-f1-unreachable-chain.test.ts` — "a mixed window (throw, not found, throw) reads ABSENT … → retry" is a deliberate pin of the commissioned "any attempt" semantics and must be REWRITTEN, not deleted, by whoever changes the rule.

## Fix-shape (prose — the gate's, for the owner to weigh; not a committed artefact)

Have `waitForConfirmation` also report `lastAnsweredAttempt` (or the elapsed ms at the last answered attempt), and have `reconfirmKnownSubmission` treat `'absent'` as definitive **only when the last answer is late enough for a mempool transaction to be in an indexed block** — e.g. `polled >= 2`, or an answer ≥ 60 s after the 400 — else `'unknown'` (rest in `submitting` for the reconciler). Regression cells: (404, throw ×29) → `'unknown'`, `scheduleRetry` 0, the row rests; CONTROL (404 ×k spanning ≥ 60 s, then throws) → `'absent'` → retry; the existing all-404 and all-throw cells unchanged. **The cost to weigh:** a genuinely absent transaction whose late attempts threw would now rest \~24 h for the reconciler instead of retrying in \~15 s — the (c) ruling's own concern — so this is a design decision for the ticket owner, not a bug fix, which is why the builder did not make it under KS-726.

## Two smaller records the gate carries, stated here so they are not lost

* (8j) the `confirmed`-before-`polled === 0` ordering in `reconfirmKnownSubmission` is unpinned by any shipped cell; the cell to add if wanted: an injected `{ confirmed: true, polled: 0 }` → row `confirmed`, no `'unknown'` log.
* (8k) `getTransaction` returns `null` when no Blockfrost client is configured (`cardano/provider.ts`), which the `polled` counter reads as "the chain answered"; pre-existing, unreachable through the production submitter without a real 64-hex hash on the row.

## Symbol search before filing (the `issues` filter over title + description + comments, `includeArchived:true`, 1,160 issues; controls 1/0 as expected)

`reconfirmKnownSubmission` → 1 (KS-726 itself, the merge seat's own comments) · `lastAnsweredAttempt` → 0 · `mixed window` → 0 · `reads 'absent'` → 0 · `unreachable chain` → 1 (KS-671, the /health chain-path mechanism — different) · `polled` → 8 (KS-726's comments, wrap comments on the review parent, and KS-683's consumer re-poll — a different mechanism; the rest archived and unrelated). No open ticket owns this.

## Related

KS-726 (the parent finding; merged as `48e65c435`, PR #805) · the gate report above (§5, §7).

title: Security (pre-existing): anchoring POST /api/anchors never checks who owns documentId, so any authenticated caller from any tenant can write to another tenant's anchor row
description:
## BLUF

`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `POST /api/anchors` (`:463-503`) upserts `anchor_store` on `(document_id, network)` **without checking who owns** `documentId` **or which tenant it belongs to.** This is **pre-existing on develop**. Facts only; **no fix shape is proposed here**. Found by the Opus gate on pull request 1549 (verdict `40bdc24d2e1f07dc`, its MAJ-1) and measured further by Seat J 9th.

## Facts

* **No ownership or tenant check.** The handler parses the body and upserts. `req.user` (role, userId, organizationId, tenantId — `index.ts:520-530`) is used **only** for the connector provenance row, never to authorise the write.
* **A human JWT skips the** `anchors:write` **scope** at the gateway: `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:873-878` with `middleware/scopes.ts:36-39` (read by the gate, not booted).
* `anchor_store` **carries no tenant and no row-level security.** Measured on a repo-built database: no tenant or owner column; `relrowsecurity = f`, `relforcerowsecurity = f`.
* `x-emitter-internal` **is trusted by mere presence** (`index.ts:524`). originate sets it on one call site only, and any peer on the compose network can send it (the F-04 class). Related: **KS-741** (that header is unstripped on the gateway's `/originate/` route) — a different defect, not linked.
* **What it does on develop today (the gate's develop control, measured on the real anchoring service):** a second POST from a **different tenant's user** for someone else's `documentId` is accepted (202, same row id) and makes the platform **re-mint the victim's own first payload** — a fresh transaction, fee and tx-hash churn, but **no falsification**, because the stored payload is write-once on develop.
* **Why it matters beyond cost:** pull request 1549 (KS-1385) as first written made `metadata_payload` overwritable, and **this gap turned that into falsification** — a tenant-B user rewrote tenant-A's attestation and public verify-by-hash answered `verified: true` with B's organisation and identity. That pull request is NO GO and its fix round narrows the overwrite; **this ticket exists because the underlying gap remains whatever that round does.**
* **Writers that reach this route** (the gate's sweep): originate's seven sites, each forwarding the **end user's or connector's own bearer** (not a service identity); Platform S's flat call through the gateway (`proxy.ts:873`) with a connector JWT; and the batch path `POST /api/anchors/batch` (`index.ts:735`), same authentication.

## Same class elsewhere

**KS-692** — `/api/status` revoke/unrevoke has no tenant ownership check. A sibling of the same class on a different route; not a duplicate.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title **and** description (not `searchIssues`, which is fuzzy): `who owns documentId` 0, `anchor_store has no tenant` 0, `ownership check` 1 (KS-692, read: a different route). Positive control `x-emitter-internal` → KS-741. Negative control: a freshly generated token written nowhere → 0. A FIRST negative control was **contaminated** — the term had been quoted inside KS-1599's own dedupe section, so it returned that ticket. Re-run with an uncontaminated token before relying on the zeros.

*Filed by Seat J 9th. Priority High, as Wednesday instructed. Not fixed here.*

title: Security: POST /api/documents/:id/version has NO per-document access check on its source - any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from another organisation's document (the sibling of the certify path KS-1557/#1619 closed)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/documents/:id/version` **checks a ROLE, a SCOPE and the TENANT, and nothing about the caller's relationship to the source document.** Any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from **another organisation's** document, and the derived row is a real child of it. This is the sibling of the path KS-1557 / pull request #1619 closed on `POST /api/certifications/issue`: the same defect class, the same service, still open on the versioning route. Measured on a scratch stack at develop `89956fe92956`. Facts only — no fix is proposed here.

## Where

`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `'/:id/version'` handler:

* `:2219` — `const ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES = DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES;`
* `:2246` — `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(req, ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES, 'documents:write')` — role or scope only.
* `:2281` — `const source = await getDocument(id, tenantId, (req as any).db);` followed by a 404 when it does not resolve, and a `metadata.documentType` guard. **There is no owner / recipient / creating-connector test anywhere in the handler** — the check `callerMayCertifyDocument` applies on the certify path (`routes/certifications.ts:119-128`, call sites `:223` legacy and `:441` lineage) has no counterpart here.

## Measured (scratch Postgres 15 at migration 054, real `documents` + `certifications` routers, `secuura_app`, both `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` and `=true` — identical results in both)

| cell | what was done | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| G1 | **a FOREIGN organisation's connector** calls `/version` on organisation A's document | **201.** The minted row is a real child: its `parent_document_id` resolves to A's document. |
| G1 (same cell) | **the discriminating control** — that **same caller**, on that **same document**, through `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` | **403** `FORBIDDEN` |
| G2 | an **interactive write-role USER of another organisation** calls `/version` on A's document | **201** |
| G3 | **the bound** — a caller in **another tenant** calls `/version` on A's document | **404** `NOT_FOUND "Document not found in this tenant"` |

G1's two halves are the finding in one line: **the two sibling routes disagree about the same caller on the same document.** G3 bounds it — it does not cross the tenant, because `getDocument` is tenant-scoped.

## Board search before filing (symbol and path, each with a control)

* `callerMayCertifyDocument` → **2** hits (KS-1557, KS-1679); `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` → **2** (KS-1202, KS-1433). Both controls fire, so the instrument discriminates rather than returning everything.
* `ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES`, `/:id/version`, `documents/:id/version`, `parent_document_id` → each returns the 12-hit fuzzy cap, and **none of the hits names this defect.** The nearest four, each a different thing: **KS-1538** (the legacy certify path — fixed), **KS-1557** (the lineage certify path — this route's sibling), **KS-1508** (`versionedById` is server-set — same route, different defect), **KS-1228** (a refused request still writes an `action_provenance` row — same route, different defect).
* **0 open hits for the source-access check itself.**

## Sequencing — this matters before anyone gates this route

The KS-1557 fix (shape (a′): `/version` records the creating connector on the document it mints, under the action value `create:connector`) **must land before any source-access gate is added here.** Otherwise a gate written with the same predicate would refuse `/version` on a version-minted document for exactly the reason certify refuses it today: a `/version`-created document has no creation provenance row of its own, so `wasCreatedByConnector` is false for the connector that actually made it. Measured on demo: **31 of 31** `/version`-minted documents have no such row.

## Open question, UNMEASURABLE from this project

**Does Platform S ever version a document it did not itself originate?** It decides the client-visible risk of closing this gap — if S does, closing it turns some S calls into 403. It cannot be answered from here: `Secuura/platform-s` returns 404 to this project's PAT (which sees exactly one repository), so no search of S's code is possible from Platform K's identity. **Stated as a question, not an assumption, and not asked of anyone here.**

## Not claimed

* No severity judgement beyond the priority on this ticket, and no fix design.
* The derived row carries the **caller's own** `newContentHash`, so this is not an alteration of the source document's bytes; the source gains a child it did not consent to, and the derived row presents as part of its lineage.
* Not measured: whether any such cross-organisation version exists in live data.

Found by Seat C 31st while measuring KS-1557 (Stuart's comment `16e8498d`) at develop `89956fe92956`, 2026-10-20.

title: didJwkRefusal's early return for a pattern-refused value is pinned by no cell: removing it leaves 183 of 183 cells green

title: auth GET /api/users/lookup refuses connector tokens, so every Platform-S transfer-custody 401s and falls back to a flat anchor — KS-739's users:read ruling cannot take effect
description:
## BLUF

**No Platform-S rights-assign or rights-reassign reaches** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` **successfully.** originate resolves `newHolderEmail` by calling auth's `GET /api/users/lookup` with the **caller's** `Authorization` header, and `/lookup` accepts only access tokens (`authenticate()`). Platform-S authenticates per Organisation with a **connector** token, so auth answers 401 *"Invalid token"*, originate passes it through ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s 4xx rule), and S degrades to a flat `/api/anchors` anchor. No `custody_events` row is written and `documents.owner_user_id` never moves.

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived) ruled 2026-09-02 that *"Platform S provisions* `users:read` *on its connector key; K does not widen* `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES`*"*. That ruling cannot take effect: the scope check sits behind an authenticator that rejects the token type before any scope is read. A missing scope would answer **403**; what S receives is **401 Invalid token**.

## Code (platform-k `develop` `0736d8b78`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1665-1671` — email-only path: `fetch(${AUTH_SERVICE_URL}/api/users/lookup?email=…, { headers: { Authorization: <caller's header> } })`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1708-1730` — a 4xx from the lookup is passed through; 401 → *"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry."* ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)).
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` — `userRoutes.get('/lookup', authenticate(), …)` — access tokens only.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:357-359` — "[KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) *(Option A): this ONE route also accepts a connector token — see authenticateAccessOrConnector. Every other route keeps plain authenticate()."* — `/stub` was widened; `/lookup` was not.
* Platform-S side: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `TransferCustodyAsync` sends `{ newHolderEmail, reason }` + `onBehalfOf` with `Authorization: Bearer <connector access token>` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1527`).

## Measured — local pair, slot 3, 2026-10-01

platform-s `f370236c` (+ [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) systemTest changes only) ↔ platform-k `0736d8b78`, fresh databases, 33/33 K containers up, `/health/deep` 200, S provisioning key accepted, 10/0/0 organisations registered.

**4 of 4** transfer-custody calls refused, identical body, under Organisation 3's connector key:

```
transfer-custody status=401 body={"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry. Upstream said: Invalid token"}} … using /api/anchors fallback.
```

* 09:21:55Z — 2 calls ([PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914)'s date-sort seed: two documents delegated to a same-org colleague).
* 09:22:55–09:31:06Z — 2 calls during `npm run test:k-live` (`verb_matrix.spec.ts` rights-assign + rights-reassign on K document `7af2374a-dd61-47e7-be50-122dcb5e412b`).

In the same window, Organisation 3's connector token **succeeded** on `originate` (201) and on lifecycle events (`rights-unassign`, `delete`) — so the key is valid; only the auth-service lookup refuses it.

## Why nothing went red

The platform-s `@k-live` cell "rights-assign and rights-unassign each reach K" asserted only that the S edge carries an anchor K resolves as not-failed — which the flat fallback also satisfies. It passed (17 passed / 1 skipped) while both custody calls 401'd. [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) tightens that cell to assert the custody transfer K records — `GET /api/documents/{id}` `owner.id` must move off its pre-assign value (measured: it reads `""` before and after today's refused transfers). The cell is **red until this ticket ships**, deliberately, and turns green once K records the transfer. Platform-S's `TransferCustodyAsync` carries a comment naming this ticket.

## Options (Kamil's call — no K code changed)

1. **Widen** `/lookup` **to** `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, as [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) did for `/stub` — makes [KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s `users:read` ruling effective (the connector key then needs that scope).
2. **originate resolves the holder with its own service credential**, not the caller's header — removes the dependency on the caller's token type.
3. **Platform-S sends** `newHolderId` — requires S to know the K user id of the recipient (S-side; it does not today).

Whichever is chosen, a recipient with no K account still gets the typed 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) measurement A) — worth confirming the S holder exists in K once the 401 is gone.

## Related

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived — ruling this ticket shows cannot take effect) · [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) (Option A connector scoping) · [PS-681](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-681/systemtest-k-live-every-share-and-rights-verb-times-out-waiting-for) (Done — Stuart's original 502 report) · [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) (platform-s: the k-live cell that hid this).

title: Fifteen guard clauses in the two anchor-heal functions are pinned by no test, including the settled and failed early-returns: dropping any one leaves all 1,523 originate cells green (v1 confirmStalePendingAnchor, v2 healBlobWithChainFact)
description:
## BLUF

**Fifteen guard clauses in the two anchor-heal functions are pinned by no test: weakening any one of them leaves all 1,523 originate unit cells green.** That includes the `settled` and `failed` early-returns on both paths, so **a failed anchor could be shown and written back as** `confirmed` **if those guards regressed.** Only the two attribution checks are pinned.

**This ticket was first filed with a wrong table, and this is the correction.** It said seven guards were unpinned and six others were "pinned elsewhere". The six were false kills: my mutants left a variable unused, which breaks the test compile under `noUnusedLocals`, and a compile failure reads as a kill. Gate AT1 found it (note N4: at least eleven). I re-measured with compile-safe mutants and a classifier that flags a kill caused by a TypeScript diagnostic. Details under "The correction".

Nothing is wrong today. The risk is that a refactor drops one of these lines and nothing reddens. Medium, in the same family as KS-1661 and KS-1640 (a blob overstating anchoring). **Whether the** `failed`**/**`settled` **finding warrants a re-rate is not mine to decide.**

## Recommendation

One cell per unpinned guard, each proven by its own **compile-safe** mutant (dropping that line must red exactly that cell). Shape, not chosen here:

* stored blob `simulated: true` with a real chain reply refuses to heal (v1 and v2);
* stored `txHash` that is not 64-hex refuses to heal (v1 and v2);
* chain reply `txHash` that is not 64-hex refuses to heal (v1 and v2);
* chain reply `verified: false` refuses to heal (v1);
* a stored row with status `failed`, `anchor_failed` or `confirmed`, or `anchored: true`, is returned unchanged and never persisted as `confirmed` (v1 and v2).

`ks1661-a-simulated-chain-reply-never-heals-a-stale-pending-row.test.ts` already has the harness for both routers.

**Write the mutants so they compile.** `(failed && false)` keeps the variable used. Deleting the use does not.

## Detail

Measured 2026-10-20 by Seat C 27th on develop `09336b240721d8961d409dbd3c0de077d03ca959` (tree `29f134c4d9e5d45bc3da52fc1c19847c69e917f4`, which includes #1630, #1631 and #1632). Each mutant weakens ONE line or clause. It was planted by line number after asserting that line's exact content, then restored and hash-checked. It then ran the **whole** originate suite (`npx jest`, 1,523 cells, the unmutated tree confirmed green first).

| id | file:line | the guard | compile-safe mutant | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A1 | `verification.ts:432` | v1 stored `simulated` | drop `blob.simulated === true` | **SURVIVED** |
| A2 | `verification.ts:434` | v1 stored tx-hash shape | drop `!REAL_TXHASH_RE.test(tx)` | **SURVIVED** |
| A3 | `verification.ts:437` | v1 `failed` early-return | `(failed && false)` | **SURVIVED** |
| A3b | `verification.ts:436` | v1 `'anchor_failed'` status | drop it from `failed` | **SURVIVED** |
| A4 | `verification.ts:437` | v1 `settled` early-return | `(settled && false)` | **SURVIVED** |
| A4b | `verification.ts:435` | v1 `anchored === true` | drop it from `settled` | **SURVIVED** |
| V4 | `verification.ts:455` | v1 incoming tx-hash shape | drop `!REAL_TXHASH_RE.test(chainTx)` | **SURVIVED** |
| V5 | `verification.ts:455` | v1 incoming `verified` | drop `chain?.verified !== true` | **SURVIVED** |
| W4 | `verificationV2.ts:130` | v2 stored `simulated` | drop `blob.simulated === true` | **SURVIVED** |
| B1 | `verificationV2.ts:132` | v2 stored tx-hash shape | drop `!REAL_TXHASH_RE.test(tx)` | **SURVIVED** |
| B2 | `verificationV2.ts:135` | v2 `failed` early-return | `(failed && false)` | **SURVIVED** |
| B2b | `verificationV2.ts:134` | v2 `'anchor_failed'` status | drop it from `failed` | **SURVIVED** |
| B3 | `verificationV2.ts:135` | v2 `settled` early-return | `(settled && false)` | **SURVIVED** |
| B3b | `verificationV2.ts:133` | v2 `anchored === true` | drop it from `settled` | **SURVIVED** |
| B5 | `verificationV2.ts:137` | v2 incoming tx-hash shape | drop `!REAL_TXHASH_RE.test(chainTx)` | **SURVIVED** |

**Pinned, for contrast** (the same instrument, a real kill with no TypeScript diagnostic):

| id | guard | killed by |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A6 | v1 attribution (`sameTx \|\| sameDoc`) | `ks584-verify-row-selection.test.ts` |
| B4 | v2 attribution (`!sameTx && !sameDoc`) | `ks584-p3-verify-list.test.ts` |

**Undecided:** v2's null-chain guard (`!chain`). No single-line mutant of it compiles under strict null checks (TS18047), so it cannot be measured this way. It was one of my false kills.

## The correction, and the mechanism

My first mutants for `failed`, `settled` and the null-chain guard were `if (settled) return blob;`, `if (failed) return blob;` and a dropped `!chain ||`. Each leaves a declared variable unused (TS6133, `noUnusedLocals: true`) or an object possibly null (TS18047). ts-jest refuses to compile the route module, so every suite that imports it fails. **The same three suites** (`ks1032-second-lines-hold-without-the-strip`, `ks1032-unconfigured-vouch-fails-closed`, `ks1041-provenance-mount-wiring`) "killed" five unrelated mutants. That was the tell, and I did not chase it. A kill is only a kill if the failure text carries no TypeScript diagnostic.

The mutation runner now classifies a kill as FALSE when the failing cells' messages contain a `TS####` code. I confirmed it on the original five (all flagged), and the compile-safe rewrites above are what give the real picture.

**Limits, stated plainly.**

* Unit suite only. It mocks the database, auth and `fetch`. The integration suites (they need a database) and the four platform suites were not run, so a guard may be pinned there.
* Each mutant weakens one line or clause. This is not an exhaustive mutation run.
* I read no environment and drove no live anchor.

## Dedupe

Searched all 2,923 issues, archived included, on 2026-10-19: `healBlobWithChainFact` 2 (KS-1661, KS-1057), `confirmStalePendingAnchor` 3 (KS-1661, KS-1634, KS-1129), `REAL_TXHASH_RE` 2 (KS-1661, KS-1640), `stale-anchor heal` 0, `guards on the stored` 0. I read the titles of 13 candidates and none is about the heal guards being unpinned. Positive control `preflight` 212 hits. Negative control: a fresh token read 0.

Related: KS-1661 (merged: adds the incoming-flag guard), KS-1640 (adjacent: the chain-first blob hard-codes `anchored: true`), KS-1634.

Filed by Seat C 27th on 2026-10-20 and **corrected the same day** (see above). The Linear actor field is shared across the fleet, so authorship is this line, not the actor.

title: KS-1709 follow-ups: non-JSON 2xx reads 'failed'; recertify unpublished with no fetch timeout; no re-anchor for a kept certification
description:
**BLUF:** Four loose ends from KS-1709, none introduced by it. QA gate 15 (1806-2, 1806-3) and Seat U 6th listed them in comments on KS-1709, and none has a ticket of its own: (1) an accepted 2xx from the anchoring service whose body is not JSON is reported as `failed`; (2) `POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` is not in the published spec; (3) its anchoring `fetch` has no timeout; (4) Platform K has no re-anchor for a kept certification.

**1. A non-JSON 2xx reads** `failed` (gate 15, 1806-2, measured at runtime). `upstream.json()` throws inside the `try` before `anchoringStatus = 'submitted'` is set (`certifications.ts:619-621` on the issue route; the same shape at `:1393-1395` on recertify, read only). On the issue route a 202 with an empty body gives 201 with `anchoringStatus: "failed"`, and a 200 with the text `ok` gives the same. In production the 202-empty case gives 503 with the provisional row deleted although anchoring had accepted the request (an orphan anchor; the gate records the production part as pre-existing). A 202 or 299 with a JSON id, and a 202 without `data.id`, give no key and `submitted`; a 409 gives `failed`. The published description says "a 4xx, a 5xx, an unreachable service or a timeout" and omits this case. The gate's likelihood note: low, since anchoring always answers JSON. The gate's fix-shape (not ruled): set `submitted` on `upstream.ok` before parsing (anchorId null when unreadable), or add "or an unreadable acceptance" to the description.

**2. Recertify is not published** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). `originate.openapi.ts:27` lists `/:id/recertify` among the endpoints not yet registered, and `secuura-api.yaml` has 0 matches for `recertify` (counted at develop `6d41673e0f79`). So the top-level `anchoringStatus` that KS-1709 added to the recertify 201 ships unpublished; `CertificationIssueResponse` covers the issue route only.

**3. Recertify's anchoring fetch has no timeout** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). The issue route's fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` (`certifications.ts:616`). The recertify fetch (`certifications.ts:1375-1395`) carries none, and the builder's own test header says so. The effective bound is the runtime's default fetch timeout, which nobody measured.

**4. No re-anchor for a kept certification** (Seat U 6th's KS-1709 wrap). A kept certification has `anchorId: null`. U 6th records that Platform K has no re-anchor for it; I did not search for one.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, findings 1806-2 and 1806-3
* the gate's probe output in the same folder: `evidence/probe/probe1806.out` (P1 to P10)

title: Chain-first verify blobs hard-code `anchored: true` and drop anchoring's status/acknowledged, so a 'submitting' or failed anchor reads isAnchored: true (v1 + v2)
description:
## BLUF

**The chain-first verify branches build their blockchain blob with** `anchored: true` **hard-coded and no** `status`**, which makes the honest-anchor guard** `settled` **BY CONSTRUCTION.** An anchoring reply that is still in flight or has failed — `status: 'submitting'`, `acknowledged: false`, the KS-726 class — is therefore presented as `isAnchored: true`, in both the v1 and the v2 verify routes.

The code says so itself. `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:130-132`:

> *"KS-1628: a failed anchor is not an anchor, whatever else the blob says. The chain-first blobs carry* `anchored: true` *and no status, so they are unaffected; a stored blob that pairs* `anchored: true` *with a failed status was on-chain before this line."*

That comment reads as a reassurance. It is in fact the statement of the defect: *unaffected by the failed-status guard* is exactly the problem, because the guard is the thing that would have caught this.

Gate O1's Minor 2 on the twelve-PR batch, 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z. Pre-existing; not in those merges.

## The mechanism, measured

`isAnchoredHonestly` (`verification.ts:120`) decides the claim:

```ts
if (FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(c.status))) return false;   // :133
const settled = c.anchored === true || c.status === 'confirmed';  // :141
```

* A **real stored** anchor row has no `anchored` boolean at all — the comment at `:136-139` says so: *"anchoring's vocabulary is pending | submitted | confirmed | failed … and there is NO* `anchored` *boolean on a real row."* For those rows only `status === 'confirmed'` earns the claim, and `'submitted'` deliberately does not, because *"the tx is in flight and may still fail — the KS-535 class."*
* A **chain-first** blob is built by hand with `anchored: true` and **no** `status` **key**. So `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(undefined))` is false — the failed guard cannot fire — and `settled` is true on the first disjunct, whatever anchoring actually reported.

**The four construction sites:**

| route | site |
| -- | -- |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:717` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1237` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1259` |
| **v2** | `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:233`, inside `chainOnlyMatch` |

The `status` argument the call sites pass does not rescue it: `verification.ts:758`, `:1297` and `verificationV2.ts:271` pass the **literal** `'anchored'`, and in any case the second argument is only consulted when there is no chain blob at all (`:149`).

**What bounds the severity.** `settled` is necessary but not sufficient: the claim also needs `typeof c.txHash === 'string'`, `REAL_TXHASH_RE` (64 hex) and `heightOk`. So the hash must already look like a real one, and it comes from the chain index. The defect is that **in-flight and failed anchors the index knows about still read as anchored** — not that an arbitrary blob does.

## Why High

On a document-authenticity platform, `isAnchored: true` is the product's central claim to a verifier. Presenting a `'submitting'` or failed anchor as anchored is the same family as KS-535 (a failed on-chain anchor reporting `status: anchored`) and KS-1634 (a simulated anchor returned unlabelled), and KS-1634 is High. The failure direction is always *over*-claiming, never under-claiming.

**Honest limit on this rating: I did not run a census.** I have not measured how many rows can reach these branches with a non-confirmed status today. The nearest evidence is KS-1634's census — 0 qualifying rows on both boxes at 2026-10-18, with kintsugi's 0 noted as contingent on one document row — and that census was for a different precondition. **A census is the first step on this ticket, and the rating should be revisited against it.**

## Recommendation

1. Carry anchoring's own fields into the chain-first blob instead of asserting the conclusion: pass `status` and `acknowledged` through, and let `isAnchoredHonestly` apply the same rules it applies to a stored row. Dropping `anchored: true` entirely is the cleaner shape, since no real row carries it — but `ks563` pins the current chain-first shape, so that is a deliberate change with a test to re-cut, not a one-liner.
2. A cell per site: a chain-first match whose anchoring status is `'submitting'` (and one that is `'failed'`) must read `isAnchored: false`. A mutant restoring the hard-coded `anchored: true` must red each of them.
3. Fold the **v2** site in with KS-1634's v2 work — it is the same four lines of construction, and splitting them across two tickets invites one to be done and the other forgotten.

## Dedupe

Over all **1,627** Secuura-PK issues including archived: `chainOnlyMatch` **→ 0 hits.** `anchored: true` → 4, each a different subject (KS-1634 the simulated-label defect, KS-1628 the route retirement, KS-834 a decision on verify auth, KS-535 the document-status variant, Done). `acknowledged` → 6, none about this presenter. `isAnchored` → 9; the nearest, KS-1637, is gate N1's residue about the removal pin reading only the router — a different mechanism, read and confirmed distinct. Positive controls on the same corpus: `verification` 360, `anchor` 313. Zero control: a nonsense token reads 0.

**Related:** KS-1634 (the same presenter, the `simulated` signal, and the v2 site it shares), KS-726 (the `status: 'submitting'` / `acknowledged: false` reply class this mis-presents; Done), KS-535 (the document-status variant; Done), KS-563 (which pins the current chain-first shape, so its cells are in scope for any change here).

---

*Filed by Seat R 51st on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z, citing gate O1's verdict section "Minor 2". The Linear actor field is shared across the fleet, so authorship is this line, not the actor. Everything above the "Why High" section I verified in the source at develop* `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`*; the severity and the census limit are my own call, stated as such. Not fixed in these merges.*

title: originate: a non-prod certification whose anchoring submission FAILED persists `confidence:'pending-onchain'` beside `anchoringStatus:'failed'` and is reported "pending-onchain" by the gateway indefinitely; and the thread-token mint REPLACES the document's blockchain blob (a fifth statusless producer, racing the anchor accept write) (QA-967/968 F4 + O1)
description:
## BLUF

Two READ ONLY findings in originate's `blockchain`-blob writers, recorded by the tier-2 gate on the #967 → #968 stack (KS-1071 / KS-1070) as Option B's blast radius — the gateway now honours a statusless blob's `confidence:'pending-onchain'` literal by ruling, and these are the producers of that literal. Neither is the PRs' change; both are pre-existing and identical at base. **F4:** `routes/certifications.ts:406-469` (and `:1131-1191`) sets `anchoringStatus='failed'` by default and `'submitted'` only if anchoring accepted (`:429`); in production a failure 503s (`:435`), but in non-prod it **persists** `{anchorId, txHash:null, blockHeight:null, anchoredAt:null, confidence:'pending-onchain', anchoringStatus:'failed'}`, and `:510` copies `certification.blockchain` verbatim onto the NEW document created at certify. The gateway reads neither `anchoringStatus` nor `anchorId`, no poller exists in `certifications.ts` (0 `updateDocument` / `pollAnchorUntilConfirmed` references), and `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` needs `bc.anchorId` (`anchorStateSync.ts:298`), which is `undefined` on the failed leg — so that document answers **pending-onchain at base,** `51e74ea7a` **and** `1b7c03a22` (the row was driven) for as long as it exists. **O1:** `routes/documents.ts:764-774` (the thread-token mint callback) writes `blockchain: { ...(create-time blob = nothing), threadToken }` via `updateDocument`, which **replaces** the blob (`documentRepo.ts:510-514`: `{...doc, ...updates, updatedAt}` — `updates.blockchain` replaces `doc.blockchain` wholesale). The auto-anchor accept write (`:880`) is also fire-and-forget; whichever resolves later wins. If the mint lands after the anchor accept, the document's `txHash` / `status` / `anchorId` are lost until the poller rewrites — and the confirmed-path rewrite (`anchorStateSync.ts:206-216`) does not carry `threadToken` back; only the failed path (`:160`) does. Gateway effect of the `{threadToken}`-only blob: off-chain-only at every SHA (driven, harmless); the race itself is originate's.

## Recommendation

One logical path — originate's statusless `pending-onchain` producers and the blob-replacing writers — so one ticket; split only if the two fixes land separately:

1. **F4:** on the failed leg, do not persist `confidence:'pending-onchain'` (write no `confidence`, or a `status` the gateway's closed mapping reads as off-chain-only), and/or make the gateway's Option-B arm read `anchoringStatus`; add a certifications cell asserting a failed submission never presents pending-onchain through the gateway. Prove the row first with the gate's Sweep B shape.
2. **O1:** merge rather than replace in the mint callback (spread the CURRENT persisted blob, not the create-time local), and carry `threadToken` through the confirmed-path rewrite as the failed path already does; a cell that lands the mint after the accept write and asserts `txHash` / `status` / `anchorId` survive. Prove the race first (it was READ, not reproduced).

## Detail

* **Where (READ ONLY at** `721b333a6`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:406-469`, `:429`, `:435`, `:510`, `:1131-1191`; `routes/documents.ts:764-774` (`:766` the only spread of a prior blob into a write — and `document` there is the create-time local from `:650`, which has no `blockchain` key), `:864-876` / `:880` (the accept write), `:895-903` (the failure write), `:1341-1351` / `:1367-1372` (the retry route's blobs); `repositories/documentRepo.ts:510-514`; `services/anchorStateSync.ts:146`, `:160`, `:206-216`, `:212`, `:247`, `:298`, `:320`, `:348`.
* **Writer census (the gate's,** `git grep -n "pending-onchain" 721b333a6 -- …/originate/src`**, non-test):** five literals — `documents.ts:1371`, `certifications.ts:467`, `:1189` (persisted), `anchors.ts:347`, `:441` (202 bodies, not writes). The status-writers never write `confidence`, and every one REPLACES the blob. Conclusion carried: no writer at develop can leave a blob carrying BOTH `status` and a stale `confidence` — which is why F2's guard is unpinned rather than wrong.
* **Serve boundary:** `GET /api/documents/:id` serves `{anchored, ...composeHonestBlockchainBlob(document.blockchain)}` (`documents.ts:1061-1072`; `anchorHonesty.ts:92-106`), which returns the blob unchanged unless `simulated === true` or the hash has a fabricated prefix — so `status` and `confidence` reach the gateway exactly as persisted.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1071-1070-967-968-1b7c03a22-tier2-r1/report.md`, §2 "Option B proved, and its blast radius" (R1), FINDINGS F4, "Open — for Wednesday" O1. NOT TESTED: no running originate; the writer census and the race are from source.
* **Related:** KS-1071 (PR #967, Option B ruled there); KS-1073 (the gateway's tier-2 statusless-blob cell — the consumer side of the same literal); KS-1074 (the poller/reconcile writers erase `threadToken` on the CONFIRM/heal path — O1 is its mirror: the mint erases the anchor fields); KS-1058 (the `markDocumentAnchorFailed` erasure already fixed).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived) and 899 comments — `pending-onchain` → KS-1057, KS-1068, KS-1071, KS-607, KS-834 + archived (none about the failed-leg persistence); `certifications.ts` → 15 issues, none this; `anchoringStatus` → 0; `thread token` / `threadToken` → KS-1074 (the mirror), KS-1058 (archived), KS-1004, KS-1068 — none describes the mint replacing the blob. Controls: `persistedStatus == null` → KS-1073; a nonsense token → 0.

title: A kept (refused-anchor) certification reads anchored: true on GET /api/documents/{id}, and POST /anchor 400s "already anchored"
description:
**BLUF:** A certification whose anchor was refused is now kept and marked unanchored (KS-1709, Kam's 2026-10-23 ruling b: "keep it, but mark it unanchored"). Its blob carries `blockchain.status` `failed`. The documents surface still reads that blob as anchored: `GET /api/documents/{id}` answers `blockchain.anchored: true`, and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored", so the documents retry route cannot re-anchor it. The comparison dates from KS-1124 F4 (2026-09-28); the ruling turns it into a contradiction on a second read surface.

**What was measured** (QA gate 15, finding 1806-1, on the KS-1709 pull request head; documentRepo mocked, the real `documentsRouter`):

* A certification is a row in `documents`, so `GET /api/documents/{certUuid}` serves it. With the blob the KS-1709 cells assert (`status: 'failed'`, `anchoringStatus: 'failed'`, `anchorId: null`), GET answers `blockchain.anchored: true` and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored".
* Controls in the same probe: a blob with `status: 'anchor_failed'` gives `anchored: false` and POST 202; a null blob gives `anchored: false` and POST 202.
* `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` returns early on `anchorId: null`, so nothing heals it.

**Where** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1200`: `anchored: !!document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed'`.
* `documents.ts:1458`: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored".
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:99-100`: `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` is `['failed', 'anchor_failed']`, so the verify surfaces already read `failed` as failed.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:1204`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` builds `checks.blockchainAnchored` as `!!certification.blockchain`, which is true for a kept failed certification (Seat U 6th recorded this in its KS-1709 wrap; I read the line and did not run it).

**The gate's fix-shape (not ruled):** use one set, for example `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES`, at both `documents.ts` sites. The regression test the gate proposed: the kept-certification blob gives GET `anchored: false` and POST `/anchor` 202.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, finding 1806-1
* the probe it names, in the same folder: `evidence/probe/_quarantine_2026-10-29/gate15-probe-docs.test.ts` and `evidence/probe/probe_docs.out`

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1200` 0 hits; `documents.ts:1458` 2 hits, read (KS-1709's description lists that line among three other sites with the same missing `else` for a non-ok anchoring response, which is a different defect; KS-772 comments describe the retry route's 400 for the stuck kintsugi document, and there is no ticket for this defect there); `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` 1 hit (KS-1640, chain-first verify blobs: a different surface); "Document is already anchored" 2 hits (KS-1650, the check is not network-bound; KS-282, archived, document versions); "status !== 'anchor_failed'" 3 hits (KS-1628, the deprecated verify route and placeholder hashes; KS-1158; KS-1004, archived); "keep it, but mark" and "kept certification": KS-1709 only. None of these describes this defect.

**Not measured:** I read the lines above at develop `6d41673e0f79` and did not re-run the gate's probe.

**Related:** KS-1709 (the ruling and the change), KS-1124 (where the `failed` blob began), KS-1640.

title: api-gateway falls back to a 60 s window where security defaults to 3,600: a NULL rate_limit_window would enforce a per-hour ceiling per minute
description:
**BLUF: the api-gateway falls back to a 60-second window where the security service defaults to 3,600. A key whose stored** `rate_limit_window` **reads as NULL or 0 would have its per-hour ceiling enforced per MINUTE — 60× more permissive. Measured UNREACHABLE from every tracked writer today, so Low; the residual is that the column is nullable and nothing refuses a NULL.**

## The two fallbacks, at develop `722e07f19cee`

* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:249` — `rateLimitWindow: data.rateLimitWindow || 60,` (building `meta` from the validate response)
* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:67` — `const DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_WINDOW = 60; // seconds`, applied at `:184` as `(user.rateLimitWindow || DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_WINDOW) * 1000`

Against: `services/security/src/index.ts:667` — `rateLimitWindow: z.number().int().min(60).max(86400).default(3600)`.

## How a NULL would get there

* The column is `rate_limit_window INTEGER DEFAULT 3600` (`migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql:561`; re-added the same way by `018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql:75`). **No** `NOT NULL`**.** A DEFAULT applies only when the column is omitted; an explicit NULL is accepted.
* `services/security/src/converters.ts:168` reads it as `Number(r.rate_limit_window)`, and `Number(null)` is `0`. Validate returns that `0`, and both gateway fallbacks treat `0` as "no window".

**The direction matters:** this case is *more permissive*, not stricter. A key with `rate_limit = 3000` and a NULL window would be enforced at 3,000 per **60 s** — 180,000 per hour.

## Measured unreachable today — every tracked writer

| writer | window it writes |
| -- | -- |
| security mint + rotate, the shared `apiKeyInsertStatement` (`security/src/index.ts:418-438`) | the parsed schema value — never absent, default 3600 |
| migration 019, JSONB path and TEXT\[\] path | literal `3600` |
| originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`routes/adminConfig.ts:1031-1048`) | literal `3600` |
| test-only inserts (originate `__tests__`) | omit it, so the column DEFAULT `3600` |

Census method: `git grep -i -E '(insert into|update) +svc_api_keys'` over the whole tree at `722e07f19cee`, excluding Markdown; positive control — it finds the security INSERT I had already read. No `UPDATE` sets `rate_limit_window`.

So the hazard needs a hand-edited row or a future writer that passes NULL. That is why this is Low.

## Not the same thing as the deliberate machine default

`DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_LIMIT = 100` with `DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_WINDOW = 60` is the intended allowance for a machine caller that has **no allowance at all** (the KS-1205 R-2 warning path). That pairing is not the defect. The defect is the **mixed** case — a real per-hour limit paired with a missing window, so the 60 s default meant for "no allowance" silently re-scales someone else's allowance.

## Fix shapes (not chosen)

1. A migration making `rate_limit_window` `NOT NULL`, **after** a census on each box that 0 rows are NULL (it must not be applied blind to a live table).
2. Map NULL to 3,600 in `converters.ts`, so the security service never reports a 0 window.
3. When `rateLimit` is present but the window is missing, use 3,600 in the gateway, not 60, and keep 60 only for the no-allowance path.

Shape 2 is the smallest, but it masks the row instead of refusing it. Shape 1 is the honest one.

Found 2026-10-19 by Seat E 3rd while tracing the KS-1195 store-and-enforce chain for gate X1 (PR #1613). Related: KS-1195.

title: KS-695 follow-up: distinguishing code for a key revoked by erasure (S's ask, KS-695 comment 7221c520)
description:
## BLUF

Platform S asked K for a distinguishing code or status for an API key that was revoked **by erasure**, so S can read that fact instead of inferring it. **This is design work, not a defect, and nothing in the merged change (pull request 1497, squash** `343a7b4e`**) depends on it.** Nobody has decided whether to build it.

## Recommendation

Decide first whether K builds it. If yes, it is a small design: see "What K does today". No action needed for the erasure itself.

## The ask, verbatim

Stuart, ticket KS-695, comment `7221c520-c6fb-4343-aedd-7bffbfdc9b75`, 2026-10-12T23:00:58Z:

> **One ask of K:** a distinguishing code or status for a key revoked *by erasure* — on the POST (for example a 401 whose `error.code` says so) or on the status GET — would let S drop the inference in (2) and read the fact directly. Until then the attempt-count rule is what S will use. Nothing here blocks part ii's gate; S's change is small and I will note on this ticket when it is on develop.

The inference in (2), same comment: *"A 401 'Invalid API key' on this route counts as 'already erased, Confirmed' only when S has already recorded at least one attempt on that organisation's erasure (the row's attempt counter is non-zero)."* S's side of this is PS-1201 (point 4) and platform-s pull request 972 (In Review at 2026-10-13T00:52Z, per the ticket).

## What K does today (read at develop `343a7b4e`, not run)

* The erasure revokes the calling key last: `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false` (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:440`), the same write the security service's rotate makes (`services/security/src/index.ts:186`). Nothing on the row records why the key is inactive.
* A repeat call is refused at the gateway before the originate route runs: a presented `sk_` key that fails `validateApiKey` is answered `401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Invalid API key"}` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:367-368`). That branch has no sub-code, so it cannot say why validation failed.
* The status GET (`GET /api/platform/organizations/erase-connector/:organisationGuid`, `routes/platformOrganizations.ts:152`) has a connector-role guard in originate. I did not trace the gateway mount of that path, so I do not know whether the same revoked key reaches it; if it does not, "a code on the status GET" would need a credential other than the revoked key.
* So any distinguishing code needs (a) a durable marker of the reason at the revoke, written in the erasure transaction, and (b) a gateway change, because the refusal happens at the gateway. Neither exists. A new `error.code` on that 401 is also a client-visible change to a shared door.

## Not covered

No S behaviour was read (K cannot read S's code); everything about S is Stuart's text above. No live check on any box.

## Dedupe (2026-10-13, Seat J 6th)

`searchIssues` with comments and archived included, five terms, 196 distinct issues. Positive control: the term `PlatformKErasureClient` found 4 issues (PS-1201, PS-699, PS-700, PS-701). Zero literal hits in title or description for "revoked by erasure". Near hit: PS-1201, the S-side counterpart, not a duplicate.

Related: KS-695 (the erasure), PS-1201.

title: KS-1598 follow-up (pull request 1548 gate i6): the admin-scope route's `upper(role) = $3` carries the same libc fold as the status guard, and users.role has no CHECK
description:
Filed from the pull request 1548 (KS-1598) Opus gate, report hash `20fb01665917ef45`, verdict `GO WITH NOTE` at 0 Major / 1 Minor / 6 Info. This is the gate's **i6**, recorded as PRE-EXISTING and deliberately NOT touched by KS-1598 round 1, so that the `COLLATE "C"` decision is taken for both folds or for neither rather than half-applied by accident.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` — the target query of `PUT /api/keys/admin-scopes/:userId`:

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM users
 WHERE id = $1::uuid AND tenant_id = $2::uuid
   AND upper(role) = $3
   AND lower(status COLLATE "C") = 'active'
 LIMIT 1
```

The status half now folds under `COLLATE "C"` (KS-1598 round 1). The role half beside it still folds under the database's default libc collation.

## Measured, on my own PostgreSQL 15.14 under en_AU.UTF-8, with controls

| stored `role` | `upper(role) = 'ADMIN'` (default) | `upper(role COLLATE "C") = 'ADMIN'` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `ADMIN`, `admin`, `Admin` | true | true |
| `admın` (U+0131 DOTLESS I), `ADMıN` | **true** | **false** |
| `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` | false | false |

* Codepoint verified: `ascii(substr(...))` = **305** = 0x131, so these are not ASCII rows in disguise.
* The gate measured the same under `en_US.UTF-8`, so this is not one locale's quirk.
* `users.role` **has NO CHECK constraint.** Probe: `pg_constraint` for `users` with a definition matching `%role%` returns **(none)**. Control, with the same probe: a definition matching `%status%` returns `users_status_vocabulary`, so the probe is not blind. That is the difference from the status column, whose vocabulary is bounded at migration `046:60` — **nothing bounds the spelling of** `role` **at the database level.**

## Why it is Info and not a defect to hotfix

* Reaching it needs a direct database write. Code read: the application's writers put literal role strings in. No route accepts an arbitrary `role` string for this column.
* It was **not** measured at the route. The gate measured the SQL predicate in isolation.
* It is pre-existing: KS-1598 introduced neither half.

## The decision this ticket asks for

Either apply `upper(role COLLATE "C")` beside the status fold, or state why the two columns are treated differently. The second is defensible — `status` is bounded by a CHECK and `role` is not — but it should be written down rather than left as an accident of which finding came first.

Minimal change if it is taken: `AND upper(role COLLATE "C") = $3`, plus one cell per fold (a U+0131 role spelling must be 404) in `ks1570b-admin-scope-route.integration.test.ts`, which already carries the equivalent U+0130 cells for `status`.

## How this differs from KS-1591 — they are NOT the same finding

**KS-1591** is `String(role).toUpperCase()` in **JavaScript**, in `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts` (`isPlatformRole`), judging the **caller's claimed** role out of a token, and it admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array as `SUPER_ADMIN`.

**This ticket** is `upper(role)` in **SQL**, against the **stored target row's** role, under the database's collation. Different site, different language's fold, different principal, different threat. Both should fold explicitly, and neither fix reaches the other.

## Provenance

Fresh-nonce negative control `v9b-bf367a4ef9ff` → 0 hits; positive control `admin_organisation_scopes` → 1. title: Security (nit): decideMint's toUpperCase admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as a key admin; plus the role-comparison sweep
description:
**BLUF:** `decideMint` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:96-97`, the `POST /api/keys` admission test) still compares `String(caller?.role ?? '').toUpperCase()` against the key-admin set, so a role spelled with U+0131 (dotless i) or U+017F (long s), or an array role, can be read as an admin role. KS-1591 fixed the same shape in `isPlatformRole` and `requireKeyAdmin` and deliberately left this site; this ticket tracks it, and the sweep of other role comparisons that KS-1591's description asks for, so that KS-1591 can close. Reachability is not established.

## Where

`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` at develop `5dccdcb29ec20393e80cbdb1e359a49caa633165` (the build on both boxes), read with `git show`:

* line 96: `const role = String(caller?.role ?? '');`
* line 97: `if (KEY_ADMIN_ROLES.has(role.toUpperCase())) {`

## What is measured and what is not

* Measured by the tier-2 gate on 2026-10-28 (the batch covering PRs 1775, 1776 and 1780, GO WITH NOTES): `decideMint` admits a role spelled with U+0131 or U+017F, and an array role, at PR 1776's head `8b92887a6fac`. The gate's note was filed on KS-1591 as a comment (`42e97e12`).
* Read by me, not run: lines 96 and 97 are unchanged at the deployed build. I ran no test of `decideMint` with those roles.
* Not established: whether any issuer, user-management path or seed can store or sign a token with such a role. That needs a token the auth service signs. KS-1591 said the same. Until someone measures it this is a nit; if any path can, it is a privilege escalation (admission to mint API keys) and should be re-rated at once.

## Recommendation

Not built. Apply the KS-1591 remedy here: fold ASCII letters only (`replace(/[a-z]/g, ...)`, as `isPlatformRole` now does) and refuse a role that is not a string, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it. Cells: a dotless-i spelling, a long-s spelling and an array role each refused by `decideMint`; a control that every ASCII spelling admitted today is still admitted.

## Sweep candidates (not findings)

Method: `git grep -n -I "toUpperCase()"` at `5dccdcb29ec2` over `Blockchain/Dev/services` and `Blockchain/Dev/packages`, tests, `dist` and `node_modules` excluded, keeping lines that also contain "role" (case-insensitive). 14 lines. Controls: the `decideMint` line is in the result (1 line from `provisioningPolicy.ts`); a nonsense token over the same paths matches 0 files. Of the 14: 2 are comments, 2 are the sites KS-1591 fixed (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:144`, `security/src/index.ts:1104`), 1 is `decideMint`, and 9 are other candidates:

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:85` and `:102` (`ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, `SCOPED_ADMIN_ROLES`; the same file KS-1591 changed at `:144`)
* `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:288`
* `services/auth/src/routes/issuerCerts.ts:71`
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:285` and `:377`
* `services/auth/src/services/password.ts:234` (whether it is a role comparison is unread)
* `services/originate/src/middleware/rbac.ts:56` and `:58`

I read none of these beyond the matching line. The census misses a comparison split across lines or through another variable name. KS-1601 tracks the SQL counterpart (`upper(role) = $3` in the admin-scope route).

## Board search (before filing)

Issues filter with `includeArchived: true`, title or description (comments excluded), read 2026-10-29: tickets whose title contains `decideMint`: 0. Tickets naming `decideMint` together with "dotless", "0131" or "017F": 0. Controls: `isPlatformRole` finds 7 tickets (KS-1701, KS-1601, KS-1591, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-976, KS-743); a random nonsense token finds 0. The only place the gap is recorded is the gate's note on KS-1591 (a comment, which this search excludes). Tickets that mention `decideMint` for other reasons, none with this fold as its subject: KS-1594, KS-1584, KS-1570, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-1533, KS-742 and KS-486.

title: m365-integration: three more reflection sites from gate AM1 - an unencoded connectionId in the success redirect, and two uncapped error texts in JSON bodies
description:
**BLUF:** Gate AM1, reviewing #1622 (KS-1641 finding 2), found **three more places in** `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` **that put text the service does not control into a response.** None is the crash #1622 fixes. One is an **unencoded** value in a redirect; two are **uncapped** error texts in JSON bodies, one of them an internal error message in a 500. All three need a valid session or a server-issued id to reach, so none is reachable by an anonymous request today.

Filed as one ticket because AM1 found them in one review pass. Measured by Seat R 55th at develop `115797747cb60009e781d80e9059dbbed69e1ac3`, file blob `1d9ea9df234832ceb8d04de116be10ee3bf421d3`. **Line numbers are develop's.** #1622 inserts 52 lines above them, so on that branch each is +52.

## The three sites

**1.** `:508` **—** `connectionId` **goes into the success redirect unencoded (AM1 N4).**

```ts
res.redirect(`…/admin/integrations?m365=success&connectionId=${connectionId}&tenant=${encodeURIComponent(connection.tenantName || '')}`);
```

`tenant` in the same template **is** encoded and `connectionId` is not. `connectionId` is `String(state)`, and it only reaches this line after `memConnections.get(connectionId)` hits. So it has to equal an id the server issued, and **it is not exploitable today.** It is fragile: if the id format ever admits `&`, `#` or `%`, the redirect's query changes shape. Fix: `encodeURIComponent(connectionId)`, the same as its neighbour.

**2.** `:742` **— an internal error message in a 500 body, with no guard at the site (AM1 N5).**

```ts
res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'Token refresh failed', details: err?.message } });
```

This is the **KS-1410 class** (thrown text in a 500 body), but in a file KS-1410 does not cover. m365 reads `NODE_ENV` 5 times, **all at** `:1536` **or later** (the PII-key fatal-start block). There are **zero** `NODE_ENV` reads before `:742`, so nothing guards this site. The route is authenticated.

**3.** `:1026` **— Graph's own error text, passed back uncapped (AM1 N5).**

```ts
return res.status(resp.status).json({ error: (err as any).error?.message || 'OneDrive API error' });
```

This is **provider** text, not an internal error: it is the same kind of thing as the OAuth `error_description` KS-1641 capped. It is authenticated, uncapped, and it forwards Graph's status code unchanged.

## Why the third one matters beyond itself

The callback's `:515` already reflects MSAL's `err.message` into a redirect: encoded, uncapped, and reachable only with a valid `state`. KS-1641 calls that **a decision, not a cap**: bound the internal message, or map it to a code and keep the detail server-side. `:742` and `:1026` are the same decision in JSON bodies, so they should be decided together with `:515`, not capped one at a time.

## Neighbours read before filing

The search's negative control (`xkqvzzpholmdrf`) returned **0** hits, so the search does discriminate.

* **KS-1410** (In Progress): same class as site 2, but it lists **six files** by name, and m365 is not one of them.
* **KS-730** (Done): lists five files, with **0** m365 mentions.
* **KS-840**: about auth's own OAuth error envelope, not m365.
* **KS-1641**: owns `:465` (the cap, #1622) and the `:515` decision. These three are AM1's notes on that PR, carved out by Wednesday's ruling so they would not widen it.

## How to fix

Site 1 is a one-line change and can ship on its own. Sites 2 and 3 should wait for the `:515` decision on KS-1641, so that one rule covers all three.

Each fix needs a cell that sends **non-ASCII text across the boundary**. KS-1641's round 1 shipped a crash because every cell was ASCII; gate AM1's B1 is that crash.

title: m365 ks1670 source-text pin: a raw connectionId by concatenation survives (gate 7 N6)
description:
**BLUF:** the source-text pin that PR 1791 added for KS-1670 (`ks1670-the-success-redirect-encodes-the-connection-id.test.ts`) has blind spots that gate 7 found with mutants N3, N4 and N6 (finding 1791-1, Low, a disclosed test gap). It is not a defect in the product line. Low. Related to KS-1670. I read the file at develop and did not re-run the gate's mutants.

**What the pin is, read at develop** `5dccdcb29ec2`**:** it reads `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` as text and boots nothing. Its needle is the string `connectionId=${` (line 10 of the test). R1 (line 32) requires every interpolation that follows that needle to be wrapped in `encodeURIComponent`. R2 (line 37) requires the exact success-redirect text `m365=success&connectionId=${encodeURIComponent(connectionId)}&tenant=${encodeURIComponent(connection.tenantName`. C1 (line 41) requires that the instrument finds exactly one such interpolation.

**The gaps, from gate 7 (tested there by mutants):**

1. N6: a raw id added by string concatenation survives. R1's needle sees only template interpolations, so a redirect built by concatenation is invisible to it by construction (the needle is the literal `connectionId=${`).
2. N4: a wrapped-then-unwrapped expression passes R1; only R2's exact text catches it, and only on the success line.
3. N3: an equivalent rewrite of the success line (same behaviour, different text) turns R2 red for no behavioural reason.
   The gate's own HTTP probe showed the behaviour the pin cannot, and it suggested lifting its cells A1, A3 and A7 into the PR as wire cells.

**What has changed since:** PR 1791 merged with an added behaviour cell, `ks1670-the-success-redirect-keeps-a-hostile-connection-id-intact.test.ts`, added on gate 7's note (it also answers the gate's finding 1791-2, the missing non-ASCII cell). Seat R 6th measured it on the PR: three of its six cells were red against the pin, and it kills the raw, `encodeURI` and double-encode mutants; N3 remains. I did not re-run that. Gate 7's finding 1791-3 (a lone surrogate makes `encodeURIComponent` throw; unreachable because ids are `conn_` plus a uuid) is not part of this ticket.

**So what is left:** the pin can still go red for an equivalent rewrite (N3), and a redirect added elsewhere by concatenation is outside R1. Whether that is worth a change, or the behaviour cell is enough and this can be closed with a note, is a decision for whoever picks it up.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** make R2 assert the behaviour (the encoded id reaches the wire) instead of the exact text; or lift the gate's A1, A3 and A7 as wire cells; or close it with a note that the behaviour cell is the real guard.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 22:3xZ): `ks1670` 0 hits; `source-text pin` 5 hits, read by title (KS-1670 itself, and KS 1602, KS 1521, KS 1328, KS 1187, which are other tests' pins); KS-1670's own text says only that the test "is a source-text pin … proves the text of the template, not the redirect on the wire" and does not name these mutants (`concatenat` 0 matches, `blind` 0); `connectionId=` 3 hits (KS-1670, KS 1641 Done, KS 423 Done), none is this. The positive control `parseScopeString` found 4; a nonsense token generated at run time found 0 and was not recorded in this ticket.

title: OAuth /authorize: a repeated state or code_challenge answers 500, and POST accepts arrays
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/oauth/authorize` answers **500** `server_error` when `state` or `code_challenge` arrives as a repeated query parameter, the same class as the `scope` crash KS-1219 fixes. On POST, JSON arrays for the same two fields do not crash: an array `state` is coerced to a comma-joined string and echoed in the redirect, and an array `code_challenge` reaches `createAuthorizationCode` as an array. Low. Related to KS-1219, whose own recommendation ("by the same shape, any other non-string authorize parameter") PR 1797 closes for `scope` only. Raised on the tier-1 gate's note 1797-2 (gate 9, 2026-10-28), then measured here; the gate's wording ("repeated `state` / `code_challenge` still 500") holds for GET only.

Every figure below is from a loopback listener driving the real router with its collaborators mocked (the same harness as the ks1219 test), on PR 1797's branch with develop `92a02a356139` merged in. `oauth.ts` is blob `91aa664ac910`, which develop did not change; the lines involved are not touched by PR 1797. Nothing was run against a live box.

**Measured, GET** (client `client-1`, a confidential app, otherwise valid request):

1. `&state=xyz&state=second` answers **500** `server_error`; a single `state=xyz` answers 200 and serves the consent page.
2. `&code_challenge=aaa&code_challenge=bbb` answers **500** `server_error`; a single `code_challenge=aaa` answers 200.
3. `&code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge_method=plain` answers 400 `invalid_request`. It is already refused, but by accident: the check at lines 361 to 367 is `PKCE_METHODS.has(codeChallengeMethod)`, which is false for an array.
4. `&scope=openid&scope=profile` answers 400 `invalid_request` (the KS-1219 fix, as the control).

**Cause, read from the file:** `generateConsentPage` calls `escapeHtml(params.state)` and `escapeHtml(params.codeChallenge || '')` (lines 1522 and 1523), and `escapeHtml(s: string)` is `s.replace(...)` (lines 1582 to 1584). An array has no `replace`, so the call throws and the handler's catch answers 500. The `as Record<string, string>` cast on `req.query` (line 492) does nothing at run time.

**Measured, POST with JSON arrays** (none of these is a 500):

1. `action: deny` with `state: ["a","b"]` answers 302 to `...?error=access_denied&state=a%2Cb`. The client's `state` comes back altered.
2. `action: approve` with `state: ["a","b"]` mints a code and answers 302 to `...?code=...&state=a%2Cb`.
3. `action: approve` with `code_challenge: ["x","y"]` answers 302, and `createAuthorizationCode` was called with `codeChallenge` equal to the array `["x","y"]` (`Array.isArray` true). **Not measured:** what the real pg driver and the column do with it, because the repository is mocked. It may store text, or it may fail.

**Scope is neither deduplicated nor bounded** (the gate's note 1797-3, pre-existing, measured here for a string scope, repository mocked): `openid openid profile openid` is stored as sent, 28 characters with the repeats; `openid,profile` is stored as `openid profile`; a 14,000-character scope made of one repeated token is stored as a 13,999-character string. Real column limits not measured.

**Not probed:** the other authorize parameters as arrays (`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type`, `email`, `password`, `action`, `mfaCode`).

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** one check ahead of the resolver on both GET and POST that every authorize parameter is a string or absent, answering 400 `invalid_request` (the existing message, so no published message changes), as KS-1219's recommendation already describes; or per-field guards in the two handlers. A decision for whoever takes it: whether POST should refuse an array `state` or coerce it, and whether `scope` should be deduplicated and capped.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 21:2xZ): `repeated state` 0 hits, `repeated code_challenge` 0, `?state=` 0; `escapeHtml` 5 hits, read by title (KS 841, KS 799 and KS 798 are the consent page posting its own form, KS 488 a review stream, KS 163 a connector XSS), none is this; `code_challenge` 13 hits, read by title (PKCE, token-exchange and consent-page work, mostly Done, plus KS 836 and KS 782 in Backlog and KS 1677, the m365 callback), none is this; `array-valued` 5 hits (KS-1219 itself; KS 1671, the same species in the m365 callback, a different service; KS 839; KS 677; KS 256). The positive control `parseScopeString` found 3 (KS 1220, KS-1219, KS 839); a nonsense token generated at run time found 0 and was not recorded in this ticket.

title: KS-968 follow-ups: the integration suite's loopback guard can be bypassed by ?host=, an untested rethrow, and four smaller gaps
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on #1485 (KS-968, Opus, GO WITH NOTE, no Major). The first is a safety property of a suite that TRUNCATES `users`: its guard against reaching a non-loopback database can be bypassed. The rest are small.

## Recommendation

One small PR: fix the guard (validate the parsed connection config, or reject any query string), pin the rethrow, move the two lookups inside the named try, and either type-check the integration file or add it to `tsconfig.test.json`'s include. Wiring the suite into any gate is the same open question as KS-1487.

## Detail (line numbers at `ebdb123d5`; they drift)

1. **Loopback guard bypass** (`services/auth/integration/ks968-platform-admin-seed-with-both-rows.integration.ts` lines 29-36): the guard checks `new URL(RAW).hostname`, but `pg-connection-string` lets `?host=` and `&port=` override it. The gate measured both: a URL with host `127.0.0.1:1` plus `?host=<socket>&port=56488` ran 6/6 against another target, and `?host=192.0.2.1` dialled that address. The suite truncates `users` and `pii_subject_keys`, so it must never be able to reach a non-loopback database.
2. **The rethrow is untested** (`userRepo.ts:1654`, `throw remediationErr`): a mutant where the catch no longer rethrows (m5) passes the integration (6/6) and unit (31/31) suites while logging the false "SUSPENDED" warn.
3. **Not every failed remediation gets the new error line:** the `getUserById` / `getUserByEmail` lookups at `userRepo.ts:1589-1590` sit outside the named try, so a database fault there logs only the generic "Failed to seed demo user".
4. **The integration file has 4 tsc errors** (lines 114, 147, 163) under `tsconfig.test.json`; nothing type-checks it and nothing runs it automatically (it is outside `src/`, so the KS-1000 ratchet does not see it).
5. **"Otherwise unchanged" is not exact for a legacy plaintext email row:** when the email row has no lookup hash, develop suspended BOTH rows (no collision happened); head leaves the id row ACTIVE.
6. **Pre-existing, noted:** a whitespace `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is seeded as a real password; two legacy plaintext duplicates of the address suspend only one (`LIMIT 1`); the H5 rewrite (`:1706`) and `createUser` (`:1758`) also swallow 23505 but only a race reaches them.

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1485, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1485/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `cb7d6fa23d5bdb5b`), Minor 1 to 5 and the pre-existing notes; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-968, KS-966, KS-1487, KS-1000.

title: MAJOR: when both platform-admin rows exist the id-row rewrite throws 23505, the seed loop swallows it, and the KS-966 F3 email arm never runs — with a green cell standing over the hole
description:
**MAJOR. When both rows exist, the platform-admin remediation throws 23505, the loop swallows it, and the email-keyed arm — the whole KS-966 F3 fix — NEVER RUNS. A green cell stands over the hole.**

**"Both rows present" is not an exotic state. It is the state Kam's own row is in**: `…0020` holding one address, and a distinct row holding `admin@secuura.com`.

Found by the #888 round-2 tier-1 gate. **Pre-existing — reproduced identically against round 1's** `userRepo.ts`**, so it is not introduced by round 2 and is equally open on** `develop` **today** (merged at `9e9a88709`).

### The mechanism — and my published one was WRONG

I argued in #888 and on KS-966 that the collision came from **rewriting the address onto the row found BY that address**. That is wrong, and it matters: **writing the same address back onto the row that already holds it cannot collide with itself.**

The collision is on the **other** side:

1. `if (byId)` (`userRepo.ts:1363`) rewrites the `…0020` row's `email_lookup_hash` to the hash of `admin@secuura.com`.
2. If a **distinct** row already holds that hash, that write violates `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` → **23505**.
3. The seed loop's `catch` (`userRepo.ts:~1506`) turns it into `logger.error('Failed to seed demo user', …)` and `continue`s — **no rethrow**.
4. `if (emailRowIsDistinct)` sits at `:1388`, *after* the throwing statement. **It never executes.**

**So I located the hazard on the wrong row, then declined a rewrite that was harmless and left standing the rewrite that actually detonates.** The gate accepted my *conclusion* (the email row should get credential-neutralisation only) and rejected my *reasoning* — and the wrong reasoning is why the hole is still open.

**The arm itself is correct and merely unreachable:** the gate neutered only the id-row guard and the email arm fired perfectly — suspended, sentinel hash, verify FALSE.

**Verified independently on** `origin/develop` **before filing:** `byId` at `:1363` precedes `emailRowIsDistinct` at `:1388`; the id-row UPDATE writes `email_lookup_hash = $3`; the loop catch logs and continues without rethrowing. And `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` **exists and is UNIQUE on the deployed demo database** (measured read-only 2026-09-07, with controls: `users` 33 columns, `uuid_generate_v4` present).

---

## ITEM 1 — the misleading green cell. Fix this first.

`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks952…`/`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`:

```
it('remediates BOTH when both exist, and the id row still gets the full identity rewrite')
```

**It passes, and it is asserting that a live hole is closed, on a credential surface.** It passes because the vitest `db` double answers `{rows: []}` to every UPDATE and **cannot enforce a unique index** — so the 23505 never happens in the test and the swallow never happens either.

The tester's words: *"the one thing here I would fix before the deploy rather than after."* It could not go into #888 because what merges must be what was gated, so it is the first item here.

**A mocked** `query` **cannot express this defect at all.** The regression test must drive the same both-exist scenario against a **real Postgres carrying** `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. That is the important half of this ticket — more than the fix.

## ITEM 2 — the fix, three shapes offered by the gate

* **Order the two remediations email-row-first**, so the credential neutralisation lands before the statement that can throw; **or**
* make the id-row rewrite **conditional on** `!emailRowIsDistinct`; **or**
* **wrap both in one transaction**, so the credential neutralisation is not lost to the identity rewrite's failure.

Whichever is chosen, **the swallowing catch is part of the defect**: a remediation whose failure is indistinguishable from success at `logger.error` level is the same class as KS-962, where the seed failure logs at `debug` and is invisible.

## ITEM 3 — do NOT probe the demo

**Likelihood on the demo is UNKNOWN.** The gate had no authorisation to contact the box and did not. **That probe is Kam's to authorise and he has not.** Do not go and look.

---

**Related:** KS-966 (#888, where the F3 arm shipped — my incorrect mechanism is corrected in a comment there) · KS-949 (the identity half) · KS-962 (the sibling swallow, at `debug`) · KS-963 (the PII cutoff).
