*Filed by s146 after the #888 merge, from the round-2 gate verdict. The mechanism above is the gate's; the develop-side verification and the deployed-index measurement are mine.*

title: e2e gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts 15.2.5 PATCHes a DSR with status 'processed', a value DSR_STATUSES does not contain — the cell 400s at every SHA and cannot pass (QA-962 O-2)
description:
## BLUF

The e2e cell `15.2.5 Process DSR — admin marks DSR as processed via API` (`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts:425-488`) creates a DSR, then PATCHes `${dsrPath}/${dsrId}` with `status: 'processed'` (line 464), and on a 4xx retries with PUT carrying the same body (line 475). The route's body schema is `status: z.enum(DSR_STATUSES)` with `DSR_STATUSES = ['pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'denied', 'extended']` (`services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:80, :89`). `'processed'` is not in the enum, so the PATCH answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR before any id or lookup logic runs, at base and at head alike (the tier-2 gate on PR #962 measured it; it is pre-existing and not #962's). The PUT fallback has no route. A test that cannot pass is a defect in the suite: it reports the product as failing to process a DSR when the product refused a status the test invented.

## Recommendation

One change in the spec file, proven by one run of the cell against a local stack:

1. send a value the enum accepts — `'processing'` for the mark-in-progress step, or `'completed'` for the terminal step (`TERMINAL_DSR_STATUSES` in `gdprService.ts:1077`) — and assert the 200 `{success:true, message:'DSR updated'}` the route returns for a real id;
2. drop the PUT fallback (no PUT route exists; the fallback only doubles the failure);
3. optionally add one negative cell asserting that `'processed'` answers 400, so the vocabulary is pinned from the e2e side too.

Keep `failOnStatusCode: false` and the NOT-IMPLEMENTED guards as they are.

## Detail

* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1029-962-ac6f4fa91-tier2-r1-relaunch-20260913b/report.md`, Observations O-2 and §3 (callers that PATCH `/dsr/:dsrId`). Recorded in the verdict comments on PR #962 and KS-1029 as "not filed by this round"; filed now on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER s196, 2026-09-12T23:44:51Z).
* **Related:** KS-1112 (the PATCH 200-vs-404 split on the same route), KS-1029 (the malformed-id guard, PR #962, Done + archived).
* **Dedupe, before filing:** a literal census over 1,101 KS issues (684 archived) and their comments on non-archived issues — `'processed'` 0 hits, `gdpr-compliance.prelaunch` 0 hits. Controls: `UUID_PATTERN` → KS-1029 (1); a nonsense token → 0.

title: change-password publishes no 422: a weak new password is documented under 400 while the route answers 422
description:
**BLUF:** the published contract for `POST /api/users/me/change-password` lists **no 422** and documents a too-weak new password under **400** ("Wrong current password or new password too weak"), while the route answers **422** for a weak password. This is a pre-existing contract gap, found by the tier-1 gate on the KS-1467 services/auth change (finding 1799-7); KS-1467 was ruled to change no OpenAPI, so it did not touch it. Low. Related to KS-1467.

**What I read, at develop** `802eb2b8ecaf`**:**

1. `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, operation `/api/users/me/change-password`, response codes: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 502, 503. There is no 422. The 400 description reads "Wrong current password or new password too weak".
2. The source of that text is `services/auth/src/auth.openapi.ts` line 1012: `400: { ...commonErrorResponses[400], description: 'Wrong current password or new password too weak' }`, and that operation's `responses` has no 422 entry.
3. The two sibling routes do publish it: reset-password has `422: ... 'New password too weak'` (a comment at `auth.openapi.ts` line 813 cites KS 255), and register has a 422 described "Weak password, or client-supplied `role` field (not permitted)".
4. The route throws `new ValidationError('New password is too weak', ...)` (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`, around line 993 at the pin), and `ValidationError` answers 422. The route-level cell for change-password in the KS-1467 PR drives the real route and reads status 422 for weak candidates.

**Not claimed:** I ran no schema-conformance tool against the yaml for this; the gate measured it on the wire (finding 1799-7). A wrong *current* password is a 400 and stays one.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** add `422: { ...commonErrorResponses[422], description: 'New password too weak' }` to the change-password operation and take "or new password too weak" out of the 400 text, then regenerate the yaml (`generate-openapi`, `check:openapi`). That changes the published contract, so it wants its own ruling; the KS-1467 ruling was no OpenAPI change. Since KS-1467 round 2 the 422 `details` is the published ZodIssue-compatible array, so documenting the 422 matches what the route sends.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 15:5xZ): `new password too weak` 0 hits; `publishes no 422` 0; `no 422` with `change-password` 0; `change-password` with `422` 7 hits (KS-1467, KS-1005, KS-732, KS-501, KS-486, KS-485, KS-480), read: none records this gap; `too weak` with `yaml` 2 hits (KS 255, KS 141), neither covers change-password; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6c` 0 hits; the positive control (title `AppError resets`) found KS-1467.

title: versionedById is caller-controlled but is now an erasure selector: reserve it as a server-set key on create, /version, /sign-cert and /sign-wallet
description:
## BLUF

`metadata.versionedById` is meant to be set by the server (`user.id`), but any writer can set it, and KS-695 part (ii) now uses it to decide which documents an organisation's erasure irreversibly blanks. Reserve it as a server-set key.

## Recommendation

Strip `versionedById` from caller-supplied `data` on create, and make the three version paths ignore a caller's value, so it can only come from `user.id`. Review the neighbouring keys that share the same spread (`versionAction`, `versionedAt`, `parentDocumentId`) in the same change.

## Detail (read by me in the tree at develop `8d34fbf0890a`, 2026-10-12)

* **Create:** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:600` builds `data` as `{ ...rawData, ... }` from the request. `stripReservedMetadataKeys` (`repositories/documentRepo.ts:158`) removes only `blockchain`, `signatures` and `walletAddress`, so a caller-supplied `versionedById` is stored as metadata.
* **/version, /sign-cert, /sign-wallet:** `documents.ts:2106`, `:2840` and `:3034` set `versionedById: user.id` and then spread the caller's `...metadata` AFTER it, so the caller's value wins.
* **Why it matters now:** the Opus gate on PR #1497 reproduced it through the real create route and the real erase route as `secuura_app`: organisation A's connector created a document with `data.versionedById = "connector:platform-s:<B's GUID>"` (201), B's erase answered `completed`, and A's title read `[erased]` (irreversible). Gate verdict: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1497/verdict.md`, finding M1. PR #1497 bounds the selector by the issuer, which stops that outcome, but that is a seatbelt on one consumer; this ticket is the root.
* The connector id is `platform-s:<Organisation GUID>`, which is the externalRef, so it is knowable.

## Done when

- [ ] A caller-supplied `versionedById` is not stored by create and is overridden by `user.id` on the three version paths; one red-first cell per route (four routes, four claims).
- [ ] Platform S does not rely on sending it (confirm with Stuart; a round-trip of a K document's `data` into a new create must not carry it).
- [ ] Measured: how many existing documents carry a `versionedById` that is not the creating connector's (a read-only count), and a recorded decision on them.

## Sequencing (Wednesday's ruling, 2026-10-12, after the second Opus gate on #1497)

**This ticket must LAND BEFORE KS-695 DEPLOYS.** With PR #1497's selector bounded by the issuer, a NULL-issuer document can still be claimed for another organisation by any writer through `versionedById` (a create without `organizationUuid`, or any `/version`, whose metadata is spread after `versionedById` and whose source has no organisation check), so the erasure's reach is only as trustworthy as this field. The gate's evidence: A's `/version` of A's own document with `metadata.versionedById` = B's connector is blanked by B's erasure and is not reached by A's.

## Not claimed

That any caller has done this. Exploiting it needs organisation A's own writer to plant B's id (a bug in a round-trip, or on purpose); B cannot do it alone. Raised by the Opus gate on #1497; filed by Seat J 3rd on Wednesday's instruction.

title: Approving a stale PENDING verification request after the subject's level rose answers 200 and stores the lower level
description:
## BLUF

**Approving a stale PENDING BASIC→ENHANCED verification request after the subject's level has already risen to HIGH answers 200 APPROVED and stores** `enhanced`**: a downgrade.**

* Submit refuses a target at or below the current level, but review re-checks nothing.
* Minor. Pre-existing: the same on develop, #1032 round 1 and #1032 round 2.
* PROBED on a stub. A real Postgres would do the same, since the level UPDATE has no level guard (read).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (N-2).

## Recommendation

Not built here.

* At review, re-check the level ordering against the subject's current level, and refuse (400) or auto-close the request. Alternatively, make the level UPDATE conditional on the stored level being below the target.
* **Regression cell:** a subject at HIGH with a PENDING ENHANCED request → approve does not lower the level.

## Detail

* **Submit's check** (read at develop `34cdcfb26`): `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:1252-1254` compares `LEVEL_ORDER` indexes for the current and target levels.
* **Review:** the approve writes the target level through `updateUser` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:796`) with no comparison.
* **The gate's row Q-SIBLING-LEVEL-ABOVE-TARGET-UPD-OK** (a PENDING BASIC→ENHANCED request, the subject now HIGH, a healthy database): head, round 1 and develop all answer 200 APPROVED and store `enhanced`.
* **Unmeasured:** how the level rose between submit and review (an admin PATCH, another approve), and whether that ordering is reachable concurrently.
* **Related:** KS-1194.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `downgrade`: 56, none about verification levels (Platform S pricing tiers and dependency or database version pins).
  * `stale PENDING`: 2 (KS-584, KS-590: verify by hash).
  * `LEVEL_ORDER`: 3 (KS-1176, KS-1190, PS-519: the gateway's level checks, not review).
  * `verification_level`: 9, none about review.
  * `already at or above`: 0.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §6 and N-2: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: KS-1236 follow-ups: the approve level check and write are not atomic, and the local level order duplicates the shared one
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on #1457 (KS-1236, head `13d3bf195`, merging 2026-10-12). Both are minor and neither blocks it. Item 1 closes a milliseconds-wide race; item 2 removes a duplicated list and a wrong comment.

## Recommendation

Do 2 as a comment-and-import fix. Do 1 only if the race matters: it needs a conditional UPDATE in the repo layer. Item 3 is an observation for a ruling.

## Detail

1. **Not atomic:** the approve pre-check (`users.ts`, the KS-1236 block) reads the subject's level and the write (`userRepo.updateUserPlatformScope`) is a separate statement. A raise that lands between them can still be lowered. Close it with a conditional UPDATE (`... WHERE verification_level < target`).
2. **Duplicate order:** the module-level `LEVEL_ORDER` that #1457 hoists omits `NONE` and `SOCIAL`, and its comment says they "cannot be compared". The canonical order is `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER` in `packages/shared/src/verification/policy-engine.ts` (`NONE < BASIC < SOCIAL < STANDARD < ...`). The outcome is safe today because the zod schema limits targets to STANDARD and above, which rank above both. Replace the local list with the shared one and fix the comment.
3. **Observation:** a refused stale request stays PENDING until a reviewer rejects it, and submit refuses any new request from that subject ("already pending") meanwhile. Consider an auto-close or a hint in the 400.

Provenance: independent Opus gate, 2026-10-12, minor findings 4, 5 and 6; found by Seat V 3rd while merging. Related: KS-1236, KS-1194, KS-1050.

title: Security: an allowedScopes of ['*'] bypasses the invalid_scope refusal entirely — validateScopes returns the request unfiltered
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

`validateScopes` (`services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:352`) begins:

```
if (allowed.includes('*')) return requested; // Wildcard - all scopes
```

So for an app whose `allowedScopes` contains `'*'`, the requested set is returned **unfiltered**. KS-822's RULE 5 refuses a request only when the filter removes everything (`grantedScopes.length === 0`), and with a wildcard the filter removes nothing — so `scope=admin:everything` on a wildcard app is **granted**, 302, and stored on the code.

Pre-existing: the wildcard branch predates KS-822 and RULE 5 did not introduce it. **Nothing drives it** — no case in the suite registers an app with `'*'`.

⚠ **Priority is UNMEASURED and deliberately not asserted.** Whether any registered OAuth app actually carries `'*'` in `allowed_scopes` is a question for a live environment, and this analysis did not look at one. It is not in the repo. So the mechanism is certain and the exposure is unknown — do not read the priority as sourced from reach.

**Done when:** a case registers a wildcard app and pins whatever behaviour is then ruled correct; and the wildcard's meaning is stated in the published contract, which today says nothing about it.

title: KS-1006 follow-ups: two inaccurate statements in the merged change, and the passwordless no-secret MFA state
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on merged #1456 (KS-1006, squash `44afaf482`): two statements in the change are inaccurate, and one gap is real. Items 1 and 2 are comment-only; item 3 needs a ruling.

## Recommendation

Fix 1 and 2 in one small PR. Rule on 3 before building anything: default is leave it (the account state is not produced by normal enrolment).

## Detail

1. `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`**, the KS-1006 comment in** `POST /me/mfa/disable`**:** it says an account with no stored secret "can still disable through POST /api/auth/mfa/disable (password or backup code)". That overclaims. A passwordless (wallet or social) account with `mfa_enabled`, no secret and no backup codes can use neither route; the `routes/mfa.ts` else-branch needs a valid TOTP or backup code.
2. `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1006-mfa-disable-refuses-when-no-secret-is-stored.test.ts` **header:** it calls the base "a latent shape, not a live bypass". That understates it. `decryptMfaSecret` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:172-189`) returns `undefined` when the DEK is missing or destroyed, or when decryption fails, so on the base a decrypt fault let any six-character string disable MFA.
3. **Gap:** such an account (MFA on, secret unreadable, no backup codes, no password) now has no way to turn MFA off. Options: admin-assisted reset, a re-enrol path, or leave.

Provenance: independent Opus gate on #1456 and #1457, 2026-10-12, minor findings 1 and 2; found by Seat V 3rd while merging. Related: KS-1006, KS-732, KS-938.

title: POST /api/users/me/mfa/disable skips code verification when mfaSecret is falsy — the second door
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/users/me/mfa/disable` (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:1064`) **skips verification when**
`mfaSecret` **is falsy** — the same "guarded on presence rather than on proof" shape KS-732 removes from
the sibling door at `POST /api/auth/mfa/disable`.

Raised by @PeterObeden as note 4 on PR #872, rated Low and explicitly offered as a separate ticket
rather than scope creep. Confirmed by reading.

## The shape

```
const { code } = req.body;
const user = await userRepo.getUserById(req.user!.userId);
if (!user.mfaEnabled) throw new BadRequestError('MFA is not enabled');
if (!code || typeof code !== 'string' || code.length !== 6) throw new BadRequestError(...);

if (user.mfaSecret && !verifyTOTP(user.mfaSecret, code)) {   // ← presence-guarded
  throw new BadRequestError('Invalid verification code');
}
```

If `mfaSecret` is falsy the code is never verified and MFA is disabled on **any** 6-character string
plus a bearer.

## Why it is Low and not High

`mfa_secret` **is** in `USER_COLS`, so unlike KS-732's password branch it is genuinely populated. The
branch is only reachable for a row with `mfa_enabled = true` **and** `mfa_secret` null/empty — a state
normal enrolment does not produce. It is a latent shape, not a live bypass, and I did not find a path
that creates that row.

**It is worth closing anyway** because the guard reads as a check, and the row state it depends on
being impossible is not enforced anywhere. That is the same reasoning KS-732 rests on.

## Suggested fix

Fail closed: `mfa_enabled` with no secret should refuse the disable (or require a backup code), never
accept an unverified one. Align with the `/api/auth/mfa/disable` handler after #872 — "the strongest
proof the account can actually produce, never nothing".

Note the two doors also differ: this one accepts no `backupCode`, so an account holding only backup
codes cannot use it. Worth deciding whether this route should exist at all, or redirect to the other.

Provenance: PR #872 review note 4, @PeterObeden, 2026-09-08. Confirmed on develop.

title: ks597 integration guard: `?host=` and `?port=` query overrides in the DSN pass the no-database guard
description:
**BLUF: the guard that refuses a non-disposable database can be bypassed by putting the host or port in the DSN's QUERY STRING instead of its authority.** `?host=` and `?port=` overrides pass it. Minor — but the guard's whole purpose is that a cell writing to a database cannot reach a shared one, and a bypass in the connection string is exactly the shape that purpose is about.

## What was measured, and what holds

The guard itself works on the authority form, measured at runtime: `203.0.113.7`, port `6432` and port `5432` are each **refused with 0 TCP attempts**, and a free loopback port fails with `ECONNREFUSED` rather than being accepted. So the guard is real and it fires early, before any connection is attempted.

**The gap:** libpq-style DSN query parameters (`?host=`, `?port=`) are not part of the authority the guard inspects, so a DSN can name a forbidden target there and pass.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Parse the DSN's query parameters as well as its authority, and apply the same host and port predicate to whichever finally wins. Whatever resolution order the client uses is the one the guard must model — otherwise the guard is checking a different DSN than the one that connects.

## Stated so the record is not read as stronger than it is

The **INSERT path of that cell was not run** in the grading round, and its red proof is READ ONLY. That is a separate limit on what the round established, recorded here because anyone picking this up will be working in the same cell.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **486 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `QUERY-OVERRIDE`, `?host=`, `query override` — **0 open hits each**. `rolbypassrls` returned 2 (KS-1306 the parent, KS-980 a different subject). Controls as above: fresh token **0**, `ssrf-guard` **2**.

Refs KS-1306

title: ks597 integration guard (KS-1340): 127.0.0.1:6433, the shared stack's pgbouncer, is accepted, and the hostaddr refusal is case- and percent-encoding-literal
description:
**BLUF:** the guard that pull request 1790 gives the ks597 integration file (KS-1340) refuses the shared stack's Postgres ports 5432 and 6432 but not **6433**, the port docker-compose publishes for the shared stack's pgbouncer, which fronts the same shared database. `postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:6433/db` is accepted, and so is `...:55412/db?port=6433`. Separately, its `hostaddr` refusal matches the lower-case key literally, so `?HOSTADDR=` and `?host%61ddr=` pass it. One guard and one logical path, so one ticket. Neither is a change to pull request 1790, which merges as gated (gate 8, 2026-10-29: #1790 GO). Filed on Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-10-28 13:38:21Z; gate 8 findings 1790-1 and 1790-2.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks597-issuer-organization-id.integration.test.ts`: the `SHARED_STACK_PORTS` list (the port `5432` plus the `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT` default read from docker-compose.yml) and the `hostaddr` test in `disposableDsnTarget()`, at the head of pull request 1790 (`3a9b1c121f6d`). The port list is pre-existing (KS-1306); the pull request did not change it.

## 1. Port 6433

docker-compose.yml publishes the shared stack's Postgres on `127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT:-6432}` (line 156) and its pgbouncer on `127.0.0.1:${PGBOUNCER_PORT:-6433}` (line 262, container port 6432), the pooler every service connects through. The guard's list is `["5432","6432"]` (printed by the probe below). KS-296 records the labels (6432 = direct Postgres, 6433 = pgbouncer) and the compose stack-safety script's list in KS-1558's description already includes 6433.

Measured by running the pull request's own guard function, extracted from the file at its head and transpiled, beside the pg client (pg 8.20.0; no database and no socket: 0 connect calls, with a control reading 1):

```
DSN                                    guard                       pg dials
control: clean loopback, free port     ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:55412    127.0.0.1:55412
control: shared postgres port 5432     REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:5432
control: shared published port 6432    REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:6432
pgbouncer published port 6433          ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
6433 named only in the query string    ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
```

Nothing was run against a pooler. Gate 8 found the same independently. Not measured: a stack started on another slot publishes pgbouncer and Postgres on other ports (KS-390's table lists 6533, 6633 and so on), and the list reads only the default; whether it should cover slot ports is a decision for whoever fixes this.

## 2. The hostaddr refusal is literal

The test is `/[?&]hostaddr(=|&|$)/`: lower case, not percent-decoded. Measured with the same probe: `?HOSTADDR=203.0.113.7` and `?host%61ddr=203.0.113.7` are accepted, and the pg client dials the authority (`127.0.0.1:55412`) for both. There is **no measured bypass**: pg ignores `hostaddr` in every spelling, and no consumer of the DSN in this file is libpq. The rule's stated reason is that libpq honours `hostaddr`; the gate states that libpq also decodes percent-escapes in a key, so the rule only partly meets that reason. I did not run libpq here.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Read the pgbouncer default from the compose file the way the Postgres one is read (`PGBOUNCER_PORT:-(\d+)\}:6432`), so the list cannot drift; and either decode and lower-case the query's keys before the `hostaddr` test, or refuse any query key outside a short allow-list.

## Also noted by the gate, not measured

Finding 1790-3: the same DSN is handed to the product as `DATABASE_URL` (Prisma), whose parser may read a duplicate or overriding query key differently from the pg client. Checking that needs a connection attempt.

## Board search before filing

Issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, run immediately before filing. `SHARED_STACK_PORTS`: 0 hits. `hostaddr` and `HOSTADDR`: only KS-1340 and KS-1793 (both mine; neither covers the spelling). `PGBOUNCER_PORT`: 3 hits (KS-1166, KS-390, KS-614) and `6433`: 6 hits (KS-1236, KS-1558, KS-296, KS-390, KS-490, KS-614); I read them: they concern slot ports, the VM firewall, a docs label fix and the compose stack-safety script's list, and none covers the ks597 guard's port list. Positive control `disposable`: 20 hits. Zero control: a fresh token never written to the board returned 0; the token is not recorded here so that it stays a control.

## Related

KS-1340 (pull request 1790, the guard). KS-1793 (the ks1263 guard with the same hole; unfixed). KS-1558 and KS-296 (where the role of 6433 is recorded).

## Provenance

Gate 8, findings 1790-1 and 1790-2 (`0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate8-batch/verdict.md`), reproduced by running the pull request's own function on 2026-10-29. Probe: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatT-5th/tools/guard_probe_followup_t5.js` in the project record.

title: O-2: RUNBOOK §2.2 documents SMOKE_BASE_URL, but scripts/smoke-test.sh ignores it
description:
The runbook (§2.2) tells an operator to point the smoke test at an environment with `SMOKE_BASE_URL`. `scripts/smoke-test.sh` **doesn't read it**, so it runs against its default target whatever the variable says.

The risk is a smoke run that looks like it checked kintsugi or demo when it actually checked something else. Found by the #1037 gate.

## What to do

Make the script honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (and print the target it's using), or correct the runbook.

---

Filed from the #1037 / KS-1101 tier-1 gate report `2026-09-18-ks1101-1037-f87506f47-tier1-r1`, at merge of `207716440e2a6282b90ed2a118614d9cf98bee1e`.

title: smoke-test.sh is not remote-clean: 12 localhost:60xx checks, RUNBOOK 2.2's remote full run, and URL credentials echoed in "Smoke target:"
description:
**BLUF:** `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is still not remote-clean after PR 1793 made its `GATEWAY` honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (KS-1250). One remote full run would show all three problems below at once, which is why they are one ticket. Low. Related to KS-1250. Filed on the tier-2 gate's note (gate 8, 2026-10-28), after a search of the board (quoted at the end).

**Nobody runs this script against kintsugi, demo or any live box to reproduce or check any of this.** A full run anchors a real document, and that run is held for Kam (the KS-1250 hold). Everything below was read from the script or measured with a stub `curl` on a private PATH against a `.invalid` host.

1. **12 hard-coded** `http://localhost:60xx` **service-port checks remain in the full run** (sections 7 onward): lines 259, 263, 267, 275, 283, 292, 305, 307, 317, 319, 327 and 329 of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` at PR 1793's head `29989b01ab05`. PR 1793 moves only `GATEWAY`, so with `SMOKE_BASE_URL` set to a remote gateway those 12 checks still hit localhost, and the run mixes two environments while reading as a result for one.
2. **RUNBOOK section 2.2 still tells an operator to do a remote full run.** `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md` lines 139 to 143: `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<prod-gateway-fqdn> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`, under the heading "Bash smoke against production gateway", with no `--quick`.
3. **The** `Smoke target:` **line echoes credentials embedded in the URL verbatim.** Measured with a stub `curl` and `--quick`: `SMOKE_BASE_URL='https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999'` (a fake credential) prints, as line 1 of the output, `Smoke target: https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999`. A base URL carrying a token or basic-auth would be written to the terminal and to any CI log. The stub recorded 9 requests, all to `smoke-target.invalid`.

Also on this ticket: **no test cell uses an** `https://` **base** (the new suite uses `http://smoke-target.invalid:9999`), so the gate's mutant M11 survives.

Fix shapes, not chosen here: route the 12 service-port checks through a base the way `GATEWAY` is, or skip them with a printed line when the base is not localhost; make section 2.2 say `--quick` or say what a remote full run does not cover; print the target as scheme, host and port only.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 13:4xZ): `remote-clean` 1 hit, KS-1250 itself; `smoke-test.sh` 11 hits, read: none is this follow-up (KS 1245 is the Done degraded-health fix, KS 1139 the arithmetic-under-errexit fix, KS 1101 a health-aggregation ticket); `SMOKE_BASE_URL` 2 hits, KS-1250 and a review comment on KS 1101 that repeats the same O-2 finding; `Smoke target` 1 hit, KS-1250; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6b` 0 hits.

title: KS-1594 follow-up (pull request 1547 round-2 gate): the non-string and null organizationId rules at originate's admin mint are pinned for one caller class only
description:
Filed from the round-2 Opus delta gate on pull request 1547 (KS-1594), report hash `ccbe317fcbf769f3`, verdict `GO WITH NOTE` at 0 Major / 1 Minor / 6 Info. 1547 merged to `develop` as `92d1316ffe31cb13b3f7e843e7891225383b2f84`. This ticket carries the Minor plus two Info items the gate asked to be recorded. **The implementation is correct today** — every item below is test coverage or a pre-existing difference, not a live defect.

## 1. The Minor: three mutants survive the 23 cells (test coverage)

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1594-admin-mint-provisioning-and-org-bound.integration.test.ts:292-293` — all four `c17` shapes use `tok('SYSTEM_ADMIN')`, so the "400 for a non-string `organizationId`" rule is pinned for a **platform** caller only. No cell anywhere in the file sends `organizationId: null`: the gate's `grep -i` found 0 such calls, against 16 `mint(` calls found by the same instrument as its control.

The three gate mutants that therefore survive:

| mutant | what it does | behaviour it restores |
| -- | -- | -- |
| R9 | narrows the 400 guard to platform callers | an ORG_ADMIN sending `organizationId: [A2]` is silently treated as absent and gets 201 bound to its own org — the round-1 m2 behaviour |
| R1 | moves the 400 guard after the (a) and (c) decisions | an ORG_ADMIN sending a non-string gets 403, not 400 |
| R7 | makes `organizationId: null` a 400 | breaks the ruled "null and absent behave the same" |

**Why it is a Minor, not a Major.** The matrix the gate ran over the real route found 0 of 900 non-string cases that were not 400, and 0 of 342 null/absent pairs that differed in status or stored org. None of the three survivors creates a false pass: in each, every FALSE PASS category stays at 0 and the deviations are status codes or own-org rows.

### The fix (the gate's own minimal fix, two cells)

1. `ORG_ADMIN(A1)`, `permissions: ['organizations:register']`, `organizationId: [A2]` → **400** and **0 rows** written.
2. `organizationId: null` with `permissions: ['read']` → the **same status and the same stored org** as with the field absent, for **SYSTEM_ADMIN** and for **ORG_ADMIN(A1)**.

Both cells must red R9, R1 and R7 respectively. Run in both tenancy modes, as the existing 23 are.

## 2. i5 — UNTESTED, carried verbatim from the gate

In the gate's own words:

> a forged `x-tenant-id` sent directly to the router is honoured; KS-1032 closes it on the merged tree by reading only, not tested end to end

What the gate measured on the gated head: `ORG_ADMIN(A1)` + `organizations:register` + `organizationId: A1` with a forged `x-tenant-id: T2` sent **directly to the router** returns **201, stored in tenant T2**, bound to A1. It is pre-existing — `develop` at `026c2d16` gave 201 too, and the security route would have refused it as cross-tenant. The gate's harness mounts the router **without** `index.ts`'s middleware, which is why it cannot answer the real question.

**The claim that is untested:** that KS-1032, now on `develop`, shuts this. The reading is that `gatewayProvenance` strips trust headers whenever `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset (fail closed), and that the KS-458 resolution reads `x-tenant-id` only on a vouched request. **Nobody has run it.**

**The instrument that would settle it:** an end-to-end request through originate's **real middleware stack** on `develop` `92d1316f` — `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, a forged `x-tenant-id: T2` — expecting the key to be stored in the **caller's own tenant**, not T2. Until that runs, "KS-1032 shuts it" is a reading, not a measurement.

## 3. i4 — pre-existing difference between the two doors

A malformed `permissions` value (a bare string, a nested array, `[null, …]`, an object) is a **400** at `services/security/src/index.ts`, because zod parses `scopes: z.array(z.string())`. At originate the same input falls back to `['read']` or is stored inertly. 720 cells in the gate's door comparison sit in this bucket; 200 agree, 395 differ on allow/refuse and 125 on refusal code.

**It is not an escape:** the classifier found **0** non-platform rows whose stored scopes are provisioning-capable. It is a divergence in refusal behaviour between two doors that are now identical on all 1680 well-formed shapes.

Decide whether originate should reject a malformed `permissions` with 400 to match security, or whether the fall-back is intended. That choice is not made here.

## Provenance

* Verdict: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1547-r2/verdict.md`, report hash `ccbe317fcbf769f3` (recipe: delete line 2, sha256 the rest, first 16 hex). Recomputed independently; a one-byte perturbation gives `80f78858246cf02d`.
* Deduped before filing: 253 distinct issues read across 5 search terms with comments and archived included. 0 near hits. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9nonce-1fe0a1cf6ffe` → 0; positive control `svc_api_keys` → 18 issues. The nonce is fresh for this filing precisely because a token already written into a description stops being a control.
* Filed by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13.

title: Security: originate POST /api/admin/api-keys is a SECOND hop 1 — an ORG_ADMIN mints an organizations:register key with no, whitespace or FOREIGN organisation, bypassing every provisioning rule
description:
## BLUF

`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:924-983` **mints API keys with a raw** `INSERT` **and applies NO provisioning rule at all.** It is a second hop 1 for the KS-1584 two-hop escape, on a different service, and KS-1584's fix does not reach it.

**Measured by the pull request 1541 Opus gate** (verdict sha256/16 `3df0f1ae2c007542`, finding **M1**, rated Major, **pre-existing on develop and outside KS-1584's diff**): an `ORG_ADMIN` can mint a key carrying `organizations:register` with **no** organisation, a **whitespace** organisation, or a **FOREIGN** organisation — and on KS-1584's head that key then mints into organisation A2 with A2's connector id, **201, measured 3 of 3**.

## Why KS-1584 does not cover it

KS-1584 put the hop-1 default deny in the **security** service's mint route and the bound in shared `decideTenantAccess`. This route reaches neither:

* it writes `svc_api_keys` **directly** with `$queryRaw`, so `decideMint` and `decideTenantAccess` never run;
* `const scopes = Array.isArray(d.permissions) && d.permissions.length > 0 ? d.permissions : ['read']` — the requested permissions are stored verbatim, with **no provisioning-capability check**;
* `const orgId = (d.organizationId as string) || req.user?.organizationId || null` — the **body wins**, unvalidated and **unnormalised**, so `'   '` is truthy and is stored as `'   '` rather than as absent.

**Reachable:** the router is guarded by `adminConfigRouter.use(authenticate(), requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'))` (`adminConfig.ts:38`), mounted at `/api/admin` (`services/originate/src/index.ts:300`), and `/api/admin` is in the api-gateway's proxied prefix list (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:392`). So an `ORG_ADMIN` token reaches it through the gateway.

## The gate's minimal fix — a PROPOSAL, not a ruling

1. **Refuse any** `permissions` **set where** `isProvisioningCapable` **holds unless the caller is a platform role.** That is the same default deny KS-1584 applied at the security route, through the one shared predicate.
2. **Store** `normaliseOrgId(orgId)`, so `''` and `'   '` are stored as **absent** rather than as a distinct organisation.
3. **Bound** `body.organizationId` **to the** `ORG_ADMIN`**'s own organisation.**

**(3) IS OPEN and needs its own ruling.** The gate's words: it is the same class as the KS-1533 arm. Today this route lets an `ORG_ADMIN` name any organisation in its tenant, and bounding it is a behaviour change for any caller that relies on that — the admin frontend and e2e paths have **not** been surveyed here. Do not build (3) without a ruling.

(1) and (2) are fail-closed and narrow. (3) is a scope decision.

## Not measured

* Whether any current caller — the admin frontend, e2e, or a seeded script — passes a foreign `organizationId` to this route today. **That survey belongs in the plan, before any build.**
* Whether a key already minted this way exists in any environment. A census belongs with the deploy seat; originate already writes one for keys.

## Round

**This is the FIFTH piece of the KS-1570 round and the round does not deploy until it merges** (Wednesday's ruling with the pull request 1541 GO; recorded in `DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md`). Pull request 1541 is merged as gated; this is its sibling.

## Dedupe

Linear's `searchIssues` is **fuzzy** — it returns hits for a nonsensical control term — so it was not used. Deduped with a literal `containsIgnoreCase` filter over title and description, controlled both ways (`zzqqxx-no-such-thing` → 0; `adminConfig` → 15). `second hop` → 0. The nearest prior art is **KS-1206** (Done): the same route, but about a missing `connector_id` and an unclamped rate limit — not the provisioning scope. `organizations:register` matches only KS-1584 and KS-568 (systemTest coverage).

Filed by Seat V 7th from the pull request 1541 gate.

title: ks1263 KS-1310 describe: the disposable-database guard reads new URL(dsn), so a ?host= or ?port= in the DSN query string passes it (same hole as KS-1340, on a guard that protects DDL)
description:
**BLUF:** the disposable-database guard in the third describe of `ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts` (the KS 1310 describe, which creates a trigger on `documents`) judges `new URL(DEFAULT_DB)`, the host and port the DSN's authority names. A `?host=` or `?port=` in the query string passes it while the pg client dials the remote host, or port 5432. It is the same hole as KS-1340, in a guard that protects schema DDL. Not fixed in pull request 1790, pull request 1792 or the KS-1600 pull request; Wednesday asked for this ticket (ANSWER 2026-10-28 12:23:51Z).

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts`, the `beforeAll` of the describe "KS-1310 ROUTE-LEVEL ...". At develop `d531abd5f34b` the block is lines 589 to 598: `new URL(DEFAULT_DB)`, hostname in `['127.0.0.1', 'localhost']`, port in 55410 to 55419, else it throws "KS-1310 installs a trigger (schema DDL) and therefore refuses any database that is not this seat's disposable one".

## Measured

The exact predicate of line 591 run beside the pg client on four DSNs (pg 8.20.0, pg-connection-string 2.12.0; constructing a Client opens no socket, so nothing was dialled):

```
DSN                                      guard accepts   pg dials
postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:55412/db        true            127.0.0.1:55412
...@127.0.0.1:55412/db?host=203.0.113.7  true            203.0.113.7:55412
...@127.0.0.1:55412/db?port=5432         true            127.0.0.1:5432
postgres://u:p@203.0.113.7:55412/db      false           203.0.113.7:55412
```

A DSN that names no port is already refused here (`Number('')` is 0, outside the range), which is not true of the ks597 guard KS-1340 fixes. Probe script: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatT-5th/tools/sibling_guard_probe_t5.js` in the project record.

## Why it matters, and its limit

The guard's own comment says a cell that writes DDL must be unable to reach a shared or real database. This describe runs `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` and `CREATE TRIGGER ... ON documents` against whatever `TEST_DATABASE_URL` names. The hole is reachable only if that variable carries such a query string (an operator mistake or an unusual DSN); it is not reachable by default, and nothing was run against a shared database to test it.

## Fix shape (the KS-1340 one; not chosen here)

Judge the host and port the pg client will dial, by asking the client (`new Client({ connectionString }).host` and `.port`), as pull request 1790 does for the ks597 guard, and keep the 55410 to 55419 range test on that answer. KS-1340 also refuses a DSN that names `hostaddr` (pg ignores it, libpq honours it).

## Board search before filing

Issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, run at 12:2xZ and again immediately before filing: `55410` gave 0 hits, `refuses any database that is not this` gave 0, `KS-1310 installs a trigger` gave 0. Positive control `disposable`: 19 hits at filing time (19 at the first run). Zero control: a fresh token never written to the board returned 0; the token is not recorded here so that it stays a control. No existing ticket covers this guard.

## Related

KS-1340 (the ks597 guard, pull request 1790). KS-1310 (added this guard; Done). KS-1499 (pull request 1792 edits the same file for other reasons and leaves this guard as it is).

title: auth social sign-in (Google / Microsoft / Apple): failures in a live environment can't be diagnosed — config is skipped silently, provider detail isn't logged, the raw provider response reaches the client — and Apple can't complete at all
description:
**BLUF:** If social sign-in were turned on in a live environment today, most failures would be hard to diagnose. A half-configured provider just vanishes. The provider's own explanation is thrown away. Logs from the gateway and the auth service can't be joined up. Separately, Sign in with Apple cannot complete at all, and its identity token is never verified. Nothing is exposed today, because the code itself notes that no deployment configures any provider (`routes/auth.ts:951-952`). That's why this is Medium. It should be fixed before any provider is switched on. Thank you, Kamil. The callback is already well defended: the state ordering, account gate, no-email refusal and the reasoning in [KS-722](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-722/security-social-sign-in-never-verifies-the-oauth-state-and-links-an) / [KS-795](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-795/ks-781-door-2-the-social-callback-account-linking-branch-mints-a) / [KS-819](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-819/ks-722-follow-up-the-oauth-state-is-consumed-before-the-request-is) all hold up. These findings are about **diagnosability and completeness**, not those decisions. Found by reading the code at develop `76698952a` (2026-10-16). Nothing was run against a live stack. Line numbers are against that commit, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/`. ## Scope * **Microsoft is personal accounts only.** `/consumers` is hardcoded (`providers/social/microsoft-personal.ts:21, :25`) and there's no tenant setting. **Entra workforce sign-in is not implemented** in platform-k. Entra appears only in the KYC Verified-ID client. Whether workforce sign-in is wanted here is a product decision, not a defect. It's noted so nobody assumes it exists. * **No frontend uses social sign-in.** No file under `frontend/` calls `/api/auth/social`. ## Per-provider matrix | Check | Google | Microsoft (personal) | Apple | Entra workforce | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | Implemented | Yes | Personal accounts only (`/consumers` hardcoded) | Partly | **No** | | Missing or half-set config | Skipped silently, not logged (`provider-factory.ts:39`) | Same | Same; no team ID, key ID or private-key config exists | n/a | | Redirect URI | `FRONTEND_URL` or a silent `localhost:8882` fallback (`:53`) | Same | Same | n/a | | Provider `?error=` | Generic 400 `OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR`; `error` logged, `error_description` dropped (`auth.ts:1011-1018`) | Same | **Unreachable**: Apple POSTs the response, only GET exists (`apple.ts:17`, `auth.ts:967`) | n/a | | State check | Yes, 403 `OAUTH_STATE_INVALID` (`auth.ts:1023-1026`) | Yes | Yes (once reachable) | n/a | | Nonce | None | None | None | n/a | | Token exchange failure | 400 that **includes the provider's raw response** (`google.ts:40`, `auth.ts:1032-1034`) | Same (`microsoft-personal.ts:39`) | Same (`apple.ts:38`) | n/a | | Client secret | Static (correct) | Static (correct) | Static; **Apple requires a signed ES256 JWT** (`apple.ts:30`) | n/a | | Identity source | userinfo over TLS (no ID-token check needed) | Graph `/me` over TLS | **ID token decoded without verification** (`apple.ts:42-44`) | n/a | | Email verified | From `verified_email` | **Hardcoded** `true` (`microsoft-personal.ts:58`) | From the token's `email_verified` claim | n/a | | Profile-fetch failure | Generic message, no HTTP status (`google.ts:50`) | Same (`microsoft-personal.ts:49`) | n/a | n/a | | Request ID on error logs | No: auth mints its own and ignores the gateway's (`requestLogger.ts:12`), and error and warn lines don't carry it | Same | Same | n/a | | User-facing result | Raw JSON from a browser redirect target (`auth.ts:1271`); no frontend | Same | Same | n/a | | Diagnostics endpoint | `GET /social/providers` lists names only (`auth.ts:921-924`) | Same | Same | n/a | ## A. Diagnosability (the question asked) 1. **Missing config is skipped silently.** * A provider whose `SOCIAL_

_CLIENT_ID` or `_CLIENT_SECRET` is unset returns `null` and is dropped with no log line (`providers/social/provider-factory.ts:39`). * When `FRONTEND_URL` is unset, the callback base quietly becomes `http://localhost:8882` (`:53`), so a deployed host would send providers a localhost redirect URI. * Nothing logs the enabled set at startup. 2. **The provider's explanation is discarded.** On `?error=`, only `error` is logged, trimmed to 200 characters (`routes/auth.ts:1011-1018`). `error_description` is not logged. That field is where providers say *which* thing is wrong, for example a redirect-URI mismatch or an unauthorised client. Not echoing it to the browser is right (errorHandler.ts §OAuthProviderError); not logging it is the gap. 3. **Profile-fetch failures lose the HTTP status.** Both read only "Failed to fetch … user profile" (`providers/social/google.ts:50`, `microsoft-personal.ts:49`). 4. **Request IDs don't join up across services.** * The gateway mints or forwards `X-Request-ID` (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:451`, `routes/proxy.ts:248`). * The auth service ignores the incoming header and mints its own (`middleware/requestLogger.ts:12`). * Neither the global error log (`middleware/errorHandler.ts:259-264`) nor the social `logger.warn` lines carry the ID. 5. **The only diagnostic surface is** `GET /social/providers`**.** It lists enabled names, never why one is disabled (`routes/auth.ts:921-924`). 6. **Browser-facing errors are raw JSON.** The callback is a browser redirect target, but it answers with JSON tokens or a JSON error (`routes/auth.ts:1271`) rather than redirecting to a frontend route with `?error=`. ## B. Security-relevant (the [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) class) 7. **The provider's raw token-endpoint response reaches the client.** Each `exchangeCode` throws with `await tokenRes.text()` (`google.ts:40`, `apple.ts:38`, `microsoft-personal.ts:39`). The route then puts that message into the 400 it returns (`routes/auth.ts:1032-1034`). This is the same "log, never echo" principle that F-4 already applies to `?error=`. 8. **The Apple ID token is not verified.** * The payload is base64-decoded and `JSON.parse`d with no signature, `iss`, `aud` or `exp` check and no JWKS fetch (`apple.ts:42-44`). * It uses `base64`, not `base64url`. * It throws a TypeError if `id_token` is absent. 9. **No nonce is used by any provider** (`getAuthUrl` in all three). 10. `microsoft-personal` **hardcodes** `emailVerified: true` (`microsoft-personal.ts:58`). The auto-link path already distrusts it (`routes/auth.ts:1119-1129`, `mayAutoLinkByEmail`), but a newly created account is stored with `emailVerified: profile.emailVerified` (`routes/auth.ts:1166`), which is therefore always `true`. ## C. Apple cannot complete 11. **The callback route doesn't match Apple's response mode.** Apple is asked for `response_mode=form_post` (`apple.ts:17`), so Apple POSTs the callback. Only `GET /social/:provider/callback` exists (`routes/auth.ts:967`), so the handler is never reached. 12. **The client secret is static.** Apple requires an ES256-signed client secret JWT (team ID, key ID, `.p8` key) that expires within six months. The code posts `SOCIAL_APPLE_CLIENT_SECRET` as-is (`apple.ts:30`), and no team ID, key ID or private-key setting exists anywhere in the repo. ## Already recorded elsewhere (one line each) * Social IDs are never persisted (`routes/auth.ts:1135-1146`, `1180-1187`). It's recorded in the service's BACKLOG.md per those comments, but I couldn't find a Linear ticket for it. Happy to raise one if you'd like it tracked separately. ## Suggested done-when (your call on the shape) * Startup logs each provider as enabled, disabled or half-configured, with key names only and never values. An unset `FRONTEND_URL` in a non-local environment fails loudly. * `error_description` and profile-fetch status are logged server-side. Neither the provider's token response nor `error_description` reaches the client. * The incoming `X-Request-ID` is reused in auth and appears on error and social log lines. * Apple either works (POST callback, signed client secret, verified ID token) or is removed from `PROVIDER_MAP` until it does. * Each fix is backed by a test that fails on today's code and passes after.

title: KS-1311 test gaps: RLS asserted on documents only, setup guard bypassed by -t/.only, env shape differs from KS-597, no CI job runs the suite (gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Four gaps from the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1490 (KS-1311), left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Filed as ONE ticket (P3); one small test-only PR later. No product file is involved.

## Recommendation

One small test-only PR, test first. Close F1 and F2 in the file itself; settle F5 by reading the KS-597 form too; make a decision on N1 (nothing in `.github` runs the originate integration config, so this suite and its predecessors are a manual instrument).

## Detail (file: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts`; gate verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1490/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `6be6317b5c2cd58b`, head `90b45bb5c8ad`)

1. **F1 (Minor), the RLS control asserts** `documents` **only.** The header says FORCE RLS is on `documents`, `shares` and `custody_events`, and the rollback cells write `shares` and `custody_events`, but `ALTER TABLE shares DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` plus the same on `custody_events` leaves all 11 cells green (gate mutant M5). Closing step: assert `relforcerowsecurity` for all three tables, or add an other-tenant INSERT/UPDATE refused on each of `shares` and `custody_events`.
2. **F2 (Minor), the SETUP guard is an ordinary cell, not a** `beforeAll`**.** A run that excludes it (`-t ROLLBACK`, `it.only`, a single-cell watch run) executes the rollback cells as a superuser and exits 0 (gate run 11: 2 passed, 9 skipped, exit 0). Closing step: also assert the role inside the existing `beforeAll`, or document in the file header that it must be run whole.
3. **F5 (Note), env-variable shape differs from KS-597.** KS-597's suite also accepts `APP_DB_USER` / `APP_DB_PASSWORD` to compose the app DSN; this suite needs `TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL` outright. Harmless, but someone with the KS-597 env set meets the refusal and has to read its message. Closing step: accept the KS-597 pair as a fallback, or name the difference in the refusal message.
4. **N1 (Note), no CI job runs the originate integration config.** A grep of `origin/develop` for `jest.integration`, `test:integration` and `TEST_DATABASE_URL` finds nothing under `.github`, so this gate and its predecessors are a manual instrument (as before; GitHub Actions is retired for this repo). Closing step: a decision, not code: either record the manual run command in `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents, or accept and say so.

Also from the gate (F3, F4): the role probe names only `withTenant`'s connection (a future route opening a different pool would not be probed); the RLS control is positive-controlled and cleans up in `finally`. No action.

Refs KS-1311.

title: The tenant-creation contract, TOKENISATION.md and the admin UI still describe a key file returned once at creation; the key service has not returned one since 2026-04-28
description:
**BLUF:** The published tenant-creation contract, `docs/TOKENISATION.md`, `docs/METERING-USAGE-API.md` and the admin UI all describe a vault key file that tenant creation returns once. The key service has not returned a key since 2026-04-28 (commit `1f1cba638`, "Audit Tier-0 ... B-5", which changed `generate-key` to persist the key wrapped server-side and answer only `{ keyId, keyHash }`), so since that commit the real service has not let `POST /api/tenants` carry a key file on success, and the admin UI's key-file dialog can never open. One logical path, three kinds of site; the checklist below names each. Low: it misleads readers and consumers, it does not break a request.

## Exercised (real entry modules, `pg` and JWT stubbed, no Docker)

* The real `generate-key` answers with the fields `algorithm, createdAt, keyHash, keyId, success, tenantId, tenantSlug, version`: no `keyFile`, no `key`.
* Tenant creation against that answer: `201` with body keys `meteringApiKey, success, tenant` (no `keyFile` key at all); with the key service refusing (403 `success: false`) the same `201` carries `keyFile: null`. So success and failure differ only as "key absent" versus "key null", and the admin UI treats both as "no key dialog".
* Files in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_probe.json` and `tenant_create_real_shape.json`.

## Checklist (develop `2b7ef12fa564`, line numbers from there)

- [ ] **Published contract.** The `keyFile` property of the 201 of `POST /api/platform/tenants`: description "The tenant's vault key material (PII/encryption), returned once at creation; null if key generation failed (mint manually later)." Source `services/tenant-provisioning/src/tenant-provisioning.openapi.ts:385`, published in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (regenerate it with `npm run generate-openapi`).
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/TOKENISATION.md`: the key file format and the example response near `:312` to `:321`, the Key Security note at `:182`, the write-path example at `:201` (`"key": "<from vault_key_hash lookup>"`; no code does that lookup and a SHA-256 hash cannot give the key back), Key Lifecycle step 4 at `:382` to `:385` ("The key file is returned to the super-admin"), and the troubleshooting step at `:486`. `docs/METERING-USAGE-API.md:120` ("alongside the vault `keyFile`").
- [ ] **Code and UI.** `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:125` to `:139`: `requestKeyGeneration` is typed as returning `keyFile`, and the handler copies `keyResult.keyFile` (undefined on the real answer). `frontend/admin/src/pages/platform/ClientList.tsx:70` (`if (result.keyFile) setKeyFileJson(...)`) with the dialog at `:323` to `:332`, and the type at `frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:1045`.

## A decision sits under this (not mine)

Either a way to deliver the tenant's key is restored or `keyFile` is retired from the contract, the docs and the UI. The design comment in `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:126` promises "a separate admin-only, audited endpoint can return the wrapped envelope"; no such route exists (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key). Related: the gateway keeps a per-session tenant key that an administrator uploads (`POST /api/platform/tenant-key`), but no route returns a key to upload, and the gateway's tokenise and detokenise helpers have no caller in the tree (none at the commit that introduced them either).

## Not covered

The admin UI was read, not rendered; consumers outside this repository (the Extranet, other repositories, runbooks) are unmeasured; live data on the boxes is unmeasured.

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `keyFile` (1 hit, KS-336, Done, the original design), `key file` (3 hits, none about tenant creation), `B-5` (KS-630, KS-612; neither concerns this), `TOKENISATION.md` (KS-525, KS-300; neither concerns this), `ClientList` (0), `vault key` (0), `keyPending` (0). None records that the key file is no longer returned.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: tenant-provisioning: the key service still writes a tenant's key row after the caller gives up, and neither the create rollback nor tenant delete removes it
description:
**BLUF:** The tokenisation service's `POST /api/generate-key` does not notice that its caller has gone: it still inserts the tenant's wrapped key row (`tenant_keys`) and an audit row afterwards. When tenant creation gives up (its fetch bound, a client disconnect) or rolls back, nothing removes that row. The create rollback deletes only `tenant_config`, `tenant_contacts` and `tenants`; tenant delete deletes `vault_entries`, `tenant_contacts`, `tenant_config` and `platform_document_registry`; tokenisation has no delete route. The result is an ACTIVE wrapped key for a tenant whose `vault_key_hash` is NULL, or for a tenant that no longer exists. Low: nothing reachable reads it today (see the vault-key trace on KS-1240).

## Exercised

A probe against the real tokenisation entry module (`pg` replaced by a recorder and the JWT middleware stubbed; no database, no Docker): the key INSERT slowed by 400 ms and the client aborting at 150 ms. Result, verbatim:

```
{ "clientOutcome": "client aborted: AbortError",
  "tenantKeysInsertsAtTheMomentTheClientGaveUp": 0,
  "tenantKeysInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1,
  "auditInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1 }
```

So the handler does not observe a client disconnect; the key row and the audit row land after the caller has left. File in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_abort_probe.json` (the probe source is beside it as a `.txt`).

## Read (develop `2b7ef12fa564`)

* `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`: the `generate-key` route is at `:220` and the key INSERT at `:238`; no `req.on('close')` handling and no delete route (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key).
* `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: the rollback at `:322` to `:324` and the tenant delete list at `:520` name no `tenant_keys`. `tenant_keys` is written by tokenisation into the main database, tenant provisioning's `platformQuery` writes the platform database.
* `migrations/029_tokenisation_tenant_keys.sql`: `UNIQUE (tenant_id, version, status)`. A second `generate-key` for a tenant that already has an active version 1 would insert `(tenant_id, 1, 'active')` again and so answer 500 (read; not executed, it needs a real Postgres).

## Why it matters

* Tenant creation now gives up on a key service that is slower than 3 s (KS-1240 part 4). A key service that is slow but not hung still completes its insert, and the tenant ends up with a key row and a NULL `vault_key_hash`.
* The decision that keeps tenant creation answering 201 with a `keyPending` flag (KS-1240) leaves such tenants in place; a later attempt to generate their key by hand would meet the unique constraint above.
* A create that is rolled back after the key was written leaves a key (and its audit row) for a tenant that no longer exists.

## Options (not chosen here)

1. A platform-admin route on tokenisation that deletes a tenant's key rows, called by the create rollback and the tenant delete.
2. Make `generate-key` idempotent per tenant (answer with the existing active key's id and hash), so a retry or a late completion can be reconciled.
3. Have tenant creation read the hash back from the key service after a timeout instead of leaving it NULL.

## Not covered

A real Postgres (the unique-constraint rejection is read), live data (how many such rows exist on the demo or kintsugi boxes is unmeasured), and any other caller of `generate-key` (the search found tenant provisioning only).

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `tenant_keys` (KS-311, KS-288, both Done and about earlier errors in these routes), `generate-key` (KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all Done or Deployed To Prod), `rotate-key` (6 hits: KS-667, KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all closed or deployed work on these routes), `wrapped key` (0), `vault key` (0), `key row` (6 hits, none about the key service), `keyPending` (0). None records this behaviour.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: Blockchain/Testing: five audit/DAST/tenant-isolation entry points default TARGET_BASE to slot 1's gateway (:6882) — an unslotted run on a slot-N worktree attacks slot 1
description:
## BLUF

Five `Blockchain/Testing` entry points fall back to `http://localhost:6882` **— slot 1's gateway — when** `TARGET_BASE` **is not passed**, instead of deriving it from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. On a slot-N worktree, forgetting the variable points ZAP (active scan), the tenant-isolation job and the internal audit at whichever stack owns slot 1, which on this host is usually someone else's. That is the [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) failure shape (a run named for one slot reaching another), in the shell harness rather than the Schemathesis Python readers [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) fixed.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`)

| File:line | Default |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh:37` | `TARGET_BASE="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh:23` | same |
| `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/05-dast-zap.sh:23` | `TARGET="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh:31` | same |
| `Blockchain/Testing/run-internal-audit.sh:30` | `TARGET_BASE="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |

## Verified from the code (29 Sep, re-read)

None of the five sources `stack_env.sh`, `slot-target.sh` or reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. The only callers that set `TARGET_BASE` are `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml:558` and `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:351` (CI, unslotted, explicit) plus two script unit tests with fixture values; `orchestrate.sh:138/159` and `run-internal-audit.sh:103` just forward whatever they resolved. `Blockchain/Testing/README.md` and `ci/README.md` never mention slots — their only `TARGET_BASE` example is `TARGET_BASE=https://secuura.com ./run-internal-audit.sh 05` — so a local run following the docs on a slot-N worktree takes the `:6882` default.

## Fix (Internal Audit Harness — Kamil's call)

Source `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` (with `PROJECT_ROOT` set — it refuses otherwise) and default `TARGET_BASE` to `http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}`; locally, refuse to start with no slot named (the [KS-1016](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1016/test-anchor-read-honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura-postgres-fails) rule), so a missing variable is an error, not a silent slot-1 run. CI stays unslotted and passes `TARGET_BASE` explicitly. Add a static check that no `Blockchain/Testing` script carries a literal slot port.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. These five scripts run ZAP active scans, tenant-isolation probes and the audit — aimed at the wrong slot they attack another session's stack, silently. That makes this a high-risk area; `Blockchain/Testing` has no slot tests today (its only test is `ci/aggregate.test.mjs`), so the PR is not done without them:

* For each of the five entry points and `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4: with no `TARGET_BASE`, the resolved target is that slot's gateway (`6882 + 100*(N-1)` from `stack_env.sh`, not a copy of the arithmetic).
* Locally with no slot named: the script refuses with the example command — it never falls back to any slot. With an explicit `TARGET_BASE` (the CI path): it is used unchanged.
* `TARGET_BASE` and the named slot disagreeing (the [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) split-target shape) refuses.
* A static guard over `Blockchain/Testing/**` failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

## Not in this ticket

`Blockchain/Testing/` is the Internal Audit Harness (its README: "standalone, free-tools-only security and compliance harness"), not the `systemTest/` test estate — every commit to it in the last 90 days is Kamil's, hence the assignment. Product-code and template slot-1 values → [KS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381/slot-1-urls-hard-coded-outside-ks-1355s-four-spots-the-three-frontends) (Kamil) and [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a). Schemathesis Python readers → [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) (done in [KS-1353: Schemathesis 4.27.5 → 4.28.0, every floor to latest, harness fixes red→green, and KS-1373 one-run-one-stack guard](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1353-schemathesis-4275-4280-every-floor-to-latest-harness-fixes-45629328f369)).

## Environment

Found 29 Sep 2026 auditing platform-k for fixed-slot URLs while pairing slot 2 for platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views).

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 4 — the `Blockchain/Testing/**` guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard extended over this tree, not a second one; and the CI-path criterion follows [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals)'s decision.

title: Blockchain/Testing slot guard: the 'another slot's gateway' refusal is bypassed by LOCALHOST, HTTP://, 0.0.0.0 and 127.0.1.1, and the Azure RUNBOOK's pre-deploy audit step now refuses until it names a slot
description:
**BLUF: the refusal KS-1382 adds for a local TARGET_BASE that is another slot's gateway only recognises lowercase localhost, 127.0.0.1, \[::1\] and host.docker.internal behind a lowercase scheme, so eight other spellings are accepted and the run aims at slot 1's stack while slot 3 is named (Low). Separately, the Azure RUNBOOK's pre-deploy audit step now refuses until it names a slot. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1786 (Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-10-28 10:26Z) and re-measured by Seat Z 3rd.**

## 1. The "another slot's gateway" refusal is bypassed by spellings that reach the same host

**Measured** with the committed [run-internal-audit.sh](<http://run-internal-audit.sh>) from PR #1786 (head 5d23044d272d), `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 SECUURA_TARGET_RESOLVE_ONLY=1 TARGET_BASE=<spelling>:<slot 1's gateway port>`, port read from stack_env.sh:

| TARGET_BASE host spelling | result |
| -- | -- |
| [http://localhost](<http://localhost>) (control) | refused, rc 2 |
| [http://127.0.0.1](<http://127.0.0.1>) (control) | refused, rc 2 |
| [HTTP://localhost](<HTTP://localhost>) | **accepted**, rc 0, TARGET_BASE unchanged |
| [http://LOCALHOST](<http://LOCALHOST>) | **accepted** |
| [http://0.0.0.0](<http://0.0.0.0>) | **accepted** |
| [http://127.0.1.1](<http://127.0.1.1>) | **accepted** |
| [http://127.1](<http://127.1>) | **accepted** |
| http://\[::ffff:127.0.0.1\] | **accepted** |
| [http://localhost](<http://localhost>). (trailing dot) | **accepted** |
| [http://127.0.0.2](<http://127.0.0.2>) | **accepted** |
| [https://audit.example.invalid](<https://audit.example.invalid>) (remote, left alone by design) | accepted |

An accepted spelling means a run that named slot 3 sends its scan to slot 1's gateway, which is the KS 1373 shape this refusal exists to stop.

**Where:** the variable \_ks1382_re in the KS-1382 resolution block, byte-identical in the five entry points (ci/orchestrate.sh, ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh, jobs/05-dast-zap.sh, jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh, [run-internal-audit.sh](<http://run-internal-audit.sh>)). The same lowercase-only set is in is_local_url at systemTest/slot-target.sh lines 94 to 96, which this change reads but does not edit.

**Fix shapes (not decided here):** fold scheme and host to lowercase before matching; treat all of 127.0.0.0/8, 0.0.0.0, a trailing-dot localhost and IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback as local; or parse the URL instead of matching a regex. The five blocks must stay byte-identical (a suite cell pins that), and each new spelling wants a cell in blockchain_testing_target_base_follows_the_slot.test.sh.

**Not measured:** only the guard's decision. Whether each spelling really connects to the local host on a given machine was not tested (127.0.0.2, for one, is not configured on macOS by default). No scan was run.

## 2. The Azure RUNBOOK's pre-deploy audit step now refuses

Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md line 56, step 0.4 "Internal-audit harness clean", runs `cd ../../Testing && ./run-internal-audit.sh` with no TARGET_BASE and no slot. Since KS-1382 that run refuses (rc 2, "No stack slot named"), so the checklist step cannot be completed as written. It was disclosed in the PR body and the READY mail; the runbook was outside KS-1382's file grant and is not updated. The fix is to say which target that step audits (a named slot, or TARGET_BASE for a remote one) and write the command.

Related: KS 1382 (the change that introduced both).

title: One role vocabulary, seven divergent lists: platform_admin is a super-role to the gateway and an ordinary tenant user to the key policy
description:
## BLUF

**The same question — "is this caller a platform role?" — is answered by at least seven separate hard-coded lists that do not agree.** The one that matters most: `platform_admin` is accepted as a super-role by the api-gateway in six places, and is **absent** from the key policy's `PLATFORM_ROLES`, so `decideTenantAccess` treats it as an ordinary tenant user.

Found while building KS-1533 arm 1 (the mint's organisation arm). It is **not** folded into that ticket: arm 1 is one call site, this is a repo-wide vocabulary problem. KS-1535 records the *policy* question of which roles may cross an organisation boundary; **this ticket is the engineering problem that there is no single answer to consult.**

## The seven lists, read at source

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65       SUPER_ROLES           super_admin SUPER_ADMIN platform_admin SYSTEM_ADMIN
services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515      SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES     super_admin SUPER_ADMIN SYSTEM_ADMIN platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:577         PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES  SYSTEM_ADMIN system_admin super_admin SUPER_ADMIN platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1094,1227   (two inline lists)    …include platform_admin, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN
services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:105  adminRoles            …includes platform_admin AND ORG_ADMIN
packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59   PLATFORM_ROLES        SYSTEM_ADMIN SUPER_ADMIN            <-- no platform_admin
services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:193                PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES  SYSTEM_ADMIN SUPER_ADMIN admin super_admin   <-- no platform_admin, but `admin`
services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1156               OAUTH_PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES  the same four as users.ts, duplicated because
                                                     "neither list in routes/users.ts is importable" (its own comment, :1138)
```

`services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1138` already says the quiet part: the lists are duplicated **because they cannot be imported**.

## The measured consequence

Running the real predicates over the vocabulary (caller in org A, target a different organisation in the **same tenant**):

| role | `isPlatformRole` | `isOrgBoundedRole` | `decideTenantAccess` verdict |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN` / `SUPER_ADMIN` / `super_admin` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` |
| `platform_admin` / `PLATFORM_ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` |
| `ADMIN` / `admin` | false | false | ALLOW `same-tenant` |
| `ORG_ADMIN` / `ISSUER_ADMIN` / `issuer_admin` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` |

Both predicates upper-case the claim (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:84`, `:123`), so this is not a casing bug — the role is in neither set. A `platform_admin` therefore passes the gateway's platform guards and then lands in the key policy as an unbounded tenant user.

**Stored roles are lower-case** on Kintsugi (J's count, 16:44Z), which is why the upper-casing in those predicates is load-bearing and why a new list written without it would be wrong on real data.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

* A role added to one list and not the others is a **silent authorisation difference**, and nothing fails when the lists drift — there is no test that compares them.
* KS-1283 already fixed one instance of this class ("a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes"). That was the symptom; this is the cause.
* The erasure path reached through KS-1533/KS-695 is irreversible, so "which list did this route consult" is a security question, not a tidiness one.

## Recommendation

One exported vocabulary in `packages/shared` (it already owns `keyRevokePolicy`), each role set named for the question it answers, and **a guard test that fails when any service re-declares one of them inline** — the KS-764 call-site-guard shape, which already works in this repo. The lists cannot simply be merged: they genuinely differ today, and reconciling them is an authorisation change per route, so the first step is a census with the differences stated, not a rename.

**Not in scope here:** whether `ADMIN` and `platform_admin` *should* be organisation-bounded. That is Kam's policy call on KS-1535 and his board card.

## Dedupe

Literal, case-insensitive over title and description, archived included. The actual results, with every hit named:

| token | hits | which |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `SUPER_ROLES` | 3 | KS-1535 (this ticket's sibling), **KS-1283** (Done — "a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes"), KS-1472 (P4 — OAuth authorize-contract wording) |
| `PLATFORM_ROLES` | 2 | KS-1535, **KS-742** (Deployed to UAT — the `/api/keys` tenant boundary) |
| `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` | 2 | KS-1535, KS-619 (P3 — gateway tenant resolution falling through to `x-tenant-id`) |
| `PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES` | 1 | KS-1535 only |
| `PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES` | 1 | KS-1535 only |
| `role vocabulary` | 1 | KS-1535 only |
| `divergent role` | 0 | — |

**KS-1283 is the nearest and is NOT this ticket:** it fixed ONE list on one file (and is Done); this is that the lists disagree across seven sites and nothing compares them. KS-742 and KS-619 are the tenant boundary, not the platform-role vocabulary.

*Corrected after filing: the first version of this paragraph said the hits were "the KS-1283 / KS-486 family" and did not name them. KS-486 was not among the results — I carried it over from a different ticket's dedupe — and KS-1472, KS-619 and KS-742 were, unnamed. The conclusion is unchanged. Recorded rather than quietly edited, because this is the second time in one session I summarised a scan without reading what it returned.*

Filed by Seat V 5th on Wednesday's ruling, 2026-10-12, found by reading the role sets while building KS-1533 arm 1.

---

## ⚠ CORRECTION to the "measured consequence" above

The table above shows `platform_admin` as ALLOW `same-tenant` from `decideTenantAccess`, and says "for arm 1 that reads as unbounded". **That is true of the function and false of the route.** On the running mint route, `decideMint` runs first and refuses `platform_admin` 403, because `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`.
