So at the mint, this vocabulary split makes a gateway super-role **over**-restricted (it cannot mint keys), not under-restricted.

**This strengthens the ticket rather than weakening it.** The same role is a platform role to the gateway, an ordinary tenant user to `decideTenantAccess`, and not an admin at all to `decideMint` — three different answers to one question across three lists on one request path. That is exactly the problem this ticket names; I had just picked the wrong one of the three as the consequence.

*Corrected by Seat V 5th after a real-HTTP cell in KS-1533 PR A read 403 where I had predicted 201.*

title: audit-locks' refusal points at a regen command that cannot regenerate systemTest/performance's lock
description:
**Priority:** Medium — it sends a reader to a command that fails or silently does nothing.

When leg 7 (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs`) refuses an advisory in any of its 43 standalone locks, its message at `:352` says: "bump the pin (containerised per-dir regen — see [lockfile-cleanroom.sh](<http://lockfile-cleanroom.sh>))". The command `lockfile-cleanroom.sh:120` prints, for the 35 locks that script itself checks (`find services packages frontend scripts -maxdepth 2`, none under `systemTest/`), is:

```
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/<dir>":/app -w /app node:24-alpine npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts
```

Two measured problems when a reader follows that pointer for an advisory in `systemTest/performance/package-lock.json` (2026-09-30):

1. The per-directory mount cannot work for a lock with a `file:` link outside its directory. That manifest carries `"secuura-observability": "file:../../observability"`, and the command fails with `npm error code EMISSINGTARGET` / `Missing target in lock file: "../observability" is referenced by "node_modules/secuura-observability" but does not exist.`, rc 1, lock unchanged. Mounting the parent (`-v "$PWD/systemTest":/app -w /app/performance`) succeeds, rc 0.
2. `npm install --package-lock-only` does not move a pin off a vulnerable range while the pin still satisfies the manifest range (`^5.2.1` here): measured in a scratch copy, 0 entries moved, `js-yaml` still 5.2.3. `npm update js-yaml --package-lock-only` moved exactly one entry, 5.2.3 -> 5.4.2.

A reader following the pointer on an advisory-driven regen therefore gets either a hard failure or a silent no-op, and the gate still refuses. Suggested shape: have `audit-locks.mjs` print its own per-lock command, mounting the lock's parent when the lock has a `file:` link that escapes its directory and using `npm update <package>` for an advisory-driven move; and note that no preflight leg clean-rooms the `systemTest/` locks.

Measured on: `develop` at `37205947ddd2775a72a417beb5b7ac8e3240fbf3`, npm 11.19.0 in `node:24-alpine`.

title: Security (multi-tenant only): POST /api/verification/verify can answer verified:true for a WRONG hash — crossTenantLookup's by-documentId fallback feeds buildResponse with hashMatch hard-coded true (QA-965 O-1)
description:
## BLUF

READ ONLY finding from the tier-2 gate on PR #965 (KS-1103), not driven: when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` and the local hash SELECT misses, strategy 1 calls `crossTenantLookup(documentId || '', computedHash)` (`routes/verification.ts:910` at `d63b27ab3`). Inside, the registry is searched by `document_id` FIRST (`:417-421`), then the tenant DB by hash, **then it falls back to** `WHERE d.external_id = $1` **by documentId (**`:457-466`**)** — and the returned row goes to `buildResponse(docRow, true, …)` (`:1087`) with `hashMatch` hard-coded **true**. So `{documentId:X, <alias>:WRONG}` with a registry hit for X answers `verified:true, hashValid:true` for a hash that does not match. Pre-existing for `contentHash` / `providedHash` / `documentHash`; #965 adds `hash` as a fourth key into the same path (no caller sends it). **Dormant in the live single-tenant configuration** (`db.ts:22, 347-359`: `tenantManager` is built only with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`); severity there would be Major (a confident false "verified"). Adjacent, not the same defect: KS-590 (Peter, parked on KS-584) covers the by-hash path resolving to an arbitrary registration and names `crossTenantLookup` as unscoped; this ticket is the by-documentId fallback plus the hard-coded `hashMatch`.

## Recommendation

1. **Prove it first, live:** one probe with multi-tenancy enabled — register X in tenant A, send `{documentId:X, contentHash:<wrong 64-hex>}` from a caller whose local SELECT misses, and record the answer. Expected today: `verified:true`. The gate could not drive it (`getTenantManager()` was null in every row).
2. **Fix-shape (for the owner):** never pass `hashMatch=true` from the by-id fallback — compute it by comparing the row's `content_hash` with the sent hash (as the local path does), or refuse the by-id fallback when a hash was supplied and does not match. Add one cell per alias (`hash`, `contentHash`, `providedHash`, `documentHash`) asserting `verified:false` / `hashValid:false` for a wrong hash with a registry hit.
3. Sequence with KS-584 / KS-590 (the resolution-model decision) so the assertion pins a chosen behaviour.

## Detail

* **Where (READ ONLY at** `d63b27ab3`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` — `:910` the `crossTenantLookup(documentId || '', computedHash)` call from strategy 1; `:417-421` registry search by `document_id`; `:457-466` the `WHERE d.external_id = $1` fallback; `:1087` `buildResponse(docRow, true, …)`; `db.ts:22, 347-359` the multi-tenancy gate.
* **Callers that send the pairing today:** mcp-server (`{documentId, contentHash}`), e2e-v2 (`{documentId, providedHash}`), USER_TESTING v2.3's "Wrong hash → verified=false" cell — the last is the exact shape that would read TRUE under multi-tenancy.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1103-965-d63b27ab3-tier2-r1/report.md`, "Observations, out of #965's scope", O-1; NOT TESTED names the path as not driven.
* **Related:** KS-1103 (PR #965, where `hash` joined the chain); KS-590 (the by-hash / cross-tenant field-disclosure half, parked on KS-584); KS-584 (the resolution-model decision).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived) and 899 comments — `crossTenantLookup` → KS-584 (archived), KS-590 only; `hashMatch` → KS-563 only (isCertified vs verified, a different flag). Neither describes the by-id fallback answering a wrong hash TRUE. Controls: `LIKE` → KS-1020; a nonsense token → 0.

title: Verify presents a later hash-only registrant as the certifier: org B registers hash H, org A registers the SAME hash and certifies its copy, and verify(H) says certified by A (no lineage path, no forged field). Product ruling: which registrant?
description:
**PRODUCT RULING PENDING - NO BUILD.** Which registrant should `POST /api/verification/verify` present as the certifier when two organisations have registered the SAME content hash? Today a later, hash-only registrant outranks the original, so one organisation can make another organisation's bytes verify as certified by itself without any forged field. This ticket carries the facts and the question; it is not an instruction to build.

## What was measured (Seat J 5th, 2026-10-12, scratch probe on the real routes, real Postgres, as `secuura_app`, single-tenant and pool mode identical)

1. Organisation B's user registers hash H (`POST /api/documents`, 201). `verify {contentHash: H}` answers `isCertified: false` and no `certification`.
2. Organisation A's user registers the SAME hash H as A's own document: **201**. Duplicate hashes across organisations are accepted; K never receives the bytes, so there is no proof of possession.
3. A calls `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `documentId` = A's own document (the legacy certify path; allowed, the caller is the owner, and PR #1525 / KS-1538 keeps it allowed) and `data.issuedBy: "Org A"`: **201**.
4. `verify {contentHash: H}` now answers `isCertified: true` and `certification.certifiedBy: "Org A"`. The two rows: B's stays `anchored` (owner B); A's is `certified` (owner A). `selectVerifiableRow` (`verification.ts`) prefers a `certified` row, so the later registrant outranks the original.
5. Also seen there: `certification.certifierOrganizationId` carries A's **user** id (`certMeta.issuerId = issuer.id`), not an organisation id.

No lineage path and no forged field is involved, so none of the KS-1557 fixes (parent access check, hash bound to the parent, reserved keys stripped, `siblingCertification` resolving the certification) closes this.

## The product question

Which registrant does verify present as the certifier for bytes registered more than once? Candidate shapes (not ranked, not ruled): present a certification only when the certifying organisation holds the ORIGINAL (earliest, or earliest anchored) registration of those bytes; or present every registrant's certification as a list and say which registrant is which (the KS-584 P3 lookup contract); or keep today's behaviour and say so in the contract.

## Relation to other tickets (read, not duplicates)

* **KS-584** (Deployed to UAT, P1) decides what correct resolution means for verify-by-hash and shipped `selectVerifiableRow` as an interim; **KS-590** (Backlog) is its parked regression. This ticket is the trust facet of the same selection: it does not ask for a different interim, it asks which registrant may be presented as certifier.
* **KS-1557** (High): the lineage-path forgery. **KS-1538** (PR #1525): the legacy certify path now needs access to the document.

## Evidence

`5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatJ-5th/evidence/ks1557/`: `probe.integration.test.ts.txt` (cell PB), `probe1557_false.json` and `probe1557_true.json` (the two runs), and the two jest logs.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for five terms on two organisations registering the same hash, `selectVerifiableRow`, duplicate hash across organisations, which registrant is the certifier, and hash-only registration without proof of possession. 200 distinct issues read. Literal matches: `selectverifiablerow` 0, `duplicate hash` 0, `multi-registrant` 0. The only issue matching two or more of eight distinctive tokens was KS-1557; I read KS-584, KS-590, KS-598 and KS-735, and none states this question. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked: "none in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

Source: Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:28Z) that it is filed now as its own High ticket with the label "product ruling pending", no build; she takes the registrant question to Kam.

title: Claude Code sessions have no secret-file guard on platform-k: add the PS-1361 hook with PS-1387's local-only exemption, covering every systemTest env and secrets file (and .env.stripe is not git-ignored)
description:
## BLUF

platform-s blocks a Claude Code session from printing a secret file ([PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule)), and is about to let through files that hold only local values ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot), [Secuura/platform-s#1199](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1387-secret-file-guard-lets-local-only-values-through-55c48feacc56), In Review). **platform-k has neither.** At `develop` `bd6697e07` the repo's tracked `.claude/` holds only `skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md`: no `settings.json` and no hook. Nothing stops a session from running `cat`, `grep` or `diff` on `Blockchain/Dev/.env` (PII keys, JWT keys, datastore passwords), `.env.local` (OAuth and IdP credentials) or any systemTest secrets file. The only protection is a rule the session has to remember. [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) exists because that failed on platform-s on 26 Oct 2026 (`terraform fmt -check -diff .` printed every dev-ps secret).

Separately, `.env.stripe`-style files, which are planned, are **not git-ignored** on platform-k today (measured below).

## Verified (28 Oct 2026, K `develop` `bd6697e07`)

**K has no guard:** `git ls-files .claude` returns only the skill file.

**systemTest env and secrets files: tracked templates, and the real file each produces (all git-ignored, checked with** `git check-ignore` **on the file path):**

| Real file (git-ignored) | Template (tracked) | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `systemTest/playwright/.env` | `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` | Playwright credentials and targets |
| `systemTest/akto/.env` | `systemTest/akto/.env.example` | Akto harness env |
| `systemTest/akto/docker.env` | `systemTest/akto/docker.env.example` | Akto container env |
| `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.example.yml` | Akto role credentials |
| `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.example.yml` | k6 credentials |
| `systemTest/schemathesis/.env-slot<N>` | written by `scripts/run.py setup` | per-slot API token |
| `.env-*` slot credential files ([KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs), root `.gitignore:14-16`) | written by tooling | slot-scoped credentials |

`systemTest/performance/config/environments.yml` is tracked. Whether it may name a secret value is not established.

**platform-k product code: env and credential files the services, frontends and deployments read.** Each was checked with `git check-ignore` on the real file path, 28 Oct 2026, `bd6697e07`.

| Real file | Template (tracked) | Ignored? | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env` | `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (canonical, [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap)); also `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | yes | PII encryption and lookup keys, JWT keypair, datastore passwords, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local` | `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` (also `env.local.example`) | yes | OAuth / IdP client secrets |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/<svc>/.env` for analytics, anchoring, api-gateway, auth, billing, governance, guardian, kyc, m365-integration, nft-certificate, originate, prism, queue, referral, security, staking, timestamping, transfer, vc-issuer, wallet-connector (20 services) | `services/<svc>/.env.example` | yes, all 20 | per-service secrets (billing: Stripe keys; m365: Microsoft app secret; kyc: provider keys) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/` real file for its second template | `services/billing/env.example` | **not established**: the real file name for this no-dot template is unknown | Stripe keys |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/.env.staging` | `deployment/azure/env.staging.example` | yes | Azure staging deployment values |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/cardano/.env` | `deployment/cardano/env.example` | yes | Cardano node / wallet configuration |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/{admin,issuer,verifier}/.env.development` | none tracked | yes | frontend local overrides |
| `Blockchain/Dev/test-wallet.env`, `Blockchain/Dev/*.wallet.env` | none | yes (`.gitignore:133-135`) | wallet seed phrases |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/ssl/*.pem`, `*.key` | none | yes (`.gitignore:70-72`) | TLS private keys |
| `.keys/`, `credentials.json`, `*-credentials.json` | none | yes (`.gitignore:93`, `:138-139`) | key material, service-account credentials |
| `USER_TESTING/Testing Harness/handoff/` | none | yes (`.gitignore:185-186`) | super-admin login handoff |
| `observability/.env`, `observability/config/alerting.env` | `observability/.env.example`, `observability/config/alerting.env.example` | yes | alerting webhooks and tokens |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/.env.stripe` (planned style) | none | **NOT ignored** | would hold Stripe keys |

Every row except the last belongs in the hook's refuse list, and none qualifies for the local-only exemption: these are product secrets, not systemTest targets. The "Holds" column is from the template names and the service's purpose, not from opening any real file.

`.env.stripe` **is not git-ignored:**

```
K  systemTest/.env.stripe          NOT-ignored
K  Blockchain/Dev/.env.stripe      NOT-ignored
```

K's root `.gitignore` names `.env`, `.env-*`, `.env.local` and a fixed list of `.env.<stage>` names, not `.env.*`. A Stripe file created today could be committed.

## Proposed scope (for the owner to decide)

1. **A PreToolUse hook for Bash, Read and Grep**, `onFailure: block`, modelled on platform-s's `.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py`:
   * it refuses any reader (cat, grep, sed, diff, jq, base64, …) pointed at the files above, plus Terraform state, plans and tfvars, and an unformatted `docker inspect` or `docker exec … env` on K containers;
   * it allows a command that only names a file (`ls`, `stat`, `test -f`, `git check-ignore`);
   * it allows a single-field `docker inspect --format`, which the K build proof uses for `org.opencontainers.image.revision`.
2. [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)**'s local-only exemption, if Kamil agrees.** A systemTest env file whose every URL / base-URL key points at `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` is readable. Anything remote, missing or unreadable stays secret. `Blockchain/Dev/.env` **and** `.env.local` **stay guarded whatever their URLs**, because they hold real PII-encryption, JWT and OAuth material.
3. **A** `.gitignore` **rule for** `.env.*` **env files** (`.env.stripe` and successors) that keeps every `*.example` template tracked.
4. **A contract test pinning what the hook refuses and allows**, as platform-s's `SecretReadHookContractTests` does. Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.

**Why it matters for running the suites.** Building K, building S and running every systemTest suite need these files created and merged from their templates. With a guard on K, the exemption in item 2 decides which K files a session can merge blind. That needs settling before the guard lands, or the env-setup step breaks the same way.

## Runs on a developer's Mac, as platform-s#1199 does

platform-s#1199 ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)) is written for a developer's own Mac running local stack slots. The platform-k guard should take the same shape:

* **Where it runs.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook on the Mac, registered in `.claude/settings.json` as `python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<name>.py"`, `onFailure: block`. `python3` ships with macOS (Xcode Command Line Tools), so no install is needed. `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the session's project folder, normally the root checkout, not a ticket worktree. A guard change therefore takes effect once the root checkout is on a `develop` that contains it.
* **What "this machine" means.** As in #1199: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `[::1]`. A systemTest env file is exempt only while every URL / base-URL key in it points there. That covers the local slots `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` 1–4, gateway `6882 + 100·(N−1)`. A file pointed at Kintsugi, demo-pk, Container Apps or any remote host stays secret, and so does a missing or unreadable file.
* **Still guarded on the Mac, as in #1199:**
  * a bare `env` / `printenv`, because the developer's shell holds real tokens;
  * the product files in the table above, which are real keys even on a laptop;
  * Terraform state, plans and tfvars.
* **K slot containers (**`secuura-s<N>-*`**, and slot 1's** `secuura-*`**).** Unlike platform-s's slot containers, they are **not** exempt. Their environment comes from `Blockchain/Dev/.env` and `.env.local` (PII and JWT keys, OAuth secrets). An unformatted `docker inspect`, or `docker exec … env` / `printenv`, is refused. A single-field `docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}'` and `--format '{{.RestartCount}}'` stay allowed, because the build proof needs them.
* **macOS tools.** The rules match on command text, so they must hold for BSD `sed`, `grep`, `stat` and `xargs` as well as GNU forms.
* **A search pattern that names a secret file is not a read** (the #1199 false-positive fix). For example, `grep -E 'tfvars|tfstate' .gitignore` is allowed. A secret file as a file operand, or as the value of `-f`, is still refused. This session's own grep of K's `.gitignore` was refused by platform-s's guard for exactly this reason.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **An automated test, offline on macOS.** A contract test, run by the K preflight and the pre-push hook with no stack up, drives the hook through `python3` on the Mac. It covers:
   * a refused and an allowed case for every file in the tables above;
   * a localhost, a remote-URL and a missing-file case for each exempt systemTest file;
   * the K-container `docker inspect` / `exec` rules;
   * a search-pattern-only grep (allowed);
   * a `.env.stripe` file that is git-ignored while its `.example` is not.

   Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.
2. **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` → security section, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, name the guard, the exemption and the file list. `Projects Documents/Stack-Slots-How-To.md` is changed only if the env-setup steps change.
3. **systemTests:** no spec, page object or fixture change. The guard's test is a contract test. Each systemTest `.env.example` should say in a comment whether its real file is exempt.

## Related

* [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) (the platform-s guard).
* [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot) / platform-s#1199 (the local-only exemption, In Review).
* [KS-1608](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1608/akto-harness-writes-credentials-to-disk-and-into-reports-reportjson) (Akto credentials written to reports, Done).
* [KS-1098](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1098/k6-runner-echo-mask-enamevalue-and-qe-namevalue-still-print-the-value) (k6 echo mask).
* [KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs) (slot credential files).
* [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap) (env template drift).

Raised from the [PS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1381/systemtest-a11y-keyboard-journey-power-user-keyboard-enter-on-the) session. **Not assigned:** the `.claude/` tooling owner on platform-k is undecided. The systemTest parts are Peter's, the rest is Kamil's.

title: e2e gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts cells 15.2.2 and 15.2.3 POST a DSR body the route refuses with 400 (subjectEmail and reason, not userId and email)
description:
## BLUF

Cells `15.2.2 Request data access` and `15.2.3 Request data erasure` in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts` POST a DSR body that the create route refuses, so each should read 400 where it asserts 200, 201 or 202. **Neither cell was run.** The shape was measured on the cell next door (15.2.5, KS-1113), which sends the same two fields, and on the route directly.

## What the code says

* The cells (develop `bd6697e079fc`): 15.2.2 sends `subjectEmail` and `reason` (lines 332-333) and asserts `[200, 201, 202].includes(res.status)` (line 339); 15.2.3 does the same (lines 357-358, assertion at 364).
* The route: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:321`, `POST /dsr`, takes `{ type, userId, email, notes }` and answers 400 `type, userId, and email are required` (line 325) when any of the first three is missing. `userId` is the uuid of a real user (the table's `user_id` is a foreign key; a non-uuid answers 404).

## Measured

Throwaway stack at develop `bd6697e079fc`: api-gateway, auth and originate run natively against one `postgres:15-alpine` and one `redis:7-alpine`; host Node v26.8.1, which is not an LTS line.

* `POST /api/gdpr/dsr` as the seeded admin with the cell's fields (`type`, `subjectEmail`, `reason`): **400** `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"type, userId, and email are required"}}`.
* The same route with the route's fields (`type`, `userId` = the admin's id from `GET /api/auth/me`, `email`, `notes`): **201** `{ success, request: { id, ... } }`.
* The 15.2.5 cell, which sends the same two wrong fields, failed at its create step in 30 ms ("Could not create DSR to test processing").
* **Not run:** cells 15.2.2 and 15.2.3 themselves.

## Fix shape

Test-only, in the spec: send the route's own fields (`userId` from `GET /api/auth/me`, `data.id`; `email`; `notes`), which makes 201 the answer the cells already accept. This is the change KS-1113 makes in 15.2.5. One test pass proves both cells, so they share this ticket.

## Dedupe, before filing

Literal census on 2026-10-28 over issue titles and descriptions, archived included, with a present control and a nonsense control: `15.2.2` 0 hits, `15.2.3` 0 hits, `gdpr-compliance.prelaunch` 1 hit (KS-1113 only), `subjectEmail` 2 hits (KS-537 and KS-466, both about the lifecycle-events payload, not the DSR route), nonsense token 0.

Related: KS-1113 (cell 15.2.5, same file).

title: ks1009 wallet-status cells pin the response BODY only: a leak through a response header or through the 500 error body passes the unit file — two gate mutants survived (pull request 1538 gate Minor M2)
description:
## BLUF

The `ks1009-wallet-status-reveals-only-existence.test.ts` cells that pin `GET /api/auth/wallet/status` to `{ exists }` read **the response body and nothing else**. Two of the gate's mutants exploited that and **survived**: one puts the user id in a response **header** with the body untouched, the other makes the **error path** echo into the 500 body. **No such leak exists in the code today** — the gate verified the real route against a real database — so this is a guard gap, not a live defect.

Source: the pull request 1538 gate (KS-1009), Sonnet tier 2, report sha256/16 `d1d48d9c8fd56dd6`, Minor M2 and §5. Filed before that merge, on Wednesday's instruction.

## The two surviving mutants

| mutant | what it does | why every cell stays green |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **N3** | returns the id in an `X-User-Id` response header, body unchanged | no cell reads response headers |
| **N8** | the error path echoes a message / param into the 500 body | no cell makes `query` throw, so the error path is never entered |

For contrast, the mutants that **were** killed (M1-M4 restoring `userId` / `role` / `createdAt` / the row spread, N1 `uid`, N2 `ref`, N5 `201`, N6 `exists:'true'`, N12 a padded extra key) all change the 200 body, which is the one surface cells 1 and 2 read.

## What the cells read today

* **Cell 1** — `Object.keys(response) === ['exists']` on the registered address.
* **Cell 2** — the raw response **text** is free of the seeded id, role and timestamp (including the literal `2026-01-02`).
* **Cell 5** — the yaml property list is exactly `['exists','message']`. **Cell 6** — the operation description.

Note `WalletStatusResponse` keeps `.passthrough()` (`services/auth/src/auth.openapi.ts` \~1517), so **Schemathesis cannot catch an added key either**. Cells 1 and 2 are the only thing pinning the trim at the handler, and they pin one surface of it.

## Fix shape (the gate's, unchanged)

1. **Header cell** — assert the registered-address response carries only the Express defaults (`x-powered-by`, `content-type`, `content-length`, `etag`, `date`, `connection`, `keep-alive`) and no id/role/date header. The gate recorded exactly that set at `content-length: 15`, so the expected list is already measured.
2. **Error-path cell** — stub `db.query` to throw, drive the route, assert the 500 body is the generic `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred"}}` and carries no seeded id, role or timestamp.

Each cell should be red-first against the matching mutant (N3 for 1, N8 for 2) before it is believed.

## Evidence that there is no live leak

Gate §2, over the **real** route with a **real** PostgreSQL 15 and the real `auth_find_user_by_wallet` SECURITY DEFINER function, as `secuura_app` (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, RLS forced on `users`; a direct `SELECT` as that role is `permission denied`, which is the control that the function is the only path):

* registered address → head answers exactly `{"exists":true}`, **15 bytes, one key**; headers are the Express defaults listed above, **no id/role/date header**.
* `%00`, `<registered>%00` and a malformed `%E0%A4%A` → **500 on both develop and head** with the identical generic body, **no row and no pg message echoed**.

So both mutant shapes are hypothetical today. The gap is that nothing would notice if they stopped being hypothetical.

## Related

* \[\[KS-1009\]\] — the parent fix (pull request 1538), where these cells live.
* \[\[KS-1053\]\] — the other Minor of the same gate (the ks949 walk timeout); commented there rather than filed, since that ticket is its home.

title: k6 runner echo mask: -e=NAME=VALUE and -qe NAME=VALUE still print the value, contrary to its JSDoc; the name set and BASE_URL userinfo are open; PASSWD is unpinned (QA-958-1..3)
description:
## BLUF

* PR #958 (KS-1094) masks secret values in the k6 runner's echoed docker command. Its tier-2 QA gate returned GO WITH FINDINGS at `ffb285752` and found three gaps in that mask. None sits on a path the shipping CLI takes today.
* **QA-958-1 (Minor, latent):** two spellings docker accepts, `-e=NAME=VALUE` and the clustered `-qe NAME=VALUE`, print the value in clear. The fix's own JSDoc says "Every spelling docker accepts is covered".
* **QA-958-2 (Polish):** credential-shaped names outside the masked word set, and a BASE_URL carrying userinfo, print in clear. No name the runner emits today falls in that gap.
* **QA-958-3 (Polish):** `PASSWD` is in the masked set, but no test cell pins it.
* Medium because a merged comment overclaims a security property, not because anything leaks today.

## Recommendation

* The name set is Peter's to confirm. The QA-958-2 list below is input to that decision. The gate recommends redacting URL userinfo in BASE_URL whichever way the name set goes.
* Then one fix round on `k6_docker.ts` and its redaction test: resolve QA-958-1 (narrow the JSDoc, or handle both spellings) and add the `PASSWD` row (QA-958-3).
* The fix-shapes below are the QA gate's proposals, not decisions. Re-read the code before editing.

## Detail

* **Source:** the tier-2 gate report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1094-958-ffb285752-tier2-r1/report.md` (findings QA-958-1..3, observation O-1).
* **Lines** under `systemTest/performance/` are cited at the gated head `ffb28575223dbd611a91242e3cd711aaeb3085b7` for the two #958 files, and at develop `8515d1db7fb52e783610812480f7a720fc193d6e` for the rest. All were re-read on 2026-09-12 and are unchanged in the merged tree `ceaa132f`.
* **No credential value appears here.** Every value the gate used was a sentinel it wrote into a fixture.
* **One ticket for three findings:** one fix round on one file and its test, proven by one run of the performance unit suite. QA-958-4 is a separate fix in other files and has its own ticket.

### QA-958-1 · Minor · latent: two docker spellings print the value

* **Where** (`runner/k6_docker.ts`):
  * :99, the JSDoc claim "Every spelling docker accepts is covered";
  * :83, `if (separator <= 0)` returns the assignment unchanged, inside `maskEnvAssignment` (:80);
  * :115, the two-argument branch matches only an exact `-e` or `--env`;
  * :122, the glued `-e` branch.
* **Measured by the gate** (a probe with `spawnSync` replaced, at the head and at the merged tree):
  * `-e=NAME=VALUE` and `-qe NAME=VALUE` both read CLEAR, the sentinel printed once, on the docker side and on the k6 side;
  * the four handled spellings read MASKED;
  * at the merge-base every valued shape leaks (48 of 48), which shows the probe can see a leak;
  * the argv is intact in every row.
* **Mechanism (read only):**
  * `-e=NAME=VALUE`: the glued branch passes `=NAME=VALUE` to `maskEnvAssignment`, where `indexOf('=')` is 0, so the guard returns it unchanged.
  * `-qe NAME=VALUE`: the previous argument is `-qe`, not `-e`, so the assignment is never inspected.
* **Does docker accept them?** Read only, not run: docker and k6 both parse flags with spf13/pflag, which reads `-e=VALUE` as the value `VALUE` and `-qe VALUE` as `-q -e VALUE`.
* **Why latent:** `buildEnvFlags()` emits only the two-argument `-e` form (`runner/env_flags.ts:143`), and `runner/cli.ts:221` hard-codes `extraFlags: []`. The shipping CLI produces neither spelling.
* **Fix-shape, the gate's proposal — one of:**
  * (a) narrow the JSDoc to the four spellings actually handled;
  * (b) handle both: strip one leading `=` after `-e`, and treat a short-flag cluster ending in `e` as the two-argument form;
  * (c) mask by value: `runK6` (:168) knows which secret-named assignments it was given, so it can replace those exact values anywhere in the rendered line. The cost is over-masking when a value is a short common substring.
* **Regression test:** two `it.each` rows (`-e=NAME=VALUE`, `-qe NAME=VALUE`), each asserting the echo lacks the value and the argv keeps it.

### QA-958-2 · Polish: names outside the set, and BASE_URL userinfo (input to the name-set decision)

* **Where:** `runner/k6_docker.ts:70`, `SECRET_ENV_NAME = /PASSWORD|PASSWD|SECRET|TOKEN|MNEMONIC|(?:^|_)KEY$/i`.
* **Printed in clear by the gate's probe**, at the head and at the merged tree:
  * `DB_PASS`;
  * `APIKEY` (no underscore);
  * `PRIVATE_KEY_PEM` (KEY is not the last segment);
  * `AUTH_BEARER`;
  * `SESSION_COOKIE`;
  * `AWS_CREDENTIALS`;
  * a name ending `_PWD`;
  * `OTP_SEED`;
  * `PERF_BASE_URL` holding a URL with userinfo.
* **Over-masking, the accepted cost:** `SORT_KEY`, a non-secret `_KEY`, reads MASKED.
* **Not a live leak.**
  * The runner emits 26 env names, the same list at head, merge-base, merged tree and develop.
  * 3 carry credentials (`ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `ISSUER_PASSWORD`, `VERIFIER_PASSWORD`), and all 3 are masked.
  * The other 23 are non-secret and print in clear.
  * `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is read from the host environment for the annotation push and is never passed to docker.
* **BASE_URL is the one conditional carrier.** If `config/environments.yml` `baseUrl` or `PERF_BASE_URL` held userinfo, the password would print:
  * in the echo (measured);
  * in the banner, `runner/cli.ts:260` (read only);
  * in `run-metadata.json` as `baseUrl`, `runner/run_metadata.ts:34` (read only);
  * in the HTML report's Target row, `runner/report_header.ts:122` (read only).
  * The tracked `environments.yml` has 4 `baseUrl` lines, 0 with userinfo.
* **Fix-shape if the set is widened, the gate's proposal:**
  * `PASS` only as a whole segment (a bare substring matches `BYPASS` and `PASSPORT`);
  * `PWD`, `CREDENTIAL`, `COOKIE`, `BEARER` and `SEED` as segments, and a `KEY` segment anywhere rather than only last;
  * for URLs, redact userinfo: parse with `new URL()` and set the password to `***`.
* **Regression test:** one row per word added, plus a userinfo row.

### QA-958-3 · Polish: PASSWD is unpinned

* The gate replaced `PASSWD` in the regex with a nonsense word. tsc rc 0; the unit suite ran 48 files / 537 tests with 0 failed.
* Every other clause of the mask reddened exactly the cells the gate predicted before the run.
* The behaviour is right (a `WALLET_PASSWD` row reads MASKED). It is only unpinned.
* **Regression test:** add a `PASSWD`-named row to the `it.each` at `tests/unit/runner/k6DockerRedaction.test.ts:178`.

### Recorded, not reconciled: O-1

* The persona passwords still travel in docker's argv as `-e NAME=VALUE`, by design: the mask covers the echo only. While the docker CLI runs, the values sit in the host process table.
* A structural alternative: pass a bare `-e NAME` and give `spawnSync` an `env` carrying the values. Docker forwards host values, which takes them out of the argv and the echo together.
* Not introduced by #958. Not measured.

title: Migration 055 test hardening (gate CN1 N2, N3, N5): the tenant scope is half pinned, REPORT is not hermetic, and the cell file's header is stale
description:
## BLUF

**Three test-only gaps that gate CN1 found in migration 055's cell file after the code was already correct.** Nothing here is a migration defect — the gate verified the shipped 055 skips every shape below. What is missing is the cells that would stop a future change re-opening them, plus one stale header. One ticket, three items, all in `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1557-055-backfill.integration.test.ts`.

Source: gate CN1's verdict on pull request 1654, notes N2, N3 and N5. 055 merged on 2026-10-20 as `32964477fe8828eb78240150e8ab59bd8179f339`.

## Item 1 (N2) — the tenant scope is only half pinned

`CROSSTENANT` kills the mutant that unscopes **both** halves of the cross-check (2 red, by assertion). **Two equally fail-open variants pass 17/17:**

* **O3** — remove `ap.tenant_id = p.tenant_id` from the `parent_agrees` half only. On the gate's fixture this credits `gx-K52` to c1 (the parent's own-tenant row names c2, and a row filed under T2 names c1) and also credits `gx-K30` to c7.
* **O4** — scope on the **child's** tenant (`d.tenant_id`) instead of the parent's. This credits `gx-K53`: the parent sits in T1 with no own-tenant row, and the child plus a planted row both sit in T2. That is the exact forgery shape the migration header gives as its reason for scoping on the parent.

The shipped code skips K52, K53 and K30. **Two cells are needed**, one per variant, so each half of the scope is pinned separately rather than only the conjunction.

Inert detail worth a comment rather than a cell: `gx-K31` (child in T2, parent in T1, corroborated in T1) is credited and its row lands in T2.

## Item 2 (N3) — the REPORT cell is not hermetic

055 is global; the `REPORT` cell compares **every** printed skipped id against a set scoped to the run's own tenant. One foreign, uncreditable, version-minted document in a third tenant therefore fails the cell by assertion. The file header's claim — *"one tenant of this run's own, so the cells cannot read another seat's rows"* — is false for that cell.

By the same mechanism (read from the code, not measured): on a **shared** integration database the FORWARD and RLS runs insert `create:connector` rows on other tenants' candidates, and `afterAll` deletes only this run's two tenants, so those rows survive the suite.

Fix shape: scope the report comparison to the run's tenants, and make the cleanup cover what the run can write — not only what it created.

## Item 3 (N5) — the test file's header still carries round-2 cite drift

* Lines 13-14 give `/:id/sign-cert` (`:2891`) and `/:id/sign-wallet` (`:3159`). At the merged head those are `:2905` and `:3173`.
* Line 18 states *"server-set on all three minting routes since KS 1508"* as the premise, and only the next paragraph corrects it. That is the premise blocker B2 was about; stating it unqualified first is the thing that misled round 2.

The **migration** header's cites were checked by the gate and are all correct (`:124`, `:158`, `:2347`, `:2905`, `:3092`, `:3173`, `:3287`, `:617-618`).

## Why this is a separate ticket

Round 3 was the last round Kam allowed on pull request 1654 (card `secuura-ks1557-055-second-nogo-round3-1020`, tapped (a)). The gate's instruction was explicit: record these, do not change code or tests in that pull request, file one follow-up. This is it.

## Not in scope here

Gate CN1's **N1** (corroboration is per parent, not per child) is a product-behaviour residue, not a test gap, and carries a kintsugi counting precondition before 055 runs there — it stays on KS-1557 and with the coordinator, not on this ticket.

title: Develop-wide push freeze: GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 (deepmerge 4.3.1, LOW, no patched version) refused by preflight legs 6 and 7 since ~2026-10-27T21:35Z
description:
## BLUF

Every push to this repository is refused by the pre-push preflight (legs 6 and 7) because a new advisory, GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4, is reported against `deepmerge` 4.3.1 and there is **no patched version**. The gate's only route is a reasoned baseline entry. The first refusal this seat saw was at 2026-10-28T03:00Z; the advisory record was updated at 2026-10-27T21:34:58Z, which is when this probably began (inference, not measured). A decision is with Kam, because the same version is a production dependency in one shipped tree (see below). Nothing is baselined and nothing was bypassed.

## What the gate printed (verbatim)

From the pre-push hook of Seat W 4th's push of branch feature/ks-1773-..., 2026-10-28 02:46Z to 03:00Z, at develop `65bc28234507` plus a 5-file change that touches no lockfile, no `package.json` and not `scripts/audit/`. Final line: `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 6 7 - fix the above before pushing. (13/16 legs ran)`

Leg 6:

```
=== 6/16  npm-audit gate (advisories vs triaged baseline — KS-470) ===
audit-gate: 10 distinct advisories reported, 10 baselined.

CLEANUP (advisory): 1 baseline entry is no longer reported — remove:
  - GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, KS-1403)

FAIL — 1 NEW advisory not in the baseline:
  - GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 [low] deepmerge: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
    https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4
  Triage it: fix the dependency, or add a reasoned entry (reason + ticket) to scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json.
FAIL — new or lapsed advisories; triage them (fix, or reasoned baseline entry with a ticket)
```

Leg 7:

```
=== 7/16  standalone-lock advisories (each service's OWN lock — KS-531) ===
audit-locks: 44 standalone lockfiles (46 tracked, minus the Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json workspace root which audit-gate covers, minus 1 declared out of scope = 46 - 1 - 1 = 44; reproduce the tracked count with `git ls-files '*package-lock.json' | wc -l`; out of scope: Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app (KS-769, expires 2027-01-01: React Native app tree, not built by any compose file (0 references against a control of 2 for services/originate) or by any workflow (0 against a control of 3 referencing services/). 81 advisories (2 critical, 45 high) pending their own triage rather than 81 unmeasured baseline rows.)), 1625 distinct packages pinned — 8 advisories match, 7 already baselined.

FAIL — 1 advisory in standalone locks and NOT in the baseline:
  - GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 [low] deepmerge: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
    pinned: 4.3.1
    in 4 lock(s): services/governance, services/originate, services/referral, services/vc-issuer
  Triage each: bump the pin (containerised per-dir regen — see lockfile-cleanroom.sh),
  or add a reasoned entry (reason + ticket + expires) to scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json.
FAIL — a standalone lock pins an advisory the root audit cannot see; triage it (bump the pin, or a reasoned baseline entry with a ticket)
```

## Reproduce

`cd Blockchain/Dev && npm run audit:gate` and `npm run audit:locks` both exit 1 at that develop (re-run 2026-10-28T03:01Z, same single advisory, working tree clean afterwards).

## The advisory

GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4, severity low: deepmerge `mergeObject()` allows prototype poisoning of returned objects. Vulnerable range >= 4.2.0, <= 4.3.1. First patched version: **none**, so bumping the pin is not available. GitHub's advisory record: published 2026-09-18, updated 2026-10-27T21:34:58Z. Seat W 3rd's last passing push ran legs 6 and 7 before about 21:16Z on 2026-10-27.

## The locks that pin deepmerge 4.3.1 (develop `65bc28234507`, read from the lockfiles)

Six in all:

* `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (the workspace root; leg 6 audits this one)
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/package-lock.json`
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/package-lock.json`
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/referral/package-lock.json`
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/package-lock.json` (these four are what leg 7 names)
* `Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app/package-lock.json`: NOT scanned by either leg. It is the one lock the gate declares out of scope (`OUT_OF_SCOPE_LOCKS` in `scripts/audit/lock-discovery.mjs`, ticket KS-769), so it does not cause this failure, but it pins the same version.

## Dev-only or shipped (Wednesday's measurement, lockfile level, develop `65bc28234507`; NOT an image read, and not re-measured by this seat)

`deepmerge` 4.3.1 is a **dev-only** dependency (via `jest-config`) in originate, governance, referral, vc-issuer and the workspace root, and those images install with `--omit=dev` / `prune --omit=dev`. In `mobile/secuura-app` it is a **production** dependency (via `@expo/config`). Under Kam's 2026-09-09 advisory rule, a package present in both a test lock and a shipped tree is Kam's decision regardless of severity, so the baseline entry is held for his ruling (default: hold).

## The gate's only route

A reasoned baseline entry in `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` (reason, ticket, expires). Nobody has added one; this ticket is the ticket such an entry would cite.

## Also in the gate output (non-failing)

Leg 6 prints `CLEANUP (advisory): 1 baseline entry is no longer reported`: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, KS-1403) can be removed from the baseline.

## Related

* KS-1723: develop-wide advisory freeze, second in five days (13 other ids).
* KS-1707: six baselined advisory rows lapse 2026-10-31 and 15 stale rows need removing. That is a second freeze three days out, so the same baseline file will be edited again.
* KS-1403: three range-widened HIGH advisories freeze every push; the stale braces row above belongs to it.
* KS-769: the mobile app tree is declared out of scope of the standalone-lock gate.

## Effect

Blocks pushing PR 1773 (KS-1773, a docs-and-wording round with its merge-in done locally at `4099c7971b35`). Any other seat that pushes is refused at legs 6 and 7 until this is resolved.

title: mcp-server api-client.ts types the response error as a string at three sites (:57, :105, :125) while the gateway's published ErrorResponse and its 401 bodies carry an object {code, message}
description:
## BLUF

**The MCP server's** `api-client.ts` **types a response's** `error` **field as a string at three sites, while the gateway's published error body carries an object** `{ code, message }`**; the one consumer that reads it,** `tools/info.ts`**, works round the mismatch with an** `as unknown as` **cast.** Nothing is failing: the cast and a string-or-`.message` test handle both shapes. It is recorded because the type says one thing and the wire says another, and a caller that trusts the type would relay `[object Object]` or the whole object.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.**

Refs KS-1620, KS-1541.

All line numbers were read at develop `061c3a4f62d563e723b8cee5fe792b4c27dc3014`. The finding is gate D's second NOTE on PR #1566, carried by KS-1620 as "Not carried here" and repeated in its PR comment as "not touched", and gate e's note on KS-1620 relayed by Wednesday. The code reads below are re-done here.

## 1 — The three declarations

`Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/api-client.ts` declares `error?: string;` at `:57`, `:105` and `:125`:

| line | function | path |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:57` | `registerDocument` | `'/api/documents'` (POST) |
| `:105` | `getWorkflowInstance` | the workflow-instance read |
| `:125` | `getConnectorInfo` | `'/api/connector/info'` |

`apiRequest` returns `{ status: res.status, ok: res.ok, data }` where `data` is the parsed body cast to the caller's type (`:41-42`), so the declared type is not checked against anything at runtime.

## 2 — What the gateway sends

In the published contract, `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`: `components.schemas.ErrorResponse` (`:123`) declares `error` as `type: object` with `code` and `message` required. `/api/connector/info` (`:15961`) answers its 401, 403 and 503 with `$ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"`.

In the gateway code: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1089-1094` answers a 401 with `error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Authentication required' }`, and `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:442` answers the same shape: `res.status(401).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Authentication required' } })`.

So for a refusal the gateway makes itself, the body's `error` is an object and the type at `api-client.ts:125` says string.

## 3 — How the one consumer copes

`Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/tools/info.ts:130` reads the field through a cast: `const gatewayError = (connectorResult?.data as unknown as { error?: unknown } | undefined)?.error;`. The next line accepts either a string or an object whose `.message` is a string and otherwise relays nothing. KS-1620 item 1 bounds the relayed text to 200 characters at the same place.

## Not established

* **The wire shape on the other two routes.** `registerDocument` (`:57`) and `getWorkflowInstance` (`:105`) are not traced here: what their non-gateway error paths send, and whether the yaml documents them with `ErrorResponse`, is not read.
* Whether any other caller of these three functions reads `data.error` expecting a string. Not searched.
* **I ran no suite.** These are source and contract reads.
* What to change, if anything. Not decided. KS-1620 records the gate's own view that it is "pre-existing and out of scope".

## Searched

Board, KS team, title + description + comment bodies, `includeArchived: true`, paged to the end. `api-client.ts` → **6 hits**: KS-1620, KS-1541, KS-1531, KS-1390, KS-1232, KS-950. `error?: string` → **1 hit**, KS-1620 (the "Not carried here" note). `data.error.message` → **2 hits**: KS-1620, KS-177 (archived, Done). `ApiResponse` → **0 hits**. KS-1620 and KS-1541 were read whole; neither holds the mismatch as a ticket. **Positive control** `KS-1531` → 27 hits. **Zero control:** a token coined for this read and written nowhere → 0 hits.

*Filed by Seat G 25th, 2026-10-27 UTC, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: originate: three L6 cells titled 'simulated true with a real hash' take the hash from a chainReply default and assert nothing about it (ks1634-v2-chain-only-match-carries-simulated.test.ts:117, ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash-verify-route.test.ts:107, ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash.test.ts:102)
description:
## BLUF

**Three originate test cells are titled "simulated true with a real hash" and exist to prove that** `chain.simulated` **is carried into the reply, but each takes its hash from a** `chainReply` **helper default (**`txHash: REAL_TX`**) and none of its assertions reads that hash. The presenter marks a reply simulated from a placeholder-shaped hash alone, so with a placeholder-shaped default these cells could pass without the fix.** Seat Y 1st measured this for one of the three; the other two are the same shape and were not measured. The item is carried over from KS-1634, where it is the only thing still open.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.**

Refs KS-1634, KS-1628.

All line numbers were read at develop `c18552d94de23b4da365ce02e02be5d06793bbcb`, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src` (`__tests__/` for the test files). develop has since moved one commit (#1770, 27 `package-lock.json` files); none of the paths below changed. This seat ran nothing.

## 1 — The three cells

* `__tests__/ks1634-v2-chain-only-match-carries-simulated.test.ts:117`: `it('RED KS-1634 L6 v2: simulated true with a real hash reads NOT on-chain', async () => {`. `:118` builds the reply as `callV2(chainReply({ simulated: true }))`. The helper `function chainReply` is at `:79` and its `txHash: REAL_TX` at `:84`; `REAL_TX` is declared at `:44`. The assertions at `:119`-`:125` are about the reply: `body.count`, `m.blockchain.simulated`, `m.blockchain.anchored`, `m.blockchain.txHash` null, `m.simulated`, `m.checks.isAnchored`.
* `__tests__/ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash-verify-route.test.ts:107`: `it('RED KS-1628 L6 verify: simulated true with a real hash is not on-chain', async () => {`. `:108` is `callSite(chainReply({ simulated: true }))`; `chainReply` is at `:75` with `txHash: REAL_TX` at `:80`. Assertions `:109`-`:112`: `body.blockchain.simulated` true, `body.blockchain.anchored` false, `body.blockchain.txHash` null, `body.checks.isAnchored` false.
* `__tests__/ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash.test.ts:102`: `it('RED KS-1628 L6 verify-file: simulated true with a real hash is not on-chain', async () => {`. `:103` is `callSite(chainReply({ simulated: true }))`; `chainReply` is at `:74` with `txHash: REAL_TX` at `:79`. Assertions `:104`-`:107`: the same four.

In none of the three does an assertion read the hash the cell sent. In the two verify files, the neighbouring cell ("the shape anchoring really sends (simulated true, txHash null)", `:115` and `:110`) overrides `txHash` with `null` and a `mock_tx_` reference, so it does not depend on the default.

## 2 — Why the hash matters here

`routes/verification.ts:52`: `const FABRICATED_TXHASH_RE = /^(tx_sim_|mock_tx_|mock_batch_tx_|tx_)/;`. `presentBlockchainHonestly` (`:54`) computes `const simulated = Boolean(b.simulated) || (tx !== undefined && FABRICATED_TXHASH_RE.test(tx));` at `:60`. So a blob whose hash matches that pattern is marked simulated whether or not `simulated` was copied into it. KS-1634's description records the same thing as a control row: "a placeholder hash, `simulated` absent: marked simulated YES". A cell meant to show that `simulated` is carried must therefore send a real hash, and it says "real hash" in its title; the only thing holding the hash real is the helper default.

## 3 — What is already pinned, and what was measured

* PR #1748 (`eedc4948b66d`) added `REAL_TX_SHAPE` (`ks1634-v2-chain-only-match-carries-simulated.test.ts:49`) and `expect(reply.txHash).toMatch(REAL_TX_SHAPE)` at `:159` and `:173`, in the two N3 cells of that file only. KS-1634's comment of 2026-10-19T16:10Z calls the gap for those two cells "one assertion in each of the two tests, checking that the hash is real".
* `REAL_TX_SHAPE` occurs in neither verify file (a search of each returned no line).
* Seat Y 1st, quoted in KS-1634's comment of 2026-10-27T07:11Z (not re-run here): with the `chainReply` default planted as a mock-prefixed hash in a copy, the v2 file reads 6 of 10 passing and both N3 cells stay green; its fixed version reads 4 of 10 with both N3 cells failing; and "the original RED cell 'simulated true with a real hash' depends on the same default and stays green under a mock-prefixed default in both files". Whether "both files" means the v2 file before and after, or two files, is not stated; the two verify files were not measured.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing.** Whether the two verify-file cells (`:107` and `:102`) stay green under a placeholder-shaped default is not measured; section 2 is a source read.
* Whether the v2 cell's assertions at `:119`-`:125` fail under such a default beyond what Seat Y 1st measured.
* What to do. Not decided.

title: CLASS: a module-level beforeAll that imports a router pays the cold Vite transform inside the hook budget - five locations, two fix shapes, no owner for the pattern
description:
## BLUF

**A test file whose module-level** `beforeAll` **imports a router pays the cold Vite transform inside the hook's budget, so the whole file's cells are skipped when the machine is loaded.** Five locations have hit this independently. Each has been fixed in its own place, by two different shapes, and **no ticket owns the pattern** — so the next service to grow such a file is on the default budget again. This ticket records the class and asks for one decision: a fleet-wide convention, or an explicit statement that per-location budgets are the convention.

Facts only; nothing is built and no fix is chosen. Raised as the class behind the tier-2 gate on #1727.

Refs KS-1734, KS-1602, KS-1155, KS-1328, KS-1729.

## The five instances, by key

| ticket | location | state | shape of the fix |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **KS-1734** | `services/security` — 10 files lapsed the 10 s hook, 1 test lapsed 5 s | merged `5c40e82cb539` | service-wide `hookTimeout`/`testTimeout` 60 s in `vitest.config.ts` |
| **KS-1602** | `services/security`, `ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts` alone | In Progress | explicit per-hook budget in the one file |
| **KS-1155** | `packages/shared` tree-walking guards over the 5 s default | In Progress | not read here |
| **KS-1328** | `services/kyc`, `db.retry.test.ts` | In Review | not read here |
| **KS-1729** | `vc-issuer` — first run after `npm ci` skips 110 cells, three files cold-import routers | Done | not read here |

The two shapes are in tension: KS-1602 budgets one file, KS-1734 budgets a whole service. Both are live in `services/security` at once — KS-1734's comment records that KS-1602's explicit per-hook budget "still overrides the default underneath, so that file's behaviour is unchanged."

## What #1727's gate measured, and the figure to carry

From the tier-2 gate on #1727 (`2026-10-27_gate-t3r4-batch/verdict.md`) and the evidence recorded on KS-1734, **quoted, not re-run by me**:

* The knob governs the failure class: `hookTimeout` forced to 25 ms → **18 files red**; `testTimeout` 25 ms → **11 files red**.
* The full ladder, each rung on a cold `.vite` cache: 1 ms → 23 of 33 files; 25 ms → 20; 100 ms → 19; 400 ms → 8; 1000 ms → 0; 10000 ms (the replaced default) → 0.
* **The governed population is WIDER than the ten files KS-1734 named.** 19 of 33 files already exceed a 100 ms hook. KS-1734's own comment carries this as a correction to its first wording — the PR had claimed the knob "governs exactly the files the ticket names", and the accurate figure is 18 at the `hookTimeout` rung, not 10.
* The hooks finish under 1 s at load1 3.3–6.6, against the 10 000 ms they blew at load1 11.21: **a >10x inflation under contention.**
* **Contention, not coldness, is the driver.** Four cold first-runs after `npm ci` at load1 3.31–4.44 each passed 33/33 — so KS-1734's red did not reproduce, and the budget change has **no red→green pair** behind it.

## The decision this ticket asks for

Not which budget — that is settled per location. The open question is the **convention**: a file that imports a router at module level inside `beforeAll` will exceed a short hook budget on a loaded box, and the budget masks the cost rather than removing it. Either

1. state a fleet-wide rule (for example: every service's `vitest.config.ts` carries a budget that clears the observed contention inflation, as `services/security` and its `vitest.integration.config.ts` now do), or
2. state that per-location budgets are the convention and that a new file is expected to set its own,

so that the sixth location is a known case rather than a new ticket.

## Not established

* No suite was run for this ticket and no measurement here is mine. Every figure above is quoted from the #1727 gate verdict or from KS-1734's comment.
* **Whether the cold Vite transform is the mechanism** in KS-1155, KS-1328 and KS-1729. Those three are cited from KS-1734's own "Same class, other places" list; their bodies were **not** read here, so the shared mechanism is KS-1734's attribution, not a finding of this ticket.
* Whether any location other than `services/security` currently lacks a budget. Not surveyed.
* Whether the >10x inflation figure generalises beyond `services/security` at this load.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `module-level beforeAll` — **0 hits**. `cold transform` — **0 hits**. `Vite transform` — **0 hits**. So no class ticket exists under any of those names.
* `hookTimeout` — **4 hits**: KS-1734, KS-1729, KS-1602, KS-1155 — the four instances, no class ticket.
* `first run after` — **4 hits**: KS-1739 (a Node 26 cbor defect, unrelated), KS-1734, KS-1729, KS-1053.
* `vitest.config.ts` — **12 hits**; the timeout family among them is the five instances above, the rest unrelated (KS-1582, KS-1319, KS-993, KS-846, KS-830, KS-177, KS-149).
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.
* **Decision recorded:** KS-1734 was read in full. This is **not** its residue — KS-1734 is scoped to `services/security` and its fix covers that whole service. What is unowned is the pattern across services, which is why this is filed rather than commented there.

*Filed by Seat G 22nd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: packages/shared tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under fleet load — 5 cells at load 32, 9 at load 25–49, 5,243 ms alone at load 27; assertions hold (green solo / with testTimeout raised / at load 11) — a load class that costs a re-run on every merge
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared`'s repo-tree-walking guard cells exceed vitest's 5 s default `testTimeout` when the box carries the fleet's load (several seats' suites + QA gates at once). The assertions hold every time — the same cells pass solo, or with `--testTimeout` raised, or on the same tree minutes later at a lower load. So a red `Test timed out in 5000ms` in these files on a loaded box is a **load class**, not a product finding — but a merge seat cannot tell that from the run alone without a solo re-run or a raised-timeout re-run, which costs minutes on every merge. Filed so the class has a name and a home (KS-1053 names it only as context for the `services/auth` ks949 cell, a different suite).

## The measurements (all 2026-09-14, all on trees where the guard files are blob-identical to develop)

* **s224 (quoted as s224's, from its STACK READY mail 02:54:51Z):** `packages/shared` 43 files / 835 — **830 passed / 5 failed at load 32**, every failure `Test timed out in 5000ms` in the tree-walking guards (`crypto-agility.guard.test.ts`, `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts:180` the CENSUS cell, `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:905`, `ks764-key-revoke-call-site-guard.test.ts:263`, `ks860-test-listeners-bind-loopback.test.ts:463`); **1 at load 34**; the same cells green solo (**5,243 ms alone at load 27** — over the 5 s budget even solo, under that load).
* **s220 (the merge seat, PRED(985)** `3239e7207`**,** `item11/suite985/`**):** run at load 25–49 — **835: 822 passed / 9 failed / 4 skipped**, all nine timeouts: `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts` (5 s), `ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` (5 s, the positive-control cell), `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts` ×4 (5 s: the CONTROL enumeration, the 🔴 corpus-is-the-shared-derivation cell, its CONTROL, the ROOTS-pinned cell), `ks764-key-revoke-call-site-guard.test.ts` (5 s, CALL_SITES), `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` ×2 (a 10 s **hook** timeout in KS-832's ACCEPTANCE BAR + LEG C 5 s), `threadToken.test.ts` (**30 s**, `parameteriseMintPolicy` different-seeds — a crypto cell, not a walk). Solo re-runs at load 47–49: four files green; `ks727` and `ks781` still one timeout each. With `--testTimeout 120000 --hookTimeout 120000` at load ~20: `ks727` **94/94**, `ks781` **231/231**. The full suite again with the raised timeouts at load 11: **43 / 835 / 0**.
* **s203 (KS-1053's context line, 2026-09-13):** three `Test timed out in 5000ms` in the same guards at load ~20.
* Not the same subject as KS-1053 (the `services/auth` ks949 cell, 5.7–6.0 s on a 5 s budget under load, mechanism unestablished) — related as the neighbouring load-class record.

## What this costs today

Every merge-seat run of `packages/shared` on a loaded box is a coin-flip red that has to be re-run solo or with the timeout raised before it can be read (the s220 protocol did both). The tree walks themselves are the guards' point (they read the whole `services/` + `packages/` tree by design); their budget is the default 5 s.

## Fix shapes (the owner's call)

1. A per-file `testTimeout` (and `hookTimeout`) for the tree-walking guards — 30–60 s — set in the test files or a `vitest.config` `test.testTimeout` override scoped to `__tests__/*guard*.test.ts`, so a slow walk under load is a slow walk, not a red. Keep the default for everything else.
2. Share one tree walk per run (a cached corpus) instead of one per cell — `entrypoint-corpus`, `ks727`, `ks781`, `ks860`, `ks879` each walk the tree; the walk is the cost.
3. `threadToken.test.ts`'s 30 s cell is a different shape (CPU-bound crypto); its own budget line.

## Done when

- [ ] the tree-walking guard cells carry an explicit timeout budget that a loaded box meets (measured: a full `packages/shared` run at load ≥ 30 reads 0 timeouts), or the walk is shared and the cells fit the default
- [ ] the merge-seat protocol no longer needs a solo re-run to read a `packages/shared` result on a loaded box

title: ks1531-connector-info-is-in-the-published-contract.test.ts:163 - the R2 cell's title names the authenticator its two assertions cannot discriminate (index.ts:1089-1095 and middleware/auth.ts:442 are the same 401)
description:
## BLUF

**The R2 cell's title says its 401 comes "from authenticateToken and not from the edge", and nothing the cell observes can establish that.** The edge auth gate's 401 body and `authenticateToken(true)`'s are identical in status, code and message, and R2's only other assertion — an absent `Allow` header — separates the *method* gate, not the *auth* gate. The file's own header already records the limit; the cell's title still makes the claim.

The claim happens to be **true**, for reasons stated in section 3 — but it is established by reading the source, not by this cell. A reader who takes the test name as evidence takes it on trust.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed**: rewording the title and finding a discriminating observable are both open, and the choice belongs to whoever owns the cell.

Refs KS-1752, KS-1531, KS-1747.

All line numbers read at develop `885d69b06f5fce7c8f58effea68623ecb25407b1`.

## 1 — The claim, and the two assertions behind it

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1531-connector-info-is-in-the-published-contract.test.ts:163`, verbatim:

`it('🔴 KS-1531 R2 — an unauthenticated GET is unchanged: still 401 UNAUTHORIZED "Authentication required", from authenticateToken and not from the edge', async () => {`

Its body is two assertions, `:165-166`:

`expect([get.status, get.code, get.message]).toEqual([401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Authentication required']);`
`expect(get.allow, 'a 401 here carries no Allow header — it did not come from the method gate').toBeNull();`

## 2 — The two 401s the title distinguishes are the same bytes

| authenticator | location | body |
| -- | -- | -- |
| the edge auth gate | `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1089-1095` | `res.status(401).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Authentication required' } })` |
| `authenticateToken(true)` | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:442` | `res.status(401).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Authentication required' } })` |

Status, code and message agree, so assertion one cannot discriminate. **Neither path sets an** `Allow` **header** — the only `res.set('Allow', …)` in that middleware is the 405 method gate at `index.ts:1071` — so assertion two cannot discriminate either; its own message says what it does separate, the *method* gate. The file header states the same conclusion at `:35-37`:

`* tip). Note also that the gate's own 401 (index.ts:1089-1094) is byte-identical`
`* to authenticateToken's (middleware/auth.ts:442), so no cell here can tell the`
`* two authenticators apart from outside.`

So the file simultaneously records the limit in its header and asserts past it in a cell title.

## 3 — The claim is nevertheless true, for two reasons neither assertion reads

Stated so nobody reads this as a product defect. Both are source reads at this tip:

1. **Registration order.** `index.ts:837` is `app.use(createHealthRoutes(services, redisService));` and the spec method/auth gate is registered at `index.ts:1054`. 837 < 1054, so a GET to this path terminates in the health router — behind its own `authenticateToken(true)` — and never reaches the edge gate.
2. **The edge gate is not armed for this route anyway.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:15971-15972` declares `security: - connectorApiKey: []` for `/api/connector/info`, and `specRouteMap.ts:46-48` adds a method to `authedMethods` only when an operation declares `bearerAuth`. The set is empty for this route, so the `if (authedMethods.has(upperMethod))` branch at `index.ts:1084` is false and the 401 at `:1089` is unreachable for it.

The consequence worth recording: **R2 would stay green if authentication did move to the edge**, because both reasons could change without either assertion noticing.

## Not established

* **No suite was run for this ticket.** Everything above is a source read. The 7/7 figure for this file and the behavioural mutants (`connectorApiKey` → `bearerAuth` fails U2 alone; `get:` → `post:` reds R1 while R2 stays green) are Seat S 4th's, recorded on KS-1752, and are not re-run here.
* Whether a discriminating observable exists at all. Making one would mean changing the product (for example distinguishing the two bodies), which is a larger question than this cell; **not proposed**.
* Whether `connectorApiKey` should arm the edge gate is KS-1747's question, not this one.

## Searched

Board, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, title + description + comments, paginated to `hasNextPage` false — never capped.

* `KS-1531 R2` → **0 hits**.
* `not from the edge` → **1 hit**, KS-1752. `from authenticateToken` → **1 hit**, KS-1752. `1089-1094` → **1 hit**, KS-1752.
* **KS-1752 was read whole**, description and all comments. Its two items are (1) the U2 cell's rationale and (2) the `svc_m365_connections` DDL default. This finding appears in one of its comments under the heading **"A finding outside this ticket, raised rather than fixed"** — the author placed it out of that ticket's scope deliberately, and KS-1752 stays open for its item 2, not for this. So the fact is on the board but owned by no ticket, which is why this is filed rather than commented there.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → **18 hits**; `fetchApiKeys` → **4 hits**. **Zero control:** a token coined for this session and written to no ticket → **0 hits**.

title: Question: what should the `error` field of mcp-server's secuura_check_workflow, secuura_register_document and secuura_register_documents carry? Three sites relay the gateway's data.error unchanged; the published contract makes it an object and api-client.ts declares a string

title: api-gateway middleware/scopes.ts:57: requireScope answers 403 with a flat body ({ error: 'Insufficient scope', required, granted, hint }), not the published { success: false, error: { code, message } } envelope; the sibling requireScopeOrRole uses the envelope, and three systemTest files read the flat text
description:
## BLUF

**The api-gateway's** `requireScope` **answers a scope refusal with a flat body,** `{ error: 'Insufficient scope', required, granted, hint }`**, where the published error envelope is** `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }`**. The sibling** `requireScopeOrRole` **in the same file answers with the envelope (code** `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`**), and so does the 401 in** `requireScope` **itself.** Three `systemTest` files read the flat shape by its text. Reported by Seat Z 2nd (STATUS C 15:57Z and READY 17:28Z, 2026-10-27; HANDOVER line 44) while working KS-1767.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed** and none is implied: the flat body is relied on by test code (item 4).

Refs KS-1767, KS-843.

All line numbers were read at develop `c18552d94de23b4da365ce02e02be5d06793bbcb`, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src` unless another path is given. Read from source only; no request was made to a gateway.

## 1 — Three refusals in one file, two shapes

`middleware/scopes.ts`:

* `:29` (in `requireScope`), the 401: `res.status(401).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Authentication required' } });` — the envelope.
* `:57`-`:62` (in `requireScope`), the **403**: `res.status(403).json({` then `error: 'Insufficient scope',` (`:58`), `required: requiredScopes,` (`:59`), `granted: userScopes,` (`:60`) and a `hint:` template string (`:61`) — **flat**; `error` is a string, there is no `success` and no `code`.
* `:148` (in `requireScopeOrRole`), the 401: the same envelope as `:29`.
* `:184`-`:192` (in `requireScopeOrRole`), the 403: `res.status(403).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE', message: ..., required: requiredScope, granted: scopes } })` — the envelope, with `required` and `granted` inside `error`.

## 2 — What the published contract says

`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/openapi/responses.ts`: the registered `ErrorResponse` schema is at `:44`, with `success: z.literal(false)` at `:48` and `error` an object holding `code`, `message` and an optional `details`. The docblock at `:40`-`:41` says: "Every service emits this on any non-2xx response". `commonErrorResponses[403]` (`:156`) uses that schema. Whether each of the six operations in item 3 publishes its 403 through `commonErrorResponses[403]` was not read.

## 3 — Which routes mount the flat gate

`requireScope(` is mounted at six places in `routes/proxy.ts`: `:445` (`'webhooks:manage'`), `:464` (`'users:read'`), `:638` (`'documents:read', 'documents:write'`), `:645` (`'certifications:read', 'certifications:write'`) and `:876` and `:882` (each `'anchors:write'`). `requireScopeOrRole(` is mounted at `:807` and `:860`.

`requireScope` lets a principal whose `authMethod` is `jwt` or `email` through before any scope test (`:35`-`:36`), so the flat 403 reaches OAuth-app and API-key callers, which carry explicit scopes (`:41`-`:42`).

## 4 — What reads the flat shape today

The text `Insufficient scope` occurs in **4 files** in the whole tree at this tip (7 lines): `middleware/scopes.ts:58` and three under `systemTest`:

* `systemTest/playwright/tests/path-spelling/scope-gate-path-spelling.spec.ts:49`: `const GATE_FINGERPRINT = { error: 'Insufficient scope', required: ['anchors:write'] };`, with the comment at `:48` "The gate's own 403 body, from `middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` — its fingerprint".
* `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/support/connector_identity.py:20`-`:23`: the comment reads "Gateway `requireScope` ... answers `{"error": "Insufficient scope", "required": [...], "granted": [...]}` — a bare string, not the usual `{error: {code, message}}` envelope." and `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE = "Insufficient scope"`; also `:91` in the `is_scope_refusal` docstring.
* `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/support/test_connector_identity.py:30`-`:31` (`_SCOPE_403 = {"error": "Insufficient scope", ...}`, commented "a bare-string `error`") and `:50`.

So the harness already treats the flat body as a known, unpublished shape.

## 5 — On the board

KS-1767 mentions it in one sentence in its PR comment of 2026-10-27T17:27Z: "The scope guard's flat 403 body (`middleware/scopes.ts:58`), seen while reading, is outside this ticket." No ticket records it.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing and sent no request.** The body is read from `res.status(403).json(...)`, not observed from a live gateway.
* **Whether each of the six mounts in item 3 is reachable for every method on its path.** It is not for `POST /api/documents`: that request is answered earlier by the gateway's own handler, `routes/verification.ts:662`, whose router is mounted at `index.ts:901` before `createProxyRoutes` at `index.ts:1107`, and no `next(` or `_next(` call occurs in `routes/verification.ts` from `:662` to `:918`; so the `:638` mount is not reached for that request. `GET /api/workflow-instances/:id` is likewise handled at `routes/verification.ts:449`. The other mounts and methods were not traced. (Added after filing, 2026-10-27 UTC, found while tracing the routes that mcp-server's `register.ts` and `info.ts` call.)
* Whether the six operations publish their 403 with the shared `ErrorResponse` or declare another shape (not read).
* Whether the flat body is deliberate. The code comment above `requireScope` does not say.

* 13 string literals: `:286` (`'1 in the baseline, 0 new'`), `:395`, `:404`, `:442`, `:519` (each `'1 in the baseline, 0 new; 0 stale baseline entries'`), `:581`, `:628`, `:915`, `:1034` (each `'0 new'`), `:934`, `:943` (each `'0 new; 0 stale baseline entries'`), `:964`, `:1002` (each `'0 errors'`).

* 2 uses of the constant `PASSED`, defined at `:1082` as `'1 in the baseline, 0 new; 0 stale baseline entries'`, at `:1175` and `:1203`.

Of the 13 literals, `:934`, `:943` and `:964` sit inside an `expect(() => ...)` or `thrownBy(() => ...)` on the same line, so they are among the 12 calls that are the subject of throw cells. The other 13 sites are ordinary calls.

The substring facts, measured here with a control on each: `'0 new' in '10 new'` is **True**, against `'3 new'` it is **False**; `'1 in the baseline, 0 new' in '11 in the baseline, 0 new'` is **True**, against `'2 in the baseline, 0 new'` it is **False**.

The `'1 in the baseline, 0 new...'` strings it judges "not weak" because `', 10 new'` does not contain `', 0 new'`.

For the `AUTH_GREEN_SUMMARY` shape, the Flow doc says the exposure is unreachable today: "a run with new errors exits 1 and the status arm catches it" (`Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html:4822`, section 65, KS-1529).
