## Items

### m1 — nothing guards the WEBSITE half of `demo-service` CORS (tamper survivor)

`docker-compose.yml:2185` now renders `${GATEWAY_PORT:-6882},${WEBSITE_PORT:-6881}`. The
`check-compose-stack-safety.mjs` cells assert `demo-service.CORS_ORIGINS` **moves** and that
api-gateway's list carries slot 2's **website** port — but nothing asserts the same for
demo-service. **Reverting demo-service's website half to a literal** `:6881` **leaves the checker**
**green** (the value still moves, because its gateway half does).

*Fix shape:* extend the website-origin assertion to every entry in `MUST_MOVE` that is a
comma-separated origin list, not api-gateway alone. Bite-check: revert one half, see it red.

### m2 — nothing guards the `.env`-then-`stack_env.sh` ORDER in `start-local.sh` (tamper survivor)

The order is load-bearing and documented in the script: `stack_env.sh` assigns the ports
unconditionally, so sourcing it **after** `.env` is what makes the slot beat a stale literal a
clone carries (KS-785). `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` asserts the source is *present* and
that the banner derives — but **swapping the two lines leaves the suite green**, because the
fixture's `.env` sets no port.

*Fix shape:* a cell whose fixture `.env` sets `GATEWAY_PORT` to a wrong literal and asserts the
slot still wins. That is the real-world case (an existing clone's `.env`), and it reds on a swap.

### m3 — the launcher census misses four shapes

`_launcher_candidates()` in `check-stack-safety.sh` matches a compose call on one line with a
literal `docker compose`/`docker-compose`. It therefore misses:
backslash-continued invocations; `$DC up` and `${var} up` where the binary is in a variable; and
**untracked** files (it scans `git ls-files`, by design for production, but a new launcher is
typically untracked while being written).

*Fix shape:* decide per shape. The variable-binary and continuation shapes are worth matching. The
untracked case is arguably correct as-is — record the decision either way rather than leaving it to
the next reader.

### m4 — two exception entries carry a reason but NO ticket, and nothing asserts one

Wednesday's ruling was "a reason **and a ticket** per entry". `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS` has:

| entry | reason | ticket |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/start-environment.sh` | yes | KS-1550 |
| `scripts/stop-environment.sh` | yes | KS-1550 |
| `observability/scripts/observability.sh` | yes | KS-200 |
| `systemTest/akto/scripts/start.sh` | yes | **none** |
| `systemTest/akto/scripts/assert-compose-project.sh` | yes | **none** |

And the `_reasonless` cell only checks the reason is non-empty — it **never asserts a ticket**, so
the gap could not have been caught by the guard itself.

*Fix shape:* give the two Akto entries a ticket (or a named standing decision, e.g. KS-666/KS-691
for the side-stack namespacing), and extend the cell to require a `KS-`/`PS-` token per entry.
This is the one item that contradicts an explicit ruling, so it is the first to do.

### m5 — the port-literal guard omits the slot-offset cardano ports

`SLOT1_HOST_PORTS` in `check-compose-stack-safety.mjs` lists
`11434, 8881, 6882, 6881, 6433, 6432, 6379` but **not** `6090`–`6094`
(`CARDANO_MOCK_PORT`, `CARDANO_N2N_PORT`, `YACI_STORE_PORT`, `CARDANO_ADMIN_PORT`,
`CARDANO_SUBMIT_PORT`), which `stack_env.sh` offsets per slot exactly as it does the others. A
localhost URL embedding one of those would not be noticed.

*Fix shape:* derive the list from `stack_env.sh`'s exported names rather than restating it — the
same principle the file's own header sets out ("this file must not be able to agree with itself
while disagreeing with `stack_env.sh`"). Then a new offset port cannot be omitted.

## Not in this ticket

The PR-text items from the same note are **information, not work**, and went into #1526's body: a
CI or box stack that sets `GATEWAY_PORT` but not `FRONTEND_URL`/`CORS_ORIGINS` now gets derived
values instead of `:6882`; some preflight comments still say `:6882`; the Makefile warns on a
missing `CORS_ORIGINS`.

The group-level widening of the static guard is **KS-1381's** (it extends the guard KS-1355
created). KS-1389's leg 13 is the other half of the slot-derivation group's point 3.

## Board search before filing

`searchIssues` (fuzzy, 5 per term) on `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS`, `launcher census`,
`KNOWN_SLOT_BLIND`, `cardano port literal guard`, `demo-service CORS website`,
`stack_env order start-local`. Nearest hits read: KS-1550 (the two environment scripts, cited as
exceptions), KS-1381 (the guard's widening), KS-1162 (workflow port literals), KS-940 / KS-912
(launcher-suite residues, a different suite). None names any of m1–m5. Filed new.

title: api-gateway unit suite: the ks1531 U2 cell pins the authedMethods set rather than the behaviour its comment claims, and startup-migrations.ts:380 defaults svc_m365_connections.status to 'active', outside the four-value enum
description:
## BLUF

**Two LOW/INFO residues that the api-gateway unit suite proves.** Proving command:
`npm run test --workspace=services/api-gateway` (`services/api-gateway/package.json:11` declares
`"test": "vitest"`); a cell for either item lives in `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/`.

Nothing here is a fix, and neither of the merged changes it came from is wrong as reviewed.

Refs KS-1746, KS-1531, KS-1700, KS-1643.

**Item 2 placement, measured by Seat G 23rd at** `c3eb63c9d23b`**:** the Wednesday brief that ordered this
split reasoned that a cell would live in `ks1062-startup-migrations-tenant-summary-first-error.test.ts`
or `ks1125-api-gateway-startup-migrations-the-tenant.test.ts`. **That reason does not hold** — both files
use `const PRODUCT = path.join(__dirname,'..','startup-migrations.ts')` only as a module-resolution
identity (`ks1062:58,77`, `ks1125:77,98`, to intercept `require('pg')`), never reading it as text, and
both assert only the tenant-summary log line. **The reason that does hold:** `ks667-vault-entries-single-owner.test.ts`
in the same suite already imports `CORE_MIGRATIONS` from `../startup-migrations` (`:22`) and asserts
regexes against the DDL strings (`:29`, `:40`), and reads the versioned `migrations/*.sql` with
`readFileSync` (`:76`) — so one api-gateway unit cell can cover all five DDLs of item 2. Census: of the
**123** files in `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/`, exactly **1** asserts on `CREATE TABLE` /
`svc_m365_connections` (that one); control, files naming `startup-migrations` → **7**.

## 1 — LOW: the U2 cell's stated rationale is false, and the cell pins a set rather than a behaviour

In `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1531-connector-info-is-in-the-published-contract.test.ts` the header at `:17-20` reads:

> `` `authedMethods` only for `bearerAuth` — so the edge auth gate stays off and `` / `authenticateToken(true) remains the only authenticator. U2 fails if the` / `declaration is ever changed to` `` `bearerAuth` ``, which would silently move`/`authentication for this route to the edge.\`

and the cell at `:114` asserts `:120` `expect([...r.authedMethods], 'the edge auth gate must NOT be armed for this route').toEqual([])`, with the same claim restated in the comment at `:118-119`.

**The consequence claimed is false.** The gate mutated the yaml declaration to `bearerAuth` and the 28-cell behaviour matrix stayed **byte-identical**, because the GET is answered by the health router before the edge gate is reached. What U2 does pin is real but narrower: the `authedMethods` set that `buildSpecMethodMap` derives from the spec. It does not pin that authentication would move.

*Line numbers I could not confirm as cited:* the verdict names `index.ts:837` (health router) and `index.ts:1054` (edge gate). At this tip the gate's own read is at `index.ts:1064` (`resolveSpecRoute`) and the auth branch at `:1084` (`if (authedMethods.has(upperMethod))`); `buildSpecMethodMap` is called at `:612` and `:654`. **I did not locate a** `createHealthRouter` **mount line** — the symbol does not appear in `index.ts` — so **the "health router answers first" ordering is NOT established by me**; it is the gate's, and its two line numbers do not match this tree.

Source: tier-1 gate verdict (#1732 LOW 1).

## 2 — INFO (schema hygiene): one of five `svc_m365_connections` DDLs defaults `status` to a value outside the enum

All five read at `c3eb63c9d23b`. The DDL header line and the `status` column line are given separately, because the sources that raised this cited sometimes one and sometimes the other:

| file | `CREATE TABLE` | `status` column | default |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts` | `:376` | `:380` | `status TEXT DEFAULT 'active'` |
| `migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql` | `:427` | `:432` | `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` |
| `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql` | `:1179` | `:1184` | `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` |
| `docker/init/04-sprint2-service-tables.sql` | `:260` | `:265` | `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` |
| `docker/init/06-m365-tables.sql` | `:9` | `:14` | `status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'pending'` |

`'active'` is **outside** the four-value enum of item 3. Two further differences in the same DDL, measured: it is the only one of the five **without** `NOT NULL` on `status` (`06-m365-tables.sql` also lacks it), and it carries a **different column set** — it has `client_id`, `sharepoint_site_url` and `metadata JSONB` and omits `tenant_name`, `scopes`, `connected_at`, `last_sync_at` and `error_message`.

**Not reachable through any writer, confirmed by me.** `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:175` holds the only `INSERT INTO svc_m365_connections` in the repo; it always supplies `status` (`$5` ← `c.status` at `:184`) and its `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status` is at `:180`. There is **no** `UPDATE svc_m365_connections` **statement at all**. So the default is unreachable today and this is hygiene, not a live defect. The same single-writer finding is independently recorded on KS-1700.

**Same class, different objects, already on the board** (named so this is not re-filed as new): KS-1528 (`platform_document_registry.tenant_id`, three declarations that disagree) and KS-1200 (`anchor_store`'s unique declared by only one migration).

Source: tier-1 gate verdict (#1725 INFO).

## Not established

*The bullets below are copied verbatim from KS-1746 and keep ITS item numbers: its item 2 is item 1 here, its item 4 is item 2 here.*

* The gateway's health-router-before-edge-gate **ordering** (item 2). The verdict's `index.ts:837` / `:1054` do not match this tree and I found no `createHealthRouter` mount; the behavioural claim is the gate's, unreproduced by me.
* Whether any stored `svc_m365_connections` row carries `status = 'active'` today (item 4). No database was read — this ticket is a source read only.
* The gate verdicts themselves were **not re-run**. Every mutant figure (`68/0`, the 28-cell matrix) is quoted from them.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

Each line is a query I ran; the controls fired in both directions.

* `specRouteMap` — 6 hits · `authedMethods` — 3. Nearest: **KS-944** (Done, archived) pins the wallet operations' `security: []` vs `bearerAuth`; **KS-1469** (trailing slash). Neither names item 2's cell, which #1732 created on 27 Oct.
* `startup-migrations` — 47 hits; the two same-class tickets named in item 4 were read, neither covers this table.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.

## Provenance

Split from KS-1746 on 2026-10-27 per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule — *"The only reason to create multiple*
*tickets is if they relate to separate workloads or separate fixes"* — the unit of ticket creation being
the test pass. KS-1746's items 2 and 4 are this ticket's items 1 and 2; their text above is byte-identical
to KS-1746's, heading ordinals excepted. KS-1746 keeps item 5 (shell/preflight suite) and holds the
`old item -> key` table.

*Originally filed by Seat G 22nd, 2026-10-27. Split out by Seat G 23rd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: KS-1512 follow-up: post-deadline discard, pin the no-window guard, body-stall comment, cell G
description:
## BLUF

The gate on PR 1522 (KS-1512 option A, verdict sha256/16 `cf710859d4177885`, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major) found three Minors and a nit that do not block the merge. Wednesday ruled them into ONE follow-up ticket. The common thread: the overall deadline bounds the *waiting between* windows, not a response **body** that arrives slowly, and one guard and one assertion are not pinned.

## Checklist

- [ ] **m1, a stalled response BODY is outside every timer, in ANY window, and the code comment overclaims.** `fetchWithTimeout` (`platform.ts:143-158`) clears its timer when `fetch()` resolves, which is at the response HEADERS; `await r.json()` (`:416`) then runs outside any timer. Measured by the gate (budget 2000 ms, a stub holding the body back after flushing headers): a stalled 8 s body in a **non-last** window gave **8014 ms**, in the **last** window **8006 ms**. Same as the old route's one request, not worse (the worst case is one stall, not 26). The comment at `:401` ("never hangs") is true for slow responses and false for a stalled body. *Fix shape:* bound the body read by the remaining budget (keep the `AbortController` live until after `r.json()`, or race the body read against a `remaining` timer), or at minimum soften the comment to "slow responses" and record the caveat. *Cell to add:* a stalled body in a NON-last window degrades within budget + margin.
- [ ] **m2, the guard "no window starts once nothing is left" (**`platform.ts:407`**) is unpinned.** The gate's mutant that removes it survives **all 18 cells**; with it removed the stub sees a second request that is aborted at once. *Fix shape:* in cell M assert `calls.length === 1` (the stub already records calls).
- [ ] **m3, a final window that answers AFTER the deadline keeps the platform half and returns late.** Measured: a last-window body at 1.5 times the budget returned in **3021 ms** (budget 2000 ms) with the platform rows served. Wednesday's ruling said a spent budget DISCARDS the platform half; today the discard applies only when another window would be needed. She accepted this for the merge because it is bounded by the same body-stall exposure as the old route. *Fix shape:* one deadline check after the body is read (`if (Date.now() >= deadline) throw`), plus a cell. Note it would not bound the time (see m1); it only stops a late result from being served as if on time. A ruling-interpretation question as well as a fix: the rows served are complete, never partial.
- [ ] **nit, cell G's second assertion cannot fail** (`ks1512-platform-audit-log-pages-the-upstream-past-its-200-clamp.test.ts`, the `calls.every(... || c.offset === 200 || c.offset === 100 || c.offset === 0)` line, around `:214`): any plausible offset satisfies it. The first assertion (the ids equal the oracle) is the real check. Delete the second or make it real.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` (the audit-log handler's platform-fetch block) and `ks1512-platform-audit-log-pages-the-upstream-past-its-200-clamp.test.ts`.
* **Evidence:** the gate's probes P1 to P5 and mutant M9, in its evidence folder under Wednesday's reference directory (`2026-10-13_gate-pr1522`). Not re-run by me.
* **Not in scope here:** the invisible degrade (KS-1545), the tie-break (KS-1544), the live read of a deep page that KS-1512 still needs after a deploy.
* **Related:** KS-1512, KS-1545.
* **Dedupe before filing (Wednesday's condition):** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles AND descriptions in team KS, archived included: `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` 0, `fetchWithTimeout` 0, `stalled body` 0, `body stall` 0, `post-deadline` 0; `routes/platform.ts` names 25 tickets, none about these findings (the nearest, KS-1545, is the invisible degrade). The same instrument returns KS-1512 for a phrase from its own title (`half of the merge is cut to 200 rows`), so it can see ticket text.

title: ks1061 mock-completeness guard: negative twin for a wrong helper path, a two-factories-in-one-file cell, and the pre-existing blind spots (KS-1159 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Four Minor notes from the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1482 (KS-1159), all in `services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1061-shared-mock-completeness.test.ts`. They were left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. None is a regression; none blocks anything. Filed as ONE ticket so they are searchable.

One small tier-2, test-only PR, test first: the two missing cells (they are the survivors of the gate's own mutations), then decide whether the pre-existing blind spots are worth widening the guard for.

## Detail

1. `VIA_HELPER` **has no negative twin for a wrong helper path or name** (`~:55`). Loosening the pattern to a bare `require(` stays green (10/10). Add a fixture that calls `require('./somewhere/else').makeSharedMock(` or a differently named helper and must be NAMED as an offender.
2. `ROOT_MOCK` **has no two-factories-in-one-file cell** (`~:54`). Dropping the `/g` flag stays green (10/10). Add a fixture with two factories in one file, one compliant and one partial: `declared` and `viaHelper` must be 2 and 1.
3. **The claim "T6b/T6c/T7 are red on develop's patterns" was false** (PR text, corrected on the PR and in the squash body): develop already has those widenings; only T8 was red there. Recorded here so the corrected statement is the one that is searched.

Comments containing the pattern, spreads and block-body factories read as conservative false-reds, which is the safe direction.

Refs KS-1159, KS-1061, KS-1000.

title: api-gateway: no cell pins the verification limiter above the audit middleware, and the production unversioned verification 307s are counted by no limiter (a decision)
description:
## BLUF

Two notes from the Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479), neither a defect in that PR:

1. **N1, a test gap.** Moving the verification limiter **below** the audit middleware (`index.ts:570`) turns **0 cells** red, and would start auditing every `429` (one audit row per throttled verification request). The position is harmless today, but nothing guards it.
2. **N2, a decision carried from KS-1469.** In production the unversioned `/api/verification*` `307`s are now counted by **no** limiter (the gate sent 305 of 305 through): the limiter sits after the redirect by design (so a followed redirect counts once), and `READ_ONLY_PATHS` exempts `/api/verification` from the global limiter. None reaches a handler, so a `307` flood costs only the redirect, but it is unbounded.

## Recommendation

* **N1:** pin the order with a behavioural cell: drive the real app with the audit middleware's `query` stubbed, send a throttled verification request, and assert that no audit row is written for the `429`. Tests first; a tamper that moves the block below the audit middleware must turn it red. Priority Low.
* **N2:** an owner decision, not a fix: is an unbounded `307` flood acceptable, or should the unversioned redirect be counted by the global limiter (drop the `/api/verification` prefix from `READ_ONLY_PATHS` for the unversioned spelling only)? Either answer should be written next to the limiter block and pinned.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479), 2026-10-12, notes N1 and N2 (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1483/verdict.md`; its tamper "limiter moved below the audit middleware": 0 red).
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived): none for the limiter's position relative to the audit middleware.

Related: KS-1479, KS-1469.

title: KS-1137 F-4 census missed a fourth suite (tenant_isolation), and the KS-1347 probe is brittle
description:

Three findings from the **PR #1528 narrow Sonnet gate** (verdict sha256/16 `244c98cbd4852491`,
GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major, 3 Minor, head `6bfd74ad7c39b43c614c5d837744780f20788fa2`). **M1 is the one**

**Confirmed independently** before filing, by a census over every `*.test.sh` in that directory

```

container_trivy_failed_scan_is_loud.test.sh            jq=2 privPATH=1 jqlink=1  (fixed by #1528)
container_trivy_image_filter.test.sh                   jq=2 privPATH=1 jqlink=1  (fixed by #1528)
tenant_isolation_stderr_own_file.test.sh               jq=1 privPATH=1 jqlink=0  (MISSED)
```

**Why #1528 missed it:** that PR's census was scoped to `*trivy*` filenames, because the ticket
names a trivy suite. The defect is not trivy-shaped — it is "any suite that preflights a binary on
one PATH and runs the subject on another". A filename is not a scope.

*Fix:* the same shape as the other three (resolve `JQ_BIN` once, `ln -sf` it into the fixture's stub
dir), **plus a census cell** that enumerates suites with both features and asserts each links `jq`,
so a fifth copy reds instead of being found by the next gate.

## M2 — the KS-1347 probe is brittle to a harmless respelling

`ks1347_proxy_out_dir_spaced_checkout.test.sh` reads the subject's `node:` imports with
`grep -E "^import .* from 'node:[a-z]+';$"`. A harmless respelling in `server.ts` — double quotes,
or `from 'node:url'` written differently — makes the inherited import set incomplete and **reds 4**
**cells while** `server.ts` **still works perfectly**. That is the inverse of the u4 defect the inheritance
was introduced to fix: too loose let the probe supply what the subject lacked; too strict reds on a
subject that is fine.

*Fix shape:* tolerate both quote styles and trailing-semicolon variation, or parse the import list
rather than matching a line shape. Keep the control that the inherited set is non-empty and names
the module the expression needs — that control is what makes the looser match safe.

## M3 (information, not work)

`systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:42` is the **last** raw `new URL(...).pathname` site in the
tree after #1528. It is [KS-1337](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1337)'s by attribution and
deliberately out of KS-1347's scope. Recorded so the census is not re-derived from scratch.

## Not in this ticket

[KS-1347](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1347)'s third acceptance box — whether `ks860` and
`ks879` should walk `systemTest/` — is still open and is **not** folded in here, because this
ticket is scoped to the #1528 gate's note. It needs a decision or a ticket of its own.

## Board search before filing

`searchIssues` (fuzzy, 5 per term) on `tenant_isolation_stderr_own_file`, `jq private PATH`,
`homebrew-only jq host`. Nearest hits read: KS-1137 (the F-4 item itself, the parent of M1),
KS-1136 (per-image trivy failure reading as clean — a different defect in the same job),
KS-1436 and KS-1336 (the tenant-isolation *subject*, not its suite's PATH handling), KS-1356
(suites skipping on hosts without Postgres binaries — the same host-shaped class, different
binary). None names the `jq`-on-the-wrong-PATH defect in `tenant_isolation_stderr_own_file.test.sh`.
Filed new.

* The **login brute-force limiter is disabled in CI *and* on the VM**, so nothing exercises it.
* Akto's rate-limiting family produces **969 results, 100% not-applicable, zero executed** — which renders in the report as "0 vulnerable", indistinguishable from a pass.

**A regression removing brute-force protection would ship green today.** This is exactly the MUST #13 rule-6 shape: a check whose input is missing scoring as clean rather than red.

## ✅ Child tickets closed (systemTest test-writing complete)

## ⬜ Still to fix (open work — systemTest only)

1. **Flip the report-only tests green** — each `xfail`/`skip` (notification BOLA, wallet verify, webhook DNS-rebind, KYC code-residual, seed-demo, billing idempotency, + the two anchor `xfail`s: missing qualified-vs-mock signal, honest-labelling of simulated anchors) becomes a hard pass only when its **A–F platform remediation / prod-like env** ships. Cross-tenant mutate/transfer-custody, cross-owner read/revoke within a tenant, forged `x-tenant-id`, and api-key isolation all landed as passing regressions. (Backend owner-scoping/header-trust remediation is Review A — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor), Kamil — not tracked here.)
4. **Other harnesses under G** — Akto OWASP re-baseline ([KS-395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-395/validate-weekend-platform-fixes-akto-owasp-security-scan) pattern) and Playwright UI-level auth/admin-gating/XSS: **not started**.
5. **S↔K connector-identity regressions (**[KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks)**)** — the only rows of the [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) data-loss register that land in G: #16 provenance never on-chain and #17 erasure pseudonymises. [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) was closed 2026-09-14 with every row dispositioned (K-side residue [KS-532](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532/sk-dr-k-side-key-store-restore-path-joint-restore-point-coverage-demo) / [KS-581](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-581/register-connector-volume-alerting-rate-limit-and-correlation-of), Kam); these two are Peter's and are **blocked on** [KS-516](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516/schemathesis-systemtest-seed-a-real-sk-api-key-documentswrite-so-the) seeding two real `sk_` keys (provisioning + operational). Not started.

## Method

For each confirmed finding: (1) write a test that **reproduces** it pre-fix (red), (2) land it alongside the remediation so it goes green, (3) keep it in the pre-merge tier so regressions fail fast. Follow `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` standards; **local commits only — no GitHub push/PR/issue interaction for any systemTest change** unless explicitly instructed, and use `KS-###` / `akto#NNNN` text refs, never GitHub issue URLs.

**Acceptance:** each A–F remediation ships with a linked regression here; the security-relevant checks run in the pre-merge suites (schemathesis pre-merge + Akto). The "Still to fix" list above is the live checklist.

title: preflight.sh:731: the -z "$hook_controls" disjunct is implied by the second disjunct, so deleting it moves no cell and no outcome; delete it or keep it as a documented refusal is undecided
description:
## BLUF

**At** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:731` **the** `-z "$hook_controls"` **disjunct is implied by the second disjunct, so deleting it changes no outcome and no test cell can go red on its deletion (an equivalent mutant).** Whether to delete the dead disjunct, or keep it as a documented refusal, is **not decided**. Until now the question was recorded only inside KS-1756's comment (2026-10-27T06:19:35Z: "Whether to delete the dead disjunct is a `preflight.sh` question and is not made here"), and KS-1756 is a ticket about to be closed, so this ticket is the question's home.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.**

Refs KS-1756, KS-1746, KS-1638.

All line numbers were read at develop `061c3a4f62d563e723b8cee5fe792b4c27dc3014`. The finding is Seat Z 1st's (STATUS 2026-10-27T05:54Z, and KS-1756's comment), relayed through Wednesday; the truth table in section 2 is re-measured here.

## 1 — The line

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:731`, verbatim:

`if [ -z "$hook_controls" ] || ! printf '%s\n' "$hook_controls" | grep -qx 'ALLOW_FORCE'; then`

The comment above it (`:725-730`) says an empty derivation "would mean the hook moved or the pattern stopped matching", and that `ALLOW_FORCE` is named "because it is the one control known to exist today". The refusal text starts at `:732`: `FAIL - could not derive the pre-push hook's own control variables from $hook_src.`

## 2 — The truth table, measured here

`/bin/bash` 3.2.57 with `set -o pipefail`. I ran the full condition and the second disjunct alone over seven derived sets: empty; `ALLOW_FORCE`; `NAME`; `FOO BAR`; `ALLOW_FORCE` then `NAME` on two lines; `NAME` then `ALLOW_FORCE` on two lines; `ALLOW_FORCE_X`.

Result: **7 of 7 identical** (refuse, pass, refuse, refuse, pass, pass, refuse). For the empty set, `printf '%s\n' ""` writes one empty line, `grep -qx 'ALLOW_FORCE'` exits 1, and `!` makes that true, so the second disjunct refuses on its own.

Control on the same harness: with the second disjunct replaced by `false`, the empty set **does** differ (refuse with the `-z` disjunct, pass without it), so the harness can tell the two forms apart.

## 3 — What the suites measured (relayed, not re-run here)

From KS-1756's comment, which is Seat Z 1st's: the mutant that deletes the disjunct reads `preflight_deps.test.sh` 82/0 with zero cells moving, so no cell can fail on it. The mutants the cells do kill are `M_accept` (an empty set is accepted: 75/0 and surviving at base, 76/6 after) and `M_2nd` (only `-z` remains: 71/4 before, 79/3 after).

## Not established

* **Whether to delete the dead disjunct or keep it.** Not decided, and not chosen here.
* **I ran no suite.** The 82/0, 76/6 and 79/3 figures are KS-1756's, not reproduced.
* Whether any other `if` in `preflight.sh` has the same implied-disjunct shape. Not searched.

## Searched

Board, KS team, title + description + comment bodies, `includeArchived: true`, paged to the end. `preflight.sh:731` → **1 hit**, KS-1756. `hook_controls` → **3 hits**: KS-1756, KS-1755 (the derivation reads `${NAME:-` only, a different defect), KS-1746. `equivalent mutant` → **1 hit**, KS-1687 (m365, unrelated). `disjunct` → **4 hits**: KS-1756, KS-1640, KS-1078 (archived), KS-1017; none of the other three contains `preflight.sh:731`, and I read their titles only. **Positive control** `KS-1531` → 24 hits. **Zero control:** a token coined for this read and written nowhere → 0 hits.

*Filed by Seat G 25th, 2026-10-27 UTC, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: Akto pin-bump tooling gaps: update-akto-images.sh reads one page of tags and points at the wrong place, 13 prose mirrors of the pin are untested, a CLAUDE.md claim is wrong, and Akto's 10-logins/hour limit can void a tier
description:
**BLUF:** four gaps in the tooling around an Akto image bump, all met while doing [KS-1478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1478/akto-image-2371-2383-release-v2383-2026-10-13-testing-image-has-no) (2.37.1 → 2.38.2). Items 1–3 were fixed and proven red → green in [KS-1478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1478/akto-image-2371-2383-release-v2383-2026-10-13-testing-image-has-no), then **backed out at Peter's instruction (update the app only, log issues)**. Item 4 was hit live. Re-verified against `develop` 3c0a52221 on 2026-10-14.

## 1. `update-akto-images.sh` reads only the first 100 tags and gives stale advice

* `systemTest/akto/scripts/update-akto-images.sh:29` and `:39` fetch **one page** (`page_size=100&ordering=last_updated`). The `a-####-merge` CI tags (several a day in October 2026) crowd that page, so an older `_local` tag can fall off it and the "latest valid pair" is computed from a truncated list.
* `:65` tells you to set `AKTO_IMAGE_VERSION` in `.env` only. The canonical pin is `package.json` `config.aktoImageVersion` (MUST #10). `:86` says to "update the image: lines in docker-compose.yml", but the Akto images have no literal version there any more.
* The pairing logic has **no test**. Today it had to answer "2.38.3 is dashboard-only, so 2.38.2", and testing skipped 2.37.5–2.37.7, 2.37.9 and 2.38.1 in one week.

## 2. 13 prose mirrors of the pin are moved by hand and never checked

`aktoPinMirrors.test.ts` ([KS-1411](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1411/akto-image-2364-23610-release-v23610-2026-10-05-both-local-tags)) checks the compose fallbacks and `.env.example`. Nothing checks the human-read copies:

* `docs/configuration.md` (image table ×2, "so the pin is X")
* `docs/quick-start.md` ("`X` is the pinned pair")
* the `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` Pin paragraph ("Currently **X**")
* `Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html` (pill, badge, versions line, tool box, resources heading, release link, config line)
* `…Flow_Diagrams.html` ("Akto image pin X")

A missed one stays green while telling the reader the wrong version.

## 3. A wrong claim in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:2744`

The Pin paragraph says every mirror, including the empty-state string in `src/report/reportServiceLogs.ts`, is "checked by `tests/unit/core/aktoPinMirrors.test.ts`". It is not: `reportServiceLogs.test.ts` checks that string, and the prose mirrors (item 2) are checked by nothing.

## 4. Akto's own login limit (10 per hour per IP) can void a tier mid-session

`src/client/aktoAuth.ts:127`: *"The rate limit is 10 logins/hour per IP. Wait \~1 hour or restart the Akto container."* Measured on 2026-10-14 (slot 1, Akto 2.38.2): after a start, three tiers and parity reads, a targeted `pre-merge` re-run failed: 5 × 65 s retries, then `COVERAGE DEGRADED` / `NO COVERAGE — 0 runs aggregated`, exit 1. The harness was honest. But it logs in to Akto per feed-har and per scan instead of reusing a session, so a normal working session (or a 13-run `security` tier plus a re-run) can exhaust the budget. Restarting `akto-dashboard` cleared it.

## The fix that was built for 1–3 (backed out), for reference

* `update-akto-images.sh` pages up to `AKTO_TAG_MAX_PAGES` (default 5), stopping on `"next":null`. It reads fixture pages from `AKTO_TAG_FIXTURE_DIR` for tests, and points at `package.json`.
* `tests/unit/scripts/updateAktoImages.test.ts` has 6 cells: a dashboard-only release is not a pair, candidate tags are ignored, page 2 is read (and with paging off the pair is missed), semver not string order, no common version, canonical pin named.
* `tests/unit/core/aktoPinDocMirrors.test.ts` has 13 anchored cells; red 13 of 13 on a stale pin; tolerant of Prettier re-wrapping.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `update-akto-images.sh` reads past the first page and names the canonical pin. **A test demonstrates it:** a fixture whose matching testing tag is only on page 2 yields the pair, and fails with paging limited to 1.
2. Every prose mirror is checked against `config.aktoImageVersion`. **A test demonstrates it:** moving only the canonical pin turns it red, naming each stale mirror. History lines ("the pin was …") are deliberately not matched.
3. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` names the correct test for each mirror.
4. The Akto client reuses one dashboard session per process (or per tier) instead of logging in per scan, **or** the harness counts its logins and refuses early with the remedy. **A test demonstrates it:** a stubbed login that answers 429 after N calls is not called more than once per tier.

title: systemTest/schemathesis: a sweep leaves governance proposals from the OLA leg's `owner` actor on the cap, which the KS-1719 slot-freeing helper never cancels — on a long-lived slot they alone fill the cap and the §11 test skips with `freed 0`
description:
## BLUF

The [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719/systemtest-preconditions-test-execute-from-draft-is-refused-skips-when) helper (`_free_active_proposal_slot`, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1687](https://linear.app/secuura/review/fixschemathesis-free-the-governance-caps-queued-proposals-too-oldest-fc6447b24b1f)) cancels only proposals the super-admin persona proposed. Its docstring assumed the sweep proposes only as `super_admin`. Measured under [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live): a sweep also proposes as an `owner`-role user, which the helper never touches. Each sweep leaves a few of that user's proposals counting toward the 20-proposal cap. On a slot that hosts sweeps for long enough, those alone fill the cap, the helper frees 0, and `test_execute_from_draft_is_refused` skips with `freed 0 proposal(s)`, which fails the pre-merge gate (a skip is INCOMPLETE, [KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)). This is the mechanism [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719/systemtest-preconditions-test-execute-from-draft-is-refused-skips-when) described, now with a named proposer.

## Measured ([KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live), 27 Oct 2026)

One `pre-merge` sweep on a fresh platform-k slot 2 at develop `dcf1ca244` (run `pre-merge-2026-10-27T11-21-02Z-slot2`, seed 1286291329, Schemathesis 4.32.1). `svc_proposals` afterwards, grouped by `proposer_id`:

| Proposer | Role | Created | Proposals | Still counted by the cap (`active`) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020` | system_admin (the seeded super-admin) | seed | 60 | 2 |
| `468839f4-cfb0-4fe2-a322-623e7699e348` | owner | 11:21:04, the run's start | 5 | 1 |
| `19d84f36-0474-4369-bf59-fd535c5ef2a9` | issuer_admin | seed | 4 (the §11 probes' drafts) | 0, all cancelled |

The `owner` user's creation time matches `provision-actors` for the OLA leg (`ks256-owner-local`, role OWNER, [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)). The identity is inferred from role and timing: `users.email` is encrypted, so it was not confirmed by email.

So about one proposal per sweep is left on the cap by a proposer the helper cannot cancel. The helper's behaviour on that cap was proven live under [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live): the create skips with `(freed 0 proposal(s) before this; only proposals proposed by the super-admin are cancelled)`.

## Fix options (systemTest only, pick in the plan)

1. The OLA leg cancels every proposal its peers created, as the §11 fixture does for its own drafts (`test_state_machine_preconditions.py` `draft_proposal` teardown).
2. The helper also frees as the `owner` actor, from the actor manifest, with the same oldest-first and own-proposals-only rules.

Option 1 is cleaner: the residue is cleared by the leg that made it, and the helper's scope stays narrow.

## Acceptance

1. **Automated test:** red on the current code, green after. Offline: a unit test driving the chosen code path over a model of the routes (as `tests/unit/support/test_precondition_probes_proposal_cap.py` does). Live: after one `pre-merge` sweep on a fresh slot, `select count(*) from svc_proposals where status in ('active','queued') and proposer_id <> <super-admin id>` is 0, or the [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live) opt-in suite (`tests/governance_cap_live`) still passes 3/3 on that slot after the sweep.
2. **Docs:** the `_free_active_proposal_slot` docstring's MEASURED paragraph (added by [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live)) updated to say the residue is now cleared; `docs/running-tests.md` and the two `Projects Documents` HTML files if the OLA leg's behaviour is described there.
3. **systemTests:** the change lives under `systemTest/schemathesis/`; no product code.

## Related

* [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live) (In Progress): the measurement and the live proof of the helper.
* [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719/systemtest-preconditions-test-execute-from-draft-is-refused-skips-when) (Done): the original skip and the helper fix ([Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1687](https://linear.app/secuura/review/fixschemathesis-free-the-governance-caps-queued-proposals-too-oldest-fc6447b24b1f)).
* [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (Done): the OLA leg and its `owner` / `ownerPeer` actors.
* [KS-1732](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1732/governance-a-failed-database-read-answers-as-empty-get-proposals) (Backlog, Kamil): the cap fails open on a database read error; not this ticket.

title: Implement real wallet signature verification (CIP-8/COSE + address binding) — needs the COSE key back in the request contract
description:
## BLUF

Implement real wallet signature verification for `POST /api/wallets/verify`.
The endpoint currently **fails closed with 501** (KS-488 C-2, PR #685) — it used
to return `verified: true` for any three non-empty strings. This ticket is the
work that makes it actually verify.

**It is not a patch.** It requires a breaking request-contract change, new crypto
dependencies, and test vectors from real wallets. That is why C-2 shipped the
refusal rather than an implementation.

## The blocker: the published contract cannot express a verifiable request

CIP-30 `signData` returns `{ signature, key }` — a COSE_Sign1 plus a **COSE_Key****
****carrying the public key**. This service already models that shape in its own
`CardanoDataSignature` (`services/wallet-connector/src/types/index.ts:149-152`).

The published request schema is `{ address, message, signature }` — **no key**.
A Cardano address is a blake2b hash of the public key, so the key cannot be
recovered from it. There is nothing to check the signature against.

The field was removed by **KS-475** as "unread", which was true — the runtime
never read it, because the runtime never verified anything
(`wallet-connector.openapi.ts:139-143`). KS-475 was a correct fix for a
spec/runtime mismatch; its side effect was to delete the one field a real
implementation needs.

**Class rule worth keeping:** when a spec and a runtime disagree, establish which
one is right *before* aligning them. Aligning documentation to a stub silently
converts "not built yet" into "not in the contract", and the next reader cannot
tell the difference.

## Work required

1. **Contract (breaking):** re-add `key` to `WalletConnectorVerifyRequest` — the
   CIP-30 COSE_Key hex. Reintroduce a response schema (C-2 deleted
   `WalletConnectorVerifyResponse` because the operation had no success shape).
   Restore `200`, and remove the C-2 `expected-statuses` exception from
   `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` in the same PR so the operation is
   held to normal positive-acceptance again.
2. **Cardano path (CIP-8/COSE):** parse COSE_Sign1, verify Ed25519 over the
   `Sig_structure`, then — **the load-bearing step** — derive the address from the
   embedded public key and check it equals the claimed `address`. Without that
   binding, an attacker supplies their own key with their own valid signature and
   "verifies" as any address they name. Verifying the signature alone is not
   verifying ownership.
3. **EVM path:** the spec's old description also promised `ecrecover`. Decide
   whether EVM is in scope at all or whether the operation is Cardano-only —
   promising both again without building both repeats the original defect.
4. **Dependencies:** COSE/CBOR + Ed25519 (`@emurgo/cardano-message-signing-nodejs`
   and `cardano-serialization-lib` are WASM; a pure-JS `cbor` + `@noble/ed25519` +
   blake2b path avoids WASM). Two known traps apply: ESM-only packages imported
   from CJS crash at runtime in a way tsc and vitest both mask, and the demo VM is
   **ARM64**, so WASM/native builds must be checked there, not just on the dev
   machine.
5. **Test vectors:** real `signData` output from at least two wallets (Eternl,
   Lace). Hand-rolled vectors would test our own encoder against itself.
6. **Negative tests that must pass:** valid signature from a *different* key
   claiming this address; replayed signature against a different message;
   malformed COSE; wrong network id.

## Reachability, for prioritisation

Authenticated and gateway-routed (`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:627`,
`authenticateToken(true)`), published in the OpenAPI spec. **No in-repo consumer**
(swept `*.ts/tsx/js/py/yaml/gs` — only the route, its spec entry and the generated
yaml), so nothing internal is blocked by the 501 today. Priority should follow
whether an external integration needs wallet-ownership proof; until then the
refusal is the correct state.

## Do not

Re-open this as a "quick fix" that returns `200 { verified: false }` or restores a
permissive default. The C-2 regression suite
(`__tests__/ks488-c2-wallet-verify-fail-closed.test.ts`, 13 tests) asserts no
response may claim `verified: true`, independently of status code, and was
mutation-tested to confirm it fails if the old behaviour returns.

title: Sweeps 2026-09-08: 28 check/operation pairs have no live owner — 18 untriaged (the /api/auth/ + /mfa/ surface has ZERO baseline coverage) and 10 citing tickets that are Done
description:
## BLUF

A `pre-merge` run on 2026-09-08 produced **69 failing check/operation pairs**. **41 are owned by a live ticket. 28 are not** — and the second group splits into two distinct defects, one of which is a recurrence of the exact pattern [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) and [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks) were created to end.

This ticket owns those 28. It does **not** cover the 2 `verify-file` pairs from the same run — those belong to [KS-791](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-791/publish-verify-file-v1v2-in-the-spec-coupled-with-the-gateway-415-fix), see Scope below.

## Finding 1 — 18 pairs are not in the baseline at all

`config/schemathesis-baseline.json` is keyed `CHECK::OPERATION`; a pair not listed fails the gate. These 18 fired and are listed nowhere.

| Check | Operation | Occurrences |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `GET /api/auth/social/{provider}/callback` | 12 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/auth/wallet/link` | 8 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/auth/social/link` | 5 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/users/me/mfa/disable` | 5 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/users/me/mfa/verify` | 5 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `GET /api/auth/social/{provider}` | 4 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate` | 4 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `DELETE /api/auth/wallet/unlink` | 3 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/auth/mfa/backup-codes/regenerate` | 3 |
| `positive_data_acceptance` | `POST /api/auth/mfa/setup/verify` | 3 |
| `negative_data_rejection` | `PUT /api/privacy/settings` | 26 |
| `negative_data_rejection` | `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` | 19 |
| `negative_data_rejection` | `PUT /api/settings/notifications` | 11 |
| `response_schema_conformance` | `PUT /api/privacy/settings` | 26 |
| `response_schema_conformance` | `PUT /api/settings/notifications` | 10 |
| `response_schema_conformance` | `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` | 4 |
| `not_a_server_error` | `POST /api/auth/social/link` | 9 |
| `not_a_server_error` | `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate` | 1 |

**13 of the 18 are on** `/api/auth/` **or** `/mfa/`**, and that is not a coincidence:**

> **The baseline holds 0 entries touching** `/api/auth/` **or** `/mfa/`**, out of 97.**

That surface has never been triaged, because the runs the baseline was built from did not cover it. `scripts/run.py` contradicts itself on whether it should:

* line 10 — `pre-merge: 6 examples, all mode, 4 phases, all endpoints **including** /api/auth/`
* line 56 — `python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge  # PR gate: 6 examples, ~17 min measured (**excludes** /api/auth/)`

**Resolve that contradiction first.** If pre-merge is meant to cover `/api/auth/`, these 13 are a real and long-standing untriaged set. If it is not, the profile has been silently covering it anyway and the gate has been failing for a reason nobody documented. Either way the docstring is wrong in one of its two places.

The `positive_data_acceptance` cluster falls inside [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)'s declared class scope — that ticket says plainly *"read the counts as a floor, not a total… 64 operations is what this seed reached"*. It is listed here rather than assumed onto [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) because the baseline is keyed per pair, deliberately, so a class umbrella does not make an individual pair triaged.

## Finding 2 — 10 pairs cite tickets that are Done

These are in the baseline, so the gate treats them as known. Their owning tickets completed on **2026-09-05** and were archived the same day.

| Ticket | Status | Pairs still firing |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks) — `negative_data_rejection` recurrence | **Deployed to UAT** (completed + archived 2026-09-05) | 8 |
| [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) — undocumented 400 on `sig.json` | **Deployed to UAT** (completed + archived 2026-09-05) | 2 |

This is the pattern [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) and [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks) exist to prevent, recurring one level up. Their own text records it: the report used to attribute failures to [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) and [KS-266](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-266/fix-post-apiauthregister-negative-data-rejection-missing-password) *"with a bare ticket reference, which reads as 'someone owns this'"* after those had shipped. The rendering was fixed. **The baseline file now does the same thing** — the fix was applied to the report, not to the allowlist.

The baseline's own header states the rule: *"every entry carries a reason, an owning ticket and an expiry… on expiry the gate fails again and the entry must be re-justified or removed."* Ten entries need re-justifying against a live owner or removing. Note that **no entry was expired** — the expiry mechanism worked correctly; it is ticket *closure*, not time, that orphaned these.

## Why this was found by hand

The run's own baseline gate did not evaluate:

```
SKIPPED — upstream gate failed: report reconciliation and the schemathesis
baseline gate were not evaluated for this run.
```

That is [KS-752](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-752/schemathesis-baseline-gate-is-unreachable-runpy-skips-it-whenever-the) exactly (*"baseline gate is unreachable: [run.py](<http://run.py>) skips it whenever the sweep fails — i.e. on every run it exists to triage"*). The comparison above was produced by invoking `scripts/runner/baseline_gate.py` directly against the run's NDJSON. **Until** [KS-752](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-752/schemathesis-baseline-gate-is-unreachable-runpy-skips-it-whenever-the) **lands, every triage of this kind has to be done by hand**, which is how a set this size went unnoticed.

## Scope — what this ticket deliberately excludes

The same run produced 2 further untriaged pairs:

* `positive_data_acceptance::POST /api/verification/verify-file` ×7
* `positive_data_acceptance::POST /api/v2/verification/verify-file` ×7

**These are NOT part of this ticket.** Both operations were first published by [KS-791](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-791/publish-verify-file-v1v2-in-the-spec-coupled-with-the-gateway-415-fix), which is In Review, so no baseline could have held them. Cause: the request body is declared `type: string, format: binary` with no `minLength`, so an empty body is schema-compliant, but the handler answers 400. Fix belongs in [KS-791](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-791/publish-verify-file-v1v2-in-the-spec-coupled-with-the-gateway-415-fix) (`z.string().min(1)`), not here.

## Where this was run

**macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)** — the Mac, not the Ubuntu VM used for the runs of record on [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) / [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks). Docker Desktop 8 CPUs / 31.3 GiB. **Stack slot 3**, gateway `:7082`. Nothing else was running on the host.

| Component | Version |  | Component | Version |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OS | macOS 26.6.2 (arm64) |  | Docker | 29.7.2 |
| Python (venv + host) | 3.14.6 |  | Docker Compose | 5.5.0 |
| Schemathesis | 4.25.2 |  | Node (services) | 24.20.0 |
| PostgreSQL | 15.19 |  | Redis | 8.10.1 |
| nginx gateway | 1.30.4 |  | Docker Desktop | 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB |

Run of record: `pre-merge-2026-09-08T14-24-23Z-slot3`, seed `385098796`, 14.9 min, ~2,016 test cases, 342 operations, **0 errored**. 69 failing pairs / 599 occurrences.

**Host caveat:** the arm64 Mac is not the amd64 CI architecture, and the [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) / [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks) runs of record were taken on the Ubuntu VM. Diffing operation lists across those runs compares two hosts as well as two dates.

## Reproduce

```bash
export SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3
source systemTest/slot-target.sh
cd systemTest/schemathesis
python3 scripts/setup.py          # acquire the API token BEFORE the run
python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge
```

Then, because the gate self-skips ([KS-752](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-752/schemathesis-baseline-gate-is-unreachable-runpy-skips-it-whenever-the)), compare by hand:

```bash
python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
from pathlib import Path
from runner.baseline_gate import extract_failure_pairs, load_baseline, evaluate, format_verdict
pairs = extract_failure_pairs(Path('output/reports/<RUN_ID>/schemathesis-output.ndjson'))
bl = load_baseline(Path('config/schemathesis-baseline.json'))
print('\n'.join(format_verdict(evaluate(pairs, bl), pairs)))
"
```

**Read the counts as a floor, not a total** — property-based generation samples, it does not enumerate. Verify any specific operation with a targeted probe, never by its absence from one run.

## Fix direction

1. **Settle the** `/api/auth/` **question first** — fix the `run.py` docstring so the profile's coverage is stated once and correctly. Everything else depends on knowing whether those 13 pairs are in scope.
2. **Re-justify or remove the 10** [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks) **/** [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) **entries.** Each needs a live owning ticket or deletion. Consider whether `baseline_gate.py` should validate that an entry's ticket is still open, so closure orphans an entry as loudly as expiry does — that would stop this recurring a third time.
3. **Triage the 18** per the [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) direction: for each operation compare the route validator against the published spec, then either tighten the spec's request schema to the runtime truth or loosen the runtime where the spec is right. Never narrow the generator — the spec is the contract. Cluster by service registration file.
4. `PUT /api/privacy/settings` and `PUT /api/settings/notifications` fail **two** checks each (`negative_data_rejection` + `response_schema_conformance`, 26 occurrences apiece). Both sides of those two contracts are worth reading together.

## Owner

Assigned to Kamil per the backend/spec-owner convention recorded on [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (*"Root cause is non-systemTest (backend/spec)… Assigned to Kamil per the backend/spec-owner convention"*), since findings 1 and 3 are spec/handler drift. **Finding 2 is systemTest-side baseline hygiene and is Peter's call** — reassign or split if that is cleaner.
