title: KS-969 round-1 gate residue: the pre-suite step and its own test suite — six items on one path
description:
## BLUF

Six findings from the **#892 / KS-969 item 1 round-1 tier-2 gate**, left open after round 2 closed
F1 (BLOCKER), F2 and F3. **One ticket, six items** (Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule). **No round 3 —**
**Wednesday spent the cap deliberately**, so these are scheduled work, not a gate on #892.

Two of them (**items 3, 4, 5**) are defects in **the suite I wrote**, not in the product. Recorded
as plainly as the rest.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `runPreSuiteStep`, `provisionActors`, `writeRejectedManifest`, `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION`,
`_run_pre_suite` · PATH `pre-suite`, `pre_suite.test.sh`, `actor_manifest` · STRING "pre-suite",
"PROVISIONED", "unredacted", "seeded actors". Only **KS-969** (parent) and **KS-966** match.

---

## ITEM 1 (MAJOR, was F4) — akto's provisioning creates actors akto cannot read

`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts`, `performance/runner/actor_manifest.ts` and
`schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` all exist and are imported by live code. **akto has no**
**manifest consumer at all** — no `actorManifest`, no `generated/actors`. Its Secuura credentials come
from `config/secrets.yml` (`.env.example:40`).

So every akto run performs a real **account-creating** provisioning pass whose output akto never
reads, then prints `PROVISIONED — 5 generated actor(s)`. Under this PR's own vocabulary
(`pre-suite.ts:17`, *"the manifest is written; suites read generated actors"*) **that banner is false**
**for akto** — on the suite whose whole job is BOLA/BFLA role enforcement, a reader is told the wrong
identity was under test.

May be deliberate staging for KS-969 item 4. **Decide: either give akto a manifest consumer, or do**
**not hook it and say why.** A green banner asserting something untrue today is the worse of the two.

## ITEM 2 (MAJOR, was F5) — the schemathesis DEGRADED banner never reaches the run record

`_run_pre_suite` uses `subprocess.run` with inherited fds while `Logger` writes the archived log
itself. Measured with `--enable-logger-file`: **pre-suite lines in the archived log = 0.**
On the fatal path the log at least records `Pre-suite provisioning step failed`; on the **DEGRADED**
path `pre_rc == 0`, so nothing is logged and **the archived artefact contains no record that the scan**
**ran on seeded accounts** — the entire point of the banner. The silent fallback, relocated into the
artefact layer.
**Fix-shape:** capture the child's output and re-emit through `Logger`, or log the outcome
unconditionally rather than only on non-zero.

## ITEM 3 (MINOR, was F6) — `pre_suite.test.sh` mutates a shared stack and clobbers the real manifest

Run against any stack answering on `localhost:6882`, the suite **creates five real accounts** with
`FIXTURE_SEED="presuite-test-$$"` — **a fresh seed every run**, so they accumulate and are never
cleaned up — and **overwrites** `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json`, leaving every consumer
pointed at throwaway identities until someone re-provisions.
**This is confirmed by consequence:** the author exhausted the local register limiter (100/hour)
during development, which is exactly this defect compounding. Round 2 partly mitigates it (a role
collapse no longer publishes the manifest), **but the account creation is unchanged.**
**Fix-shape:** a stable seed, and gate the live arm behind an explicit opt-in rather than "a stack
answered".

## ITEM 4 (MINOR, was F7) — the `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION` control is inert and its comment is wrong

`pre_suite.test.sh` comments a cell *"the SAME remote target with the documented override must NOT*
*refuse"* — but it targets `http://127.0.0.1:1`, a **local** host, so it passes through the
`LOCAL_HOSTS` branch and the override is never exercised. Proved by tamper: making the override
branch permanently unreachable still left the suite fully green. **The documented escape hatch is**
**untested in both directions.** The cell still does the job of proving the step does not refuse
everything — so this is a weakened control plus a misleading comment, not an absent one.

## ITEM 5 (MINOR, was F8) — the DEGRADED stream routing is documented and pinned by nothing

`pre-suite.ts` routes DEGRADED to stderr with a comment explaining why. Collapsing both branches to
`console.log` left the suite green, because the harness merges the streams with `2>&1`. **A**
**documented invariant with no test is a comment.**

## ITEM 6 (MINOR, was F9) — unredacted server-error passthrough, PREMISE UNVERIFIED

`provision.ts:282` interpolates the server's `error.message` verbatim into the Error, and
`pre-suite.ts` interpolates that into the DEGRADED banner. Against a stub that echoes the request
body, **the generated password appeared in the banner in cleartext.**
**The gate proved the pipe is unredacted; it did NOT prove the real endpoint echoes payloads** — it
never reached a real stack. **Recorded with the premise unverified rather than smoothed over.** Value
at risk is low (generated `.invalid` local accounts); fix-shape is trivial — redact `password` keys
before interpolation.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-2 gate on **#892 @** `f54b2dce1`, reported 2026-09-07. F1/F2/F3 closed in round 2 at
`42e778203`. Wednesday ruled **no round 3**, so these ship as their own work.

title: api-gateway: dot-segment and extra-segment spellings (/abc/., /./abc, /abc/%2e ...) are forwarded verbatim without the spec method and auth gate; whether any reaches an upstream handler is unmeasured
description:
## BLUF

A request whose path differs from a spec path by a **dot segment or a percent-encoded dot/space/slash segment** is not matched by the gateway's spec method and auth gate, so the gate has no opinion and the request is **forwarded to the upstream verbatim**. The Opus gate on PR #1472 (KS-1469) measured this on base and on the merged tree; **I reproduced it independently on the merged develop tip** `d38302a9a27e` (the real app over real HTTP, a recording stub for every upstream, `NODE_ENV=test`). Unchanged by KS-1469.

| unauthenticated `GET` | gateway | upstream saw |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/credentials/abc` (canonical) | **401** | nothing |
| `/api/credentials/abc/` (KS-1469 fixed this one) | **401** | nothing |
| `/api/credentials/abc/.` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/.` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/./` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/./` |
| `/api/credentials/./abc` | **200** | `/api/credentials/./abc` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/..` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/..` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/%2e`, `/%20`, `/%2F` | **200** | the same raw path |
| `/api/./credentials/abc`, `/api/zzz-not-in-spec/.` (controls) | **404** | nothing |

**What this does and does not show.** It shows the gateway's gate is skipped and the raw path is forwarded (the stub answers 200). It does **not** show an exposure: whether a real upstream router (Express in vc-issuer, originate, ...) ever routes `/abc/.` or `/./abc` to a handler is **not measured**. By reading, Express does not collapse dot segments, so most of these should 404 at the upstream; the per-route `authenticateToken` and the upstream's own auth are the layers behind the gate. So this is a skipped defence-in-depth layer with an unmeasured tail, not a demonstrated bypass.

## Recommendation

Two steps, the first before the second:

1. **Measure** (read-only, in process): for each service router behind a `bearerAuth` spec op, send these spellings to the real router and record whether any reaches the handler. If none does, close this as defence-in-depth.
2. **If any does, or to close the class:** do not widen the spec regexes. Add a front-door normaliser in the family of KS-858's `normaliseRepeatedSlashes` that answers `400` (or rewrites) any path containing a dot segment, raw or percent-encoded, so the gate and the router can never see different paths. Tests first, a cell per spelling above, the canonical and the not-in-spec controls kept. Priority P3.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1472, "Not changed, and not checked" (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1472/verdict.md`; rows 12 to 22 of `evidence/probe_head.out`), plus my independent run above.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `dot-segment`, `dot segment`, `normaliseRepeatedSlashes`, `path spelling`, `%2e`: nearest are KS-858 (the repeated-slash class, fixed) and KS-983 (no systemTest suite drives a path-spelling variant), neither covers dot segments.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-858, KS-983.

title: systemTest actor/credential path: provisioning is never invoked, so the generated-actor path never resolves — and exactly one site (the SYSTEM_ADMIN persona) can never use it
description:
**KS-966 item 4 was stood down on measurement.** It was scoped as *"route the 12 systemTest sites through the existing generated-actor path"*. **That path never runs**, and for one site it could not work even if it did. This is the one logical path — the systemTest actor/credential story — with its items inside it, per Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.

## Searched before filing (958 issues, including archived)

| searched | hits |
| -- | -- |
| SYMBOL `getGeneratedActor` | KS-966 only (this ticket's parent) |
| SYMBOL `ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY` | KS-966 only |
| SYMBOL `provision-actors` | KS-966 only |
| PATH `systemTest/fixtures/generated` | **none** |
| SYMBOL `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | KS-967 only (as a guarded key name, different subject) |
| STRING `actor manifest` / `actors.json` | **none** |

**No existing ticket covers this.** Four sessions worked this repo today, so the check was worth making.

---

## ITEM 1 — Wire actor provisioning into a pre-suite step

`getGeneratedActor()` reads `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json` (`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts:45`) and returns `undefined` when absent. Measured on `origin/develop`:

* **0** files tracked under `systemTest/fixtures/generated`; the manifest is **absent** on a fresh tree.
* Written **only** by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.
* **Nothing automated invokes it**: no npm script · no `.github` workflow · no shell runner · **not** `playwright/global-setup.ts` (imports only `getApiBaseUrl`) · **not** `auth/auth.setup.ts` (imports `getTestAdminEmail`/`getTestAdminPassword` and logs in with them). Its only references are its own docstring showing manual invocation.
* **CONTROL:** the same `git grep` over the same paths finds `"test:unit"` in `playwright/package.json`. The instrument fires, so the zeros are real zeros.

**So the fallbacks are the live path, not redundancy.** This item is a pre-suite hook (a Playwright setup-project dependency, or the slot runner) **with its own test** — not a tail-end edit.

## ITEM 2 — The SYSTEM_ADMIN split. **M = 1**, and here it is

Of the 12 occurrences, **8 are documentary** (comments, docstrings, `@example` blocks) and belong to KS-965, not here. **Four are executable credential sources**, and three of them are satisfied by `orgAdmin`:

| site | drives | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:83` | `resolve_credentials("orgAdmin", …)` | **already keyed to** `orgAdmin`, with env override + fallback |
| `schemathesis/scripts/setup_api_key.py:53` | `POST /api/admin/api-keys`, gated `requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN','ORG_ADMIN')` | **ORG_ADMIN is admitted** by the route |
| `schemathesis/tests/test_authentication.py:26` | `POST /auth/login` only (success / invalid / missing-field) | **login requires no role at all** |
| `schemathesis/config/fixtures.py:82` | `Persona(key="super_admin", role="SYSTEM_ADMIN", …)` — *"Cross-tenant reads via X-Tenant-Override"* | **🔴 genuinely requires SYSTEM_ADMIN** |

**So exactly ONE site cannot be served by the generated-actor path** — and it cannot be served by design, not by omission. The manifest module says so in its own words:

> *"*`orgAdmin` *stands in for* `admin`*: SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through the API, so it can never be generated."*

**That single site is the whole decision.** Either its cross-tenant persona keeps a seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN credential supplied by environment, or the suite loses cross-tenant coverage. **Nothing else in the 12 needs a ruling.**

## ITEM 3 — `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is documented, but documented WRONG

The concern raised was that it might be undocumented. **It is named** — `playwright/README.md:27` and `:152`, `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` and `:238`. **The defect is sharper than absence:**

* `playwright/.env.example:27` has it **commented out**, so `cp .env.example .env` supplies nothing.
* `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` documents its **default as the retired literal** — a value that no longer works, because #888 removed the seeder's published default *and* the `getTestAdminPassword()` fallback.

**So a runner who follows the documentation sets a password that cannot authenticate**, and with GitHub Actions retired (20 of 20 runs `startup_failure`, measured 2026-09-07) nothing fails loudly to tell them. **This is an operational precondition #888 introduced without updating its documentation.** The security change was right; this is its unpaid half.

Both of those lines also carry the retired literal and are in KS-965's documentary census — **fix them here, since here is where their wrongness is load-bearing.**

## ITEM 4 — Only then, the 12 sites

Blocked on items 1–3. Doing it first inverts the F3 error corrected on KS-968 today: removing the harmless thing and leaving the one that detonates.

---

*Filed by s146 from the KS-966 item-4 measurement. Items 3 and 4 of KS-966 are closed by comment against this ticket. The 12/8/4/1 counts are mine and were re-derived after I found my first pass had omitted* `.py` *from its extension list — which had hidden six of the eight executable files.*

title: GET /api/security/keys: the declared 200 body is {keys:[...]} but the handler answers {success,data}; organizationId's uuid format is declared and not enforced (KS-747 residuals)
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th on Wednesday's ruling (L11, 2026-10-12): the two residual findings on `GET /api/security/keys` that KS-747 did NOT cover, as ONE ticket, so KS-747 can close as "declare the parameter".

KS-747's fix (#1318, squash `f28cd1fbc7a5`) declared `organizationId` as a required uuid query parameter. It is on develop, deployed, and confirmed on the SERVED spec of Kintsugi (bytes equal to the yaml at the deployed commit; the parameter reads required, in query, format uuid). These two things remain:

## 1. The declared 200 body is `{keys: [...]}`; the handler answers `{success, data: [...]}`

Read at the deployed commit `65d7722f83a6`: `services/security/src/security.openapi.ts` registers `ApiKeyListResponse = z.object({ keys: z.array(ApiKeySchema) })` for the 200, and `services/security/src/index.ts` `app.get('/api/keys', ...)` ends `res.json({ success: true, data: keys })`. So the two cannot both be right. Peter measured the consequence on all four KS-1353 sweeps (slot 3, head `d9ce1403d`, seed 1353): `response_schema_conformance` **31 of 31** own-test 200s fail with `"keys" is a required property`, and one more inside a stateful chain, 32 calls in all (KS-747, comment of 2026-09-28T12:31Z). KS-908's merge note also records the `keys`-vs-`data` naming as pre-existing drift.

Decision needed: which side is the contract. The house envelope elsewhere is `{success, data}`, which argues for changing the DECLARED schema to match the handler, not the handler (consumers already read `data`). Not decided here.

## 2. `organizationId` is declared `format: uuid`, and nothing enforces it

The handler checks only `if (!organizationId)`; a value that is not a uuid is accepted and simply matches nothing. Peter's sweeps record **5** `negative_data_rejection` failures on this operation, and KS-747's own merge note flagged it as "U-1" (declaration and enforcement are separate) and left it unfiled. Decision needed: enforce the format (400 on a non-uuid) or stop declaring it.

This is one instance of the class **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

## Not established by me

I did not observe either finding LIVE: the one authed GET I was cleared to make was refused 403, because the only QA credential (role OWNER) is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`. Both are read from source at the deployed commit and from Peter's sweep data.

Related: KS-747, KS-908, KS-1022, KS-1361 (Done; the sweeps' baseline), KS-1015.

title: positive_data_acceptance recurs at scale — 734 failures across 64 ops (KS-255 / KS-515 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Summary

This register tracks the biggest single class in the sweeps: the API politely refusing (4xx) request bodies the published spec says are valid. The steady fix is to bring each operation's spec and validator into line, in whichever direction is right for it. A small new member was added on 2026-09-28: `POST /api/gdpr/consent`, where the database declines a value the spec allows. Details are below for whenever it's picked up. Thank you, Kamil.

+++ The register (2026-08-07) and the 2026-09-28 addendum

### Why a new ticket

The predecessors are Done and archived: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done 2026-06-15) and [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (Done 2026-07-29, itself the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked) recurrence). This is the same class recurring at a larger scale, filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

### Finding

**734** `positive_data_acceptance` **failures across 64 operations**, about 75% of all check failures in `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z` (seed `2794626967`, 22,744 cases, 317 operations; Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64 VM, Schemathesis 4.24.3, Postgres 15.18). Each failure card embeds a curl; the run also wrote 94 replayable crash files. Counts are a floor, not a total: generation samples rather than enumerates.

### Fix direction

Per [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) / [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked): compare each route's validator with the spec, then tighten the spec to the runtime truth **or** loosen the runtime where the spec is right. Never narrow the generator. Cluster by service registration file.

### Addendum 2026-09-28 ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9)): `POST /api/gdpr/consent`

* **What:** a spec-valid body answered **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` *"One or more field values cannot be stored (too long or not an allowed value)"*. It's a draw: 2 of the 6 [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps (sweeps 2 and 5, ×1 each).
* **The case:** `userId` (uuid), `purpose: "marketing"`, `source` = a 5-character string with a supplementary-plane character, `expiresInDays: 552`, plus 3 undeclared keys (allowed, since the schema doesn't set `additionalProperties: false`).
* **Where the 400 comes from:** `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:153` (`mapGdprWriteDbError`) maps Postgres **22001 / 23514 / 22007 / 22008 / 22021** to this 400. Its own comment says *"Value the spec permits but the schema can't store"*. So the refusal is deliberate; the gap is that the published contract doesn't declare the constraint.
* **Which constraint fired isn't recoverable:** the originate logs predate a slot rebuild. Candidates: `source`'s unusual character (22021 or a length limit), `expiresInDays` with no declared `maximum` (22008), or the extra keys if they reach a stored column. (An earlier note that said "extra keys → 400" was too specific.)
* **Direction:** a targeted probe per candidate names the Postgres code, then declare it in the spec (`maxLength`, `maximum`, a `pattern`, or `additionalProperties: false`).
* Listed in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) for baselining against this ticket.

+++

title: systemTest/schemathesis: plain `mypy tests/` aborts on develop with "Source file found twice under different module names" (stub_sweep/stubs/admin_list.py)
description:
## BLUF

`mypy tests/`, the mypy leg of `systemTest/schemathesis/validate-lint.sh`, exits 2 on `origin/develop` `1ae6f17d19a8` without checking any file: *"Source file found twice under different module names"*. Run with `--explicit-package-bases` it completes and reports **317 errors in 100 files**.

## Seen

Found during [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719) (PR #1687), 2026-10-26. Python 3.14.9 linux/arm64 (official `python:3.14` image), venv built from `constraints.txt` (schemathesis 4.32.1) plus the `dev` extra. Run from `systemTest/schemathesis` on a `git archive origin/develop systemTest/schemathesis` export in an empty directory, so no working-tree state is in it.

* `mypy tests/` → `tests/functional/stub_sweep/stubs/admin_list.py: error: Source file found twice under different module names: "functional.stub_sweep.stubs.admin_list" and "tests.functional.stub_sweep.stubs.admin_list"`, then `Found 1 error in 1 file (errors prevented further checking)`.
* `mypy tests/precondition_probes.py` on the KS-1719 branch → the same class: `"precondition_probes" and "tests.precondition_probes"`.
* `mypy --explicit-package-bases tests/` → `Found 317 errors in 100 files (checked 403 source files)`. mypy's own note names that flag.
* The same flag on the KS-1719 branch: 317 errors in 100 files (404 checked), 0 of them in the new file.

## Where

`systemTest/schemathesis/validate-lint.sh` runs `mypy tests/ --no-error-summary 2>/dev/null` and counts a non-zero exit as FAIL. `[tool.mypy]` in `pyproject.toml` holds only `python_version = "3.14"` (read with `tomllib`): no `files`, `mypy_path`, `explicit_package_bases` or `exclude`.

## Searched

Secuura-PK, all states, title and description: `found twice under different module names`, `explicit-package-bases`, `stub_sweep/stubs/admin_list`: 0 hits each. Control: `_free_active_proposal_slot` returned KS-1719, so the search can fire.

## Not established

* Whether Peter's or Stuart's environment aborts the same way. Measured on one machine only.
* Whether the 317 is the same set on their venv. It is "as measured here".
* What invokes `validate-lint.sh` besides running it directly. Not checked.

title: The now-live audit export is quietly wrong: at most one upstream page, the to day dropped, type unvalidated, and the spec disagrees in four places
description:
## BLUF

**KS-1506 switches** `GET /api/admin/audit/export` **back ON** — it answered **401 to every caller, a platform admin included**, and now serves. Gate V1 measured that directly: a `SUPER_ADMIN` token gets **401 on develop and 200 on the branch**. So this is not defence in depth; it is a dead endpoint becoming live.

**The now-live export has four faults, and they MUST be repaired before this export is deployed.** Three of them make the exported file quietly wrong rather than failing, which is the worst shape for an audit artefact: an operator who exports a year gets a short file with no indication that it is short. Nothing is deployed today — develop only — so there is no live exposure yet. Refs KS-1506.

## Recommendation

**Treat "the file is short or mis-scoped but looks complete" as the defect class, not four separate nits.** An audit export that silently omits rows is evidence that cannot be relied on.

1. **Page the upstream, or declare the cap in the response.** Send a `limit` and loop until `total` is reached, with a stated bound; or, if a cap is intended, put it in `meta` and in the spec so a caller can tell a truncated export from a complete one.
2. **Decide the** `to` **boundary and state it.** Either make `to` inclusive of its whole day (end-of-day, or `< to + 1 day`), or document that `to` is exclusive — and pin whichever with a cell.
3. **Validate** `type` **against** `AuditType` **and 400 an unknown value**, rather than forwarding an arbitrary string. Then pin that the filter actually filters, against a stub that honours it.
4. **Reconcile the spec with the route** (gate V1's Minor 2) — four disagreements, listed in Detail.
5. **Add a cell per repair.** The existing `ks1506` suite drives the real gateway app against a stub upstream and is the natural home; `ks745-audit-export-calls-the-list-route.test.ts` mounts the router directly and is the cheaper home for the query-string assertions.

## Detail

All source references are `services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts` at develop `b01dbdf8aa558de95e10e529f4abc2a914342fb3`, unless named otherwise.

### 1. At most the upstream's default page is returned — no `limit` is ever sent

The upstream request is built at `:139-143` and carries `from`**,** `to`**,** `type` **only**. A case-insensitive search for `limit` in the whole file returns **one** line, and it is a **comment** (`:160`). The response's `total`, `limit` and `offset` are parsed and then **discarded**: `:161` keeps `data.data.logs` alone. There is no paging loop.

So the export returns whatever single page the security service chooses to answer with. **Gate V1 measured that as 50 rows.** The route then reports `totalEntries: entries.length` (`:211`) — the length of the page it got, not the size of the range — so the response's own count agrees with the short file and nothing contradicts it.

### 2. The `to` day is dropped

`formatDate` (`:68-75`) ends in `date.toISOString().split('T')[0]`, so any time component is **truncated** and `to` becomes a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` forwarded as-is (`:141`). The truncated values are also what reach the filename (`:191`) and `meta` (`:208-209`), so the artefact names the range the caller asked for while holding a narrower one. **Gate V1 measured the** `to` **day excluded from the result.** *(The truncation is anchored above; that the upstream then treats the bound exclusively is the gate's live reading, not mine.)*

### 3. `type` is not validated and the gateway filters nothing

`:115` reads it as `(req.query.type as AuditType) || 'all'` — a **cast, not a check** — and `:142` forwards it verbatim. The gateway applies no filter of its own, so whether `type` does anything at all is entirely the security service's business. **Gate V1 measured it ignored.** An unknown value therefore yields a 200 with a filename and `meta.type` that both assert a filter nobody applied.

### 4. The published spec disagrees with the route in four places (gate V1's Minor 2)

`services/api-gateway/src/api-gateway.openapi.ts:610-647`:

| spec says | the route does |
| -- | -- |
| `from`/`to` are `.optional()` (`:622-623`) | **both are required** — 400 `"Both \"from\" and \"to\" date parameters are required"` (`:122-125`) |
| `from`/`to` are `z.string().datetime()`, an RFC-3339 **date-time** (`:622-623`) | the route's own 400 says `"Invalid date format. Use YYYY-MM-DD."` (`:134`) and truncates anything finer |
| **no** `type` **parameter is declared at all** — 0 occurrences in the whole block | `type` is read (`:115`), forwarded (`:142`), and appears in the filename (`:191`) and in `meta` (`:210`) |
| the 200 JSON body is `{ entries: [...] }` (`:635`) | the route answers `{ success, meta, data }` (`:205-215`) — there is **no** `entries` **key** |

The last row is mine, not the gate's. A spec-driven client that reads `entries` gets `undefined` from a successful export.

### What this ticket is not

* **Not** KS-745, which is about the export calling a route the security service does not serve (`/api/audit/logs` → `/api/audit`). That is repaired; this is the surface left behind it.
* **Not** KS-1512 / KS-1545 / KS-1544, which are all `GET /api/platform/audit-log` — a different route with its own paging.

**Deduped before filing:** six searches (`audit export 50 rows`, `audit export type filter ignored`, `audit-log export to date`, `audit export spec disagrees`, `platform audit export`, `audit export limit`), **18 distinct candidates** read. The nearest are KS-745 and KS-1506 itself; none covers these four. Controls on the same reader: `Mount the audit-export router behind authenticateToken` returns KS-1506 first, `Gate S1 residue` returns KS-1643 first — so the search was live.

### Attribution

Faults 1-3's **effects** (50 rows, the dropped day, the ignored filter) are **gate V1's live measurements against a real security service**, which I did not reproduce. What I added is the **source anchor** for each mechanism and the fourth spec disagreement. Named in #1608's body as the condition on deploying this export.

Filed by Seat R 52nd (lane Secuura/Blockchain-R), 2026-10-19.

title: GET /api/platform/document-lookup answers a constant 500 and logs nothing when the platform-registry query fails
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/platform/document-lookup` (public; the verifier portal uses it to resolve a document's tenant) wraps its work in a `try/catch (err)` whose catch returns a constant `500 INTERNAL_ERROR "Document lookup failed"` and **never logs** `err`. ESLint flags it: `'err' is defined but never used` (line 990 at the head of PR #1501, line 989 on the base). A platform-DB outage, a bad connection string, or a statement error all look identical to the caller and leave nothing in the gateway log.

## Recommendation

Log the thrown error through the route's existing logger (its class and field names, as the sibling fixes do, not the message to the client) and keep the constant client body, which is the right thing to send. Test first: stub `pg.Pool` to reject, then assert both the 500 with the constant body and that exactly one log line carrying the error class was written.

Same family, different handlers (not duplicates): a failure vanishes in KS-1132 (`getPlatformAdmin`), KS-1345 (`GET /api/webhooks`) and KS-1018 (the verification-store reads).

## Detail

* **Source:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`, the `router.get('/api/platform/document-lookup'` handler, the outer `catch` at the end of the handler.
* **How it was found:** ESLint output while verifying PR #1501 (KS-1359). The warning is identical on the base bytes (checked by linting the base copy) and outside that diff, so it was deferred, not fixed there.
* **Read, not run, for whoever fixes it:** a new `pg.Pool` (`max: 2`) is built per request from `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` and ended in `finally`; `req.query.hash` and `documentId` are not type-checked before they are passed as query parameters (an array form would reach the driver). Neither is measured here.
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title, description and comments, archived included: `document-lookup` 0, `Document lookup failed` 0. Control on the same instrument: `platform_document_registry` returns 10 literal matches.

title: Stack tooling is not slot-derived end to end: stack_guard lists a project twice under mixed marker labels, dev-reload.sh / start-local.sh bypass stack_env.sh, and compose defaults FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS to slot 1
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil; it matters most on a busy host. A few pieces of stack tooling still assume slot 1 instead of deriving from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`, so on slots 2–4 they can double-report a stack, miss its containers, carry slot-1 URLs, or preflight the wrong gateway. Each fix is small and follows the existing `stack_env.sh` pattern. The four spots are below. Thank you.

+++ The four spots, evidence and fix shapes

1. `stack_guard.sh` `list_other_stacks` **(lines 105–111)** reports one line per label tuple (`sort -u` on `project|owner|branch`), so a project with one `owner=unknown` container (the [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) case) shows up twice. *Fix:* group by project and append an `unknown` count; add a case to `scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh`.
2. `dev-reload.sh` **(**`:45` `CONTAINER="secuura-$SVC"`**) and** `start-local.sh` don't source `stack_env.sh`, so they only find slot 1's containers and stamp `unknown` markers on anything they create. *Fix:* source `stack_env.sh` and use `${STACK_PREFIX}` (or retire `start-local.sh` if unused); extend `check-stack-safety.sh` so every script running `docker compose up|run|restart` must source it.
3. `docker-compose.yml` **defaults** `FRONTEND_URL` (`:767`) and `CORS_ORIGINS` (`:503`, `:2179`) to slot 1's ports. *Fix:* derive them from the exported `GATEWAY_PORT` / `WEBSITE_PORT`, so an unedited `.env` is right on every slot; pin it in `stack_env.test.sh` or `check-stack-safety.sh`.
4. **The** [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) **preflight's PROVISIONED legs** default to `:6882` (`preflight.sh:94`). On a slot-N worktree they probe slot 1 unless `GATEWAY_URL` is passed. *Fix:* derive from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` via `stack_env.sh`, and fail loudly with an example command when no slot is named locally.

**Seen 2026-09-28** (Peter's Mac, `develop` `d9ce1403d`), bringing up slot 4 with slots 2 and 3 running:

```
Other Secuura stacks running on this host (NOT affected by this operation):
  secuura_slot2 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1286-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1353-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner unknown, branch unknown
```

The `owner unknown` container came from a bare `docker compose` call in the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) worktree at about 09:33 UTC. That's the same mechanism as spot 2, reached by hand, and slot 3 was restored through `start-secuura.sh` afterwards.

**Verify:** the guard prints a mixed-label project once; `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N ./scripts/dev-reload.sh api-gateway` finds `${STACK_PREFIX}-api-gateway`; an untouched `.env` renders slot-N URLs (`docker compose config`); the preflight probes slot N; `check-stack-safety.sh` goes red on a revert of any of the four.

Related: [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) (unknown markers; PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1181](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1011-markerwarn-start-secuurash-warns-loud-and-named-on-unknown-bc1340b4bef0) warns in `start-secuura.sh` only) · [KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) (slot design) · [KS-1034](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1034/check-stack-safetysh-resolves-the-wrong-repo-root-inside-a-git-hook) · [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) (the same slot-derivation theme, harness side).

+++

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 3 — the spot-3 pin in `check-stack-safety.sh` is a natural home for the point-1 guard, and spot 4 is coordinated with [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports)'s leg 13.

title: Spec: three more operations reject a "valid" empty body (KS-1364 class) — POST /api/security/keys, PUT /api/security/keys/admin-scopes/{userId}, POST /api/timestamps/verify; and POST /api/security/keys declares no body schema at all
description:
**BLUF:** Three operations not on [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s list show the same spec drift: the published spec does not mark their request body `required: true`, so Schemathesis sends a schema-"valid" request with **no body**, and the service correctly answers 400. In addition, `POST /api/security/keys` publishes **no body properties at all**. These are spec fixes, not service fixes. [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) owns the class but is In Progress, so this is a small linked ticket rather than an edit to it. Thank you, Kamil.

## Measured

Run `full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2` (platform-k slot 2, Schemathesis 4.32.1, seed 1674), check `positive_data_acceptance` ("schema-valid request rejected"), plus a control run from `develop`'s own harness (`develop` `32964477f`, same slot, seed 1674, freshly reset database):

| Operation | Branch run | Develop control | Request sent | Response |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `PUT /api/security/keys/admin-scopes/{userId}` | 7 | 5 | no body (all 7) | 400 `Validation failed`, `invalid_type` / `received: undefined` |
| `POST /api/security/keys` | 3 | 3 | no body (2 of 3) | 400 `Validation failed`, `invalid_type` / `received: undefined` |
| `POST /api/timestamps/verify` | 2 | 0 | no body (both) | 400 `Validation failed`, `hash` `Required` |

The differing counts are sampling: whether a run generates an empty body for an operation varies. `positive_data_acceptance` on `POST /api/timestamps/verify` is in neither the baseline nor [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s table; the two `/api/security/keys` operations are not in [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s table either. None of these pairs is in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json`.

**The third** `POST /api/security/keys` **case** sent a body with `name: "\n"`. The service trims it and refuses an empty name (`too_small`, `min 1`, path `name`), which is correct ([KS-202](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-202/enforce-input-trimming-on-all-user-facing-string-fields-across) trim rule). It reads as a failure only because the published schema for this operation declares no properties and no `required` list: checked in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, `paths./api/security/keys.post.requestBody` has no `required` flag and an empty schema.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The spec marks `requestBody.required: true` for all three operations (at the generator, `*.openapi.ts` then `npm run generate-openapi`, as [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) proposes).
2. `POST /api/security/keys` publishes its real body schema: the fields the service's Zod schema accepts, `name` with `minLength: 1` after trimming, and the `required` list.
3. **Automated test:** a full Schemathesis sweep on a slot reports no `positive_data_acceptance` failure for these three operations, and the offline spec checks pass (`npm run check:openapi` / the preflight). No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.
4. If [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) lands a blanket fix first, this ticket is closed as covered, with the measured re-run as evidence.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given. Found while classifying the full-run failures for [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (step 11b).

title: governance: a failed database read answers as empty - GET /proposals returns 200 [] and the active-proposal cap fails OPEN (dbGetAllProposals swallows into [])
description:
## BLUF

**In** `services/governance`**, a FAILED database read answers as if the data were empty.** `dbGetAllProposals` catches every error and returns `[]` (`governanceService.ts:254-256`), and nothing above it checks. So:

* `GET /api/governance/proposals` and `GET /api/governance/proposals/active` answer **200 with an empty list** when the database fails. A caller cannot tell "no proposals" from "the read failed".
* **The active-proposal cap fails OPEN.** `createProposal` enforces `maxActiveProposals` by reading active and queued proposals through the same helper (`:495-497`). A failed read returns `[]`, the `>=` check is false, and the cap is not applied.

This is KS-1345's class (webhooks), which does not cover governance. **Not fixed in PR #1696**, which leaves `governanceService.ts` untouched.

## Where (develop `c2505d5c6fe0`; read from source, not run against a database)

`services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`:

* `:224-258` `dbGetAllProposals`, with `} catch (err: any) { logger.error('DB get all proposals failed', …); return []; }` at `:254-256`. The error is logged server-side; the caller gets `[]`.
* Its callers:
  * `:605` `getProposals`, used by the route `GET /proposals` (`routes/governance.ts:150`) and `GET /proposals/active` (`:168`). Both answer `200 { success: true, data: [], count: 0 }`, and neither route has an error path.
  * `:495` `createProposal` — the cap check at `:496`: `if (activeProposals.length >= governanceConfig.maxActiveProposals) throw new ConflictError(…)`.
  * `:977` `getGovernanceStats`.
  * `:1013` `processExpiredProposals` — a failed read expires nothing.

## The same shape elsewhere in the file (facts; consequences not traced unless stated)

Every `catch` in `governanceService.ts` that returns a value instead of rethrowing:

| line | helper | returns on failure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:218` | `dbGetProposal` | `undefined` (read by callers as "no such proposal") |
| `:254` | `dbGetAllProposals` | `[]` |
| `:264` | `dbGetParticipant` | `undefined` |
| `:274` | `dbGetParticipantByAddress` | `undefined` |
| `:312` | `dbGetAllParticipants` | `[]` |
| `:341` | `dbGetActiveDelegations` | `[]` |
| `:447` | `getTotalVotePower` | `0`, used at `:571` (`submitProposal`) and `:979` |
| `:1025` | `processExpiredProposals` | `0` |

The three save helpers (`:166`, `:186`, `:204`) and `verifyDbReady` (`:365`) rethrow. **What a** `0` **total vote power does to quorum is not traced.**

## Why it matters

* KS-1345 records that this exact shape once hid a real defect for its whole life: a query that always failed and always read as empty.
* Here the same failure can also lift an abuse limit (the cap), not just blank a list.
* Combined with a partial failure, a failed SELECT can disable the cap while the INSERT succeeds. In a full outage the INSERT fails too, at `dbSaveProposal`, which rethrows.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

KS-1345's shape: let the read reject to the route, so it answers a constant 500 with the error logged server-side. Ruling-sensitive choices for whoever fixes it:

* whether a NOT-FOUND (`undefined`) must stay distinguishable from a FAILED read;
* whether the cap should refuse, rather than allow, when it cannot count.

## Related, NOT duplicates

* **KS-1345** — `GET /api/webhooks` swallows a failed list query into `200 []`. Same class, different service.
* **KS-1722** / PR #1696 — the proposals-list filter. Found while building it, and not touched by it.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **711** Secuura-PK issues, all states:

* `dbGetAllProposals` → KS-1722 only (the filter, not the catch).
* `governanceService.ts` → KS-1722 only.
* `DB get all proposals failed` → 0.
* `swallows a failed` → KS-1657 (originate anchors), KS-1345 (webhooks), KS-888 (`dbSaveApiKey`) — other services.
* `into 200 with an empty` and `return [];` → KS-1345 only.

KS-1345's description names only `routes/webhooks.ts:196` and `:412`. Control: `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828` finds KS-1723.

## Found by

Seat K while building KS-1722 (PR #1696), filed facts-only on the coordinator's ruling. Not measured against a running database.

title: Sweeps 2026-08-05: untracked failures across 10 ops — response-schema recurrence (KS-498 residual), 3 genuine 500s, non-envelope 5xx on by-design-503 ops, undocumented status
description:
Findings from two runs on the same code, 2026-08-05: `full-2026-08-05T08-44-00Z` and `pre-merge-2026-08-05T09-18-45Z` (Schemathesis 4.24.3, 316/318 operations, 316/317 past auth, no health-check suppression, untruncated messages). Everything else in those runs maps to [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) / [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code). The operations below map to **no ticket**.

> **Read the counts as a FLOOR, not a total.** The two runs agreed on the failing *classes* but not the failing *operations* — five ops failed in pre-merge that were absent from the full sweep. Property-based generation samples; it does not enumerate. Verify a specific operation with a targeted probe, never by its absence from one run.

## 1. response_schema_conformance recurs on 4 NEW ops ([KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) residual)

[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) is **Done** — closed 2026-07-29 having verified the class down to 2 ops, both [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) family. **None of these four are those two**, so this is a recurrence on different operations, not unfinished work. Filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` | 14 | yes |
| `POST /api/presentations/verify` | 13 | yes |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | 4 | yes |
| `PATCH /api/security/events/{id}/resolve` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret` — **added 2026-09-10** from `pr-ks-971-2026-09-10T16-31-45Z-slot1` (Schemathesis 4.25.x, `pr` profile, slot 1, develop at `688f4dded` + the [KS-971 (2/2): slot-isolate the k6 performance harness, and prove it by fault injection](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-971-22-slot-isolate-the-k6-performance-harness-and-prove-it-by-34bc0f07c5ba) systemTest branch). Runtime answers `200 {"success":true,"clientSecret":"scs_…","warning":"Store the new client_secret securely — it cannot be retrieved later."}`; the declared 200 schema requires `id`. Handler `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1079`; the route reached develop between the 2026-08-05 sweeps and 2026-08-28 ([KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) oauth-apps work), which is why it is absent above. The 2026-08-19 baseline already lists its `positive_data_acceptance` pair ([KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)) but NOT `response_schema_conformance`, so this pair fails the gate until fixed or baselined. | — | pr: yes |
| `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/session/{sessionId}` — **added 2026-10-22** ([KS-1511](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1511/audit-log-limit-follow-up-retire-the-stale-accepted-baseline-entry) control sweep `pre-merge-2026-10-22T11-15-40Z-slot1`, platform-k slot 1 on Peter's Mac, develop `f75b52721`, `pre-merge --seed 1511`). ST108 ×1: `"sessionId" is a required property` against the declared 200 schema (requires `sessionId`, `status`, `createdAt`). Same message as the sibling `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/result/{sessionId}`, already baselined under this ticket; whether both share one handler defect in `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts` is not established. Not baselined, so it fails the triaged-baseline gate whenever drawn; seen intermittently before (before-only pair in a version-bump comparison, `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` \~line 1099). | — | pre-merge: yes |

Three of the four **also** fail `negative_data_rejection` — likely one root cause ("nothing validated, so nothing shaped correctly"), not four independent drifts. Worth confirming before treating them as separate work. Fix per [KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444): runtime is truth, reconcile the declared response schema, regenerate with `npm run generate-openapi`, rebuild api-gateway on both targets (it bundles the spec).

## 2. Three genuine 500s on schema-compliant input

| Operation | Site | Mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/users/admin/create` | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:177` | `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard — a non-string `email` (e.g. `{}`) raises `TypeError` → 500 instead of a typed 4xx |
| `GET /api/users/admin/list` | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:344` **and** `:398` | `parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0` — `-1` is truthy so it passes through; Postgres rejects it (`OFFSET must not be negative`) → 500. The `|| 0` fallback only catches `NaN` |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` | not yet traced | 500 in the pre-merge run; absent from the full sweep |

**The negative-offset pattern is SIX sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reached:

* `auth/src/routes/users.ts:344`, `:398`
* `originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1006`, `:1166` — raw `LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset}`, x4 queries
* `tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:556`
* `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:374` — `Math.min` caps the upper bound only, no negative guard

**Not an injection risk** — the raw-SQL cases use Prisma `$queryRaw` tagged templates (parameterised) and `parseInt(...) || 0` always yields a number. The defect is the unvalidated negative reaching Postgres as a 500. A fix touching only `users.ts:344` leaves five siblings exposed. Suggested fix: `.int().min(0)` on `offset` at handler entry.

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

## 3. `integration_5xx_guard` fires on by-design-503 ops — non-envelope 5xx

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/timestamps` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/credentials` | 1 | yes |

Both are on `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS` in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/checks.py` (blanket `not_a_server_error` disabled because they 503 by design when their provider is unconfigured). The [KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing)/[KS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-499/unconfigured-provider-503s-on-7-write-ops-beyond-ks-268s-3-exclusions) guard replaces it and **passes** a clean declared-503 envelope — so a failure here means a 5xx that is **not** a proper 503 envelope, i.e. a genuine server error the exception list is demonstrably not hiding. Worth confirming whether it is a raw 500 or a malformed 503 body.

## 4. Undocumented status — `POST /api/referrals/apply` (6)

`status_code_conformance` fails: the operation returns a status not in its declared response set. Distinct from [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (`GET /api/documents/{id}/sig-json`, still open) — same class, different operation. Fix per [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code): either stop returning the undeclared status, or declare it — whichever reflects intended behaviour, per the "spec is the contract" rule.

## Not included here

* `POST /api/presentations` failing `not_a_server_error` — **already fixed** under [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) by adding it to `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`; live-verified it 503s by design (`VC_SIGNING_KEY is required to sign a presentation. Refusing to emit an HMAC-signed presentation falsely labelled Ed25519`) when `holderDID` is present.
* New `negative_data_rejection` ops (`POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector`, `POST /api/users/admin/create`) and the still-failing status-list trio — registered on [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data), whose register is live and In Progress.

## Please run the full sweep before closing

The fast PR gate covers none of these classes — it does not validate response bodies, does not generate negative bodies, and does not fuzz these write paths:

```bash
cd systemTest/schemathesis
python3 scripts/run.py full        # local stack on :6882
```

Full artefacts under `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/` for both run directories — NDJSON event stream (authoritative for check totals), VCR cassette, HAR, per-call metrics, replayable crash files.
