title: m365 OAuth callback: a provider error_description of ~170+ astral characters makes the nginx edge answer 502 ("upstream sent too big header") instead of the redirect - on develop
description:
**BLUF:** On **develop**, the public `GET /api/m365/callback` with a long provider `error_description` made of 4-byte characters (emoji) gets **502 BAD_GATEWAY from the nginx edge**. m365 and api-gateway both answer the expected 302. [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s merged 200-code-point cap keeps the redirect `Location` bounded, at about 2,460 characters, but not small enough for the edge: together with the gateway's other response headers it passes the edge's response-header buffer. Nothing crashes. The admin sees a gateway error instead of the OAuth outcome. Kamil, I'd be grateful for your view on the fix below.

## Where and when (develop)

The product code under test was **develop, unchanged**. The two builds below differ from develop only by a systemTest-only commit ([KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s new test file and docs), so no product code differed.

| Build | Product = develop at | Build started (UTC) | Stack |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `4111d0cf6` | `8661f5d41` | 2026-10-26 10:45:05 | platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac |
| `65ced3173` | `5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492` | 2026-10-26 11:17:45 | platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac |

Image revision labels on api-gateway, originate, m365-integration and nginx-gateway matched each build. Every container was healthy, with RestartCount 0 before and after.

**Seen 5 of 5 runs** on 2026-10-26: targeted runs at 10:59 (build `4111d0cf6`) and 11:37, the full pre-merge sweep at 11:38-11:56, and the two re-check rounds at 12:18 and 12:20 (all on `65ced3173`).

**Not measured on a develop-only harness:** the develop control sweep that day (slot 2, develop `5f6899918`, built 2026-10-26 12:20:09 UTC) has no test for this route, because the test is new on the [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) branch. The product code was identical in every run, so the result applies to develop.

## What was measured

Request (unauthenticated, as Microsoft's redirect is): `GET /api/m365/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=` + 400 × U+1F600, URL-encoded.

| Layer | Answer | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| m365-integration | 302 | its log: `OAuth callback error`, then `Request completed … statusCode 302` |
| api-gateway | 302 | its log: `path /api/callback, statusCode 302` |
| nginx edge (`secuura-nginx-gateway`) | **502** | `upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream, client: 192.168.65.1, server: localhost, request: "GET /api/m365/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=%F0%9F%98%80…` |
| caller | **502** | `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_GATEWAY","message":"The upstream service is not reachable right now."}}` |

**Control:** 150 × U+1F600 passes: 302, `Location` 1,860 characters, about 3,676 bytes of response headers in total. ASCII descriptions of 5,000 characters and a 199-character string with an emoji at the boundary also pass (302, bounded).

**Not a missing service** (the usual meaning of a 502 here, per DEV-PROCESS.md): all 33 services were up and healthy, and nginx names the cause.

## Cause: verified and assumed

* **Verified:** the edge rejects the upstream's response headers as too large. The 200-code-point cap makes the reflected `message` up to 200 × 12 = 2,400 encoded characters for astral text.
* **Assumed, not verified:** the edge uses nginx's default `proxy_buffer_size`, which is one memory page, usually 4 KB. `nginx -T` in the container shows no `proxy_buffer_size` or `proxy_buffers` directive.
* **Inferred, not measured:** the demo VM puts the same nginx gateway behind Caddy, so it is likely to behave the same.

## Suggested fix

The fix [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) already recommends removes this: put only a short **code** on the redirect URL (for example the provider's `error` code), and keep the provider's `error_description` in the server log only, as `services/auth` does. Then the `Location` stays small whatever the provider sends. Raising the edge's `proxy_buffer_size` would also stop the 502, but it would leave the reflection in place.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_m365_callback_redirect.py::TestM365CallbackReflectedText::test_ks1641_oversized_description_keeps_the_redirect_bounded_and_the_service_up[400-astral-code-points]` (added on the [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) branch) passes on a slot built from the fix: a 302 with a `Location` of at most 2,500 characters, and the service answers the next callback. A service-level unit cell with the same 400-emoji input asserting a 302 is also wanted. No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.
2. **Docs:** if the codes-only fix lands, no doc change beyond [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s. If the edge buffer is changed instead, document the value and the reason beside the nginx config.
3. **systemTests:** no further change; the cell above already exists. Update `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` → [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) when it turns green.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given.

**Related:** [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) (the reflection and redirect target; the merged cap this follows from), [KS-1670](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1670/m365-integration-three-more-reflection-sites-from-gate-am1-an) (other reflection sites in the same file).

*Raised on Peter's instruction, 2026-10-26, from the* [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) *test pass. Duplicate searches, KS and PS, including archived, all with no match: "upstream sent too big header", "proxy_buffer_size", "nginx 502 Location header", "m365 callback 502". Closest:* [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) *(Done) and* [KS-1369](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1369/api-gateway-crashes-under-load-onproxyreq-calls-setheader-after-the) *(In Progress), both gateway 502s under load, a different cause.*

title: POST /api/documents with a 10,000-character title answers 500 instead of a 4xx - on develop
description:
**BLUF:** On **develop**, `POST /api/documents` with `{"title": "x" × 10000}` answers **500** (an 89-byte body) instead of a clean 4xx. The other nine fuzzed titles in the same test pass: empty, NUL, XSS, whitespace, emoji, CJK, Hebrew, SQL-like and path-like. Nothing is logged by originate or api-gateway, so the cause is not visible from the logs. The likely cause is below, marked as unverified. Kamil, I'd be grateful if you could take a look.

## Where and when (develop)

| Run | Build / product | Build started (UTC) | Stack | Result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **develop control** pre-merge sweep, 12:23-12:40, seed 2391897950 | **develop** `5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492` (clean develop worktree) | 2026-10-26 12:20:09 | platform-k slot 2, Peter's Mac | **500** |
| pre-merge sweep, 11:38-11:56, same seed | `65ced3173` = develop `5f6899918` + a systemTest-only commit | 2026-10-26 11:17:45 | platform-k slot 1 | 500 |
| targeted re-check, 12:17:45 | same | same | slot 1 | 500 |
| targeted re-check, 12:19:52 | same | same | slot 1 | 500 |

**Seen 4 of 4 runs, including on clean develop.** Every container was healthy with RestartCount 0. Image revision labels matched each build.

## What was measured

* **Test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_fuzz_comprehensive.py::test_string_parameter_fuzzing[xxxx…]`, failing with `AssertionError: KS-1042: title 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' → 500 | assert 500 < 500`. The test's contract is "never a 5xx, and a refusal carries an error body". A 201 is acceptable for legitimate titles. Caller: ISSUER_ADMIN, which holds documents:write.
* **Edge:** nginx `"POST /api/documents HTTP/1.1" 500 89` at 11:40:41, 12:17:45 and 12:19:52.
* **api-gateway:** `method POST, path /api/documents, statusCode 500, duration 4-5ms`, with no error line before it.
* **originate:** no error line for these requests in its log.

## Cause: verified and assumed

* **Verified from source (develop):** the published `DocumentCreateRequest.title` (`services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts`) is `z.string()` with **no** `maxLength`. `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:97` declares a `title VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL` column.
* **Assumed, not verified:** the 10,000-character title reaches the insert and Postgres refuses it (`22001`, value too long), which surfaces as a 500. I have not confirmed that `:97` is the table this route writes, or that the refusal is what produces the 500. Nothing is logged, which is itself worth fixing, in the same way as [KS-1510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1510/get-apiplatformdocument-lookup-answers-a-constant-500-and-logs-nothing).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated test:** the existing `test_string_parameter_fuzzing[xxxx…]` cell passes on a slot built from the fix: a 4xx with the error envelope, or a 201 if long titles are accepted by design. Plus a service-level unit cell in originate that sends a title one character over the limit and asserts a 400 with a field-named message. No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.
2. **Docs:** the spec declares the real bound: `maxLength` on `DocumentCreateRequest.title` at the generator, then `npm run generate-openapi`, with api-gateway rebuilt or restarted so it serves the new spec. No other doc change.
3. **systemTests:** no change needed; the cell already exists and turns green with the fix. If Schemathesis then reports a `negative_data_rejection` pair for the new bound, it is triaged separately.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given.

**Related:** [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) (three other genuine 500s from earlier sweeps, different routes), [KS-1042](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1042/systemtest-no-regression-covers-the-ks-742-api-key-tenancy-class-and) (the fuzz cells were given assertions there).

*Raised on Peter's instruction, 2026-10-26, from the* [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) *test pass and its develop control. Duplicate searches, KS and PS, including archived, with no match: "document title length 500", "title maxLength", "value too long for type character varying".* [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema)*'s three 500s are on other routes.*

title: Security: seven GET-by-id routes serve any authenticated caller's object — transfers/{id}, transfers/{id}/history, delegations/{id}, analytics/exports/{id}, governance/participants/{id}, governance/proposals/{id}, security/audit/{id} (found by Schemathesis ST402)
description:
**BLUF:** Schemathesis's object-level-authorization check (ST402, WFC 906) ran for the first time on a live stack under [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) and found six GET-by-id routes where a second user is served the first user's object with an equivalent body. For five of them the code has no caller or tenant check at all; the sixth (`security/audit/{id}`) is tenant-scoped only. I would be grateful if you could look at the six routes, and rule on the three where it is unclear whether the data is meant to be shared. Thank you, Kamil.

## What was measured (not assumed)

Run `full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2` (platform-k slot 2, branch `feature/ks-1674-schemathesis-object_level_authorization-4310-never-runs` at `8a203488b`, Schemathesis 4.32.1, seed 1674). A second sweep sends only `object_level_authorization` as two **OWNER users in the same tenant** (`owner`, `ownerPeer`). 259 peer replays were sent; 6 violations. Each was independently counted in the leg's NDJSON and its JSON verdict (6 = 6). Upstream's anonymous-replay control passed for each (an unauthenticated request is refused, so the data is not public). Its "can the peer list the object" control is NOT evidence that the peer cannot: for transfers the code shows the list route returns every transfer (see the correction below).

| Route | Case id (`st replay <id>`) | What the code does (file:line, read 2026-10-20) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/transfers/{id}` | `1U6qU1` | `transfer/src/index.ts:649-661` → `dbGetTransfer` = `SELECT * FROM svc_transfers WHERE id = $1` (`:247-251`). No caller, no tenant. The row has `currentOwnerId`, `newOwnerId`, `initiatedBy`; the mutating routes read the caller from `req.user` (`:519, 797, 865, 948`). **Correction to an earlier version of this ticket:** the list `GET /api/transfers` is NOT scoped to the caller. It returns every transfer unless the caller passes their own `?ownerId=` (`:602-643`; `dbGetTransfersByOwner` at `:262-269` is used only for that client-supplied value). So any authenticated user can enumerate all transfers, and then read each one by id. |
| `GET /api/transfers/{id}/history` | `9JG2nb` | `:904-922`, same lookup; returns `statusHistory`, `approvals`, `rejections`. |
| `GET /api/delegations/{id}` | `7mMh5M` | `transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts:139-143` never reads `req.user`. The row has `delegatorId`/`delegateId`, and the list route (`:96-101`) filters by them. |
| `GET /api/analytics/exports/{id}` | `rVMsIL` | `analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts:334-338` → `memExports.get(id)`. The `ExportResult` type has no owner or tenant field at all. |
| `GET /api/governance/participants/{id}` | `eiqPHs` | `governance/src/routes/governance.ts:80`; lookup by id then wallet address, no tenant field. The gateway mounts `/api/governance` with `authenticateToken(false)` (`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1142`), i.e. optional auth: **not checked** whether the service rejects an unauthenticated caller. |
| `GET /api/security/audit/{id}` | `grR2ha` | `security/src/index.ts:898-910`: tenant-scoped (a foreign tenant gets 404), but no owner comparison. |

Lines for the analytics, governance and history rows come from a read-only code read; I re-read the transfer, delegation, analytics and audit handlers myself. The OpenAPI entries declare only `bearerAuth`; none describes an access scope.

## What is NOT established

* **Cross-tenant exposure is inferred, not measured.** Five of the six handlers carry no tenant filter, so a caller in another tenant can probably read them too. The local stack has no way to place a user in a second tenant, so the Schemathesis leg only covers two users in one tenant ([KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) keeps the cross-tenant pairing open).
* I did not trace database row-level security, and did not check whether the governance service itself refuses an unauthenticated caller.
* Whether same-tenant OWNER users are *meant* to read each other's objects is not written down anywhere I could find (no rule in the platform docs or `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`). For transfers and delegations the mutating routes already use the authenticated caller (and the delegation list is scoped to the caller), so I read those as defects. The transfer *list* is the exception: it is unscoped today, which is a second exposure (acceptance criterion 5). For **analytics exports, governance participants and security audit** it may be deliberate; those three need a ruling. Severity is left unset for you.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For each of the six routes, a caller who is not entitled to the object receives 404 (the convention `security/audit/{id}` already documents: a foreign id returns 404 so existence is not leaked), or the route is recorded as deliberately shared with the reason written beside the handler and in the OpenAPI description. Entitlement for transfers and delegations is the party fields the mutating routes already use (`currentOwnerId`/`newOwnerId`/`initiatedBy`; `delegatorId`/`delegateId`).
2. **An automated test that demonstrates the fix**, per route, red before and green after: a service-level test with two users where the second user's GET of the first user's object is refused. (No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.)
3. A live `full` sweep on a slot no longer reports the six `object_level_authorization` pairs (the Schemathesis leg from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) is the end-to-end evidence); any remaining pair is either fixed or baselined with a reason and an owner, never masked.
4. A decision recorded on whether same-tenant visibility is intended for analytics exports, governance participants and security audit entries, and, if a tenant filter is added, a cross-tenant test (a second tenant needs a way to be provisioned for it).
5. `GET /api/transfers` returns only the caller's transfers (or the ones they are a party to), not every transfer; the scope is the same rule as the by-id read, and is decided together with it.
6. The systemTest module `tests/test_get_by_id_object_authorization.py` (six tests, below) XPASSes strictly for each fixed route; the `xfail` marker on each is removed in the same change, so a fixed route is then asserted for real. A route ruled deliberately shared is moved to `test_by_design_permissive.py` instead.
7. `schemathesis-baseline.json` entries for the six `object_level_authorization::<operation>` pairs (if added meanwhile) are removed when this lands.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts` (that file is platform-s), so none are given. Same class, different routes: [KS-1699](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1699/security-three-certification-write-routes-have-no-per-record-access) (certification write routes without a per-record check), [KS-1686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1686/prism-get-apicredentialsid-returns-any-stored-prism-credential-by-id) (prism credentials by id without an owner check). Found under [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under); part of Review A ([KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor)).

## Test details (everything needed to reproduce)

**Where.** Branch `feature/ks-1674-schemathesis-object_level_authorization-4310-never-runs`, commit `8a203488b` on `develop` `32964477f` plus later uncommitted test/doc changes (a PR will follow under [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)). The platform under test is `develop` unchanged: that branch changes only `systemTest/`. Mac, Docker Desktop (8 CPUs / 31.3 GiB), Python 3.14.8, Node 24.22.0, Schemathesis 4.32.1, hypothesis 6.170.2.

**Stack.** platform-k slot 2 (`SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2`, gateway `http://localhost:6982`), built from that worktree: 33 of 33 containers healthy, 0 restarts, `/health/deep` ready, 48 migrations applied and 0 failed, admin seeded.

**Actors.** Generated by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts` (seed `local`): `owner` and `ownerPeer`, both role OWNER, in the same tenant (`ownerPeer` was added to `fixtures/actors.ts` for this). Provisioned with the bootstrap admin authenticated, so the roles are as requested. Passwords are not recorded here.

**A. The sweep that found it** (`systemTest/schemathesis`):

`systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 2 python3 scripts/setup.py` then `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 2 python3 scripts/run.py full --seed 1674` (with `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` set; 26.0 min). After the main sweep the profile runs a second sweep with only the `object_level_authorization` check (`scripts/runner/ola_leg.py`): the shipped `schemathesis.toml` plus one appended `[auth.wfc]` table (two peers, bearer tokens minted at run time), phases `fuzzing,stateful`, `--max-examples 25`, and four operations excluded (`POST /api/auth/logout`, `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/oauth/authorize`: they would revoke or lock a peer). Run directory `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2/object-level-authorization/` (NDJSON, HAR, VCR, JSON verdict, WFC, console, native HTML).

* 259 peer replays; requests by identity: owner 3,766, ownerPeer 1,276; 5.7 min, exit 1.
* 6 ST402 (failure type `ObjectLevelAuthorizationViolation`, WFC code 906), equal in NDJSON and JSON verdict.
* What the check does: a GET by `owner` of an object `owner`'s own earlier request produced is replayed as `ownerPeer`; it fails when the peer gets a 200 with an equivalent body, an anonymous replay is refused, and the peer's own list of the collection does not contain it.
* Replay any case: `st replay <case id>` (ids in the table above), or e.g. `curl -X GET -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ownerPeer token>' http://localhost:6982/api/delegations/<id>`.
* Creating requests in that run: `POST /api/delegations {"delegateId": "<uuid>", "delegationType": ["full"]}` (201); `POST /api/analytics/exports {"format": "csv", "period": "all", "type": ""}` (202); `POST /api/governance/participants/register {"stakedAmount": 0, "walletAddress": "0"}` (201); `POST /api/security/audit {"action": "read", "resourceType": "0", "userId": "<uuid>"}` (201). The two transfers came from the stateful phase.
* Sample bodies the peer received: an analytics export `{"status": "failed", "type": "", "format": "csv", "error": "Unknown export type: "}`; a governance participant (`walletAddress`, `stakedAmount`, `tier`, `votePower`, `isDRep`, ...); a delegation (`delegatorId`, `delegateId`, `delegationType`); an audit entry (`tenantId`, `userId`, `organizationId`, `action`); a transfer (`documentId`, `currentOwnerId`, `newOwnerId`, `transferType`, status history).

**B. A deterministic reproduction, no sweep needed** (new systemTest module):

`systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 2 ./venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_get_by_id_object_authorization.py -v --no-cov -rxXfE` (from `systemTest/schemathesis`; add `--runxfail` to see the failures).

* `owner` creates each object (a fixture asserts the create status and that `owner` can read it back, 200, so a refusal for the peer cannot be a broken create): transfer `{documentId: doc-<ms>-<hex>, transferType: simple, currentOwnerId/newOwnerId: two throwaway uuids, documentHash: 64 hex, documentTitle, documentType}` (201); delegation, export, participant (unique wallet address) and audit entry as above.
* `ownerPeer` then GETs it and the test asserts a refusal (403 or 404).
* Measured on slot 2, 2026-10-20, with the `xfail` markers disabled: **6 FAILED**, each `assert 200 in (403, 404)`, for `/transfers/{id}`, `/transfers/{id}/history`, `/delegations/{id}`, `/analytics/exports/{id}`, `/governance/participants/{id}`, `/security/audit/{id}`. The transfers were between two throwaway party ids, so neither peer is a party to the transfer they read.
* With the markers on: 6 xfailed (`strict=True`, `raises=AssertionError`, reason cites this ticket). Transfers, history and delegations are marked as confirmed defects; analytics, governance and audit as "ruling pending". A missing generated actor fails the module; it never skips.

**C. Same run, not part of this ticket** (recorded so nothing is lost; not classified, because that needs a control run on develop): five main-sweep pairs not in the triaged baseline (`positive_data_acceptance` on `GET /api/admin/audit/export` x10, `POST /api/security/keys` x3, `POST /api/timestamps/verify` x2, `PUT /api/security/keys/admin-scopes/{userId}` x7; `response_schema_conformance` on `GET /api/admin/audit/export` x1), and two live integration failures (`test_cross_tenant_isolation`, `test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation`).

**Not covered.** Cross-tenant reads (the local stack cannot place a user in a second tenant); database row-level security; whether the governance service rejects an unauthenticated caller.

title: not_a_server_error recurs — 17 raw 5xx across 8 ops (KS-431 / KS-449 / KS-497 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Why a new ticket

The whole predecessor chain is **Done and archived**:

* [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) — Done 2026-07-10 · [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) — Done 2026-07-13 · [KS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-449/write-path-residuals-from-ks-430-ks-431-remaining-raw-500s-request) — Done · [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) — Done 2026-07-29, archived

Each closed having fixed the raw-500 class down to its listed operations, and each time it has come back on different ones. Filed fresh per that precedent.

## Finding

**17** `not_a_server_error` **failures across 8 operations** — an unhandled value reaches a handler or the DB and throws, instead of being rejected with a mapped 4xx.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` · `POST /api/m365/outlook/exchange-token` · `POST /api/security/rate-limit/check` · `POST /api/users/admin/create` · `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`

**Three of these are the** [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) **endpoints** — `/share`, `/lifecycle-events`, and the `documents/{id}` family. Kamil shipped the connector-actor fix on 2026-08-07 (`develop` `307483672`, PR #652) and verified all three return 201 on demo for a connector. These 5xx are on *fuzzed* input rather than the connector path, so they are likely a different trigger on the same handlers — but worth confirming they are not a regression from that change.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` and `POST /api/users/admin/create` are already documented on [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) **§2** with root causes traced (`parseInt(offset) || 0` lets `-1` through to Postgres; `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard). [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) also notes **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reaches.

## Important — this count was inflated until today

`not_a_server_error` read **79 failures** on the previous sweep. It dropped to **17** once the governance active-proposal cap was cleared: the cap throws a bare `Error` that the route maps to `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and every fuzzed proposal-create was counting as a server error. That mis-mapping is filed separately. **62 of the previous 79 were that one defect** — worth knowing before sizing this.

## Where this was run

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, at `10.211.55.4`.

| Component | Version |  | Component | Version |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64) |  | Docker | 29.7.2 |
| Python (venv + host) | 3.14.6 |  | Node (services) | 24.19.0 (`node:24-alpine`) |
| Schemathesis | 4.24.3 |  | PostgreSQL | 15.18 (`postgres:15-alpine`) |
| pytest / Hypothesis | 9.1.1 / 6.165.2 |  | Redis | 8.10.0 (`redis:8-alpine`) |

Run of record: `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`, 24.1 min.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# KS-565 §2 — negative offset reaches Postgres
curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'

# KS-565 §2 — non-string email hits .toLowerCase()
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

Full sweep: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py full` — 94 replayable crash files with `code_sample` curls under `output/reports/full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z/schemathesis-crashes/`.

## Fix direction

Per [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) / [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks): classify the error at the route boundary — map known provider/validation failures to 4xx/503, keep genuine unknowns as 500 with structured logging, and guard path params and body fields before they reach the DB. Add unit tests pinning each classifier. **Fix all six negative-offset sites, not the two the sweep found** ([KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) §2 lists them).

## Note

The report had been attributing this class to [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) **with a bare ticket reference**, which reads as ownership. PR #656 now renders `KS-431 (closed — recurrence untracked)`; this ticket is the live owner.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

title: m365 OAuth callback product fix (split from KS-1641): repoint the five redirects to a declared admin route, and put only a short code on the redirect URL
description:
**BLUF:** This is the **product-code half** of [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route), split out on Peter's instruction (2026-10-26) so [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) can close on its systemTest work. Two changes are needed in m365-integration and the admin app. [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s systemTest cells already exist and are **red on develop**. They are this ticket's acceptance test and turn green when the fix lands. Kamil, I'd be grateful if you could take this one.

## The two findings (re-read at develop `5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492`, 2026-10-26)

**Finding 1: no redirect lands on a route the admin app declares.** All five admin-facing redirects in `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` target `/admin/integrations`: `:626` provider error, `:630` missing code or state, `:644` invalid state, `:677` **success**, `:684` token exchange failed.

* The admin app is mounted at `/admin/` with `<BrowserRouter basename="/admin">`, so that URL is matched as `/integrations`. `frontend/admin/src/App.tsx` declares no such route.
* The browser therefore falls to `path="*"` and lands on `/`, and the OAuth outcome is lost.
* "Integrations" is a tab inside `/settings` (`frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx`). Settings opens on `useState('general')` and reads no tab from the URL.

**Finding 2: provider and internal text is reflected into the redirect URL.**

* `:626` puts the provider's `error_description` on the URL. [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1622](https://linear.app/secuura/review/refs-ks-1641-1-of-3-sites-bound-the-provider-error-text-the-m365-oauth-02f753c1f67e) caps it at 200 code points but still reflects it.
* `:684` puts MSAL's `err.message` on the URL, uncapped.

[KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) recommends following `services/auth`: log the detail, put only a short code on the URL. The cap also leaves a bounded but large `Location` that the nginx edge refuses with **502** for long astral input ([KS-1742](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1742/m365-oauth-callback-a-provider-error-description-of-170-astral)).

## What to change ([KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s recommendation)

1. **Finding 2 first, or with finding 1**, because repointing the redirects is what makes the reflected text render:
   * On the provider-error redirect, use a short **code** (the provider's `error`, restricted to `[a-z_]`), not `error_description`.
   * Make `:684` send `token_exchange_failed`.
   * Keep the detail in the (capped) log and in `connection.errorMessage`.
   * Encode `connectionId` on `:677` ([KS-1670](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1670/m365-integration-three-more-reflection-sites-from-gate-am1-an) site 1).
2. **Finding 1:** repoint all five redirects to `/admin/settings` with a tab query the page reads (for example `?tab=integrations&m365=…&message=…`), and teach `Settings.tsx` to open the tab from the URL. If anything renders the outcome, it should render known codes from a fixed table, never URL text.

Note: the connect flow starts in `M365SetupWizard` (inside `IntegrationHub`, under `/platform/clients/:id?tab=integrations`) and opens the Microsoft sign-in in a popup, so the redirect lands in that popup. [KS-1678](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1678/m365-admin-setup-wizard-sends-a-secuura-tenant-id-as-organizationid) records that the connection's `organizationId` is the caller's org, not the client id, so a redirect back to `/platform/clients/:id` cannot be built reliably. Hence `/admin/settings`, as [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) recommends.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated tests:**
   * [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_m365_callback_redirect.py`: the three `test_ks1641_redirect_targets_a_declared_admin_route` cells, the three `test_ks1641_error_description_never_reaches_the_redirect` cells, and `test_ks1641_oversized_description_keeps_the_redirect_bounded_and_the_service_up[400-astral-code-points]` ([KS-1742](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1742/m365-oauth-callback-a-provider-error-description-of-170-astral)) all **pass** on a slot built from the fix. The other three stay green.
   * m365 unit cells for each of the five redirects (target path and code-only `message`), including a non-ASCII and a 400-emoji description, and `:684` never carrying `err.message`.
   * A browser test that `/admin/settings?tab=integrations` opens the Integrations tab (the `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` suite; platform-k's systemTest Playwright is API-only).
2. **Docs:** the `/admin/integrations` wording in `services/m365-integration/src/m365-integration.openapi.ts` (then `npm run generate-openapi`, and restart or rebuild api-gateway), `USER_TESTING/M365-Integration-Test-Guide.md:65`, the comment in `deployment/azure/services.bicep`, and the comment in `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_workflows_http.py`.
3. **systemTests:** no test change needed if the redirects target `/admin/settings`. If a new admin route is declared instead, update `ADMIN_DECLARED_ROUTES` in the test from this ticket's PR. On green, update the [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) section of `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md`.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given.

## Measured state today

Developed under [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s systemTest pass on Peter's Mac, 2026-10-26, at develop `5f6899918`:

* slot 1, built 11:17:45 UTC;
* develop control on slot 2, built 12:20:09 UTC.

The six finding cells were red in all 5 runs. The full results are on [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route).

**Related:** [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) (origin; systemTest coverage), [KS-1742](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1742/m365-oauth-callback-a-provider-error-description-of-170-astral) (edge 502, cleared by finding 2), [KS-1670](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1670/m365-integration-three-more-reflection-sites-from-gate-am1-an) (other reflection sites; site 1 above), [KS-1678](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1678/m365-admin-setup-wizard-sends-a-secuura-tenant-id-as-organizationid) (organisation id in the wizard), [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1622](https://linear.app/secuura/review/refs-ks-1641-1-of-3-sites-bound-the-provider-error-text-the-m365-oauth-02f753c1f67e) (the merged cap).

*Raised on Peter's instruction, 2026-10-26. Duplicate searches with no match beyond* [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) *itself: "m365 redirect admin settings integrations tab", "Settings.tsx tab from URL".*

title: Akto harness: reuse one scan token or scan as more than one user — deferred from KS-724, build only if credentialInvalidated fires on a non-excluded template
description:
## BLUF

This ticket holds items 2 and 3 of [KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own), split out on 2026-10-22 so [KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own) could close on item 1. Neither item is to be built unless the trigger below fires. It sits under [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) because any work it leads to is a systemTest harness change.

## Background (from [KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own))

`GET /api/sessions` keeps a rolling window of a user's 10 most recent sessions, and an evicted session is invalidated. A scan that logs in more than ten times as one user therefore revokes the token it is scanning with, and every later request returns `401 "Session has been invalidated"`.

[KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own) proposed three remedies:

1. **Assert the scan credential is still alive.** Done: `assertCredentialAlive`, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and), `f3fb25e3e`), wired into all three Akto tiers. The `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` exclusion was ruled "Accept as built" by Kam on 2026-10-18 and quoted in code via PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1565](https://linear.app/secuura/review/refs-ks-724-quote-kams-accept-as-built-ruling-beside-the-locked-561001a9bedd).
2. **Don't re-login per request.** Reuse one token, so a scan can't evict itself. *(this ticket)*
3. **Or scan as more than one user,** so no single account's window fills. *(this ticket)*

## Why these are deferred

* The gate has never caught this defect in a harness run. Its only non-zero reading was the locked-account template's 66 results, which are by design. Slot 2 `test:pr` on 2026-09-28 recorded `credentialInvalidated: 0`.
* The [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) platform log showed about 9 successful logins since the stack started and no revoke inside the failure window. The \~30 logins that evicted the token came from the [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) probe run, not the harness.
* Item 3 would add actors, tenancy variables and more logins to a suite we are trying to make deterministic ([KS-696](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-696/akto-pr-scan-is-non-deterministic-three-runs-on-near-identical-code), [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not)).

## Trigger

Build item 2 or 3 **only if** an Akto run reports `credentialInvalidated > 0` on a template other than `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE`. When it fires, attach the run artifact here and move this ticket to Todo.

## Open question to read first if it fires

**Not verified:** whether Akto already reuses one token or re-logs in per iteration (`configureBearerAuth` only writes the token; the harness has no read path for it). If Akto already reuses one token, item 2 is already true and the cause lies elsewhere.

## Source

[KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own) (description re-scope paragraph and the 2026-10-22 comment).

title: No supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack — needed for cross-tenant systemTest peers (split from KS-1674)
description:
**BLUF:** systemTest needs two ordinary (non-super-admin) users in two **different** tenants on a local slot, so the Schemathesis `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906) can test cross-tenant isolation. On develop there is no supported route that does this. This ticket asks for that capability; how it is built is your call. The systemTest side is a separate ticket, blocked by this one.

## Why it is needed

[KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), merged as `5671d5115`) runs `object_level_authorization` with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`). The ticket asked for peers across two tenants. Without them, cross-tenant exposure on findings such as [KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object) is inferred, not measured.

## Why the existing routes do not work (read on develop `5f6899918`; nothing run)

1. **Self-registration lands in the default tenant.** `POST /api/auth/register` takes the tenant from `x-tenant-id` / `x-tenant-slug` (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:217-218`), but the gateway strips client-sent trust headers (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:309-330`). A tenantless token is then given `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:503`).
2. **Tenant from email domain at login is off, and would not persist.** `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:549-586` runs only when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` (defaults to `false` in `docker-compose.yml`). Its own comment says the `UPDATE users SET tenant_id` is a no-op under fail-closed RLS ([KS-458](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-458/rls-fail-closed-flip-guc-on-checkout-flip-the-consolidated-tenant)).
3. `X-Tenant-Override` **applies only to super-admin roles** (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515-521`). A super-admin can read every object, so it cannot act as a peer. (The override is also partly broken: [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a).)
4. **Invited stub then register keeps the stub's tenant** (`auth.ts:237-242`, [KS-74](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-74/pending-invite-ux-post-apicertificationsissue-accepts-holderemail-and)), but `POST /api/users/stub` takes the tenant from the caller's own verified token (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:398`). A caller can only mint stubs in a tenant they are already in.
5. **Not verified:** a connector token carries its own tenant (`services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:116`) and is accepted on `/api/users/stub`. If a connector can be issued for a second tenant, that may already be a route. Worth checking before building anything new.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A documented, supported sequence of API calls, runnable on a local slot without editing the database by hand, that (a) creates or selects a second tenant and (b) leaves a named, non-super-admin user (OWNER or another self-service role) whose verified token carries that tenant's id.
2. The user can log in and is scoped to that tenant on later requests (the gateway forwards its `x-tenant-id`, not the default).
3. The sequence is described here, or in the relevant service docs, so systemTest can call it from `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.

Raised from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) at Peter's request (2026-10-26). The systemTest follow-up is assigned to Peter and blocked by this ticket.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): run the object_level_authorization leg with peers in two different tenants (split from KS-1674)
description:
> ⛔ **Blocked by** [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) (2026-10-27). Parked until [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) delivers a supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack. No work starts here before then.

**BLUF:** [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) made Schemathesis's `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906, ST402) run in its own `[auth.wfc]` leg, but with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant. This ticket is the remaining part of [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)'s scope: peers in two **different** tenants, so cross-tenant exposure is measured rather than inferred. It is blocked by [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack), which asks for a supported way to put a user in a second tenant.

## Today (develop, after PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), `5671d5115`)

* Peers: `["owner", "ownerPeer"]`, both OWNER in the default tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`; actors in `systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts`, provisioned by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`).
* Why: no local route places a user in a second tenant. The reasons are in [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack).

## Scope (once [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) lands)

* Provision a peer in the second tenant through the route [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) delivers (API only; no direct database writes).
* Point the leg's peers at the cross-tenant pair. Whether to keep the same-tenant pair as well (two leg runs, or three peers) is decided in the plan.
* Update the comment above the leg config, which today records the cross-tenant pairing as remaining scope on [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Red/green proof: a stub API that leaks one tenant's object to a peer in another tenant is reported as ST402 / WFC 906 on every surface (console, JSON verdict, NDJSON, HTML report), and is missed when the cross-tenant peer is removed.
2. A live run on a slot shows peer replays between the two tenants (the leg's peer-replay count, not the NDJSON check matrix, which records `success` even when the check does not run; see [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)).
3. Every new pair from the first live run is triaged: an existing ticket ([KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object), [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a)) or a new KS ticket, never masked or baselined without an owner.
4. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` and both `Projects Documents` HTML docs updated.

Split from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) at Peter's request (2026-10-26). Peter owns systemTest security work ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) G).

title: GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET: nothing provisions it and no deploy order or rotation is written — #951's control ships inert, and a gateway/originate mismatch drops gateway identity
description:
## BLUF

PR #951 (KS-1041 Step 2) adds a secret that lets originate tell a gateway-routed request from a direct one. **No tracked deploy, bootstrap or CI path supplies** `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, so every environment boots with the control **DISABLED** (fail-open by design, with a WARN). And **when the gateway and originate disagree about the secret** — originate deployed first, a gateway rollback, a rotation, or a gateway container not recreated after `.env` changes — originate drops every gateway-set identity. This is one logical path: provisioning, deploy order, rotation. It is also where the **provisioning-safety question** lives — whether switching the control on breaks the gateway's own non-proxy writes to originate (Detail, first section).

## Recommendation

Needs decisions before code. Decide:

1. where each environment's value comes from — Key Vault → `deploy.sh` `--parameters gatewayVouchSecret=…`, and a `fill_if_blank "GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET" "openssl rand -hex 32"` line in `bootstrap-env.sh` for local;
2. the gateway-first deploy order and a rotation procedure (a dual-accept window or a transition flag), written into the runbook **before any box receives the secret**;
3. whether production should REQUIRE it (`enforceProductionConfig` in originate).
4. **Before provisioning on ANY box, answer the provisioning-safety question below.** The #951 round-2 tier-1 gate (commissioned 2026-09-10 22:52Z against `02a22f4bb`) is measuring it as a separate PROVISIONING SAFETY verdict.

## Detail

**Provisioning-safety question — READ ONLY, not driven (added by s174, 2026-09-11).** The gateway's own `POST /api/documents` handler (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:879`; the verification router is not mock-gated — `index.ts:876-891`) forwards to originate through its own `http.request` (`:1044`, headers built at `:1024-1042`) carrying `x-user-id`, `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug` and **no vouch** — the file has zero `vouch` mentions at `02a22f4bb`. With `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` set, originate's provenance middleware strips those headers. The handler's own KS-39 #4 comment (`:1036-1040`) states what a missing `x-tenant-id` does: the POST writes to the fallback tenant and the new document looks invisible / 404s on the next read. The workflow-approve forward (route `:700`, `http.request` at `:785`, `x-user-id` at `:783`) has the same shape. **Unknown:** whether originate's `authenticate()` recovers the tenant from the forwarded JWT — if it does, the consequence shrinks. If the question holds, the fix is the one #951's F5 residual already names: send every gateway→originate call through one helper that adds the vouch.

**F4 — nothing supplies it.** Re-measured at `dd0a0c934` from git objects: **0 mentions** of the secret in `deployment/azure/deploy.sh`, `services.parameters.json`, `env.demo.json`, `env.dev.json`, `sync-secrets.sh`, `setup-keyvault.sh`, `deploy-all.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh`, and 0 files under `.github` (control: `services.bicep` → 10). `bootstrap-env.sh:198,200,208` generate `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY` and `DEMO_SERVICE_KEY`, not this. originate's `enforceProductionConfig` requires `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` only. The #951 tier-1 gate counted 35 `--parameters` at `deploy.sh:721-757`, none of them this. Azure deploys therefore take the bicep default `''` and wire neither app.

**F3 — mismatch.** Measured in-process by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, cells S2.1 and S4.1): a merge-base gateway, or a head gateway with the secret unset, in front of an originate that has it → gateway-set `x-tenant-id` / `x-user-id` are stripped. Consequences read from source: the metering connector shim (`originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42`) stops matching and `authenticate()` answers 401; with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` in production `extractTenantContext` answers 400 "Missing tenant context" (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:67-74`); single-tenant falls to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`originate/src/index.ts:248-256`). **No forgeability window in any order** (gate cells S2.2–S2.4) — order affects availability and tenant scoping, not the hole.

**Board searched before filing** (exact to decide, fuzzy to discover): `gatewayVouchSecret` → 0; `vouch` → 12, none about provisioning (KS-1041, KS-1080 akto-autoheal, KS-1081 env-template drift, the rest Platform S identity/verify work); `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, `deploy order`, `bootstrap-env.sh` → fuzzy noise, nothing about this secret; control `KS-1041` → 1.

Related: KS-1041 · KS-1081 (whichever env template wins must carry this variable) · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · round-1 gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (F3, F4).

title: userRepo.ts: five sibling reads still return fromRow unawaited inside try, so a failure inside fromRow escapes the KS-253 classifier (KS-999 follow-up)
description:
## BLUF

Five reads in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` still `return fromRow(...)` **unawaited from inside a** `try`. `fromRow` is `async` and reads the subject DEK, which is itself a DB read. So a failure inside `fromRow` rejects outside the `catch`, and **skips the KS-253 classifier those functions carry**. On an encrypted row, which is the normal path, pool starvation there surfaces as a raw error (a 500) instead of `ServiceUnavailable` (503). KS-999 fixes this for `getUserById` alone (PR raised 2026-09-17); these are its siblings.

## Recommendation

The same one-word fix at each site, `return await fromRow(...)`, each pinned the KS-999 way: a subject-DEK rejection inside `fromRow` → `temporarily unavailable`; a non-infrastructure rejection rethrown as-is; the classifier's log fires. It is a behaviour change on normal production paths (login, pre-auth lookups, social sign-in), so it gets its own gate against the calling routes. One test pass proves all five.

## Detail

Sites at develop `1125607e978d6ad637720c985e43e3d79fecdf88`, read at source. Every enclosing function has `isInfrastructureDbError` in its `catch` and rethrows:

| line | function | statement |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:442` | `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash` (`:436`) | `if (result.rows.length > 0) return fromRow(result.rows[0]);` |
| `:508` | `getUserByIdPreAuth` (`:505`) | same |
| `:581` | `getUserByEmail` (`:570`) | same |
| `:590` | `getUserByEmail` (`:570`), legacy arm | `if (legacy.rows.length > 0) return fromRow(legacy.rows[0]);` |
| `:623` | `getUserBySocialId` (`:614`) | same as `:442` |

* Seat A's brief named four sites (`:442/:508/:581/:623`). The source has **five**: `:590` is the legacy-row return in the same `getUserByEmail`.
* Not in scope: `:1036` `listUsersInner` returns `Promise.all(result.rows.map((r) => fromRow(r)))` outside any `try`, so no classifier is being skipped there.
* Mechanism: a promise returned from a `try` block is not caught by its `catch`. The KS-999 tier-1 gate on #907 measured the effect for `getUserById`: with the await, D1 flips from a raw unclassified error to `ServiceUnavailable`, and all 30 delivered cells still pass.
* Not measured here: which HTTP routes reach each function, and whether a 500 → 503 change breaks any contract test.

Related: KS-999 (the `getUserById` fix), KS-253 (the classifier's contract), KS-963 (where the unawaited return was first measured).

**Dedupe before filing** (seat A successor, 2026-09-17): Linear `searchIssues` with archived issues and comments included, paged, then literal case-insensitive matches over title + description + comments. Terms: `return fromRow(`, `fromRow`, `userRepo.ts`, `getUserByIdPreAuth`, `getUserBySocialId`. title: GET /api/platform/audit-log: the platform_audit_log half of the merge is cut to 200 rows whenever limit plus offset exceeds 200
description:
## BLUF

The platform audit view merges two sources and, to paginate after sorting, asks each for `limit + offset` rows. For the `platform_audit_log` source the gateway calls tenant-provisioning `GET /api/audit-log` with `limit=<limit+offset>` and `offset=0`, and that endpoint **clamps** `limit` **at 200**. So whenever `limit + offset` exceeds 200, the platform source contributes only its newest 200 rows to the merge. Deep pages therefore **omit older platform entries**, while the response `total` still sums the true totals of both sources. At the admin page's 25 rows a page this starts once the offset passes 175.

Pre-existing; not caused or worsened by PR #1501 (ticket KS-1359), which found it as the gate's Note 3.

## Recommendation

Decide the intended behaviour first, because this is an interaction between two correct-looking bounds and not a one-line bug:

* either request each source's window properly (a bounded overfetch per source, then merge), or
* make the upstream clamp consistent with the gateway's own bound (offset up to 5000 plus limit up to 200 is 5200 rows).

Test first: stub the upstream with its real 200 clamp, call the gateway with `offset=250&limit=25`, and assert the page is the rank-ordered slice of both sources. The test must be red on today's code.

## Detail

* **Gateway side:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`, the audit-log handler: `overfetch = limit + offset`, the upstream request `{ limit: String(overfetch), offset: '0' }`, then `merged = sort([...platformEntries, ...appEntries])`, `paginated = merged.slice(offset, offset + limit)`, `total: platformTotal + appTotal`.
* **Upstream side:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`, `app.get('/api/audit-log'`: `Math.min(parseInt(req.query.limit) || 50, 200)`.
* **Status of the evidence:** read from the source at develop `8ea75e7cb`, **not reproduced** against a live stack. The claim that older platform entries are absent from deep pages follows from the two code paths above; it has not been observed.
* **Related, different:** KS-1359 (the gateway's own `limit` bound, now refused above 200) and KS-1511 (its follow-up). The `audit_logs` source is not affected, since the gateway queries it directly with the full `limit + offset`.

title: KS-1510 gate follow-ups: guard the document-lookup log call, pin the Error text and a null throw, cap the line, measure the Azure limiter key
description:
## BLUF

The Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1512 (ticket KS-1510) returned **GO WITH NOTE**: 0 Major, one Minor and several notes (verdict sha256/16 `cc2a467368885a9d`). None blocks the merge. This is one checklist for one pass over `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` and the KS-1510 test file `ks1510-document-lookup-logs-the-thrown-error.test.ts`, plus one measurement owed after the deploy.

## Recommendation

Test first for (a), (b) and (c): each is a cell that is red against a named mutant today. (d) needs a decision. (e) needs a measurement on the deployed ingress and cannot be done before PR #1512 is deployed.

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a) Guard the log call (the gate's Minor 1).** The log expression inside the catch at `routes/platform.ts:995` is unguarded. A thrown value that makes `err.message`, `Object.getPrototypeOf`, `.constructor` or `Object.keys` throw (an Error with a throwing `message` getter, a Proxy with a throwing `getPrototypeOf` or `ownKeys` trap, a revoked Proxy), or a `logger.error` that itself throws, leaves the request with **no response** (hung after 2.5 s in the probe) and an unhandled rejection; the base answered the constant 500 for all 15 shapes probed. Not reachable by a caller (the value comes from `pg` or node), and the gateway survives the rejection (`index.ts:1189-1199`), so Minor. It is the same expression as `fail500` in `routes/batch.ts:28`, so the hazard is there too (not measured). Fix shape: wrap the log in try/catch, or build the string in a small non-throwing helper shared with `fail500`. Pin it with a cell that a throwing log call still answers the constant 500: mutant O4 (the log wrapped in try/catch) leaves all 8 cells green today.
- [ ] **(b) Pin the Error branch's exact logged text (Note 2).** Cell L1 asserts only that the text contains `ECONNREFUSED`. Logging `err.stack` (O1) or `String(err)` (O9) leaves L1 and L2 green, and logging the full Error object (O3) reddens only L3 and L4. A logged stack would put multi-line paths in the log unnoticed.
- [ ] **(c) A cell that throws** `null` **(Note 3).** With the `err !== null` guard removed (O11), `Object.getPrototypeOf(null)` throws inside the catch, which is the hang in (a), and every cell stays green. The gate's probe: `null` logs `thrown object` and answers 500.
- [ ] **(d) Cap the line length, or decide not to (Note 4).** The logged line is uncapped: about 15 KB if a database error echoed a maximal caller value, and one huge `fields [...]` string for an object with 100k fields. Same as `fail500`.
- [ ] **(e) Measure the limiter key on the deployed ingress (Note 1), after the deploy.** The bound of 300 log lines per minute per limiter key holds only behind a proxy that **appends** to `X-Forwarded-For` (the compose gateway behind nginx: a spoofed header is ignored, 5 of 40 requests reached the handler at cap 5). Reached directly, a rotating header gave 40 of 40 to the handler. The Azure gateway Container App has `ingress.external: true` (`deployment/azure/services.bicep:582-583`); its live behaviour, and any Front Door or CDN in front of it, is **unmeasured**.

## Detail

* **Related, pre-existing, NOT part of the checklist.** In `NODE_ENV=production` the two `winston.transports.File` transports in the api-gateway's `utils/logger.ts` (lines 36-47) write the literal text `undefined` for every call, because the logger's top-level format has no final formatter; the console JSON is the only usable production channel. KS-1348 (Done) is the **originate** half of the same defect; this service's half is now its own ticket, **KS-1526** (split out on Wednesday's ruling, confirmed at source on develop `629349dac602` with a control).
* Also found on the way: in production an unversioned call to this route is answered 307 first, and the redirect is counted by the global limiter, so a client that follows it pays two counts (150 lines per minute per key rather than 300).
* **Related:** KS-1510 (the change), KS-1346 (the `fail500` family: a different defect in the same helper family).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `platform.ts:995` 0, `throwing message getter` 0, `document-lookup` 1 (KS-1510 itself). The same instrument returned KS-1510 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: anchoring has no inbound strip for `x-emitter-internal`: a direct compose-network caller can suppress its own provenance row, and the comment over-claims
description:
**Ask:** give the anchoring service a guard against a caller setting `x-emitter-internal` itself, and correct the comment above it in the same change.

**What the gate found (note N1 of the #995 verdict):** the marker means "this is K's own originate-to-anchoring hop for an operation that already wrote its own provenance row", and anchoring skips `recordFlatAnchorProvenance` when it is present (`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, `const isInternalEmit = typeof req.headers['x-emitter-internal'] === 'string'`, line 531 on develop `a9ce2cff1594`). #995 (merged, KS-741) strips the marker at originate's own inbound. **Anchoring has no inbound strip of its own.** The gate, verbatim: *"Anchoring has no inbound strip; its middleware is helmet, cors, json, rejectNulBytes, requestLogger, then jwtAuthenticate.* `docker-compose.yml` *treats anchoring exactly as it treats originate: both are on the flat network with host ports unpublished (*`:1286` *vs* `:557`*). That is the same exposure the PR uses to justify the originate strip. So a direct compose-network caller holding a connector JWT can set the marker and suppress its own flat-anchor provenance row. This is pre-existing and not introduced by this PR."*

**The comment over-claims.** Lines 519-530 (the KS-566 block) say the header "is not spoofable, by two strips" and that *"the only value that can arrive here is one originate itself set on its outbound hop"*. That holds only for paths through the gateway or originate. #995 left that wording in place (it edited the comment to name the originate strip). The gate: *"Reword the comment, or open a ticket for an anchoring-side guard."* This is that ticket; fix the comment in the same change as the guard.

**Design caution, my reading and not the gate's:** a plain strip at anchoring's inbound would also delete the legitimate marker originate sets on its own hop, so the guard has to tell the two apart (honour the marker only on a request that carries something only originate can present), not just drop the header. Whoever picks this up should settle that first.

**Also from the same gate (note N3, minor):** #995's cell C6 checks the strip's mount order only against `/api/anchors`. A move to between `/api/documents` (`originate/src/index.ts` lines 275-276, which also builds a marked hop) and `/api/anchors` would still pass C6. Today the order is correct. Worth one more cell when the order is next touched.

**Related, read and not a duplicate:** KS-1603 (In Progress, anchoring `POST /api/anchors` never checks who owns `documentId`) records in one bullet that `x-emitter-internal` "is trusted by mere presence" and that "any peer on the compose network can send it". That is the same exposure seen from the ownership ticket; it proposes no fix for the marker and does not touch the over-claiming comment. This ticket owns the marker guard and the comment. (KS-1603's bullet says originate sets the marker at one call site; the gate found two setters, `originate/src/routes/documents.ts` lines 878 and 1375.)

**Impact, as the gate framed it:** a caller on the compose network with a connector JWT can suppress its own flat-anchor provenance row; it needs network position and a valid credential.

Source: QA gate DA5, tier 1, round 1 (verdict `2026-10-23_gate-DA5-pr989-995-tier1/verdict.md`, sha256/16 of the body `be2f26d014ae8997`). Quoted from the verdict; **not re-measured by the seat that filed this.**

title: Spec: 85 of 145 request bodies are not marked `required: true`, so Schemathesis sends "valid" empty bodies the handlers reject — 17 ops, 35 cases per sweep, 15 of them baselined against Done KS-255
description:
## Summary

One for the spec when convenient, Kamil. 85 of the spec's 145 request bodies aren't marked `required: true`, so Schemathesis reasonably sends "valid" requests with no body at all, and 17 operations answer 400 (35 cases per sweep). It isn't a blanket fix: 23 operations happily accept an empty body. So the likely shape is marking `required: true` where the Zod schema rejects an absent body. 15 of these pairs are still baselined against [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints), which is closed, so this would give them a live home. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence

**Sweep 4** (slot 3, seed 1353, 4.28.0, toml loaded): 85 operations with a non-required `requestBody`; 40 were sent a no-body positive case (237 cases); **17 operations / 35 cases** failed `positive_data_acceptance`.
