title: S↔K (K-side): erasure by external_ref, documents.title coverage, and connector-scoped org erasure — PS-690 dependency
description:
Platform-S is adopting org-owned documents with non-destructive user deletion and org dissolution ([PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user), accepted plan on that ticket). Its S→K erasure bridge ([PS-701](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-701/ps-690-phase-6-sk-erasure-bridge-lifts-the-gates), Phase 6 — the only K-dependent phase) needs three K-side changes. Everything else in [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user) proceeds without K; S records pending erasures durably and a sweep converges once these land.

## Context

S holds **no K** `users.id` — the per-user credential tier was removed in [PS-465](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-465/s-adopt-k-connector-keys-provisioning-key-per-organisation) phase 4 (`PlatformKAccount` dropped). The only per-user link S has is `Person.PersonGuid`, which K already receives as `onBehalfOf.externalRef` on every attributed write, and which K's own erasure deliberately **retains** while blanking email/displayName. The org-level identity is the connector `platform-s:<OrganisationGuid>` with the once-only operational `sk_` key.

## Asks

1. **Erasure addressable by** `external_ref`**.** K's GDPR erasure route is keyed on `users.id`, which S cannot supply. Accept `external_ref` as the subject key (resolving to the same `executeErasure` path), idempotent, with a status read so S's retry sweep can converge without double-executing.
2. `documents.title` **in erasure coverage.** S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`); K's `executeErasure` anonymises `documents.metadata`, `certification_metadata` and `owner_did` but not `title`, so real filenames survive erasure. Include title blanking for the subject's documents. Worth doing regardless of [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user).
3. **Connector-scoped (organisation) erasure for dissolution.** For `connectorId platform-s:<OrganisationGuid>`: blank the org display name and all connector documents' titles, revoke the operational key (S supplies the `svc_api_keys` id it holds in `PlatformKKeyId`), retain anchored hashes and the graph (S anchors explicit `action=delete` events for every document before calling this — [KS-389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-389/k-confirm-deleterevoke-semantics-for-ssd-soft-delete-clarification-for) semantics, never `/revoke`). Idempotent + status endpoint; S drives it from a resumable state machine and will retry until Confirmed.

## Sequencing

Lands on top of the [PS-319](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-319/sk-consistent-organisationuser-ownership-dr-credential-reconciliation)/[KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) connector-key model ([KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) currently In Review). S's Phase 6 ([PS-701](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-701/ps-690-phase-6-sk-erasure-bridge-lifts-the-gates)) is the only consumer and is gated on this ticket — until then S refuses dissolution of K-registered orgs at preview, deliberately, so no dangling K-side state can be created.

title: KS-998 item 3 gate follow-ups (#1545): the three Minors of the Opus gate, the ks884 S10 fixture collision, and three Info as text
description:
Follow-ups from the Opus tier-1 QA gate on pull request #1545 (KS-998 item 3 + the four Minors of the #1540 gate), verdict **GO WITH NOTE**: 0 Major, 3 Minor, 9 Info. Head under test `50f0552ce011ac9d8c4caddf67bc747a7fed2d5b`, report sha256/16 `4cb85c41ae671c0e`. Same shape as KS-1583, which carries the #1532 gate's follow-ups.

Scope: developer tooling only (the pre-push hook and the package-format gate). **Nothing here deploys.** Cells first, then the fix, per the gate's note that each item is "a few lines plus one cell".

### Minor 1 — a package-level `.npmrc` redirects the install to a host the lock check never allowed

`systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh:485` copies `.npmrc` into the stage and `:494` runs `npm ci` with npm's default `replace-registry-host=npmjs`, while `_check_lock_sources` (`:351`) validates only `resolved`. Measured (gate shape B1): a lockfile whose every entry is `https://registry.npmjs.org/…` with an integrity passes the check, a `systemTest/<pkg>/.npmrc` carrying `registry=https://<other host>/` arrives on the same branch, and npm then fetches the tarball from that host — **1 GET to the attacker's listener — and its postinstall runs**. Control B3, same lock without the `.npmrc`: the fetch goes to [registry.npmjs.org](<http://registry.npmjs.org>). No `systemTest/*/.npmrc` exists today.

Fix (both candidates measured at 0 GETs on B1): do not copy `.npmrc` into the stage, **or** refuse (`lockbad`) when a package `.npmrc` sets `registry`, `*:registry`, `replace-registry-host`, `strict-ssl`, `proxy`, `https-proxy`, `ca` or `cafile`. **And** pass `--replace-registry-host=never`, so npm fetches exactly the URL that was checked. One cell: the gate's B1.

Also correct the "nothing is fetched or run" sentences, which this defeats: `check-package-format.sh:153` and `:350`, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:494`, `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:401`.

### Minor 2 — "already on the remote" trusts local tracking refs, and treats "the remote has it" as "it was judged"

`.githooks/pre-push:120` runs before step 1 for every ref. Measured: a **stale** tracking ref (branch deleted or force-moved at the remote since the last fetch) lets a RED commit the remote no longer has land with rc 0 under a note saying it is already on the remote (gate rows R22, R22b, R23; develop refuses all three, and the `fetch --prune` controls are refused on the head too). Separately, fast-forwarding an existing branch onto an already-pushed RED commit lands with no gate and no preflight (R20, R21), where develop judges `remote_sha..tip`. 4 of 789 tracking refs in the project clone are already stale.

Fix: apply the `onremote` skip **only to refs the remote does not have yet** (`_jr_rsha` empty or zero), **after** step 1, so existing-branch updates keep their `remote_sha..tip` judgement. Correct the stale-ref comment at `.githooks/pre-push:116-119` (which claims a stale ref can "never" lead to a pass) and the docs (`CONTRIBUTING.md:417`, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:530`). Cells: R20 and R22.

### Minor 3 — two surviving mutants are test gaps

* **X14** (ancestor-config names listed from HEAD instead of the pushed commit) survives the gate and hook suites (435/0, 74/0). CASE 48 cannot kill it, because it keeps `.prettierrc` at both commits. Distinguishing cell: the pushed commit has `.prettierrc` and **HEAD has deleted it** (head rc 0, X14 rc 1) — the gate shipped `tools/x14_cell.sh`.
* **Y07** (the `~/.npm` fallback appended even when `npm_config_cache` is set) survives. Cell: `npm_config_cache=X` set with `HOME/.npm` present, asserting **exactly one** `npm_config_cache=X` in the install environment.

### Item 5 — `ks884` S10 is non-deterministic on the #1545 hook: a fixture SHA collision (found by Seat K 10th at the pre-squash measurement, not by the gate)

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks884_pre_push_tag_named_develop.test.sh` cell **S10** fails about half the time on the #1545 hook blob `b63a7a46dd647cac1419` and never on develop's `454605d8`: head tree 4/10, predicted merge tree 6/10 (**10/20**), develop tree **0/16**. The blob is identical in head and predicted tree, so the merge is not implicated. It prints no `not ok` line; it prints `FAIL S10 … landed=1 ks991=0 preflight-ran=0`.

Cause, proven by a harness-only probe printing both tips — **7 FAIL runs had** `s4_tip == s10_tip`**, 3 pass runs differed, 10/10 with no exception**: cell S4 pushes `docs/stale` to the fixture origin, then S10 clones that origin and builds `docs/stale10` with the same parent (`origin/develop`), the same tree (both run `echo more >> docs/readme.md`), the same message (`docs only`) and the same identity. A commit SHA depends only on the committer timestamp once those match, so within one clock second the two commits are byte-identical; S10's clone then holds `refs/remotes/origin/docs/stale` pointing **at** S10's own commit, and `pre-push:120`'s `git for-each-ref --contains "$_tip" "refs/remotes/<remote>/"` matches, because a ref contains itself.

**The hook is correct — this is not a gate bypass.** The commit genuinely is already on the remote, by SHA. The defect is the S10 fixture reproducing S4's commit. On develop the collision still happens but is invisible, because develop has no `onremote` skip. The Minor 2 fix above does **not** cure it: `docs/stale10` is a new ref, so `_jr_rsha` is zero and the skip still applies.

Fix (tested, one line, **test fixture only, no shipped file**): at `…/ks884_pre_push_tag_named_develop.test.sh:128`, inside the `s10_out` block, `echo more >> docs/readme.md` becomes `echo s10-distinct >> docs/readme.md`. Fixed: **0 runs with any FAIL out of 14**, 0 dead. Control, the unfixed suite in the same loop and conditions: **S10 FAIL in 7 of 14**. Keep an apostrophe out of that comment — inside the `s10_out="$( … )"` substitution it breaks the parse (rc 2).

### Info, as text only

1. **Info 1** — two gate cells fail when the fixture path contains a UUID: npm 11.5.1 refuses `npm config get userconfig` when the value holds a UUID-shaped string (@npmcli/redact treats it as a token), so the suite reads 433/2 on a scratchpad with a UUID and 435/0 through a UUID-free `TMPDIR`. Have the stub derive the userconfig from `node -p 'require("os").homedir()'`, or assert on `HOME` alone.
2. **Info 2** — credentials in *values*, and names the six patterns miss: userinfo in `npm_config_registry`, `npm_config_proxy`, `npm_config_https_proxy` and `HTTPS_PROXY` reaches every install script verbatim, and so does `npm_config_otp`. Add `otp` to the credential patterns and add one doc sentence on credentials in values (`CONTRIBUTING.md:403-405` and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` do not say it).
3. **Info 5** — `FORMAT_GATE_LOCK_ALLOW` without a trailing slash (`https://npm.example.com`) accepts `https://npm.example.com.evil.example/…`. The default has the slash. Document "end the prefix with `/`".

Evidence for item 5: `5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatK-10th/measurements/ks884_S10_finding.txt` (plus the failing and passing run logs beside it). Gate evidence for Minors 1-3 and the Info: the verdict and `evidence/` under the gate's own folder.

title: KS-998 item 1 gate follow-ups (#1532): the six Minors of the Opus gate, and the Info that matters
description:
## BLUF

**The Opus tier 1 gate on pull request #1532 (KS-998 item 1) returned GO WITH NOTE: 0 Major, 6 Minor, 7 Info.** This ticket carries the six Minors and the Info that matters, so they are findable after #1532 merges. Facts only, from the gate's report.

* **Report:** `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1532/verdict.md` in the Wednesday tree, sha256/16 `85bf04b8ef22923b` (recomputed by the report's own recipe, placeholder replaced: equal; a one-byte change breaks it).
* **Head it is bound to:** `3dbfdf7e36443a8665b6a106e2d8ccbb6763cd44`. Instruments: macOS, `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, node v24.7.0, npm 11.5.1.
* **None of the six hides a formatting red or lets a push pass without a check.** (1) fails closed; (2) and (3) are properties of `npm ci` that the gate now triggers automatically.

## Where each rides (Wednesday's rulings, 2026-10-13)

* **Minors 1, 2, 4, 5, 6:** the stacked **item 2** pull request (same functions), each with its cell.
* **Minor 3:** a **third pull request stacked on item 2**, so item 2 stays reviewable: the lock-source allowlist AND a scrubbed install environment, lifecycle scripts still running as ruled. A plan mail comes first.

## The six Minors

1. **The final rename races (**`check-package-format.sh`**, the** `mv` **into place).** The `[ -e node_modules ]` guard is not atomic with the `mv`; BSD `mv` onto an existing directory moves the source INSIDE it, and onto a symlink to a directory moves it into the target. `_rm_stage` can then delete a `node_modules` the gate did not make. Measured with a PATH `mv` shim: a hollow in-progress tree was deleted; a symlink arrival had our tree written into the outside target; a complete tree arrival left `node_modules/node_modules`. **Two real gate processes on one package REFUSED a correct push in 4 of 5 trials** (`mv` loses its own rename race: ENOTEMPTY). It fails closed and what can be lost is a regenerable, gitignored tree, but it falsifies "deletes only what it made". **Fix:** `rename(2)` (via `node -e 'fs.renameSync'`), which refuses a non-empty or symlink target; map that to `raced`, not `mvfail`; drop a marker file into the staged tree before the rename and require it at `$dir/node_modules/` before any move-back.
2. **The watchdog and the TERM path kill npm's pid, not its process group.** A dependency's postinstall child outlives the gate (ppid 1) on the watchdog, on SIGTERM and on SIGKILL; only a Ctrl-C to the whole group removes it. esbuild's `install.js` fallback (`downloadDirectlyFromNPM`: `https.get`, no timeout, hard-coded registry) is the process that would be orphaned against a silent registry. **Fix:** start npm in its own process group (`set -m` in bash 3.2, or `perl -e 'setpgrp; exec @ARGV'`) and signal the group: TERM, then KILL, in both the watchdog and the cleanup. Same class as KS-1331 (a different script: `run-shell-suites.sh`).
3. **The gate does not check lock sources.** A lock entry whose `resolved` points at a non-registry host is fetched, and its postinstall runs on the push (measured: 1 GET at the listener, INSTALLED, a sentinel written outside the repo; a tampered integrity was refused with EINTEGRITY). Lifecycle scripts see `NPM_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and other `*TOKEN` names from the environment, and `~/.npmrc` is in scope; `--fetch-retries=0` and `--fetch-timeout` reach lifecycle children through `npm_config_*`. This is what a manual `npm ci` does too; the difference is that it now runs automatically on push, including for a package selected by a stale base or a merge the developer did not author. **Today's four lockfiles are clean:** 411/411, 344/344, 269/269 and 217/217 entries are `registry.npmjs.org` with an integrity hash. **Ruled YES:** every non-link entry must have `resolved` starting `https://registry.npmjs.org/` and a non-empty `integrity`; every `link` must resolve inside the repo; otherwise refuse with a named reason and run nothing; AND scrub the install's environment to a minimal set (`PATH`, `HOME`, what npm needs; no `*TOKEN`, no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`).
4. `m23b` **("no EXIT trap") is NOT equivalent, contrary to the item 1 table.** On bash 3.2 the EXIT trap is what cleans up on untrapped fatal signals other than QUIT. SIGUSR1 mid-install: head kills npm and removes the stage; with the EXIT trap removed, npm stays alive and the stage stays. Same for SIGALRM and SIGPIPE. The other four survivors (`m13a`, `m23`, `m25`, `m35`) were re-derived by the gate and are equivalent. **Fix:** one cell that sends SIGUSR1 or SIGALRM mid-install and expects no orphan and no stage.
5. **Four mutants survive that are test gaps, not equivalents.** `Q8` (the post-move `-x` → `-e`): no cell has a non-executable prettier. `Q11` (the hollow re-check dropped): a raced-in hollow tree would be reported as a *formatting failure* instead of the environment refusal, the KS-991 confusion. `Q12` (`.npmrc` not copied to the stage): no fixture has a package `.npmrc`. `Q13` (the six-digit length guard dropped): a 20-digit `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` overflows and refuses at once with "timed out after 99999999999999999999s"; head exits 2 naming the variable. **Fix:** one cell each.
6. **SIGQUIT to the gate alone leaves npm and the stage.** It is not trapped and bash 3.2 does not run the EXIT trap for it: rc 131, the hung npm alive, one stage left (the next run sweeps the stage). **Fix:** add QUIT to the trap list.

## The Info that matters

* **Info 2 (pre-existing, KS-1483):** a branch deletion (`git push origin :todelete`) and a tag push were both REFUSED because HEAD's branch touched an uninstallable package: the hook computes the changed set from `@{upstream}..HEAD`, not from the pushed refs. The develop control refuses the same two pushes (KS-1063 NOTHING CHECKED), so it is not a regression of #1532. **KS-998 item 2 with KS-1483 fixes it** (per-ref judging; a deleted ref is skipped before anything runs).
* **Info 3:** `_rm_stage` with an EMPTY `STAGE_PREFIX` would delete a relative single-component directory under the cwd (demonstrated on the extracted function). Unreachable today: the prefix is assigned once, never empty, and `set -u` aborts if unset. **Defence in depth:** `[ -n "$STAGE_PREFIX" ]` and require an absolute `$d`.
* **Info 5:** `-x` is true for a *directory* named `.bin/prettier`, so it is INSTALLED and then reported as a formatting failure with rc 126. npm never produces this. Cheap: `[ -f ] && [ -x ]`.
* **Info 6:** an invalid `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` blocks every push, including pushes that touch no systemTest file (validation exits 2 before selection), and the hook's wrapper then says "fix the files named above", which is wrong for it. Loud and self-inflicted; the wrapper's wording is the defect.
* **Info 7:** esbuild's install-script network fallback, exercised under the sandbox: with `@esbuild/darwin-arm64` removed, `install.js` tries `npm install` and then a direct download. **70.4 s** with npm defaults, **0.43 s** with `npm_config_fetch_retries=0`, and that value IS inherited from the gate's `npm ci` (measured through a postinstall). Both paths verify the binary with a sha256 before use.

## NOT tested by the gate (carried as unmeasured)

Linux (GNU `mv` has the same move-into-directory behaviour, so Minor 1 is expected to apply, not measured); preflight legs 3, 4, 8 and the full A/B; a real pty Ctrl-C (emulated); a silent registry against esbuild's direct download (reasoned from the code); the `--no-update-notifier` request census (not repeated).

## Related

KS-998 (the parent, stays In Progress: item 2 and KS-1483 are unbuilt), KS-1483 (item 2 folds it in). Same class as KS-1331 (process-group signalling), in a different script. Pull request #1532, head `3dbfdf7e3644`.

title: packages/shared does not type-check src/__tests__, hiding 10 errors — add a test-inclusive tsc leg and fix them
description:
## BLUF

`npx tsc -p . --noEmit` in `packages/shared` returns **rc 0**, and always has. That is not health: `tsconfig.json` carries `"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "src/__tests__"]`, so **the package's own type-check never sees a test file**. Under a program that does include them there are **10 errors across 6 files**. The exclusion is the defect; the 10 are its consequence.

Filed from KS-1179's TYPECHECK-DEBT item on the coordinator's ruling (one ticket, not two: a single test pass proves it, because the new leg goes green only once the errors are gone).

## The 10, measured

| file | errors |
| -- | -- |
| `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` | 2x **TS2345** (`Express` not assignable), 1x TS2741 |
| `src/security/ssrf-guard.ts` | 1x **TS2349** (see below), 1x TS7006 — **TS7006 fixed in KS-1179** |
| `src/__tests__/openapi-operation-ids.test.ts` | 1x TS2352 |
| `src/__tests__/openapi-415-injection.test.ts` | 1x TS2352 |
| `src/__tests__/ks914-pinned-address.test.ts` | 2x TS6133 (unused `vi`, unused `safeOutboundRequest`) |
| `src/__tests__/walkTimeouts.test.ts` | 1x TS5097 (`.ts` import extension) |

⚠ `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`**'s three are blocked until PR #1268 merges.** That PR is open and changes the same file; two branches on one file needs a declared merged-blob equality target. Do them after it lands.

## TS2349 — carried here because it does NOT fix cleanly

`mod` is `typeof https | typeof http` and calling the union of their overloads is the error. Four shapes were measured and **each relocated it**:

| attempt | result |
| -- | -- |
| no change | **TS2349** not callable |
| cast the callee `(mod.request as typeof https.request)` | **TS2769** no overload matches — `agent` is `https.Agent \| http.Agent` |
| callee cast + `agent: agent as https.Agent` at the call site | errors 10 -> 8, clean, **but the emit changes**: `agent,` expands to `agent: agent,` |
| callee cast + the assertion on the declaration | emit identical again, **TS2352** — the two Agent types "neither sufficiently overlaps" |

The only remaining shape is `as unknown as https.Agent`. **It was refused deliberately:** in an SSRF guard, a type the compiler stops checking is the risk to avoid. The honest fix is narrowing at the branch (`isTls ? https.request(...) : http.request(...)`), which **duplicates the call and changes the emit** — a real change to the request path, and not something a type error alone justifies. Decide it here, with the guard's owner.

## Method, so this is reproducible

A probe config **outside the repo**, extending the package's own `tsconfig.json` and overriding only:

```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true, "module": "esnext", "target": "ES2022" },
  "include": ["<pkg>/src/**/*.ts"], "exclude": [] }
```

`module`/`target` are raised only because the tests use top-level `await`; leaving them at the package's `commonjs` produces **9x TS1343 and 5x TS1378 that are artefacts of the probe**, not of the tree.

**Controls, because two earlier probes gave wrong answers:**

* **A** — the probe must SEE the file: `--listFilesOnly | grep <file>` returns 1.
* **B** — the probe must REPORT an error in it: planting `const x: number = "not a number";` takes it from **10 -> 11**, the new one naming the file and line. *(First read of this control grepped for the variable name and found 0 — tsc prints the file and line, not the identifier. The probe was fine; the grep was not.)*
* A probe adding `types: ["vitest/globals","node"]` reported **2 errors, both TS2688** — its own type-resolution failure silencing everything else. A probe that reports almost nothing looks like a clean tree.
* The same 10 reproduce under `moduleResolution: node` (the package's own) as under `bundler`, so they are not a resolution artefact. *(A duplicate-*`@types/node` *theory was raised and withdrawn: the tree holds 30 copies at three majors, but this program loads exactly one.)*

## Definition of done

- [ ] `packages/shared` type-checks `src/__tests__` — a leg or script that fails on a type error in a test file, with a positive control proving it can fail
- [ ] the 10 above resolved, or each recorded with the reason (TS2349 is a decision, see above)
- [ ] the ks781 three done after #1268 merges

⚠ **The leg touches the push gate**, which is not in the KS-1179 lane. That is why this is a separate ticket rather than more of that PR.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,318 issues (includeArchived) and 3,718 comments**: `tsconfig` -> 67 total / 30 open · `src/__tests__` -> 178 / 93 · `TS2345` -> 5 / 4 (KS-1313, KS-1179, KS-932, KS-872 — the F-3 lineage and L6's, none this subject) · `TS2349` -> **0** · `type-checks` -> 23 / 14. **No open issue is about the exclusion itself.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 13 total / 11 open, fires; a fresh token never written anywhere -> **0**.

Refs KS-1179

title: ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts: the AST guard does not see a member call, a bracket call or a bare undefined/null id (gate t4s4 LOW on #1734)
description:
## BLUF

**Gate t4s4 residue on PR #1734 (KS-1589 item A), LOW, GO WITH NOTES.** The rewritten AST guard kills all five mutants the round-2 gate recorded as surviving, and the gate confirmed that. It also found **three call shapes that stay GREEN** and that the guard's header does not list. None is live in the page today.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed** — the source ticket proposes none for these, and two of the three are deliberate exclusions whose boundary is a judgement, not a defect.

Refs KS-1589, KS-1564, KS-1319, KS-1329.

Guard: `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts`, 521 lines, **13 cells**, merged as `bc958363c549` (#1734). All line numbers read at develop `885d69b06f5fce7c8f58effea68623ecb25407b1`.

## 1 — The three blind spots, as the gate recorded them

From `2026-10-27_gate-t4s4-batch/verdict.md`, the #1734 row, verbatim:

> LOW: the AST guard has three reachable blind spots it does not claim to close (namespace/member call `api.fetchApiKeys('x' || 'y')`, bracket call, a bare `undefined`/`null` passed as the id).

and from that section's vacuity probes, **GREEN, not caught**:

> `api.fetchApiKeys('x' || 'y')` through a namespace import (the checker excludes property-access names by design, "someone else's .fetchApiKeys"); `(api as any)['fetchApiKeys']('x')` (a string, not an identifier); `fetchApiKeys(undefined)` (the `PLAIN_IDENTIFIER` regex accepts `undefined`/`null`); an alias in a `.js` file (walker takes only .ts/.tsx; none exist in the tree today).

The gate adds: *"The file header says it refuses 'expressions at the call sites, not provenance'; it does not list these. The current page imports by name, so none is live today."*

## 2 — Where each one lives in the guard, read at the tip

| shape | the code that lets it through | line |
| -- | -- | -- |
| member / namespace call `api.fetchApiKeys(…)` | `fetchApiKeysArgs` requires the callee to be an identifier: `if (ts.isCallExpression(n) && ts.isIdentifier(n.expression) && n.expression.text === 'fetchApiKeys')` | `:193` |
| the same, via the value-use checker | `fetchApiKeysValueUses` excludes property access explicitly: `if (ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(p) && p.name === n) continue;` | `:224` |
| bracket call `(api as any)['fetchApiKeys']('x')` | the element-access name is a string literal, not an `Identifier`, so neither walker sees it | `:193`, `:218` |
| a bare `undefined` / `null` id | `const PLAIN_IDENTIFIER = /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$.]*$/;` — the literals `undefined` and `null` match it | `:365`, asserted at `:397` and `:404` |
| an alias in a `.js` file | `const kind = fileName.endsWith('.tsx') ? ts.ScriptKind.TSX : ts.ScriptKind.TS;` and the walk takes only `.ts`/`.tsx` | `:134` |

The guard's own statement of scope is at `:69`: *"call sites, not the provenance of a variable."* The property-access exclusion at `:224` is documented in the comment above it (`:216-223`) as deliberate — "someone else's `.fetchApiKeys` property is not this function" — and that comment also names the shape the exclusion must **not** swallow, a renaming destructure.

**One further property of the regex, mine rather than the gate's and NOT tested with a mutant:** `PLAIN_IDENTIFIER`'s tail class is `[\w$.]*`, which admits a dot, so a dotted expression passed as the id would also match. Recorded as a read of the regex text, not as a demonstrated escape.

## 3 — What the guard reads, and what type-checks it

`ADMIN_SRC` at `:99` is `process.env.KS1564_ADMIN_SRC ?? join(DEV_ROOT, 'frontend', 'admin', 'src')`, so the guard reads the admin frontend's source from a test in `packages/shared`. `KS1564_ADMIN_SRC` (`:94`, `:99`) exists so a mutant harness can point it at a copy; the gate used exactly that, with the copy's tree sha256 asserted changed per mutant.

**Nothing in the repository type-checks this file.** `packages/shared/tsconfig.json:21` excludes `src/__tests__`, and the push preflight's leg 16 ratchet carries baselines for five services only — api-gateway, auth, m365-integration, security, vc-issuer — with no `packages/shared` baseline. That is KS-1329's subject, named here because a guard that parses the TypeScript AST is exactly the kind of file a type error can rot unseen.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing.** Every green/red above is the gate's; no mutant was constructed or re-run here, and the dotted-expression note in section 2 is a read of the regex, not a mutant.
* Whether any of the three is worth closing. The property-access exclusion is deliberate and has a stated reason; closing it needs a rule for telling "the imported function, accessed as a member" from "someone else's property of the same name". **Not decided.**
* Whether a `.js` file could ever appear under `frontend/admin/src`. The gate says none exists in the tree today; I did not re-count.
* KS-1589's items **B** (the quadratic trailing trim in `ApiKeys.tsx`) and **C** (three Playwright cells that have never run) are untouched by this and by #1734 — that ticket stays open for them.

## Searched

Board, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, title + description + comments, paginated to `hasNextPage` false — never capped.

* `api.fetchApiKeys` → **0 hits**. `PLAIN_IDENTIFIER` → **0 hits**.
* `ks1564-admin-api-keys-page` → **1 hit**, KS-1589. `KS1564_ADMIN_SRC` → **1 hit**, KS-1589. `fetchApiKeys` → **4 hits**: KS-1594, KS-1589, KS-1564, KS-1514.
* **KS-1589 was read whole**, description and comment. Its item A is what #1734 merged; its comment records the five mutants now red and says the ticket stays open for B and C. **It does not carry these three shapes** — they are the gate's finding on the merged result, which is after that ticket's text.
* `blind spot` → 69 hits, too broad to decide on alone; used only to check the narrow terms were not missing a nearer ticket.
* **Decision, stated:** filed rather than commented on KS-1589, because this board files one gate-residue ticket per merged PR (KS-1637 on #1589, KS-1643 on #1606, KS-1746 on #1733 are the precedent) and because KS-1589 stays open for B and C, which are different work in different files.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → **18 hits**; `fetchApiKeys` → **4 hits**. **Zero control:** a token coined for this session and written to no ticket → **0 hits**.

*Filed by Seat G 24th, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: pre_push_stack_legs_comment.test.sh grades the prose of .githooks/pre-push by three grep -c counts; CELL 2 requires KS-1046 exactly once, and CELL 2 + CELL 3 grade the same line :386
description:
## BLUF

`pre_push_stack_legs_comment.test.sh` **grades the prose of** `.githooks/pre-push` **by three** `grep -c` **counts, and CELL 2 requires the ticket key** `KS-1046` **to occur EXACTLY ONCE in the hook — so a second comment citing that key anywhere in the 400-line hook reds a cell.** The hook names its grading suite 0 times. This is the sibling of KS-1750, which fixed the same gap for the other prose-grading pair in the same directory; this pair was found by that ticket's census and raised for filing rather than touched, because `.githooks/pre-push` is a product file and was outside it.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed** — KS-1750's own open question ("a warning comment at the subject end, or loosen the three strings") applies here unchanged and is **not decided**.

Refs KS-1750, KS-1047, KS-1046, KS-691.

All line numbers and counts below were read at develop `885d69b06f5fce7c8f58effea68623ecb25407b1`.

## 1 — The grader, read whole

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_stack_legs_comment.test.sh`, 74 lines, `TOTAL_CELLS=4` at `:12`. Its subject is another file: `:16` is

`SUBJ="${PRE_PUSH_HOOK-$REPO_ROOT/.githooks/pre-push}"`

with `REPO_ROOT` at `:15` resolving to the repository root, so by default it grades the shipped hook.

| cell | line | predicate, verbatim | required |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| CELL 1 | `:28` | `stale_hits="$(grep -c '(3, 4, 7)' "$SUBJ" \|\| true)"` | **exactly 0** (`:29`) |
| CELL 2 | `:39` | `ptr_hits="$(grep -c 'KS-1046' "$SUBJ" \|\| true)"` | **exactly 1** (`:40`) |
| CELL 3 | `:50` | `anchor_hits="$(grep -c 'KS-691: source slot-target.sh first so the stack-dependent legs' "$SUBJ" \|\| true)"` | **exactly 1** (`:51`) |
| CELL 4 | `:58-60` | `bash -n "$SUBJ"` | parses |

## 2 — The three counts, measured in the hook itself

`.githooks/pre-push` is **400 lines** at this tip. Each predicate run against it:

| predicate | count | cell's requirement | state |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `(3, 4, 7)` | **0** | 0 | satisfied |
| `KS-1046` | **1** | exactly 1 | satisfied, **with zero margin** |
| `KS-691: source slot-target.sh first so the stack-dependent legs` | **1** | exactly 1 | satisfied, with zero margin |

Controls on the same instrument and file: positive `preflight` → **26**; a zero-control token coined for this read and written nowhere → **0**.

## 3 — CELL 2 and CELL 3 grade the SAME sentence, so the control is not independent

Both hits are on **one line,** `.githooks/pre-push:386`, verbatim:

`# KS-691: source slot-target.sh first so the stack-dependent legs (the ones the preflight verdict lists as SKIPPED when the stack is down - KS-1046; not enumerated here, an enumeration drifts) probe`

CELL 3 is named "CONTROL. THE KS-691 RATIONALE COMMENT IS STILL THERE" (`:48`). It and CELL 2's pointer are the same sentence, so **editing or reflowing that one comment line reds two of the four cells at once**, and the control cell cannot witness an edit to the pinned pointer independently of CELL 2.

## 4 — The hook does not say it is graded

`pre_push_stack_legs_comment` occurs **0** times in `.githooks/pre-push`. Its only match for `graded` is the substring inside *degraded* at `:9` (`# that degraded: GitHub Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27), so`), which is unrelated. This is the same gap at the subject end that KS-1750 closed for `pre_push_hook_base.test.sh`.

## 5 — Two differences from the KS-1750 pair, both measured

* **These are patterns, not fixed strings.** All three use `grep -c` **without** `-F` (`:28`, `:39`, `:50`), where KS-1750's grader uses `grep -c -F`. None of the three strings contains a BRE metacharacter — in BRE `(` and `)` are literal — so they match literally today, but the two graders are not the same instrument.
* **The override refuses an empty value, by a different route.** `:16` uses `${PRE_PUSH_HOOK-…}`, not `${PRE_PUSH_HOOK:-…}`, so an empty `PRE_PUSH_HOOK` is passed through rather than replaced by the default; `[ -f "$SUBJ" ]` at `:17` then exits **2** with `FATAL: pre-push hook not found at`. It does **not** silently grade the shipped file. KS-1750's sibling reaches the same outcome through a dedicated empty-value refusal instead.

## 6 — The header's line number is dated, not stale

The header (`:3`, `:5`) reads "TESTS for .githooks/pre-push line :268 comment" and "The defect at tip `48e65c435`: line 268 enumerates legs". It attributes `:268` to that named tip, not to the present one; the graded comment is at `:386` here. Recorded so a reader does not treat `:268` as current.

## Not established

* **I did not run this suite.** The "4 passed / 0 failed at base" figure is Seat R 5th's, relayed through Wednesday, and is not reproduced here. What is measured above is the three cells' **inputs** — the counts in the subject file — not a run.

* Whether a **third** suite in `scripts/__tests__` grades a fourth file's prose. KS-1750's census over the 74 `.test.sh` files in that directory found this pair; I did not re-run it.
* Whether adding a second `KS-1046` citation is a thing anyone is about to do. The cell is **latent**, not live — all three counts are satisfied at this tip.
