title: api-gateway: decide and test the degraded-mode posture for session revocation — isSessionActive null (session store unreachable) continues, so a revoked session passes while the store is down (KS-257)
Published prose drifts from the routes it describes and nothing detects it — the phrase check, the marker convention, and the ~306 unswept descriptions
description:
**Ruled lines 1, 2 and 5 of KS-822's five, lifted onto one ticket so they survive that ticket closing.** They are one problem seen three ways: *published prose drifts away from the routes it describes, and nothing detects it.*

The evidence is not hypothetical. `POST /api/oauth/token`'s description was swept **twice** and was wrong in **three** places both times. One wrong sentence about client authentication reached **four** separate places (comment → contract → test header → route), and the fourth landed *inside the commit that corrected the first three*.

---

## Line 1 — targeted contract-source phrase check (~half a day, SIZED)

A retired-phrase registry checked against **contract sources only**: `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts` plus the generated `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`.

* **No marker convention needed to start** — in that surface a quotation carrying a marker is rare to nonexistent.
* Catches the **comment → contract** hop, which is the one that publishes a wrong rule to integrators.
* **The matcher must be wrap-tolerant by construction**: normalise whitespace and comment punctuation across line boundaries before matching. ~15 lines.
* ⚠ **A single-token control is NOT a valid control for a line-wrapping phrase.** That exact mistake made an earlier sweep report **0** where the true count was **4**.
* **Stated limitation, on the line rather than discovered later: this would NOT have caught F-1c.** Test headers are outside the surface and F-1c was a test header. This is the cheap 80%, not the class.

## Line 2 — repo-wide marker convention (UNSIZED, deliberately)

Not sized pending a population measurement, and **measuring the population is most of the work.**

The shape it must survive, from a real specimen produced on `develop`: in `BACKLOG.md` the retired phrase *"deletion only"* appears twice — once as the live claim and once inside a quotation of the old wording. A sweep that cannot tell a quotation from a claim makes a correct commit look like a regression, because the phrase count went **1 → 2** for an entirely correct reason.

## Line 5 — the ~306 unswept published descriptions (UNSIZED)

The other **~306** published operation descriptions have never been swept against their routes. Sizing it means sampling, and sampling is most of the work. **It pairs naturally with line 1**, which runs over the same surface.

---

## Why these are together

Line 1 is the instrument, line 2 is what the instrument needs to avoid false positives at repo scale, and line 5 is the population it would be pointed at. Building line 1 alone is defensible and cheap; building it *without* line 2's distinction is what makes a sweep that cries wolf and gets switched off.

## The standing ruling

**Wednesday priced line 1 and ruled DO NOT BUILD IT NOW** (2026-09-05T15:44:16Z), after it was proposed. That ruling is carried here unchanged — this ticket is the record, not a commission. Anyone picking it up should re-price rather than assume the half-day still holds.

*Source: KS-822 comments* `e38c5f38` *(lines 1 and 2) and* `4f901d71` *(line 5), from PR #831's tier-2 gate.*

title: KS-1402 gate AH1 residue: the transfer-custody tenant predicates are not independently proven (RLS hides the row), plus a false ks564 tripwire claim and three smaller gaps
description:
## BLUF

**Gate AH1's residue on PR #1620 (KS-1402's invited-stub holder, merged** `a0da739b6954`**). Five items,**
**and the first is the one that matters: the route's tenant predicates are NOT independently proven —**
**row-level security hides the row anyway, so dropping a predicate leaves the suite 15/15 green.**

## Recommendation

Do (a) first and on its own. It is the only item where the current tests read as stronger than they
are, and it carries a contradiction in the code comments that needs settling by measurement rather
than by reading.

## Detail — the five items

**(a) A cell that runs WITHOUT row-level security, so a dropped tenant predicate reds.**
`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` binds a tenant predicate in the holder resolution
(\~`:1712`) and in the id-path existence check (\~`:1733`). Gate AH1 measured that **dropping either**
**one still leaves** `ks1402-invited-stub-holder.integration.test.ts` **at 15/15**, because `users` is
FORCE RLS for the application role the product connects as — RLS makes the row invisible regardless
of the predicate. So the predicates are belt-and-braces that nothing currently proves.
Add a cell that connects as the **owner** (no RLS) so the predicate is the only thing standing, and
assert a cross-tenant holder is refused there.
**And settle a contradiction while doing it:** the comments at `documents.ts:1907` and `:1999`
describe tenant RLS as *inert*, which cannot be true alongside the behaviour above. One of them is
wrong — measure which, and correct it rather than deleting it.

**(b) Fix a false tripwire claim in two code comments.** `documents.ts:1945` and the suite header
`ks1402-invited-stub-holder.integration.test.ts:73` both name **auth** `ks564-connector-stub-auth`
as a guard that would red if `certifications:write` were withdrawn from `hasUsersStubScope`.
**It is not.** Gate AH1 removed that scope from `hasUsersStubScope` (auth `users.ts:257`) and
**ks564 stayed 4/4, auth unit 1076/1076**. The only real tripwire is **api-gateway**
`ks843-erasure-scope-gate.test.ts` **F-2**, which regex-reads `S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES` out of the source
and **reds 1/9**. The PR body was corrected before the merge; the two code comments were not,
because correcting them would have meant a new commit on a gated head.
*Worth recording why the wrong claim got in: it was "verified" by grepping ks564 for the string*
`certifications:write` *and finding it. The presence of a string in a test is not evidence the test*
*guards it — the measurement is to remove the thing and see what reds.*

**(c) A cell for the non-2xx fallback at** `documents.ts:1681`**.** A `void raced` mutant there
survives. It fails **safe** (the request answers 502 rather than proceeding), which is why it was a
note and not a blocker, but it is uncovered.

**(d)** `RACE` **should also assert there is exactly ONE user row and no phantom row.** The cell
currently asserts the custody event points at the winner's id. It does not assert that auth's
phantom id never materialised as a second row, which is the other half of the property.

**(e) Citation fix:** the `createInvitedStub` reference should be `auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:771`,
not `:768` (cited in `documents.ts` and in the merged commit message).

## Context worth keeping

The merged behaviour: a custody transfer naming a recipient Platform K has never seen now mints an
INVITED stub via auth's `POST /api/users/stub` instead of answering 404 (Kam's card
`secuura-ks1402-who-creates-the-holder-1019` = a). **Nothing is deployed** — KS-1402 stays In
Progress until it is live-checked.

Related: KS-1653 (widening `hasUsersStubScope` to `documents:transfer-custody` — a different change
to the same gate), KS-1654, KS-1655 (retention, including the mint-before-document-check case).

title: State the M365 source-document controller boundary in the customer DPA
description:
## Action

Add wording to the customer **DPA** stating the M365 source-document controller boundary.

## Why

From KS-234 §5.3: Secuura's m365 integration holds only an **org-scoped OAuth connection** (`svc_m365_connections`), not a per-user copy of source documents. The source documents live in the **customer's own M365 / SharePoint tenant**, where the **customer is the data controller**. On a Secuura erasure, the customer's M365 source is therefore the **customer's** erasure responsibility, not Secuura's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Customer DPA explicitly states the customer is controller of their own M365 source documents and is responsible for erasing them in their own tenant.

Refs: KS-234 §5.3. (Belongs in the DPA legal doc, not the platform repo.)

title: m365: exchangeAuthCode stores the FIRST refresh token in a process-wide MSAL cache - a second organisation's connection gets the first organisation's token and refreshes into its Microsoft 365
description:
## BLUF

`exchangeAuthCode` **hands each new Microsoft 365 connection the FIRST refresh token in a process-wide MSAL cache, not the one for the account that just signed in.** Once two organisations have connected within one process lifetime, the second organisation's connection stores the **first** organisation's refresh token. From its first token refresh onward, the second organisation reads the first organisation's Microsoft 365 as its own.

**No attacker and no leaked id is needed**: two organisations connecting normally is enough. That is KS-1673's harm (one organisation acting as another in Microsoft 365) reached by a different root cause. This is token **selection**, not organisation binding (KS-1673) and not callback state binding (KS-1677).

**Dormant today:** KS-1673's read-only measurement found 0 connections on kintsugi and demo.

## The mechanism, line by line

At develop `640bc7efdfd4` (develop is now `5ac66264b9ee`, which is #1645, docs only - m365 is unchanged). `token-manager.ts` blob `b72a62f4617d`, `index.ts` blob `ba99e5dd8cbf`.

| line | what it does |
| -- | -- |
| `token-manager.ts:26`, `:51` | ONE module-level `ConfidentialClientApplication` for the whole process, shared by every organisation. Its token cache is msal-node's default in-memory cache, living as long as the process. |
| `:85` | `acquireTokenByCode` - msal-node writes this account's tokens into that shared cache. |
| `:93` | `let refreshToken = (result as any).refreshToken \|\| ''` - always `''`; see Measured, item 1. |
| `:94`-`:101` | so the fallback runs on **every** exchange: serialise the shared cache and take `Object.values(RefreshToken)[0]` (`:99`). **Nothing filters by the account that just signed in.** |
| (whole file) | nothing ever clears the cache or removes an account. The only cache call in the file is `:96`. |
| `index.ts:628` (callback), `:746` (`/complete`) | store that refresh token on the connection being completed. |
| `index.ts:862`, `:866`-`:867` | the refresh path uses the stored token. It writes back only a non-empty one, so a wrong token, once stored, is **kept**, and every refresh mints an access token for the wrong account. |

The connection's **first** access token is its own (`:85`'s result). The swap only shows at the first refresh, about an hour later, which is why nobody would see it in a demo.

## Measured

1. **msal-node returns no refresh token.** msal-node is 3.8.10 in this tree. The msal-common it actually resolves (`require.resolve` from msal-node) is its **nested** 15.17.0, NOT the hoisted copy. Its `AuthenticationResult` (`dist/response/AuthenticationResult.d.ts:19-41`) declares **0** `refreshToken` fields, with `accessToken` read the same way at **1** as the control. My first attempt at this read was VOID (a wrong path found no file, and its control also read 0). I discarded it and redid it.
2. **The exact expression on a REAL msal-node cache.** Using msal-node 3.8.10's own `ConfidentialClientApplication`, I deserialised a cache holding org A's refresh token, then org B's. I ran `token-manager.ts:96-101`'s logic verbatim: it returns `RT-OF-ORG-A` for B's sign-in. **Control:** a cache holding only B's returns B's, so the expression is not returning a constant. `getTokenCache()` returns the **same** object on every call (`true`).

## Not measured, said plainly

Not driven end to end against Microsoft: no real sign-in, no real refresh. I relied on msal-node's documented behaviour on two points: that `acquireTokenByCode` writes the account's refresh token into the in-memory cache, and that its serialiser keeps insertion order. A restart clears the cache, so the bug needs two sign-ins inside one process lifetime.

## Board search

Exhaustive, over all **1670** issues (archived included), title + description, exact substring:

* `getTokenCache` 0
* `firstRT` 0
* `acquireTokenByCode` 0
* `object.values(refreshtokens` 0
* `token cache` 4 (KS-156, 191, 198, 1074) - all Schemathesis, performance or anchoring by title.
* `refreshtokens` 1 (KS-317, Akto)
* `token-manager` 2 (KS-37, KS-1641) - neither owns this by title.
* `msal` 6 (KS-130, 470, 493, 1379, 1670, 1671) - none about refresh-token selection.

**Positive control:** `exchangeAuthCode` returns exactly KS-1677, whose description I read and which contains it.

Linear `searchIssues` (fuzzy, indexes comments): `refresh token cache msal` 32, `exchangeAuthCode refresh token` 31, `getTokenCache` 2 (KS-1074, KS-214). Every title read; none owns this.

## How it was found

Seat R 57th, 2026-10-20, reading `exchangeAuthCode` while measuring KS-1677. Filed High on Wednesday's ruling (2026-10-20 \~06:44 AEDT). **No fix is proposed here.** The shape is a later decision.

title: Admin Dashboard API Keys page hard-codes organizationId 'default-org' on list and mint — the source of non-canonical rows, and the reason a uuid enforcement cannot ship alone (the list would break SILENTLY)
description:
## BLUF

**The Admin Dashboard's API Keys page hard-codes a non-uuid organisation id,** `'default-org'`**, on both the list and the mint.** It works today, so this is not an outage — but it is (a) the **source** of non-canonical `svc_api_keys.organization_id` rows, and (b) the reason a `format: uuid` enforcement on `GET/POST /api/keys` **cannot ship on its own**: it would break this page, and the list half would break **silently**.

Found while planning **KS-1553**, by running the caller census Wednesday required before relying on a 400. Facts only; no fix proposed here.

## Where

| site | what it sends |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/admin/src/pages/ApiKeys.tsx:75` | calls `fetchApiKeys()` with **no argument** |
| `frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:358-360` | `const orgId = organizationId \|\| 'default-org'` → `GET /api/security/keys?organizationId=default-org` |
| `frontend/admin/src/pages/ApiKeys.tsx:92` | `createApiKey({ …, organizationId: 'default-org' })` → `POST /api/security/keys` |

`'default-org'` occurs in **exactly these two files** across the tracked tree and is **not seeded** by any migration or `docker/init` script, so it exists only where this page put it.

`frontend/admin/src/pages/platform/ClientDetail.tsx:15` imports `fetchApiKeys` and never calls it — a dead import, noted so it is not mistaken for a second caller.

## Measured

2026-10-13 (Seat V 6th), own scratch PostgreSQL 15, service connected as `secuura_app`, the real routes, every arm with a control:

| check | result |
| -- | -- |
| the admin's exact mint body (`organizationId: 'default-org'`) | **201** |
| the stored value | `default-org`**, verbatim** |
| the admin's exact list (`?organizationId=default-org`) | **200, and it returns that key** |
| CONTROL: a different organisation id | 0 keys — the list really filters, so the pass is not vacuous |
| the UPPER-CASE form of the same id | **0 keys** (the KS-1553 (a) raw-compare mismatch) |
| CONTROL: a mint with **no** `organizationId` (the metering-key shape) | 201, stays absent |

So the page is **functional end to end today** on a value that is not a uuid.

## Why a uuid enforcement breaks it, and why the list half is the dangerous half

* **The list breaks SILENTLY.** `request()` (`api.ts:84-91`) turns any non-2xx into `{ok: false}`, and `fetchApiKeys` then returns `[]`. The page would show **zero keys** and set `isLive` false. **No error reaches the user** — it would simply stop listing keys it lists today.
* **The mint breaks visibly.** `createApiKey` returns `null` on a non-2xx, so the Create-Key button stops producing a key.

## What the fix needs (not done here)

The page must send the **caller's real organisation id**, from the authenticated user's claim. It cannot simply omit the field on the **list**, because `organizationId` is a **required** query parameter there (`security.openapi.ts:823`, and the handler's own `if (!organizationId)` returns 400). So this is a **feature change**, not a one-line edit, and the frontend is a **deployable surface** — under the workspace rule it ships to the local stack *and* the Azure demo, which needs a deploy seat.

## Sequencing

Per Wednesday's ruling of 2026-10-13, this is **PR 2** material and is bundled with **KS-1553 (b)** and **KS-1514 item 2**, because none of the three is safe alone: enforcement without this fix breaks the page, and this fix without enforcement leaves the seam open. PR 2 is **not started** and waits on Stuart's answer about the form Platform S sends (KS-1553 comment `2087528f`).

**KS-1553's PR 1** (normalising the list query, no 400) is deliberately scoped so that it does **not** touch this page, and it carries the admin's exact shape as a **regression pin** so the working page stays working.

## Priority

Filed **P3** by me for consistency with the residue ticket. **It may deserve higher**: it is a product-level finding about a page in the Admin Dashboard, and Wednesday is raising the hard-coded value with Kam separately. Re-prioritise on his word rather than mine.

## Related

* **KS-1553** — the raw-vs-canonical list comparison; this was found while planning it.
* **KS-1514** — item 2 is the declared-but-unenforced `uuid` on the list query.
* the data-residue ticket filed alongside this one — this page is the **source** of the rows it asks to be counted.
* Class: **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

## Not established by me

I have not opened the Admin Dashboard in a browser, and I have not counted `'default-org'` rows on any environment — I have no box access. Every number above is from my own scratch database and from reading the tracked source.

*Dedupe: all 695 Secuura-PK issues pulled and matched LITERALLY (not via the fuzzy* `searchIssues`*) on* `ApiKeys.tsx`*,* `frontend/admin`*,* `default-org`*,* `fetchApiKeys`*,* `createApiKey`*,* `Admin Dashboard`*,* `hard-coded`*,* `isLive`*,* `auth claim`*, with a bogus-symbol control returning 0.* `ApiKeys.tsx`*,* `default-org`*,* `fetchApiKeys`*,* `createApiKey` *and* `isLive` *each returned **0** existing issues; no issue matched two or more distinctive terms. The two* `Admin Dashboard` *hits (KS-749 postcss advisory, KS-746 security-event tenancy) were checked and are unrelated.*

title: Correct the spec hot-reload comment, and stop it logging success when it re-read the same bytes (a replaced bind-mounted file reloads the OLD spec)
description:
## BLUF

**Action (owner: the K lane): correct the spec hot-reload comment in** `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts`**, and if it is cheap make the reload stop reporting success when it re-read the same bytes.** On Kintsugi the deploy seat measured that after an `rsync` replaced the bind-mounted spec file the gateway DID hot-reload 1 s later and logged success, but the content it re-read was the OLD content of the dead inode. So the comment is wrong on this runtime, and the reload can say "hot-reloaded" while serving a stale contract.

## Recommendation

1. **Fix the comment** in the `Dev-only hot-reload` block (lines 611 to 641 at develop `361537eed238`). It says a replacement (`mv`, `rsync`) "fires neither watch" and that the file then reads ENOENT from inside. Measured on this runtime (node 24 alpine, Kintsugi): the file watch FIRED, no ENOENT, and the read returned the old bytes. Keep the 2026-08-17 ENOENT measurement as what it is, a node 22 result.
2. **If cheap, change what the success line claims.** Keep a hash of the raw text last loaded; when a reload re-reads a file whose hash is unchanged, log a warning ("the watch fired but the content is the same; if the file was replaced by rsync or mv this container still holds the old inode: restart api-gateway") instead of `OpenAPI spec hot-reloaded`. An inode check inside the container cannot see this, because the mount keeps pointing at the old inode before and after the host replaces the file; only "same bytes after a watch event" is observable from inside.

## Detail

* **Evidence (the deploy seat, Seat D 18th, 2026-10-12):** `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatD-18th/stepC/gw_reload_line.txt` and `gw_reload_check.txt`. The gateway logged `2026-10-12 11:06:49.123 [api-gateway] info: OpenAPI spec hot-reloaded {"path":"/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml","mappedRoutes":310}`; zero `hot-reload failed` lines; the spec readable INSIDE the running gateway (sha16 `46a449868783d729`) had zero mentions of the new route; a method-map probe of the new route answered 404.
* **310 versus 312:** Wednesday's brief says 310 is the old spec and the new one maps 312. That 312 is not in the two evidence files and I did not recompute it; treat it as reported.
* **Why it matters:** the block's own comment promises "stale but CONSISTENT". This is stale and reported fresh. Nothing is broken at runtime; the risk is that a deploy check which greps the log for "hot-reloaded" reads a pass.
* **Not reproduced by me.** I read the record; I did not run the rsync.
* **Related, not duplicates:** KS-987 (P2 Backlog: a deploy that rsyncs the spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a stale published contract; it documents the new-inode cause but not the false-success log line or this comment). KS-659 (the original "hot-reload never fires in the container" ticket) and KS-656 are archived, so they cannot be linked; they are named here instead.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, title and description): `inode`, `hot-reload`, `hot-reloaded`, `mappedRoutes`, `bind-mount`, `dead inode`. Nearest: KS-987, KS-1021 (archived Duplicate), KS-659, KS-656.

Related: KS-987.

title: KS-1564 follow-ups (pull request 1537 round-2 gate): the ks1564 source guard is satisfied by a parenthesised argument, an alias and a COMMENTED-OUT guard; describeFailure's trailing-dot trim is quadratic; the three Playwright cells have never run
description:
## BLUF

Three carried items from the **round-2 (delta) gate** on pull request 1537, Sonnet tier 2, **GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major / 2 Minor** — reports `de22859410b28af3` (round 1) and `465eec274ce18e10` (round 2). Neither Minor blocked the merge. Filed before the squash on Wednesday's instruction.

**The through-line: the ks1564 cells pin TEXT, and the browser run is what pinned BEHAVIOUR.** That is fine while the browser run exists; it is not fine as the standing regression guard, because five mutants walk straight past it.

---

## A. The source guard can be satisfied wrongly

`packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts` — the `fetchApiKeysArgs` regex and `racesAreGuarded`. **Five mutants SURVIVED 9/9**, each one a real way to break the page while the guard stays green:

| mutant | what it does | why nothing reds |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **N3** | the race guard line turned into a **comment** | cell 5 is a text-position check; the behaviour is then unguarded |
| **N6b** | `fetchApiKeys(String(orgId) \|\| ['default','org'].join('-'))` plus any other plain call | the argument regex is `[^()]*`, so an argument **containing parentheses** is not seen and the call is skipped |
| **N7** | alias call — `const f = fetchApiKeys; f('x')` | no parenthesis follows the name, so the scrape misses it |
| **N9** | the **organisations-loader** guard deleted | no cell pins it at all |
| **N10** | the Generate **in-flight** guard (`submitRef`) deleted | no cell pins it at all |

Killed, for contrast: N1, N2, N4, N12 (cell 5) and N5, N11 (cell 4); the comment-only control stayed green. One conservative false red: N8, a *comment* quoting `fetchApiKeys(orgId || 'x')`, reds cell 4 — harmless.

**Also worth recording:** the round-2 brief expected cells 4 **and** 5 to red on the old code. Only **cell 5** does. The old code already called `fetchApiKeys(orgId)`; cell 4 only reds a bad call *shape*. Nothing is wrong in the product — the expectation was half wrong, and a red-first claim built on it would have been overstated.

### Shape

Parse with a TypeScript AST, or strip comments first and match the argument by **balanced** parentheses rather than `[^()]*`. Add a cell for the organisations-loader guard and one for `submitRef`. Each new cell red-first against the mutant it is meant to catch — N3, N6b, N7, N9, N10 respectively.

### This class has a precedent, and it is \[\[KS-1319\]\]

"walkTimeouts guard: **the wiring pin passes on a commented-out line**" — same failure mode (a source scrape a comment satisfies), different guard, already Done. N3 is that class recurring in a second guard, which is the argument for doing A as a parser change rather than another regex.

---

## B. `describeFailure`'s trailing trim is quadratic

`frontend/admin/src/pages/ApiKeys.tsx:99` — `message.replace(/[.\s]*$/, '')`. Backtracking is quadratic on a long run of dots or whitespace **followed by another character**. Measured in node (V8, the browser's engine):

| input | time |
| -- | -- |
| 20k spaces + `"x"` | 230 ms |
| 40k spaces + `"x"` | 947 ms |
| 80k spaces + `"x"` | **3.84 s** |
| **control:** 80k plain letters | **0.27 ms** |

A server error message of that shape would freeze the tab. **Exposure is low** — the messages come from the platform's own services — but that text can still echo user input, so it is not structurally impossible.

### Shape

Trim in a linear way: `message.replace(/\s+$/, '').replace(/\.+$/, '')`, or a manual end-scan. A cell with an 80k-space input and a wall-clock bound would red the current code.

---

## C. The three Playwright cells have never been run

`tests/e2e/tests/sysadmin-exhaustive.admin.spec.ts` cells 3.8b.1-3.8b.3. **Not run in round 1, not run in round 2, not run by the author.** A QA pass needs the Docker stack. The gate read them against the code and they look right (`openApiKeysTab` waits for `GET /api/platform/tenants`, takes the first tenant id from `body.data.tenants ?? body.tenants`, opens `platform/clients/<id>?tab=api-keys`; `App.tsx:53-54` and `ClientDetail.tsx:54,355` render `<ApiKeys />` for that tab; every testid it uses was exercised against a stub) — but **reading is not running**.

**One concrete way the cleanup cell can red on the real stack:** 3.8b.1 revokes the key it minted by finding its row *on the current table page*. The page lists **10 per page in server order**. If the organisation already holds more than 10 keys and the new one is not on page 1, the revoke locator fails. Unknown without the real stack.

---

## What the browser run DID establish (so nobody re-does it)

Both round-1 Majors are **fixed**, proven in a browser against a stub, each with a control build of the old head that **reproduces the bug**: the stale-list overwrite (round-1 reproduction now ends on Beta; the old head still shows Alpha), A-B-A-B-B switching, Refresh in flight, a late error after a newer success, unmount mid-request, and the organisations-loader-versus-tenant-switch case. Double-click mints **one** POST (old head: two). No `window.alert`, no fake key on failure, XSS rendered as literal text.

Note the limit the gate itself drew: the organisations-loader guard **line** is not exercised even by that run, because the real route remounts the component — consistent with N9 showing no cell pins it.

---

## Related

\[\[KS-1564\]\] the parent · \[\[KS-1319\]\] the same guard class, already Done · \[\[KS-1155\]\] the walkTimeouts budget this PR's `walkTimeouts.setup.ts` touch belongs to.

title: kintsugi anchor_store: two rows are simulated=true AND status='confirmed' (block_number NULL) - a shape KS-587's Done-when and proposed guard both pass over
description:
## BLUF

**Kintsugi's** `anchor_store` **holds two rows that are simultaneously** `simulated = true` **and** `status = 'confirmed'`**.** An honestly-flagged placeholder that also claims a confirmed anchor is a contradictory pair, and it is **not** the shape KS-587 closed — KS-587's "Done when" is *satisfied* by these rows, and its proposed guard would not see them. Demo's 83 placeholder rows are the counter-case: all `failed`, all carrying an error_message.

Facts only. No row, box or code was touched, and no fix is proposed.

Refs KS-587, KS-520, KS-522.

## The measurement — Seat D 35th's, relayed, NOT re-measured here

⚠ **Provenance, stated plainly: every figure in this section is Seat D 35th's read-only measurement** of 2026-10-26T23:13Z (its STATUS A), relayed to this ticket by Wednesday. **I did not connect to either box and did not re-run any query.** Nothing here is mine.

**The two kintsugi rows:**

| field | both rows |
| -- | -- |
| created | 2026-08-20 |
| `transaction_hash` | `mock_tx_a6435a40…` and `mock_tx_2081b052…` (length **72**) |
| `simulated` | **true** |
| `status` | `confirmed` |
| `confirmations` | 1 |
| `block_number` | NULL |
| `error_message` | NULL |
| `network` | preview |

**Classifier control, same read:** over kintsugi's non-simulated rows, **31** real 64-hex hashes and **0** mock — so the classifier distinguishes the two populations rather than matching everything.

**The counter-case on demo:** **83** simulated rows, **all** `failed`, each with an error_message (the KS-587 corpus shape), and **0** simulated-and-confirmed.

## Why KS-587 does not cover this

KS-587 (Deployed to UAT, archived) — *"84 demo anchors carry mock_tx\_ hashes but are flagged simulated=false + confirmed"* — is the **inverse flag on a different box**. Read in full, three of its own lines decide the question:

* Its **"Done when"**: *"no row in* `anchor_store` *carries a mock/sim hash while claiming* `simulated = false`*, and the runbook covers reconciliation."* These rows carry `simulated = true`, so they **satisfy** it.
* Its **recommendation 1**: *"Reconcile the 84 rows — at minimum set* `simulated = true` *so the KS-520/522 honesty path engages and they stop claiming on-chain proof."* Setting `simulated = true` is exactly the state these rows are already in — and they still say `confirmed`, with `confirmations = 1`.
* Its **recommendation 3**: *"a* `mock_tx_`*/*`tx_sim_` *prefix with* `simulated = false` *is a contradiction that could be asserted in a test or a boot-time check."* That guard is keyed on `simulated = false`; it would read these two rows as correct.

So the residue KS-587 left is narrower than its own remedy assumed: the remedy addresses the **flag**, not the **status**, and `status = 'confirmed'` with `block_number` NULL was never in its scope.

KS-520 and KS-522 (both Done, archived) are the code-path pair — the fail-open fabrication, and the absence of an honest-labelling signal downstream. Neither is about rows already stored on a box.

## A documentation fact this bears on

The project's `CLAUDE.md` states that **zero** rows are `simulated = true` and `confirmed`. Per the relay, that figure was measured **on demo only**, where it holds (0 of 83). It is not true of kintsugi. *No repository file was edited by this ticket — recorded here so whoever picks this up knows the doc's scope.*

## Not established

* **How the two rows were written.** Unknown.
* **Whether any document reads them as anchored**, or is presented as verified on their basis. Not checked.
* **Whether the code path that produced them still exists.** Not checked.
* Whether `confirmations = 1` with `block_number` NULL is reachable through any current writer.
* Whether other boxes or environments hold rows in this presentation. Only kintsugi and demo were read, and by someone else.
* Anything about the correct remedy. Deleting, re-flagging or failing these rows is a product call, and the rows are **not** to be touched on the strength of this ticket.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `mock_tx_` — **23 hits**. The nearest were read: **KS-587** (the inverse flag, demo, archived — decision above), KS-589 (archived; a Schemathesis anchor-honesty consistency test for `mock_tx_`), KS-1626 (In Progress; five placeholder checks still reading `mock_batch_`), KS-1485, KS-1634, KS-683.
* `simulated` — **50 hits**, scanned; the anchor-honesty family is the set above plus KS-1661, KS-1676, KS-1629, KS-1640, KS-1650.
* `anchor_store` — **50 hits**, scanned; none names a simulated-and-confirmed row.
* `KS-587` — **28 hits** (tickets citing it). `simulated+confirmed` — **0 hits**. `simulated = true` — **6 hits**: KS-1634, KS-683, KS-670, KS-589, KS-587, KS-519 — none is this presentation.
* `KS-520` / `KS-522` — both read in full; both Done and archived, both about the code path, neither about stored rows.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.

*Filed by Seat G 22nd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's addendum. The measurement is Seat D 35th's.*

title: The demo VM runs every service as NODE_ENV=development while the code names "demo" as prod-like — ~6 production guards are silently inert, and the public API-docs exposure is one symptom
description:
## BLUF

**The live demo runs all 27 Node services with** `NODE_ENV=development`**.** The codebase explicitly
treats `demo` as a prod-like environment (`services/auth/src/index.ts:220`:
`IS_PROD_LIKE = ['production','staging','demo'].includes(NODE_ENV)`), so a set of guards written to
protect prod-like deployments do not fire on the demo. **Found 2026-08-17 (session 44) as a control**,
while disproving an unrelated claim about KS-656 — nobody was looking for it.

**Filed, deliberately not fixed.** Changing what the demo is counts as demo-affecting config and is
Kam's call. There is also a **live disagreement between three artefacts** about what the demo is
supposed to be, and flipping anything now would destroy the evidence that the question was ever open.

## The disagreement — three artefacts, three answers

| Artefact | Says the demo should be |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/src/index.ts:220` | `demo` — an explicit prod-like value |
| `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:578-582` (comment) + `deployment/azure/services.bicep:626` | prod-like: public API docs "never in demo/prod", bicep sets the flag `true` only for `dev` |
| `docker-compose.yml` (the file the VM actually runs) + the VM's `.env:165` | `development` |

**Someone may have set this deliberately** — Stuart or Peter driving Swagger against the demo is
entirely plausible, and it has probably been this way a long time. **Establish which artefact is****
****authoritative before reconciling any of it.**

## Measured on the live demo VM (read-only; values never printed)

```
docker exec <svc> printenv NODE_ENV   -> development     (26 of 26 Node services; 5 infra containers unset)
/home/secuura/secuura/Dev/.env:165    -> NODE_ENV=development
```

**The fix is not a one-line env change**, which is the part worth knowing up front:

```
docker-compose.yml:  "- NODE_ENV=development"           -> 26 occurrences  (hardcoded)
docker-compose.yml:  "- NODE_ENV=${NODE_ENV:-development}" ->  1 occurrence  (api-gateway, :319)
```

So setting `NODE_ENV=demo` in the VM's `.env` would move **exactly one service** and leave the other
26 on `development` — a change that would look applied and mostly not be.

## What is actually inert as a result — argued, and bounded

**Real:**

1. **Full API surface published unauthenticated at the internet edge.** `apiDocsGuard`
   (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:584`) is opt-in via `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS`; the VM's `.env:217` sets it
   `true`, and `docker-compose.yml:327` defaults it `false`, so the VM is overriding the default. Both
   spec routes serve real content (verified by content-type; an invented sibling path returns the
   Swagger HTML catch-all, which is the control that makes those 200s evidence). The guard's own
   comment calls this "a free attack-surface map for anyone (audit F-04)". **342 endpoints, every****
****parameter and every auth mechanism — no credentials in it.**
2. **5xx responses return the raw internal error message to the caller.**
   `api-gateway/src/index.ts:1031` masks to "An unexpected error occurred" only when
   `NODE_ENV === 'production'`; `:1038` adds `details.details = err.message` whenever it is not.
   Live example of the class from the local stack, same code path:
   `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml'` — an internal
   filesystem path in a client-visible body. (`err.stack` goes to the **logger** only, not the response.)
3. **Session/auth and CSRF cookies are not marked** `Secure` — `secure: NODE_ENV === 'production'` at
   `auth/src/routes/auth.ts:369,536,615` and `api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:60`, on an origin that
   is HTTPS-only via Caddy. ⚠ **Code-level only — deliberately NOT runtime-verified**, because
   confirming it means authenticating against the demo and minting a session.
4. **The** `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` **fail-fast cannot fire.** `auth/src/index.ts:225-227` exits 1 when the key
   is missing *in a prod-like env* — protecting PII **and** MFA TOTP secrets (KS-158). On the demo it
   degrades to a warning. **Latent, not live: the key IS set (measured present, 64 chars).** So this is
   a guard that cannot fire, not exposed PII.
5. **Password-reset and email-verification links are logged in full when SMTP send fails**
   (`auth/src/routes/auth.ts:230,686`, both gated `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`). Tokens reach the VM's
   container logs. Relevant next to KS-488 C-5, which turned the SMTP transport off by default.

**Checked and NOT true — recorded so nobody re-derives it:**

* **Mock endpoints are OFF.** `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` measured literal `false` on the gateway; the gate
  at `:752` needs `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS === 'true'`, so only one half is open.
* `CSRF_SECRET` **is set** on the gateway (36 chars), so the `:50`/`:276` production-only requirement
  not firing costs nothing today.
* **No PII is exposed** — see 4.
* Demo seeding being enabled is plausibly intentional for a demo, not counted as a defect here.

## Severity — argued as Medium, and explicitly not inflated

Every individual inert guard is either backed by a secret that is actually present (4), mitigated by
the HTTPS-only edge (3), or off on its second condition (mocks). Nothing here is exploitable for
credentials or PII as it stands. **What makes it worth fixing is that it is a class, not an item:** one
env value silently disables roughly six independent protections at once on the only internet-facing
Secuura deployment, and the artefacts disagree about whether that is intended.

**What would raise this to High:** `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` going missing (4 becomes live and silent), or
`ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` being flipped (2 of 2 conditions open). Both are one env edit away, and today
nothing would fail loudly to tell you.

## Tracked nowhere until now

Searched the board three ways before filing — `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS`, `public API docs`, `F-04`.
No result covers this. F-04 lives in **KS-491 (Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation)**, which
records the docs-exposure *finding* against the code but not the *live demo state*.

## Proposed disposition (needs Kam)

1. **Decide what the demo is** — prod-like (`demo`) or a dev sandbox that happens to face the internet.
   That single ruling resolves all six items.
2. If prod-like: the compose `NODE_ENV` hardcoding (26 sites) has to be parameterised first, or the
   change is cosmetic.
3. If it stays a sandbox: say so in the compose file and retire the "never in demo/prod" comment at
   `api-gateway/src/index.ts:578-582`, so the artefacts stop contradicting each other.

**No change has been made to the VM, its** `.env`**, or the repo.**

title: preflight.sh:722-724 derives the hook's controls from ${NAME:- only, so a control read as ${NAME}, ${NAME:?} or bare $NAME is not stripped — and broadening the pattern also catches the hook's own ZERO constant (KS-1643 nit 3)
description:
## BLUF

`preflight.sh:722-724` **derives the pre-push hook's control variables from one read shape,** `${NAME:-`**. A control read as** `${NAME}`**,** `${NAME:?}` **or bare** `$NAME` **is silently not stripped, so an in-hook suite would inherit it.** Zero such controls exist today, so nothing is missed now — this is the successor ticket the source comment and KS-1643 both say is needed, not a live defect.

**It cannot be closed by widening the pattern.** A pattern broad enough to catch the other read shapes also catches names the hook ASSIGNS itself, and stripping one of those would break the hook. Closing it needs a way to tell "read from the caller" from "assigned internally" — which is why KS-1643 recorded nit 3 and deliberately did not close it.

Nothing here is a fix. No shape is chosen and none is proposed.

Refs KS-1643 (the parent that recorded this as nit 3) and KS-1638 (the parent that asked for the stripping).

Every file:line below was read by me at develop `c3eb63c9d23b08132482f3211dbf8755312a7ca0`; every count is my own measurement in the same session, not carried from the brief that ordered this filing.

## 1 — what the derivation does today

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:722-724`, verbatim:

> `hook_controls=$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$hook_src" 2>/dev/null \` / `| grep -oE '\$\{[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*:-' \` / `| tr -d '${:-' | sort -u)`

`hook_src` is `../../.githooks/pre-push` (`:708`). Running that exact pipeline over the hook at this tip yields **one** name: `ALLOW_FORCE`, from the single live-code match at `.githooks/pre-push:77` (`${ALLOW_FORCE:-0}`). The hook is 400 lines, sha256 `74e8d270607c138b…`.

## 2 — the blind spot, and its size today

The source records it at `preflight.sh:715-721`. The operative sentences, verbatim:

> `KS-1643 nit 3, RECORDED AND NOT CLOSED:` `:-` `is the only read shape this derives. A` / `control read as` `${NAME}`, `${NAME:?}` `or bare` `$NAME` `is silently NOT stripped.`

and

> `Closing it needs a way to` / `tell "read from the caller" from "assigned internally", which is its own ticket.`

**Measured size of the gap today: zero.** Over the hook's live code (comments excluded, as `:722` does), braced ALL-CAPS reads of *any* form — `${NAME`, `${NAME:-`, `${NAME:?`, `${NAME}` — number **exactly one**, and it is the `${ALLOW_FORCE:` the derivation already finds. So no control is being missed at this tip.

Two near-misses that the ALL-CAPS pattern correctly does **not** match, recorded so a future reader does not mistake them for instances:

* `.githooks/pre-push:53` is `_remote="${1:-origin}"` — a `:-` read, but of a positional, not an `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` name.
* The hook's locals are underscore-prefixed lower-case (`$_jr_lsha`, `$_tip`, …). A `\$[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` pattern matches only their leading `$_`, 62 times, and yields no name. `preflight.sh:706-707` already notes this.

## 3 — why widening the pattern is not the fix: the `ZERO` counter-example

The hook assigns `ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` at `.githooks/pre-push:52` and reads it **bare**, at **four** lines:

| line | use |
| -- | -- |
| `:60` | `[ "$local_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue` — deleting a branch rewrites nothing |
| `:61` | `[ "$remote_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue` — brand-new branch at origin |
| `:113` | `[ "$_jr_lsha" = "$ZERO" ] && { _jr_skip=delete; return 0; }` — deleting a ref |
| `:122` | `[ "$_jr_rsha" != "$ZERO" ] && git cat-file -e …` — guards the remote-sha read |

Broadening the derivation to bare `$NAME` over live code yields exactly two names, measured: `ALLOW_FORCE` **and** `ZERO`. `ALLOW_FORCE` is a control read from the caller and must be stripped; `ZERO` is a constant the hook assigns itself and must not be. The pattern cannot tell them apart, which is precisely the discriminator the source comment says is needed.

**Mechanism of the breakage, reasoned from the source and NOT executed:** with `ZERO` stripped from the suites' environment, `"$ZERO"` expands empty inside the hook's own run. A real delete push presents `local_sha` as the all-zeros string, which does not equal the empty string, so the `:60` and `:113` guards would stop firing and a branch deletion would be judged a rewrite. Whether that is what the hook would actually do is not established here — see Not established.

A third group exists and is **not** in the blind spot, recorded so the discriminator is specified against the real set: `FORMAT_GATE_TREE` (`:363`, `:365`) and `FORMAT_GATE_BASE_MAY_BE_STALE` (`:365`) are ALL-CAPS names the hook assigns as a command prefix and never reads with `$`. A read-shape broadening does not catch them; a *name*-based one would.

## Not established

* Whether any control will ever be read in a shape other than `${NAME:-`. None exists today, so the gap is latent and its size is zero — this ticket records a known blind spot, not an observed miss.
* What discriminator separates "read from the caller" from "assigned internally". The source comment states only that one is needed. **No shape is proposed here.**
* That the `:-` derivation has no *other* blind spot. Only the read-shape axis was measured.
* That stripping `ZERO` would break the hook in the way §3 describes. That is reasoned from the four read sites, not reproduced — no mutant was run and no push was made.
* The `68/0` mutant figure and every suite ratio on KS-1643 are the author's and the gate's, quoted there, not re-run by me.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included, paginated)

Each line is a query I ran this session; counts are mine.

* `${NAME:?}` — 1 hit, KS-1643. `NAME:?` — 1 hit, KS-1643. `caller-read` — 1 hit, KS-1643.
* `hook_controls` — 1 hit, KS-1746. `hook controls` — 4 hits: KS-772, KS-1634, KS-1638, KS-1643. `read from the caller` — 2 hits: KS-772, KS-1643.
* `nit 3` — 4 hits: KS-544 (archived), KS-1385, KS-1643, KS-1746.
* `bare $NAME` — 0 hits. `assigns itself` — 0 hits.
* **Read whole before filing, and none is coverage** (a matcher for the blind-spot concepts — `${NAME}` / `${NAME:?}` / `bare $` / `read shape` / `assigned internally` / `read from the caller` / `caller-read` — scored **0** on all four, against **2** on KS-1643 as a firing control):
  * **KS-1634** (In Progress) — one occurrence of `hook controls`, inside a quoted log line. Its subject is a simulated anchor presented as anchored. A mention, not coverage.
  * **KS-772** (Todo) — one occurrence, also a quoted log line in a digest comment. A mention, not coverage.
  * **KS-1638** (In Review) — the parent that asked for the stripping. Its fix shape at its own §2 reads *"also strips* `ALLOW_FORCE` *— and arguably every variable the hook itself reads"*. That is the broader **aim**; the implementation narrowed it to the `:-` shape, and this ticket is that narrowing's residue. KS-1638 names no alternative read shape and proposes no discriminator. Not coverage.
  * **KS-1483** (Backlog) — zero occurrences of either term; its subject is the checked-out-branch guard. Not coverage.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 13 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 42 hits. **Zero control:** a fresh nonsense token → 0 hits. The token KS-1746 to KS-1751 used as their zero control is now **dead** — it returns 7 hits, because those six tickets and KS-1643 quote it; measured, not assumed.

*Filed by Seat G 23rd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief, as the successor KS-1643's comment of 2026-10-26T23:23Z says does not exist.*

title: run-shell-suites.sh signal trap: the guard's EMPTY-pgid branch has no cell (M3/M4 survive), plus the TERM-ignoring suite and two KS 1330 comment-precision gaps
description:
## BLUF

**Three LOW residues from the tier-2 gates on PR #1719 (KS-1331), filed so they are findable after the merge. Nothing here is a fix; the merged code is correct as reviewed.** The guard the round-1 gate asked for now exists and reds under its mutant; what is left is one untested *branch* of it, one declared behavioural limit, and two precision gaps in a comment.

Merged as `ec3313a80440d0eee9fd07204c024518417ff9d7`. Gate reports: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-26_gate-ru-batch/verdict.md` (round 1) and `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-26_gate-pr1719-round2/verdict.md` (round 2, GO WITH NOTES).

## (a) LOW — the empty-pgid branch of the guard has no cell

`run-shell-suites.sh`'s signal handler group-kills only when the suite's pgid is **known and differs** from the runner's own:

```
if [ -n "${rss_suite_pgid:-}" ] && [ -n "${rss_own_pgid:-}" ] \
   && [ "$rss_suite_pgid" != "$rss_own_pgid" ]; then
```

The `GUARD` cell added in round 1 reaches the **pgids-equal** case. It does **not** reach the case where `ps` fails and a pgid comes back **empty**, so both `-n` tests are load-bearing and uncovered: the gate's mutants **M3 and M4 survive 70/0**. M3's unguarded outcome is a group kill when the runner's *own* pgid is unreadable — the dangerous direction. M4's is `kill -TERM -` against no group, probably harmless but unmeasured.

**The gate's suggested approach** (not yet attempted): a PATH-shadowed `ps` stub that prints nothing, run against a **fixture copy** of the runner, asserting that a sentinel in the shared group survives (M3) and that no group kill is attempted (M4).

## (b) LOW — a suite that traps and ignores TERM survives the runner's trap

Declared by the builder in both rounds and unchanged: the trap sends TERM, so a suite that traps and ignores it keeps running after the runner has been told to stop. The runner still returns rc 143. This is the same exposure the previous pid-only kill had; the process-group change did not introduce it and does not remove it. Not tested.

## (c) LOW — two precision gaps in the rewritten KS 1330 item-3 comment

Both from the round-1 gate, which verified the comment against `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 arm64 and found it accurate on what it could measure. The gaps:

1. **"SIGINT is delivered" is true of delivery, not of the suite stopping.** A suite blocked in a **foreground external command** (e.g. `sleep 30`) did not die on an INT to its pid in **either** job-control mode in the gate's run. The comment's wording invites the stronger reading.
2. **"a suite's forked child inherits** `SIG_IGN` **for INT" is inferred, not read.** The gate measured the *effect* (an INT to the suite's group leaves the child alive, a TERM clears it) but could not read the disposition mask: macOS `ps` has no `ignored` keyword. So the mechanism is inferred and the effect measured, and the comment states the mechanism flatly.

## Board search before filing

Searched literally against identifier + title + description over **705 open issues** on this team (the `issues()` filter, not fuzzy search):

| token | open hits |
| -- | -- |
| `empty-pgid` | 0 |
| `rss_own_pgid` | 0 |
| `rss_suite_pgid` | 0 |
| `SIG_IGN` | 0 |
| `traps and ignores TERM` | 0 |
| `setpgrp` | 1 — KS 1583 |
| `process group` | 2 — KS 1583, KS 1331 |
| `run-shell-suites.sh` | 14 (positive control) |
| a fresh nonsense token | 0 (zero control) |

Both controls behaved, so the instrument discriminates in each direction.

**KS 1583 was read, not just counted: related class, NOT a duplicate.** Its Minor 2 is "the watchdog and the TERM path kill npm's pid, not its process group" — the same pid-versus-group family, but in `check-package-format.sh`'s watchdog and the npm install path, a different file and a different code path from this runner's trap. The shared trait is the family, which is why it is named here rather than closed as a duplicate.

title: KS-1232 gate follow-ups: share the allow-list predicate between the info reader and the create path (or pin drift), and decide whether arrays of non-strings are refused by both
description:
## BLUF

The Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1517 (ticket KS-1232) returned **GO**: 0 Major, 3 Minor notes (verdict sha256/16 `622027fcfb23dab5`). Two of them need a decision or a change and are the checklist below; Minor 3 is already ticketed (KS-1532 for the thrown settings read; the MCP relay wording is recorded on KS-1232).

## Recommendation

Do (a) first, since it removes a class; (b) is a contract question for Wednesday or Kam, to be answered for both read routes together.

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a) Stop duplicating the predicate, or pin drift (the gate's Minor 1).** The info reader's guard (`services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:77`) is character-identical to the create path's (`routes/verification.ts:1307`): `raw !== undefined && raw !== null && !Array.isArray(raw)`, with the same 403 text. It is **duplicated, not shared**. Drift today is guarded only by the 12-shape AGREEMENT cell in `ks1232-info-reader-refuses-a-non-array-allow-list.test.ts`; the gate's own 30-shape run (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-0`, array subclasses, a Proxy, an object with a `length`, `new String('')`, `Object.create(Array.prototype)`) found **0 disagreements**. Options: one helper imported by both routes (this edits the create path's allow-list guard, a security surface, so it needs its own gate), or a source-level cell asserting the two guards are the same executable code (a source-text check passes when the guard is commented out, so compare the code, not the text).
- [ ] **(b) Decide whether an array of non-strings is refused, by both read routes together (the gate's Minor 2; a contract question).** Neither route checks array ELEMENTS. The info reader echoes `[1,2]`, `[null]` and `[['a']]` raw (same as before this PR), and the create path accepts the same shape at its guard; reasoned from its code (`allowedTypes.includes(requestedType)`), not run, a non-empty array of non-strings then refuses every create with the "not permitted to register document type" text rather than the list text, so the two routes would answer differently for the same stored value. KS-1230 is where element types are validated on the **write** path; this item is whether the two **reads** should also refuse such an array, and with what text. Out of the ticket's "non-array" wording, so it was not changed in KS-1232.

## Detail

* **Source:** the PR #1517 gate verdict, Minors 1 and 2. The two reasoned claims in (b) are mine and are marked as such.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the change), KS-1230 (the write-side validation), KS-1204 (the create path's refusal), KS-1532 (the thrown read), KS-1531 (the undocumented route).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `array of non-strings` 0, `element types` 0, `shared predicate` 0, `share the predicate` 0, `non-string` 21 (scanned by title; none is about the allow-list's elements), `KS-1230` 4 (KS-1262, KS-1233, KS-1232, KS-1231; KS-1230 itself read). The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: Retire the Schemathesis unexpected-methods suppression released by Kam's KS-1358 ruling: three places still state the superseded KS-406 posture, plus a stale pin path
description:
## BLUF

**Kam ruled on 2026-10-27 that 405 +** `Allow` **before authentication stands and KS-406 is superseded. The Schemathesis harness still suppresses the probes that ruling released, and three places still carry KS-406's rationale as current.** KS-1358's own closing comment says this retirement "is follow-up work that nobody has picked up yet" — this ticket is that work, so it has an owner. Facts only; nothing changed.

Refs KS-1358, KS-406.

⚠ **This is not a question.** The brief that ordered this filing framed it as *"ask whether the suppression is still needed"*. It is not needed — that was decided. The three file:line facts below are what is left to act on.

## The ruling

From KS-1358's comment of 2026-10-26T21:15:26Z (comment id `82451a21-f7f0-4af3-b45c-21a5061392f8`), quoting the decision card `secuura-ks1358-405-before-auth-posture-1027`, verbatim:

> `Decision secuura-ks1358-405-before-auth-posture-1027: a — Keep 405 + Allow before auth: KS-406 superseded (recommended)`

and, from the same comment:

> **Not done here, and not in the KS-1531 change:** the harness still suppresses those probes (`unexpected-methods = []`, recorded as `DRIFT-METHOD-405`). Retiring the suppression and asserting 405 is follow-up work that nobody has picked up yet; no harness file was touched.

KS-1358 recorded the scale of what the suppression costs: across one full sweep's undeclared-method probes, **405 ×1,760**, 204 ×307 (OPTIONS), 404 ×29, 401 ×2 — and its option 1 states retiring the suppression "turns \~1,760 requests per sweep into real coverage."

## The three places, read at develop `c3eb63c9d23b08132482f3211dbf8755312a7ca0`

**1. The suppression itself.** `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml:126` — `unexpected-methods = []`, under `[phases.coverage]` at `:125`. The rationale above it, `:118-123`, states the superseded posture as current:

> `authenticated route by design (228 findings = 100% of the 2026-07-07 sweep's` / `failures), so we stop generating those probes rather than asserting a 405 the` / `platform deliberately does not send.`

"a 405 the platform deliberately does not send" is now false: the platform does send it.

**2. A test asserts the suppression holds.** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/functional/config/test_coverage_unexpected_methods.py` — the assert is at `:36` (`assert coverage.unexpected_methods == set()`), and its failure message at `:37-39` repeats the superseded rationale:

> `"schemathesis.toml must set [phases.coverage] unexpected-methods = [] — "` / `"auth-first 401 on undeclared methods is the intended posture (KS-406); "` / `"restoring the probes re-fails` `unsupported_method` `on every authenticated route."`

So retiring the suppression makes this test fail by design; it has to be retired or inverted in the same change. *(The brief cited* `:37` *for the assertion;* `:37` *is the first line of the message string,* `:36` *is the assert.)*

**3. The register prose.** `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:977-982` records the check as inert for the same superseded reason:

> `KS-406 (2026-07-08): effectively INERT on this platform — schemathesis.toml sets` / `[phases.coverage] unexpected-methods = [] because auth-first 401 on undeclared methods is` / `the intended posture (auth runs before routing), so no unexpected-method probes are` / `generated for this check to judge.`

"auth runs before routing" is the claim the ruling reverses.

**4. A stale path, found while reading the above.** `schemathesis.toml:121` says the suppression is *"Pinned by tests/unit/test_coverage_unexpected_methods.py"*. The file is at `tests/functional/config/test_coverage_unexpected_methods.py`. The pointer names a path that does not exist.

## Not established

* **Whether 405 is what the probes would now meet on every undeclared method.** KS-1358's measurement was one sweep on slot 3 at develop `d9ce1403d` on 2026-09-28 — 405 ×1,760 but also 204 ×307, 404 ×29 and **401 ×2**. The 401 ×2 is unexplained in that record. Restoring the probes without accounting for the non-405 tail would trade a suppression for a baseline.
* **No sweep was run for this ticket.** Every figure above is KS-1358's.
* Whether `expected-statuses` or the `unsupported_method` check configuration needs a matching change. Not examined.
* Whether `DRIFT-METHOD-405` in `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` is the only other record of the suppression. Only the four places above were read.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `unexpected-methods` — **6 hits**: KS-1502 (Canceled, a version bump), **KS-1358** (Done — the ruling), KS-1270, KS-1268, KS-416, **KS-406** (all Done/archived).
* `DRIFT-METHOD-405` — **1 hit**, KS-1358 only.
* `retire the suppression` — **0 hits**. `unexpected_method` — **1 hit**, KS-1268 (archived, a pin bump).
* `test_coverage_unexpected_methods` — **1 hit**, KS-1268 (archived). `schemathesis.toml` — 50 hits, scanned; the posture family is the six above.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.
* **Decision recorded.** KS-1358 was read in full, state and comments. It is **Done** and its question is answered, so the ruling needs no further comment there; what it names as unowned is filed here instead. **KS-406** is Done and archived and was already commented as superseded per KS-1358's record.

*Filed by Seat G 22nd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief and addendum.*

title: api-gateway: specRouteMap.ts:47 arms the edge auth gate only for bearerAuth, so GET /api/connector/info (connectorApiKey only) is absent from authedMethods
description:
## BLUF

`specRouteMap.ts:47` **arms the gateway's edge auth gate only for** `bearerAuth`**, so an operation secured by any other scheme is not armed there.** As of 27 Oct this is no longer hypothetical: `GET /api/connector/info` **is the first published operation secured by** `connectorApiKey` **alone**, and it is therefore absent from `authedMethods`. Facts only — whether this is a defect is for the board. Raised by the tier-1 gate on #1732 as the U2 item.

Refs KS-1531, KS-944.

## The code, read at develop `c3eb63c9d23b08132482f3211dbf8755312a7ca0`

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/specRouteMap.ts:47`, verbatim:

```
      if (Array.isArray(security) && security.some((s) => s && typeof s === 'object' && 'bearerAuth' in s)) {
```

`'bearerAuth'` is the only scheme name in the file that affects behaviour — three occurrences in all: `:27` (the field comment on `authedMethods`), `:45` (the comment above the test) and `:47` (the test itself). `authedMethods.add(upper)` at `:48` is reached only through it.

The consumer is `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts`: `resolveSpecRoute` at `:1064`, and the auth branch at `:1084` `if (authedMethods.has(upperMethod)) {`. `buildSpecMethodMap` is called at `:612` and again at `:654` (the spec-reload path).

## What the published spec now declares — measured

In `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, `securitySchemes` is at `:83` and declares exactly **two** schemes: `bearerAuth` (`:84`) and `connectorApiKey` (`:89`).

Per-operation usage across the whole file: **311** `- bearerAuth` lines, **2** `- connectorApiKey` lines. The two `connectorApiKey` uses resolve as:

| operation | security block | schemes | armed at the edge gate? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/connector/info` (path `:15961`, method `:15962`) | `:15971-15972` | `connectorApiKey` **only** | **no** |
| `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` (path `:36426`, method `:36427`) | `:36440-36442` | `bearerAuth` **and** `connectorApiKey` | yes — on the `bearerAuth` entry |

So of the two operations using the scheme, **one is secured by it alone**, and that one is not armed. The source of that declaration is `services/api-gateway/src/api-gateway.openapi.ts:908` — `security: [{ connectorApiKey: [] }]`.

## Why this is not currently an exposure, and why that is not reassuring

The tier-1 gate on #1732 mutated the yaml declaration to `bearerAuth` and recorded the 28-cell behaviour matrix as **byte-identical** — the GET is answered before the edge gate is reached, so arming it changes nothing for this route today. **That ordering is the gate's measurement and I did not reproduce it:** the verdict cites `index.ts:837` for the health router and `:1054` for the edge gate, neither of which matches this tree (see above), and the symbol `createHealthRouter` does not occur in `index.ts`. Treat the ordering as the gate's claim, not as established here.

What stands without that claim is the structural fact: the edge gate's notion of "this operation requires authentication" is **narrower than the spec's**, and it is narrow in a way no reader of the spec would expect. An operation that is authenticated by declaration is unauthenticated by the gate.

## Prior art, read and not a duplicate

**KS-944** (Done, archived) — *"The gateway's auth gate reads the spec's* `security: []` *— nothing pins the four public wallet ops"* — is the same mechanism and the same line.
