title: The pre-push hook's ALLOW_FORCE=1 path can never pass the preflight: the flag leaks into leg 14 and reds ks998 SC12
description:
**The pre-push hook's documented deliberate-force path,** `ALLOW_FORCE=1 git push …`**, can never pass the preflight: the flag leaks into leg 14, where the cell that tests its ABSENCE inherits it and goes red.**

Found 2026-10-19 by Seat R 50th, carrying out a Kam-authorised force-push (card `secuura-datasec-author-on-two-branch-commits-1019` = b: an author-only amend of #1597's one commit, tree byte-identical). The push was refused, nothing landed, and #1597 is unchanged.

## What happens

1. `.githooks/pre-push:59-82` refuses every non-fast-forward unless `ALLOW_FORCE=1`. Its own message offers that as the "deliberate case, stated explicitly", and its comment (`:46`) says it exists so a deliberate force "cannot happen by reflex".
2. With `ALLOW_FORCE=1`, the force check passes (`:78`: "proceeding with a non-fast-forward push, deliberately") — and then the **preflight still runs**, which is correct.
3. Preflight **leg 14** runs every shell suite **in-hook**. `ALLOW_FORCE` is in the hook's environment, so every suite inherits it.
4. `scripts/__tests__/ks998_pre_push_judges_the_push.test.sh` cell **SC12** ("without ALLOW_FORCE the rewrite is refused (the standing rule)", `:254`) runs a fixture push **without setting or unsetting** `ALLOW_FORCE`, expecting a refusal. It inherits `ALLOW_FORCE=1`, the fixture rewrite goes through, and the cell fails.
5. Leg 14: `90 passed, 1 failed (of 91)` → `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14` → push refused.

So **every** `ALLOW_FORCE=1` push is refused by the preflight. The deliberate path the hook advertises is unreachable.

## Measured, not inferred

The suite was run standalone (its fixtures live in `mktemp -d`; the shared `.git` was checked untouched after each run):

| environment | ks998 | SC12 "without ALLOW_FORCE" |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_FORCE` **unset** | **80 / 80** | ok |
| `ALLOW_FORCE=1` **exported** | **79 / 80** | **FAIL** — the in-hook failure, reproduced |

The pushed tree was byte-identical to one that had already passed the full preflight (13/16, nothing failed) on its first push, so the tree cannot be the cause.

## Fix shape — either part closes the immediate case

1. **Local:** SC12's "without" push becomes `env -u ALLOW_FORCE git push …`, so the cell is hermetic whatever its caller exports. The cell then tests what its name says.
2. **Structural:** the preflight's hermetic environment for leg 14 (`env_clear` at `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh`, which strips 46 slot variables) also strips `ALLOW_FORCE` — and arguably every variable the hook itself reads — so no in-hook suite inherits the pushing shell's hook controls. This is the same family as the leg-14 `GIT_*` inheritance recorded under KS-806 / the s176 incident.

Both, ideally: (1) makes the cell honest, (2) closes the class.

## Not a workaround

`--no-verify` would skip the whole preflight, not just this cell, and is forbidden to seats. Renaming or scoping the variable from outside cannot help, because the force check and leg 14 run in the same hook process.

## Consequence today

Kam's authorised force-push of #1597 is **blocked** until this is fixed or Kam rules otherwise. Related: KS-1037 (Done — where the no-force rule lives), KS-1634 (#1597).

title: KS-989 gate residue: the formatting gate fails OPEN on missing deps and reads the WORKING TREE, not the push — four items on one path
description:
## BLUF

**[#906](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/906>) shipped the KS-989 formatting gate and it works — but the QA gate found four ways it does not catch what it appears to. Two are MAJOR. One of them is the path by which instance 6 itself could still have slipped through.**

Filed as **one ticket with four items** rather than four tickets: all four are the same question — *what the new gate does and does not catch* (Kam, 2026-09-06: one larger ticket per logical path).

Parent work: [KS-989](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-989). Merged as `e69fa0dc5`.

## Items

### 1. MAJOR — the gate fails OPEN when a gated package's deps are absent

`check-package-format.sh` prints `SKIP (advisory)` and **exits 0** when `node_modules/.bin/prettier` is missing, so on a fresh clone the red is pushed and nothing says so.

**This was a stated gap in the PR body and the gate then measured it — against the real akto tree, on the real instance-6 red, with controls both sides.** That matters for how it is read: *"I said so in the PR"* is not a defence. **This is the path by which instance 6 itself could still have reached** `develop`**.**

The tension is real and should be settled deliberately rather than by whoever edits the file next: hard-failing presents an environment condition as a gate failure, which is precisely [KS-991](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-991)'s cost (`DEPS MISSING` read as a real red, five times in one day). Options worth costing: install-on-first-run (what `preflight.sh` does for its own members), a hard fail when a **tracked** file in that package is in the push, or leaving the skip and accepting it in writing.

### 2. MAJOR — the gate reads the WORKING TREE, not the commits being pushed

`npm run format:check` runs against the checkout, so a push whose commits carry a red passes if the fix is sitting uncommitted in the tree. **Proven on a bare-remote fixture: red at HEAD, fix uncommitted, red lands at origin.**

**Note in any fix that the gate's own printed remedy is what creates the divergence** — `fix: (cd systemTest/<pkg> && npm run format)` tells the author to modify the working tree, and if they push without committing that, the gate now passes on a tree that is not what they are sending.

### 3. MINOR — the fail-closed branch has no cell

The `gate script missing → REFUSED` branch in `.githooks/pre-push` is correct and is **the one branch whose entire purpose is to fail closed** — and nothing tests it. A branch like that going quietly wrong is indistinguishable from a gate that passed.

### 4. POLISH — `grep -qx` treats the path as a regex

`grep -qx "$full"` in the "is this red file in the push?" comparison interprets the path as a pattern. `-qxF` fixes it. Affects the `(in this push)` / `(NOT in this push — inherited red)` **label only**, never the pass/fail verdict.

### Robustness note — no finding attached

`< /dev/null` on the `npm run --silent format:check` invocation (line 150) would close the stdin-inheritance hazard that the fixtures cannot detect. Cheap; do it with whichever item lands first.

## Provenance

Findings from the tier-2 (through-code) QA pass on #906, 2026-09-08, relayed in Wednesday's GO mail of `04:02:45Z` — **DKIM-verified as her relay** (3 pass values present, all 8 failing-value controls absent, both header checks). The measurements are the gate's; the merge went ahead on her GO because F1 and F2 are neither regressions nor blockers on a change that fixed a red then live on the trunk.

title: Security: 9 trust-header reads outside auth middleware (pen-test F-04) — surfaced by wiring check-no-trust-header-reads.sh in KS-926
description:
**Found by RUNNING a guard that had never run.** KS-926 wired the `check-*.sh` guards; this one had no live entry point, so its findings had never been seen. Its default level is `fail`, so it is red the moment anything invokes it.

## The 9, verbatim from the guard

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1041  req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1042  req.headers['x-tenant-slug']
services/security/src/index.ts:968                    req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/prism/src/index.ts:111                       req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/index.ts:230                   req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42          req.headers['x-user-role'] === 'connector' && x-tenant-id
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:43          req.headers['x-user-id']  -> sets (req as any).user
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:45          req.headers['x-tenant-id'] -> sets (req as any).tenantId
packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:119              req.headers['x-tenant-id']
```

`metering.ts:42-45` **is the one to look at first:** it builds `req.user` and `req.tenantId` **from headers**, gated only on `x-user-role === 'connector'`. That is the trust-header vulnerability in its literal form if the header is reachable from outside.

## The guard's own instruction

> Use `req.user.*` (set by `authenticate()` middleware) instead of `req.headers['x-user-*']`. Direct header reads re-introduce the trust-header vulnerability.

The guard already excludes legitimate middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `scopes.ts`, `tenant*`, `db/tenant-context.ts`, `security/gdpr-compliance.ts`) and lines marked `F-04-allowed`, so **these 9 are outside the sanctioned set by the guard's own definition.**

## Triage needed per site

Some may be legitimate **forwarding** (api-gateway 1041-42 sets `forwardHeaders`, which is a different act from trusting) and should carry `F-04-allowed` with a reason. Others look like real trust. **Do not bulk-annotate** — that converts a finding into a silence.

## Blocks

`check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` cannot be wired into the pre-push gate until this is 0 or the legitimate sites are annotated. Related: KS-619 (gateway tenant resolution falling through to the caller's `x-tenant-id`), and KS-926.

title: Security: two cross-tenant isolation regressions fail on develop — a super-admin's X-Tenant-Override does not scope a document read or the api-key list (BUG-ISOLATION-001 / KS-4 and KS-513 are Done)
description:
**BLUF:** Two systemTest regression guards for tenant isolation fail on `develop` today, measured twice on 2026-10-20 against the same stack. The tickets they guard, [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug) (BUG-ISOLATION-001) and [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions), are both Done, so the regressions currently have no owner. This ticket gives them one. Kamil, I'd be grateful if you could look at the mechanism. My best reading is below, clearly labelled as a hypothesis.

## What fails (measured)

**1.** `tests/test_tenant_isolation.py::test_cross_tenant_isolation` **(BUG-ISOLATION-001 /** [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug)**)**
An ISSUER_ADMIN creates a document. A SYSTEM_ADMIN reads it in its own tenant context (200, the control). The same SYSTEM_ADMIN then reads it with `X-Tenant-Override: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000deadbeef`, a tenant that owns nothing. **Expected:** not 200 (the tenant predicate hides it). **Got:** 200 with the document body.

> `AssertionError: BUG-ISOLATION-001 regression: document doc-1792496776162-f65739ee was readable from a foreign tenant context (00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000deadbeef). The tenant predicate is not being applied.`

**2.** `tests/test_tenant_isolation_writes.py::test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation` **(**[KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions)**)**
A SYSTEM_ADMIN creates an API key under the Oxford override, then lists keys under the BUPA override. **Expected:** the Oxford key is not listed. **Got:** it is listed.

> `AssertionError: KS-513 cross-tenant api-key disclosure: key key_3d152a73-… created under Oxford is visible when listed under the BUPA tenant override.`

## Evidence that it is develop, not the change under test

* **Control run:** both tests run from `develop`'s own harness (a detached worktree at `develop` `32964477f`), on platform-k slot 2 built at that platform code. Both FAILED as above.
* **Branch run:** the same two tests from the [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) branch (systemTest-only changes) on the same stack, back to back. Both FAILED identically. They also failed in that branch's full run (`full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2`): live integration 426 passed / 2 failed.
* **Not the** [KS-1054](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1054/fresh-databases-are-fail-open-until-the-second-boot-039-rls-fail) **fresh-database window:** the migration runner shows `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` and its [KS-1054](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1054/fresh-databases-are-fail-open-until-the-second-boot-039-rls-fail) fix `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` already applied by the database's first boot. I could not read `pg_policy` directly (it needs the database password, which I do not handle).

## Where I'd look first (hypothesis, NOT verified)

One mechanism fits both failures: **the gateway-verified** `X-Tenant-Override` **does not reach originate as the request's tenant**, so both calls fall back to the default tenant.

* The api-key list filters `WHERE tenant_id = ${req.tenantId || 'a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'}` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:893-900`). If the override is not applied, a key created "under Oxford" and a list "under BUPA" both land in the default tenant, which is exactly what the test sees.
* The document read: `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1924-1930` states the platform-admin RLS bypass is unreachable from that route, so with the override applied the foreign tenant GUC should hide the document. A 200 means the GUC was the document's own tenant (or none was applied).
* Possibly the same class as [KS-1084](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1084/read-only-unverified-the-gateways-own-authorization-only-calls-to) (gateway calls to originate send no `x-tenant-id`, so single-tenant originate may scope to the default tenant; In Progress) or [KS-619](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-619/gateway-tenant-resolution-falls-through-to-the-callers-x-tenant-id) (gateway tenant resolution falls through to the caller's `x-tenant-id`; Backlog). I have not confirmed either; please treat this as a pointer, not a diagnosis.

## How to reproduce

From `systemTest/schemathesis` on a slot with the actors provisioned:

`systemTest/run-in-slot.sh <N> ./venv/bin/python3 -m pytest "tests/test_tenant_isolation.py::test_cross_tenant_isolation" "tests/test_tenant_isolation_writes.py::test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation" -v --no-cov`

Stack used: platform-k slot 2, 33/33 containers healthy, 48 migrations applied and 0 failed; Python 3.14.8, Schemathesis 4.32.1. The tests use the seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN (super-admin) and ISSUER_ADMIN personas, and the Oxford and BUPA seed tenants.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **The two existing integration tests above pass** on a freshly built slot and on a second boot of the same database. They are the automated tests that demonstrate the fix (no UI surface, so no Playwright test applies).
2. The root cause is written down in the fix's PR: why the override did not scope these two requests, and whether other routes that read `req.tenantId` are affected.
3. If [KS-1084](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1084/read-only-unverified-the-gateways-own-authorization-only-calls-to) or [KS-619](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-619/gateway-tenant-resolution-falls-through-to-the-callers-x-tenant-id) turns out to be the cause, this ticket is linked to it as a duplicate or blocked-by, rather than closed silently.
4. The test docstrings that cite [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug) and [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) are updated to cite this ticket while it is open, so a failing run names a live owner (systemTest; Peter will do that part once this ticket exists).

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given. Found while classifying the full-run failures for [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (step 11b).

title: vc-issuer GET /api/credentials pages on ORDER BY created_at DESC alone - rows sharing (or lacking) a created_at repeat or are skipped across pages (gate: 24 of 180 page walks; an id tie-breaker takes it to 0)
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/credentials` **pages on** `ORDER BY created_at DESC` **alone.** Rows that share a `created_at`, or have none, can be **repeated or skipped** between pages. The tier-1 gate on PR #1691 measured this, rated it **Minor** and found no leak. Only the caller's **own** rows are affected: no foreign row was ever served, and `total` stayed correct. Adding the row id as a tie-breaker took it to 0. **The sort predates PR #1691** — #1691 kept it, and did not introduce it.

## Where (develop `c2505d5c6fe0`)

* `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts:365` — `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $n OFFSET $m` in `selectList()`. Both `listReadable()` (what `GET /api/credentials` calls since #1691) and the unbound `list()` use it.
* For contrast, the by-hash read at `:286` already orders `created_at DESC, id DESC`.

## When it came in

`git log -S 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT' -- services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts` gives one commit: `e50dbde98` (2026-02-18, "Identity verification & SSI integration…"). It is already present on develop `1ae6f17d19a8` at `:227`, before #1691.

## What was measured (by the gate, relayed; not re-measured by the filer)

On PGlite (PostgreSQL 17.5): **24 of 180 page walks** repeated or skipped rows that shared a timestamp or had none. Adding `id` as a tie-breaker took it to **0**. All affected rows were the caller's own. The verdict is on the coordinator's side at `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-26_gate-pr1691-ks1683/verdict.md`.

## Facts that bound it

* `created_at` is `TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()`, nullable (`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:748`, no `NOT NULL`).
* vc-issuer's own `store()` INSERT (`credentialRepo.ts:84`) does not name `created_at`, so rows it writes get `NOW()`. **A NULL** `created_at` **can only come from another writer.** A shared timestamp is reachable for rows written in the same transaction.
* The in-memory fallback pages a `Map` in insertion order. That order is deterministic, so this ticket is about the DB path.
* Two other `ORDER BY created_at DESC` reads in vc-issuer are boot loads, not paged: `credentialRepo.ts:423` (`loadFromDb`) and `routes/presentations.ts:173`. They are outside this defect.
* `vc_credentials_store` held 0 rows on demo and 0 on kintsugi on 2026-10-20 (from KS-1683's body).

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

`ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC`, matching by-hash at `:286`. `id` is the primary key, so that is a total order. Whether NULLs should sort last (`NULLS LAST`; PostgreSQL puts NULLs first under `DESC`) is a choice for whoever fixes it.

## Related, NOT duplicates

* **KS-1544** — `platform_audit_log` paged without a tie-break (`ORDER BY created_at DESC` only). Same class, different table and service.
* **KS-1683** / PR #1691 — the change whose gate found this.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **701 open** Secuura-PK issues:

* `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT` → 2: **KS-1544** (above) and KS-1696 (GDPR deletion log — unrelated).
* `created_at DESC, id` → KS-1544.
* `tie-breaker` / `tiebreaker` / `tie breaker` / `unstable sort` / `stable sort` / `listReadable` → 0.
* `credentialRepo.list` → KS-1683 only.

Controls showing the instrument finds a known ticket: `Hook timed out in 10000ms` → KS-1729 and KS-1602; `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828` → KS-1723.

## Found by

The tier-1 gate on PR #1691 (round 1, Minor). Filed by Seat K on the coordinator's ruling, facts only. Not fixed in #1691.

## Implementation principle — use Playwright's own primitives

**Never implement something ourselves if Playwright already provides it.** Anything the framework ships — polling, stepping, retries, parallelism, artifact attachment, context isolation — is used as-is. Our code exists only to express *Secuura's* domain (personas, flows, coverage classes) or to fill a capability the framework genuinely does not have. A hand-rolled equivalent of a framework feature is a review rejection.

| Need | Mechanism | Ours or Playwright's? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Wait for an async outcome | `expect.poll` (`{ timeout, intervals, message }`) | **Playwright's.** `helpers/settle.ts` is a thin wrapper supplying the project deadlines **\[ref 8\]** |
| Ordered, named stages in a flow | `test.step()` | **Playwright's** |
| Per-persona session isolation | `playwright.request.newContext()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 2\]** |
| Persist an artifact + surface it in the report | `testInfo.outputPath()` + `testInfo.attach({ path })` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 6\]** |
| Parallelism, retries, sharding, reporters, tagging | runner config | **Playwright's** |
| Setup/teardown lifecycle | fixtures with `use()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 7\]** |
| **Capturing API exchanges as a durable artefact** | `helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` | **Ours — the framework has no equivalent** (upstream request closed unimplemented, **\[ref 5\]**). Built *on* `testInfo.attach`/`outputPath` |
| CSRF double-submit echo | `helpers/csrf.ts` | **Ours** — application-protocol concern |
| Coverage classification vs the OpenAPI spec | `coverage/*` | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |
| Persona catalogue, flow definitions | `config/`, `helpers/flow.ts`, specs | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |

## Stack isolation — Playwright runs on its own Docker instance

* ~~**CI**~~ *(moot — GitHub Actions retired 2026-08-27, see R4/R5)* — the `playwright` job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` boots via `boot-platform-stack` with `stack_prefix: pr-playwright`, gateway **6982**, postgres 6532, redis 6479, pgbouncer 6533; pointed at by `API_BASE_URL: http://localhost:6982/api`. Distinct `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` / `STACK_PREFIX` → separate containers, volumes, networks. Siblings sit on 6882 / 7082 / 7182.
* **Local** — the suite does not start or stop a server (`playwright.config.ts`); it attaches to whatever `API_BASE_URL` points at. Use its own instance for destructive flows (F14 erasure, F5 revoke).

Any environment posture we choose applies to Playwright alone. The only shared thing is the composite action's *source file*.

## Scope boundary

Playwright asserts **business outcomes of documented flows**. It does not re-test what the sibling suites own — see `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` §2–3 and the Coverage & Scenario Matrix in `QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

| Excluded from Playwright | Owner |
| -- | -- |
| Boundary values, negative **data**, fuzzing | Schemathesis |
| Status/header compliance, undeclared verbs, redirects, rate-limit headers, 429 | Schemathesis |
| RBAC matrices, cross-tenant, IDOR/BOLA | Schemathesis (+ Akto) |
| Unauthenticated 401/403 sweeps | Schemathesis + the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight |
| OWASP API Top 10, injection, SSRF, BFLA | Akto |
| Throughput, latency, saturation | Performance (k6) |
| Real Cardano chain integrity / anchor-vs-chain | anchoring Integration suite ([KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489/review-d-blockchain-anchoring-smart-contract-integrity)-D) — see Risk 3 |

**A distinction that matters, because it looks like the excluded category but is not:** a *documented business outcome that is not success* — a verification returning **Expired**, a tampered document returning **Failed**, a certifier **Rejecting** a request — is in scope. Those are product states the stakeholder guides describe, reached with valid inputs. What is excluded is malformed **data** (missing fields, oversize values, type confusion). F6 and F7 exist precisely to cover the former.

Consistent with Playwright's Best Practices — *"Only test what you control."* — which is why provider-gated paths (Stripe, M365) record a by-design 503 rather than reaching for the third party. **\[ref 1\]**

**Two existing specs are duplicates and are retired in Phase 0**: `notifications.spec.ts` (both tests assert unauth → 401/403, already swept for every bearer op by the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight) and the invalid-credentials / missing-email cases in `login.spec.ts` (negative data, owned by Schemathesis `test_authentication.py`).

## ⚠ Two platform capabilities we do not have — needed by F6 and F13

Two flows assert a documented product state that **cannot currently be reached on demand**. Neither blocks Phase 0, but both block their own flow's plan from being finalised. Raised with @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson in the comments — **and probed ourselves first** (see Risk mitigation), because the capability may already exist.

| Need | Flow | Why it is needed | What "available" looks like |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Induce an expired certification** | **F6** | The Verifier guide documents **Expired** as one of five verification result states. Verifying it requires a certification that is *already* past its expiry. If expiry is purely wall-clock with no way to set a past date, F6's expired leg is unreachable and the state stays permanently untested | Either an issuance parameter accepting a past `expiresAt` (non-prod only), or a supported way to age an existing certification. A test must be able to produce one deterministically, in-run, without clock manipulation on the host |
| **Raise a system error on demand** | **F13** | F13's only real journey is *error → resolve*. Asserting it requires a system error to exist first. Provoking one by genuinely breaking a service is not acceptable in a shared or CI stack | A non-prod-only way to emit a synthetic entry into the system-errors surface with a known signature, so the test can find it, resolve it, and assert it reflects as resolved |

**If either already exists**, this is a documentation gap rather than a build ask. **If neither is feasible**, the affected leg is recorded as a documented coverage gap rather than quietly dropped: F6 keeps its tampered + not-found legs, F13 falls back to `positive-path` for the whole read surface.

### Acceptance criterion per flow

Each flow is accepted on **one stated business outcome**, not a set of status codes. These are what the child plans must satisfy.

* **F1** — a token issued at login authenticates `GET /users/me` as the expected persona for all five accounts; a refreshed token works, and the pre-logout token stops working.
* **F2** — a document type created by admin is returned by the subsequent list, and each of the three new personas can log in at its intended role.
* **F3** — a document created by `issuer@secuura.com` is retrievable by id and its certification appears in the certification list. **The anchor leg is blocked on D1.**
* **F4** — verifying the spine document's content hash returns `verified: true` and identifies the issuing party.
* **F5** — after revoke, the same verify call that previously returned verified now reports **revoked**, and the status list reflects it.
* **F6** — a **tampered** payload verifies as failed, and an unknown hash returns `verified: false` without an error. The **expired** leg — an expired certification verifying as expired, not as valid or missing — requires the capability gap above to be closed; until then it is a documented gap, not a silent omission.
* **F7** — a rejected certification request ends in a rejected state, the requester can see the rejection, and the document is **not** certified.
* **F8** — a document certified with `x-api-key` (no bearer, no cookies) is retrievable and verifies identically to one certified by a browser persona. Proves the partner path end-to-end.
* **F9** — custody transfers from `demo@secuura.io` to `holder@secuura.com`: the recipient is notified (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**), and the prior owner can no longer mutate the document.
* **F10** — a registered webhook's test delivery appears in its delivery list (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**); rotating the secret changes the signing secret without dropping the registration.
* **F11** — a credential issued for a document verifies as a presentation and its DID resolves — **or** the by-design 503 on `POST /api/credentials` is the recorded outcome.
* **F12** — an async export reaches a downloadable state within `EXPORT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT` and the downloaded artefact contains the requesting tenant's data.
* **F13** — the audit trail contains the lifecycle events of a document **this flow created itself**. The *error → resolve* journey requires the capability gap above; until then the whole read surface is asserted as `positive-path` and **declared as such**.
* **F14** — the subject's export contains their record; after erasure the same export no longer returns personal data and the deletion log records the event.
* **F15** — a KYC session initiated at verification level `NONE` reaches a terminal reviewed state and the subject's verification level changes.
* **F16** — a wallet challenge is issued and the account reflects the linked wallet address. **Stops short of asserting signature validity** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature and is an open Known Failure ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C).
* **F17** — an authorised app receives a token that can call an in-scope operation, and revoking the grant stops it working.
* **F18** — a connector reaches a connected state and a sync lists at least one document — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F19** — a customer's purchase appears in their purchase list and their credit balance reflects it — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F20** — a proposal created by `demo@secuura.io` receives a vote from `holder@secuura.com` and reaches a terminal state — **or** the documented precondition refusal ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) is recorded.
