## Driving the flows — per-flow contexts and in-test persona switching

Each flow runs with its own isolated client session, and a single test can act as several personas in sequence so cross-persona interaction is directly observable.

Both are straightforward **because the suite has no browser**. The API analogue of a private window is `playwright.request.newContext()`, and the docs confirm the isolation property: *"If you don't want APIRequestContext to use and update cookies from the browser context, you can manually create a new instance of APIRequestContext which will have its own isolated cookies."* **\[ref 2\]**

| Isolated per flow / persona | Shared across all flows |
| -- | -- |
| Cookie jar, `XSRF-TOKEN`, storage state, `Authorization` bearer | Documents, users, anchors, webhooks — the platform's own state |

**Not hypothetical — the suite already has the bug isolation prevents.** `notifications.spec.ts` documents unauthenticated POSTs returning 403 instead of 401 because a server-set `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie rode along on the *shared* unauth context, making the outcome order-dependent.

### Switching persona inside one test

Every client takes `(api, token)` in its constructor, so the same class bound to different contexts yields `documentsAsDemo`, `documentsAsHolder`, `documentsAsVerifier`. F9's criterion is then close to verbatim:

```ts
test('custody transfers from demo to holder', async ({
    documentsAsDemo, documentsAsHolder, notificationsAsHolder,
}) => {
    const { body: doc } = await documentsAsDemo.create(buildDocumentPayload('f9'));
    await documentsAsDemo.transferCustody(doc.id, holderUserId);

    const received = await documentsAsHolder.get(doc.id);   // recipient can now read
    expect(received.status).toBe(200);

    const stale = await documentsAsDemo.revoke(doc.id);      // prior owner cannot mutate
    expect(stale.status).toBe(403);
});
```

**Calls are always asynchronous** — Playwright has no sync API. Stages within a flow are strictly sequential (each depends on prior state); independent reads may be batched with `Promise.all`, bounded by the \~2000/60s platform limit. Because batched calls complete out of order, **the exchange recorder stamps its sequence at request start** and carries a duration.

### The F3 → F4 → F5 spine is ONE test with steps — not `describe.serial`

F4 verifies *F3's* document and F5 revokes *that same* document, so the chain needs shared state. A `test.describe.serial` block is the wrong instrument **\[ref 3\]**:

* *"If one of the serial tests fails, all subsequent tests are skipped."* — downstream stages would report as **skips**, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` is explicit that a skip is neither red nor green and proves nothing.
* *"All tests in a group are retried together."* — serial buys no retry granularity over a single test.
* *"Using serial is not recommended."* — and Best Practices: *"Each test should be completely isolated from another test…"* **\[ref 1\]**

**Resolution:** `tests/spine/document-lifecycle.spec.ts` holds the chain as **one test** whose stages are `test.step()` calls sharing one document. Tagged `@smoke`. `describe.serial` is not used anywhere.

### Evidence capture — we must build our own

**Both** `video` **and** `trace` **are inert for this suite.**

* **Video** records a browser-context viewport; there is no page here. `playwright.config.ts:54-59` already says so and the docs confirm: *"Videos are saved upon browser context closure."* **\[ref 4\]**
* **Trace** is a `browserContext.tracing` facility and does not capture a standalone `APIRequestContext` created via `playwright.request.newContext()`. **\[ref 5\]**

**The upstream request was closed unimplemented — settled, not pending.** microsoft/playwright#18891 was closed by a maintainer on 30 Jun 2023: *"This issue was closed due to limited engagement (upvotes/activity), lack of recent activity, and insufficient actionability."* GitHub renders the state as "closed as completed", which is misleading — the comment is explicit that it was a housekeeping closure, **not** a shipped feature.

Per the **Implementation principle**, we build our substitute *on* Playwright's own primitives **\[ref 6\]**: `testInfo.attach(name, { path, contentType })` and `testInfo.outputPath()`.

### The exchange recorder — design and tidy-up

Today `helpers/api-report.ts` → `recordApiExchange` attaches **three entries per call**. A 40-call flow produces 120 attachments and none of it is machine-readable as a whole. Split into two modules:

`helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` **— collect + persist (new)**

* Ordered typed record per call: sequence **stamped at request start**, acting persona, enclosing `test.step()` name, method, URL, headers, bodies, status, duration, repro curl. Reuses `format.ts`'s `RequestParts` / `ResponseParts`.
* At test end (fixture teardown) writes **one** file — `testInfo.outputPath('api-exchanges.json')` — attached once with `contentType: 'application/json'`.

`helpers/api-report.ts` **— render (existing, slimmed)**

* One human-readable markdown attachment per call; cookies and curl fold into the JSON record.
* ~~Redaction unchanged: masked when ~~`~~getRedactSecrets()~~`~~ is on (default in CI, off locally).~~ *Superseded (R12):* GDPR personal data, access tokens and secret/API keys are masked in every run.

**Hard review rule, now enforced by lint (see Risk mitigation):** all transport goes through `performApiCall`.

### Constraints

* **Switching identity never means logging in again** — contexts are built from `.auth/token-<persona>.json`.
* **Context isolation does not solve data races** — hence the per-flow data strategy.
* **Teardown must be fixture-scoped, not trailing statements.** *(The docs never explicitly address the failure case — so we prove it with the mid-flow failure check.)* **\[ref 7\]**
* *(Cost note:* `RECORD_HAR=true` *sources the context from real chromium —* `fixtures/api.fixture.ts:116-128`*. Opt-in, never in the PR gate.)*

## Coverage is classified, not just counted

| Class | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `flow-verified` | Exercised inside a flow whose business-outcome criterion passes — the strongest class |
| `positive-path` | A single valid authenticated call asserting the documented success response; no flow reaches it |
| `503-tolerated` | Provider unconfigured locally; the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome (`_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`) |
| `precondition-refused` | Precondition unmeetable locally; the enveloped business 4xx is the recorded outcome ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) |
| `no-documented-flow` | Reached by no product-documented flow — a finding in its own right, triaged at the end |

The catalogue's **Expected dominant class** column is the planning-time prediction; the matrix records what actually happened. A flow landing materially weaker than predicted is a finding, not a silent downgrade.

## Toggles — two of them, and they work differently

### 1. CSRF hardening — test-side, ON by default

The gateway mounts a double-submit guard (`api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts`, mounted `index.ts:370-371` inside `if (NODE_ENV !== 'test')`): the server mints an HMAC-signed token, sets the readable `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and mirrors it in the `X-CSRF-Token` **response** header; a client echoes it back as `X-XSRF-TOKEN`.

The [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and) rewrite short-circuits `protectMiddleware` for any request carrying `Authorization: Bearer …` or `x-api-key`, so authenticated writes are **not expected to need the token today**. **We send it anyway** — the suite behaves like a correct client and keeps passing if that bypass is narrowed.

* **Local:** `getCsrfEnabled()` in `config/environment.ts`, default `true`: `readEnv('CSRF_ENABLED', 'true') !== 'false'`. Commented override in `.env.example`.
* ~~**CI:**~~ *(moot — R4)* `CSRF_ENABLED: ${{ vars.PLAYWRIGHT_CSRF_ENABLED || 'true' }}` on the `playwright` job only.

### 2. Login rate limiter (`LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED`) — platform-side, read at gateway boot

**A test cannot flip this at runtime.** `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:858` passes it into `shouldSkipLoginLimiter({ nodeEnv, disableEnv })`; `middleware/rateLimitSkip.ts:68-69` honours it **only** when the value is `'true'` **and** `NODE_ENV` is in the non-prod allow-list. Never honoured in production ([KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)).

| Where | Today | Effect |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Local | `docker-compose.yml:368` → `${LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED:-false}` | **ACTIVE** unless exported before `docker compose up -d`. *(Verified 2026-07-24: the running developer stack has it* `true` *— something in the boot path exported it. Don't infer the default from a running container.)* |
| CI | `boot-platform-stack/action.yml:123` → hardcoded `"true"` | **DISABLED** for every suite's stack, with no way to change it |

What this ticket adds: a documented local runbook line; a `getLoginLimiterDisabled()` accessor so `auth.setup.ts` can annotate the report and decide whether a login 429 gets bounded backoff; and a `login-limiter-disabled` **input** on the composite (**default** `"true"`, additive) fed by `${{ vars.PLAYWRIGHT_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED || 'true' }}` from the Playwright caller only. The design rule that makes the toggle optional: **one login per persona per run**.

*Setting either repo Variable is a human action in repo settings —* `gh variable set` *is a GitHub API call, barred for systemTest work.*

## Phase checklist

- [ ] **Phase 0 — enablers**
  - [ ] `helpers/csrf.ts` — port from `performance/helpers/csrf.ts`; wire into `performApiCall`
  - [ ] `getCsrfEnabled()` + `.env.example` entry; `tests-unit/csrf.test.ts` *(CI variable wiring dropped — R4)*
  - [ ] **Probe A** — authenticated `POST /api/documents` with `CSRF_ENABLED=false`; record the result here
  - [ ] **Probe B** — force a mid-flow failure; confirm fixture teardown ran
  - [ ] **Probe C** — attempt a certification with a past `expiresAt` (F6 feasibility)
  - [ ] **Probe D** — attempt to POST a synthetic system-errors entry (F13 feasibility)
  - [ ] **Settle D1** (anchoring) — F3 blocked until then; re-assess against mock mode (R10)
  - [ ] **Define and settle D2** (tier split) and **D3** (child-plan layout) — never written down (R9)
  - [ ] **Remove BOTH** `video` **and** `trace` **from** `playwright.config.ts`
  - [ ] `helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` **(new)** — sequence stamped at request start; teardown writes + attaches `api-exchanges.json`
  - [ ] `helpers/api-report.ts` **(slim)** — one markdown attachment per call
  - [ ] `tests-unit/exchange-recorder.test.ts` — record shape, redaction, ordering under concurrency, one file per test
  - [ ] **Always-on masking** of GDPR personal data, access tokens and secret/API keys in the recorder and `api-report.ts`, independent of `REDACT_SECRETS` (R12)
  - [ ] **oxlint rule** *(was ESLint — R7)* — forbid `api.fetch(` / direct `request.` outside `helpers/api-call.ts` (mirrors the existing `no-restricted-properties` boundary for `process.env`)
  - [ ] **Guard assertion** — `POST /api/users/admin/create` still assigns the role it is given, so a change to that unpublished endpoint fails loudly
  - [ ] `getLoginLimiterDisabled()` + platform-side-labelled `.env.example` entry + README runbook line
  - [ ] `login-limiter-disabled` input on `boot-platform-stack/action.yml` — *moot (R4), drop*
  - [ ] Wire the 5 seeded personas into `config/environment.ts` + `.env.example`; add `SECUURA_PLATFORM_API_KEY` for F8
  - [ ] Multi-persona `auth/auth.setup.ts` — one login per persona per run → `.auth/token-<persona>.json`
  - [ ] Split `fixtures/api.fixture.ts` (170 lines) into `contexts.fixture.ts` + `clients.fixture.ts`
  - [ ] `helpers/flow.ts` — `test.step()` stages labelled with the acting persona; cleanup as fixture-scoped `use()` teardown
  - [ ] `helpers/settle.ts` — a **thin wrapper over** `expect.poll`. Four deadlines: anchoring, export, notification delivery (F9), webhook delivery (F10)
  - [ ] **Webhook URL convention for F10** — external-looking, non-internal, satisfies the originate SSRF guard
  - [ ] Retire the 2 duplicate specs, recording why
- [ ] **Phase 0b — coverage instrumentation**
  - [ ] `coverage/specOperations.ts` via `api-explorer/src/loader/specLoader.ts`
  - [ ] `coverage/flowCoverage.ts` — clients declare `operations: OperationRef[]` with verification class
  - [ ] `tests-unit/coverage.test.ts` — `COVERAGE_FLOOR` ratchets 8 → the current operation total (346 on 2026-10-26, R1), per-class floors enforced
  - [ ] `npm run coverage:matrix` → `docs/api_coverage_matrix.md`; HTML report renders the same breakdown
  - [ ] **Recount and re-home** — reconcile the matrix against the current spec and assign the operations added since July to flows (R1)
  - [ ] **Residue check** — counts unchanged across two consecutive runs, with an append-only exclusion list
- [ ] **Spine** — `tests/spine/document-lifecycle.spec.ts`: one test (F3 → F4 → F5), `test.step()` stages, `@smoke`
- [ ] **Pilot** — **F10** implemented end-to-end as the vertical slice; review before writing the remaining plans
- [ ] **Flows** — a child plan per flow: F1 · F2 · F3 · F4 · F5 · F6 · F7 · F8 · F9 · F11 · F12 · F13 · F14 · F15 · F16 · F17 · F18 · F19 · F20 · F21 · F22 · F23
- [ ] **Closing — triage the** `no-documented-flow` **residuals**, recording each disposition

## Definition of done

1. **All published operations classified** (346 on 2026-10-26, R1), none unaccounted for.
2. **Class distribution meets its floors** — no downgrade out of `flow-verified` without a recorded reason.
3. **Every flow passes its stated acceptance criterion**, or records a documented gap where a platform capability is missing (F6 expired, F13 error → resolve).
4. **No residue** — two consecutive full runs leave identical record counts outside the documented append-only exclusion list.
5. **Residual triage complete.**
6. All four suites' `quality` gates green; both QA HTML docs synced.

## Verification (per phase)

 1. `cd systemTest/playwright && npm run quality`
 2. `npm run coverage:matrix` — ops moved to covered **at the intended class**, floor raised, residuals listed
 3. Live, against Playwright's own instance: `npm run test:smoke` → `npx playwright test tests/<flow>` → `npm run test:e2e`
 4. **Acceptance check** — the flow's stated criterion passes
 5. **Residue check** — counts identical outside the exclusion list
 6. **Order-independence check** — specs shuffled; identical result
 7. **Mid-flow failure check** — force a step to fail; confirm teardown cleaned up **and** `api-exchanges.json` **was still written and attached**
 8. **Open the HTML report in a browser** (systemTest CLAUDE.md MUST [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#11](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-32-drop-dead-chargeable-events-table-0d45c9c29ab9)); confirm the class distribution renders, steps show their acting persona, each test carries its `api-exchanges.json`
 9. Reconcile console ⇄ HTML report ⇄ JUnit counts
10. **Anti-duplication check** against Schemathesis/Akto/k6
11. **Doc-trace check** — every flow step cites its source doc + section
12. Before any PR: all four suites' `quality` gates green, plus the PR's Test Evidence block (R8)

## Risk mitigation

Most of the risks below are removable — not by being careful, but by deciding, probing, or automating a detector. What remains is labelled honestly rather than managed.

### 1. Prove the pattern once before repeating it 22 times

Do **Phase 0 + Phase 0b + the spine + F10** as a complete vertical slice, and only then write the remaining plans. F10 is deliberately the pilot: 7 operations, self-contained, `Own` data, and it exercises an async boundary — so it stresses every enabler without being large.

Every shared mechanism (CSRF, personas, per-persona contexts, the exchange recorder, `expect.poll` settle, fixture teardown, the coverage matrix) gets validated against the real stack **once**. If an assumption is wrong it is wrong in one flow, not twenty-three. **Reduces Risks 1, 8, 9, 11, 12** — all of which are "does the shared plumbing actually work" in disguise.

### 2. Four probes that turn a risk into a fact (each under an hour, all in Phase 0)

| Probe | Question it answers | Kills |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **A** — authenticated `POST /api/documents` with `CSRF_ENABLED=false` | Does the [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and) Bearer bypass actually hold? | Risk 1 |
| **B** — force a mid-flow failure, check cleanup ran | Does fixture teardown run on failure? | the ref-7 doc gap |
| **C** — create a certification with a past `expiresAt` | Can we reach the Expired state ourselves? | Risk 14 |
| **D** — POST a synthetic entry to system-errors | Can we raise an error on demand? | Risk 15 |

**Run C and D before waiting on a reply** — the capability may already exist, in which case the ask resolves itself and both flow plans proceed unchanged.

### 3. Three risks need a decision, not work

**D1, D2 and D3 at the top of this ticket.** They cost nothing to settle and currently block F3/the spine, the tier split, and the child-plan layout respectively. **Deciding them is the cheapest risk reduction available.**

### 4. Turn conventions into gates

A rule enforced only at review will eventually be broken. Three become automated:

| Was | Becomes | Kills |
| -- | -- | -- |
| "All transport goes through `performApiCall`" (review rule) | **oxlint rule** *(R7)* forbidding `api.fetch(` / direct `request.` outside `helpers/api-call.ts` — the repo already uses `no-restricted-properties` this way to keep `process.env` inside the config module | Risk 12 |
| "A change to `/api/users/admin/*` breaks Phase 0 silently" | **Guard assertion** that the endpoint still assigns the role it is given — fails loudly and immediately | Risk 2 |
| ~~"The composite action is shared source"~~ *(moot — R4)* | **Cross-suite diff** — after the change, run one job from each of the other three suites and compare boot output | Risk 7 |

Plus the guards already planned: the residue check (Risk 8), the order-independence check (Risk 9), and the per-class floors in `coverage.test.ts` (Risk 4).

### 5. What is irreducible — and what we do instead

Risks **5, 6, 13** and the provider-gated parts of **4** cannot be engineered away: they are properties of the local environment, the platform's state machines, and an open defect ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C). The mitigation is **honest labelling** — the verification classes and the per-flow *Expected dominant class* column make each one visible in the matrix rather than hidden inside a green run. A risk that shows up in the report is not a risk; it is a documented limitation.

## Risks

 1. **CSRF** — hardened by default; expected to be a non-issue because of the [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and>) Bearer bypass. *Mitigated by Probe A.*
 2. **Persona setup depends on an unpublished endpoint** — `/api/users/admin/*` is live but absent from the spec. Must not count toward `COVERAGE_FLOOR`. *Mitigated by the guard assertion.*
 3. **⚠ No Cardano backend on either stack — F3's anchor leg is not satisfiable as written.** Verified 2026-07-24: `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` unset on `secuura-anchoring`/`secuura-originate` (code tests `=== 'true'`, `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:459`); `CARDANO_NODE_URL=http://cardano-devnet:8090`, empty `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY`; `cardano-devnet` is behind the compose profile `devnet` and no such container exists; the CI composite's service list (`boot-platform-stack/action.yml:124-129`) excludes it. *This is **D1** — needs a decision, not work.*
 4. `503-tolerated` **and** `precondition-refused` **are weak classes** — F11, F18, F19 and F20–F23 carry most of them. *Mitigated by per-class floors + the predicted-class column.*
 5. **State-machine operations legitimately 4xx** ([KS-478](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful>)) — F20/F21/F22 must reach a satisfiable state or record the refusal. *Irreducible; labelled.*
 6. **Rate limits** — \~2000/60s; login 10/hour/IP without the override. One login per persona. *Irreducible; designed around.*
 7. ~~**The composite action is shared source, even though the stacks are not.**~~ *Moot — GitHub Actions retired (R4).*
 8. **Test-data accumulation** — 23 flows creating fixture data per run. *Mitigated by fixture-scoped teardown + the residue check.*
 9. **Data races between parallel flows** — isolation separates sessions, not platform state. *Mitigated by the per-flow data strategy + the order-independence check.*
10. **F10's webhook URL must pass the SSRF guard** ([KS-487](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto>)-B). *Settled in Phase 0 by the URL convention.*
11. **Four async boundaries** — anchoring, export, notification delivery (F9), webhook delivery (F10). All four use `expect.poll`. *Mitigated by the pilot exercising one of them.*
12. **The exchange recorder is the only evidence.** *Mitigated by the oxlint rule (R7).*
13. **F16 must not encode a known bug as expected behaviour** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature ([KS-488](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet>)-C). F16 stops at wallet linkage. *Irreducible; labelled. Schemathesis's xfail will xpass loudly when the fix lands, prompting a revisit.*
14. **F6's expired leg depends on a platform capability we do not have.** *Probe C first; then the ask to* @kamil.kreiser */* @stuart.jamieson\*; else a documented gap.\*
15. **F13's only journey depends on a platform capability we do not have.** *Probe D first; same escalation; else F13 is labelled a read surface.*

## Playwright references

Grounded in the docs for the pinned **1.61.1**. Checked 2026-07-24.

| \# | Source | What it establishes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | [Best Practices](<https://playwright.dev/docs/best-practices>) | *"Each test should be completely isolated from another test and should run independently with its own local storage, session storage, data, cookies etc."* · *"Only test what you control."* → per-flow data ownership; provider-gated paths record a by-design 503 |
| 2 | [API testing](<https://playwright.dev/docs/api-testing>) | *"…you can manually create a new instance of APIRequestContext which will have its own isolated cookies."* → the per-persona / per-flow context model |
| 3 | [Parallelism](<https://playwright.dev/docs/test-parallel>) | *"If one of the serial tests fails, all subsequent tests are skipped."* · *"All tests in a group are retried together."* · *"Using serial is not recommended."* → the spine is one stepped test |
| 4 | [Videos](<https://playwright.dev/docs/videos>) | *"Videos are saved upon browser context closure at the end of a test."* → video cannot capture an API-only test |
| 5 | [Trace viewer](<https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer>) + [microsoft/playwright#18891](<https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/18891>) + [microsoft/playwright-pytest#137](<https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-pytest/issues/137>) | Tracing is started via `browserContext.tracing`; no documented path records a standalone `APIRequestContext`. **#18891 closed 30 Jun 2023 as stale** — *"limited engagement… insufficient actionability"* — **not** implemented, despite the "closed as completed" label |
| 6 | [TestInfo](<https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo>) | `attach()`: *"Either path or body must be specified, but not both"*; *"automatically takes care of copying attached files to a location that is accessible to reporters."* · `outputPath()`: *"a path inside the testInfo.outputDir where the test can safely put a temporary file"* |
| 7 | [Fixtures](<https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures>) | *"…teardown is executed when the fixture is no longer being used by the test/hook."* — the failure case is **not** explicitly covered, hence Probe B |
| 8 | [Assertions](<https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions>) | *"You can convert any synchronous expect to an asynchronous polling one using expect.poll"*, with `{ timeout, intervals, message }` and a documented API-polling example |

## Related

A **High**-severity privilege-escalation finding was surfaced while verifying whether this work could provision an `ISSUER_APPROVER` persona at runtime, filed as a comment on [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A): a case-sensitive platform-role denylist combined with case-normalising persistence lets a tenant-scoped `ORG_ADMIN` mint a platform `SYSTEM_ADMIN` via `role: "Super_Admin"`. Not in scope here. Its systemTest regression belongs to [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) (Review G) once the fix lands.

## Notes

* ~~Work stays **local — commits only**. No push, no PR.~~ *Superseded (R8):* branch → test → commit → push → PR with a Test Evidence block → QA gate GO → merge. Still no links to other organisations' GitHub issues/PRs in git metadata.
* Branch off `develop` first, per Git Flow.

title: m365 admin setup wizard sends a Secuura tenant id as organizationId - after KS-1673 the tenant choice is ignored
description:
**BLUF:** The admin M365 setup wizard sends a **Secuura tenant id** in the `organizationId` field — or the literal `'default'` when no tenant is selected. Since KS-1673 (merged 2026-10-20, #1633), the m365 service takes the organisation from the caller's login token and **ignores** that field. So the tenant a system admin picks in the wizard no longer decides anything: the connection, or the Teams webhook, lands in the admin's **own** organisation.

**Read statically at develop** `9207fe336797`**. Not driven.**

## What the wizard sends

| line | call | sent |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `frontend/admin/src/components/M365SetupWizard.tsx:94`, `:98` | `POST /api/m365/connections/init` | `organizationId: selectedTenantId \|\| 'default'` |
| `M365SetupWizard.tsx:171` | `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` | `organizationId: selectedTenantId \|\| 'default'` |

* `selectedTenantId` comes from `useTenantStore` (`M365SetupWizard.tsx:84`).
* The store is filled only for `super_admin` / `system_admin` / `SYSTEM_ADMIN` (`frontend/admin/src/components/Layout.tsx:107-112`, via `fetchTenants()`).
* Its values are **tenant** ids. A login token's `organizationId` is an **organisation** id. These are two different id spaces.

## What happens now (after KS-1673)

* **The field is stripped and ignored** on both calls. A system admin's new connection is owned by the admin's own organisation, whichever tenant the wizard shows as selected.
* **A token with no organisation gets 403** from both calls.
* **Tenant admins**, who previously got 400 because `'default'` failed the old UUID check, now succeed under their own organisation.
* **Rows written before KS-1673** carry a tenant id in `organization_id`. They now match no token, so they are owned by nobody. **Re-connecting is the remedy** (ruled 2026-10-20). Read-only measurement on 2026-10-19 found **0** connections and **0** Teams webhooks on kintsugi and on demo.

## Open question — not decided here

Whether a system admin may set up Microsoft 365 **on behalf of a customer organisation** is a product decision. It has gone to Kamil. Until it is ruled, the fail-closed behaviour above stands, consistent with KS-1673's no-bypass ruling. **No fix is proposed in this ticket.**

## How it was found

Gate AS1's note N1 on #1633 (KS-1673 PR A). Both frontend facts were re-read at develop by Seat R 56th before filing. Five Linear searches found no existing ticket: "M365SetupWizard", "m365 setup wizard organizationId", "wizard tenant id organizationId", "selectedTenantId m365", "m365 wizard default organization". The control search returned KS-1677. KS-1490 names the same file only because of a stale host URL.

title: api-gateway crashes under load: onProxyReq calls setHeader after the proxied request's headers were sent — uncaught exception, 13 restarts, 502s on /api/auth/login
description:
## Summary

When you get a chance, Kamil — this one does hurt under load. During the [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) k6 runs, the api-gateway process exited on an uncaught exception thrown from its own proxy hook, and Docker restarted it 13 times in about five minutes. nginx answered 502 while it was down. The hook calls `setHeader` on a request whose headers were already sent, and nothing guards or catches that. A small guard plus an error path would likely settle it; your call on the shape. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, impact and a suggested direction

**The throw** (31 occurrences in the gateway log)

```
Uncaught exception {"error":"Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client"}
  at ClientRequest.setHeader (node:_http_outgoing:684:11)
  at ProxyServer.onProxyReq (/app/dist/routes/proxy.js:254:26)
  at ProxyServer.emit (/app/node_modules/eventemitter3/index.js:184:35)
  at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/app/node_modules/http-proxy/lib/http-proxy/passes/web-incoming.js:133:16)
  at tickOnSocket (node:_http_client:1116:7)
```

`dist/routes/proxy.js:254` is the hook's first statement, `proxyReq.setHeader('X-Request-ID', requestId)` — source `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:246` (mapped by reading the compiled file in the running container). None of the hook's later header writes (vouch `:276`, policy headers, `Authorization`, the [KS-453](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-453/did-endpoints-getpatchdelete-apididdid-return-502-on-malformed-did) body re-stream) checks `proxyReq.headersSent` either.

**Where:** local slot 1, api-gateway built from develop `63db8a383` ([KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) changes no service code); Apple M2 Max, four stacks up. Load: k6 `scalability` (12:54–13:15Z) then `auth-spike` (13:15–13:17Z, 150 VUs on `POST /api/auth/login`). First crash 13:12:11Z; `restartCount=13`, last start 13:17:36Z; healthy afterwards.

**What callers saw**

| Signal | Value |
| -- | -- |
| nginx, `POST /api/auth/login` during auth-spike | **11,362 × 502** + 6,123 × 429 |
| scalability | thresholds 6/6, but **14.8 %** `http_req_failed`, 65,192 failed checks |
| auth-spike | INVALID — all 17,788 logins failed |
| auth service, same second as the first crash | `DB getUserByEmail failed … timeout exceeded when trying to connect` |

The auth DB-pool timeout looks like the trigger; the gateway turning it into a process exit is the defect.

**Ruled out:** slots sharing a database (each has its own Postgres + pgbouncer network), and the harness/k6 version (the trace is inside api-gateway; other k6 scenarios pass).

**Suggested direction**

1. Return early from the hook when `proxyReq.headersSent` (or the request is destroyed).
2. Let the proxy's error path answer 502/503 rather than letting a handler throw reach `uncaughtException` (the class [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) describes for `authenticateToken`).
3. A regression test driving `onProxyReq` with an already-sent `proxyReq`, red on today's code.

**Reproduce:** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=… systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 1 bash -c 'cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:scalability'`, then `npm run test:auth-spike`; watch `docker inspect secuura-api-gateway --format '{{.RestartCount}}'` and `docker logs secuura-api-gateway | grep "Cannot set headers"`.

**Related:** [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) (async middleware without a catch — same class, different site) · [KS-744](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-744/gateway-500s-on-every-proxied-route-for-a-token-lacking) (unguarded header set in `auth.ts:377`) · [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) (back-to-back tiers' setup logins refused inside a spent request window — the 429 side of busy runs) · [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (where it was found) · [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491/review-f-edge-waf-ddos-and-anti-automation) (Review F — availability under load).

+++

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1342 (squash `67c73393dfa0`)

- [ ] **N-1342-1 (Major, not blocking):** under keep-alive agent saturation (more than 128 requests in
  flight to one upstream), a **body-parsed** POST whose headers were already sent is delivered to the
  upstream with its `Content-Length` and **zero body bytes**. The guard skips the re-stream, so the
  upstream waits and the client gets a TCP reset at exactly 60.0 s, with **no 502 and no log line**.
  At develop before #1342 the same request **crashes** the process, so the merged change is strictly
  better — this is residue, not a regression. The raw-stream `/api/auth/login` route is unaffected
  (140/140 delivered). Evidence: `evidence/runs/probe1342b.log` and `probe1342c.log` in the gate43
  batch #1341-#1345 report directory.

title: systemTest/schemathesis: test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped fails on Linux, because sys.executable keeps the symlink path and the KS-738 loop it asserts never occurs
description:
## BLUF

`tests/unit/runner/test_prevenv_bootstrap.py::TestReexecBehavesAsAProcess::test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped` fails on Linux at `origin/develop` `1ae6f17d19a8`. It expects exit 1 and the *"refusing to loop (KS-738)"* line; the script exits 0.

## Seen

Found during [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719) (PR #1687), 2026-10-26. Python 3.14.9 linux/arm64 (official `python:3.14` image), `tests/unit` with `-n 4 --no-cov`:

* `origin/develop`: **1 failed, 4343 passed, 2 skipped**. This is the one failure.
* After PR #1687: 1 failed, 4359 passed, 2 skipped. The same single failure.
* Assertion: `AssertionError: expected the loop guard's exit 1, got 0` (`assert result.returncode == 1`).
* `scripts/venv_reexec.py:30-37` states the case the guard covers: with `<root>/venv` a symlink, *"CPython sets* `sys.executable` *to the RESOLVED target"*, so the venv-membership test never becomes true and the old prelude re-exec'd forever.
* Measured on Linux: a symlink `/tmp/x/python3` → `/usr/local/bin/python3.14`, run as `/tmp/x/python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"`, prints `/tmp/x/python3`, not the resolved target. No resolved-target path means no loop for the guard to refuse.

## Searched

Secuura-PK, all states, title and description: `test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped`: 0 hits. Control: `_free_active_proposal_slot` returned KS-1719, so the search can fire.

## Not established

* That the test passes on macOS. Not run there: the host Python was 3.14.7 when this was measured, below the suite's pin, so pytest exits before collecting.
* The experiment symlinked the interpreter *file*. The test stages a symlinked venv *directory* (`_stage_tree(tmp_path, venv="symlink")`). The same CPython behaviour is inferred for the directory case, not measured.
* Which hosts run `tests/unit` on Linux today. Not checked.

title: Schemathesis: constraints.txt's documented install line skips the pip upgrade setup does, so quality:static reds on the venv's own pip
description:
**BLUF:** `systemTest/schemathesis/constraints.txt` documents the venv install as `venv/bin/python3 -m pip install -c constraints.txt -e '.[dev]'`. That line never upgrades pip. The harness's own setup does upgrade it first (`scripts/runner/dependencies.py:50-55`). So a venv built by the documented line keeps the host Python's bundled pip, and `run.py quality:static` goes red on pip-audit, flagging the venv's own pip rather than any harness dependency. No fix is in PR-3b; this is filed so it isn't lost.

Refs KS-1211. Found while running the systemTest rule-2 gates for PR-3b (vitest), which changes no Schemathesis file.

## Measured (2026-09-17, throwaway copy of `systemTest/schemathesis` at develop `19f1e5475`, 0 files differing from develop; host Python 3.14.5)

| run | venv built by | pip in venv | `quality:static` | pip-audit |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `pip3 install -c constraints.txt -e '.[dev]'` (the documented line) | 26.1.1 | **rc 1** | red: `pip 26.1.1` PYSEC-2026-196 (fix 26.1.2), PYSEC-2026-3721 (fix 26.2); 0 findings on the pinned harness dependencies |
| 2 | the same venv after `pip3 install --upgrade pip` (what `dependencies.py:50-55` does) | 26.2.1 | **rc 0** | passed |

In both runs Ruff format, Ruff lint and MyPy (src, scripts, config) passed. `quality:static` skips both pytest suites by design.

## The two paths, at source (read, not re-run)

* `constraints.txt` "HOW TO USE", Install: `venv/bin/python3 -m pip install -c constraints.txt -e '.[dev]'`. No pip upgrade.
* `scripts/runner/dependencies.py`, which `run.py setup` uses:
  * Step 2 (`:50-55`) is `pip install --upgrade pip`, run with `check=False`, so a failure there is silent.
  * Steps 3-4 (`:61`, `:73`) install with `--upgrade` and pass **no** `-c constraints.txt`. Whether setup therefore resolves outside the constraints was not measured here; KS-1002 notes `test_venv_pin_parity` catching a fresh setup that resolved 26 packages below them.

## Fix shape (prose only, for the owner)

Either add the pip upgrade to the documented install line, or pin pip in `constraints.txt` and have both paths install with `-c`. Either way, one path should build the venv the gate measures.

A regression check could build a venv from the documented line in CI-equivalent conditions and assert `quality:static` rc 0.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, archived issues included, literal match on title, description and comments)

* `constraints.txt`: 4 issues (KS-1169, KS-1016, KS-1002, KS-687) and comments on KS-1169, KS-611, KS-662, KS-684. None is about the install line or pip.
* `dependencies.py`: KS-672 (canceled, slot targeting) and a comment on KS-666.
* `pip-audit`: 7 issues and comments on 10. Each mentions pip-audit as a passing gate; none is about the venv's own pip.
* `upgrade pip`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* 1207 issues and 3441 comments were scanned.

title: Eight dashboards show a slot picker that filters nothing — latent today, wrong the day /metrics lands
description:
## What

All 12 dashboards under `observability/grafana/dashboards/` carry a `slot` template variable, so every one presents a slot picker. Only **four** actually use `$slot` in a query.

Measured 2026-09-07 by counting panel targets containing `$slot`:

| Dashboard | Panels filtering by slot |
| -- | -- |
| `k6_engineering` | 32 |
| `k6_executive` | 12 |
| `test_quality_trends` | 8 |
| `platform_engineering` | 4 |
| `platform_auth` | **0** |
| `platform_cardano` | **0** |
| `platform_document_lifecycle` | **0** |
| `platform_queue` | **0** |
| `platform_slo` | **0** |
| `platform_traffic_services` | **0** |
| `security_posture` | **0** |
| `test_openapi_coverage` | **0** |

On those eight, moving the picker changes nothing.

## Why it is not urgent, and why it is not nothing

It is **not currently misleading**, because those eight query application `/metrics` endpoints that no service implements ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)) — the panels are empty whatever the picker says. Nothing wrong is being displayed.

It becomes wrong the moment [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands. Those panels will then merge all four slots into one number, with a picker sitting above them implying they are scoped. That is precisely the defect [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) existed to remove — a plausible-looking dashboard that quietly answers about the wrong system — reintroduced through the panels nobody had to touch.

## Evidence that the other four are correct

Same sweep, evaluating every slot-aware panel for `slot1` vs `slot2` against live Prometheus during a four-slot run: **56 slot-aware panels, zero returned identical data**. Where the filter exists it discriminates properly. This ticket is only about the panels where it is absent.

## Scope

Add the `slot` filter to those panels' PromQL when their metrics start existing, or drop the picker from dashboards that will never be slot-scoped. Do it **with** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never), since the correct filter cannot be written or tested against metrics that do not yet exist.

A validator check in the shape of `observability/scripts/checks/container-join-slot.mjs` — fail the build when a dashboard declares a `slot` variable that no panel consumes — would stop it recurring, and would have caught this.

## Depends on

[KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) (no service exposes `/metrics`).

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: No service exposes /metrics — the secuura-services scrape job has never collected a single series on any slot
description:
## What

`observability/prometheus/prometheus.yml` defines a `secuura-services` scrape job over seven service targets. Every one of them is **down with HTTP 404**, and has been since the job was written — the endpoints do not exist.

Measured 2026-09-07 on a freshly rebuilt four-slot stack:

* `secuura-services` targets: **7 down, 404 Not Found** (every other job is `up`, except `kafka`, which is phase2-only and correct).
* `prom-client` is a dependency of **no** service.
* No `/metrics` route is registered anywhere under `services/*/src`, using `/health` as a positive control.

## Why it matters

This is not an observability-stack defect — the stack is healthy and correctly configured. It is that the thing it is pointed at does not exist. The consequence is that **every application-level panel across eight dashboards renders empty**:

`platform_auth`, `platform_cardano`, `platform_document_lifecycle`, `platform_queue`, `platform_slo`, `platform_traffic_services`, `security_posture`, `test_openapi_coverage`.

So the platform currently has **no application telemetry at all** — no request rates, error rates, latency, queue depth or SLO burn from the services themselves. What Grafana does show comes from cAdvisor, the DB/Redis/nginx exporters, and the test harnesses pushing their own results.

## Not to be confused with

[KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) corrected this job's **target ports** (they were 3000-3006 against services that listen on the 4000-range and 8080) and added `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh` to stop them drifting again. That work made the job name the right addresses. It did not, and could not, make the endpoints exist.

## Scope

Instrumenting the services. Roughly: add `prom-client` to the service template, register a `/metrics` route alongside the existing `/health`, and export the handful of series the existing dashboards already query.

## Blocks

* Per-slot application metrics. The scrape job uses static container names, so only slot 1 is discovered. Making slots 2-4 discoverable needs either a Docker socket mounted into Prometheus (root-equivalent) or a generated targets file plus a per-slot `docker network connect` — not worth its cost while the job collects nothing on any slot. Revisit **after** this, not before.
* The slot picker on those eight dashboards, which currently filters nothing because their panels have no slot-aware data to filter.

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: Renovate cannot bump base-image-watch.sh EXCLUDED_BASES — Blockchain/Dev/** is in ignorePaths (split from KS-1367; needs Kamil's agreement)
description:
## BLUF

Split from [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) at Peter's request (2026-10-07). [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not)'s branch (`feature/ks-1445-…`, shared with [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)) makes Renovate see `systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml` `k6Image`. The remaining part needs a change to the repo's `ignorePaths`, which sits in Kamil's work-stream E ([KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490/review-e-deployment-containers-and-cicd-supply-chain)). **This ticket waits on Kamil's agreement.** He has not commented on [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not), so there is nothing of his to quote yet.

## Re-verified from source (2026-10-07, worktree at `origin/develop` 652cf5f6e)

* `renovate.json:4` has `"ignorePaths": ["Blockchain/Dev/**"]`. Renovate skips every manager, including a `customManagers` regex, under that path.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` `EXCLUDED_BASES` names `grafana/k6:2.3.0` and every `observability/docker-compose.yml` image tag.
* Two tests fail when that list disagrees with the files Renovate does bump:
  * `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/config/k6ImagePinParity.test.ts` (k6)
  * `observability/test/compose-image-pins.test.mjs` (observability, added in [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is))
* So a Renovate PR is red until a person edits the list by hand. That is safe, because nothing slips through, but it is noise.
* Renovate app: `gh pr list --state all --author app/renovate` returns no PR ever. That is consistent with the app not being installed. The installation itself could not be read with the available token.

## Options for Kamil

1. Narrow `ignorePaths` so `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is visible, and add a regex `customManagers` entry for its quoted `"image:tag"` lines, grouped with `k6 runtime` and `observability stack images`.
2. Leave it as a hand edit. The red parity tests are the prompt, and that is documented in `systemTest/performance/docs/quick-start.md`.

## Done when

- [ ] Kamil has chosen 1 or 2. Quote his reply verbatim here.
- [ ] If 1: the config passes `renovate-config-validator --strict`, and a dry run shows one grouped update covering all three k6 sites.

title: Declared Node floor (engines.node >=18.0.0 in 5 packages) contradicts what the repo needs (22.13+) and runs on (24) - decide the floor
description:
## BLUF

**The repo declares a Node floor it cannot run on.** Five `package.json` files declare `engines.node >=18.0.0`, but a shell suite on the push path already requires **Node 22.13+**, every Docker image builds on **Node 24**, and the preflight assumes a **Node 24** host. Nothing breaks today — the real runtimes are all 24 — but the declared floor tells a developer Node 18 or 20 is fine, and on either one that suite stops with a FATAL. **This ticket records the measurements and asks for a decision. It is deliberately NOT a fix:** the floor is a choice, not a defect with one right answer.

Filed by Seat R 48th on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER of 2026-10-18T15:24:54Z), after it surfaced while raising PR #1580 (KS-1624 F1). All measurements at `develop` `6184eaa0af75c1e27eb69bbff67a7790ef494b5f`.

## Measurement 1 — what the repo DECLARES

A census of all **50** tracked `package.json` files:

| `engines.node` | files |
| -- | -- |
| `>=18.0.0` | `Blockchain/Dev/package.json`, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `services/mcp-server`, `services/tenant-provisioning`, `services/tokenisation` (**5**) |
| `>=24.11.0` | `systemTest/akto`, `systemTest/oxlint`, `systemTest/performance`, `systemTest/playwright` (**4**) |
| none | **41** |

There is **no** `.nvmrc`, `.node-version` or `.tool-versions` anywhere in the tree (0 files). So the only machine-readable statement of the platform's floor is `>=18.0.0` — and the repo's own test tooling already contradicts it with `>=24.11.0`.

## Measurement 2 — what the repo actually NEEDS

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks812_whatsapp_bot_default_api_target.test.sh` strips TypeScript types with `module.stripTypeScriptTypes`, available from **Node 22.13**. It says so in its header (line 24) and is guarded: the helper is at line 25, its first call at **line 40**, and on an older Node it exits **2** at **line 44** with `FATAL: this suite needs node 22.13+ (module.stripTypeScriptTypes)`. It runs in the full shell-suite runner. By grep it is the only script under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts`, `systemTest` or `.githooks` needing a Node newer than 18 — so 22.13 is the measured real minimum *for the tooling*, and it is above the declared floor.

## Measurement 3 — what the repo actually RUNS ON

* **Docker:** all **13** `FROM node:` lines in the tree are `node:24-alpine`. Every shipped service builds and runs on 24.
* **Preflight:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh:49` and `:58` assume a host Node **>=24** on the CI path ("Host node >=24 lets us skip docker", "CI always runs node>=24 (host path)").
* KS-355 (Done) moved CI to Node 24.

## The decision this needs (options, not a recommendation)

1. **Raise the five floors to** `>=24` — matches every runtime and the systemTest packages; Node 18 and 20 are past end-of-life. This is the value KS-1398 already suggests (see below).
2. **Raise them to** `>=22.13` — the measured minimum for the tooling, the least restrictive honest value; leaves a gap between declared and shipped runtimes.
3. **Add a pin file** (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) as well as or instead of (1)/(2), so local tooling picks the right version automatically.
4. **Leave** `>=18.0.0` and accept that a developer on 18/20 gets a FATAL from one suite.

Whichever is chosen, `ks812`'s guard can stay as it is — it already fails loudly and names the version.

## Related, and why this is a separate ticket

**KS-1398** (Backlog) carries the same value as one row of a TypeScript 7 migration *suggestion*: `engines.node | >=18.0.0 ×5 | >=24 (Node 18 and 20 are past EOL)`. That row is the same field and the same direction as option 1. It is split out here because the floor is a decision that stands on its own today — it is a live contradiction on the push path, and it should not wait on whether a TypeScript 7 move is ever approved. If the TS 7 work goes ahead and settles the floor, this ticket closes with it.

## How this was searched before filing (dedupe)

Over **1,613** issues including archived, by symbol: `engines` (6 hits), `>=18` / `Node 18` (1: KS-1398), `stripTypeScriptTypes` / `strip-types` / `NO-STRIP-TYPES` (1: KS-355), `22.13` (0), `node:24` / `24.11` (39, broad), `nvmrc` / `node-version` / `tool-versions` (1: KS-355), `Node floor` / `Node version` / `engines.node` (5: KS-1427, KS-1398, KS-1102, KS-464, KS-355). Controls: `preflight` 169 hits, a nonsense token 0. Read KS-1398, KS-355, KS-1427, KS-1102 and KS-464: only KS-1398 records the declared floor, as noted above.

title: packages/shared wallet-signature.test.ts: the only positive cell fails on develop - verifyMessageSignature returns false for a valid CIP-8 signature
description:

**Searched first:** `wallet-signature.test.ts`, the full path `packages/shared/src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts`, `accepts a valid wallet signature over the message`, `verifyMessageSignature`, `makeWalletSignature`.
