title: Node 26's semver-major Readable.read() change truncates every synchronous cbor.encode() to its first byte on host test runs - images pin node:24 and are unaffected
description:
**Node 26.0.0 removed the behaviour** `cbor`**'s synchronous encoder depends on, so on a Node 26 host every** `cbor.encode()` **of a value longer than one byte returns only its first byte. Host-side test runs are affected; the deployed images are not. The failure mode is fail-closed.**

## The mechanism

Node commit `fadb214d95` / PR 60441, *"stream: readable read one buffer at a time"*, is listed **semver-major in the v26.0.0 changelog** (2026-05-05): `Readable.prototype.read()` with no size argument no longer concatenates the internal buffer, it returns one queued chunk. Deliberate, to avoid the cost of merging buffers — **so this is not a bug and no Node patch will restore the old behaviour.** *(Commit, PR and changelog entry identified via web search, not read at source.)*

`cbor`'s synchronous `encode()` / `encodeOne()` / `encodeCanonical()` are all `_encodeAll` (`encoder.js:595-602`):

```js
_encodeAll(objs) { const bs = new NoFilter({…}); this.pipe(bs); … this.end(); return bs.read() }
```

`NoFilter.read(size)` (`nofilter@3.1.0`, `lib/index.js:285`) delegates straight to `super.read(size)`. Its own documented contract is "no size argument → return all the data in the internal buffer", which is exactly what Node 26 withdrew.

## Measured on this host (Node v26.8.1, `cbor@9.0.2`)

| value encoded | returned | correct |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `['Signature1', …]` | `84` (1 B) | \~90 B |
| `'Signature1'` | `6a` (1 B) | `6a5369676e617475726531` |
| `Buffer.alloc(4,0xab)` | `44` (1 B) | `44abababab` |
| `Map{1:-8}` | `a1` (1 B) | `a10127` |
| `Map{1:1,3:-8,-1:6,-2:<32B>}` | `a4` (1 B) | \~45 B |

Not container-specific — **every** value whose encoding exceeds one byte is truncated. `7` and `Map{}` come back correct only because they are one byte already, which is what makes this quiet. Decoding a truncated value throws `Insufficient data`.

Scoped to the synchronous path: `cbor.encodeAsync` **is correct** (`83010203`) and **the decoder is healthy** (`decodeFirstSync('83010203')` → `[1,2,3]`).

## It is the runtime, proven with zero dependencies and a second runtime

Pure `stream.PassThrough`, 4 bytes written as 3 chunks, no packages involved:

|  | Node v26.8.1 | Node v24.22.1 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 3 chunks, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| 3 chunks + `end()`, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| one 4-byte chunk, `read()` *(control)* | `83010203` | `83010203` |
| `read(4)` explicit size | `83010203` | `83010203` |

The control discriminates, so the zero is a real zero. Successive `read()` calls on Node 26 return `83`,`01`,`0203` in order — the bytes are all present, merely no longer concatenated. `read(readableLength)` is the documented approximation and was verified on Node 26.

Node 24 runs were in throwaway `docker run --rm node:24-alpine` containers from an image already present on the host; nothing was installed, downloaded or built. This laptop has **only** Homebrew `node@26` (v26.8.1) — no Node 24, no nvm/fnm/volta/asdf.

## Items

### (a) Remedy options — no choice made, this needs a ruling

1. **Pin the dev/test runtime to Node 24**, which is what every image already ships: tighten `engines.node` (today the root is `>=18.0.0`, which *permits* Node 26) and add a runtime file (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) so host runs match the images. There is currently **no** `.nvmrc` in the repo and `packages/shared` declares **no** `engines` **at all**.
2. **An upstream fix in** `cbor` **and/or** `nofilter` — have `_encodeAll` read the whole buffer (`read(readableLength)`, or drain in a loop and concatenate). Not filed upstream by this investigation; `cbor`/`nofilter` issue trackers were **not** searched.
3. ⚠ **Not an option: bumping** `cbor`**.** `cbor@10.0.12` **is broken identically — measured**, not assumed, against an on-disk copy under `@meshsdk/provider`: all four cases truncate the same way. **The open dependabot PR 635 (**`cbor` **9.0.2 → 10.0.12) does NOT fix this.**

### (b) KS-1727 is the first known symptom

`packages/shared/src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts:47-49`, the file's only positive cell. `verifyMessageSignature` exits at `wallet.ts:372` (`CIP-8: failed to extract Ed25519 public key from COSEKey`) because the COSEKey the test hands it is the 1-byte `a4`. **Both** `wallet.ts` **and the test are correct**; the four negative cells pass only because all four assert `false`, which a verifier that always returns false satisfies. On Node 24, same cbor bytes from the same disk, the positive cell `RETURNS TRUE` **(**`wallet.ts:418`**)** and the negative exits at `:391` (payload mismatch), so the KS 278 payload binding is intact.

### (c) Related — flagged, not investigated

* **KS 1734** — `services/security`, 11 of 33 test files fail on the first run after `npm ci`; records Node v26.
* **KS 1729** — vc-issuer unit suite cold-run skips; records Node v26.
* **KS 1625** — the standing contradiction that admits a Node 26 host at all: declared Node floor `engines.node >=18.0.0` versus what the images actually ship.

None of these was examined for this cause. They are named because they share the runtime, not because a link was measured.

## Scope — deployed services are NOT affected

* **All 32 Dockerfiles pin** `node:24-alpine` (75 `FROM` lines, zero exceptions), `originate` included — the service hosting `/sign-wallet`. Node 24 encodes correctly, so no deployed route carries this. **No deployed route was called.**
* The only synchronous `cbor.encode` in tracked production source is `wallet.ts:397`; the other five occurrences are inside the test file. Two `decodeFirstSync` sites, both on the healthy decoder.
* Where it would bite on a Node 26 host, it **fails closed**: a real wallet supplies a properly-encoded COSEKey, so the failure lands at `:397` and surfaces as `Ed25519 signature verification failed` — valid signatures rejected, never invalid ones accepted. **Not a forgery surface.**

## Searched first

By symbol, file path and error string, titles + descriptions, `includeArchived: true`: `cbor.encode`, `nofilter`, `Readable.read`, `_encodeAll`, `encodeAsync`, `readableHighWaterMark` — **0 hits each**. `verifyMessageSignature` → 2 hits, KS-1727 and KS 1229 (Done). Control: the same instrument returns 25 hits for `node:24-alpine` and 3 for `Node v26`, so it can fire.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether the transitive `cbor` consumers (`services/anchoring`, `services/nft-certificate`, `frontend/issuer` lockfiles, `@meshsdk/provider`) call the synchronous encode internally — not traced.
* Whether `cbor` or `nofilter` upstream has a fix or an open issue for Node ≥26.
* Which other packages on this laptop depend on the same withdrawn `read()` contract — the repo-wide blast radius of Node 26 beyond CBOR.
* When host runs first moved to Node 26, and when KS-1727's cell began failing (develop was not bisected).

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-26_seatV-2nd/` — 8 probes, 19 output files, secret-scanned.

title: services/kyc db.retry.test.ts exceeds vitest's 5 s default under fleet load — 11498 ms loaded vs 675 ms alone; KS-1155's fix covers only packages/shared's walkers
description:
## BLUF

`services/kyc/src/__tests__/db.retry.test.ts` → `db availability retry (KS-377) > reports available immediately when the probe succeeds at boot` fails `Test timed out in 5000ms` when the box carries fleet load, having taken **11498 ms**. The assertion holds: the same cell passes in **675 ms** alone. This is the KS-1155 load class in a **service** suite, which KS-1155's delivered fix does not reach.

## Why KS-1155 does not cover it

KS-1155 shipped as #1254: *"the seven tree-walking guard suites get a 60 s budget from config; **every other suite keeps the 5 s default**."* That scope is `packages/shared`'s repo-tree-walking guards. `db.retry.test.ts` is in `services/kyc`, is not a tree-walking guard, and therefore still runs on the 5 s default.

KS-1053 names the same class for the `services/auth` ks949 cell — related, a different subject.

## The measurement (2026-09-26, Seat L8, on a tree where this file is blob-identical to develop `4db87c3e4b98`)

Four ways, because a timeout must be proven load-induced rather than called flaky:

| run | result |
| -- | -- |
| full kyc suite, **while a push's shell suites ran concurrently** | **1 failed / 29 passed (30)**, 13.11 s; the failure is `Test timed out in 5000ms`, the cell having taken **11498 ms** |
| `db.retry.test.ts` **alone** at develop | **5/5, 675 ms** |
| `db.retry.test.ts` **alone** in a worktree carrying an unrelated `kyc/src/index.ts` change | **5/5, 658 ms** |
| full kyc suite re-run **once the push finished and the box was quiet** | **30/30, 965 ms** |

The suite's own reported test time in the loaded run was **428–536 ms**; the overrun is scheduling, not work.

**Not caused by any change:** the worktree's diff touches `services/kyc/src/index.ts` and adds one new test file. `db.retry.test.ts` imports `../db` dynamically and never reaches `index.ts`.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

A red `Test timed out in 5000ms` here is indistinguishable, from the run alone, from a real regression in the DB boot latch (KS-377's subject). A seat that trusts it re-runs and loses minutes; a seat that does not trust it may dismiss a genuine failure in the same file later. The class needs a home in `services/` as it now has in `packages/shared`.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. Extend KS-1155's config approach to the affected `services/*` suites — a named budget for the cells that are scheduling-sensitive, with every other cell left on the 5 s default.
2. Give this file its own `testTimeout` at the `describe`/cell level, which is the smallest change and keeps the budget beside the code that needs it.
3. Make the cell insensitive to scheduling (it uses fake timers around a retry loop), if that can be done without weakening what it pins.

**Not built this round** — outside Seat L8's queue; filed on the coordinator's instruction.

## Board search before filing (1,316 issues **including archived**, 3,705 comments; literal match)

* `db.retry.test.ts` → KS-419 and KS-382, **both archived** and both about the DB boot latch, not timeouts.
* `testTimeout` → KS-1155 only. `Test timed out` → KS-1155 only (+6 comments). `fleet load` → KS-1155, KS-1324, KS-1181, KS-1182.
* KS-1155 read in full: scoped to `packages/shared` tree-walking guards; its merged fix explicitly leaves every other suite on the 5 s default.
* **Controls:** `KS-1155` → 4 / 7 and `KS-849` → 1 / 1 both fire; a nonsense token → **0 / 0**.

No open ticket covers kyc's timeouts, so this is a new ticket rather than a comment on KS-1155.

Refs KS-1155

title: Shell suites grade with `printf ... | grep -q` under pipefail: two unrelated suites failed a loaded preflight with "printf: write error: Broken pipe" (150 such lines in 29 files)
description:
## BLUF

Two unrelated shell suites each failed once inside preflight leg 14 of a pre-push, on the same tell, `printf: write error: Broken pipe`, while the machine was heavily loaded. Both grade a result with `printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF ...` under `set -uo pipefail`. Both passed every time on a quiet machine (15 of 15 runs). **The failure was NOT reproduced under load, so the mechanism below is the explanation that fits, not a proven one.** The same line shape appears at 150 places in 29 files.

## What was seen

Two pushes ran their pre-push hook at the same time on one macOS laptop (12 CPUs). A Docker Desktop VM was at about 920% CPU and the load average read 98 / 100 / 98 at 00:45Z and my later readings of the 1-minute figure were 74 (00:52Z), 58 (01:12Z), 39 (01:13Z) and 6.65 (01:18Z), after Docker Desktop was restarted. Leg 14 took 947 s and 1007 s; the same leg took 553 s on an unloaded run earlier. Each push was a branch off develop `28dac5c12ba5` carrying a two-file change that touches neither suite. Both pushes were refused, `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14 - (13/16 legs ran)`, every other leg passing.

`check_shared_relink.test.sh` (push started 00:47:52Z, `shell suites: 90 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 92)`):

```
.../scripts/__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh: line 49: printf: write error: Broken pipe
  FAIL: F-6 inv: distroless nodejs is DENIED (exit correct, WRONG rule fired — wanted /a JavaScript runtime/)
        ::error::./services/thing/Dockerfile — re-link invariant (KS-921): final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but its base image is `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22-debian12`, a JavaScript runtime, ...
  111 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped
```

The captured output printed under the FAIL line contains the wanted text, so the rule fired and the grade was wrong. Line 49 is `if [ -n "$want_out" ] && ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$want_out"; then`.

`ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` (push started 00:49:30Z, `shell suites: 89 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 91)`):

```
.../scripts/__tests__/ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh: line 68: printf: write error: Broken pipe
FAIL CONTROL no slot named: the banner shows the historic 6882 and 6881
       want "yes yes"
        got "no yes"
ks1355_slot_blind_launchers: 22 passed, 1 failed
```

Line 68 is the helper `saw() { if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qF -- "$1"; then echo yes; else echo no; fi; }`.

## Measured on a quiet machine

* `check_shared_relink.test.sh`, 10 consecutive runs, hermetic env (`env -i HOME PATH`), load about 4.5, tree `6bb63146affd` (develop `28dac5c12ba5` plus one two-file branch): **10 of 10 passed, 112 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe".**
* `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh`, 5 consecutive runs, same env, load 3.5 to 4.9, tree `b5767aa4c527` (tree identical to develop `28dac5c12ba5`): **5 of 5 passed, 23 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe".**

## Not measured

The failure was not reproduced under load: no deliberate stress was run (it would have disturbed live pushes), so there is no measured failure rate under load. Only two failures were seen, one per suite, in one window. The mechanism is inferred from the shape: `grep -q` exits at its first match, a `printf` still writing to that pipe gets EPIPE, and `pipefail` turns the pipeline's status into failure, so a MATCH is graded as no match. It is a race between two processes, which fits "only when the machine is slow".

## The census, and its frame

`git grep -n -E 'printf [^|]*\| *grep -q'` at commit `28dac5c12ba5c00d9fc3ad04daee5230eff71619`, pathspecs `Blockchain/Dev/scripts` and `systemTest`, excluding `node_modules`: **150 lines in 29 files** (22 under `__tests__`, 7 product scripts); 26 of the 29 files mention `pipefail`. `check_shared_relink.test.sh` holds 13 of the lines, `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` 1. Not counted: 12 `echo ... | grep -q` lines (the sibling shape); other pipe-to-early-exit-reader shapes (`| head`, `| grep -m1`); any directory outside the two pathspecs. The count says nothing about which of the 150 can actually be hit: it is the number of lines with the shape.

## Siblings

* KS-1716 (In Progress): the same defect class in one script, `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh`, where the large-input case silently dropped a package. Not these suites.
* KS-1149 (Backlog, archived): a different cause of a similar-looking push failure (`rc 141` after the gate PASSED; GitHub closes the idle ssh session). Not this one: here the hook itself refuses with `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14`.

## Searched before filing (board, title and description, archived included)

`check_shared_relink` (KS-956, KS-948, KS-937: the guard itself, not this flake); `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers` (KS-1558: gate follow-ups); `write error: Broken pipe` and `Broken pipe` (KS-1716 only); `grep -q` (KS-1716, KS-1624, KS-1134, KS-998, KS-912, KS-469); `pipefail` (8 hits, none about these suites); `EPIPE` (KS-1716, KS-1598); `SIGPIPE` (KS-1716, KS-1583, KS-1149). The terms `Broken pipe`, `EPIPE` and `SIGPIPE` all find KS-1716, so the search can see this class. No open ticket names either suite as flaking.

## Update 2026-10-26 02:20Z: a third suite, at moderate load, and a measurement that weakens the first explanation

**Third occurrence.** A third push was refused at leg 14 with the same tell. Push of the KS-1513 branch, started 01:53:06Z, ended `rc 1` after 1081 s: `shell suites: 90 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 92)`, FAILED `preflight_deps.test.sh`, which printed

```
.../scripts/__tests__/preflight_deps.test.sh: line 443: printf: write error: Broken pipe
.../scripts/__tests__/preflight_deps.test.sh: line 444: printf: write error: Broken pipe
FAIL KS-1638: that refusal SHORT-CIRCUITS — a red suite present, still not run
       want "HOOKCTL-REFUSED/1", got "OTHER/1"
preflight_deps: 60 passed, 1 failed
```

Lines 443 and 444 are consecutive `elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q '...'` verdict tests; in this cell the text for 443 (`could not derive the pre-push hook's own control`) sits at byte 1871 and the text for 444 (`de-slotted`) at byte 1821 of `$out`, so both match early and both pipelines failed, which sent the cell to the `OTHER` verdict. **This one was NOT in the 60 to 98 load window:** leg 14 took 662 s (against 553 s unloaded), and my readings of the 1-minute load average over the push were between 4.0 and 13.

**Quiet-box runs of this suite:** 6 of 6 passed on that exact tree (`716e26290155`, 61 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe"), load about 6.

**What the measurement does to the explanation.** Using the suite's own `PREFLIGHT_FIXTURE_OUT` capture on the failing cell, `$out` is **2848 bytes**, 62 lines. That is far below the macOS pipe buffer (`st_blksize` 16384), so a single `write()` of it cannot meet a closed reader. The "large output, early match" form of the race is therefore NOT what happened here; for it to occur, bash 3.2's `printf` would have to deliver the string to `grep` in several small writes. I tried to reproduce that on the real captured output: 3 runs of 3000 iterations of `set -uo pipefail; printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "could not derive the pre-push hook's own control"`, load about 8 to 10, **0 of 9000 reported no-match.** Not reproduced.

**Tally of pushes of mine that reached leg 14 since 00:43Z:** 6; refused by this tell: 3 (the KS-1391 and KS-1560 first attempts, and the KS-1513 push above); passed: 3 (the KS-1560 and KS-1391 second attempts, and KS-1289). A seventh push, KS-1716, ran no preflight leg. The refused ones were three different suites. So the suites are sometimes fragile on this machine under contention from several simultaneous preflights; the mechanism is unproven.

title: kintsugi lost demo-service to the KS-641 fail-closed gate — the flag is unset on BOTH boxes and enabling it is a one-line decision with no owner
description:
**BLUF — kintsugi served** `demo-service` **for 20 hours and now refuses to start it. That is KS-641's fail-closed gate working correctly, not a bug. The point of this ticket is that the box lost a running service and the decision to restore it has no owner.**

Found during the s169 whole-estate rebuild of kintsugi (KS-601, under Kam's 2026-09-10 15:24 AEST ruling).

## What changed

|  | before the rebuild | after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-demo-service` on kintsugi | `Up 20 hours (healthy)` (measured 05:35Z) | `restarting`**, exit 1, 18 restarts** |
| image | `62fb55bf4fa1` (2026-08-19) | `c4823b0d2fc1` (2026-09-10) |

Log, every restart:

```
FATAL: DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly "true" to run demo-service.
This is a deliberate opt-in, not a default — refusing to start.
```

**The swap itself succeeded** — the container is on the new image. The service declines to start.

## Why — and why it is not a regression in the code

**KS-641** ("inbound auth + fail-closed non-prod gate on demo-service") introduced the gate. `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` is **unset on both kintsugi and demo**. The old image kintsugi was running had no such check, which is why it served for 20 hours — *it ran because the gate did not exist yet, which is the defect KS-641 fixed, not a capability that was lost.*

On **demo** this is the status quo, already recorded in the s168 handover as *"a deliberate opt-in guard working as designed"*. **On kintsugi it is new**, because kintsugi was three weeks behind and had never received KS-641.

## The decision, and why it is deliberately not taken here

`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` **stays OFF** — ruled 2026-09-10, on three grounds: it matches demo (and Kam ruled the same day that *"everything that we do this week is replicated and fixed on both servers"*, making parity an instruction); OFF is the gate's own intent as a fail-closed opt-in; and OFF is the branch that requires no signature, since enabling a fail-closed non-prod auth gate is a config change with a security shape.

**So this ticket is not a request to flip the flag.** It exists because a service that was serving is now not, on both boxes, and *"enabling it is a one-line change nobody has decided to make"* is precisely the kind of state that gets rediscovered by accident weeks later.

## What is needed

1. **A decision with a stated reason** on whether `demo-service` should run on either box at all — or a decision that it should not, recorded so the next rebuild does not re-raise this.
2. If it should run: set `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED=true` in that box's `.env` (gitignored, so this is a per-box config action, not a code change) and recreate the container.

## Note on classification, recorded because it cost a correction

This was initially reported as *"the known demo-service down"*. **That classification was borrowed from the s168 record of DEMO and applied to KINTSUGI, a different box, where nothing had established it.** The mechanism was evidenced; the *expectation* was not. Flagged here so the distinction survives: on demo this is status quo, on kintsugi it is a state change.

⚠ The rebuild did not hide it — the swap ran with an exception keyed to the **failure signature** (`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly`), not the service name, so the same service failing for any other reason still halts the run. Every hit is recorded in `.rebuild/blocked.txt` on the box.

title: vc-issuer: GET /api/credentials (list) and GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash return credentials the caller did not create - KS-1116 bound only the two /:id reads
description:
## BLUF

**Any authenticated caller can read every stored credential through** `GET /api/credentials` **(list), and any credential by its document hash through** `GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash`**.** KS-1116 binds `GET /api/credentials/:id` and `GET /api/presentations/:id` to the principal that created the row. These two routes were deliberately left out of that change, because Platform S may call them and that could not be measured from Platform K. **KS-1116 does not close the credential exposure; this ticket holds the rest of it.**

## What was measured (develop `937c7d10b`, `services/vc-issuer/src`)

* `GET /api/credentials` (list): `routes/credentials.ts:233-262` → `credentialRepo.list` (`repositories/credentialRepo.ts:139-205`). The filters are caller-supplied query parameters (`issuer`, `documentType`, `limit`, `offset`). With none supplied the WHERE clause is empty and up to `limit` full credential bodies come back, newest first. There is no owner condition on the DB path or the memory path.
* `GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash`: `routes/credentials.ts:367` → `getByHash` (`credentialRepo.ts:114-131`), `WHERE credential->'credentialSubject'->>'documentHash' = $1 LIMIT 1`, with no ORDER BY and no owner condition.
* Both routes sit behind vc-issuer's `jwtAuthenticate` (`index.ts:86-92`), and neither is in its `publicOps`. So this is a cross-principal read by an authenticated caller, not anonymous access.
* **A connector can reach both today.** The gateway mounts `/api/credentials` with `authenticateToken(false)`. Its x-api-key branch mints a connector JWT from a validated key and attaches it (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:311`, `:355-375`, `:474`), and vc-issuer accepts that JWT.
* Rows today (read-only counts, 2026-10-20): `vc_credentials_store` holds 0 rows on demo and 0 on kintsugi.
* In-repo consumers: none. Nothing in `frontend/` calls `/api/credentials` (control: the same search finds `api/` in 3+ frontend files). Outside vc-issuer, `by-hash` for this route appears only in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:38665`; anchoring's `verify-by-hash` is a different route.

## Why it was not bound in KS-1116

The Platform S repository is not visible to the Platform K project's GitHub identity. `GET repos/Secuura/platform-s` answers 404 to that token, while `GET repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura` answers 200 on the same token, and the token can list exactly one repository. So whether Platform S calls either route is **unmeasured**, not "no".

Under the KS-1116 rule a connector would see only the rows its own connector principal created. If Platform S reads credentials that users created, binding these routes breaks it.

## Open question

Does Platform S call GET /api/credentials or GET /api/credentials/by-hash, and if so for credentials created by whom?

## When it is answered

* The KS-1116 rule (`services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts`, `mayRead`) applies to both routes.
* `list` needs the owner condition in its SQL **and** on every returned record, so that pagination and `total` stay correct and the memory fallback is bound too.
* `by-hash` should return the first credential the caller may read, not the first match. With `LIMIT 1` and no ORDER BY, a caller's own credential could otherwise be hidden behind someone else's.

## Provenance

Measured by Seat C 30th on 2026-10-20 while building KS-1116. Filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-10-20 07:21 AEDT (option b: ship the two `/:id` bounds, file list + by-hash as a High follow-up).

title: services/vc-issuer test files cannot use a top-level await: the enrolled type-check refuses it with TS1378 under module: commonjs, foreclosing the module-scope fix shape
description:
## BLUF

**A test file in** `services/vc-issuer` **cannot use a top-level** `await`**.** The service compiles
`module: commonjs` / `target: es2021`, and its enrolled test-file type-check
(`tsconfig.test.json`, read by `scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs`) therefore reports **TS1378**
for one. That forecloses a fix shape KS 1729 explicitly sanctions — doing an expensive import
once at module scope, so the cost falls at collection where there is no hook timeout.

Filed on the coordinator's ruling, facts only. **No fix is proposed here**: the trade-off is
named below and belongs to whoever owns the service's compile target.

## Measured

At develop `8661f5d418b23ffb0c63a2504d707eb12189b5ad`, adding one `await freshModules();` at
module scope in each of three test files, then running
`node scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs services/vc-issuer` from `Blockchain/Dev`:

**rc 1**, one error per file, verbatim:

```
src/__tests__/ks1020-presentation-lookup-exact-or-404.test.ts(91,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
src/__tests__/ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts(192,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
src/__tests__/ks1683-credential-list-and-by-hash-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts(134,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
```

Without that line the same command is **rc 0** ("tsc examined 33 files, 19 of them under
`__tests__`; 0 errors: 0 in the baseline, 0 new; 0 stale baseline entries").

**Note the asymmetry:** vitest runs such a file fine — only the type-check refuses it. So the
pattern is available at runtime and unavailable under the gate.

## The config lines

`services/vc-issuer/tsconfig.json`:

* `"module": "commonjs"`
* `"target": "es2021"`

`services/vc-issuer/tsconfig.test.json` (what the ratchet reads) adds nothing relevant — it is:

```json
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}
```

So the refusal comes from the **service's own** compile settings, inherited by the test config.
It is not specific to the ratchet, and it applies to every service enrolled the same way.

## The trade-off, named not resolved

* Raising `module`/`target` **only in** `tsconfig.test.json` would unblock the pattern without
  touching the service build, since that config is `noEmit` — but it makes the test program's
  module semantics differ from the shipped code's, which is the kind of divergence a type-check
  exists to prevent.
* Raising them in `tsconfig.json` keeps test and source aligned but **changes the service's**
  **emit**, which is a real change to shipped output.
* Leaving it means the module-scope shape stays unavailable and callers reach for a per-hook
  timeout instead — which is what KS 1729 did, deliberately, with the reason written in-file.

## Related, NOT a duplicate

**KS 1329** — `packages/shared` does not type-check `src/__tests__`. It is the only other open
issue naming `TS1378`, and it was read before filing rather than matched on the token:

* It concerns `packages/shared`, not `services/vc-issuer`.
* Its subject is test files being **excluded** from the type-check, hiding 10 errors.
* Its TS1378 appear as **probe artefacts** — it raises `module`/`target` in an out-of-repo probe
  precisely because that package's tests **already use** top-level `await`, and says leaving
  them at `commonjs` produces "9x TS1343 and 5x TS1378 that are artefacts of the probe".

That makes KS 1329 evidence the same constraint bites elsewhere, with the opposite symptom:
there the tests already use the pattern and are simply never type-checked; here they are
type-checked and the pattern is refused.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **705** open Secuura-PK issues:

* `TS1378` -> **1** (KS 1329, above).
* `top-level await` -> 0. `top-level 'await'` -> 0.
* `module: commonjs` -> 0. `"module": "commonjs"` -> 0.
* `tsconfig.test.json` -> 4 (KS 1554, KS 1494, KS 1090, KS 1000) — all about enrolment, none
  about this refusal.

Controls showing the instrument finds known tickets: `Hook timed out in 10000ms` -> 4,
`exceed vitest's 5 s default` -> 4, `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT` -> 3.

## Found by

Seat S 2nd while building KS 1729 (pull request 1714), 2026-10-26. The module-scope shape was
built first, measured as above, and reverted in full — the three files were verified
byte-identical to develop afterwards. Measured on Node v26.8.1.

title: Security: a write-role caller can make another organisation's bytes verify CERTIFIED under a certifiedBy they choose, via the lineage path (parentDocumentId): no parent access check, and the derived row's content_hash is the caller's data.contentHash
description:
**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane; decide the fix, then build it test-first):** any write-role caller in a tenant can make another organisation's bytes verify as CERTIFIED, under an issuer name the caller chooses, through the LINEAGE path of `POST /api/certifications/issue` (`parentDocumentId` set). **No build is started by this ticket; the gate's measurement and fix-thinking are quoted below.**

## What the gate measured (Opus tier-1 gate of PR #1525, KS-1538; real routes, real Postgres, as `secuura_app`, single-tenant and pool mode, identical on base and head)

1. Org B's user registers bytes with hash H. `POST /api/verification/verify {contentHash: H}` returns `checks.isCertified: false` and no `certification`.
2. Org A's user calls `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `{type: 'verification_certificate', parentDocumentId: <B's doc OR A's OWN doc>, data: {title, contentHash: H, issuedBy: 'Org B Official Registrar'}}` and gets 201.
3. Verify of H (anonymous, and as B) now returns `checks.isCertified: true` and `certification.certifiedBy: "Org B Official Registrar"` with `certifierOrganizationId: null`. With B's document as the parent, B's document also gains a `newerVersions` entry owned by A. B's own row is untouched.

## Two independent causes

* **(a) No access check on** `parentDocumentId`**.** `certifications.ts:412-431` checks only for cycles, and `saveDocument` resolves the parent by `external_id` within the tenant (`documentRepo.ts:419-450`).
* **(b) The derived row's** `content_hash` **is taken from the caller's** `data.contentHash` (`certifications.ts:564-567`). `siblingCertification` (`verification.ts:220-236`) then treats any same-hash `signed` row carrying a `certificationId` as certification evidence for those bytes.
* **A parent access check alone would NOT close it.** The gate's ITEM5c control uses the CALLER'S OWN document as the parent and the other organisation's hash H: (b) alone is enough.

## Fix-shape the gate offers (the owner decides)

Require the same access predicate on the parent (the rule `GET /api/documents/:id` enforces, as KS-1538 now applies on the legacy path), AND bind the derived row's hash to the parent's stored hash instead of the caller's `data`. Regression test for the owner: the ITEM5c shape (A's own parent, B's hash), asserting that verify of H stays `isCertified: false`.

## Scope and status

* **Pre-existing, and PR #1525 (KS-1538) does not make it worse**: base and head behave identically on this path, and the KS-1538 guard is skipped by design when `parentDocumentId` is set. **KS-1538 does NOT close cross-organisation certification; this ticket is the open half.** Before KS-1538 the legacy path reached the same outcome more directly.
* Not measured: cross-tenant verify (the verify calls carried the tenant of the certifier); the real gateway, real JWT and real anchoring service (the principal was header-injected, anchoring was a local stub).
* Line numbers are the gate's, at the head of PR #1525. Gate evidence: the probe cells ITEM5 and ITEM5c and `matrix_table.md` in the gate's evidence folder for PR #1525 (verdict sha256/16 `0273b5bb14d3f036`).
* Related, read and distinguished: KS-563 (verify said `isCertified` for merely-anchored documents; its narrowing is why `siblingCertification` exists) and KS-549 (issuer name not persisted). Neither covers a caller choosing the certifier name or the hash.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "siblingCertification", "lineage path parentDocumentId certification access check", "certifications.ts contentHash derived row verify certified", "isCertified another organisation's bytes certifiedBy issuedBy", "verification.ts siblingCertification content_hash certificationId" and "parentDocumentId no access check cross-organisation". 282 distinct issues read. Literal matches in title or description: `siblingcertification` 0, `data.contenthash` 0. Three issues matched two or more of the seven distinctive tokens (KS-549, PS-544, PS-549); I read KS-549 and KS-563 and none covers this. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked, so this is "none in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), verdict GO WITH NOTE, finding S-1; Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:01Z) that it is filed as its own High ticket now.

title: ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts: the 10 s beforeAll hook lapses under fleet load, SKIPS all 21 cells, and then throws a misleading TypeError in afterAll
description:
Found while building KS-1598 round 1, not while looking for it: `npx vitest run` in `services/security` came back **2 failed / 341 passed**, and neither failure was in anything I had touched. Recorded here rather than left in a session log, per the workspace never-skip rule. **Nothing is being called flaky on a hunch — the measurements are below.**

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/__tests__/ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts`

* `beforeAll` at `:108`
* `afterAll` at `:125`, which is where the confusing message comes from

## What happens

Under load the `beforeAll` exceeds its hook timeout:

```
Error: Hook timed out in 10000ms.
 ❯ src/__tests__/ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts:108:3
```

`server` is then never assigned, so `afterAll` dereferences it:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'close')
 ❯ src/__tests__/ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts:125:47
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()));
```

**The run reports** `1 failed` **with** `21 skipped`**.** Zero cells executed. The headline failure a reader sees is the `TypeError` about `close`, which points at teardown and says nothing about the hook that actually lapsed. In the full suite the same load shows up differently again — a 5 s per-test timeout on the repo-walk cell at `:521` and a `fetch failed / ECONNRESET` at `:597` — so the same root cause wears three different faces.

## Measured, with the load named

| run | scope | load average (1 min) | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full security unit suite | **11.12** | 2 failed / 341 passed — the `:521` timeout and the `:597` ECONNRESET |
| 2 | this file alone | \~11 | **1 failed, 21 SKIPPED** — the `beforeAll` lapse, 0 cells executed |
| 3 | this file alone | — | 21 passed, rc 0 |
| 4 | full security unit suite | **8.21** | 31 files / **343 passed**, rc 0 |
| 5 | full security unit suite | 8.21 | 31 files / **343 passed**, rc 0 |

Other seats on this machine were running their own vitest and jest suites throughout. So: the file passes alone, the suite passes twice at the lower load, and the failures appear only at the higher load. The failing hook is in a file my change does not touch, and the failure is a **hook timeout** — a function of wall time, not of content.

## Why it matters

A 0-executed run is reported as a *failed file*, not as a run that never started. A reader (or a gate) comparing "31 files / 343" against "1 failed / 21 skipped" has to notice the word `skipped` to tell the difference between a regression and a file that never booted. That is the same class of trap as a mutation kill whose red cells carry empty messages.

It also makes the suite's verdict depend on who else is on the box, which is exactly what a push-time gate must not do.

## Fix shapes, none chosen here

* Give the hook an explicit budget sized for fleet load (the convention in this repo for the 5 s-default class is a per-file `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout`), rather than leaving it on the default.
* Make `afterAll` tolerate an unassigned `server` so the reported failure names the hook that lapsed instead of the teardown that could not run.
* Optionally: assert in `afterAll` that `beforeAll` completed, so a 0-executed run says so in its own words.

## Related, and NOT duplicates

* **KS-1155** — `packages/shared` tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under fleet load. Same class, different files.
* **KS-1328** — `services/kyc` `db.retry.test.ts`, same class.
* **KS-1521** — the budget wording and the governance source-text pin. Touches the timeout convention, not this file.
* **KS-743** and **KS-742** concern the route contract this file tests, not its harness.

## Provenance

* Deduped before filing: 325 distinct issues read across 6 search terms with comments and archived included; the token `ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract` hit **KS-743** and **KS-1521**, both of which were read and neither of which covers the hook timeout. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9b-bf367a4ef9ff` → 0 hits; positive control → 1.
* Logs: `5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatV-9th/logs/sec_unit.log` (the red), `ks742_alone_1.log` (the 21-skipped run), `ks742_alone_2.log`, `sec_unit_2.log`, `sec_unit_3.log` (343/343).
* Filed by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13.

title: KS-1533 follow-up (#1521 gate): the key list compares a raw organisation id with the canonical stored one, and normaliseOrgId leaves {uuid}, no-hyphen and zero-width forms
description:
**BLUF:** The #1521 (KS-1533 arm 1) fix-round-1 Opus delta gate returned GO WITH NOTE: 0 Major, 2 Minor (verdict sha256/16 `c5d59b0e54f23775`, head `e4d7a13e`). This is the one P3 follow-up Wednesday's GO requires. Both Minors come from the stored-form change (#1521's m1): the row now stores a canonical organisation id, but the list compares the raw query, and the normaliser leaves some non-canonical forms intact.

**Context:** Lines are on #1521's head `e4d7a13e`, which is what lands on develop. Neither item changes a status code today, and org-bounded roles fail safe on both.

- [ ] **(a) m1-r1:** `GET /api/keys` **compares the RAW query value with the now-canonical stored value.**
  * Where: `services/security/src/index.ts:1200` (`.filter(k => k.organizationId === organizationId)`).
  * Symptom (the gate measured): listing with your own organisation id in UPPER case returns 0 keys at `e4d7a13e`, against 6 on the old head. Before #1521 the mismatch ran the other way: a key minted with a padded or upper-case id was invisible under the canonical id. Low likelihood, since callers send canonical lower-case uuids.
- [ ] **(b) m2-r1:** `normaliseOrgId` **(trim, lower-case, blank = absent) leaves some non-canonical forms intact, and they are stored verbatim.**
  * Where: `index.ts:1096` (`organizationId: normaliseOrgId(data.organizationId)`); the schema is `organizationId: z.string().optional()` at `:455` / `:481`.
  * Symptom (the gate measured): `{uuid}` with braces, the no-hyphen 32-hex form, and a uuid with a leading zero-width space all store as sent, for platform, `ADMIN` and provisioner callers. Org-bounded roles are refused (the arm compares normalised ids, which do not match), so they fail safe.
- [ ] **The gate's one fix for both:** validate the POST body's `organizationId` with `z.string().trim().uuid()` (a 400 for anything else; blank stays "absent", per KS-764's one-representation rule), and normalise the list query the same way before comparing. Cells: an upper-case own id in the list query returns that organisation's keys; each of the three forms on the POST answers 400 and writes nothing.

**Overlap: KS-1514 item 2** asks to enforce `format: uuid` on the same list query (`GET /api/security/keys?organizationId=`), which is declared but not enforced. Validating the query as a uuid serves both, so build (a) and KS-1514 (2) together. KS-1514 item 1 (the `{keys}` vs `{success,data}` envelope) is separate. The class is KS-1022 (the id-format contract seam).

**Still open elsewhere, NOT this ticket:** originate's admin mint, Path 1's sibling (comment on KS-1533); the concurrent-rotate zero (KS-1549, P1, which the gate re-measured at 0 of 21).

**Dedupe (2026-10-13):** title and description searched for normaliseOrgId, /api/keys, api/security/keys, "organizationId uuid", "organizationId's uuid", uuid() and zero-width.

* Hits: KS-1152, KS-1536, KS-1514, KS-1283 (Done), KS-1377, KS-1370, KS-888, KS-1174, PS-851, KS-869, KS-619, KS-1042, KS-870, KS-748, KS-1549, KS-1535, KS-747 (Done), KS-1434 (Done), KS-188, KS-1361 (Done), KS-908, KS-1544, KS-679 (Done), KS-1435, KS-256, KS-1157, KS-1022, KS-1107, PS-1065, PS-1031, PS-1028.
* None covers (a) or (b). KS-1514 (2) is adjacent, as above, and was read in full.

Refs KS-1533, PR #1521.

title: Gateway mount-auth check scores authenticateToken(false) as green — six /api mounts satisfy neither leg of its own assertion
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-570 mount-auth check scores** `authenticateToken(false)` **as green, so six** `/api` **subtree mounts pass an assertion they do not actually satisfy.** Raised by Peter reviewing PR #730; **pre-existing on** `develop`**, not #730's doing and not its job to fix.** The fix is small — tag `authed` only when `required === true` — but the value is in whatever the retag then surfaces.

## Mechanism

`collectMounts`'s mock adds the middleware to `authTagged` regardless of the `required` argument, so `authenticateToken(false)` reads as `authed: true`. But `(false)` calls `next()` for a caller carrying no `Authorization` header at all (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:317-323`).

The guard's assertion is *"every /api mount either requires auth or is public by design with a stated reason"*. These mounts satisfy **neither** leg: they require nothing, and they are recorded in no by-design allowlist.

## The six, measured — not adopted

Measured at PR #730's head `3fe1b6f1a` (Peter's ref) and again on `develop 9b89f4fce`, comment lines excluded:

| mount | `proxy.ts` @ `3fe1b6f1a` | `proxy.ts` @ `develop 9b89f4fce` | state |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/certifications` | 521 | 521 | **defended** — `attachScopes` + `requireScope('certifications:read','certifications:write')` follow |
| `/api/credentials` | 703 | 703 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/referrals` | 786 | 777 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/governance` | 875 | 861 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/nft` | 892 | 878 | handler, then `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/billing` | 941 | 927 | straight to `proxy(...)` |

⚠ **A naive grep returns SEVEN on both refs.** The extra hit is a comment — the KS-442 note reading *"*`/api/credentials` *is already authenticateToken(false), its 401 came from the service"*. Excluding comment lines gives six on both refs, matching Peter's list exactly. Anyone re-running this should exclude comments or they will chase a mount that does not exist.

`/api/status` is deliberately **not** in this list: on `develop` it carries no auth middleware at all, and PR #730 gives it `authenticateToken(true)`.

## What is NOT established

**The anonymous-caller half is unmeasured.** Peter could not probe it (no Docker available to him) and inferred from the signature-only `authenticate()` in `@secuura/shared` that an anonymous caller would most likely 401 downstream. **That inference has not been tested and must be measured before any severity is stated on this ticket.**

Two things keep this below KS-570's severity, and it is worth being exact rather than alarming:

* the revocation check runs **before** the `required` branch, so when a token IS present, `(false)` does still catch a revoked session — the KS-570 class is genuinely covered by these mounts;
* five of the six go straight to a service that may well enforce its own auth.

## Done means

1. `collectMounts` tags `authed` only when `required === true`.
2. Each of the six is then either given real auth, or recorded in the by-design allowlist **with a stated reason** (the `/api/certifications` one is already effectively defended by `requireScope` and may only need recording).
3. **The anonymous-caller behaviour of each is measured, with a control**, before any of them is called safe.

## Two smaller notes from the same review, accepted for later, not fixed now

* `authed` is `layers.some(...)`, so it asserts the middleware is **present**, not **ordered before** the proxy.
* The `> 40` floor sits against a corpus of roughly 62, so it catches total collapse but not the loss of a third.

*Filed from PR #730's review (Peter's item 2), 2026-09-01. He offered to file it himself; filed from our notes at his suggestion since the probe setup is here.*

title: GET /api/webhooks swallows a FAILED list query into 200 with an empty list - a DB failure reads as 'no webhooks'
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/webhooks` swallows a **failed** list query into `200 {"success":true,"webhooks":[]}`, so a database failure is indistinguishable from "this organisation has no webhooks" — to the client and, on one of the two routes, to the log as well. Pre-existing; PR #1288's `control KS-1341 A0` currently **pins this as intended behaviour, which it is not.**

## The measurement

* `routes/webhooks.ts:196`: the list query carries `.catch((e: any) => { logger.warn('webhooks list query failed', { error: e?.message }); return []; })`. A rejected `$queryRaw` never reaches the catch under test; `fail500` is never called. Reproduced in all four `NODE_ENV` values by the gate28 probe.
* **The code's own comment records the harm.** `:187-190` (the KS-466 note) says a missing `::uuid` cast raised 42883 and "was silently swallowed by the `.catch` below, so this list ALWAYS returned `[]` (a pre-existing bug, independent of RLS)". The swallow hid a real defect once already.
* `GET /:id/deliveries` has the same shape at `:412` — `.catch(() => [])` — **with no log at all**, so that one is silent even server-side.

## Fix shape

Drop the `.catch` on both list queries so a rejection reaches the router's `fail500`: the thrown text logged server-side with the route named, and a constant 500 to the client.

## Regression cell

Flip `control KS-1341 A0` in `ks1341a-webhooks-500-never-answers-err-message.test.ts` from "swallowed into 200 `[]`" to expect **500 + the constant body + the logger call**. That cell exists today and asserts the opposite, so it is the pin that must move with the fix — it is deliberately recorded here so the change is not read as a regression.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1332 issues (includeArchived) and 3776 comments**: `webhooks list query failed` -> 0, `GET /:id/deliveries` -> 0, `ks1341a-webhooks-500` -> 0. Control token `b31nonce-zqx7vk-never-written` -> 0; the same scan finds `RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md` in 5 issues, so it is not blind.

## Provenance

Gate28 report `2026-09-26-batch1286-g28/report.md` (sha256 `760c86711baee5a5…`), note N-1288-3, MEASURED. Related to KS-1341 (the router whose 500s part A converted), not a sub-task of it.

Refs KS-1341

title: platform_audit_log is paged without a tie-break (ORDER BY created_at DESC only): windowed reads can repeat or skip rows that share a timestamp
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/audit-log` in tenant-provisioning pages `platform_audit_log` with `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2` and **no tie-break column**. Two rows with the same `created_at` have no defined relative order, and Postgres does not promise the same order across two separate queries. That was harmless while the gateway read the platform half in ONE request; once the gateway reads it in sequential windows (PR for KS-1512), a group of rows sharing a timestamp that straddles a window boundary can be **duplicated or skipped** on a deep page. Reasoned from the SQL and the schema; **not measured, and not seen in any data**.

## Recommendation

P4, one line in `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` (the table has `id UUID PRIMARY KEY` in both definitions). The existing index `idx_platform_audit_time` is on `created_at DESC` only, so check the plan before and after on a table of realistic size. Test first: a stub or a real table with more than 200 rows sharing one `created_at`, read in two windows, asserting no id appears twice and none is missing. It changes another service than the gateway, which is why KS-1512 did not do it.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:558` (at develop `425ad3e00ae4`): `SELECT * FROM platform_audit_log ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2`. Schema: `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:119-129` and `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/003_platform_tenancy.sql:49-59`, both with `id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` and `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()`.
* **Why a tie is plausible, not just theoretical:** `now()` is the transaction start time, so several rows inserted in one transaction share the same `created_at` to the microsecond. Whether any code path writes several `platform_audit_log` rows in one transaction I have **not checked** (the four inserts at `index.ts:283, 415, 469, 537` are separate statements; their transaction boundaries were not read).
* **A second, unrelated effect of windowed reads:** a row inserted between two windows shifts the later window by one, so one row can repeat. The old single request had neither effect. Both are rare and bounded to the deep pages (limit + offset above 200).
* **Related:** KS-1512 (the windowed read), KS-1359 (the route's bounds).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles AND descriptions in team KS, archived included: `tie-break` 0, `ORDER BY created_at` 1 (KS-1072, the latest-anchor selector, a different table and defect), `platform_audit_log` 1 (KS-1512 itself, whose description has no `tie`, `order by` or `duplicate`: 0, 0, 0; the same grep finds `overfetch` and `clamp` in it, so it can read that text). The same instrument returns KS-1512 for a phrase from its own title, so it can see ticket text.

title: Azure template: no deploy path supplies EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET (services.bicep:139 defaults to '', so both apps boot fail-closed); the vouch's twin gap is KS-1083
description:
**What is missing:** on the Container Apps (Azure template) path, no tracked deploy entry point supplies `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET`. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1690 (KS-1717), round 1, Minor 1.

**The facts, at PR #1690's head** `dfc89078979b`**:**

* `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/services.bicep:139` is `param emitterSigningSecret string = ''`. The two apps wire `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET` ONLY when that param is non-empty (originate and anchoring, both conditional).
* A grep of every tracked file names the param or the variable in only four places: `services.bicep`, the two env templates, and `docker-compose.yml:618` and `:1327`. Excluded from that grep: service source, `packages/`, tests and docs. That leaves no deploy script (`deployment/azure/*.sh`, including `deploy.sh`, `deploy-all.sh` and `setup-keyvault.sh`), no workflow under `.github/workflows/` (including `deploy-demo.yml`) and no parameters file.
* So a Container Apps deploy from this template boots both services with the variable UNSET. By design that is **fail-closed**: anchoring honours no `x-emitter-internal` marker and logs `[emitter-guard] FAIL-CLOSED …` at boot. Each connector-initiated create, share, transfer-custody, revoke or lifecycle call then writes one extra `anchor` provenance row.
* **Not measured live:** the Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31, so this is the template only.

**The same gap for the sibling secret, already recorded:** `services.bicep:131` is `param gatewayVouchSecret string = ''`, and the same grep finds no deploy entry point that passes it. KS-1083 already records that *"no tracked deploy, bootstrap or CI path supplies"* `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`. That half is KS-1083's; it is named here only so the two are fixed together if that is the cheaper route.

**Where the secret IS supplied:** the compose path that kintsugi and demo run. `docker-compose.yml` passes `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET` from the box's `.env` to originate (`:618`) and anchoring (`:1327`), and `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` to api-gateway and originate (`:452`, `:610`). The KS-1717 deploy round sets it there. **This ticket is the Azure template only.**

**Searched first:** `emitterSigningSecret` (0 hits) and `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET` (only KS-1726, which names it as a sibling and not this gap). `deploy-demo.yml` and `setup-keyvault.sh` turned up only generic mentions, plus KS-1083 for the vouch. title: No frontend declares a `test` script — six package.json files, none with one, so the issuer's vitest setup and its 12 component assertions are unreachable from any runner
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/frontend/` has nine directories, six of them with a `package.json`, and **not one declares a** `test` **script**. The root workspace runner is `"test": "npm run test --workspaces"` (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:17`), so it cannot reach them. The issuer went further than the others — it has `vitest` + `@testing-library/react` + `jsdom` in devDependencies, a `test:` block in `vite.config.ts:8-12`, and two real spec files carrying 12 assertions — and none of it can be run without typing a `vitest` invocation by hand. This is unit/component coverage only; the portals themselves are covered by the e2e-v2 browser tier, which has its own problem (`KS-1390`). Read from the tree on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Every `scripts` block under `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/package.json`:

| Frontend | `scripts` | Test files present |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `admin` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `issuer` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `check:bundle` | **2** (`blockchain-card.test.tsx`, `provenance-timeline.test.tsx`) |
| `verifier` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `website` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `outlook-addin` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `demo-overlay` | `build`, `dev` | 0 |
| `status`, `gmail-addon`, `shared` | no `package.json` | 0 |

So the two issuer specs are dead weight: present, maintained-looking, and executed by nothing. `frontend/issuer/vite.config.ts:8-12` configures the vitest environment for them, which makes it look deliberate rather than abandoned — the missing piece is one line in `package.json`.

## Why it matters

* **It is a silent zero.** `npm run test --workspaces` at `Blockchain/Dev` looks like it covers the workspaces, and `frontend/*` is a workspace glob (`package.json:6-10`). A reader has no signal that the frontend leg of that command is empty.
* **It is the same class already ticketed one layer down.** `KS-634` (Backlog) — *"No CI gate runs the services' unit suites — a 73-test suite sat dead on develop and every PR stayed green"* — and `KS-652` (Backlog) — *"1219 tests across 23 services are ungated"*. Those are about services having suites nothing runs; this is frontends having no suite to run, plus one that exists and cannot be reached. Same failure mode, opposite end.
* **The precedent for cost is in the repo.** `KS-649` had 31 auth tests dead since 6 Aug because two suites failed at module load and reported "no tests"; `KS-718` had golden-master snapshots gitignored, so a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed. Tests that cannot fail are worse than absent — they read as coverage.
* Four shipped admin pages import types from `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` (`DocumentTypes.tsx:20`, `DocumentTypeDetail.tsx:22`, `VerificationQueue.tsx:11`, `Workflows.tsx:12`) — a `__mocks__` directory on the production path, in an app with no test framework to justify the name. Worth a look in the same pass.

## Suggested shape

1. Add `"test": "vitest run"` to `frontend/issuer/package.json` so the 12 assertions that already exist can run and fail. One line; it is the whole fix for the unreachable half.
2. Decide for the other five whether a unit tier is wanted at all. "No unit tests for admin/verifier, the browser tier covers them" is a legitimate answer — but it should be written down rather than inferred from an absence, because today the two states are indistinguishable.
3. If the answer is none, make `npm run test --workspaces` honest: `--if-present`, or a note in `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` saying the frontend leg is intentionally empty.
4. Rename or relocate `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` if it is production data, so the name stops implying a test fixture.

## Acceptance

* `npm test -w frontend/issuer` runs and reports 12 passing assertions.
* A planted failure in one of those specs turns the command red (the `KS-718` lesson — prove the suite can fail before trusting it).
* The intended unit-test posture for the other frontends is stated in the repo, whatever it is.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest checking the same shape across every workspace in one pass rather than ticket by ticket: which `package.json` files declare `test`, which declare it and are never invoked by a gate, and which have test files with no script. `KS-634` / `KS-652` already hold the services half, so a single audit would close the family. The `sdk/javascript` and `sdk/python` client SDKs are a third instance — no tests at all, and not workspace members, so nothing would reach them even if they had some.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:6-10`, `:17` · `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/package.json` · `frontend/issuer/vite.config.ts:8-12` · `frontend/issuer/src/__tests__/` · `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` · related: `KS-634` (Backlog), `KS-652` (Backlog), `KS-649` (Done), `KS-718` (Done), `KS-1390`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the scripts blocks above were read from the tree at that commit; nothing was executed.

title: A push whose pre-push gate runs past ~6 min dies with rc 141 after the gate PASSED — GitHub closes the idle SSH session git opened before the hook; the launcher's core.sshCommand has no keepalive
description:
## BLUF

**A Platform K push whose pre-push gate runs longer than ~6 minutes dies with** `rc 141` **(SIGPIPE) and** `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` **— after the gate has PASSED.** git opens the SSH session to read the remote refs BEFORE the pre-push hook runs, holds it through the hook, then writes the pack; GitHub closes the idle session during a long gate, and the pack write hits a dead socket. Nothing lands, nothing is refused, and the only tell is one line above `push rc=141`. The repo's `core.sshCommand` (written by `Launch_Claude.command`) carries no keepalive, and `~/.ssh/config` has none for [github.com](<http://github.com>). Measured 2026-09-14 on three pushes from the same box through the same hook shape.

## Measured (2026-09-13/14 UTC, darwin arm64, OpenSSH default keepalives = none)

| push | branch | gate duration | outcome |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| #903 | `kamilkreiser/ks-991-stale-local-develop` | 5 min 05 s (14 legs) | landed, rc 0 |
| #918 | `feature/ks-926-wire-unreachable-guards` | 5 min 44 s (15 legs) | landed, rc 0 |
| #925 attempt 1 | `feature/ks-1046-preflight-passed-…` | 6 min 17 s (15 legs, stacked) | gate PASSED (`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`), then `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` — **rc 141, origin unchanged** |
| #925 attempt 2 | same head, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` = the same key + options + `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` | 4 min 35 s | landed, rc 0, `push_protocol.py verify` PROTOCOL-CLEAN |

So the idle cutoff sits between ~5:45 and ~6:15 of hook time, and the gate is only growing (leg 15 landed on two branches today; the shell suites are 30). `push_protocol.py verify` on attempt 1 read the tracking ref UNCHANGED = origin — a push that touched nothing; the failure is the transport, not the tree.

## Where

* `Launch_Claude.command:130` and `:135` — the two `core.sshCommand` lines the launcher writes into `2_Project_Files/.git/config` (`ssh -i <key> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`); no `ServerAliveInterval`.
* `.githooks/pre-push` → `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` — the gate whose duration crosses the cutoff.
* Records: `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-14-s214/push3-ks1046/` (`push.out` line 893, `verify1.out`, `INCIDENT_sigpipe_idle_ssh.txt`, `attempt2/`).

## Fix shape

Append ` -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` to the launcher's `core.sshCommand` value (the launcher is the owner; the fix is carded to Kam as `secuura-launcher-ssh-keepalive`). Until it lands, a seat whose gate is long retries with the same options on `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` for that one push — never an edit to the repo's `.git/config`. A control for the fix: a push whose hook is padded past 7 minutes lands with keepalives and dies without them.

## Why it matters

The failure prints no refusal and no `To github…` line; a seat reading only the gate's verdict reports a push that never happened. The two seats that pushed today with 5-minute gates were under the cutoff by chance.

title: Plan zod 4 and @azure/msal-node 7: two high advisories (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5, GHSA-xcx6-jx8p-x3h5) that no lock refresh can reach
description:
## BLUF

Two high advisories cannot be cleared by any in-range lock refresh, parent update or override, so KS-1723 baselines them for 14 days (expires 2026-11-09) on Kam's card `secuura-ks1723-zod-msal-high-baseline-1026` (ruled a, 2026-10-26 09:55:48 AEDT: "Accept both for 14 days, with two tickets (recommended)"). ## zod GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (high 7.5, CWE-770)

* Vulnerable `< 4.6.6`, first patched **4.6.6**. No 3.x release is patched.
* Held at 3.25.76 in 25 standalone locks and the workspace-root lock. Every dependent asks `^3.x`: the project's own manifests (`^3.22.0` to `^3.24.0`) and third-party `@asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi@7.3.4` (`^3.20.2`).

Product code imports only the v3 entry (`from 'zod'`: 69 lines in 68 files; `zod/v4`, `zod/v4-mini`, `zod/mini`, `zod/v4/core`: 0), so it never calls the named function directly. title: Request-body arrays are uncapped: a JSON array of failing elements costs time and memory linearly (1 MB -> 524,288 issues, 338 ms, +165 MB), and two 10 MB JSON limits multiply it
description:
## BLUF

A request body that is one large JSON array whose elements all fail validation makes `z.array(...)` build one issue object per element, with no cap, so the cost grows linearly with the body and is paid on the event loop. Measured on the zod 3.25.76 v3 entry that product code uses: 1 MB -> 524,288 issues, 338 ms blocked, +165 MB heap. Two JSON limits are 10 MB. Of 237 `z.array(` call sites, at most 232 show no length bound. This is the exposure-bounding work behind the 14-day baseline row for GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (KS-1723, Kam's card `secuura-ks1723-zod-msal-high-baseline-1026`, ruled a on 2026-10-26 09:55:48 AEDT); it does not clear that advisory.

## Measured

`z.array(z.string())` validating a JSON array of numbers (every element fails), `JSON.parse` then `safeParse`, one throwaway node process per case, `--expose-gc --max-old-space-size=1536`, one run each. Synthetic worst case, no concurrency.

| body | elements | issues | time blocked | heap delta | max RSS |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 100 KB (express default) | 51,200 | 51,200 | 41 ms | +22 MB | 86 MB |
| 1 MB (gateway, mcp-server) | 524,288 | 524,288 | 338 ms | +165 MB | 274 MB |
| 10 MB (auth service, gateway uploads) | 5,242,880 | 5,242,880 | 4.5 s | +1,382 MB | 1,620 MB |

For comparison the v4 code that ships inside zod 3.25.76 (`zod/v4`; the advisory's class; an old unpatched copy): 100 KB +45 MB; 1 MB +438 MB heap, max RSS 550 MB; 10 MB aborted (rc 134) at the 1.5 GB heap cap. zod 4.6.5 and 4.6.7 were not tested.

## Where the limits are

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:402`: `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })`.
* `index.ts:406`: `uploadBodyParser = express.json({ limit: '10mb' })`, mounted at `:407` (`/api/documents/upload`) and `:408` (`/api/nft/upload`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/index.ts:85`: `express.json({ limit: '10mb' })`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:29`: `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })`.
* 40 `express.json(` sites in services and packages; 12 name a limit; the rest take express's default of 100 KB.

## Sites (an upper bound)

Tracked product files under `services/*`, `packages/*`, `frontend/*`, excluding tests, `node_modules`, `dist`, `vendor`:

* `z.array(`: 237 lines in 46 files. 5 show a numeric `.max()` or `.length()` on the same line; 232 do not (multi-line chains are not resolved, so 232 is an upper bound).
* `.parse(req.body…)` / `.safeParse(req.body…)`: 118 sites.
* Unbounded, schema line -> parse line, read: `services/originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:132` -> `:280`; `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1181` and `:1189` -> `:1201`; `oauth.ts:1301` -> `:1309`; `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:54` -> `:62`.
* Bounded, for contrast: `services/referral/src/routes/rewards.ts:20` (`.max(50)`), `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:89` (`.max(500)`), `services/security/src/index.ts:1605` (`.max(1000)`).

## Not measured

Whether each unbounded route is authenticated; behaviour under concurrent requests; the memory limits of the deployed containers; a request through the real gateway; zod 4.x numbers.

## Searched before filing

The board (title and description, archived included), by symbol and string, never by my own phrasing: `z.array(` (4 hits: KS-1696, KS-1600, KS-1514, KS-1210, each a different bug that contains the string), `uploadBodyParser` 0, `limit: '10mb'` 0, `express.json` (6 hits, none about a size cap), `handleArrayResult` 0, `zod 4` 0, `zod@4` 0, `zod v4` 0, `msal-node 7` 0, `@azure/identity` (1: KS-1379, lock re-resolution), `GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5` and `GHSA-xcx6-jx8p-x3h5` (KS-1723 only). Control: `GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92` returns KS-749, so the search can see an id. Filed new.

title: test-account password is derivable from the redacted message, and the redaction misses JSON, URL and HTML-escaped echoes
description:
**Ask:** make the redaction in the pre-suite step actually protect the generated test-account password, or say in a comment that it is cosmetic.

**What the gate found (notes N1 and N2 of the #989 verdict):** #989 (merged, KS-973 items 5 and 6) replaces the generated password with `[REDACTED]` in the DEGRADED banner (`redactSecrets(...)` at `systemTest/fixtures/provision.ts` line 342 on develop `a9ce2cff1594`). The gate, verbatim:

* **N1:** *"The redaction can be undone by derivation.* `actors.ts:98`*:* `buildPassword = \`*Ks256-${key}-${seed}-Pw!\`*`. The redacted message names `*"${spec.key}"*`and`[*spec.email*](<http://spec.email>)`=`*ks256-<key>-<seed>@secuura-test.invalid*`, and the new test asserts both are present. `*provision-actors.ts:246*`prints the seed outright. Anyone reading the DEGRADED banner can therefore reconstruct the password. Impact is low: these are test accounts on undeliverable addresses, provisioning against a remote host is refused without`*ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION\`, and the manifest holds the passwords anyway. This is outside item 6's literal scope ("cleartext in the banner"). It is worth a ticket, either a non-derivable password (seed plus a random component) or an honest comment saying the redaction is cosmetic."*
* **N2:** *"Matching is exact-substring. An echo that JSON-escapes, URL-encodes or HTML-escapes the password would not match. The fixed parts of the password (*`Ks256-`*,* `-Pw!`*) need no escaping, but* `--seed` *is caller-supplied, so a seed containing* `"` *or* `\` *would escape in a JSON echo. This is an edge case."*

**Fix shapes the gate named (proposals):** a password that is not a pure function of the printed key and seed (the seed plus a random component, kept in the manifest which already holds the passwords), and/or redact the escaped forms of the password too (JSON, URL, HTML), with a cell per form. If neither is wanted, an honest comment at `redactSecrets` that it is cosmetic.

Related and unchanged: the manifest `generated/actors.json` stores passwords in cleartext (gitignored), which the gate noted as a pre-existing exposure by design.

Source: QA gate DA5, tier 1, round 1 (verdict `2026-10-23_gate-DA5-pr989-995-tier1/verdict.md`, sha256/16 of the body `be2f26d014ae8997`). Quoted from the verdict; **not re-measured by the seat that filed this.**

title: The e2e Playwright suite cannot run from a clean checkout — tests/e2e is not a workspace member and never gets installed; 20 of 82 fail once it does
description:
## BLUF

**The e2e Playwright suite cannot run from a clean checkout**, and that is why "Playwright — not run" keeps appearing in Test Evidence blocks. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` is **not a workspace member**, has its own `package-lock.json`, and nothing installs it — so `npx playwright test` dies at collection with `Cannot find module 'otplib'` and **the entire run aborts, including the specs that would have passed**.

Once you clear that by hand, **20 of 82 tests fail** on a healthy local stack. Neither fact was recorded anywhere: `BACKLOG.md` mentions Playwright once, unrelated (control: "schemathesis" appears 6x, so the grep discriminates).

This now matters more than it used to. With GitHub Actions retired, `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` maps every retired CI job to a local command the PR author runs as the final check — and this one does not work.

## RECOMMENDATION

Two parts, in order:

1. **Make the suite installable.** Either add `tests/e2e` to the root `workspaces` array (currently `packages/*`, `services/*`, `frontend/*`), or have the documented run command do `npm ci --prefix tests/e2e` first. It works today only by accident: the root tree happens to hoist `@playwright/test`, `dotenv` and `@types/node`, but not `otplib`.
2. **Then triage the 20.** They need an owner and a baseline, the way the Schemathesis failing set has one — otherwise the suite is unusable as a gate even once it runs, because nobody can tell a new failure from the standing 20.

## Detail — how it fails

```
Error: Cannot find module 'otplib'
   at auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:13
```

* `otplib` IS declared — `tests/e2e/package.json` devDependencies, `^13.4.0`.
* It is **not** in the root `package-lock.json` (control: `@playwright/test` is, 1 match).
* `tests/e2e/node_modules` did not exist. `npm ci` there installs 16 packages, 0 vulnerabilities, and touches nothing tracked (`**/node_modules/` is ignored at `Blockchain/Dev/.gitignore:8`).
* Playwright aborts the whole run on a collection error, so the two recruitment specs never executed either — the failure is not confined to the spec with the bad import.

## Detail — the standing 20 (measured twice, same set both times)

Run: `npx playwright test tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts tests/recruitment/happy-path-wallet.spec.ts tests/recruitment/alternative-paths.spec.ts`

**9 x** `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **— basic login UI**
2.1.1 valid login (issuer) · 2.1.2 valid login (admin) · 2.1.3 session persists on reload · 2.1.4 logout redirects + cookie cleared · 2.1.5 login after logout · 2.2.1 wrong password shows error · 2.2.2 wrong email generic error · 2.2.3 empty email blocked · 2.2.4 empty password blocked

**1 x** `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **— assertion looks wrong, not the app**
2.4.6 "SQL injection in registration name is sanitized" asserts the response body does not contain `drop table`, but registration **succeeds** and echoes `displayName` back verbatim. The payload is stored and returned as data, which is the correct behaviour; the test is asserting against an echo, not against an injection.

**5 x** `happy-path-wallet.spec.ts` — CIP-8 wallet auth via API · wallet-signed document certification · Lace connection flow · wallet-not-installed handling · transaction signing

**5 x** `alternative-paths.spec.ts` — AP-2 revoked credential · AP-3 privacy-blocked field · AP-4 tampered-document hash mismatch · AP-5 invalid wallet address · AP-5 invalid signature

## Not caused by KS-712 / #760 — controlled

Same three specs run twice on the same commit, changing only the served spec (the gateway bind-mounts it, so a restart publishes it):

| served spec | result |
| -- | -- |
| #760's widened spec | 20 failed / 62 passed |
| the pre-change spec at `26100e24f` | **20 failed / 62 passed — identical set** |

The test code is byte-identical between the two (my commit touches 0 files under `tests/e2e`), and the yaml was restored byte-identical afterwards (md5 `c5174ac31273e51f63bb22c03c32c402`).

One run showed a 21st failure — 2.3.1 registration returning 503 — which did **not** reproduce: re-run on the same commit and served spec, 3/3 pass including the two dependents that had been skipped. Transient, proven rather than assumed.

## Related

* KS-712 / #760 — where this surfaced; Peter's review made "run Playwright" a blocking requirement, which is what exposed that it cannot run.
* `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` — Manual CI-gate equivalents.

title: Harden the e2e readiness check: zero-byte browser file, webkit for the mobile project, API-only runs (KS-734 follow-up)
description:
**Ask:** fix three edges in the e2e readiness check (`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/check-e2e-ready.mjs` and `global-setup.ts`).

1. **A truncated browser passes.** The browser check is `existsSync(chromium.executablePath())`; with a zero-byte, non-executable file at that path the script printed OK and rc 0.
2. **Chromium only.** The `mobile` project uses `devices['iPhone 13']`, whose `defaultBrowserType` is webkit (measured), and `e2e:install` installs only chromium. A mobile run on a fresh checkout passes this check and then fails.
3. **An API-only run is refused.** `global-setup.ts` now calls the same check for every project, so `--project=api`, which needs no browser, is refused when chromium is absent (read from code by the gate, not run). Also, the dependency check is `require.resolve` of three declared names: presence, not version.

None is a defect in the 'refuse' direction PR #920 was asked for; they are false-green and over-refusal edges.
