title: Gate E1 follow-ups: KS-1545 logs nothing for an upstream error status; KS-1613 step() has no second-slash cell
description:
## BLUF

Gate E1 (the Opus tier-1 gate on PR #1570 / KS-1613 and PR #1572 / KS-1545 step 1, 2026-10-18, with a Fable 5.1 trial gate on the same PRs) passed both, and left two follow-ups. **First**, a gap in KS-1545 step 1's coverage: `GET /api/platform/audit-log` now logs when reading the platform half **throws**, but an upstream that **answers** with an error status, or a first window that is not a list or is `null`, still drops the platform half with **no log line** — so for those cases an operator still cannot tell an empty platform half from a dropped one. Not a regression: nothing was logged there before either. Also a NIT: the timeout warn carries the internal upstream URL. **Second**, a test gap in #1570 (KS-1613) that the Fable trial gate found: `step()`'s own suite has no header with a second `/` after the denominator, though 7 of the 16 live headers carry one.

## Recommendation

A small test-first change, briefed to the Spark queue (Wednesday briefs it), gated like any other — or folded into KS-1545 step 2 if Kam's ruling there reshapes the route:

1. Check `r.ok` (and a first window with no list) at `routes/platform.ts:421-423`, and log the same one warn line (route, cause, `windowsRead`) for an error status, with a cell per shape: a 500 with a JSON body, a 401 `{"success":false,"error":"No token provided"}` on the first window (the H13 class), a first window that is not a list, and a JSON `null` body.
2. Decide whether the timeout warn should drop the internal URL's query (`?limit=&offset=`), or keep it and say so.
3. One cell in `scripts/__tests__/ks1547_preflight_step_header_denominator.test.sh` driving a header with a second `/` after the denominator (for example leg 8's `(/api/docs/openapi.json vs .yaml …)`), so `step()`'s own suite pins the non-greedy `${1#*/}`.

## Detail

* **MINOR M1:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:421-423` **(the warn is only at** `:435`**, in the catch).** The gate's probe sent four upstream replies that empty the platform half without a throw: an HTTP 500 with a JSON body; an HTTP 401 `{"success":false,"error":"No token provided"}` on the first window; a first window whose body is not a list; a JSON `null` body. Each gave HTTP 200 with the `audit_logs` rows only and **no log line**, on develop and on the PR alike. `r.ok` is never checked, and a first window with no list is treated as an empty list. KS-1545's aim is met for connection refusals, timeouts, bodies that are not JSON and a later window that is not a list; not for an upstream that answers an error status.
* **NIT N3:** `platform.ts:435`**, the logged** `error` **text.** When the body is not JSON, V8's SyntaxError quotes up to 20 characters of the upstream body (longer bodies are cut to 10); the timeout text carries the internal upstream URL with `?limit=&offset=` (`Upstream timed out after 400ms: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/audit-log?limit=50&offset=0`). The caller's token, the request body, the rows and `err.cause` appear in no log call in any of the gate's 10 probe modes. Same expression as the KS-1510 precedent at `:1064`.
* **MINOR (#1570, test strength), from the Fable 5.1 trial gate:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1547_preflight_step_header_denominator.test.sh:56-97`**.** No cell drives a step header with a second `/` after the denominator, though 7 of the 16 live headers carry one (legs 3, 8, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16). The mutant `${1#*/}` -> `${1##*/}` on `preflight.sh:225` survives the suite 12/12 and is **not** equivalent: against the live headers it aborts those 7, i.e. every push. The Opus gate's reading of the same mutant (its PM4) is that only a different suite, `preflight_deps`, kills it; the two agree that `step()`'s own suite does not. Fable verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-18_gate-E1-pr1570-pr1572/fable/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `6af5896fb794a797` (line 3 deleted).

**Source:** the gate E1 verdict, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-18_gate-E1-pr1570-pr1572/opus/verdict.md` (Wednesday's project), sha256/16 `cc91eb9abeaa70f0` computed with line 3 deleted. PRs: [#1572](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1572>) (KS-1545 step 1), [#1570](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1570>) (KS-1613 items 1+2).

**Why its own ticket, not KS-1621:** KS-1621 holds test gaps in originate's failed-anchor writer and api-gateway's document-types catch; the main item here is a product logging gap in the platform audit route, a different logical path. The #1570 test gap rides here because Wednesday ruled it into the same ticket as M1 (ADDENDUM 2026-10-18T11:24:40Z).

**Dedupe before filing:** over all 1,610 team issues including archived, 0 hits each for `Gate E1`, `platform.ts:42x`, `platform.ts:435`, `r.ok … not checked`, an audit-log error status, `Upstream timed out after`. title: KS-1226 residue: readSuiteCounts is null on real fail-only, skip-only and todo-only lines
description:
Residue from the tier-2 review of PR #1241 (round 2 of 2, **NO GO at the cap** — gate report sha256 `b6b2c0f1ae210d92`). **#1241 is the unmerged attempt; KS-1226 is the parent.** Nothing from that attempt shipped.

## The defect

`readSuiteCounts` requires a `passed` segment, so it returns **null** on every real summary that has none. Captured verbatim from vitest 4.1.11, `--reporter=default`, piped:

```
      Tests  1 failed (1)      -> null   (correct: { passed: 0, failed: 1 })
      Tests  1 skipped (1)     -> null   (correct: { passed: 0, failed: 0 })
      Tests  1 todo (1)        -> null   (correct: { passed: 0, failed: 0 })
```

**Cost.** `childSuiteCounts` throws `could not read the child vitest summary` with the output tail. Loud, but it misattributes a zero-pass child as a parser defect — and a child where everything failed is exactly the case the reading must survive.

## Root cause

vitest renders the **final** summary with `getStateString` in `dist/chunks/utils.BS4fH3nR.js`, where `passed` is **conditional**:

```js
passed ? c.bold(c.green(`${passed} passed`)) : null,
```

There is a **second** `getStateString`, in `dist/chunks/index.UpGiHP7g.js`, belonging to the TTY-only live reporter, where `passed` is unconditional. The round-2 head comment quotes that one, and the "passed is always emitted" premise — and the refusal built on it — came from reading the wrong renderer.

## Also in this residue

* `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json` is **red at head**: `TS2532` at :79 and `TS2345` at :86, so `npm run lint` exits 2. `npm run lint` runs **both** tsconfigs; only `tsconfig.json` was run, and it is clean.
* The call site (:157 / :161) is **unpinned** — no cell reds if it stops calling `readSuiteCounts`.
* First-match reads an earlier `Tests  N passed (N)` console line as the summary: a silent `{5,0}` on a run that had 1 failure.

## Fix shape

Name-read with an **allowed-label set** and a **sum-equals-total** check instead of "require passed". Take the **last** `Tests` line, not the first. Narrow the indexed accesses so the stricter tsconfig passes. Correct the doc comment, C5's title, and the :156 citations.

## Regression cells

The three lines above to `{0,1}`, `{0,0}`, `{0,0}`. `      Tests  2 failed | 3 passed (5)` to `{3,2}`. A sum-not-equal-total line to null. The two-line output (an earlier `Tests  5 passed (5)`, then `      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)`) to `{1,1}`. One cell that **reds when :157 stops calling** `readSuiteCounts` — for example by exposing the spawn result to a pure `readChildOutput(output)` that `childSuiteCounts` calls and a cell calls with real captured fail-only output. `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit` rc 0.

Refs KS-1226

title: systemTest performance `unitSuiteSlotIndependence.test.ts`: the 15 s budget at :127 is tight under load, and the :99 summary regex returns NULL when the child summary includes "skipped"
description:
**BLUF:** two defects in one consumer, `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/utils/unitSuiteSlotIndependence.test.ts`, which spawns child vitest runs and parses their summary. Both are pre-existing and unchanged between vitest 4.1.10 and 4.1.11. Severity Polish.

1. **:127 budget (F4).** The test's 15000 ms timeout is \~13.3–13.4 s of real work at load1 \~19 on BOTH vitest versions, so it times out under load. Seen twice on 2026-09-17: at 16139 ms during the #1030 author's run, and at 17.11 s in the gate's A/B. A duration, not an assertion.
2. **:99 regex (F5).** `/Tests\s+(?:(\d+) failed \| )?(\d+) passed \((\d+)\)/` returns NULL on a summary that includes skipped tests, e.g. `Tests  1 failed | 1 skipped | 243 passed (245)`. The consumer would then throw "could not read the child vitest summary" instead of reporting the counts.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1030, findings F4 and F5 (one ticket, same file). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1030-e43af4934-tier2-r1/report.md`.

## The gate's findings, quoted

> | F4 | Consumer `unitSuiteSlotIndependence.test.ts:127` timed out at 15000 ms once at head (17.11 s, load1 20.6) under my own concurrent root installs; under the same load both sides took \~13.3–13.4 s; quiet A/B equal | measured, 10 runs | Polish (RECORD; duration, not assertion; READY saw the same at 17cbb1091) | TICKET-class (the 15 s budget vs a child-vitest matrix is \~13 s at load1 \~19 on BOTH versions) | Comparable (base vs head at equal load) |
>
> | F5 | Consumer `:99` regex returns NULL on a child summary that includes `skipped` (e.g. `Tests  1 failed \| 1 skipped \| 243 passed (245)`) → the consumer would throw "could not read the child vitest summary" | measured (probe, controls) | Polish (curio; pre-existing, format unchanged 4.1.10→4.1.11) | TICKET-class | Product |
>
> `:99` regex probe (`suites/consumer_regex_probe.out`), read from the file at head: vitest 4.1.11 passing output → failed 0 / passed 3 / total 3; 4.1.11 failing output → 1/2/3; packages/shared 4.1.11 → 0/851/851; 4.1.10 → 0/3/3. Controls: `Tests  245 passed` (no parens) → NULL; `… (245)` → match; `2 failed | 243 passed (245)` → match; `1 failed | 1 skipped | 243 passed (245)` → NULL (F5).

A/B timings from the gate (base 4.1.10 | head 4.1.11): concurrent round 1 13.42 s | 13.29 s; concurrent round 2 **timed out 17.11 s** | 6.33 s; quiet 5.98 s | 5.64 s and 5.62 s | 5.72 s.

## First item

This is a systemTest harness file, so the change goes through the systemTest rules (all four quality gates). Decide the budget: size it to the child matrix, or run the matrix without the per-test timeout. Also widen the regex to accept an optional `N skipped |` segment, with the gate's probe lines as the regression cells.

* `unitSuiteSlotIndependence`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `slot independence`: KS-1167 (a harness-guards port, Done), not this.
* `skipped |`: KS-1046, KS-1016, KS-1015, KS-687; comments on KS-1169, KS-39, KS-502, KS-519, KS-961. None concerns this regex.

title: k6 readYaml adoption: the unit suite that proves it is run by no gate, and three coverage gaps the new self-read cells leave
description:
## BLUF

PR **#1236** (KS-1110, merged `2208acc0638a`) routed both k6 unit tests through `readYaml()`, so a malformed scenarios file fails them **without printing its content** — measured: the old path printed the whole file. The gate recorded **four** non-blocking findings alongside it. They are one file and one fix pass, so they are items of one ticket rather than four, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule.

## The four items

1. **READYAML-UNGATED — the one that undoes the rest.** **No pre-push leg and no PR workflow runs this unit suite.** The cells that prove the property exist, and nothing executes them. A regression here is caught only if someone runs the suite by hand.
2. **READYAML-CANARY.** The canary that proves the old path leaked file content was measured for items A and B; it is not retained as a standing cell, so the property "a malformed file does not print its content" has no permanent witness.
3. **READYAML-ROUTING.** An **indented or dynamic** parser import would pass the new self-read cells — they read the file's own source for a top-level import, so a `js-yaml` import that is indented, conditional or dynamic is invisible to them.
4. **READYAML-SHAPES.** The shapes covered are those the two tests use; other config shapes are unasserted.

## Why item 1 leads

The other three are ordinary coverage limits. Item 1 is different in kind: it means the suite's verdict is **never produced** in the normal flow. That is the "a verdict nobody runs" shape the repo already tracks elsewhere — and it makes items 2-4 moot in practice, because even a perfect cell that nothing runs protects nothing.

## NOT claimed

Not a live failure. `systemTest/performance` reads 1088/1089 at the merged tree, and the single red is the pre-existing path-dependent `PRESUITE-URLPATH`, identical at base, head and end — not this PR.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,286 issues incl. archived, 3,631 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `readYaml` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1117**, KS-1110, KS-485). **KS-1117 read in full and is NOT a duplicate** — it is js-yaml 5.2.3 rejecting a BOM followed by `#`, a parsing defect in the loader itself.
* `scenarios.yml` -> 18 total / 5 open; `sheddingCeiling` -> 2 total / 1 open (**KS-1110**, the merged ticket this comes from).
* Controls that fire: `KS-1229` -> 5; `consumeResetToken` -> 3; nonsense control -> 0.

`Refs KS-1110`; does not close it (item C is separately open there).

## Provenance

Tier-2c QA gate `2026-09-25-batch1218-t2c` (report sha256 `70dc4c987f04…`), raised as a **non-blocking** finding and recorded at the merge. Filed on the coordinator's instruction after the batch landed; it did not hold the merge.

title: k6 runner: the pre-suite path is taken from URL.pathname, so a checkout directory containing a space fails ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
description:
## BLUF

`systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` resolves the pre-suite step with
`new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts', import.meta.url).pathname`. `URL.pathname` **is**
**percent-encoded.** A checkout whose directory contains a space yields `.../Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/...`,
which is passed to the spawn as a literal path, and the run dies with
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND … %2520 …` (the `%25` is the second round of encoding).

**This is not hypothetical on this fleet.** The QA gate's own checkout lives at
`/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/` — a path with **two spaces**. Any performance run
driven from a checkout like that cannot start its pre-suite step.

Found as a develop-own finding during the tier-2 gate on #1268 (report lines 214-219). **Not built**
**there**, and not built here: it is develop's, not that PR's.

## Measured at `00de57baeb405d0081fe8b6f192bd40d35acef61`

```
$ node -e "const u=new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts','file:///Volumes/Dev/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/x/runner/cli.ts');
           console.log(u.pathname); console.log(require('url').fileURLToPath(u));"
/Volumes/Dev/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/fixtures/pre-suite.ts     <- .pathname, what the code uses
/Volumes/Dev/Testing Agent MAIN/fixtures/pre-suite.ts         <- fileURLToPath, correct
```

`cli.ts:162` **is the only** `.pathname` **use of an** `import.meta.url` **URL in the package.** The fix-shape
already has precedent **in the same directory**, so this is a consistency fix rather than a new idea:

* `runner/actor_manifest.ts:60` — `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
* `runner/paths.ts:12` — `path.dirname(url.fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
* `gate/cli.ts:31` — the same

## Done means

1. `cli.ts:162` uses `fileURLToPath(new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts', import.meta.url))`.
2. **A regression cell in the gate's own shape: run the CLI from a copy of the tree whose path**
   **contains a space**, and assert the pre-suite step resolves and spawns. A cell that only asserts
   the string has no `%20` would pass for a path that is wrong in some other way.
3. A sweep for any other `.pathname` on an `import.meta.url` URL across `systemTest/`, so the fix is
   the class and not the one line. ~~Measured today: **1** occurrence, this one.~~ **CORRECTED 2026-09-26 (gate29, and the PR agrees): the count is 3, not 1.** Measured by `git grep` over the clone at develop: `systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` (**fixed** by PR #1291, squash `3f70224a069b`), `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts:36` and `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:42` — the last two remain open on this ticket. The original figure came from a sweep scoped to the performance package, while this DoD names `systemTest/`. Two wider sweeps add nothing to the class. title: No Playwright e2e test has run on any PR since 2026-09-07 — the suite dies at a static lint gate before any browser opens, and the job name hides it
description:
**BLUF — no Playwright test has executed on any PR since 2026-09-07. The** `Playwright suite` **job goes red at a static lint gate that runs BEFORE any browser opens, so the red names the wrong subject and the coverage hole has been invisible for three days.**

This is a **test-coverage** ticket, not a CI-config ticket. It was found while measuring CI gate failures (KS-1075) but must not be closed as gate tuning: the gate is a symptom, the missing e2e coverage is the defect.

## What happens

`Playwright suite` (job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml`) fails at **step 6, "Quality gate — static (tsc/ESLint/Prettier/knip/audit)"**. That step runs `npm run format:check && npm run lint && …` ahead of the suite. It exits 1, so **the job stops before a single browser test runs.**

```
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @param "label" declaration  jsdoc/require-param
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @throws declaration         jsdoc/require-throws
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @example declaration        jsdoc/require-example
  48:1  error  Missing JSDoc comment                     jsdoc/require-jsdoc
✖ 4 problems (4 errors, 0 warnings)
```

All four in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`. Prettier passes cleanly — it is the ESLint jsdoc rules alone. ESLint's own output says **3 of the 4 are** `--fix`**-able**.

## Why it hid — the part worth keeping

**The job's name names the wrong subject.** "Playwright suite :: failure" reads as *browser tests ran and failed*. Nobody re-reads a suite they believe is already running. The same shape as a wrapper printing a banner it did not earn: the red was true, and what it implied was false.

## Proven pre-existing, with controls

* Measured identically on **two unrelated PRs** — #938 (one nginx `location` block, zero service code) and #939 (TypeScript type declarations in one service): same rules, same line numbers, same count.
* `global-setup.ts` is touched by **neither** — 0 hits in each diff, against controls of 4 and 3 files actually touched.
* Last changed `42e778203`, **2026-09-07**, *"KS-969 round 2: a role collapse is not a success…"* — three days before either PR.

## What needs doing

1. Fix the four jsdoc errors in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts` (3 are `--fix`-able).
2. **Then confirm the suite actually runs and report what it finds** — three days of unrun e2e may be hiding real failures. A green job after the lint fix is not the same as a suite that was green all along, and it must not be reported as one.
3. Consider whether a static lint gate belongs *ahead* of the suite in the same job at all: as configured, any lint error in the harness silently converts "e2e coverage" into "no e2e coverage" while still reporting a normal-looking red.

## Related

Found during KS-1075 (CI gate measurement, commissioned by Kam as `measure-then-decide`). KS-1075 covers the two *other* gate causes — a `bash -e` swallowed diagnostic and an empty npm-audit allow-list — and should not absorb this one.

title: The Playwright env guard added in #896 reads config/ only — the variable breaking the CI run is read from fixtures/ and appears in no template
description:
## BLUF

PR #896 (KS-682) adds `systemTest/playwright/tests-unit/env-example.test.ts`. It pins `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` to every variable that `config/` **reads**. **The variable now failing the Playwright run in CI,** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`**, is read outside that scope**, so the guard stays green over exactly the gap that breaks the run.

**This is measured on #896's head** `a7b588a05f1a40b29b429e7dafa4a84d9a6283d0`**, which is unmerged. The guard does not exist on** `develop`**.** s171 found it by reading during its Phase 1 review of #896 (2026-09-10), not by running a test, so it was not filed then. Filing, not fixing: `systemTest/` is Peter's authority.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Guard scope (#896 head) | `env-example.test.ts:23-24`: `PACKAGE_ROOT` = `systemTest/playwright`, `CONFIG_DIR = path.join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'config')`. `:40` reads only `readdirSync(CONFIG_DIR)` |
| Where the variable is read (#896 head) | `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts:155`, `password: process.env.BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? ''`. This is outside `systemTest/playwright/` entirely (`:110` on `develop` `2d864ae92`) |
| How the Playwright run reaches it | `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:40` spawns `fixtures/pre-suite.ts`, which provisions the actors |
| In the `.env.example` the guard pins | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `API_BASE_URL` **1** |
| Readers inside the guard's scope | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** under `playwright/config/` · control `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **1 file** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `DATABASE_URL` **2** |
| `.github/workflows/` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** · control `API_BASE_URL` **4 files** |

## Why it matters

The guard's claim is true as written: it covers what `config/` reads. But a green guard reads as "the Playwright environment is documented", and the variable that decides whether the run can authenticate at all is read by the shared `fixtures/` the run spawns.

It also compounds with KS-969. Without `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` the pre-suite reports DEGRADED and exits 0, the actor manifest is not published, and `auth.setup` logs in with `''`. In CI that login returns HTTP 400, and 11 of the 12 tests never run. See KS-969 comment `e1358ef7`.

## Not decided here

Two questions for Peter:

* Should the guard also scan the `fixtures/` the suite spawns?
* Does `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` belong in any `.env.example` at all? It is a privileged bootstrap credential, and KS-969's open question comes first: what supplies it now that the published default is retired?

## Searched before filing

* Exact: `CONFIG_DIR` (10 hits, none about this guard), `env-example.test.ts`, `PACKAGE_ROOT`, `getTestAdminPassword` (KS-969 only).
* Fuzzy: "env-example guard", "readEnv config .env.example guard", "env drift guard fixtures directory".
* Opened, none carries this finding:
  * KS-967: a different pair of guards, the credential scanners.
  * KS-1081: two templates disagreeing with each other.
  * KS-973: pre-suite step items.
  * KS-682's 19 comments: `env-example` appears only in a bite table.
* Control: `KS-682` returns 1 hit.

Links: KS-969 · KS-966 · KS-682 · [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896>)

title: Schemathesis baseline gate is unreachable: run.py skips it whenever the sweep fails — i.e. on every run it exists to triage
description:
## BLUF

**The Schemathesis baseline gate added by KS-256 (PR #782) ships inert: it is skipped on exactly the runs it exists to triage.** Not a regression — `develop` has no baseline gate at all — but the feature does not do what its own header claims until this is fixed.

## Mechanism

`systemTest/schemathesis/scripts/run.py:533`:

```python
if not success:
    Logger.warning("SKIPPED - upstream gate failed: report reconciliation and the "
                   "schemathesis baseline gate were not evaluated for this run.")
else:
    success = evaluate_report_reconciliation(OUTPUT_DIR)
    if success:
        success = evaluate_schemathesis_baseline(...)
```

`success` already carries the sweep's own outcome. So:

* sweep **fails** -> `success` False -> **baseline gate skipped** — but a failing sweep is the only thing the baseline has to triage;
* sweep **passes** -> gate runs -> nothing to triage.

The gate is unreachable in its own use case. The 97 accepted `check::operation` pairs in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` therefore gate nothing as shipped.

## Measured

Run `pr-2026-09-02T07-06-54Z` against `custody/568-rebase` @ `8d7109411`: 10 failing operations, `Run validity: OK - 0 of 314 operations errored`, and then `SKIPPED - upstream gate failed`. The triage that would have classified all 10 as known never ran.

## Relationship to KS-256 QA F-5

F-5 (fixed in s105) made this skip **speak** — before it, the `and` short-circuit meant the gate silently never ran, which read exactly like a pass. That fix is why this is visible at all. It did not make the gate **reachable**.

## Fix

Evaluate report reconciliation and the baseline **eagerly** rather than behind `success`, and combine the verdicts afterwards. The existing code comment already names this as the tidier shape and records why it was deferred: *"a gate that fires on an INVALID run may not have the artefacts it reads, so that swap needs an invalid-run rehearsal this change does not have."*

So the work is: the eager swap **plus** an invalid-run rehearsal proving the baseline gate degrades safely when the artefacts it reads are absent or partial.

## Acceptance

A run with a failing sweep whose failures are all in the baseline must print the baseline gate's verdict, and a failing pair **absent** from the baseline must still fail the run — with a control proving the gate can fail (deliberately remove one accepted pair and confirm the run goes red).

Found in s106 while running the four suites for PR #782. Peter's triage input wanted on priority.

title: Akto CI scan throughput: ~21 s local vs ~10 min in the isolated pr-akto stack (~28×) — investigate worker starvation / run-pickup latency (KS-435 durable fix)
description:
[akto-2187-findings.md](https://uploads.linear.app/ee72b345-5a75-4c1a-9bbb-09a6955f4499/12359f7f-c7d7-4777-aa45-e997d8acaf8d/dc8d8d55-c175-422c-b4ed-85b2faed7c2f)

## Problem (split out of [KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) — the durable-fix track)

KS-435's immediate unblock raised the poll ceilings (`PR_TIMEOUT_MS` 660s→1200s, `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` 720s→1260s). But the underlying anomaly is untouched: **the same all-endpoint** `test:pr` **scan completes in \~21 s on a local host and takes \~10 min in the isolated** `pr-akto` **CI stack** — a ~28× gap that is too large to be plain CPU starvation of a co-scheduled stack.

## Evidence

* Local ([KS-433](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-433/akto-bolabflabroken-auth-finding-on-a-write-path-unmasked-by-the-ks) triage, 2026-07-11): `npm run test:pr` → COMPLETED ~21 s, 316 endpoints, 7902 results, 0 vulnerable.
* CI: three runs died at the ~594 s poll ceiling (PR #480 ×2 attempts, PR #488, develop post-merge run on `9a1ade224`); green runs (#481, #489) finished just under it — so real CI wall-clock is ~9–10 min.

## Suspects ([KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) options 2/3)

1. `akto-testing` worker CPU/IO starvation — the runner co-schedules the 31-service platform stack + Akto's dashboard/mongo/testing/puppeteer.
2. Scheduled-run pickup latency — the testing worker polls for queued runs; check `LAST_TEST_RUN_EXECUTION_DELTA` / pickup-interval behaviour under load.
3. Runner resources — larger GitHub runner class, or trim what boots in the akto job.

## Direction — right-size the runner, keep coverage intact (consolidated from [KS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-446/akto-suite-pr-durable-ci-throughput-fix-stop-the-full-scan-sitting-at), closed as duplicate)

Having weighed the two levers, the clear preference is to **increase the runner's resources (CPU/RAM)** — the isolated stack's runner is simply under-provisioned for co-hosting the full platform + full Akto stack. That is the root cause and the honest fix. In order of preference:

1. **Right-size the runner** — move the `pr-akto` job to a larger runner (more vCPU/RAM), or split the platform stack and the Akto stack onto separate runners so the akto-testing worker isn't starved. Expected to be the whole fix.
2. **Confirm it's genuinely resource starvation** vs. a stall on scheduled-run pickup (~21s local vs >594s CI) — verify (1) is the right lever before spending on it.
3. **Coverage/scope trim — avoid.** The full all-endpoint BOLA/BFLA/Broken-Auth scan is the value of the gate; narrowing it to win on runtime would quietly reduce security coverage rather than fix the real constraint. Last resort only, flagged explicitly, never silent.

## Done means

CI `Akto suite (PR)` wall-clock understood + brought down to low single-digit minutes — achieved by **more runner capacity**, not a further ceiling raise and not by reducing coverage. (Or an explicit, documented decision that ~10 min is accepted and the raised ceiling is the permanent posture — then tighten the ceilings to the measured runtime.)

Consolidates [KS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-446/akto-suite-pr-durable-ci-throughput-fix-stop-the-full-scan-sitting-at) (durable CI-throughput fix), closed as a duplicate of this ticket. Related: [KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) (parent, Done, #490), [KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling) (prior poll-ceiling class).

title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

title: Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic — three runs on near-identical code gave 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH (different endpoint) / 0 HIGH
description:
## BLUF

**Three Akto** `test:pr` **runs tonight, same harness, same command, gave three different answers — and none of the three carried a captured request or response.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot be read either way: its PASS is not evidence of absence, and its FAIL is not evidence of a defect until re-derived by hand.

## Measured — 2026-08-27, all three within ~20 minutes

| run | target | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- |
| baseline (s76) | `develop ca5b643e0` | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on a **GDPR** route |
| KS-694 fix branch | `develop` + the KS-694 role-gate fix (touches `gdpr.ts` + `systemErrors.ts` only) | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on `GET /api/documents` |
| 17-PR integration stack | `develop cc65abad5` + 17 open PRs | **0** — `verdict: PASS`, 804 clean, 2 known-FP |

The middle run is the one that rules out "the code changed": that branch touches two route files and cannot have introduced or removed a finding on `/api/documents`.

## The `/api/documents` finding does not reproduce

Derived by hand rather than trusted:

* `?userId=` **injection changes nothing.** The identical document set comes back with no `userId`, with another user's, and with a third user's.
* **Cross-tenant isolation holds.** A default-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 18 documents, an oxford-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 70, **full-id overlap 0**. (An earlier probe of my own appeared to show a shared document — that was an 8-character id truncation in my script, not a leak. Recording the false alarm so nobody re-derives it.)

## Why this matters now

Since 2026-08-27 the four local suites are the **only** merge gate (Kam: *"billing will not be fixed"*). Akto is one of the four. **Two of tonight's three runs would have produced a different merge decision on the same code.** That is the same failure mode `KS-519` names for permanently-red checks, arriving from the other direction.

## Related, already known

`KS-694` came out of the first of these runs — the finding was real but its **label** (`BOLA / ADD_USER_ID`) was wrong, and re-deriving it produced a more precise and more serious defect. Same pattern: the scanner points at something; the label and the endpoint are both unreliable.

## Suggested next step

Establish whether the variance is in the scan (endpoint sampling / timing / auth state) or the reporting, by running `test:pr` N times against a frozen commit with the stack untouched between runs, and recording the HIGH set each time. **Not started** — filed so tonight's measurement is not lost.

title: demo-service mounts no error handler — a raw 0x00 body returns express's default HTML with a stack trace and absolute paths
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing product defect, NOT introduced by PR #836** — surfaced by the tier-2 gate on that PR while it was driving a real corpus service over a raw socket. `demo-service` **mounts no error handler at all**, so an unhandled error falls through to express's default handler.

## What it returns

A **raw** `0x00` **byte in the request body** produces express's default error page: **1,324 bytes of HTML carrying a stack trace and absolute filesystem paths** (measured by the gate under `NODE_ENV=test`).

## Priority — sized from a REPO read, and the tenant is NOT read

Express's default error handler suppresses the stack **only when** `NODE_ENV === 'production'`. So the question is what the deployed demo-service runs under.

**Measured in the repo:** `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:2117` sets `NODE_ENV=development` for the `demo-service` service. That is the **only** compose file in the tree that defines `NODE_ENV` for it — `docker-compose.e2e.override.yml` mentions demo-service but sets no `NODE_ENV`. The VM demo runs that same `docker-compose.yml`.

**So the repo says the stack trace is NOT suppressed on the demo.** What I have *not* done, and will not do without an instruction: read the running container to confirm no environment override is applied at runtime. The demo was not touched. **Treat the priority as Medium-on-the-repo-read, and confirm against the running container before acting on it.**

## Fix shape

Mount an error handler on demo-service, as every other service in the estate does. The KS-727 error-handler class guard already exists and should cover this service once one is mounted.

## Provenance

Wednesday's s137 successor brief, 2026-09-05T21:53:00Z, item 1, second ticket. Gate report: `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks832-836-pass1-8d858205e/report.md`. Filed by s137.

---

title: connectorId persists but is invisible through the API — POST and GET both return null while the row holds the value
description:
## `connectorId` persists correctly but is invisible through the API — a Platform S caller cannot read back the connector it just set

Found during probe 5(ii) on the demo box, 2026-09-06, against `security` rebuilt from `db1848abf` (KS-869's code live: `connector_id` 7 occurrences in `/app/dist`, 0 in the pre-rebuild image).

### What happens

`POST /api/security/keys` with `connectorId: "probe-connector-20260906T084007Z"`:

* **HTTP 201.** Response body carries `connectorId: null`.
* `GET /api/security/keys?organizationId=…` for the same key: `connectorId: null`.
* **The database has the value**: `SELECT connector_id FROM svc_api_keys WHERE name = 'wednesday-probe-20260906T084007Z'` → `probe-connector-20260906T084007Z`.

So KS-869's write half works — the totals moved **39 rows / 0 connectors → 40 / 1**, exactly one new row with exactly one connector. What does not work is the read-back: **neither the write response nor the list response exposes the field**, so the only way to confirm a connector was recorded is direct database access, which an integrator does not have.

### Why it matters

The S↔K ownership contract has Platform S minting connector-scoped keys through this endpoint. Under KS-843's cutover the connector is load-bearing. An integrator that sets `connectorId` and reads the response back sees `null` and cannot distinguish "not persisted" from "persisted but not returned" — the two have opposite remedies.

`rowToApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:345`) does map `connectorId`, which suggests the write and list responses are served from the in-memory representation rather than a row read — that is a hypothesis, stated as one; the measurement above is not.

### Controls

* Impossible token in the same image → 0.
* Validate on the revoked probe key → `valid:false, reason:"Key revoked"`; on a key that never existed → `valid:false, reason:"Key not found"`. Different reasons, so the API's own instruments do discriminate — this is not a blanket read failure.

### Housekeeping

The probe key `wednesday-probe-20260906T084007Z` was revoked in-leg through the API (`DELETE`, HTTP 200) and the revocation confirmed two ways: `is_active = f` in the row, and `validate` → `"Key revoked"`. No probe key is live.

Related: KS-869 (the write), KS-889 (the empty backfill window), KS-887 (the write-half pin that cannot discriminate).

title: A clean stack has no supported way to obtain its first privileged account
description:
## The gap

On a freshly built stack there is no supported path to a first privileged account:

* `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` is now default-deny (B-3 hardening) and needs **both** `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` and `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED=true`.
* Registration cannot mint a privileged role — KS-82 deliberately refuses a client-supplied role.

Both of those are **correct** and neither is questioned here. The gap is that nothing owns the bootstrap step, because historically the seed accounts were simply always present, so no one had to.

## Status of the original claim — corrected

An earlier KS-487 comment (2026-09-01 11:36Z) asserted a hard **deadlock**: that a clean stack could never call `seed-demo-users` at all. **That was retracted 21 minutes later by its own author** (11:57Z) — `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:47` fires `userRepo.seedDemoUsers()`, so there is no deadlock. This ticket carries the *remaining* gap only: not "impossible", but "undocumented and unowned".

## What would close it

One of: a documented first-run procedure naming the two env vars and their intended lifetime; or a one-shot bootstrap command that creates a single named admin without the demo-persona list; or an explicit decision that operators set the env vars, written where an operator will find it (`DEV-PROCESS.md` or the deployment runbook).

## Provenance

Recorded on [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) as prose (2026-09-01, with its correction) rather than a ticket, because the Linear workspace was at its free issue cap. The cap was lifted 2026-09-06, so it is filed now. **This is the finding whose existence-only-in-prose was the reason the table was built.**

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the KS-487 stream-B table.*

title: vite is a production dependency of services/auth — esbuild and fsevents ship into the runtime image, imported by nothing
description:
## `vite` sits in auth's production `dependencies`, dragging esbuild and fsevents into the runtime image

Found by the #849 (KS-490) tier-2 gate as F-2, and measured before filing.

### The measurement

| Reading | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `dependencies.vite` | `7.3.6` |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `devDependencies.vite` | **absent** |
| runtime sources under `services/auth/src` importing `vite` (excluding `__tests__`) | **0** |
| CONTROL: runtime sources importing `express` | **15** |

The control is what makes the zero mean something — the same grep shape finds 15 files for a package auth genuinely uses at runtime, so 0 for `vite` is a real absence and not a grep that cannot match.

### Why it matters

Because `vite` is a production dependency it survives `npm prune --omit=dev` and `npm ci --omit=dev`, and it pulls `esbuild 0.28.1` and `fsevents 2.3.3` with it. Both carry install scripts, which is why auth's production set shows three `hasInstallScript` entries where the estate has only one package that actually requires compilation.

**This is not a security finding on its own** — the runtime `npm ci --ignore-scripts` means none of those install scripts ever runs, and that is why #849 passed. It is image weight and attack surface: a build toolchain shipped into a running container that no runtime code imports.

### The fix

Move `vite` to `devDependencies` in `services/auth/package.json`, regenerate the lock, and re-measure the runtime `node_modules` file count (the tester counted **5,591 files** in auth's runtime tree). Expect esbuild, rollup and fsevents to leave with it.

**Verify before assuming:** confirm nothing in auth's build path (not just `src/`) needs `vite` at runtime — a config file or a script entry could. The import walk above covers `src/` only.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #849's gate findings.*

title: timeoutMs does not bound DNS resolution — a hung lookup leaves safeOutboundRequest pending well past its declared deadline
description:
## Residual, NOT a regression — and it is the same class as the defect that opened the #868 gate

### Measured by the gate

With the lookup hung and a **300 ms** declared bound, the call was **still pending at 2503 ms**. The probe's FAIL condition was "settled", so it could have refuted the finding and did not.

### Why it matters more than the number suggests

The total deadline added in KS-914 round 1 covers connect, TLS, request, response and drain — everything **after** name resolution. `resolvePublicAddresses` is awaited *before* the deadline is armed, so a resolver that hangs is outside every bound the function advertises.

That is the same shape as the defect this whole ticket family started from: **a parameter that reads like a bound over the whole operation, bounding only part of it.** Unchanged from the parent commit — this is not a regression, it is the half that was never covered.

### Fix shape

Arm the budget before resolution and carry the remainder into the request, so `timeoutMs` means what its name says end to end. Red-proof with a lookup that never calls back and a short declared bound; the FAIL condition must be "still pending", and a resolver that answers normally is the control.

*From the #868 round-1 gate (F1). Filed by s141, 2026-09-06.*

title: KS-858 residue: the repeated-slash collapse does not complete for the /api/billing mount — leading // still 404s where /api/governance does not
description:
**BLUF** — the KS-858 edge normalisation closes the repeated-slash class on 66 of the 67 declared gateway mount classes. `/api/billing` with a **leading** `//` still 404s. **Nothing got worse** — base 404 → head 404 — but this is the class fix not being uniform, on a ticket whose whole point is the class.

**Measured by the #884 tier-1 gate, deterministic 5/5 and again on a controlled repeat:**

```
HEAD  /api/billing/SAME     -> 401 "No token provided"   (reaches the billing upstream)
HEAD  /api/billing//SAME    -> 401 "No token provided"   (interior // fixed)
HEAD  //api/billing/SAME    -> 404 "Route POST /api/billing/SAME not found"
HEAD  //api/billing//SAME   -> 404
BASE  //api/billing/SAME    -> 404 "Route POST //api/billing/SAME not found"
```

The 404 body carries the **canonical** path, which proves `req.path` was canonicalised before the 404 handler ran — the request simply never produced billing's 401.

**Positive control that this is not the general case:** `//api/governance/zzqa` returns the upstream's own `401 No token provided`, identical to its canonical spelling. So leading-`//` does reach proxy mounts in general.

**Mechanism NOT determined.** The gate's candidate, explicitly unverified: billing is the mount whose `pathRewrite` is `{'^/api': ''}` while its neighbours self-map (`{'^/api/governance': '/api/governance'}`), so the rewrite anchor and the deliberately-untouched `req.originalUrl` may interact. **Reproduce before fixing** — and reproduce it against the round-2 head, not round 1, since round 2 changed how the target is split.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` (billing mount + its pathRewrite); `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/normalisePath.ts`.
**Source:** #884 tier-1 verdict 2026-09-06T21:50:32Z, finding F-QA-3 (severity Minor). **Discovered:** 2026-09-07, session 144.

title: KS-930 residue: a whole app tree copied into a stage that names no JS runtime is still exempt — and the gate's fix-shape for it cannot be written without denying the repo's own idiom
description:
**BLUF** — #876 round 2 closed 7 of the 8 shapes in the tier-1 gate's attack table. **Row 1d stays open**: `FROM scratch` + `COPY --from=builder /app /app` is still `A_EXEMPT` at rc 0. The gate's fix-shape for it was **built and then withdrawn**, because measurement says it cannot be expressed without denying every class file in the repo. This ticket carries the residue and the evidence, so the decision is made on numbers rather than re-derived from scratch.

**Measured, all three guards, one row driver parked outside the scanned tree (self-tested to produce three distinct arms):**

| row | base `306d0db92` | round 1 `8d3e5208a` | round 2 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1a alpine + `apk add nodejs` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1c busybox + copied node binary + `/app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| **1d scratch +** `COPY --from=builder /app /app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | **EXEMPT — open** |
| 1e `ENV RUNTIME_PKG=nodejs` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1g line-continuation `apk add nodejs` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1h alpine + copied node binary + `/app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1i nginx + copied node binary + `/app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1b / 1f (controls) | denied | denied | denied |

**Why the gate's second fix-shape was withdrawn.** It reads: *"an allow-listed base should not be exempt when the stage copies a whole directory from another stage."* Two implementations were written and both were reverted:

1. **Structural** (source path is a top-level directory, fewer than two segments below root). With it in place the guard suite went **41 passed / 12 failed**, and the reds included *"F-6 inv: nginx is still EXEMPT — the case the exemption exists for"* and *"nginx behind a REGISTRY prefix is EXEMPT — not a false block"*. Cause, measured: **every** `nonjs_case` fixture — and every real class file — contains `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared`, a one-segment source.
2. **WORKDIR-aware** (source equals the source stage's working directory). Measured across the repo: `shared-builder` is declared `WORKDIR /shared` followed by `npm ci` in every Dockerfile that has it. So `/shared` **is** that stage's workdir and does hold a node tree — this rule matches it too.

`COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared` is not incidental: it is the line that makes a file a class file at all (46+ occurrences). A rule that denies it denies the entire class. The only escapes are (a) exempting `/shared` **by name** — a new allow-list, i.e. the deny-list-wearing-a-comment shape this whole round removed — or (b) accepting that the arm can essentially never grant an exemption in this repo, which removes the arm. **Both are decisions, not cleanups, which is why this is a ticket and not a commit.**

**What bounds the residue.** Every variant of row 1d that names something able to RUN the copied tree is now denied — measured: a copied `node` binary, `CMD ["node", …]`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/node"]`, `bun`, `deno`. What remains cannot execute what it copied, so it cannot produce the #851 crash-on-start that this guard exists for.

**The hole that is genuinely left:** an image that reaches a runtime through a file the guard cannot read — `CMD ["/app/start.sh"]` where `start.sh` runs node. No text signal in the Dockerfile names the runtime. That is not fixable by any parser of Dockerfiles alone.

**Also latent, not live:** the repo currently contains **no** `COPY --from=X /app /app` (census of every `COPY --from=` at head: `/app/dist`, `/app/node_modules`, `/shared`, and single sub-paths), and all 25 class files write node_modules in their final stage, so **none reaches the exemption arm at all** (verified with `SHARED_RELINK_VERBOSE=1` — every file reports `reinstall` or `copy-node_modules`).

**Pinned, not silent:** `check_shared_relink.test.sh` carries a cell named *"R2 row 1d: KNOWN OPEN …"* asserting the current exempt behaviour, so the day it changes something fails and a human reads why.

**Source:** #876 tier-1 verdict 2026-09-06T22:04:18Z, finding 1. **Discovered/measured:** 2026-09-07, session 144, during #876 round 2.

title: KS-597 fallback: resolve the issuer org from the authenticated caller org context — BLOCKED, organization_members has 0 rows
description:
**BLUF — this cannot be built today, and the blocker is data, not design.** The KS-597 ask has two resolution paths for the issuing organisation. The first (resolve from a caller-supplied `organizationUuid`) is implemented and shipping. **This ticket is the second one — *"else from the authenticated caller's org context"* — and it resolves through a table that has no rows.**

Wednesday ruled 2026-09-07 that it must **not** be written as unexercisable code: *"a fallback that resolves through a table with no rows cannot be exercised, and code that cannot be exercised is a check that cannot fail wearing a feature's clothes. Worse than absent: the next reader sees a fallback in the source and believes the case is handled."*

## 🔴 THE BLOCKER, measured

Local stack, one query, with the control in the same statement:

```
documents rows                                      59
documents.issuer_organization_id populated           0
organizations rows            (CONTROL)              6     <- the query CAN see rows
organization_members rows                            0
```

`organization_members` **is empty.** KS-597's own 2026-09-02 comment measured the same zero on the larger tree (`organizations` 151, `organization_members` 0, `documents` 95,127).

**The control is what makes the zero mean something:** `organizations` returning 6 proves the query is not simply blind. Without that line, `organization_members = 0` is indistinguishable from a query that cannot see anything — and this schema is under **forced RLS** (`relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` both true on `organizations` and `documents`), where a role without the `app.current_tenant_id` GUC set reads zero rows from a fully populated table.

## What would unblock it

Membership rows. Specifically, a path that writes `organization_members` at or before registration — org creation, invite acceptance, or a backfill from an existing signal. **Until at least one exists, any fallback written here is untestable by construction: every test would assert the null branch, and the non-null branch would never execute in any environment.**

## What NOT to do

* Do not write the fallback and mark it "covered" — see the ruling above.
* Do not reach for `documents.tenant_id` as a proxy. A tenant is not an organisation; the schema keeps both deliberately, and collapsing them would put wrong attribution in a column whose whole purpose is attribution.

## Scope note

The forward half — resolving a caller-supplied `organizationUuid` onto `documents.issuer_organization_id`, tenant-scoped, folding to NULL when unknown — is **done** and is not blocked by this. The 95k-row backfill is a separate round on Kam's `afterfix` ruling.

**Measured 2026-09-07 on the local stack; the larger-tree figures are from KS-597's own 2026-09-02 comment.**

title: Two schema sources disagree on whether users.email is unique — a statement valid against one is 42P10 against the other, so a suite can be green on a shape that never runs
description:
**BLUF** — the `users` table has **two schema sources that disagree about whether** `email` **is unique**, and a statement that is valid against one is a hard error against the other. This is not a row-level inconsistency; it is a **test environment diverging from the deployed environment on a constraint**, which means a suite can be green on a shape that never runs anywhere.

## ⛔ DO NOT RECONCILE THESE TWO FILES YET

**Nobody has established which source is authoritative.** Aligning either to the other closes the question by erasing the evidence that it was open — and whichever way it is aligned, the loser's behaviour silently becomes "the contract". Establish authority first, then change one file, deliberately, with the reasoning written down.

## The two sources

| file | declaration |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init/01-schema.sql:21` | `email TEXT NOT NULL` — **no unique index** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:20` | `email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL` |

**The first is deliberate and is documented in place.** Its own comment reads: *"email is AES-GCM ciphertext … Lookups go via the deterministic email_lookup_hash … because non-deterministic encryption can't enforce uniqueness."* A unique index on a randomly-IV'd ciphertext cannot block duplicates, so uniqueness was moved to `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` already reflects this — `createUser` conflicts on `email_lookup_hash` and says why.

**So the divergence is probably a migration that was never updated when the encryption landed** — but that is a hypothesis, and this ticket exists so it is checked rather than assumed.

## The evidence, measured

Against the running stack (built from `docker/init/01-schema.sql`), in **rolled-back** transactions:

```
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE ...
  -> ERROR: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching
            the ON CONFLICT specification            (42P10)

INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE ...
  -> INSERT 0 1
```

Index census on the live table: `users_pkey (id)`, `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq (email_lookup_hash) WHERE NOT NULL`, and six social-id uniques. **No index on** `email`**.**

## Why this is a class hazard, not one row

**KS-949 F1 is the instance.** The api-gateway startup seed used `ON CONFLICT (email)`. The round-1 QA gate reported *"fresh DB → INSERT 0 12"* — a true measurement, taken against a database built from `migrations/001`. On every environment we actually deploy, the same statement raised 42P10 and the twelve-row seed silently failed on **every** boot, caught and logged at debug level as "skipped".

**A green test against the wrong schema source is indistinguishable from a green test.** That is the hazard: not that one seed was broken, but that the instrument could not tell.

## What "establishing authority" looks like

1. Which source builds which environment today — compose/init vs the migration runner — measured, not assumed.
2. Whether any deployed database was built from `migrations/001` and therefore **does** have the unique index (if so, the same statement behaves differently per environment, which is worse than either alone).
3. Whether `migrations/001` is still executed anywhere, or is now only a historical artefact that tests happen to build from.
4. Only then: change one file, and add a check that the two cannot drift again.

## Scope

**Not** KS-949's (that fixed the instance and is deliberately silent on which source is right). **Not** KS-957's (that is a claims path — artefacts asserting things their suites cannot check; this is a schema-authority question). Filed separately per the aggregation rule: one ticket per logical path.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during KS-949 round 2.**

---

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION INHERITED BY WHOEVER SETTLES AUTHORITY

**If an environment is built from** `migrations/001`**, does auth's** `seedDemoUsers` **run before document seeding?**

This is a live consequence of the divergence, not a hypothetical, and it is recorded here because it has no other home.

**Why it only exists on one side.** `migrations/001:107` and `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:105` declare `documents.owner_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)`. `docker/init/01-schema.sql:127` — the deployed source — declares `owner_user_id UUID` with **no** foreign key (verified on the live table via `pg_constraint`; control: that file declares no user foreign keys at all).

**So on a migrations-built database the twelve seeded user rows must exist BEFORE any document referencing them is inserted, and on the deployed schema the question cannot arise.** Same tree, same code, two different ordering requirements.

**Why it is now load-bearing.** KS-949 removes the api-gateway startup migration's user INSERT (ratified 2026-09-07: it has never once succeeded — 42P10 on every boot — and auth's `seedDemoUsers` already creates all twelve rows with identical tenancy, encrypted, with `email_lookup_hash` set). After that change, **auth is the only creator of those rows.** On the deployed schema that is safe. On a migrations-built schema it depends on an ordering nobody has measured.

**What would settle it:** whether any environment is built from `migrations/001` today, and if so, the actual boot order of auth's seeder against whatever inserts documents.

**Deliberately NOT settled here**, and not guessed at. Which source a given environment used is exactly the authority question this ticket exists to answer, and answering the ordering first would be assuming it.

**Raised 2026-09-07 during KS-949 round 2.**

title: 104 flat spec files in Blockchain/Dev/tests are in no runner's path — quarantine and find out, do not delete
description:
**BLUF** — `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` holds **104 flat** `*.spec.ts` **files that appear to be in no test runner's path.** They are not a credential problem; they are a dead-code problem, and they were separated out of the KS-964 credential rotation for that reason.

## The measurement

The three playwright configs are `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`, `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/playwright.config.ts` and `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts`. Each sets `testDir: './tests'` **relative to its own directory** — so the paths they cover are `tests/e2e/tests` and `tests/e2e-v2/tests`, not the flat `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` root.

```
flat Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts tracked : 104
under tests/e2e/                            :  48
```

No workflow or script references the flat directory. **Control:** the same search finds `tests/e2e` referenced in **5** files, so the grep can find a referenced path — the zero is a real absence, not a broken search.

The names read like ad-hoc debugging left in place: `admin-sidebar-collapse-final.spec.ts`, `admin-sidebar-collapse-fresh.spec.ts`, `admin-sidebar-simple-check.spec.ts`, `debug-system-health.spec.ts`, `admin-verify-no-mock-data.spec.ts`.

## ⚠ The limit of this evidence, stated

**I checked configs and greps. An ad-hoc** `npx playwright test <file>` **by a person would not show up in either.** So this is "nothing in the repo runs them", not "nobody runs them".

**Therefore: do NOT delete.** Quarantine (rename or move), leave it a sprint, and see who shouts. That is the standing never-delete rule and it is the right instrument for exactly this uncertainty.

## Why it was separated from the credential work

43 of these files contain the retired admin password. Rewriting a credential in a spec nothing runs is work with **no security return** — and worse, it would make the rotation look larger and riskier than it is. The credential in a dead file stops mattering the moment the credential stops working, which KS-964 item 1 achieves.

## The question to answer

1. Is anything running these — a person, a habit, a README?
2. If not: quarantine, then remove after a quiet period.
3. If some are live, they move under a config's `testDir` where the runner can see them, and they get the env-var treatment from KS-964.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during the KS-964 rotation measurement.**

title: Retire the published SYSTEM_ADMIN credential (Kam: rotate-properly) — a deletion, not a rotation: no new shared secret is needed
description:
**Kam ruled** `rotate-properly` **(2026-09-07 11:43:32).** This is the ticket for that work; it was executed before it was filed, which is the cause of a naming error recorded at the bottom.

## What the measurement changed about the job

The card described a 183-occurrence credential spread across 128 files. Measured:

|  | count | files |
| -- | -- | -- |
| total | 183 | 128 |
| **executable** (something reads it) | **93** | 72 |
| **documentary** (a human reads it) | **87** | 55 |

And the executable 93 splits again — **8** env-var-with-a-published-fallback, **12** comment lines inside executable files, **73** hardcoded. Of those 73, **43 are in spec files nothing runs** (KS-964).

**So the real surface was ~32 sites, not 183.**

## The answer that collapsed it into a deletion

**No new shared credential is needed.** `systemTest/playwright/config/environment.ts` already reads `getGeneratedActor(ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY)?.password`, and `provision-actors.ts` provisions actors per run. The published default is the fallback that made that machinery moot. So: nothing to mint, nothing to distribute, and no second rotation waiting in a year.

## Ruled order (Wednesday, 2026-09-07)

1. ✅ **The 8 fallbacks** — delete the default, keep the var, fail closed. **DONE, PR #888.**
2. ✅ **The 5 CI literals** — replaced with a secrets reference. **DONE, PR #888.**
3. ⬜ **4 startup/scripts + 3 harnesses** — env var, no fallback. Same shape as (1). **NOT STARTED.**
4. ⬜ **12 systemTest sites** — route through the generated-actor path. **NOT STARTED.** Ordered last because it is a *routing* change rather than a deletion and carries the only real regression risk in the set. **Prove the actor path resolves BEFORE removing the fallback**, not after.
5. → dead specs: **KS-964**.  6. → documentary sites: **KS-965**.

## ⚠ Behaviour change already shipped in PR #888

With `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` unset, the platform SYSTEM_ADMIN is **not seeded** — unusable hash, suspended status, as the `…060` identity already is. Any environment relying on the default can no longer authenticate as that account. Deliberate.

## 🔴 A naming error to be aware of when reading the history

**PR #888, its branch** `feature/ks-964-retire-published-admin-default`**, and its commit messages all say "KS-964" and mean THIS ticket.** The identifier was guessed from the sequence before the ticket was filed, and the number went to the dead-specs ticket instead. The code and evidence are unaffected; only the label is wrong. Recorded here rather than rewritten, because rewriting pushed history is worse than a documented mislabel.

**Measured 2026-09-07.**

title: Neither credential guard can see a value in a .env.example — one scans the wrong roots and extensions, the other excludes the file and self-tests the exclusion
description:
**Two credential guards run on every push and NEITHER could see the one that mattered.** KS-966 F1 was a live exposure — `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` shipped a value for `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:381` plus `services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:382` both instruct `cp .env.example .env`, so the documented setup path seeded the platform SYSTEM_ADMIN **ACTIVE and loginable** on a credential published in this repository. It sat there through a full round-1 gate.

**This is the guards' blind AXIS, not a bug in either implementation, and it was not introduced by #888.** Both behave exactly as written. That is the problem.

### Measured, from the scripts themselves

**1.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh:28-32` — cannot reach the file on two independent axes:

```
grep -rEn --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' \
     --exclude-dir=__tests__ --exclude-dir=tests --exclude-dir=scripts \
     ... services/ packages/
```

* **Extension:** `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` only. A `.env.example` is not scannable by construction.
* **Root:** `services/` and `packages/` only. `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` is above both.

Either one alone is sufficient to miss it. Widening one and not the other changes nothing.

**2.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/no-tracked-credentials.sh:37-38` — excludes it *deliberately*:

```
EXCLUDE_RE='\.(example|sample|template)$'
```

with the comment at `:34-36` explaining that 25 `.env.example` files are tracked on purpose and are the documented way to describe required config. **And its own self-test at** `:51-53` **asserts the exclusion holds**, naming `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` as a probe that MUST be excluded:

```
for probe in "Blockchain/Dev/.env.example" "svc/config.example"; do
  echo "$probe" | grep -Eq "$EXCLUDE_RE" || { echo "SELF-TEST FAIL: did not exclude $probe"; ok=1; }
done
```

So the guard is not merely blind here — **it is tested to be blind here.** Any fix has to change that self-test too, consciously, or it will be reverted by the next person who reads it as a regression.

### Why the exclusion is right and still leaves a hole

The exclusion exists for a good reason: an example file must be allowed to *name* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, or it cannot document the variable at all. **The distinction the guards do not draw is between naming a key and assigning it a value.** `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=` is documentation. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=<something>` is a credential. A file-level exclusion cannot tell those apart; a line-level rule can.

### Shape when picked up

A check over tracked `*.env.example` files that fails on **a non-empty assignment to a credential-shaped key**, rather than on the file's existence. Keys named, not pattern-guessed — the pattern-guessing is what produces the false positives the current exclusion was written to avoid.

### Interim cover — real but partial, and it must not be mistaken for this ticket being done

#888 round 2 adds a cell (`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`, the `KS-966 F1` block) that walks the tree for `*.env.example` and fails on a non-empty `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` / `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. It is red-proved (restoring a value gives 2 red of 23 executing).

**It covers two key names in one service's test suite.** It is not a push-time gate, it does not run when only non-auth code changes, and it says nothing about any other credential-shaped key. The gap this ticket names is the guards' coverage axis, and that is still open.

title: The published admin credential survives in USER_TESTING docs while nothing on the demo seeds it any more — and the switch that would restore seeding now suspends that account
description:
## BLUF

`USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md` advertises `admin@secuura.com` **/** `admin123` at **:68** and **:177**. KS-964/KS-966 retired that published fallback in the seeder, and separately the demo's seeder does not run at all. So the doc is a published credential for an account nobody can currently prove is loginable — and the obvious remedy (turn seeding back on) **suspends** the account unless a second variable is set in the same change.

Two items, one code path (the seed-credential surface). Filed together per the aggregate rule.

## What was measured, 2026-09-08 (s149)

**On the demo VM's** `auth` **container, read-only, authorised narrowly by Wednesday (set/unset only, value never read):**

* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` = **UNSET**
* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` = **PRESENT-EMPTY**
* `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` = **UNSET**
* Instrument validated first: `NODE_ENV`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY` all read **SET** (4 of 4 boot-critical controls), a nonsense variable read UNSET, and `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` reading PRESENT-EMPTY proves the probe separates present-empty from absent.
* ⚠ **Round 1 of this read was discarded, not reported.** Its positive control was `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD`, which also read UNSET — but that variable has a *published fallback* (`seedPw(var,'demo123')`), so its absence is invisible and it cannot prove the probe can see a present value. The control was mine and it was wrong.

**Direct evidence from the running system** (`auth` container log, started 2026-09-07T05:46:39Z, 7676 lines readable):

* `"Demo user seeding skipped — set ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true to enable"` — **present ×1**
* `"Demo user seeding skipped in non-dev env"` — **0**
* `"Demo user seeding enabled in non-dev environment"` — **0**
* Controls: 3762 unrelated startup matches (log is greppable), an impossible string returns 0.

**So** `seedDemoUsersInner` **returns at its FIRST gate on the demo and never reaches any account row.** The gate block is byte-identical between `632f16dfe` (deployed) and `400517aaf` (trunk) — sha256 `e77a5c30…` both sides, with a control block that DOES differ across the same range, so the comparison can see a change.

## Items

- [ ] **1. The doc advertises a credential the platform no longer seeds.** `USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md:68` and `:177` publish `admin@secuura.com` / `admin123`. Decide and apply: correct the doc, or restore the account deliberately. **Whether that login works on the demo today is NOT established** — the row may persist from an earlier seeding era with its old hash. Answering it needs a DB read that was outside this seat's authorisation.
- [ ] **2. Turning seeding back on now suspends the platform admin.** The moment anyone sets `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` on the demo to restore seeding, `requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')` returns null (`userRepo.ts:1039,1075`), and the null branch writes `status='suspended'` plus an unusable hash — **actively suspending a pre-existing row, not merely skipping it**. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` must be set in the *same* change. This is a trap for whoever next tries to re-seed, and nothing warns them at the point of the switch.
- [ ] **3. Consider making the trap loud rather than documented** — the seeder could refuse to start (or log at `error`) when `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` is combined with a `requiredSeedPw` account whose variable is unset, instead of silently suspending it.

## Why this is filed and not fixed

Wednesday's ANSWER, 2026-09-08: *"Do not edit USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md yet… the fix depends on which way Q1 goes. File it as a ticket now so it cannot be lost."* Setting a credential on a running system is Kam's signature class and collides with his own `rotate-properly` ruling on the admin credential (2026-09-07).

**Q1 came back in a way that DE-ESCALATES the deploy:** the `632f16dfe..400517aaf` deploy does **not** suspend `admin@secuura.com`, because the seeder never runs. Item 2 is the residual risk that outlives the deploy.

## Not blocking the deploy

The 19-commit deploy is unaffected by this ticket. Recorded here so the finding cannot be lost when the deploy card closes.

title: The OAuth token endpoint is outside the credential-stuffing rate-limit zone — /api/oauth/ is not keyed in $secuura_auth_limit_key
description:
## BLUF

`/api/oauth/` **sits OUTSIDE the credential-stuffing rate-limit zone that** `/api/auth/` **sits inside.** The OAuth token endpoint — the one that exchanges codes and redeems refresh tokens — gets only the aggregate `/api/` ceiling, not the 5 r/s + burst 10 bound the config itself calls *"the credential-stuffing bound"*.

**True whether or not** [KS-823](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-823) **is fixed**, which is why this is its own ticket rather than a sub-item of it: KS-823 is about the refresh grant's missing client authentication; this is about the rate-limit zone configuration. Different logical path, per Kam's one-ticket-per-path rule.

## Measured

`Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf`, read at the demo VM's SHA `400517aaf`:

```nginx
map $request_uri $secuura_auth_limit_key {
    "~^/api/auth/"     $secuura_limit_key;
    "~^/api/v1/auth/"  $secuura_limit_key;
}
limit_req_zone $secuura_auth_limit_key zone=secuura_auth:10m rate=5r/s;
```

The map keys **two** prefixes. `/api/oauth/` is neither. The file's own comment describes the zone as *"auth at 5 r/s + burst 10 is the credential-stuffing bound"* — so the intent of the zone is explicit, and the token endpoint is outside it.

**The endpoint is reachable:** `nginx-demo.conf` `location /api/` → the gateway; `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:317` `router.use('/api/oauth', proxy('auth', …))` with no `authenticateToken` and no scope gate (deliberately — the section header reads *"AUTH / USER / SESSION (no gateway auth — handled by auth service)"*).

**Control that the map's silence is real and not a grep artefact:** the same map DOES key `/api/auth/` and `/api/v1/auth/`, and neighbouring gateway mounts in `proxy.ts` ARE guarded (`/api/webhooks` carries `authenticateToken(true), attachScopes, requireScope('webhooks:manage')`). So both instruments can produce a positive, and the negative on `/api/oauth/` means something.

**No request was made against the demo, valid or invalid.** This is a read of code and configuration only.

## Why it matters

`POST /api/oauth/token` accepts credential-bearing material — an authorization code, a refresh token, and for confidential apps a client secret. It is a guessing surface of the same class as `/api/auth/login`, and it is the one the zone was written to bound. Anything that brute-forces or sprays against it meets only the aggregate `/api/` ceiling shared with every other API path, rather than the per-key 5 r/s bound.

## Not claimed

* **No exploitability measurement.** Whether the aggregate `/api/` ceiling is in practice tight enough has NOT been measured, and doing so needs a probe that has not been authorised.
* **No claim about the local or production configs.** `nginx-demo.conf` was read; `nginx.conf` and `nginx-production.conf` were not, and they may differ. Whoever picks this up should check all three before changing one.

## Fix shape

Add `"~^/api/oauth/" $secuura_limit_key;` to the map, or widen the existing keys — then confirm the other two nginx configs and decide whether the same gap exists there. A rate-limit change wants its own verification that legitimate token exchange is not throttled.

Discovered 2026-09-08 during KS-1001's disposition pass over the P2 In Review queue, while reading KS-823's reachability.

title: e2e: "CIP-30 API availability check" calls a route that does not exist, and its assertion passes on the 404
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/.../happy-path-wallet.spec.ts:255` **calls a route that does not exist — and its assertion**
**is written so that the 404 PASSES.** The test is named *"CIP-30 API availability check"* and asserts
only `expect(response.status()).toBeLessThan(500)`, with a comment saying *"may return 404 if not*
*implemented"*. **404 < 500.** It has never been able to fail for the thing it names.

**This is not one line.** The same shape runs through the recruitment e2e suite: **13**
`toBeLessThan(500)` **assertions and 33** `if (response.ok())` **guards across 62 tests in 5 files.** An
`if (response.ok())` wrapper means that when the endpoint is absent, **zero assertions execute and the**
**test passes.**

Surfaced by @PeterObeden's `wallet/status` question on PR #802 (see KS-1009). It is a
**check-that-cannot-fail**, which is this board's most-repeated family.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| service-side references to `/api/wallet/status` | **0** — the route does not exist |
| service-side references to `/api/wallet/supported` | **0** — nor does this one |
| **CONTROL —** `/api/auth/wallet/challenge`**, used correctly in the same file** | **6** |

The control is what makes the zeros mean something: the same search over the same tree finds the route
that does exist, so the zeros are real absences rather than a search that cannot match.

**And the correct path is already known inside the same directory.** `fixtures/recruitment-data.ts:291`
defines:

