On a **fresh bare database**, `public.certifications` ends with row-level security **ENABLED and FORCED but with no** `tenant_isolation` **policy**. RLS with no policy is **default-deny**, so the table is unreadable and unwritable by the application role — and unlike the defect #1332 fixed, **this does not heal on a later boot**. It is permanent for the life of that database.

Measured across all four head paths (gateway runner boot 1 and boot 2, `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, and both combined): identical, `4c59e2ebdc37`. The **merge-base differs** (`fd91b0ab5a48`) and **does** carry `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON public.certifications` — so the merge-base heals it and the current tip does not. An app-role `INSERT` carrying the tenant GUC is **refused**.

## Why it changed

`migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` (added in #1332) creates `certifications` **before** 039 runs. 039 then finds the table present and applies its RLS `ENABLE`/`FORCE` block to it — but the branch of 039 that creates the `tenant_isolation` policy does not cover it on that path. Before #1332, `certifications` did not exist when 039 ran, so 039 skipped it entirely and a later boot created it with its policy intact.

## A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE, filed here deliberately rather than separately (N-G39-4)

`038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` lines **16-17** describe this exact condition — `certifications` with RLS forced and no `tenant_isolation` policy — as one of the things the migration **fixes**. **It does not fix it; it is the cause of it.** The same header's claim that the schema equality is "proved … across … the docker/init seeded path" is also **wider than true**: the equality holds for `certifications` only, and fails for `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` because of a pre-existing docker/init DDL difference (extra indexes and the `svc_webhooks_app_id_fkey` foreign key). Both header claims need correcting in the same change that fixes the policy, so the file does not keep asserting a fix it does not deliver.

## Fix shape (from the gate)

A migration numbered **after 039** that applies 039's `tenant_isolation` block to `certifications`, plus a **real-PostgreSQL cell driven as the application role** (`secuura_app`) asserting that an `INSERT` carrying the correct tenant GUC succeeds and one carrying a foreign tenant is refused. A source-text assertion is not sufficient here: the defect is a runtime default-deny, and only a driven app-role probe distinguishes "policy present" from "policy absent but table reachable as owner".

## Scope

Not fixed in #1332 — that PR was round 2 of 2 under the class cap and shipped GO WITH FINDINGS with this as named residue. No board ticket covered it before this one (searched by symbol: `certifications` + `tenant_isolation`, `tenant_isolation policy certifications`, `038a`, `certifications RLS force default-deny`, `certifications no tenant_isolation` — zero title-relevant results; three positive controls each returned their expected ticket first, so the search was working).

Refs KS-1054

title: Three range-widened HIGH advisories freeze every push; two have no upstream fix
description:
**BLUF:** every push on this repo is refused by the pre-push preflight on legs 6 and 7. Three HIGH advisories are reported and not baselined. **Two of the three have no upstream fix in existence.** Kam ruled option (b) on 2026-10-04.

## The refusal

Measured on a real push attempt (Seat B 55th, 2026-10-04 08:49:12 to 08:56:04Z, push rc 1, no `--no-verify`): `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 6 7 - fix the above before pushing. (12/15 legs ran)`. The other 10 legs that ran were clean; 3 skipped for "local stack not up". Nothing reached origin.

| advisory | package | pinned | locks |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm | braces | 3.0.3 | 11 standalone + workspace root |
| GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp | http-cache-semantics | 4.2.0 | services/anchoring, services/nft-certificate |
| GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv | node-forge | 1.4.0 | services/timestamping |

## The mechanism is a RANGE WIDENING, not a new publication

Instrument: GitHub advisory API, read 2026-10-04.

* GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm published 2026-09-18T18:31:41, **updated 2026-10-02T22:36:34**
* GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp published 2026-09-18T18:31:44, **updated 2026-10-02T22:36:44**
* GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv published 2026-09-03T21:31:15, **updated 2026-10-01T21:09:10**

All three were published weeks ago. All three were updated **after** the last green push (2026-10-01 \~16:0xZ, whose preflight ran these same two legs and reported "Nothing failed"). The pinned versions never moved; the advisories' affected ranges moved onto them. A repo nobody touched for 2 d 19 h froze itself.

## Two of the three cannot be fixed by any bump

Each affected range is `<=` exactly the version we pin, and each has `first_patched_version: none` (advisory API). Cross-checked against the npm registry:

* braces: latest published **is** 3.0.3 — no newer version exists
* node-forge: latest published **is** 1.4.0 — no newer version exists
* http-cache-semantics: latest **4.3.0**, which is outside `<= 4.2.0`

## Shipped exposure is FOUR paths, not fourteen

Instrument: lockfile `dev` / `devOptional` flags read from develop `88e8877a2a0d`, plus each service Dockerfile. Control: `express` in services/api-gateway reads PROD.

* braces is **DEV in 10 of 11 locks** and PROD in exactly one, services/api-gateway
* http-cache-semantics is PROD in both anchoring and nft-certificate
* node-forge is PROD in services/timestamping

Every runtime stage omits dev (api-gateway, anchoring and timestamping all `npm ci --omit=dev`; nft-certificate builds with dev then `npm prune --omit=dev` and the runner copies that tree). So the ten dev-only braces locks do not ship it.

## Reachability of the vulnerable code

Instrument: `git grep` over product code at `88e8877a2a0d`. Control: the same grep shape finds `from 'express'` in 326 files, so a zero is a reading.

* braces (CWE-674, availability): **0 direct callers**
* http-cache-semantics (CWE-524, confidentiality): **0 direct callers**; transitive, declared by `cacheable-request`
* node-forge (CWE-347, integrity, forged RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures): not transitive. `services/timestamping` declares `"node-forge": "^1.3.3"` and imports it at `src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:18` and `src/tsa/rfc3161-client.ts:12`. **The vulnerable operation is not invoked:** `verifyRealToken` performs no signature verification, and `rfc3161-client.ts` matches `verify` zero times. That is tracked separately — see the timestamping ticket.

## Kam's ruling, 2026-10-04 21:05:25 AEDT (card secuura-freeze5-high-no-fix-1004 = b)

"Fix what can be fixed, remove node-forge, accept only braces". Card option text, verbatim: *"One T1 PR: the http-cache-semantics refresh + a braces baseline row (reason, ticket, expiry no later than 31 Oct). node-forge gets removed from timestamping in the same rework the separate unsigned-token card needs; until that lands it carries a baseline row with the same expiry."*

## The fix, as ruled

1. http-cache-semantics: in-range lock refresh on services/anchoring and services/nft-certificate only, 4.2.0 to 4.3.0, **no manifest change needed** — `cacheable-request` declares `^4.0.0`. Dry resolution in scratch copies of the base manifests and locks moved exactly 1 entry per lock, 0 added, 0 removed, and npm then reported `found 0 vulnerabilities`. Contrast control: the same command for braces, whose latest is our pin, moves the lock not at all. **These are host-npm figures; the Docker daemon was down, so the containerised cleanroom re-take is outstanding.**
2. A baseline row for braces, reason and expiry per the ruling.
3. A baseline row for node-forge, with removal tracked on the timestamping ticket.

## Not covered

No containerised cleanroom re-take (Docker not running). Whether an attacker-controlled input can reach a brace pattern in api-gateway is **unmeasured**. The 15 baseline rows the same leg reports as no longer reported are out of scope here.

title: a password change or reset leaves the account's other sessions live
description:
## BLUF

A successful password change does not revoke the account's other sessions, and neither does the reset
flow. Raised from gate59's review of PR #1382 (KS 1005). **Pre-existing — not introduced by that PR.**

## N-1382-1 — no session revocation on a successful password change

A successful change makes **zero** `revokeAllUserSessions` calls. The reset flow does not revoke
either. So after a password change — including a change prompted by suspected compromise — every
other authenticated session on that account stays live.

Scope of the evidence, stated so it is not over-read: this was **measured on mocked calls only**, not
against a running stack. The count of zero is a count of calls the handler makes, not a live
observation of a surviving session.

## N-1382-2 — the e2e test for this can never fail

- [ ] Fix the e2e case so it can fail. Case 12.5.3, "other sessions should be invalidated", POSTs to
      `/api/auth/change-password` — **a route that does not exist** — and asserts only inside
      `if (status === 200)`. Because the request cannot return 200, the assertion body never runs, so
      the test passes unconditionally. It has therefore never tested the behaviour in N-1382-1, and
      the correct route is the one KS 1005 fixes.

## Adjacent, and deliberately not merged into this ticket

KS 257 ("Session revocation only enforced at the auth service") is adjacent but different — it is
about *where* revocation is enforced, not *whether* a password change triggers it — and it is
archived. Noted here so the connection is not lost.

title: revoke answers 400 "already revoked" where 404 belongs if the document is deleted mid-race
description:
**Pre-existing, and narrowed rather than introduced by the KS 1278 change.** Found while building PR #1393.

`updateDocument` in originate's document repository returns `null` for **two** different outcomes:

1. the document was not found — the inner `getDocument` read came back empty (the pre-existing path, `documentRepo.ts:538`);
2. the guarded write changed no row — the KS 1278 `ifStatusIsNot` guard refused it because the row was already in the target status.

The revoke route maps `null` to **400 BAD_REQUEST "Document is already revoked"**. For the ordinary case that is right, and deliberately so: the route 404s and 403s before the write, and 400s on the read, so by the time the guarded write runs the document exists and was not revoked at read time — a `null` can only mean the row became revoked in between, which is exactly the race KS 1278 closes.

**The residual:** if the document is **deleted** between the route's read and the guarded write, outcome 1 fires instead, and the caller is told **"Document is already revoked" with a 400** when the correct answer is **404 Document not found**. The window is narrow — it is a race, not a reachable sequential path — and nothing here is a security or data-integrity problem: no write happens, no provenance row is recorded and no anchor is emitted in either case. It is a response-classification defect only.

**Before KS 1278** the route did not read the write's result at all, so this particular confusion could not arise there; the same single `null` was already ambiguous for every other caller of `updateDocument`, which is why this is recorded as pre-existing in shape and merely surfaced at a new call site.

**What a fix would need.** Separate the two meanings rather than overload one `null` — for example a discriminated result (not-found vs guard-refused vs updated), or a cheap existence re-read on the `null` path before choosing the status code. Both touch every caller of `updateDocument`, which is why it was explicitly left out of KS 1278's scope rather than bolted on.

**Not measured.** No live sweep and no two-session test ran against a real PostgreSQL. The claim above is read off the control flow in `documentRepo.ts` and `routes/documents.ts` plus the mocked cells in PR #1393, not reproduced against a running stack.

Refs KS-1278

title: packages/shared: one test imports services/demo-service and needs cors, so the suite cannot pass on a member-only install
description:
**BLUF:** one test file in `packages/shared` needs another workspace member's dependency, so the package's suite cannot pass on an install that provides only `packages/shared`'s own closure. It passes on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`, where `cors` is hoisted from `services/*`.

**Measured** (2026-10-12, Seat F 17th; clean-room copy of develop `a31b77577` with no `node_modules`; node v24.7.0):

* `npm ci` run inside `packages/shared` is an implicit-workspace install from the root lock (npm's prefix there is `Blockchain/Dev`). A stock one has no vitest at all, so to see this I made vitest resolvable in that install (a variant lock carrying the KS-1317 vitest declaration). Then `npm test`: `Test Files  1 failed | 48 passed (49)`, `Tests  945 passed | 4 skipped (949)`.
* The one failing file is `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`: `Error: Cannot find package 'cors' imported from .../services/demo-service/src/app.ts` (`app.ts:14`), thrown from the file's `KS-832 ACCEPTANCE BAR` suite, whose 4 tests are then skipped.
* Control, same develop on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`: `node_modules/cors` present, `Test Files 48 passed (48)`, `Tests 945 passed (945)`, `tsc --noEmit -p packages/shared` rc 0. In the member-only install `node_modules/cors` is absent.
* `cors` is declared by 21 of the `services/*/package.json` files (`demo-service` among them) and not by `packages/shared`, so nothing in `packages/shared/package.json` tells a reader the suite depends on it.

**Why it matters:** the dependency is invisible and works only through hoisting, so the failure appears only when someone runs the package's tests without the full install. It is lower urgency than it looks: since the KS-1317 guard, a member-only `npm test` stops early with a message naming the full install, so this is reached only when someone supplies vitest another way.

**Suggested shapes (not prescribed):**

* Move the test to where its dependency is declared (`services/demo-service`), or to a root-level guard suite that is only run after a full install.
* Do not declare `cors` in `packages/shared`: the 25 service Dockerfiles (of the 29 that reference `packages/shared`; the other four are frontends) copy `/shared` (with its `node_modules`) from the `shared-builder` stage into the runtime image, so any new dependency there ships in every image. That is the cost that made the Spark's vitest declaration for KS-1317 the wrong shape.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` (the boot of the demo-service app, around line 5601), `Blockchain/Dev/services/demo-service/src/app.ts` line 14.

Found while raising KS-1317. Filed unassigned in Backlog on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-10-12.

title: api-gateway: an untyped create never meets the catalogue's DOCUMENT rules (enforcement.ts:101), plus two KS-1203 follow-ups (PR #1465 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Three notes from the Opus QA gate on PR #1465 (KS-1203 option A, merged as `a2f575a642638d64493997d0f68747a1d1f03dc6`), left out of that PR on purpose because a change to the gated head would have voided the GO. **Note 1 matters most:** an untyped `POST /api/documents` never meets the type catalogue's `DOCUMENT` rules, so the type's own requirements are skipped for exactly the body KS-1203 is about. It is pre-existing and outside the ruled scope. The gate graded it Minor; I filed it at Medium because it is an authorization-shaped gap.

## Recommendation

One small tier-1 PR, test first:

1. **Resolve an untyped body to the default type in** `enforceDocumentTypeRules`**, not just in the connector allow-list.** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:101` still resolves a body with no type to `''`, so the function returns `docType: {}` and enforces nothing. The catalogue's `DOCUMENT` entry (seeded at `routes/admin.ts:316-336`, described as "the default when a creation request names no documentType") is never applied to an untyped create: `isActive`, `creatorVerificationLevel`, `requireMFA`, `metadataSchema` and `requiresApproval` are all skipped. Use the shared `DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_TYPE` there. **Measure first** (read-only): what the stored `DOCUMENT` entry requires on each environment, because enforcing it on untyped creates can newly refuse callers who rely on the gap, the same lockout risk KS-1190 names.
2. **Behavioural cells for the two sites that are only source-pinned.** `originate/src/routes/documents.ts:584` and the gateway workflow gate (`enforcement.ts:264`) are covered only by a regex over the source text; the gate's three mutations turned only that cell red. Add a cell asserting that originate stores `DOCUMENT` for each of the eight untyped shapes. Note that after item 1 the workflow-gate site becomes reachable for an untyped body, and can finally be tested behaviourally.
3. **Tell operators about the new 403.** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:119-123` does not say that an untyped create from a restricted connector is checked as `DOCUMENT`. A connector operator who hits the new 403 has no hint.

## Detail

* **Source:** Opus gate on PR #1465, verdict `GO WITH NOTE`, no Major. Verdict file sha256/16 `8d8a2c2d745d81c5` (Wednesday's `reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1465/verdict.md`).
* **What PR #1465 did and did not claim:** it made the allow-list apply to the resolved default type. It did not claim the catalogue rules apply, and its comment "the check and the stored type cannot drift apart again" is true for the allow-list only.
* **Related:** KS-1203 (the parent; stays In Progress until deployed), KS-1190 (a different gap in the same enforcement code: an unknown required level fails open).

title: ks963 wallet ordering guard: three blind spots in the source scan (template interpolation, tagged/bracket/optional calls, raw-body SELECT pin)
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on #1469 (KS-1131 items 3 and 4, head `8f2145e1f`, GO WITH NOTE, no Major). The new `assertWalletNothingWrittenBeforeLookup` is a **source-scan guard, not a behavioural test**, and it has three blind spots. All Minor; none blocks the merge. Item 1 is the only one that is a coverage regression against the old cell.

## Recommendation

Fix 1 and 3 in one small test-only PR (recurse into `${}`; read the blanked body for the SELECT pin). Leave 2 unless a real write ever lands in one of those shapes; a behavioural test of `getOrCreateWalletUser` against a stubbed pool would retire the whole class and is the better long-term answer.

## Detail (line numbers at head `8f2145e1f`; they drift)

1. **Template interpolation** (`ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` lines 251-263, `blankCommentsAndStrings`): the quote branch blanks a whole template literal, `${...}` included. Planting `` const _s = `${await query("INSERT ...")}`; `` before the lookup: the OLD cell was RED (its `await` regex saw it), the NEW cell is green. A small coverage regression for an exotic shape. Fix: recurse into `${}` and keep its contents unblanked.
2. **Call shapes the regex cannot see** (line 290, `(?<![\w$.])` plus a dotted-name pattern): a tagged template (`` await query`INSERT ...` ``), a bracket call (`(userRepo as any)["createUser"]({})`) and an optional invoke (`(query as any)?.(...)`) all stay green. Measured green on OLD too except the interpolation case. Very low risk; the bracket and optional shapes are caught only when the literal `createUser(` appears.
3. **The SELECT pin reads the raw body** (line 296, `expect(body.slice(0, lookup)).toContain('SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet')`): a `// SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet` comment satisfies it, so swapping the real query text for an INSERT while leaving that comment stays 22/22 green. The OLD cell had the same gap; this PR did not introduce it.

Not a defect, recorded so nobody "fixes" it: any harmless call before the lookup (`walletAddress.toLowerCase()`, `logger.debug(...)`) reds the cell, as does renaming `getOrCreateWalletUser` or turning it into an arrow function. That is the allow-set contract the test's own docblock states (fails closed).

Provenance: Sonnet-tier QA gate on #1469, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1469/verdict.md` (read 2026-10-12); filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-1131, KS-963, KS-1155 (the load-timeout class that shares this file's neighbourhood).

title: updateDocument atomicity follow-ups: two blob writers still decide from a prior read, plus a type guard and test nits (KS-1124 gate)
description:
## BLUF

PR #1471 (KS-1124 option A) made every blob write that goes through `updateDocument` atomic. Its Opus gate (GO WITH NOTE, head `4a822bd8c244`, no Major) and Wednesday's GO list what it does not cover. Filed as ONE ticket so none is rediscovered. **None is a regression and none blocks #1471.**

## Recommendation

Fix the first two together in one tier-1 PR (they are the same defect class #1471 closed, in the two places it did not reach), test first with a forced interleaving on a real Postgres as K1-K10 do (recipe: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`). Take the guard and the nits with it or as a small tier-2 PR after.

## Detail

1. `anchorStateSync.ts:178-212`**,** `markDocumentAnchorFailed` decides from a read taken before the `UPDATE`: the `confirmed` guard (`:180`) and the `txHash` / `blockHeight` / `network` / `anchoredAt` carry (`:190-196`). A confirm write landing between the read and the write can be downgraded to `anchor_failed` with its `txHash` erased. Same family as KS-1004. (Line numbers at the PR head.)
2. `routes/certifications.ts:563` replaces `certification_metadata` wholesale, outside `updateDocument`. It drops `threadToken` from the authoritative blob, and the KS-550 heal then copies that loss into `metadata`.
3. **Hardening,** `documentRepo.ts:632/640/661/669`**.** The replace branch has no `jsonb_typeof(supplied) = 'object'` guard. A future `blockchain: null` would store `[{…}, null]` (`'{}'::jsonb || 'null'::jsonb` gives `[{}, null]`), where the old code stored `null`. No current caller can reach it (`verification.ts:393` guards `!healed`).
4. **Test nits in** `ks1124-blockchain-blob-writes-are-atomic.integration.test.ts`**.** (a) K9 (`:218-224`) seeds `anchored`, which `mapDbStatus` round-trips, so it cannot detect a status write-back; seeding `deleted` or `certified` would pin the "status not supplied keeps the stored status" semantics (only K1 reds on that mutant today). (b) `waiting()` (`:93`) counts lock waits cluster-wide, with no `datname` or `pid` filter; on a shared server a parallel job could satisfy it and make a forced interleaving vacuous. (c) `documentRepo.ts:697-702`: the returned record carries `threadToken` and the status from the first read; presentation only.
5. **Pre-existing, outside KS-1124's scope, and the largest.** Every `updateDocument` rewrites `certification_metadata` to `{ signatures, blockchain }`, which erases `issuerName`, `certificationId` and `certifiedAt` written by `certifications.ts:563` and the admin backfill. `signatures` and `data` also remain read-then-write: a concurrent sign and anchor write can drop a signature. Consider splitting this into its own ticket when it is picked up.
6. **Left in place on purpose:** the pollers' `carriedForward` (`anchorStateSync.ts:111-113`) is now redundant with the SQL carry; it was kept to keep #1471 off `anchorStateSync`. It can go with item 1.

Refs KS-1124, KS-1074, KS-1004, KS-550.

title: Verification store: a request filed during the database's startup outage is still answered from memory after it recovers (duplicate PENDING, memory approval)
description:
## BLUF

Gate finding on #1473 (KS-1018 item 3, GO WITH NOTE), residual and **inside the ruling's carve-out**, filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. With a database configured, a verification request filed while `isDbAvailable()` is false lives only in the process-local map, and a read that SUCCEEDS with no row still consults that map. So after the database recovers, the request is still visible to some reads and can be acted on. It is the same hazard class #1473 closes for failed reads, reachable only through a degraded-boot request.

## Recommendation

Small PR after #1473: stop consulting the map when a database is configured and the read succeeded (an empty DB answer is the answer), and make "memory-only" mean "no `DATABASE_URL`", not "the pool is not ready yet". Decide how a request filed during the KS-377 boot window should behave: refuse it with 503 (preferred: nothing is silently kept in a place the next replica cannot see) rather than store it in memory.

## Detail (gate probe on head `2026b2e6d0c8`, `logs/probe_head.txt`)

* `isDbAvailable()` is false both with no `DATABASE_URL` AND during the KS-377 boot window of a configured database, so "no-database mode" in the comments is broader than the name says.
* Effect measured on the head: list answers 200 without the request; a second `POST /me/verification` answers 200, so there are now two PENDING requests (one in memory, one in the database); approving answers 200 and the user's verification level is RAISED.
* Where: the success-empty memory consult at `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` in `getVerificationRequest` (and the pending and list reads' memory returns for the same condition).

## Also in the same small PR (gate notes on #1473, both comment-level)

1. **A false justification.** The comment above the success-empty consult in `users.ts` says a read that succeeds with no row "still consults the map (KS-467 depends on that)", and the header of `ks1018-item3-a-configured-database-never-answers-from-memory.test.ts` (line 17) repeats it. It is false: `ks467` mocks `isDbAvailable: () => false`; making a success-empty read return null reds 0 of 898 cells, twice. Nothing pins or depends on it. Correct both comments (or delete the behaviour as above and pin it).
2. **Dead state.** `pendingReadFails` in `ks1194-a-failed-verification-request-save-is-never-acknowledged.test.ts` is still declared and reset but no longer read since #1473 rewrote the one cell that used it. Remove it.
3. **Observation, not a defect here:** 40001 and 40P01 are retryable but answer 500, not 503; that comes from the KS-253 classifier, predates #1473, and is pinned by KS-1193 F2.

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1473, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1473/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `e647c1d64ab497e9`), defects 1 to 3; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-1018, KS-1194, KS-377, KS-467, KS-1193.

title: pre-push gate: a file renamed OUT of Blockchain/Dev is listed only by its new path, so the preflight is skipped
description:
**BLUF.** `.githooks/pre-push` builds its changed set with `git diff --name-only <base> HEAD`. Under git's default rename detection, a file moved OUT of `Blockchain/Dev/` is listed only by its NEW path, so the `^Blockchain/Dev/` filter finds nothing and the 15-leg preflight is skipped, silently, for a push that removed code from the guarded tree. It is pre-existing: the tip's hook, `302d8d081` and the KS-884 fix all skip it. Found by the KS-884 ref matrix (scenario S14).

**Recommendation.** Add `--no-renames` to the diffs that build the changed set (`.githooks/pre-push:80` and `:184`; grep the file for any other `git diff --name-only`), so the vanished old path is listed as a deletion. Add one test cell: a `git mv` out of `Blockchain/Dev/` pushed through a real hook, asserting `[preflight] ran`; it must be red against today's hook. Not built here.

**Detail.**

* Measured 2026-10-12 by Seat F 17th while working KS-884. Scenario S14: a file under `Blockchain/Dev/` renamed to `docs/` (100% similarity), pushed to a local bare remote. Result SKIP for the tip's hook, `302d8d081`'s hook and the KS-884 fix (the push lands, no `[pre-push]` output at all).
* Mechanism, checked in a scratch repo: a 40-line file committed under `Blockchain/Dev/`, then `git mv` to `docs/`. `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD` prints only `docs/guarded.txt` (0 lines match `^Blockchain/Dev/`); with `--no-renames` it prints `Blockchain/Dev/guarded.txt` and `docs/guarded.txt` (1 match).
* Scope limit: default rename detection needs about 50% similarity, so a move with heavy edits is already listed as an add plus a delete. The gap is a (near-)pure move.
* The same `all_changed` list also feeds the `systemTest/*` formatting-gate filter (KS-989), which would share the blind spot for a move out of `systemTest/`. Not measured.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatF-17th/ks884_ref_matrix.sh` (S14) and `ks884_matrix_full_OLD.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_CURRENT_302d8d0.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_FIXED.txt`.
* Related: KS-884 (PR #1474). Not caused or changed by it.

title: pre-push gate: pushing a branch that is not checked out skips the preflight, because the hook diffs HEAD and not the pushed commits
description:
**BLUF.** `.githooks/pre-push` decides whether to run the preflight from `HEAD` (`git diff --name-only "@{upstream}" HEAD` at `:80`, `"$_b" HEAD` at `:184`), and the preflight then tests the working tree. The refs git hands the hook on stdin are read only for the force-push check (`:48-69`). So `git push origin some-other-branch`, with a clean `HEAD` on another branch, skips the preflight for a `Blockchain/Dev` change in the branch actually pushed. The push lands with no `[pre-push]` output. Pre-existing; identical in the tip's hook, `302d8d081` and the KS-884 fix. Found by the KS-884 ref matrix (scenario S15).

**Recommendation.** Make the hook judge what is pushed, not what is checked out. Read the stdin lines (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>`) and:

1. Compute the changed set per pushed ref from `<local sha>` against its base, not from `HEAD`.
2. Because the preflight tests the working tree (HEAD), also FAIL CLOSED: when a pushed `<local sha>` is not `HEAD` and it changes `Blockchain/Dev`, refuse with a clear message ("check out what you push, or push with the bypass deliberately"), rather than run the wrong tree. Running the preflight in a temporary worktree of the pushed sha is the heavier alternative.
3. Handle the shapes the stdin loop already skips: branch deletes (`<local sha>` all zeros), brand-new remote branches, tags (`refs/tags/...`), and multi-ref pushes (`--all`, several refspecs).
   Add a test cell per shape (red against today's hook for the unchecked-out branch). Not built here; this is the larger of the two KS-884 follow-ups because it changes what the hook refuses.

**Detail.**

* Measured 2026-10-12 by Seat F 17th. Scenario S15: `b-other` carries a `Blockchain/Dev` change, `HEAD` is back on a clean branch at `origin/develop`, then `git push origin b-other` to a local bare remote. Result SKIP for the tip's hook, `302d8d081`'s hook and the KS-884 fix; the saved push output is only git's two `To ...` / `* [new branch]` lines, so nothing tells the pusher the gate did not run.
* Why it is more than a corner case: `git push origin <name>` from a different checkout is an ordinary shape (a seat pushes a sibling branch, or a script pushes a ref), and the result reads like a green push.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatF-17th/ks884_ref_matrix.sh` (S15) and `ks884_matrix_full_OLD.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_CURRENT_302d8d0.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_FIXED.txt`.
* Related: KS-884 (PR #1474). Not caused or changed by it.

title: authoritativeTxHash accepts mock_batch_tx_, and nothing pins the placeholder txHash carry on the failed anchor blob (KS-1158 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Two Minor notes from the Opus gate on PR #1478 (KS-1158 R1), both left out of that PR on purpose because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Neither is a regression and neither blocks anything. Filed as ONE ticket so they are searchable by symbol.

## Recommendation

Fix both in one small tier-2 PR, test first: (1) is one cell, (2) is one prefix and its cells.

## Detail

1. **Nothing pins the deliberate placeholder** `txHash` **carry** (`services/originate/src/services/anchorStateSync.ts:190`, `txHash: prior?.txHash ?? null`). #1478 decided that the `anchoredAt` carry keys on `authoritativeTxHash()` but that the failed blob still carries the prior `txHash` string itself (the KS-1004 forensic trail; readers already null a placeholder). The gate's mutation that nulls the placeholder there left all 7 new cells and the full originate suite (98 suites / 1114 tests) green. Add one cell: a `tx_sim_` prior and a `mock_tx_` prior keep their `txHash` on the `anchor_failed` blob, and a real hash is unchanged.
2. `authoritativeTxHash` **(**`anchorStateSync.ts:80`**) rejects only** `tx_` **and** `mock_tx_`**; it ACCEPTS** `mock_batch_tx_…`**,** which the non-production batch mock produces at `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1900`. Pre-existing and shared by all three hash decisions in the file; the `FABRICATED_TX_PREFIX` regexes repo-wide (see KS-608) have the same shape and should be checked in the same pass. A real Cardano hash is hex and can never contain `_`, so adding the prefix cannot reject a real hash.
   **Can it reach a document?** Measured read-only on Kintsugi (a `READ ONLY` transaction, role check printed, aggregate counts only): 26 documents and 20 `anchor_store` rows; **0 documents and 0 anchor rows mention** `mock_batch_tx_`. Control: the same predicate finds `mock_tx_` in 2 documents and 2 anchor rows, and an impossible token returns 0. So on Kintsugi today it does not. **Demo was not measured** (not authorised this round); the answer there is unknown.
   Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/ks1158/census4_mock_batch_tx.sql` and `census4_kintsugi_readonly.out`.

Refs KS-1158, KS-1004, KS-608.

title: Wallet login: two simultaneous first logins for one address issue a token for an id that is not in the database (4 of 5 rounds)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing on develop, found by the Opus gate on #1476 (KS-806) and filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. Two concurrent FIRST wallet logins for the same address both succeed with 200, only one row is created, and in 4 of 5 measured rounds one of the two responses carries an access token for a user id that does **not exist** in `users`. `userRepo.createUser` returns the object it was given, not the row `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` actually stored, and `getOrCreateWalletUser` trusts it.

## Recommendation

Make the wallet create path read back the stored row (or `RETURNING` it) and use THAT id, or fail and retry the lookup when the returned row's `wallet_address` does not match. Add a concurrency cell against a real Postgres (Seat J's native recipe). This is the same "fabricated object, not in the table" class KS-806 names; #1476 removes the collision between different wallets but not this race between two requests of the same wallet.

## Detail

* **Measured** (gate probe P4, real Postgres 15 built from the repo's init SQL + 49 migrations, app role `secuura_app` under RLS, the real route, real `/register`, real `userRepo`, real 039 lookup): 5 rounds of `Promise.all([login(A), login(A)])` for a fresh address A. Every round: both statuses 200, exactly 1 row. `idsInDb` per round: `[true,true]` (same id) once, then `[false,true]`, `[true,false]`, `[true,false]`, ... so in 4 of 5 rounds one returned id is not in the table. The token for that id then works until something looks the user up.
* **Where:** `services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts` `getOrCreateWalletUser` (lookup, then `userRepo.createUser(user)` with a fresh `uuidv4()`), and `userRepo.createUser`'s upsert on `email_lookup_hash` returning its input.
* **Not caused by #1476:** the same shape exists on develop; with the old 8-character email the collision made it worse (every second wallet), with the new email it only happens for a true double submit of one address.
* Evidence: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/logs/probe_head.out` (line 4) and `gateprobe1476.test.ts` (cell P4).

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1476, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `b4615b4a35be26fb`), Minor-4; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1460 (`updateUser` callers that discard the result), KS-1052.

title: A real-Postgres twin of the KS-1267 transfer-custody cells: the mocked flip ignores its arguments and cannot commit or roll back (PR 1486 gate note)
description:
## BLUF

A real-Postgres twin of the two KS-1267 cells in `ks1228-a-refused-request-writes-no-provenance-row.test.ts` (`/transfer-custody`: the owner flip throws, and the custody INSERT returns no row). Found by the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1486; left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Not a regression.

## Recommendation

One small tier-2, test-only PR using the faithful local Postgres recipe (`5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`) and the existing KS-1263 route-level harness, which already drives the real `/transfer-custody` route over a real database (the KS-1310 describe there seeds a document, an owner and a holder and installs a trigger as a fault vehicle). Assert on real rows: after a flip that fails there is no `action_provenance` row for the document, no `custody_events` row and the owner is unchanged; after a flip that succeeds there is one provenance row, one custody row and the owner is the NEW holder.

## Detail

The unit cells use a mocked transaction client whose `$executeRaw` **ignores its arguments** and has **no commit or rollback model**. The gate found two mutants of `routes/documents.ts` that therefore stay GREEN (31/31):

1. **Recording after the flip but before the COMMIT** (inside the transaction): a failed commit would leave a provenance row for a transfer that did not happen, and nothing can see it.
2. **The flip writing the WRONG owner** (its `SET` pointed at `fromHolderId`): the mock never looks at the value.

A twin against a real database closes both, because it reads the rows back. Also: the title of cell 3, "the custody INSERT returns no row: 500, no row, and the owner is never flipped", over-states what it asserts. The mock cannot show the owner, so the cell asserts only the WRITE ORDER (the flip statement is never issued). The PR body and squash body say so; the title is left as merged.

Refs KS-1267, KS-1263, KS-1310.

title: prisma-generate.cjs edge cases: signals skip the cleanup, a symlinked staging directory, a stale client passes the check (KS-1305 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Six Minor notes from the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1489 (KS-1305), all in `scripts/prisma-generate.cjs` and its test. The script is developer tooling. They were left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Filed as ONE ticket; one small tier-2 PR later.

## Recommendation

One small PR, test first: guard the signal paths, make the staging directory safe to reuse, and make the "client exists" check mean "this run produced it". None of it matters in the normal run; all of it is the edge cases of a script that creates and deletes a directory.

## Detail (line numbers at head `80be89ee`)

1. `:68-75`**, SIGINT and SIGTERM skip the** `finally`**:** `node_modules/.generate` is left behind (rc 130 / 143), and SIGTERM also orphans the prisma child. The next run cleans it. Install signal handlers that remove the staging directory and kill the child.
2. `:66-69`**, a symlinked** `.generate`**:** the link is removed but its **target's** `schema.prisma` is overwritten. Needs write access to `node_modules` already. Refuse a `.generate` that is a symlink, or `lstat` first.
3. `:79`**, a stale client passes the check:** OK is printed when prisma exits 0 and writes nothing, if a client from an earlier run is present. Compare the client's mtime (or a hash) against the start of the run, or remove the old client first.
4. `:65`**,** `.generate` **being a file** gives an uncaught stack trace with rc 1 instead of a message.
5. `:86`**,** `path.relative` **from another cwd** prints `../../..` noise in the OK line.
6. **Test gap:** no cell for prisma **killed by a signal** (`spawnSync` returns `status: null`; the script maps it to 1, but nothing pins that). The gate's mutant that returned 0 for a signal-killed prisma survived.

Refs KS-1305.

title: Wallet login: a suspended account stored under a mixed-case address can be evaded by logging in with the lower-case form (needs a case-insensitive lookup, a migration)
description:
## BLUF

Residual declared on #1476 (KS-806) and confirmed by its Opus delta gate (round 3), filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. A wallet account whose `wallet_address` was stored before #1476 in a NON-canonical casing and has since been SUSPENDED refuses its own casing (401), but the same wallet logging in with the lower-case form gets a NEW ACTIVE account (200). Suspension can be evaded through the double-account path.

## Recommendation

A separate PR with a migration: replace `auth_find_user_by_wallet` (migration 039, exact equality) with a case-insensitive lookup (or add a functional index on `lower(wallet_address)` and look up on the lower-cased argument), and canonicalise the stored column for existing rows in the same migration. Then the lookup in `routes/wallet.ts` needs no presented-casing-first loop. Until then #1476's raw-casing-first lookup keeps a legacy row reachable by its own casing, which is the part it can fix without a migration.

## Detail

* **Why it exists:** CIP-8 verification compares the claimed and signed address case-insensitively (`utils/cip8.ts`), so one wallet can present several casings, but `auth_find_user_by_wallet` is `WHERE wallet_address = p_wallet_address` (exact). #1476 stores new rows in the canonical lower-case form and looks up the presented casing first, then the canonical form; a legacy row in a casing the wallet does not present is not found by any lookup there.
* **Effect (gate probe D5 and the residual cell):** legacy row `L` (mixed case, SUSPENDED). Login with the mixed-case form: 401 (the suspension holds). Login with the lower-case form: no row found, a new row `N` is created, ACTIVE, 200.
* **Related, declared in #1476:** `/link` stores the raw casing (`routes/wallet.ts`), so one wallet can also become two accounts there; `/status/:walletAddress` is not canonicalised. The same migration fixes the lookup side of both; the write side of `/link` should canonicalise.
* **Not caused by #1476:** before it, every casing was a separate account anyway; #1476 closes the double account for rows it creates and leaves this one for legacy rows.

Provenance: Opus delta gate on #1476 round 3, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476-r3/verdict.md`; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1486 (concurrent first logins), KS-1460.

title: ks963 wallet ordering guard (KS-806 round 4): the purity pin on canonicalWalletAddress is a deny-list, and the allow-list matches names only
description:
## BLUF

Two Minors from the Sonnet-tier delta gate on #1476 round 4 (verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476-r4/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `f70196195b8ce128`), filed at the priority Wednesday asked for (P3). Both weaken the ks963 wallet ordering guard that #1476 round 4 extended with `PURE_BEFORE_LOOKUP`.

## Recommendation

One small test-only PR in `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts`.

## Detail

1. **Minor-1, the purity pin is a deny-list:** the cell that pins `canonicalWalletAddress` pure rejects a fixed list of tokens (await, query, fetch, require, import, process, fs, db, assignment). An impure helper that uses none of them, or a `console.log` inside it, stays green. Closing step: allow-list the function body instead (it may contain only a `return` of `walletAddress.toLowerCase()`, matched structurally), so anything else fails closed.
2. **Minor-2, the allow-list matches names only:** nothing ties the `canonicalWalletAddress` name used in `routes/wallet.ts` to the export in `utils/walletEmail.ts`, so a local impure function with the same name declared inside `wallet.ts` shadows the pure one and stays green. Closing step: assert that `wallet.ts` imports `canonicalWalletAddress` from `../utils/walletEmail` and declares no function of that name (and the same for any other name on the allow-list).

Provenance: Sonnet-tier delta gate on #1476 round 4, Minor-1 and Minor-2; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction (condition 3 of the merge GO). Related: KS-806, KS-1131, KS-1468 (the same guard's other blind spots).

title: KS-811 gate findings (#1491): the 403-code scan reads comments, and the global CSRF middleware answers unpublished CSRF_* 403s on the same path
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th as the single P3 follow-up required by Wednesday's head-bound GO on PR #1491 (KS-811 second ask), 2026-10-12T09:55:43Z. Gate verdict `2026-10-12_gate-pr1491/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `2331702dc31cc79e`. 0 Major.

The merged work is sound and stays merged: one new test file, no product file touched, and the gate derived the emitted 403 set (`FORBIDDEN` plus the four enforcement codes) and the published set independently and they matched the author's. This ticket carries the two residuals the gate named.

## Finding 1 (Minor) — the scan reads comments, so commented-out code can red or green a cell

The derivation in `ks811-post-documents-403-code-set-agrees.test.ts` scans source text without
stripping comments. Consequences the gate demonstrated:

* a commented-out `403` on the route turns three cells red, so a purely documentary edit breaks the suite;
* nearby unrelated code can be misattributed to the handler under test.

Closing step: strip comments before deriving the set (or parse rather than text-scan), then re-run the
gate's mutation set to confirm the three cells no longer answer to a comment.

## Finding 2 (Note) — the asserted set holds at handler level only

The global CSRF middleware answers unpublished `CSRF_*` 403s on this path for cookie-only requests.
So "the 403 code set of `POST /api/documents`" is true of the handler, not of the front door: a
cookie-only caller can receive a 403 whose code is not in either set the test compares.

Closing step: decide whether the published set should include the `CSRF_*` codes reachable on this
path, or whether the test's scope sentence should say handler-level explicitly. Either is acceptable;
leaving both unstated is not.

## Known blind spots — already stated in the test file header, recorded here so they are not re-found

Three of the gate's eleven mutations stayed green: the helper, the variable and the `Object.assign`
form. The file header names them. They are not regressions and are not in scope for this ticket
unless Finding 1's rework makes them cheap to close.

## Provenance

* Gate verdict read by Wednesday through its summary and findings headings; she did not re-run its
  mutations or tests, and nor did I — these two findings are quoted from it, not re-measured by me.
* Measured by me: api-gateway on the predicted merge tree over develop `17e275adaf67`, plus the
  merge prediction and its add/add conflict control.

title: KS-1477 gate notes (#1498): the older verification suites never exercise the configured arms, an unpinned DATABASE_URL shape, an undocumented 503
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th as the single P3 follow-up Wednesday ruled for the notes of the Opus gate on PR #1498 (KS-1477). Gate verdict `2026-10-12_gate-pr1498/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `7a68ba7ffec71673`, GO WITH NOTE at head `7a6cf7a651d1`. 0 Major. The two Minors and the review-ordering pin (G9) are closed in the delta commit on #1498 and are NOT in this ticket. These are the remaining notes, quoted from the verdict; none of them is re-measured by me.

## 1. Four older suites model "a configured database" in a state production cannot reach (Note 4)

`ks1193`, `ks1194`, `ks1236` and `ks1018-item3` model a configured database as `isDbAvailable() === true` with `DATABASE_URL` unset. Production never has that combination, so on the gated head those suites run the memory-only arms of the store functions, not the configured arms. Only the new `ks1477` file exercises the configured arms. The gate's mutant G11 shows the old suites still bite on some faults, so this is a coverage-model gap, not a dead suite.

Closing step: give those suites a `DATABASE_URL` for the cells that mean "configured", set and restored per file as the `ks1477` file does, so the configured arms are exercised by the suites that were written to cover them. Related: KS-1474 (no gate executes the DB-backed integration suites).

## 2. What counts as "configured" is not pinned (Note 3)

`!process.env.DATABASE_URL` matches `db.ts` exactly (`getPool` line 21, `initDb` line 230), so an empty string means memory-only in both places. A whitespace-only or malformed URL counts as configured, which means 503 for as long as the probe fails. That is the right fail-closed direction but no cell pins it: the gate's mutants G3 and G4 survived. One cell for the empty string (memory-only) and one for a whitespace-only value (configured, so 503 in the boot window) would fix the meaning in place.

## 3. The new 503 is undocumented, and memory-only mode may not work end to end (Note 5, pre-existing)

The verification routes are absent from `auth.openapi.ts`, so neither the routes nor the new 503 are published. Separately, the gate read that memory-only mode is probably unusable end to end: with no `DATABASE_URL`, `userRepo.getUserById` goes through `getPool()`, which throws, and in production `enforceProductionConfig` requires `DATABASE_URL` (`index.ts:57`). That bears on what the memory-only branch of the fix is protecting, and is worth a decision before more effort goes into it.

## 4. Operational observations the gate recorded, no action proposed (Note 1)

* The new 503 is reachable only in the probe-lag gap after recovery (`db.ts` backs off 1 s doubling to a 30 s cap, so at most about 30 s). While the database is genuinely down, `getUserById` already answers 503 first. This bound comes from the gate reading `db.ts`, not from a live run.
* There is no `Retry-After` header (`errorHandler` has none).
* `/health/ready` reports `degraded` with HTTP 200 during the boot window, so the platform keeps routing traffic to the instance during the gap.

## Provenance

Quoted from the verdict, which I read in full myself. The verdict's own NOT-tested list applies: no real Postgres, no live boot window, no multi-replica run. Opened from the PR #1498 delta cycle.

title: security converters: four rowToApiKey boundary gaps survive the whole 311-test suite - an ABSENT is_active column reads as ACTIVE
description:
## BLUF

The Opus gate on PR #1511 (KS-880, verdict sha256/16 `0114cb379ee6b923`) planted 10 of its own mutants in `services/security/src/converters.ts`. **Four survived the full security suite** — 29 files / 311 tests, rc 0, with the mutant in place. All four are field-mapping boundaries on `rowToApiKey`, and every one of them was caught by the gate's differential harness, so the mapper is right today. What is missing is a **cell** that would notice if it stopped being right.

**The security-relevant one: a mutant that defaults** `isActive` **to** `true` **when the** `is_active` **column is absent passes 311/311.** A mapper that reads a key as ACTIVE when the column is missing is the shape that silently un-revokes a key.

These gaps **predate** PR #1511 — the same cells were unpinned at base `f6f2a539f4a0`, so this is not a regression from the one-mapper-home move. Filed as the gate's Minor m1, which explicitly said they are not a reason to hold that PR.

## Recommendation

Add cells to `services/security/src/__tests__/row-converters.test.ts` pinning each boundary. The first is the one that matters:

* `isActive` for a row with **no** `is_active` key, and for `is_active: null` — must be `false`, not `true`.
* `isActive` for `is_active: 't'` (the Postgres text form) — must be `true`, so a later `=== true` tightening reds.
* `connectorId` for `connector_id: ''` — must be `undefined`, not `''`.
* `organizationId` for `organization_id: ''` — must be `null`, not `''`.

Each cell should be shown red against the corresponding mutant before it is trusted, the way the KS-880 round did.

## Detail — the four survivors, with the gate's labels

| Gate mutant | The change | Suite | Differential |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| G1 | `is_active` absent gives `isActive: true` | **SURVIVED** 311/311 | 2 diffs |
| G10 | `isActive: r.is_active === true`, so the `'t'` string is no longer active | **SURVIVED** | 3 diffs |
| G7 | connectorId `??` becomes `||`, so `''` stays `''` instead of `undefined` | **SURVIVED** | 1 diff |
| G8 | organizationId `??` becomes `||`, so `''` stays `''` instead of `null` | **SURVIVED** | 2 diffs |

**Where** (line numbers at `b3a89d83df61`, the KS-880 fix-round head; the verdict cites the gated head `c6567a74493f`, where the same three sites are 7 lines earlier because the fix round added a comment block above them):

```
converters.ts:159   organizationId: (r.organization_id as string | null) ?? null,     (gated head :152)
converters.ts:171   isActive: Boolean(r.is_active),                                   (gated head :164)
converters.ts:177   connectorId: (r.connector_id as string | null) ?? undefined,      (gated head :170)
```

`Boolean(r.is_active)` is correct for every value the gate fed it, including absent (`undefined` to `false`) and the `'t'` string (to `true`). The point of the ticket is only that nothing fails if someone changes it.

**Not in scope:** `rowToAuditLog`'s `organizationId: (r.organization_id as string) || undefined` is a different type (`AuditLog.organizationId` is optional, not nullable) and the gate measured that mapper 0-diff over 23 rows. It is not one of the four.

## Dedupe before filing

Literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description across the Secuura-PK team, **archived included**: `isActive` 8 hits, `is_active` 8, `rowToApiKey` 4, `converters.ts` 1, `parseJsonArray` 0. None is about these boundaries — the nearest are KS-1370 (validate reads a boot-only memory map), KS-908 (connectorId invisible through the API) and KS-889 (the KS-869 COALESCE backfill window), all different defects. Positive control: `rowToApiKey` returned KS-880, KS-869, KS-908 and KS-889, and `converters.ts` returned KS-880, so the scan can see; `parseJsonArray` returned 0, so it can also return nothing.

Raised by Seat V 5th from the PR #1511 Opus gate, 2026-10-12.

title: api-gateway production file logs are a column of `undefined`: the File transports carry no format (the originate half is KS-1348)
description:
## BLUF

**Under** `NODE_ENV=production` **the api-gateway's two** `File` **transports write the literal text** `undefined` **for every log call, so** `logs/error.log` **and** `logs/combined.log` **contain no usable information.** The console JSON is the only usable production channel. Found by the QA gate on PR #1512 (ticket KS-1510; verdict sha256/16 `cc2a467368885a9d`, "pre-existing, outside the PR") and **reproduced independently here, with a control**, on develop `629349dac602`. KS-1348 (Done) is the **originate** half of the same defect; this service's half had no ticket.

## Recommendation

Give each `File` transport `format: combine(json())`, the shape KS-1348 prescribed and the shape the control below uses. Test first: a cell that builds the production logger, writes one error and one info line, and reads both files back (each line valid JSON carrying the message); it is red against today's `undefined`. The module reads `NODE_ENV` once at import, so the cell needs `vi.resetModules()` and a scratch working directory. **Decide first whether the files should exist at all** (see the last bullet of Detail).

## Detail

* **Where:** `services/api-gateway/src/utils/logger.ts` on develop `629349dac602`. Lines 30-35 add the two `winston.transports.File` transports in production with only `filename`, `level`, `maxsize` and `maxFiles`. Lines 37-45 build the logger with `errors({ stack: true })` and `timestamp(...)` and **no** `json()` and no `printf()`, so nothing renders the entry. The `Console` transport is fine because lines 23-27 give it its own format. (The gate cited lines 36-47: the same code, read at an earlier line count.)
* **Measured 2026-10-13 on develop** `629349dac602`**:** imported the real module with `NODE_ENV=production`, cwd a scratch directory, one `logger.error` and one `logger.info`. `logs/error.log` is 10 bytes, exactly `undefined` plus a newline (1 of 1 lines); `logs/combined.log` is 20 bytes, `undefined` twice (2 of 2 lines). **Control:** the same two transports given `format: combine(json())` wrote 1 and 2 lines of valid JSON carrying level, message, service and timestamp, so the instrument can show content when content exists. The console line for the same calls is correct JSON.
* **Why it matters:** production is the only environment that creates these transports, so it is invisible in development and in tests. Every server-side line the gateway logs in production, including the route context lines from the `fail500` family and the new document-lookup line from KS-1510 once deployed, reaches the files as `undefined`.
* **Sweep of the other File transports on develop (**`git grep "transports.File"`**, with the known api-gateway file as the positive control, 2 hits):** `services/originate/src/utils/logger.ts:83-84` carry `format: combine(keepFileFields(), json())` (KS-1348's fix); `packages/shared/src/logger/index.ts:108-113` carry `format: json()` and are **opt-in** behind `LOG_TO_FILES=true`. The api-gateway is the only site left with a bare `File` transport. The other 18 services' `utils/logger.ts` use no `File` transport.
* **Unmeasured, and the reason to decide before fixing:** the shared logger's comment says it made its file transports opt-in because *"Container Apps mount the cwd read-only for non-root users, so winston's default mkdir('logs') throws EACCES on import"*. The api-gateway's are **unconditional** in production. Whether they write anywhere in the deployed containers, and whether anything collects `logs/*.log` (a volume, a sidecar), is **not established here**. If nothing reads the files, the better fix may be to make them opt-in like the shared logger rather than to format them.
* **Related:** KS-1348 (originate half, Done), KS-1510 and KS-1524 (where it was found). **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `winston.transports.File` 1 and `File transport` 1 (both KS-1348, whose description names `services/originate/src/utils/logger.ts` and not the gateway). The same instrument returned KS-1510 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: platform_document_registry.tenant_id has three declarations that disagree (init schema UUID, gateway CREATE TEXT, main-DB copy TEXT): decide the canonical one (UNDECIDED)
description:
## BLUF

**Nobody has decided what type** `platform_document_registry.tenant_id` **is. There are three declarations of it, and they disagree:** the platform database's init schema says `UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`; the gateway's in-code CREATE for the platform database says `TEXT`; and the MAIN database's copy of the table (created by `CORE_MIGRATIONS`) is also `TEXT`. **This is UNDECIDED.** It is the item left over when KS-1272 was closed: that ticket's defect (the de-dup `DELETE` failing `22P02` on a uuid column on every boot) is fixed by making the statement type-agnostic, and its Recommendation also asked to "decide which declaration is canonical". Nothing is broken today because both spellings now work.

## Recommendation

A decision, not a build. Pick the canonical type for the platform database's table (the init schema's `UUID` with a foreign key is the stricter reading), then decide separately whether the gateway's in-code CREATE should be aligned to it, and whether the main database should hold this table at all or hold it with the same type. Unassigned: a decision-shaped item for Wednesday or Kam.

## Detail

* **Facts at develop** `551dc9808aee` (source lines, not compiled):
  * `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:209-213`: `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`, plus `idx_doc_registry_unique` on `(content_hash, tenant_id)` at line 225.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, platform list, lines 1123-1138: `tenant_id TEXT`, then the de-dup `DELETE` at 1135-1137 using `a.tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.tenant_id` (the KS-1272 fix, PR #1104), then `uq_pdr_hash_tenant`.
  * Same file, `CORE_MIGRATIONS` (the MAIN database), lines 473-501: `tenant_id TEXT`, de-dup with `COALESCE(a.tenant_id, '') = COALESCE(b.tenant_id, '')`. That form is correct on a TEXT column and would raise `22P02` on a uuid one.
* **Why the declarations coexist:** the init script runs first on a fresh platform database, so the gateway's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op wherever that script ran. KS-1272 measured the Kintsugi platform database on 2026-09-19 (read-only): `tenant_id` is `uuid`, 0 rows, `uq_pdr_hash_tenant` present.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** a platform database built from the gateway's CREATE alone would be `TEXT` and carry no foreign key to `tenants`, while one built from the init script is `UUID` with the key; a non-UUID tenant id would then be accepted by one and refused by the other. No run was made to confirm it.
* **Related:** KS-1272 (the defect, Done), KS-598 (the registry upsert that keys on `(content_hash, tenant_id)`; the type of `tenant_id` is part of what that ticket's re-keying would have to settle).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `canonical declaration` 0; `platform_document_registry` 10 hits, of which KS-1272 and KS-598 were read; KS-590 and KS-33 are unrelated. The same instrument returned KS-1272 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: mcp-server POST /generate-package: a falsy allowedDocumentTypes ("", 0, false) reaches the package generator as [] (all types permitted) with status 200
description:
## BLUF

**The MCP server's** `POST /generate-package` **turns a falsy** `allowedDocumentTypes` **(**`""`**,** `0` **or** `false`**) into** `[]` **before it reaches the package generator, and answers 200.** `[]` is documented as "all types permitted", so a caller who sent a value that is not a list gets back a package that says the connector is unrestricted. This is the second of the two sites that shape `allowedDocumentTypes` found while working KS-1232; it was split out of KS-1232 on Wednesday's ruling because it is a different service, a different surface (a request-body value, not the gateway's answer) and a separate test pass.

## Recommendation

A decision first, then a small build. Decide what the endpoint should do with a present, non-array `allowedDocumentTypes`: refuse (a 400, since the value is the caller's) or pass it on as unusable. The gateway's own answer for the same stored value is a 403 refusal (KS-1232), so the two should not disagree about what a non-list means. Test first against the existing pin, which the change flips.

## Detail

* **Where:** `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:258`, `allowedDocumentTypes: allowedDocumentTypes || [],`, in the handler for `POST /generate-package` (line 222), which reads `allowedDocumentTypes` from the request body (line 226) and requires `apiKey` (400 without it).
* **Reachable through the gateway:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1266` mounts `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` and forwards it to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package` (line 1270); KS-1214 records the same.
* **What** `[]` **means:** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:123`, "An empty `allowedDocumentTypes` list means all types are permitted."
* **Pinned today, as a characterisation (PR #1120):** `services/mcp-server/src/__tests__/ks1232-generate-package-doctypes-default.test.ts`, the cell `RED KS-1232: allowedDocumentTypes "", 0 and false each reach the package generator as [] with status 200`, with a control that a list passes through unchanged. The fix flips that cell.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** the generated package carries the unrestricted-looking list into the agent's configuration. The gateway still enforces the real allow-list on create, so this is misinformation to the agent, not a widening; I did not run a generated package against a gateway.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the gateway's info reader, the same value), KS-1214 (the same server's `/hash` exposure; it records the `/api/mcp/generate-package` proxy).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `generate-package` 4 (KS-1214, KS-713, KS-104, KS-95; KS-1214 read, the other three are Done and unrelated), `http-server.ts:258` 1 and `allowedDocumentTypes || []` 1 (both KS-1232), `package generator` 0, `generatePackage` 0. The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: GET /api/connector/info answers [] (unrestricted) with a 200 when the platform-settings read throws, where the create path answers 503
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/connector/info` **answers a plain 200 with** `allowedDocumentTypes: []` **("all types permitted") when the platform-settings read THROWS, where the create path refuses with a 503.** Measured, with a control and a negative control (below). So during a Redis fault a connector is told it is unrestricted while every create is refused. Found while building KS-1232; it is a separate defect of the same class (KS-1231's container fail-open, KS-1256's create-path 503), not part of KS-1232's change.

## Recommendation

A small build, shape probably decided by the create path's own answers: refuse the read with the same 503 and text the create path uses, rather than swallow. The exact shape is for the owner to confirm (it is a status the info route does not answer today). Test first against the probe below.

## Detail

* **Where:** `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts`, the `catch { /* swallow – non-critical */ }` that closes the `try` around `redisService.getNotificationSettings('platform-settings')` in the `GET /api/connector/info` handler. After it, `connectorConfig` is still `{}`, so the reply is `allowedDocumentTypes: connectorConfig.allowedDocumentTypes || []`.
* **Measured at develop** `4ec53e1874d0` **(a throwaway test, not committed):** the real `createHealthRoutes` behind the real `authenticateToken(true)`, with a redis double whose `getNotificationSettings` throws. **Control:** a healthy read of the same double answers `200` and `['SSD_DOCUMENT']`. **Subject:** the thrown read answers `200` and `[]`. **Negative control (must fail, did):** the same thrown read does not answer `503`.
* **The create path's answers for the same fault** (`routes/verification.ts`, KS-1256): an explicit `isRedisAvailable()` test BEFORE the read, answering `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `Connector allow-list configuration is currently unreadable; refusing until it can be read`; and a `catch` that answers `503`, `Connector allow-list configuration could not be read; refusing until it can be read`. Its own comment says why the pre-test exists: in fallback mode the read RESOLVES to null, which a `catch` cannot observe. **The info reader has neither the pre-test nor a refusing catch.** I measured only the thrown read; the fallback-mode case is reasoned from that comment and was not run.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured on a deployment:** a connector's tooling (including the MCP server's `get_info`) would report an unrestricted list during a Redis fault. Not a widening of what the gateway lets a connector do (the create path still refuses), but misinformation of the kind KS-1232 removes for the non-array shapes.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the build that found it), KS-1231 (the container read of the same handler), KS-1256 (the create path's 503; its test file is `ks1256-unreadable-allow-list-fails-closed-with-503.test.ts`), KS-1233 (the Redis-mode TTL on the same key).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `swallow` 25 (scanned by title; none names this handler), `info reader` 4 (KS-1530, KS-1237, KS-1232, KS-1231; none is about a thrown read), `unreadable allow-list` 0, `getNotificationSettings` 1 (KS-1233, about the TTL). The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: Security: an organisation-scoped admin can mint a key for ANOTHER organisation, or carrying another organisation's connector id — the mint has no organisation arm and connector_id is not bound
description:
## BLUF

**In** `services/security`**, the API-key mint is bounded by TENANT only. An** `ORG_ADMIN` **or** `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of organisation A can mint a key that carries organisation B's** `organizationId`**, and any** `connectorId`**, inside the same tenant.** KS-764 put an organisation arm on **revoke**; the **mint** never got one. Because the connector-erasure path in KS-695 trusts the key row it is called with, that minted key erases B.

**This must land before KS-695 deploys** — same status as KS-1508. Merging KS-695 does not deploy it, so the harm is after deploy, and the data destroyed (titles, descriptions, an organisation name) is another organisation's and the erasure is irreversible.

Found by the round 4 Opus gate on PR #1497 (verdict sha256/16 `df3bc694b6b41094`, section M-1). **The security-service half below is the gate's reading of the code, which I re-read at source myself; the originate half is the gate's measurement on real Postgres. Neither the mint nor the gateway half has been measured at runtime — that is the first task here.**

## The two paths

**Path 1 — a key for another organisation.**

* `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49` — `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN` are in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`.
* `provisioningPolicy.ts:95-98` — `decideMint` returns `{allow: true, via: 'admin'}` **at once** for any of those roles, before any tenancy or organisation question.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:477-491` — the body's `organizationId` and `connectorId` are free strings.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:1017` — the route calls `decideTenantAccess((req as any).user, tenantId)` **without** the third `organisationScope` argument.
* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:161-164` says that arm is engaged *"ONLY when the caller supplies* `organisationScope`*, so the two existing callers (KS-742's list and mint) keep exactly today's behaviour"*. That was deliberate in KS-764 and is exactly the gap.
* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1189-1192` — `/api/security` is mounted behind `authenticateToken(true)` only, so the gateway adds no organisation check.

**Measured by the gate on the originate side (cell P8, real Postgres, both modes):** a key row for org B carrying a forged `connector_id` — which is what the mint above writes — gives `200 completed documentsBlanked:1`, B's name and document `[erased]`, and B's own provisioned key still active.

**Path 2 — a key for A's own organisation carrying B's connector id.**

* `svc_api_keys.connector_id` has **no uniqueness constraint** (the gate read the live indexes: pkey, org, prefix, tenant only).
* The erasure matches `versionedById = 'connector:' + connectorId` **by value**.
* **Measured by the gate (cell P6, both modes):** two organisations whose keys share one `connector_id`; A erases and gets `200 documentsBlanked:4`, taking B's unissued connector root and B's connector derivatives.
* Not hypothetical: `register-connector` writes `connectorId: platform-s:${externalRef}` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:702`), so the id is a predictable function of a value an org admin can read, and the tenant metering key already uses a constant `platform-s` id (`tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts:56`).

**Path 2 is not closed by the organisation arm alone.** Both arms are needed.

## What this ticket asks for

1. **The organisation arm of the mint.** An organisation-scoped admin may mint only for its own organisation. The shape already exists — pass `organisationScope` at `index.ts:1017` as the revoke path does at `keyRevokePolicy.ts:243` — and `decideMint`'s early return for `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` must stop short-circuiting past it. Platform roles keep their current reach.
2. **The connector-id binding.** A connector id belongs to exactly one organisation; a mint naming one already bound to another organisation in the same tenant is refused. The org-less tenant metering key must keep working.
3. **It lands before KS-695 deploys.** Tracked like KS-1508.

## Acceptance

A mint request from an `ORG_ADMIN`/`ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A naming organisation B, **or** naming a `connectorId` already bound to B, is refused **on the running service over real HTTP** — not only in a unit file — with the caller's own organisation unaffected, and a control proving the same admin may still mint for its own organisation.

## Dedupe before filing

Literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description across Secuura-PK, **archived included**: `organisationScope` **0**, `organizationScope` **0**, `connector_id has no unique` **0**, `provisioningPolicy` 2 (KS-742 tenancy, KS-835 OAuth consent), `decideMint` 2 (KS-742, KS-486), `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` 5 (KS-742, KS-643, KS-642, KS-486, KS-1514 — all either the tenant boundary or a response-shape issue), `ORG_ADMIN` 33 (so the scan can see). **The nearest neighbours are the tenant boundary (KS-742) and the revoke-only organisation arm (KS-764, Done); neither covers the mint's organisation arm or the connector-id binding.** KS-1107 is the same class on a different surface (`POST /api/auth/register` accepting a client-supplied `organizationId`) and is not this.

## Not measured, and whose it is

Counts of existing keys that already share a `connector_id` across organisations on Kintsugi are **not** measured here — that is the J lane's to run, per Wednesday. Nothing in this ticket was run against a live box.

Filed by Seat V 5th from the PR #1497 round 4 Opus gate, 2026-10-12.

title: POLICY (Kam's call): role ADMIN is a KEY_ADMIN_ROLE that the KS-764 organisation arm never engages for, so a tenant ADMIN can mint a key for any organisation in its tenant
description:
## BLUF

`ADMIN` **is in** `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` **but in neither** `PLATFORM_ROLES` **nor** `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`**, so the KS-764 organisation arm is skipped for it entirely and** `decideTenantAccess` **falls through to** `allow: 'same-tenant'`**.** After KS-1533 arm 1 closes the hole for `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, a caller with role `ADMIN` can **still** mint a key carrying any organisation's `organizationId` inside its own tenant — the same Path 1 shape, through one role.

**This is a policy question about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure, so it is Kam's to decide, not an engineering choice inside a PR.** Wednesday put it on his board as a card (`secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013`) and recommended leaving `ADMIN` unbounded. **Until he rules, KS-1533 arm 1 ships leaving** `ADMIN` **unbounded and says so plainly**, and the shared role set is NOT touched.

## The three sets, read at source

```
KEY_ADMIN_ROLES    services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN, ADMIN
PLATFORM_ROLES     packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN
ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES  packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:76
                   ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN
```

The arm is `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))` (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:173`). `ADMIN` satisfies neither predicate, so the arm is skipped and the function returns `allow: 'same-tenant'` at `:225`.

| role | what arm 1 does for it |
| -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` | platform — bypass the arm by design (KS-577 depends on it) |
| `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` | org-bounded — **the arm applies**, which is KS-1533 arm 1 |
| `ADMIN` | **neither — the arm never engages** |

## The two readings

**(a) By design, and this ticket closes as "documented".** `ADMIN` reads as a **tenant**-level admin, distinct from platform — KS-1283 is about "a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes", which treats it as a tenant role. On that reading, acting across organisations *inside its own tenant* is what a tenant admin is for, and arm 1 is complete as scoped.

**(b) A gap.** The sink is the KS-695 connector erasure, which is **irreversible** and destroys another organisation's titles, descriptions and name. KS-764's stated hazard is "an org-bounded admin in organisation A destroying organisation B's key" — if a tenant `ADMIN` may do the equivalent to B's *documents*, the boundary is only as strong as the weakest admin role.

**This ticket does not pick.** It records the question, the evidence, and what shipped in the meantime.

## If Kam rules (b)

`ADMIN` joins `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` in `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`. That is a **one-line change to a shared set that also governs the revoke route**, so it is not a local edit: it would change `DELETE /api/security/keys/:id` for every `ADMIN` caller too, and it needs its own gate and its own caller-population check (the same `caller has no organisation` 403 that KS-1533 arm 1 accepts for org-bounded roles would then apply to `ADMIN` as well). It should not be folded into KS-1533.

## Where it is pinned meanwhile

KS-1533 arm 1 carries a **documenting cell** that asserts today's behaviour — a tenant `ADMIN` minting for another organisation in its tenant succeeds — labelled as undecided policy rather than as a guarantee, so that whichever way Kam rules, the change is visible as a deliberate edit to a cell rather than a silent flip.

## Dedupe

Literal, case-insensitive over title and description, archived included: `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` **1** (KS-779 — the CALLER-side population of org-bounded accounts with no organisation claim, which is KS-1533 arm 1's accepted 403 price, not this question), `isOrgBoundedRole` **0**, `tenant ADMIN` 4 and `ADMIN role` 6 (the KS-1283 / KS-1506 / KS-486 family — a widened `SUPER_ROLES`, error-handler and review tickets, none of them this question). KS-764 (Done) created the arm and deliberately scoped it to the revoke route.

*Corrected after filing: the first version of this paragraph said* `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` *0. The scan returned KS-779. The conclusion is unchanged — no ticket asks whether* `ADMIN` *should be org-bounded — but the figure was wrong and a wrong dedupe count is worth correcting rather than leaving.*

Raised by Seat V 5th while building KS-1533 arm 1, 2026-10-12. Found by reading the role sets before writing the fix, not by a test.

---

## ADDENDUM — it is TWO roles, not one, and the verdicts are MEASURED by running the predicates
