I ran the real `isPlatformRole`, `isOrgBoundedRole` and `decideTenantAccess` over the whole role vocabulary rather than reading the sets. Caller is `{role, tenantId:'t1', organizationId:'oA'}`, target is the same tenant and a DIFFERENT organisation `oB` — i.e. exactly the KS-1533 Path 1 shape:

| role (as the JWT carries it) | isPlatformRole | isOrgBoundedRole | verdict naming ANOTHER org in the same tenant |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `super_admin` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `platform_admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `PLATFORM_ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ORG_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `issuer_admin` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `connector` | false | false | ALLOW `same-tenant` — correct: `decideMint` pins a provisioner to its own tenant on its own branch |

Both predicates upper-case the claim (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:84` and `:123`), so casing is NOT the issue — the role simply is not in either set.

### `platform_admin` is the more interesting half

`platform_admin` is treated as a **super-role by the gateway** in at least six places, while the key policy does not treat it as platform at all:

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65      SUPER_ROLES          includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515     SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES    includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:577        PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1094,1227                       include platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:105 adminRoles           includes platform_admin
packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59  PLATFORM_ROLES       does NOT
services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:193               PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES does NOT (it has `admin` instead)
```

So a `platform_admin` is "platform" to the gateway and an ordinary tenant user to the key policy. For arm 1 that means **unbounded**; more generally it is a role-vocabulary split across seven divergent lists, which is its own problem and not this ticket's to fix.

### What this changes for Kam's decision

The card is about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure. The answer is not "ADMIN" but "`ADMIN` **and** `platform_admin`**, in either casing**". If Kam rules them bounded, the edit is to `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` (or to `PLATFORM_ROLES`, for `platform_admin`) — still a shared set that governs the revoke route too, so still not a local change and still its own gate.

KS-1533 arm 1's documenting cell therefore pins **both** roles' current behaviour, labelled as undecided policy.

*Added by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12, after running the predicates while building KS-1533 arm 1.*

---

## ⚠ CORRECTION — `platform_admin` is NOT unbounded at the mint. It cannot mint at all. Only `ADMIN` is the open question.

**The addendum above is wrong about** `platform_admin`**, and the retitle that named it was wrong.** Measured on the running security service over real HTTP while writing KS-1533 PR A's cells, and confirmed by running the function:

```
role              decideMint (runs FIRST, as route middleware)
ADMIN / admin     ALLOW via admin   -> reaches decideTenantAccess -> unbounded   (the claim HOLDS)
platform_admin    DENY 403 "API key management requires an admin role"          (the claim was WRONG)
PLATFORM_ADMIN    DENY 403 — same
ISSUER_ADMIN      ALLOW via admin   -> the organisation arm applies
super_admin       ALLOW via admin   -> platform, bypasses by design
```

**What I got wrong, precisely.** I ran `decideTenantAccess` on its own and concluded `platform_admin` falls through to `allow: 'same-tenant'`. That is true *of that function*. But the mint route runs `requireKeyAdminOrProvisioner` → `decideMint` **first**, and `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` (`provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49`), so the request is refused 403 before `decideTenantAccess` is ever called. **Order is invisible to a function call** — the exact point KS-742's route-contract test makes in its header, and that I copied into KS-1533's. The real-HTTP cell is what caught it: I had written it to assert `platform_admin` mints (201), and it read 403 on the unfixed service.

**So, for Kam's decision:** the question is `ADMIN` **only**. `ADMIN` is in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`, passes `decideMint`, reaches `decideTenantAccess`, and — being in neither `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` — keeps cross-organisation mint inside its tenant. That half stands and is unchanged.

**What still stands about** `platform_admin`**:** the role-vocabulary split (KS-1536) is real — the gateway treats it as a super-role in six places. But its consequence *at the mint* is the opposite of what I wrote: a gateway super-role is **over**-restricted here (cannot mint keys), not under-restricted. That is an availability quirk, not a security hole, and it belongs on KS-1536, not on Kam's policy card.

The title is reverted to name `ADMIN` alone. KS-1533 PR A pins both facts in cells: `ADMIN` as UNDECIDED POLICY (201 today), `platform_admin` as MEASURED (403, refused by `decideMint`).

*Corrected by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12. The third time this session I have had to correct a claim of mine in place; this one was on Kam's board, so it matters more than the dedupe counts did.*

title: GET /api/connector/info has no Redis-availability 503: in the in-memory fallback mode the settings read returns null and the route answers [] (unrestricted)
description:
## BLUF

In the Redis in-memory **fallback mode**, `GET /api/connector/info` can answer `200` with `allowedDocumentTypes: []` ("all types permitted") for a connector whose allow-list it could not read, where the create path answers `503` through an explicit `isRedisAvailable()` test **before** its read. The **thrown-read** half of this is fixed by PR 1518 (ticket KS-1532); this is the other half, which a `catch` cannot observe because the read RESOLVES to null instead of throwing. Ruled by Wednesday (2026-10-12) to be filed on its own rather than widening KS-1532.

## Recommendation

Mirror the create path. Small build: add `isRedisAvailable(): boolean` to `RedisServiceLike` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts`, the type at the top of the file), and in the info reader answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `Connector allow-list configuration is currently unreadable; refusing until it can be read`, **before** the settings read when it is false. **The call site needs no change:** `index.ts:834` is `app.use(createHealthRoutes(services, redisService))` and `redisService` is the whole module (`import * as redisService from './services/redis'`, `index.ts:51`), which already exports `isRedisAvailable` (`services/redis.ts:130`). Test first: a double whose `isRedisAvailable()` is false and whose read resolves null, plus an AGREEMENT cell against the real create route (the same style as PR 1518's). The doubles that build `createHealthRoutes` in the existing test files carry no `isRedisAvailable` (they are cast), so each needs the method; the one control that would otherwise flip is the pinning cell in PR 1518's new test file, whose double must report Redis AVAILABLE so that a genuinely empty store keeps answering `[]`.

## Detail

* **MEASURED:** the reader answers `200` with `[]` when the settings read resolves to null. That is the control cell `control (UNCHANGED, and the gap stated): a read that RESOLVES to null still answers [] ...` in `src/__tests__/ks1532-info-reader-fails-closed-on-a-thrown-settings-read.test.ts` on PR 1518's head `7bc83d75708f`, with the real `createHealthRoutes`.
* **READ, NOT RUN (develop** `b2085e99ff1c`**):** `getNotificationSettings` (`services/redis.ts`, the function at lines 671-678) returns `notificationSettingsStore.get(key) || null` when `isRedisAvailable()` is false, so in the fallback mode it resolves null (or the in-memory value) without throwing. `fallbackMode = true` is set by `retryStrategy` once `times === 4` (`redis.ts:78`). The create path's own comment says the same thing and why it has the pre-test.
* **NOT MEASURED:** that a deployment reaches the fallback mode (a sustained Redis outage against a running gateway), and what an operator would then see on this route. Nothing here was run against a live stack; no deploy was touched.
* **Why it matters, said carefully:** not a widening of what the gateway lets a connector do, since the create path still refuses. It is the same misinformation class as KS-1232 and KS-1532: during the outage the connector's tooling (including the MCP `get_info` tool) would report an unrestricted list.
* **Related:** KS-1532 (the thrown-read half, PR 1518; stays open for this), KS-1256 (the create path's 503s), KS-1539 (neither catch logs).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles in team KS: `isRedisAvailable` 0, `fallback mode` 0, `fallback` 8 (none about this route: KS-1436, KS-1381, KS-1193, KS-1119, KS-959, KS-765, KS-753, KS-716), `resolves null` 0, `connector/info` 3 (KS-1531, KS-1532, KS-1232; none about the fallback mode). The same instrument returns KS-1532 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket titles.

title: A thrown allow-list read answers 503 but logs nothing: the create path and the info reader leave no server-side trace of which fault
description:
## BLUF

When the `platform-settings` read THROWS, the connector allow-list paths answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` but **log nothing**, so an operator who sees connector 503s has no server-side line saying which fault it was. Two sites: the create path's `catch` in `routes/verification.ts` (KS-1256) and, once PR 1518 (KS-1532) merges, the info reader's `catch` in `services/health.ts`. Found while building KS-1532; the PR names it and does not change it.

## Recommendation

Log the error's class and message (never the settings content, which is the allow-list itself) at warn level with the route name, in both catches, then keep the 503 exactly as it is. Test first with a captured logger: a thrown read produces one line, a healthy read produces none. KS-1510 is the precedent for this kind of change on another route (`ks1510-document-lookup-logs-the-thrown-error.test.ts`).

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, the `catch` that answers `Connector allow-list configuration could not be read; refusing until it can be read` (KS-1256); and `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts`, the same text in the info reader's `catch` (PR 1518).
* **Shapes that reach those catches** (per the create path's own comment): the Redis client's `MaxRetriesPerRequestError`, and the `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse` on malformed stored bytes (`services/redis.ts:675`). They need different responses from an operator (a Redis outage versus corrupted stored settings) and today look identical from outside.
* **Wiring note:** `createVerificationRoutes` already takes a `log` dependency; `createHealthRoutes(services, redisService)` has no logger parameter, so the info reader needs either a new parameter or the module logger. Read at develop `f39104e71688`.
* **Not covered here:** the fallback mode in which the read RESOLVES to null without throwing (no catch runs, so nothing to log); that is the second half of KS-1532.
* **Related:** KS-1532, KS-1256, KS-1510.
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles in team KS: `logs the thrown` 0, `without logging` 0, `no trace` 0, `thrown error` 1 (KS-1341, about webhook error text in 500 bodies, a different defect), `allow-list` 6 (none about logging; the same instrument returned them for that phrase, so it can see ticket titles). KS-1256's description has no log scope (grep 0; the same grep returns 2 hits on KS-1532's description, so it can read ticket text).

title: KS-1517 follow-up: stale-build residue from the #1515 round 2 gate (permanent targets read as stale, C2/A11 survivors, a null package.json crash, wording)
description:
**BLUF:** Residue from the #1515 (KS-1517) round 2 Opus gate, filed as one P3 checklist per Wednesday's ruling (2026-10-12 17:59Z). None of these is reachable on today's tree. Each item carries the shape the gate measured.

**Context:** Line numbers are on #1515 head `a7d0583d`, which is the closing amendment `0723117b` plus develop `425ad3e0`. Source: the round 2 verdict (Minors m1 to m7, plus one carried item). The closing amendment already fixed MJ1 (the note's crash and hang), m1's fixture (R2), m2 (the code check restored and the regex anchored), and the comments m7 named at CLAUDE.md 399-402 and 412-413 and `check.cjs` 102-103 and 325. They are not repeated here.

- [ ] **(a) m3. A declaration target that is permanently absent is reported as a stale build ("rebuild it"), and no rebuild can fix it.**
  * Where: `check.cjs:208-219` (`mapTargets` takes the FIRST matching `*` key in object order, where TypeScript takes the longest prefix), `:331` (the "package declares nothing for this subpath, so it is left to tsc" exemption), `:332-333` (any declared target that is absent goes to `staleFatal`, exit 2).
  * Shapes, all on complete builds:
    * X17: typesVersions names `dist/ghost.d.ts`, which the build never emits. tsc says TS7016; develop rc 1, head rc 2.
    * X16: a typo subpath under a catch-all `"*": ["dist/*.d.ts"]`. tsc says TS2307; develop rc 1, head rc 2 with "missing dist/thnig.d.ts". Under a catch-all key every subpath counts as declared, so the exemption at `:331` never applies.
    * X18: the reverse resolver divergence (first-match `*` against TypeScript's longest `sub/*`). Head rc 2 names the wrong file.
    * X17b: X17 with its TS7016 baselined. Develop rc 0, head rc 2, so a push develop accepts is refused.
  * Why it is unreachable today: both committed baselines hold 0 TS2307/TS7016 entries (measured 2026-10-13). The real shared package has no catch-all key. A stale-judged entry cannot be admitted, because the exit 2 runs before `--init` or `--update` writes. But `--init` can still admit a TS2307/TS7016 whose target is on disk at the time; the comment at `check.cjs:286-293` points here.
  * The gate's suggested fix: exit 2 only where a rebuild would plausibly help (the target lies under the package's outDir), or demote to a NEW error carrying a "may be stale" hint.
  * Docs: `CLAUDE.md:422-424` ("left to tsc") should add that it does not apply under a catch-all key.
- [ ] **(b) Two mutants survive the KS-1517 cells (measured on a green baseline, 29 of 29).**

  * A11, "only the first array target consulted" (`candidates(v)` at `:216`, `anyResolves` at `:308`). Gate shape: the array-divergence fixture. Head rc 1, A11 rc 2.
  * Add one cell per shape.
  * For the record, not survivors: C1, C5 and the amendment's isFile and try/catch mutants are killed. C4 is masked by the restored code check, and the code check and the regex anchor each mask the other; all three were measured by removing the masking guard too.
- [ ] **(c) m4. Stale builds that still read rc 1 "NEW" (the pre-PR misattribution).** Leg 16 still fails on each, so none is a silent pass. The gate judged this acceptable: the design names only what its resolver can name.
  * X19: a version-range key (TypeScript reads `>=4.0`; the resolver reads only `*`).
  * Y2: a main-only package whose sibling `index.d.ts` is missing.
  * Y3: a deep path with no typesVersions.
  * Y11: a directory target that is unbuilt.
  * Y5b: a re-export chain under `skipLibCheck:false`.
  * X2b: a nearer stale copy under `src/node_modules`.
  * Decide: fix one or more, or record each as a documented limit in CLAUDE.md.
- [ ] **(d) m5. Fatal-side crash on an installed** `@secuura` **package whose** `package.json` **is literally** `null`**.**
  * Where: `check.cjs:303` (`JSON.parse` in `packageJsonOf`), dereferenced through `declTargetsFor(found.pkg, sub)` at `:327`. `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`, rc 1. Develop is also rc 1 (TS2307).
  * The note side is already covered by the amendment's try/catch (cell "MJ1 null package.json note-side"). npm would not install such a package.
  * Fix: `JSON.parse(...) || {}` at `:303`, plus a fatal-side cell.
- [ ] **(e) m6, cosmetic.**
  * One "missing declaration target" line is printed per importing site (`check.cjs:372`); real arm B prints the same target twice. Dedupe by target.
  * "tsc itself could not resolve the module" (`:370`) is printed for TS7016 too, where tsc DID resolve the `.js`. Word it per code.

Hits: KS-1517, KS-1489 (Done), KS-1523, KS-1487 (Done), KS-1513, KS-1527, KS-1520 (Done), KS-1529, PS-549. None covers these items. KS-1527's leg-16 item is the rc-1 wording, not (f).

title: Two concurrent rotates leave a connector with zero active keys, and both callers are handed dead keys (pre-existing; measured on real Postgres)
description:
**BLUF:** Two rotates of the same connector at the same time usually leave it with **zero** active keys, and both callers are handed keys that are already dead. The #1521 Opus gate measured this on real PostgreSQL: N=2 (a double-submit or a retry) ended with 0 active keys in **9 of 10** trials; the sequential control ended with 1 active every time. It is **pre-existing**: develop is identical. It is not introduced by #1521 (KS-1533 arm 1), and that PR does not fix it.

**Where:** `services/security/src/index.ts:196-243` (`revokePriorConnectorKeys`, KS-577's revoke-on-rotate), called at `:1073`, after the key is saved at `:1055`. Line numbers on develop `b08ee629`; #1521 shifts the call site down, not the function.

**Mechanism:** each rotate first INSERTs its own new key, then runs `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2 AND id <> <its own new key> AND is_active = true` (`:226-230`). Two interleaved requests each retire the OTHER's new key, so neither survives. The connector is then down until someone mints again, and both callers believe they hold a working credential.

With `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS` set, the same UPDATE sets an expiry instead of retiring at once (`:228-230`). The race then sets both new keys to expire, and the connector reaches zero working keys when the window ends: the same outage, delayed. That is code-read; the gate measured the default, grace 0.

**Measured by the gate** (verdict `reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1521/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `b792fbae338bc782`, section P1; psql as a second reader):

* 20 concurrent platform rotates on one connector: **0 active of 21**. Head: 3 of 3 runs, plus 8 of 8 earlier runs. Develop: 3 of 3.
* N=2: **0 active in 9 of 10** trials.
* Sequential control: **1 active of 21**, every time.
* In memory mode the race does not appear (1 of 21), because no real `await` separates the insert from the revoke there. **That is why the existing suites cannot see it**: they run without a database.

**Reach:** any caller allowed to rotate. That is a platform role on `POST /api/security/keys`, and `register-connector` with `rotate` (the gateway forwards it). A client retry after a slow response is enough; no attacker is needed.

**Fix shapes (the gate's; not chosen here):**

* Do the insert and the revoke in ONE transaction under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(tenant_id || connector_id))`, so rotates of one connector serialise. KS-757 records an advisory-lock constraint elsewhere; check it does not apply here.
* Or retire only keys created BEFORE the new one (`created_at < $new` or an id sequence), so a later rotate can never retire an earlier rotate's key, and the last writer wins.
* Whichever is chosen, the cell has to run on real Postgres with real concurrency: N=2 and N=20, asserting exactly 1 active key and that the survivor is a key some caller was given. A memory-mode cell is green on the defect.

**Related:** KS-1533 (the gate that found it), KS-577 (the revoke-on-rotate it lives in), KS-1430 (the systemTest for the pre-rotation key being dead after a rotate).

**Dedupe (2026-10-13):** title and description searched for concurrent rotate, concurrent rotation, zero active, revokePriorConnectorKeys, revoke-on-rotate, double-submit, advisory_xact_lock, rotate race and rotation race. Hits: KS-1152, KS-1434 (Done), KS-1430, KS-772, KS-577, KS-576, PS-740, KS-1187, KS-869, KS-1177, PS-908, PS-287 (Done), KS-525, KS-757. None records this race. KS-577's own text and its 13 comments carry no concurrency note; every "race" hit there is inside the word "grace".

title: start-environment.sh and stop-environment.sh run the platform compose without sourcing stack_env.sh: slot-blind launchers (KS-1355 spot 2b class)
description:
## BLUF

Two platform launchers run the repo's `docker-compose.yml` **without sourcing** `stack_env.sh`, so they are blind to the stack slot: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-environment.sh` (`docker compose up -d postgres redis cardano-mock`, line 135) and `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stop-environment.sh` (`docker compose down`, line 60). From a slot-N worktree neither names the slot's compose project or container prefix. Found as a side effect of the KS-1355 census (spots 2b, 3, 4) and ruled by Wednesday (2026-10-12) to be ticketed rather than fixed in that PR, where the new stack-safety rule lists both as named exceptions that point here.

## Recommendation

P3. For each: source `stack_env.sh` (guarded as `bootstrap-env.sh` does it, so slot 1 and unslotted runs are unchanged), then the compose calls inherit `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` for slot above 1. The hazard to measure first is `stop-environment.sh`'s `docker compose down`: KS-666 found the identical shape in `stop-secuura.sh`, which "resolved the wrong project, stopped nothing, and printed ALL SERVICES STOPPED" from a slot-2 worktree. Test first with a fixture launcher run under `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2` that must resolve slot 2's project. When fixed, remove both from the exception list in `check-stack-safety.sh` (the rule then covers them).

## Detail

* **Census (develop** `b08ee6299e86`**), live compose lines in tracked** `*.sh`**:** 14 scripts run compose; 4 source `stack_env.sh` (`bootstrap-env.sh`, `dev-reload.sh`, `stop-secuura.sh`, `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`). Of the rest, `start-environment.sh` and `stop-environment.sh` are the two slot-blind PLATFORM launchers (besides `start-local.sh`, fixed in the KS-1355 PR). The others are deliberate: `verify-slot-credential-isolation.sh` stands its own `-p ks731_*` probe stacks; `observability.sh` runs its own package's compose file; the Akto scripts run the Akto stack under `assert-compose-project.sh`; `check-slot-credentials.sh` and `setup-dev-environment.sh` only PRINT compose commands.
* **NOT measured:** whether `start-environment.sh` runs anywhere but a developer laptop (KS-785 raised the same question and left it unsettled); no live stack was started.
* **Related:** KS-1355, KS-666 (the slot design and the `stop-secuura.sh` precedent), KS-785 (`start-environment.sh` also sources no `.env`), KS-1381 (it lists `start-environment.sh:241` for a display-only slot-1 URL print: a different defect).

The same instrument returns KS-1355 for a phrase from its own title (`bypass stack_env.sh`), so it can see ticket text. No existing ticket covers it.

title: Four scripts/openapi-examples *.test.ts suites are in no runner path - the redact and PII-store suites included
description:
## BLUF

**Four** `*.test.ts` **suites under** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/` **are in no runner's**
**path.** They are `node:test` + `tsx` suites, the package declares **no** `scripts` block at all,
and nothing in the repo invokes them — no npm script, no preflight leg, no `run-code-guards`
entry, no hook. Each file documents its own run line in a header comment
(`npx tsx --test scripts/openapi-examples/match.test.ts`), which is the only way they are ever
executed.

Same class as [KS-964](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-964) (104 flat `*.spec.ts` in
`Blockchain/Dev/tests/` in no runner's path) and [KS-1391](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1391)
(no frontend declares a `test` script), but a different directory, a different runner and a
different count — neither covers this.

## The measurement (develop `81ac1ea60`)

```
Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/*.test.ts tracked : 4
  match.test.ts  merge.test.ts  pii-store.test.ts  redact.test.ts
scripts block in scripts/openapi-examples/package.json    : absent
files in the repo that invoke them                        : 0
```

The invoke count is from `git grep -ln 'openapi-examples.*test\|tsx --test'`, whose only hits are
the four files themselves plus `systemTest/playwright/package.json` (a different `tsx --test`).
**Control:** the same search finds `tests/e2e` referenced in other files, and the preflight grep
finds other `scripts/` entries, so a zero here is a real absence rather than a broken search.

## How it was found

Building the KS-1347 cell for `scripts/openapi-examples/proxy/server.ts`. The natural home for
that cell was beside the subject, next to `match.test.ts` — and it would never have run. The cell
went into `scripts/__tests__/ks1347_proxy_out_dir_spaced_checkout.test.sh` instead, which
`run-shell-suites.sh` and the push preflight do reach (83 of 83 tracked suites, measured). So the
immediate consequence is already avoided; this ticket is about the four existing files.

## Why it matters

`redact.test.ts` and `pii-store.test.ts` are the suites for the **redaction and PII-store** code
that the capture proxy runs over observed traffic. If either has rotted, nothing says so. That is
the KS-676 / KS-865 shape: a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed.

## ⚠ The limit of this evidence, stated

This is "nothing in the repo runs them", not "nobody runs them" — an ad-hoc
`npx tsx --test …` by a person appears in neither a config nor a grep. **So do not delete.**
Same instrument as KS-964: find out first.

## Done when

- [ ] a decision is recorded: wire the four into a runner (a `test` script in that package plus a
      preflight leg or `run-shell-suites.sh` entry), or quarantine them
- [ ] if wired: they pass, and a cell asserts the runner reaches all four, so a fifth cannot be
      added unreached (the shape `run-shell-suites.sh --check-unreached` already uses)
- [ ] if quarantined: moved, not deleted, with a quiet period

## Board search before filing

`searchIssues` (fuzzy, returns 6 per term) on `openapi-examples`, `tsx --test`, `match.test.ts`,
`unreached test files`, `openapi examples harness`. Nearest hits read in full: **KS-964** (scoped
to `Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts`, playwright, 104 files) and **KS-1391** (frontend `test`
scripts). Neither names this directory or these files. Filed new.

title: KS-1549 follow-up (#1527 gate): a failed COMMIT can leave a valid key refused in memory, and the rotate assumes READ COMMITTED
description:
**BLUF:** The #1527 (KS-1549) Opus gate returned GO WITH NOTE: 0 Major, 2 Minor (verdict sha256/16 `2c90295b5fb0e300`, head `a430061c`). This is the one P2 follow-up Wednesday's GO requires. #1527 turns a measured 9-in-10 outage into exactly one active key under every shape the gate tried. Both Minors are narrower than the defect it fixed. Until (a) lands, **KS-888's contract ("a failed save leaves memory unchanged") has one known gap**.

**Context:** Lines are on #1527's head `a430061c`, `services/security/src/index.ts`.

- [ ] **(a) m1: a failed COMMIT can leave this process refusing a key the database still holds active.**
  * Where: `saveKeyAndRetirePriors`, `index.ts:318-326`, with the undo at `:330`; and validate's refresh at `index.ts:1447-1450`.
  * Mechanism: the rotate changes the in-memory map BEFORE COMMIT and undoes it if COMMIT fails. The undo restores the OBJECT it captured, `m`. If the OLD key is validated while the COMMIT is in flight, validate reads the row, sees it "revoked in memory", and `memApiKeys.set()`s a NEW object marked revoked (the KS-888 R2 rule: revoked if either source says so). The undo then restores the old object, which is no longer the map's entry. After the rollback the database keeps the old key active, and this process refuses it on every call.
  * Measured by the gate: 3 of 3 at head with the window widened by `pg_sleep`, 0 of 3 on develop, control green. It needs a lost connection at COMMIT.
  * Fix shapes (choose and measure): the undo re-reads the CURRENT entry by id (`memApiKeys.get(id)`) and restores that entry's fields; or the in-memory changes move after COMMIT under an in-process per-connector mutex, so they stay in lock order. Cell: the gate's widened-window shape, with a forced COMMIT failure, asserting that the old key validates again afterwards.
- [ ] **(b) m2 (latent): the fix assumes READ COMMITTED.**
  * Under REPEATABLE READ, 5 of the 8 KS-1549 cells fail with serialization errors. Today's setting is READ COMMITTED, so this is latent: a change to `default_transaction_isolation`, or to the pool's connection options, would surface it.
  * Fix shape: `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED` as the first statement of this transaction, plus a cell that runs the integration file under a REPEATABLE READ default.

**Not exercised by the gate or by me:** pgbouncer (not installed). The lock is transaction-scoped, the form `pool_mode = transaction` supports.

**Related:** KS-1549 (the fix), KS-888 (the contract with this gap), KS-1370 (validate reads the in-memory map).

**Dedupe (2026-10-13):** title and description searched for saveKeyAndRetirePriors, REPEATABLE READ, isolation level, serialization, COMMIT fail, undo, memApiKeys, revoked entry and validate writes.

* Hits: KS-605, KS-603, KS-1284, KS-1439, KS-1353, KS-1408, KS-627, KS-528, KS-888, KS-1174, KS-869, KS-889, KS-1370, plus 44 unrelated "undo" hits (mostly PS-\* UI).
* None covers either item. KS-888 and KS-1370 are the contracts this touches.

title: Count the existing non-canonical svc_api_keys.organization_id rows (every 'default-org' row included) read-only on Kintsugi and demo — facts only, no backfill
description:
## BLUF

**Rows already stored with a non-canonical** `svc_api_keys.organization_id` **keep their stored value, and a canonicalising list comparison will not find them by the canonical id.** This ticket is **facts only, no fix**: it exists so the count is taken read-only on an environment before anyone decides whether a backfill is wanted. **I cannot count them — I have no box access.** Filed on Wednesday's ruling while planning KS-1553.

## Why non-canonical rows exist

`normaliseOrgId` (`packages/shared/src/security/orgId.ts:42`) is the whole normaliser and its body is:

```ts
typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() !== '' ? v.trim().toLowerCase() : null
```

It trims, lower-cases, and treats blank as absent. It does **nothing** about braces, the no-hyphen 32-hex form, a zero-width space, or any other rendering. The mint stores whatever comes back (`services/security/src/index.ts:1242`), and the column is `TEXT`, not `UUID` — so a non-uuid string is storable and is stored verbatim.

## The measured in-repo SOURCE of such rows: the Admin Dashboard

This is the part that makes the residue more than theoretical. The Admin Dashboard hard-codes a non-uuid organisation id on **both** operations:

* `frontend/admin/src/pages/ApiKeys.tsx:92` — mints with `organizationId: 'default-org'`.
* `frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:358-360` — lists with `organizationId || 'default-org'`, and `ApiKeys.tsx:75` passes no argument, so it always sends the literal.

**Measured** (2026-10-13, Seat V 6th, own scratch PostgreSQL 15, service as `secuura_app`, the real routes, every arm with a control):

| what | result |
| -- | -- |
| the admin's exact mint body, `organizationId: 'default-org'` | **201** |
| the stored value | `default-org`**, verbatim** |
| the admin's exact list, `?organizationId=default-org` | **200, and it returns that key** |
| CONTROL: a different org id | 0 keys, so the list really filters |
| the UPPER-CASE form of the same id | **0 keys** (the KS-1553 (a) mismatch) |
| CONTROL: a mint with no `organizationId` (the metering-key shape) | 201, stays absent |

So **every key ever created through the Admin Dashboard's API Keys page carries** `organization_id = 'default-org'`, which is not a uuid. `'default-org'` appears nowhere else in the tracked tree — it is not seeded by any migration or `docker/init` script — so it exists only where that page created it.

## What needs counting, read-only, on Kintsugi and demo

A deploy seat with box access should run, per environment, and record the numbers on this ticket:

```sql
SELECT count(*) AS total,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id IS NULL)                             AS absent,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id = 'default-org')                      AS admin_literal,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$') AS canonical_uuid,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id IS NOT NULL
                          AND organization_id <> 'default-org'
                          AND organization_id !~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$') AS other_non_canonical
FROM svc_api_keys;
```

**Pair it with a control**: the five buckets must sum to `total`, or the predicate set is wrong. If `other_non_canonical` is above zero, list the distinct values (they are organisation identifiers, not secrets) so the brace / 32-hex / zero-width question is answered with data rather than inference.

## Explicitly NOT proposed here

* **No backfill.** Rewriting stored credential metadata is not something to do on the side of a validation change, and it is approval-class.
* **No fix in KS-1553's PR.** That PR states this residue and points here.
* **No claim about any environment's numbers.** I have measured only my own scratch database.

## Related

* **KS-1564** — the Admin Dashboard's hard-coded `'default-org'`: the measured **SOURCE** of these rows. Count that ticket's page as the producer when reading the numbers below.
* **KS-1553** — the raw-vs-canonical list comparison and the non-canonical forms. This residue is its stated consequence.
* **KS-1514** — item 2 (the declared-but-unenforced `uuid` on the list query) is the other half of the same seam.
* **KS-748** (P4) — `organization_id` vs `tenant_id` *coherence*. A different gap in the same column: it is about the pair being incoherent, not about the id's text form. Read in full before filing this; not a duplicate.
* **KS-889** (P2) — the `connector_id` backfill window. A different column; it names `organization_id` only as a candidate backfill source. Read in full; not a duplicate.
* Class: **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

*Dedupe: all 695 Secuura-PK issues were pulled and matched LITERALLY (not via the fuzzy* `searchIssues`*) on* `non-canonical`*,* `default-org`*,* `organization_id`*,* `organizationId`*,* `normaliseOrgId`*,* `backfill`*,* `32-hex`*,* `no-hyphen`*,* `zero-width`*, with a bogus-symbol control returning 0.* `default-org` *returned **0** existing issues. The four near-misses matching two or more terms (KS-1553, KS-1525, KS-959, KS-748, KS-889) were read before filing.*

title: API-key revoke route writes the revoke into shared memory before its database save commits; under a REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE default a revoke behind a committing rotate fails 40001 (o1), plus o4/o2/o5 from the #1529 round-2 gate
description:
## BLUF

**The API-key revoke route writes its revoke into shared in-memory state BEFORE its database save commits** — the memory-first pattern KS-1556 removed from the rotate path. With no undo left anywhere it no longer causes the n1 regression, but it is the same shape, and the round-2 gate measured a latent failure on this route. **Facts only; no build.** Filed on Wednesday's ruling as the revoke-route ticket owed from PR #1529 (KS-1556), carrying the gate's observations **o1, o4, o2 and o5** (verdict sha256/16 `b662a71501b66490`, at head `d19b7a708e5b`).

## The shape (lines at `d19b7a708e5b`, `services/security/src/index.ts`)

* `DELETE /api/keys/:id` is at `:1374`. It builds the revoked object and saves it through `dbSaveApiKey`.
* `dbSaveApiKey` (`:409`) **first statement** is `:410` `memApiKeys.set(k.id, k);` — so memory holds the revoke **before** the upsert runs, and the upsert can then wait on a row lock (a concurrent rotate's retire holds one).
* Under KS-888 R2 a revoke whose save **fails** keeps its in-memory revoke deliberately, so the key stops working in this process. That contract is kept; the question is the ordering, not the fail-closed rule.

## o1 — MEASURED by the gate, latent: a revoke behind a committing rotate fails 40001 under REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE

* Under a REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE pool default, a revoke whose save waits behind a rotate that then COMMITs fails with **SQLSTATE 40001**, and the route answers **500 "revoke not stored"** (the KS-888 log line is at `:1421`).
* At **grace 60** the database keeps the revoked key `is_active = true` with up to 60 s left, so **other replicas honour it until expiry**; this process refuses it (KS-888 R2).
* Measured in 2/2 grace-60 rows and 4/4 grace-0 rows per run (harmless at grace 0, where the rotate already retired the key). **Head and develop identical** under RR and SER; **absent at READ COMMITTED**.
* **Latent:** nothing sets that default today — the same class as KS-1556's m2, which pinned READ COMMITTED on the rotate transaction. The revoke path has no such pin.

## o4 — the DB branch of `revokePriorConnectorKeys` is unreachable but keeps the old pattern

`revokePriorConnectorKeys` (`:231`) has a memory-first branch and a DB branch; its only caller (`:348`) runs only when `!isDbAvailable()`, so the DB branch is unreachable in production. It still holds the memory-first-then-DB pattern KS-1556 removed from the rotate path; a future caller on the DB path would bring it back. Already true on develop.

## o2 and o5 — related memory-ordering observations from the same gate (pre-existing, not findings)

* **o2:** the rotate chain's bounded wait can lose memory order only when the post-COMMIT apply is delayed, which the code cannot do on its own; when forced, the key list shows a retired key as active until a validate corrects it.
* **o5:** `loadFromDb` (clear at `:536`) can leave memory stale if its SELECT straddles a rotate's COMMIT. Validate stays right. **Not measured.**

## Not decided here

Whether the revoke should apply to memory only after its save commits (as the rotate now does), take the same per-connector chain or advisory lock, or pin READ COMMITTED like the rotate. Each changes KS-888 R2's mechanics and is the owner's call.

## Related

KS-1556 / PR #1529 (the shape this mirrors), KS-888 (R2: a failed revoke save keeps the in-memory revoke), KS-1370 (validate's stale read and usage write — a **different** defect in the same function: read in full before filing; not a duplicate), KS-1549.

title: POST /api/referrals/apply takes the applicant's userId from the request body, not the token — read from source, NOT exercised (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/referrals/apply` **takes the applicant's** `userId` **from the request BODY, not from the signed-in caller's token.** Read from source, **NOT exercised**. The route is authenticated, but the token's userId is never used. Facts only, no fix. Noticed while planning KS-1223 and filed on Wednesday's ruling. It is not part of the KS-1223 pull request.

## What the code does

All read at develop `7c6b3d88`:

* The body schema `applyCodeSchema` requires `userId: z.string().uuid()` and accepts an optional `walletAddress` (`services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:23-30`).
* The route passes `body.userId` and `body.walletAddress` to `referralService.applyCode` (`referrals.ts:126-137`). Nothing in the route reads `req.user`.
* The route **is** authenticated. `services/referral/src/index.ts:81` runs `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())` before `:83` mounts `/api/referrals`, and the gateway runs `authenticateToken(false)` before proxying (`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1053-1055`).
* `applyCode` (`services/referral/src/services/referralService.ts:419`) uses the body `userId` for every identity decision:
  * the self-referral check `referralCode.ownerId === userId` (`:441`);
  * the already-referred check `dbGetReferralByReferredUser(userId)`;
  * `referredUserId` on the stored referral;
  * the signup reward, `createReward(userId, …)`, when the fraud check passes.

## What that would allow (NOT exercised)

Reading the code, a signed-in caller could:

* apply their **own** code while naming a different uuid. The self-referral check would compare the code owner with that other uuid and pass.
* create a referral, and the signup reward, for a `userId` that is not theirs.

I have **not** run this on any stack. Whether a reward is ever paid out from these rows was not traced.

## Callers

There is no product caller of `/apply` in the repo: 0 non-test hits outside the spec, the route table and the schemathesis baseline (`git grep "referrals/apply"` over all 4,392 tracked files). The route is in the published spec, so any API client can call it.

## Dedupe

The eight tickets naming `referrals/apply` (KS-1016, KS-971, KS-784, KS-565, KS-466, KS-445, KS-431, KS-430) are all schema or status-code sweeps, read in each case. None covers the body `userId`. `applyCodeSchema`, `body.userId`, `referred_user_id` and "apply on behalf" have 0 hits on the board.

title: The gateway forwards an inbound x-wallet-address to originate on POST /api/documents, and originate never reads it — dead forward (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

**The gateway hand-forwards an inbound** `x-wallet-address` **header to originate on** `POST /api/documents`**, and originate never reads it.** The forward is dead code. It carries a client-supplied value past the gateway for no consumer. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's ruling while planning KS-1223, which leaves this code untouched.

## Facts

All at develop `7c6b3d88`:

* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1383`: `if (req.headers['x-wallet-address']) forwardHeaders['x-wallet-address'] = req.headers['x-wallet-address'] …`, inside the hand-built forward to originate on POST /api/documents.
* Originate has **0** reads of `x-wallet-address`. Control: originate does read `x-user-id` from headers, in `metering.ts`.
* A `git grep -i x-wallet-address` over all 4,392 tracked files finds exactly two non-test files. One is this line. The other is `services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55`, which KS-1223 changes.
* A pin test asserts today's behaviour: `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1223-wallet-forwarded-to-originate.test.ts` (:84 RED, :87 CONTROL). Removing the forward flips it.
* Separately, `ks1041-vouch-header-strip.test.ts:113` pins that the header is **not** in the gateway's edge strip.

## Not decided here

Whether to delete the forward (one line, plus the pin test flipped) or leave it.

title: GET /api/keys has no organisation arm: an ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN lists another organisation's keys in the same tenant
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **has no organisation arm.** An `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A lists organisation B's API keys when B is in the same tenant, using B's exact id. The mint and the revoke are both organisation-bounded for these roles; the list is the only one of the three routes that is not. **Measured** at develop `7c6b3d88`, details below. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's ruling while building KS-1553 PR 1, which does **not** add the bound.

**What is exposed:** each key's **id, name, prefix, scopes and connector id**, plus `lastUsedAt`, `usageCount`, `isActive` and `createdAt`. **Not key material:** the list never returns the key or its hash.

**Not reached by Kam's ADMIN ruling.** That ruling (KS-1570) concerns the tenant-level `ADMIN` role on the mint. The roles here are `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, which are organisation-bounded on the mint (KS-1533) and on the revoke (KS-764).

## The code

At develop `7c6b3d88`, `services/security/src/index.ts:1318-1366`:

* The handler filters `k.organizationId === organizationId`, where `organizationId` is the raw query value, and then `callerIsPlatform || k.tenantId === caller.tenantId`. That second filter is KS-742's tenant bound.
* Nothing in the handler reads `caller.organizationId` or calls `isOrgBoundedRole`.
* The mint, by contrast, calls `decideTenantAccess(user, tenantId, { targetOrganizationId })` (`index.ts:1173`). That engages the organisation arm for `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES = {ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN}` (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`).
* The revoke is bounded by `decideKeyRevoke` (KS-764).

## Measured

A throwaway in-process probe, using the same harness as `ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts` (memory-backed; the list reads only `memApiKeys`). Organisation ids contain hex letters, so the upper-case form is not identical to the original.

| caller | lists | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| platform (`super_admin`) | mints for A1 and A2 | 201, 201 |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A1 | 200, 1 key |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of A1** | **A2, exact id** | **200, 1 key (the gap)** |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A2, upper-case | 200, 0 keys (only because the compare is raw; see below) |
| CONTROL: `ISSUER_ADMIN` of a tenant-B org | A2 | 200, 0 keys (the tenant filter is real) |
| CONTROL: platform | A2 | 200, 1 key |

**After KS-1553 PR 1** the list normalises the query, so the upper-case form of A2 also lists A2's key. That reveals nothing the exact id does not already reveal. PR 1 pins both as cells labelled MEASURED GAP that name this ticket, so adding a bound later is a visible edit.

## Dedupe

I scanned all 1,560 issues, archived ones included, with their comments, for list / another-organisation / organisation-arm wording. The positive control (KS-1533 matching "organisation arm") fired, and a bogus-symbol control returned 0. Nothing covers the list. KS-742 bounded the list by **tenant** only.

## Not decided here

The shape of the bound: refuse, or filter as KS-742 and `GET /api/audit` do. Also how it treats the org-less bounded accounts KS-779 recorded as intentional.

title: /health/deep reports startupMigrations.applied=46 on a deploy that applied ZERO migration files — the field sums file-based DDL with in-code idempotent steps
description:
## BLUF

`/health/deep` **reported** `startupMigrations.applied=46` **on a deploy that applied ZERO migration files.** Measured on kintsugi during the round-2 deploy (2026-10-13, pin `361537eed238`), where the migration delta was independently established as **0 migration-path files** out of 123 changed files. The field aggregates two different kinds of work under one name, so the number cannot be read as "migrations applied". Facts only; no fix proposed.

## The reading, and what it decomposes into

`GET /health/deep` body, immediately after the api-gateway recreate:

```
"startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":46,"failed":0,"lastRunAt":"2026-10-13T00:06:34.420Z"}
```

The same boot's own log lines, in order:

```
[startup-migrations] loaded 50 migration files from /app/migrations
[startup-migrations] File-based main DB migrations complete     {"applied":0,"failed":0}
[startup-migrations] File-based platform DB migrations complete {"applied":0,"failed":0}
[startup-migrations] Main DB migrations complete                {"applied":39,"failed":0}
[startup-migrations] Platform DB migrations complete            {"applied":7,"failed":0}
```

**0 + 0 file-based, then 39 + 7 = 46.** So the health body's `applied` is the sum of the **in-code idempotent** steps (tenant seeds, per-client tenant re-sync, vocabulary ensures), and the **file-based** `.sql` **counters — the ones that correspond to a schema change — are both zero and are not represented in the body at all.**

## Why the distinction matters

The in-code steps **write no row to the** `_secuura_migrations` **tracker**, so they leave no schema trace, while a file migration does. Independently measured on the same deploy:

| reading | before the swap | after the swap |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `_secuura_migrations` rows, `secuura` | 49 | 49 |
| `_secuura_migrations` rows, `secuura_platform` | 1 | 1 |
| tracker rows dated 2026-10-13 | — | **0** |
| `Applying` lines in the boot window | — | **0** (control: impossible word 0, 153 total lines) |

Newest tracker row is dated 2026-09-30. So nothing was applied in the file sense, while the health body says 46.

## The consequence

A deploy check that reads `startupMigrations.applied` as a migration count will report 46 applied migrations on a zero-migration deploy. The repo's own deploy discipline is to **read the schema state rather than a runner summary line**, precisely because a summary line has reported success over a stale image before; this field is the same shape of trap one layer out, in the health surface rather than the runner.

## Nearest class members — read in full before filing, neither is this

* **KS-1062** (Done, P2) — the *tenant* loop's `migrated` counter cannot report a failure. Same family (a migration counter that misreports) but a different counter and a correctness defect, not a reporting-aggregation one.
* **KS-1272** (Done, P4) — `Platform DB migrations INCOMPLETE — 1 FAILED {"applied":6,"failed":1}` on kintsugi. Shows these same counters in the log, but is about a failing DELETE, not about what `applied` aggregates.
* Also read and distinct: KS-1125, KS-1055, KS-1401, KS-1096.

*Dedupe: all **1,564** Secuura-PK issues were pulled **including archived** and matched LITERALLY (not via the fuzzy* `searchIssues`*) on* `startupMigrations`*,* `startup-migrations`*,* `health/deep`*,* `File-based`*,* `migrations complete`*,* `applied=46`*,* `idempotent`*,* `tracker row`*. Positive control* `secuura` *matched **998**; negative control* `zzQqXx-no-such-token-d19` *matched **0**, so the matcher discriminates.* `applied=46` *matched 0 existing issues.*

Found by Seat D 19th during the kintsugi round-2 deploy; filed on Wednesday's instruction (2026-10-13T00:16:31Z). Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatD-19th/stepFG/` and `/home/secuura/secuura/Dev/REVISION`.

title: KS-1553 (a) follow-up (pull request 1533 gate m1): a key whose stored organization_id is blank is no longer listable by any query, and the comment says it matches as before
description:
## BLUF

**Pull request 1533 (KS-1553 (a)) makes an API key whose STORED** `organization_id` **is blank (whitespace-only) unlistable by any query, and the comment above the change says the opposite.** On develop such a key was listable by the exact blank query; after pull request 1533 no query reaches it. It is still revocable by id. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's GO, as the gate's Minor **m1** (verdict sha256/16 `4fc478e33f32e0b3`, Sonnet tier 2, GO WITH NOTE).

## What the gate measured

The gate seeded `organization_id = '   '` with the service running as `secuura_app`, then called `GET /api/keys?organizationId=%20%20%20` as `super_admin`:

| tree | result |
| -- | -- |
| develop `3a871337` | 200 + that key |
| pull request 1533 head `f4828b1d` | 200 + `[]` |

The cause: the list now normalises **both** sides with `normaliseOrgId` (trim, lower-case, blank = absent). The blank stored id becomes `null`, and the null guard refuses a query that normalises to `null`, so nothing can equal it. The gate found this for every caller class (platform and tenant admins).

## The stale comment

`services/security/src/index.ts:1349-1358` (as landed) says a query that normalises to null "matches nothing, as it did before". That is true for the query side. It is **false** for a key whose **stored** id is blank: develop listed it, and the head lists it under nothing.

## How such rows could exist

Since #1521 the mint stores `normaliseOrgId(organizationId)`, so a blank id is stored as `null`, not as whitespace. A whitespace-only stored id could only come from before #1521, or from a direct write. **Whether any exist on Kintsugi or demo is unknown.** The gate read no live data and neither did I. KS-1565 already asks for a read-only count of non-canonical `organization_id` rows, and this shape could be added to that count.

## The ruling it needs

* **(a) Accept as is:** blank-stored keys are unlistable and revocable by id only. Correct the comment and add one cell that pins it.
* **(b) Make blank-stored keys listable:** this needs a way to ask for them, since a blank query now means "absent". That is a design choice, not a one-liner.

Nothing is changed until that is ruled.

title: KS-1223 follow-up (pull request 1534 gate m1-m4): bound the users read in time, bind the tenant in SQL, add the gate's missing cells, rename G8 — before any referral deploy
description:
## BLUF

**The follow-up to pull request 1534 (KS-1223): four Minors from its Opus gate**, ruled by Wednesday to be fixed in ONE follow-up pull request (Sonnet delta gate) after 1534 merges as gated. Verdict sha256/16 `19608e1f74ed846b`, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major. **m1 is a deploy precondition:** this follow-up must land before any deploy of the referral service (recorded by Wednesday in DEPLOY-BLOCKERS). Facts only, from the gate's report; line numbers are at pull request 1534's head `884a24eb`.

## m1: the users read has no time bound, so code generation hangs while `users` is locked

* **Where:** `services/referral/src/db.ts:191-196` (`getLinkedWalletAddress`). `getPool()` (`db.ts:28-32`) sets no `statement_timeout`.
* **Measured by the gate:** another session holds `LOCK TABLE users IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE` (the shape of a migration's `ALTER TABLE users`). `POST /api/referrals/generate` never answers, and the client gave up at 8 s. On release the row is written anyway, after the client has gone. Develop answered 201 at once.
* **Fix asked for:** bound the read: `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` inside its transaction, or a statement or query timeout on this pool. On timeout the route already answers 500 and writes no row.

## m2: the read binds the tenant only through RLS, not in its SQL (defence in depth)

* **Where:** `db.ts:194`, `SELECT wallet_address FROM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT 1`.
* **Measured by the gate:** under an RLS-bypassing role, a token naming tenant B reads a tenant-A row. **Exposure today: none found.** Referral connects as `secuura_app`, and the row read is always the caller's own (the signed `userId`).
* **Fix asked for:** `… WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id::text = $2`. That also makes the author's mutant M10 (the tenant guard removed) non-equivalent.

## m3: coverage. The PR's 10 cells miss six plausible regressions, and the default run has no KS-1223 pin

* The gate's mutants **Y1** (wallet read for the body `userId`), **Y2** (tenant from the `x-tenant-id` header first), **Y3** (session-wide GUC on another pooled connection), **Y4** (one error class swallowed), **Y5** (stale per-user cache) and **Y7** (wallet lower-cased) leave the 10 cells green. They die only on the gate's own cells.
* **Y9** (a `walletAddress` claim on the token wins) survives everything. It is harmless while no minter signs such a claim, but nothing pins "a token claim is ignored".
* The deleted mock test was the only KS-1223 pin in the default `npm test` run. `vitest.config.ts` now excludes `*.integration.test.ts`, as security and auth already do.
* **Fix asked for:**
  * adopt equivalents of the gate's cells **X8** (body userId and wallet fields stripped), **X9** (header tenant ignored), **X13** (link, clear, relink with no stale read), **P1/P2** (pool max 1 and 2, interleaved tenants, GUC empty afterwards), **F1** (users table missing → generic 500, no row) and **C2** (a mixed-case linked wallet is stored as sent);
  * add a cell for Y9;
  * add a cheap default-run unit pin that the header is ignored.

## m4: cell G8, "the DEMO shape", does not test the demo shape

* With its `tenants` / `tenant_config` inserts removed, it still passes (the gate's control run): the referral code never reads `tenant_config` and always uses the default pool. So G8 is G2 with a fresh tenant id.
* **Fix asked for:** rename it to what it pins ("a non-default tenant reads its wallet on the shared default pool"), or drop the platform-row seeding.

## Notes (no severity, for whoever builds the follow-up)

* **U1:** an array `userId` gives 500, a shape no minter produces.
* **X10:** a deleted or suspended user row still supplies its wallet. Token validity is the gate.
* **W1:** a whitespace-only wallet is stored as is.
* **C1/C2:** the case mismatch on the collision flag. The referred side is client-asserted, which is KS-1572.
* If `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is ever enabled, this read returns a silent null for tenants whose users live in another database (declared in pull request 1534; KS-1055).

title: An ADMIN (scoped or not) or ISSUER_ADMIN escapes its organisation bound in two hops through an organizations:register provisioning key — pre-existing, deploy-blocking for KS-1570 (pull request 1535 gate M1)
description:
## BLUF

**Any tenant-level** `ADMIN` **(scoped or not), and any** `ISSUER_ADMIN`**, can still obtain an API key that names ANY organisation of its tenant AND is bound to that organisation's connector, in two calls, through a provisioning key it is allowed to mint.** KS-1570 does not close the deploy blocker it was written for until this is fixed.

* **Pre-existing:** not in pull request 1535's diff, and identical on develop.
* **Deploy-blocking for KS-1570's purpose:** the KS-695 erasure trusts that key row's organisation and connector, and the erasure is irreversible.
* Facts only, from the pull request 1535 Opus gate (verdict sha256/16 `908a786016f5c2f2`, finding **M1**). **The fix needs Kam's ruling** (see the end). Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## The two hops (measured by the gate on 1535's head `335dfd78`, and the same on develop)

1. **Hop 1:** an `ADMIN` mints a key with `scopes: ['organizations:register']`.
   * `decideMint` takes the KEY_ADMIN early return for every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member, whatever the requested scopes (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:97`).
   * An unscoped ADMIN can do this as an **unqualified** key, which is the path Kam's KS-1570 ruling deliberately keeps open.
2. **Hop 2:** that key's connector principal is a **provisioner**: role `connector` plus `organizations:register` (`services/security/src/index.ts:1218`). It mints `{ organizationId: A2, connectorId: <A2's connector> }`.
   * **Measured: 201.** The row stores `organization_id = A2`, `connector_id = conn_of_A2`.
   * Role `connector` meets neither the org-bounded arm nor the new ADMIN-scope arm (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:170-275`).

The gate measured this for an **unscoped ADMIN**, an **ADMIN scoped to** `{A1}`, and an `ISSUER_ADMIN` **with claim A1**. So KS-1533 arm 1's organisation bound is open by the same route.

**Why it matters:** the KS-695 connector erasure trusts a key row's organisation and connector (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:125, 144, 333-345`).

## The gate's minimal fix (NOT chosen here)

Apply KS-480's limit 1 to non-platform key admins: only a platform role may mint `organizations:register` (and wildcards).

* That needs **Kam's ruling** if a tenant admin legitimately provisions. Wednesday is taking it to Kam on a card.
* No build until it is ruled.
* The gate's regression cell is `evidence/gatetests/gate1535-d-twohop.integration.test.ts` in its evidence folder. It is red on 1535's head and on develop today, and should go green.

## Not tested by the gate

* The gateway hop end to end. It built the connector bearer from auth's `generateConnectorToken` claims and this service's own `/api/keys/validate` output; the gateway proxies `/api/security/*` → security `/api/*` behind `authenticateToken`.
* The erasure actually running against a hop-2 key (a code read only).

**Context:** KS-486 (Review A) recorded that `decideMint` allows on role alone. This two-hop route to a foreign organisation's connector is not on any ticket. The board was searched for "two-hop", "escape from the scope", "provisioning key", and `organizations:register` together with admin and mint.

title: KS-1582 follow-up (pull request 1536 gate m-a, m-b, N1): pin the transaction-local timeout and its value, pin the ::text tenant compare, and handle a pg client error while checked out
description:
## BLUF

**The follow-up to pull request 1536 (KS-1582): two coverage Minors and one pre-existing note from its Sonnet delta gate** (verdict sha256/16 `7306c470a243195b`, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major). The code change behaved correctly in every probe, so these are gaps in the PR's own cells. Facts only, from the gate's report. Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## m-a: nothing pins that the timeout is transaction-local, or its value

* Where: `services/referral/src/__tests__/ks1582-referrer-wallet-read-gate-cells.integration.test.ts`, cell P (its connection probe reads only the tenant GUC) and cell B1 (`expect(ms).toBeLessThan(8_000)`). Code under test: `services/referral/src/db.ts:210` (`SET LOCAL statement_timeout = ${WALLET_READ_TIMEOUT_MS}`), the constant at `:199`.
* The gate's mutants **Z1** (`SET statement_timeout = 3000` before `BEGIN`), **Z4** (`SET` without `LOCAL` inside the transaction) and **Z3** (the value 7000) all leave the PR's 20 integration cells and 3 unit cells green.
* Z1 and Z4 would leave a permanent 3 s `statement_timeout` on a pooled connection that every other referral query also uses.
* Fix asked for:
  * in P's probe, also read `current_setting('statement_timeout')` and assert `'0'` for each distinct pid (the gate's T1 does this; its control T0 shows the probe can see a leak);
  * tighten B1 to a window around the bound, for example more than 2500 ms and less than 4500 ms.

## m-b: the stated reason for `::text` (no cast error) is not pinned

* Where: `ks1582-tenant-bound-in-sql.integration.test.ts`, which exercises only the exact tenant and one other uuid tenant; code at `db.ts:212` (`tenant_id::text = $2`).
* The gate's mutant **Z7** (`tenant_id = $2::uuid`) passes every PR cell. With it, a token whose `tenantId` is not a uuid (`not-a-uuid`, an array, a number) makes generate answer **5xx** for a signed-in user, where develop answers 201. The head answers 201 for all 13 shapes the gate tried.
* Fix asked for: one cell of the gate's M2 shape (a non-uuid, an array and a number `tenantId` under the app role answer 201 with no wallet), or a non-uuid tenant added to the bypass file's RED cell.

## N1 (pre-existing, the same on develop `c855cfc2`): an unhandled `pg` client error

* When the database kills the backend mid-read (or on a failover), the checked-out `pg` client emits an `error` event that nothing listens for. vitest reports `Uncaught Exception: Connection terminated unexpectedly`, while the request itself correctly answers 500 and the next one works.
* The identical pattern exists in `queryWithTenantGuc` in `packages/shared`.
* In production an uncaught exception exits the process, per `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts`.
* Not introduced or worsened by KS-1582: a statement timeout is an ordinary query error, not a connection error.
* Fix asked for: a `client.on('error', …)` while a client is checked out, in shared code (outside KS-1582's scope).

## Notes carried, no action asked

* N2: a read slower than 3 s now fails closed (500). That is the intended trade, and the bound is a product decision.
* N3: B1 takes about 12 s on a red run and about 3 s on a green one.

title: An ADMIN's organisation scope rows SURVIVE demotion and deletion, so the grant revives if the account is restored
description:
## BLUF

`admin_organisation_scopes` **rows are never purged when the user they grant to stops being an ADMIN, or is deleted.** The grant sits dormant and **revives silently** if the account is reactivated or re-promoted.

Raised twice and still open as a question, which is why it now has its own ticket:

* the pull request 1535 gate's **m3** (PR A);
* the pull request 1539 gate's **m2** (PR B), which measured that a user with `role='ADMIN'` and `status='deleted'` could be **granted** a scope — 200, row written.

## What IS now closed, and what is not

**Closed in PR B's delta (KS-1570):** the write side. `PUT /api/keys/admin-scopes/:userId` now requires the target to be `status = 'active'`, so a non-live user cannot be *given* a scope (404, nothing written), pinned by a cell.

**NOT closed, and deliberately out of that PR:** existing rows. Nothing removes them on demotion, on status change, or on delete. There is no cascade — `admin_organisation_scopes` has **no foreign keys** (by design: the pull request 1535 gate's m3 is why the route does write-time checks instead).

## The decision needed

1. Purge on demotion / deletion — a trigger, a cascade, or an application step on the role-change and delete paths; or
2. filter at **read** time (`getAdminOrganisationScope` joins `users` and requires live + ADMIN), which leaves the rows but makes them inert; or
3. accept it, and say so, since the account cannot authenticate while non-live.

**(2) is the cheapest fail-closed option** and needs no migration, but it adds a join to a per-decision read. Not built; this is an owner's call.

## Not measured

Whether any production or demo row is currently in this state. A census belongs with the deploy seat, not here.

Filed by Seat V 7th from the pull request 1539 gate (m2) and the 1535 gate (m3).

title: Lifecycle vocabulary: add a `timestamp` verb (a signature's RFC 3161 timestamp added after signing)
description:
From platform-s [PS-1209](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1209/timestamping-as-one-service-three-tsas-in-order-and-an-automatic-retry) phase 2 (Stuart, 2026-10-13).

## What S now does

When every timestamp authority (DigiCert, GlobalSign, Sectigo) fails at signing time, platform-s saves the signature without a timestamp. A background retry then adds the timestamp later:

* **Detached** `.p7s`**:** an RFC 3161 token is added as an unsigned attribute. The document's bytes are unchanged; the `.p7s` is replaced.
* **PDF:** a DocTimeStamp is appended as an incremental update. This is a **new file and a new hash**.
* **Office:** a XAdES `SignatureTimeStamp` is added. This is also a **new file and a new hash**.

S records each one as a new lifecycle event with the verb `timestamp`. The actor is the platform itself, with no person.

## Why this ticket

K's vocabulary has no `timestamp`. Today S therefore **never sends** these events: `TransactionAction.IsNeverAnchored` excludes the verb everywhere rows are picked to anchor, the same way the read verbs are excluded.

The consequence: for PDF and Office, the current signed copy on S (the timestamped one) has a hash K has never seen. Verify on S still recognises it from S's own ledger. But K's lineage stops at the signed copy, and an on-chain check of the timestamped copy finds nothing.

## Ask

Add `timestamp` to the lifecycle vocabulary (`LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / the anchor `documentType` enum), as a **byte-changing** verb.

* **PDF / Office:** a new K version with `parent_document_id` = the signed copy, the same shape as `sign-cert`.
* **Detached:** the content hash is unchanged. A flat anchor is enough. Optionally record the new `.p7s` hash in metadata (compare [KS-1454](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1454/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-signaturehash-the-plain)'s `signatureHash`).

Once K accepts the verb, S will:

* move `timestamp` from never-anchored to anchored;
* route the byte-changing cases through the per-verb path with versioning;
* adopt it in `CardanoAnchorService.PlatformKAnchorVerbs`.

That will be a follow-up PS ticket.

## Payload

The only non-PII fields S would send are the `timestamp` verb, the content hash, and (for detached) the `.p7s` hash. The issuing authority's name (e.g. "DigiCert SHA256 RSA4096 Timestamp Responder 2026 1") is a service, not a person, and could go in metadata if K wants it.

title: Two ungated tenant reads that KS-1032's fail-closed ruling does not cover: metering prefers req.tenantId over a verified req.user.tenantId, and extractTenantContext's header read is ungated in multi-tenant mode
description:
## BLUF

Two findings from the **pull request 1546 Opus gate** (verdict `34fb8ee6b4650ac6`, head `ad366066`), recorded as **facts with no fix shape**. Both are hardening **beyond** Kam's KS-1032 ruling ("Fail closed, deployed only after the secret is set"), which is why they are a ticket and not code in that pull request. Neither is exploitable while the provenance strip works: the gate found **0 forged-versus-bare differences across all 147 declared routes** (its cells GA5, GB3, GC7).

**Nothing here is ruled and nothing is commissioned.**

## Fact 1 — metering scopes by `req.tenantId`, not by the verified `req.user.tenantId`

* `services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts` resolves the tenant with `reqTenantId(req)`, which reads `(req as any).tenantId` and falls back to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`.
* On a box with `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` **unset or MISMATCHED**, the gateway still attaches a connector Bearer JWT carrying the key's `tenantId` (minted by auth `/internal/connector-token`), and `authenticate()` accepts it and sets `req.user`. But the handler never consults `req.user.tenantId`.
* Because the headers were stripped, the KS-458 block had already set `req.tenantId` to the default. **Measured result: 200, reading the DEFAULT tenant's usage** (gate cells GA1, GC5). A **401** happens only when the gateway's token exchange failed (GA2).
* So on such a box a partner reads **another tenant's** usage totals whenever Platform S's key tenant differs from DEFAULT. **Whether that is true on Kintsugi or demo is UNMEASURED.**
* The gate recorded a possible direction (its M1 option (c)): have `reqTenantId` prefer a verified `req.user.tenantId` when `authenticate()` set the user. **Recorded as the gate's option, not as a decision.**

## Fact 2 — `extractTenantContext`'s header read is ungated in multi-tenant mode

* Enumerating every writer of `.tenantId` in `services/originate/src` and `packages/shared/src` gives exactly **three**: `originate/src/index.ts:251` (the KS-458 resolution), `originate/src/routes/metering.ts:65`, and `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:91`.
* The third assigns straight from the **raw** `req.headers['x-tenant-id']` read at `tenant-context.ts:67`, with no provenance check.
* `resolveRequestTenantId` prefers an already-attached `req.tenantId` over its own gated header arm. So with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` the attached arm wins and carries an ungated header value: **KS-1032's part (c) is a second line in single-tenant mode only**, and the strip is the only line in multi-tenant mode.
* `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` is `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}` in `docker-compose.yml`. **Whether it is on for any live box is UNMEASURED.**
* Related: with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` and `NODE_ENV=production`, `extractTenantContext` answers **400 on every request** once the headers are stripped ("Missing tenant context", `tenant-context.ts:68-73`). Read statically, not run.

## What was already done about the texts

Pull request 1546's fix round corrected the comments and operator docs that misdescribed the above (gate findings M1, m2, m3) — `routes/metering.ts`, `utils/requestTenant.ts`, the C2 cell comment, `.env.example`, `env.example`, `docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` and `services/originate/src/index.ts`. **Only the texts. No behaviour was changed**, deliberately: gating `extractTenantContext` is outside Kam's ruling.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title **and** description (NOT `searchIssues`, which is fuzzy — it returns hits for a nonsense term, so it cannot be a membership test). Terms and counts: `reqTenantId` 1, `extractTenantContext` 2, `req.user.tenantId` 0, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` 4; **negative control** `zzqq-no-such-term-at-all` **0**, so the instrument discriminates.

Near-misses read and rejected:

* **KS-1084** — the gateway's own Authorization-only calls send **no** `x-tenant-id`, so originate defaults them. That is the header being **absent**; Fact 1 is about a **present and verified** `req.user.tenantId` being ignored in favour of `req.tenantId`. KS-1084's own stated unknown ("whether originate's `authenticate()` sets the tenant from the forwarded JWT on these routes") is partly answered here for metering.
* **KS-1091** — the cross-tenant JWT probe on originate's direct path, explicitly **not commissioned and not ruled**; about the strip, not these two reads.

No relation link added, because neither is the same defect.

Filed by Seat J 9th from the pull request 1546 gate round 1. Contributes to KS-1032; does not resolve it.

title: Security: nothing binds the forwarded `identity` block to the authenticated caller — any authenticated caller can anchor any DID at the highest trust level
description:
## BLUF

Facts only, no fix shape. From the pull request 1549 Opus gate (verdict `40bdc24d2e1f07dc`, its **INF-2**). Wednesday ruled it gets its own Medium ticket and is **not** in 1549's fix round: Kam's ruling ("Latest event's identity wins") decides **whose** identity is stored, not **who may assert** one.

## Facts

* anchoring checks the `identity` block's **shape** only. `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:109-118` says so outright: K proves SHAPE by regex/enum/type and **never SEMANTICS**.
* Nothing compares the block to the authenticated caller: the DID, `actorLevel`, `actorVerified`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust` and `orgVerified` are taken as sent.
* The gate's case "different actor, max claims" (`evidence/identity_edges.log`): all seven fields were anchored as sent.
* anchoring's direct `POST /api/anchors` has accepted this since **KS-1175**. Pull request 1549 (KS-1385) forwards the block from **six more originate sites**, each called with the end user's or a connector's bearer — so any authenticated caller of those originate routes can now place an asserted identity on chain through them.
* Measured by the gate, not re-measured here. Related: **KS-1603** (who may write an anchor row at all) — a different question from who may assert an identity.

*Filed by Seat J 9th on Wednesday's instruction. Not fixed here.*
