Project rule [KS-201](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-201/enforce-utc-for-all-datetime-handling-across-backend-services-and) requires every date to be UTC, so either answer is a defect to fix.

## Related

* [KS-1557](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1557/security-a-write-role-caller-can-make-another-organisations-bytes): the read-side change (PR 1531) this suite pins.
* [KS-1474](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1474/no-gate-executes-the-db-backed-integration-suites-the-default-test-run): no gate runs the DB-backed `*.integration.test.ts` suites, which is why a timezone-dependent red could go unnoticed.

## Not yet measured (filled in by the assignee or on request)

* The names of the 3 red cells.
* The pass/fail count for the same suite under `TZ=UTC`, to confirm the contrast.
* Whether the failing assertion is on a date value, a day boundary, or something else.

No fix is proposed here. Needs a Postgres for the integration suite (`npm run test:integration`).

title: tests/e2e callers of the retired POST /api/documents/:id/verify: rewrite against /api/verification/verify once the e2e package can run (KS-1628, KS-734)
description:
**KS-1628 retires** `POST /api/documents/:id/verify`**. These** `tests/e2e` **callers of that route will fail against a stack that has the change, and none of them was run** — `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` is a separate Playwright package that needs a live stack, which no preflight leg provides (KS-734 is the ticket for making it runnable). Wednesday ruled (b) on KS-1628 PR 2: leave them, name them, and file this ticket, because an unrun rewrite of assertions is a guess presented as a fix.

## The callers (at develop `83ed01af70fd`)

**Will fail when run:**

* `tests/e2e/tests/integration/full-certification-flow.api.spec.ts:62` — POSTs `requestedFields` / `purpose` / `legalBasis` to the retired route and asserts `result.verified`, `result.issuer.verified` and `result.blockchain.anchored`. Those are the retired gateway handler's response shape: the successor `POST /api/verification/verify` answers `checks.isAnchored`, and its `blockchain.anchored` is usually absent.
* `tests/e2e/tests/recruitment/alternative-paths.spec.ts:54, :134, :198` and `tests/e2e/tests/recruitment/fixtures/recruitment-helpers.ts:82` — call it through the endpoint map `API_ENDPOINTS.documents.verify(...)`, defined at `tests/e2e/tests/recruitment/fixtures/recruitment-data.ts:254` (and the twin map at `tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-data.ts:82`).

**Degrade cleanly, no action needed:** `tests/e2e/tests/holder-exhaustive.prelaunch.spec.ts:278` and `tests/e2e/tests/verifier-exhaustive.prelaunch.spec.ts:292` try the old route inside a fallback chain and move on at status ≥ 400.

## What "done" looks like

Once the e2e package can run (KS-734): rewrite each "will fail" caller against `POST /api/verification/verify` (`{ documentId }` or a content hash in the body), assert the successor's own shape (`verified`, `checks.isAnchored`, the honest `blockchain` blob), point the two endpoint maps at it or drop their `verify` key, and **run them**.

## After KS-1628, what the old path answers

The request meets the auth-gated `/api/documents` proxy mount: **401** unauthenticated (before any route is looked up), **originate's 404** when authenticated with a documents scope.

## Dedupe

`description: contains` over all issues: `API_ENDPOINTS.documents.verify` 0, `recruitment-helpers` 0, `full-certification-flow` 0, `holder-exhaustive` 0, `tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-data` 0, `alternative-paths.spec` 2 (KS-1010, a CIP-30 check that passes on a 404 — a different defect; KS-734, the runnable-e2e ticket this one depends on). Control: a nonsense literal returns 0.

Filed by Seat R 49th from KS-1628 PR 2. Not built.

title: audit-log limit follow-up: retire the stale accepted baseline entry after a live sweep, and pin repeated-key and array limit forms
description:
## BLUF

PR #1501 (ticket KS-1359) makes `GET /api/platform/audit-log` refuse a `limit` above 200. Its Sonnet-tier gate (GO WITH NOTE, verdict sha256/16 `1d2e0a0977c7d099`) left two loose ends that sit outside that PR's two files: **(1)** a stale accepted-baseline entry for this operation that would quietly absorb a future regression of the same fix, and **(2)** no cell for a repeated or array `limit`.

## Recommendation

1. **Retire the baseline entry, but only after a live sweep.** Delete the key `by_design_input_tolerance_guard::GET /api/platform/audit-log` from `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json` (ticket KS-1359, expires 2026-12-31) once a post-deploy sweep reads 0 failures for it. Update `systemTest/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` in the same change: line 771 still documents DRIFT-AUDITLOG-QUERY-TOLERANCE as open and line 908 still counts the six `limit=201` failures. **Do not retire it before the sweep:** nothing is deployed yet, so today the entry is still true of the running environment.
2. **Pin the repeated-key and array forms.** Add a cell to the KS-1359 test file for `?limit=5&limit=500` and `?limit[]=500` answering 400. The gate dropped the `typeof v !== 'string'` guard (its M6) and the file stayed 16/16 green, so that line is untested. It is nearly redundant today, since every array shape the gate swept already answers 400, so this is an untested line and not a defect.

## Detail

* **Why the entry matters:** with `limit` refused, an `accepted` entry on this operation means the nightly sweep stops reporting a future regression of the same guard. The entry is the only thing between that regression and a red.
* **Sources:** gate verdict Finding 1 (Minor) and Note 2; the entry is at `schemathesis-baseline.json` line 488 at develop `06d33fb4b`. Related, different defect: KS-1361 (the baseline lagging the registers).
* **Not covered here:** the gate's Note 3, a separate pre-existing truncation in the same endpoint, is filed on its own.

title: Review stream: build, supply chain and release gates
description:
**Review stream for Peter — one review, one test pass, 18 tickets.**

## The one test pass — and the assertion IS the pass

From a **clean checkout on macOS**:

1. `bash scripts/preflight/preflight.sh`
2. `bash scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh` (minutes) — clean-room `npm ci` for every standalone lock
3. `npm run test:migrations` (~40 s) — five scenarios against a throwaway `postgres:15`; a failed scenario is a **non-zero exit**, not green text
4. `bash scripts/validate-env.sh`

Every ticket in this stream is a way that sequence currently fails, or lies, on someone else's machine: bash-4 syntax macOS cannot run (KS-676), validate-env stopping at its first error so every later check silently never runs (KS-680), preflight unable to run from a git worktree (KS-691), the launcher reporting the wrong branch (KS-681), and the audit baseline expiring under the gate (KS-635, KS-751, KS-763). One reviewer, one clean checkout, one run.

Commands and wall-clocks are quoted from `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` section *Manual CI-gate equivalents*.

title: 87 documentary sites still publish the retired admin credential — wrong rather than dangerous, clean up after KS-964's code items
description:
**BLUF** — after KS-964 retires the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default, **87 documentary occurrences across 55 files still name it**. They are wrong rather than dangerous, and this is the cleanup pass for them.

## Why this is separate, and lower priority

**Once the credential no longer works, a document naming it is misleading, not exploitable.** The security value was in KS-964 item 1 (the seeder stops accepting a default) and item 2 (the CI literals). This pass is about not leaving 55 files telling a reader to log in with something that will fail.

Blocking the rotation on it would have delayed the part that mattered.

## Scope

**87 occurrences / 55 files**, classified as documentary by extension (`.md`, `.mdc`, `.txt`) — the remainder of the 183 total measured for KS-964, after 93 executable and 3 unclassified.

Known clusters include `CLI-AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS.md` (a login recipe reproduced 4 times), `USER_TESTING/Secuura-Platform-Credentials.md`, `USER_TESTING/M365-Integration-Test-Guide.md`, `docs/BROWSER-TESTING-GUIDE.md`, and the `.cursor/` rules files.

## What "fixed" looks like

Not a find-and-replace to a new value — **there is no new shared value**, which is the point of KS-964. Each site should name the **environment variable** instead, the same way KS-949 F2 handled the three files that published a password beside the platform-admin identity: say the credential is not published and name what supplies it.

## Do after, not before

This should land **after** KS-964's code items, so the docs describe the world as it then is rather than a world in transit.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during the KS-964 rotation measurement.**

title: Mount the audit-export router behind authenticateToken (it answers 401 to every caller), then settle its three unfiled residuals
description:
## BLUF

**Action (owner: the K lane): mount the audit-export router behind** `authenticateToken`**; today it answers 401 to every caller.** `app.use('/api/admin/audit', auditExportRouter)` (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:808` at develop `361537eed238`) has no `authenticateToken`, and the router reads `req.user`, which only that middleware sets. So the platform audit export, the goal of KS-745, is unreachable as shipped. It is the same shape as the batch family tracked in KS-1243 (`/api/batch/*`, 401 to every caller); KS-1243 names only the batch routes.

## Recommendation

1. **Tests first:** a platform-admin JWT reaches the export and gets the entries; an anonymous request gets 401; a tenant ADMIN gets 403 if the router gates on role (read its own guard first).
2. **Then mount it with** `authenticateToken(true)`**.**
3. **Then decide the three residuals below** (they were read at source, not measured, and were never filed).
4. KS-745 stays In Progress until this is done: its PR fixed the route the export calls, and its own comment says the goal is still unmet.

## Detail

* **The PR's three unfiled residuals (from its own text):** (1) the list route ignores the export's `type`; (2) the list defaults `limit` to 50, so an export caps at 50 entries; (3) a date-only `to` looks like it drops that day.
* **Evidence:** the Tier-1 gate on KS-745's PR proved the export unreachable as shipped (KS-745's latest comment). I read the mount line at the tip. I re-measured the sibling `/api/batch/verify` today with a valid human token and a valid `x-api-key`: 401 both times. I did NOT drive the audit export itself, and I did not measure `/api/notifications`, which is mounted the same way two lines above (`index.ts:807`).
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, title and description): `audit-export`, `audit export`, `/api/admin/audit`, `auditExportRouter`. No ticket mentions the audit export's mount. Nearest: KS-745 itself, KS-1243 (batch only), KS-1410 (`err.message` in 500 bodies; a different subject).

Related: KS-745, KS-1243.

title: api-gateway: a connector JWT presented as a Bearer is still forwarded upstream by every mount that does not use authenticateToken (KS-1198 refuses it only inside authenticateToken)
description:
## BLUF

KS-1198 (PR #1470) refuses a verified connector JWT (`type: 'connector'`) presented as a Bearer credential, but **only inside** `authenticateToken`. Gateway mounts that do not use it still forward a connector Bearer upstream verbatim. The Opus gate on #1470 measured each of these with one forward carrying the Bearer. **Exploiting it needs a signed connector JWT**, which only the gateway mints from a validated `x-api-key`; nothing client-side holds one. So this is a defence-in-depth gap on the same class as KS-1198, not an open door. Not caused by #1470.

## Recommendation

One fix, one PR, tests first: refuse a signed `type: 'connector'` Bearer at **one earlier point** that every mount passes through (a small middleware mounted before the proxies, or in the shared bearer parse), with the same 401 body and the same structured warning as KS-1198, instead of repeating the check per mount. Pin it with a cell per mount below plus a no-regression control for the gateway's own `x-api-key` flow (which sets `Authorization: Bearer <connector JWT>` itself after the check and must keep working). Rollout as for KS-1198: Kintsugi first, read the `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER_REFUSED` lines for a cycle, then consider demo. **Decision for the owner:** `/api/v2/verification` is public-by-design and originate accepts a connector principal there via `authenticate({required:false})`; refusing the Bearer there is a behaviour change for any connector that calls it that way (none found in this repository).

## Detail

Measured by the gate (each: the stub upstream saw the Bearer):

* `/api/v2/verification` (originate `authenticate({required:false})` accepts it as a connector principal), `/api/verification`, `/api/presentations/verify`, `/api/documents/:id/sig-json`, `/api/auth/*`, `/api/sessions`.
* The gateway-internal `/originate/` mount (`proxy.ts:1201`) forwards `POST /originate/api/documents` to originate `POST /api/documents`, which is KS-1198's original endpoint (measured 200, 1 forward). **Mitigation in place:** nginx closes `/originate/` with a 404 in all three confs (KS-1041) and the api-gateway has no published ports in `docker-compose.production.yml`.
* Reads or intra-cluster only, per the gate.

**Related observation (pre-existing, same file):** the gateway Bearer path accepts `type: 'refresh'` tokens as principals: `authenticateToken` is a denylist on `type`, not an `access`-only allowlist. The gate called it a ticket candidate and out of scope for #1470. Left here so it is tracked; split it out if the owner prefers a ticket of its own.

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1470 (KS-1198), 2026-10-12, defect 2 and its notes (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1470/verdict.md`).
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER`, `connector JWT`, `authenticateToken`, `type: refresh`, `sig-json`: nothing tracks the unauthenticated mounts.

Related: KS-1198, KS-1205.

title: GET /api/platform/audit-log accepts wrong-type and out-of-range query values with 200 — beyond its ruled by-design tolerance
description:
## Summary

A small one for when you have a moment, Kamil. `GET /api/platform/audit-log` seems to accept a few more query shapes than the [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) ruling allows: wrong-type and out-of-range `offset` / `limit` values come back **200**. It's been steady at 30 cases per sweep across all six [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps, so it's long-standing rather than new. Either tightening the validation or widening the ruling would settle it, and which is your call. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence and options

### Results across the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps

Slot 3, seed 1353, 2026-09-28, read from each run's `schemathesis-output.ndjson`.

| Sweep | Interactions | Statuses | `by_design_input_tolerance_guard` | `negative_data_rejection` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1: 4.27.5 | 188 | 200×60, 401×121, 405×6, 204×1 | **30** (all 200) | 32 |
| 2: 4.28.0 | 188 | same | **30** | 32 |
| 3: + deps | 188 | same | **30** | 32 |
| 4: toml loaded | 181 | 200×60, 401×121 | **30** | 0 |

Sweeps 5 and 6 match sweep 4.

* The guard lives in `config/check_predicates.py` (hook-loaded), so it ran in every sweep and never moved.
* `negative_data_rejection` ×32 = the guard's 30 + 2 unknown-parameter cases (the ruled shape). It reads 0 from sweep 4 because the toml exception is finally loaded. That's the ruling being applied, not a fix.

### The 30 cases (identical every sweep)

| Phase | Case | Count |
| -- | -- | -- |
| coverage | Incorrect type (whole query) | 10 |
| coverage | `offset`: Incorrect type | 5 |
| coverage | `limit`: Incorrect type | 5 |
| coverage | below minimum / above maximum (`offset`, `limit`) | 6 |
| fuzzing | `offset` / `limit` wrong type or below minimum | 4 |

Smallest repro: `GET /api/platform/audit-log?offset=-1` as a platform admin → **200**. The ruled shape `?offset=0&x-schemathesis-unknown-property=42` → 200 is allowed.

### Options

1. **Validate the query** (types and declared bounds) and keep the ruling narrow. The guard stays as the regression pin.
2. **Widen the ruling** on [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the), with `check_predicates.py` following it.

Sibling: [KS-1371](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1371/post-apistatusidunrevoke-accepts-index-1-below-the-declared-minimum) (unrevoke `index: -1`). Baseline side: [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

+++

title: start-secuura.sh and start-local.sh print the demo issuer password in their startup banners
description:
## BLUF

**Two platform-k start scripts print a password in clear on every successful start.** Both echo the demo issuer account's email *and its password* in their closing "Credentials" banner:

| Script | Line (`develop` `0f2422925`) | Last change |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` | `:711`, `echo -e "    Issuer:  demo@secuura.io / <password>"` | `7b14f84ff`, 2026-09-22 |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-local.sh` | `:251`, `echo "    Issuer:  demo@secuura.io  / <password>"` | `48641bda3`, 2026-09-05 |

The value is not reproduced here. The banner goes to the terminal, and from there into anything that captures stdout: CI logs, `nohup` / background-run logs (it is in this session's `$TMPDIR` start log), pasted bug reports and screenshots.

The platform-s rule (platform-s `CLAUDE.md` → *Security Considerations*) is: *"platform-k: a script or service there that prints or logs a password is raised as a **Critical** defect, assigned to Kamil."* That is why this is raised Urgent and assigned to you.

## Measured (5 Oct 2026)

* **The printed credential is live.** The same script's own login check (`start-secuura.sh:603`, which uses the same literal in a `curl` body) logged `Issuer login (demo@secuura.io)` as a success on a fresh K slot 3 (`46c3e20cf`, `--rebuild --fresh-db`).
* **Re-verified on the current** `origin/develop` `0f2422925`**:** both lines are still present, and no other `*.sh` under the repo echoes the literal.

## Severity context (stated so it can be weighed, not used to wave it through)

* This is the **published demo sample login**: platform-k `CLAUDE.md:107` names it, and [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation)'s scope note calls the demo logins deliberate, documented sample credentials. So the secret itself is already public.
* What the banner adds: it makes a known-default credential the thing every operator reads at the end of every start, on **every** compose deploy that runs these scripts. [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation) shows the same compose path seeds these defaults by default (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` defaults to `true`), and that rotating them through `.env` is silently ignored. So on a box where an operator *thinks* they rotated it, the banner still prints the old value, and the old value may still work.
* It also undercuts the "never print a password" rule both platforms hold. A script that prints one is the precedent the next script copies.

## Not covered by existing tickets (checked)

* [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has) (In Progress, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1180](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-972-banner-start-secuurash-no-longer-prints-the-retired-admin-850ff68f818a)) fixed the **Admin** half of the same banner and explicitly left the Issuer half: *"the issuer half is correct and only the admin half is stale."* Its concern was a stale credential, not a printed one. It wasn't updated here because it is In Progress.
* [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation) (Backlog) covers compose seeding of the `*123` defaults and the broken rotation channel, not scripts printing them.
* [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16) (Backlog) covers the default-password CI lint. That lint scans only `.ts/.tsx/.js` under `services/` and `packages/`, so it cannot see a `.sh` banner. That's why nothing has flagged these lines.
* [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN credential. Its item 3 covers scripts that *read* a fallback, not scripts that *print* one.

## Suggested fix (your call)

1. Print the mechanism, not the value, as [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has) did for the admin line. For example: `Issuer: demo@secuura.io (password: DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD, or the published demo default; see CLAUDE.md)`.
2. Make `start-secuura.sh:603`'s login check read the password from the environment instead of a literal, so the script doesn't carry the value at all.
3. Extend the [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16) gate, or add a small `.sh` check, so a script that echoes a known seeded password fails the gate.

## Acceptance

* Neither banner prints a password value. A stack start's captured stdout contains no seeded password.
* A guard fails if a `.sh` under `Start_Up/` or `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` echoes one.

---

*Found 5 Oct 2026 while bringing up K slot 3 for platform-s* [PS-1003](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1003/verification-policies-leaves-a-deployment-wide-block-policy-which) *(*`up-slot.sh 3`*). No K code was changed. Related:* [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has)*,* [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation)*,* [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16)*,* [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)*.*

title: QUESTION: should ks860 WALK_ROOTS and ks879 DEV_ROOT walk systemTest/ (which 499 .py files would still escape)?
description:
## BLUF

A scope question, not a defect and not a merge blocker — filed so
[KS-1347](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1347)'s third acceptance box has a home, which that
box explicitly allows ("a decision is recorded … **or a separate ticket exists for it**").
**Neither** `ks860` **nor** `ks879` **walks** `systemTest/`, so that whole tree has no loopback-bind guard
and no raw-control-byte guard, and nothing structural would have caught the KS-1347 percent-encoding
class there either. Facts and costs are measured below. **No build, and no ruling on the behaviour**
**from me** — Wednesday ruled only that this is filed separately, not what the answer is.

Same class as [KS-1141](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1141) (are `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts:44`
`SCAN_DIRS` and `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:150` `SCAN_ROOTS` the intended scopes?),
**different sites** — that ticket covers those two guards and not these. Read in full before filing.
It also records the precedent cost: KS-886's earlier widening of `ks879` from
`services/`+`packages/` to the whole Dev tree **cost ≈0.8 s per walk and found 0 offenders**.

## What each guard walks today (read at source, develop `5d5aea41feca`)

| guard | root | mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks860-test-listeners-bind-loopback.test.ts` | `Dev/services` + `Dev/packages` | `:98` `const WALK_ROOTS = ['services', 'packages']`, joined to `DEV_ROOT` at `:472` and `:726` |
| `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks879-no-raw-control-bytes-repo-wide.test.ts` | all of `Blockchain/Dev` | `:98` `DEV_ROOT = findDevRoot(process.cwd())`, `:153` `sourceFiles(DEV_ROOT)` |

`systemTest/` is a **repo-root sibling of** `Blockchain/`, so it is outside both — including outside
`ks879`, whose name says "repo-wide" but whose root is `Blockchain/Dev`.

`ks879`'s filter: `SKIP_DIRS = {node_modules, dist, build, coverage, .turbo}`,
`EXTS = [.ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs, .cjs]` (`:117-118`).
`ks879` declares `WALK_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (`:159`); `ks860` **declares no walk timeout.**

## What walking `systemTest/` would ADD (tracked files, so reproducible)

|  | today | `systemTest/` would add | change |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ks860` — test files | 552 | **+248** | +45% |
| `ks879` — `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs` | 1567 | **+545** | +35% |

## What it would COST

Measured on this host by reproducing `ks879`'s own walk (same `SKIP_DIRS` and `EXTS`), twice:

```
ks879 today      (Blockchain/Dev):  1567 files walked in 50 ms / 28 ms
ks879 + systemTest             :  2112 files walked in 44 ms / 44 ms
systemTest alone               :   545 files walked in  8 ms / 13 ms
```

So the **directory walk** is not the cost — about +10 ms. The real cost is the per-file read for
control bytes, which scales with the +35%. For comparison, KS-886's widening to the Dev tree cost
≈0.8 s per walk (KS-1141).

⚠ **The cost interacts with a known fragility.** [KS-1155](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1155)
is open on exactly this: "packages/shared tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under
fleet load". A 35% larger walk makes that worse, and `ks860` has no declared timeout at all. Any
widening should be sequenced against KS-1155 rather than before it.

## ⚠ The fact that most changes the answer

`systemTest/` **holds 499 tracked** `.py` **files, which are outside BOTH guards'** `EXTS` **entirely.**
So extending the walk root would **not** give `systemTest/` raw-control-byte coverage — it would
cover the TypeScript/JavaScript half and leave the Python half (the Schemathesis harness) exactly as
uncovered as it is now. "Walk `systemTest/` too" and "`systemTest/` is guarded" are not the same
statement, and a ruling that assumed they were would buy less than it looks.

## What a ruling should say

Following KS-1141's shape, for each of the two guards: **(a) scope INTENDED** — add one sentence to
the docblock naming the excluded trees and why, so the next reader does not re-derive this; or
**(b) widen** — the builder first measures the red set on the wider tree (KS-886's precedent: 0
offenders) and sequences it against KS-1155, then files the change. And separately: whether the
Python half needs a guard of its own, or is out of scope by design.

## Board search before filing

`searchIssues` (fuzzy, 6 per term) by symbol: `WALK_ROOTS`, `ks860`, `ks879`,
`raw control bytes systemTest`, `loopback bind guard walk root`. Nearest hits read in full:
**KS-1141** (same class, two other guards — cited above), **KS-1155** (the walk-timeout cost,
cited), KS-1140 (Done — the ks879 🔴 cell walking the tree on its own), KS-1147 (Done — a ks860
boundary case), KS-807 (the control-byte guard cannot see a raw body — a different blind spot in the
same guard family), KS-492 and KS-1042 (systemTest coverage, but security-regression scope, not
structural guards). **None names the** `systemTest/` **walk-root question for ks860 or ks879.** Filed new.

title: systemTest: pin originate's unhandledRejection posture (split from KS-572) — waits on KS-1427's ruling
description:
## Summary

Split from [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) on 2026-10-06. [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) pins what [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) actually shipped:

* `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` on the api-gateway only, in compose and bicep;
* the real [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) guard, no longer a copy;
* the live malformed-body run with `RestartCount` unchanged;
* the gateway's boot line `unhandledRejection mode: survive`.

What [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) **can't** pin yet is originate. `services/originate/src/index.ts:72-77` registers its own listener that logs and doesn't exit, so originate survives rejections, yet the gateway comment cites it as fail-fast. [KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) asks Kamil which is intended.

## Waiting on

[KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) (Kamil, Backlog): survive or fail-fast for originate, and whether `setupGracefulShutdown` gets callers.

## Test (once ruled)

* **If survive:** assert originate declares it in config (`UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive`). Extend [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture)'s "no other service declares survive" config assertion to an explicit allow-list of gateway + originate.
* **If fail-fast:** a live leg triggers an unhandled rejection in originate (only if a black-box trigger exists; otherwise a container-level check of the boot-logged mode) and asserts the process exits and restarts with the trace logged.
* **If** `setupGracefulShutdown` **gets callers:** sample one non-gateway service's boot log for `unhandledRejection mode: exit`.
* Red against the current shape, green after. Appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report).

Refs: [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) (parent work) · [KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) (blocker) · [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) · [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) (Review G). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: systemTest: SSRF regression for POST /api/teams/webhook-config (split from KS-502 §3b) — waits on KS-784's validation order
description:
## Summary

This is [KS-502](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-502/systemtest-schemathesis-skipped-security-regressions-needing-a-proper) §3b, split out on 2026-10-06 so that [KS-502](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-502/systemtest-schemathesis-skipped-security-regressions-needing-a-proper) can close on the parts we can do now (§1 billing idempotency, §2 seed-demo gate, §3a). This part waits on Kamil.

`POST /api/teams/webhook-config` carries the [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto) B-1 SSRF guard on `webhookUrl`. But `requireM365` answers **503** before validation whenever `ENTRA_*` is unconfigured, which is the case on every developer stack and slot. So `tests/test_webhook_ssrf.py::TestWebhookSsrfResidual` can never reach the guard, and has been a documented skip since July (`test_webhook_ssrf.py:207` on `develop` `f556373b9`).

## Waiting on

[KS-784](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-784/post-apiteamswebhook-config-fails-the-schemathesis-pr-sweep-on-every) (Kamil, Backlog). The 2026-09-14 requirement and its 2026-10-06 follow-up ask whether `webhookUrl` will be validated **before** `requireM365`. Neither has an answer yet.

* **If option 1 (validate first):** this becomes a plain red→green regression on any slot. Internal, metadata and rebinding hosts → 400 regardless of `ENTRA_*`.
* **If option 2 (a local test mode):** the test enables that mode and makes the same assertions.
* **If neither:** recategorise the skip as out of scope (the [KS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-519/schemathesis-systemtest-register-non-passing-tests-coverage-gaps-and) category) with this ticket as the reason, instead of leaving a bare skip.

## Done looks like

The skip is removed. The test is shown red against the current ordering and green after [KS-784](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-784/post-apiteamswebhook-config-fails-the-schemathesis-pr-sweep-on-every) lands. It appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report), the [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) coverage row flips, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` plus the QA cheat-sheet are synced.

Refs: [KS-502](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-502/systemtest-schemathesis-skipped-security-regressions-needing-a-proper) (parent work) · [KS-784](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-784/post-apiteamswebhook-config-fails-the-schemathesis-pr-sweep-on-every) (blocker) · [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto) B-1 · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) (Review G). title: SECURITY (local test stack): akto-autoheal runs as root with /var/run/docker.sock RW — env-scoping is only as strong as who holds the socket
description:
**BLUF —** `akto-autoheal` **runs as uid=0 root with** `/var/run/docker.sock` **mounted read-write, which grants host-equivalent read of EVERY container's environment through the daemon API and therefore defeats environment-variable scoping as a security control — but it is confined to the local Akto test harness: it sits on network** `akto_default` **rather than the platform's** `dev_secuura-network`**, and it is defined only in** `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml`**, so it does not exist on demo or kintsugi.**

The bound is in that sentence deliberately. A reader who stops after the first clause should not walk away believing this is live on a VM, and a reader who stops after the second should not walk away believing it is nothing.

## What was measured

| probe | result |
| -- | -- |
| containers with a bind mount of `/var/run/docker.sock` | **1 —** `akto-autoheal` (`willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0`), mount **RW=true** |
| its user | `uid=0(root) gid=0(root)`, `Config.User` empty |
| tooling present inside it | `curl` **PRESENT**, `wget` **PRESENT** (no `docker` CLI, which is not a mitigation — the daemon API is HTTP over that socket) |
| its networks | `akto_default` — **not** `dev_secuura-network` |
| defining compose file | `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` only |
| occurrences of `autoheal` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` (the file the VMs run) | **0** |

**Controls, so the zeros discriminate:**

* The bind-mount scan enumerates and prints **all six** distinct bind sources across the 38 running containers (`docker/init`, `docker/init-platform`, `docker/seed`, one `secuura-api.yaml`, one `nginx-demo.conf`, `/var/run/docker.sock`) — so it can see bind mounts, and the absence of a repo-root or `.env` mount is a real null.
* The `0` for `autoheal` in the VM compose file is measured against a positive control in the same file: `originate` returns **1**. So the grep matches when the string is there.

## Why this matters beyond the container itself

**It is the general case of the specific control being shipped in KS-1041 Step 2.** That work scopes a gateway-vouch secret to exactly two of 34 containers by declaring it per-service, and verifies the scoping by probing container environments. **Any container with root + RW** `docker.sock` **can read those same environments through the daemon regardless of how narrowly they were declared** — so env-scoping is a control whose strength is bounded by who holds the socket, and nothing today records that dependency.

That is why this is filed separately rather than inside the KS-1041 PR: a finding about the estate's secret-handling as a class, buried in another ticket's PR description, is discoverable only by someone reading that PR, and it outlives the change that surfaced it.

## Explicitly NOT proposed

No fix, no privilege change, no compose edit. Changing a test stack's privileges was outside the commission this was found under and outside the current deploy grant. **Scoped and evidenced only — the remedy is a decision for whoever picks this up.**

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) while measuring the blast radius of the KS-1041 Step 2 vouch secret, at Wednesday's instruction to establish who can read it before building a control that depends on it. All readings taken read-only against the running local stack; nothing was changed.

Related: KS-1041 (the specific control this generalises).

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): verify-by-hash must not resolve to an arbitrary registration — anchored-ancestor + cross-tenant field disclosure (KS-584 class)
description:
## Status: parked — not actionable yet

**Blocked on** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (Kamil, Urgent). That ticket has to decide *what correct resolution means* before a regression can assert it — Stuart offered three candidate shapes (prefer a row carrying chain data · return the anchored ancestor · report ambiguity) and they produce three different assertions. Writing tests now would pin a behaviour nobody has chosen.

Filed so the systemTest leg is visible from [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) rather than forgotten when [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) lands. **No work until the platform decision is made.**

## Why it belongs in Review G

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) has two consequences from one root cause, and G already owns regression coverage for both classes:

**1. Anchored-ancestor selection.** `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves a content hash with `ORDER BY d.certified_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1` and no preference for a row carrying chain data (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`). The normal certify flow creates a *second* row with the same `content_hash` (the certification's `signed_document`), which wins the ordering and carries no `certification_metadata.blockchain`. So a document with three confirmed on-chain anchors verifies with `isAnchored: false`, `blockHeight: null` — reproduced live on UAT (`1.15412159T20251122.pdf`, `f4fd83a9…`, anchors at preview blocks 4547897 / 4547901 / 4547907).

This is the **anchor-honesty class** — the same shape as [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) and the [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) D rows. A document's on-chain proof exists and the platform reports it doesn't.

**2. Cross-tenant field disclosure.** `buildResponse` returns the selected row's `title`, `issuer` / `organization_name`, `documentId`, `status`, `certifiedAt` and the lineage chain. The fallback `crossTenantLookup` is also unscoped, also `LIMIT 1`. Verifying a document you legitimately hold can return **another tenant's filename and organisation name** — and the anonymous verify path has no caller identity, so it cannot scope.

This is the **A / BUG-ISOLATION-001 class** that [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) covered for documents and api-keys. [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) is Done, so there is no open ticket carrying it, and the verify family went public under [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) — the sweep reaches these operations today.

Note `platform_document_registry` is already `UNIQUE (content_hash, tenant_id)`. K models tenancy correctly here; verify just doesn't use it.

## Sketch — to be finalised once [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decides

Placement: cross-tenant assertions with the `@pytest.mark.isolation` siblings; anchor-resolution assertions in the anchoring-integrity Integration mode.

| # | Property | Assertion | Depends on |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Certify does not un-anchor | Upload → anchor → certify → verify. `isAnchored` must stay true and the txHash must still resolve. Assert **after** certification propagates, not before — the UAT reproduction only appears once the second row exists | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |
| 2 | Multiple registrations resolve deterministically | Two rows sharing a `content_hash` → verify must not return an arbitrary one. Exact assertion depends on which of the three shapes is chosen | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |
| 3 | Ambiguity is not hidden | If the chosen shape is "report ambiguity", assert the match count / flag is present and a relying party can see it | Only if that shape wins |
| 4 | Anonymous verify discloses no tenant-owned fields | Register a document under tenant A; verify the same bytes anonymously → response carries no `title`, `organization_name`, `issuer` or lineage belonging to A | **Independent of the** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) **decision** — this one could be written now if the disclosure half is ruled on separately |
| 5 | Cross-tenant fallback is scoped | A caller with a tenant does not silently receive another tenant's registration via `crossTenantLookup` | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |

Test 4 is the only row that does not wait on the resolution semantics — the disclosure question ("should an anonymous verify name an organisation at all?") is separable, and Stuart's framing is that it can honestly answer *registered / integrity intact / not revoked / anchored yes-no* without naming anyone.

## Out of scope

Everything platform-side — row selection, tenant scoping, and what an anonymous response may contain — is [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents)**, Kamil's**. This ticket only proves the outcome once chosen. Platform-S consumption ([PS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-546/verify-shows-a-permanent-for-certification-and-never-reports-anchoring) / [PS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-547/share-link-verify-re-derives-the-document-by-hash-so-a-duplicate)) is Stuart's and not tracked here.

## References

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (platform defect, Kamil, Urgent — the blocker) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) (Review G parent) · [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A) · [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) (the closed isolation ticket this class belonged to) · [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) (anchor honesty — sibling class) · [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) (verify family made public) · [KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful) (red→green rule) · [PS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-546/verify-shows-a-permanent-for-certification-and-never-reports-anchoring) / [PS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-547/share-link-verify-re-derives-the-document-by-hash-so-a-duplicate) (S-side consumers, merged).

Evidence is Stuart's UAT reproduction and Kamil's root-cause read on [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents). Not independently re-verified by me; nothing written.

title: systemTest: the pre-rotation key is dead after rotate:true (split from KS-568 row 4) — waits on KS-577 revoke-on-rotate
description:
## Summary

[KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) row 4 proves that read-back survives key rotation. Kam ruled on 2026-08-07 that rotation must also **revoke the prior key**. As shipped, `rotate: true` mints a new key and leaves the old one valid with identical scopes. So a row-4 test that checks only the new key passes while the compromised credential stays live.

This ticket is the fourth assertion, **the old key is dead after rotation**. It's split from [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) on 2026-10-06 so that [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) can close on what holds today: rows 1–3, row 4's read-back half, rows 5–8 (row 5 is unblocked by [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578/cross-tenant-api-key-revoke-misses-the-db-row-when-the-cache-is-cold), Deployed to UAT), and the two-tier key provisioning.

## Waiting on

[KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) (Kamil, **In Review** as of 2026-10-06): implement revoke-on-rotate and agree the cutover window. The cutover window decides the assertion's timing: immediately dead, or dead after N seconds.

## Test

* Anchor under an operational key → `rotate: true` → the **old** key gets an auth error on read and on write, and the write creates no row (no 2xx-with-no-effect).
* Run with a warm and a cold key cache, the [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578/cross-tenant-api-key-revoke-misses-the-db-row-when-the-cache-is-cold) lesson.
* Red on `develop` today, green once [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) merges. It could land early as `xfail(strict=True)` citing [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement), so it flips loudly. Peter's call once [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) is in review.
* Appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report).

## Also gated by [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement)

[KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks)'s conditional bulk re-key extension waits on [KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576/bulk-re-key-one-admin-authorised-rotate-across-a-named-set-of) (Todo, Kamil), which is blocked on [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) by ruling. It stays out of [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks), and out of this ticket, until [KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576/bulk-re-key-one-admin-authorised-rotate-across-a-named-set-of) exists in code.

Refs: [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) (parent work) · [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) (blocker) · [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578/cross-tenant-api-key-revoke-misses-the-db-row-when-the-cache-is-cold) · [KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576/bulk-re-key-one-admin-authorised-rotate-across-a-named-set-of) · [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583/dr-rehearsal-lose-a-key-re-key-read-back-survives-on-pre-loss-anchors) (DR rehearsal step 4, same property) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) (Review G). title: systemTest: owner-scoped cross-tenant /api/status test (split from KS-588 test 5) — waits on KS-692's bind-creator half
description:
## Summary

This is the genuine cross-tenant form of [KS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-588/systemtest-schemathesis-apistatus-authorization-revoked-session)'s test 5, split out on 2026-10-06 so that [KS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-588/systemtest-schemathesis-apistatus-authorization-revoked-session) can close on what's testable today (tests 0–4, 6–8, plus the interim posture).

Kam's 2026-09-16 ruling on [KS-692](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-692/security-apistatus-revokeunrevoke-has-no-tenant-ownership-check-an) was "Narrow now, bind-creator later". [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1320](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-692-restrict-vc-issuer-status-writes-to-the-platform-roles-c44be83300e1) implements the narrow half: status-list writes are limited to `STATUS_WRITE_ROLES = ['SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'super_admin']` (`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts`, `develop` `f556373b9`). A status list still lives in a process-local `Map` with no owning tenant. So "tenant A cannot touch tenant B's list, while tenant A can still manage its own" has nothing to assert against yet.

## What [KS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-588/systemtest-schemathesis-apistatus-authorization-revoked-session) keeps

The interim assertion: a tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` / `OWNER` gets 403 on create, allocate, revoke and unrevoke, citing [KS-692](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-692/security-apistatus-revokeunrevoke-has-no-tenant-ownership-check-an). [KS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-588/systemtest-schemathesis-apistatus-authorization-revoked-session) needs no new platform code for that.

## Waiting on

* [KS-692](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-692/security-apistatus-revokeunrevoke-has-no-tenant-ownership-check-an) (Kamil, In Progress): the bind-creator half, i.e. lists carrying an owner.
* **Kamil's answer** on [KS-692](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-692/security-apistatus-revokeunrevoke-has-no-tenant-ownership-check-an) (asked 2026-10-06): should this test land now as `xfail(strict=True)` citing [KS-692](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-692/security-apistatus-revokeunrevoke-has-no-tenant-ownership-check-an), or only once bind-creator ships?

## Test (once unblocked)

* Tenant A creates a list → tenant A can allocate, revoke and unrevoke on it.
* Tenant B gets 403 or 404 (the cloaking choice is Kamil's) on every write, and on any read the ruling says is scoped.
* Shown red by reverting the owner check locally, then green. Appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report).

## Related, not this ticket

[KS-1352](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1352/security-a-revoked-credential-still-verifies-as-valid-by-either-route) (Kamil, In Progress): no verify route wires a `statusListResolver`. A code read on 2026-10-06 found the resolver defined only in `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts`, with no service passing one. That bears on [KS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-588/systemtest-schemathesis-apistatus-authorization-revoked-session)'s test 0, which [KS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-588/systemtest-schemathesis-apistatus-authorization-revoked-session) answers itself.

title: api-gateway per-key rate limiter never fires: enforceClientRateLimit is mounted before authenticateToken sets req.user (a 2/60s key answered 201 x5)
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing, Major: the per-key rate limiter never fires in the assembled api-gateway.**

* `enforceClientRateLimit()` is mounted with `app.use` at `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:524`. That is before any route-level `authenticateToken`, which is what sets `req.user` (the first mount is at `:899`; proxy routes mount it later).
* At `:524`, `req.user` is therefore unset for every request, and the per-key ceiling (KS-164 / KS-170) is never applied.
* Measured: a key validated with `rateLimit: 2, rateLimitWindow: 60` answered **201 five times out of five** on `POST /api/documents`, with no 429 and no `X-RateLimit-Limit` header.

## Recommendation

Not built. Wednesday is taking this to Kam as an escalation. The fix is a mount-order decision: run the limiter after authentication on each authenticated route family, or have it resolve the principal itself. It touches every authenticated route, so it needs its own gate.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 QA gate on PR #1014 (KS-1176), finding F-2. Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014-616c766a5-tier1-r1/report.md`.
* **Measured at runtime on the real app:** base 403 x5 (the level check refused first), #1014 head and merged tree 201 x5; never 429.
* **Positive control:** the SAME `enforceClientRateLimit()` mounted after the SAME `authenticateToken(true)` on a bare express app answers 200, 200, 429, 429, 429 with `X-RateLimit-Limit: 2`, on every tree. So the limiter works; its mount position does not.
* **The class-wide claim is READ only:** no `authenticateToken` is mounted in `index.ts` before the limiter, so every route family is affected; only `POST /api/documents` was measured.
* **Effect:** connector-key traffic is governed only by the global per-IP limiter (`max` 300/min outside non-prod). The KS-164 acceptance ("a key at N/min lets N through and 429s the (N+1)th") does not hold in the assembled app.
* Line numbers re-read at develop `eb1051fd39fe3edab4e0b1d1967515b758d4ba3f`.
* **Related, archived (named, not related):** KS-164, which carried the per-key allowance onto `req.user`, and KS-170 (the Redis counter).

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches:

* `enforceClientRateLimit`: 2 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-164, KS-170; both archived).
* `rateLimit`: 24 / 24 (none about the mount order of the per-key limiter; nearest KS-947, a different limiter's gate cell).
* `dt-${Date.now()}`: 123 / 0.
* `document-types`: 121 / 14 (KS-1190, KS-1176, and archived catalogue / Akto tickets).
* `verificationLevel`: 25 / 21 (nearest KS-744, a missing claim, not a non-string one).
* `connector-token`: 91 / 1 (KS-695, an incidental mention).
* `connectorMeta`: 1 / 1 (KS-164, archived).

None covers this finding. Related: KS-1176.

title: Develop-wide advisory freeze: 10 new ids in follow-redirects, vite/launch-editor, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and hono block every push (legs 6 and 7)
description:
## BLUF

Ten advisories published after the audit baseline make the pre-push preflight refuse EVERY Secuura push on develop (leg 6, npm-audit, and leg 7, standalone-lock advisories).
