title: Fresh databases are FAIL-OPEN until the second boot — 039_rls_fail_closed does not apply on boot 1 (file stage runs before the CORE stage it depends on)
description:
## BLUF

**On a freshly provisioned database,** `users.tenant_isolation` **is FAIL-OPEN after the first boot — an unset tenant GUC sees ALL rows.** `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` does not apply on boot 1 because the file stage runs **before** the CORE stage that creates a table it depends on. Seven file migrations fail on boot 1; all seven succeed on boot 2.

⚠ **PRODUCTION IS NOT IMPLICATED by this mechanism.** A long-lived database already has the dependency tables, so `039` applies on the first boot after deploy. **The exposure is freshly provisioned databases: new environments, CI and local stacks, DR restores, and newly provisioned tenant DBs.**

## Provenance — this is the QA gate's measurement, not mine

Measured by the cross-project QA agent on 2026-09-09 against PR #928, on a real `postgres:15-alpine` driven by **the product's own** `runStartupMigrations()` via `tsx`, `MIGRATIONS_DIR` pointed at the repo `migrations/`, a fresh database per side. Report: `2026-09-09-s161-batch-six-prs/report.md` §2, with boot transcripts in its `evidence/` directory.

**I have NOT re-run it.** Filed because §2 of that report says it bears on the deploy hold and asks for it loudly. The numbers below are relayed; the mechanism is the gate's, and the pre-deploy check is the gate's own recommendation.

## The measurement

```
after boot 1:  USING ( current_setting('app.current_tenant_id',true) IS NULL
                       OR current_setting(...) = ''
                       OR tenant_id::text = current_setting(...) )      <-- unset GUC sees ALL rows

after boot 2:  USING ( current_setting(...) IS NOT NULL AND <> ''
                       AND tenant_id::text = current_setting(...) )
                     OR current_setting('app.tenant_scope_bypass',true) = 'platform_admin'
               + policy users_auth_lookup
```

`039` fails on boot 1 with `type "oauth_apps" does not exist` — the file stage runs before the CORE_MIGRATIONS stage that creates that table.

**Seven file migrations fail on boot 1 and all seven succeed on boot 2:** `006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047`. `048_ks754_widen_processed_by_to_text.sql` **applied cleanly on boot 1.**

## Why it matters beyond the fresh DB

**Both #928 and #929 assume** `039` **is in force.** #929's whole justification is that fail-closed RLS with an unresolved tenant GUC produces a 0-row UPDATE. On a database where `039` has not applied, that condition does not arise from that cause — **and cross-tenant rows are visible.**

The same assumption runs through **KS-1052** (the credential-lifecycle guards) and the KS-963 work.

## 🔴 Pre-deploy check — put this on any deploy that touches these services

On the **target** database, confirm **both**:

1. `048` is present in `_secuura_migrations`.
2. `pg_policy` for `users.tenant_isolation` shows the `IS NOT NULL AND <> ''` form — **not** the `IS NULL OR = ''` form.

⚠ `run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 when migrations fail**, so compose's own gate does not catch this. The check has to be made against the database, not inferred from a runner's exit code.

## Related, un-driven, and probably the more serious half

**QA F-928-3 (read from source, NOT measured):** the tenant loop calls `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` only — **it never calls** `applyFileMigrations`. If `039` exists only as a file, **tenant databases never receive the fail-closed flip at all**, on any boot. The gate never configured `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` and provisioned no tenant DB, so this is a code-path reading and not a measurement. **It should be measured before it is believed, and if true it is worse than the boot-1 window** — a permanent state rather than a transient one.

## Fix shapes (not a ruling)

1. **Order the stages by dependency** — run the CORE stage before the file stage, or make `039` tolerate the absent table and re-assert later.
2. **Make boot-1 failure visible where it counts:** related to **F-928-2** (migration failure is still log-only; `runStartupMigrations()` is `Promise<void>`, so no call site can branch on `failed`). That is a design decision with deploy consequences and is **Kam's**, tracked separately.
3. **Provisioning-time assertion** — a new environment is not "ready" until the `pg_policy` shape check above passes.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — the credential-lifecycle guards that assume `039` is in force.
* PR **#928** (KS-950) — surfaced this; its `INCOMPLETE — 7 FAILED` log line is the first thing in the system that says so out loud.
* PR **#929** (KS-943).

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's brief item 4. Numbers relayed from the QA gate and labelled as such.*

title: Gateway tenant resolution falls through to the caller's x-tenant-id when a token has no tenantId claim — make it unconditional and fail closed
description:
**Remediation, not a defect.** Filed off the KS-486 finding-3 investigation (2026-08-13), which **disproved** an exploitable cross-tenant path — see that ticket's disproof comment for the full evidence. Nothing is currently leaking. This is the defence-in-depth gap the disproof exposed.

## The gap

The gateway overwrites the caller's `x-tenant-id` from the verified JWT — but **conditionally**:

```js
// services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:387
} else {
  if (decoded.tenantId) req.headers['x-tenant-id'] = decoded.tenantId;
  ...
}
runWithTenantId((req.headers['x-tenant-id'] as string | undefined) || decoded.tenantId, next);
```

**If a token carries no** `tenantId` **claim, the caller's own header survives** and then seeds the RLS tenant context. Downstream, `services/originate/src/index.ts:220-227` adopts the same header, and `tenantGucContext()` turns it into the RLS GUC — so since KS-458 flipped RLS fail-closed, the header is not filtered *by* the isolation control, it is the *input to* it.

The equivalent api-key path is already written the right way and is worth copying:

```js
// auth.ts:311 — KS-458: the gateway is the trust boundary
runWithTenantId(meta.tenantId, next);   // verified credential, NEVER the inbound header
```

## Why it is safe today, and why that is not enough

The conditional never fires open **because of a constraint two services away**: `svc_api_keys.tenant_id` is `NOT NULL` (migration 018, KS-33), so every API key carries a tenant → every `/api/keys/validate` returns one → every connector token carries the claim. User tokens set it from the row. Verified live: 786 keys with 0 nulls, and forged-header requests returned 404 against a 200 control.

Three things make that a thin guarantee:

1. **Migration 018 documents its own down-path** — `ALTER TABLE svc_api_keys ALTER COLUMN tenant_id DROP NOT NULL;` is written into the file. If it is ever run, the header-trust path reopens silently, with no code change and nothing to notice it by.
2. `ConnectorTokenClaims.tenantId` **is already declared optional** (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:239`) and spread conditionally (`:263`). The type system permits exactly the token this conditional cannot handle safely; only the database prevents one existing.
3. `users.tenant_id` **is nullable** (`is_nullable: YES`) — currently 0 of 82 rows are null, but that is data, not a constraint. And `admin@secuura.com` (super_admin) demonstrably issues a token today with **no** `tenantId` **claim at all**, proving the no-claim token shape is not hypothetical. For that role cross-tenant selection is by design, so it is not a defect — but it shows the branch is reachable in production traffic.

## Proposed change

Make the tenant resolution unconditional and fail closed:

* If a verified token has no `tenantId` **and** the caller is not a role legitimately entitled to select one (the existing `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` + `x-tenant-override` branch), **reject** rather than falling through to the caller's header.
* Never let an inbound `x-tenant-id` reach `runWithTenantId` or a downstream service — mirror the api-key path, which already seeds strictly from the verified credential.
* Consider stripping inbound `x-tenant-id` at the edge outright, so downstream services cannot be reached with a caller-set value even in-cluster.

## Acceptance

* A token with no `tenantId` claim, from a non-super-admin caller, **cannot** cause any tenant scope to be adopted from a request header — proved with a red test (forged header, verify the denial, with a passing control so the denial is not a dead probe).
* The super-admin `x-tenant-override` path keeps working — regression-covered, since that is a real capability.
* One open question worth answering during the work: during the KS-486 disproof, `super_admin + x-tenant-id: <other tenant>` returned **404** where the code reading predicted 200. Something beyond the JWT overwrite also blocks it and I did not locate it. Whoever picks this up should find that mechanism — it may already be most of the fix, or it may be incidental and not load-bearing.

title: READ ONLY / unverified: the gateway's own Authorization-only calls to originate send no x-tenant-id — single-tenant originate may scope them to DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
description:
## BLUF

**READ ONLY, not driven by anyone.** api-gateway calls originate directly — outside `createProxyRoutes` — at several sites and sends only `Authorization`. With no `x-tenant-id`, originate's KS-458 block (`services/originate/src/index.ts:248-256`) sets `req.tenantId` to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` in single-tenant mode, so those calls **may** read or write in the default tenant rather than the caller's. Independent of PR #951 (unchanged by it). Raised by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, Open item b) and not measured.

## Recommendation

Measure before any fix: drive one site per shape (a read, a write) as a caller in a non-default tenant on a two-tenant local stack and compare which tenant's rows come back. **Unknown that could dissolve this:** whether originate's `authenticate()` sets the tenant from the forwarded JWT on these routes. If confirmed, route gateway→originate calls through one helper that forwards the verified tenant — the same helper #951's F5 residual needs for the vouch.

## Detail

Sites at `develop` `2d864ae92` (grep for the originate URL in `services/api-gateway/src`, headers read at each):

* `routes/proxy.ts:554-556` — `GET /api/signatories`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/proxy.ts:578-579` — `GET /api/third-party-verifiers`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/verification.ts:129-138` and `:167-176` — `GET /api/documents/:id`, headers `{ Authorization }` when present
* `routes/batch.ts:146`, `:194` — batch certify / verify via `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL`, `authorization` forwarded; `x-tenant-id` 0 mentions in the file
* `routes/platform.ts:249-251` — `POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants`, `Content-Type` + `Authorization`

Not in this ticket (different shape, tracked on PR #951's body as READ ONLY): `routes/verification.ts` `POST /api/documents` and the workflow-approve forward DO send `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`, but without the vouch, so #951 would strip them once its secret is provisioned.

**Board searched before filing:** exact `getReqTenantId` → 4 (KS-174, KS-22, KS-26, KS-48 — none about gateway direct calls), `tenantGucContext` → 6 (none), `KS-458` → 1 (itself); control `KS-468` → 1. Fuzzy `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, `x-tenant-id`, `signatories`, `third-party-verifiers`, `Authorization-only` → nearest KS-468 (Done — audited the 44 gateway proxy MOUNTS, not these direct calls) and KS-619 (Backlog — `middleware/auth.ts` conditional tenant overwrite).

Related: KS-1041 · KS-468 · KS-619 · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (Open b).

title: prism GET /api/credentials/:id returns any stored prism credential by id with no owner check (cluster-internal; not routed by the gateway)
description:
## BLUF

**prism has its own** `GET /api/credentials/:id` **that returns any stored prism credential by id, with no owner check.** It reads prism's own table (`svc_prism_credentials`), not vc-issuer's, and it is reachable only from inside the cluster: the gateway does not route `/api/credentials` to prism. KS-1116 bound vc-issuer's route of the same name; this one is untouched. Gate BH1 NOTE 6 on #1648 (census side-finding).

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`, `services/prism/src/index.ts`)

* `:690` `app.get('/api/credentials/:id', …)` → `dbGetCredential(req.params.id)` (`:231`): `SELECT * FROM svc_prism_credentials WHERE id = $1`. The handler returns the credential or 404. There is no read of `req.user`, and no owner or tenant condition.
* Siblings on the same table, not examined for this ticket: `GET /api/credentials/subject/:did` (`:707`), `POST /api/credentials/revoke` (`:814`).
* Reachability: the gateway proxies only `^/api/did` to prism (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:920`; control: the same search finds 6 vcIssuer mounts). `docker-compose.yml` has prism's host port commented out ("Was: - "6001:4001""). So a caller needs to be inside the cluster network, and must still pass prism's own bearer check on `/api`.

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 6, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `svc_prism_credentials`, `dbGetCredential`, `prism/src/index.ts:690`, `prism GET /api/credentials` → 0 each (control: a never-written token → 0; `generateAccessToken` → 2).

title: Connector erasure: three permanent failures present as retryable and nothing dead-letters; the unresolvable path records no deletion log (Peter F6/F9)
description:
**BLUF — on the connector erasure path three PERMANENT failure causes are answered as if they were retryable, and nothing dead-letters. Platform S retries without bound, so two of the three spin forever. Found by Peter reviewing #790 (F6), with F9 folded in as the same class.**

The whole design of `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` is built around never stranding a retry — it deliberately never 404s, because a non-terminal answer against an unbounded retry strands an Art. 17 obligation. The mirror-image case was left open.

### F6 — permanent failures wearing a retryable face

Peter's table, verified on the tree:

| cause | response | can a retry ever succeed? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| connector key with no tenant (`validateApiKey` defaults `tenantId: ''`, so the claim is omitted) | 403 | **no** |
| non-uuid `tenantId` claim → 22P02 | 500 | **no** |
| genuine step failure inside `executeErasureImpl` | 500 | yes |

The first two are configuration faults on the key. S cannot fix them by retrying and there is nothing to move the request into, so it spins.

### F9 — the unresolvable path records nothing

`executeErasureByExternalRef`'s unresolvable branch blanks provenance identity columns and returns, writing **no** `data_deletion_log` **row**; the never-seen branch logs nothing at all. So the one branch that most needs an audit trail — K erased something for a subject it holds no user row for — leaves no record that it ran.

### Why one ticket

Both are about what this path records when it does *not* take the happy route: F6 is the request that can never succeed and is never parked; F9 is the erasure that succeeds and is never recorded. A dead-letter design wants to answer both at once.

### Not fixed in #790

A dead-letter path is a design, not a line, and #790 was already carrying four Majors. Recorded here rather than folded in silently.

Found: Peter, review of PR #790, 2026-09-02 12:46Z (F6, F9). Verified 2026-09-02 (session 110) on `feature/ks-695-ask1-erasure-by-external-ref` at `941ea960a`.

title: Security: same-tenant read gaps on certifications and owner-less documents — GET /api/certifications/:id has NO ownership check at all, and an empty owner skips the documents.ts:1124 cloak (both pre-existing, measured by gate BX1)
description:
## BLUF

**Two pre-existing read gaps in** `services/originate`**, both measured on real Postgres 15 as** `secuura_app` **(NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS) by gate BX1 while gating PR #1659.** Facts only — **no fix is proposed here**, because the remedy is a design on an auth read path and is ruled before it is built.

1. `GET /api/certifications/:id` **has no owner, holder or org check at all.** A **human-issued** certification that the documents GET *does* cloak is served **200 to every same-tenant user of any organisation**.
2. **An empty owner skips the documents cloak.** `documentRepo.ts:176` derives `''` from `owner_user_id` NULL + `issuer_user_id` NULL, and `documents.ts:1124`'s conjunction is false on `''`, so the 404 cloak never runs. Affects **bare-connector documents** (on `develop` today) and, since `3cc46ae41fed`, **holder-less connector certifications**.

Neither was introduced by PR #1659. KS-1659's fold added a new **row type** to gap 2's existing class, not a new audience, and the gate's control proves it.

## ⚠ This falsifies KS-621's central premise for one row class

KS-621 is the tracking ticket for "document reads are scoped by tenant and owner, never by organization", and it states: *"**Nothing is leaking.** Cross-org document reads are denied today, and that was proved with a control... What actually denies the read is a **per-owner 404-cloak**."* **That cloak does not run when the owner is empty.** For owner-less rows the emergent cross-org protection KS-621 describes is therefore **absent, not merely unenforced**. A comment has been left on KS-621 pointing here.

## Measured audiences (gate BX1)

**a** = same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN`, same organisation · **a2** = same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN`, **another** organisation · **b** = another tenant · **c** = the issuing connector.

| row | tree | endpoint | a | a2 | b | c |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| connector certification, no holder | landing | `GET /api/documents/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |
| **bare-connector** `POST /api/documents` (owner NULL, issuer NULL) | **develop AND landing** | `GET /api/documents/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |
| human-issued certification, no holder (owner = issuer = a UUID) | both | `GET /api/documents/:id` | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 |
| **human-issued certification** | **develop AND landing** | `GET /api/certifications/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | — |
| connector certification, no holder | landing | `GET /api/certifications/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |

The owner-less 200 body carries `"owner":{"id":""}` plus title, data and contentHash. The human-certification row being 404 on the documents path is the **positive control**: the cloak works when the owner is non-empty, so these 200s are not "everything is readable".

**Audience for the owner-less class: the whole tenant, every organisation, all roles.** ⚠ **Kam's KS-1116 ruling — owner-less rows readable by the row tenant's administrators (**`ORG_ADMIN` **/** `SYSTEM_ADMIN` **with a tenant on the token) — is NARROWER than what ships today for both row types.**

**List endpoints are not affected:** `documents.ts:321` filters on `d.owner?.id === userId` and the certifications list filters on holder or issuer id. Only **c** saw the new id in a list.

## Where

* **Gap 1:** `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:956-1010` — calls `getCertification(id, tenantId)` and returns issuer, holder, data and blockchain with no access predicate.
* **Gap 2:** `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:176` → `id: row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`; `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1124` → `if (userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient)`.

## The remedy shapes BX1 costed — options, NOT a decision

1. **Fail the cloak closed at** `documents.ts:1124` (drop the `document.owner?.id &&` conjunct). One line, covers both row types. **Cost, measured: it strands the issuing connector.** A bare connector create writes **no** `create` **row in** `action_provenance` (0 rows against 12 documents), so `wasCreatedByConnector` never admits it, and per the KS-480 §6 comment at `:1126` Platform S drives the whole lifecycle through that id. Needs a companion — record a create row, or admit a connector whose organisation matches the row's. **Does nothing for gap 1.**
2. **Cloak an empty owner to admins plus the creating connector** — the KS-1116 ruling shape. Same edit plus a tenant-admin admit; same provenance dependency; does not cover gap 1.
3. **Set the owner at write time** from the connector's organisation or a tenant administrator. Reads unchanged, but it changes custody semantics (`anchorOverwriteGuard`), needs a write-path lookup, and does nothing for existing bare-connector rows.
4. **Refuse a holder-less connector certification** (400 `HOLDER_REQUIRED`). Smallest blast radius; returns to develop's "no row" with an honest error instead of 22P02-as-payload. A **client-visible contract change for Platform S**, and the bare-document class stays as it is.
5. **For gap 1: give** `GET /api/certifications/:id` **the same predicate** as `documents.ts:1124`. **Without it, options 1 and 2 do not close certification reads.**

**Plan against Kam's KS-1116 ruling**, which is the nearest precedent: a remedy matching that audience inherits his authority; a different audience is a new decision for him.

## Not measured

No gateway and no real JWT layer — BX1 mounted the routers directly with the repo's probe-user auth mock, so **any scope gating at api-gateway is unmeasured** and could narrow these audiences in production. Also not run: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, a `system_admin` or recipient reader, an `onBehalfOf` connector certification, the derived lineage row. The remedies were not built.

## Board search before filing

`owner_user_id` (control: 9 hits), "GET /api/certifications/:id ownership check", "certifications read no ownership check same tenant", "documents.ts cloak empty owner", "owner-less document readable by same tenant", "bare connector document no owner". **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0**; `owner_user_id` returned 9. Nearest neighbours: **KS-621** (the tracking ticket whose premise this corrects), **KS-1688** (the same class on `POST /api/documents/:id/version`, a different endpoint), KS-1603/KS-1652 (anchoring ownership), KS-1683/KS-1684 (vc-issuer reads). **None owns these two endpoints.**

Related KS-1659, KS-1116, KS-621.

title: auth: revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 with no throw when the session store is down, so the admin status change and the user-erasure subscriber silently revoke nothing (session.ts:317-318)
description:
## BLUF

`revokeAllUserSessions` **answers** `0` **and does NOT throw when the Redis session store is unreachable** (`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318`: `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;`). Two callers treat that `0` as "there was nothing to revoke" and carry on reporting success. The sessions then validate again when Redis recovers.

**The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere:** `createSession` at `:156` raises `'Redis is not available — cannot create session'`. The inconsistency is the defect.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling after gate BO1 on PR #1655, which measured this failure mode on the password-reset route. **The two password routes are fixed in that PR** by a route-local guard; these two callers are deliberately out of KS-1407's scope and are why this ticket exists.

## Recommendation

Either make the shared function fail closed (a strict variant, or a throw plus an explicit opt-out for callers that genuinely tolerate a no-op), or give each caller its own availability check. It is a **wider ruling than one ticket's scope** because it changes behaviour for every caller at once, which is exactly why PR #1655 did not take it.

## The enumeration (every product caller, measured)

| caller | file:line | what it does with the `0` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **user-erasure subscriber** | `services/auth/src/services/userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` | `const sessionsRevoked = await revokeAllUserSessions(userId);` — an **erased** subject's sessions stay live while the store is down. This is the data-protection path and the reason this is High. |
| **admin status change** | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838` | inside `if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser))` — the KS 796 path whose whole point is "cut the sessions this status cannot hold". With the flag false it cuts none and the status change still answers success. |
| password change / reset | `routes/users.ts`, `routes/auth.ts` | **FIXED in #1655** — both confirm the revocation is possible before the write and re-assert after it. |

Control for the enumeration: the same search shape finds `revokeSession` in **17 files**, so it is not blind.

## Why High rather than Medium

The erasure path is a data-protection obligation: an erasure that reports success while the subject's sessions remain usable is a compliance failure, not only a bug. The admin path is the KS 796 thesis — "this status cannot hold a credential" and "cut the sessions it already has" must not be able to disagree — and under this condition they disagree silently.

## Exposure, stated precisely

While the flag is false the old sessions are refused anyway, because `getSession` returns null. **The exposure is the resurrection after recovery, not the outage itself.** That is the gate's own framing of the equivalent reset case and it applies unchanged here.

## Not measured

I did not drive these two callers against a downed store myself; the mechanism is a source reading of `session.ts:317-318` plus the gate's measurement of the identical path on reset (probe B1: 200, token burned, 0 revoked, and the old session ACTIVE again after recovery). The inference is that the same `return 0` reaches these two callers; the probe for each is not run.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `userErasedSubscriber`, "admin status change revoke sessions redis unavailable", "revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 silently", "erased subject sessions survive". No open ticket covers this. **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0** hits and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned a hit, so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407.

title: [Decision] POST /api/certifications/:id/verify has no auth handler — leave it public, or gate it?
description:
**The ask, first:** @kamil.kreiser **— should** `POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` **stay public, or be moved behind auth?** Default if you say nothing: **leave it public**. Nothing changes in code either way until you rule. This is a **product decision recorded, not a defect actioned** (category 2).

## What is measured

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:556`) is mounted with **no authentication handler** — only `mockBodyParser`. A request carrying no `Authorization` header reaches the route handler and gets the handler's own answer.

**At the KS-815 head (recorded during the KS-800 round):** C10 → **200 headerless**, with C11 → **401** as the discriminating control.

**Re-measured live on the local stack today, 2026-09-05T20:02Z, at** `develop` `0b9346f31`**:**

| case | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| SUBJECT | `POST /api/certifications/550e8400-…/verify`, **no** `Authorization` | **404** with the handler's own body — `{"verified":false,…,"error":"Certification not found","checks":{"exists":false}}` |
| SUBJECT | same, `id=test-cert-1` | **404**, same shape |
| **CONTROL** | `POST /api/documents`, **no** `Authorization`, same client and shape | **401** |

**Why the 404 is the finding and not a refusal:** an auth-guarded route never reaches its handler headerless — it answers 401 before the handler runs, as `/api/documents` does from the same client in the same second. This route answers *from inside the handler* (`checks.exists` is the handler's own field), so the request got all the way through. The 404 is "that certification does not exist", not "you are not allowed to ask".

## What it does and does not expose

The handler is **read-only** — it calls `checkDocumentExists(id, authHeader)` and returns JSON. It writes nothing. It forwards whatever `Authorization` header it received, so a caller who *has* a token is still scoped downstream; a caller with none is not stopped at the door.

Since the F-03 pen-test fix it can no longer claim `anchored: true`: certifications without real on-chain confirmation return `verified: false` and `confidence: 'pending-onchain'`. So what an unauthenticated caller learns is **existence** plus issuance status for an id they already hold.

## The two readings, so the decision is a decision

* **Leave public (the default).** Verification is the product — a relying party checking a certification they were handed should not need a Secuura account. The route leaks existence for an id you must already possess, and writes nothing.
* **Put it behind auth.** Existence-oracle on guessable or enumerable ids, and it is the only verify-family route on the gateway with no handler; the asymmetry is itself a smell for anyone reading the mount list.

## If the answer is "leave public"

Close this ticket and it becomes the written record that the posture is deliberate — which is the thing that is missing today. A future guard sweep that flags this mount then has an answer to read.

---

title: Add an OAuth marker to sessions minted by the OAuth grants (so a future deploy-step denylist can be selective) — the current forward-only window is accepted (Kam 14:53)
description:
## BLUF

**Kam ruled 2026-09-14 14:53 AEST (via Wednesday, ADDENDUM 04:53:30Z): (B) marker-only — add the OAuth session marker now; the current forward-only launder window is ACCEPTED, no deploy-time cutoff.** This supersedes his 14:45 ruling `denylist-at-deploy` (ADDENDUM 04:46:19Z), which this ticket was first filed under (title then: "Deploy step: denylist every OAuth refresh jti minted before #983/#984 (the forward-only launder window)", High) — rescoped after the merge seat measured that the pre-fix jtis are not enumerable (below). Priority Medium: no longer a deploy blocker. **The build is the next auth lane's; the deploy stays Kam's.**

**The accepted window, stated:** a refresh token minted at the OAuth grant BEFORE #983 (M31 `b9f541e6b`) / #984 (M32 `2c3315f37`) landed carries neither `client_id` nor `authMethod`, so #986's guard (`routes/auth.ts:677`, M33 `9864379e5`) cannot recognise it and it still launders at `POST /api/auth/refresh` until it expires. **Expiry mechanism:** the refresh JWT's own `exp` — `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`, default `'7d'` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:44`, `env.example:107`) — so the window closes by itself at most 7 days after the deploy that carries M31–M33 (the last pre-fix mint is at that deploy). Population unmeasured (the AUTH4 gate, report §3.7). Accepted by Kam 14:53.

## What was measured (develop M34 `b42e260c9`, END tree `cf700ee32`, read verbs only, 2026-09-14 04:4x Z)

1. **The denylist exists and is jti-keyed:** `services/auth/src/services/refreshDenylist.ts:21` `refresh_denylist:${jti}` in Redis; `denylistRefreshJti(jti, ttlSeconds)` `:28` (`setex`; fail-loud `Refresh denylist requires Redis` `:34`); `isRefreshJtiDenylisted(jti)` `:46`. Readers `routes/auth.ts:693` and `routes/oauth.ts:1047`; writers `routes/auth.ts:718` (rotation) and `:762` (logout); 0 writers in `routes/oauth.ts` (= R-2 on KS-1150).
2. **A refresh token's jti is minted in memory and never persisted:** `jwt.ts:231` `jti: crypto.randomUUID()`; no `oauth_*` token table in `migrations/`; `refresh_tokens` (`001_initial-schema.sql`) is not written by the OAuth grants.
3. **No marker distinguishes an OAuth-minted session:** both OAuth grants call `createSession(user, req.ip, req.get('user-agent'), undefined, 'browser')` — the code grant at `routes/oauth.ts:965`, the refresh grant at `:1074`; the interactive logins pass `data.clientType ?? 'browser'` (`routes/auth.ts:284`, `:441`, `:590`) or `'browser'` (`:1247`, `wallet.ts:362`); `ClientType = 'browser' | 'native' | 'api'` (`services/session.ts:107`). The Redis `Session` (`sess:<id>`, `user_sessions:<userId>`) carries `clientType`, ip, user-agent, device, expiry, activity — nothing that says "minted by the OAuth grant", and no jti.
4. **Therefore a selective deploy-step denylist ("every pre-fix OAuth refresh jti, interactive untouched") had no enumerable target set** — the fact that turned 14:45 into 14:53.

## The work (one test pass proves it — Kam's 2026-09-07 rule)

* **Mark every session the OAuth grants create.** The builder's design; the two shapes the code already offers: (i) a new `ClientType` value (`'oauth'`) passed as `createSession`'s fifth argument at `routes/oauth.ts:965` and `:1074` — note the KS-43 cohort-aware eviction in `createSession` buckets by `clientType` (`session.ts:178–230`), so a new value needs its own eviction policy decided, not inherited by accident; or (ii) a dedicated field on `Session` (e.g. `mintedBy: 'oauth'` + the `client_id`), leaving `clientType` and the eviction cohorts untouched. Either way the marker is written at mint and readable on `getSession` / `getUserSessions` (`session.ts:256`, `:329`).
* **Make it queryable at deploy time:** a read that lists a user's OAuth-minted sessions (and, if a future cutoff is ever wanted, all of them — `user_sessions:<userId>` is per-user; a global enumeration needs a set of OAuth session ids or a SCAN, decided by the builder and stated).
* **Do NOT add a cutoff** — the window is accepted (14:53). The marker exists so that a FUTURE deploy-step denylist can be selective; it does nothing for tokens already in the wild, which is why the window is accepted rather than closed.
* **Test pass:** red-first at the parent (an OAuth-grant session carries no marker / `clientType 'browser'`) → green at head (the code grant's and the refresh grant's sessions carry the marker, read back through `getSession`); an interactive login's session carries no marker (control); the KS-43 eviction cohorts behave as decided for the new value (a cell per policy); `auth.integration` OAuth cells unchanged; the ks1151 / ks1150 / ks823 / ks835 suites unchanged.

## Search before filing (every KS issue incl. archived, 1,146 issues, title + description + comments, literal; `5_Project_History/2026-09-14_s225/item6/symbol_search.log`)

`denylistRefreshJti` → KS-1151 / KS-823 / KS-486 (archived), KS-485, KS-329 (PQ hybrid — other subject), **KS-756 (Backlog, live: "Wire up the opaque refresh token that** `createSession` **already mints" — a symbol neighbour, not this work; named, not related)**; `isRefreshJtiDenylisted` → KS-486 only; `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` → KS-1151 comments; `forward-only` → KS-1151 + KS-550 (unrelated); `denylist-at-deploy` → 0. No existing work item; KS-1156 §C carries the window as a record — this ticket is the work and links to it.

**Related:** KS-1150 (R-2: the OAuth refresh grant rotates/denylists nothing — the same denylist, the other route; open), KS-1156 (the AUTH4 records; §C the window). **Named, no relation (archived):** KS-1151 (#986, M33), KS-823 (#983, M31), KS-835 (#984, M32).

## Definition of done

The marker is on develop with the red-first / green / control cells above; `getSession` returns it; the KS-43 eviction policy for the new value is decided and tested; no cutoff added; the accepted window's end date (the M31–M33 deploy + `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`) written on this ticket by whoever deploys. KS-1156 §C and KS-1150 R-2 are not closed by this ticket.
