title: Document reads are scoped by tenant and owner, never by organization — cross-org protection is emergent, not enforced
description:
**TRACKING TICKET — deliberately NOT a fix spec.** Filed off the KS-486 finding-2 disposition (2026-08-13, `develop de4781ca2`). Its purpose is to give the gap a permanent home so it cannot be lost, **without committing to a security model that has not been decided.** The fix shape is blank on purpose — see *Why there is no acceptance criteria* below. Related: [KS-619](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-619) (the finding-3 defence-in-depth ticket, same pattern).

## BLUF

**Nothing is leaking.** Cross-org document reads are denied today, and that was proved with a control. But the denial does **not** come from an organization boundary — neither the repository layer nor the route layer contains an `organization` predicate anywhere on the document-read path. What actually denies the read is a **per-owner 404-cloak**, which covers cross-org access only as a side effect.

So the property "one organization cannot read another organization's documents" is currently **emergent, not enforced**. Whether that needs to change is a product question that is on Kam's desk, not a call this ticket makes.

## What each layer actually does (verified on `develop de4781ca2`, not inherited)

**Repository layer —** `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`**: tenant only.**
Every read/write predicate is `tenant_id` and nothing else (15 occurrences). The block comment at `:190-201` documents this as deliberate, citing KS-4 and the migration-011 RLS policy. `getDocument()` (`:203`) scopes both its `external_id` and its `uuid` lookup by `AND tenant_id = $::uuid`; the update path does the same (`:461-462`). **Zero** `organization_id` **predicates in the file.** `owner_user_id` appears only in INSERT column lists and one response mapping (`:146`, `:325`, `:350`, `:384`) — never in a WHERE.

**Route layer —** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`**: owner identity, not organization.**
The denial that produces the 404 is at `:888`:

```js
if (userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient) {
  // Return 404 (not 403) to avoid leaking document existence to non-owners
  return res.status(404).json(...);
}
```

There is no organization term in that condition. Grepping `organization` across the whole file returns 12 hits and **none of them is a read predicate** — they are `onBehalfOf` resolution (`:84`, `:335`), KS-597 metadata passthrough (`:355-359`, `:398-411`), and an `issuerOrgId` on a different (write) route (`:683`).

## The correction this makes to finding 2's framing

KS-486 finding 2 was dispositioned as *"the route layer treats org as a boundary and denies cross-org, while the repo does not"*. The first half is **imprecise, and the imprecision matters**: the route enforces **ownership**, which is a different rule that happens to also deny the cross-org case that was tested.

Two consequences that an org-boundary framing would hide:

1. **It is stricter than org in one direction** — two users in the *same* organization also get 404 on each other's documents unless one is an admin or the named recipient. Anyone reasoning "org-mates can see org documents" would be wrong about current behaviour.
2. **It is weaker than org in another** — the protection is attached to `owner.id`, so any condition that makes a caller the owner, an admin, or the recipient removes it entirely, and any code path reaching `documentRepo` *without* this route check has no org protection at all. That second case is the actual risk, and it is exactly what a repo-layer predicate would cover and a route-layer one would not.

## Why it is not live-exploitable today

From the finding-2 investigation, kept because it is the evidence that this is remediation and not an incident: `demo@` (org `fb1dfc8c`) fetching a tenant-A document owned by org `a0000000-…-0010` returns **404**, while **super_admin fetching the same document returns 200** and SQL confirms the row exists, is anchored, and has an owner. The 200 is the control — without it the 404 could have been a dead probe rather than a denial.

## The open product question — this is what the ticket is waiting on

> **Is** `organization` **a security boundary in Platform K that MUST hold, or a UX/labelling grouping where** `tenant` **is the real boundary?**

Routed to Kam (not Stuart — out sick per the 2026-08-12 ruling 12). It is a statement about what Platform S's tenancy model *is*, not something derivable from Platform K's code, because:

* Tenant provisioning does `CREATE DATABASE` per tenant, so **tenant** is a hard boundary and organizations live *inside* it, many-to-one — 79 orgs across 7 tenants locally, only 4 of which sit alone in their tenant.
* The S↔K contract puts **independent end-customers in one tenant**: `register-connector` is one platform-admin-authorised handshake per Platform S Organisation, and a provisioning key is constrained to its own tenant.

## Why there is no acceptance criteria

Writing "add repository-layer organization scoping, red-proved, with an admin-bypass control" as acceptance would **pre-decide the question above** — it only makes sense if the answer is "org is a boundary". If the answer is "org is a label", that same change is wrong: it would be a real behaviour change against a 94k-document default tenant, and it could break flows that legitimately cross orgs within one tenant (lineage, transfers, shares). So the fix shape stays blank until the ruling lands, and the severity below is provisional for the same reason.

The options analysis already exists and should not be re-derived — it is on [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486) in the finding-2 disposition comment (A: declare tenant the boundary + contract line with S · B: enforce org in the repo layer · C: formalise and regression-test the existing route control). The standing recommendation there is **C now, B as target, gated on the ruling** — C being the only option that is strictly positive under *either* answer, because it pins the control that is actually protecting us today with a test.

## Provisional severity

**Medium, provisionally.** Not live-exploitable, so not Urgent/High on today's evidence. If the ruling is "org IS a security boundary", this becomes a **Must** and should be re-rated upward when its fix ticket is written; if the ruling is "org is a label", it settles as documentation plus the route-level regression test and may drop.

## Open questions carried (not tidied away)

1. **The route-level control is not fully mapped.** The finding-2 work established that the denial exists, distinguishes admin from non-admin, and produces a real 404 — it did **not** trace every path that reaches `documentRepo` to confirm all of them carry the check. The risk is precisely a path that reaches the repo without it, so this is the gap most worth closing next, and it is worth doing regardless of how the product question is answered.
2. `super_admin` **+ a forged** `x-tenant-id` **returned 404 where the code reading predicted 200** — a defence that was not located. Also carried on KS-619. A hypothesis worth testing first, raised while re-reading the route on `de4781ca2`: `routes/documents.ts:846-848` computes `adminUsingOverride = userJwtTenant && userJwtTenant !== tenantId` and **skips the cross-tenant registry fallback** when it is true (the BUG-ISOLATION-001 fix, 2026-05-02). That would produce exactly this 404. **Untested — stated as a hypothesis, not a finding.**

## Verification method + stated limits

Every citation above was read on `develop de4781ca2` in this session rather than copied forward, and the negative claims are grep-backed (`organization_id` predicate count in `documentRepo.ts`: **0**). **Limit:** the same-org corollary in point 1 of *the correction* is derived from the code, **not live-proven** — a two-user same-org test was not run, because only one user in that organization owns documents locally and user emails are encrypted at rest, so selecting a second seeded login was not cheap. It should be proved live by whoever writes the eventual fix.

title: auth: the OAuth refresh_token grant never checks the ORIGIN SESSION, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a brand-new session (oauth.ts:988-1089)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/token` **with** `grant_type=refresh_token` **never reads** `decoded.sessionId`**, so revoking a user's sessions does not reach the OAuth refresh path.** A refresh token issued before a revocation still redeems, and mints a *brand-new* session. Measured by the gate on PR #1655 (KS-1407): after `revokeAllUserSessions` (n=1, `getSession` null), the same refresh token redeemed **200**, then **200 again**, leaving the account with **2 live sessions**.

Pre-existing; **outside** that PR's diff. Filed from gate BO1's note N1.

## Recommendation

Check the origin session on this grant (or introduce a per-user credential epoch) before minting. The oracle is already in the repo: the *interactive* `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:688-689`, so the two refresh paths disagree about whether a session must still exist. Wednesday or Kam should rule whether the fix rides with a KS-1407 follow-up or stands alone.

## Where

`services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:988-1089` — the `grant_type=refresh_token` branch. It verifies the JWT, checks the jti denylist, pins `user.status === 'ACTIVE'` at `:1067`, and mints a new session at `:1078`. It never consults the session named by the token it is redeeming.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe C1)

Real `session.ts`, real `refreshDenylist.ts`, real `jwt.ts`, on the ks823 scaffold:

1. created a session and minted an OAuth pair bound to public client `pub-1`;
2. ran `revokeAllUserSessions` — returned n=1, and `getSession` then returned null;
3. redeemed the same refresh token: **200**. Redeemed again: **200**. Account left with **2 live sessions**.

* **Control in the same case:** a client-mismatch redeem was refused **400**, so the harness can produce a refusal.
* **Not run:** an authorization code issued before a revocation and exchanged after it. The code grant also mints a fresh session (`:969`), so it is plausibly a smaller sibling — unmeasured, stated as such.

## Consequence

Anyone holding an OAuth grant obtained before a password change, a password reset, an admin status change or a user erasure keeps a renewable foothold. It is the direct counterexample to KS-1407's premise that no session may outlive the password that minted it.

## Scope — what this ticket is NOT

**KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of this branch** ("the refresh grant does not rotate / denylist the presented token", `:836`/`:860`) and is still OPEN — its 2026-09-14 comment records R-1 landing as `b42e260c9897` with "R-2 / R-3 stay OPEN". **This ticket is the other half: the missing ORIGIN-SESSION check.** They are overlapping-but-distinct, not duplicates — a perfectly rotating implementation would still mint a new session for an account whose sessions were all revoked, because nothing reads `decoded.sessionId`. Do not close either as a duplicate of the other.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `updateSessionActivity`, `rotateSessionRefreshToken`, `decoded.sessionId`, "oauth refresh token revoked session", "session revoked refresh token still redeems". Nearest neighbours KS-1150 (the rotation half, above), KS-756 (the opaque session refresh handle, a different mechanism), KS-1280 (a revoked session's Bearer forwarded by originate, a different service). **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated token that was never published returned **0** hits, and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1** — so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407, KS-1150.

title: auth: a request in flight resurrects a revoked session — updateSessionActivity and rotateSessionRefreshToken write back the stale isActive:true record with a fresh 24h TTL (session.ts:270-294)
description:
## BLUF

**A revocation can be undone by any request that was already in flight.** `updateSessionActivity` (`session.ts:270-279`) and `rotateSessionRefreshToken` (`:282-294`) both do a read-modify-write: `get` the session JSON, mutate, `setex` it back. If `revokeSession` lands between the `get` and the `setex`, the **stale** `isActive:true` **record is written back with a fresh 24-hour TTL** — and the session is live again.

Worse, it becomes **unrevokable**: the revocation already removed it from `user_sessions:<id>`, so a later `revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0** and cannot find it.

Pre-existing. Filed from gate BO1's note N2 on PR #1655.

## Recommendation

Either a **revoked tombstone** that `getSession` checks, or a **conditional write** (a Lua script or a WATCH/MULTI compare-and-set) so a write cannot resurrect a record revoked since it was read. The tombstone is probably cheaper and also fixes the orphaned-from-the-set half.

## Why it matters more than a normal race

`updateSessionActivity` runs on **every authenticated request** (`middleware/authenticate.ts:160`), so the window is open continuously under load rather than at a rare moment. An attacker hammering requests on the old token widens it deliberately. It affects **every** revocation path — logout, the admin status change, user erasure, and the new password change/reset.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe B3)

The interleave was forced deterministically:

* after the revocation (returned n=1, record inactive), the in-flight write left `getSession` returning the session **ACTIVE**;
* the session was already gone from `user_sessions:<id>`, so a second `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **0** and could not reach it.
* **Control B3c** — the same steps *without* the interleave: the session stayed revoked. So the probe measures the race, not a broken teardown.
* **Not run:** a timing measurement against real Redis. The probe drives the real `session.ts` against a fake that implements the session commands, so the *window's width* in production is unmeasured; its existence is not.

## Where

* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:270-279` `updateSessionActivity`
* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:282-294` `rotateSessionRefreshToken`
* called from `services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:160`

**Board search before filing:** `updateSessionActivity` returned **0** hits; `rotateSessionRefreshToken` returned 4, none about a resurrection race (KS-756 the opaque handle, KS-1687 m365 token persistence, KS-1150 the OAuth grant, KS-329 PQC); also searched "resurrect revoked session" and "session revoked refresh token still redeems". **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0**, `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1**.

Related KS-1407.

title: m365: no connection is bound to its organisation - any authenticated user can list every site's connectionId, then list and download another org's OneDrive files
description:
**BLUF:** In m365-integration, **nothing ties a Microsoft 365 connection to the organisation that owns it.** Any authenticated user, from any tenant, can do three things:

* list every registered SharePoint site **together with its** `connectionId` (`GET /api/sites`);
* use that id to list the files in **another organisation's OneDrive**, with that organisation's own access token (`GET /api/onedrive/files`);
* **download** one of those files into the synced-document store (`POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync`).

`POST /api/connections/init` takes the organisation from the **request body**, not from the caller's token. **Measured statically. Not driven live.** It only works where `ENTRA_*` is configured and a real connection exists. That is unmeasured for any deployed environment, and KS-693 shows a normal dev machine answers 503.

Found from gate AP1's note N5 on #1627 (KS-1671). Read by Seat R 55th at develop `a66cd6a4d1726794c816fd4fefec58c728d410e5` (`services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`).

## The chain

| step | route | what it does | org check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `GET /api/sites` (`:890-903`) | with no `connectionId` query, returns **every** entry of `memSites`; each `SharePointSite` carries `connectionId` (`:104-113`) | **none** |
| 2 | `GET /api/onedrive/files` (`:1082-1110`) | `memConnections.get(String(connectionId))` (`:1087`), then lists Graph `/me/drive/...` with `connection.accessToken` (`:1091-1093`) | **none** |
| 3 | `POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync` (`:1121`) | same lookup by id alone, then fetches the item's metadata **and** `/content` from Graph with that token | **none** |
| — | `GET /api/connections/:id` (`:722-743`) | returns `organizationId`, `tenantName`, `status` and `scopes` for any id | **none** |
| — | `POST /api/connections/init` (`:612-640`) | `organizationId` comes from `initConnectionSchema.parse(req.body)` (`z.string().uuid()`), not from the token | **none** |

`connectionId` is `conn_<randomUUID>` (`:616`), so it cannot be guessed. **Step 1 is what makes it enumerable**, as soon as any site has been registered on that connection.

## What I read to answer "does any middleware bind the connection to the caller's org?"

* **api-gateway** `routes/proxy.ts:949-957`: `/api/m365` and `/api/onedrive` are `authenticateToken(true)` followed by `proxy('m365', …)`. That checks identity only; nothing scopes by organisation.
* **m365**: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate({ publicOps: ['POST /outlook/verify-hash'] }))` (`:606`) authenticates. I did not read its internals, because m365 never compares anything it sets to a connection's org. `requireM365` (`:259`) is a configuration gate (503 when unconfigured).
* **Census across all 22** `app.<verb>('/api…')` **routes in the file:** **0** read the caller's organisation from `req.user` or headers, and **0** compare `organizationId`. The census is a regex. I then read the five routes above by hand.

## Also from AP1 N5 (same route)

`GET /api/onedrive/files` interpolates a raw `folderId` into the Graph path (`:1090`: `/me/drive/items/${folderId}/children`), with no type check and no encoding. The handler's `try` → `next` means this cannot crash the process. Path text is passed to [graph.microsoft.com](<http://graph.microsoft.com>) under the connection's token.

## Priority: High, and why

It is a **cross-organisation read of customer files**: list, then download, using another organisation's Microsoft token. It is open to any authenticated user, and the enumeration needs only one registered site. Wednesday's rule for this class is High.

**What would lower it, and is not measured:** whether any deployed environment has `ENTRA_*` configured with live connections. Where it is not configured, every one of these routes answers 503 (KS-693). **Checking that means reading a live box, which I have not done.** The connection store is also in-memory and reloaded from the database (`loadFromDb`), so whatever a deployment holds is reachable once it is configured.

## Fix direction (not built)

* Bind each connection to the **caller's** organisation, taken from the verified token, never from the body.
* Every lookup by `connectionId` (or site id) must refuse a caller from a different organisation, with a 404 rather than a 403 so it does not leak that the id exists.
* `GET /api/sites` must filter to the caller's organisation.

This needs a tier-1 gate, with cross-org cells that use two organisations.

## Searched before filing

Searched "onedrive files folderId", "m365 connectionId org tenant isolation", "m365 connection ownership", "onedrive connection cross tenant" and "memConnections". The negative control `zkqvplmxhwrt` returned 0.

* **KS-1670** mentions `memConnections` only for the unencoded success redirect.
* **KS-748** and **KS-619** are about API-key and gateway tenant resolution, not m365 connections.
* The PS-1075..1084 storage tickets are Platform S design.

No ticket owns this.

title: Every API key without a connector id is the same principal (connector:api-key) within its tenant, so under KS-1116 those keys read each other's presentations and credentials
description:
## BLUF

**Every API key minted without a connector id authenticates as the SAME principal within its tenant,** `connector:api-key`**. Under KS-1116's "owner = the principal that created it", those keys therefore read each other's presentations and credentials.** Cross-tenant stays separated, because a key's tenant is fixed at mint. The shape predates KS-1116; KS-1116 is what makes the principal an ownership boundary. Gate BH1 NOTE 3 on #1648.

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`)

* `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:289`, in `generateConnectorToken` (the sk\_-key → JWT exchange the gateway performs for an `x-api-key` caller): `userId: \`connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}\`\`. A key with no connector id gets the literal fallback.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:445-448`: `tenant_id` is written on every key INSERT and is immutable per key ("a key minted for tenant A never moves to tenant B"). So the collapse is per tenant, not global.
* vc-issuer (since #1648) stamps `created_by_user_id` from `req.user.userId` and compares it on read (`services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts`). It has no special case for the fallback: `git grep "api-key"` over `services/vc-issuer/src` → 0 files.
* **Precedent in the codebase:** originate already refuses the fallback principal for erase-connector — `isFallbackConnectorId` (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:114`, used at `:146` and `:295`; KS-695, wording residue in KS-1579). There the fallback is treated as "not a distinct principal". vc-issuer treats it as one.
* Related, not this defect: KS-869 (merged) made a key's connector id persist across restarts. It does not change what a key minted WITHOUT one becomes.

## Open question

What should "the principal that created it" mean for a key with no connector id: the key itself (its key id), the fallback shared by every such key in the tenant (today), or not a principal at all (originate's erase-connector stance)?

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 3, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `connector:api-key` → KS-869, KS-1579; `generateConnectorToken` → KS-1584, KS-1409, KS-1152; none owns the shared-principal question.

title: vc-issuer: after a revoke, the credential's creator can be refused GET /api/credentials/:id on the memory fallback - revoke() stores the row with no owner entry (fails closed)
description:
## BLUF

**After** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, the credential's own creator can be refused** `GET /api/credentials/:id` **(404) whenever vc-issuer then falls back to memory.** `revoke()` writes the row into the in-memory store with no owner entry, so the KS-1116 bound reads it as owner-less. This fails CLOSED: a foreign caller is refused too, so the cost is availability, never a leak. Gate BH1 NOTE 2 on #1648.

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`, `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`)

* `revoke()` (`:288`) reads the row with `getById(id)` (`:292`) — from the database when it is available — and then calls `memoryStore.set(credential.id, revokedCredential)` (`:306`). It writes **no** `memoryOwners` entry.
* `getRecordById()` takes the owner from `memoryOwners.get(id) ?? OWNERLESS` on the memory path. So for any row this process did not itself `store()` or boot-load — one created on another replica, or after this process booted — and then revoked here, the memory copy is OWNERLESS.
* `mayRead()` refuses an OWNERLESS row under the interim reading (`ownerlessRowReadable()` returns false). With the database unavailable, or the SELECT throwing, the creator gets the unknown-id 404. Gate BH1 measured exactly that: its Q1 cell, "Alice 404".
* The foreign-caller half is pinned by cell Q1 in `ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts` (test-only follow-up to #1648). The creator's 404 is deliberately NOT asserted there, so that this ticket's fix does not have to edit a cell.

## Shape of a fix (not decided)

`revoke()` carries the owner it read — `getRecordById` instead of `getById`, writing `memoryOwners` alongside `memoryStore` — and a cell pins that the creator still reads her revoked credential on the memory path.

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 2, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `memoryOwners`, `revoke() puts`, `Map-miss` → 0; `credentialRepo.revoke` → KS-1352 only, which is revoked-credential verification, a different defect.

title: KS-962 seed-idempotence suite skips all 27 cells on hosts without Postgres binaries — would an opt-in Docker runner help it run anywhere?
description:
## Summary

No rush at all on this one, Kamil. The [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) seed-idempotence suite (`ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh`) skips all 27 of its cells on any machine without Postgres binaries, and it does so honestly and loudly, exactly as designed. The only gap is that on such hosts the guard never runs. An opt-in Docker runner might let it run anywhere, but it's your suite, so whichever approach you'd prefer is the one to go with. Happy to help build or test it.

+++ Details and options

**Observed 2026-09-28** during the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) preflight: `SKIP — no PostgreSQL binaries (initdb pg_ctl postgres psql) found; … 0/27 cells run`. Shell suites 59 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (of 60).

**What the suite needs** (read from the file): the Postgres binaries (via `KS949_PG_BIN`, then the Homebrew / Debian paths); Node ≥18, tsx and a built `packages/shared`; and auth's path includes the native `argon2`, so a macOS `node_modules` can't simply be mounted into Linux.

**One possible shape:** an opt-in container runner (Postgres 15 + Node, repo mounted read-only, `node_modules` in a named volume), off by default (e.g. `KS949_PG_DOCKER=1`). The suite already searches `/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin`, so it would need no change itself.

**Other options, equally welcome:** connect to an already-running Postgres instead of `initdb`; reuse the stack's own `postgres` container; or document `brew install postgresql@15` as a prerequisite. (Not suggested: wrapping `pg_ctl` into a container, because Postgres's 0700 data-dir check is fragile across Docker Desktop's bind mounts.)

No defect was found; this is a coverage gap on Postgres-less hosts. Related: [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) · [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9).

+++

title: Security: the synthetic wallet email buckets on walletAddress.slice(0,8) — degenerate for every addr_test1…/stake… address, so a colliding wallet takes the create branch and gets an object the account gate cannot reach
description:
Filed from the KS-796 QA pass (PASS 1 @ `1e4b6fbbe`), finding **Q5**. Severity set from the **code reading**, not from a row count — see the census section, which is the reason this is not filed Low.

## The defect

`services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts:171` builds a synthetic account email as:

```ts
email: `${walletAddress.slice(0, 8)}...@wallet.local`,
```

**Eight characters is a degenerate bucket for the address formats this platform actually uses.** Every Cardano preview-testnet address begins `addr_test1…`, so `slice(0, 8)` is the constant `addr_tes` for **all of them**. Every stake address begins `stake…`. Mainnet `addr1…` addresses give roughly 32k buckets, which is not a lot either.

So two different wallets routinely produce the **same** synthetic email. If `createUser`'s `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` behaves as written, the colliding wallet takes the **create** branch on every authentication and receives a fabricated `ACTIVE` / no-MFA user object — **an object the account gate added by KS-796 cannot reach, because it was never loaded from the row the gate would have checked.** That is a gate bypass reachable by address format alone.

## The census — recorded as UNMEASURABLE, deliberately

The gate asked for a live bucket-collision count to set severity. **I could not obtain one, and the first count I got was an artefact I nearly reported as a finding.**

**Attempt 1 (WRONG):** `users` where `email LIKE '%@wallet.local'` → **0**. That reads as a clean "no collisions".
**The control killed it:** `email LIKE '%@%'` → **also 0**. Not one row in `users` contains an `@`. `users.email` **holds** `d1:`**-encrypted values (25 of 25 rows)** — a plaintext `LIKE` against an encrypted column **cannot match anything**. The zero measured the instrument, not the data.

**Attempt 2 (correct instrument):** `users.wallet_address` is plain `varchar`, so the bucket is computable without touching the encrypted column.

|  | local | demo |
| -- | -- | -- |
| users with a non-empty `wallet_address` | **0** | **0** |
| `wallet_registrations` rows | **0** | **0** |
| colliding 8-char buckets (>1) | 0 | 0 |
| **control:** total `users` | **25** | **30** |

**This is zero POPULATION, not zero collisions.** No wallet user exists in either environment, so the census cannot distinguish *collisions do not occur* from *no wallet has ever been used here*. It supports neither a High nor a Low, and it is recorded here as what it is rather than converted into a number.

**The severity therefore rests on the address format**, which is not contingent on the table being empty: the day a second `addr_test1…` wallet authenticates, it collides with the first by construction.

## Fix shape

1. Stop deriving identity from a truncated address. Use the **full** address (or a hash of it) as the synthetic local-part, so the mapping is injective.
2. Verify `createUser`'s `ON CONFLICT` path actually updates rather than fabricating — the QA finding says "if it behaves as written", and that half is **unverified by me**.
3. A test with two distinct addresses sharing an 8-char prefix, asserting they resolve to **two** accounts — red-proofed against the current truncation.

## Not to be confused with

This is about **identity derivation**, not the account gate itself. KS-796 (merged, `a14b83b6d`) added the gate correctly; this ticket is about an object that never reaches it.

Refs: KS-796, `wallet.ts:171`.

title: Follow-up to the pull request 1539 gate: the admin-scope route's status guard does not fold case (m1), plus test gaps m2 and n1-n5
description:
## BLUF

The pull request 1539 Opus delta gate left a follow-up set of seven items. **One of them is a reachable defect on an authorisation route**; the rest are a test gap, two cosmetics, a coverage gap and one documented acceptance. They are grouped here because they are one logical path through `services/security/src/index.ts` and its three suites.

**m1 is the defect: the admin-organisation-scope route's liveness guard does not fold the case of** `users.status`**, so a live ADMIN gets 404.**

## m1 — DEFECT (reachable)

`services/security/src/index.ts:1629` (measured at develop `026c2d1614065c79fc8d96007ac0d80f19fb9363`):

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE id = $1::uuid AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND upper(role) = $3 AND status = 'active' LIMIT 1
```

`$3` is bound to the literal `'ADMIN'` (`:1630`), so the **role** is folded with `upper(role)` and the **status** is compared raw.

The repo stores this column in either case **on purpose**. `migrations/046_users_status_vocabulary.sql` constrains it with `lower(status) NOT IN ('active','pending','suspended','deactivated','invited','inactive','deleted')` (`:34`, `:41`) and states the intent at `:47`:

> Case is folded rather than forbidden: mapDbStatus already accepts either case,

So a user row holding `ACTIVE` or `Active` satisfies the CHECK constraint and **fails this guard**. `PUT /api/security/admin-scopes/:userId` then answers **404 "No ADMIN with that id in that tenant"** for a user that is present, is an ADMIN, and is live. Only a platform role can call the route, so the impact is an operator being unable to grant a scope, not an escalation.

The gate's stated fix: compare `lower(status) = 'active'`.

**This is the second case-folding defect found in this route in one day**, so the whole route was swept rather than this one site patched. **The sweep returns a negative result: m1 is the only remaining unfolded comparison.** Per site:

| Site | Comparison | Folds? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:1601` | `UUID_TEXT = z.string().uuid().transform(toLowerCase)`, applied to both `userId` and `tenantId` before any query | yes |
| `:1629` | `upper(role) = 'ADMIN'` | yes |
| `:1629` | `status = 'active'` | **NO — m1** |
| `:1638`, `:1690`, `:1693`, `:1741` | `::uuid` comparisons; uuid equality is case-insensitive by type, and the ids arrive lower-cased | yes |
| `:1641-1642` | the `known` Set compares `id::text` (Postgres renders uuid lower-case) against `UUID_TEXT` output | yes |
| `:1688` | `hashtext($1), hashtext($2)` — `hashtext` is case-sensitive, but both inputs arrive lower-cased via `UUID_TEXT`, so it folds end to end | yes, end to end |
| `:1766` | `k.keyHash === keyHash` — hex from one function | not a case question |
| `:1812` | `apiKey.isActive === false` | boolean |

## m2 — TEST GAP (no product defect)

`src/__tests__/ks1570b-concurrent-replace-is-not-a-union.integration.test.ts:100-102` and the 15 cells of `ks1570b-admin-scope-route` pin only the **final set**, not the audit chain. The gate reports that mutants **R2** (the advisory lock moved after the previous-set SELECT) and **R4** (the lock keyed on the raw un-lower-cased ids) **survive every author cell**, and are killed only by the gate's own F1 ×2, F5, F7 and F8.

The gate's stated addition: assert `aud.map(a => [a.before, a.after])` equals `[[[],[A1]],[[A1],[A2]],[[A2],[A3]]]`, plus optionally the F1 upper-versus-lower concurrent shape.

## n1 — COSMETIC

A doubled semicolon at both refactored sites: `const infra = isInfrastructureDbError(saveErr);;` at `:1398` and `:1568`. Exactly two occurrences in the file.

## n2 — COVERAGE GAP, not a behaviour change

The gate's note reads "add 53300 and 57P01 to KS-888's INFRA table (pre-existing, now visible)". Two measured corrections to how that should be read:

1. **The classifier already matches them.** `isInfrastructureDbError` (`:1134-1138`) tests `/^(08|53|57)|^(ECONNREFUSED|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|EHOSTUNREACH|ENETUNREACH|EPIPE)$/` against `String(err.code)` — a SQLSTATE **class-prefix** test. Measured directly, with controls: `53300` true, `57P01` true, `08006` true, `53100` true, `57014` true; controls `23505` false and `42501` false. So there is no behaviour to change and adding the codes as literals would be redundant.
2. **"KS-888's INFRA table" is a test fixture**, not the classifier: `src/__tests__/ks888-failed-mint-save-issues-no-key.test.ts:95`, three rows today (`08006`, `ECONNREFUSED`, a pool timeout with no code), driven through three `it.each` blocks (A2 mint, R1 revoke, V1 validate control).

So n2 is pure coverage: adding `53300` and `57P01` takes the fixture to five rows and yields six new cells, which are **green the moment they are written**. They are coverage, not a red-proof.

## n3 — DOCUMENTED, accepted

The status is read once at `:1628-1631`, before the lock at `:1688` and outside the transaction. The gate's F10 held a PUT inside its transaction and marked the target `deleted` meanwhile: the held PUT still committed **200 with its row written**, and the next PUT answered 404. The window is one transaction long and only a platform operator can act inside it. Accepted as documented; purging rows on demotion or deletion is KS-1592.

## n4 — COSMETIC

Rename the adopted cell's refusal message.

## n5 — BODY TEXT ONLY

Rephrase the "true for CONCURRENT calls only since…" line in the pull request 1539 body and correct its cell count.

## Not examined

The KS-1549 rotate lock at `:387` (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1), hashtext($2))` on a key row's tenant and a connector id) was **not** examined: no ticket, exposure unmeasured, and its inputs are database-canonical rather than caller-supplied.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title and description, because Linear's `searchIssues` is fuzzy and cannot be a membership test.

**The first negative control was VOID, and the reason is worth recording:** the token `zzqqxx-no-such-thing` returned **1** hit rather than 0, because that exact token had been written into **KS-1594's own description** as the documentation of an earlier dedupe. A control token written into the corpus it controls stops being a control.

Re-run with a fresh nonce: `qq262205d02f9fzz` → **0**, positive control `adminConfig` → **17**. Both fire.

Results with the working controls: `follow-up (pull request 1539` → 0 · `doubled semicolon` → 0 · `audit chain` → 0 · `INFRA table` → 0 · `lower(status)` → 0. The bare term `1539` returns KS-1592, KS-1591, KS-1545, KS-1543 and KS-1540 — none of which is this set. **Related:** KS-1570 (the route this follows up), KS-1591 and KS-1592 (filed from the same gate as separate findings).

Filed by Seat V 8th from the pull request 1539 delta gate's verdict.

title: Security: PUT /api/settings/notifications writes the same key namespace as platform-settings — a non-admin whose userId is "platform-settings" replaces the platform-wide settings
description:
## BLUF

**A caller whose** `userId` **is** `platform-settings` **can replace the platform-wide** `platform-settings` **record through the per-user notification-settings endpoint, bypassing** `requireAdmin` **and KS-1230's validation.** Measured with a test token. **Production refuses test tokens. Whether kintsugi or demo accept them is UNMEASURED.**

## Recommendation

Give per-user notification settings their own key space (for example `notif:user:<userId>`), or refuse reserved ids at that writer. Regression cell: a role-`user` principal whose `sub` is `platform-settings` PUTs `/api/settings/notifications`, and `platform-settings` is untouched.

## Detail

* **Two writers, one namespace.** Both write through `setNotificationSettings(key, data)` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:680`), which stores `notif:<key>`:
  * `PUT /api/admin/settings` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1123`, `requireAdmin`) writes `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', merged)` (`:1141`);
  * `PUT /api/settings/notifications` (`:1478`, `authenticateToken(true)`, no role gate) writes `setNotificationSettings(userId, body)` (`:1489`).
* **Measured by the #1045 batch gate** (`evidence/probe1045d.out`). The setup: the real `authenticateToken` and `parseTestToken`, with `configureAuth({enableTestTokens:true})`.
  * A role-`user` test token with `sub: "platform-settings"` PUT `/api/settings/notifications`. It got **200, and** `platform-settings` **was replaced** (with a malformed allow-list, or with an object container).
  * The same principal gets **403** at the admin door.
  * Control: `sub: "someone-else"` writes its own key, and platform-settings is untouched.
  * Control: `NODE_ENV=production` gives **401** (test tokens refused, `auth.ts:118-126`).
  * develop = head (pre-existing).
* **What it breaks:** the connector allow-list that KS-1204 and KS-1230 enforce can be replaced by anyone who can hold that `userId`. It can fail open, or lock every connector out. The rest of the platform settings are overwritten with it.
* **Severity (the gate):** Major where test tokens are enabled (dev/test with `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`; the compose default is false). Minor otherwise.
  * In production the attack needs a real JWT whose `userId` is `platform-settings`. That is READ only; nothing was measured.
  * Whether kintsugi or demo run with test tokens enabled is **UNMEASURED**. KS-623 records that the auth service's test-token guard fails OPEN on an unset `NODE_ENV`.
* Line references are at develop `52df64f84`.
* Found by the batch gate `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-batch1042-1045-tier1-r1/report.md` (finding N45-2), on the #1045 / KS-1230 sibling-writer census.
* Refs KS-1230. Related: KS-1231 (the `integrations` container fails open), KS-1256 (the allow-list fails open on a Redis close), KS-623 (the test-token env guard).

title: m365 OAuth callback: one unauthenticated GET with ?error[toString]=x kills the service - Express 4 allowPrototypes makes String() throw in an async handler
description:
**BLUF:** One unauthenticated `GET` can stop the m365-integration service. Express 4 parses query strings with `allowPrototypes: true`, so `?error[toString]=x` arrives as an **object whose** `toString` **is a string**. `String()` on that object throws `TypeError`. The throw happens inside an `async` handler, and m365 registers no `process.on` handler, so it becomes an unhandled rejection and **the process exits**. Develop has this today; it predates KS-1641 and #1622.

Found by gate AN1 (note N1), reviewing #1622. Filed by Seat R 55th, who reproduced the mechanism. Line numbers are at develop `bc3e2e2460fff5e961cd26b70da3ab0050fccbcc` (`m365-integration/src/index.ts` blob `829a72c9722b`).

## The three inputs

| request | value that arrives | where it throws |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/callback?error[toString]=x` | `error = { toString: 'x' }` | `:474` (`String(value)` inside `capCodePoints`), reached from the `:511` log |
| `GET /api/callback?error=a&error_description[toString]=x` | `error_description = { toString: 'x' }` | `:474`, reached from the `:512` log |
| `GET /api/callback?code=x&state[toString]=y` | `state = { toString: 'y' }` | `:521` `const connectionId = String(state)` |

Before #1622, the same three inputs threw at `:465` and `:472`. #1622 moved where the throw happens. It neither introduced the crash nor made it worse.

## Measured

* **On the real process (gate AN1):** `tsx src/index.ts`, Node v24.7.0, Express 4.22.3, qs 6.16.0. Each case ran on a fresh process, on develop AND on #1622's landing tree. Every time: the socket dropped, `/health` was refused, and the child exited with **code 1**.
* **Controls that did NOT crash (AN1):** `error_description[valueOf]=x`, `[a][b]=c`, `[]=p&[]=q`, `error=a&error=b` and `state[]=a&state[]=b` all answered 302 and the process lived.
* **Mechanism re-checked by me**, against the repo's own `node_modules`:
  * `express/lib/utils.js:290` sets `allowPrototypes: true`.
  * `qs.parse` with that option, then `String()`, **throws** `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` **on all three inputs**.
  * On the controls it returns `"[object Object]"` (`[valueOf]`) or `"a,b"` (arrays).

## Reachable without logging in

`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:936-939` mounts `/api/m365/callback` **with no** `authenticateToken` ("M365 callback must bypass auth"). It is proxied by path rewrite, which forwards the query string. **That is a static reading.** Neither AN1 nor I measured it through the gateway or against the deployed image.

## Beside it (gate AN1 N5)

`:564`, inside the callback's `catch`, calls `encodeURIComponent(err?.message || …)` with no guard. A lone surrogate in MSAL's error text would throw there unhandled, the same way. Reaching it needs a server-issued `state`, and the bug is older than #1622. The same field's reflection *decision* is tracked in KS-1641 / KS-1670.

## Census: does any other service do this? (read-only, static)

I looked for every `String(…)` or template-literal coercion of a `req.query` value inside a route handler, across `services/` and `packages/`, at develop `115797747cb6`. That snapshot is byte-identical to `bc3e2e2460ff` for everything except the two files #1622 changed.

* **9 sites. Only 2 escape as an unhandled rejection, and both are this route** (m365 `:465` and `:472` at that snapshot).
* **auth** `/social/:provider/callback` **(**`routes/auth.ts:1015-1016`**)** applies `String()` to `req.query.error` and `error_description`, also unauthenticated. **But it sits inside the handler's** `try` **(**`:968`**)**, so the throw goes to `next(error)` and the client gets an error response, not a dead process. Checked by hand.
* **api-gateway** `notifications.ts:126-127` runs in a **synchronous** handler behind a 401 check. Express 4 catches a sync throw. Checked by hand.
* **m365** `:482` **and** `:1016` are inside `try` blocks.
* **Services that register** `process.on('unhandledRejection')`**:** `packages/shared` (1 file), api-gateway (2), originate (1). **m365: 0.**
* **The census does NOT prove:**
  * It covers direct `String(x)` / `${x}` only. A method call on a query value (`.toLowerCase()` and the like, which throws on an array or object too) was searched **only in the direct** `req.query.x.method()` **form, and found 0**. That search's control matched a planted line. Calls made through a variable were not followed.
  * "Inside a try" is a brace-counting heuristic. I confirmed the two sites that mattered by hand.

## Fix (Wednesday's ruling)

Accept each query value this route reads **only when** `typeof === 'string'`. An array or object answers the same error redirect a missing value would. **Out of scope:** a process-wide `unhandledRejection` safety net. That is a design call, and KS-1427 owns the posture. For context, Express 5 (KS-775) forwards a rejected handler promise to the error middleware, which would turn this crash into a 500.

Every fix needs a cell per input that answers a bounded 302 **and** leaves the process alive (`/health` 200 afterwards), plus a plain-string control.

## Neighbours read before filing

The search's negative control (`zqwvxkplmhrt`) returned 0.

* **KS-1219:** an array-valued `scope` at OAuth `/authorize` answers **500**. Same input class, a different service, no crash.
* **KS-1427:** the shipped `unhandledRejection` posture. That is the safety net, not this route.
* **KS-1242:** an async middleware with no catch. Same escape mechanism, a different site.
* **KS-775:** the express 4 → 5 decision.
* **KS-763:** qs advisories.

None covers this site.

title: auth: 8 of 13 non-test updateUser callers discard the result (sweep that KS-1050 left open)
description:
## BLUF

KS-1050 fixed one discarding caller (`PATCH /me`) and said the rest were not swept. Swept now by reading `develop` `65d7722f8`: `services/auth` has **13 non-test callers** of `updateUser` / `updateUserPlatformScope` (the ticket said 24; others have since moved to `updateUserOrThrow`), and **8 discard the result**. `updateUser` answers `null` when its UPDATE matched no row or its read-back found nothing, so each can acknowledge a write that did not land.

## Recommendation

Convert the ones that acknowledge a security-relevant write to `updateUserOrThrow`, one ticket per test pass if split. Priority order: `auth.ts:255`, then the social-id link writes.

## Detail (line numbers at `65d7722f8`; they drift)

* `routes/users.ts:1293`, MFA auto-approve: **in flight as KS-1194 part 2** (own branch and PR).
* `routes/auth.ts:255`, claiming an invited stub on registration (`status`, `passwordHash`, names, `role: OWNER`): a 0-row update answers registration success over an inactive stub.
* `routes/auth.ts:1239` and `:1313`, the social-id link writes. `BACKLOG.md` already records that `userRepo.updateUser` silently drops every social-id write (the `fieldMap` has no social-id columns), so these discard a result that is always a no-op.
* `routes/auth.ts:1243` and `:1317`, the `SOCIAL` level raise after a social login.
* `routes/auth.ts:539` (password rehash, inside a try/catch and documented non-fatal) and `:587` (`lastLoginAt`): best-effort, low impact.
* **Checked and fine:** `routes/mfa.ts:239` tests the result and logs; `routes/users.ts:800` answers 404 on null; `routes/wallet.ts:488` and `:543` assign the result.

Provenance: read-only sweep by Seat V 3rd on 2026-10-12, reported on KS-1050; filed on Wednesday's instruction (Backlog, unassigned). Related: KS-1050, KS-1052, KS-1194, KS-943.

title: KS-1556 follow-up (#1529 round-2 gate m1): four rotate-chain guards have no behavioural cell (M10 owner-only cleanup, M3b retire exactly the returned ids, M7 grace memory expiry, M1 tenant-scoped key), plus ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS parses '10s' as 10 ms
description:
## BLUF

**Four guards in the KS-1556 rotate chain and its post-COMMIT apply are not pinned by any behavioural cell.** The code is correct today; a refactor could regress the chain's stated purpose **silently**. Test gap only — no product defect measured, and no credential-validity outcome depends on any of these (every validate on the DB path decides on the stored row). Found by the round-2 Opus delta gate on PR #1529 as its Minor **m1** (verdict sha256/16 `b662a71501b66490`, at head `d19b7a708e5b`). Facts only; no build.

## The four guards (lines at `d19b7a708e5b`, `services/security/src/index.ts`)

| mutant | guard | survives | consequence (by reading) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **M10** | `:302` `if (rotateChains.get(key) === mine) rotateChains.delete(key);` — only the OWNER of a chain entry removes it | all 26 author cells, the chain unit file and the gate's 19 cells | rotate A runs, B is queued; A finishes and deletes **B's** entry; a rotate C arriving while B runs finds no predecessor, takes a pooled client and parks on the advisory lock. That is the pool pressure the chain exists to prevent (KS-757): the gate's CH6 shows an unrelated validate waiting 1.6 s with 2 clients free, and a 503 once `connectionTimeoutMillis` (5 s) passes. Memory ordering is unaffected. **Availability.** |
| **M3b** | `:377` `for (const id of retiredIds ?? [])` — memory retires **exactly the ids the database RETURNED** | everything | if a concurrent non-rotate mint of the same connector commits after the retire's snapshot, the mutant retires that key in memory while the DB keeps it active; validate's "revoked if either says so" then **refuses a valid key** in this process. Fail-closed. **Availability.** |
| **M7** | `:379` `retireInMemory(current, grace)` — the **grace** path's post-COMMIT memory expiry | every author cell (killed only by the gate's A6) | memory keeps no expiry the DB committed; cosmetic on the DB path, because validate re-reads the stored row. |
| **M1** | the chain key is `${tenantId}:${connectorId}` — two tenants with the same connector id are independent | caught **only** by the window cell's literal `chains.has(\`${TENANT}:${c}\`)\` string — an implementation assertion | behaviour pinned only by the gate's CH5. |

## The cells the gate suggests (owner's call)

1. **Chain:** A in flight and B queued; after A finishes, issue C and assert C **waits for B**, with **0** service backends on `wait_event = 'advisory'` (kills M10).
2. **Pool pressure** like the gate's CH6.
3. **Grace 60:** after a 201, assert the prior key's memory entry **carries the expiry** (kills M7).
4. **Two tenants, one connector id:** behaviourally independent, like CH5 (pins M1 without reading the key string).
5. For M3b: a concurrent non-rotate mint landing after the retire's snapshot keeps its key active in memory.

## Folded in: o6 (cosmetic hardening, same function)

`:279-281` `rotateChainWaitMs()` uses `Number.parseInt(process.env.ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS)`, so `ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS=10s` **parses as 10 ms** — effectively no chain, and the CH6 pool pressure returns. A unit-suffixed value should be refused or parsed, not silently truncated.

## Related

KS-1556 (the PR this follows up), KS-1549 (the parent), KS-757 (the pool trap the chain prevents).

title: m365: connections probably never persist or reload - svc_m365_connections is fail-closed RLS, read as secuura_app with no tenant GUC, and the save error is swallowed
description:
**BLUF:** m365-integration probably **never saves a Microsoft 365 connection to the database, and never reloads one**, and it does so without any visible error. Its table is under fail-closed row-level security. The service reads and writes it as a role without bypass, and never sets the tenant setting the policy checks. Every save fails and is swallowed as a single warning, and every reload returns nothing. So a connection lives only in the memory of the process that created it, and is lost on restart.

**The policy also matches on** `tenant_id`**, which for this table holds the Microsoft (Entra) directory id, not the Secuura tenant.** So even a correctly set tenant would never match a row.

Found while measuring KS-1673. **This ticket rests on reading the source plus two measured flags. Nothing was driven.** By Wednesday's ruling, nothing more was measured on any box for it.

## Facts

| fact | where |
| -- | -- |
| `svc_m365_connections` is in the consolidated tenant-policy table set | `migrations/038_rls_consolidate_policy.sql:42` |
| 038 creates `tenant_isolation`, `USING` / `WITH CHECK` on `tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)` (fail-open when unset) | `038:84-93` |
| 039 re-declares it **fail-closed** on the 038 table set (an unset setting admits nothing) | `migrations/039_rls_fail_closed.sql:2-8` |
| **Measured on both kintsugi and demo** (flags only): RLS enabled = t, forced = t, 1 policy | read-only count pass, 2026-10-19 |
| **Measured on both boxes:** m365's database role is `secuura_app`, `rolsuper` = f, `rolbypassrls` = f | same pass |
| m365 never sets the tenant setting: **0** hits for `app.current_tenant_id`, `set_config`, `tenant_scope_bypass` or `withTenant` in `services/m365-integration/src/` | develop `390cc0a317c9` |
| `dbSaveConnection` catches every error and logs one warn (`'DB save connection failed'`) | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:189` |
| `svc_m365_connections.tenant_id` holds the **Entra directory id**, not the Secuura tenant UUID | repo `BACKLOG.md` (an existing entry), and the connection's `tenantId` field |
| `svc_m365_connections` has **0 rows** on both boxes | same pass. Consistent with "never saves", but also consistent with nobody having connected, so it **does not prove it** |

**Compare:** `svc_teams_webhooks` has row-level security **disabled**, with 0 policies (measured on both boxes). The two m365 tables are inconsistent with each other. The Teams side has the cross-organisation exposure tracked in KS-1673.

## Not measured

* Whether an INSERT as `secuura_app` with no setting is actually refused on these boxes. This is a static reading of 039's intent; the flags are measured.
* The service log's count of `'DB save connection failed'` lines. I measured nothing more on the boxes, by ruling.

## Why it matters

* **Correctness:** M365 connections cannot survive a restart.
* **Interaction with KS-1673:** the connections that matter are the in-memory ones, so binding in-memory connections to an organisation is the whole fix there. A future fix to this ticket must keep that binding when rows start reloading. The `organization_id` column is already written and read.

## Searched before filing

"svc_m365_connections RLS", "m365 loadFromDb connections reload", "svc_teams_webhooks row level security", "secuura_app m365 FORCE". The negative control `qzxwvkplmrty` returned 0. KS-1673, KS-1670, KS-693, KS-1335 and KS-934 were read; none owns this.

title: GET /api/platform/audit-log drops the platform half invisibly: HTTP 200, audit_logs rows only, no marker and no log line
description:
## BLUF

When the platform half of `GET /api/platform/audit-log` cannot be read, the route answers **HTTP 200 with the audit_logs rows only and that source's own** `total`, with **no marker in the body, no header, and no log line**. Neither the caller nor an operator can tell a log that has no platform entries from one whose platform half was dropped. That is the existing behaviour of a failed first window; PR 1522 (KS-1512) makes it **reachable by more routes** (a later window that fails, and the new overall budget being spent on a slow-yet-answering upstream), so the invisibility matters more after it merges. Named by Wednesday (2026-10-12) as a separate ticket rather than part of PR 1522.

## Recommendation

P3, two separable steps, the second needing a ruling. (1) **Log it:** a warn line from the `catch` naming the cause (a timeout, an HTTP failure, a window that was not a list, the budget spent), the route and how many windows had been read, never the rows. Test first with a captured logger: a failing stub produces exactly one line, a healthy read none. KS-1510 and KS-1539 are the precedent and the sibling. (2) **Decide whether the caller should see it:** an in-band signal (a response field or header) is a **contract change** to a route that is in the published spec, so it needs Kam's ruling, a spec change and a gate of its own; it is not a bug fix.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`, the `catch` whose comment reads `Tenant-provisioning down or slow — degrade gracefully and serve only audit_logs.` (read at develop `425ad3e00ae4`; the same comment-only `catch` guards the audit_logs query below it).
* **MEASURED (at PR 1522's stub, not a deployment):** cells F, H, L, M and K2 in `ks1512-platform-audit-log-pages-the-upstream-past-its-200-clamp.test.ts` assert the degraded response exactly: status 200, the audit_logs ids only, that source's total. There is no field to assert beyond that, which is the finding.
* **NOT MEASURED:** how often a deployment degrades, or whether the admin UI shows anything; nothing was run against a live stack.
* **Why now:** before PR 1522 a deep page was silently cut at 200 platform rows; after it, a slow upstream can silently drop the whole platform half. Both are invisible; the second is a more visible hole in the data.
* **Related:** KS-1512 (the windowed read and its deadline), KS-1539 (neither allow-list catch logs the thrown error: the same shape in another route), KS-1510 (the precedent for logging a thrown error on a platform route).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles AND descriptions in team KS, archived included: `degraded page` 0, `serve only audit_logs` 0, `no marker` 3 (KS-1157, KS-837, KS-569; none about this route), `platform half` 2 (KS-1544, the tie-break ticket, and an unrelated Done ticket), `degrades gracefully` 1 (KS-789, about the git hook). The same instrument returns KS-1544 for the phrase `platform half`, so it can see ticket text. No existing ticket covers it.

title: auth: no provider identity is ever stored - createUser and updateUser both drop social-id fields, so /social/link answers linked:true over nothing
description:
**BLUF:** The auth service never stores a provider identity (Google, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft personal). All three code paths that try to save one drop it silently, while the code that reads it back works. So no account can ever be found by the social account linked to it. `POST /social/link` answers `linked: true` with nothing saved, and its "already linked to another user" check can never fire. **Nothing is exposed today**, because an identity that is never stored authenticates nobody. **But the fix is security-sensitive.** The code warns that once ids persist, a risk that is latent today becomes live.

Measured by Seat R 55th at develop `4a065fb7535080190c407237f948d0af3538f2dd`. Line numbers come from a byte-identical copy of `services/auth` at `115797747cb6`. #1626 changed `routes/auth.ts` by +2/-2 at `:257` only, so they still hold.

## The three write sites, all dropped

| site | path | what happens |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `routes/auth.ts:1180` | social sign-in, **new user** | sets `newUser[`${provider}Id`] = profile.providerId` and passes it to `createUser`, whose INSERT names **no** social-id column |
| `routes/auth.ts:1249` | social sign-in, **existing account matched by email**, after the KS-795 gate | `updateUser(user.id, { [socialIdField]: providerId })`, and `updateUser` issues **no statement** for that field |
| `routes/auth.ts:1323` | `POST /social/link` (authenticated) | same `updateUser` call, then answers `{ success: true, linked: true }` |

**Why both writers drop it:**

* `updateUser`'s `fieldMap` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:801-824`) has 20 keys and **none** for a social id. A key that is not in the map is skipped, so a call carrying only a social id issues zero statements and returns the unchanged row. Control: the same read finds `walletAddress` once.
* `createUser` (`:668`): the 60 lines from its declaration mention **no** `google_id`, `apple_id`, `github_id`, `linkedin_id`, `facebook_id` or `microsoft_personal_id`.

## The columns and the reader exist

* `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:534-539` adds `google_id`, `apple_id`, `github_id` and `microsoft_personal_id`.
* `userRepo.getUserBySocialId` (`:618`) reads them through the `SECURITY DEFINER` function `auth_find_user_by_social($1, $2)`.
* It is called at `routes/auth.ts:1039` (sign-in) and `:1317` (`/social/link`). It can only ever return null for an identity this app linked.

## What follows from that

* Every social sign-in resolves its account **by email**. A provider account whose email differs from the platform account can never sign in to it, even after a "successful" link.
* `/social/link`'s conflict check at `:1318` ("This social account is already linked to another user") cannot fire. So two users can each "link" the same provider account and both get `linked: true`.
* `/social/link` also raises `verificationLevel` to `SOCIAL` at `:1327` on the strength of a link that was never stored.

## ⚠ The fix is the dangerous part, and the code says so

`routes/auth.ts:1233-1240`, verbatim in substance: the link write's danger *"is LATENT rather than current: today* `updateUser` *has no social-id fields in its fieldMap, so the write is silently dropped. The moment that persistence defect is repaired, a pre-gate link write would attach an ATTACKER's provider identity to a SUSPENDED victim's account … That is why this reordering lands BEFORE the persistence fix, not after it."*

The KS-795 F-4 comment at `:1044-1050` also notes that the email-key rules start to matter *"the day the social-id persistence defect is fixed and this lookup starts finding rows"*.

So the fix must:

* keep every link write **after** the gate;
* re-check the `:1318` conflict path, which becomes live;
* decide what happens to accounts that were "linked" while nothing persisted (there are none in the database to migrate, by construction).

It should go through a tier-1 gate.

## Priority: Medium, and why

* **Not High:** nothing exploitable is live. The defect fails closed, and normal sign-in works through the email branch.
* **Not Low:**
  * A user-facing success answer is false: `linked: true` with nothing saved.
  * A verification level is raised over it.
  * The repair re-opens the KS-795 class unless it is done deliberately.

## Where it is already written down

* The repo's `BACKLOG.md` entry: "`userRepo.updateUser` silently drops EVERY social-id write — the account-linking it performs never reaches the database". It was widened on 2026-09-05 to say that `createUser` drops it too. That entry is the source; this ticket is its Linear home, because no Linear ticket owned it.
* The code comments at `routes/auth.ts:1233-1240` and `:1298-1301`.
* **KS-1460**, the discarding-`updateUser` sweep. Gate AO1's census on #1626 noted that at `:1249` and `:1323` `updateUserOrThrow` **would not catch** this, because no write is issued at all. See KS-1460's comment `73f91c88-be30-4865-92a7-98cc7a146017`.

Searched before filing:

* Phrases: "social id link updateUser drops", "socialIdField fieldMap", "social/link linked true", "verificationLevel SOCIAL unconfirmed".
* Negative control: `qvzkxmplorft` returned 0.
* The only hits were KS-1460 (the sweep, which cannot fix this) and KS-1617 (social sign-in diagnostics).

title: renovate.json at the repo root: does Renovate for the systemTest pins conflict with the 2026-07-04 ruling "Dependabot, not Renovate" (KS-352 / KS-353)?
description:
## Found while

Aligning the docs with the rulings in the Linear tickets ([KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or)).

## What is there

`renovate.json` is tracked at the repo root. It was last changed 2026-10-07 for [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) and [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) ("Renovate sees the k6 pin"). It extends `config:recommended`, ignores `Blockchain/Dev/**`, runs before 6am on Monday, groups the observability stack images and the k6 runtime, and patches systemTest npm updates.

## The ruling it may conflict with

[KS-352](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-352/start-secuurash-rebuild-triage-npm-audit-vulnerabilities-across) and [KS-353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-353/start-secuurash-rebuild-clear-npm-dependency-deprecation-warnings) (2026-07-04): "Dependabot, not Renovate". The repo docs and `.github/dependabot.yml` follow that ruling; the docs do not mention Renovate at all.

## Question for Kamil

1. Is Renovate allowed for the **systemTest** pins (everything outside `Blockchain/Dev/**`), with Dependabot kept for the platform, or should `renovate.json` go?
2. Whichever you choose, the docs should say it. I will write the answer into the docs under this ticket's number and the date.

## Related

[KS-1446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1446/renovate-cannot-bump-base-image-watchsh-excluded-bases-blockchaindev) already asks whether Renovate may bump `base-image-watch.sh` (it is under `ignorePaths`) and says it needs Kamil's agreement; the answer to question 1 decides it.

## Not in scope

No change to `renovate.json` is proposed here. The docs-only PR for [KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or) leaves this file alone.

title: getPlatformAdmin swallows an infrastructure failure to null — platform-admin login reads "platform DB down" as "not an admin" and answers InvalidCredentialsError (the class KS-963 removed)
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` `getPlatformAdmin` (`:1714-1741` at develop after #970) catches every error from the platform-database lookup, logs `Platform admin lookup failed (platform DB may not be configured)` and **returns** `null` (`:1739-1741`). Its caller, `routes/auth.ts:345` `const platformAdmin = await userRepo.getPlatformAdmin(data.email);`, reads `null` as "not a platform admin" and falls through to the regular-user gate, which answers `InvalidCredentialsError` — the KS-253 shape ("a DB failure reported as no such user") on the highest-privilege door. This is exactly the class KS-963 / PR #970 removed from the five `getUserByIdPreAuth` callers, on a branch **outside KS-963's include** (Kam's scope named `getUserById` → widened to `getUserByIdPreAuth`). Named by the tier-1 gate as F-6 under "hunt the class"; needs its own ruling before a build.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks963-970-ae274f7cb-tier1-r1/report.md` — §9 HUNT THE CLASS (F-6 and the 15-catch census), WHAT WAS NOT TESTED item 3 (the branch was not exercised: `getPlatformAdmin` answered `null` because `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` was unset in the harness — which is itself the swallow at work).

## What is and is not established

* **READ ONLY (source at** `ae274f7cb`**):** the catch, its message, the `return null`, the caller at `auth.ts:345`, the fall-through to the regular-user gate (`auth.ts:344-482` is the platform-admin branch).
* **Catch census at head, brace-matched (the gate's):** 15 `catch` blocks in `userRepo.ts` — `return null` at `decryptPlatformAdminMfaSecret :206`, `getOrganizationTenant :541` (documented "treating as not found"), `getPlatformAdmin :1739` (this ticket); `return undefined` at `decryptPiiCol :109`, `decryptMfaSecret :186`; `return ''` at `decryptEmail :158`; void swallows at `seedDemoUsersInner :1658`, `reencryptMfaSecretIfLegacy :1708`, `reencryptPlatformAdminMfaSecretIfLegacy :1776`; rethrows at `getUserById :394`, `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash :430`, `getUserByIdPreAuth :496`, `getUserByEmail :578`, `getUserBySocialId :611`, `emailExists :638`.

The "platform DB may not be configured" comment suggests the swallow is deliberate for single-DB deployments — the ruling has to say whether "not configured" and "configured but down" are the same case.
