title: Security/correctness: three verification-store reads swallow EVERY DB error with a bare `catch { }` and answer from an in-memory map — a DB outage reads as 'no such request'
description:
## BLUF

**Three functions backing the verification-upgrade surface swallow EVERY database error with a bare** `catch { /* fall through */ }` **and then answer from an in-memory map.** A DB failure is therefore indistinguishable from "no such request" — and worse than that, the route keeps answering, from process-local state that no other replica shares.

This is the **KS-963 swallow class**, not the KS-1013 format class. Kam's KS-963 ruling made `getUserById` rethrow for exactly this reason: *a DB error is not "no such user"*. These three sites were not in that ruling's scope and still carry the pattern in a broader form — KS-963's swallow at least logged; these catch blocks are **empty**.

## The three sites

`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` (all on `develop` `5ffaaf396`)

| line | function | query |
| -- | -- | -- |
| :1154 | `getVerificationRequest(id)` | `SELECT * FROM verification_upgrade_requests WHERE id = $1` |
| :1175 | `findPendingVerificationRequest(userId)` | `... WHERE user_id = $1 AND status = 'PENDING'` |
| :1197 | `listUserVerificationRequests(userId)` | `... WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY submitted_at DESC` |

Each has the shape:

```
if (isDbAvailable()) {
  try {
    const result = await dbQuery(...);
    ...
  } catch { /* fall through */ }
}
return memVerificationRequests.get(id) || null;
```

`isDbAvailable()` **gates the attempt, but the catch gates nothing** — it absorbs a timeout, a pool exhaustion, an RLS refusal, a permissions error and a syntax error identically, with no log line at all.

## Why it matters on the admin path

`POST /api/users/verification/:requestId/review` calls `getVerificationRequest` first (`users.ts:1280`) and throws `NotFoundError` on null. So during a DB incident an admin reviewing a real, pending verification request is told **404 — no such request**, and the audit trail records nothing unusual because nothing was logged.

The in-memory map is process-local, so in a multi-replica deployment the fallback answers differ per replica — a request "exists" or does not depending on which container served the call.

## Recommendation

Distinguish the two cases, exactly as KS-963 did for `getUserById`:

1. **Rethrow infrastructure errors** (or map them to 503) instead of falling through. `getUserById` already has the shape to copy — `isInfrastructureDbError(err)` → `ServiceUnavailableError`.
2. **At minimum, log.** A silent empty catch on three DB reads means an outage on this surface is invisible in the logs.
3. **Decide deliberately whether the in-memory fallback should exist at all.** It looks like a local-dev affordance that shipped; if it is meant to survive, it needs to be honest that it is answering from a degraded source rather than presenting stale state as authoritative.

## What is NOT established

* **Not reproduced against a live stack.** This is a static reading. A QA gate is currently driving `localhost:6882` for its own live matrix and adding traffic would corrupt its results, so the repro is deliberately deferred rather than skipped — the mechanism is quoted from source, not inferred.
* **Not swept beyond** `services/auth`**.** Whether the same bare-catch-then-memory-fallback pattern exists in the other 14 services is unmeasured, and this ticket does not imply it does.
* **No severity claim about data loss.** The writes go through a separate path (`saveVerificationRequest`) that this ticket did not trace.

## Provenance

Found by s154, 2026-09-09, during the bounded auth-only `{id}` sweep commissioned as KS-1013's follow-up. It surfaced as a **negative** result: `POST /verification/:requestId/review` was my strongest candidate for a second KS-1013 instance, and the schema refuted that (`verification_upgrade_requests.id` is `VARCHAR(100)`, not UUID, so no `22P02` is raised). Reading the function to establish that is what exposed the empty catch. Related: KS-963, KS-1013.

title: A clean image build of platform-k develop fails: services/governance does not compile (TS2742 on router's inferred type) — a new slot cannot start until the image exists from an older build
description:
## Seen (2026-09-29, develop `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching governance)

Starting a fresh stack slot with no cached images (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` via platform-s's `up-slot.sh 4`) fails at the governance image:

```
docker compose -p secuura_slot4 build --progress=plain governance
#19 1.611 src/routes/governance.ts(19,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'router' cannot be
      named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'.
      This is likely not portable. A type annotation is necessary.
#19 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c npm run build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

Reproducible: the same `docker compose build governance` fails the same way on a second run. Slots 1–3 on this machine start only because they hold `secuura_slot{1,2,3}-governance` images built up to two weeks ago; slot 4 had no image and could not be built. A new developer machine, or a slot torn down with `--rmi all` (the test-discipline teardown), hits this.

The first attempt on the same slot failed one image earlier — `nft-certificate` at `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — and that one built cleanly on retry, so it was transient; governance is not.

## Suggested fix

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — give `router` an explicit type (`const router: Router = express.Router()`), the usual TS2742 remedy when a workspace package (`@secuura/shared`) carries its own `@types/express-serve-static-core`. Worth a `tsc --noEmit` over every service in the PR gate so a non-portable inferred type cannot land again.

## Impact on platform-s

Blocks pairing an S slot with a fresh K slot for the gate run on platform-s PR #889 (the S↔K remediation branch); recorded there and on [PS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-928/k-live-goes-red-on-the-second-full-run-on-a-slot-the-anchor-refresher). Related: [KS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-955/a-fresh-clone-cannot-run-the-four-platform-suites-and-fails-in-a-way) (a fresh clone cannot run the suites).

title: Test-token env guard is asymmetric: the gateway fails closed on an unset NODE_ENV, the auth service fails open
description:
Remediation for **KS-486 finding 5** (Review A register, listed Low). Re-verified on `develop de4781ca2` — **the finding is HALF-FIXED, and the register's stated impact is now wrong.** Recording the surviving half so it does not disappear along with the fixed half. Same shape as Review F's F-6.

## Fixed since the register was written

The register says the auth service gates only on `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` while the gateway additionally requires `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS`. **The auth side now requires it too** (`services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:24-27`):

```js
// Require explicit opt-in for test tokens
if (process.env.ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS !== 'true') return null;
```

So the register's impact line — *"one mis-set env var = role/tenant spoof"* — **is no longer accurate: it now takes two.**

## Still present — the env check is asymmetric, and auth's is the fail-open shape

|  | check | behaviour when `NODE_ENV` is unset / `staging` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| gateway `middleware/auth.ts:110-113` | `['development','test'].includes(env)` — allowlist | test tokens **refused** (fail closed) |
| auth `middleware/authenticate.ts:20-23` | `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` — denylist | test tokens **accepted** (fail open) |

An unsigned `test_token_<base64>` self-asserts role and tenant. So on any deployment where `NODE_ENV` is unset or set to something other than `production`/`development`/`test` **and** `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`, the two services disagree about whether that token is valid — and the one that says yes is the auth service.

## Suggested direction

Make both sides the same allowlist (`['development','test']`), so an unset or unexpected `NODE_ENV` fails closed everywhere. Ideally share one helper rather than two copies that can drift again — the drift is the actual defect here, not either individual check.

## Acceptance

* With `NODE_ENV` unset and `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`, a `test_token_…` is refused by the **auth service** as well as the gateway — red-proved (the check must fail before the fix and pass after).
* Normal dev/test flows that legitimately use test tokens still work, so the change is not proved by simply disabling the feature.

title: Pin the front door's fall-through for an unverifiable Bearer (500 on every route if it ever rethrows), and decide three smaller gaps
description:
## BLUF

**Action (owner: the K lane): pin the front door's fall-through for an unverifiable Bearer, then decide three smaller gaps.** The connector-Bearer guard from PR 1495 (KS-1470) is correct today. But nothing tests what it does with a token that does NOT verify: if its `catch` block ever rethrows, every expired, forged, `alg:none` or malformed Bearer answers **500 on every route**, and all 1060 tests stay green. The Opus gate proved it with its own mutation (G10) on the merged head.

## Recommendation

1. **Do now (one or two lines):** in cell J of `ks1470-a-connector-bearer-is-refused-before-every-mount.test.ts`, add a POSITIVE assertion that a forged type:connector token reaches the recording upstream on the sig-json mount (or gets `authenticateToken`'s `Invalid or expired token` 401 on an `authenticateToken` mount), and add an expired-token case. Show the new assertion red under the gate's G10 mutation (the guard's `catch` rethrows) and restore byte-identical.
2. **Decide (small):** Notes 2, 3 and 5 below. Note 3 is the cheapest and removes a coupling: make the guard's Bearer scheme match case-insensitive. The gate showed it stays green (G14).

## Detail

Source: the Opus gate on PR 1495, head `89c1b9388638`, verdict `GO WITH NOTE`, 0 Major; verdict file sha256/16 `72ea63d45058c59d` (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1495/verdict.md`).

**Minor 1 (the action above).** Cell J asserts only "not the connector refusal", so it passes whether the unverifiable token is forwarded, answered 401, or answered 500. Under G10 the gate's probe file showed altered-signature, expired, `alg:none` and double-space Bearers all answering 500. Not a product bug today; a guard on a future edit.

**Note 2: audit attribution of a refusal.** The refusal is audited for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE on `/api/*`, but the row has `user_id` null and the platform default tenant; the connector id and tenant exist only in the `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER_REFUSED` warning, because `audit.ts` reads `req.user`, which this path never sets. GET refusals are never audited (a property of the audit middleware). KS-1198's existing refusals behave the same. Correlate on `requestId` if needed. Decide: accept, or attribute the row.

**Note 3: the guard and the upstreams agree on the Bearer scheme only by convention.** The guard uses the literal `startsWith('Bearer ')` plus `split(' ')[1]`, as every upstream does today, so `bearer x` is "no credential" on both sides. If an upstream ever adopts case-insensitive schemes (RFC 7235), the guard needs the same change. A case-insensitive guard costs nothing now (G14).

**Note 5: a cold JWKS cache.** From `packages/shared/src/crypto/jwks.ts`: an unknown-kid refetch is limited to once per 10 s, and concurrent fetches collapse onto one in-flight fetch with a 3 s timeout. That holds on a warm cache. On a COLD cache (`keyCache.size === 0`: JWKS configured but unreachable or empty) the cooldown is bypassed, so each sequential Bearer request starts a fetch and can wait up to 3 s. This is pre-existing in `verifyJwtRs256`; PR 1495 extends it to routes that never verified before (`/health`, docs, public verify, `/api/auth/*`). Bounded at one outstanding fetch, and not an oracle. Decide whether a cold cache should also honour the cooldown.

**Not ticketed on purpose.** Note 1 (gateway-served routes now answer a connector Bearer with 401) is named in the squash body. Note 4 (a `test_token_` carrying type:connector is not refused when `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`) matches KS-1198 and is never active in demo or production.

**Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, title and description): `unverifiable`, `fall-through`, `front door`, `rejectConnectorBearer`, `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER`, `case-insensitive scheme`, `cold JWKS`, `JWKS cooldown`, `audit row`, `user_id null`. No duplicate. Nearest: **KS-1471** (the refusal warning logs a mount-relative `req.path` inside `authenticateToken`; after PR 1495 the front door logs the full canonical path, the inner site still logs the mount-relative one). Related, not the same.

Related: KS-1470, KS-1198, KS-1471.

title: Cross-tenant guard fails open for tenantless tokens (connector on /lookup and /stub; access tokens likewise)
description:
## BLUF

**The cross-tenant 404 on** `GET /api/users/lookup` **and** `POST /api/users/stub` **is skipped entirely when the caller's token carries no tenant claim.** Filed from gate54a's finding **N-1374-1** on PR #1374 (KS-1402). **Not reachable through the token exchange today** — read in the code, the exchange always issues a tenant claim — so this is a latent fail-open, not a live hole. It is filed so the guard's shape is fixed rather than left depending on a property of a different component.

## What the gate measured

* **P5: 200 at the head.** A token with no tenant claim reaches the handler and the cross-tenant branch does not fire.
* **P5b: 200 at the base too.** So this is **not a regression introduced by PR #1374** — the behaviour predates it. PR #1374 only widens which token *types* reach the route; it does not change the tenant guard.
* The guard lives at `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:759`, and it has applied to `POST /api/users/stub` since **KS 564**. `GET /api/users/lookup` joins it with PR #1374.
* **Access tokens are in scope too**, not just connector tokens: the guard keys on the presence of a tenant on the caller, not on the token type.

## Why it is not reachable today

The token exchange always issues a tenant claim. That was established **by reading the exchange code, not by exercising it** — so "unreachable" is a code reading, and a change to the exchange (or any other issuer, including a test-only or future path) could make it reachable without anything here changing.

## Fix shape

**Fail closed when the caller has no tenant**: refuse rather than fall through to the unscoped read. The route-level 404-not-200-empty convention should be preserved, so a tenantless caller gets the same 404 a cross-tenant caller gets, and the absence of a tenant is never the thing that widens a read.

## Provenance

* gate54a on PR #1374, finding N-1374-1. Report: `2026-10-05-ks1402-1374-g54a/report.md`.
* Duplicate search before filing (all 571 KS issues, title + description, searched locally): `tenantless` **0 hits**; `cross-tenant` 22; `fails open` 8; `no tenant claim` 1. Must-hit controls `connector` **86** and `tenantId` **24**, impossible-token control `zzqqxx` **0** — so the 0 is a measurement. The two closest neighbours were read and are **different mechanisms**: KS-1091 is an `x-tenant-id` header honoured on originate's direct path; KS-1119 is a `crossTenantLookup` hash fallback in verification.
* **Who builds this is not decided here.**

title: `@secuura/shared` `main` points at an untracked, never-built `dist/index.js` — anything outside vitest's alias resolves to nothing
description:
**Category 1. Low. AUTHORISED, UNFILED — Linear's free-tier cap is refusing creation.**

## BLUF

`packages/shared/package.json` `main` points at `dist/index.js`. `dist/` **is gitignored, untracked, and no install step builds it.** In a tree that has never run a build, `require.resolve('@secuura/shared')` **throws** `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

Measured 2026-09-06 during the KS-830 cell, in a fresh clone at `904ca6ef2` after a clean `npm ci` (1937 packages, exit 0):

|  | working checkout | fresh clone |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `require.resolve('@secuura/shared')` | `packages/shared/dist/index.js` | **THROWS** `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` |
| entry sha256 | `52ff4828de770b62669e828139c1d03b72834fb82c38f85ab1538fdddd38bce9` | n/a |
| `dist/` present after `npm ci` | YES (built earlier by hand) | **NO** |
| `npm ls @secuura/shared` | `@secuura/shared@0.3.0 -> ./packages/shared` | **identical** |

The workspace symlink is the same in both. The only variable is whether somebody has run a build in that tree.

## Why it is currently invisible

`packages/shared/vitest.config.ts` aliases `@secuura/shared` to `src/index.ts`, and that alias covers the whole of the shared test suite's import graph — so **the suites are green in both trees** and nothing surfaces the gap. The alias's own comment explains it was added for class identity (KS-727), not for resolvability; the resolvability fix is a side effect nobody declared.

## Why it is worth a ticket anyway

Anything in that package that runs **outside** vitest's alias — a script, a tool, a `node -e`, a consumer resolving the workspace package by name without a prior build — resolves to nothing on a fresh checkout. A new developer or a CI job that does not build first gets `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from a package that `npm ls` reports as correctly linked, which is a confusing failure to diagnose.

**Priority Low, deliberately:** nothing is broken today, no suite depends on it, and the alias hides it everywhere it currently matters. This is a trap, not a defect.

## Fix shapes (not chosen — whoever picks this up should)

* Add a `prepare` script so the workspace builds on install; or
* point `main` at `src/index.ts` and let consumers transpile; or
* declare `exports` with a source condition.

Each has consequences for the Docker builds, which is why this is filed rather than fixed in passing.

## Provenance

Found while running the KS-830 `npm ci` cell on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-09-05T23:09:26Z; carried out of KS-830 as its own item on her 23:15:00Z ruling, both SPF + DKIM `header.i=@agentmail.to` + DMARC pass. KS-830 comment `565ea3cc-bc90-47c9-aa72-319bbc397605` holds the full measurement. **It is NOT the cause of KS-830's red** — that was measured and excluded.

---

*Filed by s138 (seat A) 2026-09-06. Text authored by s137 and preserved at* `5_Project_History/unfiled-tickets-s137/unfiled-dist-resolution-trap.md`*; creation was refused by Linear's cap on 2026-09-05T23:33:40Z and retried after Kam upgraded the plan (panel, 09:45).*

title: Anchor a detached signature against the existing K document (sign without a new version)
description:
Raised from platform-s [PS-1070](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1070/signing-formats-a-detached-signature-is-bound-on-chain-by-content-hash) (Stuart, 2026-10-13). This is a platform-k change. Platform-s will switch to it once it ships on the paired K.

## Today

Platform-s now signs non-PDF documents **detached**: a CAdES `.p7s` is stored beside the unchanged file ([PS-1043](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1043/signing-formats-p1-detached-signing-baseline-signformatpolicy)). The content is unchanged, so S does not fork a K version for it. Instead S posts a **flat** `/api/anchors` anchor whose `DocumentId` is S's own transaction id (`ToHyphenatedGuid(tx.ChainId)`), not K's document id. That has two consequences:

* The signature sits outside K's lifecycle for the document.
* The anchored hash is the content hash, and the upload's anchor carries that hash too. **K's verify-by-hash therefore returns two unrelated anchors for one hash.**

## Ask

A way for S to record a **sign event against an existing K document without creating a new version**. Either of these would do:

* a sign/attest verb that keeps the document's version tip where it is; or
* a `sign` event on `/lifecycle-events` for that document.

It must carry:

* the content hash, which must equal the tip's;
* the signature's own hash, `metadata.signatureHash` ([KS-1454](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1454/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-signaturehash-the-plain), so the two should be sequenced together);
* the usual non-PII whitelist only. `PayloadJson` never leaves S.

**Verify** should then return one document with a signature event on it, not two anchors.

## Platform-s side, once this ships

S retires the flat path for detached signs in `CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `case "sign"`. That change is gated on the paired K's published spec declaring the new verb or event.

title: The developer portal page documents POST /api/verification/verify-batch, which no service and no spec implements (CSRF carries exclusions for it)
description:
## BLUF

`services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:294` lists `POST /api/verification/verify-batch` ("Verify mul\[tiple documents\]") as a public endpoint. **Nothing serves it.** The OpenAPI spec (310 paths) declares `verify` and `verify-file` for the unversioned and v2 families but no `verify-batch`; no router in `services/originate` or any other service registers `/verify-batch` under verification (the only `verify-batch` code is the separate MCP server's own root-level `/verify-batch` in `services/mcp-server`). So a developer who follows the portal gets a 404, and `csrf.ts` carries CSRF exclusions for `/api/verification/verify-batch` and `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` that cover a route nothing implements.

## Recommendation

Owner decision, then one of: (a) implement the route and add it to the spec, so the page and the exclusions are true; (b) remove the row from the portal, and drop both CSRF entries in the same change (a dead exclusion is a latent hole: a future route at that name would be silently CSRF-exempt). Priority Low. Until then the two CSRF entries are PINNED by cells (KS-1469) so they cannot vanish or change unnoticed; that pin is deliberately not a statement that the route exists.

## Detail

* Found while resolving the m1 note from the Opus gate on PR #1466 (the `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` exclusion was pinned by no cell). Evidence, from a repo-wide search at develop `b4a245fba1ca`: spec path scan (310 paths, none `verify-batch`); `git grep` for verify-batch in non-test code finds only the portal row, the two `csrf.ts` entries, and the MCP server; a control with the same grep shape finds the real `/verify` and `/verify-file` routes.
* Other rows on that page were NOT checked against the code.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `developer-portal`, `developer portal`, `verify-batch`: no ticket about this page's rows.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-1165.

title: KS-1385 residue (#1549 gate MAJ-A): the anchor-overwrite guard keys on documents.id, but originate anchors under documents.external_id, so neither of Kam's rulings reaches originate's anchors
description:
## BLUF

Pull request #1549 (KS-1385) merged under Kam's two-round cap with this as its gate residue. **The anchor-overwrite guard looks the document up by** `documents.id`**, but originate anchors under** `documents.external_id`**.** So for every anchor originate emits, the stored identity is **kept, exactly as before #1549**. Neither of Kam's rulings takes effect for real originate traffic yet:

* card `…anchor-identity-needs-ps895-ruling-1013` = (b), "Latest event's identity wins";
* card `…custodian-may-update-anchor-identity-1013` = (c), "Issuer, or anyone in the custodian's organisation".

**Fail-closed, not a security regression.** Every arm the gate measured at the merged head is develop-or-stricter. The round-1 security findings (MAJ-1 cross-tenant rewrite, MAJ-2, MIN-1 race, MIN-2, MIN-3) are answered by #1549.

## Where — each line re-read at source on #1549's head `80daaa78a2c7` by Seat J 11th

* **The guard** — `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts`:
  * `:263` `if (!isUuidShaped(documentId)) return … 'document-id-not-a-uuid'`
  * `:204` the same check inside `readOwningDocument`
  * `:227` `WHERE d.id = $1::uuid`
  * Caller: `index.ts:1369` `mayOverwriteStoredMetadata(anchor.documentId, …)`
  * `index.ts:1485` suppresses the log line for `document-id-not-a-uuid`
* **Originate, the write side:**
  * `routes/documents.ts:655` `const id = documentUuid ?? \`doc-${[Date.now](<http://Date.now>)()}-…\`\`
  * `:902-903` the anchor body sends `documentId: id`
  * `repositories/documentRepo.ts:359` `dbId = uuidv4()`
  * `:437-438` the INSERT writes `id = dbId` and `external_id = doc.id`
  * The lifecycle sites (`documents.ts:1985`, `:2397`, `:2502`) send `req.params.id`, which is the external id (transfer-custody updates `WHERE external_id = ${id}`, `:1923`/`:1944`).
* Anchoring's own OpenAPI already describes `documentId` as "doc-… external id or a UUID" (`anchoring.openapi.ts:220`).

## Evidence (the gate's, end to end on a booted anchoring service as `secuura_app`)

Wednesday's project: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-15_gate-pr1549-r2/`. Files: `verdict.md` (report sha256/16 `7b3442fc82c94a83`), `scripts/07_e2e.sh`, `cells/e2e_custody.ts`, `logs/e2e_custody_{head,dev,r1gated}.log`.

| cell | `documentId` sent | caller | result at head |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| X1 | `doc-<ts>-<rand>` | issuer org (Kam's (b) case) | **kept**, silently (0 log lines) |
| X2 | S `documentUuid` | issuer org | **kept** — `document-not-in-callers-tenant` |
| X3 | S `documentUuid` | colleague in the custodian's org (Kam's (c) case) | **kept** — `document-not-in-callers-tenant` |
| P0–P3 | `documents.id` (positive control) | same callers | replaced |

Control arms: develop keeps all 16 cells. Round-1 head `aca6efb0` replaces X1–X3 (and reproduces MAJ-1).

## ⚠ Why the cells did not catch it

**Every #1549 cell keys** `documents` **by its primary key**: the fixtures insert `id` and anchor under that same id. The round-2 matrix did too, so "S6 is the only row that changes" holds only for a key originate never sends. The gate's sweep found 0 hits for `external_id` in the guard and 0 in the cells; its control, `owner_user_id`, had 8. **The new cell must key by** `external_id` **the way** `documentRepo.saveDocument` **writes it, or drive the product's own create path.** A primary-key fixture will pass while the product does nothing.

## Proposed (the gate's, not yet ruled)

* Resolve the anchor's `documentId` against `documents.external_id`, falling back to `documents.id`, the way `getDocument` already does (`documentRepo.ts:233-245`).
* Do not short-circuit the `doc-` form at `:263` / `:204`. Keep the explicit tenant bound and the custody JOIN's own tenant bound.
* Then re-run Kam's (b) and (c) end to end on originate-shaped keys.

## Two Minors from the same gate, to carry with it

* `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1406-1409` — the `$23` comment still says "confirmed the caller's organisation is the document's issuer. Custody option (a); Kam holds card …". #1549 shipped (c).
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:896-898` — "the overwrite applies only when the caller's organisation is the document's issuer". Same stale claim.

## Not established

Whether Platform S ever anchors through the flat `POST /api/anchors` using a K-minted document's **primary** key. `documentRepo.ts:172` surfaces `documentUuid = row.id` for `doc-…` documents, so S could hold it. Such a row would be a different `anchor_store` row from the one originate's create wrote. S's wire traffic was not observed.

## Deferred

* **Why:** this is BUILD work. Kam, 2026-10-15: "Do work with the spark only until the quota resets". It waits for the reset unless it can be carved for the Spark.
* **Discovered:** 2026-10-15, by the #1549 round-2 Opus gate (Wednesday's GO of 06:19:53Z), filed by Seat J 11th.
* **KS-1385 stays open** (`contributes`).

title: validate route follow-ups from the KS-1370 gate: usage_count lost update, a cache-miss read fault mislabelled, and D1 pins no write
description:
Three gate40 findings on the merged KS-1370 change (#1338, squash `8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee`). One logical path: the `POST /api/keys/validate` route in `services/security`. Each item is copied verbatim from the gate40 report (`2026-09-29-batch1338-g40/report.md`, sha256 prefix `372924904c1f`). Facts only; none of the three blocks anything that shipped.

- [ ] **N-1338-3 (Minor, TICKET — MEASURED AT RUNTIME; LOST-UPDATE-CANDIDATE):** the seat's "`usage_count` written from a stale copy is a lost update" is **narrowed by half (ii) but not closed**. Two processes validating one key in sequence (B, B2, B, B2): **head 0 → 4 (exact); base 0 → 2 (the stale-copy loss)**. Twenty CONCURRENT validates (10 on each process): **head 0 → 12 (run 1: 11); base 0 → 9 (run 1: 10)**. The remaining loss is a read-modify-write race: `usage_count = $3` is written from a value read one statement earlier. Fix-shape: `SET usage_count = usage_count + 1, last_used_at = GREATEST(last_used_at, $2)`. Regression cell: two instances × N concurrent validates on the real DB, asserting usage_count == N. Usage is telemetry, not an auth decision, so this is a ticket, not a block.
- [ ] **N-1338-4 (Minor, TICKET — MEASURED AT RUNTIME; pre-existing, unchanged by this PR):** a failed read on a cache MISS answers **200** `valid:false, 'Key not found'` (plus a warn line). The same fault on a cache HIT now answers **503**. Both are refused, and through the gateway both become a 30 s cached 401, so this is **coherent with "A revoked key is never honoured"**. But the miss branch mislabels a database fault as an unknown key, and auth's connector-token returns 401 there instead of 502. Fix-shape: give the cache-miss branch the same 503 on a failed read (a product decision; outside card-2's scope). Cell: miss + read fault → 503.
- [ ] **N-1338-5 (Minor, TICKET — PROBED; NOT-PINNED):** D1 asserts the answer and the eviction but **not that no write was issued**. The base's vanished-row RESURRECTION therefore has no cell. The head prevents it structurally (early return), but nothing pins that. Cell: in D1, assert the mock recorded no INSERT/UPDATE (`state.usageSql.length === 0`).

Adjacent, not duplicated: KS 1174 covers the gateway collapsing every API-key failure into 401, which is the gateway half of N-1338-4's symptom, not the security route's miss branch.

Refs KS-1370

title: POST /api/oauth/authorize deny emits `Location: undefined?error=…` for an app with zero registered redirect URIs; GET 500s on the same state; PATCH /api/oauth/apps lacks .min(1)
description:
Filed from the KS-797 QA pass, findings **Q3 (Minor, INTRODUCED by #814)** and **Q5 (Minor)**. Grouped because one `.min(1)` closes the door that makes Q3 reachable.

## Q3 — introduced by #814, and stated as such

For an app with **zero** registered redirect URIs, the deny branch builds `Location: undefined?error=…`. The parent behaviour emitted `/`. Neither is right, but this is a regression introduced by the KS-797 merge and should be recorded that way rather than as pre-existing.

`GET` answers **500** for the same state.

**Deliberately not fixed inside #814.** It is a one-line fix, and #814 merged at its gated SHA — un-gating a passed gate for a Minor is the trade this project has already decided against (the same rule #812 merged under).

## Q5 — the door that makes it reachable

`PATCH /api/oauth/apps` accepts an empty `redirect_uris` array; `POST` **does not** — create carries `.min(1)` and update does not. So an app can be created valid and then patched into the zero-URI state that Q3 mishandles.

## Fix

1. `.min(1)` on the PATCH schema, matching create.
2. The deny branch refuses rather than concatenating onto `undefined`; GET returns the same refusal instead of 500.
3. A test for the zero-URI state on **both** verbs — the asymmetry is the actual bug and a test on one verb would not have caught it.

Refs: KS-797 (merged, `3ccf52f09`).

title: api-gateway auth: the CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER_REFUSED warning logs req.path, which drops the router mount prefix
description:
## BLUF

The `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER_REFUSED` warning added by KS-1198 (PR #1470) logs `req.path` at `auth.ts:411`. Inside a mounted router `req.path` is the mount-relative remainder, so a refused `GET /api/credentials/abc` logs `"path":"/abc"`. The warning exists so the first Kintsugi cycle shows WHICH call presented a connector Bearer; the prefix is exactly what tells the reader which route it was. Minor; found by the gate.

## Recommendation

Log `req.baseUrl + req.path`. **Not** `req.originalUrl`: it carries the query string, which can hold a token. Pin it with a cell that mounts the middleware under a router (the existing cell C mounts at the root, so it cannot see this). Small enough to fold into the next gateway PR that touches `auth.ts`; priority Low.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1470 (KS-1198), 2026-10-12, defect 1 (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1470/verdict.md`): measured `GET /api/credentials/abc` logs `"path":"/abc"`.
* The same trimmed-`req.path` trap was fixed for the audit trail in KS-871 and is KS-1457's subject for three reads in `audit.ts`.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived): `req.baseUrl`, `mount prefix`, `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER`: no ticket for this log field.

Related: KS-1198, KS-871, KS-1457.

title: tenantId is read through two `as unknown as` casts because it is not on JwtPayload (Peter F14)
description:
**BLUF —** `tenantId` **is not declared on** `JwtPayload`**, so every reader gets at it through two** `as unknown as` **casts. The type system is being told to look away at exactly the point tenancy is decided.**

`services/originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:15` and `routes/gdpr.ts` (`connectorContext`) both do:

```ts
const user = (req as unknown as { user?: JwtPayload }).user;
const tenantId = (user as unknown as { tenantId?: string } | undefined)?.tenantId;
```

The value is real — `ConnectorTokenClaims` carries `tenantId?: string` and the connector exchange sets it — but it is absent from the shared `JwtPayload`, so each consumer re-asserts it locally. A double `as unknown as` defeats every check that would otherwise catch a rename, a type change, or a reader that forgets the field is optional.

This matters more than a normal typing nit because `tenantId` is the tenancy boundary on the connector paths: `connectorContext` returns null when it is missing and the route fails closed 403. That fail-closed behaviour is currently guarded by a cast rather than by a type.

### Fix shape

Declare `tenantId?: string` on the shared `JwtPayload` and delete the local casts. It touches the shared type, so it wants its own PR and its own reviewer rather than riding along inside a GDPR change.

Found: Peter, review of PR #790, 2026-09-02 12:46Z (F14). Not fixed in #790 — it belongs to the shared payload type, not that PR's surface.

title: MCP get_info reports a gateway fail-closed refusal (403 or 503 from /api/connector/info) as 'endpoint may not exist yet or no API key set'
description:
## BLUF

The MCP server's `get_info` tool turns **any** non-2xx from the gateway's `GET /api/connector/info` into the note `Connector info not available (endpoint may not exist yet or no API key set)`. A fail-closed refusal (the 403s of KS-1231 and KS-1232, and the 503 of PR 1518 / KS-1532) therefore reads to an agent as "the endpoint may not exist" or "no API key", which is false: the endpoint exists, the key is set, and the gateway deliberately refused because the allow-list is malformed or could not be read. Safe (an agent never sees `[]`), but the wording sends the operator to the wrong cause. Found as Minor 2 of the PR 1518 gate (verdict sha256/16 `377ec0d1d9cad4e5`) and earlier as a recorded fact on KS-1232.

## Recommendation

A P4 wording change in the MCP server, small and test-first: when `connectorResult` is present but not `ok`, say so with the status and the gateway's own error text (for example `Connector info refused by the gateway (503): Connector allow-list configuration could not be read; refusing until it can be read`), and keep the "may not exist / no API key" note only for the cases it is true of (a thrown request, or a 404 / 401). A cell per status: 401, 403, 404, 503 and a rejected call.

## Detail

* **Where** (read at develop `b2085e99ff1c`): `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/tools/info.ts:124` (`getConnectorInfo().catch(() => null)`), `:128` (`const connector = connectorResult?.ok ? connectorResult.data : null;`), `:148` (the note); `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/api-client.ts:42` returns `{ status: res.status, ok: res.ok, data }`, so the status and the gateway's error body are available to the tool and are dropped.
* **Not a security issue:** the tool answers a note, never an empty allow-list, so a refusal never reads as "unrestricted".
* **Related:** KS-1232, KS-1532 (PR 1518), KS-1530 (the package generator's own `|| []`, a different defect in the same service). There is an existing relay test, `services/mcp-server/src/__tests__/ks1232-connector-info-relay.test.ts`, which pins that a gateway answer is relayed as it is; a new cell would sit beside it.
* **Dedupe before filing (the Wednesday condition):** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles in team KS: `Connector info not available` 0, `may not exist yet` 0, `get_info` 0, `tools/info` 0, `relay` 0, `MCP` 7 (KS-1530, KS-1437, KS-1290, KS-1214, KS-1163, KS-729, KS-530; none about this note). Over descriptions, the regex `Connector info not available|endpoint may not exist|tools/info`: KS-1530 0 and KS-1534 0 (the two tickets named as candidates), KS-1531 0, and KS-1232 2 as the positive control, so the instrument can read ticket text. No existing ticket covers it.

title: KS-759 gate follow-ups (pull request 1543): gdpr.ts connectorContext has no runtime cell at all, and 27 more JWT-claim reads go through 'any' plus 7 typed re-casts (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

Two Minors from the Sonnet through-code gate on pull request 1543 (KS-759), report sha256/16 `bb6259a0504dd87a`, GO WITH NOTE. **Facts only.** Neither is a defect of 1543. Both are about what the evidence around it does and does not cover. Filed on Wednesday's instruction as one ticket.

## 1. `routes/gdpr.ts` `connectorContext` has no runtime test at all (pre-existing)

1543 edits two copies of `connectorContext`: `routes/platformOrganizations.ts` and `routes/gdpr.ts:468-479` (callers `:521` and `:552`, both behind `requireRole(...CONNECTOR_ROLES)` on `/erasures`). **Only the platformOrganizations copy is exercised by any cell.** No file under `services/originate/src/__tests__` mounts `gdprRouter` on `/erasures` — a grep for `/erasures` finds none.

The gate proved it with mutants, each run against all 105 unit suites and all 48 erase-connector integration cells in both tenancy modes:

| mutant, in `gdpr.ts` only | unit | integration × 2 modes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| swap `tenantId` / `organizationId` | 0 fail | 0 fail |
| `organizationId: undefined` | 0 fail | 0 fail |
| `connectorContext` always returns `null` | **0 fail** | **0 fail** |

The same mutants in `platformOrganizations.ts` fail 36–51 unit and 21–28 integration cells. So the gdpr half of 1543 is protected by `tsc` and by being character-for-character the same expression as the covered half — nothing else. My own READY for 1543 cited the gdpr unit cells (7 files, 87 tests) and the three ks695 integration files as covering it; they cover the platformOrganizations copy, not this one. The gate caught that.

**Fix shape (the gate's):** one cell mounting `gdprRouter` with a connector principal that asserts `tenantId`, `organizationId` and `connectorId` reach the `/erasures` handler, and that a tenant-less principal gets the refusal. Red-first against the always-null mutant.

## 2. The "only two casts" frame is narrow: 27 more reads of the same claims go through `any`

1543's census — "repo-wide, exactly two `as unknown as { tenantId` casts" — is true **for that exact shape and nothing else.** The same hiding mechanism exists in other spellings. At 1543's head, by the gate's `git grep -E` over `Blockchain/Dev` source, tests excluded (they are fixtures, not reads):

`(req as any).user?.tenantId` **/** `?.organizationId` **— 27 non-test lines:**

* **originate — 11:** `adminConfig.ts` 947, 1069, 1070 · `certifications.ts` 378, 523 · `documents.ts` 100, 119, 391, 507, 743, 1019
* **security — 11:** `src/index.ts` 765, 819, 870, 1093, 1150, 1151, 1183, 1192, 1434, 1435, plus the reads at 1633 / 1747
* **tokenisation — 4:** `src/index.ts` 63, 66, 95, 98
* **packages/shared — 1:** `src/security/audit-logger.ts:214`

**Typed local re-casts of the same payload — 7:** `security/src/index.ts` 1179, 1352, 1415 · `anchoring/src/index.ts:474` · `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:530` · `auth/src/routes/issuerCerts.ts:119` · `auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:102`

**Consequence:** deleting `tenantId` or `organizationId` from originate's `JwtPayload` still compiles for the 11 originate `any` reads. 1543 is correct about what it fixed; "a cast hid the read" remains true for these. **The gate did not classify which of the 27 are individually safe or should become typed reads, and this ticket does not either.** No fix shape is proposed for them. Out of frame: `(req as any).tenantId` reads (a property of `req`, not of the JWT payload) are a different pattern.

## Related

\[\[KS-759\]\] the parent · \[\[KS-1593\]\] the compile-time guard follow-up from the same change · \[\[KS-1032\]\] trust-header reads outside auth middleware (a different hiding mechanism, same class of boundary)

title: api-gateway meetsVerificationLevel fails open on an unknown REQUIRED level: an off-canonical document-type level admits every authenticated caller
description:
## BLUF

The api-gateway's `meetsVerificationLevel` fails OPEN when a document type's *required* level is a string outside the known order. `indexOf` returns -1 for the requirement, and every user index is `>= -1`, so any authenticated caller passes: every human level, and a connector key.

* An anonymous caller is still refused (`enforceDocumentTypeRules` answers 401 for any non-`none` level with no user).
* So a document type stored with an off-canonical level, e.g. `standrd`, admits every authenticated principal to create it (`POST /api/documents`) and to verify it (`POST /api/documents/:id/verify`).
* This is a READ-only chain. Nothing has been measured against a stored catalogue.

## Recommendation

Not built; Backlog. **Do not make it fail closed yet.** Two measurements come first; without them, a fail-closed fix could lock out every document type whose stored level string is off-canonical:

1. **The level strings actually stored in the catalogue:** `document_type_configs` in each tenant DB, and the gateway's Redis document types. Any value outside `none, basic, social, standard, enhanced, high, government` (after lowercasing) is exposed today.
2. **Who can create or edit a document type:** the auth guards on originate's admin-config router and on the gateway's template clone. That sets how reachable an off-canonical value is.

KS-1176 (the connector-key fix) deliberately leaves this behaviour unchanged, and its PR carries a cell that pins it as it is at base, so the fix cannot move it silently.

## Detail

**The comparison** (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts` at develop `e0f41a8fafd64fa31524390cfeab320e822f3d15`):

* `:39-47` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`.
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` returns `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`, both lowercased. An unknown requirement makes `reqIdx` -1, so the result is true for every user index, including -1.
* **Creation:** `:143-151` compares `creatorVerificationLevel`. With no user, `:136-141` refuses any non-`none` string with 401, so anonymous callers are not affected.
* **Verification:** `routes/verification.ts:554-557` compares `verifierVerificationLevel` when it is not `none`, with the same -1 semantics.

**Where the level strings come from (READ):**

* originate `routes/adminConfig.ts:156-172`: `POST /document-types` checks only `name` and `code`, then inserts `creatorVerificationLevel` (default `basic`) and the other three levels as given. No level validation was found.
* api-gateway `routes/platform.ts:880-894`: the template clone inserts `creator_verification_level` / `verifier_verification_level` from `platform_document_type_templates` rows as stored. Validation was not traced.
* The gateway's Redis catalogue has a writer at `services/redis.ts:511` (`setDocumentType`). **Untraced: how the Redis catalogue is filled from those database rows**, and so whether an off-canonical DB value reaches the gateway's comparison unchanged.

**Found by** the KS-1176 census (seat A, 2026-09-17). Wednesday's ANSWER at 19:52:15Z ruled it a separate ticket, not built, with the KS-1176 fix leaving it unchanged.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches in title, description or comments:

* `meetsVerificationLevel`: 2 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-1176, PS-519).
* `creatorVerificationLevel`: 3 fuzzy, 3 literal (KS-1176, PS-519, KS-364 archived).
* `reqIdx`: 0 fuzzy, 0 literal.
* `document-types`: 121 fuzzy, 13 literal (KS-1176, PS-519, and archived catalogue, Akto and conformance tickets: KS-388, KS-397, KS-364, KS-40, KS-510, KS-357, KS-118, KS-39, KS-37, KS-465, KS-144).

None is about an unknown required level. Related: KS-1176.

title: anchoring's raw pg BIGINT reaches persisted and live readers unshaped
description:
## BLUF

`block_number` leaves anchoring's `buildResponse` (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:604`) as a **string**, the KS-584 heal path in originate persists it into the document blob unshaped, and the gateway's live chain-scan reads have no shape rule at all. Three sites, one logical path: the raw `pg` value of a `BIGINT` column is passed through where every other reader of that column converts it. Found by the tier-2 gate on PR #969 (KS-1069) as F1 (the persisted half) and O1 (the live half); PR #969 merged with E7 STRICT by ruling, so this ticket carries the root fix — not the PR.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1069-969-fb23ca6aa-tier2-r1/report.md` — §4 (the F1 chain), FINDINGS F1, Open O1, WHAT WAS NOT TESTED item 1.

## The chain (READ ONLY from source at develop `0f69129b3`; line numbers as printed there)

1. **anchoring** `src/index.ts:604` — `blockNumber: onChain?.blockNumber || row?.block_number || null,` on the DB leg of `GET /api/anchors/verify/:hash` (`:633-647`). `onChain` is the stored `metadata_payload`, which never carries `blockNumber` (`anchorSchema.ts buildFlatAnchorMetadataPayload`, 0 hits), so the value is `row.block_number` **raw**. The column is `BIGINT` (`:181`; migrations `001:717`, `003:29`). `pg` 8.20.0 returns int8 as a string by default, and **no** `setTypeParser` **/ int8 parser exists anywhere in** `Blockchain/Dev` (non-test, non-lock: 0). The same file converts that column with `Number()` at `:1314` (`blockNumber`), `:1315` (`slot`), `:1320` (`fee`) — the control that says the authors know.
2. **originate** `src/routes/verification.ts:338` — `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:293-348`) composes the healed blob with `blockHeight: chain.blockNumber ?? blob.blockHeight ?? 0`, where `chain` is anchoring's reply above; `persistHealedAnchor` **(**`:359-369`**) persists it** via `updateDocument(…, { blockchain: healed })` (`:366`) when the heal moved the status to `confirmed`. Called from `POST /api/verification/verify` (`:1082-1083`) and `/verify-file` (`:657-658`). This is the KS-584 heal path (PR #666, merged 2026-08-12) — the writer the E7 ruling's census ("every originate writer stores a number") did not see.
3. **api-gateway** `src/routes/verification.ts` — the persisted tier-1 read at `:623` (head numbering; `typeof persistedBlockHeight === 'number'`, PR #969) now refuses that string, so a healed document answers `verified:false` / `off-chain-only` where develop-before-#969 said on-chain — **only while the gateway's own live scan does not answer** (`:569-585`: anchoring unreachable, the 2.5 s timeout at `:570`, token refused, or `doc.contentHash` missing); when it does, `Number()` at `:582` coerces and `liveAnchored` wins. Tier 2 is unaffected (`rowToAnchor`).
4. **The live half (O1, MEASURED + READ ONLY):** the live chain-scan path (`:579-582`, `:645`) has no shape rule — `j.verified` truthiness (a string `'false'` counts), `liveTxHash` truthiness (`1`, a placeholder), `Number(blockNum)` coercion, no sign/integer rule (`-1`, `4242.5` on-chain), `simulated` ignored. Every L row on-chain at both SHAs. Safe today only because anchoring's `buildResponse :595-598` nulls placeholders and emits the literal `verified: true` — a response-shape accident, and its `:604` raw BIGINT pass is the same root as item 1. Blast radius = anything that can answer the gateway's `/api/anchors/verify/:hash` call.

**Evidence classes, as the report states them:** READ ONLY (the chain above) + PROBED (`pg-types` `getTypeParser(20)("4242")` → `"4242"`, `typeof string`, from the checkout's `node_modules`) + MEASURED (the shape: matrix cell `G:'4242':t1` on-chain at develop, off-chain-only at head). **Not run against a database.** F1's producible path is read from source, not reproduced end-to-end.

## Checklist (one test pass; RULED 2026-09-13)

- [ ] anchoring `src/index.ts:604`: `Number(row.block_number)` as `:1314` already does (null-safe: a null row stays null).
- [ ] originate `src/routes/verification.ts:338`: `Number(chain.blockNumber)` (or coerce once where `chain` is parsed), so the heal persists a number.
- [ ] Regression cell (prose, originate): a `submitted` blob with a real 64-hex hash healed via a stubbed anchoring reply `{verified:true, txHash, blockNumber:'4242'}` persists `typeof blockHeight === 'number'`. Red at develop (`'4242'` persisted), green after.
- [ ] The live chain-scan shape rule at api-gateway `src/routes/verification.ts:579-582, :645` (O1's class): `verified === true`, the KS-522 placeholder rule on `liveTxHash`, `Number.isInteger(h) && h > 0` on the height, `simulated` read — the same three guards PR #969 gave the persisted read, applied to the live read; cells for each.
- [ ] **The JSONB round-trip, measured in BOTH directions (KS-1069 item 1 — NOT TESTED by #969 or its gate; moved here so it survives KS-1069's archive).** Source implies type preservation: originate writes `JSON.stringify({…, blockchain})::jsonb` (`documentRepo.ts:523-532`, `:545-546`) and reads back Prisma's parsed JSONB (`:162`) — a JS number should come back a number, a string a string (which is what makes the persisted string above a string). **If that expectation were false the other way (every number read back as a string), E7's guard would refuse every persisted height and every tier-1 confirmed document — the four seeded demo documents included — would answer off-chain-only: a demo-visible blast radius.** Nothing proves it either way yet; measure against a real Postgres, both directions, before or alongside the fixes above.

## Deliberately not here

* The gateway's persisted guard itself (E7 STRICT) — shipped in #969, ruled. Coercing at the gateway was option (b); the ruling kept (a): fix the root.
* The `persistedStatus == null` carve-out — KS-1073 / KS-1068 territory.
* The presentation question (a placeholder echoed in `blockchain.txHash` with `source:'persisted'`) — recorded on the #969 verdict, not raised.

## Ancestry and neighbours (named, not related — see Dedupe)

* **KS-584** (P1, "Verify by hash selects the wrong registration: certified documents report as unanchored, and tenant fields leak") is the ancestor: its fix, PR #666 (merged 2026-08-12, verified live on demo 2026-08-14, S-side confirmation 2026-08-19), introduced the heal path at item 2. **KS-584 is archived (2026-08-19T02:00Z, Deployed to UAT)**, so Linear refuses a relation to it; it is named here instead.

A reader arriving from any of the three finds this ticket the home of the height-shape defect.

## Dedupe, before filing (s205, 2026-09-13)

Literal census over 1,118 KS issues (691 archived) and 912 comments, by SYMBOL and path — `persistHealedAnchor` 0 · `setTypeParser` 0 · `BIGINT` 0 · `liveAnchored` 0 · `confirmStalePendingAnchor` → KS-590 (comment) · `buildResponse` → KS-1119, KS-521, KS-584, KS-590 · `block_number` → KS-1004, KS-607, KS-1070, KS-1057 · `/api/anchors/verify` → KS-489, KS-590, KS-683 · `JSONB` → KS-1069, KS-1115, KS-472, KS-537, KS-593, KS-787. Every hit's description read: none names the raw BIGINT pass or the heal path's string height. Controls fired (`persistedStatus == null` → KS-1073; `crossTenantLookup` → KS-1119 + KS-584; a nonsense token → 0).

## Provenance

title: anchoring threadTokenMint test fails only under root-visible npm install layout — nested @lucid-evolution/plutus duplicate-instance (pre-existing, layout-dependent; KS-559 A/B-cleared)
description:
**Found during KS-559 validation (2026-08-04, Agent Teams pilot) — pre-existing, NOT caused by the dep sweep (controlled A/B in two independent environments: identical failure with pre-KS-559 and post-KS-559 locks).**

`services/anchoring` test `threadTokenMint.test.ts › parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId` fails with `Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type` in `applyParamsToScript` — the classic **duplicate-instance** signature: the test's `Constr` comes from the top-level `@lucid-evolution/plutus@0.1.31` while `@lucid-evolution/utils@0.1.70` serializes against its own nested `plutus@0.1.33` copy, and the cross-copy instanceof check fails.

**It is INSTALL-LAYOUT-DEPENDENT, which is why it looks flaky across setups:**

* `npm ci` in a **parentless standalone** copy of services/anchoring (= what the Dockerfile does) → **110/110 pass**. Verified on macOS host for both develop and KS-559 locks.
* `npm ci --workspaces=false` with the **monorepo root visible** as a parent dir (worktree, full-repo container mount) → **109/110, this test fails**. Verified on macOS host AND in node:24-alpine, again for both locks.

Same lock file both ways (`packages` dict byte-identical to develop) — npm physically lays the tree out differently when it can see a parent workspace root, and one layout resolves the utils→plutus import to the nested copy.

**Why it matters:** (1) any dev running anchoring tests inside the monorepo checkout with a standalone install hits a phantom red; (2) the nested plutus duplication itself (0.1.31 vs 0.1.33) is fragile — a future hoist change could flip the shipped image's behaviour. Fix options: dedupe/pin `@lucid-evolution/plutus` so one copy exists; or make the test/lib resolution layout-proof; or document the supported install layout for the suite.

Evidence + repro commands in the KS-559 PR thread and session history 2026-08-04. Credit: caught by the KS-559 deps teammate's controlled A/B refusing to accept an unqualified 110/110.

title: Write the no-allowance warning's authMethod through logField (the set is pinned by declaration, not at runtime), and pin two edge cases
description:
## BLUF

**Action (owner: the K lane): write the no-allowance warning's** `authMethod` **through** `logField`**, then pin two edge cases the KS-1496 gate left open.** The warning writes `authMethod` UNESCAPED (`rateLimitEnforce.ts`, the `(${authMethod}, tenant ...)` part of the warning). It is safe only because `MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS` holds fixed tokens. The five pins added by PR 1496 check the set's DECLARATION (read from the AST) and a list of 32 outsiders; they do not check its RUNTIME membership. The Sonnet gate showed four ways to admit a hostile value that all stay green. Escaping the field removes the dependency on the set instead of testing around it.

## Recommendation

1. **Product change (small):** `(${logField(authMethod)}, ...)`. The two real members, `api_key` and `oauth_app`, pass through `logField` byte for byte, so ordinary lines do not change. Add one cell that drives a hostile `authMethod` and reads a single, well-formed line. Once that holds, a widened set can no longer forge a log line, and M1/M2 can say so in their header.
2. **Optional:** export a frozen set or a predicate so a test can read runtime membership without the AST. Only needed if you want the membership itself pinned, not just made harmless.
3. **n2:** add a KS-1480 `O` cell that a leading or trailing space in a principal or tenant is written as typed. 4. **n3:** add an explicit cell that a lone backslash is written as a double backslash (P3 pins the quote and the typed-versus-real difference, not the backslash on its own).

## Detail

Source: the Sonnet gate on PR 1496, head `3470818891032c490112f1317a6affb880acf965`, `GO WITH NOTE`, 0 Major; verdict sha256/16 `c6d654e87e694bc5` (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1496/verdict.md`).

**m1 (Minor): the pins check the declaration, not the runtime membership.** Four mutants that stay green: `MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS.add('evil')` after the declaration (S9); the same through a cast (S10); an extra `|| user.authMethod === 'sso'` in the gate (S11); a widened copy of the set inside the gate with the declaration untouched, `new Set([...MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS, 'oauth']).has(...)` (X3). Each admits a value that the warning writes unescaped, which is the reason the pins exist. The claim ("members read from the AST") is met literally; the protection the header describes needs the product change above.

**n2:** a final `.trim()` on `logField` (X5), or a trim before the JSON step (E1), stays green: trailing whitespace on an id is silently dropped, so "ordinary ids are written byte for byte" is not pinned for edge whitespace. A pre-existing gap in the KS-1480 `O` cells. Safety is unaffected (a trimmed newline is gone, not forged).

**n3:** leaving the backslash unescaped while the quote is escaped (Q4) keeps P3 green, because the typed and real lines still differ. Other cells (E4, O3) catch it indirectly.

**Related and deliberately left out:** whether `'oauth'` should join the set is KS-1156's question. The gate agreed that omitting it from M1 was right (M2 fails the day it changes), and noted an `'oauth'` admitted OUTSIDE the declaration is invisible, which is m1 again.

**Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, title and description): `logField`, `MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS`, `authMethod`, `runtime membership`, `warnNoAllowance`, `no-allowance`, `trailing whitespace`, `byte for byte`. No duplicate. Nearest: KS-1496 (the pins), KS-1480 and KS-1464 (the warning's escaping), KS-1205, KS-1156 (the set's membership against the OAuth label).

Related: KS-1496, KS-1480, KS-1156.

title: POST /api/verification/verify refuses a title-only body with 400, while the published VerifyRequest says 'Provide ONE OR MORE of documentId, hash, title, contentHash'
description:
## BLUF

* **A title-only verify body is refused.** The served spec's `VerifyRequest` says *"Provide ONE OR MORE of documentId, hash, title, contentHash. The verifier tries chain-first, then originate-id lookup, then hash/title strategies."* A body carrying only `title` gets 400.
* **Cause:** the handler validates `title` as a string and never reads it — there is no title lookup strategy in `/verify`.
* Pre-existing; found by s193's KS-1103 probe (row E3) on develop `34be9c18a`, re-measured by s197 on `b1cb8466f`. **Not fixed this round.**

## Recommendation

* Decide the contract first: either implement a title strategy in `/verify` (the spec promises one), or remove `title` from `VerifyRequest` and the two descriptions so the spec stops promising it. Then make the 400 description list what is actually required.
* This is a product call (what a title-only verify should return — a title is not unique and proves no integrity), not a one-line fix.

## Detail

* **Spec, in** `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts` **at** `d63b27ab3` **(PR #965's head; unchanged from** `b1cb8466f`**):**
  * `:551-552` — the `VerifyRequest` description quoted above;
  * `:1915-1916` — the operation description: *"provide documentId, hash, title, or contentHash. Strategy: chain-first → originate-id lookup → hash/title fallback."*;
  * `:1944` — the 400 description: *"Missing verification input (no documentId / hash / documentData)"* — it does not list `title` either, so the spec contradicts itself on this field.
* **Handler,** `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` **at** `d63b27ab3`**:**
  * `:705` — `body('title').optional().isString()` is in the validator chain (KS-222);
  * `:735` — the destructure reads `documentId, providedHash, documentData, contentHash, documentHash, hash` — not `title`;
  * `:744-750` — a body with none of documentId / a hash alias / documentData answers 400. The handler has 0 reads of `req.body.title` (the four `title` occurrences in `:695-760` are a comment, the validator, a comment and the 400 message).
* **Measured:** `{title:'x'}` → 400, 0 lookups, on ks584-verify-row-selection's harness at develop `b1cb8466f` (s197 ITEM 0 probe, row E3; `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-13-s197/probes/`). The KS-1103 test pins this row at 400 on both sides of that fix (cell E3, status only) precisely because this ticket owns the title question.
* **History:** KS-222 (archived) put `title` into the validator chain with every other `VerifyRequest` field; nothing has ever read it. KS-1103 (PR #965) fixed the sibling case for `hash`, which HAD a lookup path; `title` has none.
* **Who is affected:** any integrator who follows the published description. The mobile app and the portals send hashes or ids, not a bare title (verify call sites: `mobile/secuura-app/src/services/api.ts:157-158`; `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127`).

### Dedupe

* **Census 1 (s193, 2026-09-12 05:4xZ):** literal, case-insensitive, over 1,100 KS issues (683 archived; title and description) and 2,954 comments (includeArchived). Positive control `hashToVerify` → KS-1103 (issue), KS-222 (comment). 0 hits for 'one or more of documentId', 'title strategies', 'title-only', 'title only', 'by id, hash, or title'. Weak hits, none covering it: 'hash/title' in a KS-474 comment (transfer snapshots); `VerifyRequest` on KS-627 (wallet verify contract) and KS-735.
* **Census 2 (s197, 2026-09-13 ~09:39 AEST), the delta since 2026-09-12T05:40Z:** searched `VerifyRequest`, `hashToVerify`, `originate.openapi.ts`, `routes/verification.ts`, the literal 'ONE OR MORE of documentId' and 'title-only' over 1 new KS issue (KS-1111) and 8 new KS comments — 0 hits each. Server-side all-time search for the two phrases: 0. Positive control (server-side `hashToVerify`) → KS-1103.
* **KS-735, opened whole:** it is about what the verify RESPONSE renders (registered title/issuer never displayed by the portal; the presented `fileName` discarded) — a different defect on the same contract. It never claims a title-only REQUEST should work. Not this ticket's home.
* **Result:** no existing home.

## Related

* KS-1103 — the `hash` sibling (PR #965).
* KS-222 (archived) — the validator chain.
* KS-735 — the verify-result display ticket on the same `VerifyRequest` contract.

title: Suggested: move platform-k (outside systemTest + observability) to TypeScript 7.0.2 — five current tools fail on TS 7 (tested), so they would be replaced first
description:
**Owner:** Kamil; the order of work is his call. **Raised:** 2026-09-30, split from [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). **Base:** `develop` @ `4f18c59a8`.
**Companion ticket:** [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) (Peter) covers `systemTest/` + `observability/`. The two tickets reference each other and never overlap.

## 1. Summary

**Suggestion (Peter, 2026-09-30): move the rest of platform-k to TypeScript 7.0.2**, the version systemTest and observability are moving to on [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). This ticket covers the rest of platform-k: 43 `package.json` files, 38 of them on TypeScript 5.x. Whether and when to move is Kamil's decision.

**We can't just change the TypeScript version number and keep our current tools.** Five of the tools we use today **stop working** when TypeScript 7 is installed. This was tested, not assumed (§2). Those tools have to be replaced (or, for tsup, fixed) before TypeScript 7 can go in. The replacements were tested too, and they work.

## 2. Why the tools have to change

### In plain English

The `typescript` package on npm has always contained two things:

1. **The compiler** (`tsc`): you run it to check and build code.
2. **A library**: other tools load it *inside their own code* to compile or check TypeScript for you. Our test runner, our script runner, our linter and our SDK bundler all work this way.

**TypeScript 7 is a rewrite, and it ships only the compiler. The library is gone.** In the `typescript@7.0.2` package the library exports exactly **2** things: `version` and `versionMajorMinor`. In 6.0.3 it exports **2,248**. Microsoft says a new, *different* library will come with TypeScript 7.1, and gives no date. The tools that depend on the old library would then have to be rewritten against the new one.

So any tool that loads TypeScript as a library crashes when TypeScript 7 is installed. It asks for functions that no longer exist. Nothing in our config can fix that, because the code the tool needs is not in the package.

### Proof: the same test on TypeScript 6 and TypeScript 7 (2026-09-30)

**Method:**

* Two fresh projects on Node 24.18.0, identical apart from the TypeScript version.
* Each tool at the version we use today.
* The same two-file source in each: one module and one test.
* Tools installed with `--legacy-peer-deps`, because npm refuses to install ts-jest next to TypeScript 7 at all.
* **TypeScript 6.0.3 is the control:** every tool must pass there, so that a failure on 7 can only be caused by 7.

| Tool (version we use) | What we use it for | Where | Its declared TypeScript support | **TypeScript 6.0.3** | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **typescript-eslint** 8.71 (parser) | Linting TypeScript | `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root | `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`: **excludes 7** | ✅ lints | ❌ `typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.` |
| **ts-jest** 29.4 + jest 29.7 | Running unit tests | governance, originate, referral, vc-issuer | `>=4.3 <7`: **excludes 7** (npm refuses the install) | ✅ 1/1 passed | ❌ `does not expose the JavaScript compiler API required by ts-jest` |
| **ts-node** 10.9 | Running `.ts` scripts | referral, vc-issuer, staking, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `deployment/cardano` | `>=2.7`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fileExists')` |
| **ts-node-dev** 2.0 | Dev server with reload | governance | `*`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ same `fileExists` crash (it runs ts-node underneath) |
| **tsup** 8.5 (`--dts`) | Building the SDK's type declarations | `sdk/javascript` | `>=4.5.0`: claims open support | ✅ `.d.ts` written\* | ❌ `TypeError … (reading 'useCaseSensitiveFileNames')`; no `.d.ts` |

\* **tsup has a second, separate problem.** Its d.ts step injects a `baseUrl` option that TypeScript 6 already rejects as deprecated (`TS5101`) and TypeScript 7 removes entirely. The control passed only with `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"`. tsup's JS build works on both versions; only the type-declaration step fails.

**Result: 5 of 5 tools pass on TypeScript 6 and fail on TypeScript 7.** Two of them say so up front in their declared ranges. The other three *claim* support but crash when run.

### Proof: the replacements work on TypeScript 7

| Replacement | Replaces | Loads the TypeScript library? | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **oxlint 1.86 + oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003** | typescript-eslint | No. Its own parser, plus TypeScript 7's Go compiler for type-aware rules | ✅ lints ([KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) spike: 4 harnesses, 9/9 planted checks) |
| **Vitest 5.0.3** | ts-jest + jest | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ 1/1 passed |
| **tsx 4.23.15** | ts-node, ts-node-dev | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ ran |
| **tsc 7.0.2** itself | — | — | ✅ type-checks the same source clean |

## 3. Options (Kamil's call)

| Option | What it means | Trade-off |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **1. Replace the tools, then TypeScript 7.0.2** (this plan) | typescript-eslint → oxlint; ts-jest → Vitest; ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx; fix or replace tsup's d.ts step | Same TypeScript version as [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). The most work, but every replacement is proven above |
| **2. Keep the tools, run two TypeScripts side by side** | TypeScript 7 for `tsc`; TypeScript 6 installed under the name `typescript` for the tools. ts-jest's own error message recommends this | Two compilers in one tree, which can disagree. **Unproven:** the TypeScript 7 package name ts-jest suggests, `@typescript/native`, **does not exist on npm** (checked 2026-09-30); `@typescript/typescript6` does (6.0.2). Needs its own proof first |
| **3. Stay on TypeScript 6.0.3 for now** | Bump 5.x → 6.0.3, which every current tool supports; revisit when the tools support TypeScript 7.1's new library | The least work now, a second migration later. Leaves platform-k on two TypeScript versions (6.0.3 here, 7.0.2 in systemTest/observability) |

## 4. Scope

**In scope: everything in platform-k except** `systemTest/` **and** `observability/`**.** That is 43 tracked `package.json` files: the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace (services, packages, frontends, sdk, tests, connectors, deployment) and `secuura-website-package`.

**Out of scope:** `systemTest/` and `observability/` → [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint).

## 5. The work, in the proposed order (Option 1)

1. **Linting:** `Blockchain/Dev` root typescript-eslint → oxlint + tsgolint.
2. **Tests:** Jest / ts-jest → Vitest in governance, originate, referral and vc-issuer. [KS-1051](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1051/develop-is-red-on-the-servicesoriginate-jest-suite-and-nothing-catches): originate's Jest suite is already red on `develop`. Also `sdk/javascript` Vitest 1 → 5, and the rest of Vitest 4 → 5.
3. **Scripts:** ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx in the six packages above.
4. **SDK types:** fix or replace tsup's d.ts step (both problems in §2).
5. **TypeScript 5 → 7.0.2**, in batches that each build clean with `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` ([KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and) shows how easily lock drift breaks a clean build). Review [KS-920](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-920/shared-ships-the-typescript-compiler-and-a-267-mb-dev-tree-into-all-24) alongside this: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into 24 runtime images, and TypeScript 7's compiler is a native per-platform binary.
6. **Playwright → 1.63.0** in the `Blockchain/Dev` root (^1.61.1; workspace-root lock), `tests/e2e` (^1.40.0, **npm-deprecated**) and `tests/e2e-v2` (1.58.2; `RUNBOOK.md:26` ties it to a cached chromium). title: KS-926 residue: the three guards that could NOT be wired, and what each needs first — a wrong diff base, a self-contradicting default, and a whole-machine read
description:
**From KS-926.** Fourteen of the seventeen unreached guards were wired. **These three were not, and each needs a fix before it can be** — recorded so the next reader inherits the reasoning rather than re-deriving it. All three reasons are measured, at `fe0fd640c`.

## 1. `check-no-demo-mutation.sh` — WRONG DIFF BASE for this branching model

Line 58 defaults to `BASE="origin/main"` and diffs `BASE...HEAD`. **Under Git Flow,** `develop` **is permanently ahead of** `main`, so every develop-based branch shows the whole develop↔main delta as its own change.

**Measured on a branch that touched nothing:** it reported 4 demo files as modified —
`deployment/azure/env.demo.json`, `migrate/Dockerfile`, `migrate/init.sql`, `migrate/run-platform.sh`.

**Fix:** base it on the merge-base with `origin/develop` (or on `GITHUB_BASE_REF` when set, which it already honours at line 51-52). Wired as-is it would demand `[demo-mutation-allowed]` from every author on every push — a `--no-verify` generator.

## 2. `check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` — its printed advice contradicts its own default

Line 48: `level="${TRUST_HEADER_LINT_MODE:-fail}"` — **the default is** `fail`**.**
Line 60, printed to the user: *"Set* `TRUST_HEADER_LINT_MODE=fail` *to switch this from warn to a hard CI gate once cleanup is complete."*

**It tells you to set a variable to the value it already has**, and describes itself as a warn-mode lint when it is a hard gate. Verified three ways: `warn` → exit 0, `fail` → exit 1, unset → **exit 1**.

**Fix:** one of — correct the message to match the default, or make the default `warn` and the message true. **Deciding which is the point**, not a formality: it is red with 9 real findings (its own ticket), so the default decides whether wiring it freezes the repo.

## 3. `check-container-isolation.sh` — not a property of the tree

It reads **whole-machine Docker state** (`docker ps -a`, `docker network ls`). Here it failed on:

* **another session's containers, days old** — `ks597-qa-pg`, `qa-ks800-wabot-negctl`, `qa-ks800-wabot-guarded`, `secuura-queue`, `secuura-guardian`
* having only **1** platform stack up, which it itself calls a *"vacuous"* comparison

**A pre-push gate that reds on a colleague's stale container is exactly the** `--no-verify` **generator KS-926 warns about.** Its home is stack start-up (`start-local.sh` / `start-environment.sh`, where `check-slot-credentials.sh` already lives), not the push.

## Where they are recorded now

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh`, `DEFERRED` bucket — each with its reason inline. The census counts them as accounted-for, so they do not fail the push, and they cannot be silently forgotten either: removing one from the bucket without wiring it fails the census.

title: Gate C follow-ups for KS-1543/KS-1462: two unpinned behaviours + one log describer
description:
## BLUF

Gate C (the Opus gate on PR #1560 / KS-1543 and PR #1561 / KS-1462, 2026-10-18) passed both as **GO WITH NOTE, 0 blocking**, and left three follow-ups on one path: two behaviours no in-repo cell pins (each proved by a mutant that survived the whole service suite), and one log line that still describes a thrown plain object as `[object Object]`. Nothing is broken: the product is right in all three places. This ticket carries the gate's cells so they can be built as test-first patches.

## Recommendation

Three small test-first changes, briefed to the Spark queue (Wednesday briefs them), each gated like any other:

1. A multi-chunk reply cell for the forward's drain (kills M1c).
2. A three-tenant cell for migrate-tenant-data (kills M4e).
3. The fail500-shaped describer for the :1579 log line, with a plain-object red.

## Detail

* **LOW-1560-1, test gap:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1068`**.** No in-repo cell pins "the reply is fully drained". Mutant **M1c** (`proxyRes.on('data', () => { proxyRes.pause(); })`) survived the whole api-gateway suite (1165/1165), because the only cell that reads the forward's `end` (ks1087, "KS-1183 — a forward that completed…") uses a one-chunk reply, which still emits `end` after a pause. The gate's own probe (a 4 MB reply and a slow chunked reply) killed it. **Fix shape:** a multi-chunk reply cell.
* **LOW-1561-1, test gap (pre-existing):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:2237`**.** Every cell, new and existing (KS-1334 C), uses ONE tenant, so "the loop goes on to the next tenant" is unpinned. Mutant **M4e** (`break;` after the per-tenant `results.push`) survived the whole originate suite; the gate's 3-tenant probe killed it (11/11). **Fix shape:** a 3-tenant cell, the middle tenant throwing.
* **INFO-1560-2:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1579`**.** The document-types log line added by #1560 describes errors as `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`, the file's existing shape at :1420. A thrown plain object logs `"[object Object]"` and `null` logs `"null"` (measured by the gate). That is the defect #1561 removes in originate. No secret leaked in the gate's probe. **Candidate fix:** the fail500-shaped describer (an Error by message, a string as is, any other object by type and field names, never field values). Same class as KS-1346 (the fail500 family; its describer is already in api-gateway's own `routes/batch.ts:24-29`, the shape to copy, but it never covered this `:1579` site) and KS-1462 item 2 (one shared describer). *Corrected 2026-10-18 by Seat R 47th: this line first said KS-1346 does not reach api-gateway, inferred from KS-1346's text; the code says otherwise.*

**Source:** the gate C verdict, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-18_gate-C-pr1560-pr1561/verdict.md` (Wednesday's project), sha256/16 `953a123d0cdf7f75` computed with line 3 deleted. PRs: [#1560](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1560>), [#1561](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1561>).

**Dedupe before filing:** over all 1,607 team issues including archived, titles and descriptions, 0 hits each for `Gate C`, `LOW-1560-1`, `LOW-1561-1`, `INFO-1560-2`, `M1c`, `M4e`, `multi-chunk`, `fully drained`, `next tenant`, `verification.ts:1579`, `adminConfig.ts:2237`. Positive controls on the same data: `KS-1543|ESLint warnings in routes/verification` 2 hits, `migrate-tenant-data` 2 hits, so the instrument reads ticket text. `[object Object]` hits KS-1614, KS-1542, KS-1462, KS-1410, KS-1346; none of them names verification.ts:1579, :1068 or adminConfig.ts:2237.

Filed by Seat R 47th on Wednesday's GO of 2026-10-18T08:29:41Z. Not built this session.
