KS-1547 follow-up (PR #1552 gate): the empty/non-digit denominator abort is pinned by no test (3 surviving mutants), the abort text drops a non-digit tail, and 3/16/17 is now accepted
description:
## BLUF

Follow-up to **KS-1547** (merged as `0bb4f17ca` via PR #1552). The Opus gate found **no product defect**: all 16 real leg headers behave identically before and after. It did find **three LOW items**, and the main one is a test gap. **The abort for an empty or non-digit denominator (**`3/`**,** `3/x`**) is pinned by no test anywhere in the tree.** Every non-digit header now takes that path. Filed on Wednesday's ruling (GO of 2026-10-15T06:30:31Z). None of these blocks; all are cheap.

Source: gate A verdict, `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-15_gate-A-pr1552-pr1554/verdict.md` in Wednesday's project, report sha256/16 `a99632143f942387`.

## The items (from the verdict; file:line on develop after the merge)

1. **Test gap: three mutants survived the new suite.** Cells: `scripts/__tests__/ks1547_preflight_step_header_denominator.test.sh:56-68`.
   * **N7**, `[ "$_hdr_total" -ne "$TOTAL_LEGS" ] 2>/dev/null`: a numeric compare lets `3/` and `3/x` THROUGH. It also survived all 8 `preflight_*` sibling suites, so this abort is pinned nowhere. That was already true before KS-1547.
   * **N5**, `%%[[:space:]:]*`: a separator list instead of "non-digit". It survives because the suite covers only TAB and colon.
   * **N4**, `%%[!1-9]*`: a digit class without 0. It survives because `TOTAL_LEGS=16` has no 0, and it would break a future 10 or 20 total.
   * **Suggested cells** (the gate's): `3/` aborts; `3/x` aborts; `3/16)` is accepted; one case with a denominator containing 0.
2. **Message fidelity**, `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:225,228,231`. A non-digit denominator now prints an empty one: `step "3/x"` printed `says /x` before and prints `says /` now. The same happens for `3/+16`, `3/-16` and Arabic-Indic digits. It still aborts, and the full header is quoted in the same line, so this is cosmetic. A fix could quote the raw tail as well as the parsed digits.
3. **A widening to decide, not a defect**, `preflight.sh:225`. Every header whose denominator is 16 followed by any non-digit is now accepted: `3/16x`, `3/16.5  T`, and `3/16/17  T` (a doubled or stale denominator). All of these aborted before. That is what "up to the first non-digit" means. `3/16/17` is the case a reviewer might not expect. If it should abort, require the digits to be followed by whitespace or end-of-string.

## Done when

Items 1 and 2 have cells that go red on the named mutants (red-first proven), and item 3 is either pinned as intended or tightened.

title: KS-1542 follow-up (PR #1554 gate): Map/Set/RegExp/Error print {}, {toJSON:()=>1} prints an accepted bound, String() throws before the catch, and a [1n] cell would kill the surviving catch mutant
description:
## BLUF

Follow-up to **KS-1542** (merged as `18de4b7ce` via PR #1554). The Opus gate found **no product defect against the stated goal**: every probed object shape is still REFUSED, and arrays and plain objects now print as JSON. It found **LOW message-fidelity items and one test gap**. All are capped at LOW because **no production caller passes** `originateForwardTimeoutMs`: `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:898` builds the routes without it, so only tests or a future wiring can reach this message. Filed on Wednesday's ruling (GO of 2026-10-15T06:30:31Z).

Source: gate A verdict, `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-15_gate-A-pr1552-pr1554/verdict.md` in Wednesday's project, report sha256/16 `a99632143f942387`.

## The items (from the verdict; `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` on develop after the merge)

1. **Information loss,** `:153-155`**.** `Map`, `Set`, `RegExp` and `Error` all print `{}`, losing both type and content, and they collide with a plain `{}`:
   * `new Map([['ms',800]])` printed `[object Map]` before;
   * `new Set([800])` printed `[object Set]`;
   * `/800/g` printed `/800/g`;
   * `Error('x')` printed `Error: x`.

   A config value from env, JSON or YAML cannot be one of these, so the impact is small. But for RegExp and Error it is a strict regression in wording.
2. **Collisions the new branch introduces,** `:155`**.**
   * An invalid `Date` prints `null`, the same text as a literal `null` refusal (it printed `Invalid Date` before).
   * `{toJSON: () => 1}` **prints** `1`**, the text of an ACCEPTED bound.** That breaks the PR's own stated invariant ("no refused bound may print what an accepted bound prints"); it printed `[object Object]` before.
   * `{toJSON: () => undefined}` prints `undefined` at runtime, although `shown` is typed `string`.
3. **Pre-existing, but the new catch looks like its cure and is not,** `:152`**.** `String(value)` runs BEFORE the object branch, so for `Object.create(null)` and a revoked Proxy, `String()` itself throws a `TypeError` that does not name `originateForwardTimeoutMs`. The value is still refused, but with the wrong message, and the try/catch at `:154-158` never gets the chance.
4. **Test gap.** Mutant M2 survived: the catch printing `String(value)` instead of `Object.prototype.toString.call(value)`. The only catch cell uses a plain-object cycle, where both give `[object Object]`. **A** `[1n]` **cell would kill it:** `String([1n])` is `1` (accepted text), and the type tag is `[object Array]`. The product comment names "a BigInt inside" as a reason for the catch, but no test covers it. Cells: `src/__tests__/ks1185-f1-workflow-approve-forward-bound-is-validated.test.ts:160-165`.

Also noted, not new: the message is unbounded (a 20,000-element array prints \~80 KB, before and after).

## Done when

The `{toJSON: () => 1}` case no longer prints an accepted bound's text, which is the PR's own invariant. A `[1n]` cell kills M2. The `String()` throw at `:152` either cannot happen or names the property. Item 1 is either pinned as acceptable or given a type-aware rendering.

title: originate migrate-tenant-data: a non-Error throw logs as [object Object], and the per-tenant error is a bare string (PR #1460 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Two **Minor** notes from the Opus QA gate on PR #1460 (KS-1334's fifth site, merged as `ba697cf3d4218383491391ed8fd280a2486d6f86`). Both sit in the per-tenant catch of `POST /api/admin/migrate-tenant-data`. They were left out of #1460 on purpose: a change to the gated head would have voided the GO. There are no consumers of this route's response (no spec entry, no frontend, no doc), so the change has no known blast radius.

title: fail500 family: a non-Error throw is logged as [object Object], so its content is lost from the log
description:
## BLUF

The `fail500` family helper logs a **non-Error** throw as `'[object Object]'`, so the thrown object's content is **lost from the log** — the body stays correctly constant, but the diagnosability the helper exists to preserve is gone. Measured at runtime by the gate29 probe on the routes #1290 converted.

## Detail

`fail500(res, context, err)` logs `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`. `String({...})` is `'[object Object]'`. So:

* an **Error** throw logs its message — correct;
* a **string** throw logs itself — correct;
* an **object** throw logs `[object Object]` — the content is gone.

At the merge-base neither kind leaked, because `err.message` on a non-Error is `undefined`; the helper is what made the log the only place the detail could live, and for objects it does not live there either.

**Fix shape:** in the family helper, log `err` itself, or `JSON.stringify` / `util.inspect` it for non-Errors.

**Family:** this is the same helper shape merged for KS730 in `routes/gdpr.ts` and `routes/systemErrors.ts`, so a fix belongs in all of them rather than in `webhooks.ts` alone.

## Also not pinned by the shipped cell (gate29 N-1290-3, measured: all green at head)

* (a) **non-Error throws** (string / object) on the three routes part B converted;
* (b) **rotate-secret throwing AFTER** `newSecret` **exists** — a rejected `$executeRaw` UPDATE, with the real `encryptField` and the key loaded. The gate probe drove this (S1) and measured the new secret **absent** from the 500 body and from every logger call, with a positive control — so today's behaviour is safe, but **no committed cell pins it**;
* (c) the **secret's absence from every log level** as an assertion.

## Done when

- [ ] the family helper preserves a non-Error throw's content in the log, in every file carrying the helper

title: systemTest (all tools): enable nightly platform test suites after full AWS migration
description:
## Reminder: re-enable the nightly system-test suites once we have fully migrated to AWS

The nightly platform test suites (Schemathesis, Playwright, Performance, Akto) are currently **disabled** — the workflow only runs on manual `workflow_dispatch`. They were prepared to run on a daily schedule but the `schedule:` cron is commented out pending the AWS migration.

### What to do when AWS migration is complete

1. In `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml`, **uncomment the** `schedule:` **block** to re-enable the daily trigger:

   ```yaml
   schedule:
     - cron: '0 14 * * *'   # 14:00 UTC — ~midnight Sydney, 22:00 Singapore
   ```
2. Re-point any `--env`/base-URL config from the local isolated stacks to the AWS targets if the nightly is meant to hit AWS rather than a fresh ghcr build.
3. Flip the STATUS header comment in the workflow back to **LIVE**.
4. Confirm the four suite check-runs appear and the shared `build` → fan-out topology still holds.

### Context

* Start time chosen: **14:00 UTC** (≈ midnight Sydney AEST/AEDT year-round, 22:00 Singapore SGT).
* All four suites already start **simultaneously** off the single schedule (each `needs: [prep, build]`), so enabling the one cron enables all four together.
* The Performance job runs a single isolated stack with all scenarios **serial**: smoke → auth-spike → (15m 429 cooldown) → smoke → spike → (15m) → smoke → stress → (15m) → smoke → scalability → (15m) → smoke → nightly soak (~4h4m). ⚠ ~5.9–6.1h total — near GitHub's 6h/job cap; re-check headroom on the AWS runners.
* Everything stays **report-only** (`continue-on-error`); no merge gating.
* Prepared on branch `feature/nightly-schedule-perf-sequence`.

title: CI: require all systemTest (all tools) PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)
description:
## Goal

Make **every** systemTest PR suite **and** the pre-merge tests actually **block a merge on failure**. The workflow YAML already runs each suite to completion and then hard-fails its check (complete-then-block); what's missing is the **settings half** — a red check only prevents merge when branch protection marks it **Required**, and a check is matched by its **check-run display name**, not its job id. The pre-merge gate specifically must be a **manual human approval** (not an auto-pass).

## Background (already in place, code side)

`.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` (build-once → isolated per-suite stacks) runs each suite `continue-on-error` then an Enforce step fails the required check on any failure:

* **Schemathesis** — blocking spec-auth ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)) + pytest ([KS-126](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-126/schemathesis-pytest-suite-runs-only-ad-hoc-locally-wire-it-into-ci-dev)) + offline quality/unit gate; [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) auth sweep stays informational by design.
* **Playwright** — blocking `quality:check` + `npm run ci`.
* **Performance** — quality/unit gate + k6 smoke, complete-then-block.
* **Akto** — quality/unit gate + PR-gate scan, complete-then-block via step-outcome (emits Allure, not JUnit).

## Tasks (settings — cannot be code)

1. **Branch protection ruleset — mark these check-run display names Required** (match by display name, not job id):
   * `build`
   * `Schemathesis suite`
   * `Playwright suite`
   * `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`
   * `Akto suite (PR-gate subset)`
     Require `build` too — in the build-once topology a `build` failure **skips** the suite jobs, so confirm a required-but-skipped check does not wedge the PR (skipped ≠ stuck).
2. **Pre-merge must be a MANUAL human-approval gate — no auto-pass.** The comprehensive `run.py pre-merge` sweep (`pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`) must require a designated human to **manually click Approve** before the PR can merge; it must never pass on its own.
   * Implement via the GitHub `pre-merge-signoff` **Environment** with **required reviewers** (an Environment reviewer *is* a manual Approve/Reject gate): pin the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` job to that Environment so the run **pauses and waits** for a human decision, and no merge proceeds until a reviewer manually approves. GitHub → Settings → Environments → `pre-merge-signoff` → add required reviewers (start with @peter).
   * Mark the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` check **Required** in the branch-protection ruleset so the manual approval is enforced, not advisory.
   * Per CLAUDE.md, "PR checks green" is **not** the pre-merge sign-off — a human must have run/confirmed the comprehensive pre-merge sweep and then manually approved.

## Notes / carve-outs

* Two deliberate non-blocking exceptions stay as-is: the rate-limited [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) Schemathesis auth sweep (429 back-off would flap the gate) and **all nightly** runs (report-only soak).
* This ticket is GitHub **settings** work; no systemTest code change is required (the YAML is already complete-then-block, and the sign-off job already targets the `pre-merge-signoff` Environment — it just needs reviewers + to be Required). Verify on a draft PR: all five suite checks Required and red-on-failure blocks merge, and the merge stays blocked until a human manually approves the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate.

---

## Precondition: the pre-merge ack checkboxes have no not-applicable path (added 2026-09-09)

**Close this before** `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` **is set to** `true`**, or turning enforcement on will require a false attestation on any PR that legitimately needs neither suite.**

`.github/pull_request_template.md` seeds two boxes under the heading **"Pre-merge acknowledgment (author)"**, instructing: *"Tick each box **only after** you have run that suite's pre-merge tier and it passed"*. `.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml` ([KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling)) matches **only**:

```
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:schemathesis-->
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:akto-->
```

A tick, or nothing. No N/A marker, no label escape, no "suite not applicable" branch. So for an offline shell gate, a docs change or a workflow tweak, the only ways to satisfy the check are to tick a box asserting a sweep that did not happen, or to leave a box that reads as an omission.

**The exemption pattern already exists in that workflow** — drafts pass green unconditionally (`if [ "${DRAFT}" = "true" ]`). And the template models the right affordance one section down, in the PII block: *"Not applicable? Say so explicitly rather than leaving the boxes blank — a blank box reads as 'not checked', which is the state this section exists to make visible."* The ack section has no equivalent.

**How it surfaced.** PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) ([KS-778](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-778/preflight-leg-10s-pin-label-parser-is-blind-to-a-quoted-uses-and-an)) changes exactly one file — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/action-pins-labelled.sh`, an offline shell gate that reads `.github/` with `git grep` and prints to stdout. Measured: **0 of 1** changed files fall under `services/`, `frontend/`, `packages/`, `migrations/`, `contracts/`, `systemTest/`, any compose file or any `.env`, so neither pre-merge suite exercises anything in it. Both boxes were left unticked with the reason stated inline, following the PII section's pattern — a workaround, not a fix; the workflow still counts it as un-acknowledged.

**Not urgent today:** enforcement is soft by default (the repository Variable `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` is unset ⇒ warn + pass), and the workflow has not executed since 2026-08-17. It becomes live the moment task 2 above is actioned.

### Fix — one of these, not all

1. **An N/A marker** the workflow recognises, e.g. `<!--ack:schemathesis:na-->`, requiring a stated reason on the same line. Smallest, keeps the human in the loop, and mirrors the PII section so the template gains one convention rather than two. The assertion becomes "I considered this suite and it does not apply" — a true statement, still auditable.
2. **A label escape**, e.g. a `no-premerge-suites` PR label that passes both ack checks, reviewable in itself.
3. **A path-based skip** — passes when the diff touches nothing the suites cover. Most automatic, but duplicates suite-scope knowledge into the workflow and will drift.

### Done means

* A PR that legitimately needs neither suite passes both ack checks **without** anyone ticking a box that asserts an unrun sweep.
* The escape requires a stated reason — an acknowledgment, not a bypass. A blank body still fails.
* Red→green with `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK=true`: a PR using the new form passes; the same PR with the reason removed fails. Proven both ways.
* Template instruction text updated to describe the not-applicable path, in the shape the PII block already uses.
* Ticking a box still means what it says today — this must not weaken the positive assertion.

*Provenance: template and workflow read at* `dbe7ba6b3` *(PR* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) *head), 2026-09-09; last workflow execution 2026-08-17 via* `gh run list --workflow=pr-premerge-ack.yml`*; surfaced at [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/921#issuecomment-5602690418](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/921#issuecomment-5602690418>)*

title: A connector restricted by allowedDocumentTypes can still create the default DOCUMENT type by sending no type (#1014 gate N-4)
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing, Minor: a connector restricted by an allow-list can still create a document of the DEFAULT type** by sending no type at all. An untyped body from a key restricted to `['SSD_DOCUMENT']` answers 201. The gateway resolves no type and forwards it, and originate (READ) stores it as `DOCUMENT`, which is outside the allow-list. 16 rows (8 on array configs), identical at base, round 1, head and merged.

## Recommendation

Not built. Owner's choice: apply the allow-list to the resolved default type, or require a restricted connector to name a type.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 round-2 delta gate on PR #1014 (KS-1176), finding **N-4** (a residue of the F-1 class). Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014r2-9ba0caf78-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* **Evidence:** the gateway is MEASURED; originate's default type is READ only (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:565`).
* **Shapes (8), each 201:** from `sk_restricted_SSD`, enforcement resolved no type and the body was forwarded:
  * untyped;
  * `documentType: ''`;
  * `type: ''`;
  * the ignored keys `DocumentType`, `document_type` and `Type`;
  * `__proto__.type`;
  * an untyped `data` carrier.
* **Layer:** at the gateway no type is created, so this is not a gateway admission of a disallowed type; at originate the type is DOCUMENT.
* The PR's own F4 cell cannot see it, because its allow-list contains the default.

### Dedupe before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches over title, description and comments:

* `stored as DOCUMENT`: 120 / 0.
* `untyped`: 6 / 5. KS-1176 comments (this gate's records), KS-1198 (the connector-JWT path), KS-1022/518/993 (unrelated).
* `allowedDocumentTypes`: 4 / 1. KS-1198 (the connector-JWT path; not the default type).

None covers this.

Related: KS-1176.

title: The approve-forward bound refusal still prints a refused array or object ambiguously: [1] reads (got 1), [] reads (got )
description:
## BLUF

After PR 1519 (KS-1518, the message half) the approve-forward bound refusal tells `1n` from `1` and `-0` from `0`, but it still prints every other non-string value with `String()`, so a refused **array or object** reads ambiguously: a refused `[1]` prints `(got 1)`, the very ambiguity of `1n`; `[]` prints `(got )`; `{}` prints `(got [object Object])`. Ruled by Wednesday (2026-10-12) to be ticketed on its own rather than folded into PR 1519, whose gate is told to check that nothing beyond `1n` and `-0` changes.

## Recommendation

P4. Print a refused non-primitive with `JSON.stringify` (guarded: a circular value throws, so fall back to a type tag such as `[object Object]` only in that case), and extend the property cell that PR 1519 adds (`no two refused bounds print the same value in the message`, in `ks1185-f1-workflow-approve-forward-bound-is-validated.test.ts`) with rows `[1]`, `[]`, `{}`, `[1,2]`. Test first: `[1]` prints the text of the VALID bound `1`, so besides distinctness the cell should assert that no refused bound prints the text of an accepted one (`1`, `800`, `2147483647`).

## Detail

* **MEASURED** (Node 24, the same `String()` the code uses): `1n` prints `1`, `0n` prints `0`, `-0` prints `0`, `[1]` prints `1`, `[]` prints nothing, `{}` prints `[object Object]`, a Symbol prints `Symbol(s)`, `2n ** 64n` prints `18446744073709551616`. The first three are what PR 1519 fixes; `[1]`, `[]` and `{}` are this ticket.
* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, `resolveOriginateForwardTimeoutMs`, the `shown` line (line 148 at develop `898a1ae11f3c`, before PR 1519 merges).
* **How reachable:** only by a future caller. `index.ts` passes no `originateForwardTimeoutMs` (a grep of the non-test sources finds the name only inside `verification.ts`), so a running gateway cannot produce this message today.
* **Related:** KS-1518, KS-1185 (the validation that introduced the message).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles AND descriptions in team KS, archived included: `originateForwardTimeoutMs` 2 (KS-1518 and KS-1185; neither description mentions arrays: `array` 0 hits in both), `[object Object]` 3 (KS-1462, KS-1410, KS-1346, all about non-Error throws in logs and 500 bodies, a different defect), `(got )` 0, `String([` 0. The same instrument returns KS-1518 for a phrase from its own title (`refusal message cannot tell`), so it can see ticket text.

## Carried over from KS-1518 (Wednesday's ruling, 2026-10-12)

KS-1518 closed with two gate notes still open. They move here because this ticket will touch the same test file (`ks1185-f1-workflow-approve-forward-bound-is-validated.test.ts`) when it is built.

- [ ] **Fix the BigInt cell's title.** `RED KS-1518 - a BigInt bound (1n) is refused at construction, because Number.isInteger refuses every non-number, and the message says 1n, not 1` overstates its reason: a mutant that rejects every non-number up front stays green, so the cell pins the refusal and not the reason. PR 1519 carried the title forward unchanged. Reword it to say what it pins.
- Informational: **the error type is not asserted** (the guard has one throw site, `resolveOriginateForwardTimeoutMs`, so there is only one type to check). Assert it when the cells are next edited, or leave it.

title: preflight step() reads the leg denominator up to the first space: a TAB or colon after it would cause a false PREFLIGHT ABORT (latent)
description:
## BLUF

The preflight's `step()` reads the leg count out of its header with `${_hdr_total%% *}`, which cuts at the first **space**. A header whose denominator is followed by a **TAB or any non-space character** (`3/16<TAB>Title`, `3/16:Title`) leaves that tail in the value, so the comparison with `TOTAL_LEGS` fails and the whole preflight **ABORTs with a message blaming the header count** that is actually correct. **Latent: all 16 current headers have a space after the denominator.** This is record R-925-A of KS-1153 (the L7 gate's SHIPS-WITH records), ruled by Wednesday (2026-10-12) to be filed on its own as P4 when KS-1153 was closed as records.

## Recommendation

P4, one line plus a cell. Cut the denominator at the first non-digit instead of the first space: `_hdr_total="${_hdr_total%%[!0-9]*}"`. Test first: a cell that feeds `step` a TAB-tailed and a colon-tailed header and asserts it does NOT abort (and a control that a genuinely wrong denominator still aborts, so the check is not weakened).

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:173` (`_hdr_total="${1#*/}"; _hdr_total="${_hdr_total%% *}"`), the comparison at `:174`, the abort text at `:176-179`. Read at develop `425ad3e00ae4`.
* **MEASURED** on that exact expression in bash: header `3/16 Title` gives `_hdr_total=[16]` (equal); `3/16<TAB>Title` gives `[16<TAB>Title]` (not equal); `3/16:Title` gives `[16:Title]` (not equal).
* **Why it is latent:** `step "N/16  Title"` is called 16 times and every one has a space right after the denominator (16 of 16 matched `step "[0-9]+/[0-9]+ `, 0 other).
* **Consequence if it happened:** a false `PREFLIGHT ABORTED — step header ... says /16<TAB>Title but TOTAL_LEGS=16`, which blocks every push until the header is "fixed" although it is right. It fails safe (loudly), so it is a polish item.
* **Related:** KS-1153 (the records this came from), KS-1046 (the verdict ratio the parse protects).
* **Dedupe before filing (Wednesday's condition):** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles AND descriptions in team KS, archived included: `R-925-A` 1, `_hdr_total` 1, `header parse` 1 (all three KS-1153 itself, the origin of this record), `step header` 0, `TOTAL_LEGS` 0, `TAB or no-space` 0. The same instrument returns KS-1153 for a phrase from its own title (`nested-guard basename resolution`), so it can see ticket text. No other ticket carries it.

title: package_format_gate.test.sh: five REAL-npm cells INTERMITTENT - red once in the full shell run (430/5), green twice run alone (435/0, develop and a branch)
description:
## BLUF

Five `REAL npm` cells in `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` went **red once** inside a full `npm run test:shell` run (**430 passed / 5 failed**), then **passed in both of two direct runs** (**435 passed / 0 failed**), one on develop and one on a branch. So the defect, if there is one, is **intermittent**, not "on develop". No harm today: these cells fail closed (a red refuses a push, it never lets one through). They are filed rather than dismissed because one red in three runs is not "flaky, proven", and a cell that reds without a code change will be read as a regression by whoever hits it next.

Filed by Seat R 45th (raise lane), 2026-10-15, on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER 02:31:25Z, Q2 (ii)).

## The three runs

All three ran in one clone of `Secuura/Distributed_Secuura` on the same machine, with the same `node_modules` (`npm ci` rc 0, 1937 packages). Run 1 left `TMPDIR` to the runner's own handling; runs 2 and 3 set a short `TMPDIR=/tmp/r45ab` and unset git's local env.

| run | tree | how | package_format_gate |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | branch `762d044b0` (KS-1547: a one-line `preflight.sh` change; this suite does not read `preflight.sh`) | inside `npm run test:shell`, all 89 suites back to back, 02:15–02:24Z | **430 passed, 5 failed** |
| 2 | same branch, `762d044b0` | `bash systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` alone, 02:25Z | **435 passed, 0 failed** |
| 3 | develop `e67e0dc1916b954a53c40db68ea81f0f905de641` | same, alone, 02:27Z | **435 passed, 0 failed** |

So the five did not reproduce on either tree when the suite ran on its own.

## The five cells, verbatim from run 1

```
FAIL REAL npm with a hanging postinstall: REFUSED as a timeout
       want "1/1", got "0/0"
FAIL ...no node_modules in the package, no stage
       want "no/0", got "yes/0"
FAIL ...so the listener was contacted and the script ran (the earlier 0 was the gate, not the fixture)
       want "1/yes", got "1/no"
FAIL the install's npm userconfig is the stage's private HOME, not the developer's ~/.npmrc
       want "1/0", got "0/0"
FAIL ...while it does see what npm and the shell need (PATH, npm_lifecycle_event, npm_config_cache)
       want "yes/yes/yes", got "no/no/no"
```

All five read `ok` in runs 2 and 3.

## What is and is not established

* **Established:** the five reds are not caused by the KS-1547 change. Runs 2 and 3 give the same result on its branch and on develop.
* **Not established:** the cause. Three readings fit, and I have not separated them:
  1. **Load or timing.** Every one of the five spawns a real `npm` and reads a timeout, a listener, or the staged env. Run 1 ran it as suite 60-something of 89 back to back, and the J-lane seat was live on the same machine.
  2. **Interference between suites.** Something an earlier suite leaves behind in run 1, such as a lingering listener, a port, an npm cache entry, or a leaked env var, could make the later suite misread.
  3. **The KS-1396 change.** KS-1396 (merged into develop as `e67e0dc1`) moved `systemTest` to TypeScript 7.0.2 and oxlint and removed ESLint there. It is the most recent change to this tree. **Named as a candidate only, not measured.** Runs 2 and 3 were on trees that already contain it and were green, so it is not enough on its own.

## What would settle it

Run the full `npm run test:shell` N times (N ≥ 5) on an idle machine and count the five cells. Then run `package_format_gate.test.sh` alone N times under a synthetic CPU load. If it reds only in the full run, the cause is interference between suites. If it reds alone under load, it is timing, and the fix is the cell's timeout margin.

## Related, not duplicates (searched first)

The search covered title and description, archived issues included, and was controlled: a fresh nonce returned 0 hits and `preflight_test_types_ratchet_leg` returned 3. `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate`, `hanging postinstall`, `REFUSED as a timeout`, `npm userconfig is the stage`, `npm_lifecycle_event`, `listener was contacted`, `no node_modules in the package` and `REAL npm` all returned **0**. `package_format_gate` returned **KS-1063** (Done, a different defect: a gate that examined nothing exits 0). `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL` returned **KS-1583** (Backlog, the KS-998 item 1 gate's six Minors, a different defect).

title: similarity-undiscriminating FP entries have no staleness detection — a tolerance can outlive its premise and keep hiding a real finding
description:
## BLUF

`similarity-undiscriminating` **false-positive entries have no staleness detection, so a tolerance can outlive the condition that justified it and silently keep hiding a real finding.** Raised by @peter in his systemTest review of [PR #783](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/783>) (2026-09-02 14:25Z). Not a blocker for that PR — a decision in its own right.

## The asymmetry

The endpoint-scoped false-positive table has two kinds, and they are guarded very differently:

| kind | offline spec check | live probe that goes red when stale |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `public-by-design` | yes | **yes** — `publicEndpointGuard.ts` fires an unauthenticated request at each entry; a 401/403 means the endpoint now enforces auth, so the suppression is stale |
| `similarity-undiscriminating` | yes | **no** — nothing ever re-measures the null attack |

Measured on the local stack 2026-09-02 while confirming #783: the guard probes **3 **`public-by-design` entries (all 200 = `public`, 0 stale) and skips all **5** similarity entries — and the control run shows each of those five returns **401**, which the classifier would call `stale`. So the kind gate is correct and necessary; it also means the similarity arm has no live evidence rule at all.

## Why it matters

The five entries carry measured `percentageMatch` figures — 35.9%, 37.5%, **0%**, 12.32%, 16.67% — and every one is **a snapshot of one day's data volatility**. The tolerance is justified by "this endpoint's body changes under the scan's own traffic, so the similarity template cannot discriminate here". That premise can stop being true without anything changing in this repo: if `/api/status` stabilises, the template would discriminate fine, and the entry keeps suppressing it. A suppression whose premise has expired is indistinguishable from a suppression that is still earned.

## The decision (Peter's two options, with his lean)

1. `expires` **per entry**, checked by the existing offline guard.
2. **A nightly null-attack re-measurement** that goes red when a figure moves above a threshold. ← **Peter's lean, and the recommendation**

His reasoning, which I would not improve on: *"an expiry only tells you time has passed, a re-measurement tells you the premise changed."*

Option 2 costs a scheduled job and a threshold nobody has picked yet; option 1 is nearly free but only ever produces a prompt to re-measure by hand — which is the work option 2 automates.

## Done when

* A decision is recorded between (1) and (2), by @kam or @peter.
* The chosen mechanism is implemented and has a red-proof: an entry whose premise has expired must make the gate go red, with a control proving the mechanism does not simply red everything.
* The `similarity-undiscriminating` kind has a stated evidence rule in the same place `public-by-design`'s live probe is documented, so the asymmetry cannot silently return.

## Context

Filed from session 111 under Peter's review of #783. Both the design (`kind` split, bound to `SIMILARITY_TEMPLATE_IDS`, now a compiler-enforced union) and the decision to list only `ADD_USER_ID` were endorsed in that review; this is the one piece he left open.

title: Three new advisories freeze every push: in-range lock refresh for shell-quote, MCP SDK and pbkdf2
description:
Preflight legs 6 (`audit-gate.mjs`, KS-470) and 7 (`audit-locks.mjs`, KS-531) FAIL on develop `b39051390ff6f252601d6f7b45f0ea6c21c31023` for three newly published advisories. Every push in the repo is frozen: PR #1404's verified merge-in, #1398, and three unraised PRs are all blocked behind it. This ticket is the in-range, lock-only refresh that clears them.

## Authority

Kam's ruling, verbatim (live board 2026-10-07 06:46:01 AEDT):

> Decision secuura-advisory-freeze-3-ghsa-1007: a — Fix the dependencies: one Claude seat does an in-range lock refresh

Option (a) as carded: "A dedicated seat bumps the three packages within range in the affected locks, measures whether each reaches a runtime image, then raises ONE PR gated T1 and merged first."

## The three advisories

| Advisory | Sev | Package | Pinned | Target | In range |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv | critical | shell-quote | 1.9.0 | 1.11.0 | yes, `concurrently@8.2.2` declares `^1.8.1` |
| GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h | high | @modelcontextprotocol/sdk | 1.29.0 | 1.31.0 | yes, `services/mcp-server` declares `^1.27.0` |
| GHSA-477h-4r7f-fvrx | moderate | pbkdf2 | 3.1.5 / 3.1.6 | 3.1.7 | yes, four parents declare `^3.1.2` / `^3.1.3` / `^3.1.5` |

Targets are the LOWEST clearing version in each case, not latest-in-range. Measured with leg 7's own instrument, the npm bulk advisory API: the three pinned versions all fire; the three targets together return `{}`.

Range check by `semver.satisfies` (semver 7.8.0): 8 must-pass arms all true, 2 must-fail controls (sdk 2.0.0 vs `^1.27.0`, pbkdf2 4.0.0 vs `^3.1.3`) both false. No major bump, no `overrides`, no manifest edit is required.

## Change set

5 locks, 7 entries, 0 manifests, 0 baseline rows, 0 source files.

```
Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json          shell-quote 1.9.0 (dev), sdk 1.29.0, pbkdf2 3.1.5
Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/...    sdk 1.29.0
Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/...        pbkdf2 3.1.6
Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/...        pbkdf2 3.1.6
Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/...     pbkdf2 3.1.6
```

`Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app` pins shell-quote 1.8.3 and is declared out of scope (KS-769, expires 2027-01-01). It is not touched.

The per-entry field set is NOT uniform, which breaks the three-fields-per-entry assumption of the previous round's editor:

* root entries carry no `resolved` / `integrity`, so they change `version` only, plus `dependencies` where it moves;
* sdk 1.29.0 to 1.31.0 moves its own `dependencies["@hono/node-server"]` from `^1.19.9` to `^1.19.9 || ^2.0.5`;
* pbkdf2 3.1.5 to 3.1.7 moves `dependencies["to-buffer"]` from `^1.2.1` to `^1.2.2`;
* pbkdf2 3.1.6 to 3.1.7 and shell-quote 1.9.0 to 1.11.0 leave every lock-relevant field equal.

No cascade: the root pins `@hono/node-server` 1.19.17 and `to-buffer` 1.2.2, and the three standalone locks pin `to-buffer` 1.2.2, so all the new ranges are already satisfied by what is pinned. Seven entries move and nothing else has to.

## Runtime reach — measured

Read from Dockerfiles at `b39051390ff6` with `git show`; no image was built.

* **The workspace-root lock reaches no runtime image.** Across 38 tracked Dockerfiles there are 82 COPY lines naming `package*.json`, and 0 of them copy the `Blockchain/Dev` root `package*.json`. The critical shell-quote finding is therefore build-tooling exposure (it arrives via `concurrently`, dev-only), not shipped code.
* **The MCP SDK reaches the mcp-server runtime image.** Its final stage copies mcp-server's own manifest and lock and runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`, where the SDK is a non-dev dependency.
* **pbkdf2 reaches 25 runtime images, not the 3 locks leg 7 names.** 25 Dockerfiles copy `--from=shared-builder /shared`; 25 of 25 of those shared-builder stages run a FULL `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (not `--omit=dev`) from `packages/shared`, whose lock pins pbkdf2 as a production dependency, and 25 of 25 copy `/shared` into their final stage. `services/anchoring` additionally installs it directly from its own lock.
* **frontend/issuer: indicated, NOT measured.** The final stage is nginx serving `dist`, so no `node_modules` ships. There are 0 direct imports of pbkdf2 in issuer source (control: `react` matches 57 files). pbkdf2 arrives via `crypto-browserify`, a direct issuer dependency, and the issuer Vite config enables `nodePolyfills` including `crypto`, whose implementation is crypto-browserify. Whether it lands in the served bundle will be settled by grepping the built `dist` during the build, with a must-hit and a must-not-hit control.

Disclosure on that measurement: the first instrument used to classify the 25 shared-builder stages returned a uniform "no npm ci" for all of them, including two Dockerfiles already read by hand. A uniform answer containing known-false cases is a blind instrument, so it was rewritten as a real FROM-stage parser and re-driven; the two hand-read files are its positive control and they agree.

Whether mcp-server exercises the SDK's OAuth client (the subject of GHSA-6qxp) is UNMEASURED. It imports only `server/mcp.js` and `server/stdio.js`, which is a suggestion, not a measurement of reachability.

## Base control

In a scratch clone at `b39051390ff6`, both legs reproduce the refusal:

* leg 6: `12 distinct advisories reported, 24 baselined.` then `FAIL — 3 NEW advisories not in the baseline` naming all three ids.
* leg 7: `43 standalone lockfiles ... 1613 distinct packages pinned — 9 advisories match, 7 already baselined.` then `FAIL — 2 advisories`: sdk in 1 lock, pbkdf2 in 3.

## Method

A surgical, data-driven lock editor writing exactly the measured per-entry field set and refusing anything else. A full regenerate was measured and rejected: `npm update` resolves to latest-in-range (sdk 1.32.1, shell-quote 1.12.0), so it cannot write the ruled lowest-clearing pins without a manifest edit or an `overrides` entry, and on the root lock it produces 12 collateral dev-flag flips plus a field-shape change. A regenerate at the ruled pins is still used as an independent cross-check witness in a throwaway scratch copy, never committed.

Integrity for each target was computed from the downloaded tarball and matched against the registry's `dist.integrity`: 3 of 3 agree, with the superseded pbkdf2 3.1.6 tarball as a firing negative control.

## Not done in this round

* No baseline row is added, re-dated or removed; `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` stays byte-identical. Option (b) was not chosen.
* Leg 6 also reports 15 baseline entries that are no longer reported (a CLEANUP advisory). Those stay out of scope here; disposition is KS-767.
* No manifest, `overrides`, range or source change. No major bump.

JSON lockfiles cannot carry comments, so the per-change WHY lives in the commit body and the PR description rather than inline, following the KS-1425 precedent.

Cross-references: KS-470 (leg 6), KS-531 (leg 7), KS-1425 (the previous in-range refresh round), KS-769 (the mobile out-of-scope declaration).

title: postcss-selector-parser 6.1.2 carries GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92 — baselined to unblock the preflight; the override was inert
description:
## BLUF

`npm audit` reports **GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92** (low) against `postcss-selector-parser@6.1.2`, which is not in the triaged baseline, so **the KS-380 pre-push preflight now refuses every push touching** `Blockchain/Dev` (gate 5/8). Accepted as a baseline entry to unblock; this ticket is the real fix.

## Where it comes from (measured, `npm ls`)

```
secuura@0.1.0 Blockchain/Dev
`-- @secuura/admin-dashboard@0.1.0 -> ./frontend/admin
    `-- tailwindcss@3.4.19
        |-- postcss-nested@6.2.0
        |   `-- postcss-selector-parser@6.1.2 deduped
        `-- postcss-selector-parser@6.1.2
```

Single path, one consumer: **tailwind's build-time CSS pipeline in the admin dashboard**. No backend service declares it. Tailwind runs at build; the admin image ships `dist/` behind nginx, so this code is never executed in a deployed runtime.

## The advisory

* Denial of service through uncontrolled AST recursion.
* Vulnerable `>= 6.1.0, < 6.1.3`; **first patched 6.1.3** (6.1.4 is current on the 6.x line). Also `>= 7.1.0, < 7.1.3` -> 7.1.3.
* Published 2026-05-26; low severity.
* Reachability requires feeding hostile CSS **selectors to our own build**, which is not an attacker-controlled input on this platform.

## Why it is baselined rather than fixed here

I tried the fix first, in the established shape — an `overrides` entry (`"postcss-selector-parser": "^6.1.4"`) beside the existing `postcss` override in `Blockchain/Dev/package.json`, which is the same toolchain and the same pattern KS-493 used.

**It did not take.** After `npm install --package-lock-only`, `package-lock.json` still resolved `node_modules/postcss-selector-parser -> 6.1.2`, so the override was inert — the same failure mode KS-185 records for the scoped `undici` override. Making it stick needs a real dependency-tree change (tailwind bump, or a nested override under `tailwindcss`/`postcss-nested`) plus a **frontend build verification**, which is not a change that belongs inside an unrelated error-handler PR. Reverted; `package.json` and `package-lock.json` were restored byte-identical (md5 vs `HEAD`).

Precedent for the baseline door: `undici` (KS-185) and `valibot` (KS-493) are both accepted in this file on exactly this reasoning — build/dev-tree only, never in a deployed runtime.

## What to do

1. Bump `tailwindcss` (3.4.19 -> current) and re-check, **or** add a nested override under `tailwindcss` + `postcss-nested`.
2. Verify `postcss-selector-parser >= 6.1.4` resolves in `package-lock.json` — not in `node_modules`, which `npm ls` reads and which is stale after `--package-lock-only`.
3. Build the admin frontend and confirm the CSS output is unchanged.
4. Remove the baseline entry; the preflight gate is the regression test.

## Discovered

2026-09-02 (s101), by the KS-380 preflight refusing the KS-727 push. Not caused by that change — the commit touches no `package.json` or lockfile (verified by `git show --stat`).

title: The demo-seed gate's predicate is tested but its CALL SITE is not — delete adminConfig.ts:1824 and every test still passes (same class as KS-914 A-2)
description:
## The demo-seed gate's PREDICATE is tested; the fact that the route CONSULTS it is not

Delete `adminConfig.ts:1824` and every existing test still passes.

### Measured 2026-09-06 (s141), from the #867 gate's B-3

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| the route consults the gate | `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1824` — `if (!isDemoSeedEnabled()) {` |
| the only test file | `src/__tests__/ks487-b3-demo-seed-gate.test.ts` |
| what it imports | `isDemoSeedEnabled, DEMO_SEED_FLAGS` from `../utils/demoSeedGate` — **and nothing else** |
| does it import `routes/adminConfig`? | **No.** Its own header says so, and gives the reason: importing it loads `config.ts`, which throws unless `DATABASE_URL`/`JWT_SECRET` are set |
| executable references to `seed-demo-users` in any originate test | **0** — the single grep hit is a line of prose in that header |
| **control** | the same grep for a covered route (`api/webhooks`) returns **13** |

So the truth table of `isDemoSeedEnabled` is well covered — the default-deny cases especially, which is the valuable half — but **nothing observes that** `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` **calls it.** Remove the call and the suite is 100% green.

### Why this is the same class as KS-914 A-2, and why that matters

The #868 gate found exactly this shape one ticket over: six cells tested `pinnedLookup` while nothing tested that `safeOutboundRequest` used it, and stripping the wiring left 778 passed / 0 failed. **A tested helper plus an unasserted call site is a guard that can be removed silently.** It is worth treating as a recurring pattern in this codebase rather than as two coincidences.

What that gate is protecting here is not small: without it, any authenticated `ORG_ADMIN` of any tenant could reset 14 named accounts — across every tenant, under `runWithPlatformScope` — to the bcrypt of `admin123` published in the same file, then sign in as one. Four of those fourteen are themselves `ORG_ADMIN` (counted 2026-09-06 at both `develop` and PR #867, with a control).

### Fix shape

An assertion that the ROUTE refuses when the gate is closed. The blocker the existing header names is real — importing `adminConfig.ts` pulls `config.ts`, which throws without env — so the options are (a) mount the router with `DATABASE_URL`/`JWT_SECRET` stubbed, the pattern `ks444-*`/`ks445-*` already use in this service, or (b) a static assertion that the call site exists, which is weaker and should be a fallback, not the plan.

**Red-proof it by deleting the** `if (!isDemoSeedEnabled())` **line and confirming the new cell reds.** A cell added without that has only been observed agreeing with correct code.

### The naming confusion the gate also flagged

Two different gates are called "the demo-seed gate" in prose: **auth's** (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`, pen-test F-05, which allows an `isDevLike` bypass) and **originate's** (`utils/demoSeedGate.ts`, deliberately stricter — both flags, no bypass). The comment block at `adminConfig.ts:1770-1800` discusses both within a few lines. Worth one clarifying sentence naming which is which, so a reader does not carry auth's bypass across to originate's route.

*Filed by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the #867 gate's finding B-3, at Wednesday's direction to file it rather than widen that PR. The measurement above is mine; the finding is the gate's.*

title: Launcher: the assembled boot prompt is asserted by no cell — KS-907's fix can vanish at 18/0, and the seat sentence misled a live seat tonight
description:
**Nothing asserts what the boot prompt actually SAYS.** The launcher computes `$GIT_SYNC_STEP`, the suite reads it from a standalone marker, and the prompt the session actually receives is checked by no cell. Two consumers have now been proven wrong through that gap in one night.

## Item 1 — `$GIT_SYNC_STEP` never reaches an assertion (QA FINDING 1, MAJOR)

The `DRY_RUN` markers at `L659` print the variable **directly**. The boot prompt consumes it **separately** at `L483`. Two independent consumers of one variable; the suite reads only the first.

QA evidence — a one-line tamper (`887c3c23`) replacing `${GIT_SYNC_STEP}` at `L483` with literal text, marker untouched:

```
suite result:  18 passed, 0 FAILED   — every cell green
boot prompt:   199 lines -> 191 lines, "pull latest on the current branch" GONE
```

Proven with an instrumented pair (shipped + tampered, each printing `$INITIAL_PROMPT` under dry-run): shipped YES, tampered NO.

**Impact:** a future edit near `L483` — a 200-line block that is edited often — silently reverts KS-907 while the guard stays 18/0. KS-907 exists because a second seat's boot fast-forwarded a live branch under the first seat, before that session had read the brief telling it it was a second seat.

## Item 2 — the seat sentence reads as an assignment, and it misled a live seat tonight

Seat A was told by its boot prompt that its working copy was `worktrees/seat-b` — **this seat's worktree.** Seat A measured the pane mapping, disbelieved the launcher, and proceeded correctly as seat A; nothing was written into the wrong tree. A seat that trusted the line would have written into another live session's worktree.

Seat A's measurement, verbatim:

> pane %130 -> pane_pid 1790 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain" (no -B) = SEAT A = me
> pane %129 -> pane_pid 89454 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain-B" = SEAT B = s140e,
>             live since 22:24:23, PID 89456, working in worktrees/seat-b

**⚠️ The mechanism is NOT what it was handed to me as, and the correction changes the fix.** It was relayed as "the seat registry decides which worktree a pane is told to use, and no cell asserts the assignment is right." Measured here: **there is no assignment mechanism at all, and the registry has nothing to do with it.**

```
L344-346:  SEAT_WORKTREES="$(ls -1 "$PROJECT_DIR/worktrees" | sed 's|^|worktrees/|' ...)"
L363:      Sync YOUR OWN working copy instead${SEAT_WORKTREES:+ (this project has: ${SEAT_WORKTREES})},
```

`SEAT_WORKTREES` is a plain directory listing, **byte-identical for every pane**. `grep -c SEAT_WORKTREES` = 3, all three above. The sentence states a true fact — but its subject is *"YOUR OWN working copy"*, so a one-entry list reads as an assignment. With exactly one worktree present, that misreading is at its maximum.

The launcher says so itself at `L261`: *"The cockpit passes NOTHING that distinguishes the seats — both panes invoke a byte-identical command line."*

So this is a **wording defect plus a missing capability**, not a wrong computed value — nothing computed the wrong seat. The existing mitigation is the very next clause (*"if you have not been told which one is yours, ask before writing anywhere"*), and it worked: this seat asked, seat A measured.

**Fix shape (two options, the first is trivially safe):**

1. Reword so the list cannot read as ownership — e.g. *"this project contains the following worktrees: …; if you have not been told which is yours, ask."*
2. Actually derive the pane's seat. The cockpit label **is** reachable — it is in the parent shell's command line, which is how both seats identified themselves tonight (`ps -o command` on the launcher's own parent shows `[cockpit] Secuura/Blockchain-B exited`). That is a feature, not a guard, and it should not be attempted while two seats are live.

## Item 3 — the premise the whole registry rests on is asserted by no cell (QA NOT-TESTED 2)

The QA agent rated this **above FINDING 1**. The launcher registers `$$` and its `lstart` believing `exec` **replaces** the process, keeping pid and start time. The dry run `exit 0`s instead of exec'ing, so the entry it writes is stale the instant it is written. `exec claude … "$INITIAL_PROMPT"` (`L663`) is the only line below the dry-run exit and **is exercised by nothing** — not the suite, not the QA pass.

If that line were ever changed to anything that forks (a wrapper, `claude &`, `bash -c`), every registry entry would be invalid on arrival, the guard would silently stop working, and all 18 cells would stay green.

## Why these are one ticket

All three are the same mechanism: **a value the launcher computes correctly, consumed somewhere no cell looks.** Items 1 and 2 are literally the same variable's journey into `$INITIAL_PROMPT`; item 3 is the assumption that the prompt is ever `exec`'d at all. One fix — emit the assembled prompt behind a `DRY_RUN_INITIAL_PROMPT` marker and assert its **text** — makes all three assertable.

## Regression tests

Two cells against the assembled prompt, not the marker: empty registry -> prompt contains PULLTEXT; one live seat -> contains ROTEXT and **not** PULLTEXT. Red-proof by deleting the `L483` interpolation and requiring exactly those cells to fail. Item 2 adds a third: the prompt's named-worktree text against the pane's own cockpit label.

⚠️ **Do not fix the launcher while two seats are live.** It is live on disk under a by-hash gate; a relaunch is gated. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Sources: QA verdict `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, read whole; item 2 from Wednesday's addendum quoting seat A, with the mechanism re-measured in this seat and corrected. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

title: Cockpit: statusline.sh:85 does shell arithmetic on rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at, so an ISO-8601 value kills the whole statusline — the lane-V pane renders none and ctx% is unreadable from inside a session
description:
Filed on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-13 11:39:04Z, after Seat V 9th could not satisfy a context-based wrap threshold because its pane shows no statusline. **This is a root cause with a one-line fix, not just a symptom report.** The file is at the workspace root (`Setup and System/statusline.sh`), outside any project folder, so this seat read it and did not edit it.

## The defect

`Setup and System/statusline.sh:85`

```sh
week_resets=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at // empty')   # :79
...
secs_left=$((week_resets - now_ts))                                                       # :85
```

`:85` performs **shell arithmetic directly on** `resets_at`, which assumes the field is epoch-seconds. When Claude Code supplies it as an **ISO-8601 string**, the arithmetic aborts:

```
/Volumes/DevMASTER/Setup and System/statusline.sh: line 85: 2026-10-17T00: value too great for base (error token is "17T00")
```

The script then exits **rc 1 having printed nothing**, so Claude Code has no statusline to render — and `ctx:NN%`, computed 30 lines earlier at `:54`, is lost with it.

## Truth table, measured by piping synthetic JSON to the real script

| `rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at` | rc | rendered |
| -- | -- | -- |
| ISO string `2026-10-17T00:00:00Z` | **1** | **nothing** |
| epoch integer | 0 | `[Secuura/Blockchain] Opus 5 \| Ultrathink \| ctx:37% \| 7d:89% renews:3d 11h \| azure:-` |
| field absent | 0 | `… ctx:37% \| 7d:89% \| azure:-` |
| `rate_limits` absent entirely | 0 | `… ctx:37% \| azure:-` |

So three of four shapes are fine and exactly one kills it. **The same ISO input against the global fallback** `~/.claude/statusline-command.sh` **returns rc 0** and renders `Opus 5 | ctx:200k used:37% | 7d:89%`, so the defect is specific to the project script.

## The observable effect, measured across panes

`tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -` and a count of lines matching `ctx:[0-9-]`:

| pane | cockpit name | `ctx:` lines | last value |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `%0` | wednesday | 1 | `ctx:74%` |
| `%83` | Secuura/Blockchain-K | 1 | `ctx:26%` |
| `%84` | Secuura/Blockchain-J | 1 | `ctx:21%` |
| `%82` | **Secuura/Blockchain-V** | **0** | **none** |
| `%1` | fleet-monitor | 0 | none (not a session pane) |

Three session panes render a figure and lane V's renders none, so the instrument discriminates. Wednesday read K at 23% and J at 16% about ten minutes earlier and this seat read 26% and 21%, so those are live values rather than stale screen text. **Which shape of** `resets_at` **a given pane receives is what decides it; that is not established here, and the fix makes it moot.**

## Why it matters beyond one cosmetic row

`ctx:NN%` is the **only** instrument for the context window. A seat whose statusline dies has no way to read it:

* both statusline scripts take the JSON on **stdin** and persist nothing (`statusline.sh:54` and `statusline-command.sh:7` both read `.context_window.used_percentage`; the only cache in the project script is `/tmp/.claude_azure_user_cache`, for `az account show`);
* the rendered line is not in the pane's scrollback — zero `ctx` hits over the full history;
* nothing under `~/.claude` holds it.

A seat in that state either guesses or substitutes a different number. This one substituted the **session token budget** ("\~2.6% of 15M remaining") for the context window, which is a different quantity entirely, and Wednesday had to correct it. Her words: *"A seat once read the budget as 3% and died at 100% of its window hours later."* So a dead statusline row removes the guard against a seat dying mid-merge.

## Fix

Convert before subtracting, and never let this block the render. Both halves matter:

1. Parse `resets_at` as a date when it is not numeric — e.g. `date -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$week_resets" +%s` on macOS — or skip the countdown when it does not parse.
2. **Guard the arithmetic** so a future field-shape change degrades the countdown rather than deleting the statusline: test `case $week_resets in (*[!0-9]*) ... esac` before `$(( ))`, and have the script emit its base line regardless. A statusline is a diagnostic; it must not be the thing that fails silently.

A self-test with the four rows of the truth table above would have caught this.

## Proposed and NOT done

A project-local `statusLine` wrapper in `.claude/settings.local.json` that tees stdin to a file, making `ctx%` readable from inside a session. **Wednesday ruled against it for now** (11:39:04Z): that file is shared by every seat in the project folder, and J 10th and K 10th were live in it at 89% weekly usage. It is recorded here as the option, not as a pending action. Fixing `:85` is the smaller and better change and needs no shared-settings edit.

## Priority

Filed **Medium** as instructed. An argument for higher exists and is recorded rather than acted on: the failure is silent, it disables the only context instrument, and it is latent for every seat whose harness sends an ISO `resets_at`. That call is not this seat's.

## Provenance

* Measured by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13, pane `Secuura/Blockchain-V` `%82`. Everything above is a reading, not a quotation, except Wednesday's sentence about the earlier seat, which is quoted as hers.
* Deduped before filing: 327 distinct issues over 5 search terms with comments and archived included; 0 near hits. `statusline.sh`, `resets_at`, `value too great for base` and `context_window.used_percentage` each → 0. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9c-f4d2b8ff74cb` → 0; positive control `cockpit` → 2 (KS-939, KS-907).

title: verify-file's cross-tenant registry lookup compares the sha256:-prefixed hash against platform_document_registry.content_hash with no normalisation, so it never matches a bare-hex registration (measured; facts only, no fix)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/verification/verify-file` searches `platform_document_registry` with the `sha256:`**-prefixed** hash, by exact equality and with no normalisation. The registry stores whatever the registering caller passed, verbatim. **So where registrations carry a bare hex hash, verify-file's entire cross-tenant path is unreachable** — a file certified in another tenant answers "not found" rather than being found through the registry.

**Facts only. No fix shape, no severity rating, and I have not measured which format real rows carry in any environment** — I have no box access. Filed on Wednesday's instruction, as a side reading from the KS-1119 proof.

## The two lines

* **The search**, `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:528-537` inside `crossTenantLookup`: when `documentId` is empty, the registry is queried as
  `SELECT * FROM platform_document_registry WHERE content_hash = $1 LIMIT 1` with `$1 = hashToVerify` — **exact equality, no** `sha256:` **handling on either side.**
* **The caller**, `:663`: `crossTenantLookup('', fileHash)`, where `fileHash` is built at `:639` as
  `` `sha256:${crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fileBuffer).digest('hex')}` `` — **always prefixed**. (`hashNorm`, the unprefixed form, is computed on the next line and is *not* what is passed.)
* **The write**, `registerInPlatformRegistry` (`:487-509`): stores `doc.contentHash` verbatim, with no normalisation either. The format in the table is therefore whatever the registering caller supplied.

Contrast: the *tenant-DB* query a few lines later (`:553-566`) is careful about exactly this — it strips the prefix into `searchHash` and matches `content_hash = $1 OR = $2 OR = $3` across all three forms. The registry query above it does not.

## The measurement

From the KS-1119 probe, on a local scratch PostgreSQL 15 with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, as `secuura_app` (`rolsuper=false`, `rolbypassrls=false`), 3/3 cells in each run. The **only** difference between the runs is the format stored in `platform_document_registry.content_hash`:

| registry row stored as | verify-file reached the cross-tenant path? |
| -- | -- |
| `sha256:<hex>` | **yes** — the registry hit, and the lookup continued into the tenant DB |
| bare `<hex>` | **no** — the registry search found nothing, `crossTenantLookup` returned `null` |

Control in both runs: a file with no registry row at all answers `verified:false`, so the instrument can tell a miss from a hit.

*(The prefixed run is also how \[\[KS-1119\]\]'s second instance was found — that is a different defect and lives there. This ticket is only about the format mismatch making the path unreachable.)*

## What is NOT established

* **Which format real rows carry**, on Kintsugi, on the demo VM, or anywhere else. That reading is on the deploy-time census list with KS-1119's.
* Whether `v1 /verify` is affected the same way. It is **not**, on the path I measured: when a `documentId` is supplied the registry is searched by `document_id` first, so the format never arises; and when only a hash is supplied, that hash is whatever the *caller* sent, which may or may not carry the prefix. I did not measure the hash-only-no-documentId shape.
* Whether this is intended. It may be that every registration is expected to be prefixed, in which case the bug is on the write side or nowhere.

## Related

\[\[KS-1119\]\] — the proof this fell out of · \[\[KS-584\]\] and \[\[KS-590\]\] — which registration a hash resolves to (a different question; this ticket is about whether the row is found at all) · \[\[KS-598\]\] — the registry upsert collapsing registrations per `(hash, tenant)`.

title: KS-1119 follow-ups (pull request 1542, Opus gate): the hash-match flag is not the lookup predicate, crossTenantLookup never retries the registry by hash, and four pre-existing verify disclosures
description:
## BLUF

Facts recorded from the Opus tier-1 gate on [pull request 1542](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1542>) (KS-1119, merged as `026c2d1614065c79fc8d96007ac0d80f19fb9363`), filed at Wednesday's instruction. **Two items are KS-1119 residue; four are PRE-EXISTING and measured identical on develop and on the merged head, recorded here so nobody reads them as covered by that merge.** No fix shape is proposed for the two items that touch which registration answers — they need the KS-584 / KS-590 review first.

Measured at develop `405e33a1061310662b10245c5154c3d75c49f0f4` and at the merged head.

## A. KS-1119 residue

**A1 — leg (b) compares the exact stored hash, while the lookup matches three forms.** `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1212`. The lookup accepts the bare digest, the `sha256:`-labelled form and a mixed-case spelling; the flag derived at :1212 compares only the exact stored value. Measured consequence under `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`: a document stored as `sha256:<hex>` with a request `contentHash` of `sha256:sha256:<hex>` answered `verified:true` before the merge and answers `verified:false, documentExists:true, hashValid:false` after it. It refuses rather than admits; no caller in this repository sends that shape; the single-label and bare-digest controls still answer verified. Mutant M2 survives on the merged head and the shape above is what reaches it — the pull request body's "no reachable trigger" was wrong and has been corrected in place.

**A2 —** `crossTenantLookup` **never falls back to the registry by hash when the tenant the documentId points to has no hash match.** Consequence, measured under multi-tenancy: the exact right hash sent with the documentId of a document in ANOTHER tenant answered `verified:true` naming the wrong document before the merge, and after it answers "This document hash is not registered" — which refuses correctly but states something false, because the hash IS registered. **No fix shape here: a retry changes WHICH registration answers, so it belongs to the KS-584 / KS-590 review.**

## B. PRE-EXISTING, identical before and after the merge

**B1 — the documentId-only answer hands any caller the stored** `contentHash`**.** `verification.ts:1344`. Under multi-tenancy this crosses tenants: a caller holding only a documentId receives the document's content hash, which is the value the whole verify contract treats as the integrity secret.

**B2 —** `{documentId: X, hash: <hash of document Y>}` **answers** `verified:true` **naming Y.** The documentId is ignored when the hash matches. **This is the one a relying party reading only the** `verified` **field would trust**: it asked about X, the answer is true, and the document described is Y.

**B3 — KS-1590 is wider than verify-file.** The same unnormalised comparison also makes `/verify`'s hash-only cross-tenant answers depend on the spelling the caller sent. Added as a comment on [KS-1590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1590) rather than restated here.

**B4 — the registry by-hash query has** `LIMIT 1` **with no** `ORDER BY`, so which tenant's registration answers an outsider is arbitrary and may change between identical calls. **Related but NOT the same query as** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584), whose quoted SQL is the `documents`-table lookup and does carry `ORDER BY d.certified_at DESC NULLS LAST`; this one is `platform_document_registry` and carries no ordering at all. Recorded against the live [KS-590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-590) because KS-584 is archived. **No fix shape: same reason as A2.**

## Dedupe

300 distinct issues read over six `searchIssues` terms with `includeComments` and `includeArchived`, then literal `containsIgnoreCase` matching on eight distinctive tokens. Positive control `platform_document_regist` found in 12 issues, so the pipeline demonstrably sees descriptions. Nine near hits were read one by one: KS-1119 (the parent), KS-1590 (B3's home), KS-584 and KS-590 (the documents-table variant of B4, distinguished above), KS-1118, KS-1133, KS-1129, PS-547, PS-514 — none covers A1, A2, B1 or B2. `verification.ts:1344` and "three-form" matched zero issues.

A first run's control token was the string `KS-1590` itself, which appears in no description and so could never fire; that run's near-hit list was discarded rather than reported.

title: originate declares handlebars as a direct prod dependency that no source file imports
description:
## Finding

`services/originate/package.json` declares `handlebars` `^4.7.9` under `dependencies` (prod), and 0 files in the repo import or require it. Measured 2026-10-08T23:4xZ at develop `1e7f90e26137` with `git grep` for `require('handlebars` and `from 'handlebars`; positive controls on the same instrument: express 339 files, ts-jest 14.

## Why it matters

originate is the only service image that carries handlebars at runtime. Its runner stage re-installs from originate's own lock with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev` (`services/originate/Dockerfile:79`), and handlebars is prod there. governance and referral prune dev deps before the runtime copy (`:54`, `:61`); vc-issuer installs `--omit=dev` (`:86`), where handlebars is dev; the Dev root lock reaches no image.

So the three handlebars advisories have image reach only because of this declaration, and no code path goes into it. Removing the declaration removes the reach; the lock refresh only patches it.

## Not done

NOT done in the lock-refresh PR, and the removal is not built. Unmeasured: whether anything loads handlebars dynamically (a string-built require, a templating config read at runtime). That check comes first.

Duplicate search, shared with the lock-refresh ticket: `handlebars` 0 hits in Linear including archived (control `pbkdf2` 3).

## Cross-reference

The lock refresh that clears the three advisories without removing this declaration: KS-1452.

title: KS-759 follow-up: nothing pins that originate's connectorContext reads stay type-checked — a cast reintroduced at either site is invisible to every suite (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

**Facts only, no fix shape chosen.** Pull request 1543 (KS-759) deletes the `as unknown as { tenantId?; organizationId? }` casts in both `connectorContext` functions, so the compiler now checks those reads. **Nothing keeps it that way.** A cast reintroduced at either site would compile, lint and pass every suite, exactly as the original did. Filed on Wednesday's instruction (ruling 3 on KS-759: no guard cell in that PR; a facts-only P3 afterwards if a guard is worth a ticket).

## The measurement that shows the gap

Same deletion of both fields from originate's `JwtPayload` (`services/originate/src/middleware/auth.ts`), same `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`:

| tree | result |
| -- | -- |
| develop `a7cffc8d` (casts present) | **rc 0, zero errors anywhere in originate** |
| pull request 1543 head `502b164e` (casts removed) | **rc 2, exactly four TS2339**, at `routes/gdpr.ts` 472 / 477 and `routes/platformOrganizations.ts` 54 / 56 |

So the protection exists only while the code stays as 1543 leaves it. Re-adding the cast restores the first row, and no suite runs a check that would notice: the change is type-only, so every runtime cell is green either way.

A related fact from the first row: with both fields deleted, **nothing else in originate fails to compile**. These two functions are the only places originate reads either field off a `JwtPayload`.

## Why a source-text guard is not enough

A grep for `as unknown as` near those reads passes when the offending line is commented out, and misses a differently-shaped cast (`as any`, an intermediate variable, a `Record<string, unknown>` widening). This repo has been bitten by that class before — KS-1319, a wiring pin that passed on a commented-out line.

## Shapes worth weighing (not chosen)

* A **tsc-level cell**: a test-only file that reads `user.tenantId` / `user.organizationId` off a `JwtPayload` value under `// @ts-expect-error` *with the fields deleted*, run by the type-check ratchet. Note originate is **not** in the test-file type-check ratchet's default list today (that list is auth, api-gateway and vc-issuer).
* Make `connectorContext` take an already-typed payload, so there is nothing to cast — a wider change that touches the callers.
* Or accept the gap: it is a typing guarantee, and the values themselves are unchanged by any cast.

## Related

\[\[KS-759\]\] the parent · \[\[KS-764\]\] where `tenantId` was declared on `JwtPayload` · \[\[KS-1319\]\] the commented-out-line class

title: security's own audit INSERT can never succeed on a repo-built database (previous_state/new_state undefined; encrypted details into jsonb) — POST /api/audit persists nothing, silently
description:
## BLUF

**On a database built from the repo,** `services/security`**'s own audit INSERT can never succeed, and** `dbSaveAuditLog` **swallows the error.** So `POST /api/security/audit` (`/api/audit` in the service) never persists its rows to `audit_logs`; they live only in the service's in-memory cache. **Measured** on a scratch PostgreSQL 15 built from `docker/init/*` and `run-migrations.sh`. Facts only, no fix. Found while building KS-1570 PR B, which avoids the path and does not change it.

## Two independent causes (develop `2cdf1d7a`)

1. **Columns that no schema source defines.**
   * `dbSaveAuditLog` (`services/security/src/index.ts:122-146`) inserts into `previous_state` and `new_state`.
   * Neither column exists in `docker/init/01-schema.sql:390` (`CREATE TABLE audit_logs`) or `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:347`, and no later migration adds them (git grep: 0 hits in docker/ and migrations/).
   * Only `prisma/schema.prisma:524-525` declares them.
   * Measured error: `column "previous_state" of relation "audit_logs" does not exist`.
2. **Encrypted text into a** `jsonb` **column.**
   * `details` is written as the output of `encryptDetails` (a `v1:…` ciphertext string). The column is `jsonb` in both schema sources.
   * The service's boot widens it to TEXT (`runDbBootTasks`, the `ALTER TABLE audit_logs ALTER COLUMN details TYPE TEXT` block). That boot step runs as `secuura_app`, which by design has no DDL rights (`docker/init/01-create-app-role.sh`; KS-92's runtime-DDL class), and it logs a failure as "non-fatal".
   * So on a fresh database the column stays `jsonb`. Measured error once cause 1 is avoided: `invalid input syntax for type json`.
   * When PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, the details are plaintext JSON and cause 2 does not apply. Cause 1 still does.

## What is not known

Whether the Kintsugi and demo databases happen to have these columns, or a widened `details` (for example from a `prisma db push`, or an earlier owner-run boot). That needs a read-only check by a deploy seat:

```sql
SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'audit_logs' AND column_name IN ('details','previous_state','new_state');
```

## Why it matters

The security service's audit endpoint reports success while persisting nothing (it fails open, silently). The gateway (`api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts:313`) and tokenisation (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:198`) write `audit_logs` with their own statements and are not covered by this ticket.

## Not decided here

The fix shape. Options: add `previous_state`/`new_state` and the TEXT widening as an owned migration; or drop the two columns from the INSERT and stop the runtime DDL.

title: Architecture P1: defuse the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert — it silently collapses registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is ever enabled
description:
**Ask:** In the same phase that touches registration (plan-sheet requirement — not later, not beside), defuse `platform_document_registry`'s armed landmine: UNIQUE `uq_pdr_hash_tenant (content_hash, tenant_id)` + `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE` in `registerInPlatformRegistry`. Either re-key the registry on the document UUID, or explicitly remove/disable the upsert.

**Why it matters:** the code path is dormant ONLY because `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED !== 'true'` on local and demo (0 registry rows in both DBs). If that flag is ever switched on with today's code, the upsert wakes and silently collapses registration pointers — newest write wins per (hash, tenant) — which directly violates ruling (b): duplicate bytes = two registrations, distinguished by UUID. A landmine that has been found and left armed is worse than one nobody found.

**Spec:** `1_Project_Definition/architecture/2026-08-07_K-side-plan-sheet.md` ("The MULTI_TENANCY landmine — inside P1, not beside it").

title: A client x-wallet-address is forwarded past the gateway strip, and referrals.ts:55 falls back to it when the principal has no walletAddress
description:
## BLUF

**A client-sent** `x-wallet-address` **reaches the upstreams, and the referral service trusts it.** The header is outside the gateway's edge strip pattern (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), so it is forwarded on every proxied route. `services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55` then uses it as the wallet address when the authenticated principal has none, directly under a comment saying direct header reads are spoofable. Pre-existing. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1028 (KS-744) as finding N-3. **Reachability and severity are UNMEASURED**, and so is the priority set here: the referral mount was not probed.

## Recommendation

Owners measure it, then decide:

1. probe `POST /api/referrals/generate` through the real gateway with a token that carries no `walletAddress` plus a client `x-wallet-address`, and read what the wallet address on a referral code drives;
2. if reachable, drop the header fallback (read the wallet from the authenticated principal only) and/or add `x-wallet-address` to the edge strip, with a cell proving a client value never reaches the handler.

## Detail

* **Measured at runtime by the gate** at the gateway on 3 mount kinds: a client `x-wallet-address` is forwarded on every forwarded http-proxy cell, on develop `19f1e5475`, the PR head and the merged tree (624 cells at develop, 714 at head; the 90 extra are exactly the cells KS-744's fix now forwards).
* **Read at develop** `0a2b1603f`**:**
  * `referrals.ts:51-55`: the comment reads "Pen-test F-04: read from authenticated req.user … NOT from raw headers. Direct header reads are spoofable.", and the next line is `const walletAddress = (authUser?.walletAddress as string) || (req.headers['x-wallet-address'] as string);`.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1286` hand-forwards a client `x-wallet-address` onward.
* **Not measured:** the referral mount itself; whether any real token lacks `walletAddress`; what a referral code's wallet address controls.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal, archived included): `x-wallet-address` (0); `referrals.ts` (1: KS-202, input trimming, Done). No ticket covers this.
* **Related:** KS-744 (the gate that found it).

title: Certifications: the legacy certify path (documentId without parentDocumentId) updates documents with no organisation or owner predicate (KS-1508 gate N-6)
description:
## BLUF

**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane): measure, then fix.** `POST /api/certifications/issue` with a `documentId` and NO `parentDocumentId` (the legacy certify path, `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:557-575` at the gate's head) runs `UPDATE documents SET status = 'certified', certification_metadata = ...` with `WHERE external_id = <the caller's documentId> AND tenant_id = <the tenant>`. **There is no organisation or owner predicate**, so a caller of one organisation in a tenant can certify, and rewrite the `certification_metadata` of, a document that belongs to another organisation of the same tenant, by naming its `documentId`.
