**Pre-existing and unrelated to PR #1516**, which did not touch this path. It was found by the gate while it enumerated writers of the `documents` table. It writes `certification_metadata`, which the KS-695 erasure does not read, so it does not affect KS-1508 or #1497.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure first (red-first cell on real Postgres, both tenancy modes, as** `secuura_app`**):** organisation A's connector or admin certifies organisation B's document by `documentId`; observe the status and the `certification_metadata` of B's row afterwards. Not run by anyone yet: this is the gate's reading of the code.
2. **Fix:** bound the `UPDATE` by the caller's organisation (the document's `issuer_organization_id`, or its owner, as the neighbouring read paths do), and refuse with a 403 that is identical for an unknown document and another organisation's, the way KS-764 bounded revoke. Look at who else calls this branch (`documentId` without `parentDocumentId`) before choosing the predicate, and check Platform S's use of it first.
3. **Consider the same predicate on the other** `documents` **writers** in `certifications.ts` once the shape is decided.

## Detail

* Why P2: it is an authorisation gap inside one tenant, on a write that changes a document's certification state, found at read-only level and not yet measured at runtime. It is not a deploy blocker for KS-695.
* Dedupe done before filing: no existing ticket on the board names this file and symbol (searched title, description and comments, archived included, for "legacy certify", "certify path", "organisation predicate", "owner predicate" and "SET status='certified'"). KS-486 (the AuthN/AuthZ/tenancy/IDOR review, Deployed to UAT) matched the phrase "owner predicate" and I did NOT read it for this path.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1516 (KS-1508), verdict sha256/16 `020f335956fb7b09` (GO WITH NOTE at head `770d0f3de074`, merged by squash `b2085e99ff1c` on Wednesday's GO of 2026-10-12 16:40Z), note N-6. Gate files: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1516/` (`verdict.md`, `gate1516-attack.integration.test.ts.txt`, `evidence_*.txt`). Line numbers are the gate's, at head `770d0f3de074`. These are the gate's readings and runs; I have not re-run them.

title: KS-1538 gate follow-ups (m1-m4): a pkey-addressed documentId passes the legacy-certify check but the UPDATE matches external_id only; check and UPDATE not in one transaction; stale provenance admits a former creator; ~0.55 ms timing difference
description:
**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane; P3, one checklist):** four Minor findings from the Opus gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), none of which blocks it. Each is quoted with the gate's measurement and its fix-shape. Decide per item whether to build, accept or close. No build is started by this ticket.

## m1. A pkey-addressed `documentId` passes the new check, but the UPDATE silently does nothing

`certifications.ts` resolves the document with `getDocument` (external_id first, then the pkey UUID), but the legacy `UPDATE documents ...` matches `external_id` only. **Measured:** the owner and a SYSTEM_ADMIN get 201 with a certification saved, while the row stays `anchored` with no `certified_at`, and nothing is logged (the new catch logs only thrown errors, not a 0-row UPDATE). **Pre-existing: identical on base.** Fix-shape: resolve to the row's `external_id` from the record the check already read before the UPDATE, or log or refuse on 0 rows.

## m2. Check and UPDATE are not in one transaction

The window spans the holder lookup and the anchoring POST, whose timeout is 10 s. **Constructed:** the owner passes the check, the owner flips to B during a 1.5 s anchoring delay (SQL simulating `transfer-custody`), and the UPDATE then lands on a document B now owns, carrying A's issuer id. Not reproduced through the real transfer route. Low severity: the caller was authorised at check time.

## m3. Stale provenance admits a former creating connector

`wasCreatedByConnector` (`provenance.ts:285-296`; the same arm `GET /api/documents/:id` uses) trusts a provenance row keyed by the document's external id. **Constructed:** connector A creates document U with `onBehalfOf`, U is deleted (superuser SQL), user B re-registers U, and connector A certifies B's document: 201, row certified. Needs a deletion plus deliberate reuse of the id. It belongs to the owner rule, not to PR #1525. Owner should consider provenance rows keyed to the pkey, or deleted with the document.

## m4. A timing oracle of about 0.55 ms (measured locally, not over a network)

The refusal bodies are byte-identical, but latency is not: for a connector, not-yours 1.474 ms (p10 1.286) vs unknown 0.923 ms (p90 1.165), so the distributions separate (A/A control 0.923 vs 0.921 ms, N=200 per series, interleaved); for humans, an unknown UUID-shaped id 1.466 ms vs not-yours 0.952 ms (the pkey fallback query). `GET /api/documents/:id` has the same shape.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "pkey UUID addressed documentId certify UPDATE external_id", "wasCreatedByConnector stale provenance former creating connector", "check and UPDATE not in one transaction certify anchoring window", "timing difference unknown not-yours refusal connector" and "legacy certify follow-ups". 315 distinct issues read. Literal matches in title or description: `wascreatedbyconnector` 0, `stale provenance` 0. The only issue matching two or more of the seven distinctive tokens was KS-1538 itself. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. Relevance-ranked: "none in the top 75 per term", not a census.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), verdict GO WITH NOTE (sha256/16 `0273b5bb14d3f036`), findings m1 to m4; Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:01Z) that they are filed as one P3 follow-up. m5 (`SUPER_ADMIN` goes 201 to 403 on this path) is stated in the PR body instead.

title: GET /api/keys has no tenant-level mode: organisation-less keys cannot be listed, so the Admin Dashboard cannot show or revoke them
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **can list only keys that carry an organisation id. An API key minted with no organisation (a tenant-level key) is never returned by any list call**, so the Admin Dashboard cannot show it and cannot offer its revoke (the page revokes by the key id it read from the list). **This is design work, not a defect:** the exclusion is deliberate in the handler. It matters now because the unqualified mint is the only mint an unscoped `ADMIN` will be allowed after KS-1570, and because Admin Dashboard change KS-1564 therefore leaves the "no organisation" option out of its dialog.

## Recommendation

Decide whether the list gets a tenant-level mode. No action is needed on KS-1564, KS-1570 PR A or PR B for this; none of them depends on it. Facts only.

## Detail (read at develop `343a7b4e`, not run)

* `services/security/src/index.ts:1319-1322`: `organizationId` is REQUIRED on `GET /api/keys`; a missing one answers 400 `organizationId required`.
* `index.ts:1356-1358`: a key is returned only when `wantedOrg !== null && normaliseOrgId(k.organizationId) === wantedOrg`. The comment at `:1347-1353` says the null case is intended: "null must not equal the stored null of every org-less, tenant-level key". So a key stored without an organisation never equals any non-null query.
* The mint allows it: `organizationId` is optional (`index.ts:627`), and an unqualified mint is allowed under the 2026-09-03 ruling (comment at `index.ts:1169-1175`). `tenant-provisioning`'s metering key is minted this way (`meteringKey.ts:45`, no `organizationId`).
* Revoke of such a key works today when the caller has the key's id (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:208`, org-less keys stay revocable). Only the list is missing, so the id has to come from somewhere other than this endpoint.
* A list for "keys in my tenant with no organisation" would also have to keep the tenant filter of KS-742 (`index.ts:1359`) and the role check, and would be a published-spec change (`security.openapi.ts` lists `organizationId` as required).

## Not covered

No dashboard behaviour was run; no key counts were taken on any environment (no box access).

## Dedupe (2026-10-13, Seat J 6th)

`searchIssues` with comments and archived included, five terms, 266 distinct issues; positive control: the term `default-org` found KS-1564, KS-1565, KS-1578. Near hits read: KS-1574 (the list has no organisation arm for ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN: a different gap on the same handler), KS-1570, KS-1533, KS-764, KS-779. None describes a tenant-level list mode.

Related: KS-1564, KS-1570, KS-1574 (same handler).

title: KS-695 erase-connector round 6 gate follow-ups (pull request 1497): description wording for whitespace-only ids, an R3 cell for the second read, a stale cell title, an inaccurate header sentence, a legacy-key divergence
description:
## BLUF

Five facts from the Opus delta gate on pull request 1497 round 6 (report sha256/16 `0d886f63f692f62a`, head `c48d71638f330eb3a603a6e123471c4a1bbdf93e`) that are not defects in the merged change but are worth fixing or recording. One checklist; split an item out when someone picks it up. The code was deliberately NOT touched while the pull request was at the gate. Each item below was checked by me against the source (the lines are the ones read), except where it says it is the gate's measurement.

- [ ] **1. The published description understates the refusal (gate Minor m-1, cell V1).** `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts:3728` and the regenerated yaml `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:31211` say a key "with an empty or absent id" authenticates as `connector:api-key` and is refused. The predicate is `isFallbackConnectorId(id) = id.trim() === '' || id === 'api-key'`, so a key whose stored connector id is **only whitespace** (a space, TAB, U+00A0, U+FEFF, U+3000, U+2028) is refused too: the gate measured 403 with nothing written on the real route in both tenancy modes, and 200 `completed` when both refusals were removed. Those ids are NOT the fallback principal: the gateway keeps a whitespace-only string as it is (`connectorId || 'api-key'`), so each is its own principal. Wording-only options: add "blank or whitespace only" to the description and the yaml, or narrow the predicate to `''` and the label. The pull request body was corrected; every real connector id is `platform-s:<guid>`.
- [ ] **2. Add an R3 cell beside R2 (gate N-1).** Mutant X2 (the second guard read moved to just BEFORE the blanking UPDATE, after the count) **survives the real-Postgres file** `ks695-ask3-erase-connector-fallback-principal.integration.test.ts` in both modes (gate: 8/8 green). Reason: R2 holds `LOCK TABLE documents IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE`, so the erase stalls at the count, and a read placed anywhere after the count still sees the key. X2 is killed by the three unit statement-order cells and by the gate's R3: `LOCK TABLE documents IN EXCLUSIVE MODE` lets the count run (a read takes ACCESS SHARE) and stalls the UPDATE itself; the key and root commit there; the code answers 403, X2 answers 200. This is the gate's measurement; I did not re-run X2.
- [ ] **3. A stale unit-cell title (gate N-2).** `__tests__/ks695-ask3-erase-connector-refusals.test.ts:279` says a key with a NULL id and one with an empty id "already got 403 from the ownership comparison and still does". After round 6 the 403 for those keys comes from the fallback refusal (the gate's direct resolver call gets `OrganisationErasureFallbackPrincipalError` for both); with both refusals removed the status is still 403, through the ownership mismatch. The cell pins the status, not the reason. Reword the title.
- [ ] **4. An inaccurate header sentence (gate N-4).** `services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:220`: "a key that was deleted or rotated away". A rotation only deactivates or shortens the old key: `retirePriorStatement` in `services/security/src/index.ts` is an `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false` (grace 0) or an `UPDATE ... SET expires_at = LEAST(...)`, and the security service source contains no `DELETE FROM svc_api_keys` (checked; the search found the two `UPDATE`s as its control). The guard reads inactive keys, so a rotated key IS seen. Only a DELETED key escapes it (the gate's cell C5: 200, 2 blanked, reachable only by a DBA delete).
- [ ] **5. A legacy key's connector id can differ between memory and the database (gate N-5; read from code only, NOT run).** The security service upserts `connector_id = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.connector_id, svc_api_keys.connector_id)` (`services/security/src/index.ts:401`, with a KS-869 comment that a pre-KS-869 row holds NULL and the next save backfills it) and validates from the in-memory key (`connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null`, `:1299`, `:1569`); the boot load reads rows (`SELECT * FROM svc_api_keys`, `:535`). So a pre-KS-869 key that is live in memory with id X while its row holds NULL would authenticate as `connector:X`, while the erasure's guard, which reads rows, would not see it as carrying X. It closes on the next save or a reload. A census of Kintsugi's keys is the deploy seat's read-only item; nothing here was run against a box.

## Recorded in the verdict, no action asked

* **N-3.** A colliding key alone, with no document, can turn another organisation's erasure into a terminal 403 (the same availability property the first guard always had); minting a named connector id is platform- or provisioner-only since KS-1533 arm 1.
* **N-6.** The added guard read costs 4.2 to 6.5 ms with 50,000 keys in one tenant (a sequential scan, no index on `connector_id`), twice per erasure; negligible against the 25 s budget.

Related: KS-695.

title: Count the referral codes already stored with a header-supplied owner wallet (svc_referral_codes.owner_wallet_address) read-only on Kintsugi and demo — facts only, KS-1223 residue
description:
## BLUF

**Referral codes already stored with a header-supplied** `svc_referral_codes.owner_wallet_address` **keep that value after the KS-1223 fix ships. The fix changes only codes generated after it is deployed.** This ticket is **facts only, no fix**. It exists so the rows can be counted read-only on an environment before anyone decides what to do with them. **I cannot count them: I have no box access.** Filed on Wednesday's instruction while planning KS-1223 (Kam ruled option (a) on 2026-10-13: the referral service reads the wallet linked to the signed-in user and stops reading the header).

## Why every stored wallet today came from the header

All measured at develop `7c6b3d88`, by `git grep` and by reading the code:

* `POST /api/referrals/generate` sets the wallet as `req.user.walletAddress || req.headers['x-wallet-address']` (`services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55`).
* No access token carries a wallet. `generateAccessToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:187-209`) signs userId, email, role, organizationId, verificationLevel, sessionId, tenantId, tenantSlug and scopes, and nothing else. So the first operand is always empty and the header is the only source.
* `generateCode` (`services/referral/src/services/referralService.ts:310`) is the only writer of the value. The route at `referrals.ts:63` is its only non-test caller. It stores `ownerWalletAddress: walletAddress` (`:353`) through `INSERT INTO svc_referral_codes` (`:62-65`). No `docker/init` or migration seeds that table.
* **A stored wallet is never rewritten.** The save is `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active, current_uses = EXCLUDED.current_uses` (`referralService.ts:64`). `owner_wallet_address` is not in that list.

So on any environment, every non-null `owner_wallet_address` was sent by the client that generated the code, unless the code was written by hand.

## Why it matters, and how much

The stored wallet is the **referrer side** of the `WALLET_COLLISION` fraud flag. That flag is an exact `===` comparison against the wallet in the `/apply` request body, and it is skipped when either side is absent (`services/referral/src/services/fraudDetection.ts:166-168`; `referralService.ts:455-456`). A header-supplied value on an old code can:

* raise the flag on an honest applicant who sends the same string, or
* hide a real collision because the stored value is not the owner's wallet.

Per J 5th's measurement, which Wednesday relayed and which I did **not** re-run, the stored wallet drives only this flag and never a payout.

## What is not known

**The count, on every environment.** It can be taken read-only with the following query. By the reasoning above, every non-null row it counts is header-set:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE owner_wallet_address IS NOT NULL) AS with_wallet,
       count(*) AS total
FROM svc_referral_codes;
```

`svc_referral_codes` is not under row-level security, so the app role sees every row.

## Not decided here

Whether those rows should be left alone, have their wallet cleared, or have it re-derived from the owner's linked wallet. Nobody has ruled on it. Count them first.

title: pre-push: when local develop is behind, the gate's changed set comes from a stale origin/develop and refuses a push for systemTest files the author never touched
description:
## BLUF

**The pre-push hook refuses a push for** `systemTest/` **files the author never touched.** When local `develop` is behind, the hook falls back to the shared checkout's `origin/develop` ref for base selection. That ref is stale, so the computed push range includes every `systemTest/` change merged since — and the KS 989 formatting gate then selects a package the author did not touch, finds no deps in a fresh worktree, checks **0 packages** and fails closed. Measured on PR #1394.

This is **not** the same as KS 998 item 1. That item was the gate failing **OPEN** on missing deps (exit 0 when prettier is absent). It now fails **CLOSED**, which is correct and is the discipline working. The defect is upstream of it: the *changed set* names a foreign package in the first place. KS 998 anticipated exactly this tension — "hard-failing presents an environment condition as a gate failure, which is precisely KS 991's" concern — and this is that case arriving.

## Measured

| Range | Paths | of which `systemTest/akto/` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| stale `origin/develop` (`32e058975d4e`) .. head `a94ec8f6a2c6` | 38 | **21** |
| the commit alone (`d784b613c81e` .. `a94ec8f6a2c6`) | 5 | **0** |

The 21 `systemTest/akto/` paths come from KS 1411's merged commits `a964e962c` and `ffca61a3d`, already on develop.

Refs at the time, in the shared checkout:

* local `develop` = `c56dd7c32edf` (2026-10-01)
* local `origin/develop` = `32e058975d4e` (two develops behind)
* the commit's real parent = `d784b613c81e`

No local ref knows `d784b613c81e` as develop, so the fallback is taken.

## Why it had not been seen before

The previous seat's push passed this gate because **its base WAS** `32e058975d4e`, identical to the stale ref, so its range was exactly its own 6 files with 0 `systemTest/` paths and the gate selected no package at all. Every seat whose base is newer than that ref hits this, and each merge into develop widens the range further. It gets worse with time rather than being a one-off.

## The misleading line

On refusal the hook prints:

```
[pre-push] systemTest formatting gate FAILED — fix the files named above.
```

It names **no file**. The gate's own preceding output is explicit that nothing was examined — `NOTHING CHECKED — every selected package was skipped, so no file's formatting was examined. This is NOT a formatting failure: the gate could not run.` The hook line contradicts it and sends the author looking for a formatting defect that does not exist.

## The gate already has what it needs

When the gate does run and fails, it labels the offending file `(NOT in this push — inherited red)`. So the information required to avoid charging an author for a foreign package is present at the point of the message.

## Remedies, in order of narrowness

1. **Derive the gate's changed set from the push's own range** — the real parent, or develop by SHA — rather than a fallback base. Narrowest, and the gate already computes the distinction for its message.
2. **Refresh** `origin/develop` **in the shared checkout.** Fixes the symptom for all seats but is a ref write in a checkout other sessions assert byte-identical across their rounds, so it needs a window with no live seat.
3. **Have each fresh worktree install the four gated** `systemTest` **packages** before its first push. Works, but it is four installs per worktree for a gate that should not have selected them.

## Reproduce

```
git -C <worktree> diff --name-only 32e058975d4e a94ec8f6a2c6 | grep -c '^systemTest/akto/'   # 21
git -C <worktree> diff --name-only d784b613c81e a94ec8f6a2c6 | grep -c '^systemTest/'        # 0
bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh < <the first range>   # 0 checked, 1 skipped, FAIL
```

After `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in `systemTest/akto` the same command reads `1 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 0 failed`, rc 0 — and a planted formatting defect in an akto file still returns rc 1, so that green is a measurement and not an install that silenced the gate.

Four `systemTest` packages declare `format:check` (akto, api-explorer, performance, playwright) and all four have `node_modules` absent in a fresh worktree, so any of them can be the one selected.

Discovered 2026-10-05 raising PR #1394 (Refs KS 723). Host Kamil's Mac Studio (2).

title: dbSaveApiKey SWALLOWS a failed INSERT — POST /api/keys answers 201 for a key that was never written; blast radius is ALL key persistence, not one column
description:
## BLUF

`dbSaveApiKey` catches every error from its INSERT and only logs it (`services/security/src/index.ts:236-238`). **A key that fails to persist still returns 201 with live key material.** Pre-existing; KS-869 grew its blast radius by taking the statement from 14 columns to 15.

## Mechanism

```ts
} catch (err: any) {
  logger.error('DB save API key failed', { error: err?.message });
}
```

The route continues and answers 201. The key exists in `memApiKeys` and validates — until the process restarts, at which point it silently does not exist.

**KS-869's contribution:** on a schema lacking `connector_id` the 15-column statement raises `42703` where the parent's 14-column one succeeded. Likelihood measured **LOW** by the gate — every deployment path lands the column (migration 018 is a single commit, and the demo now carries it) — but the failure mode is the swallow, not the column.

## Fix shape

Either a **boot assertion** that the named columns exist (fail fast, loudly, at start), or **narrow the catch** so `42703` (undefined column) and other structural errors are re-raised rather than logged. A mint that cannot persist must not answer 201.

## Acceptance

With the column absent, `POST /api/keys` does **not** return 201. A driven test: point the service at a schema without `connector_id` and assert the response is a 5xx, not a 201 — the shape that would have caught this.

title: KS-1557 read side (pull request 1531 gate observations): lookups per examined row, three mutants killed by one cell each, an undocumented pool-mode prerequisite, revoked certifications still count
description:
## BLUF

Five observations from the Opus gate on pull request 1531 (head `1ffc0d7a4ad740a91f2c04122fb55cd44477c928`, report sha256/16 `64b8bfc92d36e2b6`) that are not findings against that pull request and deserve a ticket. One checklist; split an item out when someone picks it up. Facts only, each checked by me against the source at that head unless it says otherwise.

- [ ] **1. Lookups per examined row (gate O1).** The cap bounds EXAMINED rows to 8, not lookups. An examined row can cost two logical lookups: the parent fetch (`fetchParentHash`, called at `routes/verification.ts:299` when the parent is not in the same-hash set) plus the certification lookup.
  * **Measured by the gate:** 2 lookups for v2 by `derivedDocumentId` (+8 statements); 8 parent fetches when nine claimed rows have parents outside the set (+32).
  * **By code, NOT constructed by anyone:** worst case 16 logical lookups (64 statements) when 8 same-hash rows have same-hash parents pushed out of the set by `VERIFY_ROWSET_LIMIT` (24). The v1 registry path can re-resolve one row after `crossTenantLookup` (at most 1 more).
  * The pull request body says "one lookup per examined row"; that holds for parents inside the set.
  * **Asks:** build the 16-lookup case and measure it, and decide whether the bound should be on lookups rather than rows.
- [ ] **2. Three mutants killed by ONE cell each (gate O4).** V22 (v1 cross-tenant site skips resolution), V26 (the certification fetch drops the issuer column) and G8 (cross-tenant rows not tagged `_tenantId`) are each red only in the pool-mode x-tenant cell (`MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`) and green in single-tenant mode. A second pin each, or one cell that does not lean on its environment for that path.
- [ ] **3. Rule 2 duplicates itself (gate O3).** "The parent link is set" is also enforced by the hash check: a NULL parent fails `fetchParentHash`'s UUID test (`:259-261`). So mutant V03 (the parent-link check dropped) is killed only by the unit cell "rows that fail the cheap checks do NOT consume the lookup cap"; the integration cell "has NO parent link" passes under V03.
- [ ] **4. An undocumented prerequisite (gate O8).** The pool-mode run of `ks1557-verify-trusts-certification-evidence.integration.test.ts` needs `platform_document_registry` in the SAME database as the app's `tenants` table (apply `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql` to the app database and point `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` at it). With a separate platform database the registry insert fails its foreign key as a logged warning and the x-tenant cell goes red, 1 of 17. The file header does not say so; the only trace is the two env lines at `:26-27` (checked). The previous seat and the gate both lost time to it.
- [ ] **5. A revoked certification still counts (gate O9, case P05).** When the cited certification row is REVOKED, verify still presents the derived row as certified. Identical on develop and on the head; the pull request body discloses it ("revoked certifications are not examined"). Ticket KS-521 (Done) was a revoked DOCUMENT; this is a revoked CERTIFICATION row, a different artifact. **Needs a ruling on whether verify should honour certification revocation**, and then a cell. Possibly a higher priority than this ticket; it is filed here so it is not lost.

## Recorded, no ticket

* Connector principals: rule 5 (owner equals issuer) is vacuous for connectors because both are NULL, so the 32-bit suffix is the only binding left (gate P03). The pull request body names that residual and it is the write side of KS-1557 that addresses it.
* The two rewritten ks584 tests pass on develop as well, so they are regression fixtures, not pins of the new rule (gate O7); acceptable for what they are.

Related: KS-1557, ticket KS-1561, pull request 1531.

title: A connector JWT presented directly as Bearer skips the gateway's connector gates (no connectorMeta on the RS256 path)
description:
## BLUF

A **connector JWT** (the short-lived token auth mints from a validated `sk_` key, `type: 'connector'`), presented directly as `Authorization: Bearer`, skips the gateway's connector gates.

* The gateway's RS256 path sets no `connectorMeta`, so the connector scope check and the `allowedDocumentTypes` allow-list on `POST /api/documents` never run for it. `connectorMeta` is set only on the `sk_` path (`middleware/auth.ts:292`).
* Measured: a scope-less connector JWT answers exactly like the lowest human `NONE` token on 67 create and 31 verify rows at #1014's head.

## Recommendation

Not built; defence in depth. No client path to the token was found, and originate re-checks `documents:write` for `role: connector`. The fix shape: recognise `type: 'connector'` on the Bearer path, and either refuse it at the gateway or attach `connectorMeta` so the same gates run.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 QA gate on PR #1014 (KS-1176), finding F-5 (graded Minor). Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014-616c766a5-tier1-r1/report.md`.
* **Reachability (probed):** 9 connector JWTs minted per census, 0 seen in any of 3,430 client-visible responses per tree. The mint is `/internal/connector-token`, mounted outside `/api` (READ).
* **Mitigation (READ, gate):**
  * originate's RBAC re-checks `documents:write` for connector principals, so a SCOPE-LESS connector JWT is refused 403 at persistence;
  * a SCOPED connector JWT used directly would still skip the gateway's `allowedDocumentTypes`.
* **Pre-existing:** at base the same token already got 201 on untyped bodies.
* `auth.ts:292` re-read at develop `eb1051fd39fe3edab4e0b1d1967515b758d4ba3f`.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches:

* `enforceClientRateLimit`: 2 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-164, KS-170; both archived).
* `rateLimit`: 24 / 24 (none about the mount order of the per-key limiter; nearest KS-947, a different limiter's gate cell).
* `dt-${Date.now()}`: 123 / 0.
* `document-types`: 121 / 14 (KS-1190, KS-1176, and archived catalogue / Akto tickets).
* `verificationLevel`: 25 / 21 (nearest KS-744, a missing claim, not a non-string one).
* `connector-token`: 91 / 1 (KS-695, an incidental mention).
* `connectorMeta`: 1 / 1 (KS-164, archived).

None covers this finding. Related: KS-1176.

title: Timestamping fail-closed: a mock TSA fallback must not report verified: true (extend KS-523 to the batch path)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/timestamps` and `POST /api/timestamps/batch` return **201 with** `verified: true` when the RFC-3161 call fails and the code falls back to a locally-generated mock token. On an evidentiary write path that is the wrong default: **extend KS-523's fail-closed treatment so a mock fallback cannot be reported as a verified timestamp.**

Found by @PeterObeden while re-measuring [KS-740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-740) against a working TSA — **6 of 360 requests (~1.7%)** fell back (5 × `TSA rejected the request (status=2)`, 1 × `fetch failed`), each returning 201 / `verified: true`. **Pre-existing; not KS-740's doing and not PR #787's.**

## Recommendation

A batch or single entry whose TSA call fell back to a mock must not carry `verified: true`. Preferred shape: reuse the KS-523 path that already exists rather than invent a second one — the machinery is built and proven, it is simply opt-in today.

Open design question for the ruling: **refuse the write (503, as** `requireEidas` **does today) or persist it with** `verified: false`**?** The batch case argues for the second — refusing one entry of 100 because one TSA call was rejected is a worse outcome than recording it honestly as unverified. Recommend `verified: false` per entry for the batch path and keeping the 503 for `requireEidas: true`.

## Detail — reproduced on `develop`, not taken from the report

Measured on `develop` `348623b0d`, local stack. The running container's `dist/` carries **0** occurrences of `BATCH_TSA_CONCURRENCY` and **0** of `AbortSignal.timeout`, so **none of #787's code is in the path**. `TSA_URL` / `TSA_AUTH_KEY` / `TSA_NAME` are all length 0 in the container (controls: `PATH` 60, `ZZZ_NOT_SET` 0), so every request takes the fallback.

`POST /api/timestamps` **(**`timestampType: rfc3161`**) → HTTP 201:**

| field | value |
| -- | -- |
| `verified` | `true` |
| `eidasQualified` | `false` |
| `tsaName` | `"D-Trust GmbH (mock)"` |
| `proof[0]` | `0x7b` — `{`. An ASN.1 DER SEQUENCE is `0x30` |
| decoded proof | `{…, "provider":"D-Trust GmbH", "type":"rfc3161", "mock":true}` |

`POST /api/timestamps/batch`**, 2 entries** — both identical to the above.

**Control (same endpoint, same TSA state, one field added):**

```
{"…","requireEidas":true}  →  HTTP 503 QUALIFIED_TSA_UNAVAILABLE
"requireEidas: no eIDAS-qualified TSA is reachable — refusing to fall back to a mock token"
```

The control is the point: **the fail-closed path already exists on this exact code path and works.** The only thing separating a silent mock from a refusal is whether the caller opted in.

### Where it is

* `services/timestamping/src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:301-327` — the mock fallback. It is **honestly labelled**: `eidasQualified: false`, a `(mock)`-suffixed `tsaName`, `"mock": true` inside the token. Nothing lies.
* `services/timestamping/src/index.ts:466` — `verified: true, // Mock timestamps are pre-verified`. **Unconditional**, for every timestamp type. This is the field a relying party reads first, and it is the one that does not carry the signal.
* `services/timestamping/src/index.ts:445-452` — the KS-523 fail-closed block. Fires only on `data.requireEidas`.

### Why now, and the link to #787

#787's new 5 s per-request deadline is a **new trigger** for this pre-existing fallback: a TSA that is merely slow now aborts and lands in the mock path, which returns `success: true` and logs at `info`. The bound is correct and should ship — but it widens the mouth of a funnel that was already silent. That is an argument for this ticket, not against #787.

### Fix shape

1. Carry the fallback signal to the caller: `verified: false` when the token is a mock on an `rfc3161` request (the mock-only types `opentimestamps` / `blockchain` keep today's semantics — they are mock by design, not by failure).
2. Red-proof: force a fallback (dead `TSA_URL`, or a `status=2` rejection) and assert `verified === false` on both the single and batch routes.
3. Positive control that must stay green: a real DER token still returns `verified: true`. Without this the fix is indistinguishable from hard-coding `false`.
4. Persisted rows carry the same signal — `ts_timestamps.verified` is written from the same value (`index.ts:489`), so a GET must answer consistently.

## Related

* KS-523 — the fail-closed precedent this extends.
* KS-740 — where it was found; reproduction and the control are in [comment a3a94d04](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-740#comment-a3a94d04>).
* The sibling class, same service, **not** this ticket: `verifyTimestamp` (`qualified-tsa.ts:443`) returns `isQualified: true` as a **literal** for every real DER token with an extractable signer certificate — no policy-OID or QcStatements read exists anywhere in the service (`policyOid` is request-side only, `rfc3161-client.ts:119-125`). @PeterObeden offered to raise that one.

*Filed by the Platform K agent, 2026-09-02, session 109. Probe rows labelled* `KS-740-s109-*` *in local* `ts_timestamps` *— no demo write, no chain write.*

title: QUESTION: are `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts:44` SCAN_DIRS and `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:150` SCAN_ROOTS (both `['services', 'packages']`) the INTENDED scopes now that ks879 walks the whole Dev tree?
description:
## BLUF

A scope question, not a defect and not a merge blocker — filed from the #978 (KS-885 + KS-886) tier-2 gate's class hunt (R2) so it has a home. KS-886 widened the ks879 control-byte guard from `services/` + `packages/` to the whole Dev tree because the class had lived twice under `tests/` (KS-847, KS-879). Two sibling guards in the same directory still walk `['services', 'packages']` only, and each SAYS so — the gate read both as scoped claims with no over-claim. The question is whether those scopes are what we INTEND, given what ks879 just learned. Measured by the builder; ruled by Wednesday on the measurement. KS-573 (Peter's: "a corpus inherits the blind spot of whatever found its members") is the nearest neighbour on the board and is named here, not related.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks885-886-978-13b767a7f-tier2-r1/report.md` — Records R2. Line numbers at `13b767a7f` = develop after the squash (M14).

## The two sites (read at the head)

1. `packages/shared/src/__tests__/crypto-agility.guard.test.ts:44` — `const SCAN_DIRS = ['services', 'packages'];` — its docblock `:5-6` says "introduced in an `algorithm(s):` position anywhere under services/ or packages/ — outside the one place algorithm identifiers are allowed to live"; its cells say "outside the crypto registry" / "found a non-trivial number of source files". **Claim = walk; no over-claim.** Question: is a hard-coded algorithm identifier under `frontend/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` or `Testing/` out of scope by design (the registry is server-side), or a blind spot?
2. `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:150` — `const SCAN_ROOTS = ['services', 'packages'];` — `:149` `/** Trees that hold first-party runtime source. Walked recursively, in full. */`; the titles name "every service entrypoint", never "repo-wide" / "anywhere in the tree"; its CORPUS section states what it does not cover. **Scoped claim; no over-claim.** Question: do `frontend/` (three React apps with their own `app.listen`-free entrypoints) or `tests/` "hold first-party runtime source" in the sense the guard means, or is the class (an error handler mounted before the routes it must catch) definitionally an Express-service concern?

## What a ruling should say

For each site: (a) scope INTENDED — add one sentence to the docblock naming the excluded trees and why; or (b) widen — the builder measures the walk cost and the red set on the wider tree first (ks879's widening cost ≈0.8 s per walk and found 0 offenders), then files the change as its own test pass. Either answer closes this ticket.

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over 1,125 KS issues + 914 comments (includeArchived): `SCAN_DIRS` → 0; `SCAN_ROOTS` → 0; `crypto-agility.guard` → 0; `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard` → 7 hits, none about its roots (KS-573 Peter's corpus claim — the neighbour named above; KS-764 a flake mention; KS-876 a listen site; KS-818/832/833 archived residues; KS-830 canceled). No home; filed new.

title: Slot-1 URLs outside KS-1355's four spots: m365's Entra redirect URI defaults to :6882 (compose + three code fallbacks), bootstrap leaves FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS / LLM_BASE_URL at slot 1, 20 service .env.examples and two smoke scripts pin slot 1, and dead VITE_* compose values name :6882
description:
## BLUF

On a slot-N stack, **platform-k's M365 integration builds its Entra OAuth redirect URI on slot 1's gateway** (`http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback`) unless someone sets `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` by hand — the compose default and three fallbacks in `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` all name `:6882`. And `bootstrap-env.sh` **derives only** `DATABASE_URL` **/** `REDIS_URL` **per slot**, so a fresh slot-N `.env` keeps slot 1's `FRONTEND_URL`, has no gateway origin in `CORS_ORIGINS`, and keeps `LLM_BASE_URL` on slot 1's Ollama — all three had to be edited by hand on slot 2 today. This is the remainder after [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (compose `FRONTEND_URL` / `CORS_ORIGINS` defaults, `preflight.sh:94`, `start-local.sh`, `dev-reload.sh` — excluded here). Slots are dynamic; each value should derive from `stack_env.sh`'s exported ports.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`, tracked files, re-read line by line 29 Sep)

**Runtime — the M365 callback points at slot 1**

| File:line | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:888` | `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI=${ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI:-http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback}` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:481, 595` | `process.env.ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI \|\| \`${process.env.FRONTEND_URL || '[http://localhost:6882](<http://localhost:6882>)'}/api/m365/callback\`\` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:993` | `… \|\| 'http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback'` |

**Bootstrap — derives two URLs per slot, not the rest** (`scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:229` `DATABASE_URL`, `:240` `REDIS_URL`; nothing writes these)

| Template (`env.example` is canonical since [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap); `.env.example` is its fallback) | Key | Slot-1 value |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:146` | `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6100–:6102` only — no gateway / website origin on any slot |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:372` | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `:11434` (Ollama is offset per slot in `stack_env.sh`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example:117` | `FRONTEND_URL` | `:6882` (lines 23–63 also document every social-login callback on `:6882`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:92, 95, 190` (fallback template) | `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6882`, `:6881` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/*/.env.example`, `services/billing/env.example` — **20 files** | `DATABASE_URL` `:6432`, `REDIS_URL` `:6379`; api-gateway `CORS_ORIGINS`; m365 `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`; billing `API_GATEWAY_URL` | slot 1 |

**Scripts — default to slot 1**

| File:line |  |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/auth-matrix-smoke.sh:31` | `API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh:15` | `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` — no override |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh:323–324`, `start-environment.sh:241` | print slot-1 URLs whatever the slot (display only) |

**Dead config — inert, but a slot-1 literal that reads as live**

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1841, 1876, 1910–1912` set `VITE_API_URL` / `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` / `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` to `http://localhost:6882/…` in the issuer, verifier and admin frontends' **runtime** `environment:`. Those images are static Vite builds (`RUN npm run build`, then nginx — `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin}/Dockerfile`), `import.meta.env.VITE_*` is fixed at build time, and no build arg or `.env` supplies it, so the bundles use their relative `'/api'` fallback — correct on every slot. The values are never read; delete them so nobody takes them as the source of truth.

## Fix shape (Kamil's call)

Pass `GATEWAY_PORT` into compose for `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` and drop the three `:6882` fallbacks in m365 (fail if neither `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` nor `FRONTEND_URL` is set); have `bootstrap-env.sh` write `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` from `stack_env.sh` as it does `DATABASE_URL`; source `stack_env.sh` in the two smoke scripts; remove the dead `VITE_*` lines. [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s proposed `check-stack-safety.sh` pin could take a "no literal slot port outside `stack_env.sh`" rule to hold all of it.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. A value right for the slot it was checked on is wrong on every other — and the failure is silent (a request lands on someone else's stack, or an OAuth callback on the wrong gateway). That makes this a high-risk area, so the PR is not done without unit tests that prove every changed value **for every slot 1..4, not only slot 1 or the slot the author used**:

* `scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh` extended: for `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4, a fresh bootstrap writes `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` on that slot's ports from `stack_env.sh` — and no other slot's port appears in the output.
* A render test (`docker compose config` per slot) asserting `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` resolves to that slot's gateway, and a unit test that `services/m365-integration` has no `:6882` fallback left (no-`ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`, no-`FRONTEND_URL` case refuses rather than defaulting).
* The two smoke scripts target the named slot's gateway for 1..4 and refuse locally when no slot is named.
* A static guard (e.g. in `check-stack-safety.sh`) failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 outside `stack_env.sh` — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Tests are hermetic: run unslotted AND under each slot's environment with identical results (the offline-suite rule), never spawned with the shell's slot variables leaking in.

## Not in this ticket

[KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s four spots. `Blockchain/Testing/**` `TARGET_BASE` defaults → [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) (the Internal Audit Harness, Kamil). The build break → [KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and). `docker-compose.production.yml` (deployed, not slotted).

## Correction history

First filed 29 Sep 08:29 UTC with the `VITE_*` values as the headline ("the frontends call slot 1's gateway"). Re-checked against the Dockerfiles the same morning: they are build-time variables never supplied at build, so that claim was wrong and is now listed as dead config; the template counts and canonical-template references were also corrected.

## Environment

Peter's Mac, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026. Found while pairing platform-k slot 2 for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) run.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 5 — the static guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard, shared with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s `docker-compose.yml` pin (both tickets edit that file), and the two smoke scripts follow point 2.

title: Seat handover clone recipe fails its checkout: git clone --reference of the shared 2_Project_Files stops with 'unable to parse commit 54b2a5c2' (2 seats of 2); a plain clone works
description:
**ACTION (owner: the build lane / whoever maintains the seat-handover recipe):** change the working-area recipe in the seat handovers from a `--reference ... --dissociate` clone of the shared `2_Project_Files` checkout to a plain clone from GitHub, and find out why the first one fails.

## Symptom (measured, twice)

Seat J 4th (2026-10-12) and Seat J 5th (2026-10-12T18:50Z) each ran:

```
git clone --reference "<shared 2_Project_Files>" --dissociate git@github.com:Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git <dest>
```

Both stopped with `fatal: unable to parse commit 54b2a5c26d75a28b14fdce578dd5a5aadee49039` and "Clone succeeded, but checkout failed". That commit is the tip of `main` (the PR #908 merge), the branch a clone checks out by default.

Recovery that worked both times: `git checkout -B develop origin/develop`, then `git fsck --full` (rc 0, no output) and a check that every `git ls-files -z` path exists (J 5th: 4,382 files, 0 missing).

## Control

The same clone with no `--reference` and no `--dissociate` checked out clean in 35 s (rc 0, status clean, HEAD `54b2a5c2`). One run each side, so the shared object store is implicated, not proven.

## Ruled out, read-only against the shared store

* The commit reads there: `cat-file -t` says commit, `rev-list -1` returns it.
* `git commit-graph verify` there is rc 0. Its commit-graph file is dated 30 Sep 06:16, 13 days old.
* Cause: unproven.

## Also

A clone script piped through `tee` made the harness report "completed (exit code 0)" for a clone that had failed with rc 128. The script's own printed rc was the truth. Do not pipe a step whose exit code decides what happens next.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "clone --reference dissociate", "unable to parse commit", "reference clone shared checkout", "seat handover clone recipe" and "54b2a5c2". 249 distinct issues read. Literal match for `dissociate`, `--reference`, `54b2a5c2`, "unable to parse commit", "clone recipe" and `alternates` in title or description: 0 hits. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked, so this is "0 hits in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

Source: Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (19:01Z) that this is filed as a priority 4 Backlog ticket.

title: rotate: true mints a new key but never revokes the old one — implement revoke-on-rotate and agree the cutover window
description:
## BLUF

@kamil.kreiser **ruled 2026-08-07: rotation SHOULD revoke the prior key.** He accepts that this makes an honest bulk re-key ~1.5 weeks rather than 2 days, on the reasoning that shipping the additive version would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and look like recovery.

**The cutover window is a contract question for** @stuart.jamieson**, not a unilateral K-side call** — revoking instantly means S's in-flight anchor writes 401 until it picks up the new credential.

@peter independently reached the same conclusion on KS-480 (2026-08-06): *"if someone left a company with a grudge and used the key maliciously, the company affected would not look kindly on our solution."*

## Detail

**The defect (Finding A, verified in code).** The rotate handler has **no revoke step**: on `rotate: true` it skips the early return at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:638-645` and goes straight to the mint. `dbSaveApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:196-223`) is a plain upsert on the *new* key's own id and never touches sibling rows sharing a `connectorId`. Validation keys purely off `key_hash` → `isActive` → `expiresAt` (`services/security/src/index.ts:940-1012`), so the prior key keeps validating indefinitely.

Guardrail 1's own comment concedes it — *"it invalidates nothing by itself"* (`platform.ts:501`) — so this is known at code level. What is absent is any sign the semantics were decided deliberately for the DR case that §4/§5 of KS-480 rests on.

**Consequence:** after re-keying a lost credential, the lost credential still works. Neither half of "lose a key, re-key" has a working admin path on demo today (the other half is [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578)).

**The open decision — cutover.** Options to put to @stuart.jamieson, with the consequence stated plainly rather than softened:

1. **Instant revoke.** S's in-flight anchor writes **401 until S picks up the new credential.** Cleanest containment, hardest on S.
2. **Overlap window** (old key valid for a bounded period). Softer on S; leaves a compromised credential live for exactly that window, which is the thing being fixed.
3. **S confirms adoption, then the old key dies.** Best of both, needs an S-side acknowledgement path and a fallback for when it never arrives.

**Done when:** the cutover shape is agreed with @stuart.jamieson and recorded here; `rotate: true` deactivates the prior key per that shape; a test pins that the old key no longer validates; and [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) step 4 passes.

Sizing: decision first, then 2–3 days.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*
