title: adminConfig: four admin routes return err.message in a 500 body with no NODE_ENV guard (production info leak)
description:
## BLUF

Four handlers in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` put the thrown error's `message`
straight into a 500 response body **with no** `NODE_ENV` **guard at all**, so they leak internal text in
**production** as well as everywhere else. This is a different and worse class than KS-730, which is
about the off-production ternary shape (`NODE_ENV === 'production' ? constant : err.message`).

Found while finishing KS-730 PR 3 of 3. **Not fixed there**: KS-730 enumerated 46 ternary sites and
converted exactly those; these four were never in its list, and folding four unlisted admin routes
into a tier-1 fix round would widen it well past its declared shape.

## The four sites, measured at base `d7cdecf1d2ee`

| line | route |
| -- | -- |
| `:113` | `POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants` |
| `:1859` | `POST /api/admin/backfill-certification-metadata` |
| `:2031` | `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` |
| `:2158` | `POST /api/admin/migrate-tenant-data` |

Each is the same shape:

```
res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: err.message } });
```

(`:113` is `message: err?.message || 'Refresh failed'`, the same leak with a fallback.)

**Pre-existing, not introduced:** the count is **4 at the base** `d7cdecf1d2ee` **and 4 at the KS-730 PR 3**
**head**. KS-730 PR 3 neither added nor removed any of them.

## Why it was invisible to KS-730's own guard

KS-730 PR 3's source cell asserts `liveTernaries: 0` and `helperCalls: 46`. Both are TRUE with these
four present, because the cell counts the `NODE_ENV === 'production'` shape — which these four do not
have. A green KS-730 cell therefore says nothing about them, which is exactly why they are pinned
separately rather than left to be rediscovered.

## The regression guard that already exists

`KS-730 C4 SOURCE`, in
`services/originate/src/__tests__/ks730c-adminconfig-500-never-answers-err-message.test.ts`, pins these
four **by enclosing route name**. A fifth site reds it. **Fixing one of these four will also red it** —
that is deliberate: the list is then updated as part of the fix rather than drifting silently.
**Whoever builds this ticket must update that cell's** `KNOWN` **list in the same change.**
Red-proved: adding a fifth unconditional site reds C4 and nothing else (1 of 14).

## Done means

1. The four sites answer the constant body and log the message server-side, as KS-730's 46 do
   (`fail500` already exists in this file and is the obvious vehicle).
2. `KS-730 C4 SOURCE`'s `KNOWN` list is emptied, or the cell retired with its reasoning recorded.
3. A cell drives at least one of the four end to end and proves the thrown text is absent from the
   body **under** `production` — which is what separates this class from KS-730's.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues` with `includeArchived: true` over the KS team for: `refresh-tenants`,
`backfill-certification-metadata`, `seed-demo-users`, `migrate-tenant-data`, `adminConfig`,
`unconditional err.message`, `err.message 500 no NODE_ENV guard`, `adminConfig production info leak`.
Every page literal-matched client-side, because `searchIssues` ranks fuzzily.
**0 tickets name two or more of the four routes together with** `err.message`**.**
Controls: `adminConfig` returns **18** literal hits (the matcher fires), a nonce token never written
anywhere returns **0**. Open PRs also searched: **24 non-dependabot PRs' file lists read, 0 touch**
`adminConfig.ts`**.**

Refs KS-730

title: api-gateway failed-login lockout is inert: createBruteForceProtection installs recordFailure, but no production code ever calls it — it can never block
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil. The gateway's failed-login lockout (`createBruteForceProtection`, `api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:146-192`) looks as though it never engages: it only blocks once `recordFailure()` has run, and nothing outside its own unit test seems to call it. The auth service's per-account lockout is still doing its job, so this is about the edge layer only. Either wiring it up or retiring it would be fine; whichever you prefer. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, and the two options

**What the code shows** (read-only, 2026-09-28)

* `security.ts:173-189` attaches `req.bruteForce = { recordFailure, recordSuccess }` and calls `next()`; nothing on the login's response path calls either helper.
* Searching `services/api-gateway/src` for `recordFailure` outside `middleware/security.ts` finds only `__tests__/security.test.ts:261`, which checks the helper exists.
* So `attempts` is never incremented, `blockedUntil` is never written, and the `429 "Too many failed attempts"` branch can't be reached.

**What the logs show**

* Slot 2's gateway, six hours of traffic including failed logins: **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT`, **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED`.
* The lockout that does work is the auth service's (`services/auth/src/services/accountLockout.ts`: (email, /24), 5 failures in 15 min → 15-min lock). It answers **401** (`routes/auth.ts:339-342`).

**Why it came up:** [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) first put some refused setup logins down to this lockout; on a closer look they were the global request window. It seemed worth recording that this layer isn't active, so no one leans on it.

**Options**

1. Wire it: call `recordFailure` / `recordSuccess` from the login proxy's response handling (401 / 2xx), with a test that shows a block after `freeRetries` failures.
2. Retire it: remove the middleware, its `bruteForce` config in `config/services.ts`, and the doc line at `security.ts:8`.

[KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every IP-keyed control is shared behind one address) applies either way.

**Done means:** a test red on today's code shows N+1 failed logins from one address aren't blocked at the gateway; after the change they are — or the middleware and its claims are gone.

+++

title: auth verification requests: a failed save still answers 200 — a new request vanishes, and an approve raises the user's level while the row stays PENDING
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing, Major:** the auth service acknowledges verification-request writes that did not persist. `saveVerificationRequest` (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`) catches a failed INSERT / UPDATE, logs a warning and keeps only the in-memory copy, then the route answers success.

* **New upgrade request, INSERT fails:** `POST /me/verification` answers **200 PENDING**. The request is invisible on a healthy list afterwards, and a re-POST creates a second request.
* **Admin review approve, save fails:** `POST /verification/:requestId/review` answers **200 "approved"** and **raises the user's verification level**, while the database row **stays PENDING** and can be reviewed again later.

Measured at runtime, base = head. PR #1015 (KS-1018) did not change the save side.

## Recommendation

Not built. Wednesday takes this to Kam. The decision needed: should a failed save refuse (503 / 500) instead of acknowledging, and should the approve path raise the level only after the request row is persisted? That is a product and consistency call about the verification-upgrade flow, not a one-line fix.

## Detail

* **Source:** the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1015, finding F5, rows S6a–S6d and L4 (base = head).
  * Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1018-1015-77145ce84-tier1-r1/report.md`, sections 3 and FINDINGS F5.
* **Where:** `saveVerificationRequest` writes `memVerificationRequests.set(...)` first, then attempts the INSERT … ON CONFLICT UPDATE. Its `catch` logs `DB saveVerificationRequest failed — in-memory only` and returns normally. Callers:
  * `POST /me/verification`, which answers `Verification request submitted for review`;
  * the review handler, which applies the level change.
* **Why it matters:**
  * A 200 is returned for a request row that does not exist.
  * On the approve path, a user's verification level is raised while the audit-relevant request row still reads PENDING.
  * The memory map is process-local, so other replicas never see the acknowledged request.
* **Related:**
  * KS-1018 (the read side, merged in #1015; its item 3 asks whether the in-memory fallback should exist);
  * KS-1188 F3 (a different acknowledge-after-partial-write case on backup-code sign-in, not the same defect).
* **Not tested by the gate:** a real Postgres write fault; a DB fault inside `getUserByIdPreAuth` / `updateUser` on the approve path (only the INSERT save fault was measured); multi-replica behaviour.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches:

* `saveVerificationRequest`: 1 fuzzy, 1 literal (KS-1018; the read side only).
* `verification_upgrade_requests`: 101 / 3 (KS-1018, KS-467 archived, KS-1013).
* `in-memory only`: 116 / 2 (KS-170 archived, the rate limiter; KS-443 canceled).
* `ks1018`: 1 / 1 (KS-1018).

KS-1188 was read. Its F3 is a burnt backup code told to retry, a different defect.

None covers this. Related: KS-1018.

title: A refused request still writes an action_provenance row: handleOnBehalfOf runs before the refusals on /version (and /share, /transfer-custody); unpinned on certifications/issue
description:
## BLUF

**A refused request still writes an action_provenance row for an action that never happened.** In `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `POST /api/documents/:id/version` calls `handleOnBehalfOf` (`:1951` at develop `732c13459`) near the top of the handler. For a connector sending `onBehalfOf`, that calls `recordActionProvenance` (an `INSERT INTO action_provenance` for the SOURCE document id, action `version:watermark`) BEFORE the refusals that follow. The refusals are the KS-1213 type guard (400), the content-hash 400 and the 404.

* It is pre-existing: measured on develop AND on PR #1031's head.
* #1031 (KS-1213, merged as `732c13459`) adds one more refusal after it and does not widen the class.
* On `POST /api/certifications/issue` the ordering is correct today, but nothing pins it. Moving the guard after the provenance write reds no cell.
* **Severity Minor** (the tier-1 gate on #1031, finding D1, with Q-ISSUE-AFTER-OBO). The same class is already recorded in `BACKLOG.md` for `/share` and `/transfer-custody` (with no ticket); fix the four together.

## Recommendation

Move every `handleOnBehalfOf` / `recordActionProvenance` call below each refusal in its handler, so a provenance row is written only for an action that happened. Apply this to `/version`, `/share` (`:2136`) and `/transfer-custody` (`:1595`) in `documents.ts`, and keep issue's current order. (`/revoke` already had this done by KS-566.)

* **Regression cells:**
  * a connector's refused `/version` with `onBehalfOf` (a differing type, a bad hash, an unknown id) → `recordActionProvenance` NOT called;
  * the same on a refused issue (the gate's Q-ISSUE-AFTER-OBO tamper must red it);
  * the same for `/share` and `/transfer-custody` on a 404 / 403.
* Not built here.

## Detail

* **Measured by the #1031 gate** (in-process, `recordActionProvenance` mocked and counted; `resolveOnBehalfOf` stubbed to null, so a resolved-user attribution was not exercised):
  * V-OBO (a docs connector, `/version`, `onBehalfOf` + a differing type): 400 BAD_REQUEST, derived rows 0, **provenance 1** at head.
  * V-OBO-404 and V-OBO-HASH: provenance 1 on develop and head.
  * Q-ISSUE-AFTER-OBO (the issue guard moved below the holder stub and the provenance call): a refused issue → 400 with provenance 1, and 0 cells red on the originate suite (64 / 741).
* **What the row holds:** read at `services/provenance.ts:215-218`, an INSERT for the source document id. The existing `BACKLOG.md` entry adds that `action_provenance.document_id` is deliberately not a foreign key (`migrations/041_action_provenance.sql:33-36`), so nothing downstream rejects a row for an id that does not exist, and the row carries encrypted email and display name plus an email hash.
* **Existing record of the same class:** `BACKLOG.md` "`/share` and `/transfer-custody` write an action_provenance row BEFORE the 404/403" (discovered 2026-09-01 during the #742 review). It was deferred because KS-566 moved only `/revoke`.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):
  * `handleOnBehalfOf`: 2, KS-566 (moved `/revoke` only, archived) and PS-616 (a Platform S interim), neither on this ordering.
  * `recordActionProvenance`: 0.
  * `action_provenance`: 16, none on writing before a refusal.
  * `version:watermark`: 1, KS-661 (a verb rename).
  * No ticket covers it.
* Refs KS-1213 (where it was found; KS-1213 stays In Progress).

title: The served document type comes from data.documentType, which nothing checks: a document stored as an allowed type is served as a disallowed or higher-rank type (#1014 gate N-1)
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing, Major (gate grade): the document type a document is SERVED as comes from** `data.documentType`**, which nothing checks.** A document created and stored as an allowed type can be served as a disallowed or higher-rank type. The untyped carrier `{"data":{"documentType":"DEGREE"}}` answers **201 for every principal**, including a `NONE` human, at base and after PR #1014 alike. DEGREE's creator level is `enhanced` + MFA, so that check is bypassed for the served label.

## Recommendation

Not built. Wednesday takes this to Kam. The fix is an owner's choice between: originate refuses or overwrites a `data.documentType` that differs from the resolved type; or the gateway resolves and checks `data.documentType` as well. Regression shape (the gate's): a restricted connector and a `NONE` human × `data.documentType` ∈ {disallowed, above-rank} × {typed, untyped}. The served `documentType` must equal the checked type.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 round-2 delta gate on PR #1014 (KS-1176), finding **N-1**. Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014r2-9ba0caf78-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* **Evidence:** the gateway is MEASURED AT RUNTIME (status, allow-list, hit counters, forwarded body byte-identical). Originate's stored and served type is READ only.
* **Repro (the gate's, real app):**
  * A connector key restricted to `['DOCUMENT']` sends `POST /api/documents` with `{"title":"qa","type":"DOCUMENT","data":{"title":"qa","documentType":"PROPERTY_DEED"}}`, or `{"documentType":"DOCUMENT","data":{"documentType":"SSD_DOCUMENT"}}`.
  * The gateway answers 201: the allow-list read DOCUMENT, enforcement resolved DOCUMENT, and the body is forwarded byte-identical.
* **Originate (READ,** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`**):**
  * It stores `type = DOCUMENT` (`:565`, `:574`) and keeps `data.documentType`.
  * `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:1053`) and the list (`:311`) serve `data.documentType || type`.
* **The gateway verify gate** matches `doc.documentType || doc.type` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:546` / `:551` on the merged tree).
* **Class, not instance:** the untyped carrier worked at base for all four restricted connectors, the unrestricted key, the Bearer connector JWT and the NONE human. PR #1014 adds typed carriers for connectors (403 at base, 201 at head); it adds no new capability.
* **Not a Blocker against #1014:** at the gateway layer, the stored type is allowed.

### Dedupe before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches over title, description and comments:

* `data.documentType`: 118 fuzzy / 14 literal. They cover the documentType enum and verb alignment (KS-388 archived, PS-138, KS-415/534/279 archived, KS-1172, KS-663), not the served type bypassing the check.
* `stored as DOCUMENT`: 120 / 0.
* `untyped`: 6 / 5. KS-1176 comments (this gate's own records), KS-1198 (a connector JWT skipping connector gates, a different path), KS-1022/518/993 (unrelated).

None covers this. Nearest: KS-1198 (a different bypass of the same connector gates).

Related: KS-1176.

title: api-gateway: a revoked-session JWT plus a VALID key whose connector-token exchange fails is forwarded with the revoked Bearer and no session check (plus the fall-through cells no suite has)
Declare the remaining ~157 routed-but-undocumented /api operations in the OpenAPI spec — the KS-712 remainder
description:
> **Origin.** Assembled from the measurement parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comments `ae3aab1a` (the 173-op survey) and `4b388b0b` ("the remaining ~157 operations are being sized as their own ticket"), on 2026-08-28 when `issueCreate` refused workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29 once creation worked again. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket** — every number below is the one already recorded on KS-712 and is dated to that run.

## BLUF

KS-712 established that **173 routed** `/api` **operations are absent from the OpenAPI spec**, which makes them invisible to both Schemathesis and Akto. Two slices of that gap have since been declared:

| slice | ops | where |
| -- | -- | -- |
| MFA · wallet-auth · social sign-in | 16 | [#760](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760>) |
| the two settings PUTs (+ their GETs) | 4 | [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>) / [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719) |
| **this ticket — the remainder** | **~157** | not started |

This is the mechanical bulk of the gap. It was deliberately not attempted in the KS-712 pass: *"That is a large mechanical change and wants its own PR and its own review; flagging the scope rather than half-landing it."*

## Shape of the remainder (from the KS-712 run, 2026-08-28)

Of the 173 routed-and-undocumented operations:

* **By method:** GET 83 · POST 64 · DELETE 12 · PUT 11 · PATCH 3. **90 of 173 are write methods** — the half that matters most for an untested surface.
* **By area: **`/api/admin` 58 · `/api/auth` 14 · `/api/users` 11 · `/api/workflows` 8 · `/api/anchors` 8 · `/api/platform` 7.
* **Unauthenticated response:** 401 ×149 · 400 ×8 · 200 ×15 · 204 ×1.

Subtracting the 20 already declared, the remainder is dominated by `/api/admin` (58 operations, none declared) — a single area worth about a third of the whole job.

## Suggested order

The dependency order recorded on KS-712 was MFA → wallet-auth → social callback → the rest; the first three are done. For the remainder, largest-coherent-area-first keeps each PR reviewable:

1. `/api/admin` (58)
2. `/api/users` (11) + `/api/platform` (7)
3. `/api/workflows` (8) + `/api/anchors` (8)
4. the long tail

## Constraints that apply to every slice

* **KS-424 guard:** every new operation needs an explicit `security:` block, or `check:openapi` fails.
* **The gateway BIND-MOUNTS** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — a spec change is published by *restarting* the gateway container, not by rebuilding an image. Verify the served spec, not the file on disk.
* Declaring an operation does **not** put it in Akto's scan collection — see the sibling ticket on `test:pr` never re-importing the spec. A slice of this work is only "covered" once both tools actually exercise it.
* Each slice will widen the Schemathesis failing set. Record the failing **set**, diff it against the previous run on the same instrument, and classify new entries rather than counting them.

## Two things this ticket is NOT

1. **Not a decision about behaviour.** Where declaring an operation would bless behaviour that has not been ruled on, split it out — that is exactly what happened with the two unauthenticated PUTs, which became KS-719 rather than being documented as-is.
2. **Not a total.** 173 is a floor, not a count: **60 of 105** `/api` **mount bindings did not resolve** to a defining file (dynamic mounts, re-exports, barrel files), so those services are counted only where they register absolute paths. The CI guard proposed on [KS-663](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-663) — assert every routed `/api` path appears in the spec — is the only thing that turns this from a survey into a number that stays true.

## Sizing

**Peter-sized, and deliberately routed to him** — this is mechanical spec authoring across ~157 operations in at least four PRs, on a surface he originally reported. Not a one-session job and not a job worth interleaving with security findings.

## Method (for the numbers above)

Recorded in full on KS-712 comment `ae3aab1a`: route registrations extracted from each service's **compiled** `/app/dist` **in the running container** (not parsed TypeScript — static parsing undercounts by 34% because a third of registrations are named exports), mount bindings resolved precisely rather than cross-producted, then **every candidate probed against the live gateway**, with the probe as the arbiter. `/api/docs/*` excluded as a Swagger catch-all that answers 200 on any nonsense path; the control that catches it is one nonsense path per prefix.

title: Preflight leg 2's clean-room install scans four directories, so 6 of the 36 locks #1397 changed were never clean-room installed
description:
## BLUF

`lockfile-cleanroom.sh` (preflight leg 2) prints "All 35 standalone lock(s) pass" and reads like a total. It is a *surface*. Its file list comes from four hardcoded directories, so lockfiles under `connectors/`, `systemTest/` and the workspace root are never clean-room installed by that leg. On #1397 (KS-1425) that was **6 of the 36 changed lockfiles**.

## Measured

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh`, blob `518bffeeaf4a3c47a4660f594f822f34e26c2d15` — identical at develop `4eaf7741a6a4` and at #1397's head `3e7be2044fe8`, and the file is **not** one of the 37 paths #1397 changed, so this is not a regression introduced by that PR.

* `:46` builds the whole file list: `done < <(find services packages frontend scripts -maxdepth 2 -name package-lock.json | sort)`
* `:73` and `:87` are the install itself: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` (`:87` adds `--no-workspaces`)

The 6 changed locks outside that scope, from #1397's own file list:

* `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (the workspace root)
* `Blockchain/Dev/connectors/whatsapp-bot/package-lock.json`
* `systemTest/akto/package-lock.json`
* `systemTest/api-explorer/package-lock.json`
* `systemTest/performance/package-lock.json`
* `systemTest/playwright/package-lock.json`

Measured by classifying #1397's 36 changed `package-lock.json` paths against the `find` line above: **30 inside, 6 outside**.

## Why it did not bite on #1397

It was covered, but by checks **outside leg 2**, and only because the gate chose to run them: gate70's `realci` really installed the 5 standalone locks outside leg 2 (rc 0, locks unchanged), its C6 ran `npm ci` from the root lock (rc 0, 1,937 packages, root-lock sha256 `c7306d84307789ac` unchanged), and its C3 verified every tarball's integrity. gate70 recorded this as N-1397-7 Minor: "so 6 changed locks are outside it. Covered for this PR by realci + install + c3. Wants a ticket."

None of those three is leg 2, and none runs on an ordinary push.

## Not claimed

* That any of the 6 locks is actually broken. They were installed and passed on #1397.
* A fix. Widening `find` would add install time to every push, and `--no-workspaces` behaviour differs for the root lock; the `systemTest/*` locks also sit at indent 4 and inside Prettier's scope for two of the four packages, so a naive change there has its own blast radius.

## Sibling, not duplicate

* **KS-768** is the same four-directory class in **leg 7** (`audit-locks.mjs:77-88`, 35 of 45 lockfiles).
* **KS-1394** quotes this same `find` line, but its subject is leg 7's refusal message pointing at a regen command.
* **KS-773** (Done) is a different mechanism: an explicit `SKIP=` for a path already inside the scope.

Discovered 2026-10-06 during the #1397 / KS-1425 merge (gate70 finding N-1397-7; Wednesday's Q4 ruled it residue).

title: 28 unguarded err.message values land in 500 response bodies across six services - no NODE_ENV guard in any of the six files
description:
**BLUF:** **28 handlers across six services put a thrown error's own message straight into a 500 response body, and none of the six files carries a** `NODE_ENV` **guard.** That is a production information leak. KS 1334 and KS 1341 are the same defect, already fixed per-file; this ticket covers the remaining six files as one pass.

Measured by me at develop `f01c1da5717fdcb80a5e1aeeaa8ff9f0f00edd80`. Instrument: a per-line regex `\b(?:err|error)\.message\b` for the message expression, then a separate check that the enclosing statement answers 500. Positive control: `originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts` at the same sha reads `NODE_ENV` **1** time, so a zero below is a measurement and not a broken reader.

## Sites, by file

`api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` (blob `7945e1b01837`) — **6**: :126 :147 :176 :204 :234 :290
`api-gateway/src/routes/batch.ts` (blob `f2f48dca32e5`) — **3**: :166 :214 :262
`api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts` (blob `d87c04979e2b`) — **1**: :196
`transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (blob `33dd1f110f66`) — **1**: :283
`tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` (blob `82a6f8d4b623`) — **7**: :311 (500 at :330) :353 :392 :422 :483 :544 :564
`mcp-server/src/http-server.ts` (blob `fce4a31793b3`) — **10**: nine `INTERNAL_ERROR` envelopes at :61 :76 :110 :169 :182 :192 :202 :212 :265, plus :134, which is a non-envelope 500 body (`res.status(500).json({ verified: false, error: message })`)

`NODE_ENV` **occurrences in all six files: 0.**

## Four more leaks that are NOT in a 500 and are NOT counted above

Listed so the count is not mistaken for the whole surface:

`api-gateway/src/routes/batch.ts:118` — returned into a per-item result inside a 200
`api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:163` — a **502** body, `Failed to reach security service: ${err.message}`
`mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:104` and `:163` — pushed into a `results` array that is returned with 200

## UNMEASURED

* **Which errors actually reach these handlers in production.** Whether any carries a database string, a file path, an internal hostname or a credential fragment is not measured here, and settling it needs a running system, not a source read.
* No live reach. No request was issued against any of these routes.

## Why one ticket and not six

One test pass, one ticket. The per-file precedents (KS 1334 for adminConfig, KS 1341 for the webhooks routes) each closed a single file because each was found on its own; this set was found in one screening pass over the same class.

## Scope note on the neighbouring tickets, each read before filing

* KS 730 is the **guarded** remainder — its own wording is "71 response-side sites still return `err.message` verbatim **unless** `NODE_ENV === 'production'`". The sites above have **no** guard at all, so they are a different class and do not belong on it.
* KS 1346 is a **logging** defect (a non-Error throw logged as `[object Object]`), not a response-body leak.
* KS 1214 covers the mcp-server `POST /hash` route specifically, as an authentication defect; it overlaps one file here but not this class.

Searched before filing: all 522 open Secuura-PK issues, title and description, by exact substring on each of the six paths and on the message expression. Controls: a must-hit probe for the webhooks routes returned KS 1341, a must-hit probe for adminConfig returned KS 1334, and a deliberately absent string returned 0. No open ticket covers this set.

title: KS-921 residue: the re-link guard's awk parser is still case-sensitive — a lowercase `copy --from=builder … node_modules` reports 1 of 1 CLEAN, which is the #851 outage shape exactly
description:
## The re-link guard's own coverage and correctness residue — two false cleans, two false blocks, and a blind spot in the cross-check

From the **#870 tier-1 re-gate** (PASS WITH FINDINGS, verdict 2026-09-06T12:31Z; merged at
`066cff67554a5bd5398fcc9fb4b9ade422fbbd5b`, parents `e57bd5ac2` + `2f6b30fde`). All six findings are
**in the guard itself** — none was introduced as a live break, and **blast radius today is zero,**
**measured**: all 25 real Dockerfiles use canonical uppercase keywords and the guard is green on all 25
in both modes. That is why #870 was a GO. Every one of these is prospective on **authoring**.

Filed as one ticket per Kam's creation rule — the logical path is *the guard's own residue*. P2 on the
strength of F-A.

### F-A is reproduced here, not restated

I re-measured F-A myself before filing, from the **merged** tree, with the guard scoped by its own
`DEV_DIR` argument (`check-shared-relink.sh:69`) so each fixture gets its own root:

| case | differs from its control by | expected rc | actual rc |  |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ctl_pass` | — canonical, correct | 0 | **0** | guard can say clean |
| `ctl_user_fail` | `USER` before the re-link | 1 | **1** | guard can catch the ordering violation |
| `subj_a1` | **only** `USER` → `user` (2 diff lines) | 1 | **0** | **FALSE CLEAN** |
| `ctl_a2` | `COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules` after the re-link | 1 | **1** | guard can catch the clobber |
| `subj_a2` | **only** `COPY` → `copy` (2 diff lines) | 1 | **0** | **FALSE CLEAN** |

Both false cleans print `OK — 1 Dockerfile(s) … dev-tree (KS-490): 1 of 1 clean.` under
`SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1`. Each subject is byte-identical to a control that **does** fail, so the
harness discriminates in all four directions — an rc 0 here is the guard's answer, not the harness's.

`subj_a2` is **the #851 outage shape exactly**: a whole-tree `node_modules` write clobbering
`@secuura/shared` after the re-link, reported clean.

### The checklist

- [ ] **F-A — MAJOR, false clean. The SECOND OCCURRENCE OF F-1'S OWN CLASS.** F-1's `-i` landed on the
      *shell* class selectors (`:103`, `:121`) but the **awk parser it feeds is still case-sensitive on**
      **all four keywords** — `check-shared-relink.sh:162` `/^FROM[ \t]/`, `:173` `/^COPY[ \t]/`, `:195`
      `/^RUN[ \t]/`, `:223` `/^USER[ \t]/`; `toupper` appears **nowhere** in the file (verified by grep
      on the merged tree). **The cross-check cannot help:** these files DO match the precise selector,
      so there is no divergence to report — *both layers bypassed*. Fix shape: match on
      `toupper(first token)`, the same way the selector was fixed. Cells: the two rc-0 cases above,
      each asserting rc 1 **and** the specific clause-A message.
- [ ] **F-B — MAJOR. Clause A's link TARGET has no red-proof.** The cell named for it
      (`__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh:211`, *"A: a link to a DIFFERENT target does not satisfy*
      *the rule"*) varies the **destination** (`node_modules/@secuura/other`), not the target. Widen the
      guard regex target from `\/shared` to `\/[^ \t]*` and **the suite stays 26 passed, 0 failed**
      while the tampered guard accepts a link to `/WRONG-TARGET`. Cell to add: a fixture varying the
      **target** (`ln -s /elsewhere node_modules/@secuura/shared`), expecting rc 1 and `final stage has NO`.
- [ ] **F-C — MAJOR, false block, and it is from F-4's own widening.** `check-shared-relink.sh:210`,
      group `(\/[^ \t]*\/)?` **requires a leading** `/`, so `./node_modules/@secuura/shared` and
      `app/node_modules/…` fall out and are rejected with a message that is factually wrong about the
      file — the same complaint that made F-4 a Major. F-4's own stated rule is *"any destination*
      *ENDING at node_modules/@secuura/shared"*, and `./node_…` ends there. Confirmed on the merged tree.
- [ ] **F-D — Minor.** F-5 lowercased the **declared** side only (`:202` vs `:190`, consumed at `:264`),
      so `AS builder` + `--from=Builder` still fails under STRICT — a false block the day STRICT becomes
      the default, which is the harm F-5 was filed for.
- [ ] **F-E — Minor.** `USER root:root` and `USER 0:0` false-block at `:241` — the "one literal
      spelling" shape reappearing inside F-2's own oracle.
- [ ] **F-F — Minor.** The cross-check reads only `find . -name Dockerfile` (`:85`), so a
      `Dockerfile.prod` or a `Containerfile` is invisible to **both** instruments — the F-1 failure mode
      in the one dimension the new protection does not cover. Confirmed on the merged tree.

### Why three of these are KS-926 campaign members

F-B, F-A and F-F are members **7, 8 and 9** of the KS-926 family, and they are the sharpest yet
because **they are all inside a guard written to close this exact class**:

* **7 — F-B:** a cell whose *name* claims the axis it does not vary; widen the guard and the suite
  stays 26/0. *"A cell that cannot tell the fix from its own fallback is not a regression test"* in its
  purest form.
* **8 — F-A:** a fix applied at one layer and not at the layer it feeds, so the guard is blind on the
  axis it was **just repaired for** — and blind on the precise shape of a real past outage.
* **9 — F-F:** a protection described as *"the thing that notices the NEXT miss"* that can only notice
  misses of one kind.

With the launcher's member 6, **four of the nine were found inside work produced to close the family.**
That is the finding — a guard is exactly where this class hides, because a guard is the thing nobody
tests adversarially.

### Provenance

* The six findings, their line numbers and fix shapes | the QA agent's #870 re-gate verdict, relayed
  verbatim in Wednesday's RULING mail 2026-09-06T12:34:33Z (DKIM-verified: `spf=pass`,
  `dkim=pass header.i=@agentmail.to`, `dmarc=pass`, four failing-value controls absent) | read 2026-09-06
* F-A, F-C and F-F **independently confirmed by me** against the merged tree `066cff675` — awk keyword
  matches and absent `toupper`, the `:210` leading-slash group, and `:85`'s exact-name `find` | read 2026-09-06
* The F-A reproduction table | five fixtures run against `check-shared-relink.sh` from `066cff675`,
  each scoped by its own `DEV_DIR`, under `SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1` | measured 2026-09-06
* **NOT measured by me:** F-B's 26/0-under-tamper, F-D and F-E. Those are the tester's, named as such.

title: CI-runner environment gaps (one class, two jobs): `Security Scanning` runs `audit:contract` with no install, so `audit-locks.mjs` dies on `Cannot find package 'semver'` (7 of 59 cases red); `PR Security Gates` runs the shell suites with no build, so `ks949_main_seed_idempotence` aborts on a missing `packages/shared/dist` — the jobs' setup, not the code
description:
## BLUF

Two CI jobs run test code whose runtime prerequisites the job never installs or builds. Both reds are **environment gaps on the runner**, not defects in the code under test — each suite is green locally on a tree that has a root `node_modules` and a built `packages/shared`. Recorded here as ONE ticket because one fix pass (an install/build step per job) proves both, and because both were surfaced by the same lane on the same day. **Fixing either is a** `.github/workflows/` **edit — Kam-class; nothing here is changed by the seat that filed this.** Filed on Wednesday's ADDENDUM of 2026-09-13T21:58Z; board searched first (`packages/shared is not built` 0 hits · `npm run build -w packages/shared` 0 · `Cannot find package 'semver'` 1 — the closed ticket that gave `scripts/audit/` its own `package.json`, Done + archived · `CI-runner environment` 0 · nonsense-token control 0).

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a)** `Security Scanning` **→ job** `Dependency Audit` **→ step** `Audit-contract suites`**:** `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` **cannot start.**
  * Evidence: PR #940's run 34426409872 / job 102712486541 / step 7 — the first run where this step printed anything (PR #940 dropped `bash -e` from that step). `ℹ tests 59 · pass 52 · fail 7`; the seven reds are every `audit-locks:` case in `scripts/audit/gate-exit-codes.test.mjs` (`:91`, `:104`, `:113`, `:180`, `:192`, `:201`, `:208`), each "got 1" where 3 / 2 / 0 was expected. The `:192` case's assertion captured the child's output verbatim: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'semver' imported from /home/runner/work/Distributed_Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` (Node.js v24.20.0).
  * Mechanism: the job deliberately runs **no install** — the comment above its `npm audit` step says advisories resolve straight from the lockfile so no `npm ci` is needed. That is true for `npm audit` and false for the next step's test suite: `audit-locks.mjs:50` imports `semver`, which is declared only in `scripts/audit/package.json` (a standalone member, intentionally outside the workspaces list; its own description names exactly this failure on any tree without a root install). Locally the hoisted root `node_modules` supplies it → 59/59.
  * Not the same defect as the closed root-declaration ticket: that one added the declaration; this one is the CI job never installing it.
  * Fix shape (for whoever makes it): an install in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/` (or a root `npm ci`) before `npm run audit:contract` in that job.
- [ ] **(b)** `PR Security Gates` **→ job** `Code Security Gates` **→ step 11** `All shell test suites`**:** `packages/shared` **is never built.**
  * Evidence: develop's own push run at `8861e6216` — run 34755906436 / job 103720115281: `=== Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh ===` → `FAIL — packages/shared is not built (…/Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/dist/index.js missing) — run: npm run build -w packages/shared` → `0 passed, 1 failed (of 27 cells) — aborted`; the step's verdict `shell suites: 27 passed, 2 failed (of 29)` (the other FAILED line is `manifest_readers_agree.test.sh`, a different cause with its own Backlog ticket).
  * Mechanism: the job's setup is checkout + setup-node only — no `npm ci`, no build (PR #942's body already records the no-install half for `tsx`). The suite's own guard at `ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh:113` refuses to run without `packages/shared/dist/index.js`, exactly as designed. Locally the suite is 27/27 on a built tree (the merge seat's record for the PR that shipped it).
  * Fix shape: `npm ci` + `npm run build -w packages/shared` (or the workspace build) before `bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh` in that job — the same lesson PR #887's advisory job learned in review ("build before test").
- [ ] Re-read both jobs' logs at the fixing PR's head and confirm the two FAILED lines are gone and the counts read `59/59` and `N passed, 1 failed` (the `manifest_readers_agree` red stays until its own ticket closes).

## Attribution rule while this is open

Any PR whose CI shows these two lines is carrying develop's red, not its own: READY FOR QA mails from the CI-workflows lane attribute them to this ticket by id. Neither is absorbed into #940, #941 or #942.

Related: KS-1075 (the CI-gates config ticket whose PR #940 made (a) legible).

title: run-migrations.sh exits 0 even when a migration failed, and applied=N counts skips — the summary line cannot be trusted
description:
## BLUF

`scripts/run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 unconditionally, so docker-compose's** `service_completed_successfully` **is satisfied by a run in which a migration FAILED — and** `applied=N` **counts skips as applications. The only honest field in the summary line is** `failed=`**.**

This matters right now because KS-796's migration 046 ships with a deploy note that says "verify the constraint directly after the rebuild — the runner's exit is not evidence". That note is correct, and this ticket is why it has to exist.

**Three findings, and the first two are already known and deliberate — the third is not.**

## Recommendation

Split them. (1) and (2) are a design decision with a written rationale; (3) is a plain defect.

1. **Keep or change the unconditional** `exit 0` **— a decision, not a bug.** The rationale is in the script (`:147-155`): a partial failure must not block `--force-recreate`, because dependent services gate on `service_completed_successfully`. Changing it without replacing that mechanism turns a known-tolerable state into an outage. If it changes, the replacement is a distinction between *expected* drift failures and *unexpected* ones, not a bare `exit 1`.
2. **Fix** `applied_count` **regardless.** It is free and it is what makes the summary lie.
3. **Restore the tracker the script cites.** One line.

## Detail — measured at `2ddca095d`

**(1) The exit is unconditional and deliberate.** `scripts/run-migrations.sh:158` is a bare `exit 0`, and `:147-155` prints a WARN explaining why:

> *"Exiting 0 so docker compose dependent services can recreate; otherwise* `--force-recreate` *would block on migrations* `service_completed_successfully` *condition. (BACKLOG #6 — partial-failure exit semantics.)"*

So this is a recorded trade-off, not an oversight. Worth saying plainly, because a ticket that reads it as sloppiness will get the fix wrong.

**(2)** `applied=N` **counts skips.** `apply_one` (`:88`) returns **0** on the already-applied path:

```
already_applied=$(psql … "SELECT 1 FROM _secuura_migrations WHERE filename = '$fname' …")
if [ "$already_applied" = "1" ]; then
  echo "[$TARGET_NAME] Skipping $fname (already applied)"
  return 0          # <- indistinguishable from "applied it"
fi
```

and the caller (`:138`) increments `applied_count` on any zero return. A run that applies nothing and skips forty files reports `applied=40 failed=0`. Combined with (1), **both** fields in `Summary: applied=N failed=M` can be read as success when neither is.

**(3) The tracker the script points at does not exist.** `BACKLOG #6` is cited in the code as the home of this decision. `BACKLOG.md` at this head has **28** open entries and **not one** mentions the migration runner, partial-failure exits, or exit semantics — searched for `partial-failure`, `exit semantics`, `run-migrations` and `migration runner`, all zero, against a control (`grep -c "Where:"` → **35**) proving the search works on that file.

So the reasoning for a deliberate deviation now lives only in a shell comment pointing at a reference that has gone. That is the failure mode worth fixing first: a deferral outlives its tracker, and the next person to read `exit 0` has nothing to read.

## Why it is not higher than Medium

Nothing is currently mis-deploying because of it — the KS-796 deploy note routes around it by verifying the constraint directly, and the app's `startup-migrations.ts` has its own retry path. The risk is that a future deploy trusts the summary line. Priority is Kam's / Wednesday's call.

## Provenance

* Raised as **F-8 (MINOR, pre-existing)** by the KS-796 Q1+Q3 gate, PR #819 @ `ba6c60e35`, report §2.
* Every line number, the `apply_one` return path, the BACKLOG search and its control measured independently in this session at `2ddca095d` before filing.
* Related: **KS-796** (migration 046 and its deploy note), **KS-800**.

title: Security: POST /api/notifications still creates a notification for ANY userId (BOLA) — its owning ticket KS-486 is closed and archived
description:
## BLUF

The notification BOLA recorded in Review A ([KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor), row 1: "`POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body … any authenticated user pushes spoofed `security`/`system` notifications with an `actionUrl` to any user") is **still live on** `develop`. [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) is **Deployed to UAT and archived**, so the defect has **no open owner**. This ticket is that owner. It was raised separately, not appended to [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18), because Peter's rule is that only Backlog/Todo tickets are updated, and [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18) is In Progress.

## Evidence (re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff, 2026-10-07)

* **Create:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242`. `POST /` reads `userId` from `req.body` (`:244`) and stores the row under that user. There is no self-or-admin check against the caller's token.
* **Read:** `PATCH /:id/read` (`:155`) looks only in the **caller's** rows (`getUserId(req)` → `notifications.get(userId)`).
* **Live result.** Schemathesis 4.29.4, `pre-merge`, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) branch (no service changes), run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-01-26Z-slot2`:
  * The systemTest xfail `test_notification_bola.py::TestNotificationBola::test_cannot_create_notification_for_another_user` still gets **201**. It is marked xfail citing "[KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor)-A", a closed ticket.
  * The stateful sweep's `ensure_resource_availability` pair failed. `POST /api/notifications` created a row for a generated `userId`, then `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` as the caller answered `404 Notification not found`, test case `X8K02g`. That 404 is a symptom of the BOLA: the row went to someone else.
* That stateful pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at b280b74ff, so it is untriaged.

## Why it matters

Any authenticated user can place a `security` or `system` notification with an arbitrary `actionUrl` in **any** user's inbox: in-app phishing.

## Done when

- [ ] `POST /api/notifications` refuses a `userId` other than the caller's, unless the caller is an admin or internal service (decide which; the route comment calls it "internal").
- [ ] The xfail in `test_notification_bola.py` flips to a pass, and its marker and the systemTest reason text stop citing closed [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor). Peter owns that change ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage)).
- [ ] The stateful `ensure_resource_availability` pair stops firing, or is baselined against this ticket.

Found while running [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)'s pre-merge gate.

title: Three undeclared-verb catalogue skips cite CLOSED tickets (KS-406 / KS-421) — are the defects still live?
description:
## Summary

`tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py::test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked` skips three parametrised cases, each naming a ticket that is **Done and archived**:

| Case | Cited ticket | Ticket state | Skip reason |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/tiers/calculate-discount-GET` | [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-08 | authed GET executes (200) on an undeclared verb |
| `/tiers/calculate-vote-power-GET` | [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-08 | authed GET executes (200) |
| `/billing/customers/by-email-PUT` | [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-10 | authed PUT crashes (500) |

The catalogue is doing its job — it records a known defect so the sweep does not re-report it — but it points at tickets closed a month ago. Either the defects are still live and need a current owner, or they were fixed and the entries should be removed so the tests execute.

**This is the same class the** [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) **report fix addresses**, one layer over: a stale ticket reference reads as "tracked" when nothing tracks it.

## Why you

The question is a platform one, not a harness one: **did** [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of)**'s auth-first-401 posture decision and** [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods)**'s billing classifier actually resolve these three, or not?** Once that is known, the systemTest side is mechanical (remove the entries, or repoint them at a live ticket) and I'll do it.

[KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) was a *design decision* (adopt auth-first 401 for undeclared verbs) rather than a fix, so its two entries may be permanently correct behaviour that should be recorded as accepted rather than as a tracked defect. [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) was a real fix for `GET .../payment-methods`; whether it covered the `PUT .../by-email` sibling is worth checking.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# undeclared GET — expect a safe rejection (401/403/404/405), not 200
curl -i -X GET  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:6882/api/tiers/calculate-discount
curl -i -X GET  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:6882/api/tiers/calculate-vote-power

# undeclared PUT — expect a safe rejection, not 500
curl -i -X PUT  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/billing/customers/by-email
```

The suite's own guard: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py -v -rsxX`

## Environment

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, `10.211.55.4`. Node 24.19.0, PostgreSQL 15.18, Redis 8.10.0, Python 3.14.6, Schemathesis 4.24.3. Run `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`.

## Outcome wanted

For each of the three: **live defect** (→ new ticket, repoint the entry) or **accepted/fixed** (→ remove the entry so the test executes and asserts the safe rejection). A skip is not a pass — while these sit in the catalogue the vectors are unverified.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

title: M365 routes answer 503 when ENTRA_* is unconfigured — 9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every dev machine, and the local sweep is now the merge gate
description:
## BLUF

**Four M365 operations answer** `503 Service Unavailable` **when** `ENTRA_*` **is unconfigured, and a 503 is a server error — so every Schemathesis run on a normal dev machine records 9 failures that are configuration, not defects.** This is the KS-478 / KS-451 / KS-431 "raw 5xx instead of a clean refusal" family, and it now matters more than it did: since Kam retired GitHub Actions on 2026-08-27, the local Schemathesis run **is** the merge gate, so a permanent 9-failure floor makes that gate unreadable.

Found on the first run under the new final-check rule — develop `ca5b643e0`, full 32-service stack, auth re-seeded, run validity OK (0 of 307 operations errored).

## The failures

`9 failures, 3 warnings in 72.21s` — all `Server error`, all the same body:

```
[503] Service Unavailable
{"success":false,"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
 "message":"M365 integration not configured",
 "details":{"setup":"Add Microsoft 365 Business Basic license and configure ENTRA_* env vars"}}}
```

Operations:

| operation |
| -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/init` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/{id}/refresh` |
| `POST /api/m365/documents/sync` |

Reproduce (from the report):

```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"organizationId":"e3e70682-c209-1cac-a29f-6fbed82c07cd","tenantId":"84fe882e-d558-4800-892d-eb967ea4a232"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/m365/connections/init
```

## Why this is a defect and not just "configure your env"

**A missing integration credential is a known, permanent, expected state on every developer machine and in CI — it is not an unexpected server fault. **`503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` says "the server broke or is overloaded, retry later". Neither is true: the server is healthy and retrying will never help until someone buys an M365 licence.

The service already knows exactly what is wrong — it returns a precise, actionable `details.setup` string. It has all the information needed to answer honestly and chooses a 5xx anyway.

This is the same reasoning the team already accepted for KS-478 (`raw 5xx on POST /api/governance/delegate … instead of a clean business refusal`). The only difference is that this one is triggered by configuration rather than by input.

## Options

1. `501 Not Implemented` — the literal meaning: this server does not support this function. Declares in the spec, is not a server error, and Schemathesis will not flag it.
2. `400`**/**`422` **on the call** — treats "no connection configured" as a precondition failure like every other precondition in KS-478.
3. **Do not mount the routes at all when** `ENTRA_*` **is absent**, so they 404 like any unmounted feature. Cleanest, but changes the published surface conditionally, which the OpenAPI contract work (KS-663) would need to account for.

Whichever is chosen, **the response must be declared in the OpenAPI spec** or it will simply move from a `server_error` failure to a `status_code_conformance` failure.

## Interim, so the gate is usable today

Until this is fixed the four operations should be registered as by-design tolerated in `systemTest/schemathesis` (the KS-662 / KS-518 guard pattern) **scoped to these four operations by name and to the 503-when-unconfigured case only** — not a blanket 5xx tolerance. Without that, every author running the mandated final check sees 9 red and has to learn to ignore it, which is precisely how a gate stops working.

## Provenance

Schemathesis `pr` tier, develop `ca5b643e0`, 2026-08-27T08:50:44Z, seed 2899853179.
Report: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pr-2026-08-27T08-50-44Z/`.

title: Bare arithmetic-command `((X++))` under `set -e` — exits 1 at 0 and bash ≥ 4.1 errexit kills the script: 10 errexit-live sites remain in `sync-secrets.sh` (×8) and `validate-lint.sh` (×2) after #977's docker-build.sh fix
description:
## BLUF

The class fixed in `docker-build.sh` by PR #977 round 2 (KS-877) and in `validate-env.sh` by KS-680 is still present at **10 errexit-live sites in two host scripts**. An arithmetic command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0, and a post-increment yields the OLD value — so `((COUNT++))` at COUNT=0 "fails", and bash ≥ 4.1 `set -e` exits the script on it (bash COMPAT item 45), silently. bash 3.2 (macOS) does not apply errexit to arithmetic commands, so these scripts pass on the Mac and die on Linux / CI / containers at their first count.

## Census (develop `3fc158c39`, 2026-09-13)

Instrument: the CELL 4 regex from `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh` — `^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$` — over tracked `*.sh` (`git grep -nE`, `[[:space:]]` not `\s`: BSD grep). Positive control: 2 hits on `docker-build.sh` at `a70585823`, 0 at `aede93117`.

| file | sites | errexit | context |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/sync-secrets.sh` | **8** — `:186 :192 :198 :204 :216 :221 :227 :232` (`SKIPPED`, `GENERATED`, `UPDATED`) | `set -euo pipefail` at `:20` | each inside an `if … then` BODY (not a condition) — errexit-live; the first `((SKIPPED++))` / `((GENERATED++))` / `((UPDATED++))` at 0 exits the script on bash ≥ 4.1 |
| `systemTest/schemathesis/validate-lint.sh` | **2** — `:33 :38` (`PASS_COUNT`, `FAIL_COUNT`) | `set -e` at `:6` | to be confirmed at the site (a tested context suppresses errexit) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/validate-env.sh` | 3 — `:62 :81 :99` | `set -e` at `:9` | **NOT defects** — inside `if check_required_var …` bodies, where errexit is suppressed for the whole function (KS-680 measured both ways); listed so the census is complete |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh` | 0 at `aede93117` (2 at `a70585823`) | `set -euo pipefail` | fixed in #977 round 2 |

## Fix shape (measured on 3.2.57; the shape Peter named on the archived bash-3.2 portability ticket, and KS-680's at `validate-env.sh:179-219`)

`COUNT=$((COUNT + 1))` — an assignment's exit status is 0 at every value and the effect is identical. Not `((++X))` (a pre-decrement evaluates to 0 at the last step and fails there); not `((X++)) || true` (masks the status instead of removing the failing construct).

## Durable home

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-script-portability.sh` has 7 rules and none for this construct (a "rule 8" was proposed on the portability ticket and reverted on KS-666). The census regex above is the candidate rule; the suite's CELL 4 shows the shape with its positive control.

## Searched before filing

`RUNNING++`, `((RUNNING`, `arithmetic command`, `post-increment`, `errexit`, `set -e`, `bash 4.1`, `sync-secrets`, `validate-lint` — 0 literal title hits among open issues; the archived homes (KS-680 and the docker-build portability ticket's defect (c)) surface only with `includeArchived: true`. Not fixed this round — filed on Wednesday's ruling (s208, 2026-09-13).

title: Job 04: a trivy that exits 0 with a bare `{}` still reads as a clean image
description:
**BLUF:** #1051 turns a failed, empty, partial or unparseable trivy output into `scan-failed`. One shape still passes as clean: **rc 0 with a bare** `{}`. It gives `counts:{}`, "clean", rc 0 and the clean summary, identical at develop and at #1051's head.

title: A bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker DOES exempt a quoted value in all five slot guards — the closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, contradicting systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169
description:
**BLUF:** the platform rule says a bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker exempts nothing, but on a **quoted value** (JSON, or any line where the marker is not last) the value's own closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, so **a bare marker DOES exempt**. Measured in all five harness guards' shared regex shape. Found while fixing KS-1450; not introduced by it.

## The rule it contradicts

`systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`, verbatim:

> A deliberate exception carries `slot-literal-ok: <reason>` on the same line; a bare marker exempts nothing.

## The defect

Every implementation tests for "marker, optional whitespace, then one non-whitespace character":

```
no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh   grep -vE 'slot-literal-ok:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]'
playwright/.../no-hardcoded-slot-literals.test.ts:79    const MARKER = /slot-literal-ok:\s*\S/
performance/.../noHardcodedSlotLiterals.test.ts:49      const MARKER = 'slot-literal-ok:'
schemathesis/.../test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50   _OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"
akto/tests/unit/config/noTypedSlotValues.test.ts        (same shape)
```

`[^[:space:]]` / `\S` is satisfied by **any** non-space character, including `"`. So:

```
  "reason": "x 6982 slot-literal-ok:",      -> EXEMPTED   (wrong: the reason is empty)
const p = 6982; // slot-literal-ok:          -> reported   (right)
```

Driven both ways in one call against the same regex. The only reason this has never shown up is that every existing marker sits in a `#` or `//` comment at true end-of-line, where nothing follows the colon — which is also why the suites' own controls pass: each plants its bare-marker fixture into a comment, never into a quoted value. `test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:263` asserts "the bare marker does not \[exempt\]" and passes for exactly that reason.

## Why it matters now

KS-1450 is the first change to put `slot-literal-ok` markers inside JSON string values (the six `accepted.*.reason` entries of `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json`). Before it, that file carried **zero** markers, so the gap was latent. It is recorded as a named limitation in KS-1450's PR Test Evidence rather than fixed there, because a one-guard fix would make the five guards disagree about what a bare marker means.

## Suggested fix

Require a reason character that is not structural, e.g. tighten the class to `[^[:space:]",]` (and the JS/Python equivalents) in **all five** implementations in one change, so they stay in agreement.

**Blast radius, measured before proposing it:** exactly **2** existing marker lines repo-wide would lose exemption, and **neither needs it** — `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50` (`_OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"`, a constant; the line holds no slot literal) and the shell guard's own bare-marker control line (its port is computed, not typed). So nothing that passes today would go red.

Each implementation should also gain a control that plants the bare marker into a **quoted value**, not only into a comment — the absence of that control is what hid this.

## Provenance

* Both-way measurement and the blast-radius count: Seat R 16th, 2026-10-08, during KS-1450.
* The rule: `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`.
* The guard: KS-1386 (Done, Peter).

title: observability/ reaches the platform by slot 1's container names (documented), and both .env examples suggest the nginx stub_status on :6882, a port that does not exist on the container network
description:
## BLUF

`observability/` is **slot 1 only by a documented decision**, and that decision stands. This ticket records what would need to change to make it slot-aware, so the work is ready when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)'s `/metrics` lands. It also covers **one real error to fix now**: both example env files suggest a gateway status URL on a port that does not exist inside the container network.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## 1. The concrete error (small, fix any time)

* `observability/.env.example:47` and `observability/config/alerting.env.example:55` both say:
  `# SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=http://secuura-nginx-gateway:6882/stub_status`
* **6882 is the host-side port of the gateway's** `6882:80` **publish.** Inside the container network only **80** exists. The compose default already uses it (`docker-compose.yml:331`: `${SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI:-http://secuura-nginx-gateway:80/stub_status}`), and `prometheus/prometheus.yml:48-52` explains why the old `:6882` scrape job was removed for exactly this reason.
* Anyone who uncomments the example gets an nginx exporter that cannot connect. **Fix:** change both examples to `:80`.

## 2. Where observability assumes slot 1 (documented, for when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands)

| Where | What | Documented as |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/observability.sh:57` | `docker inspect secuura-nginx-gateway` to discover the platform network | override `SECUURA_PLATFORM_NETWORK` |
| `scripts/observability.sh:96-100` | `docker exec "${SECUURA_PG_CONTAINER:-secuura-postgres}"` to read DB credentials | "SLOT 1 ONLY, deliberately" (`:88-90`) |
| `scripts/observability.sh:137-138` | `docker inspect "${SECUURA_REDIS_CONTAINER:-secuura-redis}"` | same limitation |
| `docker-compose.yml:296, 311, 331` | exporter defaults name `secuura-postgres`, `secuura-redis`, `secuura-nginx-gateway` | same |
| `prometheus/prometheus.yml:82-92` | `secuura-services` static targets `secuura-auth:4003` … labelled `slot: slot1` | "⚠ SLOT 1 ONLY" (`:74-78`) |
| `loki/alloy.river:84-92` | default `slot = "slot1"` for **every** container, then more specific rules override | README "Which stack slot am I looking at?" |

The README states the position clearly ("What is NOT per-slot: application metrics"), and the reasoning in `prometheus.yml:74-78` is sound: slot discovery needs either a Docker socket inside Prometheus or a generated targets file plus per-slot `docker network connect`, and neither is worth it while the job collects nothing ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)).

**One small thing worth considering, independent of** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)**:** `alloy.river`'s default labels non-platform containers (Akto, observability's own, a k6 container without its label) as `slot1`. A neutral default such as `unslotted` would stop those logs appearing under slot 1 in the picker. That matches the rule the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest fix adopts: an unslotted run is labelled `unslotted`, never `slot1`.

## Suggested shape (when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) is picked up)

* Derive container names from `STACK_PREFIX` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh:58-64`: `secuura` on slot 1, `secuura-s<N>` above) rather than typing `secuura-<svc>`.
