title: gate/report.ts writeGateReport overwrites the input summary when --summary does not end in -summary.json
description:
## BLUF

`systemTest/performance/gate/report.ts:325` derives the gate-report path with `const reportPath = summaryPath.replace(/-summary\.json$/, '-gate-report.json');`. When the `--summary` path does not end in `-summary.json` the replace is a no-op, `reportPath === summaryPath`, and `:346` `fs.writeFileSync(reportPath, …)` **overwrites the raw k6 summary with the gate report** — silently, with the log line claiming success. The runner's own naming (`runner/cli.ts:209`, `run_dir.ts:300`) always ends `-summary.json`, so the default pipeline is safe; the exposure is the documented `--summary` override on either CLI (`runner/cli.ts:22`, `gate/cli.ts:15`) — the by-hand re-gate path — and the loss is of the run's only raw record.

Found by the tier-2 QA gate on PR #988 (KS-704) as **F-5, Major, develop-own**: `writeGateReport` is byte-identical at that PR's base M38 `0e78c7270` and head `8cb99a002`, so it is NOT #988's regression and was not a NO GO; it exists at M38 and on every later develop. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-988-ks704-tier2-r1/report.md` §5 F-5 (evidence `cli_conv.out`, `p8`…). Filed by the merge seat s228 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 2026-09-14 09:10:43Z. Board searched first by the symbol `writeGateReport` (0 hits), the path `gate/report.ts` (4 hits: KS-704 itself, KS-1066, KS-929, KS-971 — none about this overwrite), `summaryPath.replace` (0) and `-gate-report.json` (2 archived report mentions) — every KS issue incl. archived, titles + descriptions + comments.

## Repro (the gate's, verbatim in substance; measured at runtime, replicated ×3)

From a known state (`systemTest/performance` after `npm ci`):

1. `cp tests/unit/fixtures/smoke-summary.json <dir>/summary.json` (k6's own `--summary-export` default basename).
2. `npx tsx gate/cli.ts --scenario smoke --summary <dir>/summary.json`
3. Read `<dir>/summary.json`.

**Expected** (oracle: Purpose + Product — the function's docstring and the log line say it *writes the gate report beside the summary*; `runner/cli.ts:22` documents `--summary` as a free path): a new `…-gate-report.json`; the input untouched.

**Observed:** stdout `[ci-gate] Gate report written: <dir>/summary.json`; the file's keys become `scenario,slot,slotTag,gatewayPort,runLabel,timestamp,passed,results` — the `metrics` map is gone; sha256 `a8f5ed22…` → `86143afe…`. Reproduced on the breached copy, the healthy copy and a third fresh copy.

**Control:** the same file named `smoke-summary.json` → `smoke-gate-report.json` is written beside it and the input is intact.

## Reach

* The documented `--summary` override on either CLI (`runner/cli.ts:22`, `gate/cli.ts:15`) — the path a human uses when re-gating an old run by hand. The default runner pipeline never produces a non-conforming name.
* **Sibling of the same class (read only, not reproduced):** `runner/k6_docker.ts:241` `summaryMount.replace(/-summary\.json$/, '-k6.log')` — with the same non-conforming name the k6 log path collapses onto the summary mount.

## Fix-shape (for the owner)

* Derive `reportPath` from the directory + scenario: `path.join(path.dirname(summaryPath), scenario + '-gate-report.json')`, and/or throw when `reportPath === summaryPath`.
* Apply the same shape to the `k6_docker.ts:241` sibling.

## Regression cell

A unit cell that calls `writeGateReport(results, '<tmp>/summary.json', 'smoke')` and asserts (a) the input file's sha256 is unchanged and (b) a sibling `smoke-gate-report.json` exists beside it. A second cell for the `-summary.json` control keeps the existing behaviour pinned.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `writeGateReport` never writes to its input path; a non-conforming `--summary` name yields a sibling `<scenario>-gate-report.json` (or a thrown, named error).
- [ ] The `k6_docker.ts:241` sibling handled the same way or recorded as accepted with the reason.
- [ ] The two regression cells above green; the existing `tests/unit/gate/` cells and goldens unchanged.

## Follow-up (ruled by Wednesday 2026-09-14 10:11Z, from the #988 gate F-3)

* The `reportFailedGateBreakdown` cell (`systemTest/performance/tests/unit/gate/reportFailedGateBreakdown.test.ts:103-108`) builds its expectations with `String(n)` while the product prints `toLocaleString()` — they coincide only below 1,000; build the expectation with `toLocaleString()` or add one cell with a synthetic `{ http_server_error: { passes: 1234, fails: 0, value: 1 } }` expecting `passes=1,234` under a pinned locale.

title: Base-image refresh routine + track postgres CVE-2025-68121 (redis leg already done in triage)
description:
## Context — KS-363 follow-up (residual criticals after the base-image refresh)

After KS-363 (all built images → `node:22-alpine` / `nginx:1.29-alpine`, **0 critical across the 31 built images**), residual criticals appeared only against the two pinned third-party infra images. Investigated before assuming "major bump needed" — **major bumps buy nothing for either**, and the redis finding turned out to be a stale local scan cache, not a platform exposure.

## 1. redis — RESOLVED during triage (was a stale local image, demo never affected)

* The 6 crit / 59 high initially flagged were in a **stale local Docker cache** of `redis:7-alpine` (pre-pull digest).
* The current upstream digest `sha256:6ab0b6e7…` scans **0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH** — and it is exactly what the ACR mirror holds and what `secuura02-demo-redis` runs. Verified via `az acr import --force` (digest unchanged → ACR already current).
* `redis:8-alpine` is identical (0/0) — no major bump warranted.
* Done: local image re-pulled + container recreated; demo redis app restarted (idempotent) and Running; portals/API re-verified 200.

## 2. postgres — CVE-2025-68121, unfixable by us today (local-only surface) — the one real residual

* `postgres:15-alpine`: 1 critical = **CVE-2025-68121** (Go stdlib `crypto/tls` incorrect certificate validation, in the image's Go helper binary; fixed in Go 1.24.13 / 1.25.7).
* Present **identically in** `postgres:16-alpine` **and** `postgres:17-alpine` — a major bump does not clear it. It clears when Docker Hub rebuilds the image against a patched Go toolchain.
* Demo uses managed `secuura02-demo-pg` (PG 15 flexible server), so this container image is **local dev only**.
* **Action:** periodically re-pull `postgres:15-alpine` and re-scan; close when the upstream rebuild lands.

## 3. Systemic: pinned-tag digests go stale silently

The ACR `node:22-alpine` mirror WAS genuinely stale during KS-363 (needed `--force` re-import before the demo build), and the redis false alarm came from the same mechanism on a local cache. Alpine-based images republish the same tag with fixes; mirrors/local caches keep old digests and quietly re-accumulate CVEs — and stale caches also produce misleading scan results.

**Proposal:** a lightweight refresh routine — periodically (e.g. monthly or per deploy): `az acr import --force` for the mirrored bases (`node:22-alpine`, `nginx:1.29-alpine`, `edoburu/pgbouncer:1.22.1-p0`, `redis:7-alpine`) + `docker compose pull` locally, then re-scan. Could live in `deploy.sh` or a small script + reminder.

## Scanner note

Trivy v0.58.1; the KS-363 Docker Scout baseline rated redis 0 critical — consistent with the stale-local-cache explanation (Scout scanned a fresh rebuild).

title: start-secuura.sh --rebuild leaves ~30 untagged images per slot per rebuild (and interrupted rebuilds pin them)
description:
Raised from platform-s ([PS-1012](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox>)) rather than fixed from there, because `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` is platform-k's.

## What happens

`docker compose` names each built image `<compose project>-<service>`: `platform-k-*` for slot 1, `secuura_slot2-*` for slot 2, and so on. `start-secuura.sh --rebuild` builds every service again (the serial per-service `docker compose build` from [KS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-345/start-secuurash-rebuild-hangs-on-the-full-33-service-compose-bake)). Each rebuild moves those tags to new images, and the previous image of each service is left untagged as `<none>`. That's about 30 images per slot per rebuild, some of them 0.6–2.2 GB. Nothing in the script prunes images or the build cache. A grep of `start-secuura.sh` for `prune`, `rmi` and `image rm` finds nothing.

**The worse case is an interrupted rebuild.** On 2026-10-02 the Pro had 29 `<none>` images, every one held by a container in K slot 1's project (`platform-k`) that was `Created` **but never started**: `secuura-auth`, `secuura-api-gateway`, `secuura-originate` and others. Docker won't prune an image a container uses, so those stayed until someone removed them by hand (Stuart did).

## Measured (MacBook Pro, Docker Desktop, 2026-10-07)

* `docker system df`: images 20.7 GB, of which 1.76 GB is reclaimable. The **build cache is 39.6 GB, of which 22.65 GB is reclaimable**, mostly entries last used in the previous two days by slot rebuilds.

## Suggested fix (for Kamil's judgement)

The platform-s side is doing this in [PS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox) / [Secuura/platform-s#909](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1012-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox-synced-machines-994c737d0439):

* **Label every build with its owner:** for compose, a `labels:` entry under each service's `build:` such as `com.secuura.slot-image=<project>-<service>`, or one label per project.
* **Before rebuilding,** run `docker image prune -f --filter label=…` scoped to this compose project. Without `-a`, this removes only dangling, unused images from earlier builds of this slot. It never touches another slot, platform-s, a tagged image, or an image a container still uses.
* **After an interrupted rebuild,** remove that slot's `Created`-but-never-started containers, so they stop pinning old images.
* **Don't prune the build cache automatically.** It's shared by every slot on both platforms, so pruning it makes everyone's next build cold. Documenting a manual `docker builder prune --filter until=168h -f` is enough.

title: POST /api/status/{id}/revoke accepts `index: {}` (object where integer is declared) with 200 — outside the KS-518/KS-662 ruling, which covers only `index` below `minimum`
description:
## Finding

`POST /api/status/0/revoke` with body `{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": {}}` answered **HTTP 200** `{"statusListId":"0","credentialId":"example-credentialId","revoked":true,"revokedAt":"2026-09-18T11:28:19.243Z"}` — the revoke side effect ran with an `index` that is an **object**, where the published schema declares an integer.

Surfaced by `by_design_input_tolerance_guard` ([KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)) in the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) after-sweep — `full-2026-09-18T11-19-19Z-slot1`, Schemathesis 4.27.2, coverage phase, head `52df64f84`, slot 1. The guard's own message: *"accepted a schema-violating request with HTTP 200, and the violation is NOT the one ruled by-design for this operation (*[KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) */* [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)*)."* That is the guard doing exactly what it was built for: the [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) ruling tolerates **only** `index` below the declared `minimum` on this operation; a wrong-typed `index` is a different violation and must still be rejected.

Two things make this worse than "permissive input":

* The handler **performed the revoke** and reported `revoked: true` for an index it cannot have resolved as an integer — compare [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)'s note that `GET /api/status/{id}/check/{index}` silently coerces a float to a different index. Which entry (if any) was actually flipped is unknown from the response.
* It is a **write** on a revocation status list, i.e. a legally significant record.

## Why it appeared now

Schemathesis 4.27.2 generates a different coverage-phase case set for this op (32 → 58 cases; `POST /api/status/{id}/unrevoke` 50 → 68) — the `allOf`/`additionalProperties` and example-completion fixes in that release. The platform behaviour is not new; the question had not been asked in this shape before. [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data)'s original repro set only exercised `index: -1`.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"<ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD>"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": {}}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/status/0/revoke
```

Expected **400/422**. Actual **200** with `revoked: true`.

Artefacts: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-2026-09-18T11-19-19Z-slot1/` (NDJSON `ScenarioFinished` for `POST /api/status/{id}/revoke`, check `by_design_input_tolerance_guard`).

## Fix direction

Validate `index` as an integer at the handler boundary (the Zod schema the spec is generated from already declares it) and refuse with a mapped 4xx before any list mutation. Per [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the), do **not** widen the harness exception — the guard is the arbiter; if the ruling is to be widened, that is a deliberate decision on this ticket, not a config edit.

Same class as [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) (Done, by-design for `index < minimum` only). Found by the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) bump sweep, 2026-09-18.

title: run-migrations.sh readiness probe discards "command not found" and blames the database — a missing pg_isready reads as "PostgreSQL did not become ready"
description:
## BLUF

`run-migrations.sh`**'s readiness probe throws away the one message that says what is wrong, then blames the database.** When `pg_isready` is not installed, the probe's `2>/dev/null` discards *"pg_isready: command not found"*, the loop runs its full 30 attempts against a command that never executed, and the script exits 2 with:

```
ERROR: PostgreSQL did not become ready after 30 attempts.
```

**The database was up and answering the whole time.** The reader is sent to the database, the network and the DSN — none of which is the fault.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh`, the wait loop (`MAX_RETRIES=30`, `RETRY_INTERVAL=2`):

```sh
if pg_isready -h "$PG_HOST" -p "$PG_PORT" -q 2>/dev/null; then
```

`-q` silences `pg_isready`'s own output and `2>/dev/null` silences the shell's *"command not found"*. Between them, a missing binary and an unreachable server are **byte-indistinguishable** from the script's output — and they have opposite fixes.

## Measured, 2026-09-25

On a disposable `postgres:15-alpine` instance on `127.0.0.1:55432`, built from `docker/init`:

* Host run: **exit 2**, `ERROR: PostgreSQL did not become ready after 30 attempts` (60 s of retries).
* **Control, same instant, same instance:** `pg_isready -U secuura -d secuura` **inside** the container returns `accepting connections`, **rc 0**. So the server was ready throughout.
* `which pg_isready` on the host: **absent**. `which psql`: **absent**.
* **Positive control that the script is otherwise fine:** copying the same script and `migrations/` into the container (where both binaries exist) and running it there gives `applied=49, failed=0`, rc 0, against that same database. **Only the host tooling differed.**

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic message

1. **It costs 60 seconds before it lies.** The loop cannot succeed, but it still burns all 30 attempts.
2. **The failure is attributed to the wrong system.** This is the class the repo already takes seriously — a verdict composed separately from the work (`STANDING_LINES.md`, *"a verdict line is a claim about what ran"*). Here the verdict names a component that was never consulted.
3. **It is a first-run experience.** A developer or a fresh VM without the Postgres client tools meets this before anything else, and the message points away from the fix.

## NOT claimed

* **Not a product defect and nothing shipped on it.** The script exits **2**, so it fails loudly; this is about *which* cause it names, not about a silent pass. It is **not** the same defect as KS-808 (`applied=N` counting skips / exit 0 on failure) — that is the summary lying about success, this is the probe lying about the cause.
* Whether any deployed environment or image lacks `pg_isready` was **not** measured. In the compose `migrations` service the binary is present, so this is reached by host/dev runs and by any image that drops the client tools.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. **Check the binary exists first** and say so: `command -v pg_isready >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: pg_isready is not installed — install the postgres client tools"; exit 4; }`. A distinct exit code keeps the two causes distinguishable to callers.
2. **Keep the stderr on the last attempt** so the real message survives into the log.
3. Fall back to a `psql -c 'SELECT 1'` probe (the script already depends on `psql`), which at least fails with a message about the thing it could not do.

(1) is the smallest and removes the misattribution entirely.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,285 issues incl. archived, 3,631 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `pg_isready` -> 3 total / 2 open: **KS-1161** and KS-485. **KS-1161 is NOT a duplicate** — read in full, it is the redis healthcheck exposing `REDIS_PASSWORD` via `docker inspect`.
* `run-migrations.sh` -> 13 total / 7 open (KS-1054, KS-1031, KS-980, KS-808, KS-772, KS-601, KS-485). The two nearest were read in full: **KS-1054** is fail-open RLS from migration *ordering* on boot 1; **KS-808** is the runner's `applied=N` summary counting skips. Neither owns the readiness probe.
* `did not become ready` -> **0**. `command not found` -> 8 total / 1 open (KS-1137, a different script).
* Controls that fire: `KS-808` -> 4; `run-shell-suites.sh` -> 28 / 13 open. So the search discriminates.

## Provenance

Found on 2026-09-25 while provisioning a disposable PostgreSQL for KS-980's red proof (PR #1242), on the coordinator's instruction to file it rather than carry it. Tier 3 when picked up; not this round.

title: The whole super-admin surface is silently unscanned — no system_admin block means the HAR replay fallback never fires (0 of 16 endpoints, incl. KS-694's GDPR routes)
description:
## BLUF

Every **super-admin-only** endpoint is invisible to Akto on a stock local checkout, and nothing says so. `config/secrets.yml` carries no `system_admin` block — `config/secrets.example.yml` documents one — so `resolveReplayTokens()` returns `adminToken: null`, the issuer→admin fallback never fires, and each endpoint `ISSUER_ADMIN` cannot get a 2xx from stays a spec-imported placeholder (`responseCode: -1`) that `api_selection_filters` excludes from **every** BOLA/BFLA/authz template.

The bias is the problem: the endpoints that are hardest to authenticate to are the privileged ones, so the harness systematically skips the surface where an authz defect matters most — and reports green.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2

```
collection 56068490 "OpenAPI Secuura API": 323 endpoints
  absolute (scannable)  : 307
  relative (unscannable):  16

endpoints scanned, BOLA run:
  relative : 0 / 16
  absolute : 46 / 80 sampled     <-- discriminating control
```

The 16 that never get scanned:

```
/api/admin/audit/export      /api/analytics/activity        /api/analytics/certifications
/api/analytics/governance    /api/analytics/overview        /api/analytics/revenue
/api/analytics/users         /api/analytics/verifications   /api/audit-log
/api/billing/customers/by-email  /api/gdpr/consent/check    /api/gdpr/deletion-log
/api/m365/callback           /api/oauth/authorize           /api/onedrive/files
/api/system-errors
```

The 7 `analytics` paths are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS-357). **The other 9 are not excluded by anything — they are simply unreachable by the replay persona.** They include `/api/gdpr/deletion-log`, `/api/gdpr/consent/check` and `/api/system-errors` — the exact routes **KS-694 (Urgent)** just put a role gate on, and `/api/oauth/authorize`.

Note the tell: an unscannable entry is stored as a bare path (`/api/audit-log` — the tenant-provisioning upstream path) while a scanned one is a full gateway URL (`http://localhost:6882/api/documents`). That difference is a cheap, reliable detector.

## Proof of causation

Adding the documented `system_admin` block to local `secrets.yml` (gitignored; seeded `admin@secuura.com`, per `secrets.example.yml`):

```
captured 2xx samples : 71 → 79
audit-log in api_info: /api/audit-log  →  http://localhost:6882/api/platform/audit-log
ADD_USER_ID on it    : 0 rows → 1 row
```

That change is what made **KS-708** reproducible at all. Before it, `ADD_USER_ID` reported *"188 tested, 0 vulnerable"* while never touching the endpoint under investigation.

## The documentation understates it

`secrets.example.yml:30-34` says `system_admin` is *"optional. Only needed to seed the locked-account test-role… Absent ⇒ that one role is skipped (best-effort), and* `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` *keeps skipping honestly."*

That is not the whole consequence. Absent, it also removes the entire super-admin surface from HAR replay, and therefore from every similarity-based authz template. Nobody reading that comment would expect it.

## Suggested shape

1. **Warn loudly when** `adminToken` **is null** — name the count of endpoints that will consequently have no 2xx sample. Silence is the actual defect; a skipped endpoint should never be indistinguishable from a clean one (the KS-700 / KS-709 principle, applied to coverage rather than results).
2. Correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence.
3. Consider failing `test:setup` when the block is absent, or defaulting it to the seeded local admin.

## Done means

1. A run without a system-admin token says so, with the affected endpoint count.
2. `secrets.example.yml` states the real consequence.
3. The relative-vs-absolute URL split is asserted somewhere, so this cannot silently regress.

title: 06-tenant-isolation.sh writes the runner's stderr into its JSON artefact, so a legitimate fallback run produces an unparseable result
description:
`Blockchain/Testing/jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh:71` redirects the runner's **stderr into the same file as its JSON result**:

```
TARGET_BASE="$TARGET" "$TSX_BIN" "$RUNNER" > "$OUT" 2>&1 || true
```

The runner writes its result to **stdout** (`Blockchain/Testing/tests/tenant-isolation/runner.ts:262`, `console.log(JSON.stringify({ tested, findings }, null, 2))`) and writes diagnostics to **stderr** (`runner.ts:74`, `console.error(\`login failed for ${email}: ...\`)`). With `2>&1`both land in`$OUT\`, so any stderr line corrupts the artefact.

**This is reached on a routine run, not an error path.** `runner.ts:150-151` is a deliberate two-principal fallback:

```
const principalB = await login("verifier@secuura.com", "verifier123") ||
                   await login("holder@secuura.com", "holder123");
```

Whenever the first login cannot succeed, `login()` emits its `console.error` line and the fallback proceeds to `holder@` as designed. The job still exits 0, but `$OUT` now begins with a plain-text line followed by JSON.

**Effect.** `:74` and `:75` read the artefact with `jq ... 2>/dev/null || echo "?"`, so the parse failure is swallowed and the job reports `tested=? cross-tenant_findings=?`. Measured on a merged-stream reproduction: `jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 6`, against a clean control that parses to `0`.

Before KS 1136's change, an unreadable artefact was reported as a **clean** scan — so a genuine cross-tenant finding on a fallback run read as no findings. After KS 1136 lands, the aggregator reports the artefact as unreadable instead, which turns every routine `verifier@`-fallback run **red with a false cause**. That is why this fix is the merge condition for that PR and must land first.

**Fix shape.** Send stderr to its own file so the JSON artefact stays parseable, and keep the stderr content (it is the diagnostic that explains a fallback), rather than discarding it with `2>/dev/null`.

**Not this ticket:** KS 1382 is a different line in the same file (`:31`, `TARGET_BASE` defaulting to slot 1's gateway).

Runtime change to a security-harness job — live sweep owed.

title: Connector keys are minted `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`, but neither scope is enforced anywhere — anchor reads are scope-ungated and revoke has no scope check
description:
## Summary

`register-connector` mints Platform S connector keys with nine scopes, including `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`. Neither scope is checked anywhere in the request path. So a connector key's anchor reads are not scope-gated at all: a key minted WITHOUT `anchors:read` would still read anchors. And `documents:revoke` has no effect: the revoke route checks ownership only. That breaks the deny-by-default rule ([KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) R2: scopes are the authority) for these two scopes. This is a code read; nothing has been probed live yet.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

**Minted:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:485-489` (`S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES`) includes both `'documents:revoke'` (:486) and `'anchors:read'` (:487). Vocabulary: `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:42` and `:76`.

`anchors:read` **— enforced nowhere:**

* `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` gates only the two anchor WRITES: `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch` carry `attachScopes, requireScope('anchors:write')` (:852-863).
* The catch-all `router.use('/api/anchors', authenticateToken(true), proxy('anchoring', …))` (:865-868) has no `requireScope`, so every anchor read reaches anchoring with authentication only.
* A search of `services/*/src` and `packages/shared/src` (tests excluded) finds `anchors:read` only in the minting list and the vocabulary — no check in anchoring either.

`documents:revoke` **— enforced nowhere:**

* The other document verbs check their scope through `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(...)`: create and version `documents:write` (`documents.ts:372`, `:1983`), transfer `documents:transfer-custody` (`:1599`), share `documents:share` (`:2172`).
* The revoke route (`documents.ts:2344` onward) has no scope check. It gates on `document.owner?.id !== user.id` → 403. A connector principal is never the owner, so connectors cannot revoke at all. Your own [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) finding, 2026-08-26, verbatim: *"A connector principal cannot revoke at all"*.

### Not verified

* No live probe yet with a connector key minted without `anchors:read`. Whether anchoring further limits reads per tenant was not checked.
* Severity therefore not asserted beyond "the scope is not checked".

### Related, deliberately not duplicated

* Whether connectors should be able to revoke at all is the open question you put to Stuart on [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (2026-08-26, Kam's ruling "ask Stuart to reconcile [PS-616](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-616/s-shipped-ps-569-ahead-of-ks-566-so-lifecycle-event-and-flat-anchor) first"). This ticket does not reopen that. It only records that the minted scope is dead either way: if the answer is "no", stop minting it; if "yes", the route needs the scope check plus an owner-gate change.
* Duplicate check, Platform K + Platform S, 2026-10-06: no ticket names either scope's enforcement. [KS-71](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-71/q6-scope-aware-rbac-in-originate-sk-connector-role-can-post) (Done) built scope-aware RBAC for create. [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) (Deployed) is a different class: scope-gate bypass by path spelling.

### Suggested direction (your call)

1. Gate anchor reads with `requireScope('anchors:read')` for key callers (as `/api/documents` does with `documents:read`), or stop minting the scope.
2. Resolve `documents:revoke` per the [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) answer.

systemTest coverage follows on Peter's side: [KS-571](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-571/systemtest-schemathesis-ks-539-agent-document-operation-rules) item 3 (R2, deny-by-default) / [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks).

+++

Refs: [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) / [KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) (rules R2) · [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (revoke question) · [KS-571](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-571/systemtest-schemathesis-ks-539-agent-document-operation-rules) / [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) (systemTest) · [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: unhandledRejection posture as shipped differs from KS-546's: setupGracefulShutdown has no callers, and originate survives rejections while the gateway's comment cites it as fail-fast
description:
## Summary

[KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) ruled that the api-gateway **survives** unhandled rejections and that *everything else stays fail-fast*. On `develop` `f556373b9`, two things don't match that ruling. First, the shared wrapper that would make every other service log and apply its mode, `setupGracefulShutdown`, has **no callers**, so [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify step can't be observed. Second, **originate survives** unhandled rejections: it registers its own listener, which logs and does not exit. The gateway's own comment cites originate as an example of fail-fast. Either originate is a second, undocumented `survive` service, or it's a bug. That's a ruling for you, not something to settle in systemTest.

These came up while scoping [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture), the systemTest ticket that pins the [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) posture. They're outside systemTest, so they're filed here for you.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

### 1. `setupGracefulShutdown` has no callers

* It's defined at `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts:99` and re-exported at `utils/index.ts:10`. No service imports it: `git grep setupGracefulShutdown -- Blockchain/Dev` finds only the definition, the re-export, a JSDoc example and the comment below.
* The code now says so: `packages/shared/src/index.ts:22-23` reads *"the gateway consumes these directly (the setupGracefulShutdown wrapper itself has no live consumers today)."*
* So the line [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify section says to check, `Graceful shutdown handlers registered (unhandledRejection mode: X)` (`gracefulShutdown.ts:177`), never prints. *"All other services log* `exit`*"* can't be observed on any stack.
* The only live path is the gateway, which wires `resolveUnhandledRejectionMode` + `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` itself (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1161-1171`) and logs `unhandledRejection mode: <mode>`.

### 2. originate is not fail-fast for unhandled rejections

* `services/originate/src/index.ts:72-77` calls `process.on('unhandledRejection', …)`, which logs, calls `trackError`, and **returns**. It never exits.
* Registering any listener disables Node's fatal default, so originate keeps running after an unhandled rejection. Its `uncaughtException` handler just below it *does* exit.
* The surrounding comment ([KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure)) explains why it logs: so a crash leaves a trace. It doesn't say surviving is intended.
* `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1159-1160` says *"Every other service keeps fail-fast (originate's own handler, or Node 20's fatal default)"*. That's backwards for originate. It also names Node 20, but the images are `node:24-alpine` (`services/originate/Dockerfile`).

### 3. Scope check

Only two `process.on('unhandledRejection'` registrations exist under `services/`: the gateway ([KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything), intended) and originate. Every other service has no listener, so it falls back to Node 24's fatal default and does fail fast. The `routes/verification.ts:1367` hit is a comment, not a registration.

### Not checked

Nothing was run against a stack. This is a code read only. No Platform S code is involved.

+++

## What's needed (your call)

1. **originate:** decide whether it should **survive** or be **fail-fast**.
   * If survive: say so in [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s terms. Ideally declare `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` for originate too, so the posture lives in config rather than an inline listener.
   * If fail-fast: wire originate through `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` (mode `exit`) so it still leaves the [KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure) trace before exiting.
2. `setupGracefulShutdown`**:** either have the services call it, so every service logs its mode, or delete the wrapper and amend [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify step to what can actually be observed.
3. **The gateway comment** at `api-gateway/src/index.ts:1159-1160`: correct it to match whatever (1) decides, and fix the Node version.

## How systemTest will use the answer

[KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture)'s boot-posture assertion checks that the gateway logs `survive` and a sampled non-gateway service does not. Today the only service that logs a mode at all is the gateway. [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) will assert the posture as shipped and cite this ticket. When you rule on (1) and (2), that assertion moves with your ruling, red→green.

Refs: [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) (the ruling, Done) · [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) (outage class) · [KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure) (originate's logging rationale) · [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) (systemTest pin). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: Audit jobs: a per-image trivy failure reads as a CLEAN image in 04 (`|| echo '{}'` + unguarded norm), and jobs 01/02/03/05/06/07/08 keep the unparseable-artefact hole 09 guards for 04 only
description:
## BLUF

PR #974 (KS-878 + KS-867, merged 2026-09-13) closed ONE silence: a truncated `04-container-trivy.json` is now loud in 09 (`04-trivy/unreadable-artefact`, high, rc 1). The tier-2 gate measured that the same silence family is still open in two places, both pre-existing, both in `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/` — the per-image failure path INSIDE 04 (R-2) and the artefact reads for every OTHER job in 09 (R-3). One workload, one test pass: a scan or a job that fails must never read as a clean result. KS-676 (Done, archived 2026-09-06) is the ancestor that made these two scripts runnable on macOS; KS-1127 is the runner-level neighbour (the harness's own skip tally).

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks878-867-974-8da602309-tier2-r1/report.md` — §3 (the 04 table's last rows), §11 (a) and (b), R-1 / R-2 / R-3. Line numbers below are at `8da602309` = develop after the squash (M12).

## Items (one test pass)

1. **R-2 — the per-image trivy-failure path in** `04-container-trivy.sh:86-93` **and** `:96-112` **reads a failed scan as a CLEAN image.** `:93` is `"$img" 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"` — a `trivy image` that exits non-zero with no output becomes `{}`; the `norm` jq at `:96-112` then emits `counts: {}` / `vulns: []` for that image, and 09 counts it as scanned and clean. MEASURED at both base and head (recording stubs on the private PATH):
   * no-output failure → the image's entry is `{image, counts:{}, vulns:[]}`, rc 0, "across N image(s)" — a CLEAN read;
   * partial-output failure on N ≥ 2 images → an 89-byte unparseable artefact with `CRITICAL= HIGH= across 2 image(s)`, rc 0 (at head KS-878's guard in 09 now catches THIS shape as a side effect);
   * partial-output failure on the ONLY image → `{"images":[]}` — valid JSON, rc 0, 0 findings, "across 1 image(s)", **silent at BOTH SHAs** (09's `jq -e` accepts it).
     Fix shape (the gate's, the owner's call): fail the image entry loudly when `raw` came from the `|| echo '{}'` arm or `norm` is empty — e.g. write `{"image": $img, "error": "scan-failed"}` and let 09 emit a high per image with `.error`; never print `across N` for a scan whose `norm` was empty. Regression cells: a stub `trivy` that exits 1 with and without partial output, one- and two-image corpora, asserting a non-empty `.error` per failed image and rc 1.
2. **R-3 — the other artefact reads in** `09-aggregate-report.sh` **have the hole KS-878 closed for 04 only.** `:69` (01), `:77` (02), `:91` (03), `:164` (05), `:173` (06), `:181` (07) are each `jq -r … 2>/dev/null` inside `< <(…)`: a truncated artefact yields zero findings, rc 0, 0 bytes of output. `:186` (08) is `failed=$(jq '.tests.failed // 0' "$RUN_DIR/08-aiken-tests.json")` — no `2>/dev/null`, so it is stderr-loud but rc-silent. MEASURED (08): an 11-byte `{"tests":{` + LF artefact → 0 findings, rc 0, 65 bytes of `jq: parse error: Unfinished JSON term at EOF …` on stderr, at both base and head; control `{"tests":{"passed":10,"failed":2}}` → `tests-failed:2` critical, rc 1. Fix shape: one `jq -e . "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || emit "<job>" high "<job>/unreadable-artefact"` in front of every artefact block (`:133-134` is the shape 04 now has), or a helper every block calls. Regression cells: one truncated artefact per job → one `<job>/unreadable-artefact` high and rc 1.
3. **Context, not an item — R-1:** 09's new-only rc gate (`:10-12` documents it) makes every loud finding ONE-SHOT: the second run of the same defect reads `findings 1 / new 0 / rc 0` (measured). So "must never read as a clean scan" is true for one run and false thereafter — by the aggregator's documented design, not a defect of #974; the builder should know it when writing the cells above (assert on the FIRST run, or clear the baseline in the fixture).

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over 1,125 KS issues + 914 comments (includeArchived): `jq -e` and `unreadable-artefact` → KS-878 only; `|| echo '{}'` → 0; `scan-failed` → 0; `unparseable` → 11 hits, every one another subject (date/query parsing, launcher and preflight parsers, `SERVICES_TABLE`); `04-container-trivy` → KS-676 (archived), KS-680 (archived), KS-868 (archived), KS-867, KS-878; `09-aggregate-report` → KS-676, KS-868, KS-878. No open home; filed new.

title: Bulk re-key: one admin-authorised rotate across a named set of externalRefs
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for **one** admin-authorised action that re-keys a named set of Organisations by `externalRef`, instead of N separate `register-connector` calls during an incident. The loop itself is **1–2 days**.

**It must not ship before** [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) **(revoke-on-rotate).** Built on today's additive rotate, a bulk re-key would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and *look* like recovery.

## Detail

Today's single-org path is `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` with `rotate: true` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476-729`:

* platform-admin only; guardrail 1 refuses a connector-authorised rotate with 403 (`:499-509`)
* resolves the org by `metadata->>'externalRef'` under platform scope (`:590-593`)
* mints a fresh `sk_` key via the security service (`:674-686` → `services/security/src/index.ts:800`)
* plaintext key returned exactly once (`:719-720`)

`runWithPlatformScope` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:102`) already handles the cross-tenant access, so multi-tenancy is **not** the hard part here.

**Scope**

* Extract `platform.ts:476-729` into a reusable per-org function; add a bulk route taking a list of `externalRef`s.
* Return a **per-ref result array** — partial success must be explicit. An incident operator has to know which refs failed and why.
* OpenAPI entry + `generate-openapi` regen + api-gateway rebuild (the gateway bakes the spec) + KS-380 preflight.

**Explicitly out of scope:** delivery of the key material for N keys. One response body carrying N live secrets is not the answer; that needs its own design and a security review (see the KS-480 sizing table).

**Cheaper alternative on the record** (raised because @peter asked not to have the manual path assumed away): a scripted loop over the existing admin endpoint gives one *operator action* today at near-zero build cost. It does not give one *authorisation*, which is the part actually being asked for.

**Done when:** an admin can re-key a named set of refs in one authorised call, each prior key is revoked per the [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) semantics, per-ref outcomes are explicit, and the [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) rehearsal passes all four steps.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: DR rehearsal: lose a key → re-key → read-back survives on pre-loss anchors → the old key is dead
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for this rehearsal on KS-532. **KS-532 is Done and was archived on 2026-08-04, so it rejects comments and nobody would see it** — @kamil.kreiser ruled 2026-08-07 that it gets a fresh ticket rather than a reopen. This is that ticket.

**It needs four steps, not three.** As @peter wrote it, the rehearsal **would pass today while leaving the compromised credential live** — which is the clearest possible illustration of Finding A ([KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577)).

## Detail

**The rehearsal**

1. Anchor a document; record the proof.
2. Re-key the org — `register-connector` with `rotate: true`.
3. Confirm read-back survives on the pre-loss anchor using the **new** key. *(@peter's assertion — expected to hold.)*
4. **Confirm the OLD key no longer works.** *(Added. This is the step that fails today.)*

**Why step 4 matters.** Rotation currently mints without revoking ([KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577)), so steps 1–3 would all pass on a credential that is still live and still valid with identical scopes. A rehearsal that stops at step 3 proves **read-back continuity only, not containment** — and would be reported as a successful DR rehearsal.

**Sequencing.** Steps 1–3 can be run before [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) lands, but the result must be recorded as *continuity only*, explicitly not containment. Step 4 is blocked on [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577).

**Also worth folding in** (@peter's sequencing asks on KS-480): [PS-473](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-473) first — a lost key is recoverable by rotation, a lost GUID mapping is not — and [PS-463](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-463), which is the only detection a botched re-key would have under async anchoring.

**Done when:** all four steps pass on demo and the run is recorded here with its evidence.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: Security: /api/status revoke/unrevoke has no tenant ownership check — an ISSUER_ADMIN in any tenant can revoke another tenant’s credential (KS-586’s deferred half, now untracked)
description:
## Summary

`POST /api/status/:id/revoke` and `/unrevoke` enforce an **admin-class role** but **no tenant ownership check**. An `ISSUER_ADMIN` in one tenant can revoke or un-revoke a credential in **another tenant's** status list. Reproduced live on `develop 576ebef85`.

This is the **second half of KS-586**, which fixed the role gap and explicitly deferred the tenant gap — but **KS-586 is now** `Done`**, so nothing tracks the remainder.** That is why this ticket exists.

## ⚠️ What is already FIXED — read this before working the ticket

**KS-586 is done and its fix is live. **`/api/status` is no longer "no authorization at all". Anyone picking this up from a summary of [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570) will be looking for a defect that is not there.

| probe (local, `develop 576ebef85`) | result |
| -- | -- |
| `holder@secuura.com` (**OWNER**, non-admin) → revoke | **403 **`Role OWNER is not authorized for this action` |

The role gate at `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts:42-53` (`STATUS_WRITE_ROLES`, applied as a router-level gate ahead of the route table) works. Commit `bda40c91c` on `develop`, present in the running container.

## The defect that IS live — reproduced, controls both ways

Two `ISSUER_ADMIN`s in **different tenants**:

* `demo@secuura.io` — tenant `default`
* `registrar@oxford-test.invalid` — tenant `oxford`

| # | actor | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status` create list | **201** |
| 2 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status/:id/allocate` `cred-xtenant-probe` | **200**, index 0 |
| 3 | **oxford registrar (foreign tenant)** | `POST /api/status/:id/revoke` that credential | 🔴 **200** — `{"revoked":true,"reason":"cross-tenant probe"}` |
| 4 | demo (owner) | `GET /api/status/:id/revoked` | **200** — `{"revokedIndexes":[0],"totalRevoked":1}` — the write really landed |
| 5 | **control** — oxford registrar | revoke against a **non-existent** list id | **404 **`Status list not found` |
| 6 | **control** — holder (OWNER) | revoke the same list | **403** (role gate) |

**Controls 5 and 6 are what make row 3 mean something.** Row 5 proves the 200 was a genuine authorisation pass and not a blanket accept — the same foreign caller is refused when the target does not exist. Row 6 proves role is still evaluated, so the only thing missing is the tenant comparison.

## Root cause

`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts`. The router-level gate checks **role only**:

```ts
return requireRole(...STATUS_WRITE_ROLES)(req, res, next);
```

There is no comparison of the caller's tenant to the status list's owner — **because the status list has no owner to compare to.** Status lists live in a process-local `Map` with no tenant linkage. The code says so itself (`status.ts:35-38`):

> *"Tenant scoping is NOT enforced here yet: status lists live in a process-local Map with no tenant linkage, and the ownership model is the KS-539/KS-547/KS-586 joint authorization decision — tracked on KS-586."*

**"tracked on KS-586" is no longer true.** KS-586 is `Done` (2026-08-12) and KS-547 is `Done`; KS-539 is open but scoped to *governing rules for document operations by agents*, not status-list tenancy. The deferral outlived its tracker — which is the actual reason this went untracked for two weeks.

## Why this is not a duplicate

* **KS-586** — `Done`. The **role** half. Fixed.
* **KS-570** — the **authentication** half: the gateway mount at `proxy.ts:702` has no `authenticateToken`, so revoked-session JWTs still pass. Different layer, still open.
* **KS-588** — `Backlog`. **Test coverage** for `/api/status` authorization. Would catch this once it exists; is not the fix.
* **This ticket** — the **tenant/ownership** half. No ticket held it after KS-586 closed.

## Severity

**High.** Revocation state is an integrity operation on a document-authenticity platform — an attacker with any admin-class role in any tenant can un-revoke a credential their victim revoked, or revoke a live one. Same family as [KS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-643) (cross-tenant API-key revoke) and [KS-642](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-642), and it sits on the same **KS-621 tenancy boundary** that is currently held for @kamil.kreiser's design ruling.

Not raised to Urgent: exploitation needs a valid admin-class credential in *some* tenant, so it is privilege-escalation-across-tenants, not anonymous.

## Suggested fix — NOT implemented, deliberately

The ownership model is a **KS-621 boundary decision** and is @kamil.kreiser's call, exactly as with KS-643. Filing only, per the same hold.

The prerequisite is structural: **a status list must carry an owning tenant before any check can be written.** The process-local `Map` has nowhere to put one, so this is not a middleware one-liner — it needs the list persisted with a tenant column, which is likely the same decision as KS-539's ownership model.

Note the interlock, learned from KS-578/KS-643: adding a tenant check **without** giving lists an owner would refuse every caller, since no list has a tenant to match.

## Reproduction

Local stack, `develop 576ebef85`, both accounts seeded. Full curl sequence is rows 1–6 above. Probe artefacts were written to the **local** stack only (`ks661-tenantprobe-*`); status lists are process-local and clear on a `vc-issuer` restart. **Nothing was written to demo.**

Handed over by @peter on KS-570 (2026-08-26 08:10Z): *"The one still open is the /api/status authorisation gap … I will let you file that one too, as you hold the evidence for it."* — filed with the measurement rather than the paraphrase, which is how the KS-586 half turned out to be already fixed.

title: POST /api/teams/webhook-config fails the Schemathesis pr sweep on every run — including develop — and is tracked by nothing
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/teams/webhook-config` **fails the Schemathesis** `pr` **sweep on every run, on** `develop` **as well as on feature branches, and maps to no open ticket.** Not a regression from any current PR — an unrecorded pre-existing failure, which is the shape that quietly becomes "known noise" and then becomes invisible.

Filed on Wednesday's instruction after it surfaced during #805's contract-gate run. **No fix attempted; not investigated beyond establishing that it is real, stable and unowned.**

## Evidence — three runs, one variable

| run | branch / spec served | tests | failures | this op failed? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | PR [#805](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/805>) (`Anchor.status` widened) | 316 | 12 | **yes** |
| 2 | `develop` `492152a81` | 316 | 12 | **yes** |
| 3 | #805 again | 316 | 12 | **yes** |

Run validity clean on all three — **0 of 316 operations errored**, 85-91s each, ~1,680 cases per run. Profile `pr`, local gateway, `mode: positive`, checks `not_a_server_error, response_schema_conformance, status_code_conformance, content_type_conformance, response_headers_conformance`.

**It is in the STABLE core, not the flaky slot.** Eleven operations fail in all three runs; a twelfth slot rotates between runs (`referrals/apply` → `security/rate-limit/check` → `gdpr/consent`). `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` is in the stable eleven — so it is deterministic, not noise.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Ten of the eleven stable failures are accounted for:

| operations | ticket |
| -- | -- |
| 7 × m365 / onedrive | [KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693) — *"M365 routes answer 503 when ENTRA_* is unconfigured — 9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every run"* |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) — `not_a_server_error` flags the by-design 501 |
| `POST /api/gdpr/erasures`, `GET /api/gdpr/erasures/{externalRef}` | the erasure family — [KS-695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-695), [KS-754](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-754), [KS-757](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-757), [KS-758](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-758) |
| `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` | **none — this ticket** |

**A failure nobody owns is worse than a failure somebody has deprioritised**, because the first gets absorbed into the expected red and stops being counted.

## ⚠ A count on KS-693 that should be reconciled, not inherited

[KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693)'s title asserts **"9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every run"**. This measurement finds **7** m365/onedrive operations failing, within a stable core of **11** and a total of **12**. The figures may be reconcilable (different profile, different spec revision, or the count included operations since fixed) — but **they should be checked against a run rather than carried forward**, on the same principle that made [KS-763](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-763) assert a case count for equality instead of a floor: a number in a title is a claim, and an unrechecked one drifts.

## What is NOT established here

* **Why** it fails. The failing check(s) were not isolated — the run records them, but this ticket deliberately reports the observation rather than a half-diagnosis.
* Whether it shares KS-693's cause (an unconfigured integration answering 503) or is a distinct defect. `teams` is a different integration from `m365`, so it should not be assumed.
* Whether it is by design, like [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686)'s 501 — which would make this a spec-declaration fix rather than a code fix.

## Reproduce

```
cd systemTest/schemathesis
./venv/bin/python3 scripts/run.py pr --base-url http://localhost:6882
```

Failures are in `output/reports/latest/schemathesis-output.xml` (JUnit; one `<testcase>` per operation).

## Related

[KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693) (the other permanent integration failures, and the count above) · [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) (a by-design status flagged by a check) · [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) (173 routed endpoints absent from the spec) · surfaced during [#805](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/805>)'s contract-gate run

title: tests/e2e auth-exhaustive races its OWN lockout — same commit gives 1 or 11 failures, so the suite cannot gate anything
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **is non-deterministic against an unchanged product.** It brute-forces logins, `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true`, and every run leaves **4** `lockout:*` **keys** in redis — so its own ordinary login cells race its own lockout. Until this is fixed the suite cannot be used as a gate, because a failure count carries no information.

## Measured — 2026-09-09, `develop` `b6884888d`, `lockout:*` cleared before EACH run

| run | command | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A | three specs | **23 failed / 54 passed** |
| B | three specs | **11 failed / 71 passed** |
| C | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **1 failed / 52 passed** |
| D | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **11 failed / 42 passed** |

**Nothing about the product changed between any of them.** Lockout keys were counted after every run: 4 each time, so the suite reliably creates them and unreliably outruns them.

**The flapping cells move as ONE block** — both 23-failure runs carried exactly the same 23, which is what rules out twelve independent flakes and points at a single shared cause. They are all in `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts`: 2.1.1–2.1.5, 2.2.8, 2.2.9, 2.8.1, 2.9.1, 2.9.2, 2.9.4, 2.9.5.

**The deterministic remainder is 10 recruitment/wallet cells** (red in 5 of 5 runs) plus `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`, whose assertion is wrong rather than the app — filed separately.

## Suggested fix (not prescribed)

Either serialise this file (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` or a dedicated non-parallel project), or give the brute-force cells a **dedicated account** so they cannot lock the fixture persona the rest of the file logs in with. The second is likely better: it keeps the parallelism and removes the coupling.

## Class

This is the **KS-724** family — a harness that stops testing while still producing results. There, a scan evicted its own bearer; here, a suite locks out its own persona.

## Provenance

* the four runs, lockout counts, and the identical 23-cell block | measured live on the local stack, recorded in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/BASELINE.md` | 2026-09-09
* Filed from KS-734's baseline work (s160), which made the suite installable and could then measure it.

title: Connector allow-list still fails OPEN when Redis closes or errors at runtime, on a read error (catch {}), or on LRU eviction of platform-settings
description:
**From the #1038 / KS-1233 batch gate, finding N38-1: Major, pre-existing. Not #1038's regression.**

## What's wrong

KS-1233 (#1038, merged `e51686bed`) stops `platform-settings` expiring on a TTL. But a **missing** key is still read as "no restriction". The allow-list therefore still **fails open** on every other way the key can go missing or unreadable:

* a runtime Redis close or error (the gate's row R6, measured over a stateful fake);
* a read error swallowed by a bare `catch {}`;
* LRU eviction of the key.

In each case every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

## Why it matters

It is the same fail-open class KS-1233 fixed for the TTL trigger. A connector allow-list should fail **closed** when the configuration cannot be read.

## What to do

Make the reader fail closed. A missing or unreadable `platform-settings` should refuse restricted connector operations (or fall back to a persisted source), not grant everything. Add cells for the close, error and eviction paths. Check the other readers in the gate's reader census (section C) for the same class.

---

Filed from the batch gate report `2026-09-18-batch1038-1041-tier1-r1` (FINDINGS table), at merge of develop `8b9c3f022bee76b79a47f1b8c5de8ad3ddb4a0ae`.

title: Sourcing systemTest/slot-target.sh with no slot named silently exports slot 1's targets — and preflight leg 13 + the pre-push hook depend on that, so it cannot be fixed in systemTest alone
description:
## BLUF

**No action is needed today, and nothing is broken on the trunk.** This asks for your view on one coordinated change that sits across your files and systemTest.

`systemTest/slot-target.sh`, sourced with **no** slot named, silently exports slot 1's targets. Every harness now refuses an unslotted local run in its own code, so the export itself is the last place a slot is silently defaulted. It can't simply be made to refuse, though: **preflight leg 13 and the pre-push hook source it with no slot, on purpose**, and leg 13's positive control would then refuse every push.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## What happens today

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` resolves `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT="${SECUURA_STACK_SLOT:-${STACK_SLOT:-1}}"`: an unnamed slot becomes **1**.
* `systemTest/slot-target.sh:51` records whether a slot was actually requested (`SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED`), then sources `stack_env.sh` and exports slot 1's `SECUURA_GATEWAY_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_API_URL`, `PERF_BASE_URL`, the `AKTO_*` set and `SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX=-slot1`. `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is only used by `retarget()`.
* The TypeScript harnesses still refuse an unslotted local run, because `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` itself is never exported. Akto and Schemathesis read several of these exports directly, though. [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) is adding their own entry-point guards so they no longer depend on this.

## Why it can't be fixed in systemTest alone

* `.githooks/pre-push:273-285` ([KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail)) sources it deliberately, `|| true`, so the stack-dependent legs probe *this* slot's gateway rather than preflight's own `localhost:6882` default. When the developer's shell names no slot, that is the slot-1 export.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:589-630` (leg 13, [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the)) **measures** the variables `slot-target.sh` exports under `env -i`, **with no slot named**, and has a positive control: an empty list refuses the leg. If `slot-target.sh` refused (exported nothing) when unslotted, that control would fire and **every push would be refused.**

So the three pieces have to move together, and the hook and preflight are yours.

## A possible shape (entirely your call)

1. `slot-target.sh`: when `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is empty and `CI` is not truthy, export nothing target-bearing and print a one-line notice, or `return 2`, matching the refusal the TS harnesses use (`systemTest/fixtures/slot-required.ts:76-91`).
2. **Leg 13:** measure the export set with an explicit slot (e.g. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1` inside the `env -i` subshell) rather than relying on the unslotted default. Its purpose, the full clear-list, is unchanged.
3. **Pre-push:** when no slot is named, say so and let the stack-dependent legs report SKIPPED (the [KS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1046/preflight-passed-is-printed-identically-whether-13-legs-ran-or-10-the) verdict), rather than probing slot 1.

Related: [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (stack tooling not slot-derived end to end), [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the) (leg 13's origin), [KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail) (why the hook sources it).

## Not done here

No change to `slot-target.sh`, the hook or preflight on the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) branch. Peter's ruling (2026-09-29): raise it for you rather than change your files.

Thank you, and apologies for another slot ticket. This one felt worth raising because the obvious fix would have quietly blocked every push.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 2 and 3 — `slot-target.sh` refusing when unslotted is point 2; leg 13 is coordinated with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s spot 4. This ticket had no acceptance section of its own, so these points are its acceptance, together with the three steps of its possible shape.

title: Three retired GitHub workflows bake slot-2/3/4 port literals (6982/7182/6732…) into CI env — a stack slot applied to a non-local build, typed per slot
description:
## BLUF

| `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml` | 34 | header `offsets — schemathesis 6882 · playwright 6982 · perf 7082 · akto 7182`; `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6532"` |

They are exempted in that test's `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` against this ticket; **the exemption comes out when this closes.**

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
