title: Five new advisories freeze every push: in-range lock refresh for four, baseline the two with no fix
description:
## BLUF

Five advisories published since develop's last audit baseline refresh now fail preflight legs 6 and 7, so **every push from this repo is refused**. Four have an in-range fix and are bumped in the lockfiles; two have no in-range fix and get dated baseline rows. Measured at develop `4eaf7741a6a4b2c82752d0d94f8bbacb5493aabe`.

**Authority.** Kam ruled the card `secuura-five-new-advisories-freeze-every-push-1006`, verbatim: "Decision secuura-five-new-advisories-freeze-every-push-1006: a — Fix forward (recommended)", live board 2026-10-06 13:15:04 +11:00.

## The five advisories

Vulnerable ranges read from the npm registry bulk advisory API (HTTP 200).

| Advisory | Package | Severity | Pinned | Vulnerable | Fixed |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h | proxy-addr | critical | 2.0.7 | `>=1.1.0 <2.0.8` | 2.0.8 |
| GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q | source-map-js | high | 1.2.1 | `>=1.0.0 <1.2.2` | 1.2.2 |
| GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf | postcss-selector-parser | moderate | 6.1.4, 7.1.4 | `<7.1.6` | 7.1.6 (7.x only) |
| GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c | sprintf-js | moderate | 1.0.3 | `<=1.1.3` | none published |
| GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2 | smol-toml | moderate | 1.8.0 | `<=1.8.0` | 1.9.0 |

Three controls on that API: querying only the four fixed versions returns an empty body (the fixes clear the advisories); querying only the old versions fires all four (the instrument is not uniformly silent); querying sprintf-js at its latest published 1.1.3 still fires, which is how "no fix exists" was measured rather than assumed.

## Reproduction at base

In a scratch checkout of `4eaf7741a6a4`, with only the audit script dependencies installed:

* Leg 6, the npm-audit gate, exits 1: 11 distinct advisories reported, 22 baselined, and 4 NEW advisories not in the baseline (GHSA-rj75, GHSA-jqcg, GHSA-68fv, GHSA-hp3w). smol-toml is absent from the workspace root lock, which is why leg 6 names four and leg 7 names five.
* Leg 7, the standalone-lock gate, exits 1: 43 standalone lockfiles, 1614 distinct packages pinned, 10 advisories match, 5 already baselined, then 5 advisories in standalone locks and not in the baseline.

## Scope of the change

A parent walk over all 45 tracked lockfiles, resolving each dependency by nearest-node_modules, finds **78 entries** pinning one of the five, **0** with no resolving parent and **0** whose fixed version falls outside its parent's declared range.

The fix is **54 entries across 36 lockfiles**, three fields each (version, resolved, integrity):

* proxy-addr 2.0.7 to 2.0.8 in 16 locks. 12 further locks already pin 2.0.8, which serves as an in-repo integrity control.
* source-map-js 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 in 33 locks.
* postcss-selector-parser 7.1.4 to 7.1.6 in systemTest/api-explorer only. systemTest/akto already pins 7.1.6, the second in-repo control.
* smol-toml 1.8.0 to 1.9.0 in the 4 systemTest locks.

Plus 2 rows appended to the audit baseline, 22 to 24. No manifest, no overrides block, no source file, no test and no doc changes.

The React Native tree under mobile/secuura-app is out of scope by the existing declaration (KS-769, expires 2027-01-01) and is left byte-unchanged, even though it pins source-map-js 1.2.1 and sprintf-js 1.0.3 as production dependencies there.

Every fixed version's own dependency set equals the version it replaces, per registry metadata, so a correct refresh moves exactly three fields per entry and anything else that moves is collateral.

## The two advisories with no in-range fix

Both get a dated baseline row with `decidedAt` 2026-10-06 and `expires` 2026-10-31, matching the shared re-triage date already carried by all four of develop's dated rows.

**GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c, sprintf-js 1.0.3** — 5 in-scope entries, all flagged dev, 0 production: the workspace root plus services/governance, services/originate, services/referral and services/vc-issuer. The sole parent at every path is argparse 1.0.10 requiring `~1.0.2`, itself under js-yaml 3.15.2 requiring `^1.0.7`. No published version of sprintf-js is unaffected, so there is nothing to bump to. Clearing it needs argparse 2.x, which is outside its parent's declared range and is not this change.

**GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf, postcss-selector-parser 6.1.4** — 4 in-scope entries, all flagged dev, 0 production: frontend/admin, frontend/issuer, frontend/verifier and the workspace root. Parents are tailwindcss 3.4.19 requiring `^6.1.2` and postcss-nested 6.2.0 requiring `^6.1.1`. tailwindcss 3.4.19 is the last v3 release and still requires `^6.1.2`, so no in-range fix exists on the 6.x line. Clearing it needs tailwindcss 4, a major bump, and is not this change.

The baseline schema keys a row by advisory id and carries no version or lockfile scope: `REQUIRED_FIELDS` is package, reason and ticket. A GHSA-rj75 row therefore suppresses **every** version of postcss-selector-parser, including a 7.x copy below 7.1.6. That is why the api-explorer 7.1.4 bump is required even though the row would mask it, and why this change asserts by parse that no in-scope lock pins any 7.x below 7.1.6 afterwards. The row covers 6.1.4 only by intent.

## All five are purely transitive

* Manifests declaring any of the five: **0** each. Control: a search for a declared dependency finds it in 28 manifests.
* Source files importing any of the five: **0** each. Control: the same search shape finds 333 files for a dependency that is imported.
* Source files even mentioning them by bare name: **0** each. Control: 418 files.

No application code calls into any of them, which is what makes a lockfile-only change the whole fix for four of them and bounds the risk of baselining the other two.

## Not done here, deliberately

* The 15 stale CLEANUP rows the gate reports as advisory (12 undici plus ip-address plus @hono/node-server under KS-470, and 3 undici under KS-559) stay in place. Every one is in the grandfathered no-expiry set, removing them is a code change to that set, and their disposition belongs to KS-767.
* No existing baseline row is re-dated and none is removed.
* No HIGH or CRITICAL advisory is baselined. The critical proxy-addr and high source-map-js advisories are fixed by the refresh.
* No major version bump, no overrides entry and no manifest edit. tailwindcss 3 to 4, js-yaml 3 to 4 and argparse 1 to 2 would each clear a row; each is outside its parent's declared range.

## Verification owed

The runtime effect of proxy-addr 2.0.8 on `trust proxy` handling in the 16 locks where it is a production dependency is not measured by this change, and the frontend CSS build output under source-map-js 1.2.2 and postcss-selector-parser 7.1.6 is not built. Offline green is not a live sweep, so this ticket does not go to Done on the gate verdict alone.

Related gates and prior waves, cross-referenced only: KS-470 (leg 6), KS-531 (leg 7), KS-1403, KS-1378, KS-749, KS-769.

title: updateDocument: a UUID-addressed update matches 0 rows and silently writes nothing for the 12 unguarded callers
description:
A `updateDocument(id, ...)` call whose `id` is the platform UUID (the primary key) resolves the row on the READ but matches **0 rows** on the WRITE, because the UPDATE keys on `external_id`. For the one guarded caller this surfaced as a wrong 400 and is fixed under KS-1278. **For the other 12 production callers there is no guard, so the function returns the updated record and the caller reports success while the database was never written.**

Instrument for the mechanism: read of `documentRepo.ts` at `4a1620588819` (blob `e29ebcdd79c2`) plus the caller census below. The silent-success behaviour for the unguarded callers is **inferred from the same code path, not separately probed — unmeasured against a live database.**

## Why a UUID reaches these callers

`fromDbRow` returns `id: row.external_id || row.id` and `documentUuid: isValidUuid(row.external_id) ? row.external_id : row.id`. When `external_id` is not UUID-shaped, `documentUuid` IS the primary key, and the API hands clients that value. `getDocument` accepts it via its uuid fallback. The UPDATE does not.

## Caller census

Measured with `git grep -n 'updateDocument(' <sha> -- Blockchain/Dev`, read from a file. 24 lines at `4a1620588819`, 23 at the branch base `32e058975d4e`. Controls: a must-hit token returned 2 files; a nonsense token returned rc 1 with 0 lines.

Breakdown: **13 production calls**, 1 definition, 1 comment line, 9 test-file lines.

| file:line @ 4a1620588819 | id expression | where the id comes from | can carry a platform UUID | opts | base behaviour on a UUID id |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| routes/documents.ts:800 | `id` | `:639` create path, `documentUuid ?? doc-<ts>` | no in practice | none | row inserted with that external_id, so the key matches |
| routes/documents.ts:881 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | none | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:913 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:928 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | none | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:1224 | `id` | `req.params` at `:1188` | **YES** | none | **0 rows, returns the record, reports success** |
| routes/documents.ts:1408 | `id` | `req.params` at `:1327` | **YES** | none | **0 rows, returns the record, reports success** |
| routes/documents.ts:2398 | `id` | `req.params` at `:2353`, route `/:id/revoke` | **YES** | ifStatusIsNot | 0 rows, returns null, wrong 400 — FIXED under KS-1278 |
| routes/verification.ts:396 | `String(docId)` | `persistHealedAnchor` at `:389` | **YES** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:183 | `documentId` | parameter, threaded from the create path | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:258 | `documentId` | `opts.documentId` | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:295 | `documentId` | `opts.documentId` | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:376 | `document.id` | a DocumentRecord | **YES when external_id is NULL** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:414 | `document.id` | a DocumentRecord | **YES when external_id is NULL** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |

So **12 of the 13** keep `WHERE external_id` unchanged under KS-1278, and **5 of those 12** are reachable with a value that matches no row. The NULL-`external_id` case is already in gate65's own NOT TESTED list.

This census **corrects the figure of 14** used while ruling KS-1278: 14 counted the 13 production calls plus one non-call line. The measured count is 13 production callers, 1 opted in, 12 others.

## What was searched before filing

Linear team KS titles, case-insensitive: `updateDocument` 0 hits, `documentRepo.ts` 0 hits, `external_id` 0 hits. Must-hit control: `revoke` returned 18. Inverted control: a nonsense symbol returned 0. So the filter discriminates and this class was genuinely unfiled. `searchIssues` was not used as an absence instrument.

## Not fixed here

KS-1278's round 2 narrows the fix to the single opted-in revoke path on purpose, so the blast radius is one caller. Changing the other 12 needs its own decision: for an unguarded caller a 0-row update is currently indistinguishable from a successful one, so simply re-keying them would change what several callers report. Refs KS-1278.

title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*

title: gate64 minors on the KS-1330 runner re-land (PR 1389): six findings carried forward, and the gate kit's key reader goes blind on a split <h2>
description:
gate64 returned **GO** on #1389 (KS-1330, re-landing the round-2 signal handling) at head `a7f5965a7b3f`. The PR has MERGED as squash `22b268143a6377c9a82cd03379daa596cd26d644` on develop. This ticket carries the non-blocking findings forward with the fix shape the gate gave for each, plus one defect in the **gate kit itself** that will hit every lane merging on top of PR 1390. Refs KS-1330 ## The six carried findings **N-1389-1 — Minor, MEASURED.** Leg 14 is no evidence for item 1, and the PR body says it is. Leg 14 sends no signal to the runner, so both INT arms are unreachable there. Fix: drop the leg-14 sentence from any future Test Evidence for this work; the arm's evidence is the suite, not the push. **N-1389-3 — Minor, MEASURED.** The interrupt cell cannot tell a re-raise from a plain exit 1 — the tamper stays 61/0. Fix: assert the signal-death exit status (128+SIG) rather than just non-zero, so a runner that exits 1 instead of re-raising reddens. **N-1389-4 — Minor, PROBED.** A false grep sentence and an absent file. The conclusion holds, the figures do not. Fix: re-measure per file against a must-hit control before restating it anywhere. **N-1389-5 — Minor, PROBED.** The coupling figures are wrong: 16 read-heads measured, not 2; 9 trap-INT, not 10 of 10. The conclusions hold. Fix: same as N-1389-4 — the sentence survives, the numbers must be re-taken. **N-1389-6 — Minor.** Item 3 has no pinning cell; its explanatory comment sits mid-loop rather than in the header; and there is a re-indent artefact. Fix: add one pinning cell, move the comment to the header, drop the re-indent. **N-1389-7 — Polish, MEASURED.** An interrupt under a short TMPDIR leaves the in-flight `rss-suite.*` log behind. Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR. Not in scope here: **N-1389-2** belongs to KS 1331 (the untrapped background grandchild), and **N-1389-8** / **N-1389-9** are Info. ## The gate-kit defect — the one worth acting on `c4_docs_gate64.py:61` **finds doc sections with a SAME-LINE reader, and PR 1390 split** `

` **across** **lines, so the key list silently loses half its entries.** The reader is `h2 = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if '

' in l]` followed by a key match against `lines[i]`. Both key regexes require the closing tag on the opening tag's line: cheat `— KS-(\d+)

`, flow `\(KS-(\d+)\)`. Measured on the real doc bytes, read by the GitHub contents API at each ref: | flow doc | `

` lines | same-line keys | multiline-tolerant keys | split `

` | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | develop `d784b613c81e` | 16 | 8 | 8 | 0 | | develop `c5101866e` (after PR 1390) | 16 | **4** | 8 | **5** | Keys LOST by the same-line reader: KS 1015, KS 1345, KS 1388, KS 1210. Keys kept: KS 666, KS 1404, KS 1333, KS 1005. The split `

` lines are 1671, 1790, 2504, 2618 and 2734, and the shape is ```

9. Auth surface — connector tokens on the users routes (KS 564, KS 1402)

``` The cheat sheet is unaffected (6 `

The predicted TREE was in fact sound here, because it comes from `merge-tree`, not from this reader. What degrades is the gate's judgement: the D5 key census and M8's "every doc at M equals develop's doc, key for key" ran over a 4-of-8 key list and would **PASS while blind to four sections**. A gate that passes blind is worse than one that fails. title: gate61 round-2 follow-ups on migration 049: X7 backfill order, the flow doc's stale suite figures, an ungated arm, and 039 failing for a non-superuser owner
description:
Filed by the Seat F 3rd session at the close of PR #1383. Wednesday ruled all four items **not required before that merge**. Refs KS-1401.

**Searched first** (Linear `searchIssues`, 2026-10-05): `N-1383`, `gate61 round 2`, `backfill after CREATE POLICY`, `11 cells 53 assertions`, `permission denied to create role`, `flow doc block 22`, `tenant_scope_bypass`. That endpoint is **fuzzy** — it returned five relevance-ranked hits for every term, so this is weak evidence of absence rather than proof. The nearest existing tickets are **KS-1376** (certifications ends FORCE with no policy — related, different defect), **KS-889** (a different COALESCE backfill window) and **KS-1281** (a different `permission denied` on `vc_credentials_store`). None covers the four below.

---

### r2-1 (Minor) — in the constructed X7 state the NULL row stays NULL

In gate61 round 1's constructed X7 state (`certifications` with RLS FORCE and **no** policy), migration 049's backfill leaves the `tenant_id IS NULL` row still NULL.

**Unreachable on the repo's own paths**, which is why it is Minor: the gateway runner backfills, then sets NOT NULL, then FORCEs, in that order.

* Fix shape: perform the backfill **after** `CREATE POLICY`, not before.
* Regression arm: X7's owner arm.

### r2-2 (Minor) — the FLOW document still carries the pre-fix suite figures

Block 22 of the architecture flow document still reads `11 cells, 53 assertions.` and `13 s, 13 s, 12 s`. The suite is now **12 cells, 62 assertions, 19/18/19 s**. The QA cheat sheet **is** correct, so the two platform-k documents disagree with each other.

Verified at the close of the session, both lines, with the cheat sheet as a control (zero occurrences of `53 assertions` there against one of `62 assertions`, so the check discriminates between the documents).

**Deliberately not fixed in PR #1383:** a content commit on a head that already holds a signed GO would re-gate it. This is a **docs-only** follow-up.

### r2-3 (Polish) — the COMMITTED arm does not gate the count arms

In the suite's cell 12, the assertion that the migration run committed (`rc 0`, zero `ERROR` lines) is reported **beside** the row-count assertions rather than **gating** them. If a run fails to commit, the count assertions still execute and report against a rolled-back database.

Today all three pass together so nothing is hidden, but the arrangement means a future rollback would be reported as a count failure rather than as a non-committed run. A `RAISE NOTICE` is not transactional, which is the whole reason the COMMITTED arm exists.

### r2-6 (Info, pre-existing) — 039 fails every boot for a non-superuser owner

Run as a non-superuser owner, the gateway runner fails migration 039 on every boot with `permission denied to create role`. Pre-existing, not introduced by 049.

**Why it matters here:** it bears directly on the one fact nobody has measured on the kintsugi database — the connecting role's superuser / BYPASSRLS / owner status — which is the input that decides whether gate61's N-1383-1 would have bitten that database at all. Read that role before the 049 apply round.

---

**Not a blocker for PR #1383.** Its merge is held on a separate Kam ruling (the KS-1404 anchor wiring must merge first), not on any of these.

title: gate63 minors on the KS-1404 trust-anchor wiring (PR 1388): six Minors carried forward, and the image proof was never run
description:
gate63 returned **GO** on #1388 (KS-1404, the trust-anchor wiring) with six Minor findings, none
blocking and none Major. The PR has merged; this ticket carries the findings forward with the
fix-shape the gate gave for each. Report `a68b1497f421c496…`, 276 lines.

Refs KS-1404

## The six findings

**N-1388-1 — the tsc figure does not reproduce, and no host is named.** The claim "a single
pre-existing tsc error (`rfc3161-verify.ts` TS2345), its line moving 344→349" appears in the commit
message, the PR body and flow 11.4. The gate measured TypeScript 5.9.3 on standalone member
installs and got **rc 0, zero** `error TS` **lines at both** `f01c1da5717f` and `3ce575eeb63c`; the brief
expected 59. Three different counts for one figure, none with a host. The substance holds — **0 NEW**
**errors either way** — but it sits in a client-facing doc with nothing that lets a reader
re-measure it. *Fix-shape:* name the host and install recipe beside each figure, or restate as
"0 new tsc errors (base N / head N on <host>, <recipe>)". The "1937 packages" figure in the PR body
is the same class (the gate measured 349+267 standalone, 346+311 as workspace members; I measured
1,393 package directories in the worktree — three units, one number).

**N-1388-2 — the cheat sheet's corrected note points the wrong way.** The note after the KS-1404
table (`:3776-:3779`) says the wiring row is "below"; it is at `:3748`, **above**. "is now covered"
also reads as though some environment already has the anchor in effect — none does, because no
deploy has happened. *Fix-shape:* "below" → "above", and say "this change wires every
compose-launched box; in effect once deployed". This could not be fixed in the merge-in: Q-M's M1
pins the head's section byte for byte.

**N-1388-3 — cell A does not bind the default's variable name.** Tamper T-NAME
(`${OTHER_VAR:-/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt}`) stays **6/6 green**. The default still
pins D-Trust so verification is unaffected; what breaks silently is the documented override path.
*Fix-shape:* anchor the regex to `^\$\{TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM:-(.*)\}$`. *Regression test:* T-NAME
must red cell A.

**N-1388-4 — no PR cell parses the REAL per-provider file inside the verifier.** C1 hashes the PEM
with the test's own decoder; C2 uses a synthetic root. At the base C1 reds only through A's
precondition, so its own conjunct has no independent red-first. The gate's probe P1/P2 closes the
gap at runtime for this head, as does pre-existing cell 17 (the bundle's block 1 is byte-equal to
this file). *Fix-shape:* commit P1 and P2 as cells —
`parseTrustAnchors(readFileSync(<real file>)).length === 1` at the digest, and a synthetic token with
the real file by path refused "does not chain", never "no trust anchor configured".

**N-1388-5 — a missing anchor is silent until a verify, and** `/health` **carries no anchor state.**
Fail-closed is the safe direction, but a wiring failure reproduces today's "everything refused"
state behind a green `/health`. *Fix-shape:* an `anchors: {configured, count, sha256[]}` block in
`/health`, or a boot-time log line. **Operational consequence now:** the deploy sweep must use the
in-container checks in the gate's C7(a), never `/health`.

**N-1388-6 — the image also ships the two-root bundle** (DigiCert included) at
`/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors.crt`. Q-SCOPE holds and no new privilege is created.
*Fix-shape (optional):* COPY only the per-provider file, or note it in `config/README.md`.

## OWED to the kintsugi deploy round, not done here

**C6, the local image proof, is NOT RUN — the Docker daemon was unreachable (c6 rc 20).** So the
claim that the built image actually contains `/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt` is
unverified. It is owed to the deploy round, which is a separate seat on its own GO. Nothing in
#1388 has been deployed: `TSA_URL` is present-but-empty on both live boxes, which resolves to
D-Trust by code default, and `TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM` is absent on both, so every real RFC 3161
token is still refused with `no trust anchor configured` until a deploy happens.

## Also worth recording, found while merging

`merged8.py` requires nine `targets` as (blob, mode) pairs that the gate's `## MERGE ADDENDUM` line
does not publish. I sourced each by reading `ls-tree` at the head so the mode comes from git rather
than from me, but the gap between what the gate publishes and what the merge tool demands is an
invitation to guess at a value that lands on `develop` permanently.

title: Flow doc block 18.3 states a suite reading with no seat, date or host, beside a PR body reporting a different run at the same sha
description:
## BLUF

Flow-diagram block 18.3 states a `services/auth` suite reading as "at head" with no seat, no date
and no host, while the PR body for the same sha reports a different run. A reader of the document
cannot tell that more than one reading exists at that commit, or whose machine produced the one
they are looking at.

Raised from gate60's review of PR #1384 (KS 1210) as finding N-1384-2.
**Pre-existing in that PR's documentation, not introduced by its merge-in.**
Severity Minor (D9) / Polish (D8); it blocked
nothing, and a documentation change at the time would have moved the head and forced a re-gate,
which is why it was deferred to a follow-up rather than fixed in place.

## What is actually wrong

Three readings of the same suite exist at sha 852fc9276320, and the document presents one of them
as if it were the only one:

* Seat E 2nd measured 864 of 864 with zero ks949 timeouts.
* The PR body reports a red run 1 at the same sha.
* The gate's own run on its host, 2026-10-05 at 08:05:51Z under load 2.35 rising to 6.46, also
  measured 864 of 864 with zero ks949 timeouts.

The document's sentence is **not false** — it is true of Seat E 2nd's run. The defect is that it is
unattributed, so a reader cannot reconcile it with the red run the body describes, and cannot tell
which host or load the green figure came from.

## What to do

* Attribute block 18.3's figures: name the seat, the date and the host that produced them.
* Add the run-1 reading alongside, or point the reader at the PR body where it is recorded.
* The companion D8 note is weaker and can be closed with it: the "5000 ms" figure in that block is
  a vitest timeout VALUE, not a stated suite timing, so the skill's stated-timings rule is barely
  engaged there. Polish only.

## Not covered

No live sweep. This is a documentation-attribution defect, measured by reading the committed
documents and the gate's report; nothing was exercised against a running service for it.

Refs KS-1210

title: #1387 gate62 minors: the two platform-k docs claim "all three cmp-equal" and that is false, and the new status-URI cell's first-line pin is blind to a later active :6882 line
description:
Two Minors from gate62's review of PR #1387 (KS 1388 §1, merged on Wednesday's GO of
2026-10-05T10:04:00Z). Neither is a regression introduced by that PR: both are properties of the
documentation and of the test cell it added. Filed as a later row on Wednesday's instruction — **not**
**fixed in that round.**

## 1. Both platform-k documents claim "all three cmp-equal", and that is false

**Where:** the KS 1388 block in `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` and the corresponding section in `Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

**What the documents say vs what is true.** The applied-equals-held claim is written as all three files
being `cmp`-equal to an independent apply. Measured: only the **suite file** is `cmp`-equal. Each of
the two env examples differs from the held hunk by **exactly one added line** — its `# KS 1388:` §5d
WHY comment, which the skill requires and the held patch does not carry. So the honest claim is
"one file cmp-equal, two files equal plus exactly one declared comment line each", and that is
materially different from "all three cmp-equal": a reader auditing the PR against the held artefact
would find two mismatches and have no way to tell they were intended.

**Why it matters beyond wording:** this is a claim about an *equality gate*, in the two documents a
reviewer reads instead of re-running the gate.

## 2. The new test cell's first-line pin is blind to a later active `:6882` line

**Where:** the cell added to `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh`.

**Symptom.** The cell pins the **first** occurrence of the status URI in each env example. A file
whose first line is correct but which carries a **later, active** (uncommented)
`nginx-gateway:6882` line passes. The cell cannot see the second line at all, so the regression it
exists to catch can be reintroduced below the line it reads and stay green.

**Fix shape (not applied here):** a per-file count cell —
`grep -c 'nginx-gateway:6882' <file>` asserted `== 0` — which is blind to position and therefore
cannot be satisfied by ordering. Keep the existing first-line pin as well: it carries the
positive statement about what the first line should be, which a count cannot express.

## Dup search before filing

All **543** KS issues enumerated across every state (not `searchIssues`, which saturates at 50 and
cannot prove a zero) and substring-matched locally. `"all three cmp-equal"` 0 hits, `"cmp-equal"` 0
hits; `"nginx-gateway:6882"`, `"stub_status"` and `"SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI"` each hit exactly 1 row
and it is KS 1388 itself, the parent, not a duplicate of either finding. Controls fired both ways: a
must-hit probe for the parent key returned 1 (KS 1386 cites it) and a nonsense string returned 0.

Refs KS-1388. KS 1388 stays OPEN: only §1 shipped, and its §5f live sweep has not run.

title: start-secuura.sh banner prints admin@secuura.com / admin123, which has returned 401 since PR #888
description:
## BLUF

`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` ends every successful start with a **Credentials** block that still prints `Admin: admin@secuura.com / admin123`. Since PR #888 ([KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) items 1+2) retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default, that login **returns 401** — measured on a fresh slot-2 stack on 2026-09-07. The banner now hands every operator a credential that does not work, on the one screen they are guaranteed to read.

Found during the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) four-slot isolation sweep, not by reading the script.

## Measured

```
POST /api/auth/login  {"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}
  -> 401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Invalid email or password"}
```

`demo@secuura.io / demo123` on the same banner line still authenticates (200), so the issuer half is correct and only the admin half is stale.

## Why it is its own ticket rather than a [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) sub-item

[KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)'s ruled order item 3 — *"4 startup/scripts + 3 harnesses — env var, no fallback"* — covers scripts that **read** the fallback. This is the script **printing** it: a documentary line, not an executable read, so it is not caught by that sweep's definition of "site" and would survive item 3 landing. Related to [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) so it is sequenced beside it; raised separately so it is not lost inside a routing change.

## Suggested fix

Either drop the admin line from the banner, or print the mechanism instead of a value — e.g. *"Admin: provisioned per run, see* `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`*"* — since [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)'s answer was that no shared admin credential should exist to print.

## Context

* The banner also prints `Project: <compose default>` for slot 1 while the container labels read the worktree-derived project name (`ks-682` in this sweep). Minor; noted while here, not the subject of this ticket.
* Raised from the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) sweep; platform-k base code, so filed to Kamil per the review-authority rule.

title: Compose seeds published *123 credentials by default, and the 11 rotation vars never reach the auth container from .env — every compose deploy (local, demo VM, Kintsugi)
description:
## BLUF

**Any compose deploy of this platform comes up seeding the published** `*123` **credentials, and the documented way to rotate them silently does nothing unless you happen to put them in the one undocumented file.** Two halves of the same asymmetry in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

* the single variable that **enables** published default passwords is interpolated from `.env` and **defaults to** `true`;
* the eleven variables that **replace** those passwords are not interpolated at all, and reach the container only via `.env.local` — which no example file and no doc mentions.

So the natural path (`.env`, which is what `env.example` and the deploy docs use) gives you: seeding **on**, published credentials **live**, and your rotation **ignored** — while the seeder logs that it updated the accounts.

Blast radius is **every compose deploy**: local, the demo VM, and Kintsugi. `docker-compose.local.yml` `include:`s `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, so the canonical local stack inherits it, and the demo VM + Kintsugi run that file directly.

## Recommendation

Two small changes, both in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

1. Flip the default: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-false}`, and set it explicitly to `true` in the local-dev path that actually wants it. Opting in should be an act, not an omission.
2. Interpolate the eleven rotation variables in the `auth` service's `environment:` block the same way every other secret is (`- DEMO_USER_PASSWORD=${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD:-}` …), so `.env` — the file everyone edits — is a working channel. Then document them in `env.example`.

Neither is a code change to the auth service; the seeder's logic (`userRepo.ts:965-995`) is correct as written.

## A — the gate defaults to ON, and its stated premise is dead

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:626`

```yaml
- ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-true}
```

The pen-test **F-05** fix gated the demo seeder on this variable. The auth service states the premise the gate rests on, at `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:987-991`:

> *"The hardcoded fallbacks remain only because the seeder itself is now gated on* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` *(above) — i.e. **a deploy that doesn't explicitly opt in never sees these strings**."*

That premise is false for every compose deploy, because the compose file opts in on your behalf.

The justification for the default is at `:623-625`:

> *"Defaults to true here ONLY because docker-compose.yml is the local-dev compose; production is on Container Apps where this env var is unset and the gate stays closed."*

**That reasoning died with the KS-414 VM pivot (2026-07-08).** The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31. Since the pivot, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` is not "the local-dev compose" — it is *the* deployment artefact for the demo VM and now for Kintsugi as well. The comment describes an architecture the project no longer has.

Measured on the running local stack:

```
$ docker exec secuura-auth sh -c 'echo $ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS'
true
```

## B — the eleven rotation variables never reach the container from `.env`

Derived from source rather than from any prior write-up — every `seedPw()` call site in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`:

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_APEX_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_BUPA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_DELTA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_GREENFIELD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_OXFORD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD`

| check | result | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| occurrences of each of the 11 in `docker-compose.yml` | **0 / 11** | `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` → **1** |
| present in the running `secuura-auth` container | **0 / 11** | gate present, value `true`; 95 env vars total |

Both zero-results carry a control that fires independently, so they are real absences and not a grep that could never match.

The code's own rotation instruction (`userRepo.ts:992-993`) is:

> *"For per-tenant rotation, set* `DEMO_<TENANT>_PASSWORD` *env vars in Azure Key Vault and **surface them to the auth container**."*

"Surface them to the auth container" is the whole problem — it names no channel, and only one of the two obvious ones works.

## The correction — this is NOT "rotation is impossible"

An earlier write-up of this (KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a`) concluded the documented rotation *cannot work*. **That over-claims, and the correction matters because it changes the fix.** The `auth` service does declare an env_file:

```yaml
env_file:
  - path: .env.local
    required: false
```

Tested rather than assumed: of the **66** variables declared in `.env.local`, **66** are present in the running container. `.env.local` is a fully working injection channel.

So the accurate finding is an **asymmetry of channel**, which is worse than a flat "it doesn't work" because it fails silently in exactly one direction:

| variable | channel | reaches container from `.env`? | effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` | `${…:-true}` interpolation | **yes**, and defaults **true** | published `*123` credentials get seeded |
| the 11 `*_PASSWORD` vars | `.env.local` env_file only | **no** | rotation silently ignored |

`.env` is the file `env.example` is copied to, the file the setup instructions name, and the file compose reads for `${…}` interpolation — but it is *not* an env_file for `auth`, so values placed there are invisible to the seeder. Neither `env.example` nor `.env.local.example` mentions any of the eleven, or the gate.

## Why it fails convincingly

Recorded on Kintsugi during the KS-601 Stage C build (2026-08-20) — **this half is that session's on-box measurement; I have not re-run it here**, because reproducing it locally means changing `demo@`'s password and breaking the preflight persona:

Setting the eleven in `.env` and recreating the auth container printed `Demo user updated to match seed config` account after account — on a code path that genuinely does execute an `UPDATE … password_hash`. **The old password still authenticated.** Only a negative control (attempting a login with the *old* credential and expecting it to fail) caught it. Fixed on that box with a compose override making all 11 visible, then verified both directions: old `demo123` → **401**, new credential → **200**.

That is the part worth carrying: the failure produces success-shaped log output, so anyone rotating credentials and checking the logs will believe they succeeded.

## Scope note

Not in scope here: whether the demo VM *should* keep its seeded public credentials. Those are deliberate, documented sample logins for public demos (project `CLAUDE.md`). This ticket is about a deploy coming up more permissive than its operator intended, and a rotation that reports success without doing anything.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:570-666` — `auth` service; `:626` the gate; `:623-625` the dead premise; `env_file` at `:576-578`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:965-995` — the F-05 gate, the `seedPw()` helper and its rotation instruction.
* `docker-compose.local.yml:33-35` — `include:` of `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example`, `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` — neither names the eleven or the gate.
* KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a` — the Kintsugi on-box record (superseded on the "cannot work" point by the correction above).

## Suggested owner

Unassigned deliberately. Compose/deploy topology rather than service logic — @peter or @stuart to route; happy to take it myself if neither has context loaded.

title: The default-password CI gate catches one shape and calls it clean — 16 published passwords are exempt by design, and 4 of 5 canaries walk past it
description:
## The finding

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh` is a **live CI gate** (`pr-security-gates.yml:63`, `security-scan.yml:422`). It is far blinder than its name suggests, and the documented exemption is the *small* half.

## The exemption (known, by design)

Line 34 is `| grep -v 'seedPw(' \`. With **only that line deleted** (sha-asserted both ways and restored), the lint exits 1 with **16 flagged lines — sixteen other seeded accounts' published default passwords**, invisible to it by design.

## The blind spots (not by design)

Five canaries planted through the real script:

| plant | result |
| -- | -- |
| `services/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | **SEEN** — positive control, the instrument is live |
| `services/`, `.ts`, not ending `123` | MISSED — any other password shape |
| `frontend/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `services/` and `packages/` are scanned |
| `services/`, `.sql`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `.ts/.tsx/.js`; **the seed SQL that** `fixtures.ts` **cites as source-of-truth is invisible** |
| `scripts/` subdir, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — `--exclude-dir=scripts,tests,__tests__` |

So the gate catches exactly one shape — a `*123` literal, in a `.ts/.tsx/.js` file, under `services/` or `packages/`, not in an excluded directory, and not behind `seedPw(`.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

A guard with a documented exemption is a guard with a hole of a **known** size — and the hole never appears in the guard's own green result. This one passes today, passed before [KS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-949), and would have passed with the real-person account and its published password still in place. It is a live gate that gives false assurance in CI.

- [ ] Widen the file-type and directory scope, or state the scope in the gate's own output so a green result says what it actually covered
- [ ] Decide whether the `seedPw(` exemption should survive at all now that one account (the platform admin) is held to a stricter rule than the lint enforces
- [ ] A password shape that is not `*123`

## Provenance

The exemption and the `docker-compose.yml:755` default were disclosed by the filer while doing KS-949 and **confirmed at source** by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #885 (2026-09-06T21:29:45Z); the 16-line count and the five canaries are the gate's measurement, not the filer's.

*Filed by s143 (seat A), 2026-09-07.*

title: webhooks routes reject connector principals (userId connector:<id>) - 500 after KS 1345, silent 200 before
description:
**BLUF:** a caller authenticating with an API key becomes a **connector principal** whose `userId` is non-UUID (`connector:<connectorId>`), and the webhooks routes cast that value to `uuid`. `GET /api/webhooks` answered **200** `{webhooks: []}` for such a principal before KS 1345 and answers **500 INTERNAL_ERROR** after it. `POST /api/webhooks` already answered 500 for the same principals.

Filed from gate57 finding N-1381-1 (Minor) on PR 1381. Facts only; nothing here was measured live.

## The principal class, traced at source

Measured at `3ce8cd4026a6` by reading the source, with no live reach and no database read:

* the gateway sets the connector userId: `api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:301`
* it exchanges the key for an RS256 JWT minted with the same userId by `generateConnectorToken`: `auth/src/services/jwt.ts:289`
* originate's `authenticate()` accepts that token with no `type` check: `originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:82-104`
* the gateway mounts the webhooks routes behind the `webhooks:manage` scope: `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:442-446`

So a key holding `webhooks:manage` reaches a `${userId}::uuid` cast carrying `connector:...`.

## Behaviour

* before KS 1345: **200** with an empty list, which is a silent wrong answer
* after KS 1345: **500**, logged as an error on every call
* create (`POST`, the `${userId}::uuid` cast in its INSERT, no catch) already answered 500 for these principals, so the list route is now consistent with create

## UNMEASURED

* whether any **issued** API key actually holds `webhooks:manage` — this needs a database read and was not done
* whether any other path mints a non-UUID userId
* live reach: the class was traced at source only

## The open question for the owner

A 500 for a principal-class condition is arguably a mis-mapping. It could reasonably be a 4xx, or the list could be keyed on the organisation rather than the user. That decision is the owner's and was explicitly out of scope for PR 1345, which replaced a silent wrong answer with a loud one.

Related: KS 1345 (the PR that flipped the status), KS 1341 (the same file's error-body work), KS 1256 (connector allow-list failing open — a different defect in the same principal class).

title: develop does not build since KS-1378 (#1339): analytics, billing and governance images fail `tsc` — packages/shared now locks @types/express-serve-static-core 4.19.9 / @types/pg 8.23.1, those three services still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0
description:
## BLUF

A clean build of platform-k `develop` at `0aa9b52c6` fails: `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` stops with *"Build FAILED for: analytics billing governance — not starting containers"*, so no stack comes up. The previous clean build on this Mac, at `d9ce1403d` (28 Sep), succeeded. Between the two, no `package.json` or Dockerfile of those three services changed; what changed is [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address) **(**[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1339](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1378-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address-and-undici-off-five-815a0a16d4c7), `2cb858335`**)**, which refreshed `packages/shared/package-lock.json` and several services' locks — but not these three.

## Evidence

`packages/shared/package-lock.json` (top-level `node_modules/@types/*`):

|  | before `2cb858335` | after | `services/analytics` lock at `0aa9b52c6` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `@types/express-serve-static-core` | 4.19.8 | **4.19.9** | 4.19.8 |
| `@types/pg` | 8.20.0 | **8.23.1** | 8.20.0 |
| `@types/express` | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 |

Each service image copies the built `/shared` (with its own `node_modules`) beside the service's `node_modules`, so `tsc` sees two copies of the same declarations:

```
analytics  src/index.ts(34,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'app' cannot be named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'. This is likely not portable.
           (also routes/analytics.ts:20, routes/dashboard.ts:12, routes/health.ts:7)
billing    src/db.ts(45,32): error TS2345: Argument of type 'import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool' is not assignable to parameter of type 'import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool'.
           (plus TS2742 on index.ts:33, routes/billing.ts:26, routes/webhooks.ts:29)
governance same TS2742 family
```

`#1339`'s file list refreshes the locks of queue, security, timestamping, prism and others; `services/analytics`, `services/billing` and `services/governance` are not in it.

**The mismatch is wider than the three that fail (re-checked from every lock at** `0aa9b52c6`**).** Eleven service locks still carry `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.8 / `@types/pg` 8.20.0 against shared's 4.19.9 / 8.23.1: analytics, billing, governance (fail) and **kyc, nft-certificate, referral, staking, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation, transfer, wallet-connector** (built fine in the same run — none of their exported types is inferred across the boundary today, so they are latent, one annotation-less `const app = express()` away from the same error). `services/shared` locks 4.19.8 and `vc-issuer` a third `@types/pg` (8.21.0). At the last good commit `d9ce1403d`, `packages/shared` itself locked 4.19.8 / 8.20.0 — every lock agreed, which is why that build passed. All 35 images were attempted in this run; exactly these three failed.

## Likely fix (Kamil's call)

Refresh the failing three — and the eight latent ones — to the same `@types/express-serve-static-core` / `@types/pg` versions `packages/shared` now pins (or pin those `@types` in shared to what the services use). A check that every service lock agrees with `packages/shared` on the `@types` it re-exports would stop the next bump doing this — [KS-953](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-953/class-editing-api-gatewaysrcindexts-silently-reddens-packagesshared) is the same class (a change in one package silently reddening another).

## Reproduce

```bash
git worktree add --detach <path> origin/develop      # 0aa9b52c6
cd <path> && SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=<N> ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild
```

## Environment

Peter's Mac, Docker Desktop 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026 \~09:25–09:50 BST. Found while bringing up a paired K for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) gate run.
