title: charge_events has RLS off entirely on the kintsugi database (already past 039), and 8 rows are in it — a redeploy cannot fix it
description:
## BLUF

**On a database that recorded** `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **before** `charge_events` **existed, that table ends with row-level security not enabled at all — no RLS, no FORCE, no policy — and a redeploy cannot change it.** Measured on the kintsugi database, which holds **8 rows** in that table. Both migration runners skip any file already recorded, so 039's edits are inert there, and `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` only helps a database whose 039 has not yet run. This ticket does not write the fix; "What done means" below states the constraints it must meet.

## Measured

Read on the kintsugi main database before and after the 2026-09-30 deploy, identical both times:

| table | exists | rows | RLS enabled | RLS forced | policies |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| charge_events | yes | **8** | **false** | **false** | **0** |
| certifications | yes | 0 | true | true | 0 |
| oauth_apps | yes | 0 | true | true | 2 |
| svc_webhooks | yes | 0 | true | true | 1 |

Controls: both readings showed `users` with RLS enabled and 2 policies, and a policy name that does not exist returning 0; the after-deploy reading also showed `to_regclass` on a table that does not exist returning false. So the zeros above are readings, not a blind query.

`charge_events` **is the row of that table with no ticket.** It is also the only one of the four holding data.

## Why a deploy does not fix it

* Both runners skip a migration already recorded in `_secuura_migrations`: `scripts/run-migrations.sh:118-122`, and api-gateway's startup stage at `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:137-141`, which reads `SELECT 1 FROM _secuura_migrations WHERE filename = $1 LIMIT 1` and `continue`s when a row comes back. Both were read at `91a8f6b721bc`.
* `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` has listed `charge_events` since KS 458. It skips any listed table that does not exist yet, or that has no `tenant_id` column. Nothing that runs later enables RLS on `charge_events`: no migration numbered after 039 names it, and the startup stage's RLS loop does not list it.
* `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` creates these tables **before** 039 runs, so on a fresh database 039 gives `charge_events`, `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` their policies on the first boot (`certifications` is the exception recorded in KS-1376). On this database, 038a ran on 2026-09-30 **after** 039 was already recorded; its only effect there was one tracker row, the four tables already existing.
* So 038a cannot help a database where 039 has already run, and editing 039 itself reaches nothing — the edit to it inside the deployed range was inert on this box for exactly that reason.

**Unmeasured:** why `charge_events` was skipped when this database first ran 039. The consistent reading is that it did not exist yet, as 038a's own header describes for a bare database, but the original run's log was not read, and whether the table had a `tenant_id` column at that moment was not read.

## Relationship to the existing tickets — read before filing

* **KS-1376** covers `certifications` ending RLS FORCE with no `tenant_isolation` policy, and its fix shape is *"a migration numbered after 039 that applies 039's* `tenant_isolation` *block to* `certifications`*"*. A migration numbered after 039 is unrecorded on **every** database, including ones already past 039 — so that fix, once written, should reach the `certifications` row above as well; confirm it on an already-migrated database when it lands. The `certifications` half is therefore not re-filed here.
* **KS-1054** covers fresh databases being fail-open until the second boot, addressed by Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1332 (merged).
* **KS-1055** covers per-tenant databases never receiving the file migrations.
* **What none of them states** is the case this ticket is for: `charge_events` **on an already-migrated database, with RLS never enabled and rows already present.** Searched team KS with `includeArchived`, on title and description, by `charge_events` (7 hits, none about RLS), `039_rls_fail_closed` (6), `relforcerowsecurity` (1, KS 959, which is KS 597's org-context fallback and cites forced RLS only to explain why a zero row-count needs a control), `certifications` (50, paginated) and `tenant_isolation` (20). Positive control `migration` returned 50, so the query shape works.

## Other environments

* A fresh database from `91a8f6b721bc`: when #1332 was reviewed, `charge_events` was measured with RLS enabled and forced and one fail-closed `tenant_isolation` policy on all three bare-database paths, and 038a, 039 and both runners are unchanged since. Not re-measured here.
* **demo: unmeasured.** The instrument that closes it is the same read-only catalog query — `pg_class.relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity`, the `pg_policies` count, the row count — against demo's main database.
* Any other database created before #1332 and already past 039: unmeasured.

## What done means

1. On every already-migrated database this applies to, `charge_events` has RLS enabled and forced with the `tenant_isolation` policy 039 defines, shown by the same catalog read before and after.
2. It is delivered by a path an existing database actually runs on deploy — a migration numbered after 039 — not by editing a recorded file.
3. A regression check that is red on a database where 039 was recorded before `charge_events` existed, and green after. Driven as the application role, not as a source-text assertion: the failure mode here is a runtime one, and only a driven probe separates "policy present" from "table reachable because the reader owns it".
4. The **8 existing rows stay readable to their own tenant** after the change, tested rather than assumed. This is the part that makes the change riskier than the `certifications` case, where the table is empty.

Related: KS-1054 (fresh databases, addressed by #1332). See also KS-1376 (the `certifications` row above, whose fix shape should cover it) and KS-1055 (per-tenant databases).

title: Five new advisories block EVERY push: bump morgan, nodemailer, ip-address and undici (Kam ruled (a))
description:
**BLUF — the push preflight FAILS legs 6 and 7 on develop's own dependencies, so NO push on this repo succeeds until this lands.** Five newly published advisories are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. Verified ABSENT from the baseline at develop `8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee` itself, so this is not caused by any open branch.

Kam ruled card `secuura-five-new-advisories-block-every-push-0929` = **(a)** on the live board 2026-09-29 11:43:09 AEST: *"Bump all four packages, with a quick reachability check in the same round."* **No baseline entry for any of the five.**

## The five, verbatim from preflight leg 6

| advisory | package | where |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-6vj9-mwq6-2f5v` | **nodemailer** | process-global DNS cache reuses the TLS `servername` across transports -> **cross-tenant SMTP credential disclosure**. 2 locks: services/auth, services/originate |
| `GHSA-9f6g-j8ch-79g4` | **morgan** | log injection via an unescaped double quote in quoted log fields. **10 service locks** |
| `GHSA-rpw4-54j3-4h4q` | **ip-address** | `Address6.isLinkLocal()` reads `fe80::/64` not `fe80::/10` -> SSRF / trust-boundary bypass. 3 locks incl. packages/shared |
| `GHSA-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc` | **ip-address** | no classifier for the NAT64 local-use range `64:ff9b:1::/48` -> SSRF / trust-boundary bypass |
| `GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v` | **undici** | DoS via an unhandled error in WebSocket permessage-deflate decompression. frontend/issuer |

Leg 6 reads `30 distinct advisories reported, 25 baselined`; leg 7 reads `26 match, 21 already baselined` across 43 standalone locks / 1591 pinned packages. Both name the same five.

## The routes are NOT uniform — measured, not assumed

* **morgan** — declared `^1.10.0` in 10 services, pinned 1.12.0, **1.12.1 published and inside the caret**: a lock refresh reaches it.
* **ip-address** — `packages/shared` declares `^10.2.0`, pinned 10.4.0, **10.7.2 inside the caret**: a lock refresh reaches it there. The `@cardano-sdk/dapp-connector` and `@cardano-sdk/key-management` nested 10.4.0 copies and a 9.0.5 are TRANSITIVE: `overrides` or a parent bump.
* 🔴 **nodemailer — a lock refresh CANNOT fix it.** The highest published 9.x **IS** `9.1.1`, exactly what is pinned; `^9.0.3` is at its ceiling and latest is `10.0.12`. It needs a **MAJOR** bump in `services/auth` and `services/originate`. This is the most expensive of the four *and* it is the credential-disclosure one.
* **undici** — TRANSITIVE only, under `jsdom` (a test dependency) plus a 5.29.0. `overrides` or a jsdom bump.

## Not to be confused with

`KS 729` is a **different** ip-address advisory (GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr). A bump here may also satisfy it; that is a bonus, not this ticket's claim.

## Scope

Bump, plus a per-advisory **reachability read** recorded in the PR body (FOUND / TESTED / HOW). **The proof is preflight legs 6 and 7 passing on the PR.** No baseline entry, no `--no-verify`. Filed by the Platform K build seat on Wednesday's instruction after Kam's ruling.

title: pre-push fixture guard: re-land GUARDGAPS with a call-site reader that passes the aborting `||` / `if` / `&&` shapes and flags multi-line `$(` and group openers
description:
**BLUF: the fixture guard's round-2 work was measured correct in cells 7 and 8 and shipped nothing, because cell 9's reader flags shapes that DO abort and passes shapes that swallow the abort — wrong in both directions.** This ticket re-lands the work with a reader that discriminates, and it resolves a contradiction in the earlier hold text.

## What is on `develop` today

Guard blob `52c852203edc2d7b64c3e23bc2ab3f077cf07cc6` at 6 cells, with three gaps all open: unanchored abort counts, a `repo_state` blind to the worktree, and no call-site pin. **Reach is 0 today** — all 12 of 12 call sites are bare — so nothing is currently mis-scored; the guard simply cannot see a regression.

## What the reader must do

Through the real guard, cell 9 currently **FLAGS** the named aborting shapes:
`bf || true` · `false || bf` · `if bf; then :; fi` · `bf && :`
and **PASSES** the named swallowing shapes: a multi-line `x=$(` / call / `)` and `( : noop` / call / `)`.

That is backwards. `build_fixture` aborts with an explicit `exit 2`, so only a **subshell** call site swallows it; `|| true`, `if` and `&&` do not.

## Scope

Re-land the anchored counts (cell 7), the widened `repo_state` (cell 8) and cells 11-12 from blob `5189cf31a098a62c485367beedb78def2428d787`, with `c9_scan` **admitting** `bf || true`, `false || bf`, `if bf; then :; fi` and `bf && :`, and **flagging** a previous line ending in `$(` / `(` or holding an unclosed `(`. Cell 10 computes `c9_scan`; cell 12 asserts on a subject copy.

## The contradiction to resolve, named by the gate to the filer

The earlier hold asked for a **strict whitelist** AND for the `||` shapes to be **unflagged**. Those two contradict each other. **The admitting whitelist is the one to pick** — that is the gate's own note to whoever picks this up.

## A limit worth carrying forward rather than rediscovering

Do not attempt to track shell nesting by counting parentheses. A paren-depth counter over lines called 11 of 12 real call sites offending, because a subshell can close with `) > "$WORK/c0.out" 2>/dev/null` and a multi-line `$( … )` can end with `)"`. A guard that half-parses shell is worse than one with a declared limit: read one line of context and write the limitation down.

## Evidence produced by the gate

`evidence/reader1253/reader_rows.json` · `evidence/reader1253/guard_*.stdout` · `behav_*.stdout` · `evidence/g1253/garms_rows.json`.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **483 open issues**, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `c9_scan`, `call-site reader`, `5189cf31a098`, `GUARDGAPS`, `admitting whitelist` — **0 open hits each**. Controls as above: a fresh nonsense token **0**, `run-shell-suites.sh` **16**.

Refs KS-1297

title: childSuiteCounts reads a child KILLED by its own 180 s spawnSync timeout as a PASS - a lookalike summary pair is accepted as {7,0}
description:
**BLUF:** `childSuiteCounts` **can report a clean pass for a child process that was killed.** When a child is terminated by its own 180 s `spawnSync` timeout *after* it has already logged a summary-shaped pair, the reader takes that pair as the verdict and returns `{7,0}`. The kill is invisible to it. **Measured on both sides** - at PR #1245's head `65eb964271b0d6895e90fe8f5ffcbbbb9a484050` **and** on `develop` `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086` - so this is a property of the code on the mainline, not of one branch.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## The lookalike that is accepted

A child that logs

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

and is then killed still presents that pair to the reader. `childSuiteCounts` returns `{7,0}` - seven passed, zero failed - and nothing downstream can tell that outcome apart from a genuine completion. **A verdict composed separately from the work reproduces here exactly:** the summary text is not evidence that the run finished.

## Three residues, one test pass, one ticket

1. **KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE** - the defect above.
2. **CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT** - the call site still reaches the summary through text. The shape asked for is a pure `countsFromSpawn(result)` sitting behind `childSuiteCounts`, fed a synthetic spawn result, so the decision is made from the spawn outcome rather than from scraped output.
3. **JOINED-CLAIM** - the sentence *"measured to hold on the JOINED text"* should be dropped. It is not true: **10 real shapes are misread on joined text, 3 of them silently.** A claim about where a reader is safe, which is false, is worse than no claim.

## Fix shapes, any one of which closes the first residue

* **Refuse when the spawn says so:** `result.error` or `result.signal` set, or `result.status` not `0`/`1`.
* **Require vitest's trailing** `Start at` **/** `Duration` **block**, which a killed child never reaches.
* **Use the JSON reporter** instead of parsing human output.

## Cells the next attempt should carry

* The **H1 stdout capture** returns `null`.
* A spawn result of `{status 143, ETIMEDOUT}` **throws** rather than yielding counts.

Signal 143 is SIGTERM; a status of 143 with `ETIMEDOUT` is precisely the killed-child case, and it is the discriminating fixture.

## Reusable from the capped attempt - do not rebuild these

The round-2 **stdout-only reader**, the **whole-run cells**, and the `{3,2}` **row** are sound and are the parts to start from.

## Not covered

Preflight legs 3, 4 and 8 were not run for that attempt (no local stack). They are owed by nothing here; recorded so the absence is not mistaken for a pass.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **481 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `countsFromSpawn`, `KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE`, `CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT`, `JOINED-CLAIM`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `status 143`, `capturedChildOutput` - **0 open hits each**. `spawnSync` returned 2 (KS-1111, KS-1098), neither about this reader. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `childSuiteCounts` returned **1**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

**Not duplicates, deliberately:** KS-1313 is the parent this residue falls out of, and KS-1226 is its own parent. Both stay open and neither is closed by this ticket.

Refs KS-1313

title: A PTY harness so SIGINT can be asserted for run-shell-suites.sh in the foreground, in both the standalone and in-hook environments
description:
**BLUF: there is currently no way to assert that** `run-shell-suites.sh` **handles SIGINT, because every available harness either backgrounds the runner or runs with SIGINT already ignored - and bash discards the signal in both cases.** A pseudo-terminal harness is the only route to closing that gap. Nothing is broken today; the runner's INT/TERM arms exist and are correct. What is missing is the ability to *prove* the INT arm, and today that is recorded as UNREACHABLE rather than tested.

## The two measured rules that create the gap

Both measured on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, which is the only bash on this drive - there is no Homebrew bash cellar and every local project image is busybox/Alpine with no `bash` at all.

1. **A signal IGNORED ON ENTRY to bash cannot be trapped.** `trap '...' INT` is silently not installed and `trap -p INT` comes back empty. **The in-hook preflight runs with SIGINT ignored**, so an INT arm inside the hook cannot exist at all.
2. **bash ignores SIGINT in any ASYNCHRONOUS (background) job**, whatever the parent's disposition: `trap -p INT` empty, the signal discarded, rc 0. The identical trap in the **foreground** gives rc 130.

Between them, SIGINT-to-pid is unassertable by any harness that backgrounds the runner, which is what a test harness naturally does in order to hold its pid.

## Current state, so this is not read as a defect report

The runner's signal arms were built and accepted on the ruling that each arm **probes its own reachability** and either asserts all four properties or reports UNREACHABLE naming the rule above. That is the right behaviour given the constraint. TERM is assertable and is asserted. INT is not, and says so.

## What this ticket asks for

One harness that runs `run-shell-suites.sh` **in the foreground of a pseudo-terminal** so a real SIGINT can be delivered to it and its disposition observed, usable from:

* a standalone run, and
* the in-hook environment, where the parent's disposition is the thing being worked around.

Candidate mechanisms, none chosen here: `script -q` (present on macOS and on Linux with different argument orders), a small `openpty`/`forkpty` helper, or Python's `pty` module driving the runner. The acceptance criterion is the discriminating one: **the same harness must give rc 130 on a foreground INT and must show the arm reporting UNREACHABLE when the signal is ignored on entry** - a harness that only ever produces one of those has not measured anything.

## Proposed tier

**Tier 2.** It is test-infrastructure with no runtime surface, but it is the only path to converting a standing UNREACHABLE into an assertion, and the rules above will otherwise be re-derived by whoever next touches the runner's signal handling.

## Board search before filing

Searched, over 479 open issues on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `pseudo-terminal`, `pseudoterminal`, `SIGINT`, `script -q`, `openpty`, `forkpty`, `PTY harness` - **0 open hits each**. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `run-shell-suites` returned **14**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Note for anyone re-running this search: the bare term `pty` is useless here - it is a substring of "empty" and returned **69** open hits on this corpus. Use a word boundary or a longer term.

Refs KS-1302

title: Nothing tells a PR author the 92-char squash-subject limit until a gate reads the PR — 3 of 4 titles over it in one round
description:
## BLUF

Three PR titles in one round exceeded the 92-character squash-subject limit, so the gate had to supply a subject for each. Raised as TITLE-99 (#1249, 99 chars), TITLE-93 (#1251, 93) and TITLE-94 (#1254, 94). Same defect three times in one round: **nothing tells an author the limit until a gate reads the PR.**

## Why it is worth recording rather than just doing better

The squash subject must be <= 92 chars and ASCII (MG-11). A PR title that breaks it is **not rejected anywhere** — not by GitHub, not by the pre-push hook, not by any local check. It surfaces only when a QA gate writes the merge addendum, at which point a human or a coordinator has to compose a replacement. The cost lands on the reviewer, one PR at a time, every time.

Measured this round: 3 of 4 titles over the limit, 93-99 chars. The two that were under it were under it by accident, not by check.

## Fix shapes (the reporter's proposals, not ratified)

1. A line in `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `DEV-PROCESS.md` stating the limit where authors look before opening a PR — cheapest, and catches nothing automatically.
2. A local check the author can run (a `scripts/` one-liner over `gh pr view --json title`) — catches it before the gate, still opt-in.
3. A pre-push or PR-body check — the only shape that cannot be skipped, and the most intrusive; it also does not apply cleanly, since the *title* is set after the push.

Shape 3 is noted for completeness and is probably wrong: the title is not knowable at push time. Shape 1 plus 2 is the realistic pair.

## Done when

- [ ] the 92-character limit is stated where a PR author will see it before opening the PR, **or** a check the author can run reports it, **or** a line records that supplying the subject at gate time is the accepted cost

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,307 issues (includeArchived) and 3,684 comments**: `TITLE-99` -> **0** · `92 chars` -> **0** · `squash subject` -> 2 open (KS-1294, the hook's own CI sentence; KS-871, an audit-log path) — **both read in full, neither is this**. **Searched those three terms, 0 open hits for this defect.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 10 hits, fires; `qqx7-fresh-control-never-written-anywhere` -> 0.

## Provenance

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1249`, non-blocking (N-1249-b, N-1251-a, N-1254-c), recorded at the merges of #1249, #1251 and #1254.

title: ks781 LEG F: a guard DEFINED but never called inside the parser continuation still reads guarded true (over-reports)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing limit of LEG F's guard walk, recorded by the tier-2 gate on PR #1248 (KS-1143 GF-2, merged `fa25c9b10fb4`). **A guard that is DEFINED but never CALLED inside the parser's continuation still reads** `guarded: true`**.**

This **over-reports**, which is the **unsafe** direction: the leg says something inspects the parsed body when nothing does. It is the same asymmetry KS-1143's own GF-1 was about, one step further in.

## Mechanism

GF-2 moved the walk's start from the whole wrapper body to the parser call's **continuation** — the function-valued arguments of the parser call. Inside that continuation the walk still hits on a **call node whose callee name is a known guard**. It does not establish that the call is reached: a guard call sitting in a branch that never executes, or bound and shadowed, is indistinguishable from one on the path.

Not introduced by #1248 — the predicate it replaced had the same property over a wider region, so GF-2 narrowed the region without changing this. Recorded so the remaining looseness has a name.

## Relationship to what is already open on KS-1143

KS-1143 stays In Progress for the **indirect-invocation false negative**, which is the *opposite* direction (under-reports: a continuation passed by NAME is not followed, so a genuinely mounted guard reads unguarded). **This one over-reports.** Two different directions, two different risks; they are not the same defect and should not be closed by one change without saying which each fix addresses.

## Done when

- [ ] a fixture where the guard call inside the continuation is unreachable reads `guarded: false`, **or**
- [ ] a line in the file records why reachability is deliberately out of scope for a text-level walk, so the limit is stated rather than latent

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,305 issues (includeArchived) and 3,677 comments**: `CONT-DEFERRED` -> 1 (KS-1143, this finding's own record) · `parserContinuations` -> **0** · `defined but never` -> 1 (KS-1143) · `never called` -> 17 total / 5 open, each read and none this subject (KS-1291 a stale comment, KS-1185, KS-843, KS-1143 itself). **Searched those four terms, 0 open hits for this defect.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 8 hits, fires; `zzz-nonexistent-token-l6-control` -> 0.

## Provenance

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1243`, non-blocking, recorded at the merge of #1248.

Refs KS-1143

title: readYaml routing cells: a multi-line import evades parserImportSites (prettier produces it), the loaders are unpinned, and the canary pays a child spawn per run
description:
## BLUF

Three non-blocking findings the tier-2 gate raised against PR #1243 (KS-1300 items 2-4, merged `a9ae94edbed3`). All three are cells in the same `readYaml` routing/canary family in `systemTest/performance`, so they are **one test pass** and one ticket, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule.

`Refs KS-1300` — this does **not** close it. KS-1300's own remaining item (READYAML-UNGATED: no gate runs this suite) is a different workload — wiring a suite into the hook or the preflight — and is deliberately left there rather than folded in here.

## The three items

1. **MULTILINE-IMPORT.** `parserImportSites()` reads four import positions — static at any indent, re-export, `require()`, dynamic `import()` — but each pattern is anchored per LINE. **A multi-line import is invisible**, and that is not hypothetical: this package's own prettier config wraps a long import across lines, so the formatter itself produces the evading shape. Measured at the merged tree: the guard's own positive control passes every single-line spelling and has no multi-line row.
2. **T2C-ROUTING-HOME.** The routing cells prove the SUITE does not import a parser directly. Nothing proves the **loaders** (`runner/config_loader.ts` and friends) reach `readYaml()` — the property the whole family exists for. The gate recorded this as homeless; this is its home.
3. **CANARY-IN-PACKAGE.** The retained canary spawns a `tsx` child to run the raw parse, because importing the parser into the suite would (correctly) trip the routing cell. That costs \~2.5 s of the suite's wall-clock. A cheaper in-package form — for example a child-free comparison against a captured raw-parse error — would keep the standing witness without the spawn.

## Done when

- [ ] `parserImportSites()` sees a multi-line parser import, with a positive-control row carrying the exact shape prettier produces
- [ ] a cell proves the loaders call `readYaml()`, so the property is pinned where it is actually relied on
- [ ] the canary keeps its guarantee without a per-run child spawn, or a line records why the spawn is the cheapest honest form

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,303 issues (includeArchived) and 3,677 comments**, titles + descriptions + comments: `MULTILINE-IMPORT` -> 1 (KS-1300, this finding's own record) · `T2C-ROUTING-HOME` -> 1 (same) · `CANARY-IN-PACKAGE` -> 1 (same) · `parserImportSites` -> 1 (same) · `readYamlRouting` -> 1 (same) · `multi-line import` -> 1 (same) · `multiline import` -> **0**. **Searched those seven terms, 0 open hits outside KS-1300 itself.** Controls: `readYaml` fires; a nonsense token -> 0.

## Provenance

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1243`, raised **non-blocking** against #1243 and recorded at the merge. Filed on the coordinator's instruction after the batch landed; it did not hold the merge.

Refs KS-1300

title: Nothing runs `tsc -p packages/shared` — the push preflight has no project type-check leg, so a type error is invisible (KS-872 acceptance, second half)
description:
## BLUF

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` is **not run by anything**. Not by the push preflight's fifteen legs, not by vitest (which does not type-check), not by any remaining CI. A type error in `packages/shared` is therefore red in `tsc` and **invisible everywhere the team actually looks**.

KS-872 was filed when exactly that happened: `crypto.JsonWebKey` vanished in `@types/node` 26.1.0 and the project tsc went red on develop with nobody noticing. That ticket's acceptance has two halves. The fix is one; **this is the other** — *"either the preflight gains a shared project type-check leg, or a ticket says explicitly why it should not."*

## Measured today (2026-09-25, at develop `6ab9d5021e96`)

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` exits **rc 0**, zero output, on a clean `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`. A planted `const x: number = 'not a number'` gives **rc 2 / TS2322**, and removing it returns rc 0 — so the check is live, and the original error genuinely does not reproduce.

**Why it is green is the point, and it is fragile.** `npm ci` NESTS `packages/shared/node_modules/@types/node@20.19.43` (the package declares `^20.11.5`) beside the hoisted `@types/node@26.1.0`. The nested 20.x still carries `crypto.JsonWebKey` at `crypto.d.ts:513`; in 26.1.0 that interface moved to `webcrypto.JsonWebKey` (`crypto.d.ts:3630`). **Nothing pins that nesting.** A hoist change, a dedupe, or a lockfile refresh can remove it, and the error returns — to a check that still nobody runs.

## Ask

Add a `packages/shared` project type-check leg to the push preflight (`.githooks/pre-push`), **or** record here why it should not exist. If it is added it needs a planted-error control, like every other leg — a type-check that cannot fail is the failure mode this ticket is about.

## Searched before filing

Six terms, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched on the title: `type-check leg` (50 fuzzy / **0** literal), `tsc` (50 / **12**), `preflight leg` (50 / **8**), `project type-check` (50 / **0**), `packages/shared tsc` (50 / **0**), `noEmit` (50 / **1**). **KS-872 itself has zero relations, zero inverse relations and zero children.**

Nearest, and all a different class:

* **KS-892** and **KS-933** — both *Duplicate/ARCHIVED* — say the project tsc is VACUOUS for `src/__tests__` because the tsconfig excludes it. That is *"the tsc does not cover enough"*, not *"no leg runs the tsc"*. Named rather than linked: archived issues refuse relations.
* **KS-1000 / KS-1122 / KS-848 / KS-1090** — the same excludes-`__tests__` class in auth, vc-issuer, kyc and api-gateway.
* **KS-910 / KS-1040** — preflight *leg* tickets, but legs 12 and 4.

**No open home; filed new.**

---

*Filed by Seat L3, 2026-09-25, on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER Q1b). Carries the second half of KS-872's acceptance;* `.githooks/` *is in no seat's lane this round.*

title: Lockfile edits move platform discriminators silently: an npm command inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the ROOT lock (0 version changes, 12 lines of dev/devOptional churn), and an isolated resolve on darwin/arm64 strips os/cpu/libc markers (26 entries from frontend/issuer, 30 libc lines from services/mcp-server incl. the musl markers node:24-alpine needs, 103 entries on a full root re-resolution) — cause side of KS-1154; push-gate leg PROPOSED for Kam
description:
## BLUF

Two measured hazards in how this repo's lockfiles get edited on a developer host. Both produced wrong bytes in a working tree on 2026-09-25 before a per-file check caught them; neither is visible in `git diff --numstat` as anything but a small diff.

**TRAP 1 — an npm command run inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the workspace ROOT lock, not the member's own lock.** `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*","services/*","frontend/*"]`, so `services/originate`, `services/mcp-server` and the frontends are members — while each also carries its own tracked standalone `package-lock.json`, which is what `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` reads (43 of the 45 tracked locks). Measured: `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` run **inside** `services/originate` left `services/originate/package-lock.json` **byte-unchanged** and instead rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 lines, eleven `lightningcss-*` platform binaries plus `magicast` flipping `devOptional` → `dev: true`, with **0 packages added, 0 removed, 0 version-changed**. `npm update @hono/node-server` inside `services/mcp-server` moved **nothing at all**. So the in-place route silently misses its target and dirties a file the change must not touch.

**TRAP 2 — resolving a standalone lock in an isolated copy STRIPS platform discriminators for every host but the one resolving.** The isolated route writes the right file, but re-resolves optional platform deps for the current host (Darwin/arm64) and drops the rest. Measured, same session, npm 11.5.1 / node 24.7.0:

| lock | collateral |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/issuer/package-lock.json` | **26 entries removed** — `emnapi/runtime` plus **25** `rollup/rollup-<platform>` **binaries** |
| `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` | 1 entry removed each |
| `services/mcp-server/package-lock.json` | **30 lines of** `libc` **blocks deleted** — ten `"libc": ["glibc"]` / `["musl"]` markers |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (full re-resolution) | **103 entries removed** — esbuild 75, rolldown 13, lightningcss 10, cbor-extract 5. **103 of 103 carry an** `os`**/**`cpu` **constraint; 0 do not.** |

**Every service Dockerfile is** `node:24-alpine`**, i.e. musl**, so removing a `"libc": ["musl"]` discriminator is not cosmetic. And the frontends are built in Linux containers, so removing `rollup-linux-*` breaks their build.

*(npm scope sigils are omitted above —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

## Relation to KS-1154 — read both; they are cause and symptom

**KS-1154** (Backlog) is *"Root package-lock.json carries only rollup-darwin-arm64 — npm ci on ubuntu installs no Linux rollup binary…"*. That is **one symptom**: a binary already absent from the root lock. This ticket is the **mechanism that keeps removing them**, in both directions and across every lock, plus TRAP 1, which KS-1154 does not mention at all.

KS-1154's own "Ancestors" paragraph states the link in its own words: *"The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it."* Its ancestors KS-653 and KS-376 (both Done, archived) are the two earlier recurrences. KS-1154's guard proposal is a **lockfile cell pinning the rollup set**; this ticket's proposal below is a **push-gate leg covering every discriminator in every lock**, which would have caught all three past recurrences and this one.

**Not a duplicate, and KS-1154 should not be closed by this:** KS-1154 has its own "Done when" (add `rollup-linux-x64-gnu`, green the advisory job's step 6). This ticket does not add that binary.

## The proven workaround, in use now

Both scripts live at `5_Project_History/2026-09-25_seatB-25th/raise/` and were used to build the KS-530 and KS-528 lock changes:

* `lockresolve21.sh` — copies a member's two manifests into an isolated dir **outside every workspace**, resolves there, copies the lock back. Fixes TRAP 1. Its header carries the measurement.
* `splice_lock21.py` — takes **only** the named packages' entries from npm's own output (authoritative `version` / `resolved` / `integrity` / inner pins) and splices them into the pristine lock; every other byte stays pristine. Fixes TRAP 2. It refuses if the two locks hold different keys for those packages.

Result on the two PRs built with them: **added 0 / removed 0 / version-changed N** in every lock touched, and `libc` / `os` / `cpu` / `devOptional` counts identical before and after in all seven files.

## PROPOSAL — needs Kam, not this ticket's author

**A push-gate leg: a lockfile change must not move a platform discriminator.** Per changed `package-lock.json`, compare the before/after count of `os`, `cpu`, `libc` and `devOptional` markers; refuse the push on any delta that the change does not declare. **This is a gate change, so it is Kam's call** — recorded here as a proposal, not a decision, and deliberately not built. Evidence that it works: the check read `libc` **10 → 0** on the bad `services/mcp-server` lock and **10 → 10** after the splice. It is a guard that failed when it should have.

## What was searched before filing

The whole KS board, **1,279 issues including archived**, literal substring match on title + description for: `workspace member` (3 hits, none related), `package-lock` (36), `libc` (1 — KS-366, Done/archived, a currency review), `musl` (**0**), `os/cpu` (**0**), `optional binar` (4), `platform binar` (5), `rollup-` (1 — KS-1154), `esbuild` (13), `lightningcss` (**0**), `arborist` (**0**), `devOptional` (2), `lock-regen` (6), `package-lock-only` (9). Controls: `gate` matched **930** issues (the reader fires); a symbol that cannot exist matched **0** (it does not invent). **The only candidate was KS-1154**, related above.

## Also recorded from the same session

* A **full re-resolution of the root lock does not fix** either advisory pin it was tried for: `node_modules/ip-address` stays 9.0.5 and `@prisma/dev/node_modules/@hono/node-server` stays 1.19.11, with and without `overrides`. So a regen is not a fix and is destructive — see the 103-entry row above.
* `npm install --package-lock-only` is **inert for a version bump** on npm 11.5.1: it prints `up to date` and moves nothing. `npm update <pkg>` is what moves it. A command that reports success while doing nothing.
* Resolving a workspace root **from bare manifests with no** `node_modules` crashes npm: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` at `#loadPeerSet` (`@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1314`) — peer-dependency resolution, reproducible. With `node_modules` present it completes. Not a repo defect; a constraint on how any future measurement must be run.

## Done when

- [ ] `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` carries both traps and names the two scripts as the way to edit a lockfile
- [ ] the two scripts live somewhere durable in the repo rather than in one seat's record folder
- [ ] the push-gate leg is decided by Kam — built, or recorded as declined with the reason

title: Preflight's closing verdict says a run failed on the environment even when other legs failed for real
description:
## BLUF

When preflight leg 1 cannot run (no workspace install), the closing verdict tells the operator the failure is **"an environment condition, not a finding about your change"**, even when other legs failed for real. It was measured on 2026-09-17: at develop `d7e95cd9f`, legs 5 and 7 refused because the KS-769 fuse had lapsed, yet the last lines of the run led with the environment excuse. Only a trailing "Any OTHER failures above are real and still need fixing." hedged it. The defect predates the fuse PR: `preflight.sh` blob `28d3636c1` is identical before and after it.

## Recommendation

Print the environment verdict only when leg 1's missing install is the ONLY cause of the failure. Otherwise, name the legs that really failed first. Add a regression test: a stubbed run with leg 1 reporting DEPS MISSING plus a forced leg-7 exit 3 must end with a tail that names leg 7.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` at develop `f8c7aaa39`.
  * Line 96 sets `env_fail=0` and line 230 sets `env_fail=1` when leg 1 cannot run.
  * Lines 688-702 hold the closing branch. When `fail` is non-zero and `env_fail` is non-zero, it prints `PREFLIGHT FAILED — but leg 1 could not RUN: this working tree has no workspace install. That is an environment condition, not a finding about your change` and exits 1, whatever else failed.
  * This branch came in with KS-991 (Done, archived; cited here because Linear refuses a relation to an archived issue).
* **Measured** by the tier-2 QA gate on PR #1020 (2026-09-17), running the whole `preflight.sh` in fresh worktrees with no workspace install:
  * At base `d7e95cd9f`: leg 5 `FAIL — the audit-contract suites are red`, leg 7 `FAIL — the lock-advisory gate REFUSED to report a verdict`, and a tail headed by the environment verdict.
  * At head `71bd80a35`: legs 5 and 7 OK, and the same tail. The tail cannot tell the two runs apart, although one of them has real failures.
  * The gate's drafter reproduced it in an independent run.
* **Why it matters:** the verdict is read at the end of the output, and a reader skimming it is told the change is fine and the fix is `npm ci`. That is the reading the KS-991 wording was meant to prevent, pointed in the other direction.
* **Exit code is correct:** the run still exits 1, so nothing is let through. The defect is the explanation, not the gate.
* **Polish, same owner area (carried here, not a separate ticket):** `validateOutOfScope` in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/lock-discovery.mjs` (lines 255, 257 and 277 at `f8c7aaa39`) reports a PRESENT but malformed `expires` as `missing expires (not an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date: "soon")`. The word "missing" describes a value that is there. The gate measured it with `expires: 'soon'`. It is pre-existing.
* **Searched first** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):
  * `environment condition, not a finding`: 0 hits.
  * `leg 1 could not RUN`: 0 hits.
  * `env_fail`: 1 (KS-926, unrelated guard census).
  * `PREFLIGHT FAILED`: 6, none about this verdict.
  * `preflight.sh`: 39. The nearest are KS-813 (PREFLIGHT PASSED unconditional) and KS-1046 (pass verdict has no skip tally), both about the PASS verdict, not this one.
  * `KS-991`: 1.
  * `missing expires`: 0.
* **Not fixed here.** Filed from the #1020 gate as finding F2 (Minor), with R5 as the Polish line.

title: safeOutboundRequest tests: no cell pins DNS-layer classification, ks932 cells depend on 203.0.113.7 hanging, DNS timer left armed (KS-932 gate F-1/F-2/F-3/F-6)
description:
## BLUF

Test-quality follow-up to KS-932 (PR #1004, merged as `40fe4db69`). The fix is correct: the tier-1 QA gate measured **fail-open: NO**. But the tests around `safeOutboundRequest` leave four holes:

* **F-1 (Minor):** no cell pins DNS-layer classification. Under a tamper that skips classifying the raced lookup, the ks932 file stays 3/3 and the whole shared suite 842/842, while private answers reach a socket.
* **F-2 (Minor):** ks932 cells 2–3 rely on `203.0.113.7` hanging. They go red falsely, or green vacuously, on a host that refuses fast.
* **F-3:** a TS2345 in the new test file.
* **F-6:** the DNS timer stays armed when the race rejects.
  Plus two Polish docblock drifts (F-4, F-5). All in `packages/shared`, one logical path.

## Recommendation

One test pass on `packages/shared/src/security/ssrf-guard.ts` and its tests:

* add the DNS-classification regression cell (F-1), with a connect counter and a public positive control;
* give the ks932 cells a deterministic connect seam (F-2);
* fix the TS2345 (F-3);
* clear the DNS timer when the race rejects (F-6);
* bring the `blocked` and `timeoutMs` docblocks up to date (F-4, F-5).

## Detail

Source: tier-1 QA gate on PR #1004 at `6d077d3fe35cd5f3c09d394553d320e97b1abe32`, verdict 2026-09-16 13:43:51Z. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-16-ks932-1004-6d077d3fe-tier1-r1/report.md`. The findings, verbatim from its table:

| \# | title | evidence class | severity | target | SHIPS-WITH / TICKET | oracle |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| F-1 | `safeOutboundRequest`'s DNS-layer classification is pinned by no cell (TG: seat 3/3, whole 842/842 while private answers connect) | MEASURED AT RUNTIME | Minor | #1004's test file (the carried #873 Record (a), widened) | SHIPS-WITH; TICKET for the pin | Purpose; History |
| F-2 | ks932 cells 2–3 depend on `203.0.113.7` hanging: false red (cell 3) and vacuous green (cell 2, green under its own tamper) on a fast-RST network | MEASURED AT RUNTIME | Minor | #1004's test file | SHIPS-WITH | Purpose; Comparable (`ks914-shipped-path:112`) |
| F-3 | TS2345 at `ks932-timeout-bounds-dns.test.ts:49` (mock resolves an array into `Promise<{address,family}>`), invisible to vitest and to `tsc -p packages/shared` | MEASURED (including program + control) | Polish | #1004's test file | SHIPS-WITH | Statutes & standards |
| F-6 | the DNS timer stays armed for `timeoutMs` when the race rejects (clearTimeout sits after the await) | MEASURED AT RUNTIME (L-4, by handle) | Polish | #1004 | SHIPS-WITH | Product consistency |

Polish, carried here per Wednesday's ruling (not a separate ticket):

| \# | title | evidence class | severity | target | SHIPS-WITH / TICKET | oracle |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| F-4 | `blocked` docblocks `ssrf-guard.ts:421-425` and `:519-523` do not cover an unresolved or slow-resolving host, now reachable on a working-but-slow resolver | READ + MEASURED (C-1) | Polish | owner (pre-existing drift, made reachable by #1004) | SHIPS-WITH; TICKET | Claims |
| F-5 | `timeoutMs` docblock `:460-463` says "DNS-free" and the deadline error says "(connect, transfer and drain)" although DNS now spends the same budget | READ + MEASURED (B-1) | Polish | #1004 | SHIPS-WITH | Claims |

**F-1, the regression cell the gate describes (report section 7, verbatim):**

* **The regression cell the owner should add (prose):** in the ks932 file (or `ks914-shipped-path.test.ts`), mock `lookup` to answer `[{address:'10.0.0.5', family:4}]` for `https://rebind.example.com/x`, with a connect counter (or `https.request` spy). Assert `ok false`, `reason 'blocked'`, `error` matches `/resolves to 10\.0\.0\.5, which is forbidden/`, and **0 connects**. Pair it with the public positive control (`203.0.113.7` → exactly 1 connect, through the deterministic seam of §5). Under TG it reds (measured: my R-D 10.0.0.5 cell).

**F-2, the deterministic shape the gate describes (report section 5, verbatim):**

* **Deterministic shape the owner could adopt (prose; nothing written into their tree):**
  * Give the cells a connect seam instead of relying on the internet: a `net.Socket.prototype.connect` wrapper (or an injected agent) that redirects to a 127.0.0.1 listener which accepts and never answers. That makes the hang deterministic, as in F-2.
  * Assert cell 2's bound against `timeoutMs` plus a small margin.
  * Let the control accept the transport error the way `:112` does, or assert `/deadline/` only under the deterministic seam.
  * Count the connect in cell 2, so a vacuous RST cannot pass.

Dedupe before filing (seat A, 2026-09-16): literal matches over Linear `searchIssues` (archived and comments included), title + description + comments:

* `ssrf-guard`: 7 of 98 results (KS-1160, KS-485, KS-487, KS-678, KS-914, KS-927, KS-931);
* `safeOutboundRequest`: 10 of 10 (KS-1061, KS-1160, KS-485, KS-681, KS-914, KS-927, KS-928, KS-931, KS-932, KS-934).
  None is about DNS-layer classification coverage, the ks932 cells' network dependence, or the armed DNS timer. KS-914 (the rebind pin) is the nearest neighbour and a different defect. Filed new.

title: Root package-lock.json carries only rollup-darwin-arm64 — npm ci on ubuntu installs no Linux rollup binary, so frontend/demo-overlay and frontend/outlook-addin die at vite build (npm/cli#4828); the advisory workspace-suites job stays red at step 6 on every PR until the lock carries rollup-linux-x64-gnu
description:
## BLUF

*(npm scope sigils are omitted throughout —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` records exactly ONE rollup platform binary — `node_modules/rollup/rollup-darwin-arm64` (the lock was generated on macOS arm64); `rollup-linux-x64-gnu` appears only inside an `optionalDependencies` list (lock line 19376), never as an installed entry. So `npm ci` on `ubuntu-latest` installs no Linux rollup binary, and the two vite-6 frontends — `frontend/demo-overlay` and `frontend/outlook-addin` (rollup 4.60.4) — die at `vite build` with `Error: Cannot find module … rollup-linux-x64-gnu`. Upstream: npm/cli#4828 (npm's optional-platform-dependency flaw). Measured live by the L9 gate on PR #887's advisory job (`pr` run 34786655660 / job 103803259738, step 6): the four vite-8 frontends (rolldown) and all 26 service/package builds green; these two red. **Consequence:** `pr-platform-suites.yml`'s `Workspace unit suites (advisory, non-blocking)` job stays red at step 6 on EVERY PR until the lockfile carries `rollup-linux-x64-gnu` — advisory, blocks nothing, but the job cannot say anything useful until then. A macOS pass is not runner evidence for this job.

The gate's TICKET line, verbatim: *"the rollup-linux-x64-gnu lockfile matter — Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json -> node_modules/rollup/rollup-* (only rollup-darwin-arm64 installed; rollup-linux-x64-gnu only in an optionalDependencies list at :19376); frontend/demo-overlay, frontend/outlook-addin; pr-platform-suites.yml workspace-suites step 6; npm/cli#4828 — a KS or KS-1148 (c)."*

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-L9-940-941-942-887-ks1075-1077-1078-961-tier2-r1/report.md` (§2 the live job; §4b(iv) the mechanism — `git grep -o -E '"node_modules/rollup/rollup-[a-z0-9-]+"' 3aee3deed -- Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` → `rollup-darwin-arm64` only; findings register R-4). First recorded by s215 as an adjacent finding in KS-1148's comment (2026-09-13T22:32Z): "a DIFFERENT class from (a)/(b), so not added to the checklist".

**Why its own ticket, not KS-1148 (c):** KS-1148's class is *the runner never installs or builds* — its fix is an install/build step per job. This job DOES install and build; the defect is the lock's CONTENT, and `npm ci` on Linux cannot install a binary the lock does not carry. One fix, one file, a different owner's action — the 2026-09-07 one-ticket-per-fix rule. Related: KS-1148 (the runner-gap class this was first noted under), KS-961 (#887, the advisory job that surfaces it).

**Ancestors (archived — named, not related):** KS-653 (Done — root-workspace `npm run build` broken for 5 of 6 vite frontends: the same npm/cli#4828 class on rolldown's `darwin-arm64` binding; fixed by regenerating the root lock's optional native bindings) and KS-376 (Done — the esbuild platform-binary subtree inconsistent in the same lock, same class). The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it.

## Fix shape (the builder's call)

* Make the root lock carry ALL rollup platform binaries (as it once did for esbuild's 25/26 variants): a lock regeneration that records every `rollup/rollup-*` optional binary (npm ≥ 10 records all platforms when run with `--package-lock-only` from a clean state; or add `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` as an explicit optionalDependency at the root so the lock pins it), then verify on a Linux `npm ci` (the advisory job itself is the instrument: step 6 green for `demo-overlay` and `outlook-addin`).
* Regression guard: a lockfile cell that asserts the `rollup/rollup-*` entry set covers `darwin-arm64` AND `linux-x64-gnu` (the two hosts that build this repo), so a future macOS regen cannot drop the Linux binary silently.

## Done when

- [ ] `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` carries `node_modules/rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` (and keeps `rollup-darwin-arm64`)
- [ ] `pr-platform-suites.yml` `Workspace unit suites` step 6 builds `frontend/demo-overlay` and `frontend/outlook-addin` green on a Linux runner (read from the live job at the fixing PR's head)
- [ ] a guard cell pins the platform-binary set, red-first on the current lock

title: The push preflight has no `services/auth` unit-suite leg — 14 `step` legs, 0 hits for services/auth or vitest; a merge that reddens auth's vitest passes the preflight (the F-973-1 class)
description:
## BLUF

A gap, not a fix: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (blob `acfb7fa3e` at develop M15 `1c38077ba`, 521 lines) runs 14 `step` legs and none of them runs a service's unit suite — `services/auth` 0 hits, `vitest` 0 hits, `services/originate` 0 hits (controls: `step` 20 hits). So a commit that turns `services/auth`'s vitest red still prints `PREFLIGHT PASSED.` and pushes. The tier-1 gate on PR #973 (KS-950 / KS-962) found the auth suite's red-first pair (`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:344` and `:382`, 2 failed of 30 against M6's `startup-migrations.ts`) by running the suite itself; nothing in the push path would have. Same class as KS-1051 (develop RED on the originate jest suite and nothing catches it) and KS-1046 (the verdict has no skip accounting); this ticket names the auth instance and the cross-service-reader shape that makes it bite. One ticket, one leg.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks950-962-973-ca2a9109c-tier1-r2/report.md` — §2 F-973-1 (the red-first pair), §11 the cross-service reader class ("the preflight … 14 `step` legs, 0 hits for `services/auth` … has no auth-vitest leg"), CLOSING 6.

## The shape that makes it bite

* `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` reads ANOTHER service's source text (`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, `:376` and `:380-382`) and pins that the gateway seeds no user row. A change to the gateway file alone can red the auth suite — a red no per-service run of "the touched service's tests" sees, and no preflight leg runs either.
* The preflight's 14 legs at M15 (`:99` … `:423`): spec drift, lockfile clean-room, spec-auth conformance, path resolvability, audit-contract suites, npm-audit gate, standalone-lock advisories, served-spec consistency, no tracked credentials, script modes, pinned actions, shell suites reached, runtime stage re-link, shell suites run. None invokes `npx vitest run` or `jest` for any service.

## Ask

Decide whether a service unit-suite leg belongs in the preflight (auth first, since it is the service whose suite reads across services), or whether the merge gate stays the only instrument — and say which in the KS-1046 / KS-1051 write-up. Not a fix to build blind: the preflight already runs minutes per push (KS-1135, KS-1127 are its runner-level neighbours).

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over the KS board, title + description, includeArchived (s211 ITEM 0 (g)): `auth vitest` 0 · `auth-vitest` 0 · `preflight leg` 24 · `preflight.sh` 21 · `step(` 2 (KS-813 — "PREFLIGHT PASSED is unconditional, step() only prints a banner", a neighbour; KS-525 — Playwright's test.step) · `services/auth` 112 (a page; none by title a preflight-leg ticket). Of the 45 preflight hits none names `services/auth` together with `vitest`; KS-1051 is the nearest neighbour (a service suite with no gate), KS-1046 the class parent, KS-813 the verdict-side neighbour. Filed new; related KS-1046 + KS-1051.

title: ks949 suite coverage (KS-950 / KS-962, #973): ID3's capture half has no size assertion (`WHERE false` in both captures reads 27/27), and a one-arm `IS DISTINCT FROM` guard is invisible to the suite (Tg3 0 red)
description:
## BLUF

PR #973 (KS-950 + KS-962, round 2 of 2, GO WITH FINDINGS 0/0/0 at `ca2a9109c`, merged 2026-09-13 by the merge seat s211) shipped the real-PostgreSQL suite `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh` (27 cells) and the two-arm `IS DISTINCT FROM` re-sync guard in `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:1043`. The tier-1 gate's two coverage NOTES (CN-1, CN-2) are the suite's blind spots, not defects in the product: everything shipped; nothing here blocks anything. One file, one test pass; the builder's call on both fix shapes, which are the gate's PROPOSALS, not ratified.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks950-962-973-ca2a9109c-tier1-r2/report.md` — §0 BLUF (the two coverage NOTES), §4 the tamper table (Tg3 and Ti rows), §6 the R5 control. Line numbers at `ca2a9109c` = develop after the squash.

## Items (one test pass)

1. **CN-1 — ID3's capture half has no size assertion.** ID3 (`:304-318`) pins the guard on two things only the guard changes: the command tag and `updated_at`. Its `updated_at` capture runs twice — `UPD_B` at `:308` and `UPD_A` at `:310` — and the cell compares the two lists. With `WHERE false` planted in BOTH captures (SNAP `:261` untouched; the gate's Ti tamper on a scratch copy), ID3 reads GREEN and the suite `27 passed, 0 failed (of 27 cells)`, with the instrument line `UPD_B captured lines: 0  UPD_A: 0` (control copy on the real WHERE: `12  12`). Two empty lists are identical, so the cell cannot tell "nothing moved" from "nothing was captured". **Proposal (the gate's):** after `:310`, fold `[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$UPD_B" | grep -c .)" = 12 ]` into ID3's condition, so a capture that returns fewer than the 12 ids reds the cell.
2. **CN-2 — a one-arm guard is invisible to the suite.** With the slug arm deleted from the guard at `:1043` (`AND (u.tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM v.tenant_id::uuid)` only — the gate's Tg3, marker 1→0) the suite reads `27 passed, 0 failed`, ID3 `UPDATE 0`: AG4 plants drift on BOTH columns, so either arm alone repairs its fixture. The gate's own R5 control shows the miss is real: on a fresh slug-ONLY drift the id-arm-only statement reads `UPDATE 0` (the drift stays), where the shipped two-arm statement reads `UPDATE 1` (repaired). **Proposal (the gate's):** an AG cell that plants slug-only drift on a second id (`c1…0001` → `slug-only-drift`), asserts `UPDATE 1` and the slug restored — reds under Tg3, green at head.
3. For context (no change asked): the guard's WHY comment and the two-arm statement are correct as shipped (R2 `UPDATE 0` with all 17 rows byte-identical; R3 `UPDATE 1` with exactly 1 of 12 `updated_at` moved; R7 `UPDATE 0` on the no-change boot — the gate's rows, its own socket-only instance).

By symbol over the KS board, title + description, includeArchived (s211 ITEM 0 (g)): `ID3` 0 · `AG4` 0 · `UPD_B` 0 · `slug-only` 0 · `ks949_main_seed_idempotence` 2 (KS-1127 — the runner counting an exit-0 SKIP as passed, another subject; KS-962 — the parent, the suite's history) · `IS DISTINCT FROM` 3 (KS-542, KS-294, KS-275, all archived — each the English "is distinct from", not the operator). No home for a coverage cell; filed new. KS-1127 and KS-1135 are the runner-level neighbours of this suite (named, not related).

title: ks781 LEG F guard walk: a MENTION of a guard-bound local reads as a mount (`:2318`) — `void controlByteGuard; next();` leaves 19 admin routes `{ 19, true }`; and guard-BEFORE-parser reads `guarded: true` (no order predicate)
description:
## BLUF

PR #981 (KS-828 + KS-900, merged 2026-09-13) gave LEG F sight of the control-byte guard LEAVING a wrapped router (`{ routes, guarded }` per router module) and closed KS-828's T3 (`admin.ts:560` `controlByteGuard(req, res, next);` → `next();` now reds LEG F). The tier-2 gate measured two ways the new predicate still blesses an unguarded parser — both MEASURED AT RUNTIME, both the ticket's own class (KS-828's T3 is one token away from GF-1). GF-1 was DISCLOSED by the builder (PR body: "the same looseness the parser reach already has … stated rather than widened here") — a disclosed limit is still the limit, and this one errs in the UNSAFE direction (the parser-side mention at `:2293` over-reports, R-1). Fix shapes are the GATE'S PROPOSALS, not ratified. One file, one test pass.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks828-900-981-04807ea0e-tier2-r1/report.md` — §6 GF-1, GF-2, Records R-1; §4 Tg1, Tg-ORDER. Line numbers at `04807ea0e` = develop after the squash.

## Items (one test pass)

1. **GF-1 (Minor) — a guard MENTION counts as a guard mount.** `routerParserAnalysis` `:2318` `if (ts.isIdentifier(m) && (guardSyms.has(m.text) || guardedWrappers.has(m.text))) { hit = true; return; }`. Repro at `04807ea0e`: `admin.ts:560` `controlByteGuard(req, res, next);` → `void controlByteGuard; next();` (anchor count 1) → `npx vitest run src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` in `packages/shared` → `Tests 231 passed (231)`; LEG F reads admin.ts `{ 19, true }` with the guard never invoked on 19 parsing routes. Fixture forms: W2's `g(req, res, next)` → `void g; next()` stays GREEN; a scratch cell with `const _ = g; next();` → `{ 2, true }`. Oracle: the file's own docblocks `:2307-2308` / `:2485-2488` ("a guard MENTIONED is not a guard MOUNTED") and the LEG F message `:2463-2464` ("`false` means the parser runs and nothing after it inspects the body"). **Proposal:** hit only on a CALL node — `ts.isCallExpression(m) && ts.isIdentifier(m.expression) && (guardSyms.has(m.expression.text) || guardedWrappers.has(m.expression.text))` (or a `guardCallName(m, b)` helper). Regression cells: the `void g; next();` fixture must read `{ 2, false }`; the admin.ts `void controlByteGuard; next();` form must red LEG F.
2. **GF-2 (Minor, borderline Record — Wednesday rates) — guard BEFORE parser reads** `guarded: true`**.** Fixture P7 (exactly `wrapperModule`'s shape with the body `g(req, res, () => raw(req, res, next));`) → `{"routes":2,"guarded":true}` — the guard inspects an unparsed `req.body`, the KS-800 class in the file's own name ("body-parser ORDER"). Not a regression against the parent (which saw no guard at all), but the LEG F message defines `true` as "something after the parser inspects the body", and this shape is `true` with nothing after the parser. **Proposal:** start the guard walk from the parser call's callback argument (`raw(req, res, cb)` → walk `cb`), not from the whole wrapper body. Regression: P7's fixture reads `false`; W2/W3 still `true`.
3. **R-1, for context (no change asked):** `:2293` `ts.isIdentifier(m) && syms.has(m.text)` — a MENTION of a parser-bound local admits a wrapper (P8 `void raw; next()` → `{ 2, false }`): pre-existing (KS-816), over-reports, SAFE direction. Whether item 1's fix should also tighten `:2293` is the builder's call; the asymmetry (safe on the parser side, unsafe on the guard side) is why the guard side is the item.

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over 1,131 KS issues + 908 comments (includeArchived): `controlByteGuard` → KS-828 only (its own disclosure); `guardSyms` 0; `guardedWrappers` 0; `routerParserAnalysis` 0; `ks781-p3-3` → 12 hits, none on the guard-walk predicate (KS-802 the parser regex; KS-905 the IIFE clause; KS-953 line pins; KS-831 archived, the KS-800 guard-side ticket where LEG F was born — named, not related). No home; filed new.

title: run-shell-suites.sh restores git discovery but does not isolate suites: a suite that runs git from its cwd writes the repository it runs in (KS-1086 QA-6)
description:
## BLUF

* **The boundary.** KS-1086's fix (PR #953) clears the hook's repository-local git variables before the shell suites run. A suite's `git` calls then fall back to normal discovery. That restores discovery; it does not isolate.
* **The consequence.** A suite that runs `git` from its working directory, without first moving into a temp repo of its own, still writes to whichever repository it started in. Under a push, that is the pushing repository.
* **Today, no current suite does this.** All 18 ran under the fixed runner from a linked worktree, and the shared config, refs and HEADs came out identical. This is a boundary for a future suite, not a live defect.

## Recommendation

Low priority. Decide whether the runner should enforce isolation, or whether the fixture convention is enough.

The gate named two fix shapes:

* run each suite with its cwd in a fresh temp dir;
* or have the runner snapshot its own repo's config, refs and HEADs around the loop, and fail loudly on any change.

The second overlaps KS-948's proposed runner-level check that a suite run left nothing behind, so one change could close both. This is filing only; nothing is scheduled.

## Detail

**Source.** Tier-1 QA gate on PR #953 @ `de1ab62c0`, finding QA-6 (Observation), arm M3. MEASURED in scratch repositories.

* The suite was `git config qa.cwdplant 1` with no `cd`, run under the head runner from a linked worktree.
* It saw `GIT_DIR=unset`, with a cwd of `<worktree>/Blockchain/Dev`.
* The shared config gained `[qa] cwdplant = 1`.

**Current suites.** Gate arm F2 ran all 18 real suites under the head runner from a linked worktree. Shared config, refs, main HEAD and worktree HEADs were IDENTICAL.

**Scope, reasoned from the mechanism and NOT run:** the same would happen from a normal clone, and from a manual `npm run test:shell`.

**Where.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`, in the suite loop (`bash "$REPO_ROOT/$rel"`). Each suite starts in the runner's own cwd.

**Board searched before filing.** The issue columns search title and description, archived included; the comment column searches comment bodies.

| term | issues | comments on |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `run-shell-suites` | KS-1086, KS-1046, KS-948, KS-926, KS-910, KS-903 | KS-1027, KS-1086, KS-909, KS-926, KS-936, KS-945, KS-948 |
| `run_shell_suites` | KS-1086, KS-971 | KS-1086, KS-731 |
| `git_local_env` | 0 | 0 |
| `local-env-vars` | 0 | 0 |
| `suite isolation` | 0 | 0 |
| `temp dir` | PS-529 | KS-1027, KS-682 |
| control: `leg 14` | KS-1086 | KS-1086, KS-485, KS-731, KS-772, KS-926 |

None of them covers a suite writing the repository it runs in through a cwd-relative `git` call. Two are adjacent but do not cover it:

* **KS-948:** a backtick in a case name executes as a command. Its fix shape includes a runner-level left-nothing-behind check.
* **KS-903:** a survey of repo-root derivations, including the env-dependent ones.

**Report.** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1086-953-de1ab62c0-tier1/report.md`

title: Launcher preflight: four findings — a concurrent seat clobbers the warnings file, KS-907 miscounts sessions, F-02 names a missing key, rule 7 still says extranet
description:
## BLUF

Four defects in `Launch_Claude.command`. **This ticket files them; it does not fix them.** None blocks a session today. Each one either loses a boot warning, misreports seat state, or tells a seat to do something wrong.

1. **The warnings file is one file per project, so a second seat's launch overwrites the first seat's warnings.** Measured by s172 on 2026-09-11: s173's launch at 07:11:31 overwrote s172's at 07:11:14, 17 s apart, and s172's own warnings were lost.
2. **The KS-907 seat registry counted a session running in** `Testing Agent MAIN` **as "a live session on this project".** Measured by s173 on 2026-09-11. The mechanism is not verified.
3. **The F-02 remedy tells the operator to** `ssh-add ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` **— a file that does not exist on this machine.** git works regardless, through the repo-local `core.sshCommand` → `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw`.
4. **Launch-prompt rule 7 still prescribes "an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment".** That contradicts Kam's 2026-09-05 ruling that everything goes through the tickets. The project `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was corrected on 2026-09-11; the launcher was not.

A fifth finding already has a home: the SessionStart hook still tells every seat to `POST /api/seen`. That is **KS-925**, and the evidence is added there.

## Recommendation

Fix all four in the **master launcher template** as well as this copy. Per the launcher notes, `Launch_Claude.command` is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing one copy fixes no other project. One pass proves all four:

* launch two seats about 10 s apart and check both warnings survive;
* run with a non-Blockchain Claude session alive and check it is not counted;
* read the F-02 text against `ls`;
* grep the assembled boot prompt for `extranet to-do` and expect 0.

## Detail

**1 — clobbered warnings file.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:90` writes `PREFLIGHT_LOG="$PROJECT_DIR/4_Credentials/.launch_preflight_last.txt"`, one path per project. The boot prompt then tells the seat to relay that file verbatim (`:392`).
* s172 (PID 64454, launched 07:11:14 AEST) read a file stamped `# launch 2026-09-10T21:11:31Z`, which is s173's launch.
* In that file, the KS-907 line listed s172's own PID as an "other" seat.
* Control from s176 today: the stamp `2026-09-10T22:36:54Z` equals `ps -o lstart= -p $PPID`. The file is not always clobbered — only when two launches race.
* Workaround in use: compare the stamp with your own start before relaying the warnings.

**2 — KS-907 miscount.**

* s173 attributed one of the two "other live sessions" in its KS-907 line to the fleet QA agent, by its cwd (`Testing Agent MAIN`).
* The registry lives at `Launch_Claude.command:244-379`. It reads `ps -eo pid=,command=` at `:328`.
* Not re-measured here, and which predicate matched is not verified.

**3 — F-02 names a missing key.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:107`, `:133` and `:138` all say `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw`.
* On this machine (s176, 2026-09-11 ~23:3xZ), `ls ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` → `No such file or directory`.
* `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw` is present, and `git fetch` returned rc 0 through `core.sshCommand` while the F-02 warning was showing.

**4 — rule 7.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:476` says: *"notify Stuart AND Peter — an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment @-mentioning them"*.
* Kam, 2026-09-05 13:55, verbatim: *"The team is not using the extranet much. I mentioned this yesterday. If anything needs to be escalated, please tell me and I'll send a WhatsApp message. Otherwise, everything has to be done through the tickets."*
* The project-root `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was rewritten to "on the tickets only" by s176 on 2026-09-11, as ruled by Wednesday. The pre-edit copy is in `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-11-s176/`.

**Searched before filing:**

* `launch_preflight_last` — 14 KS hits. KS-907 and KS-911 name the file only as test hygiene ("every run overwrites it"); none covers the clobber.
* `secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` — no launcher ticket.
* `extranet-session-check` and `api/seen` — found **KS-925**, which is finding 5, so it is not duplicated here.
* `Launch_Claude.command` — KS-907, KS-925, KS-655, KS-911, KS-912, KS-681, KS-78; none covers these four.
* Control: `KS-907` → 1 hit.

Filed by s176. Findings 1 and 2 are other seats' measurements, credited above. Findings 3 and 4 were re-measured at source by s176.

title: A PR's Test Evidence must state whether the preflight RAN — the hook skips systemTest/docs/vault-only pushes and emits nothing at all
description:
## The ask

**A PR's Test Evidence block must state whether the preflight gate RAN.** One line:

```
preflight: 13/13 legs ran
preflight: NOT RUN (systemTest-only push — skipped by design)
```

⚠ **Scope, explicitly: this is about the RECORD, not the FLOW.** Do **not** change `.githooks/pre-push`'s skip behaviour. Skipping cheap pushes (vault-only / docs-only / systemTest-only) is a deliberate workflow property that keeps the hook out of the way, and changing it would land on Peter and Stuart without either being asked. **Additive only.**

## The defect

`.githooks/pre-push` *"skips instantly for vault-only / docs-only / systemTest-only pushes"*. When it skips it emits **zero** `[pre-push]` lines — no SKIP notice, nothing.

So for those PRs the natural reading — *"it was pushed, therefore the preflight passed"* — is **wrong**, and nothing in the PR says so. **The only thing that made PR #927 honest was the author volunteering it. A property that holds because the author remembered is not a property.**

The exposure is a client human's assumption: **Peter reads PRs personally**, and the assumption is wrong for every systemTest-only, docs-only and vault-only PR.

## Evidence — CORRECTED 2026-09-09, see below for what was withdrawn

**1. The hook executed directly, the way git invokes it** (ref line on stdin), in the ks1027 worktree:

```
printf 'refs/heads/… <local> refs/heads/… <remote>' | bash .githooks/pre-push origin <url>
  → ZERO output, exit 0
```

**2. The decisive predicate, recomputable by anyone** — files changed against the merge-base with `origin/develop`, matched against the hook's `^Blockchain/Dev/` test:

```
ks1027 (#927)  2 files, both systemTest/__tests__/*.sh        matches: 0  → hook SKIPS, silently
ks927  (#926)  services/originate/.../*.test.ts               matches: 1  → hook RUNS
ks950  (#928)  services/api-gateway/startup-migrations.ts     matches: 1  → hook RUNS
```

The two neighbouring cases are the control: the same instrument distinguishes a skip from a run, so the ks1027 zero is a real skip and not a blind test.

## 🔴 WITHDRAWN — the original evidence line, and why it is worth leaving visible

This ticket first cited: *"Measured on PR #927:* `grep -c -i preflight` *over the full push output = 0."*

**That zero was mine, not the hook's.** The push had been run as `git push … 2>&1 | tail -5`, which **discarded the hook's output before it was grepped.** The absence measured was one the filer had created. The finding was right; the provenance was not, and it has been replaced above rather than quietly patched.

🔑 **This ticket's own thesis, demonstrated on its own filer.** The claim here is that *an absent gate-signal is indistinguishable from a present one that nobody notices*. **The filer could not tell "the hook skipped" from "I truncated the output" by reading the record — hours after writing it.** If the argument above is ever doubted, that is the strongest thing in the ticket.

## Suggested fix (shape, not detail)

Additive, in the PR template / evidence convention rather than in the hook:

* The evidence block carries a **preflight line, always** — the ratio when it ran, or `NOT RUN` plus the reason when the hook skipped.
* Optionally the hook could print one line when it skips (`[pre-push] skipped — systemTest-only push; the preflight gate did not run`) so the operator has something to paste. **Additive output, not a change to what the hook gates.**

## What is NOT established

* **No measurement that anyone has actually been misled.** Filed on the exposure, not on an observed incident — say it that way if it is quoted.
* Whether **docs-only** and **vault-only** pushes behave identically. **Not measured** — only the systemTest-only case was executed. The hook's own comment groups all three, which is a reason to expect it, not evidence of it.

Filed by s161 on Wednesday's ruling, 2026-09-09. Related to KS-1046 and PR #927.

title: The review-stream overlay covers 57 of 114 active tickets, and DEV-PROCESS still says 'nothing left over'
description:
## BLUF

**The review-stream overlay Kam adopted on 2026-09-03 now covers exactly half the board, and** `DEV-PROCESS.md` **still says it covers all of it.** A handover organised by stream today silently omits **22 of the 32** PR-bearing tickets.

## Measured, 2026-09-09

`DEV-PROCESS.md` §*The four review streams, built 2026-09-03* states:

> All **97** active Platform K tickets now sit under four parents — 40 + 19 + 18 + 20, nothing left over

The doc's per-parent figures (40/19/18/20) do not match any parent's current child count either.

## Why it bites right now

Building the review blocks for Kam's handover, **22 of the 32 tickets that carry an open PR have no stream parent** — including every one of today's ready items: KS-926, KS-963, KS-968, KS-991, KS-992, KS-993, KS-1026, KS-936, KS-942, KS-945, KS-961, KS-909, KS-931, KS-791, KS-798/799/841, KS-764, KS-682, KS-971, KS-229, KS-1004.

The rule in the same doc is *"Every new K-side ticket that reaches Todo is parented into one of the four"*. That step is not happening — and nothing fails when it is skipped, which is why it went unnoticed for six days. **Same family as KS-926: a rule with no check behind it.**

⚠ There is also a **discoverability trap in the doc's own shape**: three parents are findable by title (`Review stream: …`) but the fourth, **KS-485**, is titled *"Security review — plan, methodology & handover (Platform K)"*. A title search for review-stream parents returns **3 of 4**. This session hit exactly that and only caught KS-485 by reading DEV-PROCESS.

## Checklist

- [ ] Parent the 22 PR-bearing tickets into their stream (placement already derived per-PR in the s159 review-block report — reuse it rather than re-deriving)
- [ ] Sweep the remaining unparented active tickets (52 total with no parent)
- [ ] Correct the counts in `DEV-PROCESS.md` §*The four review streams* — or, better, stop hardcoding a number that decays and point at a query
- [ ] Rename KS-485 so all four parents are findable by title, **or** name all four explicitly in the doc so a title search is not the discovery path
- [ ] Decide where the check lives so an unparented Todo cannot sit unnoticed — the board equivalent of KS-926's census

Linear GraphQL, team KS, `state.type in (started, unstarted)`, direct `parent` field. PR->ticket map from the 43 open PRs. Measured 2026-09-09 by the Platform K s159 seat.

title: The merge gate cannot see a WITHDRAWN approval — #813 reads approved+clean against the reviewer's written refusal
description:
## BLUF

**A reviewer can withdraw an approval and BOTH GitHub instruments keep reporting the PR as approved.** The repo's merge gate is *"approval is the signal, the author merges"* (CLAUDE.md, Kam 2026-08-25). On PR #813 that gate currently reads GREEN against the reviewer's explicit written refusal.

## The instance

Peter, on #813 (KS-791, verify-file):

* **14:52:21Z 2026-09-08** — submitted `APPROVED` at `54225cbbd`
* **14:56:21Z 2026-09-08** — submitted `COMMENTED` at the same commit: *"My earlier approval on this PR was premature and I'm withdrawing it — I'll ask a maintainer to dismiss it, since I can't retract it myself."*

Nobody dismissed it. Measured today:

| instrument | reads #813 as |
| -- | -- |
| `GET /pulls/813/reviews` | `PeterObeden: APPROVED`, `commit_id == head.sha` -> **at-head approval** |
| search index `is:pr is:open review:approved` | **matches #813** |
| `mergeable_state` | `clean` |
| Peter's own prose | **withdrawn, holding for complete systemTest evidence** |

`commit_id == head.sha` **does not catch this.** That discriminator exists for a *stale* approval — one the head moved past. A **withdrawn** approval sits at the head, because the head never moved. The check we rely on is blind to it by construction.

## It is not a one-off — swept, with the arithmetic closed

Across all **43** open PRs, exactly **two** carry an `APPROVED` later followed by a `COMMENTED` review from the same reviewer: **#813** and **#785**. Both comment bodies say *"holding"*. No others.

* **#785** (KS-229) — also holding; there the last `APPROVED` sits at a **superseded** commit, so the `commit_id` check *does* catch it — but the **search index still counts it approved**.
* So the index's headline **"10 approved"** is really **8**.

## Why it matters

A withdrawn approval is invisible to every automated read of this repo's merge gate. The only instrument that sees it is the reviewer's prose. Any session — human or agent — that clears the queue by "approved + clean" will merge #813 against a written refusal.

## Checklist

- [ ] Ask a maintainer to **dismiss** the stale `APPROVED` on #813 (Peter asked for this on 2026-09-08 and it has not happened)
- [ ] Same for #785's superseded approvals
- [ ] Add the withdrawn-approval case to the boot/pre-merge sweep: an `APPROVED` is only live if **no later review from the same user exists at or after it** — not merely `commit_id == head.sha`
- [ ] Write the rule into `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` next to the existing at-head paragraph, which currently names only staleness as the failure mode
- [ ] Decide whether a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` should be the house convention for withdrawal, since GitHub gives a reviewer no retract action

## Provenance

`/pulls/{n}/reviews` for all 43 open PRs + `search/issues` index counts (10 approved / 2 changes_requested / 30 none = 42 open at sweep time, +#918 opened during the session = 43). Measured 2026-09-09 by the Platform K s159 seat.
