title: KS-930 round-2 gate residue: the guard and its suite write three claims that are false and cannot notice — a census wrong at every SHA, a clause that cannot fail, and a CONTROL that does not control
description:
**BLUF** — the KS-930 round-2 tier-1 gate raised three defects that are not about what the guard *does* but about what its own artefacts *say*. They are one logical path: **a suite and a guard that write claims which are false, and cannot notice.** Kam ruled round 3 regression-only, so these were deliberately left; this ticket carries them with the gate's evidence so nobody re-derives it.

All three were measured by the gate at head `3047bcb1dd852561d8ae3267b02f0056f881c999`. Line numbers below are that SHA's unless marked; round 3 (`a15a5146e`) added 23 lines to the guard above them.

---

**F6 (MINOR) — a hand-written census figure that is wrong at every SHA in the series, and no cell derives any census at all.**

The guard states, twice, that `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}node:24-alpine` is *"56 of the 79 FROM lines in this very repo"* (guard `:352-353` and `:389` at that SHA; `:375` and `:412` after round 3).

Measured over `Blockchain/Dev` Dockerfiles, excluding node_modules — **independently reproduced in the round-3 session, agreeing with the gate exactly**:

| SHA | files | FROM lines | `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}node:` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| base `306d0db92` | 35 | 95 | **62** |
| round 1 `8d3e5208a` | 35 | 95 | **62** |
| round 2 `3047bcb1d` | 35 | 95 | **62** |
| round 3 `a15a5146e` | 35 | 95 | **62** |

The claim **was never true anywhere in this PR series**. It entered at round 1. Negative control on the pipeline: the same search for `ZZZ_NOT_PRESENT}node:` returns 0, so it can return zero and is not matching everything.

*Not pinned either.* The gate added one extra valid class Dockerfile at head, moving the derived class 25 → 26. The guard printed `26 of 26 clean` and **the suite stayed 71 passed / 0 failed**. Nothing noticed.

Two other hand-written figures ARE currently correct: "the class is 25" and "18 of 25 class files".

**Shape of the fix:** the banner already forbids hand-maintained numbers — delete the two prose sites, or derive them. If a figure is worth keeping, one cell must DERIVE it from the tree and compare against a single declared constant. A parity assertion between two hand-written copies would drift together and stay green.

---

**F5 (MINOR) — a clause that cannot change the outcome for any input, self-declared as dead in the same round, and still shipped.**

`base_ships_no_js_runtime`, guard `:377` at that SHA (`:400` after round 3):

```
if (nm ~ /\$/) return 0
```

Gate tamper T7b neutered it to `/QQNEVERMATCHQQ/`: **suite 71 passed, 0 failed.** Differential probe over ten `$`-bearing FROM spellings (`$NODE_IMAGE`, `${NODE_IMAGE}`, `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}nginx${TAG}`, `${MY_PREFIX}scratch$X`, …): verdicts **byte-identical on all ten**. Plant-point control for that probe: a third variant adding `ubuntu` to `NON_JS_BASES` moves `FROM ubuntu:24.04` rc 1 → rc 0, so the probe CAN see a change in this function — it sees none from this clause.

Structural reason: the function returns `(nm in NON_JS_BASES)`, and no key in that array contains `$`, so a name containing `$` is a non-member either way.

The sharp edge: the guard's own comment names this pattern — *"a clause that cannot fail … reproduced, in the round that reports it, by the author"* — while removing the `!= "FROM"` guard next to it and leaving this one.

---

**F4 (MAJOR — red-proof gap) — a third of the tooling clause has no red-proof, and the cell named CONTROL cannot fail for the reason its name asserts.**

Gate tamper T9 deleted `npm|yarn|pnpm` from the tooling clause, leaving `node_modules` and the word-arm intact: **suite 71 passed, 0 failed.** Nothing reds.

A discriminator exists and no cell has it:

```
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN npm run build        # not an install, so no node_modules write; only `npm` signals
CMD ["/bin/sh"]
head          rc 1 "names a JavaScript runtime or its tooling"
T9-neutered   rc 0 "the re-link invariant does not apply"
```

The only `RUN npm run build` lines in the suite sit in BUILDER stages of green fixtures, where nodeish is never read.

Consequence for the named cell: **"R2 row 1b CONTROL: apk add nodejs npm was already denied"** is now satisfied by the *new* word-arm — `nodejs` matches it — so it survives T9 untouched. It is a control that no longer controls.

⚠ Round 3 **widened** this clause (added `npx`) and red-proofed only the `npx` token. `npm|yarn|pnpm` remains unproved, so this finding is live at `a15a5146e`.

---

**Why one ticket.** All three are the same failure: an artefact asserting something its suite cannot check. Fixing them separately would produce three commits that each re-derive the same instrument. The fix is one pass over guard and suite: delete or derive every hand-written figure, delete the clauses that cannot fail, and add the red-proofs that the tampers above show are missing — using the gate's own discriminators, which are written out here.

**Source:** `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura KS-930 round 2 (#876, tier 1)`, 2026-09-06T23:28Z, forwarded verbatim. F6 independently re-measured 2026-09-07; F4 and F5 are the gate's measurements, not re-run here.

title: Launcher suite: four side-effect and guarded-surface gaps from the KS-911/912 gate (incl. a SILENT destructive path on settings.local.json)
description:
Four pre-existing launcher findings from the KS-911/KS-912 by-hash gate (`PASS WITH FINDINGS`, 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z). **None was introduced by KS-911/912** — the tester says so explicitly — and none blocked the relaunch. Grouped as one path: the suite's no-damage claim and its side-effect surface.

`L`-numbers are against the shipped launcher `sha256 932a2cc3aebe6cf838bf885ac92eec08e259f0572c0e08910088ac58e269f55c`.

- [ ] **F-2 (MINOR) — the guard fails OPEN for a live seat when suite eviction composes with the documented** `SECUURA_SEAT_SCAN=0` **escape hatch.** Measured with one live fixture seat throughout:

  ```
  boot, scan OFF, BEFORE the suite : count=1, says pull: NO
  run the suite                    : seat still ALIVE, entry EVICTED from the registry
  boot, scan OFF, AFTER the suite  : count=0, says pull: YES
  ```

  Needs both halves, so it is narrow — but the escape hatch exists for the day the scan over-matches, which is also a day someone may run the suite. **Fix:** back up and restore the real `SEAT_FILE` the way the suite already backs up the preflight log, or route every registry case through `LAUNCH_TMPDIR` so the suite never writes the real registry.
- [ ] **F-3 (MINOR) — the "must not damage the live project" claim guards 1 of the 2 repos the launcher writes.** The launcher writes `user.name`/`user.email` to `${PROJECT_DIR%/*}/Extranet` at `L202-208` (KS-148) exactly as it does to `2_Project_Files`, but only `2_Project_Files/.git/config` is hashed before and after. Evidence: with the sandbox Extranet's email set to `kamil.kreiser@datasec.com.au`, **one** suite execution rewrote it to `kamil.kreiser@secuura.ai` — md5 `61238ef0` -> `8a2f8bda`, **cells that noticed: 0**. The write is intended and idempotent in steady state, so this is a guarded-surface gap rather than a launcher defect — but it is the one place workspace hard rule #5 (never mix GitHub accounts) is enforced, so it belongs inside the assertion. **Fix:** hash the Extranet config alongside `REPO_CFG`, skipping cleanly when the clone is absent.
- [ ] **F-4 (MINOR) —** `.claude/settings.local.json` **is rewritten on every launcher run (8 per suite execution) and guarded by no cell, and its failure mode is silent destruction.** A hand-formatted one-line file was reformatted by a single dry run (md5 `01ab75cd` -> `561024c9`); unrelated keys survive. But the embedded python at `L221-242` does `except Exception: data = {}` — so an **unparseable** file is silently discarded. Measured: a file containing `not json at all` came back as a fresh two-key JSON document, prior content gone, **nothing on stdout or stderr**. Pre-existing, but it sits inside the suite's own no-damage claim and it is a silent destructive path.
- [ ] **F-5 (POLISH) — the fix quotes its own detector.** The KS-911 F1 comment at `L246-247` reproduces the removed sentinel verbatim, so `grep -rl 'do not edit the sentinels'` still lists `Launch_Claude.command` itself. Any future check written as "is the sentinel gone?" reads non-zero forever. **Fix:** describe the removed wording instead of reproducing it.

**Not a finding, recorded so the next person to touch the trap sees it:** the suite's EXIT trap kills its fixtures with job control live, so bash prints `Terminated: 15` to stderr *after* the totals. Cosmetic, predates this change, same family as the operator-pane noise F-2 of KS-911 removed.

⚠️ **Do not fix while two seats are live** — the launcher is live on disk under a by-hash gate. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Source: `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, forwarded whole and read here. F-1 and the registry's `exec` premise are filed separately — different mechanism. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

title: KS-921 residues: five Dockerfile shapes the re-link guard cannot read, an nginx final stage it can NEVER pass, and one A_FAIL branch no test can red
description:
## KS-921 gate residues F-3, F-6, F-7 — five legitimate Dockerfile shapes the guard cannot read, one it can never pass, and one branch no test can red

From the #870 gate. Deliberately **not** fixed in that PR: F-1/F-2/F-4/F-5 were, because they are false cleans and false blocks that bite today; these three are shapes with **no live exposure** and one design question that deserves a decision rather than a patch.

**Live exposure today is zero, measured:** all seven frontend Dockerfiles use nginx/alpine final stages, **none** consumes `shared-builder`, and no frontend source imports `@secuura/shared` (0 files). So nothing in the tree hits these paths now — which is exactly why they should be recorded rather than left to be discovered by whoever first writes one.

### F-6 comes first, because it is the one with no answer

**For an nginx final stage the guard offers no route forward.** A static-serving final stage legitimately has no `node_modules` at all, so clause A's `final stage writes node_modules nowhere` fires and there is no way to make the file green except by adding a pointless `node_modules` write purely to satisfy the check.

**A guard with no green path for a legitimate shape is a design question, not a bug.** The options are roughly: exempt a final stage that writes no `node_modules` and consumes no builder tree; require an explicit opt-out marker; or narrow the class further so such files never enter it. **This is the first item on this ticket and it should be decided before anything below it is coded**, because the answer changes what the other shapes need.

### F-3 — five legitimate shapes the parser cannot read

1. **BuildKit heredoc** — `RUN <<EOF … EOF`. The parser joins on trailing `\` and treats each logical line independently, so a re-link inside a heredoc body is invisible.
2. **An nginx final stage with no** `node_modules` — see F-6.
3. **The non-final-stage write.** Clause A is stated over the FINAL stage. A Dockerfile whose runtime stage is not the last `FROM` in the file (a valid multi-target build) is judged against the wrong stage.
4. `npm i` **shorthand.** The install detector matches `npm ci|install`; `npm i` alone is not matched, so a stage installing that way reads as writing no `node_modules`.
5. **The JSON** `COPY` **form** — `COPY ["--from=builder", "/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]`. Valid Dockerfile, unreadable to a whitespace-token parser.

Plus the two parser edges the gate noted.

### F-7 — and this one is the same family as three tickets already on this board

**The** `A_FAIL` **branch for "final stage writes node_modules nowhere" is pinned by NO test.**

Measured 2026-09-06, by neutering it (`note("A_FAIL", …)` → `note("A_OK", …)`) and re-running:

```
suite with the branch neutered ............ 26 passed, 0 failed
"final stage has NO" ...................... pinned by 4 cells
"runs BEFORE the last instruction" ........ pinned by 1 cell
"runs after a non-root" ................... pinned by 1 cell
"writes node_modules nowhere" ............. pinned by 0 cells
```

The tamper was restored and the file verified byte-identical by sha256.

**A branch no cell can red is a check that cannot fail** — and it is the fourth mechanism of that family on this board tonight, alongside [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926) (a check nothing runs), [KS-927](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-927) (a check running with the half that would notice already dead) and [KS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-928) (a check whose wiring is unasserted). Here the guard runs, the suite runs, the wiring is asserted — **and one branch of it still cannot be shown to work.**

Note the ordering trap for whoever fixes it: this branch is also *unreachable in practice for the current class*, since every one of the 25 files writes `node_modules` in its final stage. Pinning it needs a fixture, and the fixture is the nginx shape from F-6 — **so F-6's decision and F-7's cell are the same piece of work.**

### Fix shape

Decide F-6 first. Then a cell per F-3 shape, each red-proofed by the shape it describes, and the F-7 cell falling out of F-6's chosen semantics. **No shape should be "supported" without a cell that reds without it** — the guard already shipped one branch without that and this ticket is the receipt.

*Filed by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the #870 gate at Wednesday's direction to ticket rather than widen that PR. The F-7 measurement above is mine; the shapes are the gate's.*

title: Launcher boot step tells every agent session to POST /api/seen as EXTRANET_ME=kam, which clears Kam's own unread flags — and the extranet is input-only
description:
## What is wrong

`Launch_Claude.command:522` (boot step 7) instructs every session:

> "…GET the summary for this operator (EXTRANET_ME), and fold my open tasks + replies-to-me + new documents into the confirmation below; **mark seen afterwards**."

which routes to the `extranet` skill's step 3:

> `POST $EXTRANET_URL/api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` so "new" resets next session.

And in this project's `4_Credentials/.env`:

```
EXTRANET_ME=kam
```

So the "operator" an agent marks caught-up as **is Kam himself**. An agent that follows the boot step clears **Kam's** unread flags on his own portal — the tasks, replies and documents he has not yet read. The next time he opens the extranet, the things an agent read on his behalf are no longer marked new to him.

It is the human's signal, and an automated session destroys it as a side effect of booting.

## Why it is a defect and not a preference

Two independent reasons, either of which is sufficient:

1. `EXTRANET_ME` **is doing two jobs.** It identifies *whose* summary to fetch — correct, an agent working for Kam should see Kam's queue — and it also identifies *who has now seen it* — wrong, because the agent saw it and Kam did not. One variable, two meanings, and the second one is only ever wrong when an agent uses it.
2. **The extranet is input-only for agents** (standing rule for this project). `POST /api/seen` is a write. The boot step asks for a write the operating rules forbid, so the instruction cannot be followed as stated regardless of who `EXTRANET_ME` names.

## Reproduced

Not by running it — running it *is* the defect, and it is not reversible from the API. Established from the artefacts instead:

* `4_Credentials/.env:4` → `EXTRANET_ME=kam` (agent key on line 3 not reproduced here)
* `Launch_Claude.command:522` → the "mark seen afterwards" instruction
* `Notes (MASTER)/skills/Current/extranet.md:27` → the `POST /api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` step
* `…/extranet.md:111` → `POST /api/seen | {person}` in the endpoint table

The three artefacts compose into the behaviour without needing to execute it. **This session declined the step and said so rather than skipping it silently** — that is the current mitigation, and it relies on every future session making the same judgement, which is not a control.

## Fix shape

Any of these closes it; the first is the smallest:

1. **Drop "mark seen afterwards" from the launcher's step 7** and the corresponding step from the skill, for agent sessions. The summary is read-only; nothing needs the flag reset, and "new since last session" is more useful to an agent unreset anyway.
2. **Separate the two meanings** — `EXTRANET_ME` for whose queue to read, a distinct `EXTRANET_SEEN_AS` for whose flags to clear, unset by default so the write never happens unless someone deliberately sets it.
3. **Make** `/api/seen` **refuse an agent key** for a person other than the key's own identity, server-side, so no launcher wording can cause it. This one belongs to the extranet app rather than the launcher.

## Scope

The launcher is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing this copy does not fix the others — the same boot step exists in every project's launcher, and any project whose `EXTRANET_ME` names a human has the same defect. Whoever picks this up should decide at the template level, not here.

Filed at Wednesday's direction (2026-09-06) after this session declined the boot step. Not applied mid-queue: the launcher is not this seat's to edit.

title: KS-907 suite residues: CASE 2 never asserts the pruning it is named for, a cell count printed as a launcher-run count, and a grep -qc diagnostic
description:
## BLUF

**Three residues in** `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` **from the KS-907 by-hash gate (F3, F4, F6 — all Polish). The worst is F4: CASE 2, the cell the suite calls "the one that matters most", never asserts the thing it is named for. All three reproduced here before filing.**

Ships with the launcher follow-up by the same by-hash mechanism — the suite sits at the project root, outside git, like the launcher.

## F4 — CASE 2 asserts the consequence, not the act

CASE 2 exists to prove that a **dead** registry entry is *pruned*, because a guard that latched on a stale PID would pin every future launch of the project into read-only mode. It asserts `DRY_COUNT = 0` and that the step carries the pull text — both of which are the *downstream effect*. **It never checks that the dead pid left the file.**

So a launcher that read the entry, counted it as not-live, and left it in the registry forever would pass CASE 2 while the file grew without bound.

**Fix shape:** assert the dead pid is absent from `$SEAT_FILE` after the run, and — the control that makes it discriminate — that the *live* pid in CASE 1 is still **present**. Presence and absence in the same batch.

## F3 — the hygiene cell prints the cell count and calls them launcher runs

The label is built from `$((pass+fail))`:

> `2_Project_Files/.git/config is byte-identical after 12 launcher runs`

**12 is the number of cells that had run at that point. The true number of launcher invocations is 6** — measured: `run_launcher` is called exactly 6 times (control, live, dead, recycled, scan, scanoff).

The assertion itself is sound; only the number in the sentence is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that overstates the evidence. The figure `12` was carried into KS-907's READY and its ticket comment; both are corrected to 6.

**Fix shape:** count the invocations in `run_launcher` and print that.

## F6 — `grep -qc` with `echo $?` as a diagnostic

`Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh:98`, inside the CONTROL's failure message:

```
pull-text=$(grep -qc "$PULLTEXT" "$WORK/control.step" 2>/dev/null; echo $?)
```

`-q` and `-c` contradict: `-q` wins, so nothing is counted and the `echo $?` prints an exit status labelled as if it were a count. It appears only in a `bad()` message, so it has never been rendered — which is exactly why it survived.

**Fix shape:** use the same `grep -q … && echo YES || echo NO` form the neighbouring field already uses.

## Declared limit, recorded not fixed (F5)

The process scan matches the project directory as a **substring** of the argv, so a sibling project directory named `Blockchain-<anything>` would be counted as a seat of this project. No such sibling exists (measured). The failure direction is safe — a false positive costs a read-only boot — and it is recorded on KS-907 as a limit rather than worked.

Residues of the KS-907 tier-2 by-hash gate (F3, F4, F6; Polish). Parent: KS-907.

title: KS-907 launcher residues: a sentinel comment describing a test that does not exist, and a 2>/dev/null placed after the append it silences
description:
## BLUF

**Two residues in** `Launch_Claude.command` **from the KS-907 by-hash gate (F1, F2 — both Minor). One is a comment describing a test that does not exist; the other is a** `2>/dev/null` **placed *after* the append it is meant to silence, so a failed open still prints. Both reproduced here before filing.**

⚠ **Ships by the BY-HASH mechanism, not as an in-place edit.** The hash that passed the gate (`9609c8453da8d7743a4b3ed2a94db6b09bef588c29f83e57b16255963a0929f1`) is the hash that runs. Any fix takes a new `.pre-` copy, the three hashes in the READY, and a narrow tier-2 gate on the diff — the same shape KS-907 used.

## F1 — a sentinel comment that describes a test that does not exist

`Launch_Claude.command:244`:

```
# ── KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY — BEGIN (do not edit the sentinels; the test extracts here) ──
```

The suite does **not** extract between the sentinels. It runs the real launcher via `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` and parses the `DRY_RUN_*` markers — which is the better design, and it is what shipped. The sentinel wording is left over from a design that was replaced.

Measured: `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` contains **0** references to `KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY`, against a control of **2** occurrences of `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` — so the suite really does not touch the sentinels, and the same grep can find what is there.

Consequence: nothing guards the sentinels, and the comment tells a future editor to preserve something for a reason that is not true. This is the same class as the KS-904 slip in the same session — a comment asserting a guard that is not in the code.

**Fix shape:** either delete the sentinels and the claim, or make them real by having the suite assert exactly one `BEGIN` and one `END`. Prefer the first: the dry-run markers already are the contract, and a second contract nothing checks is worse than none.

## F2 — `2>/dev/null` placed after the append it is meant to silence

`Launch_Claude.command:292` and `:295`:

```
printf '%s' "$SEAT_KEPT" > "$SEAT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s|%s\n' "$$" "$SEAT_SELF_STARTED" >> "$SEAT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
```

Redirections apply left to right. The file is opened **before** `2>/dev/null` takes effect, so a failed open writes its error to the still-live stderr. The `|| true` swallows the status but not the noise, and a boot that cannot write its registry prints a bare shell error into the operator's pane.

Reproduced under `/bin/bash 3.2.57` — the shell the launcher runs under, not the zsh this repo's tooling defaults to:

|  | stderr |
| -- | -- |
| **A** `>> file 2>/dev/null` (the shipped shape) | `/bin/bash: line 2: /nonexistent-dir-xyz/f: No such file or directory` |
| **B** `2>/dev/null >> file` (redirect first) | *(none)* |
| **control** — a successful append, shape A | *(none)* |

The control matters: shape A is not simply always noisy, so the difference is the ordering and not the instrument.

*(An earlier A/B of mine did not discriminate because the Bash tool runs **zsh**, where both orderings reported the error.* `BASH_VERSION` *was empty — that is the tell.)*

**Fix shape:** move the redirection ahead of the target, at both sites.

## Regression

A launch whose registry directory is unwritable must produce no shell error on stderr — with a control launch that writes successfully, so the cell can fail.

Residues of the KS-907 tier-2 by-hash gate (F1, F2; Minor). Parent: KS-907.

title: Audit the eleven cwd- and script-relative repo-root derivations under scripts/ and systemTest/ — one family, several blind in different ways
description: ## BLUF**The** `$(cd ../.. && pwd)` **/** `$(dirname "$0")/../..` **family appears eleven times across** `scripts/` **and** `systemTest/`**, in at least three variants with different failure modes.** KS-859 fixed one of them (`no-tracked-credentials.sh`); the rest are unaudited.## ScopeEnumerate every repo-root derivation under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` and `systemTest/`, classify each as script-relative, cwd-relative, or git-derived, and record for each whether it is:- **layout-dependent** (breaks where the repo root is not two levels up — the KS-859 defect), and/or- **cwd-dependent** (breaks when invoked from elsewhere — worse), and/or- **env-dependent** (breaks under an inherited git environment).Known starting points, measured at `34347a8fa`: `action-pins-labelled.sh:46` and `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57` are cwd-relative. `run-shell-suites.sh:45` **is NOT blind** — its KS-731 zero-suites guard fails loudly, and is the model for what a safe one looks like.## Why one ticket rather than elevenThis is a survey, not a defect: the deliverable is the classification plus a ticket per genuinely-blind site. Filing eleven speculative tickets before measuring would be the aggregation shape Kam withdrew.## Fix shapeThe audit first. Then, per blind site, the KS-859 idiom — ask git from a self-derived directory with the environment scrubbed — and a shared helper if the count justifies one.Charter named by the #858 gate as its round-2 work. Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: no-tracked-credentials.sh cites two scripts as "structurally immune" exemplars — both use a WORSE cwd-relative root derivation
description: ## BLUF**The comment added by #858 points the next reader at two scripts as exemplars of the safe idiom. Both use a strictly worse one.**`no-tracked-credentials.sh:81-82` says:> `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh` and `action-pins-labelled.sh` already derive their root this way and are structurally immune; this is the same idiom.Measured at the merged tip `34347a8fa`:`action-pins-labelled.sh:46          REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57  REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"`That is **cwd-relative**, not script-relative. It depends on the caller's working directory, where the idiom the comment describes (`$(dirname "$0")/../..`) does not. They are not immune, and they are not the same idiom.## Why it mattersThe comment is load-bearing prose: it exists to tell the next person what shape to copy. Pointing at a worse form is how the family spreads.## Fix shapeCorrect the comment to describe the idiom without endorsing those two, and either fix their derivations or reference the audit ticket that covers them.Residue of the #858 tier-2 gate (F-QA-01, Minor). Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: packages/shared project tsc is RED on develop — crypto.JsonWebKey is gone in @types/node 26.1.0; a live type error no gate owns
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared`'s **project** `tsc` reports **1 error** on develop, and no gate owns it.

```
src/crypto/jwks.ts(129,51): TS2694 — namespace 'crypto' has no exported member 'JsonWebKey'
```

`crypto.JsonWebKey` was removed in `@types/node` **26.1.0**. Found by the KS-843 round-3 gate.

## Not caused by the KS-843 work — measured

`git diff 59248bf38 e1d9d9380 -- '*packages/shared*'` is **EMPTY**. The toolchain moved under the shared install some time after 12:38; the source did not change.

## Why nothing caught it

The push preflight's twelve legs do not include a `packages/shared` project type-check, and the vitest suite is green (**709/709**) because vitest does not type-check. So this is red in `tsc` and invisible everywhere the team actually looks.

## Fix shape

Either import `JsonWebKey` from where `@types/node` 26.x now exposes it, or declare the shape locally (it is a small, stable JWK interface). Check whether the dependency bump was intended before pinning around it — an unintended `@types/node` major arriving via a transitive install is itself worth knowing.

## Acceptance

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` exits 0 **with a planted-error control proving the check is live**; `packages/shared` stays 709/709; and the reason it went unnoticed is closed — either the preflight gains a shared project type-check leg, or a ticket says explicitly why it should not.

title: KS-386 residues from the round-2 gate: G-1 column ordinal drift, G-2 the second-image orphan, G-3 the in-memory docstring is wrong at the wire, G-4 two write spellings the guard cannot see
description:
## BLUF

Four Minors from the KS-386 round-2 tier-1 re-gate, none blocking. All four shipped as-is under the two-round cap — the gate PASSED and #839 merged as `b6ae609e6`. **This description is taken from the gate report's own findings section**, `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks386-839-regate-3b5a09403/report.md` §3, with its evidence file names; every fix-shape below is the report's, and the report marks all four *advisory only — no change was made by the tester*.

---

## G-1 · MINOR · A fresh-init schema and a migrated schema still differ: `user_id` and `created_at` are in **opposite ordinal positions**

**Oracle:** product, internal consistency. The claim under test was the builder's own — "the two shipped schemas now match the migrated one."
**Evidence class: MEASURED.** `pg_attribute` projection of both schemas, `evidence/cols-qa_i.txt` vs `evidence/cols-qa_mig.txt`, diff in `evidence/schema-diff-freshinit-vs-migrated.txt`:

```
  fresh-init (i)          migrated (mig)
  4|user_id|text|f||      4|created_at|timestamp with time zone|f|now()|
  5|created_at|…|now()|   5|user_id|text|f||
```

Sorted by name the two are **identical** — names, types, nullability, defaults, comment, both indexes. The difference is ordinal position only.
**Cause (read, not speculated):** `init.sql` and `docker/init/04` declare `user_id` *between* `mime_type` and `created_at`; migration 035 `ADD COLUMN`s it, so on a migrated database it lands last. No DDL reconciles the two short of a table rewrite.
**Blast radius:** nothing in the service is positional — the only INSERT names its columns and every read is by name. It bites anything comparing schemas structurally (a `pg_dump` diff, a drift detector, a snapshot test) or any future `INSERT … VALUES` with no column list, **which would write a** `user_id` **into** `created_at` **on one of the two shapes.**
**Falsifying tamper:** reorder `user_id` and `created_at` in `init.sql` to match 035's result and the ordered diff goes empty.
**Fix-shape:** accept and document the ordinal difference in the comment block that already explains the coupling, or move the `user_id` declaration in both shipped files to sit after `created_at`.

## G-2 · MINOR · A partial write leaves an orphan attestation, and the 500 says "No document was accepted" **when one was**

**Oracle:** explainability — "the most serious defect class is claiming something true that isn't."
**Evidence class: MEASURED**, driven on the tester's own copy of schema (i) with a trigger failing the **second** image only (`RAISE EXCEPTION` on `mime_type = 'image/jpeg'`, the back image).
**Repro:** schema (i) → install a constraint/trigger rejecting only the second INSERT → boot kyc at `3b5a09403` → initiate (bearer) 201 → `/document` with front PNG + back JPEG → `/selfie`.
**Observed:**

* `/document` → **500** `KYC_ATTESTATION_WRITE_FAILED` **— "No document was accepted."**
* `svc_kyc_images` holds **the front row anyway** (`data` NULL, `user_id` set) — *the message is false about the state it describes*. `dbSaveImage` is called once per image and each `query()` is its own autocommit statement; there is no transaction around the pair.
* `/selfie` then answers **200** `success:true` and writes **a second row**.
* `svc_kyc_verifications` for that subject: `documents` **IS NULL**, `liveness_completed` **true**. The record claims a completed liveness check for a subject whose document step failed, and two attestation rows exist that nothing references.

**Privacy or correctness?** **Correctness and honesty, not privacy.** The orphan rows carry `user_id`, so the KS-291 erasure path (`DELETE … WHERE user_id = $1`) still reaches them; nothing becomes undeletable and no payload is held. What is exposed is a compliance record asserting more than happened, and a client sentence that contradicts the database.
**Not introduced by #839** — the pair was untransacted before it too, and the builder named it without widening. What **is** new is the sentence "No document was accepted", now a specific claim the state can contradict.
**Fix-shape:** wrap the front/back pair in the existing `transaction()` helper — the orphan disappears and the sentence becomes true. **Regression test the owner should add:** drive `/document` against a DB that rejects the *second* insert, assert `count(*) = 0`, and assert `/selfie` does not then succeed.

## G-3 · MINOR · `dbSaveImage`'s "ONE HONEST LIMIT" docstring is wrong about the path this gate is about

**Oracle:** product — the code contradicts its own comment. **MEASURED** (two boots, driven) **and READ** (`index.ts:290-293`, `db.ts:125-147`).
The docstring, added by this diff, says *"when* `isDbAvailable()` *is false this returns early and writes nothing, and the route still answers 200."* Driven both ways into that state, the route answers **404** `NOT_FOUND` **"Verification not found"**, not 200 — `dbGetVerification` returns `undefined` before `dbSaveImage` is ever called, because nothing keeps verifications in memory.
**Why it matters even though reality is better than described:** this docstring is the written scope of F-1(b)'s exemption. A future reader will believe there is a live 200-with-no-row hole here and either chase it or, worse, treat a genuine one as already known.
**Also worth the owner's eye, pre-existing, not #839:** in that state `POST /api/kyc/initiate` still returns **201 with a** `verificationId` that is never persisted anywhere and 404s on the very next call.
**Falsifying tamper:** the finding *is* the tamper — boot with no `DATABASE_URL` and drive; a 200 from `/document` would refute it. **Fix-shape:** restate the limit as "the route 404s because the verification itself was never persisted", or delete the paragraph.
**Owned:** that sentence is mine, written in round 2 while trying to be explicit about a limit.

## G-4 · MINOR (carried from pass-1's H-b hunts, now louder) · The retitled cell claims "exactly ONE write path IN THIS FILE" while two spellings *in that file* are invisible

**Oracle:** explainability — a guard's title is a claim, and this one over-reaches.
**Evidence class: MEASURED.** Both planted in `index.ts` as **real payload writes**:

* `INSERT INTO "svc_kyc_images" (id, data, mime_type) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)` → **0 failed / 26**
* `INSERT INTO public.svc_kyc_images (id, data, mime_type) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)` → **0 failed / 26**

Both reader functions return `[]` on both. An `UPDATE` split across lines **is** caught (1 failed / 25), so the blindness is specifically about how the table **name** is spelled, not about whitespace.
F-2 as filed — the corpus overclaim — **is** closed. This is the residue: the docstring's "OTHER LIMIT" paragraph names the behavioural limit and the string-literal limit but says nothing about name spellings, and the retitle to "IN THIS FILE" makes the in-file claim stronger than the regex supports.
**Likelihood in operation: low** — nobody in this codebase quotes or schema-qualifies that identifier today, verified by `git grep -a`.
**Fix-shape:** match `(INSERT\s+INTO|UPDATE)\s+(?:"?public"?\.)?"?svc_kyc_images"?`, or name the spellings in the docstring's limits paragraph as the corpus limit is now named.

---

## Scope

One ticket, four items, product. G-3 is docs-only and can land with any of the others. G-1 and G-4 are decisions as much as fixes; G-2 is the only one with real design weight.

## Provenance

KS-386 round-2 tier-1 re-gate, verdict 2026-09-06T00:43:59Z, PASS, scored 1.0. #839 merged `b6ae609e6847b399ef695c9cd69fe1ef671693df`. Text from the report's §3 findings, read at `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks386-839-regate-3b5a09403/report.md`.

title: Make the authorize rules DATA the resolver iterates, so the GET/POST agreement guard is structural instead of textual
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

`ks804-authorize-get-post-agree-per-rule.test.ts`'s `RULES` table is a hand-maintained literal. Its header once promised that a rule added to one handler and not the other "fails here by construction, because the table below is the list of rules" — corrected in KS-822 F-8, because it is the list of rules *someone wrote down*, not the list the code has.

F-8 enforced the half that could be enforced: the table's `expected` set must equal the refusal-message set `resolveAuthorizeClient` can return. **That guard is TEXTUAL and has three named limits, each measured rather than asserted:**

* a rule that **REUSES** an existing message is invisible to it — F-6 and F-7 both did, and their RULES rows are hand-added, which is the only thing making those rules driven;
* it is a **SOURCE-TEXT** guard: it sees a literal appear or disappear and **cannot see a rule stop working while its literal stays on the page** (a condition-shaped tamper on RULE 5 reds the behaviour cases and leaves the guard green);
* its span is anchored on the function signature as text, so a `return {` + `ok: true,` written with different whitespace ends it early or not at all.

**The real fix the header already names: make the rules DATA the resolver iterates**, so the table is derived rather than maintained and the guard becomes structural instead of textual. That is a route refactor of `resolveAuthorizeClient`, not a change to the suite, which is why it was not taken inside KS-822.

**Done when:** the resolver's app rules are a list it walks; the suite derives its cases from that list; a new rule is driven through both handlers without anyone adding a row; and the three limits above are closed or explicitly re-stated against the new shape.

title: Publish a `request:` block for POST /api/oauth/token — the endpoint's shape is asserted nowhere, and adding it moves what Schemathesis generates
description:
**Ruled line 3 of KS-822's five, lifted onto its own ticket so it survives that ticket closing.**

`POST /api/oauth/token` publishes **no** `request:` **block**. That is why its description spells the form fields out in prose — `grant_type`, `code`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token` are described in a sentence rather than declared as a schema an integrator or a tool can read.

## Why it was NOT added in #831, and the reason still holds

Publishing a form-body schema where none exists **changes what Schemathesis generates against a live auth endpoint.** That is not a docs-only change, and #831 was a prose-scoped round. It wants its own change **with the suite actually run** — the point is precisely that the generator's behaviour moves, so a change that does not run the suite has not been tested.

## What it is worth

The token endpoint's published contract has been tightened repeatedly (KS-820 client authentication; KS-822 F-2d bound the status→code split to assertions). All of that is in prose. A `request:` block is the half a machine can check, and its absence is why the endpoint's shape is asserted nowhere in the spec.

## Done when

* A `request:` block declaring the form body, with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` as the media type the endpoint actually accepts (it is in `FORM_ALLOWED_PATHS` — the only path that is).
* **Schemathesis run before and after**, with the operation's case counts and outcomes compared. A change that moves the generator and reports no delta has not been measured.
* The prose reduced to what the schema cannot say, rather than left to drift beside it.

*Source: KS-822 comment* `e38c5f38` *(line 3), from PR #831's tier-2 gate. Nothing was built for it in KS-822's round.*

title: Audit gate baseline data model: an unvalidated `scope` lets a GREEN root gate advertise a row leg 7 still needs, and suppression matches by advisory id alone
description:
## BLUF

**Two Minor findings in the audit gate's BASELINE DATA MODEL, both from the #829 fuse gate (tier 2, PASS — merged at** `ec5431f6b`**). Neither blocked the merge. F1 is the one s133 walked into and which cost a refused push; F2 means a baseline row silently covers more than it was written about.** Filed beside KS-763 as the gate ruled. Fix-shapes below are the tester's, quoted as **hypotheses** — run each against the unfixed instrument before building on it.

## F1 (Minor) — a green root gate can advertise a row for deletion that a second gate still needs

`scope: "standalone-locks"` is **optional and unvalidated**: `baseline-contract.mjs:41` REQUIRED_FIELDS is `package` / `reason` / `ticket` only. But the root gate's CLEANUP advice keys on that field (`audit-gate.mjs:203-205`).

So an advisory that lives **only in a standalone lock**, baselined without the marker, is advertised for deletion by a **GREEN** root gate — while leg 7 (`audit:locks`) still needs the row. That is exactly what happened on 2026-09-05: `audit:gate` printed `CLEANUP … remove: GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6` and the push preflight then refused the deletion, because the root audit reads the **hoisted workspace tree** and cannot see standalone locks. Deleting on the root gate's word would have broken the push gate for every author.

The class is swept clean at head — one such row, and it is marked.

**Fix-shape (hypothesis):** either `validateBaseline` refuses a row that the root audit does not report and that lacks `scope`, or the root gate declines to list for cleanup any row it cannot positively attribute. **Regression:** a locks-only advisory baselined without `scope` must NOT appear in CLEANUP.

## F2 (Minor) — suppression matches by ADVISORY ID ALONE

`baseline[id]` at `audit-locks.mjs:286-289` and `audit-gate.mjs:194-197`. A row written about one version and one path silently covers **every** version and **every** path of that advisory.

Demonstrated by this very PR: the regen added a **vulnerable-range qs instance** (nested `qs` 6.15.3 under body-parser 1.20.6) and **no gate output changed**.

**Fix-shape (hypothesis):** record the measured versions on the row; **warn — not fail** — when a matched instance falls outside them.

## F3 (polish) — a wording fix on the record

"before the regen leg 7 refused" described the **deletion-only attempt**, not the parent SHA. The parent is GREEN 30/30. The refusal is the head-baseline + parent-lock cell, which the tester reproduced exactly. Correct the phrasing wherever it is repeated.

## F4 (polish) — the mysql2 row's clocks disagree

`GHSA-rgwj-5xj2-c3m3` mixes a local date with ISO dates, and its `decidedAt` still reads `2026-09-03` under a **2026-09-04** ruling by Kam. Verified on develop `ec5431f6b`: `decidedAt: "2026-09-03"`, `expires: "2026-09-24"`. Being fixed in the BACKLOG docs commit if it is a one-line change; otherwise it stays here as this ticket's fourth line.

## For the record — the tester's own retraction

qs 6.15.3 was **already** in four locks at the parent (`frontend/issuer`, `services/vc-issuer`, `services/mcp-server`, `packages/shared`::body-parser). The nesting is an existing repo pattern, so the hazard disclosed on #829 is **milder** than first read. The two #801 rows cover the nested instance by id, tamper-proven.

**Not commissioned, said so:** the reachability re-check. The tester checked the mysql2 **row** (id → package by tamper; 3.15.3 in exactly two locks), not the measurement behind it.

## Provenance

Gate mail `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura FUSE #829 PASS 1 @ b7fc43473 (tier 2 narrow)` 2026-09-05T15:18:05Z; routed here by Wednesday's GO 2026-09-05T15:21:12Z. Sits beside KS-763 (the fuse ticket #829 carries on its mysql2 row).

title: Gate integrity: the auth suite's green is not deterministic — three head runs gave 534/0, 534/0, and 534 with 2 FAILED
description:
## BLUF

**A security PR merged on one green run is merged on a sample.** The KS-820+821 gate ran the auth
suite three times at the head and got **534/0, 534/0, and 534 with 2 FAILED** — the failing file
(`ks431-oauth-app-update.test.ts`) is **byte-identical at both SHAs**, failing with
`TypeError: fetch failed` plus a stale 500. The suite's green is a sample, and every gate in this
class currently reads one draw of it as a verdict.

## Mechanism — measured, and the same one twice

**21 of the 40 auth test files open a server per request** (`app.listen(0)`). s132's `BACKLOG.md`
entry — `auth.integration.test.ts` failing 1 run in 3 with a registration helper getting 501 — is
**the same mechanism in another file**, and is carried here **as a hypothesis, not a diagnosis**:
its preconditions are all measured (a server per REQUEST, no agent passed,
`http.globalAgent.keepAlive === true` on node 24, `501` absent from all of `services/auth/src`) but
the link has never been reproduced deterministically.

## Why it is worth its own ticket

The flake and the gate are separate problems. Even once the flake is diagnosed, **a gate that reads**
**a single run cannot tell a real red from a draw** — that is the part that decides whether security
work merges correctly.

## Shapes, neither yet run

* **The flake:** listen once per suite, or pass an agent with `keepAlive: false`.
* **The gate:** run the suite N times, or make the runner report the draw rather than the verdict.
  Whichever is chosen, prove it by reproducing a red first — a fix that cannot be shown to change
  the failure rate has not been shown to do anything.

---

*Filed by s133 from the KS-820+821 tier-1 gate (PASS 1 @* `0e8d3e60a`*, report* `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-05-s132-ks820-821-pass1-0e8d3e60a/report.md` *at the QA tree), on Wednesday's disposition ruling of 2026-09-05T13:01:20Z. Inherited — not introduced by #825.*

title: Compose resolves the SHELL over .env while the checker resolves .env over the shell — a green credential check over a stack running the shared literal
description:
## BLUF

`docker compose` resolves the **shell environment over the project** `.env`; `source` resolves the `.env` **over the shell**. The credential checker uses `source`. So in one shell, with one correctly-rotated `.env`, **the checker prints a full green bill of health and** `rc=0` **while compose resolves both datastore passwords to the shared literals from git history.**

This is **F-800-05 reopened by a new route** — a confident green over an exposed stack — and it lands on the surface Stuart and Peter are asked to trust on rotation day (`APP_DB_PASSWORD` rotation 2026-09-05 09:00).

Found by the compose-precedence probe named as the highest-value next step in the 2026-09-04 through-code gate on #800's fix round. **No fix is written.** Filed separately from #800 on Wednesday's ruling: the fix is a behaviour change to the start path, not a change to the checker's parser.

## Recommendation

Fix on its own branch off `develop`, not on #800. Two candidate shapes, neither chosen here:

* **(a)** have `start-environment.sh` source `.env` on the same path, so the shell and compose agree — this also makes FR-1's safety claim true, which is the same defect from the other side; or
* **(b)** have the checker "be the consumer" for real: read the values the way compose does (shell first, `.env` second) rather than the way `source` does.

**(b) is the one that matches what the script claims about itself.** See the claim-defect below.

## Detail

### The measurement, and why the discriminator is the keeper

`${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-secuura_dev_password}` means **the compose default IS the shared literal**. So a naive probe — export the shared literal, see whether compose renders the shared literal — **cannot distinguish "the shell won" from "compose saw nothing and fell back to its default."** It returns the alarming-looking answer for the reassuring reason, or the reassuring answer for no reason at all.

A **three-way sentinel** was used instead:

| rendered value | meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `rotated_probe_pg_A1` (the fixture) | the `.env` won — no inversion |
| `AMBIENT_SHELL_pg_B2` (the sentinel) | **the shell won — inversion real** |
| `secuura_dev_password` (compose default) | neither was seen — the probe did not vary its subject |

Result, `docker compose config` only (render-only; no `-o`, no `--lock-image-digests`, no `up`), fixture supplied via `--env-file` from a scratchpad file:

| run | interp-env PG | interp-env Redis | rendered postgres service |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **CONTROL** — no ambient export | fixture wins | fixture wins | fixture wins |
| **TREATMENT** — shell exports sentinel | **SHELL WINS** | **SHELL WINS** | **SHELL WINS** |

**The control is what makes the treatment readable.** It proves `--env-file` was honoured, that the fixture is genuinely the file compose read, and — since nothing unrecognised appeared — that no real `.env` leaked into the probe. The only thing differing between the two runs is the ambient export.

### The real-world shape, both instruments in one shell

Shell still exports the old shared literals; `.env` correctly rotated:

* **checker** → `✓ POSTGRES_PASSWORD is per-clone`, `✓ REDIS_PASSWORD is per-clone`, `rc=0`
* **compose** → `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secuura_dev_password`, `REDIS_PASSWORD=secuura_redis_dev`

### The claim in shipped source that this refutes

`check-slot-credentials.sh:96-99` carries the justification for the entire sourcing design:

> *"it cannot drift from the consumer, **because it IS the consumer**."*

It is not the consumer. Compose is, and compose resolves with the opposite precedence. (The sentence itself is being corrected on #800's branch alongside FR-1/FR-6; the behavioural fix is this ticket.)

### Blast radius — bounded, and it lands on FR-1's caller

Measured per caller at `e26cfce2b`, with a bash-semantics control:

* `start-local.sh` — checker L63, `source .env` L103 with **no** `set -a`. A plain assignment to an **already-exported** variable keeps the export attribute and updates the value, so the stale ambient **is overwritten** by the rotated `.env` before compose runs. Control: with the variable not previously exported, a child process sees nothing. **This path is neutralised — by accident. Nothing anywhere records that the L103** `source` **is load-bearing**, so moving or removing it silently opens this hole.
* `start-environment.sh` — checker L91, **no** `source` **anywhere in its 283 lines**, `docker compose up` L135. The stale export survives untouched from the operator's shell into compose. **This is the live path, and it is the same caller QA FR-1 named.**

### The precondition is self-priming

`check-slot-credentials.sh:164`, in the UNREADABLE arm, tells the operator:

> `See the parse error with:  sh -n '<file>'  (or: set -a; . '<file>')`

**Running that second form in an interactive shell is exactly the act that exports these two variables into it.** So the script hands the operator the command that arms the trap — and the operator most likely to type it is the one whose `.env` is malformed, i.e. mid-rotation. (The suggestion is being dropped from that message on #800's branch as part of the upgraded FR-8; that removes one route to the precondition, **not** the precedence defect itself.)

### Not established

Whether `start-environment.sh` runs anywhere but a developer laptop — laptop only, or also the demo/UAT VM. That bounds the severity and it was not settled from the tree.

---

Discovered 2026-09-04 (s122) by the compose-precedence probe. Related: PR #800 (`e26cfce2b`), QA FR-1 (same caller), QA FR-8 (the self-priming message).

title: mobile/secuura-app has 81 unscanned advisories (2 critical) — nothing has ever audited that tree
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app` carries **81 npm advisories — 2 critical, 45 high, 32 moderate, 3 low** — and nothing has ever scanned it. It was invisible to `audit-locks.mjs`, whose discovery walked four directories under `Blockchain/Dev` and could not reach it. Measured 2026-09-03 (session 114) while widening that discovery under KS-763 / KS-768.

## Why it is filed rather than baselined

Widening the lockfile corpus from 35 to 44 tracked locks took the gate's unbaselined count to 86. **81 of those 86 are this one tree.** Writing 81 baseline rows nobody measured would be exactly the failure KS-763 exists to fix — a suppression carrying no real reason.

So the tree is **declared out of scope** in `scripts/audit/lock-discovery.mjs` (`OUT_OF_SCOPE_LOCKS`), enumerated with a reason and this ticket, and the gate now **prints** the exclusion on every run. The old blind spot was accidental and invisible; this one is declared and counted. This ticket is the thing that stops the declaration becoming permanent by default.

## What is known

* **Not built by any compose file** — 0 references to `mobile/secuura-app` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` or `docker-compose.local.yml`, against a control of 2 for `services/originate`.
* **Not built by any workflow** — 0 of the workflows reference it, against a control of 3 referencing `services/`.
* 2 of the 81 are CRITICAL: `GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p` (shell-quote 1.8.3) and `GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw` (tar 7.5.2). Also `axios 1.13.2` with two highs.

## What is NOT known — the honest boundary

**Reachability is not cleared, only deferred.** "Not built by compose or CI" is evidence about the BUILD. It is not evidence that the source never ships by another route (a developer build, an app-store pipeline outside this repo, or a tree that is simply dead and should be deleted). **No such sweep was done.**

## Done when

One of, decided rather than defaulted:

1. The tree is **dead** → delete it, and remove the `OUT_OF_SCOPE_LOCKS` entry with it; or
2. The tree is **live** → it comes back into scope, the lock is regenerated, and whatever remains gets measured baseline rows with fuses; or
3. The tree is **dormant but kept** → the exclusion stays, with an owner and a review date recorded here.

Whichever it is, the `OUT_OF_SCOPE_LOCKS` entry is removed or re-justified — an exclusion with no live ticket behind it is the accidental blind spot again, wearing a comment.

title: Frontends: react-router v6 → v7 migration (3 moderate client-runtime advisories — open redirect/XSS, constructor injection)
description:
## Why

Three of the KS-493-baselined advisories sit on `react-router`/`react-router-dom` v6 in the three portal frontends (admin / issuer / verifier) and are **client-runtime** classes, not build tooling:

* GHSA-337j-9hxr-rhxg — arbitrary constructor injection via deserialization (moderate)
* GHSA-wrjc-x8rr-h8h6 — open redirect via backslash in `<Link>`/`useNavigate` (moderate)
* GHSA-jjmj-jmhj-qwj2 — open redirect leading to XSS (moderate)

npm marks the fix as `react-router-dom@7.18.2` with `isSemVerMajor: true` — a v6 → v7 migration, NOT a lockfile bump, so it cannot ride the KS-493 lock-regen wave.

## Scope

* Migrate `frontend/admin`, `frontend/issuer`, `frontend/verifier` from RRD v6 to v7 (route object/API changes, `RouterProvider` shape, relative-path semantics).
* Verify the three portals end-to-end on local + demo after the migration.
* Remove the three GHSA entries from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` in the same PR (gate goes green on real fix, not suppression).

## Links

Parent register: KS-493 (Review H). Baseline entries expire **2026-08-19** — if this migration is not done by then, re-reason those three entries against THIS ticket with a new expiry instead of letting the gate lapse red.

title: [Decision] OAuth consent: a proper two-step MFA challenge on /api/oauth/authorize (the design half of KS-781)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/authorize` **should challenge for the second factor as a proper two-step consent flow, rather than accepting** `mfaCode` **in the same body as the password.** This is the **product-design** half of [KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781); that ticket carries the **security** half.

**Filed deliberately before KS-781 closes.** Wednesday's ruling (2026-09-03): *"a deferral that lives only in a PR comment is a claim that outlives every tracker it names."* This exists so the design question survives the fix.

## The split, and why it is this way round

KS-781 closes a live hole: that route is a second, password-only login with no MFA, no lockout and no status check. **The ruled fix there is minimal — accept** `mfaCode` **in the authorize body, mirroring** `/api/auth/login`**.** Two reasons, both worth preserving here:

1. A security defect must not wait on a design decision.
2. **Mirroring** `login` **keeps ONE MFA semantics across both login routes.** Two different MFA shapes on two login routes would recreate the very class that produced [KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) — paths that must agree, drifting because nothing compares them — while closing a single instance of it.

So the minimal fix is not a stopgap that this ticket replaces in shame; it is the correct first move. This ticket is the upgrade.

## What a proper flow looks like

`POST /api/oauth/authorize` currently does password verification and code issuance in one request, then 302s. A second-factor challenge needs an intermediate state:

1. credentials verified → if `user.mfaEnabled`, **do not** mint an authorization code; return/redirect to an MFA challenge bearing a short-lived, single-use challenge token bound to (user, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, scope, state);
2. the challenge is satisfied (TOTP, or backup code, matching `login`'s semantics);
3. only then mint the authorization code and 302.

**Open questions this ticket exists to answer** — none of them decided:

* Does the challenge render server-side, or does the OAuth client host it? The latter needs the challenge token to be safe to hand to a client.
* **Where does the challenge state live?** Redis with a TTL is the obvious answer and matches the lockout store; it is also a new short-lived-secret surface.
* How does this interact with PKCE (`code_challenge` / `code_challenge_method`) — the challenge token must not become a way to bypass or re-bind PKCE parameters.
* Backup codes: `login` accepts them ([`auth.ts:507-514`](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura>)). Consent should too, or the asymmetry needs stating.
* Rate limiting on the challenge step. [KS-733](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-733) already records that `/api/users/me/mfa/*` is unthrottled and ~450x more attackable than `/api/auth/login` — a new TOTP-accepting surface must not repeat that.

## A coverage note that matters for whatever ships here

[KS-548](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-548) measured why the current defect went unseen: `POST /api/oauth/authorize` declares `security: []`, is one of only **2 operations of 318** declaring a 3xx, and **its 302 path is never exercised** — generated `client_id`/`redirect_uri` values reference no registered client, so it 400s per RFC 6749 first, and Schemathesis has no per-operation don't-follow-redirects switch.

**So this route is structurally invisible to the sweep, and a redirect-based challenge flow adds MORE redirect surface to a route the fuzzers already cannot reach.** Whatever ships here needs its own tests; it will not be caught by the platform suites.

## Not in scope

The three checks themselves (MFA gate, lockout, status refusal) and the shared `assertLoginAllowed` extraction — those are KS-781's.

## Related

[KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781) (the security half — the minimal `mfaCode` fix; **this ticket must not block it**) · [KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) (the class: two paths that must agree) · [KS-548](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-548) (why the sweep cannot reach this route) · [KS-733](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-733) (unthrottled TOTP surface) · [KS-722](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-722) (other shapes on the social handler)

title: Upgrade ip-address off GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (high, SSRF) — express-rate-limit 8.4.1→8.5.1+ in mcp-server, @meshsdk/@cardano-sdk 9.0.5 line in root + frontend/issuer
description:
## BLUF

`ip-address` **is on GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (high, SSRF / trust-boundary bypass; patched in 10.3.1) in three lockfiles.** Two of the three are the *same* root cause and are a **patch-level bump of a different package**; the third is a `@meshsdk` major-version question. This ticket is the live owner of the audit-baseline exception for that advisory (`scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`, `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr`), which now expires **2026-09-30**.

Filed at Peter's request on PR #738 (2026-08-31): the exception previously pointed at KS-559, which is **Done AND archived**, so on expiry the row would be orphaned again — the exact state KS-635 was filed about. KS-635 remains in `reason` as the deciding ref; this ticket is what `ticket` points at, and its due date is set to the row's expiry so the two cannot drift.

## The advisory

```
GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr  —  high
ip-address: Address4 decodes leading-zero octets as decimal while resolvers
decode them as octal, allowing SSRF and trust-boundary bypass
vulnerable: <= 10.3.0        first patched: 10.3.1        published 2026-08-03
```

## Where it actually is — measured, not inferred

Every `package-lock.json` outside `node_modules` was parsed for an `ip-address` entry:

| lockfile | resolved | vulnerable? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `services/mcp-server` | **10.1.0** | ✅ yes |
| root `Blockchain/Dev` | **9.0.5** + 10.4.0 (nested) | ✅ the 9.0.5 |
| `frontend/issuer` | **9.0.5** + 10.4.0 (nested) | ✅ the 9.0.5 |
| `packages/shared` | 10.4.0 | ❌ already patched |
| `services/anchoring` | 10.4.0 | ❌ already patched |

⚠ This corrects the review table on #738 in one place: root and `frontend/issuer` carry **both** 9.0.5 and 10.4.0 — the 10.4.0 copies are nested under `@cardano-sdk/dapp-connector` and `@cardano-sdk/key-management`, which already declare `^10.2.0`. Only the hoisted 9.0.5 is exposed.

## Leg 1 — `services/mcp-server`: a patch bump of `express-rate-limit`, not an `ip-address` override

```
services/mcp-server: express-rate-limit@8.4.1  declares  ip-address: "10.1.0"   <- EXACT pin
```

An `ip-address` override would violate that exact pin. But the pin moved upstream:

| express-rate-limit | declares |
| -- | -- |
| 8.0.2 – 8.5.0 | `ip-address: "10.1.0"` (exact — vulnerable) |
| **8.5.1 – 8.7.0** | `ip-address: "^10.2.0"` → resolves 10.4.0 ≥ 10.3.1 ✅ |

**So the fix is** `express-rate-limit` **8.4.1 → ≥ 8.5.1 (latest 8.7.0) — a patch/minor bump, no override, no major.** The path is already proven inside this repo: the root lock carries `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/node_modules/express-rate-limit@8.5.2`, which declares `^10.2.0` and resolves **10.4.0** today.

*(Instrument note: a first probe read* `express-rate-limit@10.1.0` *as having zero dependencies. It has none because **it does not exist** — the registry 404s it, against a 200 on 8.7.0. The "10.1.0" was the pinned* ip-address *version, not an express-rate-limit version. Corrected before it reached this ticket.)*

## Leg 2 — root + `frontend/issuer`: a `@meshsdk` / `@cardano-sdk` major question

```
node_modules/ip-address = 9.0.5
  declared by @cardano-sdk/core : ip-address ^9.0.5
  reached via @meshsdk/core-cst, @meshsdk/provider, @meshsdk/transaction
```

`^9.0.5` **cannot** reach the 10.x line, so no override satisfies the declared range. Newer `@cardano-sdk/core` — the copies vendored under `@cardano-sdk/dapp-connector` and `@cardano-sdk/key-management` in this same tree — already declare `^10.2.0`. **The fix is bumping** `@meshsdk/*` **so it pulls a** `@cardano-sdk/core` **on the 10.x line.**

This is the same `@meshsdk` family that owns the three **permanent** `undici` acceptances in the baseline (`GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524`, `GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5`, `GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm`, all `frontend/issuer -> @meshsdk -> @utxorpc/sdk -> @connectrpc/connect-node`), and the family behind the multi-pinned `@lucid-evolution` packages on #720. Worth doing as one sweep rather than three.

## Exposure — stated honestly, not minimised

Not assessed in this ticket. The advisory is an SSRF / trust-boundary bypass in `Address4` parsing, and whether any first-party request path reaches it through `@cardano-sdk` has **not** been swept. The baseline row is a time-boxed exception precisely because that sweep was never done — do not read it as a bounded-exposure acceptance the way the `qs` row (KS-531) is.

## Scope

- [ ] **Leg 1:** `services/mcp-server` — `express-rate-limit` 8.4.1 → ≥ 8.5.1; regenerate the standalone lock **in** `node:24-alpine` (host regen drops optional binaries); confirm `ip-address` resolves ≥ 10.3.1.
- [ ] **Leg 2:** root + `frontend/issuer` — `@meshsdk/*` bump onto a `@cardano-sdk/core` 10.x; assess against the undici acceptances and #720's `@lucid-evolution` pins in the same pass.
- [ ] Re-run `node scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` and `node scripts/audit/audit-gate.mjs` — both must exit 0 **with the** `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr` **baseline row removed**, which is the real done-state.
- [ ] Remove the row from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. Its expiry (2026-09-30) is this ticket's due date; if the work slips, the date moves **here** and on the row together, with a reason — never silently.
- [ ] Second instance of the same pattern, out of scope but named: `GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26` (`qs`) is owned by **KS-531, also Done and archived**, expiring 2026-11-11. Flagged on 2026-08-21 and again by Peter on #738. It needs a live owner before that date.

## Refs

* KS-635 — the deciding ref for the date move (`reason` field on the row)
* KS-559 — original owner, **Done AND archived**; lineage only
* PR #738 — the date alignment 2026-08-31 → 2026-09-30 that this ticket unblocks
* KS-531 — the `qs` twin of this pattern
* Advisory: [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr](<https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr>)

*Filed 2026-09-01 (session 94). Every version figure above was read out of the lockfiles and the npm registry in-session, with a firing control on each instrument.*

title: PR #1339's standalone locks were re-resolved from bare manifests: ~1,000 non-target moves, incl. runtime bullmq/msgpackr 2 and @azure/identity/msal-node 6
description:
Raised from **gate41's finding N-1339-2** (Major, non-blocking) on PR #1339 (KS-1378, the four-package advisory bump). Wednesday ruled this a ticket rather than a fold-in for round 2, because the only mechanism the gate's own fix-shape offers is `npm install --package-lock-only`, and host npm 11.5.1 dies with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` on this machine — measured by Seat B 43rd even on a bare `package.json` in an empty temp dir, so it is the host npm build and not the workspace layout.

## What happened

#1339's 13 standalone `package-lock.json` files were regenerated **from their bare manifests** rather than from their committed locks. That resolved every dependency afresh, so about **1,000 versions moved that the bump did not target**. All are inside their declared ranges, so nothing is a range violation — but nothing exercises them either: the suites run from the **root** lock, which moved **0** non-target versions.

## The moves that matter (gate-measured)

* `services/queue`: **bullmq 5.76.2 → 5.81.5**, pulling **msgpackr 1 → 2** — runtime.
* `services/m365-integration` and `packages/shared`: **@azure/identity 4.13.1 → 4.13.3**, pulling **@azure/msal-node 5 → 6** — runtime.
* `services/originate`: minimatch 3 → 10, plus dev-only eslint-cache majors.

## Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from gate41's report

> Fix-shape: regenerate each standalone lock FROM its committed lock (`npm install <pkg>@<ver> --package-lock-only`), or declare the drift and add a standalone-install smoke (build + boot) per service.

## The condition attached to #1339 merging without this

Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat B 44th, 2026-09-29T03:54:40Z: the two runtime moves above **get a clean standalone** `npm ci` **plus that service's own suite in the next gate**, so what ships untested by the root-lock suites is tested once. **Merged is not deployed:** no deploy carries these until this ticket is done or Kam says otherwise.

## Blocked on, and why it is not just "run the command"

`npm install` in any form is unavailable on this host. Seat B 43rd's workaround for #1339 was `node:24-alpine` (npm 11.19.0), mounted at `/src` — **never** `/dev`, which clobbers the container's `/dev/null` and dies rc 127 before starting. Whoever takes this needs either that container route explicitly permitted, or a working host npm.

## Neighbours (cross-reference only)

KS-1290 (an npm command inside a workspace member moves platform discriminators silently) and KS-1154 (the root lock carries only the darwin rollup binary) are the same family — lockfile regeneration doing more than it was asked to — but neither covers this drift.

Discovered 2026-09-29 by gate41 on PR #1339; ticketed by the Platform K build seat under Wednesday's ruling.

title: 13 new advisories block every push: axios 1.18.1 ×12 (7 high — SSRF, proxy bypass, ReDoS, prototype pollution; runtime in services/kyc) and dompurify 3.4.13 — all fixed in range (axios 1.20.0, dompurify 3.4.16)
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 on** `develop`**'s own dependencies again, so no push on this repo succeeds until this lands.** Thirteen advisories published on 2026-09-30 are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`: **twelve against axios 1.18.1 (7 high)** and one against dompurify 3.4.13 (low). **No lock changed to cause this.** No `axios`/`dompurify` line in any lock moved between `377989cf3`, where both legs were rc 0 on 2026-09-30 \~02:45Z, and `4f18c59a8`.

**Every one is fixed inside the declared ranges, so this is a lock refresh, not a manifest bump.** That was checked against each advisory's `vulnerable_versions`, not inferred. `frontend/issuer` already pins axios 1.20.0 / dompurify 3.4.16 and is flagged by neither leg.

Measured at `develop` `4f18c59a8`, twice (2026-09-30 \~22:55Z and 23:11Z, identical ID sets), on Stuart's Mac: `npm run audit:gate` rc 1 (`24 distinct advisories reported, 26 baselined` → 13 NEW); `npm run audit:locks` rc 1 (`1611 distinct packages pinned — 18 advisories match, 6 already baselined` → 12 NEW).

## The thirteen, and the fix version measured for each

Each advisory's `vulnerable_versions` comes from the npm bulk-advisory endpoint, the same data the gates read, and was checked with `semver.satisfies` against both the pinned version and the candidate fix.

| advisory | sev | summary (from the gate) | vulnerable | 1.18.1 | 1.20.0 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-r4gj-5m52-g5wh` | high | `maxRedirects: 0` not enforced by fetch adapter → redirect-based SSRF | `>=1.17.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-mghh-pgcx-3jjj` | high | ReDoS in `shouldBypassProxy`, reachable via untrusted redirect `Location` | `>=1.15.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v` | high | HTTP/2 adapter bypasses configured DNS lookup and proxy controls | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8` | high | DoS via unhandled `error` in HTTP/2 session init | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-c29m-xwm3-cm6r` | high | ReDoS in `fromDataURI` data: URL parser | `>=1.16.1 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` | high | prototype-pollution gadget in `toFormData` options | `>=1.15.1 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-m8m8-qj5v-23w3` | high | Node HTTP adapter prototype-pollution gadget → request socket hijack | `>=1.15.2 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-44g4-m2mj-wpvx` | moderate | CIDR-form `NO_PROXY` entries ignored → proxy exclusion bypass | `>=1.15.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8` | moderate | prototype-pollution gadget in fetch adapter alters outbound requests | `>=1.7.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` | moderate | prototype pollution in default instance overrides HTTP method | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32` | moderate | header injection via inherited headers after minimal interceptor | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2` | moderate | fetch adapter header injection via inherited FormData `getHeaders` | `>=1.12.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p` | low | **dompurify** `IN_PLACE` hook leaves detached event handlers armed → DOM XSS | `>=3.4.13 <=3.4.15` | 3.4.13 VULN | 3.4.16 ok |

## Where, and why a lock refresh reaches it — measured

| lock | pinned | declared range | leg |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `services/kyc` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.8.2` (`dependencies`) | 7 |
| `frontend/admin` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.5` | 7 |
| `frontend/verifier` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.2` | 7 |
| `Blockchain/Dev` root (workspace) | axios 1.18.1 (one copy, hoisted) | admin/issuer/verifier/kyc as above + `@meshsdk/provider` `^1.7.2` | 6 |
| `Blockchain/Dev` root (workspace) | dompurify 3.4.13 | `frontend/issuer` `^3.4.13` | 6 |
| `frontend/issuer` | axios **1.20.0**, dompurify **3.4.16** | — | not flagged |

Every range admits axios 1.20.0 and dompurify 3.4.16, `@meshsdk/provider`'s `^1.7.2` included, so the root lock can stay on a single copy.

`services/kyc` **is runtime exposure, not build-tree only.** axios is in `dependencies`, the image installs with `npm ci --omit=dev` (`services/kyc/Dockerfile:63`), and `src/providers/microsoft-entra-client.ts` imports it for outbound calls. The redirect-SSRF and proxy-bypass rows are the ones to read against that client. Reachability was **not** assessed here. The frontends' exposure (browser bundle vs build tree) was not measured either.

## Done means

1. axios ≥ 1.20.0 in `services/kyc`, `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` and the root lock, and dompurify ≥ 3.4.16 in the root lock. Each lock is regenerated **containerised** (`node:24-alpine`; host npm 11.5.1 dies with `edgesOut`, see [KS-1379](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1379/pr-1339s-standalone-locks-were-re-resolved-from-bare-manifests-1000)), with a no-target control run as [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1358](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1380-15-locks-agree-with-packagesshared-on-types-esc-4199-pg-8231-020075b0edd2) did so that every move is attributable.
2. Legs 6 and 7 green at the PR head with **no** baseline row for any of the thirteen.
3. The `services/kyc` suite and image build at the head, since it is the runtime consumer.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd Blockchain/Dev
npm run audit:gate    # leg 6
npm run audit:locks   # leg 7
```

Found on 2026-09-30 while verifying [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1358](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1380-15-locks-agree-with-packagesshared-on-types-esc-4199-pg-8231-020075b0edd2) ([KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and)) for Stuart. [KS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1395/two-advisories-published-after-ks-1378-block-every-push-again-undici), the previous batch, is closed. This is the next one.

title: Thirteen advisories published 2026-09-30 block every push: axios 1.18.1 in four locks and dompurify 3.4.13 in the workspace root
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 on** `develop`**'s own dependencies, so no push on this repo succeeds until this is triaged.** Thirteen advisories published 2026-09-30 between 15:01:07Z and 15:37:57Z (GitHub advisory API) are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. Measured at `develop` `4f18c59a89db16cb8b06b7850aeb64e6f81f95ee`: `npm run audit:gate` and `npm run audit:locks` from `Blockchain/Dev`, **both rc 1**; `npm run audit:contract` rc 0.

**None of these is one of KS-1378's five**, and none is one of the two KS 1395 names. This is the fourth separate batch since 2026-09-29: KS-1378's five, KS 1395's two, six more cleared by an in-range lock refresh under KS-1378 (Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1356), and these thirteen.

## The thirteen (summaries from the GitHub advisory API)

Twelve are **axios**, every one fixed in **1.20.0** on the 1.x line (`GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` and `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` also name 0.34.0 for the 0.x line, which no lock here uses). Seven high, five moderate (GitHub labels the five `medium`):

| advisory | sev | summary |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-c29m-xwm3-cm6r` | high | ReDoS in the `fromDataURI` `data:` URL parser freezes the Node event loop |
| `GHSA-mghh-pgcx-3jjj` | high | ReDoS (O(N²)) in `shouldBypassProxy` host normalization, reachable via untrusted redirect `Location` |
| `GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` | high | Prototype pollution gadget in `toFormData` options |
| `GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v` | high | HTTP/2 adapter bypasses the configured DNS lookup and proxy controls |
| `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8` | high | DoS via an unhandled `error` event in HTTP/2 `ClientHttp2Session` initialization |
| `GHSA-m8m8-qj5v-23w3` | high | Node HTTP adapter prototype-pollution gadget allows request socket hijack via inherited `createConnection` |
| `GHSA-r4gj-5m52-g5wh` | high | `maxRedirects: 0` is not enforced by the fetch adapter, allowing redirect-based SSRF |
| `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8` | moderate | Prototype pollution gadget in the fetch adapter can alter outbound requests |
| `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` | moderate | Prototype-pollution gadget in the default instance allows an inherited `Object.prototype` method to override the HTTP method |
| `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32` | moderate | Header injection via inherited `headers` after a minimal interceptor |
| `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2` | moderate | Fetch adapter header injection via inherited `FormData` `getHeaders` |
| `GHSA-44g4-m2mj-wpvx` | moderate | CIDR-form `NO_PROXY` entries are ignored, causing proxy exclusion bypass for internal IP ranges |

One is **dompurify** `GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p` (low): `IN_PLACE` node-removing `afterSanitize` hook leaves detached subtree event handlers armed, causing DOM XSS. Vulnerable `>= 3.4.13, <= 3.4.15`; `first_patched_version` **3.4.16**.

## Where they are pinned — measured across all 45 tracked locks at `develop`, not assumed

| lock | axios | dompurify |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (workspace root) | **1.18.1** | **3.4.13** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/package-lock.json` | **1.18.1** | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/verifier/package-lock.json` | **1.18.1** | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/package-lock.json` | **1.18.1** | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/package-lock.json` | 1.20.0 (already patched) | 3.4.16 (already patched) |
| `systemTest/akto/package-lock.json` | 1.20.0 (already patched) | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app/package-lock.json` | 1.13.2 (inside six of the twelve ranges; see below) | — |

No other tracked lock pins either package.

**Four locks need the change, not the three leg 7 names.** The workspace root lock pins both packages and is covered by leg 6, not leg 7. `mobile/secuura-app` is out of scope under KS 769 (expires 2026-10-19), and leg 7 excludes it under that ruling.
