Its axios 1.13.2 sits inside six of the twelve axios ranges (`GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v`, `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8`, `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8`, `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g`, `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32`, `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2`). After the refresh, that is the only copy of any of the thirteen left in the 45 tracked locks, and it is KS 769's to decide.

**Why leg 7 never reported the dompurify advisory:** leg 7 scans the 43 standalone locks, and the only standalone copy of dompurify is `frontend/issuer`'s, which is already at the patched 3.4.16. The vulnerable copy is in the workspace root lock, which is leg 6's. Both instruments are behaving correctly.

## The route — an in-range lock refresh, not a manifest bump

Every affected manifest already admits the patched version, so no `package.json` changes:

* `frontend/admin` declares `axios ^1.6.5`
* `frontend/verifier` declares `axios ^1.6.2`
* `services/kyc` declares `axios ^1.8.2`
* `frontend/issuer` declares `dompurify ^3.4.13` (the root lock's copy is the workspace hoist of this)

Neither package is declared at the workspace root itself. The refresh is Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1363: those five lock entries move and nothing else. Each moved axios entry also records axios 1.20.0's own `form-data ^4.0.6` range; form-data 4.0.6 was already locked everywhere.

## Reachability

* `services/kyc`: **one** source file imports `axios` (`src/providers/microsoft-entra-client.ts`). A real service path, and the image ships `node_modules`.
* `frontend/admin`: **zero** source files import `axios`. `frontend/verifier`: **zero**. Declared but unused; their final images are nginx plus the built `dist/`, and the builder stage is discarded.
* `frontend/issuer/src/utils/sanitize.ts` imports `dompurify`. **No test anywhere covers that file** — searched `frontend/`, `services/` and `packages/` for a spec naming `sanitize` or `dompurify`.

## Done means

1. Legs 6 and 7 both rc 0 at the PR head, with `audit:contract` still rc 0, and **no baseline row added, removed or changed** (26 baselined before and after).
2. Each of the thirteen advisories shown absent from both legs, against the lock entry that cleared it.
3. Every lock move proved by `cmp` plus a lock parse against a pristine control tree at the same base — never by npm's `up to date` banner, which has read as success on this repo before while nothing moved.
4. Locks regenerated containerised in `node:24-alpine`, with the container's npm version recorded.
5. The images and suites that consume the moved locks built and run.

## Not in scope

* The three frontends declare no `test` script at all, so "suites before and after" cannot be satisfied for them — that is KS 1391.
* `services/kyc`'s suite needs `packages/shared` built first, or one file fails to load with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@secuura/shared"`. That is the same class as the stale-`packages/shared/dist` entry at `BACKLOG.md:6`: there the dist is stale, here it is absent.
* The fourteen grandfathered dead baseline rows (thirteen undici plus `GHSA-v2v4-37r5-5v8g`) among the fifteen entries leg 6's cleanup list names on every run; the fifteenth, `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr` (KS 729), is not grandfathered.

title: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler and a 267 MB dev tree into all 24 runtime images — KS-490 closed the service tree only
description:
## KS-490 closed the SERVICE tree and left the SHARED tree open — `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into all 24 runtime images

KS-490's two PRs (#849, #851) removed the build toolchain from the runtime *stages* and pruned each service's *own* `node_modules`. **Neither touches** `/shared`, and every runtime stage copies it wholesale.

### Measured on the live demo box, in RUNNING containers

| Reading | `secuura-security` | `secuura-governance` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/shared/node_modules/typescript` | **present, 22.9 MB** | **present, 22.9 MB** |
| `bin/tsc` | **present** | **present** |
| `/shared` total | **267.2 MB** | **267.2 MB** |
| top-level entries under `/shared/node_modules` | **243** | **243** |

*(The #851 gate's tester reported 342 packages; I counted **243 top-level entries** with* `ls | wc -l`*, which counts a scoped* `@org` *directory once regardless of what it contains. Both numbers are probably right about different things — stating my instrument rather than reconciling them by assertion.)*

### It is footprint and attack surface, NOT loadability — measured, with a control

```
require.resolve('typescript', {paths:['/app']})  ->  MODULE_NOT_FOUND
require.resolve('express',    {paths:['/app']})  ->  resolves
```

The control is what makes the first line meaningful: the resolver works, and `typescript` genuinely is not reachable from the app's module paths. So no runtime code can load it — but a compiler binary and 267 MB of dev tree are present in every running container, which is exactly what KS-490 exists to remove.

### Cause

`shared-builder` runs `npm ci` **without** `--omit=dev` and is never pruned, and all 24 runtime stages `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared`.

### Fix shape — and the hazard it carries

Prune `shared-builder` after its build: one place, all 24 services.

⚠ **This is exactly the hazard #851 just fixed.** `@secuura/shared` is a hand-made undeclared symlink; pruning removed it, and three runtime stages that did not re-create it shipped images that crashed on start with `Cannot find module '@secuura/shared'`. **A** `/shared` **prune therefore needs a real start probe per service, not reasoning** — the same shape of evidence #851 ended up needing. See [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) and #851's fix commit.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #851's gate findings (F1).*

title: The e2e-v2 harness is platform-k's only browser, portal and accessibility coverage — 222 tests, runnable by hand, named in no gate and absent from the gate inventory
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/` holds **24 spec files and 222 tests** across four tiers — including every browser journey and the only accessibility coverage platform-k has — and it is wired into nothing. It is not in `.githooks/pre-push`, it has no row in the "Manual CI-gate equivalents" table that `KS-685` commissioned, and the workflow its own README points at (`.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`) does not exist on `develop`. Meanwhile the suite people *are* pointed at, `systemTest/playwright`, is API-only: 3 spec files, 11 tests, no browser. So the documented estate says platform-k has a Playwright tier, and the thing that actually opens a browser is the one nobody is told to run. Counted on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026. Nothing was executed — this is about wiring, not results.

## What is there

Measured from the tree, not from the docs:

| Tier | Specs | Tests | What it covers |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `tier1-api` | 12 | 174 | API over HTTP |
| `tier2-smoke` | 5 | 43 | Smoke journeys |
| `tier3-e2e` | 4 | 40 | **Real browser journeys** — issuer, admin, verifier |
| `tier4-a11y` | 3 | 6 | **axe on admin, issuer and verifier** |
| **Total** | **24** | **222** |  |

It is runnable today. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` declares `test`, `test:api`, `test:smoke`, `test:e2e`, `test:a11y`, `install:browsers` and `report`, and `playwright.config.ts` defines the four matching projects (`api`, `smoke`, `e2e`, `a11y`). `@axe-core/playwright` is a devDependency there.

## What is missing

1. **No gate names it.** `grep -rn "e2e-v2" .githooks/pre-push Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` returns nothing. The manual-gate table at `DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` maps *former CI job → local command* for 13 rows and has no row for e2e-v2, and none for accessibility at all.
2. **Its README cites a workflow that does not exist.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` sends the reader to `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`; `git ls-tree origin/develop .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is empty.
3. **The plan doc under-reports it.** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` still says *"only the verifier portal has a tier-4 spec. Issuer + admin coverage is a follow-up."* That follow-up is `KS-44`, which is **Done** — there are three tier-4 specs in the tree today. The row understates the coverage that exists.

## Why it matters

* It is the whole UI answer. Without it the honest statement about platform-k is that no browser opens anywhere in the estate — `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` says so itself, and `DEV-PROCESS.md:141` spells it out: *"Despite the name, this suite drives no browser… Read a green here as '12 API assertions passed', not as 'the portals work'."*
* It is the whole accessibility answer. There is no `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` anywhere in the repo and no axe inside any frontend, so `tier4-a11y` is the only thing that would catch a regression against WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549 — relevant to the same obligations the platform-s side tracks. WCAG 2.2: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549 v3.2.1: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA Directive 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>)
* An ungated suite rots quietly. `KS-557` / `KS-560` are the precedent — the tier reported 126 failures, of which only 11 were real, and the cause was a harness defect that had gone unnoticed. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` keeps that lesson as a standing rule.
* Actions being retired makes this the *only* route to the coverage, not a redundant one.

## Suggested shape

1. Give e2e-v2 a row in the `DEV-PROCESS.md` manual-gate table: the exact command, the pass criterion, and a measured wall-clock — matching the 13 rows already there.
2. Decide the tier split deliberately. `tier4-a11y` is 6 tests and needs only a running stack; it is the cheapest thing in the estate to make routine. `tier3-e2e` is slower and flakier (single-session collisions, `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md` § "Worker-session collisions") so it may belong in a nightly/manual tier rather than a per-push one.
3. Fix the two stale pointers: the dead workflow reference in `tests/e2e/README.md:4`, and the tier-4 row in `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` that `KS-44` has already overtaken.
4. Say in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` where the browser tier actually lives, so "Playwright" stops meaning two different things in the same repo.

## Acceptance

* `DEV-PROCESS.md`'s gate table has an e2e-v2 row (or rows) with a command and a measured time.
* A named person can run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source.
* No document points at `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`, and the tier-4 row reflects the three specs that exist.

## Decision needed before fixing — naming the three Playwright estates

Worth settling the naming in the same pass: `systemTest/playwright` (API-only, 11 tests) and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2` (browser, 222 tests) are both "Playwright", and a third corpus sits at `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` (`KS-734`, In Review — not a workspace member, cannot install from a clean checkout; `KS-1038`, Backlog — races its own lockout). Three Playwright estates with one name is the reason a reader can believe the portals are covered when the suite in the gate never opens a browser. One decision about which survives, which is gated, and what each is called would close this ticket and shrink two others.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` · `playwright.config.ts:29-73` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, `:141` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:316-345` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` · `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` · related: `KS-1076` (Urgent, Todo — no Playwright e2e on a PR since 7 Sep), `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-44` (Done), `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-685`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — no stack started, no suite executed; all counts measured from the tree at that commit. GitHub Actions executes nothing on this repo (billing), so no workflow is a live alternative to the local route.

title: Repo hygiene: 31 spec files under Blockchain/Dev/tests that no Playwright config covers, 708 branches on the remote, and a duplicated website package a major React version behind
description:
## BLUF

Three separate bits of accumulated debt, none urgent, all cheap to decide and none of which anyone will notice until it misleads someone. Grouped because they are one afternoon together and three tickets apart. Measured on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026 — branch count taken from the GitHub API, not the local clone, which is shallow here.

| \# | Where | Seen | Suggest |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` | **31 spec files** sitting directly in that directory, covered by no Playwright config. The repo has exactly three configs — `systemTest/playwright` (`testDir: ./tests`), `tests/e2e-v2` (`testDir: ./tests/tierN`), `tests/e2e` (`testDir: ./tests`) — and none of them resolves to `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` itself. Names read as exploratory leftovers: `admin-sidebar-collapse-{test,fresh,final}.spec.ts`, `issuer-portal-{quick,full,detailed,complete}.spec.ts`, several near-identical variants of one check | Delete, or move the ones worth keeping into `tests/e2e-v2/tests/tierN/` where a config can see them |
| 2 | The remote | **708 branches** (`gh api repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/branches --paginate`), of which 706 are neither `main` nor `develop`. The oldest carry no commit since March; ten are Dependabot branches whose PRs are open and stale | Prune merged and abandoned branches. Worth agreeing a rule — delete-on-merge, plus a sweep for anything with no commit in N months |
| 3 | `secuura-website-package/` | A hand-off bundle whose `source/` duplicates `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/` under the **same package name** `@secuura/website` v1.0.0, drifted to React 18 / Vite 5 / eslint 8 against the live copy's React 19 / Vite 8 / eslint 10; `diff -rq` over the two `src/` trees reports 19 differing files. Nothing outside itself references it — no compose service, no CI, no script | Decide: is it a deliverable that should be generated from `frontend/website` on demand, or dead weight? Either way it should not be a second copy of a shipped app under the same name |

## Why it matters

Each one is a small lie the repository tells a reader.

* **Row 1** — 31 files named `*.spec.ts` look like test coverage. They are not run by anything, cannot fail, and sit next to `tests/e2e`, `tests/e2e-v2` and `tests/connectors`, which are real. Someone counting specs to answer "how well is the admin portal covered?" gets a wrong answer. Same class as `KS-718`, where gitignored snapshots meant a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed.
* **Row 2** — 706 stale branches makes `git branch -r` useless for finding live work and slows every clone and fetch. It also hides the ten stale Dependabot branches behind noise.
* **Row 3** — two packages with the same name and different major versions of React is the shape that produces "it works in my build" confusion. `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` is the only place that mentions it, so nothing in the live docs explains why it exists.

None of this is a defect in the running platform, which is why Low.

## Suggested shape

1. Row 1 is a judgement call per file, but the duplicated-variant names (`-quick`, `-full`, `-detailed`, `-complete`, `-fresh`, `-final`) suggest most can go. Anything worth keeping earns a home under a config; anything else is deleted in one commit.
2. Row 2: agree the retention rule first, then sweep once. GitHub's automatic delete-on-merge setting would stop the recurrence.
3. Row 3: if the bundle is a customer deliverable, generate it from `frontend/website` at release time and stop tracking the copy. If it is not, delete it.

## Acceptance

* Every `*.spec.ts` in the repo is either reachable from a Playwright config or gone.
* Branch count is back to something a person can read, and the rule that keeps it there is written down.
* `@secuura/website` names exactly one package.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest doing row 1 together with `KS-1390` (the e2e-v2 harness is in no gate) and `KS-734` (the `tests/e2e` corpus cannot install from a clean checkout) rather than separately — all three are about which Playwright corpus is real, and the answer to "which of these three trees survives" settles all of them at once. Row 2 is independent and can go any time.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` (31 files) · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` · `secuura-website-package/source/package.json` vs `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/package.json` · `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` · related: `KS-1390`, `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-718` (Done).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — file counts and the package comparison read from the tree at that commit; the branch total came from the GitHub API because the local clone is shallow and its own count differs. Nothing was executed and nothing was deleted.

title: Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation
description:
> ## ✅ F-9 RESOLVED — added 2026-08-17. **The row is FALSE at the live edge: all three portals already serve their own CSP. Do NOT add one at the gateway — it would break them.**
>
> **F-9 is closed on this ticket. KS-491 itself stays OPEN** for the two rows that are still live: the **strategic WAF gap** and the **absent Caddyfile**.
>
> ### 1. The claim, tested at the internet-facing edge
>
> Three read-only GETs against `https://secuura02-demo.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com`:
>
> | Path | CSP served? | Distinguishing directive |
> | -- | -- | -- |
> | `/` (issuer) | **yes** | `script-src … 'unsafe-eval'` — issuer only |
> | `/admin/` | **yes** | `connect-src … wss://*.secuura.io` — admin only |
> | `/verify/` | **yes** | `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.secuura.io https://secuura.io` |
>
> **They differ from one another, and that difference is the discriminator.** A single `add_header` at the gateway would make all three byte-identical. Control: `/api/health` returns a **fourth, different** CSP from the API service — so a CSP on this host is not a gateway-wide artefact.
>
> Source side agrees: **8** `Content-Security-Policy` occurrences across `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin,outlook-addin}/nginx.conf`, and the gateway does **not** `proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy`, so downstream policies pass through untouched. It *does* hide-and-re-add `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and HSTS — which is why those five are gateway-owned and CSP is not. The file is internally consistent.
>
> ### 2. The gateway's abstention is a decision, and it is NEWER than this row
>
> `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf:240-245`, immediately above the live header block:
>
> > *"CSP is DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE. It is app-specific — issuer, admin and verifier each ship their own — and a single generic policy at the gateway would either be too loose to be worth having or would break a portal. Owning it here would also silently override a tighter downstream policy. That stays with the apps; tracked as its own decision, not smuggled in."*
>
> `git log -S"DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE"` attributes it to exactly one commit — `045c658ec`**, 2026-08-13, "KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge…" (#678)** — the same hardening pass that fixed F-2, F-6 and F-7. Sentinel control returns empty. **The missing gateway CSP is not an oversight this review caught; it is a decision the F-remediation took afterwards, in writing.**
>
> ### 3. Why "just add one" is actively harmful, not merely redundant
>
> Two `Content-Security-Policy` headers are **not merged**. Each policy is enforced independently, so a resource must satisfy **both** — the effective policy is the **intersection**. Intersecting the commented-out `:595` policy against what admin actually serves:
>
> | directive | `:595` policy | admin's live policy | effective | consequence |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `connect-src` | `'self' https://*.blockfrost.io` | `'self' http://localhost:* https://*.secuura.io wss://*.secuura.io` | `'self'` | **admin's XHR/WebSocket blocked** |
> | `script-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` | `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` | `'self'` | **wasm blocked, all three portals** |
> | `img-src` | `'self' data: https:` | `'self' data: https: blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob images blocked** |
> | `worker-src` | absent → falls back to `script-src` | `'self' blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob workers blocked** |
>
> That is the portal-breaking outcome the in-file comment predicts, arrived at independently.
>
> ### 4. Recorded so it is not re-derived
>
> Two things stated explicitly because a later reader will otherwise repeat the work:
>
> * `frame-ancestors` **is NOT part of the breakage.** It does not fall back to `default-src`, so an unspecified `frame-ancestors` in a gateway policy leaves each portal's own value governing. An earlier note of mine claimed otherwise; it was wrong and the four rows above stand without it.
> * `outlook-addin` **is not routed through this gateway** (0 matches for `outlook` in `nginx-demo.conf`), so its policy is unaffected either way.
>
> ### 5. The real question this surfaced → **KS-648**
>
> The policies exist and are well-formed, but two directives are weak: `'unsafe-eval'` **on the issuer alone** (the other two manage on `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) and `'unsafe-inline'` **styles on all three**. That is an app-level quality question, exactly as the in-file comment says — filed as [KS-648](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-648), Low, in the Security Review project. **Not** part of F-9.
>
> *Established read-only: three GETs,* `git log -S`*, and greps over the tree. No code changed, nothing deployed, no probe whose success path writes. F-9's deploy authorisation was retired rather than released.*

---

> ## ⚠️ STATUS BANNER — added 2026-08-16. **The table below says "0** `limit_req`**, 0** `client_max_body_size`**". That is now FALSE, and the fix is CONFIRMED LIVE ON THE VM.**
>
> **This resolves the open question of whether F's edge hardening was merged-but-undeployed. It is deployed.** Established read-only, with no rate-limit or body-cap probe against the live demo.
>
> ### F-2 / F-7 — fixed in code **and live**
>
> | Measure | Register says | Repo today | **Running container** |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `limit_req` | **0** | **9** | **9** |
> | `limit_conn` | 0 | **4** | — |
> | `client_max_body_size` | **0** | **12m** (`:215`) | — |
>
> **The proof that it is live, rather than merely merged:**
>
> * `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` on the VM is **byte-identical to the repo copy** — md5 `8be17f5b075d51a170269cd404dc6a87` on both.
> * The **running** `secuura-nginx-gateway` **container** serves `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` at the **same md5**, so this is the config nginx actually loaded, not just a file sitting on the host disk.
> * Ordering closes it: conf mtime `2026-08-13T00:09:07Z`, container start `2026-08-14T05:06:57Z` — **the container started after the file's last modification**, so it cannot be serving an older copy. `nginx -t` passes.
>
> This matters because **the conf is bind-mounted, not baked into the image** — an image rebuild proves nothing about it either way, which is exactly why the merge alone was not evidence. Shipped by KS-613/#678 and KS-616/#679.
>
> ### Why the earlier "unestablished" reading was right at the time
>
> A single GET returns HSTS, CSP and `X-Frame-Options`, and **none of those discriminate**: the CSP cannot come from this conf (its own is commented out — see below), and Caddy terminates TLS in front, making HSTS unattributable. **Reading the mounted file was the check that discriminates**; the header response was not.
>
> ### Still open
>
> * **F-9 partial — CSP is still commented out at** `nginx-demo.conf:595`**.** `X-Frame-Options` and HSTS are active; the CSP line is inert. Verified today.
> * The **strategic Crit row (no WAF anywhere)** stands unchanged — it is a greenfield gap, not a stale row.
> * **Caddyfile still absent from the repo**, so the TLS edge remains unversioned.
>
> *Banner added during the session-38 closure sweep. Ticket left **open** for F-9's CSP, the WAF row, and the Caddyfile.*

---

Work-stream **F** of the [Platform K security review](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485>). Forward-looking edge & resilience posture for a millions-of-users, continuously-attacked target. Largely a **gap analysis** — what's ABSENT matters as much as what's present. Recon complete on `develop` @ `fcf2d878c`.

**Scope / checklist**

* WAF: is any WAF present (nginx ModSecurity / Front Door / App Gateway WAF / Cloudflare)? Where would it integrate? (Product owner explicitly wants WAF.)
* Edge config: nginx gateway + Caddy — security headers, request-size limits, timeouts, TLS.
* Rate limiting / DDoS: edge + app tier; connection/request caps; Slowloris/large-body.
* Bot / anti-automation: CAPTCHA on signup/login/verify.
* Secret manager (runtime) & observability/alerting; network segmentation of infra services.

## Findings / recommendations (develop @ fcf2d878c)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere — no ModSecurity, no Front Door/App Gateway WAF; Cloudflare is DNS-only (grey-cloud), so no Cloudflare WAF. Greenfield. Integration point: in front of Caddy (Front Door WAF) or a ModSecurity sidecar at the gateway. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` (0 `limit_req`, 0 `client_max_body_size`) | The **live** gateway conf has no edge rate-limit and no request-body cap. The hardened `nginx-production.conf:21-22,216` (10r/s, 2r/s auth, `client_max_body_size 10m`) is for the **decommissioned** Container Apps path only — never runs today. Port these to the live conf. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | The actual TLS edge (Caddy on the VM) is **not version-controlled** → TLS ciphers/protocols, HSTS, timeouts, body limits unauditable and drift-prone. Commit the Caddyfile. |
| High | `docker-compose.yml:63-64` (`6432:5432`), `:118-119` (`6379:6379`) | Postgres + Redis publish to host `0.0.0.0` ("remove in production" comments, but active). On the VM these are internet-reachable unless the NSG/ufw blocks them — relies on an external firewall, not config. Bind to the internal network. |
| High | repo-wide absent | **No** CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile on signup, login, or public verify. Only IP/velocity limits stand between a botnet and account/verify abuse. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on error; if Redis is down the per-client counter degrades to per-replica in-memory (inflated ceiling — [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` (no `limit_conn`/`client_body_timeout`/`client_header_timeout`) | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |
| Low | `nginx-demo.conf` (no active HSTS/CSP `add_header`) | Gateway emits no security headers of its own; relies wholly on downstream helmet + Caddy. Single point of omission if a service skips helmet. |

**GREEN (verified):** app-tier defence is real and layered — `express-rate-limit` global limiter (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:448`, 300/min prod), per-route login (15/15min, `:849`), register (`:861`), verification (`:469`) limiters; per-API-key distributed Redis limiter (`rateLimitEnforce.ts`); **application-level account lockout** on login (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:285-303`). Helmet provides per-service CSP + HSTS + nosniff. A standalone `observability/` module exists. The pen-tested `nginx-production.conf` is a strong hardening template — it just isn't the config in production.

**Acceptance:** WAF introduced at the edge; live gateway/Caddy config carries rate-limits/body-caps/headers; pg/redis bound internal; bot protection on public auth/verify; each with a verification test where feasible (Review G). Several items here are **new-build recommendations**, not code defects — track as remediation issues with owners.

title: Unauthenticated /system/status, /api/system/status and /api/system/health/dashboard publish internal service URLs, ports, versions and which third-party keys are unset
description:
## BLUF

* **Three gateway routes answer 200 with no credential and publish a map of the platform's internals:** `GET /system/status`, `GET /api/system/status` and `GET /api/system/health/dashboard`.
* **What the bodies carry:**
  * internal service URLs and ports (`http://auth:4003`, `http://anchoring:4005`, …);
  * service versions;
  * gateway uptime, Node version and environment (`development`);
  * which third-party keys are unset (Blockfrost, Stripe and WalletConnect reported "missing").
* **Measured on kintsugi, an internet-reachable host.** Pre-existing, found by the kintsugi deploy gate on `4554b25e2` (finding F-3, Minor).

## Recommendation

* **The fix:** gate these routes behind admin auth, or serve a public variant with hosts, ports, versions and key state stripped.
* **Keep** `/status/` **working.** The public `/status/` page reads `/system/status`, so the fix has to keep that page working. The page's other defects are on KS-864.

## Detail

* **Probed by the gate** 2026-09-11 22:55:20–22:55:22Z, with no credential; all three returned 200. Bodies are in `evidence/wire/h2_*.body`.
* **Oracle:** statutes and standards, following the audit's own F-04 reasoning about attack-surface maps. The spec side of F-04 is on KS-491.
* **Related, not graded by the gate:** Swagger UI and the raw spec are public on kintsugi (`ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS` on).
  * The gateway comment allows that on a dev portal, but the host is internet-reachable.
  * KS-658 covers the same guard on the demo VM.

### Evidence

* **Report:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-kintsugi-deploy-4554b25e2-tier1-r1/report.md`, section `### F-3 — Unauthenticated status endpoints publish internal topology`.

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive census over all 1,089 KS issues (682 archived; title and description) and 2,946 comments (includeArchived), run 2026-09-12 by s188. Per-ticket comment counts equal direct API reads on 9 of 9 tickets.
* **Hits:**
  * `health/dashboard`: 6 (all archived, schema work)
  * `/system/status`: 5 (4 archived; KS-487's is an XSS payload)
  * `http://auth:4003`: 1 (archived)
  * `attack-surface`: 3 (1 archived; KS-491 and KS-658 concern the spec and the docs guard, not these routes)
* **Result:** no existing home.

title: Published spec points integrators at 18 URLs on domains we do not own (one is for sale) — E1 only inspects emails, never URLs
description:
## BLUF

**The published OpenAPI spec points integrators at 18 URLs on two domains Secuura does not own — one of which is currently for sale.** The guard rule that fixtures.ts names as enforcing our domain policy (**E1**) only ever inspects **email addresses**; it does not look at URLs at all, so this has never been checkable.

The sharpest instance is one line:

```yaml
# components.schemas.AnalyticsExport.example
url: https://exports.secuura.com/exp_01HC9ZQ2ABCDEFGHIJKLMN/document...
```

`secuura.com` is **not ours**. The project `CLAUDE.md` records it as *"not owned (parked for sale on Afternic/GoDaddy; **do not link to it**)"* — and the customer-facing API documentation links to it, on the field a client reads to fetch a completed analytics export.

## Measured

Every URL appearing inside an `example:` block in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, by host:

| host | count | status |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `api.example.com` | 6 | fine — RFC 2606 reserved |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | `secuura.io` is not a domain we control |
| `exports.secuura.com` | **1** | **not owned; parked for sale** |

`fixtures.ts` already states the policy and the reason, for emails:

> *"*`secuura.io` *is not a domain we are known to control (we hold [secuura.ai](<http://secuura.ai>) and [secuura.net](<http://secuura.net>)), so publishing it in customer-facing docs points integrators at third-party infrastructure. Enforced by guard rule E1."*

The policy is right. The enforcement claim is not.

The 17 `example.secuura.io` occurrences span **12 schemas**: `OAuthAppCreateRequest` (redirect URIs), `WebhookCreateRequest`, `WebhookUpdateRequest`, `M365TeamsWebhookConfigRequest`, `M365CompleteConnectionRequest`, `M365AddSiteRequest`, `BillingCheckoutBundleRequest`, `BillingCheckoutCustomRequest`, `BillingCheckoutSessionResponse`, `DidService`, `DidCreateRequest`, `DidUpdateRequest`.

Note what those fields are: OAuth **redirect URIs**, **webhook delivery targets**, and **billing checkout** URLs. If a domain we do not own is documented as the canonical shape for a redirect target, the failure mode is not cosmetic.

## Why the guard never caught it — the mechanism

`scripts/spec-examples/check/rules-global.mjs:67-77`:

```js
/** E1 — an address outside the single reserved example domain. */
function checkEmailDomain(text, docPath, allow, findings) {
  for (const match of text.match(EMAIL_RE) ?? []) {
    const domain = match.split('@')[1].toLowerCase();
    ...
```

It iterates `EMAIL_RE` matches and splits on `@`. A bare URL produces no match, so it is never examined. E1 is an *email*-domain rule wearing a *domain*-rule name — which is exactly why fixtures.ts's "Enforced by guard rule E1" reads as covering more than it does.

The gate is green today (`check:openapi` PASS, 394 example blocks, *"every published example resolves to the fixture set"*) **with all 18 of these published**, so a passing run is not evidence here.

## Recommendation

1. **Add a URL-host rule to the global rules** (an E-rule sibling of E1) accepting only RFC 2606 reserved hosts plus an explicit allow-list of domains we actually own (`secuura.ai`, `secuura.net`). Anything else fails the gate. This is the piece that makes the rest stay fixed.
2. **Add** `FX.webhookUrl` **/** `FX.redirectUri` **/** `FX.exportUrl` on `example.com`, and repoint all 18. Needs the matching accept-list entry in `scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs` — the duplication trap recorded on KS-665.
3. **Fix** `exports.secuura.com` **first and separately** if 1–2 will not land quickly. It is one line, and it is the one pointing at a domain a third party can currently buy.

## Relationship to other tickets

* **KS-665** carries an open *"webhook example URL"* decision from the KS-256 §4 review — *"*`POST /api/webhooks` *publishes a URL the API refuses because the host cannot resolve, and fixing it collides with E1's reserved-domain rule."* This ticket supersedes the framing of that item: it is not one example needing a judgement call, it is **18 across 13 schemas with no guard coverage**, and there is no collision with E1 because E1 never sees URLs.
* **KS-256 / PR #568** is the branch these examples were generated on. **No change is requested there** — the branch is reviewed and waiting on sign-off, and this predates it in kind.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — measured by walking every `example:`/`examples:` block and extracting URLs by host.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/spec-examples/check/rules-global.mjs:60-77` — `applyGlobalRules` and `checkEmailDomain`; no URL inspection anywhere in E1–E4.
* `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/openapi/examples/fixtures.ts` — `EXAMPLE_DOMAIN`, and the comment claiming E1 enforcement.
* Project `CLAUDE.md` — `secuura.com` not owned, "do not link to it".

Found while working KS-665 item 2.

title: ci.yml's contract job cannot work — all three Aiken steps use `contracts/secuura` from the repo root, where no such directory exists; deploy-demo.yml has the same steps correct
description:
## BLUF

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds and tests the Aiken contracts with `cd contracts/secuura`, relative to the repo root. There is no `contracts/` at the repo root — the project is at `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` — and the workflow sets no `working-directory` and no `defaults.run.working-directory`. All three steps are wrong the same way: `aiken build` (`:205-208`), `aiken check` (`:210-213`), and the artifact path `contracts/secuura/plutus.json` (`:219`). The job would fail on the first `cd`. Latent today because Actions executes nothing on this repo, and wrong the moment it returns. The fix already exists in the tree: `deploy-demo.yml` does the identical steps with `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura`. Verified on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Aiken appears in exactly two workflows, and they disagree.

**Broken —** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :207  — no such directory from the repo root
          aiken build

      - name: Run contract tests
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :212
          aiken check

      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: contracts/secuura/plutus.json   # :219
```

`grep -n "working-directory\|defaults:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, so there is no job-level default to rescue the relative path.

**Correct —** `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:84-100`, same steps:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Run contract tests
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json
```

So this is a straight port of a fix that was already made once, into the file that did not get it.

## Why it matters

The contracts are the best-covered thing in platform-k and the least exercised. Measured on this commit: **10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks**, including property/fuzz modules built on `aiken-lang/fuzz` v2.2.0 (`contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23`). The only routes to running them are:

* `ci.yml` — broken as above, and dispatch-only anyway (`on: workflow_dispatch`, header *"CI/CD PIPELINE (DISABLED — DEPLOY VIA CURSOR)"*).
* `deploy-demo.yml` — correct, but fenced behind an explicit opt-in input because it targets the Azure Container Apps estate that was deleted in the 2026-07-08 cost pivot (`:35-39`, `:52-70`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` — by hand, as a deploy prerequisite.

`KS-637` (Backlog, High) already records that the nightly Internal Audit has failed 40 runs straight and that *"the Aiken tests run nowhere else"*. This ticket is the narrower, immediately-fixable half: even if a runner came back tomorrow, the general-purpose job would still fail on the `cd`, so the contract tests would still not run. On-chain validators are the one area where a regression is unrecoverable after deploy — `KS-246` (Backlog) holds the external Aiken audit as the mainnet-readiness gate, and an audit is worth much less if the suite it rests on has no working automated home.

## Suggested shape

1. Port `deploy-demo.yml`'s shape into `ci.yml`: `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` on both run steps, and `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json` as the artifact path. Three lines.
2. Consider a job-level `defaults.run.working-directory` if other steps in that job are also root-relative — worth a read of the whole job rather than patching three lines blind.
3. While there: `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` instructs the reader to `cd /Volumes/KK_DEV_Local/NEW STRUCTURE/…`, a former machine's absolute path, and recommends `aiken test` where every script and workflow in the repo uses `aiken check`. Same defect class — a documented path that cannot work anywhere but one laptop.
4. Add a contracts row to the manual-gate table in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, which has none, so `aiken check` has a named local home while Actions is down.

## Acceptance

* `ci.yml`'s contract job reaches `aiken check` from a clean checkout — provable today by running the same commands locally from the repo root, without needing a runner.
* `TESTING.md` contains no machine-specific absolute path and names `aiken check`.
* `DEV-PROCESS.md` lists the contract command with its measured wall-clock, like the 13 rows already there.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Recommend one grep across `.github/workflows/` for every root-relative `cd ` and every `path:` in an upload step, rather than fixing this instance alone. The repo moved to the `Blockchain/Dev/` layout at some point and `deploy-demo.yml` was evidently updated while `ci.yml` was not, so other files may carry the same stale assumption — and none of them can fail visibly while Actions is retired, which is exactly the condition in which this class accumulates.

## References

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:198-219` · `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:79-100` · `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/` (10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks) · `contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23` · `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` · `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` · Aiken docs: [https://aiken-lang.org/](<https://aiken-lang.org/>) · related: `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-246` (Backlog), `KS-552` (Done — the Container Apps pivot that fenced deploy-demo.yml).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the two workflow files were read and compared at that commit; nothing was executed and no runner was invoked. GitHub Actions on this repo answers every job with *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed…"*, so the defect cannot surface until billing is restored.

title: Verify policy for a credential id with NO stored record — KS-1352 ships pass-through, and the unknown-id case is unruled
description:
**BLUF — a policy question, not a defect report. Nothing is built for this.**

KS-1352 made `POST /api/credentials/verify` refuse a credential that its stored issuer record **or** the status list marks revoked. It deliberately does **not** change the answer for a credential id that **no authority holds a record for**. That case needs a ruling.

**What ships today (pass-through).** The stored-record arm ABSTAINS when `credentialRepo.getById()` returns nothing: the status-list arm and the cryptographic proof still decide, so an unknown id verifies exactly as it did before KS-1352.

**Why it was not decided in KS-1352.** The ruling on that ticket is that a *revoked* credential fails. An unknown credential is a different case, and failing closed would have widened the ruling with a measured cost: `credentialRepo.loadFromDb()` returns silently when the database is unavailable (`credentialRepo.ts:212`) and the memory store then starts empty, so a fail-closed rule would refuse **every** credential on a process with no database.

**The gap this leaves, stated plainly.** A credential that was genuinely revoked but whose stored record was lost — the swallowed-DB-write path at `credentialRepo.ts:78`, or a replica that never issued it — still verifies as valid. That is a thinner version of the defect KS-1352 fixed.

**The options.**

1. **Pass-through (today).** An unknown id verifies on its proof alone. Preserves availability; keeps the gap above.
2. **Fail-closed with a distinct reason.** `verified: false`, `checks.status: false`, reason `no issuer record` — deliberately not the word "revoked", so `determineStatus()` does not mislabel it. Closes the gap; refuses every credential wherever the store cannot answer.
3. **Conditional.** Fail closed only when the store is known-answerable (database reachable), pass through otherwise. Closes the gap in normal operation but is itself fail-open during an outage.

**Where the boundary is pinned.** Cell `C2` in `services/vc-issuer/src/__tests__/ks1352-revoked-credential-fails-verify.test.ts` asserts that an id with no stored record still verifies true, so option 1 cannot be changed by accident — whichever option is chosen, that cell is the one to edit.

Measured on develop `0d156d12`. A literal board search found no existing ticket covering this (`unknown-id`, `not in the store`, `unknown credential`, `verify policy`, `storedRecordResolver` all 0; positive controls on the same query shape returned 1, 2 and 23).

description:

title: Review stream: API contract and the four platform suites
description:
**Review stream for Peter — one review, one test pass, 19 tickets.**

## The one test pass

1. Regenerate the OpenAPI spec, then **restart** the api-gateway container. The yaml is bind-mounted, so a restart publishes it and a rebuild does not.
2. `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge --base-url http://localhost:6882` — **13.4 min measured** (~2,016 cases over 318 operations). Report **the failing SET of operation ids and its diff against the develop baseline set**, never a bare count.
3. `node scripts/preflight/spec-auth-conformance.mjs --base http://localhost:6882` (seconds) — every bearer-authed operation must reject unauthenticated.
4. `cd systemTest/playwright && npm run quality:static && npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e` — **3.8 s measured**, all three must pass.
5. `cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:smoke` — **53 s measured**. Read **the printed** `Status:` **line, not the exit code**, which is 0 either way.

## Two traps that make this run lie

* **A second back-to-back Schemathesis run fails at *setup* with 401**, not on a finding: the fuzz tiers change the test persona's password. `docker restart secuura-auth` re-seeds it. The `Run validity: OK` line does not catch this — it counts schemathesis operations, not pytest setup errors.
* **A partial stack produces a confident FALSE RED. **`docker-compose.local.yml` defines 38 services; when some are down the gateway answers `502 BAD_GATEWAY` and the suites score it as a defect indistinguishable from a real one. Run `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml ps` first and confirm every service is up.

Commands and wall-clocks are quoted from `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` section *Manual CI-gate equivalents*.

title: The `require-pr-gates` ruleset survived the Actions retirement: 7 required checks that can never report, 0 required approvals, and ALWAYS bypass for admins
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **and** `main` **carry an ACTIVE ruleset that enforces nothing for an admin and is unsatisfiable for everyone else.** It requires seven status-check contexts whose workflows no longer exist, requires **zero** approving reviews, and grants `ALWAYS` bypass to org and repo admins.

The retirement of Actions is well tracked ([KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify), [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql)). **What is not tracked is the ruleset left pointing at it.** A branch that looks protected in the settings UI, and in the API reports `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` on a PR with no reviews and no checks, is worse than one that is plainly unprotected — the reassurance is the problem.

Found while reviewing [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), after asking the ordinary question "could this merge without an approval?". It can.

## What the ruleset actually says

`require-pr-gates` — `target: BRANCH`, `enforcement: ACTIVE`, conditions `refs/heads/develop` + `refs/heads/main`.

| rule | setting |
| -- | -- |
| `PULL_REQUEST` | required |
| — `requiredApprovingReviewCount` | **0** |
| — `requireCodeOwnerReview` | false |
| — `requireLastPushApproval` | false |
| — `requiredReviewThreadResolution` | false |
| — `dismissStaleReviewsOnPush` | false |
| `REQUIRED_STATUS_CHECKS` | 7 contexts (below) |
| — `strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy` | false |
| `DELETION` / `NON_FAST_FORWARD` | both on — these two DO work |

Required contexts: `Code Security Gates` · `Standalone locks pass clean-room npm ci` · `build / Build + push platform images (fresh)` · `Schemathesis suite` · `Playwright suite` · `Performance suite (k6 smoke)` · `Akto suite (PR)`.

Bypass actors, **both** `bypassMode: ALWAYS`: organization admins, and repository role `5` (admin).

## The three problems, separately

**1 — Seven required checks that can never report.** Every recent workflow run is `startup_failure` at **0s** (`gh run list`). The workflows producing these contexts were retired. So for a contributor without admin the ruleset is not strict, it is **unsatisfiable** — nothing they push can ever go green, and the failure reads as "waiting for a check" rather than "this check no longer exists".

**2 — Zero required approvals.** A PR is required; an approval is not. On `main` as well as `develop`, which is the part I would not have guessed. `main` is meant to be the releasable branch (CLAUDE.md → Branching Model), and it currently asks for no human sign-off at all.

**3 —** `ALWAYS` **bypass for admins hides both.** Anyone who could notice problems 1 and 2 is exactly the population the ruleset never applies to. GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus` for the viewer, so an admin sees `CLEAN` and no warning of any kind.

## The demonstration

[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), read 2026-09-08:

```
mergeable:         MERGEABLE
mergeStateStatus:  CLEAN
reviewDecision:    null      (no reviews of ANY kind ever submitted)
statusCheckRollup: 0 checks
```

Mergeable right now, by any admin, with no approval and no green check — and nothing on the PR page says so. That PR happens to be under active review, so no harm is in flight; it is the state that is the finding, not the PR.

## Reproduce

```
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner:"Secuura", name:"Distributed_Secuura") {
  rulesets(first:5){ nodes{ name target enforcement
    conditions{ refName{ include exclude } }
    bypassActors(first:20){ nodes{ bypassMode organizationAdmin repositoryRoleDatabaseId } }
    rules(first:30){ nodes{ type parameters{ __typename
      ... on PullRequestParameters { requiredApprovingReviewCount requireCodeOwnerReview requireLastPushApproval requiredReviewThreadResolution dismissStaleReviewsOnPush }
      ... on RequiredStatusChecksParameters { strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy requiredStatusChecks{ context } } } } } } } }'
```

Note the REST endpoints (`/branches/develop/protection`, `/rulesets`) answer **403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro"** on this private repo, which is why this is easy to miss — the obvious check reports nothing rather than reporting the truth. GraphQL answers fine.

## Suggested shape — not a decree, and deliberately not one change

These are three decisions, not one, and they belong to different owners:

1. **Drop the seven dead contexts** from the ruleset, or repoint them at whatever replaced Actions. Leaving a required check that cannot report is the worst of the three states. *(Cheap; no policy decision.)*
2. **Decide the approval count deliberately**, for `main` and `develop` separately. If 0 is intended on a 4-seat team, say so in CONTRIBUTING and this ticket closes on that; if it is a leftover, 1 on `develop` and 1 on `main` is the obvious floor.
3. **Reconsider** `ALWAYS` **bypass.** `pull_request` mode instead of `ALWAYS` keeps admins able to unblock an emergency while still surfacing the state to them.

**(1) is worth doing regardless of how (2) and (3) land.**

## Relationship to what is already tracked

Points **forward** to the gate we want. This ticket is the **residue behind us**: the ruleset that already exists and no longer means anything. They should probably be sequenced — clean this up, then build [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) on the cleared ground.

Cause; this is effect.

title: POST /api/teams/notify: a permanently failing webhook is never rotated past, because last_sent_at is written only on success
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/teams/notify` now bounds its row set and **rotates** it, so a repeat call reaches rows the
previous call did not (#1274, F-1274-1). The rotation key is
`ORDER BY last_sent_at ASC NULLS FIRST, created_at ASC`.

`last_sent_at` **is written only after a SUCCESSFUL send.** A webhook that always fails — a dead peer,
or one the SSRF guard blocks — keeps a NULL `last_sent_at` for ever and therefore sorts to the **head**
**of every call**. With `TEAMS_NOTIFY_MAX_ROWS` or more permanently-failing rows, the starvation
F-1274-1 identified **returns in full**: the healthy rows past the limit are never reached by any
number of calls.

This is a **known, pinned limit of the F-1274-1 fix**, not a regression it introduced. Before that fix
the order was a fixed `created_at ASC` and *nothing* rotated.

## Where

`services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`, the notify route. The write is inside the success branch:

```ts
if (resp.ok) {
  sent.push(wh.id);
  await query('UPDATE svc_teams_webhooks SET last_sent_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1', [wh.id]);
} else {
  failed.push(wh.id);       // <- no write, so last_sent_at stays NULL
}
```

The `!result.ok` branch (guard-blocked or request-failed) likewise does not write.

## It is already pinned in code

`R3` in `src/__tests__/ks934-teams-notify-request-path-bound.test.ts` asserts the CURRENT behaviour:
with `MAX_ROWS` permanently-failing rows, a second call attempts **exactly the same set** and never
reaches the last five. **R3 is a pin, not a fix.**

⚠ **When this ticket is built, R3 WILL RED. That is the intended signal, not a breakage** — it must be
rewritten to assert the new behaviour in the same change.

Red-proved: writing `last_sent_at` on a failed attempt too (one of the fix shapes below) reds **R3 and**
**only R3** — 1 of 8 cells. So R3 discriminates today rather than passing vacuously.

## Why it was not fixed in #1274's fix round

Both available shapes reach past a fix round's declared scope:

1. **write** `last_sent_at` **on every ATTEMPT.** This changes the meaning of a **published** field —
   `lastSentAt` is returned by `GET /api/teams/webhooks` (`index.ts`, the list route) — so "last sent"
   would start meaning "last tried". A consumer cannot tell the difference and is not warned.
2. **add a** `last_attempted_at` **column.** DDL in **two** places (`docker/init/06-m365-tables.sql` and
   `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`) plus an `information_schema`-guarded backfill for
   existing deploys, then order by it.

Shape 2 is the honest one — it leaves the published field alone — but it is a schema change and
belongs in its own pass with its own review.

## Done means

1. A rotation key that advances on an ATTEMPT, not only on a success, by whichever shape is chosen.
2. A cell: `MAX_ROWS` permanently-failing rows, two calls, the second REACHES the rows past the limit.
3. `R3` rewritten in the same change (it pins the behaviour being replaced).
4. If shape 1 is chosen, the published `lastSentAt` field's meaning is documented where it is
   returned, or renamed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`last_sent_at`, `last_attempted_at`, `svc_teams_webhooks`, `teams/notify starvation`,
`permanently failing webhook`, `NULLS FIRST`, `teams notify rotation` — **0 literal hits each**.
Controls: `webhook` **43**, `adminConfig` **19**, `teams` **11** (the matcher fires); a nonce token
never written anywhere **0**. Noted for a later reader: KS-934's own description contains neither
`svc_teams_webhooks` nor `last_sent_at`, so those zeros are a property of the corpus, not of the
matcher.

Refs KS-934

title: The api-gateway user seed throws 42P10 on every boot and has never seeded anything — remove its INSERT, do NOT repoint the conflict target
description:
**Reverted out of #885 by Kam's** `split` **ruling (2026-09-07 12:13).** The defect is real; the fix that was written for it was wrong, and this ticket carries both so the next attempt does not repeat it.

## The defect

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts` seeds twelve users with `ON CONFLICT (email)`. **There is no unique index on** `users.email` **in the deployed schema**, so the statement raises **42P10** — *"there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification"* — on **every** run, fresh database included. Measured in a rolled-back transaction; `ON CONFLICT (id)` returns `INSERT 0 1` on the same table.

The failure is caught and emitted as `log('debug', 'User seed skipped')`. One statement, twelve rows: a debug-level "skipped" for a twelve-row seed that has never once succeeded.

## ⛔ WHAT NOT TO DO — the fix that was reverted

Moving the conflict target to the primary key **makes the statement run**, and running it is worse than not:

* it writes **PLAINTEXT** into `users.email`, a column where **all 25 rows measured are AES-GCM ciphertext**;
* it never sets `email_lookup_hash`, which is the only unique index on the table and the column the auth service looks users up by.

So twelve rows would become plaintext-bearing **and unfindable by the login path**. **The bug was preventing the migration from corrupting the column, and fixing it released it.**

## ✅ THE RATIFIED SHAPE — remove the INSERT

Wednesday ratified 2026-09-07: **the migration should not create these rows at all.**

Evidence:

1. **Auth's** `seedDemoUsers` **already creates all twelve**, with **identical** `tenant_id`/`tenant_slug` — verified id by id, including the contested `…060` (`a0000000-…-099` / `secuura-co` in both, and that is what the live row holds).
2. **On a stack where this statement has thrown every boot since encryption landed, all twelve rows exist**, all ciphertext, all with `email_lookup_hash` set. *We are not removing a load-bearing statement; we are deleting one that has never borne load, and nobody noticed.*
3. Its own justification — *"so document FK constraints work"* — is **false on the deployed schema**: `pg_constraint` reports no FK on `documents.owner_user_id`, and `docker/init/01-schema.sql:127` declares it with no `REFERENCES`. (It IS declared in `migrations/001:107` — that divergence is **KS-960**.)

**Keep** the primary-key conflict target, used **only** to re-sync `tenant_id`/`tenant_slug` on rows that already exist — its original tail and its only defensible job. It loses authority over `email`, names, role and status: PII, or auth's.

## The suite

`scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh` was written for the reverted fix and removed with it (12 cells, real Postgres, statement extracted from source with its sha256 printed, CONTROL-1 asserting the old form still fails 42P10). **It returns with this round, rewritten for the new contract.**

**Required of the new cell (Wednesday):** drive **both** seeders against **one** real database in **both** orders, on the `docker/init` shape, and **do NOT stub** `isEncryptedPii` — that stub is what blinded the old suite. The contract to assert: the statement must **not** modify `email` or `email_lookup_hash` on an existing row, with a control proving the cell would have caught the old behaviour.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during KS-949 rounds 2 and 3.**

title: KS-256 review follow-ups: 5 example-fixable 400s, the tsx transpile-only spec-gate trap (§10), and a new `userAgent: Demo Issuer` instance
description:
The three items left open from @kksecura's 2026-08-19 review of PR #568. Split out per his own §8 reasoning — the parameter-example work is the bigger half of the same problem, and bundling it would expand a PR he has already reviewed twice.

**Every figure below was re-verified against the branch head** `92feea4a9`**, not carried over from the review.**

---

## 1. §4 — the five example-fixable 400s are still published

His triage stands unchallenged: **5 strictly example-fixable**, or **8 counting parameter examples**. My original "at most 4" was low. All five are still live in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`:

| # | Defect | Count at head |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `example-documentId` violates `SAFE_ID_PATTERN` | **17** |
| 2 | `example-code` exceeds the documented max of 8 | **3** |
| 3 | `example-challengeId` is not a uuid | **1** |
| 4 | `example-country` is not exactly 2 chars | **2** |
| 5 | `transfer-custody` pins two mutually exclusive fields | 1 |

Number 5 is the sharpest, because the spec contradicts itself **four lines apart** (`secuura-api.yaml:6318-6322`):

```yaml
description: Exactly ONE of `newHolderId` / `newHolderEmail` is required — neither is 400, both is 400.
example:
  newHolderId: example-newHolderId
  newHolderEmail: demo.issuer@example.com     # ← publishing exactly what the line above calls a 400
```

A reader copying that example gets a guaranteed 400, and the description already tells them why.

**Fix direction:** these land in the Zod sources (`services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`), then `npm run generate-openapi`. Numbers 1–4 need the placeholder to satisfy the constraint the schema already documents; number 5 needs the example to pin one field only.

## 2. The bigger half — parameter examples

Verified at head: **132 path parameters, 2 carrying an example.** That is the §7 gap on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own body, and it is why this is a follow-up rather than a patch. Together with `operationId`/`links` ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) — 0 of 613 links covered) it is the next real coverage step, and it dwarfs the five above.

## 3. §10 — the trap that produced the build failure, recorded nowhere

`npm run generate-openapi` runs the `*.openapi.ts` files through `tsx`**, which is transpile-only**. A type error in the very file the generator reads therefore **cannot** fail the spec gate.

That is exactly how the `documentUuid` breakage shipped: `check:openapi` was **green** — drift clean, E1–E9 0 findings across 354 blocks — while `originate` would not compile, and the failure only surfaced in the Docker build (30/34 images, `originate` + `migrations` red, no containers started).

`check:openapi` **green is not evidence the images build.** Nothing in `scripts/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `package.json` says so today. Options, in increasing order of strength:

1. Document it where the gate is defined and in `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Add a `tsc --noEmit` pass over the `*.openapi.ts` sources to `check:openapi`, so the gate covers the files it consumes.

Option 2 would have caught the original defect at the gate rather than in a 50-minute image build. @kksecura offered the wording or is happy for us to take it — his call.

## 4. A new instance of the §3 class his sweep did not reach

`secuura-api.yaml:7265` publishes:

```yaml
userAgent: Demo Issuer
```

Same mechanism as the 16 `address` fields fixed in `704c8c0f2`: a legitimate `FIXTURE_PERSON_VALUES` member landing on a **non-person** field, so **E5 passes it** — the guard is working to spec and the spec is wrong for the field. Not a leak; a documentation defect, since no client sends `Demo Issuer` as a user agent.

**Verified the rest are correct** — the other 21 `Demo Issuer` hits are all on genuine name fields and should stay:

```
17  displayName     2  channelName     1  fullName     1  name
 1  userAgent   ← the defect
```

**Fix direction:** same as §3 — either give `userAgent` its own fixture, or stop masking-category-3 claiming it. Worth deciding once for the class rather than per field, since `address` and `userAgent` are now two instances of it.

---

## Why these are not on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)

[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own acceptance already carries the 26×400 triage as an open box, and its two remaining boxes are gated on [KS-660](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-660/ci-every-needs-build-suite-job-dies-in-3s-with-zero-steps-develop-is) (CI executes zero steps). Items 1 and 4 here are small, item 2 is large, and item 3 is a gate change — none of them belongs in a PR that has been reviewed twice and is waiting on sign-off.

*— raised by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-19. Figures verified at* `92feea4a9`*.*

title: Add OpenAPI inline examples to all 329 operations — eliminate coverage-phase no-test-cases skips
description:
> ### ✅ 2026-08-12 — branch current with `develop`, ready for review
>
> Head `72c33c20a`. Merged develop (#666/#667/#669/#670/#671/#672) and regenerated the spec — the
> regenerated output was byte-identical to the auto-merged YAML, so there was no drift to reconcile.
> The spec now carries **319 operationIds** ([KS-62](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-62/openapi-specification-compliance-optional-features) / #670, was 0) alongside **355 example blocks**;
> the two workstreams compose without contention. `check:openapi` PASS (drift + E1–E9, 0 findings) ·
> `packages/shared` 279/279 · full preflight PASS on push including the new `audit:locks` gate.
>
> **Remaining is not authoring** — it is Kam's sign-off and review pass, then the pre-merge suites.
>
> **PII key question (C1/C2) — CLOSED.** Kam answered 2026-07-29 (he holds the pair locally); with A3
> settled as option (c) the captures have no remaining purpose, so no re-supply is needed. The two raw
> capture directories are confirmed deleted, retiring the 233 live JWTs. The obsolete red banner that
> stood here has been removed as it invited.

> ### 📎 One plan attachment — "[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) *implementation plan — the only current version"*
>
> Its `OUTSTANDING ACTIONS` section (groups A–G) is the authoritative pick-up list, mirrored in the
> consolidated comment. **Critical path: B1 → A1 → E1.** Earlier revisions have been deleted rather
> than left alongside it — two files each claiming to be current is how someone picks up a stale plan.

---

## Goal

Give every OpenAPI operation at least one realistic, **runnable** example, so Schemathesis and Akto can generate meaningful test cases instead of falling back to unconstrained fuzz.

This is the prerequisite annotation work for [KS-227](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-227/schemathesis-gate-cicd-on-no-test-cases-skips-once-schema-annotation) (CI gate on coverage skips).

> **⚠ Approach changed 2026-07.** This ticket originally proposed hand-editing `example:` blocks into `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`. **That is not possible** — the spec is *generated* from Zod schemas by `scripts/generate-openapi.ts`, and `npm run check:openapi` fails the build on any hand-edit. Examples must land in the Zod source. The original approach is preserved in the issue's description history.

---

## Where examples actually live

```
services/<svc>/src/<svc>.openapi.ts     ← .openapi({ description, example }) — EDIT HERE
        │  npm run generate-openapi
        ▼
docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml           ← GENERATED. Never hand-edit.
```

The `api-gateway` image bundles the generated spec — but **how you pick a spec change up differs by target** (corrected 2026-08-19, Kamil's review §9):

* **Deployed targets** (Container Apps / the VM's built images) — the spec is baked in, so **rebuild api-gateway**.
* **Local compose** — the spec is **bind-mounted**, not baked (`docker-compose.yml:434`), and since [KS-656](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-656/api-gateway-apidocsopenapiyaml-500s-on-a-dead-spec-bind-mount-while) the gateway reads it into memory **once at boot**, so `docker restart secuura-api-gateway` is what picks it up. A rebuild works only incidentally, by recreating the container.
* **Verify by checksum, not by a 200.** The dev `fs.watch` hot-reload does not fire in the container ([KS-659](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-659/api-gateway-spec-hot-reload-never-fires-in-the-container-a-spec-regen)), and after a `git checkout` the single-file bind mount points at a dead inode — the route keeps answering **200 with the previous branch's spec**.

## Measured baseline vs current (2026-08-05)

| Metric | develop | branch |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Operations in spec | **318** | 318 |
| Named component schemas | **350** | 350 |
| …carrying an example | **14** | **344** |
| Example blocks | 23 | **354** |
| — request only | 6 | **113** |
| — response only | 4 | **172** |

**Examples-phase skips: 303 → 196.** All −107 came from the request-body examples; the 168 response examples moved it by **exactly zero**, because that phase seeds from what a caller *sends*. Detail in the 2026-08-05 comment.

### Superseded 2026-07-20 baseline (for the record)

| Metric | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Operations in spec | **310** (not 329) |
| Named component schemas | **335** |
| …carrying an example | **14** |
| Typed properties | **1,817** |
| …carrying an example | **4** |
| …carrying *any* constraint (`format`/`pattern`/`enum`/`min`/`max`) | **425 (23.4%)** |

**The last row is the real constraint on this ticket.** 76.6% of properties are declared bare `type: string`, so anything generating from the schema — example synthesis, Schemathesis, Akto — has nothing to work with. `createdAt` is a bare string.

## Correction to the original premise

`no_test_cases_generated` **does not appear anywhere in this codebase**, and is not the skip reason the report emits — our HTML report reads a free-text `skip_reason` (`src/html_report/panels/operations.py:51`). The original acceptance criterion was written against a term that does not exist in Schemathesis 4.22.4. Any criterion phrased in terms of it needs restating against the actual skip vocabulary.

---

## The approach: harvest → redact → triage → synthesise → codemod

Built as a self-contained harness in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/` (see its README). **Default OFF** behind `HARVEST_EXAMPLES`, four independent guards, zero runs in CI — the condition of Kamil's approval.

**1. Harvest.** A capture proxy sits transparently in front of the API on `:6882` while the existing test suites run, recording real request/response pairs. **platform-k only** — `config.tiers` defaults to `['platform-k']`; platform-s moved to [PS-348](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-348/harvest-openapi-example-values-from-the-platform-s-test-suite-ks-256) with its machinery retained. Reach is ~13 of 310 operations (~4%) — real traffic simply does not exercise most endpoints.

**2. Redact — in memory, before any write (R15b).** No raw capture artifact is ever written to disk. Credentials become named placeholders (`<password>`, `<accessToken>`) so a reader knows what to supply. Identifiers normalise to seed fixtures so examples stay runnable after a DB reset (R7).

**3. Triage (Gate 5a) — human, mandatory.** Unrecognised fields land as `REDACTED_UNREVIEWED` and are ineligible to publish. Only fields a human explicitly moves to `ALLOWED_FIELDS` may appear as observed. **Enforced in code**, not by convention.

**4. Synthesise.** Everything harvest cannot reach is generated deterministically from the schema — ~96% of output.

**5. Codemod (Gate 5b) — ✅ WRITTEN AND RUN (2026-08-05).** `scripts/spec-examples/apply-spec-examples.ts` — absent-only, AST-derived text splice, masking before shape-fitting, `--regenerate` round-trips byte-identical. 330 examples landed. [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) no longer gates it (merged #603, 07-29). Superseded text follows: The step that writes `.openapi({ example })` into the Zod files. **Nothing ships until this exists, and** [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) **gates it.**

## Status

| Piece | State |
| -- | -- |
| Capture proxy | working |
| Harvest | **platform-k only**; platform-s deferred to [PS-348](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-348/harvest-openapi-example-values-from-the-platform-s-test-suite-ks-256) |
| `pipeline.ts` | **built** — 335 merged (14 tier-0 untouched + 321 synthesised, 0 harvested) |
| Triage (Gate 5a) | **done** — 18 `ALLOWED_FIELDS` entries. **Dormant**: redaction is in-memory, so they apply only to a *future* harvest |
| PII store | built, empty; lives outside the repo, guarded by a build-failing check |
| **Codemod (Gate 5b)** | **✅ WRITTEN + RUN 2026-08-05** — 330 examples landed, 14 curated untouched. Guards: `check-spec-examples` E1–E9 **blocking**; `verify-spec-examples` V1–V5 **advisory** (non-deterministic). Was: **not written — this is what remains, and** [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) **gates it** |
| Kamil's review (2026-07) | **10 of \~12 fixed**. Each fix carries a `KAMIL-REVIEW` tag and his stated reason, quoted, at the point of change |
| **Kamil's review (2026-08-19)** | **8 of 10 addressed** — §1 build fix, §2 E8/E9 coverage bound, §3 the 16 `address` examples, §4 the 26x400 correction, §5 ack wording, §6 the false `MIN_OBSERVATIONS` comment, §7 PII checkbox, §8 perf gate split to PR #723, §9 restart-not-rebuild, §10 recorded in a commit. **The 2 remaining were deferred by him**, not missed: the `verify/` sub-threshold count ("not for this PR") and the baseline ticket. **Both his stated blockers are cleared** and verified on the pushed head |
| **Pre-merge ack** | **GRANTED for this PR by Kamil, 2026-08-19** — he re-ran the sweep independently, 91 failures, every class mapping to an open ticket. His condition for a *standing* rule (a `schemathesis-baseline.json` keyed by check+operation with ticket + expiry) is now **built and enforced** on this branch: 97 pairs, gate fails on any untriaged pair |

PR: [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#568](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-256-openapi-examples-14-344-schemas-gate-5b-codemod-e1-e9-guard-709ed550b02d) — OPEN, ready for review, head `72c33c20a` (squashed to `c7f55881d` 2026-08-05, then merged current with `develop` 2026-08-12). Review requested from @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson.

**Local verification is green** — `check:openapi` PASS (drift + E1-E9) · `tsc` 22/22 services · 279/279 shared · 160/160 performance · Playwright 12/12 on generated actors · GDPR IDOR 6/6. The **Schemathesis sweep still FAILS** on fuzz-phase findings (a different set each run — it reseeds); none are example-driven. Akto has not been re-run.

## Open decisions — ✅ ALL THREE RESOLVED 2026-07-29 by @kamil.kreiser (kept for the record)

1. **publish-vs-enrich (BLOCKING).** Peter's. The 321 synthesised proposals are structurally valid but mostly `example-<fieldname>`, because of the 76.6% figure above. Either publish as-is (real coverage, low value), or enrich the Zod schemas with `.datetime()`/`.uuid()`/`.regex()` first. An enrichment codemod was written and reverted: 131 evidence-backed rewrites, 23.4% → 28.5%. These modules are documentation-only — nothing calls `.parse()` on them — so added formats **cannot reject a request**. Plan §7.0-G. ⚠ Interacts with #2.
2. **R3 amendment.** Kamil's. Whether Schemathesis 2xx *responses* become an admissible value source — **166 operations versus harvest's 13**. Highest-leverage open item; if admitted, #1 may resolve itself.
3. `Accept-Encoding`**.** Kamil's. He asked for it to be stripped; we decode instead. Declared and argued on PR #568 and in plan §7.0-F.

*(The former item 4 — the seven volatile-id examples — is now* [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no), which **blocks this ticket**. It could not be fixed by substitution: no document is seeded, so every candidate replacement still 404s.)

## Acceptance

**No fixed number** — per Peter, the target is "how many we can get", measured and reported rather than gated on. Ceiling is 335/335 schemas, since synthesis reaches every named schema; the open question is example *quality*, not reach.

- [X] **DONE** Codemod written, and examples landed in `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts` (330 examples, 14 -> 344 schemas). No longer gated by [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no)
- [X] **DONE** `npm run generate-openapi` re-run; `npm run check:openapi` passes — now also runs the blocking E1-E9 guard, 0 findings across 354 example blocks

title: routes/webhooks.ts returns the thrown error text on 7 unconditional 500s, measured leaking under NODE_ENV=production
description:
**BLUF:** `routes/webhooks.ts` **carries 7 unconditional** `message: err.message` **500 responses, and they leak under** `NODE_ENV=production` — measured, not inferred. `DELETE /api/webhooks/:id` returns the **thrown text**; rotate-secret returns **internal configuration text**. Same defect class as the systemErrors / gdpr / adminConfig work just merged, but a different route file and a different PR set, which is why it is its own ticket.

## Why High rather than Polish

Those three merges removed this pattern on the grounds that a thrown message can carry internal detail to a client. The reasoning applies unchanged here, and here it is **measured reaching the client in production mode** — including configuration text from rotate-secret, the most sensitive of the group. Nothing about the fix is novel; what is missing is that it was not applied to this file.

## Fix shape (the same one already merged three times)

Return a generic message for 5xx and keep the thrown text in the log only. Where a 4xx legitimately explains itself, gate the echo on the error marking itself safe to expose, as the demo-service handler now does.

## Not claimed

The count of 7 and the two named routes are the gate's measurement. Whether any further file in this family remains was not swept here.

## Board search before filing

Searched over 489 open issues, literal match on identifier + title + description: `routes/webhooks.ts`, `rotate-secret` — 0 open hits each; `err.message` fires and a fresh nonsense token returns 0, so the instrument discriminates both ways.
