title: Per-tenant DB readiness: the dormant per-tenant-database path, and the five tickets that each break it
description:
## BLUF

**Every tenant shares one database today.** Isolation comes from a `tenant_id` column plus
fail-closed RLS. A per-tenant-database path exists in the code and is **switched off**. This is the
parent for the five tickets that each break that path in a different way, so the work has one place
rather than five.

**Nothing is built by this ticket.** It exists because Kam ruled option (c) on KS-1304 — *"Leave it*
*until per-tenant databases are actually planned. Nothing changes. The ticket keeps the measurement for*
*whoever builds per-tenant databases"* (2026-09-26 07:19) — with the note **"start planning the**
**database"**. This ticket is the artefact that carries that ruling onto the board.

## Measured at `00de57baeb405d0081fe8b6f192bd40d35acef61` (develop's tip), by this seat

Re-measured here rather than carried over from the planning document, which read an older tree.

1. **The flag is set in 0 config files.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` occurs in exactly **two source**
   **files** — `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-pool-manager.ts:152` and
   `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245` — and in **no** `.env`, `.example`, `.yml`,
   `.yaml` or `.json` config file. *Control: 25 config files do mention* `DATABASE_URL`*, so the*
   *config-file search is not blind.*
2. **Every tenant is seeded onto the shared database, and the code says so in its own comment.**
   `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:1116-1144` writes all eight `tenant_config` rows
   with the same `db_name`, `db_host` and `db_port`, derived from `DATABASE_URL`. The comment at
   `:1116-1117` reads: *"Ensure all tenants have a tenant_config entry pointing to the shared*
   *'secuura' database. On Azure there is a single DB; per-tenant DBs are not provisioned."*
3. **The docs state the opposite.** `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md:13` — *"Each client (tenant) receives an*
   *isolated PostgreSQL database"* — and `:16` — *"Each tenant has its own PostgreSQL database*
   *(*`secuura_tenant_{slug}`*)"*. `docs/RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md:35` — *"Real isolation is per-tenant*
   *databases."* **The second of those is internally contradictory**: the two lines immediately above
   it say RLS is *"permanently on its fail-open branch — inert today"*, so that document simultaneously
   says isolation comes from per-tenant databases and that the mechanism which would route to them is
   not in use. A reader of either doc will overestimate the isolation that exists.

A docs PR correcting both files is raised separately and links here.

## The five tickets, and why each blocks switching the path on

* **KS-1304** — `documents.ts` mixes a tenant-pool read with a default-pool write. Ruled (c): left
  until per-tenant databases are planned. `adminConfig.ts` carries 9 of the 11 `withTenant(` sites.
* **KS-1235** — auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC.
* **KS-1055** — per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations. Measured on that ticket: a new
  tenant database comes up with RLS forced on and **zero policies**, so the app can read nothing.
* **KS-1054** — migration-runner ordering and exit status.
* **KS-598** — the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert silently collapses. **KS-598 keeps KS-772 as its**
  **parent** (Stuart's review stream — re-parenting it would silently remove an item from a human's
  queue) and is linked here as *related* instead.

## What this ticket is NOT

* It does not choose between building the opt-in dedicated-database tier and deleting the dormant path
  and hardening RLS. **That decision is Kam's**, and it turns on whether a named customer or contract
  needs physical separation (data residency, per-tenant restore or deletion, customer-held keys) or
  whether this is defence in depth.
* It carries **facts only**. The planning document's recommendations and phasing are deliberately not
  reproduced here, so the board does not record a plan as though it were agreed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`per-tenant DB readiness` **0**, `tenant database readiness` **0**, `dedicated database tier` **0**;
`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` returns **3** — KS-1055, KS-1304, KS-1235, i.e. the children, **no parent**;
`per-tenant database` returns 2, both children. Controls: `tenant` **49** literal hits and
`multi-tenancy` **8** (the matcher fires), a nonce token never written anywhere **0**.

title: m365 /api/teams/notify: a serial per-row loop with no LIMIT and no aggregate bound, inside the request handler — N rows x the guard's 10s default
description:
## No aggregate bound over an unbounded row set, in a request handler

`POST /api/teams/notify` loops over every active webhook row **serially**, inside the request handler, with **no** `LIMIT` **on the query** and **no aggregate deadline** over the loop.

The gate confirmed the call site passes **no** `timeoutMs`, so each row rides `safeOutboundRequest`'s 10 s default. Worst case is `rows x 10s` with the HTTP request held open throughout.

KS-914 improved the per-row behaviour — before it, `fetch` was called with no signal at all — but the aggregate was never bounded and still is not.

### Fix shape

A `LIMIT` with paging, or an aggregate deadline over the loop, or move the dispatch off the request path entirely (which is the shape the webhooks dispatcher already uses). **Concurrency is not the fix on its own** — it changes the constant, not the bound.

Red-proof with N rows against a destination that never answers, asserting the handler returns within an aggregate bound rather than N x per-row.

*From the #868 round-1 gate (F4). Filed by s141, 2026-09-06.*

title: entrypoint-corpus guard: a parenthesised return of a guarded call reads `guarded:false`, and the file's own rule-3 comment claims both return shapes are covered
description:
**BLUF: the guard reads** `guarded:false` **for call shapes the file's own comment says it covers.** Its rule-3 comment states *"Both return shapes are covered: a concise arrow body, and an explicit* `return`*"* — yet `return (() => g())` and `() => (() => g())`, when called, both read `guarded:false`, while the truth and `develop` both read **true**. `(() => g()).call(null)` reads false as well, and is not named anywhere.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## What is wrong, precisely

The defect is **parenthesisation**. A guarded call wrapped in parentheses — whether returned explicitly or as a concise arrow body — is not recognised, so a correctly-guarded call site is reported as unguarded. The reading is wrong in the **unsafe-looking** direction: it accuses safe code.

Three shapes, measured at runtime:

| shape | guard reads | truth / develop |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `return (() => g())` then called | `guarded:false` | true |
| `() => (() => g())` then called | `guarded:false` | true |
| `(() => g()).call(null)` | `guarded:false` | true |

The third came from a call-shape table the round was commissioned to make **"read as the truth or be NAMED"**. It does neither: it reads false and is unnamed.

**Evidence produced by the gate:** `evidence/1268/probe_readings_head.jsonl`, rows 23, 40 and 41.

## Why this is its own ticket

It is the same defect **class** as the round's first attempt, which is why the round capped. The fix is a reader change: recognise a parenthesised expression as transparent when deciding whether the inner call is guarded, and either read `.call`/`.apply` invocation forms as the truth or name them as unsupported. **A guard whose own comment claims coverage it does not have is worse than one with a stated limit**, because the comment is what the next reader trusts.

## Not in this ticket

The round's other work — the `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts` change at blob `8a4ce36a3a96` — is sound and is being re-raised separately by its author. This ticket is only the reader defect.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **486 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `guarded:false`, `parenthesised`, `rule-3`, `concise arrow` — **0 open hits each**. `entrypoint-corpus` returned 3 (KS-1155, KS-1142, KS-1140), none of them this reader defect. Controls: a fresh nonsense token **0**, `ssrf-guard` **2**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Refs KS-1316

title: Under multi-tenancy, auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC: with fail-closed RLS every approve's level UPDATE matches 0 rows
description:
## BLUF

**With** `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` **on, auth's** `db.ts` **sends every statement that carries a tenant argument through** `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query()`**: a raw pool query with no tenant GUC.** Under fail-closed RLS, a tenant-scoped UPDATE then matches 0 rows.

* On the verification approve, develop answers a false **200 APPROVED while the level stays basic**. #1032's head instead refuses every approve (503, PENDING).
* **Major while that configuration runs; latent today.** The auth container in `services.bicep` does not set `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (read).
* **Evidence class:** MEASURED on the real `db.ts` and `TenantPoolManager` with `pg` faked and RLS MODELLED. Whether the runtime database role enforces RLS on that pool is unverified (no Postgres was run).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (E-1, an escalation candidate).

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here.

* Route the tenant-pool branch through the GUC path (`queryWithTenantGuc`, with the GUC in the same transaction), or drop the tenant-pool branch while per-tenant databases are off.
* **Resolve the overlap first.** KS-174 (In Progress) step 1 plans this remedy: "Tenant-pool-manager (or a query wrapper) sets `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction". It never names `tenantManager`, `getPool` or auth's `db.ts`. KS-458 (Done) bundled the GUC for the default pool only. If KS-174 is the live home, merge this ticket into it; this one carries the measured location and consequence.
* **Census every** `query(…, tenantId)` **caller** before fixing. The gate's single-line grep found one, which is not a count.
* **Regression cell:** with multi-tenancy on and fail-closed RLS, an approve whose UPDATE carries the tenant either raises the level or is refused. Never a 200 over an unchanged level.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**,** `services/auth/src/db.ts:47-70`**:**
  * `query(text, params, tenantId)`: `if (tenantId && tenantManager)` returns `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query(text, params)` (`:53-60`). No GUC. The `try` does not `await`, so a rejected query is not caught by its fallback.
  * Only without a tenant manager does it use `runWithTenantId(tenantId, () => queryWithTenantGuc(getPool(), …))` (the KS-458 path).
* **When the branch is taken** (the gate's read): `initTenantManager` needs `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED === 'true'` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`. `TenantPoolManager.getPool` returns the default pool unless `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'` and the tenant resolves to another database.
* **The gate's pool table** (approve, RLS modelled on):
  * manager on, no per-tenant DB: the UPDATE runs on the default pool with no GUC and matches 0 rows. Develop answers 200 APPROVED with the level basic (a false success). Head answers 503 PENDING basic, even with no fault.
  * a distinct tenant DB: the level UPDATE lands in the tenant database while the request row stays in the default database (a pre-existing split).
* **Callers read so far:** `getUserById(id, tenantId)` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:407`) and `updateUser`'s UPDATE (`:796`). The census is not done.
* **Config** (READ; unverifiable without `az`, not run):
  * the auth container in `services.bicep` has no `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (the only bicep hit, `:798`, is originate's);
  * `env.dev.json` / `env.demo.json` set it `true` in a shared block (whether [deploy.sh](<http://deploy.sh>) consumes it was not re-read);
  * `docker-compose.yml` auth uses `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}`;
  * `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is set nowhere in deployment or compose.
* **Related:** KS-1194 (where it was measured), KS-174, KS-458, KS-1055 (per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations).
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `tenantManager.getPool`: 0 of 3 scanned.
  * `getPool`: 1, KS-213 (originate's per-tenant pool fan-out through pgbouncer; a different defect).
  * `applyTenantGuc`: 0, but the search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`: 12, and `tenant GUC`: 19. The closest are KS-174 (above), KS-458, KS-468 (GUC not seeded on gateway proxy routes) and KS-1055. None names the tenant-pool branch in auth's `db.ts`.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §7 and E-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: originate documents.ts is the first router to mix a tenant-pool READ with a default-pool WRITE — on a dedicated-DB tenant it fails closed
description:
## BLUF

At #1239's head the `/share` and `/transfer-custody` handlers **read** through `req.db` (the tenant pool set by `extractTenantContext`) and **write** through `withTenant`, which always uses `tenantManager.getDefaultPool()`. **On a tenant whose config resolves to a dedicated database those are two different databases.**

`documents.ts` **is the first router to do this.** Every other non-test `withTenant` call site — 9, all in `routes/adminConfig.ts` — sits under `adminConfig.ts:30` `(req as any).db = prisma // Always shared DB`, so that router reads and writes one database by design.

## Reach, measured

* A pool other than `getDefaultPool()` **is** reachable in code: `getPool` returns a dedicated `Pool` when `perTenantDbEnabled` (`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'`) **and** the tenant's config resolves elsewhere.
* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` **appears in 0 tracked config files** — compose, deployment and bicep; bicep sets only `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`. So it is **latent and gated on a variable no template sets**.

## Behaviour on a dedicated-DB tenant, by reading

It **fails closed** rather than misplacing rows: `/share`'s target subquery runs in the default DB → NULL → `SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` → 404. `/transfer-custody`'s INSERT names a `document_id` absent from the default DB's `documents` → 23503 → rollback → 500.

**That is the right failure direction**, and it is why this is Minor rather than Major. It is still a router whose read and write disagree about which database it is talking to.

## NOT claimed

**Live proof NOT RUN** — no slot was available, and no per-tenant-DB tenant was provisioned. The reach above is static: read from `tenant-context.ts:93`, `tenant-pool-manager.ts:152/201-260` and `db.ts:308`, not executed.

## Related, and NOT a duplicate

**KS-1235** concerns **auth**'s `db.ts` sending tenant-scoped statements through `getPool(tenantId).query()` with **no tenant GUC** under fail-closed RLS. Same neighbourhood — tenant pool versus default pool — but a different service and a different mechanism (a missing GUC there, a read/write pool mismatch here). Read in full before filing.

## Fix shape

`withTenant` checks out from `getPool(tenantId)` (or takes the request's pool). Cell: a manager stub whose `getPool(t) !== getDefaultPool()` must see **both** writes on `getPool(t)`'s client.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,291 issues incl. archived, 3,644 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1235**, KS-1055, KS-1054); `getPool(` -> 2 / 1 (KS-1235). **KS-1235 read in full — related, not a duplicate** (see above).
* `getDefaultPool` -> 1 total / **0 open**. `tenantPool` -> **0**.
* Control that fires: `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5. Nonsense control -> **0**.

`Refs KS-1263`; does not close it. Ruled TICKET (Minor) by the tier-1c gate, explicitly **not** part of #1239's round 2.

title: KYC mock document flow: a 1.5s timer writes back a STALE verification and silently clobbers the selfie's liveness result
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/kyc/:id/document` schedules a **1.5-second** `setTimeout` that closes over the verification object it loaded, mutates it, and writes it back. `POST /api/kyc/:id/selfie` loads a **fresh** object. So a selfie that arrives within ~1.5 s of the document upload has its liveness result **silently overwritten** by the stale object when the timer fires.

## The mechanism, read from the code at `8b91ab0ae`

1. `/document` (`services/kyc/src/index.ts`) does `await dbSaveVerification(verification)` and then, `if (KYC_PROVIDER === 'mock')`, `setTimeout(() => { …; dbSaveVerification(verification).catch(() => {}); }, 1500)`. The closure holds the object **as it was at upload time**.
2. `/selfie` does `const verification = await dbGetVerification(req.params.id)` — a **different object** — sets `livenessCompleted = true`, `livenessScore = 0.95`, marks the `facial` and `liveness` checks passed, and saves.
3. `dbSaveVerification` is a full upsert: `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET … liveness_completed = EXCLUDED.liveness_completed, liveness_score = EXCLUDED.liveness_score, checks = EXCLUDED.checks, …`.

So at t+1.5 s the stale object writes `liveness_completed = false`, `liveness_score = NULL` and a `checks` array without the two passes. **The three clobbered columns are named explicitly in the upsert** — this is not a guess about ORM behaviour.

The `.catch(() => {})` on that write means the overwrite is also silent if it fails.

## Scope and priority

`KYC_PROVIDER === 'mock'` gates the timer, so this is the **mock/demo path**, not a live-provider path. It is still the path every demo and every local test drives, and a verification that loses its liveness pass looks like a subject who never completed one. **Pre-existing** — not introduced by KS-386.

## Fix shape (not chosen)

Re-read the verification inside the timer before mutating it, or narrow the timer's write to the document fields it actually owns. Both change concurrency behaviour, so this wants its own gate rather than a drive-by.

## Provenance

Found by the KS-386 #839 tier-1 gate as F-5 and ruled by Wednesday 2026-09-06 as a ticket, not part of that round. Reproduced from the source independently before filing: the fresh-load in `/selfie`, the closure in `/document`, and the upsert's `DO UPDATE SET` column list were each read and are quoted above.

title: vc-issuer credentialRepo.store() falls back to memory SILENTLY when the database is unavailable — the caller is told it was stored
description:
## BLUF

`credentialRepo.store()` **in vc-issuer writes to the in-memory map and returns SILENTLY when the database is unavailable.** The caller is told the credential was stored. Nothing is logged, so there is no artefact anywhere that the write did not reach PostgreSQL — and on restart the credential is simply gone.

**Pre-existing, and deliberately NOT counted against PR #1231** (merged 2026-09-25 as `b83f986fd3e4`). That PR made the *table-absent* fallback LOUD — two WARNs per store. **This is the sibling path it did not touch:** `store()` then `if (!isDbAvailable()) return;` with no log at all. Raised by the tier-2b QA gate as **P-1** and ruled by the coordinator to be tracked separately rather than folded into #1231's scope.

## Why it matters, stated without overclaiming

A silent success on a durability-critical write is the failure mode that cannot be investigated after the fact: there is no line to grep, no counter, no artefact. The credential is served from memory for the life of the process and then disappears. Every other symptom (a verifier 404, a revoke that finds nothing) surfaces far from the cause.

**What is NOT claimed here:** that this is currently happening in any deployed environment. It is a code path, found by reading, with the trigger condition (`isDbAvailable()` false) unmeasured in Azure or on kintsugi.

## UNMEASURED — stated rather than glossed

Carried verbatim from the gate's findings on #1231, because they bound what this ticket knows:

* **Azure reach UNMEASURED.** Whether this path is reachable in the deployed environment was not measured; the Azure role and the table's state were not read.
* **The least-privilege SELECT is UNMEASURED.** Whether the runtime role can even perform the existence check that gates the fallback is unknown.
* The **kintsugi log observation** owed against KS-1281 would, if done, also say whether the loud sibling path fires there. That observation has not been made.

So the *severity* of this ticket rests on an unmeasured reach. **Measure the reach before choosing a fix shape** — if the path is unreachable in every deployed environment, a log line is the whole fix; if it is reachable, the question is whether a silent memory write is acceptable at all for credentials.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. **Log it** — match what #1231 did for the table-absent path: a WARN naming the credential id and the reason. Smallest change; makes the event investigable.
2. **Refuse it** — treat a store with no database as an error the caller must handle, rather than a success. Correct if credentials must be durable, and a behaviour change that needs its own decision.

(1) is strictly an improvement and does not foreclose (2).

* Controls that fire: `KS-1281` -> 1; `consumeResetToken` -> 2. So the search discriminates.

title: Rate-limit refusals name the wrong field: 400 says "Key required" when the key was fine, and 403 says "Caller has no tenant" when the caller has one
description:
## BLUF

**Every new refusal path returns a message that names the wrong thing.** A 400 says the key is missing when the key was fine; a 403 says the caller has no tenant when the caller has a perfectly good one. Charter §4d: a 4xx must not be scored as a healthy rejection without knowing *why* it was returned — and these messages actively mislead about the why.

Recoverable rather than silent: `details` carries the truth on the 400.

## ITEM 1 — `/reset` answers 400 "Key required" for failures that have nothing to do with the key

`index.ts:1358` — the top-level message is a constant:

```
{"key":"login","tenantId":"   "}      -> 400 "Key required"  details:[{path:["tenantId"],message:"must not be blank"}]
{"key":"login","tenantId":"\ud800"}   -> 400 "Key required"  details:[{path:["tenantId"],message:"must not contain an unpaired surrogate"}]
{"key":"login","tenantId":257 c.p.}   -> 400 "Key required"  details:[{path:["tenantId"],message:"must not exceed 256 characters"}]
```

The key was supplied and was fine in all three. **KS-970 item 6 has just PUBLISHED "Refused with** `400` **if present but blank"** — so the contract now promises a refusal whose top-level message names a different field.

**Fix-shape:** derive the message from the first failing path, or make it generic ("Invalid request body").

## ITEM 2 — the 403 "Caller has no tenant" now fires when the caller HAS a tenant

`index.ts:1267` (`/check`) and `index.ts:1377` (`/reset`). After KS-970 item 2 this fires when the caller has a good tenant and the *user* claim or the *body* is unusable:

```
claims {tenantId:'…a', userId:123}  -> 403 "Caller has no tenant"   <- false: the caller has tenant …a
```

**Fix-shape:** split it, so "no claim to scope by" and "present but unusable" say different things.

## ⚠ AN IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD I MEASURED, WHICH THE FINDING DOES NOT MENTION

`"Caller has no tenant"` appears at **FOUR** sites, not two: `index.ts:665`, `:716`, `:1267`, `:1377`. **A fix that greps for the string will touch all four and two of them are correct.**

Verified at `0281b0faa`:

* `:665` **and** `:716` **are NOT instances.** Both guard `if (!isPlatformRole(...) && !callerTenantId)` — they test the tenant claim *directly*, so the message is literally true there.
* `:1267` **and** `:1377` **ARE the instances.** Both sit behind `if (scope === null)`, and `scope` is null for **three** different reasons — no tenant claim, a MALFORMED tenant, or a MALFORMED user/`sub`. The message asserts only the first.

So the finding named the right two sites. **The other two share the string and not the defect**, and that distinction is the thing to carry into the fix.

## REGRESSION TEST

**Assert the message TEXT, not just the status.** Every cell here passes today on status alone, which is why the defect shipped: a 400 is a 400 and a 403 is a 403 whatever they say. Include a cell for `:665` or `:716` asserting the message stays "Caller has no tenant" there, so a fix does not over-reach into the two correct sites.

## RELATED, NOT MERGED IN

Item 2's root cause is the same tri-state as **KS-975**. Kept separate because the fix lives in the error-construction path rather than in the tri-state itself — but whoever takes one should read the other.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

STRING `Caller has no tenant`, `Key required` · SYMBOL `resetRateLimitSchema`, `checkRateLimitSchema`, `explicitScope`, `principalScope` · PATH `services/security/src/index.ts`. Linear's search is fuzzy on multi-word phrases and returned ~20 loosely-related hits for each string; **none on inspection concerns these routes' message construction.** The precise symbol searches return only **KS-970** (parent) and **KS-645** (a closed Duplicate about `/reset`'s role check, a different property). Control: a `KS-970` search is non-zero, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-1 gate on **#894 over #893**, verdict 2026-09-07T09:45:45Z, quoted verbatim by the coordinator. **All four call sites re-verified against** `0281b0faa` **before filing** — which is how the two non-instances were found.

title: Published bound vs runtime bound on rate-limit scope: /check enforces code UNITS against a published code-POINT maxLength, and scopeField bounds the untrimmed string
description:
## BLUF

**Two places where the PUBLISHED bound does not match the bound the runtime enforces.** F-1 is MAJOR and leads: `/api/rate-limit/check` publishes `maxLength: 256` and enforces **UTF-16 code units**, on the route with **no role gate** — so the published contract is wrong for every unauthenticated integrator on the one endpoint anybody can reach.

**Correcting the grouping rationale I was handed:** these are the same **CLASS**, not the same fix. They sit in different schemas in different files and the edits differ — F-1 changes the counting UNIT, F-5 changes WHAT is counted. They are one ticket because they are one logical path (published contract vs runtime bound), not because one change closes both.

## ITEM 1 (MAJOR, gate F-1) — `/check` publishes code points and enforces code units

Measured at `0281b0faa`:

```
RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX = 256                                rateLimitScope.ts:48
/reset  key: boundedByCodePoints(z.string().min(1))     requestSchemas.ts:81
        -> [...value].length <= 256   = CODE POINTS
/check  key: z.string().min(1).max(RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX)  index.ts:513
        -> zod .max() on a string     = UTF-16 CODE UNITS
```

The published contract states the bound **counts code points** in as many words (`security.openapi.ts:560`, and again at `:570` and `:581`).

So a key of **256 astral characters is 256 code points and 512 code units**: inside the published limit, refused by `/check`.

**Not introduced by #894.** `/check` was always `.max()`; KS-970 item 4 aligned `/reset` and thereby revealed the asymmetry. It was deliberately NOT folded into #894, because that would have moved a gated head and turned a clean GO into a re-gate.

**Fix-shape:** `boundedByCodePoints` on `/check`'s `key`, matching `/reset`.

## ITEM 2 (POLISH, gate F-5) — the published bound measures a string the runtime does not use

`scopeField()` validates the **raw** string; `claim()` scopes by the **trimmed** one. Verified in code at `0281b0faa`: `rateLimitScope.ts:88` trims, while `requestSchemas.ts:68-70` applies `[...value].length <= RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX` to the raw value (only the blank-check at `:67` trims).

Gate measurement:

```
tenantId = " " + "a"x256   raw 257 c.p. / trimmed 256 c.p.  ->  400 "must not exceed 256 characters"
tenantId =       "a"x256                                     ->  accepted
...and both would target the SAME bucket (explicitScope equal -> true)
```

So a caller is refused for exceeding a bound on a value that, after the runtime's own normalisation, is inside it.

**The house standard already prescribes the idiom that avoids this** — `2_Project_Files/CLAUDE.md:173-181` (KS-202): `.trim()` **before** `.min()`/`.max()`. It also notes `z.string().trim().min(1)` already rejects `'   '`, i.e. the platform's existing idiom would have closed KS-970 item 1 without a bespoke refine and kept the bound on the value actually used.

**Also:** item 6's published descriptions state the blank and surrogate refusals but never say values are trimmed, so `" acme "` is published as a distinct valid value that silently targets `acme`.

**Fix-shape:** `z.string().trim()` at the head of `scopeField()`, and one clause in the published description saying leading/trailing whitespace is stripped.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `checkRateLimitSchema`, `scopeField`, `boundedByCodePoints`, `RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX`, `rateLimitScope`, `explicitScope`, `principalScope` · STRING `maxLength`, `code points` · PATH `services/security/src/index.ts`, `requestSchemas.ts`, `rateLimitScope.ts`.

`scopeField` and `boundedByCodePoints` return **0** hits. `rateLimitScope`/`explicitScope`/`principalScope`/`maxLength` return **KS-970 only** (this work's parent). `checkRateLimitSchema` **returns KS-645 — checked, and it is NOT this**: KS-645 is a closed **Duplicate** about `/api/rate-limit/reset`'s role check, a different property of a different route. Control: a `KS-970` search returns a non-zero hit, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-1 gate on **#894 over #893**, verdict 2026-09-07T09:45:45Z. Findings quoted verbatim by the coordinator; **every code claim above re-verified against** `0281b0faa` **before filing**, not taken on relay.

title: rateLimitScope tri-state: a MALFORMED `sub` silently became a 403 on the ungated /check, and `null` still slips through explicitScope's second line
description:
## BLUF

**Two arms of the ABSENT-vs-MALFORMED tri-state in** `rateLimitScope.ts` **that nothing pins.** Item 1 is a **behaviour change that already shipped on a live, ungated route** and is currently reversible without a single test going red. Item 2 is a hole in a backstop, not reachable at the wire today.

**Correcting the framing I was handed:** the grouping described both as *"unpinned arms rather than live defects"*. That is right for item 2 and **understates item 1** — item 1 changed a live response from **200 to 403** on `/api/rate-limit/check`, which has **no role gate**. Unpinned, yes; but not merely theoretical.

## ITEM 1 (MINOR by severity, but a live behaviour change — gate F-2) — a MALFORMED `sub` became a refusal, undisclosed and unpinned

**Location:** `rateLimitScope.ts:118` — `const user_ = rawUser === ABSENT ? claim(user?.sub) : rawUser;`

Gate measurement, same input at both SHAs:

| claims | #893 `ab1053141` | #894 `e02d0fecc` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `{tenantId:'…a', sub:123}` | `t:…\|u:` (tenant bucket, **200**) | `null` **-> 403** |
| `{tenantId:'…a', sub:'  '}` | `t:…\|u:` (**200**) | `null` **-> 403** |

`sub` inherits the refusal because `claim(user?.sub)` can itself return `MALFORMED`, and `:121` refuses on `MALFORMED`.

**Verified in code at** `0281b0faa`**:** the comment at `:114-116` does address `sub` — but only to say a MALFORMED `userId` must not route around via `sub`. It never states that a MALFORMED `sub` is itself a refusal. So the gate's reading is right: the documented tri-state covers `userId`, and the new cells cover `sub` only as a good string.

**It is unpinned, proved by the gate:** restoring #893's behaviour (map a MALFORMED `sub` back to `ABSENT`) leaves **all 179 cells green**. A future change can silently revert it. **A check that cannot fail wearing a feature's clothes.**

**Fix-shape:** decide it deliberately, say so in the comment, and pin it — one cell each way (`sub: 123` refuses; `sub: 'u1'` scopes), so the arm has a failure mode.

## ITEM 2 (MINOR, gate F-4) — `explicitScope`'s second line still has item 1's exact hole for `null`

**Location:** `rateLimitScope.ts:86` — `if (value === undefined || value === null) return ABSENT;`

The design is stated at `:228-231`: *"The schema refuses these first; this is the second line, for any caller that bypasses it."* Across 14 shapes the second line refuses 12 (`'   '`, `'\t\n'`, `''`, NBSP, BOM, U+3000, `123`, `{}`, `[]`, `false`, `NaN`, `0`) and **treats JSON** `null` **as ABSENT**, which falls through to `principalScope(caller)` — reproducing item 1's exact shape: a **present** field silently retargeting the caller's own bucket.

**Honestly bounded, and this is the half not to lose: NOT reachable at the wire today.** `z.string()....optional()` rejects `null` — the gate drove it: `{"key":"login","tenantId":null}` -> `400 invalid_type, expected string, received null`, caller's bucket untouched. Independently confirmed here before filing: `scopeField()` is a non-nullable `z.string()`, and the only product caller of `explicitScope` (`index.ts:1373`) passes already-validated `parsedBody.data`.

So this is **a hole in the backstop, not a live defect**. It matters only because the backstop exists precisely for the case where the schema is bypassed — and `null` is exactly what a client library serialising an unset field would send.

**Fix-shape:** `explicitScope` should treat `null` in a **body** as MALFORMED while `principalScope` keeps treating a `null` **claim** as ABSENT — different questions about different inputs. **Regression test:** extend the second-line cell with `explicitScope({tenantId: null}, caller)` -> `null`, plus a CONTROL that `explicitScope({}, caller)` still returns the caller's own scope.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `rateLimitScope`, `explicitScope`, `principalScope`, `claim(`, `MALFORMED`, `ABSENT`, `scopeField` · PATH `services/security/src/rateLimitScope.ts`. Only **KS-970** (this work's parent) returns an open hit; `scopeField` returns 0. Control: a `KS-970` search is non-zero, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-1 gate on **#894 over #893**, verdict 2026-09-07T09:45:45Z, quoted verbatim by the coordinator. **Every code claim re-verified against** `0281b0faa` **before filing.**

title: start-secuura.sh never waits for five default-profile, healthchecked services — demo-service, mcp-server, pgbouncer, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation — "All 27 containers are healthy" can print while they are still booting
description:
## BLUF

`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`'s health wait, `--status` report and timeout diagnostic all iterate `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES` — 27 names (the [KS-312](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-312/cut-midnight-zk-selective-disclosure-remove-service-privacy-ui) cut of the original list). The compose files declare **33** default-profile, long-running containers. Six are not on the list. One is `stack-marker` ([KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) label carrier, correctly excluded). The other **five are real services with healthchecks and** `restart: unless-stopped` that the script has never waited for:

| service | healthcheck | in the wait list |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `demo-service` | yes | no |
| `mcp-server` | yes | no |
| `pgbouncer` | yes | **no** — and every service's `DATABASE_URL` goes through it |
| `tenant-provisioning` | yes | no |
| `tokenisation` | yes | no |

So `✓ All 27 containers are healthy` and `Containers: 27/27 running` can print while any of these is still starting or already `unhealthy`; the post-start checks that depend on them (anything through pgbouncer, tenant provisioning, tokenisation) then race the boot. Not new — measured the same on `develop` before [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s); [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) only made the list slot-correct and added the test that exposed the gap.

## How it was found

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_expected_services.test.sh` ([KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s), PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)) derives the set the script should wait for from the compose files — every `container_name: ${STACK_PREFIX:-secuura}-<svc>` (40) − `profiles:`-gated (5: cardano-mock, cardano-devnet, guardian, queue, ollama) − `restart: "no"` one-shots (2: migrations, demo-overlay) = 33 — and asserts equality with `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES`. To make that green without deciding platform-k base-code behaviour on Peter's ticket, the five above (plus `stack-marker`) sit in the test's `KNOWN_UNWAITED` list, each annotated "as above — script-behaviour call for Kamil". **This ticket is that call.**

## Decision needed (Kamil — platform-k base code)

Either:

1. **Wait for them.** Add the five suffixes to `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES` (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`, the `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES=(` block; the count comment says 27 → 32) and delete their five lines from `KNOWN_UNWAITED` in the test. The wait treats `health=none` as healthy, so a service without a healthcheck costs nothing; these five have one, so the wait becomes real. Or —
2. **Deliberately not wait**, per service, with the reason written next to it in `KNOWN_UNWAITED` (e.g. "demo-service is only reachable via a deleted gateway location, [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto) B-6") — the test then keeps the exception honest, failing if the service is ever removed.

Red→green either way: the test is green now only because of the exceptions; removing a line from `KNOWN_UNWAITED` makes it red until the script waits for that service.

## Where

* `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` — `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES=(` block (27 entries).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_expected_services.test.sh` — `KNOWN_UNWAITED` (6 entries).
* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` — the five services' `healthcheck:` blocks.

Live context: on the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-2/slot-4 runs the summary reads `33 running, 30–31 healthy` while the wait reported 27/27 — the gap is these services plus the two one-shots.

title: kyc `livenessVideo` is accepted by spec and runtime, then silently discarded — no code path reads it
description:
## BLUF

`livenessVideo` is accepted by both the OpenAPI spec and the runtime Zod schema on `POST /api/kyc/{id}/selfie`, and **no code path anywhere reads, stores or processes it.** A caller who uploads liveness evidence gets `success: true` and the bytes are discarded.

## Recommendation

Decide which half is right, then make the other match — do not align one to the other by reflex. Either implement storage + liveness processing, or remove the field from the schema and the spec. Documenting it as inert (done in KS-487 B-4) is a stopgap, not the fix.

## Detail

* Declared: `services/kyc/src/index.ts` `submitSelfieSchema` (`livenessVideo: z.string().optional()`) and `services/kyc/src/kyc.openapi.ts` `KycSelfieUploadRequestSchema`.
* Repo-wide grep for `livenessVideo` returns **only those two declarations plus a comment** — no reader, no writer, no persistence.
* Meanwhile the handler sets `livenessCompleted: true` and `livenessScore: 0.95` in mock mode regardless of what was sent (and regardless of whether `livenessVideo` was sent at all).

This is the KS-624/625/KS-488-C-2 family: a contract that advertises a capability the runtime does not have. Found while fixing KS-487 B-4 (magic-byte verification on the sibling image fields).

Filed from session 30. Not fixed in the B-4 PR — that PR's scope is image content verification, and silently deleting or implementing a published field is a contract change that deserves its own decision.

title: KS-754 gate F-4: DEPLOY CONDITION — apply 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, or every connector erasure shreds the DEK then aborts forever (and run-migrations.sh exits 0 when migrations fail)
description:
🔴 **THIS IS A DEPLOY CONDITION, not only a ticket. No deploy is authorised by the #914 gate.**

## The condition — for whoever rolls originate

**Apply migration 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, and confirm** `processed_by` **is** `text` **in the target DB first.**

## What happens if you don't — driven, not theorised (gate scenario S2)

Head code against a DB where 048 has not landed: **every connector erasure anonymises the user, destroys the DEK, then aborts.** `USER_ERASED=0`, DSR left `processing`. The cause (`22P02`) is **not transient**, so the connector's unbounded retry **never** succeeds — each iteration re-runs steps 1–11. This turns the F-1 finding from transient into **deterministic**.

## Why the existing guard does not save you — and this is its own defect

`docker-compose.yml` **does** gate originate on `migrations: service_completed_successfully`. But `scripts/run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 when migrations fail, by design** (its own closing block; BACKLOG #6). **So compose's condition is satisfied by a run in which 048 failed.**

On **Azure** there is no such ordering at all: migrations run at **api-gateway** boot (`startup-migrations.ts`) while originate is a separate app.

## Fixes — two, and they are separable

1. The deploy-ordering condition above, recorded where a deployer reads it (PR body + `DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` / the DR runbook), not only here.
2. `run-migrations.sh` **must not exit 0 on a failed migration** — that is a gate that cannot fail (KS-926 family), and it is what makes the compose guard decorative.

## Related

F-1 (same erasure path, made deterministic by this) and the KS-926 checks-that-cannot-fail campaign.

Report: `.../2026-09-09-qa-gate-ks754-pr914/report.md`

title: F-2: /health/services still reads response.ok only — a degraded service reads healthy there
description:
`/health/services` is the one aggregate #1037 didn't change. It still decides health from `response.ok` alone, so a 200 `{status:'degraded'}` reads **healthy**.

## Why it's low

It's **opt-in: 404 by default**, and the gate found the flag that enables it **set nowhere**. When opted in, it reads healthy. Graded SHIPS-WITH.

## What to do

Either route it through the same body-aware reading `services/health.ts` now uses, or remove the endpoint if nothing is meant to opt in.

---

title: A connector allow-list fails open when platform-settings integrations is not a clean array; one admin Settings save lifts every restriction
description:
## BLUF

**A connector restricted by a document-type allow-list becomes UNRESTRICTED whenever the stored platform-settings** `integrations` **container is not a clean array of object entries. One ordinary save on the admin portal's Settings page produces exactly such a container.**

* Major, pre-existing: the same at develop before PR #1035, at #1035's head and on the merged tree.
* It widens authorisation through the product's own UI, and it is silent: `GET /api/connector/info` then tells the connector `[]`.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-1, D1). Filed as its own ticket, not folded into KS-1230, per Wednesday's ruling.

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here. An escalation candidate (the gate's grading).

* **Read side, fail closed, in both readers:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1212-1219` (the create path) and `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:45-52` (the info reader). For the calling connector, any of these should refuse instead of reading as no restriction:
  * a non-array `integrations`;
  * a non-object entry;
  * a duplicate id;
  * a non-object `config`.
* **Portal:** `frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` must not regroup `integrations`, or any array, through `key.split('.')`. It flattens every category into `category.key` form values on load (`:37-42`) and splits them back on save (`:66`), which turns an array into `{"0": entry}`.
* **Regression cells:** each container shape below × {typed, untyped} → 403. A Settings-save round trip keeps `integrations` an array.

## Detail

* **Repro** (measured at runtime by the gate: the real route, both boots):
  1. As SYSTEM_ADMIN, `PUT /api/admin/settings` with `integrations: [{ id: "c1", config: { allowedDocumentTypes: ["SSD_DOCUMENT"] } }]` and a `general.platformName`.
  2. Connector `c1` sends `POST /api/documents` with `documentType: "DOCUMENT"` → 403.
  3. On the admin portal Settings page, change the platform name and save. The PUT body carries `integrations` as `{"0": {...}}`. The portal transform was PROBED by emulation and confirmed by reading `Settings.tsx`; no browser was driven.
  4. The same create → **201, forwarded to originate**.
* **Stored containers measured fail-open.** Each gives typed `DOCUMENT` → 201 forwarded, and info tells `[]`:
  * `{"0": entry}`;
  * `[null, entry]` (`.find` throws on `null.id`);
  * `[{id, config: {}}, entry]` (duplicate id, first wins);
  * `[{id, config: "SSD_DOCUMENT"}]`;
  * `"x"` (`.find` is not a function);
  * `null`.
  * Control: `[entry]` → 403.
* **Mechanism:** the container parse sits inside `try { … } catch {}`. A throw or a miss leaves `connectorConfig = {}`, which reads as no restriction. The same parse is in the info reader.
* **Related:**
  * KS-1204: PR #1035 made the leaf value fail closed, but the container above it still fails open;
  * KS-1230: write-side validation of the value, a different defect;
  * the 24 h platform-settings TTL expiry, the same fail-open class, filed separately.
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `Settings.tsx`: 0 of 118 scanned.
  * `connectorConfig`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned only 1 result, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `integrations`: 15, none about the container parse (the security-review umbrellas KS-485, KS-488 and KS-492, harness tickets and m365 redirect tickets).
  * `platform-settings`: 3. KS-1230 (write-side validation of the allow-list value), KS-1176 (comments) and KS-37 (admin SPA tests); none covers the container.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`. Line references re-read at develop `34cdcfb26`.
* Refs KS-1204.

title: Dead-estate pointers in RUNTIME SOURCE outside deployment/azure — system-status.ts hard-codes secuura-staging-* hosts, westeurope and a dead URL suffix
description:
## BLUF

KS-490 (3) / PR #852 closed every dead-estate pointer under `deployment/azure` — **6 of 6, and that claim is correct for that directory.** The class does not stop there: it extends into `services/`, where the pointers sit in **runtime source**, not in a template nobody consumes.

title: OpenAPI compliance: documentation gaps across the spec (descriptions, parameter docs, operationId)
description:
## Overview

A compliance matrix over our API definitions identified gaps in the documentation features clients rely on. Still no urgency — this remains a reminder ticket, best addressed per-API as each is touched.

## Which standard

The original analysis was run against **OpenAPI 3.2.0**, and that is now the current released specification (Sept 2025) — the links below point at it. We publish `openapi: 3.1.0` today. The distinction does not affect this ticket: `summary`, `description`, `operationId` and the Schema Object are documentation fields whose meaning is unchanged between the two versions, and 3.2 is a non-breaking feature release over 3.1.

**Repo policy, landed 2026-07-10:** CLAUDE.md now carries a MUST rule — *the OpenAPI spec is the contract, never a validator's defaults* — and states the version stance explicitly: **cite 3.2, emit 3.1**, until Akto is proven against 3.2. The QA cheat sheet's spec pill reads `OpenAPI 3.1 (3.2 target)`. No emitted artefact changed: `secuura-api.yaml` still declares `3.1.0` and the generator still constructs `OpenApiGeneratorV31`.

Adopting 3.2 is a separate piece of work with its own blocker — [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence). In short: Akto parses specs with Java `swagger-parser`, whose 3.2 support ([swagger-api/swagger-parser#2248](<https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-parser/issues/2248>)) is still open with no activity, so a 3.2 document would be rejected outright at import and every Akto scan would run against an empty collection. **Any spec-version bump needs testing against Akto first.** Nothing in this ticket requires it — every item below is valid under both versions.

* [OpenAPI 3.2.0](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0>) — [Operation Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#operation-object>) (`summary`, `description`, `operationId`) · [Parameter Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#parameter-object>) (`description`) · [Schema Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#schema-object>)

*(Attached file autogenerated from the* `api-explorer` *code.)*

## Current state — re-measured 2026-07-10

Counted directly from the published spec: **316 operations** across **284 paths**, with **183 declared parameters**.

| Feature | Missing | Coverage | Since original |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `operationId` | **316 / 316** | 100% missing | *not previously measured* |
| Parameter `description` | **183 / 183** | 100% missing | (was 140 endpoints) |
| Operation `description` | 225 / 316 | 71.2% missing | improved (was 250) |
| 2xx response schema | 8 / 316 | 2.5% missing | improved (was 10) |
| Request body schema | 0 / 128 | ✅ complete | **resolved** (was 42) |
| 4xx/5xx error response | 0 / 316 | ✅ complete | **resolved** (was 1) |
| Operation `summary` | 0 / 316 | ✅ complete | — |

Two of the original six gaps have closed entirely, and two others narrowed — good progress from work done in the meantime. The remaining picture is dominated by three items.

## What stands out now

`operationId` **— 0 of 316.** Not measured in the original pass, and the most consequential omission. Per the [Operation Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#operation-object>) it is optional, but it is the handle that tooling keys on: `openapi-generator` derives client method names from it, and OpenAPI `links` **must** reference an operation by `operationId`. Its absence is a hard blocker for [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) (stateful POST→GET→DELETE chains) — you cannot declare a link to an operation that has no id. Worth doing first for that reason alone.

**Parameter descriptions — 183 of 183.** Every declared parameter lacks a `description`. Cheap to add where the source `*.openapi.ts` registration already knows what the parameter means, and it is the field a developer reads in Swagger UI before anything else.

**Operation descriptions — 225 of 316.** All 316 have a `summary`, so nothing is anonymous; the gap is the longer-form explanation. Lower priority than the two above.

## Suggested sequencing

1. `operationId` **on every operation** — mechanical, unblocks [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete)'s `links` work, and improves generated clients immediately.
2. **Parameter** `description`**s** — 183 fields, most one line each.
3. **Operation** `description`**s** — incrementally, as each API is touched.
4. **The 8 operations missing a 2xx response schema** — small, and each is likely a deliberate no-content response worth confirming rather than assuming.

Note that `secuura-api.yaml` is **generated** and byte-compared by `npm run check:openapi`, so all of the above are edits to the per-service `*.openapi.ts` registrations, followed by `npm run generate-openapi`. All four items emit constructs valid under 3.1 as well as 3.2, so none of them wait on [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence).

Each API can be updated independently, so there is flexibility in scheduling. Happy to help with any of it — particularly step 1, which is the one with a downstream dependency.

## Related

* [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) — stateful `links` + `operationId`. **Depends on step 1 here**; also blocked by [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and).
* [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence) — OpenAPI 3.2 readiness; Akto cannot parse 3.2 yet, so the version bump must be tested against it first.
* [KS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-424/openapi-auth-contract-make-security-explicit-on-every-operation) — makes `security` explicit on every operation (a separate Operation Object field with the same "implied vs stated" problem).
* [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) — OpenAPI inline examples; [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) — request schema tightening. Parallel work in the same generated file.

title: A duplicated x-api-key header defeats key authentication via header joining
description:
Sending **two** `x-api-key` **headers** — in either order — **defeats key authentication**.

## Mechanism

Node joins the repeated header's values into one string; the joined string fails key validation; the request then **falls through to the anonymous / JWT principal**, which on an optional mount answers **200**.

## Measured

Identical at the #1034 head and at develop `34cdcfb26`, so it is **pre-existing** and not #1034's. The gate listed it as a ticket candidate without assigning a severity; filed here as High because it is an authentication-bypass shape.

This is **KS-736 / KS-1207 territory** — whoever picks it up should read those first, since the fall-through-to-anonymous pattern is the same one they cover.

## What to do

Reject a repeated `x-api-key` outright rather than validating the joined value, and make the failure a refusal rather than a fall-through.

---

Filed from the #1034 / KS-1215 tier-1 gate report `2026-09-18-ks1215-1034-e4624218b-tier1-r1`, at merge of `a105cd32b1ed9c6927ae6e797f8259224d8480c6`. Pre-existing unless stated; **not** introduced by #1034.

title: PUT /api/admin/settings stores a connector's allowedDocumentTypes in any shape - validate it as an array of strings at write time
description:
## BLUF

`PUT /api/admin/settings` **stores a connector's** `allowedDocumentTypes` **in any shape.** It should validate the value as an array of strings at write time, so a malformed allow-list can never be stored.

* This is the write-side twin of PR #1035 (KS-1204). #1035 makes the READ side refuse every create when the stored allow-list is not an array (fail closed). The write still accepts a string, an object or an empty string, so an admin can lock a connector out of all creates with one malformed save, and learn it only from 403s.
* The frontend types it as `string[]` (`frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:1075`), but the API does not enforce that.

## Recommendation

In `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` `PUT /api/admin/settings` (`:1123-1129` at develop `732c13459`), validate every `integrations[].config.allowedDocumentTypes` present in the body as an array of strings (absent stays allowed). Refuse a malformed body with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the path, before the merge and the write.

* **Regression cells:** a string, an object and an empty string → 400, and the stored settings are unchanged; an array of strings, an empty array and an absent key → 200.
* Consider the same check for the other integration config fields the gateway reads (for example `workflowPolicy`) only if a reader depends on their shape; not required here.
* Not built here.

## Detail

* **Today:** the handler reads the stored `platform-settings`, shallow-merges the request body over it (`{ ...existing, ...body }`), writes it, and answers 200 with the merged settings. It does no validation.
* **Why it matters after #1035:** the read side refuses a non-array allow-list with 403 for every create, including the type it names and untyped bodies. So a malformed value is no longer a silent widening, but it becomes a silent outage for that connector. It is caught only by the connector's failed creates.
* **Migration residual (stated on #1035):** whether any such stored config exists today is unmeasured.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):
  * `allowedDocumentTypes`: 3. KS-1204 (the read side), KS-1203 (an untyped create stored as DOCUMENT) and KS-1198 (a connector JWT presented directly as Bearer); none covers validating the write.
  * `PUT /api/admin/settings`: 1 (KS-1204, which names the write as the only path).
  * `admin/settings`: 0. The fuzzy search did not return KS-1204 for this shorter term, so the zero is the search, not the board.
* Refs KS-1204 (stays In Progress).

title: /system/status tells operators to 'start the service locally (npm run dev)' for a DEGRADED optional service that is already up
description:

title: POST /api/certifications/:id/verify forwards a revoked session's Bearer to originate: the gateway's session check never runs on this route
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (api-gateway `routes/verification.ts:784`, mounted with no `authenticateToken`) forwards whatever `Authorization` the caller sent to originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:788`). Measured in-process: a **REVOKED** session's JWT, alone or beside a valid connector key, reaches originate as that user's Bearer, because the gateway's session check never runs on this route. On `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`:488`, `authenticateToken(true)`) the same revoked JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`. What originate does with that token is **NOT measured**.

## Recommendation

Measure originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` with a revoked session's JWT. That sets the severity, which the gate graded Minor pending that measurement.

## Detail

* Surfaced by the #1070-#1076 gate (`2026-09-19-batch1070-1076-tier1-r1`, finding N76-2).
* Pre-existing, not introduced by that batch: api-gateway product bytes are identical at develop `51dbedd39` and at every head of the batch. `verification.ts` is unchanged at develop `f9c28a8b8`.
* How the gate measured it: in-process, the real gateway app with loopback doubles; not against a live stack or a real session store.
* Related: KS-834, the pending decision on whether this route stays public. KS-834's text says a caller who sends a token "is still scoped downstream"; this finding is that a *revoked* session's token passes the gateway here unchecked.
* Also related: the revocation property established on the authenticated mounts (KS-1207, KS-1215).
* Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included):
  * literal title/description contains `certifications/:id/verify`: KS-834, KS-815 (archived, a control-byte guard);
  * `certifications/{id}/verify`: 0; `verification.ts:78`: 0;
  * `api/certifications/`: 38, none about Bearer forwarding;
  * `searchIssues("certifications verify")`, literal re-match: KS-834, KS-815.
  * None records the revoked-session forwarding.

title: Gateway health aggregates read anchoring's HTTP status only, so its degraded body (#728) never reaches /health/deep, /system/status or the health dashboard
description:
## BLUF

* **Anchoring now reports** `degraded` **honestly, but no public health surface can show it.**
  * Since #728 (KS-671), anchoring's `/health` answers HTTP 200 with `status: 'degraded'` and `degradedReasons` when the chain is unreachable. Keeping the 200 is deliberate.
  * All three public gateway health aggregates classify a service by HTTP status alone, so they show anchoring as `up` while it cannot reach the chain.
* **This is the** `/health/ready` **middle path the KS-671 review offered to split out** (KS-671 comments `eba1c64d` and `0c76ac61`, 2026-09-08). It was never filed.
* **Pre-existing, found by the kintsugi deploy gate on** `4554b25e2` (finding F-2, Minor). The aggregate code is older than #728; #728 is what made it matter.

## Recommendation

* **The fix:** make each aggregate read anchoring's body `status` and map `degraded` to a state other than `up`, with the regression cell below.
* Until then, `/health/deep` and `/status/` cannot show anchoring's chain health.

## Detail

### Mechanism, read at `4554b25e2`

* **Anchoring keeps the 200 on purpose.** `services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, around lines 336–347, keeps HTTP 200 on degraded, with the comment "Wiring an alert to `status: 'degraded'` is the monitoring change, tracked on KS-671".
* **The aggregates key on** `response.ok`**:**
  * `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:132` → `/health/deep` and `/health/ready` (the same handler, `health.ts:166-167`);
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/system-status.ts:333` → `/system/status` and `/api/system/status`;
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/health-dashboard.ts:59` → `/api/system/health/dashboard`.
* **No public route reaches anchoring's own** `/health`**.** The gateway mounts anchoring at `/api/anchors` and `/api/anchoring` only (`proxy.ts:765-781`).
* **The fields never surface.** `degradedReasons` and `reachability` appear in none of the four public aggregate bodies (the gate's `evidence/wire/`).

### Why a ticket of its own

* **It was left out of #728.** #728 is merged and running on kintsugi. The aggregate half was named on KS-671 as an offered split and left out of that push.
* **Its only record would go stale.** KS-671 moves on when #728 reaches demo, and the code comment above would then point at a closed ticket.
* **Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule:** a separate fix gets its own ticket.

### Regression test (the gate's)

* A stub anchoring that returns 200 with `{status: 'degraded'}` must not appear as `up` in `/health/deep`.

### Not tested

title: api-gateway: connector-key principals (verificationLevel 'api_key') fail meetsVerificationLevel against 'none' — every Platform-S originate 403s once the doc-type catalogue is seeded
description:
**BLUF:** `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key', 'none')` **returns false because** `'api_key'` **is not in** `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER` **(**`indexOf` **→ -1, and** `-1 >= 0` **is false). So once the document-type catalogue is seeded, every** `POST /api/documents` **from a Platform-S connector key is refused with** `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` **— even though** [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) **seeded** `SSD_DOCUMENT` **as "deliberately friction-free" with** `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`**. Fix is a few lines in** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`**; this is the K-side root cause of** [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api).

## Symptom

Platform-S app log, on every upload under a connector key (135–142 occurrences per full S suite run):

```
CardanoAnchor: originate POST status=403 body={"success":false,"error":{
  "code":"INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL",
  "message":"This document type requires NONE verification. Your current level is API_KEY."}}
```

S then falls back to flat `/api/anchors`, which succeeds — so the anchor badge goes green but **no K document exists**: no content-hash resolution for `/api/verification/verify`, no lineage root, no lifecycle events. S's `@k-live` suite fails 11/14 on this alone.

Reproduced 2026-09-16 on Peter's Mac, slot 4 pair: platform-k `0b25f823f` (develop, fresh worktree, fresh volumes) ↔ platform-s `2fa69634` and again `d36ff71e` (develop). Two full S suite runs, 12 failures each, 11 of them this.

## Builds under test

| Platform | Branch | Commit (full SHA) | Slot |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| platform-k | `develop` | `0b25f823f6660ac52b665f14055799ff0c3b616d` | 4 — gateway `:7182`, `secuura_slot4`, fresh worktree + fresh volumes |
| platform-s (run 1) | `develop` | `2fa696340967313fef214bfe1232f17a69cec410` | 4 — `https://localhost:5422`, `ssd-slot4` |
| platform-s (run 2) | `develop` | `d36ff71e5d347089c5cff08a0892bd8cb0e45385` | 4 — same slot, `--rebuild --reset`; `/Health/Data` `build.Commit` matched |

## Cause

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`

* `:39` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` = `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`
* `middleware/auth.ts:276` sets `verificationLevel: 'api_key'` on every connector-key principal.

`'api_key'` is not in the order → `indexOf` = `-1` → `-1 >= 0` is false → a connector key fails even `none`. Any other unknown level string fails the same way.

The check is only reached when `resolveDocumentType` finds the type. On an unseeded K it returns null and `:110-127` (the [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) fallback) passes through — which is why the failure appears and disappears between rebuilds, and why [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) saw the suite "green 2h earlier against the previous K". `routes/admin.ts:283-303` seeds `SSD_DOCUMENT` with `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'` and says why: *"deliberately friction-free … gating either would break those paths."* The ordering bug defeats that intent. Confirmed on the live K: `GET /api/document-types` lists `SSD_DOCUMENT`, `creatorVerificationLevel: none`.

## Fix (either; the first is narrower)

1. In `meetsVerificationLevel`, an unknown `userLevel` satisfies `requiredLevel === 'none'` only — treat `indexOf === -1` as index 0 when the requirement is `none`, and still refuse any higher requirement, so a connector key cannot originate a `STANDARD`-gated type by accident.
2. Or place `'api_key'` explicitly in the order — but where a machine credential ranks against human KYC levels is a product decision, not a bug fix.

Either way the message should stop rendering `NONE` as harder to meet than `API_KEY`.

## Verification

* Unit: `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','none') === true`; `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','standard') === false`; an arbitrary unknown string behaves the same as `'api_key'`.
* Live: S upload under a connector key against a **seeded** K → originate `201`; S `@k-live` `chain_match.spec.ts` green; `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves the document by content hash.

## Related

* [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) — the S side (surface K's `error.code` instead of the "revoked or wrongly scoped" guess); its open question "deliberate tightening or seed drift?" is answered here: neither.
* [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) — the catalogue seed that arms the check.

title: In Redis mode platform-settings expires 24 h after the last admin write, which erases every connector allow-list
description:
## BLUF

**In Redis mode the gateway stores platform-settings with a 24 h TTL, and nothing refreshes it.** So, by reading the code: 24 h after the last admin settings write, every connector allow-list disappears and every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

* **Major, pending measurement.** This is READ ONLY: no Redis was run.
* The same fail-open class as the container fail-open ticket filed alongside it.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-A).

## Recommendation

An escalation candidate (the gate's grading). Not built here.

1. **Measure first**, read-only, in a non-production gateway running in Redis mode: store an allow-list, `EXPIRE` the key (or wait out the TTL), then create as the restricted connector. The code reading predicts 201.
2. **If confirmed**, the owner decides the fix. Either platform-settings must not expire (no TTL, or a refresh), or a missing platform-settings must not read as "no restriction" for a connector that had one. It may be sequenced with the container fail-open read-side fix.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**:**
  * `services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:27`: `privacy: 86400` (24 hours);
  * `redis.ts:680-687`: `setNotificationSettings` writes `notif:<key>` with `setex(…, TTL.privacy, …)` when Redis is available;
  * after expiry, `getNotificationSettings('platform-settings')` returns null, and `routes/verification.ts:1214-1216` turns that into `integrations []`, which means no restriction;
  * the only `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', …)` call is `routes/admin.ts:1127` (`PUT /api/admin/settings`), so nothing re-writes the key.
* **Why local runs never show it:** the in-memory fallback (no Redis) is a Map with no TTL.
* **It also affects KS-1204's migration-residual reading.** A key past its TTL reads as absent, which means "no restriction stored anywhere", not "no malformed list". So a reading must quote the key's TTL beside the shapes.
* **Not measured:** Redis mode was not run (KS-535).
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `TTL.privacy`: 0 of 114 scanned.
  * `setNotificationSettings`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `platform-settings`: 3 (KS-1230, KS-1176, KS-37); none covers expiry.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-A: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1204.

title: A STRING allowedDocumentTypes substring-matches, and no cell pins documentType-over-type precedence (#1014 gate N-2 + N-3)
description:

* **N-2:** with `allowedDocumentTypes: "SSD_DOCUMENT"` (a string), `"SSD_DOCUMENT".includes("DOCUMENT")` is true, so a connector naming `DOCUMENT` passes the allow-list. Admitted-disallowed rows: **base 0, round 1 15, head and merged 11**, all DOCUMENT. At base the level check refused them 403; #1014's level change removed that accidental stop.

## Recommendation

**Built next by Seat A as a tier-1 follow-up PR** (Wednesday's ruling in the #1014 GO, 22:41:29Z), `Refs` this ticket:

* a fail-closed non-array guard on the allow-list;
* a precedence cell: the both-present disagreeing pair in both directions → 403 naming `documentType`'s value / 201 with the `documentType` type.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 round-2 delta gate on PR #1014 (KS-1176), findings **N-2** and **N-3**. Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014r2-9ba0caf78-tier1-r2/report.md`.

No other platform-settings writer was found. So the only route is an admin API write of a non-array.

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches over title, description and comments:
