* `precedence`: 136 / 19. The nearest class is KS-1118 (`documentHash`-over-`hash` precedence unpinned on verify), a different field and route.

None covers this.

Related: KS-1176.

title: Push preflight blocks the whole repo — two qs advisories (GHSA-4mjr / GHSA-x5fp) unbaselined across 27 standalone locks; fixed in qs@6.16.0
description:
## BLUF

**Two** `qs` **advisories landed and the push preflight now refuses every push to this repo** — legs 5/8 (root `npm audit`) and 6/8 (standalone-lock advisories, KS-531) both FAIL. Both are fixed in `qs@6.16.0`; the tree pins **6.14.2, 6.15.1 and 6.15.3** across **27 standalone lockfiles** plus the root.

This is a **hard block on the whole repo**, not a warning — no author can push until it is triaged.

## The advisories

| GHSA | summary | severity | vulnerable | patched |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g` | qs: DoS via attacker-controlled `isBuffer` | moderate | `>= 2.2.5, < 6.16.0` | **6.16.0** |
| `GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx` | qs: array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing | moderate | `>= 6.14.2, <= 6.15.3` | **6.16.0** |

## Blast radius — 27 of the standalone locks

`frontend/issuer`, `packages/shared`, `services/`: `analytics`, `anchoring`, `api-gateway`, `auth`, `billing`, `demo-service`, `governance`, `guardian`, `kyc`, `m365-integration`, `mcp-server`, `nft-certificate`, `originate`, `prism`, `queue`, `referral`, `security`, `shared`, `staking`, `tenant-provisioning`, `timestamping`, `tokenisation`, `transfer`, `vc-issuer`, `wallet-connector`.

`qs` is Express's query-string parser, so this is a **runtime** path on every HTTP service, not a build-tree-only acceptance like the `undici` entries in the baseline.

## Why this ticket exists rather than a same-session fix

The fix is a single version bump, but it lands in **27 standalone lockfiles**, each of which must be regenerated **containerised** (`node:24-alpine`, per `lockfile-cleanroom.sh`) — a host regen drops optional platform binaries. That is a platform-wide dependency change with its own review surface. Folding it into an unrelated in-flight PR would be wrong, and doing it unreviewed at 02:3x is worse.

## Done means

1. `qs` pinned at `>= 6.16.0` in the root lock and all 27 standalone locks, regenerated containerised.
2. Preflight legs **5/8 and 6/8 green** without a baseline entry for either GHSA.
3. Any temporary baseline entry added to unblock pushes is **removed in the same PR** — an exception that outlives its fix is the failure mode `audit-baseline.json` exists to prevent.

## Note on the interim

If a time-boxed baseline entry is used to unblock the queue, it must carry `reason`, `ticket` (this one) and `expires` per the KS-105 ticketed-exception model, so the gate re-fires rather than forgetting.

title: [Decision] Own the express 4 -> 5 call before the qs fuse lapses 2026-09-10 - KS-409 was archived and nothing replaced it
description:
## BLUF

**Nothing currently owns the express 4 -> 5 decision, and the two qs advisories un-baseline on 2026-09-10.** KS-409 (*Express 4 -> 5 migration, all 15 services*) was **archived on 2026-09-02T10:26:32** while it was still the remedy named by the qs baseline entries. When the fuse lapses, the push gate re-fires on `GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g` and `GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx` and blocks every author, with no ticket to re-fire onto.

**This ticket owns that decision. The decision itself is Kam's / Peter's, not the builder's.**

## The measurement (re-derived 2026-09-03, session 118)

Parsed **all 45 tracked** `package-lock.json` from the git blobs at develop `e02e15811` -- not read off a baseline row. Both advisories patch only in **qs 6.16.0**.

* **29 of 45 locks carry qs.** Resolved pins: `6.14.2` (26 locks), `6.15.1` (24), `6.15.3` (5) -- all vulnerable to both.
* **Declaring parents and their ranges: **`express@4.22.1 -> ~6.14.0` (26 locks) - `express@4.22.2 -> ~6.15.1` (2) - `express@5.2.1 -> ^6.14.0` (2) - `body-parser@1.20.4 -> ~6.14.0` (1) - `body-parser@1.20.6 -> ~6.15.1` (27) - `body-parser@2.3.0 -> ^6.15.2` (2) - `stripe@14.25.0 -> ^6.11.0` (2) - `url@0.11.4 -> ^6.12.3` (2).
* **Exactly ONE lock of 29 can reach 6.16.0** -- `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer`, whose only declaring parent is `url@0.11.4` at `^6.12.3`, with no express or body-parser in the path.
* The other **28** each carry at least one **tilde-capped** parent. Both locks that already hold **express 5.2.1** (`Blockchain/Dev` root and `services/mcp-server`) *also* carry express 4 and `body-parser@1.20.6` in the same tree -- **the caret parent sits beside a tilde parent, it does not replace it.**
* The gate is keyed by **GHSA, not by instance**, so clearing 1 lock of 29 removes no advisory.

## The options (the decision)

1. **Complete the express 4 -> 5 migration across the services** -- removes the tilde-capped parents rather than overriding past them. This is the fix shape. It is a real migration with its own blast radius (15 services) and wants its own plan.
2. **A deliberate** `overrides` **on qs** -- reaches 6.16.0 by violating two declared parent ranges. Fast, and it is a decision about deliberately contradicting a dependency's declared range, not a bump. Explicitly **not** taken by the builder.
3. **Re-baseline with a new expiry** -- moves the fuse, decides nothing, and should only be chosen with a named date and a named owner.

## Why the framing changed

Peter measured on #797 (2026-09-03) that fast-uri -- and by the same reading qs -- sits under **production** dependencies in `anchoring`, `originate`, `nft-certificate` and `mcp-server`, not only in build trees. qs is Express's query-string parser: **a runtime path on every HTTP service.** These entries are an **exposure that is time-boxed**, not a clearance. Reachability of the two specific defects has **not** been measured.

## Done means

- [ ] Kam or Peter rules between options 1-3, on this ticket.
- [ ] The ruling is written into `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`'s two qs `reason` fields **before 2026-09-10**, so the file the gate reads matches the record.
- [ ] If the ruling is option 1, the migration is planned as its own work with its own tickets.

## Provenance

Measurements: `git ls-tree -r e02e15811` + `json.load` of each lock blob, session 118, 2026-09-03. KS-409 archived state read from the Linear API the same session. The production-dependency reading is **Peter Obeden's**, from his #797 review of 2026-09-03T07:43:41Z. Related: KS-763 (the time-box), KS-531 (the superseded remedy note), KS-409 (archived; cited by identifier only -- archived issues refuse relations).

title: Bundled js-yaml copies ship in service runtime images and are invisible to audit-gate/audit-locks
description:
**BLUF:** two service runtime trees carry their own bundled copies of js-yaml code. Both audit gates (`audit-gate`, `audit-locks`) look for packages by name, so neither copy can ever be reported. The originate copy accepts the GHSA-2883 input shape, the same way vulnerable js-yaml 3.15.1 does. Whether any request path reaches either copy is **NOT traced**. **Severity: UNMEASURED.** It is not "High" until the first item below is measured.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1027 (finding F1, recorded as pre-existing and not moved by #1027). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1027-d7fc6cc55-tier2-r1/report.md`, "F1 detail".

## First item: a measurement, not a fix

1. **Runtime load trace in a built originate image.** Does anything load `confbox/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs` at start-up or on a request, and does `/shared`'s `@effect/platform` `httpApiSwagger` bundle load at all?
2. **Input reach.** Does any code path parse attacker-controlled YAML through either copy?

Only after both are measured: set a severity, and decide the fix shape (below).

## The gate's F1 paragraph, quoted

> * **Instrument, count-from-the-cause:** besides the package census (`*/node_modules/<name>/package.json`), every runtime tree was grepped for js-yaml's exception class `YAMLException` in `*.js/*.cjs/*.mjs`. Positive control (full installs): 8/9/8/8 files, including `node_modules/js-yaml/lib/*`. Runtime trees: governance 0, referral 0, vc-issuer 0, **originate 1** (`confbox/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs`), **/shared 2** (`@effect/platform/dist/{esm,cjs}/internal/httpApiSwagger.js`, a swagger-ui bundle with its own `YAMLException$1`). The package-name census reads NONE in the same trees. That is the blind spot: the drafter's D1 "none" is true of packages and false of code.
> * **Where they ship:** originate runner `:79 npm ci --omit=dev` keeps confbox (lock `node_modules/confbox` 0.2.4, `node_modules/c12` 3.3.4, `node_modules/@prisma/config` 7.8.0, none dev-flagged). Every service image `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared` (governance :74, originate :88, referral :89, vc-issuer :81), and shared-builder is a full `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, never pruned.
> * **Not moved by #1027:** develop vs head lock entries are identical for confbox, c12, @prisma/config and @effect/platform, and the `packages/shared` diff is empty (evidence/parse.out, and the census step in evidence/runtime.out).
> * **Vulnerable shape present?** Neither bundle contains `maxTotalMergeKeys` (count 0; js-yaml 3.15.2's loader.js has 7). The confbox chunk carries a "4.1.1" string once (version identity by string only, not proven). Bounded probe (evidence/loader_probe.out), shape derived from the 3.15.1→3.15.2 loader.js diff (evidence/dev_jsyaml.out):
>
> | input | js-yaml 3.15.1 | js-yaml 3.15.2 | confbox 0.2.4 bundled |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | CONTROL in-bounds, 5 empty merges (45 B) | accepted `{x:1}` | accepted `{x:1}` | accepted `{x:1}` |
> | 1 key × 150 empty merges (625 B) | accepted | **THREW abnormal merge sequence size** | accepted |
> | 200 keys × 100 empty merges (82 KB) | accepted 4.6 ms | **THREW exceeded maxTotalMergeKeys (10000)** | accepted 5.3 ms |
> | 4000 keys × 100 (1.65 MB) | accepted 31.6 ms | **THREW** 1.3 ms | accepted 37.8 ms |
>
> Cost was linear and bounded within these sizes. No super-linear amplification was demonstrated.
>
> * **Reachability (assumed, not traced):** 0 tracked files under `Blockchain/Dev/services` or `packages` import confbox, c12 or @prisma/config, 0 import `@effect/platform`, and 0 mention `HttpApiSwagger` (control: `from 'express'` in 250 files). No `prisma.config*` is tracked. Plausibly unreachable from request handling. A runtime load trace in a running image was NOT done (no image, by bounds).
> * **Fix-shape (for the owner, prose only):** decide whether bundled-copy advisories are in the audit gates' contract. If yes, add a code-signature leg (e.g. a `YAMLException`/version-banner census over each image's runtime tree), with a positive control on a full install. If no, state the exclusion in the gate's OK line. Regression test the owner could add: a fixture runtime tree carrying a bundled copy must be reported, or explicitly named as out of scope.

## In short

* **originate runtime:** `confbox@0.2.4/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs`, on a prod chain (`c12` ← `@prisma/config`). Probed: it accepts the GHSA-2883 shape as js-yaml 3.15.1 does.
* `/shared` **in every service image:** the `@effect/platform@0.71.7` `httpApiSwagger` bundle carries its own js-yaml copy. **Not probed.**
* **0 tracked source importers** of confbox, c12, @prisma/config or @effect/platform.
* **Runtime reachability: NOT traced.**

## Board search before filing (2026-09-17, team Secuura-PK, archived issues included, literal match on title, description and comments)

* `confbox`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `@effect/platform`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `YAMLException`: 4 issues (KS-1117, KS-1109, KS-1108, KS-1099) and 1 comment thread (KS-1099). All four are about k6 and Akto config-loader error handling, not bundled copies.
* `GHSA-2883`: KS-1211 only, plus comments on KS-1024 and KS-1211 (the audit-baseline row).
* Control: `js-yaml` hits 13 issues, so the search can match. 1205 issues and 3440 comments were scanned.

title: Root-of-service `overrides.postcss: "8.5.23"` (KS-531) now overrules vite 8.3.0's `postcss ^8.5.28` in 18 service locks — is the exact pin stale?
description:
**BLUF:** in 18 service lockfiles, vite 8.3.0 (dev) now declares `postcss ^8.5.28`. Each of those services' `package.json` carries `overrides.postcss: "8.5.23"` (added by KS-531 on 2026-08-12, commit 3418e9b92), which holds postcss at 8.5.23. npm itself reports `postcss@8.5.23 overridden` with rc 0. It is dev-only, with 0 runtime reach. **First item: decide whether the exact KS-531 pin is now stale** and should float, or be removed now that the advisories it cleared are fixed upstream.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1030 (vitest 4.1.11, merged as `bb848b828`), finding F1. Severity Polish (RECORD). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1030-e43af4934-tier2-r1/report.md`.

## The gate's finding, quoted

> | F1 | In 18 service locks the regenerated vite 8.3.0 (dev) declares `postcss ^8.5.28`, but a pre-existing root `overrides.postcss: "8.5.23"` (KS-531, 3418e9b92, 2026-08-12) holds postcss at 8.5.23; at base vite 8.1.3's `^8.5.16` was satisfied | measured (parse + `npm ls` + cleanroom) | **Polish** (RECORD; dev-only, 0 runtime reach) | seat evidence (READY "every declarer's range satisfied") + TICKET-class for Wednesday (is the exact KS-531 pin now stale?) | Product (npm itself prints `postcss@8.5.23 overridden`, rc 0); Comparable (the 4 locks with no override — mcp-server, vc-issuer, both systemTest — moved postcss to 8.5.28) |

Gate self-audit note: its first edge check reported 18 false BADs because it ignored `overrides`. It was fixed to honour them, with a planted override control, and is confirmed by `npm ls`.

## Also recorded against the #1030 author

The READY said "every declarer's range satisfied". The seat's verifier checked the declarers of each **moved** entry. It did not check a moved entry's **own** dependency ranges against unmoved resolutions. That is how vite 8.3.0 → postcss 8.5.23 was missed. The verifier is being extended.

title: A verified token without a role or userId claim still 500s every proxied route (x-user-role / x-user-id set unguarded) — KS-744 residue
description:
## BLUF

A verified JWT that lacks the `role` or `userId` claim still makes every proxied route answer **500**, with the internal message `Invalid value "undefined" for header "x-user-role"` (or `"x-user-id"`). The upstream is never reached. The mechanism is KS-744's: the verified-JWT branch of `authenticateToken` copies the claim onto a forwarded header unguarded (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:388` `x-user-id`, `:390` `x-user-role`, the same line numbers at develop `d7e95cd9f` and at KS-744's local fix `6252f06ac`), and the proxy's outbound `setHeader` throws. KS-744 fixes only `email` and `verificationLevel`. Latent today: no signer mints a token without `userId` or `role` (READ in KS-744's brief).

## Recommendation

A shape decision first, not a copy of KS-744's guard. A token with no principal id or no role arguably should be refused **401** at the gateway rather than forwarded without `x-user-id` / `x-user-role`, because those headers are what the upstreams authorise on. Proposal: in the verified-JWT branch, answer 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` when `decoded.userId` or `decoded.role` is missing, before any header is set; cells for each claim on the KS-744 harness. Not built. Low: latent, but it leaks an internal error string (the KS-703 / KS-727 shape).

## Detail

* **Source:** the residue line of Wednesday's KS-744 brief (P3, measured by the brief writer at `d7e95cd9f`) and seat A's KS-744 build, 2026-09-17.
* **Re-measured by seat A** at the KS-744 head `6252f06ac7c913619888cb20e07cc5a0c846043d` (local, not pushed), 02:25Z, in-process. The harness is the KS-744 test's own: the real `authenticateToken(true)` and a real `http-proxy-middleware` proxy on a bare express app, in front of a recording upstream on loopback, with RS256 tokens carrying every claim except the one named:
  * no `role` → **500**, 0 upstream hits, `{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Invalid value \"undefined\" for header \"x-user-role\""}`;
  * no `userId` → **500**, 0 hits, the same for `x-user-id`;
  * control, no `email` (fixed by KS-744) → 200, 1 hit;
  * control, every claim → 200, 1 hit.
* **The 500 body** in that harness comes from its own error handler; the gateway's real error shape is quoted on KS-744.
* **Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-09-17_seatA-4th/tickets/ks744-residue/` (`rows.json`, `probe.out`, the probe file, run once and moved out of the worktree).
* **Not measured:** the real app's error handler for this case; running upstream services.

### Search before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches only: `x-user-role` 109 fuzzy / 4 literal (KS-1032, KS-741, KS-1041, KS-1091: trust-header reads and stripping, not a missing claim) · `x-user-id` 103 / 8 (KS-1087, KS-1032, KS-1084, KS-1041, KS-1083, KS-719, KS-736, KS-708: none about a missing claim) · `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE` 101 / 2 (KS-744, the parent; KS-742 by mention) · `Invalid value` 113 / 5 (KS-744; KS-465, KS-703, KS-386, KS-283 unrelated) · `decoded.role` 111 / 1 (KS-486, archived review). None covers it. Related: KS-744.

title: POST /api/documents/upload never reaches the gateway's blocked-extension / MIME screen (proxy.ts:551-620): 415 with a multipart body, 405 without
description:
## BLUF

**The gateway's upload screen never runs.** `POST /api/documents/upload` has a hand-forward branch in the gateway (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:551-620`) that refuses blocked file extensions (`BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS`, `:134`) and blocked MIME types before forwarding to originate. On the real app no request reaches it: a multipart request with a body is answered `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` by `middleware/contentType.ts`, and an empty multipart request `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`. Pre-existing. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1028 (KS-744) as finding N-2. **Severity is unmeasured**, and so is the priority set here: whether uploads reach originate by another path was not measured.

## Recommendation

The owners decide what the route should be:

* if gateway-side upload screening is meant to exist, make the route reachable (the JSON-only content-type rule would need a narrow, exact-path exception for multipart, like the KS-791 one for `application/octet-stream`), with a cell proving a blocked extension is refused through the real app;
* if uploads are meant to go some other way, remove or document the dead branch.
  First measure whether and how uploads reach originate today.

## Detail

* **Measured at runtime by the gate** on the real gateway app: 297 + 297 cells per tree (every token, every leg), 0 upstream hits, identical on develop `19f1e5475`, the PR head `e39521cfb` and the merged tree. Multipart with a body → 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`. Empty multipart → 405 `"Method POST not allowed for /api/documents/{id}."` (the spec method gate).
* **Read at develop** `0a2b1603f`**:** the route is `router.post('/api/documents/upload', authenticateToken(true), …)` at `proxy.ts:551`; the extension check is at `:564`, the MIME check follows it, and the forward to originate's `/api/documents/upload` at `:592`.
* **Why the 415:** `contentType.ts` enforces `application/json` on `/api/*` writes (KS-439, a content-type-confusion defence). Its KS-791 comment records that `multipart` returned 415 on every path, and it relaxes only two exact verify paths for `application/octet-stream`.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal, archived included): `documents/upload` (2: PS-449 and PS-424, Platform S add-in work, archived); `BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS` (0); `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` (3: KS-663 In Review, KS-439 Done, KS-781 Deployed). None covers the unreachable screen. KS-439 is archived, so no relation is added.
* **Related:** KS-744 (the gate that found it).

title: mcp-server POST /hash hashes any server-local file named by a caller-supplied filePath, with no auth - measure deployed exposure first
description:
## BLUF

**mcp-server's REST mirror** `POST /hash` **returns the SHA-256 of any server-local file named by a caller-supplied** `filePath`**, with no authentication.** On error it echoes `err.message`, which tells the caller whether a path exists. **Severity is UNMEASURED:** it depends on whether the deployed port is reachable by untrusted callers. Pre-existing, found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1022 (finding O1).

## Recommendation

1. **Measure the deployed exposure first.** On the VM demo (and any other deployed target), establish whether `mcp-server:4023` is reachable from outside the compose network or by any untrusted caller. **Set this ticket's priority from that measurement** (the gate: Major if reachable).
2. Then fix, for example by dropping the `filePath` branch from the HTTP mirror (it has no remote use: a remote caller has no business naming server paths), and returning a generic error message.

## Detail

**MEASURED (the QA gate, 2026-09-17, report** `2026-09-17-ks1211-1022-ff49d0242-tier1-r1`**):** `POST /hash` with `{"filePath": "<scratch file>"}` over HTTP returned **200** with the file's SHA-256.

**READ (this seat, develop** `ee40d3099`**):**

* `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:41-64`:
  * `const { filePath, content } = req.body;` and, if `filePath` is set, `hashFile(filePath)`, which is `readFile(filePath)` at `src/hashing.ts:5-6`;
  * the catch at `:60-62` returns `{ error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: err.message } }`.
* `:29` `express.json` and `:33` `rejectNulBytes()` are the only middleware; no auth is mounted.
* A second `doc.filePath` → `hashFile` read is at `:93-94`.
* **The image runs this server:** `services/mcp-server/Dockerfile:73` is `CMD ["node", "dist/http-server.js"]`, with `EXPOSE 4023`.
* `docker-compose.yml` sets `MCP_HTTP_PORT=4023`. The host port mapping was removed (pen-test F-04; it was `"6023:4023"`), so by repo config the port is reachable **from inside the compose network**.
* **The gateway forwards only one mcp route:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1237-1241` proxies `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package`, and no `/hash` route through the gateway was found.
* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx{,-demo,-production}.conf`: 0 references to `mcp` or `4023` (control: 15 or 16 `proxy_pass` lines each).
* So by repo config the endpoint is internal-only. **The deployed hosts are NOT measured.** Any container on the same network, or a mis-published port, reaches it.

**Pre-existing:** the mcp-server source is identical at develop and at PR #1022's head (the gate's reading). Not introduced by the hono bump.

**Searched before filing** (Linear, team KS, title or description, archived included):

* `/hash` 12 hits;
* `filePath` 2;
* `http-server.ts` 2;
* `POST /hash` 0;
* `hashFile` 0;
* `mcp-server` 27.

The only mcp-related hits naming `/hash` are KS-713 (mcp-server scan coverage) and KS-104 (whether to expose mcp-server via the gateway), both Done and archived. Neither owns this finding; they are referenced here in text only.

title: Security: an absolute-form request target bypasses the KS-843 erasure door's scope/role gate (a connector without subjects:erase reaches originate)
description:
## BLUF

An absolute-form request target (`POST http://<any host>/api/gdpr/erasures`, and `/api/v1/` in production) **bypasses the KS-843 erasure door's scope/role gate**: it answers **200, and originate receives the POST, for a connector WITHOUT** `subjects:erase`. The origin-form control answers 403 with no upstream hit. The `GET` status read and the user role are bypassed the same way. A credential is still required: no credential or an invalid token answers 401. **Pre-existing:** base == head. Found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1011 (KS-871); **not caused by that PR**.

## Recommendation

Treat as Urgent until two conditions are measured (below). One of them is already READ as true: originate does not re-check the scope. Fix shape (the gate's, described, not authored): collapse repeated slashes only in the PATH part after the scheme/host, as `middleware/normalisePath.ts` does with `pathOffset`, or gate the door on `req.path` rather than `req.url`. Regression cells: an absolute-form erasure `POST` and `GET`, in test and production mode. **Not built.** Wednesday takes this to Kam; building waits for his word on priority.

## Detail

**Measured by the gate** (`Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/report.md`, finding F-1011-4; raw runs in `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/evidence/bypass_run.out`, replicated 2× on each of base/head × NODE_ENV test/production). Setup: a connector without `subjects:erase`, `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED=true`, a real app with a recording upstream.

| request | test (base = head) | production (base = head) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| CONTROL `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` | 403, no upstream | 307 → 403, no upstream |
| `POST http://127.0.0.1/api/gdpr/erasures` | **200, originate hit** | 307 → 403 |
| `POST http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/gdpr/erasures` | **200, hit** | **200, hit** |
| `POST http://qa-anything.invalid/api/v1/gdpr/erasures` (any host) | **200, hit** | **200, hit** |
| user role, `POST http://127.0.0.1/api/gdpr/erasures` | **200, hit** | 307 → 403 |
| `GET http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/gdpr/erasures/abc` (status read) | **200, hit** | **200, hit** |
| CONTROL absolute-form, no credential / invalid token | 401 / 401 | 307 → 401 |
| CONTROL origin-form WITH the scope | 200, hit | 307 → 200, hit |

**Suspected mechanism** (the gate's, READ, not instrumented): inside `router.use('/api/gdpr')`, `req.url` for an absolute-form target keeps its `http://host` prefix. The wrapper at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:734-745` collapses `/{2,}` across the whole `req.url`, turning `http://h/erasures` into `http:/h/erasures`. The door's `/erasures` mount (`proxy.ts:726-728`) then never matches, and the catch-all `router.use('/api/gdpr', authenticateToken(true), proxy)` forwards the request.

**Severity conditions** (the seat A successor's READS, 2026-09-17, develop `1125607e9`):

1. **Does originate re-check** `subjects:erase`**? READ: NO.**
   * `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:164` runs `gdprRouter.use(authenticate())`, and the erasure routes are `gdprRouter.post('/erasures', requireRole(...CONNECTOR_ROLES), …)` (`:488`) and `gdprRouter.get('/erasures/:externalRef', requireRole(...CONNECTOR_ROLES), …)` (`:523`), with `CONNECTOR_ROLES = ['connector']` (`:431`).
   * The string `subjects:erase` appears nowhere in `services/originate/src` (git grep at the tip; the only hits are in api-gateway).
   * So a connector token WITHOUT the scope that reaches originate **executes** `gdpr.executeErasureByExternalRef` (`:498`).
   * The user-role bypass reaches originate, but originate refuses it by role (READ; not driven against a real originate).
   * Instrument that closes this: drive a scope-less connector through a real originate and check the erasure ran.
2. **Does the edge forward an absolute-form target to the gateway? UNMEASURED.**
   * Local and production compose publish NO gateway host port (`docker-compose.yml` api-gateway: "No external ports — accessed via nginx-gateway at /api/"; `docker-compose.production.yml`: "No external ports; all traffic flows through nginx-gateway").
   * Every nginx front proxies `/api/` as `proxy_pass http://api_gateway_pool$request_uri;` (`docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:184-185`, `nginx-demo.conf:401`, `nginx-production.conf:337`). Whether nginx's `$request_uri` keeps the `http://host` of an absolute-form request line decides it. I believe nginx parses scheme and host apart from the URI (so it would forward origin-form), but **that is not measured**.
   * The VM demo fronts nginx with Caddy (`deployment/caddy/Caddyfile:34`, `reverse_proxy localhost:6882`). Caddy is also expected to re-emit origin-form. **Not measured.**
   * The Container Apps template exposes the gateway app DIRECTLY (`deployment/azure/services.bicep:576-585`, `${resourcePrefix}-api`, `external: true`, `targetPort: 8080`). That estate is decommissioned, but it is the production-scale template. Whether its Envoy ingress forwards absolute-form is **not measured**.
   * The kintsugi host's front end is outside the repo and was not read.
   * Instrument that closes this: send `POST http://x/api/v1/gdpr/erasures` as a raw request line through each front end (local nginx slot, the VM Caddy, kintsugi) and read what the gateway receives.

Related: KS-843 (the door), KS-858 (the path-normalisation class; archived, so named here rather than linked), KS-954 (a KS-858 residue in the same collapse).

**Dedupe before filing** (seat A successor, 2026-09-17): Linear `searchIssues` with archived issues and comments included, paged, then literal case-insensitive matches over title + description + comments. Terms: `absolute-form`, `erasures`, `proxy.ts`, `subjects:erase`. The `absolute-form` and `subjects:erase` hits are quoted in full below. The broad terms returned 25 (`erasures`) and 62 (`proxy.ts`) literal hits, all read as other subjects (the KS-843/KS-695 erasure work, KS-858/KS-954 slash normalisation, limiter and auth-mount classes).

```
TERM 'absolute-form': scanned 113 fuzzy results over 3 page(s); literal hits 1
    KS-858 [Deployed to UAT ARCHIVED] in comments :: Security CLASS: a scope gate mounted as an exact route above a catch-all prefix can be bypassed by p
TERM 'erasures': scanned 84 fuzzy results over 2 page(s); literal hits 25
TERM 'proxy.ts': scanned 109 fuzzy results over 3 page(s); literal hits 62
TERM 'subjects:erase': scanned 104 fuzzy results over 3 page(s); literal hits 6
    KS-843 [In Progress] in title,desc,comments :: KS-695 F5: build the dedicated `subjects:erase` scope gate on POST /api/gdpr/erasures — Kam ruled it
    KS-855 [Backlog] in desc :: The OAuth `AVAILABLE_SCOPES` list is a second, divergent scope vocabulary — derive it from SCOPES or
    KS-577 [In Review] in comments :: rotate: true mints a new key but never revokes the old one — implement revoke-on-rotate and agree th
    KS-695 [In Progress] in comments :: S↔K (K-side): erasure by external_ref, documents.title coverage, and connector-scoped org erasure — 
    PS-740 [Tested Not Deployed] in comments :: S↔K key recovery: a KeyInvalid state, a supported inlet for a rotated connector key, and grant-drive
    KS-1152 [Backlog] in desc :: L5 gate records (#799/#880/#985): jwt.ts citation ×5, security log title, dist typeof discriminator,
```

The one `absolute-form` hit (a KS-858 comment, 2026-09-08) describes the normaliser's own cells driving absolute-form targets, not this door bypass. No existing ticket covers it.

title: connectorId is never persisted — svc_api_keys.connector_id is written by nothing and read by nothing, so it dies on restart; blocks KS-577 and nulls KS-843's cutover evidence
description:
## BLUF

`svc_api_keys.connector_id` **exists as a column and NOTHING in the security service ever writes it or reads it.** A key's `connectorId` lives only in the in-process `memApiKeys` map, from the moment it is minted until the service restarts. After a restart it is gone — and the boot loader cannot bring it back, because the row mapper does not map the column.

Two consequences, one of which lands on a ticket shipped today.

## Measured (static, with a control that fires)

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| the column exists | `migrations/018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql:79` — `ALTER TABLE svc_api_keys ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS connector_id TEXT` |
| nothing writes it | `dbSaveApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:197`) — `connector_id` is **not** in the INSERT column list |
| nothing reads it | `rowToApiKey` (`:309`) — **not** mapped |
| anywhere in the service | `grep -n "connector_id" services/security/src/*.ts` → **0 hits**, against a control on `key_prefix` → **2 hits**, so the grep discriminates |
| memory is rebuilt from those rows | `loadFromDb()` (`:334`) warms `memApiKeys` from `svc_api_keys` through `rowToApiKey` |

`connectorId` is in the `ApiKey` interface (`:132`), set in memory at mint (`:985`), and returned by validate (`:1182` — `connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null`). All in-process only.

## Consequence 1 — it blocks KS-577 (revoke-on-rotate)

KS-577 requires finding a connector's **prior** keys in order to revoke them on rotate. The only identifier tying sibling keys together is `connectorId` (`platform-s:<externalRef>`, set at `platform.ts` mint time). **There is no durable copy of it**, so after any restart of the security service the association needed to find the prior key does not exist in the database at all. KS-577 cannot be built on `connectorId` until this is fixed.

## Consequence 2 — it degrades KS-843's cutover evidence

Traced end to end:

```
security  /api/keys/validate  ->  connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null      (index.ts:1182)
gateway   auth.ts:230         ->  meta.connectorId = data.connectorId || ''
gateway   auth.ts:272         ->  userId = `connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}`
gateway   auth.ts:281         ->  req.user.connectorId = meta.connectorId
scopes.ts (KS-843 grace log)  ->  connectorId: user.connectorId ?? null
```

**After a restart, every Platform S connector key validates with** `connectorId: null`**.** So:

* the `[KS-843]` grace-log line — the operator's *only* evidence for flipping `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` — records `connectorId: null`, and cannot say **which** connector was admitted;
* `userId` collapses to `connector:api-key` for every connector, so audit attribution loses the same distinction.

KS-843's cutover is stated as "flip to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key". **That log cannot show which key it is, after a restart.**

## Honesty about the evidence

This is a **static** read of the write path and the read path, with a grep control that fires. **I did not drive a restart and observe a null**, because that means restarting a container on the local stack while gates are running. The static chain is unambiguous, but it is not a driven observation and is not offered as one. Driving it is a ~10-minute job if wanted.

## Fix shape

Write `connector_id` in `dbSaveApiKey`'s INSERT (and in the `ON CONFLICT` set, since it is immutable per key it can be omitted there), and map it in `rowToApiKey`. The column already exists, so **no migration is needed**. Existing rows backfill as NULL — which is what they effectively are today, so nothing regresses; a backfill from any surviving source is a separate question.

## Acceptance

A key minted with a `connectorId` still validates with that same `connectorId` **after the security service restarts**, driven not read; `rowToApiKey` maps the column; the `[KS-843]` grace log names the connector after a restart; `userId` is `connector:platform-s:<ref>`, not `connector:api-key`. Then KS-577 becomes buildable.

title: The latest-anchor selector documents a `confirmedAt` tiebreak it does not implement — and since KS-1057 that selector decides the verdict
description:
**BLUF:** `verification.ts:240` says *"Latest = highest blockNumber, fall back to most-recent confirmedAt."* **There is no secondary key.** The sort is `(b.blockNumber || 0) - (a.blockNumber || 0)` and `confirmedAt` is never consulted.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:240-242`, read at PR #935 head `dd9463b37`.

**Failure scenario:** two anchors on one document with equal `blockNumber` (including the common `0`/null case, which `|| 0` collapses). Ties break only on `Array.prototype.sort` stability over whatever order anchoring returned — `ORDER BY created_at DESC`. That is an **undocumented cross-service coupling**: anchoring can change its ORDER BY and silently change the gateway's verdict. The gate drove two equal-`blockNumber` anchors and **flipped the verdict**.

**Why it matters now and did not before:** until KS-1057 the selected anchor's `status` was dropped on the way into the blob, so which anchor won was cosmetic. **It is now the verdict** — `status: latest.status` is carried at line 265. A cosmetic selector became a decisive one in the same commit that fixed F1.

**Fix shape:** implement the documented tiebreak (or correct the comment to say there is none), and pin it with a cell driving two equal-`blockNumber` anchors.

Source: QA tier-1 gate round 2 on #935, finding F9 (POLISH). Confirmed at source by s165 before filing. Related: KS-1057.

title: anchor_store's (document_id, network) unique is declared only by migration 031 and anchoring's fresh-DB path; 9 other schema sources omit it (#1016 gate R-1016-5)
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing; reported, NOT reconciled.** Ten places create `anchor_store`. Only migration 031, which replaced 007's `(document_id)` unique, and anchoring's own fresh-database path declare the `(document_id, network)` unique. The other **nine** `CREATE TABLE` sources carry none. Anchoring's `ensureTables` returns early when the table already exists, so on a database built from one of those nine sources the unique exists only if migrations 007/031 ran. Both upserts depend on it: `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)` in anchoring and in originate. Which source a deployed database is built from was NOT determined.

## Recommendation

Not built. The owner decides **which schema source is authoritative** for `anchor_store`, then reconciles the others to it or retires them. Until then, the one-row-per-`(document_id, network)` assumption holds only where migration 031 ran. The KS-1072 selector's tie reachability rests on that assumption.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 QA gate on PR #1016 (KS-1072), Record R-1016-5 and §12. Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1072-1016-a226d94fe-tier1-r1/report.md`. The gate's evidence class is READ ONLY.
* **Re-read by Seat A at develop** `7e89318bcedbc9a35757d4298ace54a6a23020bd`**.** Instruments: `git grep -n -i 'CREATE TABLE.*anchor_store'` gave 10 hits; `git grep -n -i 'document_id, *network'` located the unique.
  * **No unique (9):**
    * `docker/init/01-schema.sql:188`
    * `docker/init/03-service-tables.sql:89`
    * `docker/init/06-consolidate-anchors.sql:26`
    * `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:150`, `:733` and `:2045`
    * `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:704`
    * `migrations/003_consolidate-anchors.sql:16`
    * `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:316`
  * **Unique:**
    * `migrations/031_anchor_store_network_unique.sql:39-40`: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS anchor_store_document_network_uniq ON anchor_store (document_id, network)`.
    * anchoring `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:209`, the same index. It is reached only when `ensureTables` does not return early.
  * **The early return:** anchoring `index.ts:172-175` reads `to_regclass('public.anchor_store')` and `to_regclass('public.anchor_batches')`; when both exist it sets `tablesEnsured = true` and returns.

title: workflow-approve: the forward to originate has no timeout, so an originate that never answers leaves the approve unanswered and a late 201 creates the document after the caller got nothing (KS-1087 gate F1)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` waits for originate's status on the forward (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:994-1012`, PR #1008, merged as `f7c2f4acb28875e3665a61c8eaaad5c54bd3aa55`), and nothing bounds that wait. An originate that accepts the connection and never answers leaves the approve unanswered. The instance is already persisted `approved` and the pending document is kept. If originate answers 201 after the client (or nginx, at 120 s / 60 s) has given up, the document IS created and the pending one deleted, while the caller was told nothing (or 504). This is new with #1008: before it, the route answered 200 within milliseconds.

## Recommendation

Build it as its own tier-1 PR (Wednesday's ruling on the #1008 GO; this supersedes the gate's SHIPS-WITH tag):

* give the forward a request timeout that destroys the request and resolves `0`, so the route answers 502 `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED` with `status: 0` within the bound and keeps the pending document;
* add `'error'` / `'aborted'` / `'close'` handling on `proxyRes`, so that moving the resolve into `'end'` later can never hang the mid-body rows (the gate's G5 measurement below).
* Red-proof: the gate's accepts-and-never-answers row (→ 502 within the bound, delete 0) plus a late-201 row.

## Detail

Found by the tier-1 QA gate (round 1) on PR #1008 (Part of KS-1087, item 1) at `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d`, 2026-09-17. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1087-1008-dd7086d5a-tier1-r1/report.md`, Findings F1, items 1, 2 and 6.

**F1, verbatim from the report's findings table:** "The forward has no timeout. An originate that accepts and never answers leaves the approve unanswered (NO RESPONSE at 6 s and 15 s in-process; nothing in-process bounds it). The instance is already `approved`, the document kept. If originate answers 201 after the client (or nginx at 120 s/60 s) gave up, the document IS created and the pending one deleted while the caller was told nothing or 504. New with #1008 (base answered 200 in ms)."

* Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME (the nginx bound READ ONLY). Gate severity: Minor (needs a hung originate or a network black hole; one socket held per request; an honest-outcome breach on late success).
* Fix shape (the gate's): `proxyReq.setTimeout(n, () => proxyReq.destroy(err))` resolving 0, plus `proxyRes.on('error'/'aborted')` resolving 0 if the resolve ever moves to `'end'`. Regression test: accepts-and-never-answers → 502 within n, delete 0.

**Measured rows (item 1, real** `createVerificationRoutes`**, counting originate stub):**

* accepts, never answers: base 200 in 6 ms, delete 1; head **NO RESPONSE at 6,005 ms and at 15,002 ms**, hits 1, delete 0, instance already `approved`; merged the same.
* answers 201 after 3 s, client gave up at 1 s: client NO RESPONSE; after originate answers, **delete 1** (the document was created and the pending one deleted after the client left).
* answers 401 after 3 s, client gave up at 1 s: client NO RESPONSE; after, delete 0, kept.

**Why the handlers matter (item 2, tamper G5):** moving `resolveStatus` into `'end'` leaves the 388-cell suite green, but on the gate's harness turns both mid-body rows (201 headers then reset mid-body; 201 headers, body never ends) into **NO RESPONSE at 2.5 s, delete 0**, because the wrapper has no `'error'`/`'aborted'`/`'close'` listener on `proxyRes` (parser: 0). Deleting on 2xx headers is right as written: originate persists at `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:667` before its single `res.status(201).json(...)` at `:911` (blob `c3a818ac8`, unchanged at `f7c2f4acb`).

**Not established:** whether any environment has workflow-gated document types (this decides reachability in operation); nginx's bound was READ, not measured; no in-repo caller of the POST route (gate item 9).

**Folded into the same PR (the gate's Polish, F3–F6, per the #1008 GO):** the ks1087 test's stateless originate stub cannot observe the strand (F3); tampers G4 (`>= 300` → `>= 400`), G5 and G6 (the 502 body echoing originate's body) are invisible to all 388 cells (F4); five lines fail an including tsc in `ks1087-workflow-approve-deletes-the-pending-document.test.ts` (TS18047 `:65`/`:66`, TS6133 `_deadPort` `:119`, TS18046 `:171`/`:172`) (F5); dead `deadApp`/`deadServer`/`_deadAppDeleteCount`/`_deadPort` scaffolding at `:87-120` (F6).

Related: KS-1087 (item 2, the forward credential, stays open), and the sibling ticket for F2 (the stranded `approved` instance).

**Dedupe before filing** (seat A successor, 2026-09-17): Linear `searchIssues` with archived issues and comments included, paged, then filtered to LITERAL case-insensitive matches over title + description + comments. Positive control: `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED` found KS-1087's comment.

title: workflow-approve persists the instance approved before the forward, so a refused forward strands it: re-approve and reject answer 400, no re-forward path, the kept document unusable until TTL (KS-1087 gate F2)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` persists the instance `approved` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:970-972`) BEFORE it forwards the pending document to originate. So after any refused forward the workflow is stranded:

* a retry answers 400 "Workflow already completed" and never forwards (originate hits 0);
* reject answers 400;
* there is no re-forward path;
* the kept pending document stays unusable (403 `PENDING_APPROVAL`, relayed) until its Redis TTL.

The persist-before-forward predates PR #1008. Before #1008 the same input also reached `approved` and silently deleted the pending document; #1008 (merged `f7c2f4acb28875e3665a61c8eaaad5c54bd3aa55`) keeps the document and answers 502, which makes the strand visible and recoverable in principle.

## Recommendation

A design call beside KS-1087 item 2, not a fix round on #1008. Two shapes:

* persist `approved` only after originate answers 2xx; or
* add a re-forward / retry path for an `approved` instance whose pending document still exists.

Regression test (the gate's): a stateful store, originate 401 then 201 → the second attempt forwards and deletes exactly once.

## Detail

Found by the tier-1 QA gate (round 1) on PR #1008 (Part of KS-1087, item 1) at `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d`, 2026-09-17. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1087-1008-dd7086d5a-tier1-r1/report.md`, Findings F2 and item 3.

**F2, verbatim from the report's findings table:** "Stranded `approved` instance. After any refused forward the instance is `approved`, re-approve/reject 400, no re-forward path, and the kept document is unusable until its TTL. The persist at `:970-972` predates #1008; base reaches the same instance state and silently loses the document."

* Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME (stateful store); the downstream 403 is RELAYED.
* Gate severity: **Major** (product state; data orphaned). Reach NOT ESTABLISHED: it depends on workflow-gated document types existing, and on KS-1087 item 2 (originate answering 401 today is relayed from the #951 r2 report).

**Measured rows (item 3):** approve with originate 401, then originate fixed to 201 and approve again, then reject.

* stateful store, head / merged / production / development: 1st approve **502**, hits 1, delete 0, pending kept, instance `approved` · 2nd approve **400 "Workflow already completed"**, hits **0** · reject **400** "…cannot be rejected" · final: instance `approved`, pending document kept, never forwarded.
* stateful store, base `93629700c`: 1st approve **200**, hits 1, **delete 1** (document lost; originate refused) · 2nd 400, hits 0 · reject 400 · final: instance `approved`, no document, pending deleted.
* stateless stub (the shape the ks1087 test uses), head: 502, then 200 + delete 1, then reject 200. The stub reads a retry path that does not exist (gate F3).
* A second approve while the first hangs: 400, originate hits 1 in total.

**Not tested (report):** the downstream 403 `PENDING_APPROVAL` on sign/anchor/share and `GET /api/documents/:id` answering `pending_approval` for a stranded document (relayed from the drafter's read); the Redis TTL value (`TTL.workflow * 24` at `redis.ts:565/603` was read, `TTL.workflow` was not); true concurrency on the final step.

Related: KS-1087 (item 2), and KS-1183 (gate F1: the forward has no timeout).

title: workflow-approve deletes the pending document and answers 200 "Document has been created" without reading originate's response — a refused forward (401, measured) loses the document
description:
## BLUF

* **Approving the last step of a workflow can silently lose the document.** `POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` forwards the pending document to originate, deletes it from Redis without reading originate's response, and answers **200** `approved`**, "All workflow steps approved. Document has been created."**
* **Measured** by the QA agent's round-2 tier-1 gate on #951 (`02a22f4bb`, 2026-09-11):
  * the recorded forward (`x-user-id` only, no bearer) replayed into the real originate app gets **401**, with the gateway vouch secret unset and set alike;
  * with originate answering 401, the real gateway handler still returns **200** `approved` and **deletes the pending document**.
* **Pre-existing, not #951.** The same code is on develop `2d864ae92`.
* **NOT established: whether any environment has workflow-gated document types.** Reachability for real users is unknown. The gate assessed severity as Major; priority is left for the humans.

## Recommendation

1. Report approval and delete the pending document **only after originate returns 2xx**. On any other status, or a network error, keep the pending document and return an error to the caller.
2. Forward a credential originate accepts. Today the forward carries `x-user-id` alone, and originate answers 401.
3. Regression test: an originate stub returning 401 must not yield 200 `approved`, and the pending document must survive. Add the same cell for a network error.
4. If `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is ever provisioned, this forward is also on KS-1083's vouch precondition list.

## Detail

**Code on develop** `2d864ae92`**,** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` (at `02a22f4bb`: route `:700`, `x-user-id` `:783`, `http.request` `:785`):

* `:781` `router.post('/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve', authenticateToken(true), …)`
* `:860-864` forward headers: `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and `x-user-id` from `pendingDoc.createdBy`. No `Authorization`, no `x-tenant-id`.
* `:866` `http.request` to originate `/api/documents`. The response callback only logs "Workflow approved — document forwarded to originate" on `end` (`:871`), whatever the status.
* `:880` `proxyReq.end()`, then `:881` `await redisService.deletePendingDocument(documentId)`, before any response has been read.
* `:889` the 200 body: `status: 'approved'`, `message: 'All workflow steps approved. Document has been created.'`

**Consequence by case:**

| originate outcome | pending document | caller is told | evidence |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 401 | deleted | 200 approved, "created" | MEASURED (gate P2, F2b) |
| other 4xx / 5xx | deleted | 200 approved, "created" | READ |
| network error | deleted; "Failed to forward" logged | 200 approved, "created" | READ, not driven |

**Correction carried here:** KS-1084's body says this forward sends `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`. It sends `x-user-id` only (`:864`). A dated correction comment is on KS-1084.

**Board searched before filing** (team KS, archived included; titles, descriptions and comments):

* `/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` → 0 issues, 0 comments
* `/api/workflows/:workflowId/approve` → 0, 0
* `workflow-approve` → KS-1083 and KS-1084, which name only this forward's vouch/tenant shape, not the lost document
* `workflow approve`, `workflowApprove`, `pending document`, `pendingDocument`, `approved and deletes` → 0 each
* `verification.ts:8` → KS-1083 and KS-501 (Done, an unrelated crash)
* controls: `verification.ts` → 33 issues; a nonsense term → 0

**NOT tested:** a live stack; any environment's workflow configuration; the sibling route `POST /api/workflows/:workflowId/approve` (`:943`), which was not examined.

**Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-02a22f4bb-tier1-r2/report.md`, section "Open", O-1. Filed by Platform K seat s177 on Wednesday's brief; the QA agent cannot post.

title: register-connector: volume alerting, rate limit, and correlation of refused re-key attempts
description:
## BLUF

`register-connector` is the highest-blast-radius admin operation on the platform and has **no volume alerting and no rate limit**. Bulk re-key ([KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576)) makes it cheaper to trigger, which raises the cost of leaving it unmonitored.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

The route (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476`) refuses connector-authorised rotates (`:499-509`) but nothing observes the pattern of use:

* no alert on an unusual **volume** of rotations in a window
* no rate limit on the route itself
* refused re-key attempts are not correlated — a series of 403s from a connector credential probing the rotate path looks like nothing

### Added 2026-09-14 — register #15 from [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) (`externalRef` collision / wrong environment)

Carried here on closing [KS-533](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533>) (register row #15, Low likelihood, ⚠️ manual merge to recover). Same route, same blast radius, so it belongs with the rate-limit/alerting work rather than on its own ticket.

**Scenario:** a reused or typo'd OrganisationGuid, or a staging S registering against prod K. Duplicate orgs split provenance; `rotate: true` aimed at the wrong org kills a prod key.

**State on** `develop` **today** (`platform.ts:495,537`): `externalRef` is trimmed and checked for presence and `≤128` chars only — no shape check, although §4 defines it as S's Org GUID. Nothing ties the provisioning credential to an environment, so a staging S holding a prod-shaped key is indistinguishable from prod S.

**Add to the done-when:**

* `externalRef` validated as a GUID (400 on anything else) — a typo cannot mint a second org.
* Environment-scoped provisioning credentials: a key minted for one environment is refused by another (env tag in the key record or prefix, checked at `register-connector`), so a staging S cannot register or rotate against prod K.

**Done when:** an anomalous rotation volume raises an alert, the route is rate-limited, and refused attempts are correlated well enough that a probing pattern is visible rather than scattered across logs.

---
