Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.

title: userRepo.ts: ILIKE search on encrypted PII columns can never match — :1017 and :1061 compare ciphertext to a pattern
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` runs a text search over columns that hold ciphertext. `listUsersInner` (`:1017`) and `countUsersInner` (`:1061`) both push `(email ILIKE $n OR first_name ILIKE $n OR last_name ILIKE $n OR display_name ILIKE $n)` with the pattern `%<search>%`. Every one of those four columns is written through `encryptPiiCol` (`:832-840` — the `encryptedCols` map: `first_name`, `last_name`, `display_name`, `phone_number`, `email`, `mfa_secret`; `:671`, `:703-705`, `:712`, `:847`, `:856`), with AAD bound to the user id, so the stored value is a per-row ciphertext and an `ILIKE` over it answers a different question from the one asked: a search for a known user's name or address returns nothing, without an error, and looks like "no such user". It is the runtime form of the trap KS-968's schema comment now warns about at the column (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`, the `users.email` comment landed by PR #905): comparing ciphertext to a literal or a pattern never errors and never matches.

The file's own docblock at `:562-568` records the rule for equality — `getUserByEmail` moved to an HMAC lookup against `email_lookup_hash` "rather than LIKE/LOWER on the encrypted blob — the encrypted column is non-deterministic so direct equality doesn't work" — and the two search sites were left on the old shape. Measured and recorded by s232 on KS-968 (comment `1079a310`, 2026-09-14) while landing #905; filed by the merge seat s228 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 2026-09-14 11:00:17Z. Board searched first — every KS issue incl. archived, titles + descriptions + comments: `ILIKE` 1 hit (KS-968's own comments), `userRepo.ts:1017` 1 (the same), `userRepo.ts:1061` 0, `searchUsers` 0, `listUsers` 2 (KS-968; KS-703 archived, a NUL-byte 500 — unrelated). No existing home.

## Where it hurts

* Any admin or tenant user-list with a `search` term (`listUsersInner` / `countUsersInner` are the search arm of the users listing; both take `search`, `role`, `tenantId`). The count and the page disagree with reality in the same direction, so the UI shows an empty, internally consistent result.
* Rows still holding legacy plaintext (the migration-window fallback the docblock describes) WOULD match — so the search "works" on exactly the rows that should not exist any more, and silently stops working as rows are backfilled. A test seeded with plaintext passes; production does not.

## Fix-shape (for the owner)

Pick one, and say which in the PR:

1. **Searchable-hash columns per searched field** — the `email_lookup_hash` pattern (`lookupHash(normalised)`) extended to `first_name` / `last_name` / `display_name`, with an exact-or-prefix match on the hash instead of a substring `ILIKE` (a substring search over a keyed hash is not possible; the product decision is whether prefix/exact search is enough).
2. **Resolve the search through the existing hash for email only** and drop the name columns from the predicate, documenting that the listing searches by exact email.
3. **Drop the search arm** and remove `search` from both signatures and their callers.

Whichever lands, the docblock at `:562-568` should name the search sites as covered.

## Regression cell

Seed one user through `createUser` (so the columns are ciphertext, not plaintext), then call `listUsersInner` with `search` = that user's display name (and separately the email) and assert the user is returned and `countUsersInner` reads 1; a control search for a name no user has reads 0. On develop today the first two assertions red (0 rows) — the cell is red-first by construction.

## Definition of done

- [ ] A search for a known, encrypted-at-rest user's name or email returns that user through both `listUsersInner` and `countUsersInner`, or the search arm is removed with its callers.
- [ ] The regression cell above green; the docblock at `:562-568` names the search sites.
- [ ] KS-968's schema comment stays true (the column is never compared to a literal or a pattern).

title: A backtick in a shell-suite case name executes as a command and rewrote package.json mid-run — every cell still PASSED; 9 suites share the pattern
description:
## A backtick in a shell-suite case name is COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — it runs, and the pass/fail column says nothing

Found by walking into it on KS-945. **Nine tracked shell suites share the vulnerable call-site**
**pattern.** No suite carries a live instance right now, so this is a latent hazard, not an outage.

### What happened

Case names are passed as the first argument to a helper (`expect "name" <exit> '<body>' …`), so the
name sits in a **double-quoted shell word at the call site**. Seven KS-945 case names were written
with markdown-style backticks for readability:

```
expect "KS-945: `npm add` is an install" 1 '…'
expect "KS-945: `npm init <package-spec>` installs, unlike `npm init -y`" 1 '…'
```

The shell ran them. During a suite run this executed `npm add`, `npm it`, `pnpm add`, `yarn` and
`npm init` **for real, in the working tree**:

* `npm init` rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` — 14 insertions, 4 deletions, including rewriting
  the unicode escapes in two long `// overrides` comments and changing the `repository.url`.
* The package managers rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 insertions, 31 deletions.

Both were restored from `HEAD` and verified byte-identical, `git status` clean on both paths. Nothing
was committed and nothing left the machine.

### Why it belongs to the KS-926 family

**It was invisible in the pass/fail column. Every affected cell still PASSED.** The suite reported
`50 passed, 0 failed` while rewriting two tracked files underneath itself.

It surfaced only because a *red-proof* run — a deliberate tamper, run for an unrelated reason —
printed package-manager output **inside its FAIL lines**:

```
FAIL: KS-945: bare yarn install v1.22.22
FAIL: KS-945: [ERR_PNPM_MISSING_PACKAGE_NAME] `pnpm add` requires the package name is an install
FAIL: KS-945:  installs, unlike Wrote to …/Blockchain/Dev/package.json:
```

A green run could not show it, because the substitution output was swallowed into a name that was
never printed on success. **The tamper is what made it visible** — which is the family's own thesis.

### Scope, with a control

* **0 of 14** tracked `*.test.sh` currently contain an unescaped backtick in a case name. **That zero**
  **discriminates:** the same query run against a deliberately bad file detects it (verified in the
  same batch), so it is a real zero and not a query that cannot match.
* **9 of 14** use the `expect()` helper and therefore share the call-site shape:
  `run_in_slot`, `slot_target`, `stop_secuura`, `stack_guard`, `check_shared_relink`,
  `check_container_isolation`, `preflight_deps`, `stack_env`, `check_script_portability`.

### Fix shape

`check_shared_relink.test.sh` now carries a per-suite check that refuses an unescaped backtick in any
case name (added in KS-945, red-proofed **without executing the tamper** — the check is a grep, so it
was run against a bad name directly). **That guard should move up into**
`run-shell-suites.sh` **so it covers all fourteen**, rather than being re-implemented per suite — which
is itself the KS-926 mechanism-1 shape: a check that exists in one place and is absent everywhere else.

Worth considering alongside: have the helper reject a name containing a backtick outright, so the
failure is a clear message rather than a silent execution.

### Provenance

* the executed commands and the two rewritten files | observed in a red-proof run of
  `check_shared_relink.test.sh`; `git diff --stat` on both paths before restore; restore verified with
  `git diff --quiet HEAD` | measured 2026-09-07
* 0 of 14 and 9 of 14, with the known-bad control | `git ls-files '*.test.sh'` piped through the same
  query, plus a purpose-built bad file that the query detects | measured 2026-09-07

title: redis healthcheck passes REDIS_PASSWORD as a `-a` argv — readable via `docker inspect` / `docker events` / `ps` by anyone on the host
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:228` defines the redis container's healthcheck as

```
test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-a", "${REDIS_PASSWORD:-secuura_redis_dev}", "ping"]
```

Compose renders `${REDIS_PASSWORD}` into the container's **config** at create time, so the plaintext password is exposed on every surface that shows the healthcheck command: `docker inspect <redis>` (`.Config.Healthcheck.Test`), `docker events` (each `exec_create: redis-cli -a <password> ping`, every healthcheck interval), and `ps` inside the container while the probe runs. Any account that can talk to the Docker socket reads it without touching `.env`.

Work-stream **B** (crypto & secrets — [KS-487](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487>), Done 2026-09-14, so filed as a sibling rather than appended). Pre-existing; not introduced or changed by [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s).

## Measured — 2026-09-14, slot 4, Peter's Mac

Recording `docker events` for the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-4 deploy window (07:03–07:16 UTC, 431 events) captured the bootstrap-generated slot-4 `REDIS_PASSWORD` in clear, once per healthcheck tick, as the `exec_create` action string on `secuura-s4-redis`. The recording was deleted; no value is quoted here or in the PR/ticket. The same value is visible at any time via `docker inspect secuura-s4-redis --format '{{.Config.Healthcheck.Test}}'`.

## Why it matters

* Since [KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read) the password is per-clone and generated, so a leak is no longer "the shared literal everyone knows" — it is the actual credential for that stack's Redis (sessions, rate-limit state, cache).
* Anyone reproducing a run with `docker events` / `docker inspect` in a log, a PR, or a support bundle ships the password with it. The `secuura-test-discipline` "never read a secrets file" rule is bypassed by a command that reads no file.
* The VM demo stack (`/home/secuura/secuura/Dev`) uses the same compose file, so the demo Redis password is exposed the same way to anyone with socket access there.

## Fix direction

Keep the password out of argv. Options, in order of preference:

1. `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "redis-cli ping"]` with `REDISCLI_AUTH` supplied via the service's `environment:` — `redis-cli` reads the password from `REDISCLI_AUTH` and it never appears in the command. (Environment is still readable via `docker inspect .Config.Env`, so pair with 2 if that surface matters.)
2. Mount the password as a file/secret and `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "REDISCLI_AUTH=$(cat /run/secrets/redis_password) redis-cli ping"]`.
3. Auth-less liveness: `redis-cli ping` unauthenticated answers `NOAUTH` when the server is up — the same signal `start-secuura.sh` already treats as "responding" ([KS-260](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-260/start-secuurash-verification-false-negatives-redis-noauth-counted-as)). Cheapest, and sufficient if the healthcheck only needs liveness.

Check whether `pgbouncer`/`postgres` healthchecks (`pg_isready -h localhost -p 6432`, no password — fine) or any other service put a credential on a command line: grep `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.local.yml` for `-a `, `--password`, `PGPASSWORD=`, `:${…PASSWORD` inside `test:` / `command:` / `entrypoint:`.

**Red→green:** a static check (`check-stack-safety.sh` shape, or `check_slot_credentials.test.sh`) that greps rendered `docker compose config` for any `*PASSWORD*` value inside `healthcheck.test`, `command` or `entrypoint` — red on develop, green after; plus `docker inspect … .Config.Healthcheck.Test` on a running stack showing no credential.

## Where

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:228`
* Surfaces: `docker inspect` (Healthcheck.Test), `docker events` (exec_create), in-container `ps`.

Found during the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-4 verification ([Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)).

title: services/shared (@secuura/service-utils) cannot build — no tsconfig.json, so main/types point at a dist that can never exist; its src/ half is dead but types/ is live in billing
description:
## BLUF

`services/shared` **(**`@secuura/service-utils`**) cannot build, and nothing imports it.** It declares `"build": "tsc"` and points `main`/`types` at `dist/`, but it has **no** `tsconfig.json`, so `npm run build` exits 1 and produces no `dist` — meaning `main: dist/index.js` and `types: dist/index.d.ts` reference a path that can never exist. It carries **15 TypeScript source files** that no code in the repo imports.

Found 2026-08-17 (session 43) while sweeping `BACKLOG.md` against Linear. **This defect was tracked nowhere.** The `BACKLOG.md` entry cites **KS-617**, but KS-617 is closed and is about a Redis-outage circuit-breaker latch — an unrelated ticket. So the entry could never have been reconciled by anyone working KS-617.

## Measured

Build, in a clean `node:24-alpine` container from its own standalone lock:

```
npm ci                 -> exit 0
ls tsconfig.json       -> No such file or directory
npm run build          -> EXIT 1     (tsc prints its help and exits non-zero)
ls dist                -> No such file or directory
```

Control that the absence is specific rather than a quirk of my check: **24 other** `services/*` **directories DO have a** `tsconfig.json`; this is the only one that does not.

Consumers:

| search (`*.ts`, excl. `node_modules`) | hits |
| -- | -- |
| `@secuura/service-utils` | **0** |
| `@secuura/shared` *(control)* | 243 |
| `express` *(control)* | 413 |

So the zero is real, not a grep that could not match. It is also declared as a dependency by exactly one `package.json` — its own.

Its `src/` is not empty: **15** `.ts` **files**, including `cache/redis-client.ts`, `cache/connection-pool.ts`, `cache/cache-middleware.ts`, `cache/compression.ts`, and `index.ts`.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

1. **It is a workspace member, so it is inside** `npm run build --workspaces`**.** That is the build KS-653 just repaired to 6/6 for the frontends; this member is a latent failure in the same command.
2. **It has a standalone** `package-lock.json`**,** so it is one of the 33 locks the KS-531 audit (`audit-locks.mjs`) and the clean-room gate (`lockfile-cleanroom.sh`) walk on every preflight and every PR — real gate time spent on a package nothing uses.
3. **It is one of the three** `vite 7.3.6` **pinners** cited in KS-482's analysis (`services/analytics`, `services/auth`, `services/shared`). Worth knowing that one of those three "consumers" is an orphan — this is recorded for accuracy, **not** a re-litigation of KS-482, which is closed and whose override was removed anyway.
4. Fifteen files of cache/Redis utility code sitting unreferenced is either **dead code to delete** or **a package someone meant to wire up and did not** — and nobody can tell which from the current state.

## The decision this needs

Not a mechanical fix — a call between:

* **Retire it.** Delete `services/shared`, removing a lock from the audit set and a latent failure from the workspace build.
* **Repair it.** Add a `tsconfig.json` matching the other 24 services, make `npm run build` produce `dist/`, and either wire up the consumers that were intended or accept it as a published-but-unused package.

Retiring is cheaper and is the honest default for code with zero importers; repairing is right only if something is meant to consume it. **Whoever knows the intent behind** `cache/connection-pool.ts` **should decide** — I have deliberately not guessed.

## Acceptance

1. Either `services/shared` is gone, or `npm run build` in it exits 0 and produces the `dist/` its `main`/`types` promise.
2. If repaired, at least one consumer imports it, or the `package.json` stops advertising an entry point that nothing uses.
3. `BACKLOG.md`'s entry is removed in favour of this ticket (its KS-617 reference is wrong and cannot be reconciled).

title: OAuth /token grant hardening (measured by the #982 gate, pre-existing): the authorization_code grant has no status pin (:809), the refresh grant does not rotate/denylist the presented token (:836/:860), a 503-class lookup error is mapped to 500 (:889-891)
description:
## BLUF

Three pre-existing gaps on ONE logical path — `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts`, `POST /api/oauth/token` — measured by the #982 (KS-790) tier-1 gate on 2026-09-14 and NOT graded against #982 (none changes its GO). One test pass, one fix on one file, three items:

* **R-1 — the** `authorization_code` **grant has NO status pin.** `routes/oauth.ts:809` `if (!user) {` — a SUSPENDED user's code mints 200 + a token pair (measured at the gated head in both stub legs). The refresh grant refuses the same user at `:868` `if (!user || user.status !== 'ACTIVE') {`; `/api/auth/refresh` pins ACTIVE at `auth.ts:687`; the authorize gates pin it too. Severity as a standalone defect: **Major** (a credential minted for a disabled account; the window is a 5-minute code minted before a suspension that post-dates the authorize gate's own status check).
* **R-2 — the** `refresh_token` **grant does not rotate / denylist the presented token.** `:836` `// Verify and rotate refresh token. verifyRefreshToken THROWS` (the comment says rotate; nothing rotates) and `:860` `if (decoded.jti && (await isRefreshJtiDenylisted(decoded.jti))) {` — the grant verifies, checks the denylist, mints. The same refresh token was accepted twice (200 / 200), 0 jtis denylisted by the product. The oracle is `/api/auth/refresh`: `auth.ts:695` `await rotateSessionRefreshToken(session.id, tokens.refreshToken);` and `:698` `await denylistRefreshJti(payload.jti, remaining);`. RFC 6749 §10.4 (rotation for public clients). **KS-823 (#983) rewrites this branch — the #983 gate re-measures R-2 at the new head.**
* **R-3 — a 503-class lookup error is mapped to 500.** `:889-891` `} catch (error: any) { logger.error('OAuth token error', { error: error.message }); res.status(500).json({ … code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'server_error' }) }` intercepts before `errorHandler.ts:77-80` (`export class ServiceUnavailableError extends AppError { … super(message, 503, 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE')`) can give the class its 503. Measured at both SHAs: ECONNREFUSED in the lookup → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR server_error`, the code already burned. A retryable outage reads as a bug.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-ks790-982-e62eab87a-tier1-r1/report.md` §8 (lines 195–203), §3a/§3b. Line refs are at `e62eab87a` (`oauth.ts` 1,260 lines there; develop-before-M19 `:800` for R-1's site).

**Neighbours, from the board census by symbol (title + description + comments, archived included):**

* KS-756 (nearest — the SESSION refresh handle; its item 4 names `routes/oauth.ts` `:254-271` as the OAuth refresh path that "moves in the same change or it becomes the bypass") — related, not the home.
* KS-999 (getUserById's decrypt path escapes the KS-253 classifier → 500 where 503 is mandated) — R-3's direct neighbour: with KS-999 fixed, this route's own catch still maps the class to 500. KS-1018 and KS-1132 are the same 503-class on other subjects.
* KS-486 (archived, Review A) — its 2026-08-13 row "G2 | Refresh rotation + jti denylist | VERIFIED | … replay refused at `routes/auth.ts:583` and `routes/oauth.ts:271`" read the CHECK at `oauth.ts:271` (now `:860`) as replay-refused. The measurement above says otherwise for the OAuth grant: the check exists, nothing on the OAuth path denylists a jti (only `auth.ts:698` does, on the session path). Named here as the ancestor; no relation (archived).
* KS-790 (#982 — the pre-auth lookup swap that made R-1 reachable at all: at develop the RLS-scoped lookup returned null for every code under migration 039, masking the missing pin).

## Proposed fix shapes (the gate's PROPOSALS, the builder's call)

1. R-1: `if (!user || user.status !== 'ACTIVE')` at `:809` with the same 400 `invalid_grant`; regression: the ks790 harness's cell 5 mirrored onto the code grant (a SUSPENDED-user code → 400).
2. R-2: on a successful refresh grant, denylist the presented jti for its remaining lifetime (the `auth.ts:696-699` shape) and, if a session backs it, rotate the session record; regression: a replayed refresh token → 400 + its jti denylisted. Re-measure after #983 lands (it rewrites the branch).
3. R-3: let `ServiceUnavailableError` (and any `AppError`) fall through to `errorHandler`, or map the class to 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` inside the route's catch; regression: a `ServiceUnavailableError` from either lookup → 503, not 500.

## Done when

- [ ] a SUSPENDED user's authorization code is refused with 400 `invalid_grant` at the code grant (R-1), with a red-first cell
- [ ] a replayed OAuth refresh token is refused with 400 and its jti reads as denylisted (R-2), with a red-first cell — measured on the post-#983 branch
- [ ] a `ServiceUnavailableError` from either user lookup on `/token` answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (R-3), with a red-first cell
- [ ] the ks790 / ks820-821 / ks823 harnesses stay green; `services/auth` full suite green; PR with a Test Evidence block

## Provenance

* Measured by the #982 gate (tier 1, round 1) on its own by-SHA copies of `e62eab87a` and develop M18 `8861e6216`, 2026-09-14 07:49–08:15 AEST; verdict GO 22:15:10Z; the three records stated at the same prominence as the findings and ruled to ONE ticket by Wednesday (22:40Z).
* Filed by the s220 merge seat before KS-790's close, so the relation is legal (Linear refuses a relation onto an archived issue). Dedupe census: `isRefreshJtiDenylisted` 0 title/description hits (1 comment hit: KS-486, archived) · `oauth.ts:809` / `:836` / `:860` / `:889` 0 · `refresh_token grant` 0 · `OAuth token error` 0 · `status pin` 0 · `ServiceUnavailableError` 1 (KS-1018) · `getUserByIdPreAuth` 5 · `routes/oauth.ts` 14 · `authorization_code` 4 — every hit's description and comments read; no existing home.

title: The aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR — wire it advisory (Kam: wire-nonblocking), and it is RED on develop today
description:
**Kam ruled** `wire-nonblocking`**, 2026-09-07 11:41.** Wire the aggregate workspace suite into the PR workflow as an ADVISORY, non-blocking job first, and decide on making it blocking from the evidence it produces.

## The gap

`npm run test --workspaces --if-present` exists in exactly **two** workflows:

| file | trigger | when it runs |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `ci.yml:51` | `workflow_dispatch` **only** | never, unless someone presses it |
| `deploy-demo.yml:140` | deploy | **after merge**, on the way to an environment |

So the aggregate workspace suite has **never met a PR**. Merged code is the first code it sees.

## ⚠ The job cannot run today, and that is measured

Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27). Measured 2026-09-07 via the Actions API: the **twenty most recent runs are all run-level** `startup_failure` **with zero jobs**, including runs triggered minutes earlier by a push.

**A workflow being configured to run on** `pull_request` **is not evidence that it runs.** That reading is what made this gap look smaller than it is — the trigger block is present and correct, and nothing executes.

So the deliverable is two things: the job, correct for when or if Actions returns, and a row in `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` under **Manual CI-gate equivalents** carrying the local command and its baseline — which is the gate that actually operates.

## 🔴 THE MEASURED BASELINE — and it decides the blocking question

Run on develop `61df129e9`:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| wall-clock | **32 s** |
| workspaces with a `test` script | **26** |
| skipped **silently** by `--if-present` | **6** — all of `frontend/`: admin, demo-overlay, issuer, outlook-addin, verifier, website |
| exit code | **1** |
| failing workspaces | **2** |

The two failures:

* `@secuura/anchoring-service` — **1 of 172**, `threadTokenMint` emulator round-trip ("parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId")
* `@secuura/originate` — **2 of 480**, `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard` (500s where 201 is expected; already carried on the backlog)

**Both are PRE-EXISTING on develop**, verified by running each workspace on develop with no branch changes in the tree.

**So the aggregate lane is RED today.** Had it been wired blocking, it would have blocked every PR in the repo from the moment it landed — including Peter's and Stuart's. Kam's advisory-first ruling was right, and **making it blocking requires those two suites green first.** That is the next decision, not this one.

## Also worth carrying

`--if-present` skips six workspaces **without a word**, so a green run does not say how many suites executed. The job prints the with-test/skipped counts *before* running the suites for that reason. The step itself carries no `|| true` and no exit-code laundering — the job-level `continue-on-error` is what makes it advisory, which keeps the real result visible in the log rather than rewriting it to success.

## Open

- [ ] Make it blocking — **blocked on** the anchoring `threadTokenMint` failure and the originate `ks444` failures.
- [ ] Decide whether the six frontend workspaces should have a `test` script or be explicitly declared as having none.

title: Wire up the opaque refresh token that createSession already mints — one write site, zero read sites (KS-329 ruling (a) prerequisite)
description:
**BLUF —** `createSession` **has minted an opaque refresh token on every session since the session service was written, and nothing has ever read it. One write site, zero read sites, measured with a control. Wiring it up is the prerequisite Kam's KS-329 ruling (a) actually names, it is not PQC work, and it can ship without committing to ML-DSA at all.**

**Recommendation:** do this first, on its own; leave KS-329 to be the algorithm swap, which gets materially smaller once the refresh path carries no signature.

### The measurement

`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:143`:

```
refreshToken: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex'),
```

* Write sites for `session.refreshToken`: **1** — `session.ts:289`, inside `rotateSessionRefreshToken`.
* Read / compare sites across all of `services/`: **0**. The only other occurrence of the identifier anywhere is a comment at `routes/auth.ts:635`.
* **Control:** the same grep against `session.isActive` — a field that genuinely is compared — returns **6** read sites (`session.ts:265, 304, 346, 357, 363`, `oauth.ts:391`). The search can find comparisons; the zero is real.
* `session.token` (`session.ts:142`, same `randomBytes(32)` shape) has **zero** read sites too.

The code already says it. `routes/auth.ts:634-635`:

> `// The session-record rotation alone is not enough — nothing in the`
> `// /refresh path compared the incoming JWT against session.refreshToken.`

The other half of the ruling is already live: `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:606-607` (`verifyRefreshToken` → `getSession(payload.sessionId)`). Both halves exist. What is missing is the wire between them — the cookie carries the JWT, the lookup keys off a claim *inside* that JWT, and the opaque handle sits in Redis unread.

### Why it stands on its own merits, independent of PQC

* **It removes a signature from a path that does not need one.** The refresh token is presented to exactly one endpoint, which already loads server-side state. A signed 942–1071 B JWT is doing work a 64 B handle does better.
* **It makes the size ceiling disappear permanently.** Measured on develop `8c9559cfd`: an ML-DSA-65 refresh token signs to **5018–5147 B** on real payloads against **3976 B** of usable cookie value (RFC 6265 §6.1 counts name + attributes; the exact options at `auth.ts:644-650` cost 120 B). Over by 1042–1171 B. ML-DSA-44 fits by **14 bytes** on the widest real profile — a coincidence, not a design. A 64 B handle leaves 3912 B spare for any future algorithm.
* **It simplifies reuse detection.** Today's A-05 control is sound — `denylistRefreshJti` throws rather than skips when Redis is down (`refreshDenylist.ts:30-35`), and the TTL matches the token's own remaining life — but a handle compared against the session record gives the same guarantee by construction, with no `jti`, no denylist and no TTL arithmetic.

### Scope

1. Redis reverse index `refresh:<handle> → sessionId`. Sessions are keyed `sess:<id>` and `user_sessions:<userId>` — there is currently no way to find a session *by* refresh token.
2. `POST /api/auth/refresh` — look up by handle, compare against `session.refreshToken`, rotate; drop `verifyRefreshToken` from the path.
3. The three cookie-set sites carry the handle instead of the JWT: `routes/auth.ts:394` (register), `:565` (login), `:644` (refresh).
4. `routes/oauth.ts` — `:242` and `:289` emit `refresh_token` in the body, and `:254-271` runs its **own** refresh path with its own `verifyRefreshToken` + denylist check. It moves in the same change or it becomes the bypass.
5. `shouldEmitRefreshTokenInBody` (`auth.ts:100-102`) — native/api clients take the token in the body and are not cookie-capped, but they should carry the handle too rather than leaving two token formats to verify forever.
6. **Transition, and this is the decision worth making explicitly rather than discovering:** live cookies hold JWTs. Either accept both formats for one refresh lifetime (7 days) then drop the JWT branch, or accept a single forced re-login across the estate.
7. `generateRefreshToken` / `verifyRefreshToken` / `generateTokenPair` shrink or go.

### Sizing

**1–2 days**, dominated by item 6 (the transition window) and item 4 (oauth's parallel path), not by the handle itself. Failing-test-first; the reverse index and the both-formats window each want their own test with a negative control.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against develop `8c9559cfd` — a read of the working tree plus local signing runs with the tree's own `jose` 6.2.3 on Node v24.7.0. No code changed, no platform writes. Full numbers, the per-profile size table and the nginx buffer check are in the KS-329 design note (comment `a9c84d3b`).

Prerequisite for KS-329. Ruling: Kam, 2026-09-02 19:35 AEST, decision card `secuura-ks329-refresh-token-size` (KS-329 comment `f62f6761`).

title: A platform admin who loses their TOTP device has no self-service recovery — TOTP-only branch, no backup codes
description:
## BLUF

**A platform admin who loses their TOTP device has no self-service recovery.** The platform-admin login branch accepts TOTP only — there is no backup-code path, and no alternative second factor. Recovery today means someone with database access editing `platform_admins`.

Surfaced while correcting a comment on [#804](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/804>) (KS-737). **The wording was the trivial half; this is the half that matters**, filed rather than left in a PR comment — a gap recorded only in a comment is a claim that outlives every tracker it names.

## The asymmetry, and note it runs the SAFE direction

|  | second factors accepted |
| -- | -- |
| regular user (`auth.ts:501-531`) | TOTP **or** a backup code (`verifyBackupCode`, `auth.ts:507-514`) |
| **platform admin** | **TOTP only** |

`#804`'s code comment describes the platform-admin branch as "shaped exactly like the regular-user branch below". It is not — and the difference makes the privileged path **stricter**, which is the right direction and the opposite of the defect KS-737 closed. Nothing here is a security regression.

**The problem is availability, not authorisation.** The strictest possible second factor with no recovery path is a lockout waiting for a lost or wiped phone, on precisely the accounts whose lockout is most expensive. And it interacts badly with two things already on the board:

* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) — per-person platform-admin identities. Today the seeded admin is shared; once identities are per-person, one person's lost device locks **that person** out with no path back, and there is no second admin who can help them without DB access.
* [KS-171](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-171) — `platform_admins.mfa_secret` handling. Any recovery mechanism has to not undo that work.

## Options, none chosen

1. **Backup codes for platform admins**, matching the user branch. Simplest, reuses `verifyBackupCode` and its KS-622 factor-1 proof. But it widens the privileged surface, and KS-622 exists because that path was got wrong once.
2. **A second platform admin can re-enrol the first.** Better separation, needs per-person identities ([KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)) and an audit trail to be meaningful.
3. **A documented, audited break-glass** — explicitly operator-run against the database, with the audit row as the deliverable. Honest about what happens today rather than pretending a product path exists.

**(2) is the right long-term shape and (3) is what should exist tonight**, because (3) is a runbook rather than code and the current answer is "someone edits the table and nobody records it". But that is a call for @kamil.kreiser, not an implementer's choice.

## Done when

* A platform admin who has lost their TOTP device has a defined, **audited** path back that does not require ad-hoc database editing.
* Whatever ships, the `auth.ts` comment stops claiming the two branches are identically shaped — that wording is what hid this.

## Related

[KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) (#804, where this surfaced) · [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) (per-person platform-admin identities) · [KS-622](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-622) (backup codes needing factor-1 proof) · [KS-171](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-171) (platform-admin MFA secret storage) · [KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781) (the other doors that skip MFA entirely)

title: deepmerge-ts GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (high) — override to 8.0.1 in originate; hoisted root lock baselined to 2026-10-31 on reachability
description:
**Ask:** remove the `expires: 2026-10-31` entry for `GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx` from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` once Prisma ships a `@prisma/config` that pulls `deepmerge-ts` 8.x — at which point the override below can go too.

Same class as [KS-585](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-585/js-yaml-3142-ships-in-runtime-images-ghsa-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj-and-dev) / [KS-599](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-599/bump-nanoid-ghsa-2v37-7h3g-55p8-high-dompurify-ghsa-55q2-fjhq-7xh7): a freshly-published advisory tripping the [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) npm-audit preflight gate with no code change on our side. Work-stream **H** ([KS-493](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-493/review-h-dependency-currency-and-known-vuln-package-upgrades-all)) per CLAUDE.md.

> ## 🌿 The work is already written — branch `fix/deepmerge-ts-ghsa-ggr8`
>
> **Use this branch, not Linear's auto-suggested** `feature/ks-664-…`**.** It was cut before this
> ticket existed and already carries both commits, verified:
>
> | commit | what |
> | -- | -- |
> | `307bc11ef` | `overrides: deepmerge-ts ^8.0.1` in `services/originate/package.json` + regenerated standalone lock |
> | `c28b09a65` | the reasoned `audit-baseline.json` entry citing this ticket, `expires: 2026-10-31` |
>
> **⚠ It exists ONLY on the Ubuntu VM (**`~/dev/Distributed_Secuura`**) — never pushed, no second copy.**
> Push it before anything else, or the work is one `git branch -D` from gone. It branches from
> `origin/develop`, touches **3 files**, and contains **no backend source** — only dependency
> metadata and build tooling.
>
> With it applied the full preflight **PASSES, exit 0** (legs 5 and 6 both green) — the first clean
> preflight on that VM. Without it, every `Blockchain/Dev` push from the VM fails the audit gate.
>
> Author of record is PeterD (the VM's git identity); the work is assigned here per the
> work-stream H ownership rule.

## The advisory

**GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx \[high\]** — *"DeepmergeTS has stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs."* Merging an object containing a cycle or very deep nesting recurses until the call stack blows and the process crashes. Affects `<8.0.0`; we pinned **7.1.5**.

Note the advisory carries **no CVSS vector** (score reports 0) — "high" is the publisher's own label, not a scored assessment.

## Why an override, not a dependency bump

It is transitive and **upstream has not fixed it**:

```
services/originate
  └─ prisma@^7.8.0            ← devDependencies
       └─ @prisma/config
            └─ deepmerge-ts   ← pinned EXACTLY 7.1.5 by @prisma/config
```

Checked against the registry on 2026-08-19: `@prisma/config@latest` **(7.9.1) still pins** `deepmerge-ts@7.1.5`, and `prisma` already resolves to the latest 7.9.x via `^7.8.0`. So bumping Prisma changes nothing; an `overrides` entry is the only route until Prisma moves.

## Reachability today: none that ships

* `prisma` is the **CLI**, in `devDependencies`. The runtime deps are `@prisma/client` + `@prisma/adapter-pg`, neither of which pulls `deepmerge-ts`.
* `services/originate/Dockerfile:79` runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`, so it is **not in the runtime image**. No deployed service carries this code. (The lock entry is even marked `"devOptional": true`.)
* The vulnerable path is `@prisma/config` deep-merging **Prisma's own config file** at CLI invocation — developer-authored input, not untrusted API input — and the impact is a crashed CLI, not a compromised service.

Build-time only, developer-input only, crash not compromise. Accepted on reachability, not absence — same standard as [KS-599](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-599/bump-nanoid-ghsa-2v37-7h3g-55p8-high-dompurify-ghsa-55q2-fjhq-7xh7).

## What has been done

**Fixed where it actually ships** — `services/originate` standalone lock (the one the Dockerfile's `npm ci` consumes) now resolves **8.0.1** via an `overrides` entry. Regenerated with the containerised procedure (`scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh:113`), because a plain `npm install --package-lock-only` in a member dir silently does nothing — npm walks up to the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root and refuses to write a member lock.

Surgical: **655 packages before and after, exactly one version changed** (7.1.5 → 8.0.1), 13 insertions. Verified by real container install — `deepmerge-ts` 8.0.1 installed, and `@prisma/config` **loads successfully against it** despite still declaring 7.1.5. Preflight **leg 6 (**`audit:locks`**) goes green**.

## Why the root lock is baselined rather than fixed — measured, not assumed

Preflight **leg 5 (**`audit:gate`**)** resolves the **hoisted workspace tree**, whose root lock still pins 7.1.5. npm will not re-resolve it incrementally: it reports `up to date` and skips, even with the override present in the root `package.json`, and even run containerised.

A full root-lock rebuild *does* apply the override, but the delta was measured and **rejected**:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| entries before → after | 1,970 → 2,830 |
| added / removed / version-changed | **956 / 96 / 11** |
| diff | **13,406 lines** |

It **downgraded** `@effect/schema` 0.68.27→0.66.16, `@lucid-evolution/core-types` 0.3.0→0.1.24, `@anastasia-labs/cardano-multiplatform-lib-*` 6.2.0-1→6.0.2-3 and `@prisma/get-platform` 7.8.0→7.2.0; **dropped** `@azure/keyvault-secrets`, `@noble/post-quantum` and `pglite`; and **added darwin-arm64 binaries** while resolving on Linux. Exactly the drift the clean-room guard exists to catch. Reverted; root `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched.

So there is no safe code fix for the hoisted view, and the baseline entry covers only that view — what ships is genuinely fixed.

## Removal path

1. Watch for a `@prisma/config` release depending on `deepmerge-ts` ^8.
2. Bump `prisma`, drop the `overrides` entry in `services/originate/package.json`, regen the standalone lock in `node:24-alpine`.
3. Remove the `GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx` entry from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`.

⚠ The `expires: 2026-10-31` is a forcing function: on expiry the gate fails again and **blocks every** `Blockchain/Dev` **push** — see [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635/audit-baseline-exception-expires-2026-08-31-and-will-block-every-push) for the same mechanism biting on 2026-08-31.

## How it surfaced

Only became visible on 2026-08-19, when the pre-push preflight was made runnable on Linux at all (PR #724 — `.githooks/pre-push` invoked a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` script with `sh`, and dash rejects `set -o pipefail`, so the gate had been aborting before leg 1 on the Ubuntu VM). Surfaced during [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) validation but unrelated to that work.

*— raised by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-19.*

title: anchor_store.status has no CHECK constraint — an out-of-union status can be stored silently (producer side of KS-1071 F10)
description:
**BLUF:** `anchor_store.status` is `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` with **no CHECK constraint**, so a status outside anchoring's union (`'pending' | 'submitted' | 'confirmed' | 'failed'`, `anchoring/src/index.ts:112`) can be written silently. KS-1071 closed the *consumer* side (the gateway's one status→confidence mapping now falls **closed** on any out-of-union value); this ticket is the *producer* side — a schema guard so the value cannot be stored in the first place.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:714` and `003_consolidate-anchors.sql:26` — the column, verified 0 CHECKs in the block against a control of 5 elsewhere in 001 (KS-1071's measurement).

**Fix shape:** a new migration adding `CHECK (status IN ('pending','submitted','confirmed','failed'))` on `anchor_store.status` — after a read-only census of the live rows on every environment (a row already holding another value would fail the migration; that row is a finding, not a reason to skip the constraint). Consider a shared TS status union exported from anchoring alongside it, so the code and the schema cannot drift apart silently.

**Why deferred from KS-1071:** a migration is out of that PR's scope by ruling (Wednesday, 2026-09-13 plan confirmation s199: "CHECK constraint → one Low ticket, not this round"). Migrations on this repo are baked into the `migrations` image — see the project CLAUDE.md note on rebuilding it, and KS-1031/#914's "migration 048 first" line before any deploy.

**Not covered here:** originate's own `document.blockchain.status` vocabulary (`anchor_failed`, `submitted`, `confirmed`) is a JSONB field, not this column; it lands on the gateway mapping's closed default and needs no schema change.

Source: KS-1071 F10 (QA tier-1 gate round 2 on #935); filed by s199 after a literal census of 1,104 issues for `anchor_store` + `CHECK` found no home (the only hit was KS-1071 itself). Related: KS-1071.

title: PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId} answers "DSR not found" with 200 for a canonical absent id and 404 for a non-canonical one, while GET answers 404 for both — align or document (QA-962 F-2)
description:
## BLUF

After PR #962 (KS-1029), `PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/:dsrId` answers "DSR not found" with two different statuses depending on the spelling of the id:

* a canonical (8-4-4-4-12) id that names no row → `200 {success:false, message:'DSR not found'}` — unchanged from base, deliberately preserved by #962;
* a non-canonical id (malformed, hyphenless, braced, uppercase hyphenless, hyphen-after-any-four) → `404 NOT_FOUND 'DSR not found'`, no DB call.

`GET /dsr/:dsrId` answers 404 for both (`getDSR` swallows the 22P02 and returns null). Neither PATCH answer is spec-invalid: the spec's own 200 description reads "DSR updated (success=false if id not found)" and 404 is declared. This is an internal-consistency gap, not a defect in #962. Measured at runtime by the tier-2 gate on #962 (rows A1 vs M1).

## Recommendation

One decision, then one small change: either

1. align PATCH's canonical-absent answer with GET's 404 (change `routes/gdpr.ts`'s `res.json({ success: updated, ... })` branch to 404 when `updated` is false, update the spec's 200 description, and add one cell), or
2. document the split in the spec's 200 and 404 descriptions and in the route's comment, and add one cell pinning each answer.

Whichever is chosen, keep KS-754's behaviour (a DB error stays a loud 500) and the body checks before the guard.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts` — the PATCH `/dsr/:dsrId` handler's `res.json({ success: updated, message: updated ? 'DSR updated' : 'DSR not found' })` (the 200 path) and the `UUID_PATTERN` guard #962 added (the 404 path); `originate.openapi.ts` PATCH `/api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId}` responses 200 and 404.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1029-962-ac6f4fa91-tier2-r1-relaunch-20260913b/report.md`, FINDINGS F-2 and §2 (rows A1, M1; the GET sibling in §4).
* **Related:** KS-1029 (PR #962, the guard), KS-754 (the 200 `{success:false}` path on a real id, fixed by #914).
* **Dedupe, before filing:** a literal census over 1,101 KS issues (684 archived) and their comments — `routes/gdpr.ts` (9 issues), `success:false` / `success: false` (8 / 10), `DSR not found` (KS-1029, KS-754 only), `/dsr/:dsrId` and `/dsr/{dsrId}`. The only issues naming both the route and `success:false` are KS-1029 (its base/head table) and KS-730 (err.message leaks). None describes the 200-vs-404 split. Controls: `UUID_PATTERN` → KS-1029 (1); a nonsense token → 0.

title: POST /api/auth/register accepts a client-supplied organizationId with no existence or membership check — impact not traced
description:
## BLUF

* `POST /api/auth/register` **lets an anonymous caller choose the organisation its new account belongs to.**
  * `registerSchema` accepts `organizationId` as any UUID (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:139`).
  * The handler stores it on the new user unchanged (`auth.ts:233`, `organizationId: data.organizationId`).
  * Nothing checks that the organisation exists, or that the caller has any relationship to it.
* **Impact NOT traced.** What an account carrying another organisation's id can reach has not been established. That covers the token's `organizationId`, organisation-scoped reads and the KS-597 issuer binding. Nothing was exercised on any environment.
* **Found by s189** while measuring the public account-creation path for KS-1100, on develop `4554b25e2`, which is the code kintsugi runs.

## Recommendation

* **Trace every consumer of a user's** `organizationId` **before choosing a fix.** Then either drop `organizationId` from the public register schema, or bind it to a verified invitation or membership.
* **Do not exercise it on a running environment** without explicit authorisation. Registering under another organisation's id is testing an exploit.
* **Priority High:** it sits on the organisation trust boundary Kam ruled `bind` (card `secuura-org-trust-boundary-within-tenant`, shipped in #954).

## Detail

### Code (develop `4554b25e2`)

* `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:133-142` defines `registerSchema` with `organizationId: z.string().uuid().optional()` and `.strip()`.
* `auth.ts:156` is `authRoutes.post('/register', ...)`. It is unauthenticated, and the gateway exempts it from CSRF (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:85`).
* `auth.ts:221-243` builds the new `User`:
  * the role is fixed server-side as `OWNER`, and a client-sent `role` is refused (KS-82);
  * but `organizationId: data.organizationId` comes straight from the request body.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:611-672`: `createUser` writes that value to `users.organization_id`.
* **Contrast:** `POST /api/users/admin/create` requires an ORG_ADMIN or SYSTEM_ADMIN caller and pins the tenant (KS-467). The public route has no equivalent check on the organisation.

### Not established

* Which reads, grants or attributions key off `users.organization_id`, or the token's `organizationId`, for an OWNER.
* Whether any downstream check already neutralises it. One candidate is originate's KS-597 binding (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:454-469`).

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive search over KS issue titles, descriptions and all comments, archived included. Run 2026-09-12 by s189.
* **Results:**
  * `registerSchema`: 3 issues and 4 comments, across KS-283, KS-202, KS-94, KS-266, KS-255 and KS-82. All are Done and archived, and none mentions `organizationId`.
  * `organizationId: data.organizationId`: 0.
  * `register accepts organizationId`: 0.
  * `self-assign organization`: 0.
* **Controls (the instrument can hit):** `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash` found KS-732 and KS-1005; `UUID_V4_RE` found KS-663.

### Related

* KS-1100: where this was found.
* KS-597: issuer organisation attribution (option B, #954).

title: Verify results show the user nothing about what was registered — a renamed file confirms green with no explanation (PS-723)
description:
## BLUF

**A verify result shows the user nothing about what was registered, so a renamed file confirms green with no way to notice the rename.** Stuart hit this on PS-723 and ruled the direction: *"it should be explained to the user, otherwise confusion will result… b should also have the note to the user that the filename has changed."*

The API is not the problem — it already returns the registered `title`, `issuer` and `certifiedAt`. **The portal never displays them**, because it reads a nested shape the backend does not emit. And the portal already sends the presented filename, which the backend silently discards. So both halves of the comparison exist today and nothing joins them.

## RECOMMENDATION

Render the registered metadata beside the confirmation, plus a plain-language line that verification is **content-based** — a rename neither breaks nor fakes it. Where the presented filename differs from the registered title, say so explicitly rather than leaving the user to spot it.

One decision is **not mine and should be made before any code**: the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2. That is Peter's call.

## 1. What the verify response actually returns

Measured live, `POST /api/verification/verify` with `contentHash` — the path a renamed-file verify takes:

```
verified: true
title: "E2E Test Certificate"     <- the REGISTERED title
issuer: "demo"
documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt
certification: { certifiedAt, certifiedBy, certifierOrganizationId }
checks: { documentExists, hashValid, integrityVerified, ... }
```

So the metadata Stuart wants shown is already on the wire.

⚠ **The OpenAPI schema understates this. **`VerifyResponse` declares 20 properties and **none** is `title` / `originalFilename` / `registeredAt` / `registrant`; the live response carries `title` and `issuer` anyway. Same declared-vs-actual family as **KS-712** — worth fixing in the same pass so the contract stops lying about this endpoint.

## 2. Why nothing renders — the mechanism

`frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx:423` guards the entire "Document Details" card:

```tsx
{result.verified && result.document && ( ...Title... Issuer... )}
```

* The API returns `title` and `issuer` **at the top level** and emits **no** `document` **object** (measured top-level keys: `verified, documentId, title, documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt, issuer, blockchain, certification, checks, verifiedAt`).
* `result.document` is therefore undefined, the guard is falsy, and **the card never renders**.
* The portal references `result.document.*` **5** times and `result.title` **0** times. Control: `result.verified` matches **14** times, so the grep discriminates.
* The data is **not** lost in parsing — `VerifyResponseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the top-level `title` survives into the parsed object and is simply never read.
* The schema *does* declare `document: DocumentSummarySchema.nullable().optional()` carrying `title` + `issuer`. **The frontend was written against a nested shape the backend does not produce** — one side moved and the other did not.
* Confirmed on the path in use: all three verifier call sites hit **v1 **`/verification/verify`. v2 is a different shape entirely (`count, hash, matches, verifiedAt`) and the portal does not use it.

### The contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix

Either the **frontend reads the flat fields**, or the **backend nests them** under `document` to match the schema the client already expects. Both work; they differ in blast radius (the backend shape is consumed by the Outlook add-in and issuer too). Naming it rather than picking it.

## 3. `fileName` is already sent, and silently discarded

`frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127` sends `{ contentHash, fileName: file.name }` and `:138` threads `fileName` into the result object. So the **client already holds both halves** of the comparison — presented name and registered title — and needs no new input to detect a mismatch.

Server-side, however:

* `VerifyRequest` declares only `documentId, hash, title, contentHash` — `fileName` **is not in the contract.**
* **No backend route handler reads it**: 0 files under `services/*/src/routes/` reference `fileName`, against a control of **8** referencing `contentHash`.

So the field is sent on every verify and thrown away. Either consume it (and declare it) or stop sending it — the current state is a silent no-op.

## 4. Scope — three surfaces, per Stuart, not just the verifier portal

His comment names them: *"This affects Outlook plug ins, and Verify functionality in 'Views' and directly from the menu."* Verify call sites in the tree:

| app | file |
| -- | -- |
| verifier portal | `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx`, `ResultPage.tsx` |
| **Outlook add-in** | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/utils/api.ts` |
| issuer portal | `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts`, `components/admin/ConnectorsPage.tsx` |

Whatever wording is agreed should land on all of them, or the same confusion simply moves to whichever surface is left out.

## 5. Design constraint — the KS-695 erasure interplay

**KS-695 item 2 brings** `documents.title` **INTO erasure coverage**, because S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`). For S-originated documents that field **is** the original filename — exactly what this ticket wants displayed. Item 3 goes further: connector-scoped dissolution blanks all connector documents' titles.

So the two pull opposite ways: PS-723 wants the registered name shown; KS-695 makes that same field erasable PII that can legitimately be blank. Both are correct on their own terms.

**This must be specified, not discovered:** decide what a verify result shows for a document whose title has been erased — a blank, or an explicit *"registered name erased"* state. Rendering empty silently would recreate today's confusion in a new form.

## Not in scope here

No fix in this ticket — it is the specification and the evidence. No change to PS-723, which is Stuart's.

## Related

* **PS-723** — *Verify still confirms if filename has changed* (Stuart, 2026-09-01). The originating report and his ruling.
* **KS-712** — the declared-vs-actual spec gap this endpoint also exhibits.
* **KS-695** — `documents.title` erasure coverage; the design constraint in §5.

title: Verifier shows 'Verification Failed' / 'INVALID' for an id that is not in the registry, with no next step
description:
## BLUF

* **Enter an id that is not registered, and the verifier shows "Verification Failed" and "INVALID" with no next step.** The API behind it said `"Document not found in the registry"`.
* **A mistyped id reads like a document that failed verification.** Honesty holds: it never claims verified.
* **Pre-existing,** found by the kintsugi deploy gate on `4554b25e2` (finding F-7, Polish).

## Recommendation

* **Show "not in the registry" as its own result,** and tell the user what to do next: check the id, or verify by file instead.

## Detail

* **Measured by the gate:**
  * A random v4 id in Enter ID → `/verify/result/<id>` shows "Verification Failed" and "INVALID" (`evidence/u2-verify-enter-random-id.png`).
  * `POST /api/verification/verify` → 200 with `"Document not found in the registry"`; 0 console errors.
* **Oracle:** user desires. The message is not precise about what went wrong or what to do.
* **Related:** KS-735, on the same verifier result page, which shows nothing about what was registered on a success.

### Evidence

* **Report:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-kintsugi-deploy-4554b25e2-tier1-r1/report.md`, section `### F-7 — The verifier tells a user with a mistyped id their document is "INVALID"`.

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive census over all 1,089 KS issues (682 archived; title and description) and 2,946 comments (includeArchived), run 2026-09-12 by s188.
* **Completeness control:** per-ticket comment counts equal direct API reads on 9 of 9 tickets.
* **Searched:**
  * `not found in the registry`: 0
  * `Verification Failed`: 2 (both archived — KS-40, a different case, and KS-521)
  * `Enter ID`: 2 (archived)
  * `mistyped`: 0
* **Result:** no existing home.

title: Verifier mode tabs (Upload File / Enter ID / Scan QR) lose their accessible name at phone width — WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2
description:

title: The OpenAPI spec is now a consumed contract, but nothing in CI stops it drifting — plus two known spec/code divergences
description:
Raised by Platform S, 2026-08-19, from a full S↔K audit against K develop `74a330fc0`. **Nothing is broken today** — the spec is in sync. This is about keeping it that way now that something depends on it.

## What changed on our side

[PS-614](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614>) (merged, S develop `2403313`) makes Platform S read `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at gate time and fail its build when S's lifecycle-verb vocabulary disagrees with K's published enum, in either direction.

We built it because of [KS-556](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556>): K added `protect`/`unprotect`/`restore` on 2026-08-03, S adopted them on 2026-08-18, and for 15 days those events anchored with **no** `documentType` **at all**. Nothing failed, because every guard S had compared one hand-maintained copy of K's list against another. Reading K's own spec is the fix.

**Your spec is a strong contract, and that is why we chose it.** Verified: it is *generated* (`scripts/generate-openapi.ts:28`) from the same `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` constants the runtime validates against, and the enums match exactly — 22 and 13, diffed programmatically, empty symmetric difference. That is a better guarantee than a hand-written spec could give.

## The gap

`check:openapi` **is not wired into any CI workflow.** It exists as an npm script (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:43`), but grepping all 17 files in `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` returns **zero** hits. (`quality:static` in `pr-platform-suites.yml:238` runs in `systemTest/playwright`, a different workspace.)

So the spec is correct today by diligence, not by enforcement — and it is now load-bearing for a consumer outside this repo. A PR that changes a verb without regenerating would leave S's gate green while S sends something K rejects, which is the [KS-388](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388>) 400-the-whole-anchor case.

**Ask:** run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow.

## Two divergences worth closing while you are there

**1.** `/api/v2/verification/verify-file` **is in code but absent from the spec.** Handler at `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:497`; `verify-file` does not appear in `secuura-api.yaml` at all. The v1 equivalent is missing too. It is the only verify variant where the **server** computes the hash — i.e. the one a client cannot lie to — so it is the one most worth publishing. Invisible to a spec-reading consumer today.

**2.** `documentUuid` **is stricter in code than in the spec.** Code requires UUID **v4** specifically (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:350` `UUID_V4_RE`, 400s v1/v5/v7); the spec publishes `format: uuid` (`secuura-api.yaml:4556-4557`), which any RFC 4122 version satisfies. A client generating a v7 UUID passes spec validation and is rejected at runtime. We happen to send v4 ([PS-570](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-570>) enforces the version nibble before sending), so this has not bitten us — but it would bite a new integrator. Either publish the v4 constraint or relax the code.

## One observation, no action implied

`emitLifecycleAnchor` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1120-1128`) posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to `/api/anchors` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `metadata.timestamp`. So lifecycle events recorded through **K's own** endpoints anchor unlabelled, while the same verbs sent by S on the flat path carry the verb on-chain. Consistent with [KS-319](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-319>)'s scope, but it means the [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary) / [KS-534](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-534>) / [KS-415](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-415>) vocabulary only ever reaches the ledger via the flat path. Flagging in case that is not intended.

## Verification

* A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating the spec **fails** CI.
* `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec.
* `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches what the code enforces.

*Everything above verified read-only against develop* `74a330fc0`*. Happy to review a draft against our gate before you merge — we are the consumer and can tell you quickly whether it reads correctly from our side.*

title: KS-1041 residual: the cross-tenant JWT probe on originate's direct path — reasoned, never run, not commissioned
description:
## BLUF

* **Recorded from KS-1041, so it stays on a live ticket when KS-1041 is archived.** It was outside KS-1041's Step 1 and Step 2, and it is **not commissioned and not ruled**.
* **The open question:** can a caller already inside the compose network, holding a **valid** JWT, go straight to originate and have an `x-tenant-id` for **another** tenant honoured?
  * KS-1041 **measured** only the credential-free connector-header case.
  * This wider case was **reasoned, never tested**.
* **What has changed since:**
  * #938 (Step 1, `0f8fb33c3`) closed nginx `/originate/`.
  * #951 (Step 2) adds originate middleware that strips unvouched trust headers — but only once `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is provisioned. That is unset everywhere (PROVISIONING SAFETY: UNSAFE, KS-1083), so originate's direct path behaves as before.

## Recommendation

No action until Kam rules. Running the probe needs a fresh commission — KS-1041 `116ed2d6`: *"If it should be run, that goes back to Kam."*

## Detail

* **KS-1041's measured/reasoned split, verbatim** (`116ed2d6`):
  * MEASURED:
    * direct to `originate:4000`, no headers → 401;
    * direct, with forged `x-user-role: connector` + `x-tenant-id` → 200;
    * the same request through `api-gateway:8080` → 401;
    * not externally reachable, but reachable by any of the 34 peers on `dev_secuura-network`.
  * REASONED: *"the same door is open wider, including a cross-tenant read — needs a valid JWT and a probe nobody has run."*
* **Why it was not run:**
  * `ba0f7402`: *"That the same door is open wider (a peer with a valid JWT setting* `x-tenant-id` *for another tenant) is reasoned, not tested — it needs a probe I have not run and will not run without a fresh commission."*
  * `47e0b331`: *"Not done and deliberately so: the cross-tenant JWT probe. It is the next measurement and belongs to a seat with room to act on the answer."*
* **Where it sits:** `originate/src/index.ts:230` reads `x-tenant-id` before auth (`ba0f7402`). Once the secret is provisioned, #951's middleware strips unvouched trust headers ahead of it; KS-1083 holds that precondition.
* **Neighbours, not duplicates:**
  * KS-619 — the gateway's conditional `x-tenant-id` overwrite (the gateway path, not originate's direct path);
  * KS-1032 — trust-header reads outside auth middleware (a code census);
  * KS-1084 — the gateway's Authorization-only calls to originate.
* **Why its own ticket, not a comment on KS-1032:** this is a live measurement, and KS-1032 is a code census and guard. Separate workloads get separate tickets under Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.
* **Board searched before filing** (literal, live tickets only):
  * `JWT probe` 0 · `valid JWT` 0 · `gateway-only ingress` 0 · `flat network` 0 · `tenant confusion` 0;
  * `originate:4000` → KS-1041 only;
  * `another tenant` → 6, none about originate's direct path;
  * `cross-tenant` → 62 literal hits, none about this probe.

title: [Tracker] 2026-06-10 platform assurance review — gap-analysis + remediation
description:
Umbrella tracker for the 2026-06-10 assurance review (SDLC/supply-chain, OWASP, SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001, GDPR/privacy) + full e2e across local/dev/demo. Modelled on [KS-169](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-169/tracker-2026-05-29-security-review-findings-remediation)/[KS-79](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-79/tracker-2026-05-14-audit-follow-ups-security-review-test-infra-rot). Full write-up: `Notes (MASTER)/Secuura/platform-k-assurance-gap-analysis-2026-06-10.md`.

## Headline

App-layer security is strong (argon2id+HIBP, AES-256-GCM field encryption w/ AAD, trust-header stripping, parameterised SQL, RS256 migration, CSRF). **No data-subject PII on-chain** (hashes+IDs+org-name only, with an active `@`-in-issuerName guard). Material risk clusters: a live IDOR, inert tenant RLS, CI security gates not on PR, no data-tier resilience, GDPR program architecture-ready not operational.

## E2E (all envs)

* **Local** Tier 1 API: 113 pass (2 "fails" both non-defects — 429 limiter artifact + local single-tenant `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` artifact); Tier 2 smoke: 35 pass; Tier 3: see thread.
* **Dev**: live-runner dispatched (run `12a05762…`) — tenant isolation is the real test here (MT on).
* **Demo (prod)**: read-only health/verify only — healthy.
* Test-infra: tenant-isolation specs should skip when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`; e2e-v2 tier1 hits the login limiter (cf [KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)).

## Findings

### 🔴 Urgent

* [KS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-228/urgent-idor-gdpr-exportconsentdsr-routes-lack-ownership-check-any) — IDOR on GDPR export/consent/DSR routes (any authed user reads any user's PII). *Fixed.*
  * [KS-258](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-258/testschemathesis-add-gdpr-idor-ownership-guard-regression-tests-ks-228) — Schemathesis regression test suite for [KS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-228/urgent-idor-gdpr-exportconsentdsr-routes-lack-ownership-check-any) fix. Closes `idor_rbac: coverage: PARTIAL` noted in `schemathesis_tests.yaml`. *Backlog.*

### 🟠 High — new tickets

* **CI security gates not enforced on PR** — [KS-105](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-105/ks-49-phase-01-ci-orchestrator-typescript-aggregator-canonical-finding) contract gate + Trivy/Semgrep/Gitleaks/SCA(npm-audit) are `workflow_dispatch`-only. → see linked ticket.
* **Dependabot inactive** — config at dead `Blockchain/Dev/.github/` path, none at repo root. → linked.
* **No DB HA / geo-redundant backups** — HA disabled, 7-day retention, single region/pgbouncer. → linked.
* **No tested DB restore / DR runbook.** → linked.
* **Document the GDPR Art. 17 erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability position** (DPIA note). → linked.

### 🟠 High — already tracked

* RLS fail-open / per-tenant-DB isolation — [KS-160](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-160/tenant-rls-fail-open-when-appcurrent-tenant-id-is-unset-migration) ([KS-172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-172/ks-160-step-1-inventory-tenant-scoped-vs-cross-tenant-query-paths-rls)/173/174).
* JWT HS256→RS256 cutover — [KS-167](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-167/jwt-symmetric-asymmetric-signing-for-production-rs256eddsa-key-vault) ([KS-183](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-183/jwt-asym-step-e-verifiers-verify-rs256-via-public-key-gateway)/184).

### 🟡 Medium (promote to tickets as picked up)

* Per-route rate limiters use in-memory store (per-replica) → ×replica-count (extends [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)).
* Audit log: login `user_id` null + reads unaudited + not tamper-resistant (no hash-chain/WORM).
* Log Analytics retention 30d → raise to ≥90d/1yr (SOC2 window / ISO).
* MFA not mandatory for admin/privileged roles.
* Two divergent MFA-enable flows; `users.ts:707` persists secret pre-verification (cf [KS-158](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-158/mfa-totp-secrets-stored-plaintext-in-mfa-pending-setups-and-likely-in)/171).
* App ships no CSP (relies entirely on nginx) — add gateway-level fallback.
* `requireScope()` is a no-op for human users — no central deny-by-default for function-level authz.
* Cookie consent banner not wired to server-side consent API + bundled/implied consent (GDPR Art. 7).
* No KYC document-image retention policy (Art. 5(1)(e)).
* No Article 30 ROPA / sub-processor register; `Secuura-Compliance-Report.md` overstates posture (do not show customers as-is).
* Breach response not operationalised (no IR runbook / 72h trigger).
* Verify PII keys are Key-Vault-sourced in demo/prod (Art. 32).
* Silent migration-failure handling (log-and-skip → drift).
* Dead duplicate workflow tree `Blockchain/Dev/.github/`; no [SECURITY.md/disclosure/patch-SLA](<http://SECURITY.md/disclosure/patch-SLA>); no CODEOWNERS; base images not digest-pinned + version drift.

### 🟢 Low

* argon2→bcrypt silent fallback (no prod hard-fail); webhook SSRF allowlist unverified; CSRF fails-open on missing Origin (non-prod, documented); strip unused `metadata.ownerId` from anchoring schema; document issuer-org-name-on-chain decision; fix stale `encryptedField.ts` header (says not-live, is live); aggregate auth fail-open on Redis outage.

## Note

`Secuura-Compliance-Report.md` self-certifies "Compliant" vs GDPR/HIPAA/PCI-DSS/SOC2 while unreviewed — flag for downgrade to "design-intent" before any customer/auditor sees it.

title: Anchor-status standoff: a consumer repolls anchors K reports as terminally failed — K's labelling is already honest (KS-587), so the fix is terminal-state handling, not a new K signal
description:
## BLUF

**The standoff is real, but its stated mechanism is wrong — and measuring demo inverted the ownership.** The premise going in was *"K reports simulated anchors as* `confirmed`*; Platform S's honesty rule refuses a* `mock_tx_` *hash; S repolls forever."* Measured on demo tonight, **K does not report them as confirmed.** All 83 simulated anchors on demo are flagged `simulated = true`, `status = failed`, carrying the explicit error `KS-587: simulated placeholder — never on chain; marked …`. **Zero rows on demo are** `simulated = true` **and** `confirmed`**.** K already fixed this — that is what **KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587** were.

So the accurate statement is: **a consumer is polling anchors that K reports as terminally** `failed`**, forever.** That is not a labelling defect on our side. It is a missing terminal-state rule on the consumer side.

## Recommendation

1. **Layer 1 — the actual fix, PS-side (Stuart's):** treat `status: failed` as **terminal** and stop polling. No new K signal is required; the one already published is sufficient and has been since KS-587 deployed.
2. **Layer 2 — K exposes** `simulated` **machine-readably: ALREADY DONE. This is a no-op, closed here, and no work should be raised for it.** Verified in the **shipped** demo image, not just the source tree.
3. **Layer 3 — env hygiene (Stuart's call):** whatever is polling demo from `52.74.18.212` should not be pointed at demo at all.
4. **Layer 4 — per-environment Blockfrost keys:** still open, still pending the credential question below.

## Detail — what was measured, on demo, read-only

**Demo is not simulating.** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is **absent** from the anchoring container's environment (0 matches against a 22-line env, so the read itself is proven). Boot logs: `Cardano integration active — real blockchain anchoring enabled`, `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"`, network `preview`.

`anchor_store` **composition — 285 rows total:**

| shape | `simulated` | `status` | n | first | last |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| real 64-hex | false | **confirmed** | **194** | 2026-07-08 | 2026-08-14 |
| `mock_tx_*` | **true** | **failed** | **83** | 2026-07-31 | 2026-08-01 |
| NULL | false | failed | 6 | 2026-07-11 | 2026-08-05 |
| real 64-hex | false | failed | 2 | 2026-08-04 | 2026-08-10 |

Crosstab, stated plainly because it is the whole argument: `simulated = true` appears **only** with `status = failed`. **There is no (**`simulated = true`**,** `confirmed`**) row on demo.** Controls: `simulated` is never NULL (0 of 285); totals reconcile 194 + 83 + 6 + 2 = 285.

**The loop's corpus is fully resident on demo — the cross-instance hypothesis is dead.** All **71** distinct anchor ids the loop requests are present in demo's `anchor_store`: **71 present / 0 absent**. Controls both fired: a fabricated id `anchor_0000…0000` matched **0**, a known-real id matched **1**. So these anchors were minted **on demo**; they were not minted on a simulated instance elsewhere and verified here.

**And every one of them is a failed anchor:**

|  | n |
| -- | -- |
| `simulated = true`, `failed`, mock hash | **68** |
| `simulated = false`, `failed`, NULL hash | **3** |
| **confirmed** | **0** |

That is the finding. The loop is polling **71 anchors that can never succeed**, 68 of which K has explicitly labelled as simulated placeholders that were never on chain.

**The** `simulated` **flag is machine-readable, and it ships.** In the **running** demo image (`/app/dist/index.js`, and `docker inspect` shows **no bind-mounts**, so the image *is* what serves):

* `...(simulated ? { simulated: true, simulatedTxRef: rawTxHash } : {})` — 3 emit sites
* `verified: !txView.simulated && anchor.status === 'confirmed'`
* a placeholder hash is moved to `simulatedTxRef` and `transactionHash` is set to **null**, so a mock hash is never presented as a transaction hash

Control: a nonsense token grepped for in the same file returned 0. Source agrees (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `honestTxView`, `anchoring.openapi.ts` `simulated: z.boolean().optional()` + `simulatedTxRef`).

**The Blockfrost split — both "zero Blockfrost calls" and "quota exhausted" are true at once.** They describe **different routes**:

| route | behaviour | last 60 min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` | **pure DB read**, ~1 ms, no Blockfrost | **1,970 × 200** |
| `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` | **live Blockfrost** | **608 × 200 · 460 × 500** |

**457** of those 500s carry Blockfrost's own string `"Usage is over limit."` (against 3,935 total anchoring log lines). So Stuart's agent's *"zero Blockfrost calls in two hours"* is **correct for status GETs** — that is exactly what they observed, and it is a real property of the code. Our *"quota exhausted"* is **correct for verify-by-hash**. Neither observation refutes the other; the earlier reconciliation hypothesis (creation-simulated / verify-live) was the right shape but the wrong axis — it is **status-read vs verify-by-hash**, not creation vs verification.

**Traffic, for scale.** Last 6 h at demo's edge: **23,515 requests from** `52.74.18.212`**, of 23,515 total — 100.0%** of demo's inbound. Split: `POST /api/verification/verify` 11,620 · `GET /api/anchors/{id}` 9,704 · `GET /api/documents/{id}` 2,190 — **all 200 at the gateway.** ~3,919/hr, consistent with the ~3,850/hr measured on KS-670 across 08-14 → 08-21.

## Attribution, corrected gently

Stuart's agent read the honesty rule as **S's**. The record says the honest-labelling rule was implemented **in K**: **KS-520** (Urgent, Done) — anchoring fabricated a `tx_sim_` hash and marked the document anchored under `SIMULATE_ANCHORING`; **KS-522** (High, Done) — a simulated anchor presented as genuinely verified, no honest-labelling signal; **KS-587** (High, Deployed to UAT) — *"84 demo anchors carry* `mock_tx_` *hashes but are flagged* `simulated=false` *+ confirmed"*. KS-587 is the direct ancestor of this ticket: it found **84** mis-flagged rows and remediated them. Tonight demo holds **83** rows carrying its remediation message. **The defect Stuart's agent describes is one K already found and fixed** — which is worth saying clearly, because it means no K change is needed and the polling behaviour is unaffected by anything we ship.

Credit where due: their diagnosis of the *mechanism* — a consumer refusing a mock hash and retrying forever — is correct and is what made this tractable. Only the direction of the labelling defect was off, and their own caveat (which K instance they queried was unstated) is what prompted the measurement that found it.

## What their numbers describe

Their **1,638 anchors, all simulated** is **not demo** — demo has **285** anchors, of which 83 are simulated. Since all 71 polled ids resolve on demo, the polling target is demo; the 1,638-row instance they inspected is a different K (most likely one of the local development stacks). **Not asserted, and it does not change the finding:** the fix is terminal-state handling regardless of which K holds the larger simulated corpus.

## Still open

* **The credential question, unanswered since 2026-08-20:** does the local K stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key or its own? If demo's, per-environment key scoping becomes the durable fix, and Kintsugi (its own free-tier project per environment) is the working precedent.
* **The Blockfrost allowance *period* is still unverified** — nothing here should be sized on a 50k/day assumption.

## Provenance

* Demo measurements | read-only SSH to `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-08-21 10:26–10:40Z | container env, `docker logs`, `psql` SELECTs, and one `docker inspect`. **No writes, no config change, no key action, no restarts.** Two scratch files created under the VM's `/tmp` during extraction were removed in the same command.
* Loop corpus | demo nginx gateway logs, 6 h window | two of my own extraction patterns were wrong on the first pass (`doc_` vs `doc-`, and verify hashes ride in the POST body rather than the URL); both corrected before any figure here was written down.
* KS-520 / KS-522 / KS-587 / PS-522 | live Linear reads, 2026-08-21 | `PS-522` returns nothing; `KS-999` used as a not-found control.

title: CLAUDE.md's "rebuild local after any merge to develop" needs its written exception — a merge with zero buildable surface is a measured no-op
description:
## The ask
