* *The* `PreviousChainId` *mirror does not exist in K* — the only matches in the K tree are the migration comment, the OpenAPI description and the repo/route prose. No column, no code.

## Why this matters

Anchoring is the product claim. A provenance record that reads identically for *"this share was revoked"* and *"this share was never revoked"* is not a weaker record — for that question it is a **wrong** one, and the reader has no way to know. It also means K's own `share-revoke` verb currently under-counts real revokes by an unknown amount, so nobody can measure the size of this from the K side either.

## Done when

1. **Decide the contract**, with S: does a revoke-to-NoAccess emit `share-revoke` (K's own vocabulary), or does `share-permission-change` carry a payload field K agrees to schema and read? Either is defensible; the current state — where it depends on which S UI path the user clicked — is not.
2. **If the payload route is chosen**, K stops treating this one payload as free-form: a declared shape, validated at the route, documented in `VOCABULARY.md`.
3. **Correct migration 037's header** so it stops claiming a `PreviousChainId` mirror the schema does not implement — or implement the chain link, which is what makes an omission detectable at all.
4. **Decide whether K should be able to detect an omission** (a per-document event sequence, or a periodic S↔K reconciliation). This is the bigger of the two and may well be its own ticket; recording the question here so it is not lost.
5. **Measure the current divergence** once the contract is agreed — how many `share-permission-change` rows are in fact revokes.

Nothing here is actionable without S. Filed as a line in the **KS-772** S↔K integration-contract stream.

## Provenance

* The S-side behaviours that raise the question | Stuart's PS-749 review split (PS-764/765/766/767) and his own 2026-09-03T23:33:13Z correction retracting two of four, relayed via Wednesday | not independently verified — S-side, and out of this ticket's scope
* Every K-side statement above | read-only on `origin/develop` at `492152a81`: `migrations/037_document_lifecycle_events.sql`, `services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts`, `services/originate/src/repositories/lifecycleEventRepo.ts`, `docs/VOCABULARY.md` | read 2026-09-04

title: The control-byte guard cannot see a raw body — findNulBytePath returns null for every Buffer, and the doc claims otherwise
description:
## BLUF

**The control-byte guard cannot see a raw body.** `findNulBytePath` and
`findControlBytePath` both return `null` for **every** `Buffer`, so a request parsed
by `express.raw()` passes the guard whatever bytes it carries. The guard's own doc
comment says every field is covered; that is not true of raw bodies. Nothing is
exploitable on `develop` today — the one live `express.raw` is path-scoped and its
payload is not persisted as text — but the guarantee KS-471/KS-472 states is wider
than the guarantee the code delivers.

**This ticket asks a question rather than answering it: should a webhook payload be**
**scanned at all, or declared out of the class in writing?** Both are defensible. What
is not defensible is the current state, where the doc claims one and the code does
the other.

## Recommendation

Decide first, then implement — the implementation differs completely by answer:

* **(A) Scan raw bodies.** Teach `findControlBytePath` to walk a `Buffer` (a byte
  scan, not `Object.entries`), and mount the guard after `express.raw` on
  `/webhooks`. Cost: a byte walk on every webhook body. Risk: a signed webhook
  payload whose signature covers the raw bytes must not be altered — rejection is
  fine, mutation is not, and the guard only rejects.
* **(B) Declare raw bodies out.** Say so in the guard's doc comment and in
  `mountBodyParsers`'s, and add a leg asserting that no `express.raw`/`express.text`
  mount feeds a handler that persists its body as text. The exclusion becomes a
  **declared set with a reason**, which is the shape the KS-800 gate asked for.

## Detail — measured, not quoted

Against `packages/shared/dist/middleware/index.js` built from this branch's source:

```
Buffer [61 00 62]            findNulBytePath       null
Buffer [61 00 62]            findControlBytePath   null
CONTROL {f: "a"+NUL+"b"}     findNulBytePath       "f"      <- the walker works
CONTROL {a: 0} (a number)    findNulBytePath       null     <- not a numeric artefact
CONTROL {s: buf.toString()}  findNulBytePath       "s"      <- same bytes, as a string
```

Two controls that could have disagreed and did not: the identical bytes presented as
a **string** are found, so the failure is Buffer-specific and not a broken walker;
and a literal number `0` is correctly not a NUL, so the null is not a numeric
artefact either.

**Cause.** The walker recurses with `Object.entries(value)`. On a `Buffer` that
yields numeric indices with **number** values, and no branch of the walker matches a
number — so it returns `null` without ever looking at a byte.

**Every raw/text parser in tracked source** (`git ls-files` over `*.ts`/`*.js`, so
build output cannot inflate it):

| Site | Status |
| -- | -- |
| `services/billing/src/index.ts:50` | **LIVE** — `app.use('/webhooks', express.raw({type:'application/json'}), webhookRoutes)`, path-scoped, mounted **before** the guard |
| `services/billing/src/__tests__/ks488-c4-webhook-idempotency-fail-closed.test.ts:63` | test harness, same shape |
| `packages/shared/src/middleware/request-limits.ts:92` | `express.raw` factory — **shared exports a way to mount one** |
| `packages/shared/src/middleware/request-limits.ts:102` | `express.text` factory, same |

The last two matter beyond this ticket: they are the same two factories recorded as
**KS-800 F-16**. `express.text` sets `req.body` to a **string**, which the guard
*can* walk — so for text bodies ordering is real protection and the KS-802 widening
of `PARSER_CALL` is load-bearing. For `raw` it is not: ordering a raw parser before
the guard buys nothing at all. **Detection is not protection, and the two cases**
**differ.** Whatever is decided here should be written into `PARSER_CALL`'s comment so
the next reader does not infer that a detected raw mount is a guarded one.

## Provenance

* The Buffer behaviour and its two controls: measured in this session against a
  fresh `tsc` build; command and output above.
* The parser-site table: `git ls-files | grep -nE` at `55894a5b5`.
* Raised by the KS-802 gate (report §4, PR #818 @ `8a9fa6bde`) and folded to a ticket
  by Wednesday's ruling 2026-09-05 06:35:12Z. Related: **KS-800** (F-16), **KS-802**.

title: The OAuth error code travels in error.message and the contract never says so; and authorize refusals answer JSON where RFC 6749 redirects
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

Two related contract defects in the OAuth error envelope, both **pre-existing** (KS-804's shape, not KS-822's changes).

**1. The OAuth code travels in the wrong field and the contract never names it.** Every refusal from the authorize and token endpoints answers `{ success: false, error: { code: 'BAD_REQUEST', message: '<oauth_code>', description } }` — so `error.code` is the platform's HTTP-ish code and the **OAuth** code (`invalid_client`, `invalid_grant`, `invalid_scope`, `unsupported_response_type`) is in `error.message`. The published descriptions name those codes but never say which field carries them, so an integrator has to guess or read a response.

**2. RFC 6749 4.1.2.1 delivers authorize errors by REDIRECT, not a JSON 400.** For an authorize request with a *valid* client and redirect URI, the RFC says the server redirects back with `error=...&state=...` rather than answering the user agent with JSON. This platform answers JSON 400 for the whole rule set. That is a design question, not a bug to fix quietly — the deny path already redirects, so the two halves of the same endpoint disagree.

**Done when:** the contract states which field carries the OAuth code; and a decision is recorded on whether authorize refusals should redirect per the RFC, with the deny path's existing behaviour as the reference point.

title: OAuth app_type: a CASED row is neither normalised by 047 nor refused by its CHECK, and docker/init's unnamed constraint defeats 047's idempotence guard
description:
## BLUF

Two DDL defects left by KS-821's migration 047. **F-2 is the one that matters: a cased row such as**
`'Public'` **is silently and permanently bricked** — it is not normalised and not refused, and the
app's users get the false message *"Invalid or expired authorization code"* forever.

## F-2 (Major) — the case hole survives 047 in both directions

* 047's normalisation predicate is `lower(app_type) NOT IN (...)`, so `'Public'` **does not match**
  and is left untouched.
* The CHECK it adds **permits** `'Public'` as well, so the row is legal forever.
* Every consuming rule is an **exact** match, so `'Public'` is a third string to all of them and
  takes the else-branch — the app can never satisfy the rule it is judged by.

**Fix-shape (the tester's — a HYPOTHESIS until run against the unfixed product):** either normalise
on the exact set and `SET app_type = lower(app_type)`, or fold case at the three exact-match
consumers — `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:276`, `:615`, and
`services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:209`. Measure which before choosing; a CHECK that permits a
value the code cannot honour is the defect, so the constraint's own predicate is in scope too.

## F-3 (Minor) — a second identical constraint

`docker/init`'s inline CHECK is **UNNAMED**, so Postgres names it `oauth_apps_app_type_check` — the
same name 047's idempotence guard looks for is not the name it looks for. The guard misses it and
adds a **second identical constraint** on a fresh database.

## Scope note

`app_type` is now inside `CreateOAuthAppSchema` case-folded (KS-821), so the **API** can no longer
mint a cased row. This ticket is about rows arriving any other way — a direct DB write, a restore,
a seed, or anything predating 047.

---

*Filed by s133 from the KS-820+821 tier-1 gate (PASS 1 @* `0e8d3e60a`*, report* `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-05-s132-ks820-821-pass1-0e8d3e60a/report.md` *at the QA tree), on Wednesday's disposition ruling of 2026-09-05T13:01:20Z. Inherited — not introduced by #825.*

title: #568 publishes 17 URLs on secuura.io — an unresolving, seemingly unowned domain (KS-669 class; no guard rule covers URLs)
description:
## BLUF

**#568 publishes 17 URLs on** `secuura.io` **— a domain that does not resolve and that we do not appear to own.** This is the same class as [[KS-669]] (`exports.secuura.com`, an unowned for-sale domain in the published spec), three weeks on, and it is back because **no guard rule covers URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only sees email addresses.

Filed separately from KS-669 rather than as a comment on it, deliberately: KS-669 is In Progress with its own scope (17 of its 18 URLs are still open work) and its operative defect is that it is **unassigned**. Folding a second, differently-sourced class into it makes it bigger, not more actionable. Cross-linked both ways.

**Stated fairly in both directions: #568 is a net improvement here.** It *removes* all **3** `demo@secuura.io` addresses that `develop` publishes today — E1 doing exactly its job. The URL class is the part nothing checks.

---

## Evidence

**DNS, with a control set** (2026-08-21):

| Domain | rcode | NS | SOA |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none | none |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns2.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns4.afternic.com.` | present |

The three controls resolve, so the resolver works and the NXDOMAIN discriminates.

⚠ **A limit on this evidence, stated rather than glossed:** `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` describes the TLD, not the domain. **I am reporting DNS only — NXDOMAIN with no NS and no SOA. I am not claiming a registration status.** Someone with registrar access should confirm ownership before this is closed either way.

**Occurrences in the published spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`):

| Pattern | `c114ceddd` (#568) | `origin/develop` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | **0** |
| `demo@secuura.io` | **0** | **3** |

Repo-wide on #568 the string appears **35** times across 7 files — the 17 published ones plus 18 in the generating sources (`auth`, `billing`, `m365-integration`, `originate`, `prism` `.openapi.ts`, and `synthesize.ts`). Fixing the source fixes both.

**The 17, by field** — these are not all cosmetic:

* `redirectUri` ×1 · `webhookUrl` ×1 · `successUrl` ×2 · `cancelUrl` ×2 · `siteUrl` ×1
* `serviceEndpoint` ×5 · `url` ×3 · bare array items ×2

`redirectUri`, `webhookUrl`, `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` and `serviceEndpoint` are all fields an integrator may copy into a working configuration. A published spec that points them at an unregistered domain is a domain anyone can register.

**Source** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`:

```ts
case 'uri':
case 'url':
    return 'https://example.secuura.io/resource';
```

Every `format: uri` / `format: url` field gets this one literal.

---

## Fix direction

Use a domain reserved for the purpose. `example.com` **is reserved by RFC 2606 / RFC 6761** and can never be registered by anyone — which is the same guarantee the email side already relies on (E1 permits `example.com` addresses). `https://example.com/resource` is a one-line change at `synthesize.ts:203`, plus a regeneration.

**Then close the hole that let it back in:** add a URL rule to the guard — an example whose value parses as a URL must have a host in the reserved set (`example.com`/`.org`/`.net`, `localhost`), or be allowlisted with a reason. Without it this class returns a third time. That rule belongs with the guard-coverage work in the sibling ticket.

---

## Calls needed from @PeterD

1. **Do we own** `secuura.io`**?** If we do, this drops to "point it somewhere real or use `example.com` anyway". If we don't, it should not be in a published spec at all.
2. Is `example.com` acceptable as the synthesised URL host, or do you want a real owned host (e.g. under `secuura.ai`)?

---

**Verified by:** @kamil.kreiser, 2026-08-21 — DNS with control set, occurrence counts on both refs, source line read. Working tree untouched. Related: KS-669 (same class, `exports.secuura.com`), KS-256/#568, KS-665.

title: Per-person platform-admin identities — the shared seeded admin cannot carry attribution or approval
description:
## BLUF

Platform-admin is a **shared** seeded account today, so no rule that depends on *which person* acted can be made real — including the two-approver shape for bulk re-key ([KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582)) and any honest attribution on a recovery action.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

Every guardrail on the `register-connector` path is currently "platform-admin or refuse" (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:499-509`). That is a capability check, not an identity check. Consequences:

* An approval rule ("two approvers for a batch") cannot be enforced — the same shared credential can satisfy both sides.
* Recovery-action audit records the role, not the person.
* Off-boarding a person does not remove their platform-admin access, because the access is not theirs.

**Gates:** [KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) (approval shape) cannot be implemented until this lands.

**Done when:** platform-admin actions attribute to a named person, and the shared seeded account is no longer a route to platform-admin in any environment that matters.

---

Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: [Decision] Approval shape for bulk re-key — two approvers for a batch, one for a single-org rotation
description:
## BLUF

@peter's proposal: a **batch** re-key needs two approvers; a **single-org** rotation needs one. The shape needs deciding, but it **cannot be implemented until** [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) **lands** — the shared platform-admin account cannot make a two-approver rule real, because the same credential can satisfy both approvals.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

Open questions for the decision:

* Who counts as an approver, and is the *requester* allowed to be one of the two?
* Is approval synchronous (the call blocks) or a request/approve/execute flow with a record between the steps?
* What is the break-glass path when a genuine incident cannot wait for a second approver, and what does it cost in audit terms?
* Does the second approval cover the whole batch, or the specific list of refs (so the list cannot be edited after approval)?

**Blocked on:** [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) (per-person platform-admin identities).

**Done when:** the shape is agreed and recorded here, with the break-glass path named explicitly rather than left implicit.

---

Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: Append-only recovery audit held outside the estate being recovered
description:
## BLUF

Today's audit for the credential-recovery path is **best-effort, fire-and-forget, and lives inside the estate being recovered** — so the one incident where it matters most is the one where it is least trustworthy.

Carried over from @peter's §4 candidate on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

* The rotate handler's audit write is `.catch(() => {})` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:698-709`. A failed audit write is silently dropped and the rotate still succeeds.
* `GET /api/audit` is memory-backed (`services/security/src/index.ts:597`), and under fail-closed RLS the boot warm loads nothing (see [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578)).
* The records live in the same Postgres instance as the data being recovered. A compromise or loss that triggers a bulk re-key is exactly the event that can take the evidence of the re-key with it.

**Scope:** an append-only record of recovery actions (who, which refs, when, outcome per ref) written outside the estate, where a failed write is a **loud** failure rather than a swallowed one.

**Done when:** a bulk re-key produces a durable, append-only record that survives loss of the primary estate, and a failed audit write cannot pass silently.

Sizing: 3–5 days.

---

Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: Phase 2 — JWT RS256 → hybrid (RS256 + ML-DSA-65)
description:
> **⚠ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 (session 19) — the shim blocker below is DEAD, and the real blocker is different. Kam's ruling needed on a design change; see the pinned comment for the measurements.**
>
> `jose` 6.2.8 signs and verifies ML-DSA JWTs on Node 24 today — **no liboqs, no WASM shim**. Measured: RS256 435 B / ML-DSA-44 3326 B / **ML-DSA-65 4511 B** / ML-DSA-87 6269 B, and ML-DSA **verifies faster than RS256** (0.3 ms vs 0.5 ms), so performance is not the constraint.
>
> **The real blocker is token size against the refresh-token COOKIE.** `generateRefreshToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts`) returns a *signed JWT* which `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:367,534,613` sets as the `refresh_token` cookie; browsers cap one cookie at **4096 bytes**. ML-DSA-65 measured 4511 B on a *three-field* payload — the real refresh payload is larger. It does not fit. That forces a design change (opaque refresh token + server-side session lookup — the pattern already exists at `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:133`, cookie chunking, or access-token-only migration) — **Kam's ruling, not an implementation detail.**
>
> Residual risk from the original refusal, still real: Node reports `ExperimentalWarning: The ML-DSA-65 Web Crypto API algorithm is an experimental feature and might change at any time`. Available ≠ production-hardened.
>
> Also: auth signs with `jsonwebtoken` 9.0.2, which has no ML-DSA support — any rollout starts by moving auth's signing path to `jose`.

Migrate JWT signing to hybrid via the Phase-0 registry.

- [X] `~~jsonwebtoken~~`~~ / ~~`~~jose~~`~~ don't yet ship ML-DSA — add a COSE/JOSE PQC shim (liboqs-node or a vetted WASM ML-DSA lib) behind the crypto abstraction.~~ **OBSOLETE 2026-08-12:** `jose` **6.2.8 ships ML-DSA; no shim required. Replaced by: migrate auth's signing from** `jsonwebtoken` **to** `jose`**.**
- [ ] Roll out **verifier-first** (api-gateway, originate accept both), then signer (auth), then drop classical.
- [ ] Entra ID / CIAM (RS256) is **Microsoft-owned** — only ensure `obeden-ssd` doesn't hard-fail on their token-alg rotation; track their PQC timeline.

Blocked by Phase 0. Ref: plan §5 Phase 2.

title: No table references `users`: 0 of the database's 29 foreign keys point at it, across 52 user-reference columns — KS-697 was this hole being exercised
description:
## BLUF

**No table in the platform database has a foreign key to** `users`**.** Not one — across **52** columns named `%user_id` / `%holder_id` / `%_by_id`. The schema *does* use foreign keys (**29** of them), which is what makes this a gap rather than a deliberate house style.

Every one of those 52 columns can therefore hold a uuid that references nobody, and nothing in the database will object.

## Measured — live local DB, `develop cc65abad5`

| measure | value |
| -- | -- |
| foreign keys in the database | **29** |
| of those, pointing at `users` | **0** |
| columns named like a user reference | **52** |
| FKs on `shares` (any) | **0** |
| FKs on `custody_events` | **1** — `document_id` only |

The `custody_events` row is the tell: that table *does* carry an FK, on `document_id`, and `to_holder_id` sits beside it without one.

## Why this is being filed now

[KS-697](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-697) was exactly this hole being exercised: `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` accepted an invented `newHolderId`, returned 201, and **minted an anchor** for a custody chain pointing at a user that has never existed. That route is fixed in application code ([PR #751](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/751>)) — but the fix is one handler, and the underlying condition covers 51 other columns.

Known second instance, unfixed: `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` format-checks `recipients[].userId` (KS-536) but **never checks it exists** — `shares.recipient_user_id` is cast to `::uuid` and inserted with no FK behind it. Lower blast radius than custody (no ownership flip, no anchor), but the same class.

## Not a "just add the FKs" ticket

Recording the reasons up front so whoever picks this up does not discover them the hard way:

1. `users` **is** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` **fail-closed** (migration 039). FK validation runs as the referencing statement's role, so adding FKs to an RLS-forced table needs thought about which role validates the reference and whether the tenant GUC is set at that moment. This is the KS-458 surface.
2. **Multi-tenancy may put** `users` **in a different database** from the referencing table under the per-tenant-DB model — a cross-database FK is not expressible. That has to be established per table before anything is added.
3. **Existing rows may already violate** what a new FK would assert. KS-697 alone wrote several on local. Any `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT` needs a survey first, and `NOT VALID` + a later `VALIDATE` is probably the shape.
4. **A count guard will lie here. **`users` under FORCE RLS returns 0 rows to a non-superuser without the tenant GUC — an "are there orphans?" query can read clean on a table full of them. Set `app.tenant_scope_bypass` before counting.

## Suggested first step

Not a migration. An **inventory**: for each of the 52 columns, which are genuinely user references, which live in the same database as `users`, and how many current rows are already orphaned. That survey decides whether this is one migration, several, or an application-layer rule instead.

Found during KS-697, 2026-08-27. Filed separately so it does not die when that ticket closes.

title: Platform S — upload your test suite so the extranet live runner executes it (GitHub Actions)
description:
## What this is

The extranet **Testing** tab has a **Run on Dev / Run on Demo** button ([KS-138](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-138/extranet-live-test-runner-trigger-schemathesis-api-e2e-v2-e2e-on)). It triggers a GitHub Actions workflow (`extranet-test-run.yml` in `Secuura/Distributed_Secuura`) that runs test suites **live** against the chosen environment and posts a dashboard back into the portal. Draft workflow + generator are staged in `secuura-extranet/ci/` (`extranet-test-run.yml`, `build-dashboard.mjs`, `README.md`).

This ticket: **add the Platform S test suite** so the runner executes it. (Peter's Platform K suites already exist — see the sibling ticket.)

## How to upload test code so the runner runs it

1. **Commit the suite into the repo** (`Secuura/Distributed_Secuura`, on `main`) — e.g. `systemTest/platform-s/` or `tests/platform-s/`.
2. **Target via env vars, never hardcode** — read the base URL from env so the same code hits dev or demo:
   * Dev API: `https://secuura-dev-api.gentlebush-21213dc4.uksouth.azurecontainerapps.io`
   * Demo API: `https://secuura-demo-api.blackmoss-2a7eea0b.uksouth.azurecontainerapps.io` (and `https://secuura.com` for the app)
   * Use the same `API_BASE_URL` / `BASE_URL` convention the existing suites use.
3. **Runnable headless on an ubuntu GitHub runner** — a deterministic install + run (Node or Python), no GUI, no Chrome-MCP-only steps.
4. **Emit machine-readable results** — a JSON summary (Playwright-style `{stats:{expected,unexpected,skipped}}` is ideal, since the dashboard generator already reads that) plus optionally an HTML report. The runner builds the combined dashboard + posts it back.
5. **No committed credentials** — the harness auto-detects the seeded demo/dev logins from the URL; for authed calls, log in at runtime to get a token.
6. **Wire a workflow step**: add an install+run step for your suite to `extranet-test-run.yml` (gated by the `env` input, `continue-on-error: true`) and point `build-dashboard.mjs` at your results. Ping Kam/Claude and we'll add the step.

## Done when

Platform S tests run green headless against **dev** from the workflow, produce a results JSON the dashboard reads, and appear in the extranet Testing → Platform S tab after a run.

Refs: [KS-138](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-138/extranet-live-test-runner-trigger-schemathesis-api-e2e-v2-e2e-on) (the runner), [KS-136](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-136/platform-s-registration-login-issue-jwt) (Platform S auth/JWT). Sibling: Platform K wiring (Peter).

title: prism issues VCs with random bytes as the Ed25519 proof and verifies them as passed — the A-11 fraud pattern fixed in vc-issuer, never fixed here
description:
## BLUF

`services/prism` issues verifiable credentials whose `Ed25519Signature2020` proof is **64 random bytes**, and its `/verify` returns `passed: true` without checking anything. This is the identical pattern that was ruled fraud-grade and **fixed in** `vc-issuer` **under Audit A-11** — `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:125-128` says so in its own comment. It was never fixed in prism.

**Tracking ticket in the KS-621 pattern: severity is provisional and the fix shape is deliberately blank.** The by-design-or-remediate ruling is Kam's, and it turns on the deciding question below. Filed off [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) Review D pass-2 (peter, 2026-07-21) — the finding has had no home since.

## The finding, re-verified at `c13b5ba9a` (2026-08-13)

Peter's citations are unmoved — verified line-by-line, not assumed:

| Site | Code |
| -- | -- |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:658-663` | `type: 'Ed25519Signature2020'` … `proofValue: crypto.randomBytes(64).toString('base64')` |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:787` | `checks.push({ check: 'proof', passed: true }); // Mock verification` |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:35` | `const PRISM_MODE = process.env.PRISM_MODE \|\| 'mock';` |

## Two corrections to the original framing — both make it read differently

**1.** `PRISM_MODE` **is decorative. It is never branched on.** Peter's write-up says *"*`PRISM_MODE` *defaults to* `'mock'` *with no production gate on the issue path → a prod deploy that **forgets the flag** forges credentials."* Measured: `PRISM_MODE` occurs **5 times** in the file — the declaration (`:35`), the `/health` response (`:376`), the `/api` info response (`:390`), the boot log (`:893`) and the boot banner (`:899`). `grep -c "if.*PRISM_MODE\|PRISM_MODE ===\|switch.*PRISM_MODE"` returns **0**.

So the risk is not a forgotten flag. **The flag has no effect at all**, and it is *already set to a non-mock value in both deploy paths*: `docker-compose.yml:965` sets `PRISM_MODE=basic`, and `deployment/azure/services.bicep:980` sets `PRISM_MODE=basic`. The behaviour is byte-identical to mock.

**2. The service actively misreports its own mode.** Because `:376` and `:390` echo `PRISM_MODE` into `/health` and `/api`, prism currently answers `mode: "basic"` to any operator, monitor or auditor asking whether it is mocked — while forging every signature. That is worse than a missing gate: a missing gate is silent, this one answers the question wrongly. Anyone who checked "is this service mocked?" the obvious way would have been told no.

## Reachability — the reason severity is provisional, not asserted

Bounded to what I could prove, and it cuts **toward** lower live risk:

* **The gateway does not route to prism's credential path.** `/api/credentials` → `vcIssuer` (`proxy.ts:697-699`), `/api/presentations` → `vcIssuer` (`:712,:715-717`). The **only** prism mapping is `/api/did` (`proxy.ts:645-647`), authenticated.
* **Zero internal consumers.** Repo-wide, `PRISM_SERVICE_URL` / `prism:4001` has no caller outside the gateway's own service-config and system-status listing. No frontend calls `/api/prism`.
* **But the service is live**: `secuura-prism` is Up + healthy in the local stack, and it was in the Container Apps bicep. The forging path is **one route mapping away** from being reachable, with nothing in the code to stop it.

This is the same disposition class as [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)'s C-2 wallet-verify stub — **latent, not live**: reachable in principle, no current consumer trusting the result.

## The deciding question (this is what the ruling turns on)

**Does** `services/prism` **have a future in which it runs for real — or is it a stub that should refuse to issue at all?**

The question as originally posed — *"does prism ever run non-mock?"* — assumes a mode switch that could be flipped. There isn't one. So the real question is narrower and sharper:

* If prism is **dead or demo-only scaffolding** → the honest fix is to make it *say so* (refuse to issue, or label the proof honestly per the KS-520/522 precedent, where a `mock_tx_` anchor is never presented as on-chain proof), and stop `/health` reporting `basic`.
* If prism is **intended to become a real DID/VC service** → this is a Wave-2 integrity item and the A-11 remediation already applied to vc-issuer is the template.

**Fix shape deliberately blank pending that ruling.** Specifying it now would pre-decide the product question, which is the KS-621 lesson.

## Provisional severity

**High**, per Wednesday's SCORE ruling (session 25) — carried as given. Recorded honestly: the reachability evidence above argues this is *latent*, while the reachable half of the same finding class sits in the vc-issuer holder-binding ticket. If Kam re-ranks the pair, the argument for putting the reachable one first is in both tickets.

## Adjacent, deliberately not filed as a third ticket

Peter's pass-2 also carries a **Low**: `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:100` — `const issuer = req.body.issuer || defaultIssuer`, caller-controlled, then signed with the platform `VC_SIGNING_KEY` at `:146`. The A-11 gate (`:129-145`) removed the hardcoded-key fallback but **not** the caller-supplied issuer identity, so the finding survives its own fix. The session-26 brief scoped this to two tickets, so it is recorded here rather than filed unasked — flagging it for a ruling on whether it needs its own home.

title: GET /api/anchors/{id} and verify report different statuses for the same anchor — 91 UAT anchors read "failed" while verify says confirmed
description:
Raised from the S side 2026-08-12 (S ticket: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>)). @kamil.kreiser — one authenticated call settles this; details below.

## The observation

Platform S polls `GET /api/anchors/{id}` to learn when an anchor confirms. On UAT, **91 transactions are stuck reporting** `failed` — while `POST /api/verification/verify`, asked about the same document's content hash, reports the **same anchor id** as confirmed on chain.

Concretely, anchor `anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2`:

```
POST /api/verification/verify  {"providedHash":"6ffa6a0d4378007a480af701b6113cc0252544bcfde93cf11c2654c8bbe2367e"}

  verified   : true              status  : anchored
  anchorId   : anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  bc.status  : confirmed         txHash  : e64759a924ea314e…
  anchoredAt : 2026-08-09T06:18:39.090Z
  checks     : documentExists ✓ hashValid ✓ isCertified ✓ isAnchored ✓ integrityVerified ✓
```

S recorded its failure for that same anchor at **06:32:20** — **fourteen minutes after** `anchoredAt`. So this is not a race between a poll and a late confirmation.

A second sample behaves identically: document ref `doc-1785566174843-631e2310` (an originate/upload), `verified: true`, `confirmed`, txHash `38adf13132f6856a…`, while S has it marked failed.

## What has been ruled out on the S side

Both plausible S-side causes were eliminated before raising this:

* **Not a failed/unauthenticated read.** All six affected organisations are registered with connector keys, and each has rows that *did* confirm — org 6: 77 confirmed vs 58 failed, org 9: 39 vs 20, org 13: 8 vs 6. Reads plainly work for these tenants.
* **Not an S mapping bug.** For an `anchor_…` reference S takes the `status` field from `/api/anchors/{id}` **verbatim** — no interpretation layer is involved. S is reporting the exact word it is given.

Spread is across every verb (share 39, upload 16, share-attach-consent 13, certify 5, sign 5, watermark 4, and the share-edit verbs), so it is not verb-specific.

## The question

Does `GET /api/anchors/{id}` return a stale or different status than the anchor's true state?

Candidates worth checking:

1. The anchors read serves a row that `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` ([KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure)) later healed, without the anchors view reflecting the heal.
2. There are two anchor records and the endpoints resolve different ones — the [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so)/584 "answer from the row that evidences its claims" family, except here it is the *anchors* endpoint that looks wrong.
3. `/api/anchors/{id}` is correct and verify is optimistic — in which case S's reading is right and the bug is elsewhere.

**The one call that settles it:**

```
GET /api/anchors/anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
```

on demo-pk, authenticated. If it returns `status: failed` while verify reports that anchor confirmed with tx `e64759a924ea314e…`, the inconsistency is confirmed and the question becomes which is authoritative. I could not make this call myself — the endpoint requires auth — so the diagnosis above is inferred from S's behaviour plus the eliminations, not directly observed.

## Why it matters to S

1. Users see **"anchor failed" on documents that are anchored and confirmed on chain** — a false negative on a trust surface.
2. **S never collects the real transaction hash.** Those rows keep their `anchor_…` placeholder permanently, so the chain evidence K is holding is silently lost to S.
3. It makes S's anchoring-failure count unusable as an alert signal.

## What S has done meanwhile

S no longer takes a bare `failed` as final ([Secuura/platform-s#440](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-577-dont-take-anchor-failed-as-final-when-ks-own-verify-disagrees-4a8640ddf0ac), merged). When the anchors endpoint reports failed, S asks verify and prefers the evidenced answer **only** when verify names the same `anchorId`, reports it anchored, not simulated, and carries a real 64-hex transaction hash.

That is a mitigation, not a fix — it recovers the lost hashes and stops the false failures, but the two endpoints still disagree, and S is now quietly compensating for it. Worth resolving at source.

Related: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>), [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure), [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so).

title: BM-2: Verification is a configurable workflow via smart contracts — record the workflow path, not casual views
description:
## BLUF

**Verification is a CONFIGURABLE WORKFLOW, not a fixed function.** Clients configure verification workflows via smart contracts; Secuura does NOT prescribe compliance. The workflow PATH is verified against the smart contract and recorded; simple interactions like document VIEWING are NOT recorded on-chain (noise). A third-party verifier (e.g. recruiter verifying a university document) sees the inspectable steps (identity checks, domain matching). End-user sees a binary "verified"; audit/legal sees full rigor.

## Carried ruling (PS-556, Kam 2026-08-11)

A verification is a **public, repeatable READ** — it sits OUTSIDE canonical lineage (lineage = versions from certifications/modifications). If a verification act is recorded at all, **S records it for S's own reporting/lineage annotation — K does NOT become a source of record for verification acts.**

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam).

title: Tokenise personal/identifying data — mint a privacy token (Platform S/K by journey origin) and thread it through the APIs
description:
## Context

GDPR data-minimisation / privacy. Spun out of the KS-234 DPIA work: today an individual/sole-trader **issuer name can land in plaintext on the immutable Cardano chain** (KS-234 §5.1, accepted as a disclosed residual *pending this ticket*). Tokenising identifying data also complements KS-291 (per-subject DEK / crypto-shred) by keeping plaintext PII out of immutable artefacts in the first place.

## Goal

Replace plaintext personal / identifying data with a generated **token**, so the token (not the plaintext) is what flows through the system and onto the chain.

## Requirements

* **Token generation owned by the platform where the client journey starts** — generated by **Platform S or Platform K** depending on origin. A journey beginning on Platform S mints the token there; one beginning on Platform K mints it there.
* **Incorporate the token into the APIs** — request/response contracts on both platforms carry the token (in place of, or alongside, the plaintext identifier); downstream services + the on-chain anchor consume the token.
* **Initial implementation on Platform S** (Platform K to follow once the S contract is proven).
* Define the token scheme: stable per-subject/per-identity, non-reversible without the mapping, and the mapping store + its lifecycle (incl. erasure interaction).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Token scheme + ownership defined (which platform mints, by journey origin).
- [ ] Platform S generates and threads the token through its APIs.
- [ ] On-chain anchor uses the token, not the plaintext issuer/personal name (closes the KS-234 §5.1 residual for new anchors).
- [ ] Platform K follow-up scoped (separate sub-task/ticket).

Refs: KS-234 (origin), KS-291 (per-subject DEK / crypto-shred).

title: [Decision] Erasure: multi-step to trigger, but irreversible + complete once executed — confirm no recoverable off-chain link survives (incl. backups)
description:
Decision/confirmation for **Stuart** (split out of [KS-234](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-234/document-the-gdpr-art-17-erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability-position)). This is the foundation of the whole GDPR Art.17 position, so it needs an explicit sign-off.

## Requirement (Kam)

Erasing a data subject should take **multiple deliberate steps** (guard against accidental deletion), but **once executed it must be gone for good — irreversible and complete.**

## Why it's the crux

Our Art.17 position is "anonymisation by destruction": the permanent on-chain record (a hash + opaque tokens) becomes anonymous because the orphaned token **marries to nothing recoverable by anyone**. That only holds if **every** off-chain link is genuinely destroyed — not just the live DB row, but the M365 source documents, KYC images, search indexes, logs, the PII vault (`vault_entries`), and crucially **immutable backups** (you cannot delete a row from a 7-year immutable backup).

## The mechanism that makes "gone for good" true even in backups

**Crypto-shredding.** All PII is AES-256-GCM encrypted (per-tenant DEKs already exist). On erasure, **destroy the key** → the ciphertext sitting in backups becomes permanently unrecoverable. Today `gdprService.executeErasure` does row anonymise/soft-delete + a `USER_ERASED` fan-out, but does **not** destroy encryption keys — so a backup may still hold recoverable ciphertext. Closing that is what turns "deleted from the live DB" into "gone for good everywhere."

## For Stuart to confirm / decide

1. **Multi-step trigger** — e.g. request → admin approval → typed confirmation. Confirm the controls/UX (no one-click irreversible deletes).
2. **"Gone for good" = key-destruction (crypto-shred) on erasure**, not just row-delete. Confirm we adopt this as the guarantee.
3. **Full-surface coverage** — confirm the destruction reaches every off-chain place a recoverable link could survive: live DB, `vault_entries`, M365 source docs, KYC images, search indexes, application logs, **backups** (via key-destruction). Enumerate + confirm none retains a recoverable link. Anything that does → file as an implementation gap.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Erasure model confirmed: multi-step trigger + irreversible + crypto-shred + full off-chain surface coverage.
- [ ] Residual-link gaps (if any) filed as implementation tickets.

Related: [KS-234](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-234/document-the-gdpr-art-17-erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability-position) (DPIA note), tracker [KS-229](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-229/tracker-2026-06-10-platform-assurance-review-gap-analysis-remediation).

title: Consolidate Platform K billing onto Platform S's Stripe integration (one company, one Stripe)
description:
## Decision (Kam, 2026-05-21)

Platform K will use the **same Stripe integration as Platform S** — same company, so one Stripe account/integration, not two. Platform K should **not** maintain its own separate Stripe.

## Current state

* **Platform S** (`platform-s-main`, [ASP.NET](<http://ASP.NET>) Core) has a mature **subscription** Stripe integration: `Services/Stripe/StripeSubscriptionClient.cs`, `Controllers/StripeController.cs` + `StripeProductController.cs`, `Services/Idv/StripeIdvService.cs` (Stripe Identity). Hosted-checkout subscriptions (monthly/yearly; sgd/gbp/usd/eur), webhook `/stripe/webhook` (checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.deleted, invoice.payment_failed). Keys in `StripeCredentialsManager.cs` / appsettings.
* **Platform K** has its own *separate* billing service (`Blockchain/Dev/services/billing`, Node, Stripe test mode) doing credits/bundles for certifications — a duplicate Stripe integration.

## Priority / why not urgent

Payments are **not on Platform K's critical path** (core = Cardano cert: Issue → Verify → Revoke), so this doesn't block stable/testable. Medium. The billing-500-on-bad-input papercut is **dropped** — no point hardening a service that's being consolidated away.

## Action

1. @stuart.jamieson **— please provide the Stripe integration details, or point to where they live:** the company Stripe account/keys (test + live), the subscription/product model, and how Platform K should hook in (share Platform S's billing surface, call its API, or have Platform S own the subscription that covers K usage).
2. Based on that: either **remove/disable** Platform K's `services/billing` (if K stays payment-free) or **wire it to the shared integration**. Also decide whether to keep Platform K billing deployed on dev meanwhile (relates to [KS-96](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-96/8-dev-services-return-502-unreachable)).

**Open question for the team:** is Platform S the single billing surface for the company, with Platform K payment-free (or deferring to the S subscription)?

Filed 2026-05-21.
